name: p-Anisic Acid
description:
p-Anisic Acid (CAS 100-09-4 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3945 designation, is an aromatic organic acid derived from anise that delivers a characteristic sweet, floral-herbal note in flavor and fragrance applications.

It functions as a flavoring agent, mild preservative, and pH modifier across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food manufacturing. In flavor formulations, it contributes anise-like top notes to confectionery and baked goods.

It is also used in beverage products where natural-profile aromatics are required. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative booster and fragrance fixative in creams, lotions, and rinse-off products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing active ingredients and as a mild antimicrobial agent in topical preparations. In food-grade applications, it supports pH regulation in acidified products.

This is particularly useful where both buffering capacity and flavor contribution are commercially desirable. p-Anisic Acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Food and flavor grades conforming to FEMA 3945 standards are the most common commercial forms. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to USP and BP specifications for high-purity requirements.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities for specialty formulators to bulk drum supply for industrial buyers. This ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale manufacturing operations worldwide.

name: Terephthalic acid
description:
Terephthalic acid (CAS 100-21-0 ), commonly abbreviated as PTA in commodity markets, is a dicarboxylic acid that serves as a primary monomer in the production of polyester resins and fibers.

Its role as a building block in high-volume polymer synthesis makes it one of the most traded industrial organic acids globally. This chemical is the foundational raw material for polyethylene terephthalate.

It is consumed in enormous volumes for beverage bottles, food packaging films, and textile-grade polyester fiber. In engineering plastics, it contributes to polybutylene terephthalate formulations.

These formulations are used in automotive and electrical components. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use the acid as a crosslinking monomer in alkyd and powder coating resins.

Controlled molecular architecture is critical to end-product performance in these sectors. Specialty applications include use as a catalyst precursor and pH-buffering agent in select industrial process formulations.

The material is supplied as a white powder or fine crystalline solid. Purified terephthalic acid is the dominant commercial specification for polymer-grade applications in the global market.

Technical and industrial grades are available for non-fiber and non-packaging end uses. Packaging options typically range from multi-wall bags to bulk supersacks for industrial logistics.

This reflects its high-volume commodity status across the chemical supply chain. All batches are tested to ensure they meet rigorous industrial and chemical manufacturing requirements.

name: 2-Diethylethanolamine
description:
2-Diethylethanolamine (CAS 100-37-8 ), also known as DEAE, is an amino alcohol used across industrial and specialty chemical manufacturing as a pH regulator, corrosion inhibitor, and emulsifier.

Its dual amine-alcohol functionality makes it a building block for synthesizing active compounds and a direct-use additive in formulated products. In metalworking and industrial lubricants, DEAE neutralizes acidic byproducts.

This process occurs in cutting fluids and coolants, extending fluid life and protecting ferrous metal surfaces from corrosion. Water treatment programs use it to condition boiler feed water and cooling tower circuits.

By controlling pH, it reduces scale and corrosion in closed-loop systems. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a neutralizing agent for waterborne resin systems, improving dispersion stability and film formation.

This is particularly effective in architectural and industrial paints. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, especially in compounds requiring an aminoethanol backbone.

2-Diethylethanolamine is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial applications.

These applications include coatings, metalworking, and water treatment. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or equivalent specifications is available for API synthesis and regulated manufacturing.

name: Ethylbenzene
description:
Ethylbenzene (CAS 100-41-4 ), commonly abbreviated as EB, is a high-volume aromatic hydrocarbon produced primarily as an intermediate in petrochemical manufacturing. It functions as a solvent and chemical building block across industrial, pharmaceutical, and specialty chemical supply chains.

The dominant industrial use is as a precursor in styrene monomer production, where EB undergoes catalytic dehydrogenation. This makes it a critical procurement target for polymer and resin manufacturers seeking reliable raw material streams.

In solvent applications, it is used in coatings, adhesives, and ink formulations where aromatic solvency and controlled evaporation rate are required. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source EB as a process solvent for active ingredient synthesis and purification steps.

At trace levels, it also appears in flavor and fragrance compounding, where its characteristic aromatic profile contributes to specific formulation targets. This versatility ensures its presence in diverse chemical manufacturing portfolios globally.

Ethylbenzene is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk tanker, ISO container, and drum formats. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 99% to 99.9%+ for demanding synthesis applications.

Buyers in regulated industries may require documentation aligned with pharmaceutical-grade solvent standards such as USP or Ph. Eur. monographs. These quality benchmarks ensure the material meets the rigorous safety and purity requirements of the global market.

name: Styrene
description:
Styrene (CAS 100-42-5 ), also known as vinylbenzene, is a reactive liquid monomer that forms the chemical backbone of a broad range of synthetic polymers and resins.

At trace levels, it also carries FEMA 3233 status as a recognized flavoring agent. Its primary commercial value lies in polymerization, converting into materials for plastics and coatings.

Polystyrene and expanded polystyrene (EPS) production account for the largest share of industrial consumption, supplying rigid packaging, insulation board, and disposable foodservice items.

In coatings and adhesives, styrene copolymerizes with acrylates or butadiene to build binders with controlled hardness. Styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) and latex systems depend on it as a core monomer.

These systems are essential for sealants, carpet backing, and pressure-sensitive adhesives. At food-grade purity, it is used in controlled trace quantities as a flavoring ingredient in approved formulations.

Styrene is supplied as an inhibited liquid, typically stabilized with 4-tert-butylcatechol (TBC) to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transit.

Standard commercial grades include technical-grade and polymer-grade, with purity specifications commonly at 99.5% or higher. Food-grade material meeting FCC standards is available.

name: Benzyl chloride
description:
Benzyl chloride (CAS 100-44-7 ), also known as omega-chlorotoluene, is a reactive chlorinated aromatic compound used as a chemical intermediate and alkylating agent across multiple industrial sectors.

It functions primarily as a building block in the synthesis of a broad range of downstream chemicals, from agrochemicals to pharmaceutical actives. In pharmaceuticals, it serves as a key alkylating intermediate.

This compound is essential in the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients, including antihistamines and analgesics. Agrochemical manufacturers use it to synthesize herbicides, fungicides, and insecticides where benzyl group introduction is required.

In plastics and polymers, it acts as a polymerization initiator and chain modifier, contributing to the production of quaternary ammonium compounds and ion-exchange resins. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

The printing and packaging industry applies it in the manufacture of benzyl-based dyes and pigment intermediates used in inks and coatings. It is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in standard industrial packaging.

Logistics options include drums and ISO tank containers for bulk orders. It is available in technical and high-purity grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ depending on the application.

Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical buyers commonly require certificate of analysis documentation confirming low residual toluene and acid content. Our material meets rigorous industrial and USP or BP standards where applicable.

name: Benzylamine
description:
Benzylamine (CAS 100-46-9 ), also known as BZA, is a primary aromatic amine used as a reactive building block and functional intermediate across chemical manufacturing. It serves as a curing agent, stabilizer, and flavoring precursor depending on the formulation context.

In polymer and rubber processing, BZA acts as a crosslinking agent and curing accelerator, influencing the mechanical properties and durability of finished materials. Flavor chemists use it as a precursor in synthesizing nitrogen-containing aroma compounds.

Controlled reactions yield target flavor profiles for food and beverage applications. In antioxidant formulations, BZA contributes to stabilizer packages that protect polymers from oxidative degradation during processing and end-use.

It also functions as an intermediate in producing pharmaceutically relevant compounds and agrochemical actives. This makes it a sourcing target for fine chemical manufacturers running multi-step synthesis programs.

Benzylamine is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels suited for synthesis and formulation work. Technical grade and reagent grade are the most commonly available specifications for industrial use.

Purity levels range from 98% to 99%+ depending on the intended application and specific manufacturing requirements. Packaging options generally include drums and IBC containers for bulk procurement needs.

name: Benzonitrile
description:
Benzonitrile (CAS 100-47-0 ), also known as phenyl cyanide, is an aromatic nitrile solvent and chemical intermediate used across pharmaceutical synthesis, flavor chemistry, and catalyst manufacturing.

Its role is primarily as a reactive building block and polar aprotic solvent in multi-step organic synthesis. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

This is particularly important where nitrile-to-amine or nitrile-to-amide transformations are required. Flavor and fragrance formulators use it as a precursor to benzylamine derivatives and aromatic aroma compounds.

These compounds are frequently found in finished flavor blends. In catalyst development, it acts as a ligand precursor and stabilizing agent in transition metal catalyst systems, including palladium-based catalysts.

Specialty chemical producers also employ it as a solvent in electrochemical applications and high-polarity reaction media. It is often used where conventional solvents are unsuitable for specific chemical reactions.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from laboratory quantities to bulk drums and IBC containers. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification available.

High-purity grades of 99% or greater are available for pharmaceutical and catalyst applications. Buyers sourcing for regulated end uses should confirm purity certificates and residual impurity profiles with suppliers.

name: 4-cyanopyridine
description:
4-Cyanopyridine (CAS 100-48-1 ), also known as isonicotinic acid nitrile and abbreviated as 4-CP, is a pyridine-based nitrile building block used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a reactive intermediate, enabling the construction of more complex heterocyclic structures through its dual nitrile and pyridine functionalities in various chemical processes.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, 4-CP is a key precursor in the synthesis of antifungal agents, antivirals, and other nitrogen-containing active pharmaceutical ingredients for the global market.

It is used in the production of ligands and coordination complexes that serve as catalysts or catalyst precursors in organometallic chemistry and advanced material science applications.

Agrochemical formulators use it as a building block for pyridine-derived herbicides and fungicides. In flavor chemistry, isonicotinic acid nitrile contributes to select fragrance and flavor compound synthesis.

This is particularly useful where pyridine-ring structures are required. 4-Cyanopyridine is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid for industrial and laboratory use.

Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications suitable for pharmaceutical intermediate and research applications. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale to bulk orders.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for multi-hundred kilogram bulk orders for industrial synthesis. We maintain strict adherence to safety and handling protocols for all chemical shipments.

name: Benzyl alcohol
description:
Benzyl alcohol (CAS 100-51-6 ), also known as phenylmethyl alcohol, is an aromatic alcohol used across pharmaceuticals, personal care, and industrial manufacturing as a solvent and preservative.

Its low volatility and broad solubility profile make it a practical choice where controlled evaporation and compatibility with diverse formulation systems are procurement priorities for manufacturers.

In pharmaceuticals, it functions as a bacteriostatic preservative in injectable formulations and as a solvent for active ingredients in topical preparations. It is a versatile chemical intermediate.

Personal care formulators use it as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products, and as a fragrance component with a mild scent, listed under FEMA 2137 for flavor applications.

Industrial coatings and printing inks rely on it as a slow-evaporating solvent that aids pigment dispersion and improves film formation. In adhesives, it acts as a reactive diluent and processing solvent.

Benzyl alcohol is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tankers. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , covering both regulated and industrial requirements.

Purity levels typically range from 99% for pharmaceutical and food-grade material to lower specifications for technical applications. This ensures compliance with global safety and quality standards.

name: Benzaldehyde
description:
Benzaldehyde (CAS 100-52-7 ), also known as benzoic aldehyde, is the simplest aromatic aldehyde and a primary aroma chemical recognized under FEMA 2127 . It delivers the characteristic bitter almond scent that underpins its commercial value across flavor, fragrance, and synthesis markets.

In industry, it functions as a key intermediate for pharmaceutical synthesis, a flavoring agent, and a reactive building block for polymer and fine chemical production. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to impart almond, cherry, and marzipan flavor profiles.

These applications are common in confectionery, baked goods, and liqueurs. Pharmaceutical producers rely on it as a synthetic intermediate for active ingredients including ampicillin and other semi-synthetic penicillins. It is a vital component in modern medicine production.

In polymer chemistry, it acts as a monomer or chain-transfer agent in certain resin and coating formulations. Personal care formulators incorporate it into perfume compounds and functional fragrance blends where a sharp, almond-floral note is required for the final product.

Benzaldehyde is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is standard for flavor applications, while technical-grade product serves industrial synthesis and polymer uses.

Natural benzaldehyde, derived from bitter almond or stone fruit processing, is available as a distinct commercial grade. This specific grade commands a premium in flavor and fragrance markets due to its natural origin and high purity standards for consumers.

In rubber and tire production, HMTA acts as a vulcanization accelerator and crosslinking agent for resorcinol-based adhesion systems, improving fiber-to-rubber bonding in belts and tires.

Phenolic resin manufacturers use it as the primary curing agent for novolac resins, enabling production of molding compounds, abrasive wheels, and friction materials for industrial use.

In pharmaceuticals, it is used as a urinary tract antiseptic active ingredient and as a tablet excipient under controlled release conditions for various medical applications.

Leather and textile processors apply it as a biocidal preservative and crosslinking agent in tanning and finishing formulations to ensure material durability and resistance.

Hexamine is supplied as a white crystalline powder or compressed tablet form. Standard commercial grades include pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , BP , Ph.Eur. ) and technical-grade material.

In personal care formulations, it encapsulates fragrance compounds and active ingredients, extending scent longevity. It also improves controlled release in skin and hair products while functioning as a dietary fiber ingredient.

In functional food and nutraceutical applications, it supports fat absorption management. Alpha cyclodextrin is supplied as a white crystalline powder available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material.

In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it acts as a boundary lubricant and surface-active additive, reducing friction in cutting fluids and specialty greases. It also serves as a reference standard and biomarker material in analytical research.

Supply purity and traceability are procurement priorities for this material. Pentadecanoic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid or powder. It is available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications for various industrial needs.

High-purity grades of 98 to 99 percent are commonly stocked for analytical and food flavoring applications. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk orders depending on grade and end-use requirements for the chemical industry.

The material meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency in manufacturing. It is essential for developers looking for reliable fatty acid components that provide specific skin-feel modification and chemical stability in diverse environments.

name: Ammonium stearate
description:
Ammonium stearate ( CAS 1002-89-7 ), the ammonium salt of stearic acid, functions as an emulsifier, rheology modifier, and foam control agent across multiple industrial sectors.

It enables stable dispersion of hydrophobic materials in aqueous systems, making it a practical processing aid where pH-sensitive formulations require controlled viscosity and surface activity.

In construction, it is used in waterproofing compounds and masonry treatments where controlled emulsion stability is critical to coating performance for long-term durability.

Rubber and tire manufacturers incorporate it as a processing aid and dispersing agent during compounding, improving filler distribution and surface finish of the final product.

Personal care formulators use it to build viscosity and stabilize emulsions in creams and lotions without relying on synthetic thickeners, ensuring a smooth application profile.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a softening and finishing agent, improving surface feel and aiding uniform dye or coating penetration across the material.

Ammonium stearate is supplied as a paste or aqueous solution, with dry powder or flake forms available for specific applications depending on the manufacturing requirements.

Standard concentrations in solution form typically range around 33–35% active content. Technical and industrial grades are the most common supply specifications for global distribution.

name: Hydrolyzed corn protein
description:
Hydrolyzed corn protein ( CAS 100209-41-4 ), also marketed under the trade name Peptino, is produced by breaking down corn-derived proteins into peptides and amino acids. It functions as a flavor enhancer and moisturizing agent across food manufacturing and personal care formulation.

In savory food production, it delivers umami depth to soups, sauces, seasonings, and processed meat products, reducing the need for added MSG or yeast extracts. This versatile ingredient is essential for modern food science applications.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into hair care and skin care products such as conditioners, serums, and masks. Its peptide fractions improve moisture retention and surface conditioning for high-end personal care lines.

In animal feed applications, it supplies digestible protein fractions that support palatability and amino acid availability in compound feed formulations. This ensures optimal nutrition and growth for various livestock species.

Flavor manufacturers also use it as a base material for producing reaction flavors through Maillard processing. This chemical reaction creates complex profiles necessary for authentic savory and roasted flavor development.

Hydrolyzed corn protein is supplied as a liquid, paste, or spray-dried powder, depending on the intended processing environment. Food-grade specifications are standard, with some grades meeting requirements for clean-label lines.

Buyers should confirm hydrolysis degree, nitrogen content, and sodium levels when evaluating grades for specific formulation targets. Quality control ensures that the product meets the necessary industrial and safety standards.

name: Hydrolysed vegetable protein

Hydrolysed vegetable protein ( CAS 100209-45-8 ), also sold as protein hydrolyzates, vegetable, is produced by breaking down plant-derived proteins into peptides and free amino acids. It delivers a savory, umami-rich taste profile that food manufacturers rely on to build depth of flavor.

In food manufacturing, it functions as a flavor base or enhancer in soups, sauces, gravies, marinades, and snack seasonings. This versatile ingredient reduces the need for added MSG or yeast extracts in various processed and seasoned products.

Meat processors incorporate it into cured and reformed products to reinforce savory notes and improve taste consistency across batches. In animal nutrition, it serves as a highly digestible protein source and palatability enhancer in compound feeds.

It is particularly effective for young livestock and aquaculture diets where feed intake is critical for growth. Formulators in savory snack coatings and dry seasoning blends also use it as a humectant component to support moisture retention.

Hydrolysed vegetable protein is supplied as a brown liquid, paste, or spray-dried powder depending on processing method and end-use requirements. Common source materials include soy, wheat, corn, and pea protein, with the source typically specified.

name: Barium nitrate
description:
Barium nitrate (CAS 10022-31-8 ), also known as barium dinitrate, is an inorganic oxidizing salt used across pyrotechnic, metallurgical, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It delivers controlled oxidation and characteristic green flame coloration.

This material is a critical component in formulations where precise combustion chemistry is required. In aerospace and defense, it serves as a primary oxidizer in signal flares, tracer ammunition, and pyrotechnic delay compositions.

Reliable ignition and burn rate consistency are essential procurement criteria for these applications. The mining industry uses it in blasting agents and detonator compositions, where its oxidizing capacity supports controlled explosive performance.

In metallurgy, it functions as a heat treatment salt bath additive for steel hardening processes. This provides a stable high-temperature oxidizing medium necessary for achieving specific material properties in industrial metalworking.

Specialty glass and optical manufacturing also sources this chemical as a refining agent. It is used to reduce bubbles and improve clarity in finished glass products, ensuring high optical quality for technical glass applications.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with particle size and bulk density varying by grade. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, meeting specifications relevant to pyrotechnic processing.

High-purity grades are available for optical glass and specialty chemical uses where trace metal content must be tightly controlled. These grades ensure the integrity of sensitive chemical reactions and high-end manufacturing outputs.

name: Heptyl glucoside
description:
Heptyl glucoside (CAS 100231-64-9 ) is a mild, plant-derived nonionic surfactant produced by combining glucose with a seven-carbon fatty alcohol. It belongs to the alkyl polyglucoside family, a class recognized for skin compatibility and biodegradability.

This chemical profile makes it highly attractive to formulators sourcing alternatives to conventional surfactants. In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in facial cleansers, shampoos, and body washes.

Low irritation potential is a formulation priority for these applications. Home care and industrial cleaning products use it to boost soil removal and grease dispersion across a wide range of pH conditions.

Its foam-modulating behavior makes it useful in controlled-foam formulations such as liquid detergents and rinse-aid systems. In food-contact applications, its bio-based origin supports sustainability criteria.

Heptyl glucoside is typically supplied as a liquid or aqueous solution, with concentration levels varying by manufacturer. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades for various industrial needs.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity standards relevant to personal care manufacturing. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) depending on the specific order volume required.

name: Nitrous oxide
description:
Nitrous oxide (CAS 10024-97-2 ), also known as E942 and commonly referenced as N2O, is a compressed gas used across pharmaceutical manufacturing and food processing as an aerosol propellant and packaging medium.

Its rapid solubility and inert behavior under pressure make it a preferred choice where product integrity and contamination control are critical sourcing criteria for industrial and medical applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, nitrous oxide is used as a carrier gas and propellant in metered-dose inhalers and topical aerosol formulations. The food industry relies on this gas as a pressurizing agent.

It is used in whipped cream dispensers and other pressurized food-grade packaging, where it dissolves into fat-based products without imparting off-flavors or altering the chemical profile of the contents.

Medical and dental facilities source it as an inhalation analgesic for procedural sedation, requiring pharmaceutical-grade supply with stringent purity documentation and safety certifications for patient use.

It also functions as a specialty oxidizer in certain analytical and combustion processes. Nitrous oxide is supplied as a liquefied compressed gas in cylinders and bulk dewars for various volume needs.

Fill quantities range from small laboratory cylinders to large-volume industrial supply. Recognized grades include pharmaceutical ( Ph. Eur. , USP ), food-grade ( FCC , E942-compliant), and technical grade.

Grade selection directly affects documentation requirements, so buyers should confirm intended application before specifying supply. This ensures compliance with regional safety and quality regulations.

name: Disulfur dichloride
description:
Disulfur dichloride (CAS 10025-67-9 ), also known as Sulphur Monochloride or S2Cl2, is a reactive sulfur chloride compound used industrially as a cross-linking agent and chemical intermediate.

It functions primarily as a vulcanizing agent in rubber processing and as a precursor in synthesis and catalytic applications. In rubber and tire manufacturing, S2Cl2 cold-vulcanizes natural and synthetic rubber.

This process occurs at low temperatures, enabling processing of heat-sensitive articles such as thin-walled goods and surgical items. In agrochemical production, it serves as an intermediate in synthesizing sulfur-containing pesticides.

It is also used for crop protection compounds. Mining and metallurgical operations use it in the extraction and refining of certain metals, particularly in chlorination-based processes for recovering platinum group metals.

It also functions as a reagent and catalyst precursor in organic synthesis, facilitating the introduction of sulfur and chlorine functionalities into target molecules. This makes it a versatile tool for chemical plants.

Disulfur dichloride is supplied as an amber to yellow fuming liquid, typically in drum or IBC packaging suited to its highly reactive nature. It is available in technical grade for various industrial uses.

Purity specifications commonly range from 95% to 98% depending on the intended application. Buyers should confirm stabilizer content and moisture levels, as these affect reactivity and shelf life in downstream processes.

name: Stannous chloride dihydrate
description:
Stannous chloride dihydrate (CAS 10025-69-1 ), also known as tin dichloride, is a tin(II) salt used across industrial manufacturing as a reducing agent, catalyst, and surface treatment chemical.

Its ability to donate electrons in controlled reactions makes it a practical choice for processes requiring metal deposition, dye fixation, or polymer stabilization in various sectors.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a mordant to fix dyes onto fiber substrates, improving color fastness and uniformity in finished goods during the manufacturing cycle.

Printed circuit board and electroplating operations use it as a tin source and reducing agent for sensitizing non-conductive surfaces prior to the critical metallization phase.

In plastics and polymer production, it functions as a catalyst precursor for polymerization reactions and as a stabilizer component in PVC formulations for industrial applications.

Paper and packaging manufacturers apply it in flame-retardant treatments, where it contributes to reduced combustibility in coated substrates and specialized paper products.

Stannous chloride dihydrate is supplied as white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and reagent grade, with purity levels ranging from 98% to 99%+.

Some suppliers offer it to ACS or BP specifications depending on the end-use requirement. This ensures the material meets the necessary chemical standards for your specific facility.

name: Antimony trichloride
description:
Antimony trichloride (CAS 10025-91-9 ) is an inorganic antimony salt used industrially as a catalyst and flame retardant precursor. It functions as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of antimony-based compounds.

This chemical acts as a Lewis acid catalyst in organic and polymer chemistry. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it serves as a precursor to antimony trioxide, which is incorporated into flame retardant systems.

These systems are essential for PET, polyolefins, and engineering resins. Electronics manufacturers use antimony trichloride-derived compounds in the treatment of circuit board substrates and semiconductor components.

These applications require controlled flame retardancy for safety and performance. In metalworking and surface finishing, it is applied in bluing and browning formulations for steel to produce protective layers.

These oxide layers provide durability on various metal surfaces. Lewis acid catalysis applications include Friedel-Crafts type reactions and chlorination processes in specialty chemical production facilities.

The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow crystalline solid or in molten form for bulk transfer. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for most industrial buyers.

Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5% depending on the specific batch. Packaging options commonly include drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to moisture-sensitive materials.

name: Zirconium tetrachloride
description:
Zirconium tetrachloride (CAS 10026-11-6 ), also referred to as ZrCl4 or zirconium chloride, is an inorganic salt used as a catalyst and chemical intermediate across metallurgical and electronic manufacturing processes.

It serves as a primary precursor for producing high-purity zirconium compounds and advanced zirconium-based materials. In catalyst manufacturing, it is a key starting material for Ziegler-Natta systems.

These systems are used in polyolefin production, where it initiates controlled polymerization of ethylene and propylene. Electronics manufacturers rely on it as a precursor for zirconium oxide thin films.

These films are deposited via CVD and ALD processes in semiconductor fabrication. In the metals industry, it functions as an intermediate in the production of zirconium metal and zirconium sponge.

This occurs through reduction processes. Specialty chemical producers also use it to synthesize organozirconium compounds and coordination complexes for research and various industrial applications.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granular solid. It is available in technical and high-purity grades, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.9%+.

These high-purity options are ideal for semiconductor and catalyst applications. Packaging options generally include sealed, moisture-resistant containers due to its reactivity with atmospheric humidity.

name: Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate

It functions primarily as a cobalt source in catalyst preparation, micronutrient formulations, and surface treatment processes. In agriculture, it is incorporated into trace element fertilizers and animal feed supplements.

This product is used to correct cobalt deficiency in soils and livestock, particularly in ruminant nutrition programs. Catalyst manufacturers use it as a cobalt precursor in the production of hydroprocessing catalysts.

In Fischer-Tropsch catalysts, controlled cobalt loading is critical to performance. In the ceramics and pigment industries, it serves as a raw material for cobalt-based colorants applied to glass, glazes, and specialty coatings.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators source it as a cobalt intermediate where precise metal content and low impurity profiles are required. Cobalt nitrate hexahydrate is supplied as red-pink crystalline granules or flakes.

Battery and electroplating industries use it as a cobalt source in electrodeposition baths and as a precursor in the synthesis of cobalt-based cathode materials. These applications are critical for the production of modern energy storage systems.

name: Nickel fluoride
description:
Nickel fluoride (CAS 10028-18-9 ), commonly referenced as NiF2, is an inorganic nickel salt used across specialty chemical manufacturing and surface treatment processes. It functions primarily as a fluorinating agent and catalyst precursor.

The material also serves as a surface modification additive in industrial and technical applications. In metal finishing and coatings, NiF2 is used to produce fluoride-containing nickel plating baths and conversion coatings.

These coatings improve corrosion resistance on substrate surfaces. As a catalyst precursor, it is incorporated into fluorination reactions and hydrogenation processes where controlled nickel activity is required for the reaction.

In specialty adhesive and sealant formulations, it contributes to surface wetting and adhesion promotion on difficult-to-bond substrates. This makes it a versatile component in high-performance industrial bonding.

Limited use exists in antimicrobial and preservation applications within industrial formulations where biocidal metal ion activity is relevant. Nickel fluoride is supplied as a crystalline powder or anhydrous solid.

Particle size and purity specifications vary by application requirement. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with high-purity grades available for catalyst and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Buyers typically source this material in kilogram to metric ton quantities depending on process scale and consumption rates. It remains a critical component for manufacturers requiring precise fluoride and nickel delivery.

name: Ferric sulfate
description:
Ferric sulfate (CAS 10028-22-5 ), also supplied as ferric sulfate anhydrous, is an iron-based inorganic salt used industrially as a coagulant, oxidizing agent, and catalyst precursor across water treatment, mining, and chemical processing sectors.

Its ability to precipitate dissolved contaminants and facilitate metal leaching drives demand across multiple process industries. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it functions as a primary coagulant to remove suspended solids.

The compound is highly effective at removing phosphates and heavy metals from effluent streams. Hydrometallurgical operations use it to oxidize sulfide ores during heap leaching, particularly in copper and gold recovery processes.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a mordant and fixative to bind dyes to fiber substrates, improving color fastness and consistency. This ensures high-quality results in large-scale manufacturing environments.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an astringent and hemostatic agent in topical formulations. It also serves as a catalyst precursor in select organic synthesis routes for specialized chemical production.

Ferric sulfate is available as a granular solid, powder, or concentrated aqueous solution. Standard technical and industrial grades are the most common supply forms for bulk industrial procurement and logistics.

Solution concentrations typically range from 40–50% by weight for water treatment applications. Purity specifications vary by end use, with higher-purity grades available for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical applications.

description:

name: Hydrogenated palm stearin
description:
Hydrogenated palm stearin (CAS 100298-99-5 ), also supplied under the designation glycerides, mixed hydrogenated palm kernel-oil stearin and hydrogenated palm-oil, is a fully or partially hydrogenated solid fat derived from the stearin fraction of palm oil.

It functions as a structuring agent and emulsifier across food, personal care, and industrial formulations where controlled melting behavior and solid fat content are critical to product performance.

In food manufacturing, it provides the solid fat structure required in shortenings, margarines, and bakery fats where precise plasticity and stability at ambient temperatures determine shelf life and texture.

Personal care formulators use it to build body and consistency in stick products, balms, and cream formulations where a clean melt point and skin-feel are key selection criteria for the final product.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a rheology modifier to control viscosity, set speed, and film hardness. It also functions as a release agent and processing aid in confectionery and industrial applications.

These applications rely on controlled slip and non-tack properties. Hydrogenated palm stearin is supplied as a solid, typically in flake, pastille, or block form, with iodine value and slip melting point specifications.

Specifications vary by grade to meet specific industrial needs. Food-grade material is available to meet standard industry specifications for edible fats. Technical grades are offered for industrial coatings and adhesives.

These technical grades are also suitable for elastomer applications. The material ensures consistent performance across a wide range of manufacturing environments and specialized chemical processing requirements.

name: Isothiazolinone
description:
Isothiazolinone (CAS 1003-07-2 ), also referred to as 3-Isothiazolone, is the core heterocyclic scaffold underlying a broad class of industrial biocides and preservatives.

It functions as the active structural basis for formulated antimicrobial agents used across water-based systems, personal care products, and industrial process fluids.

In personal care and cosmetics, isothiazolinone-based actives are incorporated into rinse-off and leave-on formulations to control microbial growth and extend shelf life.

Pulp and paper manufacturers use isothiazolinone chemistry to prevent slime-forming bacteria and fungi in process water and coating systems for industrial use.

In metalworking and lubricant fluids, it controls microbial contamination that would otherwise degrade fluid performance and corrode equipment during manufacturing.

Water treatment and oil and gas operations rely on isothiazolinone-derived biocides to manage biofilm formation in cooling towers, injection water, and produced water streams.

Isothiazolinone is supplied as a technical-grade material, typically as a liquid concentrate or aqueous solution, and is commonly blended into formulated biocide products.

Concentration levels in commercial blends vary depending on the target application and regulatory requirements. Technical-grade specifications are standard for industrial supply.

name: 2-bromothiophene
description:

It serves as a reactive intermediate for introducing the thiophene scaffold into complex organic molecules through cross-coupling and metal-catalyzed reactions in various industrial settings.

In pharmaceutical development, this compound is a key precursor for active pharmaceutical ingredients where the thiophene ring is a core structural element, including antifungal and antihistamine compounds.

Flavor and fragrance chemists use it to access thienyl-containing aroma compounds through further functionalization. It participates in Suzuki, Kumada, and Negishi coupling reactions for advanced intermediates.

Specialty chemical producers also use it as a starting material for liquid crystal components and conducting polymer monomers, supporting innovation in agrochemical and materials science applications.

The product is supplied as a liquid in standard commercial quantities ranging from laboratory-scale packaging to bulk drums. Technical and high-purity grades are available for diverse industrial needs.

It reacts with sodium bicarbonate to produce CO₂ during mixing, giving formulators precise control over dough rise and texture. Food manufacturers incorporate it as an acidulant and buffering agent.

It is frequently utilized in tablet and mineral supplement formulations. Agricultural buyers source MCP as a soluble phosphorus fertilizer component, particularly in fertigation systems and compound production.

name: Copper nitrate trihydrate
description:

These catalysts are used in hydrogenation, oxidation, and exhaust gas treatment systems. Textile and leather processors apply it in dyeing and tanning operations, where it acts as a mordant to fix colorants and improve wash fastness.

In printed circuit board and metal finishing operations, it supports etching, patination, and surface oxidation treatments on copper and copper alloys. This versatility makes it essential for modern electronics manufacturing.

Agricultural formulators use it as a copper-source micronutrient in foliar sprays and soil correction products targeting copper-deficient crops. It ensures healthy plant growth and improves overall yield in various farming sectors.

Copper nitrate trihydrate is supplied as blue crystalline granules or powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with laboratory-grade material available for catalyst and analytical applications.

Bulk supply is common in 25 kg bags or drums, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+. The material must be stored in a cool, dry area away from combustible materials due to its oxidizing properties.

name: Calcium sulfate hemihydrate
description:
Calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CAS 10034-76-1 ), also known as gypsum hemihydrate, is a partially dehydrated calcium sulfate produced by controlled calcination of natural gypsum.

It reacts with water to form a rigid, dimensionally stable set mass, making it a core binder and setting agent across construction, industrial, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

In building and construction, it is the primary binder in plaster, drywall compounds, and prefabricated gypsum boards, where controlled set time and surface hardness are critical.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet diluent and binder, where its compressibility and inert profile support high-volume solid dosage production for various medications.

In pulp and paper operations, it functions as a filler and surface treatment agent to improve sheet formation, opacity, and printability for high-quality paper products.

Dental and orthopedic casting applications also rely on it for precision mold fabrication, where dimensional accuracy after setting is the primary requirement for the user.

The material is supplied as a fine white powder in both alpha and beta crystal forms, with alpha-hemihydrate offering higher density and compressive strength than the beta form.

Standard grades include USP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade ( FCC ) for regulated applications, alongside technical and construction grades for industrial use.

description:

name: Sodium hypophosphite monohydrate
description:
Sodium hypophosphite monohydrate (CAS 10039-56-2 ) is the stable, water-soluble hydrated salt form of sodium hypophosphite, supplied commercially for use as a reducing agent and catalyst component across multiple industrial sectors.

It functions primarily as a chemical reducing agent in electroless metal plating and as a process aid in textile and polymer manufacturing. In electronics manufacturing, it acts as the primary reducing agent in electroless nickel plating baths.

This material deposits uniform nickel coatings onto substrates regardless of geometry. Textile processors use it as a catalyst activator in flame-retardant finishing treatments, particularly in durable press and phosphorus-based flame-retardant systems.

These systems are frequently applied to cotton fabrics for safety. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an antioxidant stabilizer and reducing agent in certain formulations where oxygen-sensitive active ingredients require protection.

Water treatment applications include its use as a sequestering agent to control metal ion activity and inhibit scale formation in industrial process water systems. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of industrial equipment.

Sodium hypophosphite monohydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical or reagent grade, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Bulk supply is available in bags or drums, with pharmaceutical-grade material supplied to USP or BP specifications where required. This ensures compliance with international quality and safety standards.

name: Ceramides
description:
Ceramides (CAS 100403-19-8 ), commercially known as Ceramide NP , Ceramide IIIB, and CER NP, are sphingolipid-based actives that restore and reinforce the skin's natural lipid barrier.

They are a primary ingredient class in premium skincare and pharmaceutical topical formulations where barrier repair and moisture retention are the core performance targets for the end user.

In moisturizers, serums, and barrier creams, Ceramide NP replenishes depleted intercellular lipids in the stratum corneum, directly addressing dry, compromised, or aging skin conditions effectively.

Dermatological formulations for eczema and atopic dermatitis rely on ceramide-based systems to restore the lipid matrix disrupted by these conditions and improve overall patient outcomes.

In prestige and clinical skincare lines, Ceramide NP is frequently combined with cholesterol and fatty acids in a defined molar ratio to replicate the natural lamellar structure of skin lipids.

Hair care products, particularly conditioning treatments and bond-repair systems, use ceramides to smooth the cuticle layer and reduce moisture loss along the hair shaft for better texture.

Ceramide NP is supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher.

Synthetic and plant-derived variants are both commercially available, and grade selection is a key sourcing decision for formulators targeting clean-label or vegan positioning in the market.

name: Docusate
description:
Docusate (CAS 10041-19-7 ), also known as dioctyl sodium sulfosuccinate (DOSS), is an anionic surfactant used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial cleaning markets.

It functions primarily as a wetting agent, emulsifier, and dispersant, lowering surface tension to improve the penetration and spreadability of formulations in various chemical applications.

In pharmaceuticals, docusate is used as a stool softener excipient and as a solubilizing agent in oral and topical drug formulations. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into shampoos and conditioners.

It is also used in skin cleansers where it improves ingredient dispersion and enhances product texture. Industrial and institutional cleaning products rely on it to boost the wetting of active agents.

In paper and leather processing, it acts as a dispersant to improve dye uptake and surface treatment uniformity. Docusate is commercially available as a liquid or waxy solid depending on the form.

Sodium, calcium, and potassium salts are the most common counterion forms. Pharmaceutical-grade material is supplied to USP and BP specifications for high-purity manufacturing requirements.

Technical-grade material serves industrial cleaning and textile applications where standard performance is needed. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers for bulk procurement needs.

name: Hydroxyethyl-2-nitro-p-toluidine
description:
Hydroxyethyl-2-nitro-p-toluidine (CAS 100418-33-5 ), also known as 4-(2-Hydroxyethylamino)-3-nitrotoluene, is a nitroaniline-derived colorant intermediate used in the production of dyes and pigments for industrial coloring applications.

Its hydroxyethyl functional group enables reactive bonding to substrates, making it relevant to surface modification processes across several manufacturing sectors. In textile dyeing, it functions as a precursor or coupling component.

It is used in the synthesis of azo dyes applied to fiber substrates, contributing to depth of shade and wash fastness. Leather finishing operations use nitroaniline-based colorants of this type to achieve uniform surface coloration.

In the printing and packaging industry, it supports the formulation of specialty inks where reactive dye chemistry is required for adhesion to coated or treated surfaces. This ensures high-quality results on various materials.

Paper manufacturers incorporate such intermediates into surface treatment processes to achieve tinted or colored paper grades with consistent tone. This chemical is essential for maintaining color uniformity in large-scale production.

Hydroxyethyl-2-nitro-p-toluidine is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline material. It is available primarily in technical grade, suited for industrial dye synthesis and colorant manufacturing processes.

Packaging is commonly offered in kilogram-scale quantities for laboratory and pilot use, with bulk options available for production-scale procurement. This flexibility supports both research and industrial applications.

name: Strontium nitrate
description:
Strontium nitrate (CAS 10042-76-9 ) is an inorganic salt supplying both strontium and nitrate ions to industrial formulations and pyrotechnic compositions. It is the primary oxidizer responsible for producing a characteristic crimson flame in signal flares and fireworks.

Procurement demand for this chemical spans defense contracting, specialty chemical manufacturing, and corrosion protection applications. In pyrotechnics and defense, it functions as the oxidizing agent in red signal flares and tracer ammunition.

Military illumination rounds utilize this compound where consistent burn characteristics are a qualification requirement. Automotive airbag inflator formulations have historically incorporated it as an oxidizer component in gas-generating propellant mixtures.

Corrosion-inhibiting primers for aerospace aluminum substrates use this material as an active pigment. It is frequently used to replace chromate-based systems in compliant coating formulations to meet modern environmental standards.

In the textile and paper sectors, it is used in specialty flame-retardant treatments where halogen-free chemistry is required. This versatility makes it a critical component across several diverse manufacturing and safety industries.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 99% to 99.5% on a dry basis for industrial use.

Packaging is available in bags and bulk quantities suited to industrial-scale consumption. Our supply chain ensures that the material meets rigorous safety and handling protocols required for high-purity inorganic nitrates.

name: Aluminum sulfate
description:
Aluminum sulfate (CAS 10043-01-3 ), commonly known as alum, is an inorganic salt used across municipal and industrial sectors primarily as a coagulant and flocculant. It destabilizes suspended particles in water and process streams, enabling their removal through settling or filtration.

In water and wastewater treatment, this chemical is dosed into raw water to aggregate colloidal solids, turbidity, and organic matter ahead of clarification stages. This process is essential for ensuring high-quality output in municipal systems.

Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it to size paper with rosin, improving water resistance and controlling fiber retention on the wire. This application remains a cornerstone of the industrial manufacturing process for various paper grades.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a mordant and tanning auxiliary, fixing dyes and preparing hides for further treatment. These properties make it indispensable for achieving consistent color and texture in finished goods.

Building and construction applications include use as a set accelerator in concrete and cement formulations, reducing cure time under controlled conditions. This allows for faster project completion and improved structural integrity in specific environments.

The product is supplied as granules, powder, and liquid solution, with the anhydrous and hydrated forms both commercially available. Standard grades include technical, water treatment, and paper-grade specifications to meet diverse needs.

Purity and iron content are tightly controlled depending on the end use to ensure compliance with industrial requirements. Bulk supply in dry or liquid form is standard for high-volume water treatment and industrial buyers globally.

name: Boron nitride
description:
Boron nitride (CAS 10043-11-5 ) is a synthetic inorganic compound produced in both hexagonal and cubic crystalline forms. In personal care and industrial applications, it functions as a dry lubricant and texture modifier.

It also serves as a thermal management material depending on the grade and structure selected. In cosmetics and personal care, hexagonal BN is used as a slip agent and soft-focus pigment in pressed powders.

It is frequently found in foundations and eyeshadows, where it improves skin feel and light diffusion without adding color. Cubic boron nitride is used in cutting tools and abrasive wheels for high-precision machining.

This material is ideal for hardened metals where diamond tooling is unsuitable. In biotechnology and life sciences, BN-based coatings are evaluated for biocompatible surface applications and thermal interface materials.

These materials are also used in laboratory and diagnostic equipment. High-purity hexagonal grades serve as mold release agents and lubricants in high-temperature ceramic and metal processing operations.

The product is supplied as a fine white powder, with hexagonal and cubic forms available depending on the intended application. Cosmetic-grade h-BN is offered at defined particle size distributions.

These distributions are specifically suited to skin-contact formulations. Technical and high-purity grades are available for industrial, electronic, and advanced materials applications across various sectors.

name: Boric acid
description:
Boric acid (CAS 10043-35-3 ), also known as boracic acid and approved as food preservative E284 , is an inorganic boron compound sourced for its buffering and biocidal functions.

It acts as a pH buffer, preservative, and fire-suppressing agent depending on the application and concentration. Procurement teams across multiple sectors source it as a cost-effective, multifunctional mineral input.

In glass fiber and fiberglass manufacturing, it lowers melt viscosity and improves tensile strength in the final reinforcement product. Textile and leather processors apply it as a flame retardant finish and mold inhibitor.

Wood treatment and building products manufacturers use it to protect timber against fungi, insects, and fire. This is often done in combination with other boron salts to ensure long-term structural integrity and safety.

In personal care and pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a pH buffer and mild preservative in topical formulations and ophthalmic solutions. It is valued for its stability and compatibility with various ingredients.

Boric acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granular forms preferred for dust-sensitive handling. Standard commercial grades include technical, USP , BP , and Ph. Eur.

Food-grade material is available to E284 specification for permitted preservation uses. Bulk supply is typically offered in 25 kg bags or big bags, with purity levels commonly at 99.5% or higher for industrial use.

name: Calcium chloride
description:
Calcium chloride (CAS 10043-52-4 ), also known by its food designation E509 , is an inorganic salt sourced for its rapid moisture absorption and exothermic dissolution.

It provides strong ionic activity across industrial and food-grade applications. It functions as a desiccant, de-icer, accelerant, and preservative depending on the specific sector and formulation.

In road and pavement maintenance, it is applied as a dust suppressant and de-icing agent. It performs at lower temperatures than competing salts to ensure safety and infrastructure longevity.

Oil and gas operators use it to formulate dense brine solutions for wellbore stabilization and completion fluids. This ensures efficient drilling operations in challenging geological environments.

Food manufacturers rely on this compound as a firming agent in canned vegetables and tofu production. It is also essential for cheese coagulation processes to maintain texture and quality.

In concrete and construction, it accelerates cement hydration to shorten setting times in cold-weather pours. This allows for faster project completion and improved structural integrity.

The product is supplied as white flakes, pellets, powder, and liquid solution. Common solution concentrations are 32–38% for industrial use, while solid forms are available at 74–80% and 94–97% purity.

Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical grade. Food and pharmaceutical grades meet stricter limits on heavy metals and impurities to ensure safety and compliance.

name: Potassium aluminium sulfate
description:
Potassium aluminium sulfate (CAS 10043-67-1 ), commercially known as potassium alum and approved as E522 , is an inorganic double salt used across food, water treatment, and industrial processing.

It functions primarily as a coagulant, astringent, and pH buffer, with performance characteristics that suit both regulated food-grade and heavy-duty industrial applications. In water treatment, it acts as a flocculant to aggregate particles.

This process clarifies drinking water and wastewater streams effectively. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a firming agent and leavening component in baked goods, pickled products, and starch-based formulations.

Tanneries and leather processors apply it as a primary tanning and preserving agent. Its astringent action fixes hides without the environmental burden of chromium-based alternatives, making it a preferred choice in the industry.

In textile dyeing, it functions as a mordant to bond dyes to natural fibers, improving wash fastness and color consistency. Potassium aluminium sulfate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as larger crystals.

Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical-grade, with anhydrous and dodecahydrate forms both available commercially. Buyers typically specify grade and crystal size based on dissolution rate requirements.

The material is also available in compliance with Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , and ACS standards upon request. These quality benchmarks ensure the product meets the rigorous safety and purity needs of global chemical markets.

Contact us for supply of Potassium aluminium sulfate

name: Magnesium phosphate
description:
Magnesium phosphate (CAS 10043-83-1 ), also known as newberyite in its mineral form, is an inorganic salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural industries as a pH buffer and stabilizer.

It regulates acidity in formulations and provides a bioavailable source of both magnesium and phosphate in nutritional applications. In food manufacturing, it functions as a buffering agent and anti-caking additive.

This compound is frequently utilized in dry blends, baked goods, and dietary supplements. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an excipient in tablet and capsule production, where controlled pH and mineral content are critical.

In agriculture and animal feed, it supplies essential magnesium and phosphorus to correct soil deficiencies and support livestock nutrition. Water treatment operations apply it to adjust pH and inhibit scale formation.

Magnesium phosphate is supplied as a white powder or granules depending on the intended application. Food-grade and USP / BP grades are available for nutritional and pharmaceutical use.

Technical-grade material serves industrial and agricultural markets. Packaging options typically range from small bags to bulk quantities to accommodate both formulation-scale and large-volume procurement needs.

name: Ferric phosphate
description:
Ferric phosphate (CAS 10045-86-0 ), also known as iron phosphate and FePO4, is an inorganic iron salt used across food, agricultural, and industrial applications. It functions primarily as an iron source in nutritional fortification and as a coagulant in water treatment.

In food manufacturing, ferric phosphate is used to fortify cereals, infant formula, and flour with bioavailable iron without altering taste or color. This provides a key advantage over other iron salts in sensitive formulations.

In agriculture, it is the active ingredient in approved molluscicide pellets used to control slugs and snails in crop protection programs. Water treatment facilities use it as a coagulant and flocculant to remove phosphorus from effluents.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it as an iron supplement ingredient in tablet and capsule formulations targeting iron deficiency. It is supplied as a fine powder or micronized powder depending on the intended application.

Food-grade and USP / BP grades are available for nutritional and pharmaceutical use, while technical-grade material is supplied for agricultural and water treatment applications. Purity levels and particle size specifications vary by grade.

Buyers should confirm compliance requirements before sourcing to ensure the material meets specific industry needs. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale industrial and food production requirements.

name: Chlorine dioxide
description:
Chlorine dioxide (CAS 10049-04-4 ), also known commercially as Alcide, is a selective oxidizing biocide used across water treatment, food processing, and industrial sanitation. Unlike chlorine-based alternatives, it remains effective across a broad pH range.

This stability makes it a preferred active in systems where consistent microbial control is critical. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it disinfects distribution systems and controls biofilm without generating trihalomethanes.

Food processing facilities use it to sanitize surfaces, equipment, and wash water for fresh produce, poultry, and seafood. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it as a bleaching agent to brighten cellulose fibers effectively.

This application minimizes fiber degradation compared to elemental chlorine. In pharmaceutical and healthcare environments, it functions as a sporicidal agent for cleanroom decontamination and hard surface disinfection.

Chlorine dioxide is supplied as an aqueous solution or generated on-site from precursor systems, as the pure gas is unstable for bulk transport. Stabilized solution concentrates are available for dilution prior to use.

These concentrates are suitable for food-grade and industrial applications. Grades are available to meet food processing compliance requirements, with technical-grade solutions supplied for industrial water treatment and pulp bleaching.

name: Potassium peroxymonosulfate
description:
Potassium peroxymonosulfate (CAS 10058-23-8 ), commercially recognized as Oxone, is a dry, stable oxidizing agent used across industrial and specialty applications. Unlike liquid peroxide systems, it delivers controlled oxidation in solid form.

This material is highly practical for formulated products and process chemicals where handling and shelf life matter. In water treatment, it serves as a non-chlorine shock oxidizer for pools and municipal systems.

It effectively breaks down organic contaminants without the byproduct concerns associated with chlorine. Electronics manufacturers rely on it as a microetch and circuit board cleaner for precision manufacturing.

The compound selectively removes copper oxides and prepares surfaces for plating. Personal care formulators incorporate it into denture cleansers and hair color activators for its reliable oxidizing action.

It delivers bleaching and sanitizing performance in dry tablet or powder formats. Pulp, paper, and textile processors use it for bleaching and biocidal treatment where chlorine-free processing is required.

The product is supplied as a white granular or powder solid, typically as a triple salt compound. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering for most large-scale operations.

Specifications vary by active oxygen content to meet specific industrial needs. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on the application volume and storage requirements.

name: Iron pyrophosphate
description:
Iron pyrophosphate (CAS 10058-44-3 ), also recognized commercially as ferric pyrophosphate, is an inorganic iron salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural markets as a bioavailable iron source and mineral supplement.

Unlike many iron compounds, it delivers iron with minimal organoleptic impact, making it a preferred choice where taste and color neutrality matter. In food fortification, it is incorporated into infant formulas and breakfast cereals.

It is used in flour to meet iron enrichment targets without discoloring or imparting metallic off-notes to the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in iron-deficiency treatments, including oral supplements.

In micronized form, it is utilized in intravenous dialysis solutions. In animal nutrition, it functions as a mineral premix component for livestock and poultry feed, supporting iron status in production animals.

Flame retardant formulations also incorporate this compound as a char-promoting additive in polymer systems where halogen-free performance is required. It is supplied as a fine powder for various industrial uses.

Micronized grades are available for applications requiring enhanced dispersibility and bioavailability. Standard grades include food-grade and USP / Ph.Eur. specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher.

Packaging ranges from small pharmaceutical-grade quantities to bulk industrial volumes. This versatile mineral source ensures high stability and performance across diverse manufacturing sectors and global supply chains.

name: Hydrolyzed wheat gluten
description:
Hydrolyzed wheat gluten (CAS 100684-25-1 ), also referenced commercially as wheat gluten hydrolyzate, is a protein-derived ingredient produced by breaking down wheat gluten into shorter peptide chains and free amino acids.

It functions as a functional protein additive across food manufacturing and personal care formulation, delivering emulsification, film-forming, and texture-modifying performance for various industrial applications.

In food production, it improves dough strength, water retention, and crumb structure in baked goods, and acts as a flavor precursor in savory seasonings and processed meat systems for manufacturers.

Formulators use it in plant-based protein products to enhance binding and mouthfeel without synthetic additives. In personal care, it is incorporated into shampoos, conditioners, and leave-in treatments.

The hydrolyzed peptides bond to hair fiber, improving tensile strength and surface smoothness. Skin care formulators also use it as a film-former in serums and masks targeting elasticity and moisture retention.

Hydrolyzed wheat gluten is supplied as a spray-dried powder or as a liquid concentrate, with powder being the dominant commercial form for food and cosmetic applications in the global market.

Food-grade specifications are standard, with some suppliers offering material compliant with FCC or kosher/halal certification requirements to meet strict international regulatory standards.

Molecular weight fractions vary by degree of hydrolysis, a key specification buyers should confirm for targeted application performance when sourcing this ingredient for specific chemical formulations.

name: Hydrogenated vegetable oil glycerides
description:
Hydrogenated vegetable oil glycerides (CAS 100684-29-5 ), also marketed as vegetable-oil glycerides hydrogenated, are derived from the controlled hydrogenation of plant-based oils.

This process produces a stable, solid-to-semi-solid fat fraction. The resulting material functions as a multi-role functional ingredient across food manufacturing, cosmetic formulation, and industrial lubrication.

In food production, these glycerides act as structuring agents and emulsifiers in shortenings, margarine, and bakery fats. They improve texture and extend shelf stability in various applications.

Cosmetic formulators use them to build viscosity and provide emollient body in creams, balms, and stick formats. A controlled melt profile is commercially important for these personal care products.

In personal care emulsions, they support oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems. They stabilize the interface and reduce phase separation over time to ensure a high-quality finished product.

Industrial lubricant manufacturers incorporate them as base components or additives in food-grade and biodegradable formulations. This is essential where plant-derived content is a sourcing requirement.

These glycerides are supplied as flakes, pastilles, or solid blocks. Some suppliers offer material compliant with Ph.Eur. or USP monographs for pharmaceutical excipient use.

Iodine value and melting point ranges vary by grade. Buyers typically specify these parameters when qualifying supply to ensure the material meets their specific manufacturing needs.

name: Decaglyceryl dipalmitate
description:
Decaglyceryl dipalmitate (CAS 100895-09-8 ), also supplied under the trade name Polyaldo 10-2P and identified as Polyglyceryl-10 dipalmitate, is a polyglycerol ester of palmitic acid used as an emulsifier and texture modifier across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

Its high hydrophilic character positions it as an oil-in-water emulsifier suited to applications where clean-label or mild surfactant options are required. In food manufacturing, it stabilizes emulsions in low-fat spreads, dressings, and bakery fillings.

Consistent texture and shelf stability are critical purchasing criteria for these applications. Cosmetic formulators use it to build stable oil-in-water creams and lotions, where it also contributes moisturizing performance by supporting the skin barrier within the emulsion matrix.

In leave-on and rinse-off personal care products, it helps control viscosity and improve sensory profile without relying on ethoxylated surfactants. Coatings and adhesive applications utilize it as a dispersing and wetting agent for pigment and filler systems.

Decaglyceryl dipalmitate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or flake. Food-grade material is available meeting standard polyglycerol ester specifications for use in regulated food applications, and cosmetic-grade material is offered for personal care manufacturing.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on the supplier. This versatile ingredient ensures high performance across diverse industrial sectors while meeting strict regulatory requirements for safety and quality.

name: Stachyose tetrahydrate
description:
Stachyose tetrahydrate (CAS 10094-58-3 ), also known as Lupeose, is a naturally occurring tetrasaccharide sourced primarily from legumes. It is used commercially as a prebiotic, humectant, and functional food ingredient.

It supports beneficial gut microbiota by selectively fermenting bifidobacteria and lactobacilli. This makes it a recognized ingredient in functional nutrition and health-oriented formulations across the global food industry.

In food and nutrition, it is incorporated into prebiotic supplements, infant formula adjuncts, and functional beverages. Gut health positioning is a primary formulation priority for these specific product categories.

Personal care formulators use it as a humectant in skin-conditioning products. Its moisture-retention profile supports hydration claims in various serums, creams, and leave-on treatments for cosmetic applications.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers include it in probiotic delivery systems and dietary supplements targeting digestive health. Its chelating behavior also makes it relevant in formulations where metal ion sequestration is needed.

This behavior contributes significantly to overall product stability in complex chemical environments. Stachyose tetrahydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy integration into dry or liquid blends.

Food-grade and reagent-grade specifications are the most commonly available. Purity levels are typically at 95% or higher depending on the intended application and the specific requirements of the manufacturer.

Packaging ranges from small research quantities to bulk industrial supply. Documentation is provided to support food and cosmetic compliance requirements for international distribution and regulatory safety standards.

name: 2,2-Dimethylolbutanoic acid
description:
2,2-Dimethylolbutanoic acid (CAS 10097-02-6 ), commonly abbreviated as DMBA, is a difunctional hydroxyl acid monomer used to introduce ionic or hydrophilic character into polymer backbones.

It enables water dispersibility in polyurethane and polyester systems without requiring external emulsifiers. DMBA is a primary building block in waterborne polyurethane dispersions (PUDs) for industrial use.

In these systems, its carboxyl group is neutralized with amines to create self-emulsifying resin systems for coatings and industrial adhesives. This process is essential for modern chemical manufacturing.

In two-component waterborne coatings, it contributes to crosslink density and film hardness while maintaining low VOC profiles demanded by modern formulation standards. This ensures high performance in various applications.

Sealant and elastomer manufacturers use DMBA to tune the hydrophilicity and adhesion performance of polyurethane prepolymers. This versatility makes it a staple in the specialty chemicals sector.

Specialty polymer producers also incorporate it into UV-curable and radiation-curable resin systems targeting graphic arts and packaging applications. It provides excellent stability and processing characteristics.

DMBA is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in technical and high-purity grades, with specifications typically aligned to the requirements of polyurethane resin manufacturers.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities suited to continuous production environments. Our logistics team ensures that all material meets rigorous industrial quality benchmarks for global shipping.

name: L-lysine hydrochloride
description:
L-Lysine Hydrochloride ( CAS 10098-89-2 ), also known as L-Lysine Monohydrochloride, is the stabilized salt form of the essential amino acid lysine. It offers improved solubility and shelf stability over the free base form.

It functions as a nutritional supplement, feed additive, and pharmaceutical excipient across multiple industries. In animal nutrition, it is incorporated into compound feeds for swine, poultry, and aquaculture.

This additive helps to correct lysine deficiency in cereal-based diets and support lean muscle development. Food and beverage manufacturers use it to fortify protein-enriched products and meal replacements.

It is particularly useful in functional foods where lysine is the limiting amino acid. Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it as an active ingredient in oral supplements and infusion solutions.

In food applications, it also contributes mild flavor-modifying and acidulant properties in certain formulations. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling.

It is available in feed-grade, food-grade ( FCC compliant), and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) specifications. These grades ensure compliance with various global regulatory requirements.
