name: Lanthanum chloride
description:
Lanthanum chloride (CAS 10099-58-8 ) is an inorganic rare earth salt used in industrial water treatment and pharmaceutical research applications. It functions primarily as a phosphate-binding and flocculating agent.

This chemical enables the efficient removal of dissolved contaminants from aqueous systems. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it precipitates soluble phosphates from wastewater effluent, reducing eutrophication risk.

Formulators developing antimicrobial or preservation systems incorporate it as a biocidal active against microbial growth. It is highly effective in process water and various specialty formulations for industrial use.

In pharmaceutical and biochemical research, it serves as a calcium channel blocker surrogate in laboratory assays. This application supports drug discovery workflows and advanced medical research projects.

Catalyst manufacturers also use this compound as a precursor or promoter in rare earth catalyst systems. These systems are essential for modern refining and complex chemical synthesis processes across the globe.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an anhydrous solid. The heptahydrate form is commonly available for solution-based applications requiring high solubility and consistent performance.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-purity reagent grade. Purity levels typically range from 99% to 99.99% depending on the specific end-use requirements of the manufacturer.

Packaging is available in laboratory quantities through to bulk industrial volumes for large-scale operations. We ensure all shipments meet rigorous safety and quality standards for global distribution.

name: Triphenyl phosphite
description:
Triphenyl phosphite (CAS 101-02-0 ), also sold under the trade name Advance TPP, is an organophosphorus ester used as a stabilizer and processing aid across polymer, rubber, and lubricant manufacturing.

TPP functions primarily as a secondary antioxidant and co-stabilizer, intercepting hydroperoxides during thermal processing to protect finished materials from degradation. In plastics compounding, it is incorporated into PVC and polyolefins.

The additive is used in engineering resins to suppress discoloration and extend service life during high-temperature processing. Rubber and tire manufacturers use it as a processing stabilizer and mild plasticizer.

This chemical improves flow and reduces premature vulcanization side reactions in various rubber applications. Lubricant formulators add TPP as an antioxidant component in industrial oils and metalworking fluids.

Oxidative stability under load is a key formulation requirement where this product excels. It also acts as an intermediate in the synthesis of other phosphorus-based flame retardants and specialty additives.

The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid at ambient conditions. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels, typically specified at 99%+ purity with defined acid value.

Color limits are strictly monitored to ensure consistency across different production batches. Packaging is available in drums and IBC containers suited to bulk industrial procurement for global distribution.

name: Triclocarban
description:
Triclocarban (CAS 101-20-2 ), also known as TCC and 3,4,4'-trichlorocarbanilide, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used primarily in personal care and hygiene product manufacturing.

It delivers bacteriostatic and fungistatic activity against a wide range of gram-positive organisms, making it a recognized biocide ingredient for rinse-off and leave-on formulations.

TCC is most commonly incorporated into bar soaps and solid cleansers at concentrations designed to meet antimicrobial efficacy standards for consumer and institutional hygiene products.

In textile and fiber processing, it is applied as a durable antimicrobial finish to inhibit odor-causing bacterial growth on fabrics. This ensures long-lasting freshness in industrial materials.

Pharmaceutical and medicated skincare formulators use TCC as an active ingredient in topical antibacterial preparations targeting skin hygiene. It is a staple in specialized medical cleansers.

Flame retardant applications in specialty polymer systems represent an additional industrial use case where halogenated urea compounds are evaluated for performance and stability.

Triclocarban is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical and cosmetic specifications, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

name: Diphenylmethane diisocyanate
description:
Diphenylmethane diisocyanate ( CAS 101-68-8 ), commonly known as MDI, is a core isocyanate monomer used to produce polyurethane polymers across rigid, flexible, and elastomeric applications.

It reacts with polyols to build polymer chains, enabling manufacturers to engineer foam density, hardness, and durability to precise specifications for various industrial uses.

In building and construction, MDI is the primary reactant in rigid polyurethane and polyisocyanurate insulation panels, where it delivers high thermal resistance in thin cross-sections.

Automotive manufacturers rely on MDI-based systems for structural foam components, seating, headliners, and interior trim parts requiring consistent load-bearing performance and safety.

In adhesives and sealants, MDI functions as a crosslinker that bonds dissimilar substrates including wood, metal, and composites under demanding mechanical and environmental conditions.

Coatings and elastomer formulators use MDI to produce abrasion-resistant surfaces for industrial flooring, rollers, and protective linings that must withstand heavy daily wear.

MDI is supplied as a liquid in several commercially distinct forms: pure 4,4'-MDI, polymeric MDI (pMDI), and modified MDI variants including prepolymers and carbodiimide-modified grades.

Polymeric MDI is the dominant commercial form for foam applications, while pure MDI grades serve elastomer formulators requiring tighter isomer control for high-end manufacturing.

name: 4,4-Diaminodiphenylmethane
description:
4,4-Diaminodiphenylmethane (CAS 101-77-9 ), commercially known as MDA, is an aromatic diamine used as a curing agent and polymer building block across rubber, coatings, and adhesive manufacturing.

Its two reactive amine groups enable controlled cross-linking and chain extension in high-performance polymer systems. In polyurethane and epoxy formulations, MDA functions as a hardener.

This process produces cured systems with elevated thermal and mechanical resistance suitable for industrial coatings and structural adhesives. Rubber compounders use it as an antioxidant and cross-linking agent.

It is frequently utilized in tire components and elastomeric seals where long-term heat stability is required. In polyurea and polyamide synthesis, MDA serves as a diamine monomer.

This contributes to the backbone of engineering polymers used in films, fibers, and molded parts. Textile and leather processing operations also apply MDA-derived intermediates in dye chemistry.

In these applications, it acts as a precursor to azo colorants for fiber dyeing. MDA is supplied as a solid, typically off-white to tan flakes or pastilles, and in molten form for bulk delivery.

It functions as a reactive building block and curing agent in systems where thermal stability and mechanical durability are critical requirements. ODA is a primary monomer in the production of polyimide films and resins.

In these applications, it reacts with dianhydrides to deliver materials used in flexible electronics, aerospace components, and high-temperature insulation. In epoxy formulations, it acts as a curing agent to produce thermosets.

These materials feature elevated glass transition temperatures suited for structural composites and printed circuit board laminates. Polyurethane and polyurea systems incorporate ODA to introduce aromatic chain segments.

This improves rigidity and heat resistance in foam and coating applications. Specialty colorant and pigment manufacturers also use it as an intermediate in synthesizing azo dyes and pigments for printing inks.

name: Dicyclohexylamine
description:
Dicyclohexylamine (CAS 101-83-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DCHA, is a secondary aliphatic amine used as a chemical intermediate, catalyst, and neutralizing agent across pharmaceutical, polymer, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its basicity and reactivity make it a building block for a range of downstream synthesis processes. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DCHA forms stable salt complexes with acidic active ingredients, improving crystallization and purification.

This material assists in the handling of intermediates during synthesis. Rubber and polymer producers use it as a vulcanization accelerator precursor and corrosion inhibitor component in metalworking and vapor-phase protection formulations.

In organic synthesis and catalysis, DCHA acts as a base catalyst for condensation and esterification reactions. This is particularly useful where a hindered, non-nucleophilic amine is required for specific chemical transformations.

It also appears in flavor chemistry applications under FEMA -regulated use, where it contributes to specific fragrance and flavor profiles in approved formulations. The compound is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid.

Standard packaging includes drum and IBC options for industrial scale. Technical grade is the most common commercial form, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to meet purity requirements for API intermediate applications.

Buyers should confirm specification sheets against their synthesis or regulatory requirements, as purity thresholds vary by application. Adherence to USP or EP standards may be necessary depending on the final use case.

name: Diphenyl ether
description:

With FEMA 3667 designation, it is recognized as a flavor material delivering a distinctive geranium-like, rose-nuanced character. In fragrance formulation, DPE contributes a floral note to fine fragrances.

It is frequently utilized in soaps and cosmetic products where lasting aromatic character is required. As a FEMA-designated flavoring agent, it is used at controlled trace levels in food and beverage applications.

The compound imparts subtle floral nuances to various consumer goods. In personal care manufacturing, it functions as a scenting component in lotions, creams, and rinse-off products for daily use.

Pharmaceutical and healthcare product formulators also incorporate it where both fragrance masking and mild preservative-adjacent properties are relevant to the finished formulation and stability.

Diphenyl ether is supplied as a colorless to pale liquid in standard packaging suited for fragrance and flavor industry handling. It is available in flavor and fragrance grade for industrial use.

The supply conforms to FEMA 3667 specifications as the primary quality benchmark for buyers in these sectors. Drum and smaller lot quantities are typical for specialty fragrance and flavor procurement channels.

name: alpha-hexylcinnamaldehyde
description:
Alpha-hexylcinnamaldehyde (CAS 101-86-0 ), also known commercially as alpha-hexyl cinnamic aldehyde, is a synthetic fragrance aldehyde widely recognized for its warm, floral-jasmine scent profile.

It functions as both a fragrance ingredient in personal care formulations and a UV-absorbing stabilizer in polymer and coating systems. In personal care, it is used to impart jasmine-type floral notes.

This ingredient is found in fine fragrances, body lotions, soaps, and shampoos, where it contributes to both top and heart note development. Polymer and plastics manufacturers incorporate it as a UV stabilizer.

This application protects materials from photodegradation during outdoor exposure, extending product service life. In printing inks and packaging coatings, it supports light stability in pigmented systems.

This is particularly useful where UV-induced color fading is a quality concern. Food-grade applications include its use as a flavoring agent in baked goods, confectionery, and beverages.

In these applications, it delivers subtle floral-fruity character at low use levels. Alpha-hexylcinnamaldehyde is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for industrial and commercial use.

It is available in cosmetic/fragrance grade and food-grade specifications, with the latter conforming to standards recognized by regulatory bodies governing flavor ingredients.

Bulk supply is typically offered in drums or intermediate bulk containers. Our material meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency across all manufacturing batches and applications.

name: Ethyl phenylacetate
description:
Ethyl phenylacetate (CAS 101-97-3 ), also known by its FEMA 2452 designation, is a synthetic ester used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient across food and personal care markets.

It delivers a characteristic honey-like, rose, and sweet floral scent profile that forms the basis of its commercial value. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavoring agent.

It is used in confectionery, baked goods, and beverages where honey, floral, or fruity notes are required. Fragrance compounders incorporate it into perfumes, eau de toilette, and body care formulations.

These applications help to build sweet, rosy top and middle notes. Personal care manufacturers use it in scented lotions, soaps, and hair care products where a soft floral character is the target profile.

It also appears in tobacco flavoring blends, where its sweetness rounds out harsher aromatic notes. The compound is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in standard packaging ranging from small drums to bulk quantities.

Food-grade material conforming to FEMA and FCC specifications is the primary commercial form, supporting its use in regulated flavor applications across the global food industry.

Technical-grade material is available for fragrance and non-food industrial use where food certification is not a sourcing requirement. This ensures versatility for various manufacturing needs.

name: Calcium sulfate dihydrate
description:
Calcium sulfate dihydrate (CAS 10101-41-4 ), commonly known as gypsum, is the naturally occurring and synthetically produced hydrated form of calcium sulfate approved as food additive E516 .

It functions primarily as a firming agent, calcium fortifier, and pH regulator across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing. In food production, it conditions dough in bread manufacturing.

It acts as a coagulant in tofu processing, where controlled calcium ion release determines final texture. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet diluent and binder in various formulations.

Its low solubility supports controlled disintegration in direct compression formulations. In agriculture, it supplies both calcium and sulfur to soil without significantly altering the pH levels.

This makes it a preferred amendment for high-value crops and compacted clay soils. The construction industry consumes the largest volumes as the base material for plasterboard and wall plaster.

It is also used as a cement retarder application. Calcium sulfate dihydrate is supplied as a white powder or as crushed mineral in varying particle size distributions for industrial use.

Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP / Ph.Eur. for pharmaceutical use, and technical grade for construction and agricultural applications.

Bulk quantities are standard for construction and agricultural supply, while finer milled grades serve food and pharma procurement requirements for global manufacturers.

name: Zirconium silicate
description:
Zirconium silicate (CAS 10101-52-7 ), also sold under the trade name Ultrox, is a naturally occurring mineral processed into fine powder for industrial use. It functions primarily as an opacifier, surface modifier, and refractory filler across ceramics, coatings, and specialty formulations.

Procurement teams source it for its thermal stability and opacity contribution in demanding manufacturing environments. In ceramic glazes and tile manufacturing, it delivers whiteness and opacity without compromising firing performance at high temperatures.

Coatings and enamel formulators incorporate it to improve surface hardness and chemical resistance in industrial and architectural finishes. Personal care manufacturers use milled grades as a mild abrasive and opacifying agent in toothpaste and cosmetic formulations.

In plastics and elastomers, it acts as a functional filler that contributes flame retardancy and dimensional stability to finished components. Zirconium silicate is supplied as a fine white powder, with particle size distribution being the primary specification variable.

Micronized grades are standard for cosmetic and coating applications. Technical and ceramic grades are distinguished by zirconia content, typically expressed as ZrO₂ percentage, and by D50 particle size.

Supply is available in bulk bags and smaller packaged quantities to suit both large-scale ceramic producers and specialty formulators. This material remains a critical component for achieving high-performance finishes in the global chemical and materials market.

name: Trisodium phosphate dodecahydrate
description:
Trisodium phosphate dodecahydrate (CAS 10101-89-0 ), commonly known as TSP, is the hydrated crystalline form of trisodium phosphate used across industrial and institutional markets. It functions as a heavy-duty cleaner, pH buffer, and sequestrant.

This chemical acts as a flame retardant across a broad range of manufacturing and processing applications. In industrial cleaning and surface preparation, TSP cuts through grease, oils, and mineral deposits on metal and concrete.

It is frequently applied to painted surfaces prior to coating or refinishing to ensure proper adhesion. Water treatment facilities use it to adjust pH and sequester calcium and magnesium ions, preventing scale formation.

This sequestration is vital for maintaining distribution systems and boilers in high-pressure environments. Textile and paper processing operations rely on TSP to control bath pH and chelate interfering metal ions.

These properties are essential during bleaching and dyeing stages to ensure color consistency. In flame retardant formulations and building materials, it contributes phosphate-based fire resistance to coatings and adhesives.

The product is also utilized in construction products to enhance safety and durability. Trisodium phosphate dodecahydrate is supplied as white crystalline granules or powder for easy handling and dissolution.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and food-grade specifications meeting FCC requirements. Industrial supply is typically available in bulk bags or multi-wall sacks for large-scale operations.

Food-grade material is packaged specifically to meet handling and contamination control requirements. This ensures the material remains stable and effective throughout the supply chain and final application.

name: Nickel sulfate hexahydrate
description:
Nickel sulfate hexahydrate (CAS 10101-97-0 ) is the primary nickel salt used in electroplating and surface finishing operations. It supplies soluble nickel ions to plating baths, enabling controlled deposition of nickel onto metal substrates.

Across electronics, metalworking, and battery material manufacturing, it functions as the foundational nickel source in both process chemistry and catalyst preparation. In electroplating, it is the core electrolyte component.

It is used in Watts baths and sulfamate-based systems to plate connectors, automotive parts, and consumer hardware. Battery cathode precursor manufacturing relies on it as a nickel feedstock for producing active materials.

These materials include nickel-cobalt-manganese (NCM) and nickel-cobalt-aluminum (NCA). In catalyst production, it serves as a precursor for hydrogenation catalysts used in edible oil processing and petrochemical refining.

Agricultural micronutrient formulations incorporate it to correct nickel deficiency in crops, particularly in legume cultivation. The product is supplied as blue-green crystalline granules or powder for industrial use.

Standard commercial grades include electroplating grade, battery grade, and technical grade. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5%+, ensuring performance across various chemical applications.

High-purity battery-grade material is subject to tighter specifications on trace metal impurities. This reflects the increasing demand from lithium-ion cathode manufacturers for high-quality chemical precursors.

name: Sodium thiosulfate pentahydrate
description:
Sodium thiosulfate pentahydrate (CAS 10102-17-7 ), also known commercially as antichlor, is an inorganic salt used across industrial and pharmaceutical supply chains as a reducing and dechlorination agent.

It neutralizes excess oxidants in solution, making it a go-to input wherever chlorine or heavy metal control is required. In water treatment, it dechlorinates municipal and process water prior to discharge.

This chemical helps facilities meet regulatory limits without the need for complex equipment. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an antidote formulation ingredient and as a stabilizer in injectable preparations.

It is essential where oxidative degradation must be controlled. Textile and paper producers apply it to neutralize residual chlorine after bleaching, preventing fiber or pulp damage that would compromise quality.

In food processing, it functions as an antioxidant and dough conditioner, supplied to specification for direct food contact applications. The material is supplied as white crystalline granules or powder.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical grade, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher. These standards ensure reliability across diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Sodium selenite
description:
Sodium selenite (CAS 10102-18-8 ), also supplied under the formula designation Na2SeO3, is an inorganic selenium compound used as a controlled selenium source across nutritional, agricultural, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It delivers a bioavailable form of the trace mineral selenium where precise, low-level dosing is required. In animal feed production, it is incorporated into premixes and mineral supplements to meet selenium requirements.

This is essential in livestock and poultry, where deficiency causes muscular disorders and reduced reproductive performance. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as the active selenium source in parenteral nutrition solutions.

It is also used in dietary supplement tablets targeting selenium-deficient populations. In human food fortification, it is added at regulated trace levels to functional foods and nutritional products where selenium status is a target.

Fertilizer and agrochemical producers also use it in foliar sprays and soil treatments to correct selenium-deficient growing conditions. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

Standard grades include feed-grade, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Packaging is handled under strict containment protocols given the low exposure levels.

Material is commonly available in small-quantity technical packs through to bulk industrial quantities. This ensures that manufacturers can source the exact volume required for their specific production processes and safety standards.

name: Sodium tellurite
description:
Sodium tellurite (CAS 10102-20-2 ), also referenced as disodium tellurite in reagent catalogs, is an inorganic tellurium salt used primarily as a selective inhibitor.

It serves as a trace-element source in microbiological and biochemical applications. Its ability to suppress non-target bacterial growth makes it a valued tool in diagnostic and research workflows.

In clinical and pharmaceutical microbiology, it is incorporated into selective culture media to isolate Corynebacterium diphtheriae and other tellurite-tolerant organisms.

Biotechnology researchers use it as a tellurium source in studies investigating bacterial tellurite resistance mechanisms and the biosynthesis of tellurium nanoparticles.

Pharmaceutical-grade preparations are used in controlled laboratory settings to evaluate antimicrobial susceptibility and screen microbial strains for industrial fermentation programs.

It also serves as a reference standard material in analytical chemistry workflows requiring certified tellurium content. The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

It is available in reagent-grade and laboratory-grade specifications, with high-purity grades offered for research and pharmaceutical applications.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to larger bulk formats for institutional or industrial buyers, ensuring consistent quality for all technical requirements.

Printing and packaging applications include its use as a pigment component in molybdate orange and red colorants for inks and coatings. Sodium molybdate dihydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

name: Sodium aluminum sulfate
description:
Sodium aluminum sulfate ( CAS 10102-71-3 ), also known as sodium alum and listed as E521 in food applications, is a double salt used across food processing and water treatment.

It functions primarily as an acidulant, coagulant, and pH buffer depending on the application context. In food production, it acts as a leavening acid in baking powders and self-rising flours.

This chemical controls gas release timing for consistent texture in baked goods. Water treatment facilities use it as a coagulant and flocculant to aggregate suspended solids and clarify drinking water.

It is also effective for industrial effluent streams. In textile and leather processing, it serves as a mordant and fixing agent, improving dye uptake and bonding to various fiber substrates.

Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it for pH control and sizing retention, influencing paper surface quality and ink absorption. Sodium alum is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules.

Food-grade material is available to E521 specifications and FCC standards, suitable for direct food contact applications. Technical-grade material is offered for industrial water treatment.

This grade is ideal for manufacturing use where food compliance is not required. Our product ensures high purity and consistent performance across all industrial and food-related applications.

name: Calcium bromate
description:
Calcium bromate ( CAS 10102-75-7 ) is an inorganic calcium salt of bromic acid used industrially as an oxidizing agent. In food processing, it functions as a dough conditioner and flour treatment agent.

It works by strengthening gluten networks to improve bread volume and crumb structure. In commercial baking, it is applied as a flour improver to accelerate dough maturation and achieve consistent loaf height.

This is particularly useful in high-volume bread production. Water treatment facilities have evaluated bromate salts for biocidal and oxidizing roles in disinfection processes to ensure safety and efficiency.

As a bleaching agent, it supports flour whitening in markets where oxidative treatment of wheat flour is permitted by local food regulations. Its oxidizing capacity also positions it for specialty chemical formulations.

These formulations often require controlled bromate ion release for specific industrial reactions. Calcium bromate is typically supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid for easy handling.

It is available in technical and food-grade specifications, with food-grade material subject to purity standards aligned with regional food additive regulations such as FCC or USP .

Packaging is commonly offered in multi-kilogram bags or drums suited to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures the material remains stable and secure during transport and long-term storage at facilities.

name: Copper pyrophosphate
description:
Copper pyrophosphate (CAS 10102-90-6 ) is an inorganic copper salt used primarily as an electrolytic bath component in industrial metal finishing and electroplating operations. It deposits uniform, adherent copper layers across complex geometries.

This chemical provides a high-performance alternative to traditional methods without the toxicity concerns associated with cyanide-based copper plating systems. It is essential for achieving high-quality surface finishes in modern manufacturing.

In printed circuit board manufacturing, copper pyrophosphate electrolytes enable through-hole plating and fine-line circuitry deposition where dimensional accuracy and conductivity are critical. These properties are vital for high-end electronics.

Textile and paper industries use it as a surface modification agent to impart antimicrobial or conductive properties to fiber substrates and coated materials. It allows for specialized functional coatings on various industrial surfaces.

Leather finishing operations apply copper pyrophosphate-based treatments to achieve controlled surface chemistry and improved dye uptake. Packaging and printing processes also incorporate it to enhance ink adhesion or substrate wettability.

Copper pyrophosphate is supplied as a blue-green crystalline powder or fine granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically ranging from 97% to 99% for industrial use.

Buyers sourcing for electronics or precision plating applications should confirm bath-grade specifications with the supplier. This includes checking trace metal impurity limits to ensure the material meets specific process requirements.

name: Mercury chloride
description:
Mercury(I) chloride (CAS 10112-91-1 ), commercially known as calomel, is an inorganic mercury salt used as a reference electrode material and catalyst in specialized industrial and laboratory settings.

Its electrochemical stability makes it a benchmark compound in analytical chemistry and precision measurement applications. Calomel is the active material in saturated calomel electrodes (SCE).

These serve as standard reference electrodes in electrochemical analysis, pH measurement, and corrosion testing across laboratory and industrial quality control environments.

In electronics manufacturing, it supports calibration processes where stable, reproducible electrode potentials are required. Pharmaceutical and chemical research facilities use it as a catalyst.

It is utilized in select organic synthesis reactions where mercury-based catalysis offers specific selectivity advantages. Historically significant in pharmaceutical compounding, it remains a reference compound.

It is used in regulatory and analytical standards work. Mercury(I) chloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder available in reagent-grade and analytical-grade specifications.

These grades meet laboratory and industrial purity requirements. Packaging is typically offered in small quantities consistent with its specialized, low-volume demand profile.

name: Calcium nitrate
description:
Calcium nitrate (CAS 10124-37-5 ), also known as Norway saltpeter, is an inorganic salt supplying both calcium and nitrate ions in a single compound. It functions as a fertilizer nutrient source and concrete accelerator.

This versatile chemical also acts as a biocidal agent across multiple industrial sectors. In agriculture, it delivers water-soluble calcium and nitrogen directly to crops through fertigation systems.

The compound supports cell wall development and reduces post-harvest defects in fruits and vegetables. Concrete and construction applications rely on it as a set accelerator in ready-mix formulations.

It is particularly effective in cold-weather pours where faster strength development is critical. Wastewater treatment plants dose it into anaerobic systems to suppress hydrogen sulfide generation.

This process helps control odor in collection networks and functions as a corrosion inhibitor in concrete reinforcement. It reduces chloride-induced rebar degradation in marine and infrastructure projects.

The product is supplied as white granules, prills, or in liquid solution form. Standard agricultural grades meet fertilizer specifications with defined nitrogen and calcium content for global trade.

Technical grades serve construction and water treatment applications where specific purity is required. Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement, with granular product being the most common form.

name: Cobalt sulfate
description:
Cobalt sulfate (CAS 10124-43-3 ), also known as cobalt monosulfate, is an inorganic cobalt salt used across electroplating, battery manufacturing, and agricultural micronutrient applications.

It serves as a primary cobalt source in processes requiring controlled cobalt ion delivery at industrial scale. In electroplating and surface finishing, it is used in bath formulations to deposit cobalt.

These cobalt-alloy coatings improve hardness and wear resistance on metal components. Battery and energy storage manufacturers use it as a precursor in synthesizing cathode active materials for lithium-ion chemistries.

In agriculture, it is applied as a micronutrient supplement in fertilizers and animal feed to address cobalt deficiencies in livestock and soil. This ensures proper health and growth in various environments.

Catalyst producers also use this chemical as a precursor for cobalt-based catalysts in hydroprocessing and chemical synthesis operations. It is a versatile component for many high-tech industrial sectors.

The material is supplied primarily as a heptahydrate crystalline solid, with the anhydrous form available for specific technical applications. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and battery-grade.

Battery-grade material is subject to tighter purity specifications relevant to cathode precursor production. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities for large-volume industrial buyers.

name: Hexasodium Hexametaphosphate
description:
Hexasodium Hexametaphosphate , also known by its CAS 10124-56-8 , is a condensed phosphate salt used across food, industrial, and water treatment applications. It functions primarily as a sequestrant and dispersant.

The chemical works by binding calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions to prevent scale formation, precipitation, and product degradation. This makes it essential for maintaining stability in complex formulations.

In food processing, this compound controls mineral interference in dairy, seafood, and processed meat products. It is highly effective at improving texture retention and moisture binding during production cycles.

Water treatment operations use the material to inhibit scale and corrosion in boiler systems, cooling towers, and municipal pipelines. It ensures the longevity of infrastructure by preventing mineral buildup.

In mining and mineral processing, it acts as a dispersant in ore slurries, improving separation efficiency and reducing reagent consumption. This helps optimize the extraction process for various minerals.

Textile and paper manufacturing rely on this phosphate to sequester hardness ions in process water. This prevents interference with dyes, bleaches, and sizing agents, ensuring consistent product quality.

The product is supplied as a white powder or granule. Food-grade material is available meeting FCC specifications, while technical-grade product is offered for various industrial applications.

Purity levels and P₂O₅ content are the primary quality parameters buyers should confirm against their process requirements. Proper grade selection ensures optimal performance in specific chemical environments.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a primary surfactant in liquid soaps, shampoos, and cleansing bars, contributing lather and skin-compatible cleansing performance. Food-grade applications include emulsification and pH buffering in processed food systems.

These applications are common where fatty acid salts are permitted as functional additives. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a degreasing and wetting agent to prepare fiber and hide surfaces before dyeing or finishing.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface treatment and dispersion of coating formulations. Potassium laurate is supplied as a liquid solution or paste, with concentration typically ranging from 20% to 40% active content.

Its defined hydroxylation pattern makes it a target structure for enzyme inhibition studies and bioactivity screening programs. In pharmaceutical research, it serves as an analytical reference standard for method validation and purity testing.

Biotechnology laboratories use it as a substrate or inhibitor probe in enzyme assay development, particularly where chromone scaffolds are under investigation for bioactivity profiling and chromatographic calibration.

It functions as an anionic surfactant, wetting agent, and emulsifier across a broad range of industrial and personal care applications. In textile processing, it improves dye penetration and fiber lubrication.

This material is essential during scouring, dyeing, and finishing operations. Leather manufacturers use it as a fat-liquoring agent to soften hides and improve flexibility in the tanning process.

In personal care formulations, it acts as an emulsifier and skin-conditioning agent in bath oils, hair preparations, and cream-based products. It provides excellent stability in various aqueous systems.

Its high lauric content generates dense, stable lather in various cleaning applications. Personal care formulators use it as a precursor for surfactants, emulsifiers, and conditioning agents in shampoos, body washes, and skin creams.

Industrial cleaning product manufacturers rely on it to produce fatty acid soaps and alkanolamides. These components perform reliably across a wide range of pH and temperature conditions in heavy-duty industrial settings.

In the food industry, it serves as a feedstock for producing food-grade emulsifiers and surface-active agents. These are used extensively in bakery and confectionery processing to improve texture and shelf stability.

name: Cobalt dinitrate
description:
Cobalt dinitrate ( CAS 10141-05-6 ), commercially available as cobalt(II) nitrate, is an inorganic cobalt salt used primarily as a catalyst precursor and micronutrient source across industrial and agricultural applications.

Its high solubility makes it a preferred cobalt delivery form where controlled uptake or precise impregnation is required. In heterogeneous catalysis, it serves as the standard precursor for preparing cobalt-based catalysts.

Used in Fischer-Tropsch synthesis and hydroprocessing, the nitrate decomposes cleanly during calcination to yield active cobalt oxide phases. Fertilizer formulators incorporate it into micronutrient blends to correct cobalt deficiency.

In soils supporting legume cultivation, it directly improves nitrogen fixation efficiency. Animal feed manufacturers use it as a cobalt supplementation source in ruminant nutrition programs to support vitamin B12 synthesis.

It also functions as an impregnation agent in the production of supported catalysts for petrochemical refining. The material is supplied as a red crystalline solid or in hexahydrate form for various uses.

The hexahydrate is the most commercially prevalent grade, while technical and reagent grades are standard across the market. Bulk quantities are available for industrial catalyst production and specialty applications.

description:
Trimethylolmelamine (CAS 1017-56-7 ), also known commercially as Lyofix DM and Glazamine M, is a trifunctional melamine-formaldehyde resin intermediate used as a crosslinker and curing agent across textile, coatings, and polymer applications.

By reacting with hydroxyl, carboxyl, and amide groups, it builds durable network structures in finished goods. In textile finishing, it imparts crease resistance and dimensional stability to cellulosic fabrics.

It forms covalent bonds with cotton fibers under acid-catalyzed cure conditions. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to crosslink alkyd, acrylic, and polyester resins, improving hardness and chemical resistance.

It also enhances film integrity in industrial and decorative systems. Paper and leather processors apply it as a wet-strength agent and surface binder, enhancing durability under moisture exposure.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a binder resin component where controlled rheology and adhesion to substrate are critical to print quality. Trimethylolmelamine is supplied as an aqueous solution.

Solids content is typically in the range of 70–80%, and less commonly as a dry powder for specific formulation requirements. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering.

Buyers should confirm methylol group content and free formaldehyde levels when evaluating grades for low-emission or regulated-end-use applications to ensure compliance with safety standards.

name: DL-alpha-tocopherol
description:
DL-alpha-tocopherol (CAS 10191-41-0 ), also known as Vitamin E, is the synthetic racemic form of alpha-tocopherol produced through chemical synthesis rather than natural extraction.

It functions as an antioxidant and stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial applications, protecting sensitive materials from oxidative degradation during storage and processing.

In food and nutritional products, it prevents rancidity in oils, fats, and fortified foods, and serves as a source of Vitamin E activity in dietary supplements and functional foods.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as both an active ingredient and an excipient in soft gel capsules, emulsions, and topical formulations where oxidative stability is critical for the product.

In personal care, it protects lipid-based ingredients in creams, serums, and hair care products from oxidation while supporting shelf-life extension and maintaining formulation integrity over time.

Plastics and polymer processors incorporate it as an antioxidant stabilizer in polyolefin compounds, and feed manufacturers use it for Vitamin E supplementation in animal nutrition programs.

DL-alpha-tocopherol is supplied as a viscous amber oil in bulk drums or intermediate bulk containers. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and Ph. Eur. specifications.

Potency is typically expressed in IU/g or mg/g. Technical-grade material is also available for polymer and industrial stabilization applications requiring high-performance antioxidant properties.

name: Ammonium sulfite
description:
Ammonium sulfite (CAS 10196-04-0 ), also referenced as diammonium sulfite, is an inorganic salt used industrially as a reducing and oxygen-scavenging agent. It functions primarily as a preservative and process chemical.

In pulp and paper processing, it acts as a delignification aid, helping break down lignin during chemical pulping to improve fiber yield and paper quality. This ensures high-performance material output.

Textile and leather operations use it as a reducing agent in dyeing and tanning processes. Controlled reduction chemistry is critical to achieving consistent color and material finish across large production batches.

In water treatment, it serves as an oxygen scavenger to protect boiler systems and pipelines from oxidative corrosion. This application is vital for maintaining the longevity of industrial infrastructure and equipment.

Food and nutrition applications include its use as a preservative and antioxidant to inhibit microbial growth. It prevents oxidative degradation in certain processed food products to maintain shelf stability and safety.

Ammonium sulfite is typically supplied as a white crystalline powder or in aqueous solution form. Technical grade is the most common specification for industrial applications requiring high-volume chemical processing.

Food-grade material is available for use in regulated food processing environments. Buyers should confirm purity levels and solution concentration with suppliers, as these vary significantly by the intended application.

Compliance with international quality standards such as FCC or USP may be required depending on the region. Always review the technical data sheet to ensure the material meets your specific requirements.

name: Zinc nitrate hexahydrate
description:
Zinc nitrate hexahydrate (CAS 10196-18-6 ) is a water-soluble zinc salt supplying both zinc and nitrate ions in a single, readily dissolved form. It functions as a corrosion inhibitor, coagulant, and source of reactive zinc across a range of industrial processes.

In agriculture, it is used as a foliar micronutrient source and in fertilizer blends where fast zinc availability is required for crop uptake. Water treatment operations apply it as a coagulation aid and corrosion inhibitor in distribution systems.

In cooling water circuits, it provides essential protection against oxidative damage. In mining and metals processing, it supports surface treatment and galvanizing operations where controlled zinc deposition is needed for high-quality finishes.

Construction chemistry formulators incorporate it into concrete admixtures and cementitious coatings to inhibit corrosion of embedded steel reinforcement. This ensures the long-term structural integrity of various infrastructure projects.

Zinc nitrate hexahydrate is supplied as white crystalline granules or prills, with liquid solution grades also available for direct dosing applications. These formats allow for flexible integration into existing manufacturing workflows.

Standard supply grades include technical and agricultural quality, with specifications typically aligned to purity thresholds of 98% or higher. This ensures consistent performance across demanding industrial and chemical synthesis applications.

Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags and drums to bulk intermediate bulk containers depending on application volume. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery of high-purity chemical precursors to meet your specific production schedules.

name: Diphenylguanidine
description:
Diphenylguanidine (CAS 102-06-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DPG and sold under the trade name Vulkazit, is a secondary accelerator used in rubber vulcanization. It activates primary accelerators and improves cure efficiency across a broad range of rubber compounds.

In tire manufacturing, DPG functions as a co-accelerator alongside thiazoles and sulfenamides, improving crosslink density and reducing cure time in both natural and synthetic rubber compounds.

It is used in industrial rubber goods, including belts, hoses, and seals, where consistent cure rates and mechanical performance are critical to product specification. In leather processing, DPG acts as a retanning auxiliary.

It serves as a pH modifier, influencing dye uptake and leather softness in finishing formulations. Printing ink and textile applications use DPG as a curing agent in certain resin systems where controlled crosslinking is required.

Diphenylguanidine is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as pre-dispersed granules suited for mixing operations. Standard commercial grades are available for rubber industry use, with product specifications covering purity.

Specifications typically cover melting point range and ash content. Technical grade is the predominant market form, with product conforming to established rubber chemical standards such as ISO and ASTM test methods.

name: Diphenyl carbonate
description:
Diphenyl carbonate (CAS 102-09-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DPC, is a key monomer and reagent used across polymer synthesis, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

It functions primarily as a carbonylating agent and transesterification reagent, enabling solvent-free and phosgene-free reaction pathways that are increasingly preferred in industrial processing.

In polycarbonate production, DPC reacts with bisphenol A via melt transesterification to produce engineering-grade polycarbonates without the use of phosgene, making this route attractive for manufacturers.

Pharmaceutical and agrochemical producers use DPC as a carbonate transfer reagent in the synthesis of carbamates, carbonates, and other active intermediates for various chemical applications.

In polycarbonate diol and polyurethane manufacturing, it contributes to building aliphatic carbonate segments that improve hydrolytic stability in the final polymer products and coatings.

DPC also appears in fragrance and flavor applications as a low-level fixative and esterification intermediate, though this remains a secondary commercial use for the chemical industry.

Diphenyl carbonate is supplied as a white crystalline solid, typically in flake or powder form, and in molten bulk for large-volume polymer-grade supply for industrial facilities.

Standard grades include technical and high-purity polymer-grade material, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP standards available for regulated synthesis applications.

name: Isoamyl phenylacetate
description:
Isoamyl phenylacetate (CAS 102-19-2 ), also known as 3-methylbutyl phenylacetate, is a synthetic ester used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient in food and cosmetic applications.

Carrying FEMA number 2081 , it delivers a characteristic rose-honey-like scent profile that underpins its commercial value in both flavor and fragrance formulation.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it contributes floral and fruity nuances to confectionery, baked goods, and non-alcoholic beverages where rose or honey-type flavor profiles are targeted.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into fine perfumery and functional fragrance blends, particularly in floral bouquets where a warm, honeyed depth is required for the final product.

Personal care manufacturers use it in scented lotions, hair care products, and soap bases to achieve lasting floral character at moderate use levels during the production process.

It also appears in flavor compound blends sold to industrial food processors seeking consistent, cost-effective rose-honey notes for large-scale manufacturing and distribution.

Isoamyl phenylacetate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Food-grade material conforming to FEMA 2081 status is the standard commercial form for flavor applications.

Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care use. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on supplier and application volume requirements.

name: Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine
description:
Tetrakis(2-hydroxypropyl)ethylenediamine , also known as CAS 102-60-3 , is a multifunctional amine alcohol used across industrial formulations for chelation, pH buffering, and crosslinking.

Its combination of amine and hydroxyl groups makes it effective at sequestering metal ions and acting as a reactive building block in polymer systems. In water treatment, it sequesters heavy metal ions.

This process prevents scale formation and improves process water quality. Coatings and adhesives formulators use it as a crosslinking agent and curing component, particularly in epoxy and polyurethane systems.

In these applications, controlled reactivity is required for optimal performance. In home care and industrial cleaning products, it functions as a chelating agent that deactivates hardness ions.

This action improves surfactant efficiency and formulation stability. Plastics and polymer manufacturers incorporate it as a reactive intermediate or stabilizer to modify network structure and processing behavior.

The product is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow viscous liquid. It is available in technical grade, with concentrations typically around 85–100%, suited to industrial processing requirements.

Bulk supply in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) is standard across the market. This ensures reliable logistics and handling for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing facilities.

name: Tripropylamine
description:
Tripropylamine (CAS 102-69-2 ), also abbreviated as TPA, is a tertiary aliphatic amine used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and polymer chemistry. It functions primarily as a catalyst and pH buffer.

This chemical serves as a solvent in reactions requiring a non-nucleophilic base with moderate volatility. In pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, it acts as a base catalyst or acid scavenger in condensation reactions.

Controlled basicity is critical to yield and purity during acylation processes. Agrochemical formulators use it to neutralize acidic herbicide and pesticide concentrates, improving stability and handling characteristics of the final formulation.

In polymer and resin production, it serves as a curing catalyst and process aid. This is particularly useful in systems where a slower-acting tertiary amine is preferred over more reactive alternatives in the manufacturing cycle.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers incorporate it as a pH stabilizer to extend fluid service life. This application helps reduce corrosion in metal-cutting applications and maintains the integrity of industrial fluids.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for this amine.

Purity is typically maintained at 99% or above to meet industrial requirements. It is also listed under FEMA 4247 , which is relevant for flavor and fragrance procurement channels requiring documented ingredient status.

name: Triallylamine
description:
Triallylamine (CAS 102-70-5 ), commonly abbreviated as TAA, is a trifunctional allylic amine used as a reactive monomer and cross-linking agent in polymer chemistry.

Its three polymerizable double bonds allow it to form dense network structures during curing, making it a valued building block for specialty polymer synthesis.

In rubber and tire manufacturing, TAA functions as a co-agent during peroxide curing, improving cross-link density and heat resistance in finished compounds.

Polymer formulators incorporate it into acrylic and vinyl-based systems to produce tightly cross-linked networks with enhanced mechanical performance.

It also serves as a monomer in the synthesis of ion-exchange resins and functional hydrogels, where controlled network architecture is critical to end-product performance.

In specialty coatings and adhesives, TAA contributes to improved cohesive strength by participating directly in the polymer backbone during cure.

Triallylamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to ISO tank quantities for industrial use.

Technical grade is the primary commercial form, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher for research and specialty polymer applications.

name: Triethanolamine

Triethanolamine (CAS 102-71-6 ), commonly abbreviated as TEA, is an amino alcohol used across industrial and personal care manufacturing as a pH adjuster, emulsifier, and neutralizing agent.

Its dual amine-alcohol functionality makes it effective at stabilizing formulations and activating crosslinking reactions in coating systems. In coatings and adhesives, TEA acts as a curing accelerator.

It serves as a crosslinker in epoxy and polyurethane systems, improving adhesion and film integrity. Personal care manufacturers use it to neutralize carbomer and acrylate polymers for stable gels.

It is frequently used in lotions, sunscreens, and hair products. Pharmaceutical formulators rely on TEA to adjust pH in topical preparations, ensuring API stability and skin compatibility in ointments.

In metalworking and industrial cleaning fluids, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and emulsifying agent, extending fluid service life. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

This chemical improves dispersion and stability in hard candies, chewing gum bases, and baked goods. Fragrance formulators use it to fix and extend volatile aroma compounds in perfumes and flavor emulsions.

Controlled release is a formulation priority in these applications. In personal care, it functions as a plasticizer in film-forming products such as nail coatings and hair fixatives for consumer use.

name: 2-(morpholinothio)benzothiazole
description:
2-(Morpholinothio)benzothiazole ( CAS 102-77-2 ), commercially known as MBS, Santocure MOR, or Sulfenax MOR, is a delayed-action rubber vulcanization accelerator. It controls the rate and onset of cure in sulfur-based vulcanization systems.

This chemical gives processors a reliable processing safety window before crosslinking begins. In tire manufacturing, MBS is used in tread and sidewall compounds where scorch resistance and consistent cure profiles are critical.

It performs effectively in technical rubber goods such as seals, gaskets, and industrial hoses. In these applications, controlled crosslink density determines long-term mechanical performance and dimensional stability.

Latex compounding operations use MBS to manage cure timing in dipped goods and foam products without premature gelation. It is also applied in conveyor belt and automotive rubber component production.

It is often used in combination with secondary accelerators such as DPG or TMTD to fine-tune cure rate and state of cure. MBS is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or in pre-dispersed granules.

These forms are suited to continuous mixing operations. Standard commercial grades meet rubber chemical purity specifications, with active content typically confirmed by melting point and HPLC assay.

Technical grade is the predominant market form for industrial use. Buyers should confirm particle size distribution where dust control or dispersion consistency is a specific process requirement.

name: n-butyldiethanolamine
description:
N-Butyldiethanolamine ( CAS 102-79-4 ), commonly abbreviated as BDEA, is a tertiary alkanolamine combining both amine and hydroxyl functionality in a single molecule. It functions primarily as a pH regulator and corrosion inhibitor.

This versatile chemical serves as a vital intermediate across various industrial formulation markets. In metalworking and industrial lubricants, BDEA neutralizes acidic components in cutting fluids and coolants effectively.

This neutralization process extends fluid service life and protects both ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces from corrosion. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a neutralizing amine for waterborne resin systems.

In these systems, controlled basicity improves dispersion stability and film formation. In oil and gas applications, it is used in gas treating and corrosion inhibitor packages for specialized industrial needs.

It is particularly useful where a less volatile amine with dual functional groups is required. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use BDEA as a reactive intermediate or cure modifier for processing.

These applications allow manufacturers to adjust processing characteristics and adhesion performance. BDEA is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels suitable for industrial formulation needs.

In metalworking and cutting fluid formulations, DBEA functions as a corrosion inhibitor and pH buffer, protecting ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces during machining operations.

Textile and leather processing operations use it as an emulsifier and dispersant in dyeing auxiliaries and finishing agents, improving dye uptake and surface uniformity across materials.

Water treatment programs incorporate DBEA as a neutralizing amine to control pH and inhibit corrosion in industrial cooling and boiler systems, ensuring long-term equipment protection.

In paper manufacturing, it supports sizing formulations and acts as a carrier solvent for surface treatment chemicals, enhancing the overall quality of the final paper products.

Dibutylethanolamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, with purity typically at 99% or higher.

name: Tributylamine
description:
Tributylamine (CAS 102-82-9 ), also known as Tri-n-butylamine, is a tertiary aliphatic amine used across chemical manufacturing as a catalyst, acid scavenger, and corrosion inhibitor.

Its combination of basicity and solubility in organic media makes it a practical processing aid in synthesis and formulation workflows. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a base catalyst.

It serves as an acid scavenger during API synthesis, neutralizing HCl and other acidic byproducts to drive reactions to completion. Polymer producers use it as a catalyst in polyurethane and epoxy systems.

Controlled basicity is critical to cure rate and final material properties in these systems. In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor for metal surfaces.

It protects ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces under high-load conditions. Upstream oil and gas operations employ it in drilling fluid additives and gas treatment processes to manage corrosive acidic species.

Tributylamine is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger volume requirements. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

This grade covers the majority of industrial synthesis and formulation applications. High-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical use cases where tighter impurity profiles are required.

It combines a tertiary and primary amine group in a single molecule, enabling it to act simultaneously as a catalyst, curing agent, and corrosion inhibitor depending on the application.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and pH buffer, protecting ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces during machining and storage.

Epoxy and polyurethane formulators use it as a curing agent and cross-linker, where its dual amine functionality allows controlled network formation in coatings and adhesives.

In sealant and elastomer systems, it supports cure acceleration and adhesion promotion to metal substrates. Polymer producers also incorporate it as a reactive intermediate or catalyst.

N,N-Dibutylaminopropylamine is supplied as a liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial form available from amine manufacturers and distributors.

It functions as a builder, binder, and alkalinity source across industrial cleaning, surface treatment, and construction applications. In industrial and institutional cleaning formulations, it boosts detergency.

The compound emulsifies oils and provides the high pH needed to break down grease on metal and hard surfaces. Textile and paper processors use it as a scouring and desizing aid for production.

Its buffering capacity controls bath alkalinity throughout wet processing stages. In construction and coatings, it acts as a binder and adhesion promoter in cement-based products and refractory coatings.

It is also utilized in silicate paints and water treatment operations as a corrosion inhibitor. It forms a protective silicate film on metal pipe surfaces to reduce scaling and metal leaching.

Sodium metasilicate pentahydrate is supplied as white granules or powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 97% or higher for industrial use.

Bulk supply in bags or big bags is standard for industrial buyers. Some suppliers offer technical-grade material meeting specific silica-to-alkali ratio requirements for specialized manufacturing.

description:
3-Butoxy-1-propanol (CAS 10215-33-5 ), also marketed as Dowanol 37B, is a glycol ether-type solvent used across cleaning, coatings, and printing applications. It combines slow evaporation with strong solvency to support formulation stability.

This chemical supports surface wetting in demanding industrial processes. In home care and industrial cleaning concentrates, it improves soil release and helps maintain clarity in aqueous formulations at low use levels.

Coatings formulators use it as a coalescing aid and coupling solvent in waterborne systems. In these environments, controlled evaporation reduces surface defects in architectural and industrial finishes during the drying phase.

In printing inks, it supports pigment dispersion and flow control across flexographic and gravure processes. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust open time and improve substrate adhesion in solvent-borne systems.

3-Butoxy-1-propanol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. It is typically offered at technical grade for industrial use.

name: Hydrazine hydrate
description:
Hydrazine hydrate (CAS 10217-52-4 ), also known as hydrazine monohydrate, is a concentrated aqueous form of hydrazine used as a reducing agent and chemical intermediate across industrial manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an oxygen scavenger in process systems and as a reactive building block in synthesis. In boiler and steam systems, it removes dissolved oxygen from feedwater to prevent corrosion.

This protects high-pressure equipment in power generation and industrial utilities. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a key intermediate in synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients, including antituberculosis compounds.

In agrochemical production, it serves as a precursor in the synthesis of herbicides, fungicides, and plant growth regulators. Water treatment operations also deploy it as a biocide and reducing agent.

It is particularly effective in closed-loop cooling systems where oxygen control is critical. Hydrazine hydrate is supplied as a liquid, with 64% and 80% aqueous concentrations being the most standard grades.

Technical grade is the primary specification for industrial water treatment and chemical synthesis applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available for API manufacturing, supplied with documentation.

This material is manufactured to meet relevant pharmacopoeial standards such as USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , and EP to ensure the highest level of purity for sensitive applications.

name: 2,2-dibromo-3-nitrilopropionamide
description:
2,2-Dibromo-3-nitrilopropionamide (CAS 10222-01-2 ), commercially known as DBNPA, is a fast-acting, broad-spectrum biocide used across industrial water systems, process fluids, and preservation applications.

Its rapid kill rate and hydrolytic degradability make it a preferred active ingredient where residue minimization is a sourcing priority. In industrial water treatment, it controls microbial growth in cooling towers.

It is also utilized in reverse osmosis systems and process water circuits where biological fouling reduces operational efficiency. Pulp and paper manufacturers use it to suppress slime-forming bacteria and fungi.

This application in white water systems protects paper machine runnability and product quality. Oil and gas operators apply the chemical to injection water and produced water systems to inhibit sulfate-reducing bacteria.

These bacteria are responsible for souring and pipeline corrosion. In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it functions as a preservation biocide in cutting fluids and emulsions to extend fluid service life.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder and in liquid concentrate formulations at varying active concentrations. Technical grade is the standard for industrial applications.

Product specifications are typically aligned to active content and halogen purity requirements. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on concentration and application format.

name: Isopropyl laurate

Isopropyl laurate (CAS 10233-13-3 ) is a synthetic ester of isopropyl alcohol and lauric acid used as an emollient, solvent, and carrier across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel that makes it a preferred alternative to heavier oils in topical formulations. In cosmetics and personal care, it functions as an emollient and spreading agent.

It is commonly used in lotions, creams, and color cosmetics, improving texture and skin absorption of active ingredients. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a carrier solvent in topical drug delivery systems.

Its skin-penetration-enhancing properties support consistent active ingredient release. In food-grade applications, it serves as a plasticizer and carrier for flavors and coatings, particularly where a low-viscosity ester is required.

It also appears in industrial formulations as a solvent for resins and waxes where a biodegradable, low-toxicity alternative to conventional solvents is preferred. Isopropyl laurate is supplied as a clear liquid.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with food-grade material meeting FCC standards for relevant applications. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers.

Technical-grade material is also available for non-cosmetic industrial uses. This versatile ester provides high stability and excellent compatibility with a wide range of lipophilic ingredients in various formulations.

name: Cupric sulfate monohydrate
description:
Cupric sulfate monohydrate (CAS 10257-54-2 ) is a copper-based inorganic salt supplied in a lower-hydration form than the common pentahydrate. It offers higher copper content by weight for dose-sensitive applications.

Known in regulatory contexts as Copper sulfate, monohydrate, it functions as a biocide, coagulant, and micronutrient source. It is used extensively across industrial and agricultural supply chains for various chemical processes.

In water treatment, it controls algae and microbial growth in reservoirs, cooling towers, and municipal systems. This is particularly useful where precise copper dosing is required to maintain water quality standards.

Mining and hydrometallurgical operations use it in leaching circuits and electroplating baths to manage copper ion concentration. It ensures stability and efficiency in metal recovery and surface finishing applications.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a mordant and preservative in dyeing and tanning processes. Consistent metal content per batch directly affects color fastness and the overall durability of the material.

In agriculture, it serves as a copper source in animal feed supplements and as an active ingredient in fungicidal formulations. It is also used in algaecidal products to protect crops and livestock health.

Cupric sulfate monohydrate is available as a powder or granule, with particle size influencing dissolution rate. Technical and agricultural grades are the most commonly sourced for large-scale industrial operations.

Specifications are aligned to EPA pesticide registration requirements and feed-grade standards where applicable. Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for specialized formulators.

name: Calcium sulfite
description:
Calcium sulfite (CAS 10257-55-3 ), also recognized in food applications as E226 , is an inorganic calcium salt used commercially as a preservative, antioxidant, and reducing agent across food processing, water treatment, and industrial manufacturing.

It inhibits oxidative degradation and microbial growth, extending shelf life in regulated food applications and controlling unwanted chemical reactions in industrial processes. In food and beverage production, it functions as a preservative and antioxidant.

This additive is used in products such as wine, dried fruits, and processed vegetables, where oxidation control is critical to shelf life and color retention. Pulp and paper manufacturers use it as a bleaching and delignification agent.

In sulfite pulping processes, it breaks down lignin to produce high-quality cellulose fiber. Water treatment operations apply it to dechlorinate process water and potable water supplies by neutralizing residual chlorine before discharge or further processing.

It also serves flour treatment applications, where it conditions dough by modifying gluten structure to improve processing behavior. This versatility makes it a staple in both the chemical manufacturing and food science sectors.

The product is supplied as a white powder or fine crystalline solid. Food-grade material is available to the required specification for use in regulated food and beverage applications, ensuring safety and compliance.

Technical-grade material is offered for industrial uses including paper processing and water treatment. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale industrial requirements and specialized food production needs.

Personal care formulators use it as a skin-conditioning carrier and solvent for fragrance concentrates, active ingredients, and lipophilic extracts in serums, creams, and oils. Its low polarity supports solubilization of fragrance materials.

name: Hydrated silica

Hydrated silica (CAS 10279-57-9 ), also known as silicon dioxide hydrate, is an amorphous, water-containing form of silica produced through controlled precipitation processes.

It functions as a functional filler, rheology modifier, and surface-active agent across a broad range of industrial and consumer product applications. In oral care, it is the primary abrasive agent.

In toothpaste formulations, particle size and hardness are tightly controlled to meet RDA specifications. Rubber and tire manufacturers incorporate it as a reinforcing filler to improve tread wear.

It is used in high-performance compounds to improve rolling resistance. In food processing, it acts as an anti-caking agent and flow aid in powdered ingredients, keeping bulk materials free-flowing.

Printing ink and coating formulators use it to control viscosity, matting, and surface texture in both solvent-based and water-based systems. It is supplied as a fine white powder.

Personal care grades are produced to meet cosmetic-specific purity and RDA benchmarks. Technical and rubber-grade variants are also commercially available for specific manufacturing needs.

name: Ethyl 4-(dimethylamino)benzoate
description:

Radiation-curable adhesives and sealants incorporate it to achieve through-cure in pigmented or thick-film formulations. This is essential where surface cure alone is insufficient for the application.

Photopolymer resin systems for plastics and polymer composites use it to improve depth of cure. It also helps to reduce oxygen inhibition at the surface during the manufacturing process.

The compound serves as a building block in the synthesis of UV stabilizer intermediates. It is also utilized in the production of specialty dye compounds for industrial colorant applications.

The product is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white crystalline powder or solid. Technical and photoinitiator-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most industrial buyers.

Purity specifications are typically at 98% or higher for this material. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk drum supply for large-scale industrial formulation use.

name: Phosphorous acid
description:
Phosphorous acid (CAS 10294-56-1 ) is an inorganic acid used industrially as a reducing agent, chelating agent, and corrosion inhibitor across a broad range of chemical processing applications.

It functions primarily to control pH, sequester metal ions, and stabilize formulations against oxidative degradation. In water treatment, it acts as a scale inhibitor and corrosion control agent in cooling water systems.

Agricultural formulations use it as a precursor to phosphonate-based fungicides and as a direct active component in crop protection products targeting oomycete pathogens. It is essential for modern farming.

In textile and leather processing, it supports pH regulation during dyeing and tanning operations where precise acid control affects product consistency. This ensures high-quality finishes in manufacturing.

In construction, it functions as a dispersant and rheology modifier in cement and concrete admixtures, improving workability and flow without excess water addition during the mixing process.

Textile and leather processors use it as a leveling or retanning auxiliary, where controlled charge density helps achieve uniform dye penetration and surface treatment for high-quality finishes.

In paper manufacturing, it supports wet-end chemistry as a retention and drainage aid, contributing to fiber flocculation and sheet formation during the industrial production cycle.

Coating and adhesive formulators incorporate it where crosslinking density and film cohesion need to be tuned through polymer network interactions to ensure long-term durability and performance.

name: 2-Ethylhexyl acetate
description:
2-Ethylhexyl acetate (CAS 103-09-3 ) is a slow-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and personal care formulations. Its low evaporation rate makes it a practical choice for extending open time.

In industrial coatings and printing inks, this ester controls solvent release to reduce surface defects such as blushing and pinholes. It is particularly effective in high-solids and alkyd formulations.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to adjust viscosity and working time in solvent-borne systems. In personal care, it acts as a lightweight carrier and skin-conditioning agent for consumers.

It is commonly found in formulations such as sunscreens, color cosmetics, and leave-on products. Metalworking formulators incorporate it as a coupling solvent and lubricity modifier in cutting fluids.

The product is also used in rust-preventive compounds to ensure long-term protection. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger volumes.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial and coatings applications. Cosmetic-grade material meeting purity specifications for personal care use is also available from select suppliers.
