name: 2-ethylhexyl acrylate
description:
2-Ethylhexyl acrylate (CAS 103-11-7 ), commonly abbreviated as 2-EHA, is a long-chain acrylic monomer used to introduce flexibility and low-temperature performance into polymer systems.

It copolymerizes readily with harder monomers to balance softness, tack, and durability across a broad range of formulated products. In pressure-sensitive adhesives, it is a primary soft monomer.

This monomer controls peel strength and tack in tapes, labels, and protective films. Architectural and industrial coatings rely on it to lower glass transition temperature, improving film flexibility.

It provides resistance to cracking in exterior applications. Sealants and elastomeric compounds incorporate 2-EHA-based polymers where elongation and weathering resistance are critical performance requirements.

In personal care, it appears in film-forming polymers used for hair fixatives and skin-adhesive formulations where soft, flexible films are required for the end user and application.

2-Ethylhexyl acrylate is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats standard for reactive monomers. Technical grade is the predominant specification.

name: 4,4'-dithiodimorpholine
description:
4,4'-Dithiodimorpholine (CAS 103-34-4 ), commonly known as DTDM or Morpholine disulfide, is a sulfur-donor curing agent used in rubber vulcanization. It releases active sulfur during processing to form cross-links within elastomer networks.

This chemical enables controlled cure without relying on elemental sulfur alone. In tire manufacturing, DTDM is used in efficient vulcanization (EV) and semi-EV systems to produce compounds with improved heat aging resistance.

It helps reduce reversion, which is critical for components like sidewalls and inner liners. Rubber goods producers use it in mechanical goods, belts, and hoses where long-term thermal stability under dynamic stress is a priority.

It functions effectively as a secondary curative alongside accelerators such as CBS or TBBS. This allows formulators to fine-tune crosslink density and polysulfide distribution for specific industrial requirements.

Accel R is a recognized trade designation under which this material is supplied for compounding applications. DTDM is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or as pre-dispersed masterbatch forms.

These forms are suited for mixing line integration in large scale facilities. Technical and rubber-grade specifications are standard across the market, with purity typically confirmed by active sulfur content.

The melting point range is also a key indicator of quality for this material. Packaging is available in multi-kilogram bags through to bulk quantities for industrial compounders and chemical distributors.

In flavor and fragrance applications, it serves as a chemical intermediate for synthesizing quaternary ammonium compounds and other nitrogen-based actives used in preservation and biocidal formulations. It is a versatile component for many industrial sectors.

Food-contact and nutraceutical applications leverage its solvent properties for flavor and active ingredient delivery in encapsulated formats for high-performance results.

name: Sodium aluminium phosphate
description:
Sodium aluminium phosphate (CAS 10305-76-7 ), also known commercially as E541 , is a leavening acid and buffering agent used primarily in food manufacturing. The acidic form reacts with sodium bicarbonate to generate carbon dioxide.

This reaction controls the rise and texture of baked goods. In baking powders and self-rising flours, it functions as a slow-acting leavening acid, releasing gas during oven heat rather than at room temperature.

This gives manufacturers greater control over dough handling and product consistency. Processed cheese production relies on it as an emulsifying salt, improving melt characteristics and preventing fat separation.

It is used in sliced and block formats, as well as in dry cake mixes and pancake batters. A delayed leavening response is commercially desirable for shelf-stable formulations in these specific applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a pH buffering agent in solid dosage forms and antacid preparations. It is supplied as a white powder in both acidic and basic grades for various uses.

The acidic form (SALP) is the predominant commercial specification. Food-grade material conforming to E541 specifications under EU food additive regulations is the standard trade form for global distribution.

name: Bakuchiol
description:

This compound is recognized for its retinol-like activity without the photosensitivity concerns associated with vitamin A derivatives. In skincare formulations, it is used as a retinol alternative in anti-aging serums and creams.

It is particularly effective in facial oils targeting fine lines and uneven skin tone within clean beauty and sensitive-skin product lines. It is also incorporated into suncare formulations for its antioxidant activity.

This ingredient helps to stabilize UV-exposed skin and protect against oxidative stress from environmental exposure. Formulators use it in combination with conventional actives such as niacinamide or peptides.

Its compatibility with a broad pH range supports multi-active product development. In pharmaceutical topicals, it is evaluated as a functional ingredient in preparations targeting skin renewal and barrier support.

The material is supplied as a pale yellow to amber viscous liquid. Standard commercial grades include cosmetic-grade and high-purity specifications, with leading market grades typically standardized to high purity.

name: Barium chloride dihydrate
description:
Barium chloride dihydrate (CAS 10326-27-9 ), also known as Baryta Muriatica or BaCl2·2H2O, is an inorganic barium salt supplied in hydrated crystalline form. It functions as a chemical intermediate, precipitating agent, and process additive across water treatment, metallurgical, and textile industries.

In water treatment, it removes sulfate ions through precipitation, helping industrial facilities manage effluent composition and meet discharge standards. Textile and leather processors use it in dyeing and finishing baths.

In these applications, it acts as a mordant and fixative to improve color retention on fiber substrates. In metallurgy and metal surface treatment, it serves in heat treatment salt baths for steel hardening processes.

This material provides controlled thermal environments for case hardening. Pulp and paper operations apply it as a process chemical for sulfate removal and as a catalyst precursor in select chemical synthesis workflows.

Barium chloride dihydrate is available as white crystalline granules or powder. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and reagent or laboratory grade, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

Sodium perborate monohydrate (CAS 10332-33-9 ) is a stable, water-soluble oxidizing salt used industrially as a bleaching and antimicrobial agent. It releases active oxygen upon dissolution, enabling controlled bleaching and disinfection across multiple sectors.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into tooth-whitening formulations, denture cleansers, and oxidative hair color products where controlled peroxide release is critical. These applications rely on the material's stability and predictable performance during the formulation process.

Pulp and paper producers use it as a bleaching agent to achieve target brightness levels while managing effluent impact. In water treatment and industrial disinfection, it functions as a biocide effective against bacteria, fungi, and algae in recirculating systems.

Sodium perborate monohydrate is supplied as a white granular or powder material. It is available in technical grade for industrial bleaching and cleaning applications, as well as in higher-purity grades meeting specifications relevant to personal care.

Standard packaging ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk quantities suited to large-scale industrial procurement. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and efficacy throughout the supply chain and storage period.

In skin and body care formulations, it acts as a lightweight emollient that improves spreadability and skin feel without a heavy or greasy residue. Color cosmetics manufacturers use it as a dispersing medium for pigments and actives.

This ingredient helps achieve uniform distribution in foundations, lipsticks, and pressed powders. It also functions as a plasticizer in lip and stick-format products, where it adjusts hardness and flexibility of the wax matrix.

In hair care applications, it serves as a carrier for conditioning agents in serums and leave-on treatments. This versatility makes it a staple for formulators looking to enhance the application profile of diverse beauty products.

Behenyl benzoate is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on temperature conditions during handling and storage. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification suitable for use in personal care product formulations.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into nail care products, hair sprays, and aerosol formulations. In these applications, a slow-evaporating carrier improves spreadability and finish quality for the consumer.

name: Ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer
description:
Ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer (CAS 103470-05-9 ), also identified by E-number E1050 , is a thermoplastic resin used across adhesives, coatings, and packaging applications.

The vinyl acetate content determines flexibility and adhesion characteristics, allowing formulators to select grades precisely matched to processing and end-use requirements.

In hot-melt adhesive formulations, EVA provides the backbone resin for packaging seals, bookbinding, and product assembly lines where fast set times and strong bonds are required.

Flexible packaging films and shrink wraps rely on EVA to deliver softness and heat-seal performance without compromising clarity for the final consumer product.

Coatings and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a rheology modifier and film-forming agent in waterborne systems to improve the overall durability of the finish.

In the rubber and footwear sector, EVA foam compounds are used for midsoles and cushioning components where controlled density and resilience are critical for performance.

Ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer is supplied as pellets, granules, and emulsion dispersions depending on the intended processing method and the specific machinery used.

Grades vary primarily by vinyl acetate content, typically ranging from 9% to 40% VA, with higher VA content delivering increased flexibility and tackiness for industrial use.

name: Lansoprazole
description:
Lansoprazole (CAS 103577-45-3 ), also referenced under development codes AG-1749 and A-65006, and widely recognized by the brand name Prevacid, is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) active pharmaceutical ingredient.

It is used in the treatment of acid-related gastrointestinal disorders and functions by irreversibly blocking gastric acid secretion, making it a core API in prescription and over-the-counter drug formulations globally.

Lansoprazole is formulated into delayed-release capsules and orally disintegrating tablets targeting conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcer disease, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

It is also incorporated into combination therapy regimens for Helicobacter pylori eradication, typically alongside antibiotics and bismuth compounds for effective clinical outcomes in patients.

Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a bulk API for solid dosage form production across regulated and semi-regulated markets. Contract development and manufacturing organizations utilize it in novel delivery formats.

These formats include enteric-coated pellet systems designed to protect the compound from gastric degradation. Lansoprazole is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in bulk quantities for manufacturing.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. pharmacopoeial grades to meet the regulatory requirements of major markets including the US, EU, and UK. This ensures high quality for global distribution.

Packaging is typically offered in double-polyethylene-lined fiber drums under controlled storage conditions. This ensures the stability and integrity of the pharmaceutical ingredient during long-term transit.

This chemical enables broad-spectrum SPF performance at relatively low use levels. Coating and polymer manufacturers incorporate it to prevent UV-induced yellowing, chalking, and mechanical degradation in materials.

In adhesives, sealants, and elastomers, it extends service life by stabilizing the polymer matrix against prolonged UV exposure. Plastic compounders use it in films, sheets, and molded parts for resistance.

Bisoctrizole is supplied primarily as a micronized aqueous dispersion, the standard form for cosmetic applications. Powder and suspension variants also exist for various industrial and manufacturing uses.

name: Sodium metaphosphate
description:
Sodium metaphosphate (CAS 10361-03-2 ) is an inorganic phosphate salt available in several polymeric forms, including Kurrol's salt and Maddrell's salt. Each form features distinct chain lengths and solubility profiles relevant to industrial sourcing decisions.

It functions primarily as a sequestrant, buffering agent, and scale inhibitor across a range of process industries. In water treatment, it controls scale formation and corrosion in cooling towers and municipal distribution systems.

The compound works by sequestering calcium and magnesium ions to prevent buildup. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a pH buffer and preservative in processed products, where it also improves moisture retention in meat and dairy applications.

Textile and leather processors apply it to sequester hardness ions in dyebaths and tanning liquors. This prevents mineral interference that degrades color consistency and finish quality during the manufacturing process.

In paper manufacturing, it supports pulp processing by controlling metal ion contamination. Without this control, metal ions would otherwise affect bleaching efficiency and the final brightness of the paper product.

Sodium metaphosphate is supplied as a white powder or granules depending on the polymeric form and intended application. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification for use in regulated industries.

Technical-grade product is supplied for industrial water treatment and various process applications. Grades vary by chain length and solubility, so buyers should confirm the specific polymerization form when sourcing.

Dipotassium peroxymonosulfate (CAS 10361-76-9 ), also known as potassium peroxymonosulfate or K2SO5, is the potassium salt form of peroxymonosulfuric acid used commercially as a non-chlorine oxidizing agent.

name: Lithium sulfate
description:

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a reagent and process chemical in the production of lithium-based active ingredients, particularly for psychiatric and neurological drug formulations.

Biotechnology and life sciences applications include its use as a protein crystallization agent, where controlled ionic conditions are critical for structural analysis and drug discovery workflows.

Water treatment operations employ it as a biocidal additive to inhibit microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water circuits throughout the facility.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor in select inorganic synthesis processes, where lithium ion activity influences reaction selectivity and yield during the production cycle.

The product is available as a white crystalline powder in both anhydrous and monohydrate forms. Standard supply grades include technical grade for industrial applications and high-purity grades.

These high-purity options meet pharmaceutical and reagent specifications. Packaging typically ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to bulk industrial supply depending on requirements.

name: Magnesium nitrate
description:
Magnesium nitrate (CAS 10377-60-3 ), also known commercially as Magniosan, is an inorganic salt supplying both magnesium and nitrate ions in a single, highly soluble compound. It functions primarily as a nutrient source in fertilizer systems and as a process chemical across water treatment and industrial manufacturing.

In agriculture, it is used in liquid fertilizer blends and foliar spray formulations where simultaneous delivery of magnesium and nitrate nitrogen corrects soil deficiencies and supports crop yield. Water treatment operations use it as a pH buffering agent and process additive.

These systems require controlled alkalinity without introducing chloride or sulfate ions. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a fixative and auxiliary chemical during dyeing and tanning operations, helping to stabilize process chemistry and improve consistency.

Paper manufacturing incorporates it as a process aid where controlled ionic balance is required during pulp treatment. Magnesium nitrate is available as a crystalline solid and in solution form, with hexahydrate being the predominant commercial grade.

Technical grade is standard across industrial applications, while fertilizer-grade material meeting specific nutrient content specifications is available for agricultural use. Packaging ranges from bulk quantities to bagged formats suited to both industrial and agricultural procurement channels.

name: Manganese nitrate
description:
Manganese nitrate (CAS 10377-66-9 ) is an inorganic manganese salt used as a precursor and catalyst across several industrial processes. It delivers a soluble, reactive source of manganese where controlled deposition or oxidation chemistry is required.

In textile dyeing and finishing, it serves as an oxidation catalyst for producing manganese-based colorants and for fixing certain dye systems onto fabric. The leather and paper industries use it as a component in tanning and bleaching processes.

In these applications, controlled manganese release drives oxidative reactions. In agriculture, it functions as a micronutrient source in fertilizer formulations targeting manganese-deficient soils, particularly for crops sensitive to trace element imbalances.

Water treatment operations apply it to support oxidative removal of iron and manganese from potable and process water streams. This ensures that water quality meets the necessary standards for both human consumption and industrial use.

Manganese nitrate is commercially available as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 50% concentration, and in anhydrous or tetrahydrate solid form. This versatility allows it to be integrated into various liquid or solid manufacturing workflows.

Technical grade is the standard offering across industrial supply channels. Purity specifications and solution concentration should be confirmed against application requirements, as catalyst and agricultural uses may carry different acceptance criteria.

name: Monoethanolamine borate
description:
Monoethanolamine borate (CAS 10377-81-8 ), also known as ethanolamine borate, is a boron-nitrogen compound used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor, pH buffer, and chelating agent.

It combines the functional properties of both ethanolamine and borate chemistry, making it effective across metal-contact and aqueous formulation environments.

In metalworking fluids and cutting oils, it inhibits ferrous and non-ferrous metal corrosion while maintaining alkaline pH stability over extended service life.

Coating formulations incorporate it as a buffering agent to control cure conditions and improve adhesion to metal substrates during the application process.

Water treatment programs use it to sequester hardness ions and prevent scale deposition in recirculating systems. It is highly effective in these industrial environments.

In adhesives and sealants, it functions as a crosslinking aid and pH stabilizer, particularly in systems sensitive to metal ion contamination or fluctuations.

Monoethanolamine borate is typically supplied as a liquid solution, with concentration varying by application requirement and supplier specification for the end user.

It is generally available in technical grade for industrial applications including metalworking, coatings, and water treatment. Bulk liquid supply is the standard format.

name: Tetrasodium edetate dihydrate
description:
Tetrasodium edetate dihydrate (CAS 10378-23-1 ), commercially known as EDTA-4Na, is a fully neutralized sodium salt of EDTA supplied in hydrated form. It functions as a chelating and sequestering agent, binding metal ions such as calcium and magnesium.

By binding iron and copper, it prevents these metal ions from interfering with formulations, processes, or finished products. In personal care and cosmetics, EDTA-4Na stabilizes formulations by deactivating trace metals that would otherwise degrade preservative systems.

This prevents rancidity and ensures long-term product integrity for consumer use. Water treatment operations use it to sequester hardness ions and control scale formation in industrial circuits, improving overall system efficiency and reducing maintenance costs.

Textile and leather processing relies on it to prevent metal-catalyzed oxidation during bleaching and dyeing. This protects color consistency and fabric integrity throughout the manufacturing cycle, ensuring high-quality results for industrial textile producers.

In food-compatible applications, it functions as a sequestrant to maintain product stability and extend shelf life where metal contamination is a processing risk. This makes it a versatile additive for various sensitive manufacturing environments.

Tetrasodium edetate dihydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications and food-grade specifications meeting FCC and BP standards for high purity requirements.

Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities, with concentration typically expressed on a dihydrate basis. This ensures accurate dosing and handling for large-scale chemical operations and specialized laboratory applications alike.

name: Olive oil peg-7 esters
description:
Olive oil PEG-7 esters (CAS 103819-46-1 ), also known as olive oil ethoxylated, is a mild nonionic surfactant derived from the ethoxylation of olive oil fatty acids. It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and moisturizing additive across personal care, cleaning, and textile processing applications.

In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic formulations, it emulsifies oils and conditioning agents while contributing skin-feel benefits that support moisturizing claims in lotions, cleansers, and hair care products.

Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it to improve surface wetting and soil dispersion on both hard surfaces and fabrics. Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a fiber lubricant and wetting agent.

These properties ensure even dye penetration and surface treatment during manufacturing. In food-contact or food-adjacent applications, it can serve as an emulsification aid where ethoxylated vegetable oil derivatives meet applicable regulatory requirements.

Olive oil PEG-7 esters are typically supplied as a liquid or semi-liquid at ambient temperature. Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly available, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity and color specifications.

name: p-toluenesulfonic acid
description:
p-Toluenesulfonic acid (CAS 104-15-4 ), commonly known as tosic acid or pTSA, is a strong organic acid used primarily as an acid catalyst and pH regulator across industrial manufacturing.

Its high solubility in organic solvents makes it a practical alternative to mineral acids in reactions where aqueous conditions are undesirable for the specific chemical process.

In coatings and thermoset systems, pTSA functions as a curing catalyst for amino and phenolic resins, accelerating crosslinking in baked enamel and industrial coating formulations.

Polymer and adhesive manufacturers use it to catalyze esterification, condensation, and polymerization reactions where precise acid control is critical to end-product consistency and performance.

In textile and leather processing, it supports dye fixation and acts as a pH regulator during finishing operations. Printing ink formulators use tosic acid as a dispersing aid and stabilizer.

These applications improve color consistency and shelf stability for pigment systems. p-Toluenesulfonic acid is supplied as a white crystalline solid and as a monohydrate for industrial use.

The monohydrate form is the most common commercial grade due to its handling stability. Technical and industrial grades are standard across the market for various manufacturing needs.

High-purity grades meeting defined specifications are available for applications requiring tighter quality control in catalyst or specialty chemical use within the global supply chain.

description:
N,N,4-Trimethylpiperazine-1-ethylamine (CAS 104-19-8 ), also known commercially as Addocat PP, is a tertiary amine used as a catalyst in polyurethane and polymer systems.

In polyurethane foam and elastomer production, it functions as a blowing and gelation catalyst, balancing the competing reactions that determine cell structure and mechanical performance.

Coatings formulators use it to tune cure speed in two-component polyurethane systems, particularly where pot life and through-cure need to be matched to specific application conditions.

In adhesive and sealant manufacturing, it supports crosslink density development, directly affecting bond strength and flexibility in the cured product. It is a versatile additive for many industries.

It is also used in rigid and flexible polymer systems where controlled amine catalysis is required during processing. This ensures consistent quality and performance across various polymer grades.

N,N,4-Trimethylpiperazine-1-ethylamine is supplied as a liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial catalyst applications and large-scale chemical processing.

It is typically available in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial-scale polyurethane and polymer processing operations. This ensures reliable supply chains for global manufacturing needs.

In these applications, it improves hardness, load-bearing capacity, and thermal resistance in finished parts such as industrial wheels, rollers, and mining screens. It is essential for heavy-duty industrial components.

In printing and packaging, it contributes to the formulation of high-durability inks and coatings where chemical resistance is a key performance requirement. This ensures longevity in harsh environments.

Formulators in the personal care sector incorporate it into film-forming systems and specialty polymer bases. It also functions as a reactive diol in polyester synthesis for various industrial resins.

In printing inks, it functions as a high-boiling solvent and rheology modifier, improving flow and reducing premature drying on press. Coatings formulators incorporate it to extend open time in systems.

This is particularly useful where resin compatibility and leveling performance are priorities. In personal care, it acts as a solvent and carrier in fragrance formulations, emollients, and skin-conditioning products.

It is highly valued where a low-odor, slow-release profile is required. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to adjust viscosity and improve substrate wetting in various solvent-borne systems.

The chemical is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. It is typically offered in technical grade for industrial use.

Purity specifications are commonly at 99% or above. Buyers should confirm purity, water content, and color (APHA) against their formulation requirements when evaluating specific supplier lots for production.

name: 2-ethylhexylamine
description:
2-Ethylhexylamine (CAS 104-75-6 ) is a branched-chain primary amine used as a chemical intermediate and functional additive across several industrial sectors. Its long, branched carbon chain makes it effective where oil-soluble amine character is needed.

This chemical is essential for corrosion protection, pH control, and emulsification in non-aqueous systems. In oilfield and refinery operations, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and neutralizing amine in pipeline treatment and process fluid formulations.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers use it to build amine-based additives that protect metal surfaces. These additives stabilize emulsions under demanding conditions, ensuring long-term performance in industrial machinery and automotive applications.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a curing agent component or pH modifier. This improves resin compatibility and film performance, making it a versatile choice for high-performance industrial coatings and specialized adhesive products.

Water treatment formulators incorporate it into corrosion inhibitor packages for industrial cooling and boiler systems. It is often selected where oil-soluble amines are preferred over water-soluble alternatives to ensure system integrity.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk isotanks for global distribution. It is available primarily in technical grade, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher depending on the specific supplier specification.

Buyers should confirm amine content and water specification when sourcing for sensitive formulation or synthesis applications. Proper handling and storage are required to maintain the quality and stability of the material over its shelf life.

name: 2-ethylhexanol
description:
2-Ethylhexanol (CAS 104-76-7 ), also known as isooctyl alcohol, is a branched-chain fatty alcohol used across chemical manufacturing as a solvent, plasticizer precursor, and chemical intermediate.

Its primary commercial role is as a building block for dioctyl phthalate (DOP) and other plasticizers, as well as acrylate esters used in coatings and adhesives for industrial applications.

In plastics processing, it reacts with phthalic anhydride or adipic acid to produce plasticizers that soften PVC in flexible films, cables, and flooring. This ensures durability and flexibility.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use 2-ethylhexyl acrylate to control film flexibility and tack in pressure-sensitive and architectural coatings. It is essential for high-performance finishes.

In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it functions as a coupling solvent and intermediate for antiwear additive synthesis. This helps maintain stability in demanding mechanical environments.

Personal care and fragrance manufacturers use it under FEMA 3151 as a low-volatility solvent and carrier in fragrance compositions and emollient systems for various consumer goods.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial and chemical synthesis applications.

Food and flavor-grade material conforming to the required standards is available for fragrance and flavor carrier applications. We ensure high purity for all specialized manufacturing needs.

name: P-tolunitrile
description:
P-tolunitrile (CAS 104-85-8 ), also known as 4-cyanotoluene, is an aromatic nitrile compound used as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients and specialty chemicals.

It functions primarily as a building block in pharmaceutical, fragrance, and agrochemical manufacturing rather than as a finished product. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a precursor to active pharmaceutical ingredients.

The nitrile group undergoes hydrolysis, reduction, or cyclization to produce target molecules. Fragrance manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the production of aromatic compounds where controlled functionalization is required.

In agrochemical production, it contributes to the synthesis of herbicides and fungicides through established nitrile chemistry pathways. Industrial cleaning and biocide formulations may incorporate derivatives produced from this intermediate.

P-tolunitrile is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, with purity grades typically ranging from technical to high-purity for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical applications.

It is available in standard packaging configurations including drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and impurity profiles directly with the supplier.

This ensures suitability for regulated synthesis processes. The material is handled according to standard industrial safety protocols for aromatic nitriles to maintain product integrity and operational safety.

name: 5-ethyl-2-methylpyridine
description:
5-Ethyl-2-methylpyridine (CAS 104-90-5 ), commercially known as 5-ethyl-2-picoline or MEP, is a pyridine-base intermediate used as a building block in the synthesis of vitamins, agrochemicals, and pharmaceutical compounds.

It also carries FEMA 3546 status, recognizing its role as a flavoring agent in food applications. MEP is a primary raw material in the industrial production of nicotinic acid and nicotinamide.

In these processes, it undergoes catalytic oxidation at scale. In agrochemical manufacturing, it serves as a precursor to active ingredients in herbicide and pesticide formulations for global distribution.

Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring agent to impart roasted, nutty, or popcorn-like notes in processed products at permitted use levels. It is highly valued for its specific profile.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into compositions targeting savory or tobacco-adjacent scent profiles. 5-Ethyl-2-picoline is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or ISO tank containers for bulk orders.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels commonly at 98% or higher by GC. Food-grade material meeting FEMA compliance is available for flavor and fragrance applications.

These materials are produced to meet rigorous quality standards for industrial use. Our logistics network ensures that all shipments of this intermediate arrive safely and meet your specific production requirements.

name: Cetyl ricinoleate
description:
Cetyl ricinoleate (CAS 10401-55-5 ), also marketed under trade names such as TEGOSOFT CR and JEECHEM CER, is the hexadecyl ester of ricinoleic acid derived from castor oil.

It functions as an emollient, lubricant, and dispersing agent across personal care and industrial formulations. In cosmetics, it is used in lipsticks, lip glosses, and color cosmetics to improve texture.

This ingredient helps extend wear and deliver a smooth, non-greasy skin feel without contributing heaviness to the formula. Sunscreen and skin care formulations incorporate it to enhance spreadability.

It also serves to boost moisturization on the skin surface. In industrial lubricants and metalworking fluids, it provides boundary lubrication and reduces friction between metal surfaces.

Textile and leather processing operations use it as a softening and conditioning agent. This helps to improve the hand feel and flexibility of finished materials during the manufacturing process.

Cetyl ricinoleate is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white waxy solid or low-viscosity liquid depending on temperature and grade. Cosmetic-grade material is the most commonly traded specification.

The product typically meets purity requirements suitable for personal care applications. It is available in drum and bulk quantities from specialty oleochemical suppliers for global distribution.

name: Copper citrate
description:
Copper citrate (CAS 10402-15-0 ) is an inorganic copper salt of citric acid used across agriculture, food, and industrial applications as a source of bioavailable copper and a broad-spectrum biocide.

Its chelated structure allows controlled copper release, making it effective in formulations where sustained activity or nutritional delivery is required. In agriculture, it is registered as a pesticide and fungicide active ingredient.

It is applied to control fungal and bacterial pathogens on crops where copper bioavailability must be balanced against phytotoxicity risk. Food and feed manufacturers use it as a copper fortification agent in nutritional premixes.

It is also used in mineral supplements and animal feed where a soluble, chelated copper source is preferred over inorganic sulfates. Water treatment formulators incorporate it for algae and microbial control.

This includes use in industrial cooling systems and potable water applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a copper source in parenteral nutrition solutions and micronutrient supplement formulations.

Copper citrate is available as a fine powder or crystalline solid. It is supplied in technical grade for agricultural and industrial uses, and in food-grade or USP -compliant specifications for applications.

These high-purity grades are essential for nutritional and pharmaceutical applications. Bulk packaging in fiber drums or bags is standard, with smaller quantities available for laboratory and formulation development use.

name: Flazasulfuron
description:
Flazasulfuron (CAS 104040-78-0 ), also known by the development codes SL-160 and OK-1166 and the trade name Shibagen, is a sulfonylurea herbicide used in selective weed control across a range of crops and non-crop settings.

It inhibits acetolactate synthase (ALS), delivering broad-spectrum control of grasses and broadleaf weeds at low application rates. In viticulture and orchards, it is applied for season-long weed suppression between rows.

This reduces competition without crop damage. Turf management programs use it to control difficult grass species, including annual bluegrass, in amenity and sports turf. It is also registered for use in sugarcane and citrus plantations.

In these agricultural settings, residual soil activity extends the weed-free window between applications. Non-crop and industrial vegetation management programs rely on it for right-of-way and perimeter control.

The compound is supplied as a technical-grade active ingredient and in formulated end products, most commonly as a wettable granule (WG) or water-dispersible granule. Technical material is available for formulation.

Agrochemical manufacturers requiring a high-purity input for herbicide product development can utilize this material. Standard purity for technical grade is typically 95% or above to ensure consistent performance.

name: Eicosapentaenoic acid
description:
Eicosapentaenoic acid ( CAS 10417-94-4 ), commonly known as EPA or Timnodonic acid, is a long-chain omega-3 fatty acid sourced primarily from marine oils and microalgae. It functions as a bioactive nutritional ingredient and pharmaceutical active across finished dosage forms.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, EPA is incorporated into prescription-grade omega-3 concentrates and softgel capsules targeting cardiovascular and metabolic indications. High-purity concentrated forms are required to meet clinical dosing standards.

Functional food and dietary supplement producers use EPA to fortify products such as infant formula, nutrition bars, and enriched dairy. These are typically in encapsulated or emulsified formats to protect oxidation-sensitive material through processing.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, EPA-enriched oils are used in anti-aging serums and barrier-repair creams. The fatty acid supports skin lipid matrix compatibility and overall dermal health in specialty topical applications.

Aquaculture and animal nutrition manufacturers also source EPA-rich concentrates to optimize feed formulations for farmed fish and specialty livestock. This ensures the nutritional profile of the end products meets consumer expectations.

EPA is available as a free fatty acid, ethyl ester, or triglyceride concentrate in liquid form. Purity levels range from standard fish oil concentrates to highly refined grades exceeding 90% EPA content for specific uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is supplied to USP and EP specifications, while food-grade material conforms to FCC standards. Bulk supply is typically handled under nitrogen-blanketed, cold-chain conditions to preserve stability.

name: Ceramide
description:
Ceramide (CAS 104404-17-3 ), also known as N-Acyl Sphingosine, is a sphingolipid naturally present in the skin's stratum corneum that functions as a critical structural component of the epidermal barrier.

In commercial formulations, it acts as a moisturizing and barrier-restoring agent, helping skin retain water and resist environmental stressors. It is primarily used in premium skincare formulations like moisturizers and serums.

These products replenish depleted lipid content in compromised or aging skin. In hair care, it integrates into conditioners and treatment masks to smooth the cuticle surface and reduce moisture loss along the hair shaft.

Pharmaceutical topical products targeting eczema, psoriasis, or post-procedural skin recovery incorporate this ingredient to support barrier function without active drug claims. It is a versatile component for medical skin health.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers also use it as a reference lipid in membrane studies and liposomal delivery system development. This makes it essential for advanced laboratory applications and formulation science.

The material is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder or waxy solid, depending on the specific type and purity grade. Cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent.

Purity levels are typically confirmed by HPLC to ensure consistency. Both synthetic and plant-derived variants are available, and buyers should confirm the source and type when evaluating their supply chain needs.

Common variations include Ceramide NP, AP, or EOP. Ensuring the correct grade and origin is vital for maintaining the efficacy and safety of the final consumer or industrial product.

name: Quinacridone
description:
Quinacridone (CAS 1047-16-1 ), also marketed as C.I. Pigment Violet 19, PV19, and CINQUASIA RED, is a high-performance organic pigment valued across demanding colorant applications.

It delivers exceptional lightfastness, heat stability, and color strength that synthetic alternatives struggle to match, making it a benchmark pigment in premium color formulations.

In automotive OEM and refinish coatings, PV19 produces clean violet-to-red hues that retain color integrity under prolonged UV exposure and high-bake oven cycles.

Plastics compounders incorporate it into engineering polymers where processing temperatures would degrade conventional organic pigments. Printing ink manufacturers rely on it for high-end packaging.

These inks require consistent gamut and resistance to bleed or migration. Cosmetic formulators use C.I. Pigment Violet 19 in color cosmetics such as lipsticks and eyeshadows.

Regulatory compliance and batch-to-batch color consistency are critical sourcing criteria. Quinacridone is supplied as a dry powder in both crude and finished pigment forms.

Particle size and surface treatment vary by application target. Standard commercial grades include uncoated pigment grades for ink and coating systems, and resin-coated or flushed grades.

These are optimized for plastics and high-viscosity applications. Cosmetic-grade material is available with documentation supporting compliance with regional color additive regulations.

name: Strontium chloride
description:
Strontium chloride (CAS 10476-85-4 ) is an inorganic salt supplied primarily for its strontium ion content, which drives its utility across pyrotechnics, electrochemistry, and specialty chemical synthesis.

It functions as a strontium source in processes where controlled ion delivery, flame coloration, or precursor chemistry is required. In pyrotechnics and signal flares, it produces the characteristic crimson-red flame color.

This color defines military and commercial formulations. Battery manufacturers use it as an electrolyte additive or precursor in strontium-based electrode materials for high-performance applications.

In catalyst preparation, it acts as a precursor to strontium oxide and mixed-metal oxide systems used in petrochemical and polymer processing. It is a vital component for these industrial sectors.

Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical producers also use it as a pH buffer and ionic medium in select synthesis and formulation processes. It ensures stability and precision in complex chemical reactions.

Strontium chloride is available as an anhydrous powder and as the hexahydrate crystalline form, with the hexahydrate being the more commonly traded grade for most industrial buyers.

Standard supply specifications include technical grade and reagent grade, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+. Packaging is offered in bulk bags and fiber drums suited to procurement.

name: Sodium perborate tetrahydrate
description:
Sodium perborate tetrahydrate (CAS 10486-00-7 ) is an oxygen-releasing bleaching agent used across cleaning, textile, and personal care manufacturing. It delivers controlled oxidative action upon dissolution, making it a practical alternative to chlorine-based bleaches.

In laundry detergent formulations, it acts as the primary bleaching component, targeting stains from tea, wine, and organic soils at elevated wash temperatures. This ensures color safety and fabric integrity are maintained during the cleaning process.

Textile processors use it to bleach natural fibers such as cotton and linen without the fiber degradation associated with hypochlorite treatments. This makes it a preferred choice for high-quality textile manufacturing and finishing.

In personal care manufacturing, it is incorporated into tooth whitening powders and denture cleansers where peroxide release must be gradual and controlled. This application highlights its versatility in sensitive consumer product formulations.

Industrial and institutional cleaning products also rely on it for disinfection and stain removal in hard surface applications. Its stability and efficacy make it a reliable component for heavy-duty professional cleaning solutions.

Sodium perborate tetrahydrate is supplied as a white granular or powder material. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial cleaning and textile applications, meeting various industrial requirements.

Detergent-grade material is also available to meet specific formulation purity requirements for consumer goods. It is commonly traded in bulk bags and smaller formats to serve both large-scale manufacturers and specialty formulators.

name: Ethyl bromoacetate
description:
Ethyl bromoacetate ( CAS 105-36-2 ), also known commercially as Antol, is a reactive alkylating ester used as a key building block in organic synthesis. It functions primarily as an intermediate in the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

The compound is essential for specialty chemicals, where its reactive bromomethyl group enables carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bond formation. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a precursor in the synthesis of amino acids and peptides.

It is also used for a broad range of API scaffolds requiring acetic acid ester functionalization. Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it as a synthetic intermediate in fragrance molecule production for specific olfactory profiles.

The chemical contributes to the construction of esters and lactones. It also has documented use as a biocidal and preservative agent in industrial applications, where its reactivity toward biological nucleophiles provides antimicrobial effect.

In flavor and fragrance chemistry, Antol is referenced as a starting material for aroma compounds requiring bromoacetate chemistry. The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for various industrial processes.

It is available in technical and reagent grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 97% to 99%+. Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a carbon-chain extender in the production of barbiturates, amino acids, and other active pharmaceutical ingredients. Personal care formulators use it as a carrier solvent and reactive intermediate.

Diethyl malonate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. Standard commercial grades include technical and food-grade ( FCC ) specifications.

name: Diethyl carbonate
description:
Diethyl carbonate ( CAS 105-58-8 ), also known as DEC or Eufin, is a low-toxicity carbonate ester solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, battery electrolyte production, and specialty chemical synthesis.

Its low water reactivity and miscibility with a broad range of organic solvents make it a preferred alternative to more hazardous polar aprotic solvents in regulated production environments.

In lithium-ion battery electrolyte formulations, DEC is a primary co-solvent that improves ionic conductivity and low-temperature performance for high-performance energy storage systems.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reaction solvent and carbonylation reagent in the synthesis of carbamates, polycarbonates, and active pharmaceutical ingredients for various medical applications.

In food and flavor applications, it functions as a beverage preservative and fermentation inhibitor, particularly in wine and fruit juices where microbial control is required without heat treatment.

Specialty chemical producers also use DEC as a methylation and ethylation agent in catalyst preparation and fine chemical synthesis, offering high selectivity and safety in industrial processes.

Diethyl carbonate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical, anhydrous, and high-purity specifications suited to battery use.

FCC grade material is available for food and beverage use cases requiring regulatory compliance documentation. Our logistics team ensures reliable delivery of high-purity chemicals to global facilities.

name: Methyldiethanolamine
description:
Methyldiethanolamine ( CAS 105-59-9 ), commonly known as MDEA, is a tertiary amine alcohol used across gas processing, water treatment, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a selective acid gas absorbent and pH buffer.

In natural gas and refinery operations, MDEA is the preferred solvent for selective H2S removal from gas streams containing CO2. This process offers lower regeneration energy costs than competing amines used in the industry.

Personal care formulators use it as a pH adjuster and neutralizing agent in creams, lotions, and hair care products. In these applications, it also contributes mild conditioning properties to the final consumer formulations.

Water treatment programs rely on MDEA to control pH and inhibit corrosion in industrial cooling and boiler systems. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of critical infrastructure in various manufacturing plants.

In polymer and coatings chemistry, it functions as a curing co-agent and crosslinker intermediate. It is frequently utilized in polyurethane and epoxy formulations to enhance the structural integrity of the finished materials.

MDEA is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid, typically in concentrations of 99% and above. Aqueous solutions at various concentrations are also available to meet specific process requirements for global clients.

The material is typically provided in a standard commercial specification. However, pharmaceutical-grade material is available for regulated applications requiring compliance with specific industry safety and purity protocols.

name: Caprolactam
description:
Caprolactam (CAS 105-60-2 ), commonly abbreviated as CPL, is the primary monomer used to produce Nylon 6, one of the world's most commercially significant engineering polymers.

Epsilon-Caprolactam undergoes ring-opening polymerization to yield polycaprolactam, forming the backbone of synthetic fiber and resin production at industrial scale.

The dominant use of CPL is in synthetic fiber manufacturing, where polymerized Nylon 6 is extruded into yarn for apparel, hosiery, carpeting, and technical textiles.

In plastics and engineering resins, it feeds the production of injection-molded components including automotive parts, gears, and structural housings for various industries.

Caprolactam also serves as a building block for polyurethane coatings and adhesives used in leather finishing and industrial paper treatments across the global market.

Specialty applications include its use as a blocking agent for isocyanates in reactive coating systems, where controlled deblocking at elevated temperatures enables precise cure profiles.

Caprolactam is supplied as a white crystalline solid or in molten liquid form for bulk industrial shipment to ensure efficient processing for large-scale manufacturers.

Standard commercial grades include technical-grade and fiber-grade CPL, with purity levels typically at 99.5% or higher to meet strict downstream polymerization requirements.

name: Dibutyl maleate
description:
Dibutyl maleate (CAS 105-76-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DBM, is a reactive diester monomer used across polymer chemistry and surface coating formulations. Known commercially as Staflex DBM and RC Comonomer DBM, it functions primarily as a reactive plasticizer.

It serves as a copolymerizable building block in resin systems. In acrylic and vinyl polymer production, DBM is incorporated as a comonomer to modify flexibility, adhesion, and film-forming properties in emulsion polymerization systems.

Printing inks and packaging coatings use it to improve substrate adhesion and control the mechanical properties of the cured film. In PVC and synthetic rubber compounding, it acts as a reactive plasticizer that bonds into the polymer matrix.

This bonding prevents the substance from migrating out over time, which is a critical advantage for long-life flexible articles. Personal care formulators have also evaluated DBM as an emollient ester component in skin-conditioning systems.

Dibutyl maleate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial packaging including drums and IBCs. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 99% or above.

In plastics compounding, it improves flexibility and cold-temperature performance in PVC formulations where standard phthalate or general-purpose adipates fall short. Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators use it as a base fluid or additive.

This chemical helps to reduce friction in cutting oils, rolling lubricants, and gear fluids. In textile processing, it acts as a fiber lubricant and softening agent, improving handle and reducing mechanical stress during yarn and fabric production.

Leather finishing formulations incorporate it as a softener to enhance suppleness and durability in treated hides. This versatile ester provides consistent performance across a wide range of thermal conditions and mechanical environments.

name: Dibutyl adipate
description:
Dibutyl adipate (CAS 105-99-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DBA, is a diester plasticizer and emollient derived from adipic acid and butanol. It functions as a plasticizer, lubricant, and skin-conditioning agent across personal care, food-contact, and industrial applications.

In personal care formulations, DBA acts as an emollient and spreading agent in creams, lotions, lip products, and color cosmetics. It provides a non-greasy skin feel without the heaviness of heavier esters, making it ideal for modern cosmetic formulations.

Food-contact and flavor applications use it as a solvent carrier for flavor compounds and as a plasticizer in food-grade films and packaging materials. This versatility allows for its use in various sensitive manufacturing environments.

In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it serves as a synthetic base fluid or co-fluid where low-temperature performance and oxidative stability are required. It is highly valued for its consistent performance in demanding industrial settings.

It also functions as a plasticizer for cellulose-based coatings and specialty polymers where flexibility at low temperatures is a formulation requirement. This ensures that coatings remain durable and crack-resistant in cold climates.

Dibutyl adipate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Cosmetic-grade and technical-grade are the most commonly available specifications for global distribution and industrial procurement.

name: 2-Adamantanamine hydrochloride
description:
2-Adamantanamine hydrochloride (CAS 10523-68-9 ), also known as 2-Aminoadamantane hydrochloride, is a bridged-ring amine salt used as a building block in pharmaceutical synthesis.

Its rigid adamantane scaffold is valued in drug design for improving metabolic stability and receptor selectivity in candidate molecules. The compound serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of CNS-active pharmaceuticals.

The adamantane core is incorporated to enhance binding affinity at specific neurological targets. In antiviral and antidiabetic drug development, adamantane-derived amines are used to construct scaffolds for DPP-4 inhibitors.

These amines also function as ion channel modulators. Medicinal chemistry programs use this compound in SAR studies to evaluate the effect of the bridged ring system on pharmacokinetic profiles.

Biotech research applications include its use as a coupling partner in the preparation of labeled probes. These are frequently utilized in conjugates for receptor binding assays during drug discovery phases.

2-Adamantanamine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots to support both early-stage discovery and process development.

Material is typically offered to pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Documentation includes CoA, HPLC purity data, and residual solvent profiles aligned with ICH guidelines to ensure high quality standards.

name: Tetraacetylethylenediamine
description:
Tetraacetylethylenediamine (CAS 10543-57-4 ), commonly known as TAED, is a bleach activator used in detergent and cleaning formulations to boost oxidative performance at lower wash temperatures.

It reacts with hydrogen peroxide or perborate salts to generate peracetic acid in situ, enabling effective bleaching without elevated heat. In laundry detergents, TAED is the standard activator.

It works with sodium percarbonate and sodium perborate systems, allowing cold-water washing to achieve stain removal performance comparable to hot-wash cycles. This saves significant energy during use.

Textile and paper processors use it to activate peroxide bleaching baths, reducing energy costs while maintaining whiteness targets on cellulosic substrates. It is highly efficient in these industrial settings.

Personal care formulators incorporate TAED into tooth-whitening systems and oxidative hair color products where controlled peracid generation is required. It ensures safety and efficacy in consumer goods.

Industrial and institutional cleaning products rely on it to deliver sanitizing and biocidal action through in-situ peracetic acid formation in hard surface and food-contact applications for safety.

TAED is supplied as a white to off-white granular powder or compacted granule, with granule grades engineered for controlled dissolution rates in detergent manufacturing. This allows for precise dosing.

Standard commercial specifications typically range from 94% to 98% active content, with detergent-grade being the dominant market form. Bulk supply is available in bags and big bags for operations.

name: Nitrogen trioxide
description:
Nitrogen trioxide (CAS 10544-73-7 ), also known as dinitrogen trioxide, is an unstable nitrogen oxide that functions as a reactive oxidizing intermediate in industrial chemical processes.

It is generated in situ during nitric acid production and nitrogen oxide chemistry, where it acts as a key oxidant and pH-influencing species in aqueous systems.

In water treatment, nitrogen trioxide species contribute to oxidative disinfection and pH regulation within nitrous acid equilibria, supporting process control in municipal systems.

Pulp and paper operations utilize nitrogen oxide chemistry in bleaching sequences where selective oxidation brightens cellulose fiber without the use of chlorine-based agents.

Mining and metals processing draws on its corrosion-inhibiting behavior in acidic leach circuits, where controlled nitrogen oxide atmospheres protect critical process equipment.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations leverage its oxidizing capacity in heavy-duty descaling and surface preparation products targeting mineral deposits and organic soils.

Nitrogen trioxide is not commercially supplied as an isolated, stable product. It is generated on-site or in-process from nitrogen oxide precursors and nitric acid systems.

Buyers typically source it indirectly through nitric oxide supply chains, with technical-grade nitrogen oxides available in pressurized cylinders or bulk liquid form.

name: 8(S)-HETE
description:
8(S)-HETE (CAS 105500-09-2 ), also referenced in research contexts as 8(R)-HETE when specifying stereoisomeric counterparts, is a hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid produced endogenously.

It is formed through lipoxygenase-mediated oxidation of arachidonic acid. It functions as a bioactive lipid mediator used primarily as a reference standard and research reagent in eicosanoid biology.

In pharmaceutical research, it is used as an analytical reference standard for quantifying hydroxy-fatty acid profiles in biological samples. This supports drug discovery programs targeting lipid signaling pathways.

Biotechnology laboratories employ it in receptor binding assays and enzyme activity studies focused on lipoxygenase and cytochrome P450 pathways. It is also used in cell-based assays investigating signaling.

Precise stereochemical identity is critical for reproducible results in these studies. Metabolomics and lipidomics platforms use it as a certified reference material for method validation and calibration.

The product is supplied as a solution, typically in ethanol or a compatible organic solvent, given its instability in neat form. Standard pack sizes are small-scale, ranging from microgram to low-milligram quantities.

Material is generally available at research-grade purity with a certificate of analysis confirming stereochemical identity and concentration. It meets rigorous internal quality standards for analytical consistency.

description:

In wheat cultivation, this active ingredient is formulated into emulsifiable concentrates and wettable powder products for field application against problematic grass weeds such as wild oat and ryegrass. It is commonly co-formulated with safeners to improve crop tolerance.

Agrochemical manufacturers source the technical-grade active ingredient for blending into finished herbicide formulations distributed across major grain-producing markets. This ensures effective weed control while maintaining the safety of the primary cereal crops.

Contract formulators also incorporate it into premix products targeting resistance management programs in high-intensity cereal farming regions. These specialized formulations are essential for maintaining long-term efficacy in modern agricultural practices.

The chemical is supplied as a technical-grade active ingredient, typically as a solid or concentrated form for downstream formulation use. Standard purity for technical grade is generally 95% or higher, meeting requirements for agrochemical registration.

name: Sodium metaborate tetrahydrate
description:
Sodium metaborate tetrahydrate (CAS 10555-76-7 ) is a hydrated boron-sodium salt used industrially as a pH buffer and corrosion inhibitor across water treatment, construction, and agricultural applications.

It releases borate ions in solution, making it effective for alkalinity control and metal surface protection in process systems. In water treatment, it functions as a buffering agent to maintain stable alkalinity.

The compound helps inhibit corrosion in cooling water and industrial circulation systems. Textile, leather, and paper processing operations use it to regulate bath pH during dyeing, tanning, and pulp treatment.

Consistent alkalinity directly affects product quality in these industrial processes. In building and construction, it serves as a component in cement and concrete formulations requiring controlled setting chemistry.

It is also utilized for borate-based preservation in various building materials. Agricultural applications include its use as a boron micronutrient source in soil amendment and foliar treatment products.

Controlled solubility is a key formulation requirement for these agricultural uses. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid for easy handling and dissolution.

It is available in technical grade for industrial applications including water treatment and construction. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on application volume.

name: Dimethyldipropylenetriamine

Dimethyldipropylenetriamine (CAS 10563-29-8 ) is a polyamine compound used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor, chelating agent, and pH buffer across water treatment and surface protection applications.

Its triamine structure allows it to coordinate with metal ions and interact with surfaces, making it functional across multiple chemistries simultaneously in various industrial environments.

In water treatment systems, it controls corrosion in recirculating and industrial cooling circuits by forming protective complexes with metal surfaces and sequestering dissolved metal ions.

This sequestration prevents ions that would otherwise accelerate degradation. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a curing agent or adhesion promoter in epoxy-based systems for film integrity.

In these systems, its amine groups react with resin components to build durability. In adhesives and sealants, it contributes to crosslink density and substrate bonding performance.

This is particularly effective on metal and concrete surfaces. Metalworking fluid formulators use it for pH stabilization and to inhibit ferrous corrosion in cutting and grinding operations.

name: Sodium dichromate
description:
Sodium dichromate (CAS 10588-01-9 ), also known as sodium bichromate, is an inorganic chromium(VI) salt supplied primarily as a strong oxidizing agent and corrosion inhibitor across heavy industry.

It is one of the most commercially significant hexavalent chromium compounds, used in metal surface treatment, chemical synthesis, and industrial processing for various sectors.

In metal finishing and anticorrosion systems, it functions as a passivation agent for aluminum, zinc, and magnesium surfaces, forming protective oxide layers that extend component service life.

The leather industry relies on it as a precursor in chrome tanning processes, where it oxidizes tanning auxiliaries to produce consistent, durable hides for manufacturing.

In mining and metallurgy, it serves in ore processing and as a flotation reagent for separating sulfide minerals. Pulp and paper operations use it as a bleaching oxidant.

It is also utilized in the production of chromate-based pigments for specialty papers and coatings. The compound is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as the dihydrate form.

The dihydrate is the most common commercial grade and is available in technical grade for industrial applications, typically at high purity concentrations for chemical synthesis.

name: 12-hydroxystearic acid
description:
12-Hydroxystearic acid (CAS 106-14-9 ), commonly abbreviated as 12-HSA, is a hydroxy fatty acid derived from castor oil hydrogenation. It functions as a primary building block for rheology modifiers and lubricant thickeners.

This versatile chemical serves as a critical component for emulsifiers across multiple industrial sectors. In lubricant manufacturing, it is the key precursor for lithium and calcium soap greases.

The material determines thickener structure and ultimately controls grease consistency and performance. Plastics processors use it as an internal and external lubricant in PVC and other polymer compounds.

It reduces friction during extrusion and improves the surface finish of finished parts. Personal care formulators incorporate it into stick products, balms, and anhydrous formulations to build structure.

It modifies texture without relying on synthetic waxes and functions as a dispersing agent in pigment pastes. It also acts as an emulsifier in industrial coatings, helping stabilize particle distribution.

name: Geraniol
description:
Geraniol (CAS 106-24-1 ), also recognized by its FEMA number 2507 , is a naturally derived terpene alcohol sourced from rose, citronella, and palmarosa essential oils. It functions as a fragrance ingredient and flavoring agent across personal care, food, and industrial applications.

In personal care and cosmetics, geraniol imparts a fresh, floral-rose character to perfumes, lotions, soaps, and hair care products. It also contributes to surface-active behavior in formulation systems for various consumer goods.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it as an approved flavoring agent to deliver citrus and rose notes in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods. In flavor compound blending, it serves as a key building block for producing citronellol and citral.

Printing and packaging applications utilize its reactive alcohol functionality in UV-curable and cross-linking resin systems. This is particularly useful in industrial settings where controlled reactivity is required for high-performance coatings.

Geraniol is supplied as a pale yellow to colorless liquid in both natural and synthetic grades. Standard specifications include food-grade ( FCC -compliant) and fragrance-grade material for diverse manufacturing needs.

Purity levels typically range from 95% to 98%+, ensuring high quality for sensitive applications. Bulk quantities are available in drums and IBCs, with smaller packaging options for laboratory and formulation use.

name: Isoamyl butyrate
description:
Isoamyl butyrate ( CAS 106-27-4 ), also known as isopentyl butyrate, is a synthetic ester used commercially as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient. It delivers a characteristic banana, pear, and tropical fruit profile.

This profile makes it a go-to choice for flavor houses and fragrance compounders. FEMA 2060 status confirms its recognized safety standing for use in food applications across the global market.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to create or reinforce banana, pear, and tropical fruit notes in confectionery, beverages, baked goods, and dairy products. It is highly versatile for these uses.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products, including shampoos, body lotions, and soaps, where fruity top notes are required. It provides a consistent and pleasant aromatic experience.

It also appears in functional flavor blends where a low-cost, stable ester is needed to anchor volatile top-note compositions. This stability is essential for maintaining the integrity of complex flavor profiles.

Confectionery manufacturers sourcing banana-flavored coatings and fillings frequently specify it as a primary flavoring agent. Its reliability makes it a staple in large-scale industrial food production.

Isoamyl butyrate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. It is available in food-grade and flavor-grade specifications aligned with FEMA and FCC standards.

Technical-grade material is also available for fragrance and non-food applications where food compliance is not required. This ensures a range of options for different manufacturing and regulatory needs.

name: Ethyl heptanoate
description:
Ethyl heptanoate ( CAS 106-30-9 ), also known commercially as wine oil or oenanthic ether, is an ester used primarily as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient. It delivers a characteristic fruity, cognac-like, and wine-adjacent aroma profile.

This profile makes it a target compound for flavor houses and fragrance formulators sourcing finished ingredient inputs. In food and beverage flavoring, it is used to replicate or reinforce cognac, brandy, and fruit notes.

The compound carries FEMA 2437 status for use in approved flavor applications in both alcoholic and non-alcoholic product formulations. Fragrance manufacturers incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional compositions.

It is particularly useful where wine-like or fruity top notes are required. In personal care, it functions as a fragrance component in skin and hair care products, contributing to scent profiles in lotions and creams.

The ingredient is also utilized in rinse-off formulations. Its ester character supports mild emollient and skin-conditioning performance in cosmetic bases, providing functional benefits alongside its aromatic properties.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and smaller packaging formats suited to flavor and fragrance procurement volumes. It is available in food-grade quality meeting FEMA standards.

Purity levels are maintained to meet flavor industry requirements. Technical-grade material is also available for fragrance and cosmetic applications where food compliance is not required for the final formulation.

name: Propyl propionate
description:
Propyl propionate (CAS 106-36-5 ) is an ester solvent and flavoring agent used across coatings, personal care, and food applications. FEMA 2958 designation confirms its recognized status as a flavoring ingredient in food-grade contexts.

It delivers a fruity, rum-like aroma profile that supports its dual role in both industrial solvent systems and flavor formulations. In coatings and printing inks, it functions as a fast-evaporating solvent that improves flow and film formation.

This chemical improves film formation without leaving residue. Adhesive formulators use it as a carrier solvent to control viscosity and open time in solvent-based systems, ensuring consistent application and performance in industrial settings.

In personal care, it acts as a solvent and emollient carrier in fragrance compositions, nail care products, and aerosol formulations. Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it as a flavoring agent to impart fruity, sweet notes.

These sweet notes are ideal for confectionery, beverages, and baked goods. Propyl propionate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for flavor and cosmetic applications.

It is available in technical grade for coatings and adhesive use, and in food-grade purity aligned with FEMA and flavor industry standards. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and regulatory compliance documentation when sourcing.

Particular attention should be paid to FCC certification when sourcing for food or cosmetic end uses. This ensures the material meets the rigorous safety and quality requirements necessary for consumer-facing products and global trade.

name: p-Cresol
description:
p-Cresol (CAS 106-44-5 ), also known by its FEMA 2337 designation in flavor applications, is a methylphenol derivative used across fragrance, pharmaceutical, and industrial chemistry.

It acts as a chemical building block and functional additive, serving as a precursor, preservative, and stabilizer depending on the specific formulation context and industrial requirements.

In flavors and fragrances, it contributes phenolic, smoky, and medicinal character to food flavorings and fine fragrance compositions at controlled use levels for optimal sensory profiles.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing antioxidants, disinfectants, and active pharmaceutical ingredients, ensuring high performance in medical applications.

In coatings and polymer systems, it functions as an antioxidant stabilizer to protect resins and elastomers from oxidative degradation during processing and throughout their service life.

Personal care formulators incorporate it at low concentrations for its preservative and antimicrobial properties in select cosmetic systems, maintaining product integrity and safety.

The product is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on temperature conditions during handling. It is available in technical grade for industrial and coating applications.

Higher-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical intermediate and flavor use. Packaging typically ranges from drums to ISO containers for bulk procurement and global distribution.

name: 1,4-dichlorobenzene
description:
1,4-Dichlorobenzene (CAS 106-46-7 ), commonly sourced as PDCB or para-dichlorobenzene, is an aromatic chlorinated compound used industrially as a biocide, chemical intermediate, and moth-repellent active.

Its controlled sublimation profile makes it effective in slow-release preservation and fumigant applications without liquid handling. In textile and leather processing, PDCB acts as a moth-proofing agent.

It protects stored wool, fur, and natural fiber goods during warehousing and transit. It functions as a key intermediate in the synthesis of polyphenylene sulfide (PPS), a high-performance engineering polymer.

This polymer is used in automotive and electrical components. In printing and packaging, it contributes to specialty solvent formulations and carrier systems for pigment dispersion in various industrial processes.

PDCB also serves as a chemical building block in flame retardant production, where chlorinated aromatic structures are incorporated into polymer matrices to meet specific fire resistance requirements.

1,4-Dichlorobenzene is supplied as white crystalline flakes or compressed solid forms such as cakes and blocks, depending on the end application. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher for industrial use. Bulk supply is available in fiber drums or bags, with smaller packaged formats offered for specialty or consumer-adjacent end uses.
