name: 4-chloroaniline
description:
4-Chloroaniline ( CAS 106-47-8 ), also known as para-Chloroaniline or p-Chloroaniline, is an aromatic amine intermediate used across dye, agrochemical, and polymer manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a building block for synthesizing pigments, biocides, and curing agents rather than as a finished product in its own right for industrial applications.

In dye and pigment production, it serves as a key intermediate for azo dyes used in textile and leather coloring, where consistent purity directly affects color yield and batch reproducibility.

Agrochemical formulators use it to produce herbicide and pesticide active ingredients, making raw material specification a critical procurement decision for large scale manufacturing.

In polymer and rubber applications, it contributes to the synthesis of curing agents and cross-linkers that influence final material hardness and thermal resistance in various environments.

Personal care and cosmetics manufacturers source it as an intermediate in the production of certain hair dye precursors and preservative compounds used in global consumer markets.

This chemical is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical intermediate use.

It is typically packaged in drums or IBCs, with bulk quantities available for industrial-scale procurement. Specialty chemical applications may require specific handling and storage protocols.

name: p-toluidine

It functions primarily as a building block and curing agent across several manufacturing industries. In dye and pigment manufacturing, it is a key intermediate for azo dyes used in textile dyeing and leather finishing.

Rubber and elastomer producers use it as a curing and cross-linking agent to control vulcanization characteristics in finished compounds. In printing inks and packaging coatings, it contributes to the synthesis of colorants.

These colorants require specific hue and fastness properties for high-performance applications. Personal care and cosmetic formulators source it as a precursor in the production of hair dye intermediates.

It is also utilized in oxidative colorant systems for professional salon products. The material is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline solid or low-melting flake for industrial handling.

name: p-phenylenediamine
description:
p-Phenylenediamine ( CAS 106-50-3 ), commonly abbreviated as PPD or p-Diaminobenzene, is an aromatic diamine used across polymer, textile, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as a curing agent, dye intermediate, and antioxidant precursor in industrial formulations.

In rubber and polymer processing, PPD derivatives serve as antiozonants and antidegradants, extending the service life of tires, belts, and industrial rubber goods. The textile and leather industries rely on PPD as a key intermediate in the synthesis of azo dyes and sulfur dyes.

These applications enable deep, wash-resistant coloration on fiber substrates. In aramid fiber production, including high-performance materials like Kevlar, it acts as a monomer in polycondensation reactions. This contributes directly to tensile strength and flame resistance.

Hair dye formulations in personal care use PPD as an oxidative colorant intermediate. In these applications, it reacts with hydrogen peroxide to produce permanent color. This chemical is essential for achieving long-lasting results in professional cosmetic products.

p-Phenylenediamine is supplied as a crystalline solid, typically in flake or powder form. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial polymer and dye applications. This ensures the material meets the necessary specifications for large-scale manufacturing.

Material is commonly packaged in sealed, nitrogen-purged containers to maintain quality during storage and transit. Proper handling and storage are critical to prevent oxidation and ensure the chemical stability of the product upon arrival at your facility.

name: 1,4-benzoquinone
description:
1,4-Benzoquinone (CAS 106-51-4 ), also known as quinone or p-BQ, is an oxidizing intermediate used across chemical synthesis, dye manufacturing, and surface treatment processes.

It functions primarily as a catalyst, oxidant, and chemical building block in industrial production. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, p-BQ serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active compounds.

This includes antifungal and antimalarial agents. Dye and pigment producers use it as a precursor for hydroquinone-based colorants and as an oxidant in coupling reactions for printing inks and packaging colorants.

In rubber and polymer processing, it acts as a polymerization inhibitor and crosslinking agent, helping control reaction rates during production. This ensures stability and consistency in the final product.

Personal care formulators incorporate quinone derivatives as intermediates in hair dye chemistry, where controlled oxidation is critical to color development. It is essential for achieving specific shades.

1,4-Benzoquinone is supplied as a yellow crystalline solid, typically in powder or flake form. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for industrial applications.

Higher-purity grades are available to meet pharmaceutical synthesis requirements. It is packaged in fiber drums or sealed containers due to its sensitivity to moisture and light during storage.

Proper handling is required during transit to maintain the integrity of the material. Our supply chain ensures that all chemical building blocks meet rigorous industrial safety protocols.

name: 1,4-dimethylpiperazine
description:
1,4-Dimethylpiperazine (CAS 106-58-1 ), commercially known as Texacat DMP, is a tertiary diamine used as a catalyst and curing agent across polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing. The abbreviation DMP is commonly used in procurement and formulation contexts.

It accelerates reaction systems and acts as a building block in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients and industrial intermediates. In polyurethane production, DMP functions as a tertiary amine catalyst that promotes gel and blow reactions.

This chemical influences foam structure and cure speed during the manufacturing process. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to accelerate epoxy curing, controlling open time and final film hardness in various industrial applications.

In elastomer and sealant systems, it supports cross-linking reactions that determine flexibility and durability of the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a synthetic intermediate for piperazine-based APIs.

Its dimethyl substitution pattern is a specific structural requirement for many complex molecules. 1,4-Dimethylpiperazine is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or bulk containers for large-scale industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher for catalyst and synthesis applications. This ensures consistent performance in sensitive chemical reactions and polymer formulations.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting tighter impurity profiles is available for API manufacturing, with documentation aligned to ICH guidelines. We ensure all batches meet rigorous internal quality standards for reliability and safety.

name: 2-(2-Hydroxypropoxy)-1-propanol
description:
2-(2-Hydroxypropoxy)-1-propanol (CAS 106-62-7 ), commonly known as dipropylene glycol, is a diol solvent and humectant used across cleaning, coatings, and personal care manufacturing.

Its low volatility and miscibility with water and organic solvents make it a practical carrier and coupling agent in formulated products. In home care and industrial cleaning, it functions as a coupling solvent.

This material keeps surfactant-based formulations stable and improves soil removal in hard-surface cleaners. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use it as a coalescing aid and plasticizing solvent.

It helps to improve film formation and flexibility in waterborne systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a humectant and solvent carrier in lotions, serums, and fragrance bases.

It is ideal for applications where controlled moisture retention is required. In polymer processing, it acts as a reactive intermediate or plasticizer in polyurethane and polyester resin systems.

The product is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include industrial and fragrance-grade specifications for various uses.

Fragrance grade meets purity requirements set by IFRA and major flavor and fragrance buyers. Technical grade is available for coatings and polymer applications where cosmetic-grade purity is not required.

name: Dimethyl succinate
description:
Dimethyl succinate (CAS 106-65-0 ), also known by FEMA 2396 , is a diester solvent and flavoring agent used across personal care formulation and food manufacturing. It functions as a carrier solvent and humectant.

In food and beverage manufacturing, dimethyl succinate delivers a mild fruity, wine-like flavor note. It is used in flavoring systems for confectionery, baked goods, and beverages under regulatory approval.

Personal care formulators use it as a low-viscosity carrier solvent to improve spreadability and skin feel in emollients and lotions. Its humectant behavior supports moisture retention in leave-on cosmetic formulations.

This material is a practical alternative to heavier ester solvents in fragrance delivery systems. It also functions as a co-solvent in fragrance concentrates, helping to solubilize aromatic ingredients at controlled dilution.

Dimethyl succinate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to both industrial and specialty formulation volumes. This ensures reliable logistics for large-scale manufacturing needs.

Food-grade material conforming to established standards is the primary commercial specification for flavor and cosmetic applications. Technical-grade material is available for solvent and process applications.

Whether used for its aromatic properties or its solvent capabilities, this diester provides consistent performance. It remains a versatile component for chemists developing modern consumer and industrial products.

name: Dimethyl sebacate
description:
Dimethyl sebacate (CAS 106-79-6 ), also known as DMS, is a dibasic ester derived from sebacic acid used as a plasticizer, lubricant base fluid, and emollient across multiple industrial sectors.

Dimethyl decanedioate is a recognized alternative name in polymer and lubricant sourcing contexts. Its low volatility and thermal stability make it a practical choice for demanding formulation and processing environments.

In plastics and polymer processing, DMS functions as a plasticizer for PVC, cellulosics, and synthetic resins, improving flexibility and processing characteristics in finished films and coatings.

Lubricant formulators use it as a base fluid or co-fluid in synthetic lubricants and metalworking fluids where oxidative stability at elevated temperatures is a requirement for industrial use.

In personal care, it acts as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent in creams, serums, and color cosmetics, providing a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel for high-end consumer products.

At flavor-grade purity, it contributes fruity and fatty notes to food and beverage formulations. Dimethyl sebacate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Standard grades include technical and high-purity options, with food- and flavor-grade material available for regulated applications. Specifications are typically aligned with FCC purity benchmarks.

Depending on the intended end use, our material meets rigorous quality controls. This ensures consistent performance across automotive, cosmetic, and food manufacturing supply chains globally.

name: Epichlorohydrin
description:
Epichlorohydrin (CAS 106-89-8 ), commonly abbreviated as ECH, is a reactive chlorinated epoxide monomer that serves as a foundational building block in polymer synthesis.

Its bifunctional reactivity, combining an epoxide ring with a reactive chlorine, makes it indispensable for producing a broad range of crosslinked resins and specialty polymers.

ECH is the primary raw material in epoxy resin manufacturing, where it reacts with bisphenol A to produce the base resins used in coatings, adhesives, and structural composites.

In the textile and paper industries, ECH-derived polyamide-epichlorohydrin resins are applied as wet-strength agents, improving paper durability under moisture and fixing dyes to fiber substrates.

Flame retardant formulations incorporate ECH as a reactive intermediate to introduce chlorine into polymer backbones, providing durable fire resistance in plastics and coatings.

It also functions as a crosslinking agent in the production of glycerol, synthetic glycerin, and water treatment resins used for ion exchange applications.

Epichlorohydrin is supplied as a colorless liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank containers, drums, and intermediate bulk containers for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 99% or above. Procurement volumes range from drum quantities to full bulk shipments.

name: Glycidyl methacrylate
description:
Glycidyl methacrylate (GMA, CAS 106-91-2 ), also known as 2,3-Epoxypropyl methacrylate, is a bifunctional reactive monomer combining an epoxide group with a methacrylate group in a single molecule.

This dual reactivity allows it to participate in both free-radical polymerization and ring-opening crosslinking reactions, making it a valued building block for specialty polymer systems.

GMA is primarily used in the production of functional acrylic copolymers for powder coatings, where its epoxide groups react with carboxylic acid curatives to deliver durable, high-gloss finishes.

In adhesives and reactive hot melts, it introduces crosslinkable sites that improve bond strength and chemical resistance in the cured film. Formulators use it as a compatibilizer and reactive coupling agent.

When blending immiscible polymers such as polyesters and polyolefins, it acts as a bridge. It also serves as a surface-functionalizing monomer in specialty coatings and grafting processes for textiles.

This monomer is essential for packaging films where controlled surface chemistry is required. Glycidyl methacrylate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering, with purity levels commonly at 97% or higher. Bulk liquid and drum packaging are the typical supply formats for industrial buyers.

name: Allyl glycidyl ether
description:
Allyl glycidyl ether ( CAS 106-92-3 ), commonly abbreviated as AGE, is a bifunctional reactive monomer carrying both an epoxide and an allyl group. This dual reactivity allows it to bridge different polymerization chemistries.

It is a valued building block in specialty polymer synthesis and surface modification applications. AGE is used as a reactive diluent and crosslinker in epoxy resin formulations, where it reduces viscosity.

It remains chemically incorporated into the cured network rather than migrating out over time. In polymer modification, it introduces pendant allyl functionality onto epoxy backbones, enabling subsequent grafting.

This allows for further crosslinking for coatings, adhesives, and sealants. Silicone and rubber compounders use AGE to compatibilize inorganic fillers or couple dissimilar polymer phases during production.

This improves mechanical performance in the final vulcanizate. It also serves as a functional monomer in the production of ion-exchange resins and specialty hydrogels used in separation and filtration media.

Allyl glycidyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger volumes. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification.

Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher for this material. Stabilized grades formulated to inhibit premature polymerization during storage and transport are also available from most producers.

name: 1,2-dibromoethane
description:
1,2-Dibromoethane (CAS 106-93-4 ), also known as EDB and ethylene bromide, is a brominated organic compound used industrially as a chemical intermediate and flame retardant precursor.

Historically significant as a soil and grain fumigant, its agricultural use is now heavily restricted or banned in many jurisdictions, shifting commercial relevance toward polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing.

In plastics and polymer systems, it functions as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of flame retardant additives, contributing bromine content to formulations targeting fire performance standards.

EDB serves as a key alkylating and brominating agent in the production of specialty organic compounds, including pharmaceutical and agrochemical intermediates for various industrial applications.

In leaded fuel systems, it was historically compounded with lead scavengers to prevent engine deposit buildup, though this application is now obsolete in most global markets today.

Residual demand exists in controlled laboratory and industrial synthesis where its reactivity profile supports specific halogenation reactions required for complex chemical manufacturing processes.

1,2-Dibromoethane is supplied as a liquid in drums or IBC containers. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Procurement is subject to regulatory controls in many regions, and buyers should verify import and handling compliance before sourcing this material for their specific industrial needs.

name: 1-bromopropane
description:
1-Bromopropane (CAS 106-94-5 ), commercially known as n-propyl bromide or nPB, is a short-chain alkyl halide used primarily as an industrial solvent and chemical intermediate.

It gained traction as a cleaning and degreasing solvent following restrictions on ozone-depleting alternatives, and serves as a key building block in pharmaceutical and polymer synthesis.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, nPB functions as a reaction solvent and alkylating agent for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty intermediates for various applications.

Precision cleaning applications, including electronics defluxing, metal degreasing, and aerospace component cleaning, rely on its solvency for oils, greases, and flux residues.

In polymer chemistry, it acts as a catalyst precursor and chain-transfer agent in controlled polymerization processes to ensure high quality and consistent chemical performance.

Flame retardant formulations also incorporate 1-bromopropane as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of brominated compounds used across several industrial manufacturing sectors.

name: Allyl bromide
description:
Allyl bromide (CAS 106-95-6 ) is a reactive alkylating agent used primarily as a chemical building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. Known commercially as 3-bromopropene, it introduces the allyl group into target molecules.

This process occurs through nucleophilic substitution reactions, enabling the construction of complex active pharmaceutical ingredients and fine chemicals. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in synthesizing APIs.

This is particularly useful where allylation of nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur nucleophiles is required. Biotechnology and life sciences researchers use it to functionalize biomolecules and synthesize allylated nucleosides or amino acid derivatives.

These materials are often used for research-scale production. The compound also supports the manufacture of agrochemical intermediates and specialty monomers where controlled allyl group incorporation is critical to the target structure.

Quaternary ammonium biocides with allyl functionality are produced using this substance as the alkylating precursor. The product is supplied as a liquid, typically in stabilized form to prevent premature polymerization during storage.

It is available in technical and high-purity grades to meet the requirements of pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis and research applications. This ensures compatibility with various industrial and laboratory protocols.

Standard packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities through to bulk drum supply for industrial-scale production. All batches are tested to ensure they meet rigorous internal quality standards and customer specifications.

name: Butane
description:
Butane (CAS 106-97-8 ), also identified as R-600 and E943a , is a liquefied petroleum gas supplied as a compressed or liquefied gas for use across energy, industrial, and food-grade applications.

It functions primarily as a fuel, propellant, and extraction solvent across multiple sectors. In the food and beverage industry, butane is approved as a propellant and extraction solvent under the E943a designation.

It is used in aerosol food products and edible oil extraction processes. In oil and gas, it serves as a blending component in LPG formulations and as a feedstock for petrochemical synthesis, including production of butylene.

Automotive applications include use as a fuel blend component in LPG vehicle systems, where its vapor pressure characteristics determine seasonal blending ratios. It is also used in synthetic rubber manufacturing.

As a refrigerant designated R-600, it is also used in domestic and light commercial refrigeration systems as a low-GWP alternative. Butane is supplied as a liquefied compressed gas in cylinders and bulk tanks.

ISO containers are also available for transport. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are both commercially available, with food-grade product conforming to FCC requirements for use as a solvent.

It is suitable for direct food contact as a propellant. Purity grades typically range from commercial LPG blends to high-purity instrument and extraction grades to meet specific industrial requirements.

name: 1,3-butadiene
description:
1,3-Butadiene (CAS 106-99-0 ), commonly abbreviated as BD, is a gaseous diene monomer that serves as the primary building block for synthetic rubber and a broad range of polymer systems.

Divinyl is an older recognized synonym occasionally encountered in legacy technical literature. Its commercial significance lies almost entirely in large-scale polymerization processes.

It forms the backbone of elastomers and copolymer resins consumed across multiple industries. BD is the principal monomer in the production of polybutadiene rubber (PBR) and styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR).

Both of these materials are processed into automotive tires, conveyor belts, and mechanical seals. In plastics, it is copolymerized with acrylonitrile and styrene to produce ABS resin.

This structural material is used in automotive components, electronics housings, and consumer goods. Nitrile rubber (NBR) is a critical material for fuel-resistant hoses, gaskets, and industrial gloves.

Styrene-butadiene latex derived from BD is also used as a binder in paper coatings and carpet backing adhesives. 1,3-Butadiene is supplied as a liquefied gas under pressure.

It is typically delivered in cylinders or bulk pressurized tankers for industrial-volume buyers. It is available in polymerization-grade and technical-grade specifications for various uses.

Polymerization grade commands strict purity thresholds to prevent inhibitor interference in downstream processes. This ensures high performance in the manufacturing of advanced synthetic materials.

name: Ammonium acrylate
description:
Ammonium acrylate (CAS 10604-69-0 ) is the ammonium salt of acrylic acid, used primarily as a reactive monomer and polymerization building block in industrial polymer synthesis. It enables the production of water-soluble and hydrophilic polymers suited to performance-driven formulations.

These polymers are utilized across water treatment, agriculture, and plastics manufacturing. In water treatment, the chemical is polymerized into flocculants and scale inhibitors used in municipal and industrial effluent processing.

Polymer manufacturers incorporate it into superabsorbent polymer (SAP) chains and hydrogel networks for controlled-release agricultural applications. This includes slow-release fertilizer coatings and soil conditioning products.

It also functions as a co-monomer in acrylic dispersions and latex systems where water solubility and charge density must be precisely controlled. In pH-sensitive polymer systems, its buffering capacity helps stabilize reaction conditions.

This stabilization improves batch consistency during the polymerization process. The material is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration ranges varying by grade and the intended industrial polymerization process.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to monomer purity requirements. Packaging is commonly available in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for various scales.

These options support both laboratory-scale evaluation and full production volumes. The chemical remains a critical component for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in specialized acrylic and hydrogel applications.

name: Ascorbyl stearate
description:
Ascorbyl stearate (CAS 10605-09-1 ), also designated E304ii , is a fat-soluble ester of vitamin C used as an antioxidant in oil-based systems where water-soluble ascorbic acid cannot function effectively.

It protects lipid-containing formulations from oxidative degradation, extending shelf life across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical products. In food manufacturing, it is incorporated into fats and oils.

It is used in fat-rich products such as margarine and baked goods to prevent rancidity and color deterioration. Cosmetic formulators use it in emollients, creams, and serums where it stabilizes the oil phase.

The compound contributes antioxidant activity to the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers apply it to lipid-based drug delivery systems and soft gel capsules to protect active ingredients sensitive to oxidation.

It also functions as a co-antioxidant alongside tocopherols in nutraceutical oil blends, improving overall oxidative stability. Ascorbyl stearate is supplied as a white to off-white powder for industrial use.

It is available in food-grade quality meeting E304ii specifications under EU food additive regulations, as well as in pharmaceutical-grade quality conforming to USP or Ph. Eur. standards.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in fiber drums or multi-layer bags suited for temperature-controlled storage. This ensures the material remains stable and effective for various manufacturing applications.

name: Carbendazim
description:
Carbendazim (CAS 10605-21-7 ), also known as MBC and marketed under the trade name Mecarzole, is a systemic benzimidazole fungicide used across agricultural and industrial sectors.

It controls a broad spectrum of fungal pathogens by inhibiting fungal cell division, making it a go-to active ingredient for crop protection and material preservation programs.

In agriculture, it is formulated into wettable powders, suspension concentrates, and seed treatment products targeting diseases such as powdery mildew, Botrytis, and Fusarium in cereals and fruits.

Industrial preservation represents a significant non-agricultural market. It is incorporated into paints, coatings, and adhesives to prevent fungal degradation during storage and on applied surfaces.

Textile and leather processors use carbendazim-based formulations to protect finished goods and raw materials from mold and mildew during transit and warehousing operations.

In personal care manufacturing, it functions as a preservative booster in certain rinse-off and leave-on formulations where fungal contamination control is required for product stability.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder, with technical grade being the standard form for formulation manufacturers. It meets high industrial and agricultural quality standards.

Suspension concentrate and wettable powder pre-formulations are also commercially available. Buyers should confirm regulatory status in their target market, as approvals vary significantly by region.

name: Chlorinated paraffin
description:
Chlorinated paraffin (CAS 106232-86-4 ), also marketed as CPW and classified under Alkanes, C22-40, chloro, is a high-carbon-chain chlorinated wax used across industrial manufacturing.

It serves as a plasticizer, flame retardant, and lubricant additive. Its long-chain structure positions it specifically in applications demanding thermal stability and low volatility for various processes.

In PVC compounding, it functions as a secondary plasticizer and flame retardant, reducing formulation cost while meeting fire performance requirements in cables, flooring, and wall coverings.

Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as an extreme-pressure additive in cutting and forming lubricants, where it improves tool life during heavy-duty machining operations for the user.

Rubber and sealant manufacturers use it to improve flexibility and fire resistance in gaskets, roofing membranes, and construction sealants. It is a versatile component for many industrial needs.

In textile and leather finishing, it is applied as a flame-retardant treatment for industrial fabrics and upholstery materials. This ensures safety standards are met in commercial environments.

Chlorinated paraffin is supplied as a viscous liquid or waxy solid, depending on chlorine content and chain length. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form for most buyers.

Chlorine content is typically specified by buyers as part of product selection. Drum and IBC packaging are the common supply formats for industrial volumes in the global chemical market.

name: Dimethylthiotoluenediamine
description:
Dimethylthiotoluenediamine , commercially known as DMTDA, is an aromatic diamine curative used primarily in polyurethane and polyurea elastomer systems. It functions as a chain extender and crosslinker, controlling the mechanical properties and cure profile of finished elastomeric components.

In cast polyurethane elastomers, DMTDA reacts with isocyanate-terminated prepolymers to produce parts requiring high load-bearing capacity and abrasion resistance. These applications include industrial wheels, rollers, and mining screens.

Polyurea coating systems for automotive underbody protection, pipeline linings, and industrial flooring rely on this chemical to achieve controlled gel times and improved flexibility. It is a critical component for durable surface protection.

In aerospace and defense applications, it is used in structural adhesives and composite matrix systems where precise cure kinetics are critical to part performance. This ensures the integrity of high-stress components.

Lubricant additive formulations also incorporate CAS 106264-79-3 as an antioxidant and metal deactivator component in gear oils and hydraulic fluids. This versatility makes it valuable across multiple industrial sectors.

DMTDA is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature, with a characteristic amber to brown color. Standard commercial grades meet technical and industrial specifications, with purity typically reported at 95% or higher.

The product is available in drums and IBC totes, with bulk quantities accessible through established chemical distributors. Proper handling and storage are required to maintain the chemical stability and performance of the material.

name: Aspartame acesulfame salt
description:
Aspartame acesulfame salt ( CAS 106372-55-8 ), also known commercially as Twinsweet and approved as E962 , is a high-intensity sweetener combining aspartame and acesulfame in a fixed molar ratio.

The combination delivers a synergistic sweetness profile that exceeds the individual potency of either component. This allows formulators to achieve target sweetness at lower total sweetener loading across various applications.

In carbonated soft drinks and flavored waters, this salt provides clean, sugar-like sweetness with reduced aftertaste compared to single-sweetener systems. It is highly effective for maintaining flavor integrity in beverages.

Confectionery manufacturers use it in sugar-free chewing gum and hard candies where the blend's stability under processing conditions supports consistent flavor delivery. It remains stable during typical manufacturing heat cycles.

Dairy and dessert applications, including yogurts and ice creams, benefit from its ability to round out sweetness. It eliminates the bitterness sometimes associated with acesulfame K alone in these formulations.

It also appears in tabletop sweetener blends and dietary supplement formats where calorie reduction is a primary formulation target. The ingredient is versatile for both liquid and solid dosage forms.

Aspartame acesulfame salt is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available to food-grade and NF specifications, supporting use across both food manufacturing and nutraceutical applications.

Standard commercial supply is typically offered in bulk bags and smaller packaging to serve both large-scale production and development-scale procurement. This ensures flexibility for diverse industrial requirements.

Pulp and paper operations use it as a defoamer and process aid to control foam buildup during pulping and coating stages. Textile and leather processing rely on it for wetting, scouring, and dispersing agents.

The compound produces gas without leaving residual salts that affect taste. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a pH buffer and excipient in tablet formulations where controlled alkalinity is required during processing.

In agriculture, it functions as a nitrogen source in fertilizer blends and as a feed additive where buffering of digestive pH is targeted. Personal care formulators apply it as a pH regulator in creams and cleansing products.

These applications require mild alkaline adjustment to maintain product stability. Ammonium bicarbonate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade material.

name: Dibutyltin diacetate
description:
Dibutyltin diacetate (CAS 1067-33-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DBTDA, is an organotin compound used as a catalyst for curing and cross-linking reactions across polymer and sealant manufacturing.

It accelerates condensation and addition reactions that would otherwise require elevated temperatures or extended processing times. In silicone sealant and elastomer production, DBTDA catalyzes room-temperature vulcanization.

This enables one- and two-component systems used in construction, automotive, and electronics assembly. Polyurethane formulators use it to control gel time and cross-link density in coatings and adhesives.

Precise cure profiles are critical to end-product performance in these sectors. It also functions as a stabilizer catalyst in PVC compounding, where it supports thermal stability during processing.

Adhesive manufacturers targeting structural bonding applications select DBTDA when consistent pot life and cure speed are required across varying ambient conditions.

Dibutyltin diacetate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical grade, which is the standard specification for industrial catalyst applications in coatings and sealants.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) to suit both laboratory-scale evaluation and full production volumes for polymer processing.

name: Vinyltris(2-methoxyethoxy)silane
description:
Vinyltris(2-methoxyethoxy)silane , also known by CAS 1067-53-4 , is an organosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic fillers and organic polymer matrices. It bonds mineral surfaces to resin systems, improving adhesion and mechanical strength.

This chemical improves moisture resistance in composite materials and is commercially known as Silane A-172. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it treats silica and glass fiber reinforcements to improve filler-matrix adhesion.

This treatment directly impacts compound durability and tensile performance in industrial applications. Plastics compounders use it to surface-treat mineral fillers such as talc, kaolin, and wollastonite before incorporation.

These fillers are typically integrated into polyolefin or thermoplastic systems for enhanced stability. Automotive sealants and adhesives rely on it as a crosslinking agent to achieve durable bonds to glass and metal.

These bonds remain stable even under humid conditions, ensuring long-term structural integrity. In printing and packaging, it functions as an adhesion promoter in UV-curable coatings and inks applied to glass.

It is also effective on mineral-filled substrates where high-performance adhesion is required. The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 97% or higher purity for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with packaging ranging from drums to IBC containers. This variety of packaging options is designed to suit bulk compounding operations and logistics.

Some suppliers offer pre-hydrolyzed or diluted formulations for direct surface treatment applications. These specialized versions allow for easier integration into specific manufacturing workflows and coating processes.

name: Neodymium neodecanoate
description:
Neodymium neodecanoate (CAS 106726-11-8 ) is an organoneodymium carboxylate salt used as a catalyst component and polymerization initiator in industrial chemical processes. It delivers controlled rare-earth metal activity in a soluble, hydrocarbon-compatible form.

This chemical suits both polymer synthesis and specialty lubricant applications. Its primary commercial use is as a precursor in Ziegler-Natta and rare-earth catalyst systems for the production of high-cis polybutadiene.

These stereoregular elastomers are essential in tire manufacturing and rubber compounding. In coordination polymerization, it enables precise control over polymer microstructure, which directly affects mechanical performance.

Lubricant additive formulators incorporate it into metal-working fluids and specialty grease formulations. Organometallic neodymium compounds contribute to extreme-pressure and friction-modifying performance in these settings.

It also serves as a catalyst precursor in the synthesis of other neodymium-based organometallic complexes. These are used for research-scale and specialty chemical production across various industrial sectors.

Neodymium neodecanoate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid solution in hydrocarbon solvents. The neodymium content is specified by weight percentage to ensure accurate dosing in industrial reactions.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with concentration and purity confirmed by ICP metal analysis. Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities to bulk drums depending on the application volume.

name: Allyl chloride
description:
Allyl chloride (CAS 107-05-1 ), also known as 3-Chloropropene, is a reactive organochlorine compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of allyl-based derivatives.

It serves as a foundational building block in the production of agrochemicals, flame retardants, and specialty polymers. In agriculture, it is a precursor in the manufacture of allyl-based pesticides.

These soil fumigants are used to control nematodes and soil-borne pathogens in commercial crop production. Polymer manufacturers use it to produce epichlorohydrin, a key intermediate for epoxy resins.

It is also essential for glycerol synthesis. In flame retardant formulations, derived compounds are incorporated into plastics and textiles to meet fire resistance standards for industrial applications.

Water treatment chemical producers also utilize it as a building block for quaternary ammonium biocides. These target microbial control in industrial water systems and large-scale cooling towers.

The product is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, typically in drums or ISO tank containers suited for large-volume industrial procurement. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Purity levels are commonly at 99% or higher. Buyers should confirm stabilizer content and packaging compatibility given the compound's reactivity during storage and transport to ensure safety.

name: Propylamine
description:
Propylamine (CAS 107-10-8 ) is a primary aliphatic amine used as a reactive intermediate and pH modifier across pharmaceutical, polymer, and flavor chemistry. With FEMA 4237 status, it is also recognized in flavor applications under regulated conditions.

Its reactivity toward carbonyl compounds, acids, and isocyanates makes it a building block for a broad range of synthesized end products. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients.

It is particularly useful for antihistamines and cardiovascular compounds. Polymer producers use it as a curing agent and cross-linker for epoxy systems, where amine reactivity directly influences cure rate and final mechanical properties.

In flavor formulation, it contributes to specific aroma profiles at controlled concentrations under FEMA guidelines. Personal care chemists incorporate it as a pH buffer and neutralizing agent in formulations requiring precise alkalinity control.

Propylamine is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity grades suited to pharmaceutical and industrial synthesis. Technical grade is standard for polymer and chemical manufacturing applications across various industries.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available where API synthesis or regulated flavor use requires tighter specification and documentation. This ensures compliance with rigorous safety and quality standards for sensitive chemical processes.

name: Allylamine
description:
Allylamine (CAS 107-11-9 ), also referred to as 3-aminopropene, is a reactive primary amine and vinyl monomer used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical production, and polymer manufacturing.

Its bifunctional structure, combining an amine group with a terminal double bond, makes it a sought-after building block for multi-step synthesis and polymerization processes.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, allylamine serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of antifungal active ingredients, including terbinafine and naftifine for various medical applications.

Agrochemical producers use it as a precursor in the preparation of herbicides and fungicides where controlled amine reactivity is required for effective crop protection and management.

In polymer chemistry, it undergoes free-radical polymerization to produce polyallylamine, a cationic polymer used in water treatment, paper manufacturing, and surface coating formulations.

It also functions as a pH buffer and chain-initiating component in specialty resin and hydrogel systems, providing essential structural properties for advanced material science applications.

Allylamine is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in technical grade for industrial and polymer applications, as well as high-purity grades for specific needs.

Our material meets pharmaceutical intermediate specifications. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers, with bulk quantities available for commercial-scale procurement.

name: Acrylonitrile
description:
Acrylonitrile (CAS 107-13-1 ), also known as vinyl cyanide or by the trade names Ventox and Fumigrain, is a reactive monomer used as a foundational building block in large-scale polymer manufacturing.

As AN, it is a primary feedstock for producing acrylic fibers, ABS resins, and nitrile rubber across multiple industrial sectors. In textile manufacturing, AN is polymerized to produce acrylic fibers used in apparel and carpeting.

These fibers are also utilized in industrial fabrics. The rubber and tire industry relies on it as a co-monomer in nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR), which is compounded into fuel-resistant hoses, seals, and gaskets.

In plastics, it is a key co-monomer in ABS and SAN resins, supplying rigidity and chemical resistance to molded components and packaging. Historically, Ventox and Fumigrain formulations have also been applied as fumigants.

These were used as grain and commodity fumigants for pest control in stored agricultural products. Acrylonitrile is supplied as a stabilized liquid, typically inhibited with monomethyl ether of hydroquinone (MEHQ).

This inhibitor prevents premature polymerization during storage and transport. It is available in technical and polymerization grades, with purity specifications commonly at 99% or higher to meet industrial needs.

Bulk quantities are supplied in ISO tank containers or rail tankers, with drum packaging available for smaller-volume procurement. This ensures flexible logistics for various manufacturing scales and requirements.

name: Ethylenediamine
description:
Ethylenediamine (CAS 107-15-3 ), also known as EDA, is a primary diamine used as a reactive building block and chelating agent across chemical manufacturing. It functions as a curing agent and complexing ligand.

It is a vital intermediate in the synthesis of agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and specialty polymers. In agriculture, EDA is a key intermediate in the production of herbicides, fungicides, and chelated micronutrient fertilizers.

It binds metal ions to improve plant-available nutrient delivery. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to synthesize active ingredients including antihistamines and bronchodilators, as well as to form stable drug salts.

These salts improve solubility for various medical applications. Epoxy resin formulators apply EDA as a curing and cross-linking agent, controlling hardness and chemical resistance in coatings and adhesives.

It is also used in composite materials and water treatment operations to produce chelating agents such as EDTA. These sequester hardness ions and prevent scale formation in industrial systems.

The product is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid, typically in concentrations of 99% and above. It is available in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities to support large-volume manufacturing.

Technical and synthesis grades are the most common commercial specifications. Purity documentation is available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements and various industrial quality standards.

name: Allyl alcohol
description:
Allyl alcohol (CAS 107-18-6 ), also known as vinyl carbinol, is a reactive aliphatic alcohol used as a chemical intermediate and monomer building block across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and polymer manufacturing.

Its unsaturated structure makes it a direct precursor in multi-step synthesis routes where controlled reactivity is a sourcing priority for industrial chemical processors and laboratory researchers alike.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients and fine chemicals requiring an allylic hydroxyl group for specific molecular configurations.

Agrochemical producers use it as a building block in herbicide and pesticide synthesis, particularly where allylation reactions are part of the process chain to ensure effective product performance.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a reactive monomer and crosslinking agent in the production of allyl resins, specialty coatings, and modified polyols for high-performance industrial applications.

It also acts as a carrier solvent in select formulations where its reactivity can be incorporated into the final product rather than removed, providing efficiency in complex manufacturing cycles.

Allyl alcohol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger industrial volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP standards is available for regulated synthesis applications. We ensure consistent quality and reliable logistics for all global supply requirements.

name: Propargyl alcohol
description:
Propargyl alcohol (CAS 107-19-7 ), also known as acetylene carbinol, is a reactive acetylenic alcohol used as a corrosion inhibitor and chemical intermediate across industrial sectors.

Its terminal alkyne group makes it a practical building block for synthesizing specialty polymers, surfactants, and pharmaceutical precursors for various high-performance applications.

In oil and gas production, it is formulated into acidizing fluids used during well stimulation, where it inhibits corrosion of steel tubulars and downhole equipment exposed to hydrochloric acid.

Metalworking and electroplating operations use it as a corrosion inhibitor additive in pickling baths and acid cleaning solutions to protect metal surfaces during intensive processing.

As a monomer and building block, it serves in the synthesis of propargylic esters, ethers, and specialty acrylates used in UV-curable coatings and modern polymer systems.

In agrochemical and pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key intermediate in the production of active ingredients and complex fine chemical synthesis chains.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 99% purity for industrial and synthesis-grade applications, ensuring consistent performance in sensitive chemical reactions.

name: Ethylene glycol
description:
Ethylene glycol (CAS 107-21-1 ), commonly traded as MEG or monoethylene glycol, is a dihydric alcohol used across industrial manufacturing as an antifreeze agent, solvent, and polymer building block.

Its low freezing point depression and high boiling point make it a primary functional ingredient in heat transfer and coolant systems. Demand is driven largely by polyester fiber and PET resin production.

In the automotive and HVAC sectors, MEG is the base component in engine coolants and antifreeze formulations, protecting systems across wide temperature ranges. It acts as a core monomer in these processes.

Polyester manufacturers consume it at scale as a co-monomer in PET bottle-grade resin, packaging film, and textile fiber production. In personal care, it functions as a humectant and solvent in lotions.

It is also used in creams and hair care formulations where moisture retention and ingredient solubility are required. Paper and leather processing operations use it as a conditioning and softening agent.

These applications improve the flexibility and workability of finished materials. Ethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk tankers, IBC containers, and drums for global distribution.

Standard commercial grades include technical-grade for industrial and polymer applications, and fiber-grade MEG meeting purity specifications required by polyester producers for high-quality manufacturing.

Antifreeze-grade and inhibited formulations are also available for direct use in coolant applications. Our supply chain ensures consistent availability and adherence to rigorous industrial safety protocols.

name: Glyoxal
description:
Glyoxal (CAS 107-22-2 ), also known as oxal, is a dialdehyde compound used industrially as a crosslinking agent, biocide, and chemical intermediate across a broad range of manufacturing sectors.

Its reactivity with hydroxyl, amine, and amide groups makes it a practical choice for insolubilizing and stabilizing substrates in both wet and dry processing environments.

In textile and paper manufacturing, this compound crosslinks cellulose fibers to impart wrinkle resistance and wet strength to finished goods. Leather processors use it as a tanning auxiliary and fixative.

These applications improve fiber structure and dimensional stability in hides. Water treatment formulators incorporate it as a biocide active for controlling microbial growth in industrial cooling systems.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a binder crosslinker in coating formulations, improving water resistance and ink adhesion on coated paper and board substrates.

The product is commercially supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 40% concentration, though 30% grades are also available for specific industrial applications.

Technical grade is the standard for industrial use in textiles, paper, and water treatment. Pharmaceutical and specialty grades with tighter purity specifications are available for regulated applications.

name: Methyl formate
description:
Methyl formate (CAS 107-31-3 ), also known as R-611, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, fumigation, and flavoring applications. Its high solvency power and reactivity as a formylating agent make it a practical choice for both process chemistry and specialty formulations.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, methyl formate functions as a reaction solvent and intermediate in the synthesis of formic acid, formamide derivatives, and active pharmaceutical ingredients. As a fumigant and grain preservative, it offers broad-spectrum biocidal activity.

It is effective against insects and molds in stored commodities, with a low residue profile that supports food safety compliance. Flavor chemists use it as a fruity top-note ingredient in food and beverage formulations, where its low use levels deliver high olfactory impact.

In industrial foam production, it serves as a blowing agent alternative under the R-611 designation, replacing more regulated halocarbons in polyurethane systems. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing and agricultural preservation.

Methyl formate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard for industrial and fumigation use, while higher-purity grades are available to meet pharmaceutical and food-grade processing requirements.

These high-purity options often align with international quality standards such as FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , or ACS depending on the specific application. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and packaging options directly with suppliers.

Grade designations vary by regional market, so technical data sheets should be reviewed for compliance. Proper handling and storage are essential due to the high volatility and flammability of this ester solvent in industrial environments.

name: Taurine
description:
Taurine (CAS 107-35-7 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3813 designation, is a naturally occurring sulfonic amino acid sourced through both synthetic production and fermentation.

It functions as a buffering agent, osmoregulator, and bioactive ingredient across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In energy drinks, it is dosed to support electrolyte balance.

It is a standard label claim ingredient that drives consumer purchasing. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active excipient in ophthalmic solutions and bile acid conjugation therapies.

It is also utilized in parenteral nutrition formulations. In pet food production, it is a mandatory additive for feline diets, where deficiency causes documented cardiac conditions.

This makes it a specification-critical ingredient for compliant formulas. Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair care and skin conditioning products for moisture-retention.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in packaging ranging from kilogram quantities to multi-tonne bulk. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and USP .

Pharmaceutical-grade ( BP / Ph. Eur. ) is also available, with purity typically at 98.5% or higher. Feed-grade material is available for animal nutrition applications.

These materials are subject to separate regulatory specifications. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for all industrial and laboratory requirements.

name: Isethionic acid
description:

Its sodium and potassium salts, sodium isethionate and potassium isethionate, are independently traded and specified in formulation work, making them distinct procurement targets for global manufacturers.

In personal care manufacturing, these compounds serve as key intermediates in synthesizing acyl isethionate surfactants, the basis of mild, skin-compatible cleansing bars and liquid wash systems.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent and solvent carrier in drug salt formation, particularly where improved solubility or controlled pH is required for stability.

Textile and leather processors apply it in dyeing and finishing baths, where its buffering capacity helps maintain consistent process pH and improves dye uptake uniformity across materials.

Paper treatment operations use isethionate salts as dispersing agents to improve fiber compatibility and surface chemistry. Isethionic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically around 70% concentration.

Sodium isethionate is available as a white powder or granules, commonly offered in technical and cosmetic-grade specifications. Potassium isethionate is available from specialty suppliers in technical-grade form.

name: Hexylene glycol

Hexylene glycol (CAS 107-41-5 ), also marketed as MPD, is a multifunctional diol solvent used across coatings, personal care, and polymer manufacturing. It functions as a solvent, humectant, and coupling agent.

The product improves film formation and leveling in waterborne systems, ensuring a high-quality finish. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skin creams, lotions, and toners as a humectant and preservation booster.

It enhances the efficacy of antimicrobial systems at low use levels, providing value in cosmetic formulations. In adhesives and sealants, it functions as a reactive diluent and stabilizer for better performance.

The solvent extends open time and improves substrate wetting during application. Polymer processors also use it as a plasticizer intermediate and chain extender in polyurethane and polyester resin production.

The material is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk quantities including IBC totes and tanker loads. Drum packaging is also available for smaller volumes to meet diverse logistical needs.

name: Betaine
description:
Betaine (CAS 107-43-7 ), also known as glycine betaine and TMG (trimethylglycine), is a naturally derived amino acid derivative sourced primarily from sugar beet molasses. It functions as a humectant and osmoprotectant across personal care, food, pharmaceutical, and animal feed applications.

In cosmetic formulations, betaine improves moisture retention in skin and hair care products while reducing the irritation potential of surfactant-based systems. This makes it a key consideration for sensitive-skin product lines and high-end personal care formulations.

Food and nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it as a methyl donor in dietary supplements targeting homocysteine metabolism and athletic performance. It is highly valued for its stability and ease of integration into various dry and liquid supplement formats.

In animal feed, it acts as a methyl group source and osmolyte that supports gut health and lean muscle deposition in poultry and swine production. This application helps producers maintain animal health and optimize growth rates in commercial farming environments.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an excipient and active ingredient in products addressing liver function and metabolic support. Its role as a metabolic regulator makes it a versatile component in specialized medical and therapeutic applications.

Betaine is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in anhydrous or monohydrate forms, with the anhydrous grade being the more common commercial specification. This ensures high purity and consistent performance across different manufacturing processes.

Food-grade and feed-grade certifications are standard, with USP and Ph.Eur. grades available for pharmaceutical procurement. These standards ensure the material meets rigorous safety and quality requirements for global distribution.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags, with container-load volumes available for industrial buyers. Our logistics network ensures reliable supply chains for large-scale production needs across the chemical and food industries.

name: Hexamethyldisiloxane
description:
Hexamethyldisiloxane (CAS 107-46-0 ), commonly referenced as HMDSO, is a low-viscosity silicone fluid used as a solvent, carrier, and surface-modifying agent across specialty chemical manufacturing.

It conditions surfaces, aids dispersion of silicone-based materials, and supports film formation in coating and personal care applications. In silicone coatings and release liners, it acts as a reactive diluent.

The material functions as a processing solvent, improving flow and substrate wetting during application. Personal care formulators use it as a lightweight carrier fluid in skin-feel emollients and dry-touch formulations.

It is ideal for hair conditioning products where fast evaporation and a non-greasy finish are required. In adhesives and sealants manufacturing, it functions as a solvent for silicone polymers and as a surface primer.

The chemical promotes adhesion on low-energy substrates. Plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition processes use HMDSO as a precursor to deposit hydrophobic or barrier silica coatings on plastics and films.

Hexamethyldisiloxane is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical and high-purity grades are available, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+.

Tetradecamethylcycloheptasiloxane (CAS 107-50-6 ), commercially known as Cyclomethicone 7, is a cyclic siloxane used across personal care, industrial coatings, and automotive applications. It functions as a lubricant, foam suppressant, and surface modifier.

Automotive and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it to reduce friction and improve surface release in precision components and mold-release systems. It is highly valued for its ability to provide a non-greasy application.

In coatings and sealant systems, it contributes to substrate wetting and surface leveling, improving adhesion and film uniformity. This ensures a high-quality finish across various industrial and commercial surface applications.

Foam control applications in industrial processing benefit from its ability to destabilize surface foam without contaminating the bulk phase. This makes it an efficient additive for maintaining process stability in chemical manufacturing.

name: Octamethyltrisiloxane

Textile and leather finishing operations use it to impart softness, water repellency, and surface slip to treated substrates. It provides a smooth finish while maintaining the integrity of the underlying material.

In metalworking and automotive lubricant formulations, it serves as a base fluid or co-solvent. It is valued where thermal stability and low surface tension are required for consistent film formation on metal parts.

These polymers enhance flocculant performance and sludge dewatering efficiency in industrial effluent systems. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers incorporate TBA to enhance water resistance and substrate adhesion.

name: Distearyldimethylammonium chloride
description:
Distearyldimethylammonium chloride (CAS 107-64-2 ), also known as DSDMAC or Varisoft 100, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a cationic surfactant across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning applications.

Its strong affinity for negatively charged surfaces drives its use as a conditioning agent, softener, and antistatic treatment. In fabric softeners and rinse conditioners, DSDMAC deposits onto fiber surfaces to reduce static charge.

This action improves tactile softness, making it a primary active in both consumer and institutional laundry formulations. Hair conditioners and detangling treatments rely on it to coat damaged, negatively charged hair strands.

This process improves combability and reduces flyaway. Textile and leather processors use it as a fiber lubricant and softening agent during finishing operations, where uniform surface deposition is critical to end-product quality.

In paper manufacturing, it functions as a surface modifier to improve softness and reduce interfiber friction in tissue and specialty paper grades. The compound is supplied as a paste, flake, or aqueous dispersion.

Active content typically ranges from 50% to 90% depending on grade. Both technical and cosmetic grades are available, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care formulations.

Buyers should confirm active content, solvent carrier, and viscosity profile when sourcing for specific process or formulation requirements. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance standards for the application.

name: tert-butyl peroxyacetate
description:
Tert-butyl peroxyacetate (CAS 107-71-1 ), also known as tert-butyl peracetate and sold under the trade name Lupersol 70, is an organic peroxide used as a free-radical source in polymer manufacturing.

It delivers controlled radical generation across a defined temperature range, supporting both polymerization initiation and cross-linking processes for various industrial applications.

In plastics and polymer production, it initiates free-radical polymerization of vinyl monomers including styrene, acrylates, and vinyl acetate, enabling consistent molecular weight control.

Rubber and tire manufacturers use it as a cross-linking agent to cure elastomers, improving mechanical strength and heat resistance in finished compounds and specialty materials.

It also functions as a co-initiator in high-temperature polymerization systems where precise radical flux is required to meet specific product performance requirements and specifications.

Formulators working with polyethylene and specialty resins select it for grafting reactions where other peroxides would decompose too rapidly for the intended chemical process.

Tert-butyl peroxyacetate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at 75% active concentration in a diluent to reduce handling hazards associated with the pure form.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with supply governed by peroxide-specific transport and storage regulations. Packaging ranges from small drums to IBC containers.

name: Hydroxycitronellol
description:
Hydroxycitronellol ( CAS 107-74-4 ), also known by FEMA 2586 , is a fragrance alcohol used across personal care, flavor, and pharmaceutical applications. It delivers a soft, clean floral character that makes it a recognized building block in perfumery and flavor compounding.

In fine fragrance and personal care formulations, it contributes a delicate lily-of-the-valley note to perfumes, lotions, and skin care products. Flavor manufacturers use it as an approved FEMA ingredient in food and beverage applications.

This versatile chemical is ideal for scenarios where a light floral-green character is required. Its solvent and carrier properties support active ingredient delivery in topical pharmaceutical preparations and cosmetic bases.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a solvent component in ink and coating formulations. This is particularly useful where low odor profile and compatibility with resins are priorities for the manufacturer.

Hydroxycitronellol is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Fragrance-grade and flavor-grade specifications are the standard commercial forms available from fragrance ingredient suppliers for various industries.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial solvent applications in printing and coatings. This ensures that the product meets the specific needs of heavy industrial and chemical processing sectors.

name: Hydroxycitronellal
description:
Hydroxycitronellal (CAS 107-75-5 ), also known as Citronellal hydrate, is a synthetic fragrance aldehyde used extensively in perfumery and flavor compounding. With a soft, sweet, lily-of-the-valley floral character, it functions as a key odorant and fixative.

In fine fragrance and functional perfumery, it forms the floral heart of lily, muguet, and sweet floral accords across eau de parfum, cologne, and body care formats. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, lotions, and soaps.

This versatile ingredient is essential where a clean, long-lasting floral note is required. As a FEMA 2583 -listed flavoring agent, it is used at controlled levels in food and beverage applications to impart delicate floral-sweet nuances.

Printing and packaging fragrance systems also utilize it in scented inks and coatings where stable, diffusible floral character is needed. Its chemical stability makes it a reliable choice for diverse industrial applications.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in fragrance-grade and food-grade specifications to meet the sourcing requirements of both flavor houses and cosmetic manufacturers.

Standard packaging ranges from drums to IBCs for bulk procurement. Our material meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency in every batch, supporting large-scale manufacturing needs across the globe.

name: 1,3-Butanediol
description:
1,3-Butanediol (CAS 107-88-0 ), also known as 1,3-Butylene glycol, is a short-chain diol used across personal care, polymer, and coatings industries. It functions primarily as a humectant, plasticizer, and reactive intermediate.

In personal care, it conditions and retains moisture in skin creams, serums, and hair products. It is often preferred over propylene glycol for its lighter skin feel and excellent safety profile in topical applications.

Polymer manufacturers use it as a chain extender and cross-linking agent in polyurethane synthesis. This directly influences the hardness and flexibility of the final elastomer produced for industrial use.

Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it to improve film flexibility and substrate adhesion. It is effective in both solvent-borne and waterborne systems for various commercial coating projects.

It also functions as a plasticizer in specialty sealants and elastomers where controlled softness and elongation are required. This versatility makes it a staple component in modern chemical manufacturing.

1,3-Butanediol is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Bulk tanker options are also available for high-volume buyers requiring consistent large-scale deliveries.

Cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly traded. Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements suitable for leave-on and rinse-off personal care formulations.

Technical-grade supply serves polymer and industrial coating applications where cosmetic-grade purity is not required. This ensures cost-effective sourcing for heavy industrial and manufacturing sectors.

name: Butyric acid
description:
Butyric acid (CAS 107-92-6 ), also known by its FEMA 2221 designation in flavor applications, is a short-chain fatty acid produced commercially for use across food, feed, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a flavoring agent, pH regulator, and precursor for ester synthesis across multiple industrial sectors. In food and beverage production, it delivers characteristic dairy, rancid, and fermented flavor notes.

These notes are used in cheese flavors, butter emulations, and savory seasonings. The pharmaceutical and nutraceutical sectors use the acid and its salts, particularly sodium and calcium butyrate, as gut health actives.

It is also used as enteric coating components in tablet and capsule formulations. In animal nutrition, it is incorporated into feed additives to support intestinal integrity in poultry and swine, acting as an antimicrobial.

It also serves as a growth-performance enhancer in these applications. Fragrance and cosmetic formulators use it as a building block for butyrate esters, which contribute fruity and creamy scent profiles to finished products.

The product is supplied as a liquid in standard commercial and technical grades. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is available for flavor and feed applications to ensure high quality.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply meeting USP or BP standards is also accessible for regulated formulation use. This ensures compliance with international safety and purity requirements for sensitive applications.

name: trans-Crotonic acid
description:
Trans-Crotonic acid (CAS 107-93-7 ), also known by its FEMA 3908 designation, is an unsaturated organic acid used as a flavoring agent and acidulant in food and cosmetic applications.

It functions as a pH regulator, preservative component, and reactive monomer in polymer synthesis for coating and adhesive systems. In food and beverage formulations, it contributes flavor modulation and mild acidulant activity.

The material is recognized under its FEMA code for use in approved flavoring compositions. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into film-forming polymers and fixative resins for hair care products.

In these applications, it provides controlled hold and flexibility. In industrial coating systems, it acts as a copolymerizable monomer to modify resin hardness, adhesion, and film durability for various surfaces.

Its buffering capacity also makes it relevant in preservation systems where pH control supports antimicrobial efficacy. Trans-Crotonic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid for industrial use.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade material meeting FEMA specifications and technical-grade product for polymer applications. Packaging is typically offered in kilogram quantities for specialty use and larger bulk formats.

name: Beta Alanine
description:
Beta Alanine (CAS 107-95-9 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3252 designation in flavoring applications, is a naturally occurring amino acid used as a functional ingredient across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

Unlike most amino acids, it acts on buffering capacity and moisture retention rather than protein synthesis, making it a distinct procurement target for formulators working across multiple categories and industrial sectors.

In sports nutrition and dietary supplement manufacturing, it is the primary precursor to carnosine, driving its inclusion in pre-workout blends and endurance formulations at clinically referenced loading doses for athletes.

Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring agent and acidulant, contributing mild tartness and pH modulation in functional drinks and fortified products. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into buffered preparations.

In these medical applications, amino acid-based pH control is often preferred over inorganic salts. In personal care, its humectant properties support moisture-binding in skin-conditioning products and various topical formulations.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include food-grade and USP -compliant specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material available for highly regulated applications.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags, with documentation packages supporting both food and pharma supply chains. This ensures compliance with global safety and quality standards for industrial procurement.

name: 3-mercaptopropionic acid
description:
3-Mercaptopropionic acid (CAS 107-96-0 ), also known as beta-mercaptopropionic acid and abbreviated as 3-MPA, is a bifunctional thiol acid used across polymer chemistry and pharmaceutical synthesis.

Its dual reactive sites, a thiol group and a carboxylic acid, make it a practical building block and chain transfer agent in industrial processes and food flavoring applications.

In polymer manufacturing, 3-MPA acts as a chain transfer agent during free-radical polymerization, allowing formulators to control molecular weight in acrylic and vinyl-based resins.

The pharmaceutical and biotech sectors use it as a linker or intermediate in peptide conjugation and nanoparticle surface functionalization, particularly in gold nanoparticle synthesis.

Assigned FEMA 4587 , it is approved as a flavoring agent in food applications where sulfur-containing compounds contribute to meat, savory, and roasted flavor profiles.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor and stabilizer in PVC processing, where it supports organotin-based heat stabilizer formulations for industrial manufacturing.

3-Mercaptopropionic acid is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity variants to meet specific synthesis requirements.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available for bioconjugation needs. Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities up to bulk drum supply for large-scale operations.

name: Sarcosine
description:
Sarcosine (CAS 107-97-1 ), also known as N-methylglycine, is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative used across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a buffering agent and chelator.

This versatile compound acts as a mild surfactant intermediate, supporting formulation stability and ingredient performance across multiple product categories. In personal care, it is a key building block for sarcosinates.

These mild, foam-boosting surfactants are used in shampoos, facial cleansers, and toothpaste formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a pH buffering component and as a synthetic intermediate in API production.

In food and nutrition applications, it serves as a source of the N-methyl amino acid backbone in specialty nutritional compounds. Research and nutraceutical producers also source it as a reference standard.

It is frequently used as a functional ingredient in cognitive health and metabolic support product development. Sarcosine is supplied as a white crystalline powder available in technical grade for industrial synthesis.

High-purity grades are available, including USP and Ph. Eur. specifications, for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical use. These standards ensure the material meets rigorous safety and quality requirements.

Food-grade material meeting FCC standards is also commercially available for nutrition and supplement applications. This ensures suitability for human consumption in various dietary and health-focused products.
