name: 1-Methoxy-2-propanol
description:
1-Methoxy-2-propanol (CAS 107-98-2 ), commonly known as PGME or Propylene Glycol Methyl Ether, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and personal care formulations.

Its controlled evaporation rate and broad solvency make it a preferred choice where film formation, flow, and compatibility with diverse resin systems are critical procurement considerations for manufacturers.

In architectural and industrial coatings, PGME improves flow and leveling in waterborne and solvent-based systems, reducing surface defects in the final film. This ensures a high-quality finish for industrial applications.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to dissolve or dilute resin components, ensuring consistent viscosity and open time in formulations. In printing inks, it supports pigment dispersion and controls drying speed.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a solvent and carrier in products such as hair sprays, skin toners, and nail treatments where low odor and skin compatibility are required for consumer safety.

1-Methoxy-2-propanol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial-grade material, with high-purity grades available for cosmetic use.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and isomer content, particularly the ratio relative to 2-methoxy-1-propanol, when sourcing for sensitive formulation work to ensure consistent performance and safety.

name: Mono(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate
description:
Mono(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (CAS 1070-03-7 ), also known as ethylhexyl acid phosphate, is an organophosphate ester used across industrial processing as a chelating agent and corrosion inhibitor.

Its acid phosphate structure enables selective metal ion coordination and surface-active behavior in demanding process environments. It is also widely utilized as a high-performance lubrication additive.

In solvent extraction and hydrometallurgical processing, it functions as a metal extractant for separating and recovering rare earth elements and cobalt from various leach solutions.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as an anti-wear and extreme-pressure additive. It forms protective phosphate films on metal surfaces under high-load conditions.

In textile processing, it acts as a fiber lubricant and antistatic agent, improving yarn runnability during spinning and weaving operations. This enhances overall production efficiency.

Leather and paper manufacturers use it as a processing aid to control metal ion activity. This improves surface treatment compatibility and ensures consistent quality in the final products.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically as a mixture with the diester analog, with mono-ester content specified by grade. Technical-grade material is the standard offering.

Purity and ester ratio are confirmed by acid value and phosphorus content analysis. This ensures the material meets the necessary specifications for industrial and chemical applications.

name: Tetramethylene glycol diacrylate
description:
Tetramethylene glycol diacrylate (CAS 1070-70-8 ), commercially abbreviated as BDDA, is a bifunctional acrylate monomer derived from 1,4-butanediol. It functions as a reactive crosslinker and diluent in UV- and peroxide-curable polymer systems.

This monomer is essential for building network density and improving mechanical performance in cured materials. In UV-curable coatings and printing inks, BDDA controls viscosity while contributing to crosslink density.

These properties directly affect cure speed and film hardness in industrial applications. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to tune flexibility and cohesive strength in radiation-cured systems where elongation is critical.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a crosslinking agent during polymerization to modify gel content. This modification improves the swelling resistance and dimensional stability of the final material produced.

Personal care applications include its use as a crosslinker in gel-forming polymer networks. In these formulations, the network tightness determines the specific texture and product consistency required for the consumer.

BDDA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering for this chemical.

Purity levels are commonly specified at 98% or higher to ensure consistent performance in sensitive reactions. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on the specific order volume and logistics needs.

name: Ammonium butyl phosphorodithioate
description:
Ammonium butyl phosphorodithioate (CAS 1071-18-7 ), also known as O,O-dibutyl phosphorodithioate ammonium salt, is a sulfur- and phosphorus-bearing organosalt used as a functional additive.

It acts as both a corrosion inhibitor and an extreme-pressure lubricant component, protecting metal surfaces under demanding operating conditions in mineral processing and lubrication systems.

In mining and mineral processing, it functions as a flotation collector or depressant aid, improving selective separation of sulfide ores during the extraction process.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it into metalworking fluids and gear oils where its phosphorodithioate chemistry delivers anti-wear and extreme-pressure performance on metal contacts.

It is also used in hydraulic fluid formulations where corrosion protection of metal components is a primary performance requirement for industrial maintenance fluids.

Targeting copper alloy and steel systems, this chemical benefits from its dual corrosion-inhibiting and lubrication functionality across various heavy-duty industrial applications.

Ammonium butyl phosphorodithioate is typically supplied as a liquid or solution, suited for direct blending into oil- or water-based formulations for manufacturing.

It is available in technical grade for industrial applications. Bulk supply in drums or intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) is standard for industrial procurement volumes.

name: Glyphosate
description:
Glyphosate (CAS 1071-83-6 ) is a broad-spectrum, non-selective herbicide used globally to control annual and perennial weeds across agricultural and non-agricultural settings. Sold under trade names such as Glyfos, it is the active ingredient in some of the most widely distributed herbicide formulations in the world.

In row crop agriculture, including corn, soy, and canola, glyphosate is applied pre- and post-emergence to eliminate competing vegetation, particularly in herbicide-tolerant crop systems. Plantation and orchard managers use it for ground cover suppression between tree rows without damaging established crops.

It is also used in non-crop applications such as industrial site maintenance, railway corridors, and utility rights-of-way where total vegetation control is required. Formulators producing herbicide concentrates incorporate glyphosate as the primary active substance for improved solubility and uptake.

Typically, these formulations utilize the isopropylamine or potassium salt versions of the chemical to ensure maximum efficacy. Glyphosate is supplied as a technical-grade acid, as well as in formulated liquid concentrates most commonly as the isopropylamine salt in aqueous solution.

Varying active ingredient concentrations are available to meet specific industrial needs. Dry formulations including soluble granules and soluble powders are also commercially available for diverse application methods. Material is sourced to agricultural technical specifications for global distribution.

Purity levels and impurity profiles are typically aligned with FAO/WHO or equivalent regulatory standards. This ensures that the chemical meets the rigorous safety and performance requirements necessary for large-scale agricultural and industrial deployment across international markets.

name: Adipic dihydrazide
description:
Adipic dihydrazide (CAS 1071-93-8 ), commonly abbreviated as ADH, is a bifunctional hydrazide used as a crosslinker and curing agent across coatings, adhesives, and polymer systems.

It reacts with carbonyl-functional resins at ambient or low temperatures, enabling formulations to cure without elevated heat. In waterborne coatings, ADH crosslinks ketone-functional acrylic dispersions.

This process improves hardness, water resistance, and film durability in architectural and industrial finishes. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to build cohesive strength in emulsion-based systems.

It is particularly effective where thermal curing is impractical. In polymer chemistry, ADH acts as a chain extender and building block for polyurethanes, polyamides, and hydrogel networks.

These applications require controlled crosslink density for optimal performance. Personal care applications include its use as a stabilizer in formulations where carbonyl-reactive chemistry helps protect ingredients.

This specific chemistry helps protect active ingredients from degradation over time. Adipic dihydrazide is supplied as a white crystalline powder available in technical and high-purity grades.

Specifications are typically defined by assay content, moisture levels, and melting point range. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale bags to bulk quantities suitable for industrial procurement.

Contact us for supply of Adipic dihydrazide

name: Lead stearate
description:
Lead stearate (CAS 1072-35-1 ), also sold under the trade name Stabinex NC18, is a lead-based metallic soap used primarily as a heat stabilizer and lubricant in PVC and other polymer processing.

Lead distearate functions by neutralizing degradation byproducts at elevated processing temperatures, extending the service life of finished plastic components during industrial manufacturing.

In PVC compounding, it acts as a primary heat stabilizer, preventing discoloration and degradation during extrusion and calendering of cables, pipes, and profiles for construction use.

Rubber processors use it as an internal lubricant and processing aid, reducing friction between compound and equipment surfaces during mixing and molding operations in the factory.

In the plastics industry, it also functions as a mold release agent, improving surface finish and cycle times in high-volume production environments for various technical applications.

Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it into greases and extreme-pressure formulations where its film-forming characteristics reduce wear under heavy loads.

Lead stearate is supplied as a white powder or fine granules. It is available in technical grade, with product specifications typically defined by lead content, acid value, and melting point.

Packaging is offered in bags or drums suited to bulk industrial procurement. This material ensures consistent performance across a wide range of demanding chemical processing requirements.

name: Potassium phthalimide
description:
Potassium phthalimide (CAS 1074-82-4 ), also known as potassium phthalimidate, is a potassium salt of phthalimide used primarily as a synthetic building block in organic chemistry manufacturing.

It serves as a nucleophilic nitrogen source in the Gabriel synthesis, enabling the production of primary amines and amino acid derivatives at industrial scale for various chemical sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key intermediate for synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients, including amino acids, antifungals, and other nitrogen-containing compounds.

Textile and leather processors use phthalimide-derived compounds to impart flame retardancy and durable finishing properties to treated substrates during the manufacturing and finishing stages.

In polymer and plastics production, it contributes to the synthesis of flame-retardant additives and specialty monomers incorporated into engineering resins for high-performance applications.

Personal care formulators access phthalimide chemistry through downstream derivatives used in preservation and conditioning actives to ensure product stability and efficacy in consumer goods.

Potassium phthalimide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in technical and pharmaceutical-intermediate grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% upward.

Packaging options generally include multi-kilogram bags and drum quantities suited to both laboratory-scale procurement and bulk industrial orders to meet diverse supply chain requirements.

name: TIPA-laureth sulfate
description:
TIPA-laureth sulfate (CAS 107600-36-2 ), also known as Triisopropanolamine Laureth Sulfate, is an anionic surfactant formed from the neutralization of laureth sulfate with triisopropanolamine.

It functions as a primary cleansing, foaming, and emulsifying agent across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid cleansers, it delivers effective soil removal.

The compound provides stable foam while maintaining compatibility with conditioning actives. Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it where mildly alkaline pH and good grease-cutting performance are required.

Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a wetting and dispersing agent during scouring and dyeing stages. Paper manufacturing also draws on its emulsifying properties to support pulp processing.

The chemical is utilized in surface treatment steps and is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous paste. Active matter content commonly ranges around 25–35% depending on the specific formulation requirements.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant personal care industry standards for use in rinse-off and leave-on products. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers.

name: Alpha lipoic acid
description:
Alpha lipoic acid (CAS 1077-28-7 ) is a sulfur-containing antioxidant compound used across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as an antioxidant and cellular cofactor.

The material is used in both finished dosage forms and active ingredient formulations. In nutraceuticals and dietary supplements, it is formulated into capsules, tablets, and functional foods targeting metabolic support.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into anti-aging creams and serums where its antioxidant activity supports oxidative stability. Its skin-conditioning performance makes it a versatile choice for high-end topical applications.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in intravenous and oral preparations. This is common in markets where it holds drug status for specific neuropathic indications and therapeutic uses.

In food-grade applications, it is evaluated as an antioxidant stabilizer in fortified products and functional beverage systems. It helps maintain the integrity of complex formulations during the manufacturing process.

The product is supplied as a fine crystalline yellow powder. Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications for global compliance and safety.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade options are also available for non-pharmaceutical applications. Bulk quantities are provided for industrial-scale formulation to meet the demands of large-scale production facilities.

R-alpha lipoic acid is also available as a distinct enantiomer-specific grade for premium supplement applications. This specialized version offers targeted benefits for manufacturers seeking high-potency ingredients.

name: Dimethylethanolamine
description:
Dimethylethanolamine (CAS 108-01-0 ), also known as DMAE, is a bifunctional amine-alcohol used across industrial and specialty chemical sectors as a pH regulator, catalyst, and corrosion inhibitor.

Its dual amine and hydroxyl functionality makes it a building block and process chemical in coatings, water treatment, and polymer manufacturing. In waterborne coatings and resin systems, it neutralizes acidic binders.

This improves dispersion stability and film formation. Water treatment programs use it to condition boiler and cooling water systems, where it inhibits corrosion by maintaining alkaline pH in steam condensate lines.

As a catalyst in polyurethane foam production, it controls gel and blow reaction timing. This is a critical parameter for foam manufacturers managing cycle times and cell structure during the production process.

In metalworking fluids and lubricant formulations, it buffers pH to extend fluid service life and protect ferrous metal surfaces. This ensures long-term stability and performance in demanding industrial environments.

Dimethylethanolamine is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications including coatings, water treatment, and polymer processing for various sectors.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC totes, with tank truck quantities available for high-volume industrial buyers. We ensure reliable logistics and consistent quality for all our chemical distribution partners.

name: Vinyl acetate
description:
Vinyl acetate (CAS 108-05-4 ), commercially known as VAM or vinyl acetate monomer, is a reactive liquid monomer used as the primary building block for a range of polymer systems.

It undergoes polymerization to produce polyvinyl acetate (PVAc) and serves as a co-monomer in ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) and polyvinyl alcohol (PVOH) production processes.

In adhesives and packaging, VAM polymerizes into PVAc emulsions used in wood glues, paper laminates, and flexible packaging coatings for various industrial applications.

Textile and nonwoven manufacturers use EVA copolymers derived from VAM for binder systems and fabric finishing treatments to enhance material durability and performance.

In the plastics sector, VAM co-polymerizes with ethylene to produce EVA resins used in foam compounds, hot-melt adhesives, and flexible film extrusion for global markets.

At flavor-grade purity, vinyl acetate also functions as a synthetic flavoring intermediate in food and fragrance applications, meeting specific industry requirements for safety.

Vinyl acetate is supplied as a stabilized liquid monomer, typically inhibited with hydroquinone to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport phases.

It is available in technical and monomer grades, with high-purity specifications meeting requirements for polymer-grade and flavor applications in bulk tankers or drums.

Contact us for supply of Vinyl acetate

name: Methyl isobutyl ketone
description:
Methyl isobutyl ketone ( CAS 108-10-1 ), commonly known as MIBK, is a mid-boiling ketone solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and extraction processes. Its slow evaporation rate and strong solvency make it a preferred choice.

Controlled drying and resin compatibility are critical procurement considerations for this versatile chemical. In industrial coatings and lacquers, MIBK dissolves nitrocellulose, epoxy, and vinyl resins to produce high-gloss finishes.

These film-forming finishes exhibit minimal blushing during the application process. Adhesive formulators rely on it as a carrier solvent in contact cements and pressure-sensitive adhesive systems where clean release is required.

In plastics processing, it functions as a cross-linking and curing solvent for polymer systems including rubber and synthetic resins. At food-grade and FEMA 2731 -approved purity, it is also used as a flavoring agent.

In small quantities, it can impart fruity, sweet notes to food and beverage formulations. MIBK is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities for various industrial and commercial needs.

Technical grade is the most common specification for industrial solvent applications. Food-grade material meeting specific requirements is available for flavor use, ensuring compliance with necessary safety and quality protocols.

Purity levels typically range from 99% upward depending on the intended application grade. This high level of purity ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing sectors and specialized chemical processes.

name: 4-Methyl-2-Pentanol
description:
4-Methyl-2-Pentanol (CAS 108-11-2 ), commercially known as MIBC (Methyl Isobutyl Carbinol), is a branched-chain aliphatic alcohol used as a solvent and process chemical across multiple industrial sectors.

Its selective solvency and low water miscibility make it a practical choice for extraction, froth flotation, and formulation work. In mineral processing, MIBC is the dominant frother in froth flotation circuits.

It controls bubble size and stability to improve ore recovery for copper, zinc, and lead concentrates. Polymer and resin manufacturers use it as a process solvent and viscosity modifier during production and coating formulations.

In personal care, it functions as a carrier solvent in fragrance compounds and specialty cosmetic formulations where controlled evaporation is required. At flavor-grade specifications, MIBC also appears in flavoring applications.

These applications occur where its characteristic odor profile meets regulatory thresholds. MIBC is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities for various industrial needs.

Technical grade is the standard for mining and industrial solvent applications, while higher-purity grades are available for cosmetic and flavor end uses. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and water content limits.

When sourcing for sensitive formulation work, ensure the product meets necessary FCC or USP requirements. Proper handling and storage are essential to maintain the chemical integrity of the alcohol over time.

Diisopropyl ether (CAS 108-20-3 ), also known as isopropyl ether or DIPE, is a low-polarity ether solvent used across pharmaceutical, chemical, and flavor extraction processes.

Its selective solvency and low water miscibility make it a practical choice for liquid-liquid extraction and azeotropic drying operations in various industrial settings.

In pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturing, DIPE is used as an extraction solvent to isolate active compounds and intermediates from aqueous reaction mixtures effectively.

Flavor and fragrance producers use it to extract and concentrate aromatic compounds from natural raw materials, where clean solvent removal is critical to end-product quality.

It also functions as a reaction solvent in organic synthesis, particularly where a low-boiling, recoverable ether is preferred over higher-residue alternatives for the process.

In fuel blending, DIPE serves as an oxygenate additive to improve octane ratings in gasoline formulations, demonstrating its versatility across different chemical sectors.

Diisopropyl ether is supplied as a liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for large-volume industrial buyers requiring consistent supply chains.

name: Isopropyl acetate
description:
Isopropyl acetate (CAS 108-21-4 ), also known by its FEMA 2926 designation, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across food flavoring and cosmetic formulation.

Its clean, fruity odor profile makes it a functional ingredient in both flavor systems and fragrance blends. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavoring agent to impart fruity notes.

It is commonly used to provide pear-like notes in confectionery, baked goods, and beverages. Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it as a carrier solvent in nail care products for quick-dry results.

The rapid evaporation rate supports efficient formulations in the beauty industry. It also serves as a processing solvent in flavor concentrate production, helping to dissolve and homogenize aromatic compounds.

This ensures proper incorporation into finished products before distribution. In fragrance compounding, it contributes both as a diluent and as a character note in fruity or floral compositions.

Isopropyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. Food-grade material is available meeting FEMA and FCC specifications.

These quality standards support compliance requirements for flavor applications. Technical-grade supply is also standard for cosmetic and industrial solvent end uses across various global markets.

name: Isopropyl chloroformate
description:
Isopropyl chloroformate ( CAS 108-23-6 ), also known as isopropyl chlorocarbonate, is a reactive acylating agent used in organic synthesis to introduce the isopropoxycarbonyl protecting group onto amines, alcohols, and other nucleophiles.

Its primary commercial role is as a building block and activating reagent in the manufacture of active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty intermediates. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it activates carboxylic acids as mixed anhydrides.

This process enables peptide bond formation under mild conditions, a step critical in the production of peptide-based APIs and small-molecule drugs. Agrochemical manufacturers use it to introduce carbamate linkages in crop protection compounds.

It also serves in the preparation of isopropyl carbonate esters used as intermediates in fine chemical and biotechnology research workflows. Contract synthesis labs and API producers rely on it for protecting group strategies.

These strategies are essential during the multi-step synthesis of complex molecules. Isopropyl chloroformate is supplied as a liquid, typically in stabilized form to control reactivity during storage and transport.

It is available in technical and synthesis grades, with purity levels commonly ranging from 97% to 99%+ for pharmaceutical intermediate applications. Packaging is offered in small quantities for laboratory use.

Bulk drum supply is also available for industrial-scale synthesis. This chemical is a vital component for manufacturers requiring high-purity reagents for sensitive chemical reactions and large-scale production cycles.

name: Acetic anhydride
description:
Acetic anhydride (CAS 108-24-7 ) is a high-volume acetylating agent used across chemical manufacturing to introduce acetyl groups into organic compounds. It functions as both a reactive intermediate and a solvent in synthesis processes.

In pharmaceuticals, it is a critical intermediate in the production of aspirin, acetaminophen, and various cellulose acetate-based excipients. The textile and paper industries rely on it for acetylating cellulose.

This process produces cellulose acetate fibers and coatings with improved dimensional stability. In agrochemical manufacturing, it serves in the synthesis of herbicide and pesticide active ingredients requiring acetylation steps.

Plastics producers use it to initiate acetylation of polyvinyl alcohol, yielding polyvinyl acetate and related polymer intermediates. Acetic anhydride is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk quantities for industrial procurement.

Available packaging includes ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats suited to large-scale operations. Technical grade is the standard offering for most industrial synthesis and chemical manufacturing applications.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications is available for regulated manufacturing environments. These grades ensure the purity documentation and traceability required for compliance.

name: Isopropyl xanthate
description:
Isopropyl xanthate (CAS 108-25-8 ), also known as Proxan, is a xanthate collector used in the selective flotation of sulfide ores. It functions by adsorbing onto mineral surfaces to render them hydrophobic.

This chemical process enables the efficient separation of valuable minerals from gangue in froth flotation circuits. In copper, lead, and zinc sulfide processing, it acts as a primary collector to concentrate target minerals.

This concentration occurs ahead of smelting to ensure high-purity outputs. Gold and silver recovery operations use it to float sulfide-associated precious metals that would otherwise report to tailings during the process.

Nickel and molybdenum concentrators select it for its controlled collecting power, which allows grade-recovery balance to be tuned at the dosing stage. It is also applied in complex polymetallic ore circuits.

In these circuits, selective depression of non-target sulfides is required alongside collector addition. Isopropyl xanthate is supplied as a yellow to pale-green powder or granule for industrial use.

The granular form is often preferred for safer handling and dust reduction in plant environments. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for mining reagent applications.

Typical commercial packaging includes 25 kg bags and bulk quantities suited to concentrator-scale consumption. This ensures reliable supply chains for large-scale mineral processing and extraction facilities worldwide.

name: 3-methyl-5-pyrazolone
description:
3-Methyl-5-pyrazolone (CAS 108-26-9 ) is a pyrazolone building block used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of azo dyes, pigments, and pharmaceutical compounds.

Its reactive methylene group makes it a key coupling component in colorant manufacturing and a starting material for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) synthesis.

In dye and pigment production, it couples with diazonium salts to produce yellow and orange azo colorants used across textile, leather, and paper dyeing processes.

Printing ink formulators rely on these derived pigments for packaging inks where color fastness and substrate adhesion are critical performance requirements.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a precursor to pyrazolone-based APIs and intermediates, including analgesic and anti-inflammatory compound classes.

Specialty chemical manufacturers also use it in the production of heterocyclic compounds for agrochemical and research applications.

3-Methyl-5-pyrazolone is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet API intermediate specifications. Bulk quantities are typically offered in multi-kilogram and metric ton packaging.

name: Maleic anhydride
description:
Maleic anhydride (CAS 108-31-6 ), also known as MA, is a high-volume reactive monomer and chemical intermediate used across polymer, resin, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a building block for unsaturated polyester resins, copolymers, and maleic acid derivatives, enabling cross-linking, surface modification, and functional grafting in downstream formulations.

In plastics and polymer processing, MA is grafted onto polyolefins such as polyethylene and polypropylene to improve adhesion, compatibility, and surface wettability in compounded materials.

Unsaturated polyester resin producers rely on it as a core monomer for laminates, gel coats, and fiber-reinforced composites used in construction and automotive parts.

In textile and paper treatment, maleic anhydride-derived copolymers are used as sizing agents and surface modifiers to improve fiber bonding and coating adhesion.

Personal care formulators use MA-based copolymers as film-forming and fixative agents in hair care products. Maleic anhydride is supplied as molten liquid for bulk industrial delivery.

It is also available as briquettes and flakes for easier handling in smaller volumes. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels, typically at 99%+ purity.

Specifications are aligned to major resin and polymer manufacturing requirements. Packaging ranges from bulk tankers and ISO containers to drums and supersacks depending on volume requirements.

name: Propylene carbonate
description:
Propylene carbonate (CAS 108-32-7 ), commonly abbreviated as PC, is a cyclic carbonate solvent used across energy, electronics, and personal care manufacturing. It dissolves a broad range of polar and nonpolar compounds.

This material is a preferred carrier in formulations where low volatility and high solvency are both required. In lithium-ion battery electrolytes, PC functions as a primary solvent or co-solvent, supporting ion transport.

It performs exceptionally well at low temperatures where other solvents underperform. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a solvent and humectant in skin creams, hair treatments, and color cosmetics.

The compound aids active ingredient penetration without leaving a greasy residue. The oil and gas industry uses PC as a solvent for natural gas purification, specifically for selective absorption of CO₂ and H₂S.

This is utilized in the Fluor Solvent process for efficient gas treatment. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a non-aqueous carrier in topical and oral formulations where aqueous systems are incompatible.

Propylene carbonate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tankers. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with the battery-grade variant subject to strict limits.

The battery-grade material must meet rigorous moisture and metal ion requirements. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. compendial standards for regulated applications.

name: m-toluidine
description:
m-Toluidine (CAS 108-44-1 ), also known as m-aminotoluene, is an aromatic amine used as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of dyes, pigments, and specialty organic compounds.

It serves as a building block for azo colorants and downstream chemical manufacturing across multiple industrial sectors. In textile and leather processing, it is used to produce azo dyes that deliver consistent color performance.

Pigment manufacturers rely on it as a coupling or diazotization component in the production of organic colorants for inks and printing formulations. This ensures high-quality results in various industrial printing applications.

In plastics and polymer systems, it functions as a curing agent or cross-linker in epoxy and resin formulations where controlled reactivity is required. This makes it essential for specialized material engineering.

Cosmetic and personal care manufacturers source it as a precursor in the synthesis of approved colorant intermediates used in hair dye formulations. Its chemical properties allow for precise color development.

m-Toluidine is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, typically available in technical grade for industrial synthesis applications. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs).

These packaging options are suited for bulk procurement and large-scale manufacturing needs. Purity specifications generally range from 98% to 99%+, ensuring high performance in sensitive chemical reactions.

Documentation is available to support quality assurance and regulatory compliance requirements. This ensures that all industrial standards are met for safety and efficacy in global supply chains.

name: Resorcinol
description:
Resorcinol (CAS 108-46-3 ), also known as Resorzin, is a dihydric phenol used across rubber, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries as a bonding agent and chemical intermediate.

Its reactivity with resins and proteins makes it a reliable functional input across structurally diverse manufacturing processes. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it is a core component of latex systems.

These systems bond textile cords and fabrics to rubber compounds to improve structural integrity in tires and conveyor belts. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an active ingredient in topical preparations.

It targets acne, seborrheic dermatitis, and keratotic skin conditions, where it acts as a keratolytic agent. In hair color formulations, it functions as a coupling component that develops color when combined.

It also serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of UV absorbers, flame retardants, and specialty resins used in coatings and adhesives. The material is supplied as white to off-white crystalline flakes.

Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications. Bulk supply is available in fiber drums or bags for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material typically requires tighter purity and packaging controls. This ensures the product meets the rigorous safety standards required for medical and personal care applications.

2,2'-Oxydipropanol (CAS 108-61-2 ), also known as dipropylene glycol, is a diol solvent and humectant used across industrial and consumer formulation segments.

It functions as a carrier, plasticizer, and coupling agent in applications where controlled evaporation and low toxicity are commercially relevant selection criteria.

In personal care and cosmetics, it acts as a humectant and solvent for fragrances, active ingredients, and preservative systems in lotions, creams, and hair care products.

Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and lubricating agent during fiber treatment and finishing operations to ensure high-quality material output.

Printing ink and packaging formulators incorporate it as a solvent carrier to control viscosity and adhesion in water-based and UV-curable systems for industrial use.

Polymer and plastics manufacturers use it as a plasticizer intermediate and reactive diol in polyurethane and polyester resin production for various durable goods.

The material is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. It is available in technical grade and cosmetic/personal care grade.

name: Diisooctyl adipate
description:
Diisooctyl adipate (CAS 108-63-4 ), also known as Bis(1-methylheptyl) adipate, is an ester-based plasticizer derived from adipic acid and isooctyl alcohol. It improves flexibility and low-temperature performance in polymer and rubber compounds.

This chemical provides essential lubrication in industrial fluid formulations. In PVC processing, it functions as a primary or secondary plasticizer to achieve flexible films, sheeting, and profiles with good cold-weather performance.

Rubber compounders use it to improve elasticity and processability in seals, gaskets, and extruded profiles. This is particularly useful where low-temperature flexibility is a critical specification for the final product.

In synthetic and mineral-based lubricant formulations, it contributes to viscosity control and reduces friction. It is commonly utilized in metalworking fluids and gear oils to enhance overall performance and stability.

It also appears in specialty coatings and adhesives where a non-migrating, low-volatility plasticizing component is required. This ensures the longevity and durability of the adhesive bond or coating layer over time.

name: Propylene glycol methyl ether acetate
description:
Propylene glycol methyl ether acetate (CAS 108-65-6 ), commonly sourced and specified as PGMEA or methoxypropyl acetate, is a slow-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, electronics, and printing industries.

Its controlled evaporation rate supports film formation and flow in high-performance formulations where solvent balance is critical to end-product quality. In architectural and industrial coatings, it functions as a coalescing solvent.

It acts as a viscosity modifier, improving leveling and film integrity in both solvent-borne and high-solids systems. Semiconductor and PCB manufacturers rely on it as a carrier solvent for photoresists and anti-reflective coatings.

In these high-tech applications, purity specifications are tightly controlled to ensure performance. In printing inks, particularly UV-curable and gravure formulations, it dissolves resins and controls ink rheology to meet press requirements.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to adjust open time and application viscosity in structural and pressure-sensitive systems. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing and industrial processing.

PGMEA is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Electronic-grade and standard technical-grade are the primary commercial specifications available for various industrial needs.

Electronic-grade material carries tighter purity and metals content requirements for semiconductor applications. Standard technical-grade material is available for coatings, inks, and adhesive end uses across the global market.

name: Cyanuric chloride
description:
Cyanuric chloride (CAS 108-77-0 ), also known as sym-trichlorotriazine, is a reactive triazine intermediate used across chemical synthesis and industrial manufacturing. Its three replaceable chlorine atoms make it a building block for producing dyes and agrochemicals.

This versatile compound is essential for manufacturing UV stabilizers and flame retardants at a commercial scale. In textile processing, it acts as a coupling agent for reactive dyes, bonding colorants permanently to cellulose fibers in cotton dyeing operations.

Coatings and polymer formulators use it to synthesize UV absorbers and light stabilizers that protect resins, films, and surface coatings from photodegradation. These applications ensure long-term durability for materials exposed to sunlight.

Water treatment chemical producers rely on it as a precursor to chlorinated isocyanurates used for disinfection and algae control. It plays a critical role in maintaining safety standards for industrial and municipal water systems.

In flame retardant production, it serves as a core scaffold for nitrogen-based FR additives incorporated into plastics and elastomers. This functionality is vital for meeting fire safety regulations in the construction and automotive sectors.

Cyanuric chloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or flakes. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 98% or higher for industrial synthesis applications.

It is packaged in moisture-controlled containers given its reactivity with water during storage and transport. Proper handling ensures the material maintains its chemical integrity for high-precision manufacturing processes.

name: Melamine
description:
Melamine (CAS 108-78-1 ) is a nitrogen-rich triazine compound used primarily as a reactive monomer in the production of thermosetting resins and as a flame retardant additive across multiple industrial sectors.

Cyanuric triamide is an alternative designation occasionally encountered in technical literature, though the market universally trades under the melamine name. Its high nitrogen content makes it commercially valuable.

This chemical is essential for resin crosslinking and for suppressing combustion in polymer systems. The dominant use is in melamine-formaldehyde (MF) resin production, where it reacts with formaldehyde to form durable thermosets.

These resins are used in laminates, surface coatings, and wood-based panel adhesives. In coatings and adhesives, MF resins provide hard, scratch-resistant finishes for furniture, flooring, and automotive topcoats.

Textile and paper processors use melamine-based resins to impart wet strength, crease resistance, and dimensional stability to finished goods. It is a versatile component for high-performance industrial manufacturing.

As a flame retardant, melamine is compounded into polyurethane foams, epoxy systems, and engineering plastics where halogen-free fire performance is required. This ensures safety compliance in various construction materials.

Melamine is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bulk bags, supersacks, and 25 kg bags. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically at 99.8% or higher for industrial use.

Specifications are assessed against established industrial standards depending on the end-use application. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for large-scale chemical manufacturing operations.

name: Cyanuric acid
description:
Cyanuric acid (CAS 108-80-5 ) is a triazine-based compound used industrially as a stabilizer, biocide precursor, and flame retardant intermediate. In water treatment, it extends the effective life of chlorine-based disinfectants by reducing UV degradation.

Across polymer and textile applications, it functions as a building block for flame retardant systems and crosslinking agents. In swimming pool and recreational water treatment, it stabilizes free chlorine against photodegradation.

This stabilization reduces chemical consumption and maintains consistent sanitizer levels. Polymer formulators use it as a precursor to melamine cyanurate, a halogen-free flame retardant additive incorporated into nylon and engineering plastics.

In textile and leather processing, it serves as a component in crosslinking systems that improve dye fixation and substrate durability. Paper treatment applications include its use in wet-strength resin formulations.

It also acts as a chlorine stabilizer in bleaching processes. Cyanuric acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in granular form, with granules preferred in water treatment for easier handling and controlled dissolution.

Standard commercial grades include technical and water treatment grades, with purity typically at 98% or higher. Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities, supporting both industrial formulators and pool chemical blenders.

name: Diisobutyl ketone
description:
Diisobutyl ketone (CAS 108-83-8 ), also known as DIBK or Valerone, is a slow-evaporating ketone solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and flavor applications.

Its controlled evaporation rate makes it a preferred carrier in formulations where extended open time or gradual release is commercially valuable for industrial and specialty chemical processes.

In coatings and lacquers, DIBK functions as a high-boiling solvent that improves flow and leveling in nitrocellulose and acrylic systems, reducing surface defects in the final film.

Adhesive formulators use it to control viscosity and working time in contact cement and pressure-sensitive adhesive systems. In the flavor industry, it is approved under FEMA 3537 .

As a flavoring agent, it contributes fruity, sweet notes to food and beverage products. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a solvent carrier in nail care products and aerosol formulations.

It is highly valued where compatibility with resins and slow evaporation are required. Diisobutyl ketone is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC quantities.

Technical grade is the most common supply form for solvent applications, while flavor-grade material is available for food and cosmetic use. Buyers should confirm purity specifications.

Grade documentation is essential when sourcing for regulated end-use categories. Ensure all materials meet necessary safety and regulatory requirements for your specific application needs.

name: Methylcyclohexane
description:
Methylcyclohexane (CAS 108-87-2 ), also known commercially as MCH and toluene hexahydride, is a saturated alicyclic hydrocarbon solvent used across industrial and specialty chemical applications.

It functions as a non-polar solvent and process carrier where low water miscibility and controlled evaporation are required. In catalyst research and chemical synthesis, MCH serves as a hydrogen carrier.

This occurs in thermochemical energy storage systems, where cyclical dehydrogenation to toluene enables hydrogen release on demand. Formulators in personal care use it as a solvent carrier in fragrance concentrates.

It is also utilized in aerosol delivery systems requiring clean evaporation profiles. In flavor and fragrance manufacturing, MCH acts as an extraction and dilution solvent for sensitive aroma compounds.

This is particularly useful where residual solvent control is critical to finished product compliance. Industrial coatings and adhesive processors also select it as a hydrocarbon diluent.

It is preferred in applications where aromatic solvents must be avoided. Methylcyclohexane is supplied as a clear liquid in standard bulk quantities including drums, IBCs, and isotanks.

Technical grade is the most common commercial specification, with high-purity grades available for catalyst and specialty synthesis applications. Buyers should confirm purity thresholds before sourcing.

Residual aromatic content should be checked against process or regulatory requirements. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance standards for specific industrial or laboratory use.

name: Toluene
description:
Toluene (CAS 108-88-3 ) is an aromatic hydrocarbon solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and chemical manufacturing to dissolve, dilute, and carry a broad range of resins, polymers, and active substances.

It delivers fast, controlled evaporation rates that make it a preferred solvent where film formation and dry time are critical process variables. In coatings and industrial paints, it dissolves nitrocellulose, epoxy, and polyurethane resins.

This enables smooth application and consistent film build. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to formulate contact cements and pressure-sensitive systems for footwear, automotive interiors, and flexible packaging.

In printing inks, it acts as the primary carrier solvent for gravure and flexographic formulations, controlling viscosity and ink transfer onto film substrates. The oil and gas sector uses it as a process solvent.

It also serves as a reference compound in octane blending and fuel additive production. The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities for industrial use.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and refined grades meeting ASTM specifications, with purity levels typically at 99.5% and above. Reagent and ACS grades are available for laboratory applications.

In pharmaceuticals, it serves as a key precursor in the synthesis of isonicotinic acid derivatives and active pharmaceutical ingredients targeting cardiovascular and neurological conditions. Agrochemical producers use it to manufacture herbicides.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it acts as a curing catalyst and crosslinking accelerator for epoxy systems, influencing cure rate and final film performance. It is also known as p-picoline or gamma-picoline.

At trace concentrations, it contributes roasted and nutty flavor notes in food applications, with usage governed by FEMA -recognized flavor standards. This versatility makes it essential for various industrial sectors.

The compound is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purities, typically 98% and 99%+ grades for pharmaceutical and synthesis applications. Technical-grade material is available for industrial catalyst use.

name: Cyclohexylamine
description:
Cyclohexylamine (CAS 108-91-8 ), commonly abbreviated as CHA, is a primary aliphatic amine used across industrial and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions as a corrosion inhibitor, pH buffer, and reactive intermediate.

In boiler water and steam condensate systems, CHA neutralizes acidic condensate and forms a protective film on metal surfaces. This reduces corrosion-related downtime in industrial utilities and steam distribution networks.

Rubber and tire manufacturers use it as a precursor to sulfenamide accelerators, which control vulcanization rates. These accelerators are essential for tire compounds and various industrial rubber goods production.

In agrochemical production, CHA serves as a building block for herbicide and pesticide active ingredients. This includes cyclohexylamine salt formulations of glyphosate used in modern agricultural applications.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as an intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients. It is also frequently utilized as a counterion in drug salt formation processes.

Cyclohexylamine is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in standard bulk and intermediate packaging. Options include drums and ISO tank containers to suit different logistics and storage needs.

Technical grade and high-purity grades are available, with specifications aligned to industrial synthesis requirements. Buyers sourcing for regulated applications typically require documentation such as GMP compliance.

A certificate of analysis with purity confirmation is provided to ensure the material meets strict quality standards. This ensures reliability for both large-scale industrial use and specialized chemical synthesis.

name: Cyclohexanone
description:
Cyclohexanone (CAS 108-94-1 ), also known commercially as Sextone and Pimelin Ketone, is a cyclic ketone solvent used across industrial and specialty chemical applications.

With FEMA 3909 status, it also holds a recognized position in flavor and fragrance work. Its solvency strength and compatibility with resins and polymers make it a practical choice.

In coatings and lacquer formulations, it dissolves nitrocellulose, vinyl resins, and synthetic rubbers where weaker solvents fall short. It is a key component for high-performance systems.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators use it as a carrier solvent in nail products and specialty adhesive systems requiring controlled evaporation. It ensures consistent application and finish.

In flavor and fragrance compounding, its FEMA-approved status permits use as a flavoring agent where a mild, earthy ketone note is required. It serves as a versatile process solvent.

It also functions as a process solvent in polymer and resin manufacturing, particularly where high solvency power and controlled boiling point are procurement priorities for the facility.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher.

Food-grade and flavor-compliant specifications are available for applications requiring regulatory alignment. All batches are tested to ensure they meet the necessary industrial requirements.

name: Phenol
description:
Phenol (CAS 108-95-2 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3223 designation, is a high-volume industrial chemical used as a building block for resins, pharmaceutical intermediates, and specialty chemicals.

It functions as a disinfectant, preservative, and reactive intermediate across manufacturing sectors ranging from polymer production to personal care. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of analgesics, antiseptics, and active pharmaceutical ingredients, and is used as a preservative in injectable formulations. Resin and polymer producers rely on it as a primary feedstock.

It is used for phenol-formaldehyde resins found in adhesives, laminates, and molded industrial components. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a pH buffer and antimicrobial agent in topical formulations.

Textile and leather processing operations use phenol-derived compounds for dyestuff synthesis and as a carrier solvent in fiber dyeing processes. Phenol is supplied as a liquefied melt or in solid crystalline flake form.

Liquid is the standard for bulk industrial shipment. Available grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications, as well as technical grade for industrial resin and chemical synthesis use.

Bulk quantities are typically shipped in heated ISO tanks or steel drums to maintain product in liquid state. This ensures the material remains ready for immediate use in large-scale manufacturing environments.

name: 3-picoline
description:
3-Picoline (CAS 108-99-6 ), also known as beta-picoline, is a methylpyridine isomer used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of vitamins, agrochemicals, and pharmaceutical actives.

It serves as a building block rather than a finished ingredient, making it a procurement priority for manufacturers operating upstream in their supply chains across various industrial sectors.

In the pharmaceutical and nutrition industries, this compound is the principal precursor for nicotinamide (Vitamin B3) and nicotinic acid synthesis, ensuring high-quality output for global health markets.

Agrochemical producers use it to manufacture pyridine-based herbicides and insecticides, particularly in active ingredient synthesis where chemical stability and reactivity are essential for performance.

In flavor chemistry, trace concentrations contribute roasted, nutty, or meaty notes to processed food formulations, while resin formulators employ it as a catalyst in select polymerization processes.

The material is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, typically in drums or ISO tank containers for large-volume orders to meet the logistical needs of global chemical manufacturing facilities.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels commonly at 99% or higher by GC, ensuring consistent results in standard industrial applications and chemical reactions.

Pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available from select manufacturers where downstream API synthesis demands tighter impurity profiles and adherence to rigorous quality control protocols during production.

name: Polyquaternium-7
description:
Polyquaternium-7 (CAS 108464-53-5 ), also known as dimethyldiallylammonium chloride acrylamide polymer, is a cationic conditioning polymer used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

It deposits onto negatively charged surfaces such as hair, skin, and hard substrates to deliver conditioning, detangling, and film-forming effects. In shampoos and conditioners, it reduces combing friction.

This polymer improves wet and dry feel without weighing hair down. Body washes and skin cleansers incorporate it to leave a smooth, conditioned after-feel on skin following rinse-off during daily use.

In home care and institutional cleaning products, it functions as a soil-release and surface-conditioning agent. It is frequently utilized in hard surface cleaners and various fabric care formulations.

It also acts as a rheology modifier in liquid formulations, contributing to viscosity stability and suspension of active ingredients. This ensures a consistent product performance over its entire shelf life.

Polyquaternium-7 is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at active concentrations ranging from 5% to 12%. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suitable for personal care applications.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial cleaning end uses. Packaging is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for commercial volumes and large scale manufacturing.

name: n-methylpiperazine
description:
N-Methylpiperazine (CAS 109-01-3 ) is a cyclic diamine building block used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer chemistry, and industrial process chemistry. Its secondary and tertiary amine groups make it a reactive intermediate for constructing drug molecules.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key structural component in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, including several antipsychotics, antivirals, and antibiotics where the piperazine ring is incorporated.

Polymer and epoxy formulators use it as a curing agent and cross-linker, where controlled reactivity with epoxide groups influences network density and final mechanical properties in industrial applications.

In water treatment, it functions as a biocide intermediate and corrosion inhibitor precursor, contributing to formulations that control microbial growth in industrial cooling and process water systems.

Catalyst manufacturers also use it as a ligand precursor and amine catalyst in polyurethane and specialty polymer production, providing essential functionality for high-performance chemical manufacturing.

N-Methylpiperazine is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers requiring consistent supply chains.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting specifications relevant to API intermediate production. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99%+ depending on the application.

name: N-methylmorpholine
description:
N-methylmorpholine (CAS 109-02-4 ), commonly abbreviated as NMM, is a tertiary amine solvent and catalyst used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer processing, and specialty coatings.

It functions primarily as a base catalyst and reaction solvent where controlled basicity and miscibility with water and organic media are required for process efficiency in industrial settings.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, NMM acts as a non-nucleophilic base in peptide coupling reactions, enabling cleaner synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients at scale for global distribution.

Polyurethane foam and elastomer producers use it as a catalyst to control gel and blow reaction timing, directly affecting final product density and mechanical performance in various applications.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it promotes crosslinking and improves adhesion to difficult substrates, particularly in industrial and protective coating systems used in harsh environments.

Printing ink manufacturers incorporate NMM as a co-solvent to improve pigment dispersion and resin compatibility in high-performance ink systems designed for modern commercial printing needs.

N-methylmorpholine is supplied as a liquid in standard bulk quantities including drums and IBC containers, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and specialty use by researchers.

It functions primarily as a chemical intermediate, enabling the construction of more complex active molecules across multiple regulated industries. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, alpha-picoline serves as a precursor to vinylpyridine derivatives.

It is essential for the production of antihistamines and vitamins including B6 and melatonin-related compounds. Agrochemical producers use it to synthesize herbicides and insecticides, particularly chloropyrifos-related intermediates.

In flavor and fragrance applications, 2-picoline contributes to the synthesis of specific aroma compounds where its reactivity at the methyl group is commercially exploited. It also functions as a catalyst or co-solvent.

The material is utilized in select organic synthesis processes, including resin and polymer production. 2-Methylpyridine is supplied as a liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available.

name: Triethylene glycol dimethacrylate
description:
Triethylene glycol dimethacrylate (CAS 109-16-0 ), also known as TEGDMA or Tedma, is a bifunctional methacrylate monomer used as a reactive crosslinker and diluent in UV- and peroxide-cured polymer systems.

It bridges polymer chains during cure, improving hardness, chemical resistance, and dimensional stability in the final material. In dental composites and restorative materials, TEGDMA functions as a reactive diluent.

This monomer lowers resin viscosity while contributing to the crosslinked network structure. UV-curable coatings and inks rely on it to increase crosslink density, improving scratch resistance and adhesion to substrates.

It is effective on surfaces like plastics and metals. Structural adhesives and anaerobic sealants incorporate TEGDMA to control cure speed and enhance mechanical strength in bonded assemblies.

It also serves as a comonomer in acrylic and methacrylic polymer formulations where tight control over network architecture is required. TEGDMA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities.

Standard technical-grade material is the most common commercial form, with inhibitor levels specified to suit storage and processing requirements. Purity grades suitable for dental and medical device applications are available.

name: Diethylene glycol distearate
description:
Diethylene glycol distearate ( CAS 109-30-8 ), also known commercially as Witconol CAD, is a diester of diethylene glycol and stearic acid used across personal care, textile, and polymer applications.

It functions as an emulsifier, rheology modifier, and plasticizer, helping formulators control texture, consistency, and surface properties in finished products. In personal care formulations, it builds pearlescent opacity.

It thickens creams, lotions, and shampoos without requiring additional thickening agents. Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and lubricating agent, improving hand feel and reducing fiber-to-fiber friction.

In plastics compounding, it acts as an internal plasticizer and processing aid, improving flow and reducing brittleness in polymer blends. Paper and coating applications rely on it for surface conditioning.

It also serves as a dispersing aid in pigment-loaded formulations. Diethylene glycol distearate is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form for ease of handling.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of personal care versus industrial end uses. Packaging options commonly include bags and fiber drums.

name: Isodecyl pelargonate
description:
Isodecyl pelargonate (CAS 109-32-0 ) is an ester of nonanoic acid and isodecyl alcohol, used industrially as a plasticizer, lubricant base fluid, and emollient carrier.

Its low-viscosity ester profile makes it a practical formulation component across both industrial lubricant and personal care applications. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it functions as a synthetic base fluid.

It contributes lubricity and compatibility with additive packages in cutting oils and specialty greases. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a lightweight emollient and solvent carrier in skin creams and serums.

In color cosmetics, its dry skin feel and spreadability support finished product aesthetics. As a plasticizer, it is used to improve flexibility and processing characteristics in polymer and resin systems.

Its solvency profile also supports dispersion of actives and pigments in both cosmetic and industrial coating formulations. Isodecyl pelargonate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material typically meeting purity standards relevant to personal care manufacturing. Packaging options commonly include drums and IBCs.

Octyl stearate (CAS 109-36-4 ) is a fatty acid ester produced from stearic acid and octanol, used across personal care, plastics, and industrial lubrication. It functions as an emollient, plasticizer, and carrier medium depending on the application.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a skin-conditioning emollient and solvent carrier for active ingredients in creams, lotions, and color cosmetics. Plastics and polymer processors use it as an internal plasticizer and lubricant.

This material helps to improve flexibility and processing flow in PVC and similar compounds. In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it serves as a base fluid or additive component in cutting oils and release agents.

It is particularly effective where a non-volatile, film-forming lubricant is required. Its low polarity also makes it a useful dispersing medium for pigments and waxes in coatings and specialty formulations.

Octyl stearate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Technical and cosmetic grades are the standard commercial offerings, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity specifications relevant to personal care manufacturing.

It enhances cold-temperature performance in films, coatings, and cable jacketing. Food manufacturers use it as a flavoring ingredient under FEMA 2373 , where it contributes fruity, fatty notes.

It is frequently utilized in confectionery, beverages, and dairy formulations. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it performs as a base fluid or additive where low-viscosity stability is required.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate DBS as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent. It is commonly found in creams, lip products, and various color cosmetics for its unique performance properties.

name: 3-Dimethylaminopropylamine
description:
3-Dimethylaminopropylamine (CAS 109-55-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DMAPA, is a bifunctional diamine used as a reactive intermediate and process chemical across specialty chemical manufacturing.

It combines a primary and a tertiary amine in a single molecule, making it a building block for synthesizing surfactants, polymers, and active ingredients for various industrial applications.

In personal care, it is the key reactant in producing cocamidopropyl betaine, the amphoteric surfactant found in shampoos, body washes, and mild cleansing formulations for consumer use.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing active compounds and as a pH-buffering agent in formulation chemistry to ensure stability and efficacy of the final product.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a curing agent and chain extender for epoxy systems and polyurethane coatings. It also serves as a corrosion inhibitor precursor and stabilizer additive.

This chemical is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers and large-scale operations.

Technical grade is the most common commercial specification, though higher-purity grades are available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements and specific manufacturing standards.

Buyers should confirm amine content and water specification when sourcing for surfactant synthesis, where consistent purity directly affects downstream yield and overall product quality.

name: Propyl acetate
description:
Propyl acetate (CAS 109-60-4 ), also known by its abbreviation NPAC, is an ester solvent and flavoring agent used across printing, personal care, and food industries.

It dissolves a broad range of resins, coatings, and fragrance materials, offering a moderate evaporation rate that suits both industrial solvent applications and sensory formulation work.

In printing and packaging, NPAC is used as a carrier solvent in flexographic and gravure inks, where its evaporation profile supports print quality and press-speed requirements.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into nail care products, hair sprays, and perfume bases as a solvent and diluent for film-forming resins and fragrance concentrates.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavoring ingredient — FEMA 2925 — contributing fruity, pear-like top notes to confectionery, beverages, and baked goods.

It also serves as a process solvent in flavor extraction and concentration operations. Propyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities.

Technical grade is standard for industrial solvent applications, while food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is available for flavor and food processing use.

Purity levels of 99% and above are typical across commercial supply. This versatile ester remains a staple for manufacturers requiring reliable solvency and aromatic properties.

name: Butyl bromide
description:
Butyl bromide ( CAS 109-65-9 ), also known as 1-bromobutane, is a reactive alkyl halide used as a chemical building block and alkylating agent across pharmaceutical and industrial manufacturing.

Its primary commercial role is introducing a butyl group into target molecules during synthesis, making it a key intermediate in multi-step production processes for various sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to synthesize active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates where controlled alkylation is required to achieve specific molecular structures.

Polymer and plastics producers use it as a precursor in catalyst systems and in the preparation of flame retardant additives for thermoplastic formulations to enhance material safety.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a chemical intermediate in the production of finishing agents and preservation compounds used to improve the durability of final products.

It also serves as a reagent in Grignard reactions, where it reacts with magnesium to form butylmagnesium bromide for downstream organic synthesis and complex chemical transformations.

The material is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging including drums and intermediate bulk containers. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for industrial use.

High-purity grades are available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements. Suppliers typically offer material with defined purity thresholds and low water content to support sensitive applications.

name: 1-bromo-3-chloropropane
description:
1-Bromo-3-chloropropane (CAS 109-70-6 ), also known as trimethylene chlorobromide, is a bifunctional alkyl halide used as a chemical intermediate and flame retardant precursor in industrial manufacturing.

Its dual halogen functionality makes it a reactive building block for synthesizing specialty compounds across multiple sectors. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in producing flame retardant additives.

These additives are incorporated into construction materials such as insulation panels and cable sheathing. The textile and leather industries use it in the synthesis of biocidal and preservative agents applied during processing.

It also functions as a crosslinking and chain-extension intermediate in polymer chemistry, enabling controlled modification of material properties for construction-grade applications. This versatility is key for industrial producers.

Specialty chemical producers use it to prepare quaternary ammonium compounds and other antimicrobial actives. These are used in paper treatment and industrial preservation formulations to ensure product longevity and safety.

1-Bromo-3-chloropropane is supplied as a liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC packaging. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification available from bulk chemical suppliers for large-scale use.

Purity levels typically range from 97% to 99%+, with high-purity offerings suited to synthesis applications. This ensures that halide impurities do not affect downstream reaction yields or final product quality.

name: n-Butylamine
description:
n-Butylamine (CAS 109-73-9 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3130 designation in flavor applications, is a primary aliphatic amine used across chemical synthesis, polymer processing, and flavor manufacturing.

It functions as a reactive intermediate and pH modifier in a broad range of industrial formulations. In flavor and fragrance production, n-butylamine contributes to the synthesis of aroma compounds.

The material is approved under FEMA 3130 for use in food-grade flavor systems. Polymer and rubber manufacturers use it as a curing agent and cross-linking intermediate in various industrial processes.

It is particularly useful in the production of vulcanized rubber and epoxy systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a pH-adjusting agent in products where controlled alkalinity is required.

This chemical also serves as a building block in the synthesis of agrochemical intermediates, pharmaceuticals, and corrosion inhibitors. n-Butylamine is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or IBCs.

Bulk tanker quantities are suited to industrial-scale procurement for large facilities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for flavor and pharmaceutical synthesis.

Buyers should confirm concentration and grade specifications against their regulatory requirements. This is particularly important for food-contact or flavor end uses to ensure compliance with safety standards.

name: Butanethiol
description:
Butanethiol (CAS 109-79-5 ), also known as n-butyl mercaptan, is a sulfur-containing organic compound used commercially as an odorant and flavoring agent. Its intensely low odor threshold makes it effective for gas leak detection and trace-level sensory applications.

FEMA 3478 designates it as an approved flavoring substance for food use. In the oil and gas industry, butanethiol is blended into natural gas and LPG as a stenching agent, providing the characteristic warning odor.

This warning odor enables leak detection at extremely low concentrations. Food and beverage formulators use it at trace levels to contribute sulfurous, onion-like, or savory top notes in processed flavors for various applications.

It functions as a building block in flavor systems targeting meat, roasted, and allium profiles. Fragrance and flavor houses also incorporate it into reference standards and specialty aroma compositions requiring controlled sulfur character.

Butanethiol is supplied as a liquid, typically in small containers suited to its high odor intensity and handling requirements. It is available in technical grade for industrial odorant applications and in food-grade specifications.

The material is compliant with FEMA and relevant flavor safety standards. Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to drum volumes depending on end-use volume requirements and specific industrial or food-grade needs.

name: n-methylethanolamine
description:
N-Methylethanolamine (CAS 109-83-1 ), commercially abbreviated as MMEA, is a secondary amino alcohol used across chemical manufacturing as a pH regulator, buffering agent, and reactive intermediate.

Its dual functional groups, a secondary amine and a hydroxyl, make it a building block for surfactants, corrosion inhibitors, and specialty polymers. In coatings and adhesives, MMEA functions as a neutralizing agent.

It is used for waterborne resin systems, improving dispersion stability and film formation. Personal care formulators use it to adjust pH in emulsions and creams, where it also contributes mild humectant properties.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers employ MMEA as a synthesis intermediate in active ingredient production and as a buffering component in topical preparations. It is a versatile component for many industries.

In industrial gas treatment and sealant systems, it acts as an absorbent for acid gases and a reactive modifier for polymer crosslinking. This makes it essential for high-performance industrial applications.

N-Methylethanolamine is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger procurement volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

This grade is suitable for industrial and coating applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP specifications is available for regulated manufacturing use and specialized applications.
