name: Ethylene glycol monomethyl ether
description:
Ethylene glycol monomethyl ether (CAS 109-86-4 ), also known as Methyl Glycol or EGME, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, printing, and polymer processing.

Its controlled evaporation rate and compatibility with both water-based and solvent-based systems make it a practical choice for formulators managing film formation and flow during production.

In industrial coatings and lacquers, EGME improves flow, leveling, and film uniformity, reducing surface defects in spray and brush applications. Printing ink manufacturers use it to control drying speed.

It helps maintain viscosity stability across solvent and water-reducible ink systems. In adhesive and sealant formulations, it functions as a carrier solvent that aids resin dissolution and extends open time.

Polymer and resin producers also incorporate it as a reactive diluent or curing co-solvent in epoxy and nitrocellulose-based systems. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Ethylene glycol monomethyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher.

Buyers should confirm purity, water content, and acidity specifications against their formulation or process requirements. Proper storage and handling are essential for maintaining chemical integrity.

name: Dimethoxymethane
description:
Dimethoxymethane (CAS 109-87-5 ), commercially known as Methylal, is a fast-evaporating solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, specialty chemical synthesis, and flavoring applications.

Its low boiling point and clean evaporation profile make it a preferred choice where residue-free solvent performance is a procurement priority for industrial manufacturers and labs.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Methylal functions as a reaction solvent and extraction medium where controlled evaporation and low residual contamination are critical to API quality.

Flavor formulators incorporate it as a carrier solvent and flavoring agent, particularly in applications requiring rapid volatilization of aromatic compounds in various mixtures.

In specialty chemical synthesis, it acts as a formaldehyde equivalent and catalyst precursor for producing polyoxymethylene dimethyl ethers and other acetal-based intermediates.

Industrial cleaning and aerosol formulations also use it as a co-solvent to improve solvency and reduce VOC content in finished products across many different sectors.

Dimethoxymethane is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger industrial volumes and high-capacity manufacturing needs.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet FCC and USP compliance requirements. Technical-grade material is standard for industrial solvent use.

name: Diethylamine
description:
Diethylamine (CAS 109-89-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DEA, is a secondary aliphatic amine used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production. It functions primarily as a chemical intermediate, pH buffer, and catalyst in the construction of more complex molecules.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DEA acts as a buffering agent and reaction intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, including antihistamines and local anesthetics. Rubber and polymer producers use it as a curing accelerator and cross-linking agent.

This chemical improves processing efficiency in latex and elastomer formulations. In agrochemical production, it serves as a key intermediate for herbicide and fungicide synthesis, particularly in the manufacture of dithiocarbamate-based compounds.

Personal care formulators incorporate DEA into pH adjustment systems for creams, lotions, and hair care products where controlled alkalinity is required. Diethylamine is supplied as a colorless liquid, typically in bulk quantities via ISO tank, drum, or intermediate bulk container.

Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with the latter conforming to USP or Ph. Eur. specifications where purity requirements are critical. Concentration is typically 99%+ for high-purity grades used in regulated applications.

name: Pyrrole
description:
Pyrrole (CAS 109-97-7 ), also known by its older designations pyrrhol and imidole, is a five-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle used as a key synthetic building block across pharmaceutical and agrochemical manufacturing.

Its reactivity at multiple ring positions makes it a high-demand intermediate for constructing complex molecular architectures in commercial synthesis workflows and advanced materials production for global industrial sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this compound serves as a precursor to a broad range of active ingredients, including antifungal agents and kinase inhibitors, where the intact ring is incorporated into the final drug structure.

Agrochemical producers use it to synthesize pyrrole-based insecticides and fungicides, with chlorfenapyr being one of the most commercially significant derivatives currently utilized in the global agricultural market.

In polymer and materials science, it undergoes oxidative polymerization to produce polypyrrole, a conductive polymer used in antistatic coatings, biosensors, and various energy storage applications for modern electronics.

It also carries FEMA 3386 status, supporting its use as a flavor ingredient in food and beverage formulations at trace concentrations, adhering to strict safety guidelines for food-grade chemical additives.

The product is supplied as a liquid in standard commercial and high-purity grades. Technical grade material is available for polymer synthesis, while reagent grades serve pharmaceutical and biotechnology applications.

Packaging typically ranges from small containers for laboratory procurement to bulk quantities for industrial-scale users, ensuring flexible supply chain solutions for diverse manufacturing requirements and research needs.

name: Tetrahydrofuran
description:
Tetrahydrofuran (CAS 109-99-9 ), commonly known as THF or oxolane, is a cyclic ether solvent with exceptional miscibility across both polar and non-polar systems. It dissolves a broad range of polymers, resins, and active compounds.

This versatile solvent handles materials that resist other common liquids, making it a go-to choice for demanding formulation and synthesis work. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used as a reaction solvent and extraction medium.

Its ability to solvate organolithium and Grignard reagents is critical to process chemistry during API synthesis. PVC adhesives and coatings rely on this chemical as the primary solvent, enabling strong substrate bonding in pipe fittings.

It is also utilized in footwear and industrial laminates. It functions as a polymerization solvent in the production of polytetramethylene ether glycol (PTMEG), a key intermediate for spandex fibers and polyurethane elastomers.

In analytical and QC laboratories, it serves as a standard HPLC mobile phase component for separating polymers and pharmaceutical compounds. The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities.

Anhydrous and stabilized grades are the most common commercial forms, with stabilizer-free variants available for sensitive synthesis applications. Technical and reagent-grade specifications are standard for industrial use.

HPLC-grade is available for laboratory and analytical procurement. Our material meets rigorous industry requirements to ensure consistent performance across all manufacturing and research applications.

name: Nicotinamide mononucleotide
description:
Nicotinamide mononucleotide (CAS 1094-61-7 ), commonly abbreviated as NMN and also recognized commercially as beta-NMN, is a nucleotide derivative of niacinamide that functions as a direct biosynthetic precursor to NAD+.

Demand is driven by its role in supporting cellular energy metabolism pathways, making it a sought-after active ingredient across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic supply chains globally.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, NMN is formulated into capsules, tablets, and sublingual powders targeting NAD+ replenishment. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into anti-aging serums and moisturizing creams.

Its humectant properties and antioxidant activity support skin barrier function and formulation stability. Pharmaceutical and biotech researchers use NMN as an intermediate in the synthesis of NAD+ analogs.

It also serves as a reference standard in metabolic pathway studies and as a biochemical reagent in cell culture and enzymatic assay development within life sciences laboratories and research facilities.

NMN is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include 98%+ purity material suitable for research and supplement applications, with higher-specification pharmaceutical-grade material available.

Bulk quantities are typically offered alongside smaller research-scale packaging to serve both industrial formulators and laboratory procurement needs. All batches are tested to ensure they meet strict quality standards.

name: Morpholine oleate
description:
Morpholine oleate (CAS 1095-66-5 ) is the salt formed between morpholine and oleic acid, functioning as a corrosion inhibitor, emulsifier, and lubrication additive across several industrial sectors.

It combines the amine basicity of morpholine with the fatty acid character of oleic acid, making it effective in water-based and oil-based systems where both surface protection and emulsification are required.

In metalworking fluids and rust-preventive formulations, it protects ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces by forming a protective film that displaces moisture and inhibits oxidation.

Textile and leather processing operations use it as a softening and lubricating agent during fiber treatment and finishing stages. In coatings and emulsion systems, it acts as an emulsifier.

This compound helps to stabilize oil-in-water dispersions and improve coating adhesion to metal substrates. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to improve wetting and dispersion of pigments.

Morpholine oleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste at ambient temperature. It is available primarily in technical grade, with purity specifications tailored to industrial end-use requirements.

Packaging options commonly include drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for bulk industrial supply. This ensures safe handling and efficient transport for large-scale manufacturing operations.

name: Furan
description:
Furan (CAS 110-00-9 ), also known as furfurane or tetrole, is a five-membered oxygen-containing heterocyclic compound used as a reactive building block and solvent in chemical synthesis.

Its primary commercial role is as a precursor and intermediate in the production of specialty polymers and pharmaceutical compounds. In polymer chemistry, it serves as a monomer in Diels-Alder-based systems.

This enables the production of thermally reversible resins and bio-based plastics with controlled crosslinking behavior. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic intermediate in the construction of drug scaffolds.

Its ring structure is frequently incorporated into active pharmaceutical ingredients. As a low-boiling solvent, it is employed in laboratory-scale and pilot-plant synthesis where rapid removal is a requirement.

Furan also functions as a starting material for producing tetrahydrofuran (THF) and other downstream derivatives used across solvent and polymer supply chains. It is supplied as a stabilized liquid.

The product is typically available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications. It is offered in packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drum supply, depending on purity requirements.

Buyers should confirm stabilizer content and purity grade, commonly 99%+, when specifying for pharmaceutical or polymer synthesis applications to ensure consistent performance in sensitive reactions.

name: Tetrahydrothiophene
description:
Tetrahydrothiophene (CAS 110-01-0 ), also known as THT and thiophane, is a saturated sulfur-containing heterocyclic compound used commercially as an odorant and corrosion inhibitor across energy and industrial sectors.

Its distinctive, persistent odor makes it the standard gas-odorization agent in natural gas and LPG distribution networks across Europe and many other markets. THT is injected into natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas pipelines.

This injection occurs at low concentrations to provide the characteristic warning odor required by safety regulations, enabling leak detection by end users. In industrial cleaning and maintenance formulations, it functions as a sulfur-based corrosion inhibitor.

It protects metal surfaces exposed to aggressive process environments. Water treatment operations use THT-based chemistry where controlled sulfur dosing is required to manage scaling or microbial activity in distribution systems.

As a flavoring reference compound, it is also evaluated in fragrance and flavor research for its role in characterizing sulfurous aroma profiles. Tetrahydrothiophene is supplied as a clear liquid in drums and IBCs.

Bulk tanker quantities are also available, suited to pipeline odorization programs. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher.

Specialty grades meeting tighter purity thresholds are available for analytical and flavor research applications. These high-purity options ensure consistent performance in sensitive laboratory and industrial environments.

It provides a characteristic sulfurous, meat-like aromatic profile that underpins a range of synthetic flavor systems. In food flavoring, thiophene derivatives are used to recreate roasted, cooked meat, and savory notes.

These compounds are essential in processed food products, seasonings, and flavor blends. It also functions as a key building block in the synthesis of more complex heterocyclic flavor compounds for the industry.

The ring structure is modified to produce targeted aroma profiles for various applications. Fragrance formulators use thiophene-based intermediates in specialty compositions requiring sulfurous or roasted character.

Beyond flavor and fragrance, it serves as a synthetic intermediate in fine chemical and pharmaceutical manufacturing. The thiophene ring is frequently incorporated into active compound structures for medicine.

name: di-tert-butyl peroxide
description:
Di-tert-butyl peroxide (CAS 110-05-4 ), commonly known as DTBP, is an organic peroxide used as a high-temperature free-radical initiator and cross-linking agent across rubber and polymer manufacturing.

Its relatively high decomposition temperature makes it the preferred choice where lower-temperature peroxides would activate prematurely during compounding or processing. In rubber and tire production, DTBP initiates cross-linking.

It is used for EPDM, silicone, and natural rubber compounds, delivering vulcanizates with improved heat resistance compared to sulfur-cured alternatives. Polyethylene and polypropylene producers use it to initiate reactions.

These reactions include controlled degradation or grafting, modifying melt flow and mechanical properties for film, pipe, and wire insulation grades. It also functions as a polymerization initiator for styrenic and acrylic monomers.

A high-temperature kick-off point is required to match reactor conditions. In the production of unsaturated polyester resins, DTBP enables elevated-temperature cure cycles that reduce cycle times in compression molding.

Di-tert-butyl peroxide is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at concentrations of 98% or higher for industrial use. It is also available in diluted or blended formulations on inert carriers for transport.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with product conforming to relevant peroxide handling classifications for storage and logistics. This ensures safety and stability during the supply chain process.

name: Succinic acid
description:
Succinic acid (CAS 110-15-6 ), also known commercially as E363 , is a dicarboxylic acid produced via fermentation or petrochemical synthesis and used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an acidulant, pH buffer, and flavor modifier, with secondary roles in catalysis and preservation. In food and beverage production, E363 acts as an acidulant and masking agent.

It contributes a mild, tart taste profile to dry beverage mixes, seasonings, and baked goods. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent in tablet and capsule production for precise pH control.

This control affects active ingredient stability and bioavailability. In personal care, it supports pH regulation in skin care formulations and acts as a catalyst precursor in certain esterification reactions.

These reactions are used to produce emollients and conditioning agents. It also functions as a mild preservative and fermentation intermediate in specialty chemical synthesis for various industrial uses.

Succinic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both food-grade and technical-grade specifications. Food and pharmaceutical applications are typically served by FCC , USP , and Ph. Eur. compliant grades.

Standard packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities. Bio-based variants are increasingly available to meet sustainability sourcing requirements and environmental standards for modern manufacturing.

name: Maleic acid
description:
Maleic acid (CAS 110-16-7 ), also known commercially as Toxilic acid, is an unsaturated dicarboxylic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as an acidulant, pH buffer, and flavoring agent in finished formulations.

In food and beverage production, maleic acid adjusts tartness and acidity profiles in beverages, confectionery, and fruit-flavored products where a sharp, clean acid note is required. This versatile chemical ensures consistent flavor profiles across various batches.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it to form maleate salts with active ingredients, improving stability and solubility of oral dosage forms. This process is critical for enhancing the bioavailability of certain medications in the healthcare sector.

In personal care, it is incorporated into hair treatment products, particularly bond-repair and straightening systems, where it helps restore and cross-link damaged hair structure. It is a key component in modern professional hair care lines.

It also functions as a pH regulator in topical formulations, ensuring product stability and compatibility with skin-contact applications. Maintaining the correct pH is essential for the shelf life and safety of cosmetic emulsions.

Maleic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) specifications, with technical grade available for industrial applications.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on grade and application requirements. Our logistics team ensures that all shipments meet the necessary safety and quality standards for global distribution.

name: Fumaric acid
description:
Fumaric acid (CAS 110-17-8 ), also designated E297 , is a naturally occurring organic acid used commercially as an acidulant, pH regulator, and preservative across food and personal care manufacturing.

Its low cost relative to citric and tartaric acid, combined with high acidity efficiency at low use levels, makes it a practical choice for formulators managing both performance and input costs.

In food and beverage production, fumaric acid acidulates baked goods, fruit-flavored drinks, and gelatin desserts, delivering a tart, clean flavor profile at lower inclusion rates than competing acids.

It functions as a leavening acid in dry baking mixes, reacting with sodium bicarbonate to control gas release and improve texture consistency. This ensures a reliable result in large-scale production.

Personal care formulators use it to adjust pH in rinse-off products and topical formulations where buffering stability across varying temperatures is a priority. It is highly valued for its stability.

It also acts as a preservative aid in certain food systems, inhibiting microbial growth and extending shelf life in dry and semi-moist applications. This helps maintain product safety over time.

Fumaric acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder in standard granulations suited to both direct blending and dissolution processes. It is easy to handle in most industrial environments.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the predominant commercial form. Technical-grade material is available for non-food industrial applications requiring less purity.

name: N,n,n',n'-tetramethylethylenediamine
description:
N,N,N',N'-Tetramethylethylenediamine (CAS 110-18-9 ), commercially known as TMEDA or TEMED, is a chelating diamine used as a ligand and catalyst activator across organometallic chemistry, polymer production, and life sciences.

It coordinates strongly with metal ions and alkyllithium reagents, enabling controlled reactivity in synthetic and industrial processes. In organolithium chemistry, TMEDA activates n-BuLi and similar reagents by breaking aggregates.

This improves reaction selectivity in pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis. Polymer manufacturers use it as an accelerator in acrylamide gel polymerization, most notably in PAGE gel systems for electrophoresis in biotech and diagnostic workflows.

In coordination chemistry and catalyst preparation, it acts as a bidentate ligand to stabilize metal complexes used in polymerization and fine chemical production. Specialty resin and rubber producers also employ it as a tertiary amine catalyst.

This helps to drive urethane and epoxy cure reactions. TMEDA is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically at 99%+ purity for synthesis-grade applications. Electrophoresis-grade material is available for life science users.

This material is designed to meet the tighter purity requirements of diagnostic end users. Bulk quantities are offered in drums and IBCs for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and pharmaceutical procurement.

name: Isobutyl acetate
description:
Isobutyl acetate (CAS 110-19-0 ), also known by its FEMA 2175 designation, is an ester solvent and flavoring agent used across food, cosmetic, and coating applications.

It delivers a characteristic fruity, pear-like aroma that makes it commercially valuable in both flavor formulation and fragrance blending for various consumer products.

In food and beverage manufacturing, isobutyl acetate is used as a flavoring ingredient to impart pear, apple, and tropical fruit notes in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it as a fast-evaporating solvent in nail lacquers, perfumes, and aerosol products where clean dry-down is required for the user.

It also functions as an industrial solvent for nitrocellulose lacquers, printing inks, and surface coatings, where its moderate evaporation rate supports film formation and flow.

In fragrance compounding, it serves as a carrier and modifier to adjust the volatility profile of finished blends, ensuring consistent performance across different applications.

Isobutyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and FEMA 2175 specifications is available for flavor use.

Technical-grade product is offered for industrial solvent use in coatings and inks, providing a reliable solution for manufacturers requiring high-purity chemical components.

name: Oleoyl sarcosine
description:
Oleoyl sarcosine (CAS 110-25-8 ), also known as Sarkosyl O, is an oleic acid-derived sarcosine condensate used across metalworking and personal care markets. It functions primarily as a corrosion inhibitor, surfactant, and foam modifier in both aqueous and oil-based systems.

In metalworking fluids and rust-preventive oils, it adsorbs onto metal surfaces to form a protective barrier that suppresses corrosion without interfering with lubrication performance. Cutting fluid and grinding fluid formulators incorporate it to control foam.

This chemical maintains emulsion stability under high-shear conditions. In personal care, it acts as a mild surfactant and conditioning agent in shampoos, facial cleansers, and shaving products where low irritation is a formulation priority.

Industrial cleaning and degreasing compounds use it to improve soil removal and wetting on metal substrates. This versatility makes it a staple for manufacturers requiring high-performance surface protection and cleaning efficiency.

Oleoyl sarcosine is supplied as an amber to yellow liquid at ambient temperature. It is available in technical grade for industrial and metalworking applications, as well as in cosmetic-grade specifications for personal care formulations.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with purity typically specified at 95% or higher depending on end-use requirements. Our logistics network ensures timely delivery for large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Methylenebisacrylamide
description:
Methylenebisacrylamide (CAS 110-26-9 ), commonly abbreviated as MBA, is a bifunctional crosslinking monomer used to build three-dimensional polymer networks. It links polymer chains during free-radical polymerization.

This chemical controls gel structure, swelling behavior, and network density in the final material. In polyacrylamide gel production, MBA determines crosslink density, making it a critical input for electrophoresis gels.

These gels are used extensively in laboratory and diagnostic manufacturing. Personal care formulators incorporate it into superabsorbent hydrogel systems and crosslinked thickeners where controlled water retention is required.

Polymer manufacturers use MBA to produce ion-exchange resins and water treatment gels. In these applications, network tightness directly affects ion selectivity and capacity for industrial filtration systems.

It also functions as a crosslinker in contact lens materials and drug delivery matrices. Precise swelling ratios are a specification requirement for these high-performance medical and pharmaceutical applications.

MBA is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Technical and high-purity laboratory grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically at 99% or above for demanding polymerization.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory and specialty formulators to bulk bags for industrial polymer producers. This ensures flexibility for both research and large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Isopropyl myristate
description:
Isopropyl myristate (CAS 110-27-0 ), commonly abbreviated as IPM, is a synthetic ester used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations as an emollient, solvent, and lubricant carrier.

It improves the spreadability and skin absorption of active ingredients without leaving a heavy or greasy residue. This is a key performance factor for formulators selecting between various ester carriers.

In personal care, IPM functions as an emollient and texture modifier in lotions, creams, color cosmetics, and hair care products. It effectively reduces tackiness and enhances the overall skin feel of the product.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a penetration enhancer and carrier in topical drug formulations. This includes transdermal patches and medicated creams to improve active delivery through the skin barrier.

In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it acts as a non-greasy base carrier and surface wetting agent. It is particularly useful in cutting oils and release agents where clean application is required.

It also serves as a solvent and dispersant for pigments, fragrances, and UV filters in formulated end products. Isopropyl myristate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk and drum quantities.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications. These standards support regulated drug product manufacturing and ensure high purity for sensitive applications.

Cosmetic and technical grades are also commercially available for personal care and industrial applications. These grades provide versatile solutions for manufacturers requiring reliable chemical performance.

name: Ethylene distearamide
description:
Ethylene distearamide ( CAS 110-30-5 ), commonly known as EBS, is a synthetic wax derived from stearic acid and ethylenediamine. It functions as a lubricant, slip agent, and dispersing aid across a broad range of industrial manufacturing processes.

In plastics processing, EBS acts as an internal and external lubricant that reduces melt viscosity, prevents die buildup, and improves surface finish in extruded and injection-molded parts.

Pigment and filler manufacturers use it as a coating agent to improve powder flowability and dispersion in masterbatches and compounded systems. This ensures a more uniform distribution of additives.

In textile and leather finishing, EBS provides durable slip and anti-blocking properties to coated fabrics and treated surfaces. This prevents sticking and enhances the tactile quality of the material.

Printing ink and packaging formulators incorporate it as a wax additive to control rub resistance and gloss on finished substrates. It is essential for maintaining the integrity of printed designs.

EBS is supplied as a white powder or fine granules, with particle size selections available to suit different blending and dosing requirements. This versatility allows for seamless integration into production.

Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% upward. These high standards ensure consistent performance in demanding applications.

Some grades are produced to food-contact compliance standards, making them suitable for use in packaging materials subject to regulatory requirements. This ensures safety and reliability for global manufacturers.

name: Ethylene dioleamide
description:
Ethylene dioleamide (CAS 110-31-6 ) is a bis-amide derived from oleic acid and ethylenediamine, used commercially as an internal lubricant, slip agent, and surface modifier across polymer and rubber processing.

It reduces interparticle and surface friction during compounding and forming operations without migrating aggressively to the surface. In plastics processing, it functions as an internal lubricant and slip additive.

In polyolefin and PVC compounds, it improves mold release and reduces die buildup during extrusion. Rubber and tire manufacturers incorporate it to aid mixing dispersion and reduce compound sticking to processing equipment.

In metalworking lubricant formulations, it contributes boundary lubrication performance in drawing and stamping compounds where metal-on-metal contact must be controlled. It also acts as a plasticizer and softener.

In specialty polymer blends, flexibility and surface feel are key processing targets. Ethylene dioleamide is supplied as a waxy solid or flake, with melting point characteristics that suit both melt-blending and solvent-based incorporation.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial rubber and plastics applications. Purity specifications and particle size can vary by supplier, and buyers should confirm suitability against their compounding process requirements.

name: Isobutyl palmitate
description:
Isobutyl palmitate (CAS 110-34-9 ) is a synthetic ester of palmitic acid used as an emollient, solvent, and carrier in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations. It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel that makes it a preferred alternative to heavier oils and waxes.

In cosmetic formulations, it functions as an emollient and spreading agent in creams, lotions, and body oils, improving texture and skin absorption without residue. Sunscreen and color cosmetic manufacturers use it as a solvent and dispersant for UV filters and pigments.

This chemical enhances uniform distribution across the skin for various topical applications. In lip care and hair care products, it acts as a softener and plasticizer, contributing to flexibility and gloss in sticks, balms, and conditioning treatments.

Pharmaceutical topical formulations incorporate it as a carrier for active ingredients, supporting consistent delivery across semi-solid dosage forms such as ointments and creams. It is highly valued for its stability and compatibility with diverse ingredients.

Isobutyl palmitate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical supply typically conforming to relevant pharmacopoeial standards such as USP or Ph.Eur. .

The material may also meet other international quality benchmarks including BP , EP , or FCC depending on the specific batch requirements. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with packaging options ranging from drums to containers.

name: Ethyl decanoate
description:
Ethyl decanoate ( CAS 110-38-3 ), also known by its FEMA 2432 designation and commercially as ethyl caprate, is a fatty acid ester used across food flavoring, personal care, and industrial lubrication applications.

It delivers a characteristic fruity, brandy-like aroma profile that drives its demand in flavor and fragrance formulation. In food and beverage production, ethyl caprate is used as a flavoring agent in spirits and wines.

It contributes grape and cognac notes at low use levels in fruit-based products. Personal care formulators incorporate it as an emollient ester and emulsifier in skin creams, hair conditioners, and cosmetic oils.

Its skin-feel and dispersing properties support finished product texture in various formulations. In lubricant formulations, it functions as a base fluid or additive component in specialty and biodegradable lubricants.

Ester-based fluids are often preferred for these specific industrial needs. Metalworking applications also draw on its lubricity and compatibility with other ester blends for cutting and processing fluids.

Ethyl decanoate is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial and commercial buyers. Food-grade material conforming to FEMA standards is the most commonly traded specification.

Technical-grade product is available for lubricant and industrial end uses. This versatile chemical serves a wide range of sectors from high-end cosmetics to heavy-duty industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Diethyl sebacate
description:
Diethyl sebacate ( CAS 110-40-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DES, is an ester of sebacic acid used across lubrication, plastics, flavoring, and cosmetic formulations. FEMA 2376 recognition positions it as a regulated flavoring ingredient in food applications.

Its low volatility and compatibility with a broad range of substrates make it a functional choice across both industrial and consumer-grade products. In lubricant and metalworking fluids, DES functions as a synthetic base fluid or co-fluid.

This material offers thermal stability in high-performance formulations. Polymer and plastics manufacturers use it as a plasticizer to improve flexibility and processing characteristics in resins and coatings for various industrial uses.

In flavor systems, it contributes fruity, fatty notes to food and beverage products under its established regulatory approval. Personal care formulators incorporate DES as an emollient and moisturizing agent in skin creams.

It is also frequently utilized in hair conditioners and cosmetic serums to enhance texture. Diethyl sebacate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk quantities for large-scale manufacturing.

It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the distinct purity requirements of flavor, cosmetic, and industrial applications. Cosmetic and food-grade material is typically evaluated against FCC standards.

name: 2-heptanone
description:
2-Heptanone (CAS 110-43-0 ), also known as methyl amyl ketone or MAK, is a medium-chain ketone solvent used across industrial, cosmetic, and food applications. It delivers strong solvency for resins and coatings while contributing a fruity, banana-like character valued in flavor and fragrance work.

In coatings and industrial cleaning, this compound dissolves nitrocellulose, acrylics, and vinyl resins, offering a slower evaporation rate that improves flow and leveling in spray-applied finishes. Metalworking and lubricant formulators use it as a carrier solvent to aid in the deposition of active compounds onto metal surfaces.

In personal care, it functions as a solvent and fragrance ingredient in nail care products, hair preparations, and skin formulations. Food manufacturers use it as a flavoring agent under FEMA 2544 to impart fruity, cheese-like, or banana notes in baked goods, dairy products, and beverages.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drums and IBC totes for bulk industrial procurement. It is available in technical grade for solvent and metalworking applications and in food/flavor grade meeting FEMA and FCC specifications for use in consumable products.

name: Sorbic acid
description:
Sorbic acid (CAS 110-44-1 ), also designated E200 , is a naturally derived organic acid used commercially as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial preservative. It inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and fungi across food, cosmetic, and personal care formulations.

This versatile ingredient extends shelf life without significantly altering product taste or odor. In food manufacturing, it is applied to baked goods, dairy products, wines, and processed meats to control spoilage organisms and meet regulatory requirements.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and leave-on products as a preservative active. This is particularly useful where pH-sensitive systems limit the use of parabens or formaldehyde releasers.

At low concentrations, it contributes mild acidulant functionality in beverage and flavor systems. In these applications, it is also recognized under FEMA 3921 as an approved flavoring agent for various industrial uses.

In personal care, it is frequently paired with potassium sorbate to balance solubility and efficacy across water-based formulations. This combination ensures stability and safety in a wide range of consumer-facing products.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and BP specifications, with food-grade being the most commonly sourced for applications.

Typical purity is 99% or higher for regulated end uses. Our supply chain ensures that all batches meet the rigorous quality standards required for global distribution in the food, beverage, and cosmetic industries.

name: Pyridine-borane
description:
Pyridine-borane (CAS 110-51-0 ) is a stabilized borane complex that delivers controlled hydride-reducing activity under mild conditions. It functions as a selective reducing agent in synthetic chemistry.

This reagent offers greater handling safety and solution stability than free borane reagents. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it reduces imines and iminium ions in reductive amination reactions.

This is a critical step in producing active pharmaceutical ingredients and chiral intermediates. Electronics manufacturers use it in electroless plating baths and surface treatment processes.

It is utilized where controlled boron deposition is required. Biotechnology researchers rely on it for reductive amination of biomolecules including proteins, peptides, and oligosaccharides.

Selectivity and aqueous compatibility are priorities in these applications. It also serves synthetic chemistry workflows requiring mild reduction of aldehydes and ketones without over-reduction.

This prevents the degradation of sensitive functional groups during the process. The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically in concentrations around 8 M in solution.

It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for process-scale use. Technical and high-purity grades are offered to meet synthetic and manufacturing requirements.

Purity specifications are commonly at 97% or above. This ensures the material meets the rigorous standards necessary for pharmaceutical and industrial chemical production cycles.

name: Hexane
description:
Hexane (CAS 110-54-3 ), commercially recognized as n-hexane, is a straight-chain aliphatic hydrocarbon solvent used across extraction, formulation, and industrial cleaning processes.

Its fast evaporation rate and low residue profile make it a preferred solvent where clean separation and high-purity output are critical procurement requirements for industrial buyers.

In edible oil production, n-hexane extracts oil from soybeans, sunflower seeds, and other oilseeds at commercial scale, delivering high yields with minimal co-extraction of non-target compounds.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to purify active ingredients and recrystallize intermediates where solvent selectivity directly affects the final product quality and consistency.

In adhesive and rubber cement formulations for footwear, packaging, and automotive assembly, hexane controls viscosity and drying speed to ensure optimal bonding performance during manufacturing.

Electronics and precision parts manufacturers rely on it for degreasing metal surfaces and cleaning components prior to coating or bonding to ensure a residue-free finish on parts.

Hexane is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade hexane and high-purity grades meeting USP specifications.

Purity levels typically range from 85% mixed hexane isomers in technical grades to 95%+ n-hexane content in higher-specification grades suitable for sensitive extraction applications.

name: Pentylamine
description:
Pentylamine (CAS 110-58-7 ), also known as amylamine and recognized under FEMA 4242 , is a primary aliphatic amine used across chemical synthesis and industrial processing.

It functions as a reactive building block, pH modifier, and corrosion inhibitor depending on the application context. In agrochemical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of herbicides and fungicides.

Pharmaceutical producers use it as a building block for API synthesis, where its primary amine group enables condensation and alkylation reactions with drug precursors. This versatility makes it essential for modern medicine.

In metalworking and industrial water treatment, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor, forming protective films on metal surfaces in fluid formulations. This helps maintain the integrity of industrial equipment over time.

Polymer chemists incorporate it as a chain initiator or modifier in polymerization processes, influencing molecular weight and end-group functionality in specialty resins. It is a critical component for material science.

Pentylamine is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to ISO tank containers for bulk orders. Technical and reagent grades are the most common commercial specifications available.

Buyers sourcing for pharmaceutical intermediates should confirm purity levels and documentation requirements with their supplier prior to procurement. Proper handling and storage are required to maintain product stability.

name: 1,4-butanediol
description:
1,4-Butanediol (CAS 110-63-4 ), commonly abbreviated as BDO, is a four-carbon diol used as a chemical intermediate and solvent across polymer, pharmaceutical, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It is a primary building block for engineering plastics, elastic fibers, and polyurethane systems, connecting raw material supply chains to high-volume industrial production.

BDO is a key monomer in the production of polybutylene terephthalate (PBT) and polyurethane, where it functions as a chain extender and diol component in both rigid and flexible formulations.

In the manufacture of spandex and elastic fibers, it reacts with diisocyanates to control segment structure and mechanical performance. This ensures high durability and elasticity in the final product.

As a solvent and carrier in pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing, BDO supports active ingredient delivery in topical and liquid formulations. It also serves as a precursor to gamma-butyrolactone and tetrahydrofuran.

Both of these downstream industrial solvents are produced at scale for various chemical processes. BDO is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk quantities including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats.

Technical and industrial grades are the most common commercial forms, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical applications. These meet rigorous industry requirements.

Specifications typically align with customer-defined purity thresholds, with ≥99% purity standard for most industrial procurement. This ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing environments.

name: 1,2-dimethoxyethane
description:
1,2-Dimethoxyethane (CAS 110-71-4 ), commercially known as monoglyme or DME, is an ether-based solvent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer chemistry, and electrochemical applications.

Its ability to coordinate with metal ions and dissolve a broad range of reactive intermediates makes it a preferred solvent in demanding synthesis environments. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DME supports Grignard reactions.

It is also used in organolithium chemistry and other moisture-sensitive syntheses where a stable, non-protic solvent is required. Battery and energy storage manufacturers use it as a co-solvent or primary electrolyte solvent.

DME is utilized in lithium-ion and lithium-metal cell formulations. Polymer chemists rely on DME in controlled polymerization processes, including anionic and ring-opening polymerizations, where solvent coordination affects results.

It also functions as a reaction medium in palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions, where its chelating behavior stabilizes catalyst systems and improves yields. This makes it essential for high-performance chemistry.

1,2-Dimethoxyethane is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to IBC containers and bulk quantities. Technical grade and anhydrous grades are the most commonly sourced specifications.

Anhydrous DME is used where strict moisture control is critical to reaction outcomes. High-purity grades suitable for battery electrolyte applications are available from select suppliers to meet industry requirements.

Its ability to dissolve both polar and non-polar resins makes it a practical choice where single-solvent systems need broad resin compatibility for industrial applications.

In industrial coatings and lacquers, EGEE functions as a coalescing and flow-control solvent, improving film formation and leveling in alkyd, epoxy, and nitrocellulose systems.

Printing ink formulators use it to control drying speed and maintain viscosity stability across gravure and flexographic processes to ensure consistent print quality.

In adhesive and sealant production, it supports resin dissolution and open-time extension in solvent-borne systems. Plastics processing operations also employ EGEE as a carrier solvent.

It is used for surface treatments and polymer coatings where controlled evaporation is critical to finish quality. 2-Ethoxyethanol is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial packaging.

Options include drums and IBCs, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume procurement. It is available primarily in technical grade for most industrial coating and ink applications.

name: Cyclohexane
description:
Cyclohexane (CAS 110-82-7 ) is a cyclic hydrocarbon solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, industrial cleaning, and chemical synthesis. It delivers strong non-polar solvency with low water miscibility.

This makes it a preferred extraction and reaction medium where aromatic solvents are restricted. In pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturing, it serves as a recrystallization solvent and reaction medium.

It is used for active ingredient synthesis, particularly where residual solvent profiles must meet strict regulatory limits. Industrial cleaning formulations use it to degrease precision components and remove contaminants.

It effectively removes hydrocarbon-based contaminants from metal surfaces. In the flavor and fragrance industry, it functions as an extraction solvent for natural raw materials, helping isolate aromatic compounds.

Chemical producers also use it as a feedstock and process solvent in nylon intermediate production. It is specifically utilized in the oxidation pathway to adipic acid and caprolactam for industrial use.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is standard for industrial and cleaning applications, while high-purity material is available for specialized use.

HPLC-grade material is available for pharmaceutical and analytical use. Reagent-grade specifications are also offered for laboratory and synthesis applications to meet various industrial requirements.

name: Piperazine

Piperazine (CAS 110-85-0 ), also known commercially as Vermizine, is a cyclic diamine used as a reactive building block and process chemical across pharmaceutical manufacturing and polymer production.

Its bifunctional amine structure makes it a reliable intermediate for synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty materials. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key structural unit.

This chemical is used in the synthesis of numerous drug compounds, including antipsychotics, antihistamines, and antiparasitic agents. Polymer chemists use it as a curing agent and cross-linker in epoxy resin systems.

Controlled amine reactivity determines final mechanical performance in these systems. It also functions as a monomer in the production of polyamide membranes used in water treatment and industrial filtration.

In agrochemical synthesis, piperazine derivatives are incorporated into fungicide and pesticide formulations as core intermediates. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing processes.

The product is supplied as white crystalline flakes or anhydrous powder, with piperazine hexahydrate available as an alternative hydrated form. Standard commercial grades include pharmaceutical-grade material.

The material meets USP and BP specifications, as well as technical-grade product for industrial polymer and chemical synthesis applications. Bulk quantities are typically offered in multi-kilogram bags.

These drums are suited to industrial procurement volumes and large-scale manufacturing needs. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure consistent quality and performance in all applications.

name: Pyridine
description:
Pyridine ( CAS 110-86-1 ), also known by the abbreviation Py, is a foundational heterocyclic base used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

With FEMA 2966 status, it also holds a recognized role as a flavoring agent in food applications. In industrial settings, it functions primarily as a solvent, catalyst, and chemical intermediate.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, pyridine serves as a reaction solvent and base catalyst in the synthesis of antihistamines, sulfonamides, and vitamins, where its ability to neutralize acids drives reaction efficiency.

Agrochemical producers rely on it as a key intermediate in herbicide and insecticide synthesis, particularly for pyridine-derived active ingredients. It is essential for large-scale crop protection manufacturing.

In food and flavor formulation, it contributes characteristic roasted and meaty notes to flavor systems at controlled concentrations under FEMA guidelines. This makes it a versatile tool for flavor chemists.

Home care and industrial cleaning product formulators use pyridine-based derivatives as biocidal actives in disinfectant and preservation systems. These applications ensure high standards of hygiene and safety.

Pyridine is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade meeting USP and BP specifications.

Buyers sourcing for regulated applications should confirm grade compliance with supplier documentation prior to procurement. Proper handling and storage are required to maintain the integrity of the chemical product.

name: Piperidine
description:
Piperidine (CAS 110-89-4 ), also abbreviated as PIP, is a saturated six-membered nitrogen heterocycle used as a chemical building block and catalyst across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and polymer manufacturing.

Its secondary amine functionality makes it a reactive intermediate for constructing complex molecules and initiating polymerization processes. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a core structural unit in the production of active ingredients.

This includes analgesics, antihistamines, and CNS drugs, many of which contain the piperidine ring in their final structure. Agrochemical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of fungicides and insecticides.

In these applications, the nitrogen ring contributes significantly to biological activity. In rubber and polymer production, PIP functions as a vulcanization accelerator and polymerization initiator, influencing cure rates.

It also acts as a base catalyst in condensation reactions and resin systems, including applications involving solid-phase synthesis supports. Piperidine is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in standard commercial packaging.

Technical and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with pharmaceutical-grade product typically meeting USP or Ph. Eur. specifications. Buyers should confirm purity levels and residual solvent compliance.

Compliance should be based on the intended end-use application. Standard commercial packaging options range from drums to ISO tank containers to ensure safe transport and storage for industrial users.

name: Morpholine
description:
Morpholine (CAS 110-91-8 ) is a cyclic amine and ether used across industrial chemistry as a corrosion inhibitor, chemical intermediate, and curing agent. Its dual amine-ether functionality makes it a building block for a broad range of downstream synthesis applications.

In steam boiler and water treatment systems, morpholine is dosed to neutralize carbonic acid and suppress corrosion in condensate return lines. It serves as a well-established alternative to volatile amines in these environments.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic intermediate in the production of active ingredients, where its secondary amine group enables targeted derivatization. This versatility is critical for complex chemical synthesis.

In rubber and polymer processing, morpholine-based accelerators and crosslinkers improve cure rates and mechanical performance in finished elastomer products. These additives are essential for high-performance industrial rubber goods.

Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate morpholine as a pH buffer and biocide component to extend fluid service life. This helps control microbial growth in demanding cutting and grinding operations across the manufacturing sector.

Morpholine is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial form, with high-purity grades available for specialized pharmaceutical synthesis applications.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and water content when sourcing for API intermediate use. Ensuring the material meets specific industrial requirements is vital for maintaining process stability and final product quality.

name: Glutaric acid
description:
Glutaric acid (CAS 110-94-1 ), also known commercially as glutarate, is a five-carbon dicarboxylic acid used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food applications as a pH buffer, acidulant, and reactive intermediate.

Its bifunctional acid structure makes it a practical building block for synthesis and a reliable acidifying agent in formulated products. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a co-former in active pharmaceutical ingredient salt development.

This material is essential for cocrystal development, improving solubility and stability profiles of drug candidates. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a mild acidulant and buffering agent in skin care products.

Controlled pH levels directly affect preservative efficacy and product shelf life in cosmetic formulations. In food and flavoring applications, it contributes a clean, mild acidic note and supports preservation in processed food systems.

It also serves as a precursor in the synthesis of polyesters, plasticizers, and specialty polymers used across industrial coating and resin formulations. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with the latter typically conforming to USP or BP specifications. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial synthesis and polymer applications.

name: Diisopropanolamine
description:
Diisopropanolamine ( CAS 110-97-4 ), commonly abbreviated as DIPA, is a secondary alkanolamine used across industrial and personal care formulations. It functions primarily as a pH regulator, neutralizing agent, and curing component, depending on the application.

Procurement teams source it as a cost-effective alternative to triethanolamine where lower viscosity or different reactivity profiles are required. In coatings and industrial fluids, DIPA neutralizes acidic resins and dispersants to stabilize emulsions.

It is used to control pH in waterborne systems effectively. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a crosslinking agent and curing accelerator, particularly in polyurethane and epoxy-based systems to ensure structural integrity.

Water treatment applications rely on DIPA to scavenge acidic gases such as CO₂ and H₂S in gas purification processes. This makes it a vital component for environmental management and industrial gas scrubbing operations.

In personal care, it neutralizes carbomers and anionic polymers in creams, lotions, and hair care products. It adjusts pH without the odor concerns associated with some competing amines, improving the final user experience.

DIPA is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperatures and as a solid or flake form in cooler conditions, given its relatively high melting point. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial coatings and gas treatment.

Cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity specifications is available for personal care formulations. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for manufacturers requiring high-performance chemical intermediates for global distribution.

This chemical enables the uniform dispersion of active ingredients and additives across a broad range of formulations. In personal care, it acts as a solvent and humectant in lotions, fragrances, and skin-conditioning products.

The material improves spreadability and moisture retention in various cosmetic applications. Coatings and adhesives formulators use it as a reactive diluent and plasticizing co-solvent to control viscosity and enhance film flexibility.

In polyurethane production, it serves as a chain extender and polyol building block, influencing the mechanical properties of foams, elastomers, and sealants. It also functions as a stabilizer and carrier in UV-absorber systems.

The product is utilized in preservative blends where solubility of actives is a formulation constraint. It is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities for industrial use.

name: Vitamin F
description:
Vitamin F (CAS 11006-87-4 ), commonly referred to as essential fatty acids (EFAs), is a collective term for the polyunsaturated fatty acids linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid. These are compounds that the body cannot synthesize and must obtain externally.

In commercial supply, it functions as a bioactive nutritional ingredient and skin-conditioning agent across food, pharmaceutical, feed, and cosmetic manufacturing. It is a critical component for maintaining cellular health and metabolic functions.

In functional food and dietary supplement production, it is incorporated into fortified oils, capsules, and nutritional blends to deliver omega fatty acid content. These applications rely on the ingredient's high bioavailability and stability in various formulations.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it in facial creams, serums, and hair care products to support skin barrier function. It is particularly effective at improving product performance on dry or damaged skin and enhancing topical absorption.

In animal feed, it is added to compound feeds and premixes to support growth performance and coat condition in livestock and companion animals. This ensures that animals receive the necessary nutrients for optimal health and development.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use EFA concentrates as active ingredients in softgel formulations targeting nutritional deficiency. These products are often manufactured to meet rigorous international quality standards for safety and efficacy.

Vitamin F is supplied as liquid oil blends, softgel fills, or microencapsulated powder depending on the target application. Food-grade and feed-grade specifications are the most commonly available for industrial and commercial use.

Some suppliers offer USP or Ph.Eur. -compliant EFA concentrates for pharmaceutical use. These high-purity grades ensure compliance with global regulatory requirements for specialized medical and therapeutic applications.

name: Meadowlactone
description:
Meadowlactone (CAS 110071-67-5 ), also known as Meadowfoam delta lactone and S-HETEL, is a naturally derived lactone obtained from meadowfoam seed oil. It delivers a distinctive creamy, coconut-like aroma profile that positions it as a premium ingredient in fragrance and flavor development.

In fine fragrance and personal care formulations, it contributes warm, milky-coconut nuances to perfumes, body lotions, and hair care products where a natural-origin claim adds commercial value.

Flavor houses use it to build creamy, tropical, and dairy-adjacent profiles in confectionery, baked goods, and beverage applications. Its lactone character makes it effective at low use levels, supporting cost-efficient formulation.

This ingredient is highly effective in both leave-on and rinse-off cosmetic systems. Formulators in natural and clean-label product lines source it specifically as a plant-derived alternative to synthetic coconut and lactonic aroma chemicals.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity grades suited to both fragrance and flavor end uses. Food-grade material is available for flavor applications, with supply conforming to FEMA -recognized usage standards.

Quantities range from small fragrance-house samples through to bulk commercial volumes depending on supplier. This versatile material ensures consistent performance across a wide variety of industrial and consumer applications.

name: Phycocyanin
description:
Phycocyanin (CAS 11016-15-2 ), commonly specified as C-Phycocyanin in commercial and research procurement, is a blue pigment protein extracted from Spirulina and other cyanobacteria.

It delivers an intense, natural blue color across food, cosmetic, and biotech applications where synthetic dyes are being replaced or restricted for industrial use.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to produce blue and blue-green hues in confectionery, dairy products, beverages, and plant-based formulations without synthetic colorants.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into color cosmetics, particularly eyeshadows, lip products, and skincare lines, to meet demand for naturally derived pigments.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical development, it functions as an antioxidant active in supplement capsules, functional food matrices, and research-grade formulations.

Biotechnology and life sciences buyers source it as a fluorescent label and detection reagent in flow cytometry and immunoassay applications for precise laboratory results.

The material is supplied as a fine powder or water-soluble spray-dried powder, with liquid extract forms also available for direct incorporation into aqueous systems.

Grades are differentiated by purity ratio, with food-grade, reagent-grade, and high-purity analytical specifications available to suit different industrial end-use requirements.

name: Anthocyanins
description:
Anthocyanins (CAS 11029-12-2 ), also sourced and traded as grape anthocyanins, are water-soluble plant pigments extracted primarily from grape skins, berries, and other dark-colored botanical sources.

They function as natural colorants and antioxidant actives across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical manufacturing. In food and beverage production, they deliver stable red-to-purple hues in confectionery and dairy products.

These pigments are used in soft drinks and functional foods without synthetic dyes. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement formulators incorporate them as antioxidant actives in capsules, tablets, and standardized botanical extracts.

Cosmetic manufacturers use grape anthocyanins in serums, creams, and color cosmetics where both pigmentation and antioxidant stabilization of the finished formula are required for high-quality results.

In printing and packaging, they serve as bio-based colorant inputs for pH-sensitive or natural-origin ink systems. Anthocyanins are supplied as spray-dried powders, liquid extracts, and concentrated solutions.

Powder is the most common commercial form for industrial handling. Standardized grades are available specifying anthocyanin content by percentage, typically characterized against cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents.

Food-grade and USP -referenced specifications are the most commonly requested, with organic-certified material available from select sources to meet specific industrial manufacturing requirements.

Contact us for supply of Anthocyanins

name: Vitamin K2
description:
Vitamin K2 (CAS 11032-49-8 ), also known as menaquinone, is a fat-soluble vitamin used across food fortification, dietary supplement manufacturing, and pharmaceutical formulation.

The MK-4 subtype (menatetrenone) is the most commercially prominent short-chain form, while longer-chain variants such as MK-7 are increasingly specified in premium supplement applications.

In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is formulated into softgels, tablets, and capsules targeting bone and cardiovascular health product lines for global distribution.

Food and beverage producers incorporate it into fortified dairy alternatives, functional drinks, and enriched infant formula to meet specific nutritional labeling requirements.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use menatetrenone as an active ingredient in prescription and OTC products, particularly in markets where it holds official drug status.

In animal nutrition, it is included in poultry and livestock feed premixes to support coagulation function and bone development across various agricultural sectors.

The material is supplied as a fine powder, oil suspension, or microencapsulated form to support dispersion in both oil-based and water-based manufacturing systems.

Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with USP and Ph.Eur. specifications available for highly regulated industrial applications.

Contact us for supply of Vitamin K2

name: Poloxamine
description:
Poloxamine (CAS 110617-70-4 ) is a tetrafunctional block copolymer surfactant built on an ethylenediamine core with polyethylene oxide–polypropylene oxide arms. Individual grades such as Tetronic 304 and Poloxamine 1107 differ in molecular weight and hydrophilic–lipophilic balance.

Grade selection is a critical procurement decision for this material. It functions as a non-ionic surfactant for emulsification, wetting, and surface modification across multiple industrial sectors and specialized manufacturing processes.

In pharmaceutical formulations, specific grades are used to stabilize drug suspensions and improve wetting of poorly soluble actives. It is also utilized to modify surface properties of nanoparticles or advanced drug delivery systems.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skin creams, cleansers, and conditioning products. These applications rely on the material for controlled emulsification and consistent moisturizing performance in high-end cosmetic formulations.

In industrial and household cleaning formulations, it delivers low-foam wetting and soil dispersion across a range of pH conditions. Agricultural formulations use it as a dispersant and wetting agent in pesticide and herbicide concentrates.

These agricultural applications help to improve spray coverage and active ingredient uptake on various crops. Poloxamine is supplied as a liquid or solid depending on the specific grade, with higher molecular weight variants available as waxy solids.

Grades are differentiated by their polyoxypropylene–polyoxyethylene ratio, and buyers should specify the target grade by name. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. standards for select grades.

Technical-grade supply remains the standard for most industrial applications. The material is valued for its versatility and stability in complex chemical environments, making it a staple for global chemical procurement teams.

name: Sodium tetrapropylenebenzenesulfonate
description:
Sodium tetrapropylenebenzenesulfonate (CAS 11067-82-6 ), also known as TPBS, is an anionic surfactant derived from branched alkylbenzene feedstocks. It functions as a detergent and emulsifier across industrial cleaning and formulation applications.

Its resistance to hard water conditions supports consistent performance in various environments. In household and industrial detergent formulations, TPBS delivers effective grease and soil removal across a range of wash temperatures.

Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform penetration of treatment baths and dye liquors. This ensures high-quality finishes and consistent results during the manufacturing process.

In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber dispersion and process cleanliness during pulping and coating operations. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it as an emulsifier to stabilize aqueous systems and improve substrate wetting.

Sodium tetrapropylenebenzenesulfonate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with active matter content commonly ranging from 40% to 90%. This versatility allows for precise dosing in complex chemical formulations.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications varying by active content and electrolyte level to suit different requirements. It meets rigorous industrial benchmarks for stability and performance.

Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or drums is the norm for industrial procurement volumes. This ensures efficient logistics and handling for large-scale manufacturing facilities and chemical distribution networks.

name: Apocarotenal

Apocarotenal (CAS 1107-26-2 ), also known as β-apo-8′-carotenal and listed as E160e in the EU, is a carotenoid-derived colorant used to deliver orange-to-red hues in food, supplement, and cosmetic formulations.

It functions as both a pigment and an antioxidant stabilizer, offering formulators a natural-origin coloring option with dual functional value. In food manufacturing, E160e is used to color beverages and dairy products.

It is also applied to margarine and processed foods where a warm orange tone is required within regulatory limits. Supplement and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into softgels and tablets for color standardization.

The compound serves as a provitamin A source in these applications. In cosmetics, it is used to achieve natural-looking orange and peach tones in skin care and color cosmetics without synthetic azo dyes.

Pharmaceutical coating applications also use it to tint tablet films and capsule shells to a consistent, recognizable color. Apocarotenal is supplied as a crystalline powder and in oil suspension or emulsified liquid forms.

These formats are suited to both fat-soluble and water-dispersible formulations. Standard grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications, with concentrations typically standardized at 10% in oil or emulsion formats.

Bulk supply is available for industrial use, with smaller quantities offered for formulation development. This ensures versatility across various manufacturing scales and specific technical requirements for global distribution.

name: Tetrahydromethyl-1,3-isobenzofurandione
description:
Methyltetrahydrophthalic anhydride ( CAS 11070-44-3 ), commercially known as MTHPA, is a reactive cyclic anhydride used primarily as a curing agent and hardener for epoxy resin systems.

It delivers controlled crosslink density in thermoset formulations, making it a preferred choice where long pot life and low viscosity processing are required for industrial manufacturing.

MTHPA is extensively used in epoxy casting and encapsulation compounds for electrical and electronic components, where its liquid form enables void-free impregnation of transformers and coils.

In industrial coatings, it functions as a crosslinker to build chemical and corrosion resistance in high-performance protective finishes applied to metal substrates and heavy machinery.

Structural adhesives and composite laminates rely on MTHPA to achieve high glass transition temperatures and mechanical durability in demanding service environments and aerospace applications.

It also serves as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of polyester resins and specialty lubricant additives where controlled acid functionality is required for chemical stability.

MTHPA is supplied as a low-viscosity liquid at ambient temperature, typically available in drum and IBC quantities for industrial procurement and large-scale chemical distribution.

Standard commercial grades are offered at purities of 96% and above, with technical and electronic grades available to meet specific application requirements and manufacturing standards.

name: Cassia gum
description:
Cassia gum (CAS 11078-30-1 ), also approved as E427 , is a natural polysaccharide derived from the endosperm of Senna obtusifolia seeds. It functions as a high-performance thickener and gelling agent.

This versatile additive delivers viscosity control and texture modification across food and industrial formulations. In food manufacturing, it is used to stabilize dairy analogues, pet food, and processed meat products.

It is particularly effective where firm gel texture and water-binding are required. Textile and paper processors apply it as a sizing and coating agent to improve surface strength and reduce fiber breakage.

In construction, this gum thickens tile adhesives, joint compounds, and cement-based mortars. It is essential for controlling workability and open time during the application of various building materials.

Home care formulators incorporate it into liquid detergents and cleaning gels as a rheology modifier. This maintains suspension stability under varying temperature conditions and improves product shelf life.

The product is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder. It is available in food-grade specification meeting EU regulatory requirements, as well as technical grade for diverse industrial applications.

Particle size and viscosity grades are offered to suit specific processing equipment and end-use viscosity targets. This ensures optimal performance across a wide range of manufacturing environments.

name: Glucomannan
description:
Glucomannan (CAS 11078-31-2 ), also known as D-Gluco-D-mannan, is a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide extracted primarily from konjac root. It functions as a gelling agent, thickener, and water-binding ingredient across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food production, this ingredient is used to build texture in low-calorie noodles, jellies, and meat analogues. High gel strength at low concentrations reduces the need for other hydrocolloids in complex formulations.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a binder and controlled-release matrix in solid dosage forms. It leverages viscosity-building behavior to regulate active ingredient release profiles effectively during the manufacturing process.

Personal care manufacturers use it to thicken and stabilize emulsions, creams, and serums. Its film-forming capacity also supports moisture retention in skin-contact products, providing a smooth and consistent application for consumers.

It is also applied as a dietary fiber ingredient in functional food and nutraceutical formats. These include capsules, powders, and meal-replacement products targeting satiety and digestive health claims in the wellness sector.

The material is supplied as a fine off-white to cream powder, with particle size and viscosity grades available to suit different processing requirements. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are standard in the global market.

Some suppliers offer material compliant with USP or Ph.Eur. monographs to ensure high quality. Bulk quantities are typically available in 25 kg bags for industrial use and large-scale production lines.

High-purity konjac flour grades are distinguished by their specific glucomannan content percentage. This allows manufacturers to select the precise grade needed for their specific thickening or gelling applications.
