name: Decaglyceryl decaoleate
description:
Decaglyceryl decaoleate (CAS 11094-60-3 ), also sold as Polyglyceryl-10 decaoleate, is a polyglycerol ester of oleic acid used primarily as a non-ionic emulsifier and moisturizing agent.

It bridges oil and water phases in formulations where stability and skin compatibility are both procurement priorities. In cosmetics, it functions as an emulsifier and skin-conditioning agent in creams and lotions.

This ingredient enables stable oil-in-water or water-in-oil systems without synthetic ethoxylated alternatives. Food manufacturers use it to improve fat dispersion and texture in various processed foods.

It is particularly effective where clean-label or natural emulsifier positioning is required. In coating and adhesive formulations, it acts as a wetting and dispersing agent for industrial use.

The material improves substrate adhesion and surface uniformity across different applications. Its humectant character also supports moisture-retention performance in leave-on personal care products.

Common applications include body butters and hair treatments where hydration is essential. Decaglyceryl decaoleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste at ambient temperature.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially available. Some suppliers offer material compliant with FCC or relevant EU food additive standards for global distribution.

Packaging is commonly available in drums and IBCs for industrial volumes. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing facilities.

name: Hydrotalcite
description:
Hydrotalcite (CAS 11097-59-9 ), also known as magnesium aluminum hydroxycarbonate, is a synthetic layered double hydroxide mineral used across industrial and pharmaceutical applications.

Its layered structure gives it strong anion-exchange and buffering capacity, making it effective as an acid scavenger, stabilizer, and sequestrant in demanding processing environments.

In PVC and polyolefin compounding, it functions as an acid scavenger and thermal stabilizer, neutralizing chloride byproducts that would otherwise degrade the polymer or corrode equipment.

Rubber formulators incorporate it to improve heat stability and extend service life in high-temperature vulcanization processes. In water treatment, it sequesters heavy metal ions and phosphates.

This process supports effluent compliance in industrial discharge applications through anion exchange. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an antacid active ingredient in solid oral dosage forms.

Its controlled buffering profile is a key formulation parameter for these medical applications. The material is supplied as a fine white powder in both synthetic and naturally derived forms.

Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications, as well as technical-grade material for polymer and industrial applications.

Particle size distribution and surface treatment variants are available to meet specific compounding or dispersion requirements for various manufacturing and chemical processing needs.

name: Aluminum sesquichlorohydrate
description:
Aluminum sesquichlorohydrate (CAS 11097-68-0 ), also known commercially as Aloxicoll and Astringen, is an inorganic aluminum salt used primarily as an antiperspirant active and as a coagulant in water treatment processes.

It occupies a mid-range position in the aluminum chlorohydrate family, offering a balance between astringency and skin compatibility that makes it a preferred active in personal care formulations.

In antiperspirant and deodorant products, it functions as the active ingredient by temporarily blocking eccrine sweat gland ducts, reducing perspiration output. Formulators incorporate it into roll-ons and sticks.

It is also used in aerosol formats where a moderately high aluminum content is required without the harshness associated with stronger aluminum salts. This makes it ideal for sensitive skin applications.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, it acts as a coagulant to destabilize suspended particles and colloidal matter, supporting clarification and sedimentation stages during the purification process.

It also finds use in pH buffering applications within treatment systems where controlled aluminum ion release is operationally advantageous. This ensures stability across various industrial water cycles.

Aluminum sesquichlorohydrate is supplied as an aqueous solution or as a dry powder, depending on the application and logistics requirements. Solution concentrations and powder grades are available to meet specifications.

Buyers should confirm grade suitability as cosmetic-grade material is held to tighter purity standards than technical-grade product intended for water treatment. Proper selection ensures optimal performance.

name: Glyceryl Stearate
description:
Glyceryl Stearate (CAS 11099-07-3 ), also known as Glyceryl Monostearate (GMS), is a mono-ester of glycerol and stearic acid used commercially as an emulsifier, plasticizer, and moisturizing agent.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems across food, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and polymer manufacturing. In personal care, it anchors emulsions in creams and lotions, improving texture and preventing phase separation.

Food manufacturers use GMS to extend the softness of baked goods, control fat crystallization in margarines, and improve the mouthfeel of ice cream. It is a versatile additive for texture and stability.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a tablet lubricant and controlled-release matrix component in solid dosage forms. It ensures consistent delivery and processing efficiency in manufacturing environments.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal lubricant and anti-static agent in PVC and polyolefin compounds. This reduces friction during extrusion and molding, enhancing the final product quality.

Glyceryl Stearate is supplied as white to off-white flakes, beads, or powder. Standard grades include food-grade meeting FCC specifications and pharmaceutical-grade meeting USP , BP , or Ph.Eur. standards.

Technical-grade options are also available for industrial polymer applications. Purity levels typically range from 40% monoglyceride content in standard grades to 90% or more in distilled or high-purity GMS variants.

name: Squalane
description:
Squalane (CAS 111-01-3 ), also marketed under trade names Cosbiol and Robane, is a fully saturated hydrocarbon oil derived from squalene through hydrogenation. It functions as a stable emollient, carrier, and solvent across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

In personal care, it is used as an emollient base in facial oils, moisturizers, and hair serums. Its non-greasy skin feel and oxidative stability justify premium positioning over standard plant oils in high-end formulations.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a carrier oil in topical drug delivery systems and as an adjuvant component in injectable emulsion formulations. It provides excellent skin compatibility and stability for active ingredients.

Food-grade material serves as a surface treatment agent and carrier for fat-soluble flavor compounds in encapsulation systems. It is valued for its inert nature and ability to protect sensitive compounds from oxidation.

In specialty lubricant and catalyst research applications, it functions as an inert hydrocarbon solvent. Thermal stability under process conditions is a primary selection factor for these industrial and technical uses.

The product is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Established grades include cosmetic-grade, food-grade ( FCC ), and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications.

Sourcing origin, such as plant-derived sugarcane or olive versus shark-derived, is a commercially significant distinction. This choice affects regulatory compliance, sustainability claims, and overall supply chain transparency.

name: Glyceryl Monooleate
description:
Glyceryl Monooleate (CAS 111-03-5 ), commonly abbreviated as GMO, is a monoglyceride ester used as an emulsifier and humectant across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

Recognized under FEMA 2526 , it functions by stabilizing oil-water interfaces and retaining moisture in finished products. In food manufacturing, GMO is used to improve texture and shelf life.

It is frequently utilized in baked goods, margarine, and dairy-based products by preventing fat separation and starch retrogradation. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and hair conditioners.

In these personal care applications, it supports emulsion stability and delivers a smooth, moisturizing skin feel. As a flavoring agent, it appears in systems where its oleic acid profile contributes to creamy taste profiles.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications, it acts as an excipient and solubilizer in lipid-based drug delivery systems and softgel formulations. It is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid or semi-solid.

The physical state depends on temperature and purity grade. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications, with food-grade material meeting FCC standards for safety and quality.

name: Methyl heptine carbonate
description:
Methyl heptine carbonate (CAS 111-12-6 ), also known as Methyl 2-Octynoate and commercially as Folione, is a high-impact aroma chemical used in flavor and fragrance manufacturing.

At trace concentrations, it delivers a sharp, violet-leaf and green character that defines its value to formulators working with fine fragrance and flavor systems.

In perfumery, it anchors green, leafy topnotes in fine fragrances, colognes, and functional fragrance products where naturalistic freshness is required for the final profile.

Flavor houses use it at very low usage levels to replicate violet, orris, and green vegetable profiles in confectionery, beverage, and savory applications across the industry.

It carries FEMA 2729 status supporting its use in food-grade flavor formulations. In personal care, it appears in shampoos, body washes, and fabric care products.

Its potency means small quantities contribute significantly to finished formulations, which remains a key consideration for industrial cost-in-use calculations and efficiency.

The chemical is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at high purity levels suited to fragrance and flavor end uses. It is available in fragrance-grade and food-grade specifications.

name: Heptanoic acid

name: Tetramethylhexamethylenediamine
description:
Tetramethylhexamethylenediamine ( CAS 111-18-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TMHDA, is a tertiary diamine used across polymer chemistry, catalysis, and specialty chemical synthesis.

Known also as 1,6-Bis(dimethylamino)hexane, it functions primarily as a catalyst, curing agent, and pH modifier in industrial formulations. In polyurethane and epoxy systems, it acts as a curing and crosslinking agent.

It influences gel time and final network density, which are parameters critical to formulators specifying mechanical performance. It serves as a catalyst precursor in organometallic and coordination chemistry.

Its bifunctional amine structure supports ligand design for pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis. In personal care formulations, it contributes to pH regulation in systems requiring controlled alkalinity.

This is achieved without introducing ionic burden. Polymer producers also use it as a chain extender or modifier in specialty nylon and polyamide development for various industrial applications.

TMHDA is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purity levels, typically 98% or higher. Technical grade is the most common specification for industrial polymer and catalyst applications.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply is available from select manufacturers where synthesis intermediates require tighter impurity profiles. Buyers should confirm specification documentation on a supplier-by-supplier basis.

name: Sebacic acid
description:
Sebacic acid (CAS 111-20-6 ) is a straight-chain dicarboxylic acid derived primarily from castor oil, used as a monomer and intermediate across polymer, lubricant, and personal care manufacturing.

FEMA 4943 status covers its use as a flavoring agent in food applications. Its bifunctional acid structure makes it a reliable building block for esterification and condensation reactions at industrial scale.

In polymer manufacturing, sebacic acid is reacted with diols or diamines to produce polyesters and polyamides with improved low-temperature flexibility, targeting engineering plastics and specialty films.

Lubricant formulators use sebacate esters synthesized from sebacic acid and branched alcohols as base fluids and additives in aviation, automotive, and high-performance greases where thermal stability is required.

In personal care, sebacic acid functions as an emollient precursor and pH buffer in skin-conditioning formulations and emulsions. Food and flavor manufacturers apply it at trace levels as a flavoring compound.

Sebacic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or flake. Standard commercial grades include technical, food-grade, and USP / BP specifications to meet requirements across industrial and regulated applications.

Purity levels typically range from 99% for high-grade material down to technical grades suited for polymer and lubricant synthesis. This material is handled according to standard industrial safety protocols.

name: 1-bromohexane
description:
1-Bromohexane (CAS 111-25-1 ), also known as hexyl bromide, is a straight-chain alkyl bromide used as a reactive intermediate in organic synthesis. It functions primarily as an alkylating agent, introducing the hexyl chain into target molecules.

This versatile chemical is utilized across pharmaceutical, polymer, and specialty chemical manufacturing sectors. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is used to N- or O-alkylate active pharmaceutical intermediates for drug development.

This process enables the construction of drug candidates with defined lipophilicity profiles. Polymer chemists use it to functionalize monomers and modify backbone structures, influencing solubility and processing behavior in specialty plastics.

In the production of quaternary ammonium compounds, it reacts with tertiary amines to yield surfactants. These products serve as phase-transfer catalysts used in textile processing and various industrial formulation chemistry applications.

Fragrance and flavor manufacturers also employ it as a precursor in synthesizing hexyl esters and ethers. These derivatives are essential for creating targeted sensory profiles in consumer goods and food-grade additives.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Smaller packaging options are available for laboratory and pilot-scale procurement to meet specific research and development requirements.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available to meet fine chemical specifications. Purity documentation including GC analysis and COA is standard for regulated supply chains.

name: 1-hexanol
description:
1-Hexanol (CAS 111-27-3 ), also known as n-hexyl alcohol, is a medium-chain primary alcohol used as a chemical intermediate, solvent, and fragrance ingredient across industrial and consumer product manufacturing.

Its controlled reactivity with isocyanates, acids, and anhydrides makes it a practical building block in polymer and coating chemistries. In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a reactive diluent and chain extender.

This chemical influences crosslink density and film flexibility in polyurethane and alkyd systems. Plasticizer and polymer synthesis rely on it as an esterification feedstock, producing hexyl esters for resins.

These esters modify the softness and processing behavior of PVC and similar materials. Personal care formulators incorporate n-hexyl alcohol as an emollient and emulsifier co-ingredient in skin and hair products.

The compound supports texture and phase stability in cosmetic formulations. Assigned FEMA 2567 , it also serves as a flavoring agent in food-grade applications, contributing a mild floral-green note.

It is used in beverages, confectionery, and fragrance compositions. 1-Hexanol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers.

Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications. Food and flavor applications typically require material meeting FCC or equivalent quality standards for safety and compliance.

name: 1,5-pentanediol
description:
1,5-Pentanediol (CAS 111-29-5 ), also known as pentamethylene glycol, is a bifunctional diol used as a reactive building block and process solvent across polymer, personal care, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its two terminal hydroxyl groups make it a practical monomer for condensation reactions and a functional carrier in formulation work. In polymer production, it reacts with diisocyanates or diacids to build polyurethane and polyester chains.

This chemical influences flexibility and molecular weight in coatings, adhesives, and elastomers. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a humectant and solvent in skin-conditioning products where it supports ingredient solubilization.

It provides moisture retention without the heaviness of longer-chain glycols. In plasticizer and cross-linking applications, it acts as a chain extender or curing co-agent in specialty resins and films for industrial use.

Food and flavor manufacturers use it as a carrier solvent for flavor concentrates and aroma compounds. This is particularly useful where regulatory-compliant glycol solvents are required for specific manufacturing processes.

1,5-Pentanediol is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for personal care and food-contact applications.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and relevant compliance documentation based on end-use requirements. This includes checking for FCC or other food-grade certifications to ensure the material meets all safety standards.

name: Glutaraldehyde
description:
Glutaraldehyde (CAS 111-30-8 ), also known as glutaric dialdehyde and commercially supplied as GA 50%, is a reactive dialdehyde used across industrial and life science sectors as a biocide and fixative.

Its dual aldehyde groups allow it to form stable bonds with proteins and other biological substrates, making it effective for preservation, sterilization, and material hardening applications in various fields.

In water treatment, it controls microbial growth in cooling towers, oilfield injection systems, and industrial process water where oxidizing biocides are unsuitable for the specific operating environment.

Leather and textile processors use it to cross-link collagen fibers during tanning and to improve wet strength and dimensional stability in treated materials during the manufacturing process.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it functions as a tissue fixative and enzyme immobilization agent, supporting histology, diagnostic kit manufacturing, and specialized biosensor production.

Personal care formulators apply it at low concentrations as a preservative booster in rinse-off products where broad-spectrum antimicrobial performance is required for product safety and shelf life.

This chemical is most commonly supplied as a 50% aqueous solution, with 25% and lower-concentration grades available for applications requiring diluted handling and specific safety protocols.

Technical and biocide-grade specifications are standard across the market, with purity and concentration verified by titration or GC methods. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes for volume.

name: 3-Ethoxy-1-propanol
description:
3-Ethoxy-1-propanol (CAS 111-35-3 ) is a glycol ether-type solvent used across coatings, cleaning, and printing applications. Its moderate evaporation rate and compatibility with both polar and non-polar systems make it a practical choice.

Formulators utilize this chemical for managing drying profiles and substrate wetting. In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a coalescing solvent and carrier, improving film formation and flow in water-based and solvent-borne systems.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations use it to enhance grease and soil removal while maintaining compatibility with surfactant blends. Printing ink manufacturers incorporate it to control viscosity and drying speed.

The solvent is effective across flexographic and gravure processes. In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a processing aid and plasticizer component, improving workability in resin systems and various industrial applications.

This product is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging suited to industrial volumes. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification available for this specific chemical compound.

Bulk quantities are accessible through standard solvent supply channels. Purity levels typically meet industrial formulation requirements, ensuring consistent performance across large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing operations.

name: Diethylenetriamine
description:
Diethylenetriamine (CAS 111-40-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DETA, is a polyamine building block used across adhesive, coating, and polymer manufacturing. Its multiple reactive amine groups make it a functional intermediate for curing agents and chemical synthesis.

Buyers source it primarily as a reactive component rather than a finished additive. In epoxy systems, DETA acts as a room-temperature curing agent for coatings, flooring compounds, and structural adhesives.

Controlled crosslink density determines final film hardness and chemical resistance in these applications. Textile and paper processors use it to produce wet-strength resins and softening agents that improve substrate durability.

In polymer synthesis, DETA serves as a monomer for polyamide resins and imidazoline derivatives used in corrosion inhibitors and fuel additives. These derivatives are essential for industrial maintenance and protection.

Personal care formulators incorporate DETA-derived intermediates into conditioning agents and chelating systems for rinse-off and leave-on products. This versatility makes it a staple in specialty chemical portfolios.

Diethylenetriamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically at 99% minimum.

Buyers requiring tighter amine content or color specifications can source material against defined CoA parameters. Quality is maintained according to industry standards to ensure consistent performance in reactive processes.

name: Aminoethylethanolamine
description:
Aminoethylethanolamine (CAS 111-41-1 ), commonly abbreviated as AEEA, is a bifunctional amine-alcohol used across polymer chemistry, surface treatment, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its dual reactive sites, a primary amine and a hydroxyl group, make it a building block for curing agents, crosslinkers, and pH-buffering intermediates. Monoethanol ethylenediamine is a recognized alternative name.

In coatings and adhesives, AEEA functions as a curing agent and crosslinker for epoxy systems, contributing to film hardness and adhesion performance in industrial finishes.

Textile and leather processors use it as a chemical intermediate for softeners, fixatives, and antistatic treatments applied during fabric and hide finishing processes.

In flame retardant formulations for plastics and polymers, AEEA serves as a reactive intermediate that becomes chemically incorporated into the polymer matrix rather than acting as an additive.

Paper treatment chemicals also draw on AEEA as a pH buffer and wet-strength resin intermediate. It is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Bulk tanker options are available for high-volume procurement. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial applications, ensuring consistent performance across batches.

Purity levels are typically specified at 98–99% minimum. Buyers should confirm moisture content and amine value when qualifying suppliers to ensure the material meets specific process requirements.

name: Diethanolamine
description:
Diethanolamine (CAS 111-42-2 ), commonly abbreviated as DEA, is a bifunctional amino alcohol used across industrial and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, surfactant intermediate, and emulsifying agent in formulated products.

In personal care and cosmetics, DEA reacts with fatty acids to produce diethanolamide surfactants used in shampoos, liquid soaps, and foam-boosting cleansers. Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and wetting agent.

These applications improve dye uptake and fiber handling during finishing operations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an alkalizing agent to adjust the pH of topical creams, ointments, and liquid formulations.

Paper manufacturers apply it as a process chemical to control pH during pulp treatment and coating formulations. Diethanolamine is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow viscous liquid, typically at 85% and 99% purity grades.

Technical grade is standard for industrial applications in textiles, paper, and chemical synthesis. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications generally require higher-purity material meeting USP or BP specifications.

name: Dichloroethyl ether
description:
Dichloroethyl ether ( CAS 111-44-4 ), also known as Bis(2-chloroethyl)ether or DCEE, is a chlorinated solvent used across industrial manufacturing and chemical processing.

It functions as a selective solvent, biocidal agent, and flame-retardant intermediate in demanding industrial applications. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a solvent for fats and greases.

This chemical enables effective scouring and finishing operations by dissolving resins that resist conventional solvent systems. Plastics and polymer manufacturers use it as a reactive intermediate.

Its chlorine content contributes to fire-suppression performance in finished materials through the synthesis of flame-retardant additives. In printing, it supports ink and coating formulations.

The compound provides aggressive solvent action on difficult substrates for the packaging industry. Its biocidal properties also make it relevant as a preservation agent in industrial fluids.

It is frequently utilized in paper processing treatments where microbial control is required. DCEE is supplied as a liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial-scale procurement.

It is available primarily in technical grade, reflecting its industrial rather than pharmaceutical or food-related end uses. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and packaging requirements.

Concentrations and inhibitor packages may vary by source, so direct consultation with suppliers is recommended. This ensures the material meets the specific needs of your manufacturing process.

name: Diethylene glycol
description:
Diethylene glycol (CAS 111-46-6 ), commonly sourced as DEG, is a hygroscopic diol used across industrial manufacturing as a solvent, plasticizer, and chemical intermediate.

Its moderate volatility and water miscibility make it a practical carrier and processing aid in formulations where slower evaporation is commercially advantageous for the manufacturer.

In polyester resin and polyurethane production, DEG functions as a monomer or co-monomer, directly influencing the flexibility and softness of the finished polymer during the synthesis process.

Natural gas processors use it as a dehydration agent to remove water vapor from gas streams before pipeline transmission. Textile and leather finishing operations apply DEG as a softening agent.

These applications improve the hand-feel and workability of treated materials. Printing ink and packaging adhesive formulators incorporate it as a solvent and humectant to control viscosity.

This prevents premature drying during processing. Diethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank, flexi-tank, and drum packaging options.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, meeting purity requirements suitable for industrial polymer, solvent, and gas processing applications across various global markets.

High-purity grades are available for specialty applications where tighter quality parameters are required by the end formulation to ensure consistent performance and chemical stability.

name: Ethylene glycol diacetate
description:
Ethylene glycol diacetate (CAS 111-55-7 ), also known as glycol diacetate or EGDA, is a diester solvent used across industrial, cosmetic, and flavoring applications.

It functions as a slow-evaporating carrier solvent and curing agent, offering controlled release characteristics that suit formulations requiring extended processing windows.

In plastics and polymer processing, EGDA acts as a reactive diluent and cross-linking aid in coatings, adhesives, and resin systems where controlled cure rates are critical.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a carrier solvent in fragrance concentrates and cosmetic bases, where its low volatility supports even distribution of active ingredients.

The flavor and fragrance industry uses EGDA as a flavoring agent with a mild fruity ester note, suitable for confectionery and beverage applications.

Industrial coatings manufacturers also select it as a high-boiling coalescing solvent to improve film formation in water-based and solvent-borne systems.

Ethylene glycol diacetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial solvent and coatings applications.

Flavor-grade material meeting purity specifications for food and fragrance use is available from select suppliers to ensure compliance with global regulatory requirements.

name: Stearic monoethanolamide
description:
Stearic monoethanolamide (CAS 111-57-9 ), also known as stearoyl ethanolamide or stearoyl-EA, is a fatty acid amide derived from stearic acid and ethanolamine. It functions as a rheology modifier, emulsifier, and moisturizing agent across personal care and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

In cosmetic formulations, it thickens creams, lotions, and hair conditioners while contributing to a smooth, non-greasy skin feel. This makes it a preferred co-emulsifier in oil-in-water systems for various beauty products.

Solid bar soap and syndet bar manufacturers use it to improve hardness, lather structure, and skin conditioning properties. In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it supports emulsion stability and acts as a co-emulsifier in dermal delivery systems.

Controlled viscosity is critical in these applications to ensure consistent application. It also appears in leave-on hair treatments, where its film-forming character aids moisture retention and improves overall hair manageability.

Stearic monoethanolamide is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form for ease of handling and dosing. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for global markets.

These grades meet the purity requirements of different regulatory frameworks and quality standards. Minimum purity grades and packaging formats vary by supplier, with bulk quantities available for industrial-scale formulators and manufacturers.

name: Glycol monostearate
description:
Glycol monostearate (CAS 111-60-4 ), also sold as ethylene glycol monostearate or glycol stearate, is a fatty acid ester used across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, opacifier, and rheology modifier, giving formulators control over texture, appearance, and product stability in various applications.

In personal care, it is the go-to opacifying agent in shampoos, conditioners, and body washes, producing the characteristic pearlescent sheen consumers associate with premium products.

Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier in baked goods and confectionery coatings, where it improves fat distribution and extends shelf texture for better consumer experiences.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into topical creams and ointments to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions and adjust viscosity according to strict USP or BP standards.

In plastics processing, it acts as a plasticizer and internal lubricant, improving flow and reducing brittleness in polymer compounds during the manufacturing and extrusion process.

The material is supplied as white flakes or beads, with flake form being the most common for industrial and cosmetic use. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade.

Purity is typically at 90% minimum, though higher-purity pharmaceutical grades are also available. Bulk supply is standard in 25 kg bags or fiber drums for global distribution.

name: Ethyl stearate
description:
Ethyl stearate (CAS 111-61-5 ), also recognized by its FEMA 3490 designation in flavoring applications, is a fatty acid ester derived from stearic acid used as a plasticizer and lubricant.

It serves as an emulsifier and carrier across food, cosmetic, and industrial sectors. Its low polarity and ester structure make it effective for solubilizing lipophilic actives and modifying surface properties.

In food and flavoring, it functions as a carrier and fixative for flavor compounds, recognized under FEMA 3490 for use in approved applications. Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions.

It is used in hair products where it softens texture and aids dispersion of active ingredients. Industrial lubricant manufacturers use it as a base fluid or additive in metalworking fluids and release agents.

Its film-forming character reduces surface friction in various industrial settings. In plastics processing, it acts as an internal or external plasticizer and processing aid to improve flow and reduce brittleness.

Ethyl stearate is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid or as a liquid above its melting point. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications for diverse manufacturing needs.

Food-grade material conforms to relevant purity standards for flavoring use. Bulk supply is typically offered in drums or IBCs, with smaller packaging available for specialty or laboratory applications.

name: Ethyl oleate
description:
Ethyl oleate (CAS 111-62-6 ), also known by its FEMA 2450 designation in flavor applications, is a fatty acid ester derived from oleic acid and ethanol. It functions as a low-viscosity carrier solvent, emollient, and lubricant across pharmaceutical, food, and industrial formulations.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it acts as an injectable vehicle and solubilizer for lipophilic active compounds. It offers low toxicity and good miscibility with oils, making it a preferred choice for complex delivery systems.

Flavor formulators use it as a fruity, waxy flavor modifier in food products where a mild fatty note is required. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skin-feel emollients and hair conditioning formulations for better performance.

Its low viscosity aids spreadability without leaving a heavy residue on the skin or hair. In metalworking and specialty lubricant blends, it functions as a biodegradable base fluid or co-solvent where environmental compliance is a priority.

This material is supplied as a clear, pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities for large-scale operations. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP /NF) specifications are the most commercially available options for buyers.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial lubricant applications where high-purity standards are less critical. Purity levels typically range from 95% to 99%+ depending on the intended application and regulatory requirement.

The product meets rigorous safety standards for use in sensitive applications across the global supply chain. Its versatility as a solvent and lubricant makes it a staple ingredient for diverse manufacturing sectors worldwide.

name: 1-heptanol
description:
1-Heptanol (CAS 111-70-6 ), also known as heptyl alcohol, is a medium-chain fatty alcohol used as a chemical intermediate, solvent, and fragrance ingredient across industrial and consumer product manufacturing.

With FEMA number 2548 , it is recognized in flavor and fragrance applications under that designation by formulators and buyers in those sectors. In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a reactive diluent.

It acts as a crosslinking co-agent, improving flow and cure characteristics in resin systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it as an emollient and emulsifier component in skin and hair products.

This material is ideal where a light, non-greasy carrier is required. Flavor and fragrance houses use it to contribute green, citrus-like top notes in fine fragrance compositions and food-grade flavoring systems.

In plastics processing, it serves as a plasticizer intermediate and stabilizer component during polymer compounding. 1-Heptanol is supplied as a clear liquid in standard bulk packaging including drums and IBCs.

Larger volume isotank shipments are available for industrial buyers. Technical grade is the most common supply form for industrial applications, while fragrance and flavor applications typically require higher-purity specifications.

These applications often require material meeting FCC or equivalent standards. Buyers should confirm purity levels and odor profile specifications directly with suppliers when sourcing for flavor or cosmetic end uses.

name: Butylethanolamine
description:
Butylethanolamine ( CAS 111-75-1 ), also known as 2-butylaminoethanol, is a bifunctional amine-alcohol used across industrial formulations where both pH control and surface-active behavior are required.

Its dual functional groups make it effective as a corrosion inhibitor, emulsifier, and buffering agent in metalworking, coatings, and textile processing. In metalworking fluids, it neutralizes acidic byproducts.

This chemical provides corrosion protection on ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces, extending fluid service life. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a neutralizing amine for waterborne resin systems.

It improves dispersion stability and film formation without introducing excessive volatility. In textile and leather processing, it functions as an emulsification aid in lubricating and softening baths.

This helps to maintain bath stability across variable process conditions. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to adjust pH during formulation, ensuring compatibility between reactive components.

Butylethanolamine is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Purity levels typically range from 98% and above, with certificates of analysis provided against agreed-upon specifications. This ensures consistent performance across various industrial applications.

name: 2-butoxyethanol
description:
2-Butoxyethanol (CAS 111-76-2 ), also known as EGBE or Butyl Cellosolve, is a glycol ether solvent used across industrial cleaning, coatings, and personal care manufacturing. Its ability to couple water and oil phases makes it a practical choice for formulating products.

This versatile chemical is ideal for products that require both solubility and controlled evaporation. In coatings and paints, EGBE improves flow and leveling in water-based and solvent-borne systems, reducing surface defects in architectural and industrial finishes.

Printing ink manufacturers use it to control viscosity and drying speed in flexographic and gravure formulations. Industrial and institutional cleaners rely on it to degrease hard surfaces, cutting through oils and soils in degreasers and all-purpose sprays.

It is also a key component in automotive cleaning products. In personal care, it functions as a solvent carrier in nail care products and hair dyes where controlled solubility of actives is required for effective application and performance.

2-Butoxyethanol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. Standard commercial supply is technical grade, suitable for industrial cleaning and coatings applications.

High-purity grades meeting tighter specifications are available for personal care and specialty formulation end uses. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery of this essential solvent to meet your specific manufacturing and production timelines.

name: Diethylene glycol monomethyl ether
description:
Diethylene glycol monomethyl ether ( CAS 111-77-3 ), also known as Methyl Carbitol and commonly abbreviated as DGME, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, printing, and personal care manufacturing.

Its controlled evaporation rate and broad solvency profile make it a preferred carrier in formulations requiring extended open time or improved film formation. In architectural and industrial coatings, DGME functions as a coalescing agent.

It acts as a viscosity modifier, improving flow and leveling in waterborne systems. Printing ink formulators use it to control drying speed and maintain pigment dispersion stability in flexographic and gravure applications.

In personal care, it acts as a solvent and humectant in rinse-off and leave-on formulations, helping to solubilize active ingredients and improve skin feel. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate DGME as a reactive diluent.

It serves as a processing aid to optimize application viscosity and curing behavior. DGME is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities, with bulk availability for high-volume users.

Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, meeting purity requirements for industrial solvent applications. Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care end uses where tighter impurity limits are required.

name: Methyl laurate
description:
Methyl laurate (CAS 111-82-0 ), also sold as methyl dodecylate, is a fatty acid methyl ester derived from lauric acid used across personal care, food, and industrial lubricant markets.

It functions as an emollient, emulsifier, and lubricant base, and carries FEMA 2715 status for flavoring applications. In personal care formulations, it acts as a lightweight emollient and carrier.

It is used in skin creams, hair conditioners, and cleansing oils, offering good spreadability without heavy residue. Food and flavor manufacturers use it as a flavoring agent to impart coconut and fatty notes.

It is commonly found in confectionery, dairy, and beverage products. Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it as a bio-based ester lubricant base fluid or additive for performance.

Its ester structure provides film-forming properties suitable for cutting fluids and release agents. It also serves as a chemical intermediate in the production of surfactants, esters, and other oleochemical derivatives.

Methyl laurate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical grade for industrial and lubricant applications, and in food or flavor grade meeting purity standards.

The material is available in grades appropriate for FEMA-listed use. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with cosmetic-grade material available from oleochemical producers.

name: Pioglitazone
description:
Pioglitazone (CAS 111025-46-8 ) is an oral antidiabetic active pharmaceutical ingredient belonging to the thiazolidinedione class. It functions as an insulin sensitizer, targeting peripheral tissue resistance in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Pharmaceutical intermediates suppliers also supply it to support synthesis research and formulation development pipelines targeting metabolic disease indications. This supports the growth of the global pharmaceutical market.

Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) source it for bioequivalence study batches and commercial-scale tablet production. Pioglitazone is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications, including USP and Ph.Eur. compliant material. The hydrochloride salt form is the predominant commercial grade used in finished dosage manufacturing.

Bulk API is typically offered in kilogram to multi-kilogram quantities with full regulatory documentation support. This includes CoA, DMF references, and ICH-compliant impurity profiling for quality assurance.

name: Sodium pyroantimonate
description:
Sodium pyroantimonate (CAS 11112-10-0 ), also known as antimonic acid sodium salt, is an inorganic antimony compound used industrially as a flame retardant and rheology modifier. It functions by suppressing combustion in polymer systems and adjusting flow behavior in specialty formulations.

In plastics and rubber compounding, sodium pyroantimonate acts as a flame retardant synergist. It is particularly effective alongside halogenated systems where antimony enhances char formation and gas-phase flame inhibition during the combustion process.

The textile and nonwoven sector uses it to impart fire resistance to fiber treatments and fabric coatings applied during finishing processes. This ensures that materials meet stringent safety standards required for industrial and commercial use.

In paper manufacturing, it contributes to flame-retardant barrier coatings where controlled rheology during application is critical to coating uniformity. This allows for a consistent protective layer across the entire surface of the paper substrate.

Leather processing operations use it as a rheology modifier in aqueous treatment baths. In these applications, consistent viscosity directly affects penetration depth and the final surface finish quality of the treated leather goods.

Sodium pyroantimonate is supplied as a white powder or fine crystalline solid. It is available in technical grade, with purity levels typically specified to meet industrial processing requirements in plastics, rubber, and textile applications.

Enramycin (CAS 11115-82-5 ), also known as Enduracidin, is a polypeptide antibiotic produced by fermentation of Streptomyces fungicidicus. In commercial use, it functions as an antimicrobial growth promoter and feed preservative.

The compound works by inhibiting gram-positive bacterial cell wall synthesis in livestock. In animal nutrition, it is incorporated into medicated premixes and compound feeds for broilers, swine, and cattle.

This additive helps to improve feed conversion ratios and suppress pathogenic gut flora. It is used in veterinary pharmaceutical formulations where targeted activity against Clostridium species is required.

In biotechnology and life sciences research, Enduracidin serves as a reference compound for studying bacterial cell wall biosynthesis inhibition. Its structural complexity positions it as a pharmaceutical intermediate.

Enramycin is supplied as a powder, typically standardized to 8% or 4% active content in premix carrier form for feed applications. Pure technical and research-grade material is available for laboratory use.

This chemical enables precise reaction initiation without the thermal requirements of conventional initiators. In polymer chemistry, it initiates radical polymerization of acrylates, methacrylates, and vinyl monomers.

The compound supports the production of specialty plastics and adhesive systems. Pharmaceutical synthesis relies on it as a boron-based reagent for hydroboration and stereoselective carbon–carbon bond-forming reactions.

It is essential in active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing and biotechnology research. Scientists use it in the preparation of functional polymers for drug delivery scaffolds and surface modification applications.

It also serves as a catalyst precursor in transition-metal-catalyzed processes where controlled generation of reactive intermediates is required. The material is supplied as a liquid, typically as a solution.

name: Trimethylolpropane caprylate caprate
description:
Trimethylolpropane caprylate caprate (CAS 11138-60-6 ), commercially known as Emkarate 1550 or Emkarate DE 155, is a synthetic ester derived from trimethylolpropane with mixed C8/C10 fatty acids.

It functions as a high-performance base fluid and functional additive across lubrication, personal care, and polymer processing applications. In lubricant formulations, it serves as a synthetic base oil.

This material is ideal for compressor oils, refrigeration lubricants, and high-temperature greases where thermal stability and low volatility are critical selection criteria for industrial manufacturers.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as an emollient carrier and skin-feel modifier in creams, serums, and color cosmetics. Its light texture and oxidative stability distinguish it from mineral oil.

As a plasticizer in PVC and polymer compounds, it improves flexibility and processability without the regulatory concerns associated with phthalate-based options. It is a versatile choice for modern compounding.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a reactive diluent or solvent carrier, aiding application viscosity and film formation. This ensures consistent performance across various industrial coating applications.

The product is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly available for global distribution.

Cosmetic grades typically meet purity and color standards required for personal care registration. Bulk supply is standard for industrial lubricant and polymer processing customers worldwide.

name: Xanthan gum
description:
Xanthan gum (CAS 11138-66-2 ), also known commercially as Kelzan and labeled E415 in food applications, is a high-performance polysaccharide produced by microbial fermentation.

It functions as a rheology modifier, stabilizer, and emulsifier across a broad range of industries, delivering consistent viscosity and suspension control at low use levels.

In food manufacturing, it stabilizes dressings, sauces, and gluten-free baked goods by preventing phase separation and improving texture at concentrations below 1%.

Personal care formulators rely on it to build viscosity in shampoos, lotions, and gels without compromising clarity or skin feel during application or storage.

Oilfield operations use xanthan gum in drilling fluids and completion muds, where it maintains suspension of solids under high-salinity and high-temperature conditions.

In agrochemical formulations, it keeps active ingredients evenly dispersed in suspension concentrates and wettable powders throughout storage and application cycles.

Xanthan gum is supplied as a cream to off-white free-flowing powder in standard mesh sizes. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant) and pharmaceutical-grade.

Standard quality certifications include USP and Ph. Eur. , alongside technical-grade for industrial use. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities.

name: Potassium aspartate
description:
Potassium aspartate ( CAS 1115-63-5 ) is the potassium salt of aspartic acid, supplied as a bioavailable source of both potassium and the amino acid aspartate for use across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications.

Monopotassium aspartate is the form most commonly referenced in supplement and pharmaceutical procurement contexts. In dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, it delivers potassium in a form with higher gastrointestinal tolerability.

This makes it a preferred choice for electrolyte tablets, capsules, and sports nutrition formulas compared to inorganic salts. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient or excipient in preparations targeting potassium replenishment.

It is often used in combination with magnesium aspartate for clinical applications. In food and beverage applications, it functions as a flavor modifier and acidulant, contributing a mild taste profile suited to functional drinks.

The compound is also utilized in fortified foods and specialized nutritional products. Feed formulators incorporate it into animal nutrition programs where amino acid-bound mineral delivery improves uptake efficiency.

Potassium aspartate is available as a white crystalline powder. It is supplied in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with USP and Ph. Eur. grades available for regulated applications.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or fiber drums suited to industrial and commercial formulation scale. This ensures stability and ease of handling during large-scale manufacturing processes.

name: Metformin hydrochloride
description:
Metformin hydrochloride (CAS 1115-70-4 ) is the active pharmaceutical ingredient form of metformin, supplied as its stable salt for pharmaceutical manufacturing. Known under the alternative designation N,N-Dimethylbiguanide hydrochloride, it is one of the highest-volume oral antidiabetic APIs in global pharmaceutical production.

The primary application is as the API in immediate-release and extended-release oral solid dosage forms, including tablets and film-coated tablets manufactured to pharmacopeial specifications. It is also incorporated into fixed-dose combination products alongside other antidiabetic agents.

This requires precise blending and granulation compatibility during the manufacturing process. Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers source it in bulk for high-throughput tableting lines where consistent particle size and compressibility are critical procurement criteria.

Research institutions and formulation development labs source smaller quantities for bioequivalence studies and novel delivery system development. Metformin hydrochloride is available as a white crystalline powder in bulk quantities suited to commercial-scale pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It is supplied to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades, with grade selection typically driven by the target market's regulatory requirements. Standard packaging ranges from multi-kilogram drums to metric-ton quantities for large-volume generic manufacturers.

name: Trioctylamine
description:
Trioctylamine (CAS 1116-76-3 ), also known as TOA or tri-n-caprylylamine, is a long-chain tertiary amine used across extraction, catalysis, and surface modification processes.

Its high selectivity for acidic species makes it a preferred extractant in hydrometallurgical and chemical purification operations. In solvent extraction, TOA selectively recovers acids and rare earth metals.

It is also used for valuable intermediates from aqueous process streams, making it a standard reagent in metal refining and pharmaceutical purification. Polymer and coating formulators incorporate it as a catalyst.

It is used in curing systems, particularly where controlled reactivity and compatibility with organic matrices are required. In personal care and cosmetic formulations, TOA functions as an emulsifier and pH modifier.

It supports stable dispersion of active ingredients across oil-and-water systems. It also serves as a phase-transfer catalyst and surface modifier in adhesive and sealant manufacturing, improving substrate wetting.

Trioctylamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade material, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 99%+ for demanding applications.

Packaging options are commonly available in drum and IBC quantities to support both laboratory-scale evaluation and bulk industrial procurement for various manufacturing sectors.

name: Dimethylglycine
description:
Dimethylglycine (CAS 1118-68-9 ), commonly abbreviated as DMG, is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biotechnology applications. It functions as a buffering agent, chelator, and humectant.

This versatile compound supports formulation stability and active ingredient performance in finished products. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, DMG serves as a precursor compound and pH buffer in various delivery systems.

It is frequently utilized in tablet, capsule, and liquid formulations requiring precise acid-base control. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into moisturizing creams, serums, and skin-conditioning products to enhance texture.

Its humectant properties support water retention in the skin matrix, making it a valuable additive for personal care. Biotechnology and cell culture applications rely on DMG as a chelating agent to sequester metal ions.

This sequestration prevents interference with assay accuracy or cell viability during sensitive laboratory processes. It also appears in topical and oral healthcare formulations where controlled buffering capacity is a critical quality parameter.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a synthetic intermediate for active pharmaceutical ingredients where controlled reactivity at the methylene position is required for complex synthesis.

Flavor and fragrance formulators incorporate it into compositions targeting fruity, herbaceous, or green scent profiles, particularly in fine fragrance and food flavoring applications.

Cosmetic chemists use it as a carrier and reactive component in skin-care and hair-care formulations where controlled release or film-forming properties are needed for performance.

name: Nonanoic acid
description:
Nonanoic acid (CAS 112-05-0 ), also known as pelargonic acid, is a nine-carbon saturated fatty acid derived primarily from oleic acid oxidation. It functions as a pH regulator and emulsifier.

This versatile chemical intermediate is used across lubricant, personal care, and food manufacturing applications. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it serves as a precursor to nonanoate ester base fluids.

It is also utilized in corrosion inhibitors used in cutting oils and hydraulic fluids. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into emulsified skin and hair products where its fatty acid profile supports texture.

The material provides stability in finished formulations across various cosmetic lines. As a FEMA 2784 -listed flavoring agent, it contributes to fruit and dairy flavor profiles in food and beverage products.

It also acts as a catalyst intermediate and pH buffer in specialty chemical synthesis. This is particularly useful where controlled acidity is required in complex esterification reactions during manufacturing.

Nonanoic acid is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in bulk and intermediate packaging formats. Food-grade and technical-grade designations are the most common commercial specifications available.

Buyers sourcing for flavor applications should confirm FEMA compliance for their specific needs. Industrial buyers typically specify technical-grade material with defined acid value and purity thresholds for use.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional fragrance compositions to build floral-fruity accords. Personal care formulators use it in shampoos, body washes, and skin care products.

It is ideal where a recognizable fruit-forward scent profile is part of the consumer experience. It also appears in household and fabric care fragrances where low-cost, high-impact aroma performance is a priority.

The product is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid. It is available in flavor-grade quality meeting the required status, supporting use in various food-contact applications and industrial formulations.

Standard commercial packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities. Documentation typically includes COA, MSDS, and flavor compliance certifications to ensure full regulatory transparency for global buyers.

name: Glycol monobutyl ether acetate
description:
Glycol monobutyl ether acetate (CAS 112-07-2 ), also known as 2-butoxyethyl acetate and commonly abbreviated as EGBEA, is a slow-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings and specialty formulations.

Its controlled evaporation rate supports film formation and flow in high-solids and waterborne systems. In architectural and industrial coatings, EGBEA functions as a coalescing and flow-control solvent.

It improves leveling and reduces surface defects in alkyd, epoxy, and polyurethane finishes. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust open time and enhance substrate wetting in formulations.

In printing inks, it supports pigment dispersion and controls drying speed across gravure and screen printing processes. Personal care formulators use it as a carrier solvent in nail lacquers.

It is particularly useful in surface-treatment products where slow evaporation is commercially desirable. EGBEA is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers.

Bulk tanker options are available for high-volume requirements. It is predominantly traded at technical grade, with purity specifications typically reaching 99% or above for standard use.

Solvent-grade product is the standard commercial offering for most applications. Documentation packages generally include COA and standard regulatory compliance data for quality assurance.

name: Isopropyl stearate
description:
Isopropyl stearate (CAS 112-10-7 ), also sold under the trade name Wickenol 127, is an ester of isopropyl alcohol and stearic acid used as an emollient, lubricant, and solvent carrier across personal care and industrial markets.

Its low viscosity and good spreadability make it a practical formulation base where dry, non-greasy skin feel or controlled lubricity is required. In personal care formulations, it functions as an emollient and carrier in creams and lotions.

It is frequently used in color cosmetics, contributing a lightweight skin feel without the heaviness of heavier esters or mineral oils. Textile and leather finishing operations use it as a softening and lubricating agent.

This material improves fiber pliability and reduces friction during processing. Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it as a base fluid or co-solvent where biodegradable ester-based lubrication is preferred.

It serves as an effective alternative to petroleum-derived products. It also acts as a plasticizer and solvent carrier in specialty coatings and paper treatment formulations, providing consistent performance across various applications.

Isopropyl stearate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid at ambient conditions. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the diverse needs of global manufacturing clients.

Cosmetic-grade material typically meets purity and color standards required by personal care manufacturers. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to ensure efficient logistics and handling for large-scale production.

name: Isopropyl oleate
description:
Isopropyl oleate (CAS 112-11-8 ) is an ester of oleic acid and isopropyl alcohol used across personal care and industrial formulations as an emollient, solvent carrier, and lubricant base.

Its low viscosity and good solvency for oils and actives make it a practical choice for formulators and industrial buyers sourcing functional esters. In personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning emollient.

It is used in creams, lotions, and hair oils, improving spreadability and active ingredient delivery. Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it as a base fluid or co-solvent in cutting fluids.

It is also utilized in rust preventatives and release agents where bio-based ester chemistry is preferred. It acts as a plasticizer and softening agent in specialty coatings and polymer formulations.

These applications often require flexible, non-migrating additives. As a solvent carrier, it dissolves lipophilic actives and pigment dispersions in cosmetic and industrial coating applications where mineral oil alternatives are needed.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial and lubricant applications, while cosmetic-grade material is also available.

Material meeting specific purity specifications is available for personal care use. Bulk availability varies by supplier, and buyers should confirm acid value and iodine value specifications against their requirements.

name: Diethylene glycol monoethyl ether acetate

It is used in gravure and screen printing inks, improving flow and reducing premature drying on press. Coatings and resin formulators use it to dissolve nitrocellulose, epoxy, and polyurethane systems.

Its solvency balance helps achieve target viscosity and film quality. In personal care, it acts as a solvent and carrier in nail lacquers and fragrance formulations where compatibility is a key selection factor.

name: Lauryldimethylamine
description:
Lauryldimethylamine (CAS 112-18-5 ), also known as LDMA, is a long-chain tertiary amine used as a chemical intermediate, emulsifier, and surface-active agent across industrial and personal care manufacturing.

It is frequently used in foam boosters for shampoos, conditioners, and liquid cleansers. Coatings and adhesives formulators use it as a curing catalyst for epoxy systems and as a wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion.

It also functions as a corrosion inhibitor and emulsification aid in industrial process fluids and metalworking formulations. Sealant and elastomer manufacturers incorporate it as a stabilizer to protect polymer systems.

This protection is vital during processing and storage. Lauryldimethylamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial applications.

Purity levels are typically at 95% or higher depending on the supplier specification. Bulk quantities are available in drums and IBC totes, with documentation commonly provided to support sourcing requirements.

name: Triethylenetetramine
description:
Triethylenetetramine (CAS 112-24-3 ), commonly abbreviated as TETA, is a polyamine used across polymer, textile, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a curing agent, cross-linker, and pH buffer in industrial formulations.

In epoxy resin systems, TETA acts as a room-temperature hardener, enabling cross-linking in coatings, adhesives, and composite materials where controlled cure speed and mechanical strength are required.

Textile and leather processors use it as a pH regulator and fixative in dyeing and finishing baths, improving dye uptake and process consistency. This ensures high-quality results across various industrial applications.

In flame retardant formulations, it serves as a reactive intermediate or building block for nitrogen-containing compounds that contribute to char formation in polymer matrices. This enhances the safety profile of materials.

Personal care formulators incorporate TETA as a pH adjuster in select rinse-off products and as a chelating component in formulations requiring amine-based buffering. It provides stability and performance in these settings.

TETA is supplied as an amber to light yellow liquid in standard industrial packaging including drums and IBCs. Technical grade is the most common commercial form for large-scale manufacturing needs.

Higher-purity grades are available for specialty polymer and personal care applications. Buyers should confirm amine content and purity specification against their curing or formulation requirements before sourcing.

It is used for active ingredients in creams, gels, and liquid dosage forms. Air disinfection systems also employ TEG as a low-toxicity antimicrobial agent dispersed as a fine mist.

Moisture content and purity levels are key specification parameters buyers should confirm against application requirements to ensure optimal performance in their specific industrial processes.

name: Tetraethylenepentamine
description:
Tetraethylenepentamine (CAS 112-57-2 ), commonly known as TEPA or Tetren, is a polyamine used across coatings, polymer, and textile industries as a curing agent, crosslinker, and pH modifier.

Its multiple reactive amine groups make it a functional building block for epoxy systems, chelating formulations, and specialty chemical synthesis. In epoxy coatings and adhesives, TEPA acts as a hardener.

This material crosslinks resin networks to deliver durable, chemically resistant films suited for industrial and protective coating applications. Polymer manufacturers use it as a reactive intermediate.

It is essential in producing polyamide resins and flame-retardant additives, where its nitrogen-rich structure contributes to char formation under heat exposure. In textile and paper processing, it functions well.

TEPA serves as a wet-strength resin precursor and fiber treatment agent, improving substrate durability and dye uptake. Personal care formulators incorporate it at low concentrations for pH adjustment.

This is particularly useful in rinse-off products where controlled alkalinity is required. TEPA is supplied as a viscous amber liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 95% to 98% depending on the supplier. Some producers offer blended or diluted formulations.

These variations target specific epoxy curing or chelation applications. The product is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and performance in diverse manufacturing environments.

name: Diethylene glycol monohexyl ether
description:
Diethylene glycol monohexyl ether (CAS 112-59-4 ), also known commercially as Hexyl Carbitol, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, cleaning, and metalworking formulations.

Its combination of hydrophilic and lipophilic character makes it effective as both a solvent carrier and an emulsifier in water-based and solvent-based systems. In architectural and industrial coatings, it functions as a coalescing aid.

It serves as a coupling solvent, improving film formation and flow in waterborne latex paints. Printing ink formulators use it to control viscosity and drying rate in packaging inks, particularly where extended open time is required.

In metalworking and industrial cleaning compounds, it acts as a degreasing solvent and emulsifier, helping to lift and disperse oils from metal surfaces. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a reactive diluent.

It is used as a processing solvent to adjust application viscosity without compromising final bond strength. This versatile chemical is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Specifications are aligned with industrial solvent requirements, and material is generally available with standard COA documentation.

The documentation covers purity, water content, and color to ensure consistency. This product meets the rigorous demands of chemical manufacturing and large-scale industrial applications across various global markets.

name: Tetraethylene glycol
description:
Tetraethylene glycol (CAS 112-60-7 ), commonly abbreviated as TEG, is a mid-chain polyethylene glycol marketed under the designation PEG-4 in cosmetic and personal care contexts.

It functions as a hygroscopic solvent, humectant, and reactive intermediate across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and polymer manufacturing applications. In personal care formulations, TEG acts as a humectant.

It serves as a solvent carrier for active ingredients in creams, serums, and cleansing products, improving texture and moisture retention. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solvent and co-solvent.

In topical and oral preparations, its low volatility supports stable, consistent dosing. In polymer chemistry, TEG serves as a reactive diol for cross-linking and curing polyurethane and epoxy systems.

This contributes to controlled network density in coatings and adhesives. It also functions as a plasticizer and processing aid in specialty plastic formulations requiring flexible, low-migration performance.

Tetraethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications suited to industrial applications.

Pharmaceutical and cosmetic supply chains typically require material meeting USP or Ph. Eur. compendial standards. Such grades are available from qualified API and specialty chemical distributors.

name: Methyl stearate
description:
Methyl stearate (CAS 112-61-8 ) is a fatty acid methyl ester derived from stearic acid, produced primarily through the esterification of stearic acid with methanol. It functions as a lubricant, emulsifier, and surface-active agent across industrial, cosmetic, and food-related manufacturing processes.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as a base fluid or additive component where controlled viscosity and film-forming behavior reduce friction in machining and metal processing operations.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into creams, lotions, and hair conditioners as an emollient and emulsifier that improves texture and skin feel without contributing heavy residue.

Food-grade methyl stearate is used as a processing aid and release agent in baked goods and confectionery production. It also serves as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of fatty alcohols and surfactants.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white solid or flake at ambient temperature, transitioning to a clear liquid above its melting point. It is available in technical grade for industrial and oleochemical applications.

We also offer food-grade specifications meeting FCC standards. Bulk quantities are typically offered in drums or flexi-bags, with purity levels commonly at 95% or higher depending on the specific grade required.

name: Methyl oleate
description:
Methyl oleate (CAS 112-62-9 ) is the methyl ester of oleic acid, produced by esterification of oleic acid with methanol. It functions as a lubricant base, emulsifier, and carrier across food, personal care, and industrial applications.

Buyers source it as a bio-based alternative to petroleum-derived esters in formulation and process chemistry. In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it serves as a base fluid and additive in cutting oils and rolling fluids.

It is used in biodegradable lubricant formulations where low toxicity and good lubricity are procurement priorities. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, hair conditioners, and color cosmetics.

It acts as an emollient carrier and emulsifier that supports even active distribution across formulations. Food-grade material is used as a flavoring agent and processing aid in fat-based food systems.

It also functions as a reactive intermediate and solvent in the production of surfactants, fatty acid derivatives, and oleochemical synthesis. The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid.

Standard commercial grades include technical, food-grade, and high-purity variants meeting FCC or USP specifications depending on the intended application. This ensures compliance for sensitive uses.

Bulk supply is available in drums and ISO tank quantities, with purity levels typically ranging from 70% to 99%+ depending on grade. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing and supply.

name: Dimethylhexadecylamine
description:
Dimethylhexadecylamine (CAS 112-69-6 ), also known commercially as Dimethyl palmitamine, is a long-chain tertiary amine derived from palmitic acid. It functions as a surface-active intermediate and conditioning agent across lubricant and personal care manufacturing.

In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor precursor and lubricity additive. This improves metal surface protection in cutting fluids and rust-preventive coatings during heavy industrial processes.

Quaternization of this amine produces cationic surfactants used in fabric softeners, hair conditioners, and rinse-off personal care products. These applications rely on its substantivity to negatively charged surfaces for effective performance.

In mineral processing, it serves as a flotation collector for silicate and oxide ores. It selectively modifies mineral surfaces to aid separation, making it a vital component in large-scale mining and extraction operations.

Personal care formulators also use it as an emulsification aid and conditioning intermediate in cream and lotion systems. It is particularly effective in targeting hair and skin applications where smooth texture and moisture retention are required.

The product is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on ambient temperature and purity grade. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with high-purity grades available for specialty chemical synthesis.

It is also used for quaternary ammonium salt production and other complex chemical reactions. The material is typically offered in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers seeking reliable bulk supply chains.

name: 1-tridecanol

In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as an emulsifier and consistency agent in creams, lotions, and conditioning formulations. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use it as a surface-active component.

This material helps to improve substrate wetting and the dispersion of pigments or fillers. In textile and leather processing, it supports lubrication and surface treatment steps where controlled wetting behavior is required.

It also serves as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of specialty surfactants, esters, and ethoxylates for industrial end uses. 1-Tridecanol is typically supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid or flake.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications generally ranging from 95% upward depending on the application. Packaging is available in bags or drums suited to industrial procurement volumes.
