name: Myristyl alcohol
description:
Myristyl alcohol (CAS 112-72-1 ), also supplied under the names tetradecyl alcohol and Nacol 14-95, is a long-chain fatty alcohol derived primarily from natural fats and oils.

It functions as an emulsifier, emollient, and viscosity modifier across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations. In cosmetics and skincare, it builds body and improves texture.

It is used in creams, lotions, and hair conditioners while contributing to a smooth skin feel without greasiness. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a consistency agent and emulsion stabilizer.

In topical ointments and cream bases, controlled rheology is critical to product performance. In lubricant formulations, it acts as a friction modifier and surface-active component.

It is utilized in metalworking fluids and specialty greases. Food-grade material finds use as a processing aid and release agent in certain food manufacturing applications.

Myristyl alcohol is supplied as white flakes or pastilles, with purity typically ranging from 95% to 98% minimum. Standard commercial grades include technical and cosmetic grades.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications. Bulk supply is available in bags or fiber drums for various procurement requirements.

Packaging options are suited to both industrial and GMP-compliant needs. This ensures the material meets the rigorous standards required for high-quality chemical manufacturing and distribution.

name: Diethylene glycol dibutyl ether
description:
Diethylene glycol dibutyl ether (CAS 112-73-2 ), commercially known as Dibutyl Carbitol, is a high-boiling glycol ether solvent used across industrial and specialty chemical applications. Its low volatility and strong solvency make it a preferred carrier in formulations.

Controlled evaporation and compatibility with resins or active components are critical procurement considerations for this material. In polymer and coatings systems, it functions as a coalescing solvent and plasticizer carrier, improving film formation.

It is used as a reaction medium and catalyst solvent in curing and cross-linking processes, particularly where thermal stability at elevated temperatures is required. This ensures consistent performance in demanding industrial environments.

Specialty printing inks and electronic paste formulations rely on it as a high-boiling carrier to control rheology and drying profiles. This allows for precision in high-tech manufacturing and specialized printing applications.

In extraction and separation processes, its selective solvency supports liquid-liquid extraction of metal ions and organic compounds at industrial scale. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical processing and refining.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities to meet various logistical needs. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher.

High-purity grades are available for electronic and specialty chemical applications where trace contaminant limits are tightly controlled. These grades meet the rigorous demands of sensitive manufacturing and laboratory environments.

name: Tetradecyldimethylamine
description:
Tetradecyldimethylamine (CAS 112-75-4 ) is a long-chain tertiary amine used as a chemical intermediate and functional surfactant across cleaning, personal care, and textile processing industries.

Its primary commercial value lies in conversion to quaternary ammonium compounds, amine oxides, and betaines. These downstream actives drive formulation performance in various industrial applications.

In home care and industrial cleaning, it serves as a precursor to quats and amine oxides used in fabric softeners and disinfectants. It is also essential for hard surface cleaners and detergents.

Personal care formulators use it to produce conditioning agents and foam boosters for shampoos and rinse-off products. Textile and leather processors apply it in surface modification treatments.

These treatments improve fiber wettability and dye uptake during the manufacturing process. It also functions as an emulsifier and dispersant in paper processing for uniform coating and sizing.

The chemical is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity grades suited for industrial synthesis. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly at 95% or higher.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers, reflecting its use as a bulk intermediate. This ensures efficient handling in continuous manufacturing processes and large-scale chemical production.

name: Oleic acid
description:
Oleic acid (CAS 112-80-1 ) is a long-chain monounsaturated fatty acid derived primarily from animal and vegetable fats. It features FEMA 2815 recognition supporting its use as a flavoring agent in food applications.

It functions industrially as an emulsifier, lubricant, surfactant, and surface modifier across a broad range of manufacturing sectors. In personal care and cosmetics, it acts as an emollient carrier and emulsification agent.

These phase-transfer catalysts function as biocides or surface-active agents in plastic formulations. Personal care formulators use cetyl bromide-derived intermediates to produce conditioning agents and cationic surfactants.

These are frequently found in hair care and skin treatment products. In lubricant additive development, it acts as a building block for long-chain esters and antioxidant stabilizers that improve thermal performance.

These stabilizers are essential in metalworking fluids. Flame retardant synthesis also draws on its reactive bromine functionality to produce halogenated compounds incorporated into various polymer matrices.

1-Bromohexadecane is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. Standard commercial grades are available at purities of 95% and 97% or higher.

name: Behenic acid
description:
Behenic acid (CAS 112-85-6 ) is a long-chain saturated fatty acid derived primarily from vegetable oils including rapeseed and peanut. Its high melting point and low solubility make it a functional ingredient for structuring and lubrication.

This material is essential for emulsification across multiple industrial sectors. In personal care, it functions as a thickener and emollient in hair conditioners, creams, and solid cosmetic formats where a waxy texture is required.

Polymer and plastics processors use it as an internal and external lubricant to improve mold release. It helps reduce friction during compounding and extrusion, ensuring high-quality finishes in various manufacturing processes.

In food applications, it serves as a processing aid and stabilizer in fat-based systems. It is particularly useful where controlled crystallization is commercially relevant for maintaining the desired texture and shelf life.

Metalworking lubricant formulators incorporate it into greases and solid lubricant blends. Its high-temperature stability supports performance under load, making it a reliable choice for heavy-duty industrial machinery applications.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically ranging from 85% to 99%+ depending on the grade.

Higher-purity grades are standard for cosmetic and food applications to ensure safety and performance. Technical grades serve polymer and lubricant end uses where specific chemical purity is less critical than functional performance.

name: Erucic acid
description:
Erucic acid (CAS 112-86-7 ), commercially available under the trade name Prifrac 2990, is a long-chain C22 monounsaturated fatty acid derived primarily from rapeseed and mustard seed oils.

In plastics processing, it is used as a slip agent in polyolefin films. It migrates to the film surface to reduce friction and prevent blocking during high-speed packaging operations.

Lubricant formulators use it as a feedstock for erucamide and ester derivatives. These provide boundary lubrication in metalworking fluids and gear oils for heavy industrial use.

In personal care, it contributes to emollient and emulsification systems in creams and conditioners. The long-chain fatty acid structure supports texture and spreadability on the skin.

It also serves as a chemical intermediate for the production of surfactants, waxes, and specialty coatings. These applications require high carbon-chain functionality for performance.

The product is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white solid or liquid depending on temperature. It is typically available in technical and oleochemical grades for various uses.

High-purity grades with defined content are available for specialty chemical synthesis. Bulk supply is standard in drums and ISO tanks, with flaked or pastille forms available.

description:

Personal care formulators incorporate it into emollient systems and carrier bases where a non-polar, low-viscosity fluid is needed to improve skin feel. It is also utilized in lubricant and metalworking formulations as a base fluid component.

The chemical functions as a synthetic intermediate for high-performance gear oils and cutting fluids. Upstream oil and gas operations use it as a process chemical in drilling fluid formulations requiring thermal stability at elevated temperatures.

1-Octadecene is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities with bulk availability for large-scale industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial processes.

Purity levels commonly range from 90% to 97%+ depending on application requirements. Higher-purity cuts are available for specialty polymer and fine chemical synthesis where olefin content and isomer profile are critical to process consistency.

name: Oleylamine
description:

Personal care formulators incorporate it as an emulsifier and conditioning agent in hair and skin products. In these applications, it aids the dispersion of oil-phase ingredients for better stability.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a curing co-agent and surface modifier. It improves adhesion and compatibility between polymer matrices and fillers in various industrial settings.

Nanoparticle synthesis represents a growing industrial use for this chemical. It serves as a stabilizing ligand and capping agent controlling particle size and dispersion in specialty coatings and electronics.

Metalworking lubricant formulators incorporate it to enhance film-forming performance and reduce tool wear in cutting and drawing compounds. In personal care manufacturing, it supports emulsion stability and foam modulation.

These products are designed to address androgenetic and diffuse hair thinning in both professional and retail hair care lines. It is frequently combined with other actives such as minoxidil or niacinamide.

name: Aminomethyl propanediol
description:
Aminomethyl propanediol ( CAS 115-69-5 ), commonly abbreviated as AMPD, is a multifunctional amino alcohol used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial coating formulations.

It acts primarily as a pH buffer and neutralizing agent, adjusting and stabilizing formulation pH without introducing unwanted ionic species into the final chemical mixture.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, AMPD neutralizes carbomer and acrylate polymers to build viscosity in creams, lotions, and gels for consumer use.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent in topical preparations where controlled pH stability is critical to product shelf life and overall efficacy.

In waterborne coatings and adhesives, it functions as a neutralizer for resin systems, improving dispersion stability and film formation during the manufacturing process.

Its secondary hydroxyl groups also support moisture retention in formulations where humectancy is a secondary performance requirement alongside precise pH control.

AMPD is supplied as a white crystalline solid or as an aqueous solution, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to USP and BP specifications.

Standard commercial grades include technical and cosmetic grades, with packaging typically ranging from small drums to bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes.

It combines amine-based pH buffering with diol functionality, making it effective for neutralizing acidic resins and stabilizing emulsions in industrial systems.

In architectural and industrial coatings, AEPD neutralizes acrylic and polyurethane dispersions to improve stability, rheology, and film formation for better performance.

Personal care formulators use it as a pH adjuster and emulsifier in creams, lotions, and hair care products where low odor and skin compatibility are priorities.

In water-based inks for packaging and commercial printing, it helps stabilize pigment dispersions and controls pH to maintain print consistency over time.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust cure chemistry and improve compatibility between resin components in complex chemical formulations.

AEPD is supplied as a white crystalline solid or as a concentrated aqueous solution, typically at 85% active content for various industrial applications.

Technical and industrial grades are the most common market forms, with specifications aligned to coatings and personal care end-use requirements and standards.

name: Pentaerythritol
description:
Pentaerythritol (CAS 115-77-5 ) is a polyol building block used across coatings, lubricants, and polymer manufacturing. Its four reactive hydroxyl groups make it a high-functionality platform for esterification and crosslinking reactions.

It is commercially recognized under the abbreviation PE in industrial supply chains. In alkyd resin production, it reacts with fatty acids and phthalic anhydride to produce resins used in decorative and industrial paints.

Esterified with rosin or tall oil, it produces tackifiers and binders for printing inks and adhesives. In synthetic lubricant formulations, its esters deliver high thermal stability in aviation and industrial gear oils.

Performance under extreme temperature is a procurement specification for these lubricants. As a building block for hindered phenol antioxidants, it protects polyolefins, PVC, and rubber compounds during processing.

Pentaerythritol is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Two principal commercial grades are available: mono-pentaerythritol with minimum 98% purity and technical-grade blends containing di-pentaerythritol.

These grades are specified for certain resin and ester applications. Food-contact and FCC -compliant grades are available for applications where regulatory documentation is required for the supply chain.

name: Pentaerythrityl tetrastearate
description:
Pentaerythrityl tetrastearate (CAS 115-83-3 ), commonly abbreviated as PETS and also marketed as Pentaerythritol tetrastearate, is a waxy ester derived from pentaerythritol and stearic acid.

It functions as an internal and external lubricant, mold release agent, and processing aid across polymer, coatings, and personal care manufacturing. In plastics processing, PETS reduces friction between polymer chains.

It is used during extrusion and injection molding, improving throughput and surface finish on engineering thermoplastics such as PVC, ABS, and polyamides. Lubricant formulators incorporate it into high-temperature grease.

Its ester structure provides film stability under load in metalworking compounds. In coatings and adhesive systems, it modifies rheology and improves substrate slip without compromising adhesion.

Personal care manufacturers use it as a structuring agent and emollient in lipsticks, creams, and hair care products where a waxy, non-greasy texture is required for the final formulation.

Pentaerythrityl tetrastearate is supplied as a white to off-white flake or powder. Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly stocked forms for industrial and commercial use.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements for personal care applications. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific grade and supplier requirements.

name: Triphenyl phosphate
description:
Triphenyl phosphate (CAS 115-86-6 ), commonly abbreviated as TPP, is an organophosphate ester used commercially as a flame retardant and plasticizer across a broad range of industrial materials.

It functions by releasing phosphoric acid derivatives during combustion, interrupting the flame cycle without relying on halogenated chemistry. In plastics and polymer compounding, TPP is incorporated into cellulose acetate and PVC.

It is used in engineering resins to meet UL 94 or similar flammability standards while simultaneously improving flexibility. Electronics manufacturers use it as a flame-retardant additive in circuit board laminates and connector housings.

It is also used in encapsulant resins where thermal stability under load is a qualification requirement. Lubricant formulators add TPP to hydraulic fluids and gear oils where fire-resistant performance is specified.

This is particularly important in aerospace and industrial environments with ignition risk. In construction materials, it is used to treat rigid foam insulation and sealant formulations requiring passive fire protection.

Triphenyl phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline solid or flake, with purity grades typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ for industrial and specialty polymer applications.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with high-purity grades available for electronics and aerospace end uses where trace impurity limits are tightly controlled.

name: Linalyl acetate
description:
Linalyl acetate ( CAS 115-95-7 ), also known by its FEMA 2636 designation, is a naturally occurring ester found in lavender, bergamot, and clary sage oils. It is widely sourced as an isolated or synthetic aroma chemical for industrial use.

It delivers a fresh, floral-citrus character that positions it as a core building block in fragrance and flavor formulation. In fine fragrance and personal care, it anchors lavender, fougère, and citrus accords across perfumes and lotions.

Body lotions and hair care products frequently utilize this ester for its aromatic profile. Functional formulations such as fabric softeners and household cleaners rely on it to reinforce clean, floral scent profiles at cost-effective use levels.

In food and beverage flavoring, it contributes bergamot and citrus top notes to confectionery, baked goods, and tea-type flavor systems. It also appears in oral care and functional beverage applications where a light floral-citrus lift is required.

Linalyl acetate is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in both natural-isolated and synthetic grades. Natural material, typically derived from lavender or bergamot fractions, commands a price premium for natural-compliant formulations.

Synthetic material is available to FEMA/GRAS and food-grade standards, with fragrance-grade material meeting standard industry purity benchmarks. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for high-volume manufacturing requirements.

Tris(2-chloroethyl)phosphate (CAS 115-96-8 ), commonly abbreviated as TCEP, is a chlorinated organophosphate flame retardant used across a broad range of polymer and coating systems.

In rigid and flexible polyurethane foams, TCEP imparts flame retardancy to insulation panels, upholstery components, and construction boards where fire performance standards must be met.

Coating formulators incorporate it into intumescent and protective coatings for metal, wood, and concrete substrates in building and construction applications for enhanced safety.

Textile and nonwoven manufacturers apply TCEP-based treatments to technical fabrics used in automotive interiors and protective workwear requiring compliance with fire safety regulations.

Adhesive and sealant producers use it in formulations where both flame retardancy and low-temperature flexibility are required, particularly in aerospace and defense assembly applications.

name: Distearyl thiodipropionate
description:
Distearyl thiodipropionate (CAS 115863-90-6 ), also designated E390 , is a thioester-based secondary antioxidant used to protect polymers, lubricants, and fatty materials from oxidative degradation.

It functions by decomposing hydroperoxides before they can initiate chain-breaking reactions, extending the service life of finished products. In plastics and polymer processing, it is compounded alongside primary antioxidants.

When used with hindered phenolics, it provides synergistic long-term thermal stabilization in polyolefins, PVC, and engineering resins. Lubricant formulators incorporate it to retard oxidative thickening and deposit formation.

This additive is essential for industrial oils and greases exposed to elevated operating temperatures. In food-contact and packaging applications, E390 approval supports its use as an antioxidant in fats, oils, and wax coatings.

Regulatory compliance is a key sourcing requirement for these applications. Personal care manufacturers use it to stabilize emollient-rich formulations and wax-based products against rancidity during shelf life.

Distearyl thiodipropionate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake. Food-grade material conforming to E390 specifications is available for regulated applications, ensuring high purity and safety.

Technical-grade product is also offered for polymer and industrial use where specific food standards are not required. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific grade.

name: Rhodoxanthin
description:
Rhodoxanthin (CAS 116-30-3 ), also designated E161F , is a naturally occurring carotenoid pigment found in certain plant species and used commercially as a colorant and antioxidant.

It delivers red-to-purple hues in food and feed applications where carotenoid-based coloring is preferred over synthetic dyes. In animal feed formulations, it is used to enhance pigmentation.

This additive is vital for egg yolks, poultry skin, and aquaculture species, where color intensity directly affects market value. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a natural colorant where needed.

As an antioxidant, it supports oxidative stability in formulations sensitive to lipid degradation, extending shelf life in fat-containing products. It is essential for agricultural nutrition programs.

It contributes to carotenoid supplementation alongside other xanthophylls in compound feed blends. Rhodoxanthin is typically supplied as a powder or as a standardized concentrate for dispersion.

It is available in feed-grade and food-grade specifications, with purity and carotenoid content defined by the applicable E161F regulatory standards for global compliance.

Buyers should confirm concentration levels and carrier composition when evaluating suppliers, as these vary across the market. Proper storage is required to maintain the potency of the pigment.

name: 2-methylbutyric acid
description:
2-Methylbutyric acid (CAS 116-53-0 ), also known by its FEMA 2695 designation, is a short-chain branched organic acid used primarily as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient.

It delivers a characteristic pungent, cheesy, and fruity odor profile that underpins its demand in both food and personal care formulations. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavor compound.

It contributes to dairy, fruit, and savory taste profiles in products such as cheese analogs, snack seasonings, and processed meat flavors. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products.

These include soaps, shampoos, and fine fragrances where its sharp, fermented note adds depth to complex scent compositions. At controlled concentrations, it also acts as a pH modifier and mild preservative.

In cosmetic formulations, its acidic buffering supports product stability. Flavor houses source it as a building block for synthesizing more complex ester-based aroma chemicals for various industries.

The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in food-grade quality meeting FEMA and FCC standards, as well as technical grade for industrial and fragrance applications.

Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on application volume. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale specialty labs and large-scale manufacturing facilities.

name: PEG-25 PABA
description:
PEG-25 PABA (CAS 116242-27-4 ) is a PEG-esterified derivative of para-aminobenzoic acid used as a water-soluble UV filter in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations. It absorbs UVB radiation, protecting both the end user and the formulation itself from photodegradation.

In sunscreen and daily SPF products, it provides UVB protection within water-based systems where conventional oil-soluble UV filters are unsuitable. Formulators incorporate it into lotions, gels, and sprays to achieve broad water compatibility.

This ingredient allows for high UV absorbance performance without the greasy feel often associated with oil-based alternatives. In hair care products such as leave-on conditioners and styling formulations, it helps shield hair fiber from UV-induced color fading.

It also prevents protein degradation caused by sun exposure, maintaining the structural integrity of the hair. Pharmaceutical topical preparations also use it where photostability of the active ingredient is a critical formulation requirement.

PEG-25 PABA is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous solution for easy handling. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, aligned with requirements for use in leave-on and rinse-off personal care products.

Buyers should confirm concentration, water content, and compliance with regional UV filter approval lists before sourcing. This includes checking Annex VI of the EU Cosmetics Regulation to ensure full regulatory compliance for the intended market.

name: Decabromodiphenyl ether
description:
Decabromodiphenyl ether (CAS 1163-19-5 ), commonly known as DecaBDE or BDE-209, is a brominated flame retardant used across polymer-intensive industries to meet fire safety and regulatory standards.

Decabromodiphenyl oxide is the alternate name most frequently encountered in technical specifications and compliance documentation. It functions by interrupting combustion in the gas phase, enabling treated materials to achieve required flammability ratings.

In plastics and polymer compounding, DecaBDE is incorporated into ABS, HIPS, and polyolefin formulations used in electronic housings, connectors, and cable jacketing.

Textile and upholstery manufacturers apply it to back-coatings on curtains, seating fabrics, and protective workwear where fire performance standards must be met.

Automotive and aerospace component suppliers use it in interior trim materials, wire insulation, and structural composites requiring UL 94 or equivalent certification.

Building and construction applications include flame-retarded panels, insulation facings, and roofing membranes where fire classification is a procurement requirement.

DecaBDE is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as masterbatch pellets for direct compounding use. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 97% or higher.

Bulk supply is available in bags and supersacks, with some suppliers offering pre-compounded concentrates for specific polymer systems to ensure uniform dispersion during manufacturing.

name: Duloxetine

It is sourced by pharmaceutical manufacturers as a bulk API for formulation into branded and generic prescription medications. The primary application is in the manufacture of delayed-release oral capsules.

These capsules target major depressive disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, and diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain. These are product categories with sustained global generic demand for manufacturers.

Contract manufacturers and generic drug developers procure this API to produce enteric-coated pellet formulations. These pellets protect the compound through gastric transit for optimal patient absorption.

Specialty pharma companies also incorporate it into combination or modified-release formats under development. Procurement of this API is subject to ICH Q7 GMP compliance requirements for all suppliers.

Supplier qualification and documentation are central purchasing considerations for this material. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in bulk quantities suited to commercial-scale manufacturing.

It is available in hydrochloride salt form, which is the standard pharmaceutical grade used in registered drug products. Certificates of Analysis aligned with USP and EP monograph specifications are standard.

These documents are expected by qualified buyers to ensure the highest quality standards are met. This ensures the material is suitable for use in finished-dose antidepressant and pain management drug products.

name: Dodecyl gallate
description:
Dodecyl gallate (CAS 1166-52-5 ), also sold as lauryl gallate and approved as E312 , is a lipophilic antioxidant used to protect fats and oils.

Its fat-soluble character makes it effective in applications where water-soluble antioxidants cannot perform, protecting oil-based formulations from oxidative degradation.

In food manufacturing, E312 is used to stabilize edible oils, fats, and fat-containing products such as margarines, shortenings, and fried snack coatings, extending shelf life.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into lipstick bases, creams, and oil-rich emollients where oxidative stability directly affects product shelf life and sensory quality.

In plastics and polymer processing, it functions as a stabilizer against UV-induced and thermal oxidative degradation, protecting polyolefins and similar materials during compounding.

It also finds use in industrial lubricants and technical oils requiring long-term antioxidant protection. Dodecyl gallate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

Standard grades include food-grade material meeting FCC and E312 purity specifications, as well as technical-grade material for polymer and industrial applications.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to bulk sacks for industrial procurement, ensuring reliable supply for various manufacturing requirements.

name: Oleyl Cetyl Alcohol Ethoxylates
description:
Oleyl Cetyl Alcohol Ethoxylates (CAS 116810-31-2 ), also supplied as Oleyl Cetyl Alcohol 25, 50, and 80 EO grades, are nonionic surfactants produced by ethoxylating a blend of C16 and C18 unsaturated fatty alcohols.

They function as emulsifiers, dispersants, and cleaning agents across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations. In home care and industrial cleaning, these ethoxylates act as primary or co-surfactants.

They are used in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and laundry formulations, improving soil lift and rinse performance. Textile and leather processors use them as wetting and scouring agents for better results.

This enables uniform dye penetration and effective removal of processing oils during manufacturing. Personal care formulators incorporate them as emulsifiers and moisturizing agents in various creams and lotions.

They are ideal for conditioning rinses where stable oil-in-water emulsification is required. In agrochemical formulations, they support the dispersion and emulsification of active ingredients in crop protection products.

Oleyl Cetyl Alcohol Ethoxylates are typically supplied as liquid or paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation. Standard commercial grades are defined by EO chain length, such as 25, 50, and 80 moles.

This variety allows formulators to select the specific HLB range for their unique applications. Technical and industrial grades are the primary market offering for these versatile chemical compounds.

name: Tetrachlorophthalic anhydride
description:
Tetrachlorophthalic anhydride (CAS 117-08-8 ), commonly abbreviated as TCPA, is a chlorinated cyclic anhydride used as a reactive flame retardant and chemical intermediate across polymer and coating systems.

Unlike additive flame retardants, it bonds directly into polymer backbones, delivering durable fire resistance without migration losses. In epoxy resin formulations for printed circuit boards, TCPA acts as a curing agent.

It simultaneously imparts halogenated flame retardancy to the cured matrix. Polyester and alkyd resin producers incorporate it as a monomer to build fire-retardant properties into coatings used in construction panels.

Industrial textiles and paper treatment processes use TCPA-derived intermediates to meet flame resistance standards required in packaging and protective fabrics. It also functions as a plasticizer precursor in PVC compounding.

Its chlorine content contributes to both flexibility and reduced flammability in finished profiles and films. Tetrachlorophthalic anhydride is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Bulk quantities are available in fiber drums or multi-wall bags suited for industrial procurement volumes.

Cosmetic and skincare formulators incorporate it into creams and serums for its UV-stabilizing and oxidative protection properties. This is particularly common in high-end anti-aging product lines.

name: Dioctyl phthalate
description:
Dioctyl phthalate (CAS 117-81-7 ), commercially abbreviated as DEHP, is a high-molecular-weight phthalate ester used primarily as a plasticizer to increase flexibility and processability in PVC and other polymer systems.

It remains one of the most established general-purpose plasticizers in industrial formulation, valued for its broad compatibility with vinyl resins and low volatility at processing temperatures.

In PVC compounding, DEHP is incorporated into flexible films, cables, hoses, and flooring materials where sustained flexibility under mechanical stress is required for long-term performance.

The printing and packaging sector uses it as a plasticizer in inks and coatings to prevent cracking and improve adhesion on flexible substrates. It also functions as a solvent and carrier in certain industrial formulations.

In adhesives and sealants, it aids dispersion and controls viscosity during processing. In legacy personal care and cosmetic formulations, DEHP has been used as a film-forming aid and solvent in nail products.

Regulatory restrictions have significantly reduced its use in the cosmetic sector. Dioctyl phthalate is supplied as a clear, oily liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial plasticizer applications. Buyers should confirm regional regulatory compliance requirements before sourcing this chemical.

DEHP is subject to restriction under REACH and other frameworks in certain end-use categories. Proper handling and storage protocols must be followed to ensure safety and environmental compliance.

name: Rabeprazole
description:
Rabeprazole (CAS 117976-89-3 ), also referenced in development literature as E-3810 and LY307640, is a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the treatment of acid-related gastrointestinal disorders.

It functions by irreversibly suppressing gastric acid secretion, making it a target API for finished dosage form manufacturers and generic drug developers worldwide. Rabeprazole is the active ingredient in delayed-release oral solid dosage forms.

These are primarily enteric-coated tablets and capsules formulated to treat conditions such as gastroesophageal reflux disease, peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source the API to produce bioequivalent formulations.

These formulations are intended for regulated markets in the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) also procure it for combination therapies, including H. pylori eradication regimens paired with antibiotics.

Formulators working on pediatric or modified-release formats may source it as an intermediate for specialized dosage development. Rabeprazole is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

The sodium salt form (Rabeprazole Sodium) is the predominant commercial grade. Material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. pharmacopoeial standards, supporting regulatory submissions across major markets.

Packaging is typically offered under inert atmosphere or moisture-controlled conditions to maintain API integrity during storage and transit. This ensures the chemical stability required for long-term pharmaceutical manufacturing.

name: Homosalate
description:
Homosalate ( CAS 118-56-9 ), also known as homomenthyl salicylate or HMS, is an organic UV filter used in sunscreen and sun care formulations. It absorbs UVB radiation in the 295–315 nm range, protecting both the skin and the stability of other active ingredients in a formula.

HMS is a primary UVB-filtering agent in leave-on sun care products including sunscreen lotions, sprays, and daily moisturizers with SPF. Formulators use it as a solvent co-ingredient to dissolve other solid UV filters such as avobenzone.

This improves overall formula clarity and homogeneity across various applications. In color cosmetics and lip products with SPF claims, it contributes UV protection without adding opacity or texture to the final product.

Pharmaceutical topical preparations requiring photostability also incorporate homosalate to prevent UV-induced degradation of light-sensitive actives. This ensures the efficacy of the medicinal components remains intact during exposure.

Homosalate is supplied as a clear, oily liquid suitable for direct incorporation into emulsions and anhydrous systems. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard for personal care and OTC sunscreen applications.

The material is provided with purity typically at or above 97 percent. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with documentation packages aligned to EU Cosmetics Regulation and FDA OTC monograph requirements.

name: Benzyl salicylate
description:
Benzyl salicylate (CAS 118-58-1 ), also recognized under FEMA 2151 , is an ester used across fragrance, cosmetic, and coating formulations. It functions primarily as a UV absorber and fixative.

This chemical extends the stability of light-sensitive ingredients while contributing a mild, balsamic scent character. In personal care and cosmetics, it is incorporated into sunscreens, lotions, and hair products.

It works to absorb UV radiation and protect both the formula and the end user's skin from photodegradation. Fragrance formulators use it as a fixative that slows the evaporation of top notes.

This improves the longevity of fine fragrances and functional perfumery in soaps and detergents. Coating and adhesive manufacturers add it to UV-stabilized systems where degradation must be controlled.

In these systems, light-induced degradation of the binder or colorant is mitigated. In printing inks and packaging coatings, it supports color retention and formula stability under prolonged light exposure.

Benzyl salicylate is supplied as a clear, pale liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Standard grades include cosmetic and fragrance-grade material meeting IFRA and industry purity specifications.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial coating and ink applications. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale manufacturing requirements across various sectors.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into sunscreen and cosmetic formulations for its UV-absorbing properties, helping protect both the end product and the consumer from UV degradation.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an intermediate and carrier solvent in topical preparations and medicated products. It is valued for its stability and compatibility in these systems.

In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a UV stabilizer and antioxidant additive to extend the service life of finished materials by preventing degradation from light exposure.

Ethyl salicylate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. Food-grade material is available in compliance with FEMA standards.

Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are also offered to meet the requirements of UV stabilizer and personal care end uses, ensuring high quality for industrial applications.

name: Maltol

This occurs during vulcanization and in-service flexing. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to stabilize resin systems against discoloration and viscosity drift during storage and cure cycles.

In plastics processing, it protects polyolefins and engineering resins during high-temperature extrusion and injection molding. This ensures the structural integrity and appearance of the final plastic components.

4,4'-methylenebis(2,6-di-tert-butylphenol) is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical and food-contact grades are available, with the specific designation relevant for buyers sourcing into food-packaging.

name: Trinitrotoluene
description:
Trinitrotoluene (CAS 118-96-7 ), commonly known as TNT, is a high-explosive compound used as a benchmark energetic material in military and commercial blasting applications.

Its reliable detonation characteristics and chemical stability during storage make it a reference standard against which other explosives are measured for performance and safety.

In defense and munitions manufacturing, TNT is used as a melt-cast explosive fill for artillery shells, bombs, and warheads, either alone or in combination with RDX or HMX.

These combinations form composite explosives such as Composition B and Pentolite. Commercial mining and demolition operations use TNT-based formulations where controlled fragmentation is required.

It also serves as a primary reference material in explosive equivalency calculations, allowing engineers to express the yield of other energetic materials in TNT equivalent units.

Research and testing facilities procure it as a calibration standard for blast modeling and detonation studies. TNT is supplied as cast solid blocks, pellets, or flakes.

Molten liquid form is available for industrial filling operations. Military-specification grades dominate procurement, with purity requirements typically governed by defense standards such as MIL-DTL-248 .

Supply is subject to strict regulatory licensing, and sourcing is handled through authorized defense contractors and licensed explosive distributors to ensure compliance and safety.

name: Copper carbonate
description:
Copper carbonate ( CAS 1184-64-1 ), also known as cupric carbonate, is an inorganic copper salt used across agriculture, water treatment, and industrial processing. It functions primarily as a copper source for biocidal, nutritional, and chemical applications.

In agriculture, it serves as a fungicide and soil amendment, supplying bioavailable copper to correct deficiencies in crops and livestock feed formulations. This ensures optimal growth and health in various agricultural settings.

Water treatment operations use it to control algae and microbial growth in reservoirs, irrigation systems, and aquaculture environments. It provides a reliable method for maintaining water quality and preventing biological fouling.

In mining and metallurgy, it acts as a precursor in copper refining and ore flotation processes where copper chemistry must be precisely introduced. This allows for efficient extraction and processing of valuable mineral resources.

As a pigment, it provides stable blue-green coloration in ceramic glazes, specialty coatings, and artist materials. Its chemical stability makes it a preferred choice for long-lasting aesthetic applications in various industries.

Copper carbonate is supplied as a fine powder, typically in shades of green reflecting its mineral form. Standard grades include technical, feed-grade, and agricultural-grade, with specifications varying by copper content.

Quality is commonly expressed as minimum assay percentages to meet specific industrial requirements. Bulk packaging in bags or drums is standard, with smaller quantities available for laboratory or formulation use.

name: Vinylsulfonic acid
description:
Vinylsulfonic acid (CAS 1184-84-5 ), also known as Ethylenesulfonic acid, is a reactive sulfonic acid monomer used to introduce permanent anionic functionality into polymer chains. It enables formulators and polymer chemists to engineer surface charge and ionic character.

This monomer allows for the direct integration of hydrophilicity into copolymer structures. In textile and leather processing, it is copolymerized into finishing agents that improve dye uptake and substrate wettability without washing out over time.

Water treatment polymers incorporate this acid to produce scale inhibitors and dispersants that perform across a broad pH range. Paper manufacturers use it in surface sizing and retention aid formulations where controlled charge density is critical.

The chemical is essential for sheet formation and coating adhesion in the paper industry. In specialty plastics, it functions as a comonomer in ion-exchange resins and antistatic coatings where permanent sulfonate groups are required.

Vinylsulfonic acid is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with 25% and 50% concentrations being the most commercially standard. Technical grade is the primary market offering, suitable for industrial polymerization and formulation use.

The product is handled according to rigorous industrial safety protocols to ensure stability. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes depending on volume requirements, providing flexibility for various manufacturing scales and logistics needs.

This chemical improves durability and adhesion to glass, metal, and mineral substrates. The electronics industry uses it to deposit hydrophobic, dielectric thin films on semiconductor components and circuit boards.

In adhesives and elastomers, it contributes to moisture-cure systems and improves the bond strength between polymer matrices and inorganic fillers. This ensures high performance in demanding industrial environments.

Personal care formulators incorporate MTMS-derived silicones to achieve water-resistant, smooth-feel finishes in hair and skin products. It is a versatile component for creating high-quality consumer goods.

It acts as a pH buffer and moisture-retaining agent in formulations where precise ionic balance and skin compatibility are required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, NAG serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active compounds.

Its unique properties support water retention in the stratum corneum. It is also evaluated in amino acid-based infusion solutions and nutraceutical preparations targeting metabolic support pathways for various health applications.

name: Glyceryl distearate
description:
Glyceryl distearate (CAS 1188-58-5 ), also known as glycerol distearate, is a diester of glycerol and stearic acid used as an emulsifier and rheology modifier across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems while contributing texture and consistency to finished products. In personal care, it functions as a co-emulsifier and thickener in creams, lotions, and body butters.

This ingredient helps to build viscosity and improve skin feel without heavy residue. Food manufacturers incorporate it as an emulsifier in fat-based systems, including confectionery coatings and bakery shortenings.

In these applications, it controls fat crystallization and improves product texture. In plastics processing, it acts as a lubricant and plasticizer that reduces melt viscosity and improves surface release during extrusion.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to modify rheology and improve substrate wetting in wax-based and hot-melt systems. Glyceryl distearate is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid.

It is available in flake, bead, or powder form depending on the supplier and intended application. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly traded for various global markets.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial polymer and coatings applications. Purity grades typically align with FCC and Ph.Eur. standards for regulated end-use markets.

name: 1,3-butyleneglycol dimethacrylate

It introduces covalent network formation during curing, improving hardness, chemical resistance, and dimensional stability in finished materials. In UV- and peroxide-cured coatings, it acts as a crosslinking comonomer.

This monomer controls cure speed and final film hardness without requiring solvent. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to build cohesive strength and improve resistance to solvents and elevated temperatures.

In printing inks, particularly energy-curable systems, it reduces viscosity while contributing to network density. This enables faster press speeds and sharper print definition in industrial applications.

Polymer and resin manufacturers also use it as a building block for acrylic sheet and dental composites. It is essential for specialty molding compounds where controlled crosslink density is a key performance variable.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically with an inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial use.

This compound protects lipid-containing products from oxidative degradation. Compared to alpha-tocopherol, its stronger antioxidant activity in certain lipid matrices makes it a preferred choice for formulators targeting oxidative stability.

In food manufacturing, E309 is used to extend the shelf life of oils, fats, and fat-containing products by inhibiting rancidity. Animal feed producers incorporate it to preserve the oxidative quality of feed ingredients.

This additive supports antioxidant status in livestock nutrition. Cosmetic formulators use it in skin creams, serums, and hair care products where lipid oxidation would otherwise compromise product stability and shelf life.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers apply it as an antioxidant excipient in oil-based drug delivery systems and softgel formulations. Delta-tocopherol is supplied as a viscous oil, typically in concentrated or mixed tocopherol extract form.

It is available in food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with some suppliers offering material compliant with FCC or Ph. Eur. standards. Bulk supply is standard in drums or IBC containers.

Topical pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulators use it as a counterirritant active and fragrance fixative in muscle rubs, liniments, and analgesic creams for pain relief applications.

Coatings and ink manufacturers incorporate it as a UV stabilizer and solvent carrier, where its absorption profile helps protect substrates from photodegradation and environmental wear.

In adhesives and sealant systems, it also contributes antimicrobial preservation, extending shelf life in moisture-sensitive formulations and preventing degradation during long-term storage.

Methyl salicylate is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Food-grade material meeting FCC and FEMA specifications is standard for flavor and oral care applications.

name: Benzoin
description:
Benzoin (CAS 119-53-9 ), also known by its FEMA 2132 designation in flavor applications, is an aromatic carbonyl compound sourced from natural resin or produced synthetically for industrial use.

It functions primarily as a photoinitiator in UV-curable systems and as a fragrance and flavoring ingredient across multiple industries. In coatings, adhesives, and printing inks, it acts as a photoinitiator.

By absorbing UV radiation, it triggers free-radical polymerization to cure resin systems rapidly without heat. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a flavoring agent to impart sweet, balsamic, and vanilla-adjacent notes.

These applications are common in confectionery, baked goods, and beverages. Personal care formulators incorporate it into perfumes, soaps, and cosmetic preparations for its warm, resinous fragrance character.

In polymer processing, it also functions as an antioxidant and stabilizer, protecting materials during high-temperature compounding. Benzoin is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

It is available in food-grade quality aligned with FEMA specifications and in technical grade for industrial photoinitiator and polymer stabilization applications. Purity levels of 98% and above are standard.

name: Benzophenone

The compound absorbs UV radiation to trigger cross-linking and deliver fast, durable surface finishes. Polymer formulators incorporate it as a UV stabilizer in plastics to slow photodegradation and extend service life.

The compound also functions as a fragrance fixative in select industrial and consumer formulations. In these specific applications, its regulatory status governs the permitted use levels for manufacturers.

description:
Ethyl linolenate (CAS 1191-41-9 ) is the ethyl ester form of alpha-linolenic acid (ALA), an omega-3 fatty acid. It functions as a bioavailable lipid ingredient used across nutraceutical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it serves as a concentrated omega-3 source in softgel and encapsulated formats. Precise fatty acid profiling is critical for these applications to ensure consistent product efficacy.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin-conditioning emulsions and serums. Its lipid profile supports barrier restoration and moisture retention in finished products, making it a versatile ingredient for high-end skincare lines.

Pharmaceutical developers use this compound as a reference standard or active lipid component in drug delivery systems. It is particularly effective in systems targeting omega-3 enrichment for various therapeutic applications.

name: Sodium myristyl sulfate
description:
Sodium myristyl sulfate ( CAS 1191-50-0 ), also known as sodium tetradecyl sulfate, is an anionic surfactant derived from myristic acid. It delivers strong foaming, emulsification, and cleansing performance across pharmaceutical and personal care applications.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, facial cleansers, and body washes where dense, stable foam is a key performance requirement.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an emulsifying and dispersing agent in topical creams, ointments, and gel formulations. It also appears in specialty cleansing systems where controlled degreasing is needed.

This ingredient is utilized without the harshness associated with shorter-chain sulfates. In cosmetic emulsion development, its C14 chain length positions it between lauryl and cetyl sulfates.

This specific molecular structure gives formulators a mid-range option for adjusting foam texture and skin feel. Sodium myristyl sulfate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or paste.

name: Pentaglyme
description:
Pentaglyme (CAS 1191-87-3 ), also known as 2,5,8,11,14,17-Hexaoxaoctadecane, is a high-boiling, aprotic polyether solvent used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial cleaning formulations.

description:

Cosmetic formulators incorporate the material into serums, creams, and spot-treatment products targeting hyperpigmentation, melasma, and uneven skin tone. It is used as a key active in OTC brightening formulations where melanin synthesis inhibition is the targeted mechanism.

description:

The chemical is essential for producing high-performance hoses and other industrial rubber goods. Some industrial formulations use MBTS as a biocide or preservation agent in latex systems to inhibit microbial degradation during storage.

MBTS is supplied as a pale yellow powder or as pre-dispersed granules and masterbatch forms. These formats are suited for automated dosing in rubber compounding lines to ensure precision and safety in the workplace.

name: Catechol
description:
Catechol (CAS 120-80-9 ), also known as Pelagol Grey C and oxyphenic acid, is an aromatic diol used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing. It functions primarily as an antioxidant and intermediate.

In cosmetics and hair care, it acts as an oxidative coupler in permanent hair dye formulations, producing grey and dark tones when combined with primary intermediates. It is essential for achieving specific color profiles.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a key synthetic intermediate in the production of catecholamine-based active ingredients. This includes certain cardiovascular and neurological compounds used in modern medicine.

In the textile and leather industries, it contributes to dyeing processes and tanning formulations where controlled oxidative chemistry is required. It ensures consistent results in industrial chemical processing.

As a stabilizer and antioxidant, it is incorporated into industrial formulations to inhibit oxidative degradation in rubber and polymer processing. This extends the lifespan and durability of various synthetic materials.

The product is supplied as white to off-white crystalline flakes or powder. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial and dyestuff applications, while higher-purity grades are available for specific needs.

These higher-purity grades are designed to meet pharmaceutical intermediate specifications. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on the specific application requirements of the client.

name: Cyclopentanone
description:
Cyclopentanone (CAS 120-92-3 ), also known commercially as adipic ketone and by FEMA 3910 , is a cyclic ketone used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient across food and personal care applications.

Its characteristic mint-like, earthy, and slightly woody odor profile makes it a valued building block for flavor and fragrance houses sourcing aroma chemicals for diverse formulations.

In food flavoring, this compound is used at trace levels to contribute nuanced background notes in savory, dairy, and roasted flavor systems. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products.

These applications include soaps, lotions, and hair care, where it adds depth to woody and green accords. It also functions as an intermediate in the synthesis of more complex aroma molecules.

This versatility makes it highly relevant to flavor and fragrance manufacturers operating their own chemical synthesis programs. The material is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

These formats are suited to industrial flavor and fragrance production. It is available in flavor-grade quality meeting FEMA and relevant purity specifications for use in food-contact applications.

Buyers should confirm compliance documentation, including CoA and purity levels, when sourcing for regulated flavor applications. This ensures the material meets all necessary safety and quality standards.

name: 2-imidazolidinone
description:
2-Imidazolidinone (CAS 120-93-4 ), commercially known as ethylene urea, is a cyclic urea derivative used as a reactive intermediate and functional additive across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It acts as a building block for synthesis and a surface-active agent in formulation chemistry. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients and heterocyclic scaffolds.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair and skin products for its film-forming and conditioning properties. It is particularly effective in curl-retention and smoothing treatments for high-end cosmetic lines.

The compound functions as a catalyst precursor and reactant in the production of specialty resins and textile finishing agents. It is widely utilized in the creation of wrinkle-resistant fabric treatments for the garment industry.

In biotechnology applications, it supports surface modification processes where controlled wetting is critical. Substrate interaction is essential to assay or coating performance in advanced laboratory settings.

This chemical is available as a white crystalline solid, typically supplied in powder or granular form. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity pharmaceutical-grade material for various uses.

Purity levels commonly range from 98% to 99% or higher depending on the specific application requirements. Packaging options range from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk metric ton supply for industrial procurement.

name: Vitamin K
description:
Vitamin K (CAS 12001-79-5 ), also known as Phytol Naphthoquinone, is a fat-soluble vitamin used across food, pharmaceutical, and animal nutrition industries. It functions as a coagulation-supporting nutrient and antioxidant stabilizer in finished formulations.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, it is incorporated into capsules, tablets, and fortified products targeting bone health and cardiovascular nutrition. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in injectable and oral dosage forms.

In animal feed and premix production, it is added to poultry, swine, and aquaculture feeds to meet nutritional specification requirements. Food producers also apply it in fortified dairy and infant formula products where regulatory nutrient thresholds must be met.

Vitamin K is supplied as a fine powder or oil-based concentrate, depending on the intended formulation matrix. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications.

The material is also available in food-grade specifications compliant with FCC standards. Feed-grade material is available for agricultural and premix applications, typically in stabilized powder form for blending compatibility.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and purity for all industrial applications. We provide comprehensive documentation and technical support to meet the rigorous demands of global chemical and nutritional manufacturing sectors.

name: Clopidogrel bisulfate
description:
Clopidogrel bisulfate (CAS 120202-66-6 ), also marketed under the salt forms clopidogrel hydrogen sulfate, is the active pharmaceutical ingredient form of clopidogrel used in the manufacture of antiplatelet medications.

It is the commercially dominant salt form selected for finished dose production due to its stability profile and processability in solid oral dosage manufacturing. Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as the API in tablet formulations.

These formulations target cardiovascular indications, where precise polymorph control and purity are critical to regulatory submission. Contract development and manufacturing organizations source it as a starting point for 75 mg oral solid dose products.

This dosage represents the most common commercial strength globally. Formulators working on combination cardiovascular products also specify this salt form when developing fixed-dose combinations requiring compatibility with standard tablet excipients.

Clopidogrel bisulfate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications aligned with USP and EP monograph requirements for global compliance.

Polymorph Form I is the standard commercially supplied crystalline form for this material. Packaging typically ranges from small analytical quantities through multi-kilogram lots to support clinical batch manufacturing.

These supply options are designed to facilitate both research and commercial-scale production. The material maintains high stability and purity standards necessary for the rigorous demands of the pharmaceutical industry.

name: Fluorozirconic acid
description:
Fluorozirconic acid (CAS 12021-95-3 ), also known as hexafluorozirconic acid, is an inorganic acid used industrially as a surface treatment and metal finishing agent. It deposits zirconium-based conversion coatings on metal substrates.

This chemical provides corrosion resistance and adhesion promotion without chromium-based chemistry. In metal pretreatment, it forms thin zirconium oxide conversion coatings on aluminum, steel, and galvanized surfaces prior to painting.

It serves as a direct chromate-free alternative increasingly required by automotive and appliance OEMs. Electronics manufacturers use it for etching and surface conditioning of metal components where controlled oxide layer formation is critical.

The acid is essential to downstream bonding processes in high-tech manufacturing. In water treatment, it functions as a pH-regulating and complexing agent in specific process streams to maintain chemical balance.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a fixing and surface modification agent to improve fiber bonding and finish durability. This versatility makes it a staple in modern industrial chemical inventories.

Fluorozirconic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 45% concentration being the most commonly traded commercial form. Technical grade is the standard market offering for most industrial applications.

Concentration and purity specifications vary by application requirement to meet specific client needs. Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or drums is the typical packaging format for industrial buyers globally.

name: Silicomolybdic acid
description:
Silicomolybdic acid (CAS 12027-12-2 ), also known as 12-molybdosilicic acid, is a heteropolyacid used industrially as a catalyst and analytical reagent. Its strong acidity and oxidizing character make it a functional building block in catalyst systems.

It serves as a reliable detection agent in laboratory and process environments. In analytical chemistry and pharmaceutical quality control, it serves as a colorimetric reagent for detecting silica, phosphates, and reducing agents in solution.

Catalyst manufacturers use it as a precursor to molybdenum-based catalysts applied in oxidation and acid-catalyzed reactions. In mining and metals processing, it supports the selective precipitation and quantification of specific ions.

This material is essential during ore analysis and process monitoring. Water treatment laboratories employ it for silica determination in boiler water, cooling systems, and ultrapure water quality programs.

Silicomolybdic acid is supplied as a yellow-green crystalline solid or as an aqueous solution. Solution concentrations are typically standardized for analytical use to ensure consistency in industrial applications.

Technical and reagent-grade specifications are the most commonly available. Reagent grade meets purity requirements for laboratory and analytical applications, ensuring high performance in sensitive chemical environments.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory procurement to bulk quantities for industrial catalyst or process chemistry supply. This flexibility allows for efficient distribution across various sectors.

name: Silicotungstic acid
description:
Silicotungstic acid (CAS 12027-38-2 ), also known as 12-tungstosilicic acid, is a heteropolyacid used industrially as a strong acid catalyst and analytical reagent.

Its combination of high proton activity and thermal stability makes it a practical choice for acid-catalyzed synthesis and precipitation-based analytical workflows.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a precipitating agent for alkaloid identification and quantification in quality control testing processes.

Catalyst applications include acid-catalyzed esterification, alkylation, and condensation reactions where a recoverable solid acid is preferred over mineral acids.

Research and fine chemical producers use it as a catalyst precursor for supported heteropolyacid systems on silica or alumina carriers for various industrial uses.

It also serves in electrochemical and materials research as a proton-conducting component in membrane and electrode formulations for advanced technology.

Silicotungstic acid is supplied as a crystalline solid or powder, typically as the hydrated form. Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available.

Purity specifications range from technical quality up to ACS reagent grade for analytical applications. Packaging is offered in laboratory-scale or bulk quantities.

name: Ammonium heptamolybdate
description:
Ammonium heptamolybdate (CAS 12027-67-7 ), commonly abbreviated as AHM, is an inorganic molybdenum salt used as a primary source of soluble molybdenum across industrial and agricultural processes.

It functions as a catalyst precursor, corrosion inhibitor, and micronutrient source depending on the application sector. In agriculture, AHM is used to formulate molybdenum-based micronutrient fertilizers.

These foliar sprays are essential where molybdenum deficiency in soil limits nitrogen fixation in leguminous crops. Catalyst manufacturers use it as a precursor in the production of hydrodesulfurization catalysts.

It is also used for selective oxidation catalysts for petroleum refining. In water treatment and industrial cooling systems, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor by forming a protective oxide layer on metal surfaces.

This process reduces pipe and equipment degradation. Mining and metal processing operations use AHM in analytical reagent applications, including phosphate and silicate determination in ore and process water testing.

Ammonium heptamolybdate is supplied as a white to slightly greenish crystalline powder or granule. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and reagent or analytical grade for high-specification applications.

Purity levels typically range from 99% upward. Agricultural and industrial grades are available in bulk packaging, with specifications aligned to customer process requirements and industrial standards.

name: Sodium stannate trihydrate
description:
Sodium stannate trihydrate (CAS 12027-70-2 ), also sold as sodium stannate, is an inorganic tin salt used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor, flame retardant additive, and surface treatment agent.

It functions by depositing tin-based compounds onto substrates or into formulations to modify surface chemistry and improve material performance across various industrial sectors.

In electroplating and electronics manufacturing, it serves as a tin source in alkaline plating baths, producing uniform, solderable tin coatings on metal components and circuits.

Textile processors apply it as a mordant and flame-retardant treatment for natural fibers, particularly wool, improving both dye fixation and fire resistance in a single process step.

In water treatment, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor for metal pipework and industrial cooling systems. Paper and packaging manufacturers use it as a surface sizing agent.

In specialty coatings, controlled tin deposition improves barrier properties. Sodium stannate trihydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid for easy handling.

Technical and industrial grades are the most common commercial forms, with purity levels typically specified at 95% or higher to ensure consistent performance in chemical processes.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on application volume requirements. Proper storage in a cool, dry environment is recommended to maintain product stability.

name: Aluminum calcium oxide
description:
Aluminum calcium oxide (CAS 12042-68-1 ) is an inorganic mineral compound used across construction, water treatment, and metallurgical processing. It functions primarily as a binder, flocculant, and flux, depending on the application and grade.

In construction, it is the active phase in calcium aluminate cements, which deliver rapid strength gain and high-temperature resistance in refractory castables, industrial flooring, and sewer infrastructure.

Water treatment facilities use it as a coagulant and flocculant to remove suspended solids, phosphates, and turbidity from municipal and industrial effluents. It is essential for maintaining water quality standards.

In steelmaking and foundry operations, it acts as a slag conditioner and flux, improving melt fluidity and facilitating impurity removal during refining. This ensures high-quality metal production and efficiency.

Specialty refractory manufacturers also incorporate it into monolithic linings and kiln furniture formulations that must withstand sustained thermal cycling. Its durability makes it a preferred choice for extreme environments.

Aluminum calcium oxide is supplied as powder or granules, with particle size and alumina-to-calcium ratio varying by application. Established grades include technical and refractory grades for various industries.

Cement-grade material conforms to standards such as ASTM C1157 or equivalent. High-purity grades are available for demanding refractory and water treatment applications where consistent phase composition is critical.

These high-purity options ensure process performance and reliability in sensitive industrial systems. The material remains a versatile component in modern chemical engineering and infrastructure development.

name: Aluminum chlorohydrate
description:
Aluminum chlorohydrate (CAS 12042-91-0 ), commonly abbreviated as ACH, is an inorganic aluminum salt used as a coagulant and flocculant across municipal and industrial water treatment systems.

It should not be confused with Polyaluminium Chloride (PAC), which represents a broader family of aluminum chloride hydroxide compounds with varying basicity in industrial applications.

In personal care manufacturing, ACH functions as the active antiperspirant ingredient in topical formulations. In drinking water and wastewater treatment, it destabilizes suspended particles and colloids.

This enables efficient sedimentation and filtration at lower dosage rates than alum. Antiperspirant roll-ons, sticks, and aerosols rely on ACH as the active agent that temporarily reduces sweat gland output.

It is the most commonly specified active in OTC antiperspirant products. Pulp and paper producers use ACH for pitch control and retention aid applications during sheet formation to improve efficiency.

Industrial effluent treatment operations also apply it for phosphate removal and turbidity reduction. ACH is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous solution at various concentrations.

It is also available as a spray-dried powder for personal care applications. Cosmetic and antiperspirant grades are available to meet USP and personal care industry specifications.

Technical and water treatment grades are supplied in bulk liquid form for large-volume industrial procurement. These grades ensure compliance-driven discharge scenarios for municipal facilities.

name: Barium titanate
description:
Barium titanate (CAS 12047-27-7 ), also known as barium metatitanate and abbreviated as BTO, is a piezoelectric ceramic material central to the electronics and advanced materials industries.

It converts mechanical stress into electrical signals and vice versa, making it the functional core of sensors, actuators, and capacitor components in various industrial sectors.

In electronics manufacturing, BTO is the primary dielectric material in multilayer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), where its high permittivity enables compact, high-capacity components for circuits.

Piezoelectric transducers and ultrasonic sensors rely on BTO's electromechanical response for precision signal conversion in medical, industrial, and sonar equipment applications worldwide.

In plastics and polymer compounding, BTO is incorporated as a functional filler to impart dielectric and piezoelectric properties to flexible composite films used in smart packaging.

Emerging water treatment applications use BTO-based photocatalytic systems to drive pollutant degradation under UV or mechanical activation, showcasing the material's versatility in green tech.

Barium titanate is supplied as a fine ceramic powder, with particle size and crystalline phase specified to match end-use performance requirements for high-purity electronic and technical grades.

Purity levels typically range from 99% upward for electronic applications. Bulk and smaller research-quantity packaging are both available through industrial ceramic and specialty chemical channels.

name: Polyglyceryl-2 triisostearate
description:
Polyglyceryl-2 triisostearate (CAS 120486-24-0 ), sold under trade names including Neorex PGIS, Salacos 43V, and Cithrol PG23IS, is a polyglycerol ester of isostearic acid.

It is used as an emulsifier and texture modifier in cosmetic and industrial formulations. It enables stable oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems while contributing to skin feel and product consistency.

In color cosmetics, it functions as a primary emulsifier and dispersant in lipsticks, foundations, and pressed powders. It helps bind pigments uniformly and improves payoff for the end user.

Skincare formulators use it in anhydrous balms and oil-based serums where it modifies rheology. It delivers a non-greasy, moisturizing skin feel that is highly valued in premium personal care products.

In suncare products, it stabilizes UV filter dispersions and supports water-resistant film formation. Coatings and adhesive applications utilize it as a dispersing agent for pigments and fillers.

This material is effective in specialty resin systems where high-performance dispersion is required. It is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or semi-solid at ambient temperature for easy handling.

It is available in cosmetic-grade quality, meeting the purity requirements expected for personal care raw material supply. Standard pack sizes range from drums to IBCs for various needs.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement to ensure consistent supply chains. This versatile ester remains a staple for formulators seeking reliable emulsification and pigment wetting.
