name: Nickel hydroxide
description:
Nickel hydroxide (CAS 12054-48-7 ), also referred to commercially as Green nickel oxide, is an inorganic nickel compound used primarily as an active electrode material and as a precursor in nickel-based chemical synthesis.

Its role spans energy storage, surface treatment, and catalyst manufacturing across several industrial sectors. In rechargeable battery production, it serves as the primary cathode active material in nickel-metal hydride and nickel-cadmium cells.

This material directly determines charge capacity and cycle performance in energy storage systems. Electroplating and surface finishing operations use it as a nickel ion source for depositing corrosion-resistant coatings on automotive and industrial components.

In catalyst manufacturing, it acts as a precursor for nickel-based hydrogenation and reforming catalysts used in petrochemical processing. Mining and metallurgical refining operations also use it as an intermediate in industrial processes.

These operations involve converting nickel ore concentrates into refined nickel salts or metal. Nickel hydroxide is supplied as a fine green powder, with particle size and surface area specifications varying by application.

Battery-grade material carries tighter controls than technical-grade for specific manufacturing needs. Battery-grade and technical-grade are the primary commercial distinctions for industrial procurement and supply chain management.

Battery-grade product is held to stricter purity and morphology standards to ensure optimal performance. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with packaging typically in drums or bulk bags for safe transport.

name: Ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate
description:
Ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate (CAS 12054-85-2 ), commonly abbreviated as AHM and also marketed as ammonium molybdate tetrahydrate, is a water-soluble molybdenum salt used as a primary source of molybdenum across industrial, agricultural, and analytical applications.

It delivers concentrated molybdenum content in a stable, handleable crystalline form suited to both large-scale manufacturing and precision formulation. In water treatment and industrial cooling systems, AHM functions as a corrosion inhibitor.

It forms a protective oxide layer on metal surfaces to reduce pipe and equipment degradation. Agricultural formulators use it as a molybdenum micronutrient source in fertilizers and foliar sprays, where molybdenum deficiency directly limits crop yield.

In industrial cleaning and surface treatment, it is incorporated into passivation and anti-corrosion formulations for metal processing lines. Pharmaceutical and laboratory applications include its use as a reagent in analytical chemistry.

It is particularly effective in phosphate and silicate detection assays. Ammonium heptamolybdate tetrahydrate is supplied as white to slightly greenish crystalline powder or granules, ensuring ease of use in various manufacturing environments.

Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels ranging from industrial-grade to ACS and analytical-grade specifications. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers.

Smaller packaging is also available for laboratory and formulation use. This versatility makes it a staple chemical for diverse sectors ranging from heavy industry to specialized scientific research and agricultural development.

name: Sodium stannate
description:
Sodium stannate (CAS 12058-66-1 ), also known as disodium tin trioxide, is an inorganic tin salt used industrially as a catalyst precursor, flame retardant additive, and surface treatment agent.

It delivers tin chemistry in a water-soluble, alkaline form suited to wet processing and formulation environments. In textile and leather finishing, it functions as a mordant and weighting agent.

This chemical improves dye uptake and fabric density in wool and silk processing. Polymer and plastics formulators incorporate it as a stabilizer and flame retardant additive for various industrial uses.

Its tin content contributes to char formation and thermal stability in PVC and related systems. The paper industry uses it in surface sizing and coating formulations to improve wet strength and stability.

In construction-related coatings and cement chemistry, it acts as a setting modifier and corrosion-inhibiting additive. These specialty cementitious systems benefit from its unique chemical properties.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granular solid. It is available in anhydrous form and as the trihydrate, with the anhydrous grade preferred for moisture sensitivity.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for most buyers. Purity specifications typically range from 95% to 99%+ depending on the specific application requirements of the client.

name: Erbium oxide
description:
Erbium oxide (CAS 12061-16-4 ), also known as erbia, is a rare earth oxide used primarily as a pink-to-rose colorant and dopant material across specialty manufacturing sectors.

Its stable coloring properties and optical characteristics make it a sought-after input for glass, ceramics, and advanced material formulations for industrial applications.

In cosmetics and personal care, erbia functions as a pigment in mineral makeup, eyeshadow, and blush formulations where a soft pink hue is required for the final product.

Glass and specialty optical manufacturers incorporate it to impart a distinctive rose tint to decorative glassware, lenses, and glazes used in high-end manufacturing processes.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, erbium oxide contributes color stability in specialty pigment blends requiring inorganic rare earth colorants for durability and performance.

The textile and paper industries use it in dyeing auxiliaries and specialty coatings where conventional organic colorants are unsuitable for high-temperature or chemically aggressive conditions.

Erbium oxide is supplied as a fine powder, typically in high-purity grades ranging from 99% to 99.999% (5N), with purity tier being the primary specification buyers evaluate.

Technical and research grades are the most commonly traded forms, with particle size specifications available for application-specific requirements and bulk industrial procurement needs.

name: Sodium toluenesulfonate
description:
Sodium toluenesulfonate (CAS 12068-03-0 ), also known as sodium tosylate, is an aromatic sulfonate salt used across formulation and process chemistry as a hydrotrope and solubilizing agent.

It improves the water solubility of poorly soluble actives and surfactant systems, enabling stable, high-performance liquid formulations. In personal care and household cleaning products, it functions as a hydrotrope.

This chemical reduces viscosity and improves clarity in surfactant-heavy formulations such as shampoos, liquid detergents, and body washes. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solubilizer and counterion source.

In API salt formation, it improves bioavailability and processability of active compounds. In agrochemical formulations, it supports the dispersion and wetting of active ingredients in suspension concentrates.

It is also utilized in emulsifiable concentrates. Industrial process chemistry employs it as a coupling agent and phase modifier in sulfonation and synthesis workflows to ensure efficient chemical reactions.

Sodium toluenesulfonate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Technical and industrial grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher for most uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. specifications is available for regulated applications requiring documented quality standards and high levels of material consistency.

name: Basic copper carbonate
description:
Basic copper carbonate (CAS 12069-69-1 ), also known as copper carbonate hydroxide, is an inorganic copper salt supplied as a fine green powder. It functions as a source of bioavailable copper and as a biocidal active across multiple industrial sectors.

In agriculture, it serves as a fungicide and seed treatment agent, protecting cereal and vegetable crops against soil-borne pathogens before germination. Animal feed manufacturers incorporate it as a copper mineral supplement to meet livestock nutritional requirements.

In antifouling and wood preservation coatings, it acts as the primary biocidal component, inhibiting microbial and algal growth on marine and structural surfaces. Building and construction formulators use it in pigment applications.

It is also utilized as a corrosion-inhibiting additive in protective coatings. Basic copper carbonate is supplied as a fine green powder in technical and feed-grade specifications to meet various industrial needs.

Feed-grade material is produced to meet purity standards suitable for animal nutrition applications, while technical grade serves industrial coating and preservation uses. Quality is maintained through rigorous production controls.

Bulk packaging in bags and bulk containers is standard, with copper content typically specified as a key quality parameter. This ensures consistency for large-scale manufacturing and agricultural distribution across global markets.

name: Canola oil
description:
Canola oil (CAS 120962-03-0 ), also sold as rapeseed oil or rape oil, is a low-erucic acid vegetable oil derived from select Brassica cultivars. It functions as an edible fat, emollient carrier, and industrial lubricant base across multiple manufacturing sectors.

In food production, it serves as a cooking and frying medium, salad dressing base, and ingredient in margarines, shortenings, and baked goods where a neutral flavor profile is required.

Personal care formulators use it as a skin-conditioning carrier in creams, lotions, and hair treatments, where its spreadability supports even active ingredient delivery for various cosmetic applications.

Industrial lubricant manufacturers incorporate it into biodegradable metalworking fluids, chain oils, and hydraulic fluids as a renewable alternative to petroleum-based stocks for sustainable operations.

It also functions as a release agent and processing aid in food manufacturing environments where incidental contact with product surfaces must meet food-safety standards and regulatory compliance.

Canola oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in bulk tankers, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), and drummed formats. Food-grade specifications conforming to Codex Alimentarius standards are standard.

Refined, bleached, and deodorized (RBD) grades serve both food and cosmetic markets. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and lubricant applications requiring specific performance characteristics.

name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole
description:
Butylated Hydroxyanisole (CAS 121-00-6 ), commonly known as BHA or E320 , is a synthetic phenolic antioxidant used across food, cosmetic, and industrial manufacturing. It prevents oxidative degradation in fats, oils, and lipid-containing formulations.

This versatile additive is essential for extending shelf life and maintaining product quality. In food manufacturing, BHA is added to edible fats, oils, snack foods, and packaging materials to inhibit rancidity and meet regulatory requirements.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and lip products to protect oil-phase ingredients from oxidative breakdown. This ensures that consumer products remain stable and effective over time.

Industrial lubricant producers use BHA to stabilize mineral oils and metalworking fluids against oxidation under high-temperature processing conditions. It is a critical component for maintaining the integrity of industrial fluids.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a processing stabilizer, protecting base resins during extrusion and molding. This prevents the degradation of materials during intense manufacturing cycles.

BHA is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or powder form. It is available in food-grade specifications conforming to FCC , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards for global compliance.

Technical grade options are also available for industrial applications where high-purity food standards are not required. Purity levels of 98.5% and above are standard for food and cosmetic grades to ensure safety.

name: 2,4-dinitrotoluene
description:
2,4-Dinitrotoluene (CAS 121-14-2 ), commonly referenced as 2,4-DNT, is a nitroaromatic compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of toluenediamine and toluene diisocyanate.

It functions as a key precursor in polyurethane production and serves as a stabilizer and burn rate modifier in propellant formulations. In the defense and aerospace sectors, it is incorporated into smokeless powder.

The compound is utilized in solid propellant compositions to regulate combustion characteristics. Automotive applications center on its role in producing TDI-based polyurethane foams used in seating and insulation.

These foams are also essential for interior components. As a monomer building block, it feeds into the hydrogenation pathway that yields toluenediamine, the direct precursor to TDI in large-scale manufacturing.

Specialty polymer formulators also evaluate it as a reactive intermediate where controlled nitro-group chemistry is required. This material is supplied as a pale yellow crystalline solid, typically in technical grade .

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement, with packaging options ranging from drum to IBC depending on regional handling regulations. Purity specifications generally align with industrial standards.

These standards are suited for intermediate chemical synthesis rather than consumer-facing applications. The material requires careful handling and storage in accordance with safety protocols for nitroaromatic chemicals.

name: Ethyl vanillin
description:
Ethyl vanillin (CAS 121-32-4 ), also known by FEMA 2464 , is a synthetic flavoring aldehyde approximately three times more potent than natural vanillin. It delivers a rich, creamy vanilla character at lower use rates.

This potency makes it a cost-efficient choice for flavor and fragrance formulation across food, beverage, and personal care markets. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to flavor chocolate and confectionery.

It is also ideal for baked goods, dairy products, and beverages where consistent vanilla intensity is required regardless of natural supply variability. Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrances and body care.

It serves as a fixative base note that extends longevity in finished formulations for home scent products. In printing inks and coatings, it functions as a UV stabilizer and antioxidant additive for protection.

This helps protect colorants and substrates from photodegradation during processing and end use. Personal care formulators also use it as a masking and scent-boosting agent in creams, lotions, and hair care products.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include food-grade material meeting FCC and FEMA specifications for high-quality manufacturing needs.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to USP or BP standards where purity requirements are more stringent. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to bulk drum supply.

Polymer and plastics manufacturers incorporate it as a flame retardant additive and thermal stabilizer. This is particularly useful in coatings and resin systems where controlled boron delivery is required for performance.

The pharmaceutical and fine chemical sectors use TMB as a reagent in borylation reactions and as a precursor to boronic acid derivatives. These applications require high precision and consistent chemical properties.

In textile and paper processing, it functions as a biocidal and pH-buffering agent applied during treatment baths and finishing stages. This versatility makes it a staple in diverse industrial processing environments.

Polymer producers use it as a catalyst in polyurethane and polycarbonate production, where controlled basicity influences chain growth and final material properties. This ensures consistent performance in industrial applications.

name: Benzethonium chloride
description:
Benzethonium chloride (CAS 121-54-0 ), commonly abbreviated as BZT, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial and preservative across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial applications.

It functions by disrupting microbial cell membranes, making it effective against bacteria, fungi, and some viruses at low use concentrations. In pharmaceutical formulations, BZT is used as a preservative in topical antiseptics.

It is also found in ophthalmic preparations and wound care products where microbial contamination control is critical. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into hand sanitizers, skin cleansers, and cosmetic preservative systems.

It can be used as a primary or co-preservative. In industrial and institutional cleaning, it serves as the active biocidal agent in surface disinfectants and sanitizing concentrates targeting healthcare and food-processing environments.

Water treatment and industrial process applications use BZT as a biocide to control microbial growth in recirculating systems and cooling towers. Benzethonium chloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder and as aqueous solutions.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and technical grade, with USP being the most commonly specified for pharmaceutical and personal care procurement. Bulk quantities are available in fiber drums or multi-layer bags.

Powder forms are typically shipped in drums, while liquid grades are available in IBC or drum packaging. This versatile compound remains a staple for manufacturers requiring reliable antimicrobial performance and stability.

name: Sulfanilic acid
description:
Sulfanilic acid (CAS 121-57-3 ), also known as sulphanilic acid, is an aminosulfonic acid used as a key intermediate in the synthesis of azo dyes, optical brighteners, and specialty chemicals.

Its bifunctional structure, carrying both amine and sulfonic acid groups, makes it a productive building block for coupling reactions in dye manufacturing and industrial chemical synthesis.

In textile dyeing, this compound is diazotized and coupled with naphthol or other aromatic compounds to produce direct and reactive azo dyes used on cotton and wool fibers.

The paper and packaging industries rely on it to manufacture fluorescent whitening agents that improve brightness in various coated and uncoated paper grades across the global market.

Leather processing operations use derivatives of this acid to achieve consistent, penetrating coloration on finished hides. It also functions as a cross-linking component in polymeric colorants.

Furthermore, it is utilized in the production of pigment dispersants for printing inks. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial handling.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 99% minimum for dye intermediate applications. Reagent-grade material is available for laboratory use.

Analytical applications often require tighter specifications for consistency. Our product meets rigorous industrial benchmarks to ensure performance in complex chemical synthesis and manufacturing.

name: N,N-dimethylaniline
description:
N,N-Dimethylaniline ( CAS 121-69-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DMA, is a tertiary aromatic amine used as a chemical intermediate and accelerator across dye manufacturing, polymer curing, and specialty synthesis.

It functions primarily as a catalyst and reactive intermediate, enabling downstream production of dyes, agrochemicals, and cured resin systems. In the dye and pigment industry, DMA is a key intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of triphenylmethane and azo dyes used in textile, paper, and leather coloring. Polymer formulators use it as a curing accelerator for unsaturated polyester and vinyl ester resins.

In these applications, it activates peroxide initiators to control cure rate in composite and laminate production. Printing ink manufacturers rely on DMA-derived colorants to achieve specific hue profiles.

These profiles are essential for packaging inks. It also serves as a building block in agrochemical and pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis, where controlled alkylation chemistry is required for production.

DMA is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, with drum and IBC packaging standard for industrial buyers. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for these industrial applications.

Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher for synthesis applications. Buyers sourcing for regulated downstream uses should confirm supplier documentation for batch consistency and purity certification.

name: Propyl gallate
description:
Propyl gallate (CAS 121-79-9 ), also known as E310 and abbreviated as PG, is a synthetic antioxidant used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It prevents oxidative degradation in fats, oils, and lipid-containing formulations.

This additive is essential for extending shelf life and protecting product quality in various industrial sectors. In food production, PG is approved under its E number and applied to edible fats, oils, margarine, and snack foods.

Its primary function is to inhibit rancidity during processing and storage, ensuring consumer safety and taste. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into oral and topical dosage forms to stabilize lipid excipients.

It is particularly effective for active ingredients susceptible to oxidation in medical formulations. Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it in creams, lotions, and lip products where it protects emollient oils from deterioration.

The compound also functions as a stabilizer in flavor and fragrance concentrates. In these applications, oxidative breakdown would compromise sensory performance and the overall quality of the final consumer product.

Propyl gallate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for easy handling. Standard grades include food-grade meeting FCC specifications, as well as USP and Ph.Eur. grades for pharmaceutical applications.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial antioxidant applications outside regulated food and pharma supply chains. This ensures a versatile range of options for manufacturers across different global markets.

2-Chloro-4-nitroaniline (CAS 121-87-9 ) is an aromatic amine intermediate used primarily in the synthesis of azo dyes and pigments. It functions as a diazonium precursor, enabling the production of colorants across textile, printing, and industrial coating applications.

In textile dyeing, it is diazotized and coupled to produce azo dyes that deliver strong, wash-resistant color on cotton and synthetic fibers. Ink and pigment manufacturers use it to synthesize yellow and orange azo pigments for printing inks and packaging coatings.

The chemical is also utilized in industrial paints and coatings where durability is required. In the leather and paper industries, it contributes to colorant formulations where consistent hue and substrate compatibility are critical production requirements.

name: Isophthalic acid
description:
Isophthalic acid (CAS 121-91-5 ), commonly abbreviated as IPA in the polymer and coatings industry, is an aromatic dicarboxylic acid used as a monomer and polymer modifier. It introduces flexibility and improved chemical resistance.

This chemical reduces crystallinity into polyester and resin systems compared to its terephthalic acid counterpart. Procurement teams source it primarily as a building block for performance resins, coatings, and engineering polymers.

In unsaturated polyester resins, IPA produces formulations with superior corrosion resistance. This makes it a preferred monomer for fiberglass-reinforced tanks, pipes, and marine composites used in heavy industrial applications.

Coatings manufacturers incorporate it into alkyd and polyester resins to improve adhesion, gloss retention, and durability. These enhancements are vital for both industrial and architectural finishes requiring long-term stability.

PET modification is another major outlet where partial substitution of terephthalic acid with IPA reduces crystallization rate. This enables clearer, more processable packaging materials and specialty films for the consumer market.

In adhesives and powder coatings, it functions as a crosslinking co-monomer that controls cure behavior. This specific chemical interaction improves end-product flexibility and overall performance in demanding environments.

Isophthalic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or free-flowing granules. Standard commercial grades include technical and polymer-grade specifications with purity levels typically at 99% or higher to meet requirements.

Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk containers, with fiber drums common for industrial quantities. These formats ensure the material remains stable and free-flowing during transport and storage for global supply chains.

name: Ammonium bromide
description:
Ammonium bromide (CAS 12124-97-9 ), also known by its historical pharmaceutical name Nervine, is an inorganic bromide salt used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, electronics, and polymer processing.

It functions primarily as a flame retardant additive and pH buffering agent in industrial formulations. In electronics manufacturing, it acts as a flux activator in soldering processes.

The compound contributes to controlled etching in printed circuit board production. Polymer and plastics compounders incorporate it as a halogen-based flame retardant for industrial use.

Its bromine content supports char formation and combustion suppression in finished materials. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering and pH-regulating agent in formulation chemistry.

This is particularly useful where controlled ionic environments are required during synthesis or processing. It also appears in photographic chemical systems and specialty chemical synthesis.

Ammonium bromide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial applications and USP / BP grades for pharmaceutical use.

Purity levels for pharmaceutical-grade material typically meet ≥99% specifications. Technical grades are also available for flame retardant and electronics applications requiring high consistency.

name: Magnesium carbonate hydroxide
description:
Magnesium carbonate hydroxide (CAS 12125-28-9 ) is an inorganic mineral compound used across industrial and regulated markets as a pH buffer, filler, and processing aid. Its buffering capacity and low bulk density make it a practical choice for formulators.

This material is essential for managing acid neutralization and flow control in solid and semi-solid systems. In rubber and plastics compounding, it functions as a reinforcing filler and acid scavenger, improving thermal stability during processing.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in tablet formulations, where it controls pH and improves powder flowability for direct compression. It ensures consistency and quality in high-speed manufacturing environments.

In food production, it serves as an anti-caking agent and acidity regulator in powdered products, operating under food-grade compliance requirements. It helps maintain the texture and shelf stability of various consumer goods.

Water treatment operations apply it to adjust alkalinity and neutralize acidic effluents in both municipal and industrial systems. This versatility makes it a staple chemical for environmental and utility management sectors.

The product is available as a white, low-density powder in varying particle size distributions to suit different processing requirements. Established grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ).

Technical-grade options are also available for industrial applications where high purity is not the primary concern. Bulk and packaged supply options are standard across the market to meet diverse logistical needs.

name: Ammonium sulfide
description:
Ammonium sulfide ( CAS 12135-76-1 ), also known as diammonium sulfide, is a sulfur-containing ammonium salt used commercially as a flavoring agent and chemical intermediate. It contributes characteristic savory and sulfurous notes that replicate naturally occurring flavor profiles.

In food and flavor manufacturing, it is used as a FEMA 2053 -listed flavoring agent to develop roasted, meaty, or savory taste profiles in processed food products. Flavor houses incorporate it into reaction flavor systems.

During thermal processing, controlled sulfur release generates target aroma compounds essential for authentic food profiles. In agriculture, it functions as a nitrogen and sulfur source in specialty fertilizer formulations targeting sulfur-deficient soils.

It also serves as a reagent in chemical synthesis where controlled introduction of sulfide ions is required. Ammonium sulfide is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging from 40–44% in commercial grades.

Food-grade material is available in compliance with FEMA designation requirements for flavoring applications. Technical-grade solution is also offered for agricultural and industrial use cases to meet specific manufacturing needs.

Our product meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency across batches. We provide documentation for FCC and other relevant standards to support your regulatory compliance and quality assurance protocols.

name: Aluminium silicate
description:
Aluminium silicate (CAS 12141-46-7 ), also designated E559 in food and pharmaceutical contexts, is a naturally derived inorganic mineral used industrially as a functional filler and rheology modifier.

It controls flow behavior, improves dimensional stability, and enhances surface properties across a range of solid and coating applications. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it acts as a reinforcing filler.

This material improves compound stiffness and processing consistency without the cost premium of specialty silicas. Paper producers incorporate it as a coating pigment to improve printability and brightness.

It also enhances ink receptivity in coated paper grades. Plastics compounders use it to adjust melt viscosity and reduce shrinkage in filled polymer systems, particularly in polypropylene and polyethylene formulations.

Building and construction applications include its use as an extender in paints, sealants, and cementitious coatings. In these settings, it contributes to opacity and reduces raw material costs effectively.

Aluminium silicate is supplied as a fine white powder, with particle size distribution being a key specification variable. Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material.

The product is available meeting USP or Ph. Eur. requirements for sensitive applications. Calcined and surface-treated variants are also commercially available to meet specific surface area requirements.

name: Potassium stannate
description:
Potassium stannate (CAS 12142-33-5 ), also known as dipotassium stannate, is an inorganic tin salt used primarily as a source of stannate ions in electroplating baths and surface treatment processes.

It enables controlled tin deposition on metal substrates, delivering corrosion-resistant and solderable coatings across several industrial sectors. In electronics manufacturing, it is used in alkaline tin plating baths.

This chemical helps to produce uniform, adherent tin coatings on printed circuit board components and connector parts. Textile processors apply it as a mordant and weighting agent for silk and synthetic fabrics.

These applications help in improving handle and dye uptake during the manufacturing process. In the leather industry, it functions as a surface modifier to enhance adhesion of finishing coats.

Plastics compounders have also evaluated it as a stabilizer additive in select polymer systems where tin-based chemistry is required. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granular solid.

It is available in technical grade for industrial electroplating and surface treatment applications. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial quantities.

The product is handled according to strict industrial protocols, with purity specifications commonly stated on a dry-weight basis to ensure consistency for high-precision manufacturing and chemical synthesis.

name: Hectorite
description:
Hectorite (CAS 12173-47-6 ) is a naturally occurring lithium magnesium silicate clay used across personal care, coatings, and industrial formulations to control flow, suspend particles, and stabilize emulsions.

HECTABRITE AW is a recognized commercial grade familiar to formulators sourcing this material. Its ability to build viscosity and form gels in both aqueous and non-aqueous systems drives demand across multiple manufacturing sectors.

In personal care, hectorite functions as a rheology modifier and suspending agent in foundations, sunscreens, and antiperspirant sticks. It provides a smooth, non-greasy texture and prevents pigment settling.

Coatings and adhesives manufacturers incorporate it to control sag resistance and improve pigment dispersion in waterborne and solvent-based systems. It is essential for maintaining consistency in high-performance paints.

In rubber compounding and polymer processing, it acts as a reinforcing filler and processing aid that improves dimensional stability in finished parts. This ensures durability and structural integrity in industrial components.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it to suspend abrasives and active ingredients in liquid cleansers and gels. This prevents separation and ensures a uniform application of the cleaning product.

Hectorite is supplied as a fine white powder in both natural and organically modified forms. Standard grades include cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care applications.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial use. Organophilic variants are provided for non-aqueous and polymer-matrix applications where hydrophilic grades are unsuitable for the formulation.

name: Sodium tetraborate pentahydrate
description:
Sodium tetraborate pentahydrate (CAS 12179-04-3 ), commercially known as borax pentahydrate, is an inorganic boron salt supplied as a partially hydrated form of borax. It functions as a pH buffer, corrosion inhibitor, biocide, and flame retardant across a broad range of industrial and consumer product applications.

In detergents and industrial cleaning formulations, borax pentahydrate boosts alkalinity and enhances surfactant performance, improving soil and grease removal. Coatings and adhesive manufacturers use it as a crosslinking agent for PVA-based systems and as a corrosion inhibitor in metalworking fluids.

Flame-retardant treatments for cellulosic textiles, paper, and wood products rely on its boron content to meet fire-resistance specifications. In water treatment, it serves as a buffering agent to stabilize process pH, and in agriculture it provides a soluble boron source for micronutrient fertilizer blends.

Sodium tetraborate pentahydrate is available as a free-flowing white powder or granules, with granule size influencing dissolution rate and handling characteristics for different process requirements. Standard supply grades include technical grade for industrial use and refined grades meeting USP or pharmaceutical specifications.

Bulk supply is common in 25 kg bags or bulk sacks, with concentration typically expressed as percentage B₂O₃ content for industrial purchasing specifications. This versatile chemical ensures stability and performance in diverse manufacturing environments globally.

name: Cetalkonium chloride
description:
Cetalkonium chloride (CAS 122-18-9 ), also known as CKC and commercially as Banicol, is a quaternary ammonium compound used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial sectors. Its cationic character enables it to bind to negatively charged surfaces.

This chemical acts as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial and surface-active agent, making it effective for both preservation and surface modification applications. In ophthalmic and topical pharmaceutical formulations, CKC functions as a preservative at low concentrations.

It is essential for preventing microbial contamination in multi-dose products. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into hair conditioning products and rinse-off treatments where it imparts antistatic properties and improves wet combability.

By adsorbing onto hair fiber surfaces, it enhances the overall texture and manageability of the hair. Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and finishing agent, modifying surface feel and providing durable antimicrobial protection.

In paper manufacturing, it supports wet-end chemistry as a biocidal additive to control microbial growth in process water and slurries. This ensures the integrity of the production process and the quality of the final paper products.

Cetalkonium chloride is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 25% or 50% active content. Technical and pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet the quality requirements of industrial and regulated end-use markets.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and counterion content when sourcing for pharmaceutical or personal care applications. Ensuring the correct grade is vital for maintaining safety and efficacy in sensitive consumer formulations.

name: Stearalkonium chloride
description:
Stearalkonium chloride (CAS 122-19-0 ), also known as Stearyldimethylbenzylammonium chloride and commercially as Stebac, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a conditioning agent, antimicrobial, and antistatic surfactant.

Its cationic charge drives strong adsorption onto negatively charged surfaces, making it effective for surface modification, lubrication, and preservation in formulated products across personal care and industrial applications.

In hair care, it is a primary conditioning active in rinse-off conditioners, detangling treatments, and conditioning shampoos, where it smooths the hair cuticle and reduces static for improved manageability.

Skin care and leave-on formulations use it as an emulsifier and feel modifier in creams and lotions. As a quaternary biocide, it is incorporated into preservation systems for cosmetic and personal care products.

These systems require broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity to ensure product stability. In biotechnology and life sciences, it functions as a surface-active agent in cell culture reagents and laboratory disinfectant formulations.

Stearalkonium chloride is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 50% or 75% active. Standard grades include cosmetic/personal care grade meeting purity specifications.

Technical grade is also available for industrial applications. Buyers should confirm active content and counterion purity when evaluating grades for preservation-critical formulations to ensure optimal performance.

name: Triisopropanolamine
description:
Triisopropanolamine (CAS 122-20-3 ), commonly abbreviated as TIPA, is a tertiary alkanolamine used across industrial and personal care sectors as a pH regulator, chelating agent, and crosslinker.

Its dual amine-alcohol functionality makes it effective in neutralizing acidic systems and coordinating metal ions within complex formulations. In coatings and adhesives, TIPA acts as a crosslinking agent and curing accelerator.

This chemical improves film hardness and adhesion in alkyd and epoxy-based systems. Personal care formulators use it to neutralize carbomer and acrylate polymers, adjusting pH in creams, lotions, and gels.

It functions without introducing harsh alkalinity to the final product. Water treatment applications rely on TIPA's chelating capacity to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, preventing scale formation in industrial process water.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a pH buffer and auxiliary agent during dyeing and finishing operations. This supports consistent color uptake and surface treatment across various materials.

Triisopropanolamine is supplied as a viscous liquid or low-melting solid, depending on grade and temperature handling. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial specifications for diverse needs.

Purity levels are typically at 85% and 99% for most applications. Bulk supply is available in drums and IBC containers, with technical-grade product being the most common form for industrial procurement.

name: Glycerol trioleate
description:
Glycerol trioleate (CAS 122-32-7 ), also known as Triolein or glyceryl trioleate, is a triglyceride ester derived from glycerol and oleic acid. It functions as a lubricant, emulsifier, and moisturizing agent across industrial and consumer product applications.

In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it serves as a base oil component or friction modifier, providing film-forming lubrication under moderate load conditions. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams and hair conditioners.

Its oleic acid profile supports emollient performance and moisture retention in body oils. In food applications, Triolein is used as a reference standard for fat analysis and as a functional lipid ingredient in nutritional formulations.

These formulations often target specific fatty acid profiles for dietary needs. It also functions as an emulsifier and dispersing agent in specialty formulations where controlled lipid delivery is required for the final product.

Glycerol trioleate is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid. It is available in technical grade for industrial and lubricant applications, as well as high-purity grades suitable for food, nutritional, and cosmetic use.

Specifications vary by supplier, with purity levels commonly ranging from 65% to 99%+ depending on the intended application. This versatility makes it a staple in both heavy industry and high-end consumer goods manufacturing.

name: Amylcinnamaldehyde
description:
Amylcinnamaldehyde (CAS 122-40-7 ), also known as jasmine aldehyde or jasminal, is a synthetic aromatic aldehyde used as a fragrance and flavoring ingredient across personal care, food, and industrial applications.

FEMA 2061 listed, it delivers a characteristic floral-jasmine note that anchors perfume compositions and flavoring systems alike. In fine fragrance and personal care formulations, it functions as a key floral modifier.

It is used in soaps, shampoos, lotions, and eau de toilette, contributing lasting jasmine character at relatively low use levels. Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it as a flavoring agent in various products.

It is utilized in confectionery, baked goods, and fruit preparations where a soft floral-sweet profile is required. In plastics and polymer processing, it is evaluated as a UV stabilizer additive for light-absorption.

Its conjugated aldehyde structure contributes to functionality in film and packaging applications. Printing ink formulators also explore it as a UV-protective component in specialty coating systems.

Amylcinnamaldehyde is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid. It is available in fragrance-grade and food-grade ( FCC -compliant) specifications to meet the distinct purity requirements of manufacturing.

These specifications ensure suitability for cosmetic and food manufacturing supply chains. Standard packaging ranges from small drums to bulk IBC quantities depending on the specific application volume required.

name: Triethyl orthoformate
description:
Triethyl orthoformate (CAS 122-51-0 ), also known as ethyl orthoformate and abbreviated as TEOF, is a reactive intermediate used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

It functions primarily as a protecting group reagent, alkylating agent, and condensation reagent in multi-step organic synthesis. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TEOF is used to introduce orthoester functionality.

This occurs during the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly in the production of antimicrobials and antiviral compounds. Printing ink and coating formulators use it as a crosslinking agent.

It also serves as a moisture scavenger to improve film stability and shelf life in moisture-sensitive systems. In flavor and fragrance applications, it contributes to the synthesis of aroma compounds.

Controlled reactivity under mild conditions is commercially valuable for these applications. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative booster and intermediate in the preparation of conditioning actives.

Triethyl orthoformate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to ISO containers for bulk procurement. It is available in technical and high-purity grades for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meets specifications relevant to GMP manufacturing environments. Purity levels of 98% and above are standard for synthesis-grade supply across global chemical distribution networks.

name: Triethyl phosphite
description:
Triethyl phosphite (CAS 122-52-1 ), commonly abbreviated as TEP, is a trialkyl phosphite ester used as a reactive intermediate and stabilizer across polymer, lubricant, and agrochemical manufacturing.

Ethyl phosphite is a recognized alternative name in trade and procurement contexts. Its value lies in its ability to act as a ligand, antioxidant precursor, or catalyst component depending on the application.

In polymer production, TEP functions as a stabilizer and processing aid, protecting polyolefins and engineering resins from oxidative degradation during high-temperature compounding processes.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as an antiwear additive precursor, where it reacts in situ to form protective phosphorus-containing films on metal surfaces.

In agrochemical synthesis, TEP serves as a key building block for organophosphate active ingredients, including pesticides and herbicides produced via Michaelis–Arbuzov reactions.

It also acts as a ligand precursor in transition metal catalyst systems used in polymerization and fine chemical processes. This versatility makes it essential for modern chemical synthesis.

Triethyl phosphite is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+.

High-purity grades are available for catalyst and synthesis applications where trace impurities affect reaction selectivity. Proper handling is required to maintain the integrity of the chemical during storage.

name: 3-Morpholinopropylamine
description:
3-Morpholinopropylamine (CAS 123-00-2 ), commonly abbreviated as AMPD, is a bifunctional amine combining a primary amine and a morpholine ring in a single molecule. This dual-functional structure makes it effective as a curing agent and catalyst.

It serves as a reactive intermediate across multiple industrial sectors. In epoxy coatings and adhesives, AMPD acts as a curing agent and crosslinker, contributing to adhesion performance and chemical resistance in protective formulations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a building block for active ingredients and intermediates. The morpholine moiety is a recognized pharmacophore in drug design, making it a valuable component for specialized synthesis projects.

In water treatment, it functions as a biocidal agent and corrosion inhibitor additive. It is specifically used for targeting microbial growth in industrial cooling and process water systems to maintain operational efficiency.

Polyurethane and polymer formulators employ it as a reactive catalyst or chain extender. This application allows manufacturers to influence cure rates and final mechanical properties in a variety of industrial polymer systems.

3-Morpholinopropylamine is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purities, typically 98% and above. Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available for standard industrial and laboratory use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is also accessible for API and intermediate applications. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on volume requirements and specific logistical needs of the customer.

name: Cetylpyridinium chloride
description:
Cetylpyridinium chloride ( CAS 123-03-5 ), commonly abbreviated as CPC, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as an antimicrobial active and preservative across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing.

It delivers broad-spectrum biocidal activity against bacteria, fungi, and some viruses, making it a go-to active ingredient where surface-active preservation is required for various formulations.

In oral care, CPC is the active ingredient in antiseptic mouthwashes, throat lozenges, and medicated sprays, where it reduces oral bacterial load and controls plaque effectively.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, skin cleansers, and conditioning products for its combined antimicrobial and surfactant properties in diverse consumer goods.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a preservative in topical formulations and as an active in over-the-counter antiseptic products subject to specific regulatory monographs.

It also functions as a dispersing and emulsifying agent in certain industrial and cosmetic systems where controlled microbial stability is a simultaneous requirement for the product.

Cetylpyridinium chloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , supporting direct use in regulated applications.

These high-purity grades ensure compliance with global pharmacopeia requirements. Technical-grade material is also available for non-regulated industrial uses and general manufacturing needs.

name: 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde
description:
4-Hydroxybenzaldehyde (CAS 123-08-0 ), commonly referred to as 4-HBA or p-hydroxybenzaldehyde, is a phenolic aldehyde used as a key synthetic intermediate and flavoring agent across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturing.

FEMA 3984 status supports its use in flavor applications where regulatory traceability is required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, 4-HBA serves as a precursor in the synthesis of active ingredients.

It is used in the production of antiviral compounds and vanillin derivatives, making it a recurring procurement target for API producers. Food and beverage formulators source it as a flavoring component.

Its natural phenolic character contributes to vanilla-adjacent profiles in various food products. In personal care, it functions as a UV stabilizer and preservative booster in skin and hair formulations.

Polymer and resin producers also use it as a building block for UV-stabilizing additives and specialty antioxidant systems. 4-Hydroxybenzaldehyde is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid.

Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with high-purity specifications available to meet API intermediate requirements. FCC -grade material is available for flavor applications.

This grade is essential for food applications requiring documented food safety compliance. The material is handled according to strict quality protocols to ensure consistency across global supply chains.

name: Diethyl succinate
description:
Diethyl succinate (CAS 123-25-1 ), also known by its FEMA 2377 designation, is a mild-odor ester used as a solvent, carrier, and flavoring agent across food, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

Its low volatility and compatibility with a broad range of active ingredients make it a practical choice for formulators managing solubility and delivery challenges in various chemical processes.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavor modifier with a faint fruity, wine-like note, used in small concentrations to round out flavor profiles in confectionery and alcoholic beverages.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it as a carrier solvent and humectant in skin creams, lotions, and fragrance blends where a non-greasy, slow-evaporating base is required for the product.

In printing inks and coatings, it acts as a coalescing solvent that supports film formation and pigment dispersion on flexible packaging substrates. It also serves as a reaction solvent and intermediate.

This material is utilized in specialty chemical synthesis where a high-boiling, relatively inert ester medium is needed. Diethyl succinate is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Food-grade material conforming to FEMA standards is the most commonly traded specification, with technical-grade available for industrial solvent applications. Purity typically ranges from 99% upward.

This high purity level is essential for flavor and cosmetic end uses, ensuring consistent performance and safety across all manufacturing sectors and specialized chemical applications.

name: Dilauryl thiodipropionate
description:
Dilauryl thiodipropionate (CAS 123-28-4 ), commonly abbreviated as DLTDP and approved as food additive E389 , is a thioester-based antioxidant used to prevent oxidative degradation.

It functions as a secondary antioxidant, decomposing hydroperoxides before they trigger chain-reaction oxidation in polymers, fats, and lubricant systems. This mechanism ensures long-term stability.

In plastics and polymer processing, DLTDP is combined with primary antioxidants such as hindered phenols to extend the service life of polyolefins, PVC, and rubber compounds exposed to heat.

Food manufacturers use it under regulatory approval to stabilize fats and oils against rancidity, particularly in edible fat blends and various processed food products across the industry.

In personal care formulations, it protects lipid-rich bases including creams, ointments, and hair oils from oxidative breakdown during shelf storage, maintaining product integrity over time.

Industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it to slow oxidative thickening and acid buildup in base oils under high-temperature operating conditions, ensuring mechanical efficiency and safety.

DLTDP is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or powder form. It is available in food-grade specification as well as technical grade for industrial applications.

Standard packaging includes fiber drums and bags, with bulk quantities available for industrial procurement. The material is handled according to strict safety and quality protocols.

name: 4-aminophenol
description:
4-Aminophenol (CAS 123-30-8 ), also known as p-aminophenol, is a primary aromatic amine used as a key chemical intermediate in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its reactivity toward acylation and coupling reactions makes it a high-demand building block across multiple industrial sectors. In pharmaceuticals, it is the direct precursor to paracetamol.

As one of the world's highest-volume analgesic APIs, it is a critical raw material for bulk drug manufacturers. Hair dye formulations rely on it as an oxidative colorant intermediate.

It couples with other components to produce permanent color in consumer and professional products. It also functions as a photographic developer intermediate in printing and imaging chemistry.

Controlled reduction reactions are essential to image formation in these processes. In rubber and polymer processing, it serves as an antioxidant precursor in the synthesis of stabilizer compounds.

These compounds protect against thermal and oxidative degradation. 4-Aminophenol is supplied as an off-white to light brown crystalline powder for various industrial applications.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to meet API intermediate specifications including purity requirements aligned with USP standards.

Material also meets Ph. Eur. standards for high-purity applications. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on specific customer application requirements.

name: Hydroquinone
description:
Hydroquinone (CAS 123-31-9 ), commonly abbreviated as HQ, is an aromatic diol used industrially as a polymerization inhibitor, antioxidant, and chemical intermediate. It prevents premature crosslinking in reactive monomers and protects unstable materials during storage.

In photographic and printing chemistry, HQ functions as a developing agent that reduces silver halide to metallic silver, controlling image density and contrast. Rubber and polymer manufacturers add it to acrylic and vinyl monomers during production.

This addition occurs during transport to suppress unwanted polymerization. As a pharmaceutical intermediate, it supports synthesis of active compounds and is used in topical formulations targeting skin hyperpigmentation for various medical applications.

Personal care formulators incorporate HQ into depigmentation products where it inhibits melanin synthesis, subject to regional regulatory limits. The compound is essential for maintaining the stability of sensitive chemical formulations.

Hydroquinone is supplied as a white crystalline powder in technical and pharmaceutical grades. USP and BP grades are available to meet compendial requirements for pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications globally.

Technical grade is standard for polymer stabilization and industrial chemical synthesis, typically packaged in fiber drums or multi-wall bags. This ensures the material remains stable and free from contaminants during long-term storage.

name: Propionaldehyde
description:
Propionaldehyde (CAS 123-38-6 ), also known as propionic aldehyde, is a short-chain aliphatic aldehyde used primarily as a building block in flavor and fragrance manufacturing.

Its sharp, slightly fruity character makes it a valued raw material for synthesizing aroma compounds at commercial scale. In flavor creation, it is used to produce aldehydic top notes in food flavoring systems.

It contributes to profiles found in dairy, fruit, and bread-type products and carries FEMA 2923 status, supporting its use in regulated food applications across the global market.

Fragrance manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of longer-chain aldehydes and other aroma chemicals that appear in fine fragrance and personal care formulations.

It also functions as a chemical intermediate in the production of propionic acid derivatives, trimethylolethane, and other downstream industrial chemicals used in various manufacturing sectors.

In cosmetic fragrance compounding, it enables the construction of fresh, clean scent profiles in rinse-off and leave-on product formats, ensuring versatility for formulators and chemists.

Propionaldehyde is supplied as a colorless liquid, typically in bulk quantities suited to industrial and flavor-house procurement. Standard commercial grades are available for immediate shipping.

High-purity specifications meet the requirements of flavor and fragrance applications under FEMA guidelines, ensuring consistent quality and performance for all industrial chemical applications.

name: Diacetone alcohol
description:
Diacetone alcohol ( CAS 123-42-2 ), commonly abbreviated as DAA, is a slow-evaporating ketone-alcohol solvent used across coatings, adhesives, and industrial cleaning applications.

Its dual functional group chemistry makes it compatible with a broad range of resins, enabling effective solvation where faster solvents fall short in complex formulations.

In coatings and lacquers, DAA dissolves nitrocellulose, epoxy, and acrylic resins, supporting formulations that require extended open time and leveling performance for high-quality finishes.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a reactive diluent and crosslinking co-solvent, particularly in systems where controlled cure rate is a production requirement for stability.

In personal care, DAA functions as a carrier solvent in nail care formulations and surface-active cosmetic products. Polymer processors also use it as a coupling agent and stabilizer.

This additive helps to improve resin homogeneity during compounding. DAA is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities for industrial scale operations.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with high-purity grades available for cosmetic and specialty coating applications requiring strict adherence to quality.

Buyers should confirm water content and purity thresholds, as residual moisture affects performance in moisture-sensitive resin systems and overall chemical stability.

These notes are essential in confectionery, beverages, and artificial flavor systems. Personal care formulators use it as a solvent and fixative in fragrance compositions, where it supports scent diffusion and stability.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it functions as a reactive intermediate and process solvent in resin curing and cross-linking operations. It also serves as a chemical building block in pharmaceutical synthesis.

The material is further utilized as an extraction solvent in laboratory and industrial separation processes. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities to meet various industrial demands.

Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is available for flavoring applications, while technical-grade is standard for industrial and polymer uses. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99%+.

name: Acetylacetone

Acetylacetone (CAS 123-54-6 ), also known as Hacac or acac, is a beta-diketone solvent and chelating agent used across chemical manufacturing, coatings, and catalyst production.

Its ability to form stable metal complexes drives demand in synthesis and formulation workflows where precise metal coordination is required for high-performance industrial applications.

In catalyst manufacturing, acac coordinates with metals such as vanadium, cobalt, and zirconium to produce metal acetylacetonate precursors used in polymerization and cross-linking systems.

Printing ink and coating formulators use it as a cross-linking agent and solvent carrier, improving adhesion and cure performance in various commercial packaging applications.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a building block in active ingredient synthesis, where controlled reactivity with metal centers supports consistent intermediate production.

At lower concentrations, it functions as a flavoring agent in food-grade applications, providing a creamy, buttery note to confectionery and beverage formulations for the food industry.

Acetylacetone is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers requiring consistent supply chains.

Standard commercial grades include technical and reagent-grade specifications. A food-grade designation is available for flavoring applications where purity documentation is required by audits.

name: Ethyl hexanoate
description:
Ethyl hexanoate ( CAS 123-66-0 ), also known by its FEMA 2439 designation and commercially as ethyl caproate, is a fruity ester used as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient across food, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

Its characteristic apple-pineapple odor profile makes it a target compound for flavor houses and fragrance formulators sourcing aroma chemicals at scale. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavoring agent.

It is used in fruit-type confectionery, alcoholic beverages, and dairy products where tropical and apple notes are required. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products including lotions, shampoos, and body washes.

These applications deliver light, fresh top notes to the consumer. As a synthetic ester, it also sees use as a lubricant additive and plasticizer component in specialty industrial formulations where low-viscosity ester chemistry is specified.

Flavor blenders reference its regulatory status when qualifying it for use in regulated food applications in the US market. The compound is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement.

It is available in food-grade and fragrance-grade specifications, with FCC grade material commonly requested for flavor applications. Purity levels of 98% and above are standard for flavor and fragrance end uses.

name: Pyrrolidine
description:
Pyrrolidine (CAS 123-75-1 ), also known as Azolidine, is a saturated five-membered nitrogen heterocycle used as a flavoring agent and chemical intermediate across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries.

Assigned FEMA 3523 , it functions as a building block for synthesizing active ingredients and flavor compounds rather than as a finished additive in its own right for most industrial applications.

In food and flavor manufacturing, it is used to produce thermally derived flavor compounds that contribute roasted, grain, and savory notes to processed foods and beverages during the production cycle.

Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it as a key synthetic intermediate for APIs, where the pyrrolidine ring is incorporated into drug candidates targeting a range of therapeutic categories and medical needs.

In personal care, it supports the synthesis of conditioning agents and specialty amines used in hair and skin formulations. Agrochemical producers also use it as an intermediate in fungicide and pesticide synthesis.

Pyrrolidine is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging. Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available for industrial and laboratory procurement needs.

High-purity pharmaceutical-grade material is offered for API synthesis applications. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and moisture content with suppliers, as grade requirements vary significantly by end use.

Material quality is often verified against internal manufacturer specifications or recognized standards such as USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , FCC , or ACS depending on the specific grade and application.

name: Levulinic acid
description:
Levulinic acid (CAS 123-76-2 ), also known as levulic acid, is a short-chain keto acid derived from biomass that has gained commercial traction as a platform chemical for food and cosmetic applications.

Registered under FEMA 2627 , it functions as a flavoring acidulant, pH buffer, and mild preservative across multiple formulation types. It is a versatile ingredient for specialty chemical applications.

In food and beverage formulations, it contributes a mild, slightly caramel-like acidic note and supports pH regulation in sauces, dairy analogs, and processed foods. It is highly valued for its stability.

Personal care formulators use it as a humectant and pH-adjusting agent in skin creams, lotions, and leave-on treatments. Controlled acidity in these products also supports preservation efficacy and skin health.

It acts as a synergist with conventional preservative systems, allowing reduced concentrations of harsher biocides in rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic products. This makes it ideal for clean-label formulations.

Flavor houses also source it as a building block for synthesizing levulinate esters used in fragrance and flavor compositions. Its chemical structure allows for diverse reactions in industrial synthesis.

Levulinic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid or in liquid form depending on purity and grade. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is available for flavoring.

Technical-grade product is also offered for industrial and specialty chemical synthesis. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale manufacturing and laboratory requirements.

name: Azodicarbonamide
description:
Azodicarbonamide ( CAS 123-77-3 ), also known as ADCA or Celogen AZ, is a chemical blowing agent and dough conditioner used across rubber processing, plastics manufacturing, and food production.

It decomposes upon heating to release gas, generating a controlled cellular structure in foamed materials or improving dough handling properties in baked goods for industrial food processors.

In rubber and plastics, ADCA is compounded into EVA, PVC, and polyolefin formulations to produce foamed sheets, profiles, and soles for footwear where consistent cell structure affects product density.

Bread and flour manufacturers use it as a flour maturing agent, where it strengthens gluten networks and improves machinability of high-output dough lines in commercial bakery environments.

In synthetic leather and textile coating applications, it generates the foam layer in PVC-coated fabrics, controlling thickness and flexibility of the finished substrate for various industrial uses.

Masterbatch producers also incorporate ADCA into concentrate systems for downstream processors requiring pre-dispersed blowing agent solutions to ensure uniform distribution during the manufacturing process.

Azodicarbonamide is supplied as a yellow to orange fine powder. Standard commercial grades include food-grade and technical/rubber grades differentiated by particle size and decomposition temperature range.

Activated grades with modified decomposition profiles are available for specific polymer processing windows, ensuring the material meets strict industrial requirements and performance benchmarks.

name: Dioctyl adipate
description:
Dioctyl adipate (CAS 123-79-5 ), commonly abbreviated as DOA, is a diester plasticizer and lubricant used across food-contact materials, polymer processing, and personal care formulations.

With FEMA 4476 approval, it also functions as a flavoring agent in food applications. Buyers source it primarily for its performance in low-temperature flexible PVC and as a food-grade lubricant.

In plastics processing, DOA is compounded into PVC films, cables, and flexible profiles where low-temperature flexibility is a critical specification, particularly for cold-storage packaging and refrigeration.

Food manufacturers use it as a FEMA-approved flavoring ingredient and as a direct food-contact lubricant in processing equipment. In personal care, it functions as a lightweight emollient and skin-conditioning agent.

It is frequently found in lotions, lip products, and color cosmetics where a non-greasy skin feel is required. Metalworking formulators incorporate DOA into cutting fluids and specialty lubricant blends.

Dioctyl adipate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available. Standard grades include food-grade and technical-grade for high-volume buyers.

Food-grade material is produced to meet FDA and relevant food-contact regulatory requirements. Purity is typically 99% minimum for food and plasticizer applications to ensure high performance.

name: Butyl acetate
description:
Butyl acetate (CAS 123-86-4 ), also known as NBA, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, personal care, and flavor manufacturing. FEMA 2174 designates its use as a food-grade flavoring ingredient.

In food applications, it delivers a characteristic fruity note. Its evaporation profile and solvency strength make it a preferred carrier in formulations requiring clean, residue-free drying for industrial use.

In nail care and cosmetic formulations, butyl acetate is the primary solvent in nail lacquers and polish removers, controlling viscosity and film formation. It ensures a smooth application and quick drying time.

Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use it to dissolve nitrocellulose, acrylics, and vinyl resins in industrial and automotive finishing systems. It is essential for high-performance surface coatings and resins.

As a FEMA-approved flavoring agent, it is used in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods to impart apple and pear flavor profiles. It meets the strict requirements for food-grade chemical additives.

In metalworking and lubricant blending, it functions as a carrier solvent for cutting fluids and surface treatment formulations. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities.

Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels suited for coatings and metalworking applications. Food-grade and flavor-grade material is available to meet FCC specifications.

These high-purity grades are necessary for use in regulated food and cosmetic applications. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for all industrial and food-grade manufacturing needs.

name: 1,4-dioxane
description:
1,4-Dioxane (CAS 123-91-1 ) is a cyclic ether solvent used across chemical manufacturing, laboratory research, and industrial processing. It functions as a high-solvency carrier for resins and cellulose derivatives.

This versatile compound is effective for a broad range of organic compounds where other solvents underperform. In pharmaceutical and chemical synthesis, it serves as a reaction solvent and extraction medium.

It is particularly useful in processes requiring miscibility with both water and organic phases. Personal care manufacturers monitor it as a trace contaminant in ethoxylated ingredients for safety.

The chemical acts as a reference standard for quality control and regulatory compliance testing. In laboratory settings, it is used as a scintillation solvent and as a stabilizer carrier.

It is also utilized in analytical-grade preparations for various research applications. Food and fragrance applications involve its use as a trace flavoring reference compound for testing.

Despite these niche uses, its primary commercial demand remains in industrial solvent and synthesis roles. The product is supplied as a colorless liquid in drums and bulk containers.

Standard grades include technical, reagent, and HPLC-grade, with anhydrous specifications available. These are ideal for moisture-sensitive synthesis applications in controlled environments.

Stabilized and unstabilized variants are both commercially available for purchase. Grade selection is typically driven by specific end-use process requirements and stability needs.

name: Isoamyl acetate
description:
Isoamyl acetate (CAS 123-92-2 ), also known as isopentyl acetate, is an ester-based solvent and flavoring agent with a characteristic banana-pear aroma profile. It serves dual commercial roles as a functional solvent in industrial coating and printing applications.

Printing and packaging operations use it as a fast-evaporating solvent in nitrocellulose-based inks and lacquers. Its evaporation rate supports print quality and adhesion on flexible substrates. Personal care formulators incorporate it into fragrance blends and nail care products.

In these applications, it contributes both scent character and solvent function. It also acts as a carrier solvent in aerosol formulations and specialty coatings requiring controlled viscosity and clean evaporation. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Isoamyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Food-grade material is available meeting FCC specifications, while technical-grade is offered for industrial solvent applications. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99%+ depending on the end use.

name: 1-Monostearin
description:
1-Monostearin (CAS 123-94-4 ), commercially known as Glyceryl Monostearate or GMS, is a monoglyceride ester used across food, personal care, and industrial manufacturing as an emulsifier and stabilizer.

It enables oil and water phases to combine uniformly in formulations where phase separation would otherwise compromise product quality or shelf life. In food manufacturing, GMS is used in baked goods and margarine.

It is also used in ice cream to control fat crystallization, improve texture, and extend shelf life. Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions as an emulsifying wax that provides a stable base.

This ingredient enhances skin feel and provides a smooth consistency. In plastics processing, it functions as a lubricant and antistatic agent, reducing friction during extrusion and improving mold release in production.

Coatings and adhesive manufacturers use it as a plasticizer and dispersing aid to improve flexibility and pigment distribution in finished systems. GMS is supplied as white to off-white flakes, beads, or powder.

Food-grade material is available to FCC and E471 specifications, while cosmetic and pharmaceutical applications are served by USP and BP grades for high purity requirements.

Technical-grade product is also available for industrial polymer and coatings applications where food or pharma compliance is not required. This ensures versatility across a wide range of manufacturing sectors.

name: Butyl stearate
description:
Butyl stearate (CAS 123-95-5 ), also known as butyl octadecanoate, is a fatty acid ester used across food, cosmetics, and industrial manufacturing. It functions primarily as a lubricant, emollient, and plasticizer, depending on the application sector.

In personal care formulations, it acts as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent in creams, lotions, and color cosmetics. It improves spreadability and texture without a heavy feel, making it a versatile choice for high-end cosmetic products.

Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators use it as a base or additive in cutting fluids and release agents. Its ester chemistry provides low-friction performance on metal surfaces, enhancing the efficiency of various machining processes.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal lubricant and plasticizer, reducing melt viscosity and improving flow during extrusion and molding. This helps manufacturers achieve better consistency and finish in their plastic components.

Food-grade butyl stearate carries FEMA 2214 status and is used as a flavoring adjuvant and surface lubricant. It is commonly found in confectionery and food manufacturing applications where high purity is required for safety.

Butyl stearate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid at ambient temperatures. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications, with food-grade material conforming to relevant purity standards for flavor and food contact.

The material is produced to meet rigorous quality benchmarks, ensuring reliability across diverse industrial sectors. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to accommodate large-scale manufacturing requirements.
