name: Azelaic acid
description:
Azelaic acid (CAS 123-99-9 ) is a saturated dicarboxylic acid used as a functional building block and active ingredient across cosmetic, polymer, and industrial lubricant applications.

It is commercially recognized under the pharmaceutical trade names Skinoren and Skinorem, particularly in dermatological product sourcing contexts for various global markets.

In personal care and pharmaceutical formulations, this acid is the active ingredient in topical products targeting acne and hyperpigmentation, where it functions as a pH-regulating and antimicrobial agent.

Polymer manufacturers use it as a monomer to produce polyamides and polyesters with improved flexibility and low-temperature performance, particularly in specialty coatings and adhesives.

In lubricant formulations, azelaic acid esters produced through esterification with branched alcohols serve as synthetic base fluids and plasticizers suited to high-performance and low-temperature applications.

It also acts as a corrosion inhibitor and dispersant additive in metalworking fluids. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules for easy handling and processing.

Standard commercial grades include technical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical grades, with the latter meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications for high-purity manufacturing requirements.

Purity levels of 98–99%+ are typical for high-specification applications, while technical-grade material is available for polymer and lubricant end uses across the chemical industry.

name: Sodium Iron DTPA
description:
Sodium Iron DTPA (CAS 12389-75-2 ), also known as DTPA Fe or Iron Chelate, is a synthetic iron-chelated micronutrient used to deliver bioavailable iron in conditions where conventional iron salts fail.

It maintains iron in a soluble, plant-accessible form across a broad pH range, making it the preferred iron source in alkaline and calcareous soils. In agriculture, it is applied as a foliar spray or soil drench.

This product is used to correct iron-deficiency chlorosis in high-value crops including citrus, grapes, and ornamentals where soil pH limits iron uptake. Hydroponic and fertigation systems rely on it as a stable iron source.

In these nutrient solutions, competing ions would otherwise precipitate unformulated iron salts. Water treatment operations use it to sequester iron and prevent scale formation or discoloration in industrial and municipal systems.

It also functions as a stabilizer in certain industrial formulations where free iron ions would catalyze oxidative degradation. Sodium Iron DTPA is supplied as a water-soluble powder or liquid concentrate.

Liquid forms are typically offered at 6% or 11% iron content by weight. Technical and agricultural grades are the most commonly traded specifications for this chemical compound in the global market.

Purity and chelated iron content are the primary quality parameters referenced in procurement and product certification. These standards ensure the efficacy of the chelate in various industrial and agricultural applications.

name: Adipic acid
description:
Adipic acid (CAS 124-04-9 ), also supplied as molten adipic acid and approved under E355 , is a dicarboxylic acid used across food, polymer, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions as an acidulant, pH buffer, and monomer feedstock depending on the application. In food production, it acts as an acidulant and leavening agent in dry beverage mixes and baked goods.

Its low hygroscopicity gives it a handling advantage over alternatives in gelatin desserts. Nylon 6,6 production is its largest industrial outlet, where it reacts with hexamethylenediamine.

This process forms the polymer backbone used in engineering plastics, fibers, and automotive components. In personal care formulations, it functions as a pH adjuster and buffering agent.

It is commonly found in creams, cleansers, and rinse-off products. It also serves as a precursor in polyurethane polyol and plasticizer synthesis where controlled chain length is required.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in molten liquid form for bulk industrial delivery. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant) and technical-grade.

Food applications require material meeting purity specifications for direct use. Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk tanker shipments for molten supply to various manufacturing facilities.

name: Caprylic acid
description:
Caprylic acid (CAS 124-07-2 ), also known as octylic acid, is a saturated C8 fatty acid derived primarily from coconut and palm kernel oil. It functions as a pH regulator, emulsifier, and antimicrobial agent across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food production, caprylic acid is used as a flavoring agent and acidulant, with FEMA 2799 status supporting its use in dairy, baked goods, and beverage formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient and stabilizer in lipid-based drug delivery systems.

This versatile fatty acid is particularly effective for oral and topical formulations. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams and hair products where it supports emulsion stability and acts as a conditioning agent.

In metalworking and lubricant applications, it serves as a feedstock for ester-based lubricants and corrosion inhibitors. Caprylic acid is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid that meets rigorous industrial requirements.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5% to ensure consistent performance in sensitive chemical processes.

Packaging options generally include drums and IBC containers, with bulk tanker supply available for high-volume industrial buyers. This ensures flexible logistics for manufacturers across the global chemical supply chain.

name: Hexamethylenediamine
description:
Hexamethylenediamine ( CAS 124-09-4 ), commercially abbreviated as HMDA, is a primary diamine monomer central to the production of polyamide resins and polymer intermediates. It functions as a difunctional building block and crosslinking agent across polymer chemistry and coatings.

HMDA is the principal monomer in nylon 6,6 production, where it reacts with adipic acid to form the salt precursor used in fiber, film, and engineering plastics. In coatings and adhesives, it acts as a curing agent for epoxy systems.

This chemical improves crosslink density and chemical resistance in industrial finishes. Polyurethane and polyurea formulations use HMDA-derived intermediates to control chain extension and mechanical performance in elastomers and sealants.

Personal care formulators apply it in limited concentrations for pH adjustment in rinse-off products where amine buffering is required. Hexamethylenediamine is supplied as a molten liquid for bulk industrial shipment.

It is also available as a solid flake or crystalline form for smaller-volume packaging. Technical grade is the standard for polymer and coatings applications. Purity specifications typically range from 99%+ for monomer-grade material.

Documentation is available to support compliance in regulated manufacturing environments. This ensures that the material meets the necessary industrial requirements for high-performance polymer synthesis and chemical processing.

name: Diethylene glycol monobutyl ether acetate
description:
Diethylene glycol monobutyl ether acetate (CAS 124-17-4 ), also known as Butyl Carbitol Acetate or DGMBA, is a slow-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, printing inks, and specialty formulations.

Its controlled evaporation rate makes it a preferred carrier in systems requiring extended open time and film leveling. In industrial coatings and architectural paints, DGMBA functions as a coalescing solvent and flow promoter.

This chemical improves surface finish and reduces defects in high-solids and waterborne systems. Printing ink manufacturers use it to control viscosity and drying speed in gravure and screen printing formulations.

In plastics processing, it acts as a plasticizer and coupling agent, supporting flexibility and adhesion in polymer-based coatings and adhesives. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a carrier solvent.

It is frequently used in nail lacquers and specialty cosmetic products where slow evaporation and resin compatibility are required. The material is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, meeting typical purity thresholds for industrial solvent applications. Some suppliers offer material conforming to defined purity specifications.

These specifications ensure the product is suitable for cosmetic-grade end uses. The chemical remains a versatile component for manufacturers seeking reliable evaporation profiles and high solvency power.

name: Spermidine
description:
Spermidine (CAS 124-20-9 ), also abbreviated as SPD, is a naturally occurring polyamine sourced from plant and microbial origins, available in both synthetic and natural-extract forms.

In commercial supply, it functions as a bioactive ingredient targeting cellular renewal pathways, a biochemical reagent in research workflows, and a functional additive in premium formulations.

In cosmetics and personal care, SPD is incorporated into anti-aging serums and scalp treatments where it supports hair follicle longevity and skin renewal at the cellular level.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as the active ingredient in longevity-focused dietary supplements, capsules, and functional foods — a fast-growing category driven by autophagy research.

In biotechnology, spermidine is a critical reagent in cell culture media, nucleic acid stabilization protocols, and enzyme activity studies for various laboratory applications.

Food-grade applications include functional food fortification, where wheat germ extract standardized to spermidine content is the most commercially established delivery format for manufacturers.

Spermidine is supplied as a trihydrochloride salt in powder form, which offers improved stability over the free base. Standard grades include research-grade (high-purity ≥98%) and cosmetic/nutraceutical-grade material.

Wheat germ extract standardized to defined spermidine content is also commercially available as a natural-source alternative for food and supplement applications meeting specific quality requirements.

name: Dodecylamine
description:
Dodecylamine (CAS 124-22-1 ), also known as Laurylamine, is a long-chain primary amine used across surfactant manufacturing, polymer processing, and surface treatment applications. Its twelve-carbon chain structure positions it as a building block for cationic and amphoteric surfactants.

This chemical serves as a vital component in the production of corrosion inhibitors and flotation agents. In mineral processing, it functions as a collector agent in froth flotation, selectively binding to silica and oxide mineral surfaces to enable ore separation.

Polymer formulators use it as a curing agent and crosslinker in epoxy systems, improving adhesion and mechanical performance in coatings and adhesives. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as an intermediate in the synthesis of quaternary ammonium compounds.

These compounds and amine oxides are frequently used in conditioning and cleansing formulations. In plastics, it acts as a surface modifier for fillers and pigments, improving dispersion and compatibility within polymer matrices during the manufacturing process.

Dodecylamine is supplied as a solid flake or liquid melt, depending on temperature and packaging format. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade material, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 99%+ to meet industrial requirements.

Bulk quantities are available in drums and IBCs, with some suppliers offering flaked product for easier handling in solid-state processing. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and performance in diverse chemical environments.

name: Stearamide
description:
Stearamide (CAS 124-26-5 ), also sold under trade names Kemamide S and Adogen 42, is the amide derivative of stearic acid used as a slip agent, lubricant, and surface modifier across plastics, personal care, and industrial processing.

It reduces surface friction and controls interfilm adhesion without altering bulk material properties. In plastics and polymer film production, it functions as an internal and external slip agent, migrating to the film surface.

This migration reduces the coefficient of friction in polyethylene and polypropylene packaging. Textile and leather finishing operations use it as a softening and lubricating additive to improve hand feel and reduce fiber-on-fiber abrasion.

In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it acts as a solid lubricant component and release agent in drawing compounds and stamping formulations. This versatility makes it essential for high-performance manufacturing environments.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into stick formulations, creams, and waxes where controlled texture and emollient structuring are required. It provides stability and consistency to various cosmetic and topical applications.

Stearamide is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake, with particle size and melt point specifications varying by grade. Technical and industrial grades are standard for plastics and lubricant applications.

Cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care use is available from select suppliers. We ensure all batches meet rigorous internal quality controls to guarantee performance and consistency for our global clients.

name: Dimethyloctadecylamine
description:
Dimethyloctadecylamine (CAS 124-28-7 ), also known commercially as Dimantine, is a long-chain tertiary amine used as a building block for cationic surfactants and corrosion inhibitors. Its C18 fatty chain structure makes it a preferred intermediate where controlled surface activity is required.

This chemical is essential for quaternary ammonium compounds across industrial and personal care markets. In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and boundary lubricant additive, forming protective films on metal surfaces.

These films help to reduce wear and oxidation in heavy machinery. Quaternization of this amine yields fabric softeners, hair conditioning agents, and antistatic compounds used in various rinse-off and leave-on personal care formulations.

It also serves as a flotation collector intermediate in mineral processing. In this application, its affinity for mineral surfaces improves ore separation efficiency, making it a vital component for mining operations and resource extraction.

Formulators in the coatings and asphalt industries use it to produce emulsifiers. These specialized emulsifiers improve the adhesion and dispersion of bituminous materials, ensuring better performance in road construction and industrial coatings.

The product is supplied as a low-melting waxy solid or liquid at elevated temperatures, typically in flake or molten bulk form. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels commonly ranging from 95% to 99%.

It is available in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities depending on application volume requirements. This versatility in packaging ensures that both small-scale formulators and large industrial manufacturers can meet their specific production needs.

name: Octadecylamine
description:
Octadecylamine (CAS 124-30-1 ), also known as stearamine, is a long-chain primary amine derived from stearic acid. It functions as a surface-active agent and chemical intermediate.

This versatile compound serves as a corrosion inhibitor and chemical intermediate across a broad range of industrial manufacturing processes. It is essential for various high-performance applications.

In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor and boundary lubricant additive. It forms a protective monolayer on metal surfaces to prevent oxidation and wear.

Textile and paper manufacturers use it as a softening and antistatic agent. This improves the handle of materials and significantly reduces static buildup in finished consumer and industrial goods.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal lubricant and slip agent. It effectively reduces friction between polymer surfaces during complex extrusion and film production cycles.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into conditioning products and emulsions. It contributes to surface adhesion and emulsification performance in high-quality cosmetic formulations.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form. Technical grade is the most common offering, with purity levels ranging from 90% to 99%.

name: Carbon dioxide
description:
Carbon dioxide (CAS 124-38-9 ), also supplied under the refrigerant designation R744 and approved food additive E-290 , is one of the most broadly sourced industrial gases in global supply chains.

It functions as a pH modifier, preservative, carbonation agent, and refrigerant across food processing, energy, and industrial applications. In food and beverage production, CO₂ is injected into soft drinks and beer.

This process delivers carbonation and contributes mild acidity to the final product. Cold chain logistics and perishable food packaging rely on it in solid form and as a modified atmosphere gas to suppress microbial growth.

In oil and gas operations, it is injected into reservoirs for enhanced oil recovery. It is also used in supercritical extraction processes for natural flavors, hops, and caffeine to ensure high purity and efficiency.

Water treatment facilities use it to neutralize alkaline effluent and stabilize pH before discharge or distribution. Carbon dioxide is supplied as a compressed gas in cylinders or as a cryogenic liquid in bulk tankers.

It is also available as dry ice in block or pellet form for various cooling needs. Food-grade and beverage-grade specifications are available meeting FCC and E-290 purity standards for safety.

Industrial and technical grades are also standard for non-food processing applications. These grades ensure reliable performance across manufacturing, chemical synthesis, and environmental management sectors worldwide.

name: Dimethylamine
description:
Dimethylamine (CAS 124-40-3 ), commonly abbreviated as DMA, is a secondary amine supplied primarily as an aqueous solution or compressed gas. It functions as a chemical intermediate and pH modifier across food, agricultural, and industrial manufacturing processes.

In food and flavoring applications, DMA contributes to characteristic fishy and fermented notes, and its presence is monitored as a quality marker in seafood processing. As a building block in synthesis, it is used to produce dimethylformamide (DMF) and dimethylacetamide.

These solvents are critical to pharmaceutical and polymer manufacturing. In agrochemical production, DMA serves as a precursor to herbicide salts, particularly dimethylamine salts of glyphosate and 2,4-D formulations.

It also appears in the manufacture of surfactants, ion exchange resins, and rubber accelerators where controlled amine functionality is required. DMA is supplied as a compressed liquefied gas or as aqueous solutions.

The most common concentrations for aqueous solutions are 40% and 60%. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial synthesis, with solution grades available for applications requiring easier handling and metered dosing.

Packaging ranges from cylinders and ISO tanks for gas supply to IBCs and bulk tankers for aqueous solution delivery. This ensures safe transport and storage for various industrial and laboratory requirements.

name: Sodium methoxide
description:
Sodium methoxide (CAS 124-41-4 ), also sold as sodium methylate and abbreviated NaOMe, is a strong alkoxide base used industrially as a catalyst and chemical intermediate. Its reactivity with esters, fats, and acidic compounds drives transesterification, condensation, and neutralization processes across multiple manufacturing sectors.

In biodiesel production, NaOMe catalyzes the transesterification of vegetable oils and animal fats, converting triglycerides into fatty acid methyl esters at commercial scale. Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it to drive condensation and cyclization reactions in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

Controlled basicity is critical to yield and purity in these chemical processes. In polymer processing, it initiates anionic polymerization and acts as a catalyst precursor for producing specialty plastics and resins. These applications require high-purity reagents to ensure consistent results.

Food-grade sodium methylate is also used in edible oil refining to remove free fatty acids and adjust the composition of fats and shortenings. This process is essential for the production of high-quality food products and industrial ingredients used globally.

Sodium methoxide is supplied as a liquid solution, most commonly at 25% and 30% in methanol, and as a dry powder or granules for applications requiring solvent-free handling. This versatility allows manufacturers to choose the best form for their specific operational needs.

Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material to meet the purity requirements of each sector. Solution concentrations and moisture specifications vary by grade, with pharmaceutical supply typically held to tighter limits for safety and efficacy.

name: Carbamide peroxide
description:
Carbamide peroxide (CAS 124-43-6 ), also known as urea peroxide and designated E927b , is a stable solid oxidant that releases active oxygen upon contact with water.

This controlled release makes it a practical alternative to liquid hydrogen peroxide in bleaching, whitening, and antimicrobial applications across multiple industries and manufacturing sectors.

In personal care and cosmetics, it is the active ingredient in tooth whitening gels, ear drops, and hair bleach formulations, where its solid form allows precise dosing and extended shelf life.

Textile and paper processors use it as a bleaching agent for fibers and pulp, particularly where dry or low-moisture processing conditions are preferred for efficiency and safety.

In water treatment, it functions as an oxidizing biocide for disinfection and odor control in both industrial and municipal systems, providing a stable source of active oxygen for purification.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into topical antiseptic preparations and oral care products, sourcing it to USP or BP specifications to ensure the highest levels of purity.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder, typically at 35% active oxygen content by weight. Standard commercial grades include pharmaceutical and food-grade specifications to meet requirements.

Technical grade is also available for industrial bleaching and water treatment applications. This versatile oxidant remains a staple for companies requiring stable, high-performance bleaching agents.

name: Methanesulfonyl chloride
description:
Methanesulfonyl chloride ( CAS 124-63-0 ), commonly known as mesyl chloride, is a highly reactive sulfonylating agent used across pharmaceutical and agrochemical synthesis.

It converts hydroxyl groups into mesylate leaving groups, enabling downstream substitution, elimination, and cyclization reactions in multi-step synthesis workflows for various industries.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to prepare mesylate intermediates that facilitate the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients where controlled stereochemistry is required.

Agrochemical producers rely on it during the synthesis of herbicides, fungicides, and insecticides where sulfonylation steps are critical to building the target molecule effectively.

It also supports the preparation of sulfonamide compounds used in drug discovery and medicinal chemistry programs. Contract research organizations use it for protecting group chemistry.

Methanesulfonyl chloride is supplied as a liquid in standard packaging formats ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums for industrial-scale synthesis and production.

It is available in technical and high-purity grades, with reagent-grade and synthesis-grade specifications commonly offered to meet pharmaceutical and agrochemical manufacturing requirements.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and moisture-control packaging when sourcing for GMP-aligned production environments to ensure the highest quality and performance standards.

name: Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium chloride
description:
Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium chloride (CAS 124-64-1 ), commonly sourced as THPC, is a reactive phosphorus-based flame retardant used across textile, leather, and industrial substrate treatments.

It functions by chemically bonding into fibrous or polymer matrices during curing, delivering durable flame retardancy rather than surface-level protection for various materials.

In textile finishing, THPC is reacted with nitrogen-containing compounds such as urea or melamine to produce wash-durable flame-retardant finishes on cotton and cellulosic fabrics.

This process is widely specified for workwear, military, and protective clothing. Leather processors apply it during wet finishing to meet fire resistance standards required in automotive upholstery.

In pulp and paper manufacturing, it functions as both a flame retardant and a cross-linking agent, improving dimensional stability in treated specialty papers and industrial products.

Building and construction applications include flame-retardant treatment of nonwoven materials and insulation substrates where regulatory compliance drives specific material requirements.

THPC is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 80% active content, which is the standard commercial concentration for industrial use in most manufacturing sectors.

It is available in technical grade, with supply in drums and intermediate bulk containers to suit both formulators and large-scale processors requiring consistent chemical supply.

name: Aminomethylpropanol
description:
Aminomethylpropanol (CAS 124-68-5 ), commercially known as AMP, is a multifunctional amino alcohol used across personal care, coatings, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH adjuster and neutralizing agent.

This versatile chemical enables formulators to control alkalinity in aqueous systems with precision. In personal care formulations, including lotions and shampoos, AMP neutralizes carbomer and acrylate polymers to build viscosity.

It is also essential for stabilizing emulsions in various cosmetic products. Coatings manufacturers use it to neutralize waterborne resins, improving dispersion stability and film formation in architectural and industrial paints.

Pharmaceutical and topical formulations rely on AMP to buffer active ingredients and adjust final product pH within required specification ranges. Its mild biocidal contribution also supports preservation efficacy in cosmetic systems.

This is particularly useful where broad-spectrum protection is required for long-term stability. Aminomethylpropanol is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 95% and 100% concentrations for industrial use.

Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly traded forms, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care applications. Bulk supply is available in drums and IBC containers.

Smaller packaging options are also available for laboratory and specialty use. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure quality and consistency across all manufacturing batches.

name: Isoborneol
description:

In fragrance compounding, isoborneol is used to impart cool, woody, and camphor-like notes in fine fragrances, functional perfumery, and scented personal care products for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a synthetic intermediate, particularly in the production of camphor USP and related active ingredients used in various medical and topical applications.

In cosmetic formulations such as creams, balms, and topical products, it functions as a carrier component where its terpene character supports penetration-enhancing blends for skin care.

FEMA 2158 status supports its use as a flavoring agent in food and beverage applications where camphoraceous profiles are required for specific consumer taste profiles and products.

Isoborneol is supplied as a white crystalline solid or flake. It is available in fragrance-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher for clients.

name: Almond oil PEG-6 esters

In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetics, including bath oils and hair conditioners, it functions as a self-emulsifying component that also contributes moisturization to the finished formula.

Solubilizing fragrance and lipophilic actives in aqueous personal care bases is a key procurement driver, reducing the need for additional co-emulsifiers in complex chemical systems.

In food-contact and nutraceutical coating applications, it supports uniform oil dispersion across tablet or confectionery surfaces to ensure consistent product appearance and performance.

Coatings and adhesive formulations use it as a surface-active wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and film uniformity during the application and curing processes.

Almond oil PEG-6 esters is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity oily liquid, suitable for direct incorporation into batch processes for efficient manufacturing workflows.

name: 2-ethylhexyl diphenyl phosphate

2-Ethylhexyl diphenyl phosphate (CAS 1241-94-7 ), commercially known as Santicizer 141, Phosflex 362, Disflamoll, or by the abbreviation EHDPP, is an organophosphate ester used across polymer and coating systems.

In vinyl and cellulosic polymer compounds, EHDPP functions as a primary or secondary plasticizer, delivering flame retardancy without requiring a separate halogenated additive for the mixture.

Coating formulators use it in fire-retardant architectural and industrial coatings where both flexibility and reduced combustibility are specification requirements for the final application.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to lower viscosity during processing while meeting flammability standards in construction and transportation end markets globally.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it contributes anti-wear performance and thermal stability under high-load conditions, enhancing the durability of the mechanical systems.

EHDPP is supplied as a clear liquid at ambient temperature, suitable for direct blending into polymer melts, solvent-based coatings, and various industrial fluid systems.

name: Tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate

Tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate (CAS 1244733-77-4 ), commercially known as Levagard PP, is a chlorinated organophosphate flame retardant used across rigid and flexible polymer systems.

In polyurethane foam manufacturing, it is incorporated directly into the polyol blend to meet fire performance standards. This includes rigid insulation panels and flexible seating foam applications.

Automotive and aerospace interior components use it to achieve UL 94 ratings in molded plastic parts. Common uses include dashboards, seat backs, and various cabin panels for safety compliance.

Electronics manufacturers apply it in encapsulants, potting compounds, and cable jacketing. It provides halogenated flame retardancy alongside excellent processing compatibility for sensitive components.

In building and construction, it is used in spray-applied and boardstock insulation systems. These applications are critical where building codes mandate specific fire classifications for safety.

This versatile biopolymer is utilized across food, personal care, construction, and oilfield applications. In cement and concrete systems, it suspends aggregates and controls bleed water without retarding set time.

This is a critical performance requirement for self-leveling and shotcrete formulations. Oilfield drilling and completion fluids use the gum to maintain viscosity and particle suspension under high-temperature conditions.

It remains stable in high-salinity environments where many other biopolymers fail. In food applications, it stabilizes emulsions and controls texture in beverages, dressings, and dairy-style products at low use levels.

name: Phosphotungstic acid
description:
Phosphotungstic acid (CAS 12501-23-4 ), also known as phosphowolframic acid, is a heteropolyacid used industrially as a strong acid catalyst and precipitating reagent. Its high acidity and oxidizing capacity make it a functional choice across catalysis and analytical chemistry.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a precipitating agent for alkaloids and basic nitrogen compounds during purification and quality control workflows. Histology and electron microscopy laboratories use it as a tissue staining reagent.

This chemical provides contrast enhancement for collagen and connective tissue structures in biological samples. As a solid acid catalyst, it supports acid-catalyzed organic synthesis reactions including esterification and condensation processes.

These processes are highly relevant to fine chemical production. In printing and packaging, it contributes to the formulation of certain inks and dye fixatives where controlled precipitation of colorants is required for the final product.

Phosphotungstic acid is supplied as a crystalline solid, typically as a hydrated powder or granules. It is available in reagent-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet various industrial and laboratory requirements.

Reagent-grade material commonly meets purity thresholds suitable for laboratory and pharmaceutical use. Bulk quantities are accessible for industrial catalyst and manufacturing applications with various packaging options.

Packaging options range from laboratory-scale units to multi-kilogram consignments. This ensures that both small-scale research facilities and large-scale industrial manufacturers can source the material according to their specific needs.

name: Polyquaternium-51
description:
Polyquaternium-51 (CAS 125275-25-4 ) is a phospholipid-based cationic polymer designed to mimic the moisture-retention behavior of cell membranes. It delivers durable hydration and surface conditioning in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations.

In skincare and facial care products, it forms a biomimetic film on the skin surface that binds moisture and reduces transepidermal water loss without occlusion. This makes it an essential ingredient for high-end moisturizing serums.

Hair care formulators use it in conditioners and leave-on treatments, where it improves wet combability. It imparts a smooth, substantive feel through electrostatic deposition on damaged hair fibers during the washing process.

Ophthalmic formulations, including contact lens solutions and eye drops, rely on its biocompatibility and surface-wetting properties. These characteristics improve overall comfort and lens lubrication for the end user.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it functions as a rheology modifier and surface conditioner. This supports uniform active ingredient distribution across the skin surface for better therapeutic outcomes and absorption.

The material is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active polymer content typically ranging from 30% to 50% depending on the grade. Standard commercial grades correspond to the PMB and Purebright product lines.

The product is available in cosmetic and pharmaceutical quality to meet various regulatory requirements. Packaging is typically in drums or intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial liquid handling and storage.

name: Light stabilizer UV-571
description:
Light Stabilizer UV-571 (CAS 125304-04-3 ), also marketed as Benzotriazolyl Dodecyl p-Cresol, is a benzotriazole-based UV absorber that protects organic materials from photodegradation caused by UV radiation.

Its long dodecyl chain improves compatibility with non-polar substrates and reduces volatility during high-temperature processing. This makes it an ideal choice for demanding industrial manufacturing environments.

In polyolefins, PVC, and engineering plastics, UV-571 is incorporated to extend service life in outdoor applications such as agricultural films, automotive parts, and construction profiles.

Coating formulators use it in industrial and automotive topcoats where long-term gloss retention and color stability are required. It provides a robust barrier against the harmful effects of sunlight.

Rubber compounders add it to EPDM and other elastomers used in weatherstripping, roofing membranes, and outdoor sealing profiles. It ensures flexibility and durability under constant environmental exposure.

It is also used in pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealants where UV-induced yellowing or embrittlement would compromise bond integrity. This helps maintain the structural performance of the adhesive over time.

UV-571 is supplied as a light yellow to pale amber liquid or low-melting solid, depending on temperature and grade. It is available in technical grade, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Purity is confirmed by HPLC to ensure consistent performance. Packaging options generally include drums and IBC containers suited to bulk industrial procurement and large-scale chemical distribution.

name: Bispyribac
description:
Bispyribac (CAS 125401-75-4 ) is a pyrimidinyloxybenzoic acid herbicide used in rice cultivation to control a broad spectrum of weeds. Bispyribac sodium, its commercially dominant salt form, is the active ingredient found in selective post-emergence herbicide formulations.

These formulations target grassy and broadleaf weeds in paddy fields. The primary use is selective weed control in transplanted and direct-seeded rice, where it inhibits acetolactate synthase (ALS) to suppress weeds such as barnyardgrass and sedges.

It effectively manages broadleaf species without damaging the crop. Formulated as aqueous solutions or water-dispersible granules, it is applied post-emergence at low use rates, making it a cost-efficient active for rice-growing regions.

Agrochemical manufacturers incorporate it into single-active and combination herbicide products registered for paddy and upland rice systems. It is also used as a reference standard in residue analysis and regulatory submission workflows.

Bispyribac sodium is the primary commercial form supplied as a technical-grade solid or as formulated concentrates. Standard supply formats include technical material (TC) and soluble concentrate (SC) formulations at defined concentrations.

Material is typically assessed against established agrochemical purity specifications aligned with FAO/WHO guidelines. This ensures the chemical meets the necessary safety and efficacy requirements for global agricultural distribution and application.

Contact us for supply of Bispyribac

name: Behenyl polyethylene glycol methacrylate
description:
Behenyl polyethylene glycol methacrylate ( CAS 125441-87-4 ), also known by the abbreviation BEPEGMA, is a polymerizable macromonomer combining a long-chain C18–C22 alkyl group with a PEG spacer.

It is used to build amphiphilic functionality directly into polymer backbones, enabling rheology control, emulsification, and surface modification within a single copolymerizable unit for various industries.

In personal care formulations, it is copolymerized into associative thickeners and film-forming polymers that provide viscosity control and sensory enhancement in creams, lotions, and styling products.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulators incorporate it into polymer systems where both surface-active behavior and thickening are required in a single ingredient for high performance.

In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a reactive compatibilizer or surface-modifying comonomer, improving substrate wetting and adhesion in coatings and dispersions during the manufacturing process.

It is also used to synthesize comb-type or graft copolymers where the PEG side chains provide steric stabilization in aqueous dispersion systems, ensuring long-term stability and shelf life.

Behenyl polyethylene glycol methacrylate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or viscous paste, depending on the PEG chain length of the specific grade provided by the chemical manufacturer.

It is available in technical grade for industrial polymer synthesis applications. Specifications and molecular weight distributions vary by supplier, so buyers should confirm purity prior to sourcing.

name: Zinc glucoheptonate
description:
Zinc glucoheptonate (CAS 12565-63-8 ) is a zinc salt of glucoheptonic acid used as a bioavailable zinc source in nutritional and agricultural applications. Its chelated structure improves zinc uptake compared to inorganic zinc salts.

This makes it a preferred form for fortification and supplementation. Zinc alpha-glucoheptonate is a recognized alternative name buyers may encounter in technical specifications and regulatory filings during procurement.

In food and dietary supplement manufacturing, it functions as a zinc fortification agent in functional foods, beverages, and mineral premixes. It is ideal where clean-label mineral sources are required for production.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it in oral zinc supplements and effervescent tablets. Its chelated form supports consistent dosing and formulation stability across various delivery systems and medicinal applications.

In agriculture and animal feed, it supplies bioavailable zinc to support crop nutrition programs. It is also used in livestock feed blends targeting mineral deficiency correction and overall animal health improvements.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into skincare and haircare products. In these applications, zinc delivery and mild antioxidant stabilization are primary formulation objectives for high-quality cosmetic goods.

Zinc glucoheptonate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with material commonly tested against FCC and USP standards.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers requiring large volumes for manufacturing. Smaller quantities are also available for formulation development and pilot-scale testing in laboratory environments.

Contact us for supply of Zinc glucoheptonate

name: Tridecyl Ethylhexanoate
description:
Tridecyl Ethylhexanoate (CAS 125804-07-1 ), also known as Tridecyl 2-ethylhexanoate, is a synthetic ester used as a lubricant and plasticizer across industrial formulations. It delivers low-viscosity lubrication and polymer softening without volatility concerns.

In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it functions as a base fluid or additive component in cutting oils, rolling fluids, and release agents where clean, low-residue performance is required for the application.

Formulators in the coatings and sealants sector incorporate it to improve flexibility and substrate adhesion in finished films. It provides consistent performance across a wide range of temperature conditions and environments.

In plastics processing, it acts as a secondary plasticizer to enhance the softness and workability of polymer compounds. This is particularly useful in applications requiring high levels of low-temperature flexibility.

Adhesive manufacturers use it to adjust tack and flow properties in both hot-melt and solvent-based systems. Its chemical stability ensures that the final adhesive product maintains its integrity over long periods of storage.

Tridecyl Ethylhexanoate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in technical grade, suited to industrial lubricant, polymer, and coating applications where high purity and performance are essential.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with packaging options varying by supplier volume requirements. This ensures efficient handling and integration into large-scale manufacturing and production lines.

Contact us for supply of Tridecyl Ethylhexanoate

name: 3-bromo-1-chloro-5,5-dimethylhydantoin
description:
3-Bromo-1-chloro-5,5-dimethylhydantoin ( CAS 126-06-7 ), commonly known as BCDMH, is a halogenated hydantoin compound that functions as a dual-action biocide. It releases both bromine and chlorine upon contact with water.

It is used across water treatment, food processing sanitation, and personal care applications as a controlled-release disinfectant and oxidizer. In recreational and industrial water treatment, tablets or granules are used.

These maintain microbial control in pools, spas, cooling towers, and process water systems where stable halogen release is required. Food processing facilities use it as a sanitizing agent for equipment and surfaces.

It is particularly effective in wash water where bromine-based disinfection offers performance advantages over chlorine alone. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a preservative and antimicrobial active.

It is commonly found in rinse-off formulations and industrial cleaning products. Pulp and paper operations also apply it for slime control in process water, where consistent oxidizing activity reduces biofilm formation.

BCDMH is supplied as compressed tablets, granules, and powder to suit different dosing and dissolution requirements. Standard grades include technical and water treatment grades for industrial use.

Purity specifications are typically at 96% or higher active halogen content. Packaging ranges from small drum quantities to bulk totes for high-volume industrial procurement and global distribution.

name: Sucrose acetate isobutyrate

Sucrose acetate isobutyrate (CAS 126-13-6 ), commercially known as SAIB or E444 , is a food-grade ester derived from sucrose used primarily as a density-adjusting agent and emulsion stabilizer.

Its high viscosity and compatibility with flavor oils make it a functional ingredient in beverage and personal care manufacturing. In carbonated and non-carbonated beverages, SAIB acts as a weighting agent.

It is used for citrus and other flavor emulsions, preventing oil separation and maintaining a uniform appearance throughout shelf life. Beverage formulators use it alongside brominated vegetable oil alternatives.

This helps to meet clean-label and regulatory requirements in global markets. In personal care, it functions as a film-forming agent and fixative in hair sprays and styling products, contributing to hold and gloss.

Cosmetic formulators also incorporate it as a carrier solvent in fragrance and color cosmetic applications where controlled viscosity and low water solubility are procurement requirements for high-end manufacturing.

SAIB is supplied as a clear, viscous liquid in bulk and intermediate packaging formats suited to food and cosmetic manufacturing. It is available in food-grade quality compliant with EU regulations.

The material meets FCC standards for use in the United States. Technical-grade material is also available for non-food industrial applications, ensuring versatility across various chemical processing sectors.

name: Neopentyl glycol
description:
Neopentyl glycol (CAS 126-30-7 ), commonly abbreviated as NPG, is a diol monomer used as a foundational building block in polymer and resin synthesis. Its symmetrical structure resists hydrolysis and oxidation, giving finished materials improved durability.

This chemical is a key factor for formulators specifying long-life coatings and resins. NPG is a primary raw material in alkyd, polyester, and polyurethane resin production, where it improves weatherability and chemical resistance.

In industrial and architectural coatings, it provides essential stability. In printing inks, it contributes to binder systems that require adhesion stability across various substrates and challenging exposure conditions.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use NPG-based polyesters to achieve flexible yet durable bond lines. These are frequently utilized in construction and automotive assemblies to ensure long-term structural integrity.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a humectant and solvent carrier in emollients. Its low irritation profile supports use in skin-contact products, making it a versatile choice for cosmetic applications.

The product is supplied as white crystalline flakes or powder, with molten liquid form available for bulk industrial shipments. Standard commercial grades include technical and polymer-grade specifications.

These grades are perfectly suited to resin and coating production. Cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity thresholds is also available for personal care applications requiring high-quality standards.

name: Sulfolane
description:
Sulfolane (CAS 126-33-0 ), also known as thiophane dioxide, is a high-boiling, water-miscible polar aprotic solvent used across extraction, purification, and reaction processes in demanding industrial applications.

Its thermal stability and selectivity make it a preferred solvent where conventional options fall short. In natural gas and refinery operations, it is the active solvent in the Sulfinol and other licensed processes.

This chemical is essential for removing hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide from gas streams. Petrochemical producers use it in aromatic extraction units, particularly BTX separation, where it selectively recovers benzene, toluene, and xylene.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a reaction solvent for synthesis steps requiring a stable, high-polarity medium. It is particularly useful in environments that must tolerate strong bases and nucleophiles during production.

In electronics, it is used in electrolyte formulations and as a processing solvent where low volatility is critical. Chemical inertness ensures product consistency in these highly sensitive manufacturing environments.

The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for specialized applications.

Specifications commonly reference purity by GC, water content, and color (APHA) depending on the end-use requirement. This ensures the material meets the rigorous demands of both the pharmaceutical and electronics industries.

description:
Silver citrate (CAS 126-45-4 ) is an inorganic silver salt used as an antimicrobial and biocidal agent across pharmaceutical and biomedical applications. Trisilver citrate is a recognized alternative name buyers may encounter in technical literature and supplier documentation.

It functions by releasing silver ions in controlled concentrations to inhibit microbial growth in formulated products and treated materials. In pharmaceutical and wound care formulations, it serves as an active antimicrobial ingredient.

This compound is preferred where controlled silver ion release is required without the harshness associated with silver nitrate. Biomedical device manufacturers incorporate it into coatings and surface treatments to reduce microbial colonization.

It is frequently used on catheters, implants, and surgical instruments to maintain sterility. In biotechnology, it is used as a preservative component in reagent systems and biological media where low-toxicity antimicrobial protection is needed.

Research and diagnostic product developers also source it as a reference compound or active ingredient in antimicrobial testing protocols. The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder for various industrial uses.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and technical-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting purity requirements relevant to drug substance and excipient applications.

Packaging is typically offered in small laboratory quantities through to kilogram-scale lots, reflecting its primary use in high-value, low-volume formulations. This ensures flexibility for both research and production needs.

name: Dipentaerythritol
description:
Dipentaerythritol (CAS 126-58-9 ), also known commercially as Dipentek and abbreviated as DiPE, is a high-functionality polyol produced as a co-product in pentaerythritol manufacturing.

Its six hydroxyl groups make it a reactive building block for high-performance resins, esters, and crosslinked polymer systems across coatings, adhesives, and polymer industries.

In alkyd and radiation-curable coatings, DiPE reacts with fatty acids and isocyanates to produce resins with superior hardness, durability, and crosslink density compared to standard systems.

Lubricant ester synthesis is another primary outlet, where DiPE-based synthetic esters deliver high thermal stability and low volatility for demanding aerospace and industrial applications.

In UV-curable adhesives and sealants, it functions as a core acrylate ester intermediate, enabling tight network formation and fast cure response during the manufacturing process.

Personal care formulators use DiPE-derived esters as emollient carriers and film-forming agents in long-wear cosmetic products to improve texture and performance for the end user.

Dipentaerythritol is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 90% minimum for most uses.

Some suppliers offer high-purity grades targeting ester synthesis applications where tighter hydroxyl value specifications are required to meet specific industrial performance criteria.

name: Triisobutyl phosphate
description:
Triisobutyl phosphate (CAS 126-71-6 ), also known as TIBP, is an organophosphate ester used across industrial and specialty chemical applications as a solvent, plasticizer, and defoamer.

Its controlled surface activity makes it effective at suppressing foam in process systems, while its solvency profile supports formulation work in coatings and polymer systems.

In coatings and adhesives, TIBP functions as a coalescing solvent and plasticizer, improving film formation and flexibility in finished products for various industrial applications.

Textile and paper processing operations use it as a defoaming agent in aqueous systems where foam buildup disrupts throughput and product quality during the manufacturing cycle.

Printing ink formulators incorporate TIBP as a solvent carrier to control viscosity and pigment dispersion, ensuring consistent application and color quality in high-speed printing.

In polymer and elastomer compounding, it acts as a secondary plasticizer and flame-retardant additive, contributing to both processability and compliance with fire performance requirements.

Triisobutyl phosphate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging. Technical grade is the primary commercial form, meeting purity specifications for industrial use.

Textile and upholstery manufacturers applied it as a flame-retardant finish for synthetic fabrics, particularly in applications requiring compliance with flammability testing requirements.

Electronics and electrical component producers used it to achieve UL 94 flame ratings in housings and insulating materials. Paper and leather processing operations also employed it where surface flame retardancy was required.

In nuclear fuel reprocessing and rare earth metal extraction, TBP functions as a selective solvent for separating metal ions from aqueous streams, a well-established role in hydrometallurgical processing.

Printing ink and surface coating formulators use it as a solvent and defoamer, where it reduces surface tension in high-speed application processes to ensure a smooth finish.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, TBP acts as a plasticizer and flame-retardant additive, incorporated into cellulose acetate, PVC, and polyurethane systems to improve flexibility.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid producers also use TBP as an anti-wear additive and carrier solvent for active ingredients in cutting and hydraulic fluid formulations for heavy machinery.

Tributyl phosphate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for large-volume industrial buyers requiring consistent supply chains.

name: Sodium epichlorohydrinsulfonate
description:
Sodium epichlorohydrinsulfonate (CAS 126-83-0 ), also known as CHPS-Na, is a chlorinated sulfonate salt used as a reactive intermediate and functional additive in specialty chemical formulations.

It combines a reactive chlorohydrin group with a sulfonate moiety, enabling covalent bonding in polymer and surface modification processes. In personal care formulations, CHPS-Na functions as a humectant and conditioning agent.

This chemical contributes to moisture retention in skin and hair care products. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic building block for active ingredients and excipient modification where controlled reactivity is required.

Its biocidal activity supports preservation applications in topical formulations where both antimicrobial efficacy and compatibility with ionic systems are needed. In polymer chemistry, it serves as a sulfonating agent.

Sodium 2-ethylhexyl sulfate (CAS 126-92-1 ), also known commercially as Tergemist, is an anionic surfactant used across industrial and personal care applications. It functions primarily as an emulsifier, dispersant, and wetting agent.

This chemical enables uniform mixing of incompatible phases in aqueous systems. In textile and leather processing, it improves dye penetration and ensures even distribution of treatment chemicals across fiber surfaces.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, body washes, and cleansing products where controlled foaming and emulsification are required. It is valued for its stability and performance in various formulations.

Water treatment operations use it as a dispersant to stabilize suspensions and prevent scale or particulate buildup in process water. This helps maintain the efficiency of industrial cooling and heating systems.

In printing and packaging, it supports ink dispersion and substrate wetting, improving adhesion and print uniformity on treated surfaces. This ensures high-quality results on a variety of different materials.

Sodium 2-ethylhexyl sulfate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations commonly available in the 35–40% range. This concentration allows for easy handling and dilution.

name: Sodium diacetate
description:
Sodium diacetate (CAS 126-96-5 ), also designated E262ii , is a compound of sodium acetate and acetic acid used commercially as a preservative, acidulant, and flavoring agent.

It delivers controlled acetic acid activity in solid form, giving formulators the functional profile of vinegar without handling liquid acid. In food manufacturing, it extends shelf life in baked goods.

It is used in meat products and snack seasonings by inhibiting mold and bacterial growth while contributing a mild vinegar flavor. Snack food producers apply it as a dry seasoning component on chips.

On crackers, it replicates salt-and-vinegar taste profiles with consistent dosing. As a pH buffer, it stabilizes acidic conditions in processed and packaged foods where liquid acidulants are impractical.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a buffering agent and mild preservative booster in products requiring controlled acidity. This ensures stability and safety in various cosmetic applications.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granular forms preferred in dry blending and seasoning applications for improved flowability and handling.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC and E262ii specifications is the standard commercial offering. Technical-grade material is available for non-food industrial applications where certification is not required.

name: Monoethanolamine thioglycolate
description:
Monoethanolamine thioglycolate (CAS 126-97-6 ), also known as ethanolamine thioglycolate, is a salt formed from monoethanolamine and thioglycolic acid used primarily as a reducing agent in hair treatment formulations.

It breaks disulfide bonds in keratin, enabling permanent restructuring of hair fiber. The compound is the active ingredient in professional and consumer permanent wave solutions, where it softens and reshapes the hair's internal protein structure.

Before neutralization fixes the new curl pattern, the chemical works to modify the protein bonds. Depilatory creams rely on it to degrade the disulfide linkages in hair at the skin surface, enabling chemical hair removal without mechanical abrasion.

Straightening and relaxing formulations for coarse or curly hair use it as an alternative to lye-based systems. This is particularly common in formulations targeting sensitive scalp conditions where milder chemical agents are preferred for safety.

It also functions in hair bond-breaking pre-treatments used ahead of color or bleach services to reduce mechanical damage. Monoethanolamine thioglycolate is supplied as a liquid, typically as an aqueous solution for industrial use.

Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial form, with specifications aligned to industry requirements for active content and pH range. Buyers should confirm concentration and purity certificates when sourcing for regulated personal care markets.

name: Chloroprene
description:
Chloroprene (CAS 126-99-8 ), also known as 2-chlorobutadiene, is the primary monomer used in the production of polychloroprene, one of the most commercially significant synthetic elastomers.

It undergoes controlled polymerization to yield a rubber with strong resistance to oils, weathering, and flame. These properties determine its suitability across demanding industrial applications.

The dominant use of this monomer is in the manufacture of neoprene rubber, where it is polymerized to produce sheets, adhesives, foams, and molded goods for global markets.

In the automotive and construction sectors, polychloroprene is processed into belts, hoses, seals, and gaskets. These components must perform under mechanical stress and chemical exposure.

Adhesive formulators rely on polychloroprene-based contact adhesives for bonding dissimilar substrates. This is common in footwear, furniture, and panel assembly industries.

Specialty wire and cable jacketing also depends on polychloroprene for its flame-retardant characteristics. This is essential for safety in demanding electrical installations.

The product is supplied as a stabilized liquid monomer, typically in bulk or isotank quantities. It is handled under inhibited conditions to prevent premature polymerization during transit.

Technical-grade specifications are standard for industrial supply. Purity levels and inhibitor content are defined per buyer or process requirements to ensure consistent performance.

name: Carminic acid
description:
Carminic acid (CAS 1260-17-9 ), also sold as Natural Red 4 and approved under E120 , is a natural red colorant derived from cochineal insects. It delivers stable, vivid red-to-purple hues across a wide pH range.

This makes it a preferred alternative to synthetic dyes in regulated markets. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to color products such as yogurts, confectionery, meat preparations, and fruit drinks.

It is ideal where clean-label or natural positioning is required. Personal care formulators incorporate it into lipsticks, blushers, and other color cosmetics where pigment stability and regulatory acceptance are critical sourcing criteria.

Textile and leather processors use it to achieve rich crimson shades on natural fibers, particularly wool and silk. Mordant-assisted dyeing produces excellent wash fastness for these specific industrial applications.

Printing ink producers also source it for specialty applications requiring natural-origin colorants with defined hue consistency. The material is supplied as a dark red to purple powder or as a liquid extract.

Concentration is typically expressed as carminic acid content. Food-grade material is available to FCC and E120 specifications, while cosmetic-grade supply meets EU and FDA compliance requirements.

Purity grades range from standard extract concentrations up to high-purity isolated carminic acid for technical and analytical use. This ensures versatility across various manufacturing and laboratory environments.

name: Ferrovanadium
description:
Ferrovanadium (CAS 12604-58-9 ), also referenced in procurement as Ferro V, is a master alloy of iron and vanadium used primarily to introduce vanadium into steel and other ferrous alloys during the melting process.

It allows steelmakers to achieve precise vanadium additions with minimal oxidation loss, improving control over final alloy composition. In high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel production, it refines grain structure and increases yield strength.

This makes it a standard additive for structural steel, pipelines, and reinforcing bar. Tool steel and high-speed steel manufacturers use it to boost hardness and wear resistance in cutting tools, dies, and drill bits.

In the aerospace and defense sectors, it contributes to titanium alloy formulations where vanadium content is required to stabilize the beta phase. Specialty applications include its use as a catalyst precursor in certain chemical processing environments.

It also serves as a performance additive in metalworking contexts. Ferrovanadium is supplied as lumps, granules, or crushed material, with vanadium content typically ranging from 40% to 80% V by weight.

Standard commercial grades include FeV40, FeV50, FeV60, and FeV80, corresponding to nominal vanadium concentrations. Buyers can source against ASTM , EN, or customer-specific compositional specifications depending on end-use requirements.

name: Nickel carbonate hydroxide
description:
Nickel carbonate hydroxide (CAS 12607-70-4 ), also referred to as trinickel carbonate tetrahydroxide, is an inorganic nickel salt used primarily as a catalyst precursor and as a source compound in nickel-based chemical processing.

Its controlled decomposition behavior and high nickel content make it a preferred starting material where precise metal loading and purity are critical procurement considerations for industrial manufacturers.

In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for producing nickel oxide and reduced nickel catalysts used in hydrogenation, reforming, and methanation processes across various chemical sectors.

Battery and electrochemical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing nickel-based active materials for rechargeable cell chemistries, ensuring high performance and stability in energy storage.

In the pigments and colorants sector, it functions as a raw material for producing green nickel-based inorganic pigments used in ceramics and specialty coatings for high-durability industrial applications.

Metallurgical operations also source it for nickel salt production and as a feedstock in refining and plating chemical preparation, where consistent chemical properties are required for quality control.

Nickel carbonate hydroxide is supplied as a fine green powder, with particle size and nickel content being key specification parameters for industrial buyers seeking reliable chemical performance.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with nickel content typically specified on a dry-weight basis. Purity and trace metal profiles vary by supplier, making certificate of analysis review standard practice.

name: Cyclodextrin
description:
Cyclodextrin (CAS 12619-70-4 ), also supplied under trade names such as Celdex, Ringdex P, and Rhodocap L 20, is a family of cyclic oligosaccharides produced from starch by enzymatic conversion.

In industry, cyclodextrins function as molecular encapsulants, trapping active ingredients within their cavity structure to improve stability, control release, and mask unwanted tastes or odors.

In food manufacturing, cyclodextrins encapsulate flavors, vitamins, and sensitive ingredients to extend shelf life and protect against heat or oxidation during processing stages.

Pharmaceutical formulators use them to improve the solubility and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble active compounds in oral, topical, and injectable dosage forms for patients.

In biotechnology, cyclodextrins serve as excipients in protein stabilization and as tools for cholesterol removal in cell culture media. Flavor houses also apply them for delivery.

They provide controlled-release taste profiles in confectionery, beverages, and functional food products. Cyclodextrin is available in powder and granular forms with alpha, beta, and gamma variants.

Beta-cyclodextrin is the most commercially prevalent type and is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. It meets various global quality standards for industrial use.

Hydroxypropyl beta-cyclodextrin, a chemically modified derivative, is also widely stocked for pharmaceutical and biotech applications where enhanced aqueous solubility is required for the final product.

name: 2-ethylhexyl phosphate
description:
2-Ethylhexyl phosphate (CAS 12645-31-7 ), also known as phosphated 2-ethyl hexanol, is a phosphate ester used across industrial sectors as a corrosion inhibitor, chelating agent, and pH buffer.

Its acid functionality allows it to interact with metal surfaces and dissolved ions, making it a functional additive in demanding process environments. In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it acts as an extreme-pressure additive.

It serves as a corrosion inhibitor, protecting ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces under high-load conditions. Water treatment programs incorporate it to sequester hardness ions and control scale formation in cooling towers.

In industrial water circuits, it provides essential stability. In mining and hydrometallurgy, it functions as a metal extractant or modifier in solvent extraction systems, supporting the selective separation of target metals.

This chemical is effective for separating metals from leach solutions. It is also used in phosphating baths and surface treatment processes where controlled acid activity and metal ion chelation are required for the process.

2-Ethylhexyl phosphate is typically supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature. It is available in technical grade, suited to industrial applications in lubricants, water treatment, and extractive metallurgy.

Bulk supply in drums and IBCs is standard for industrial procurement volumes. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing operations and specialized chemical processing facilities.

These applications are ideal where UV resistance and thermal stability are critical. Plastics processors incorporate it into PVC, polyolefins, and engineering polymers requiring color consistency through high-temperature compounding.

Printing inks for packaging and industrial graphics rely on it for strong tinting strength and batch-to-batch color reproducibility. Construction materials, including traffic paints, use it for long-term exterior durability.

This material accelerates oxidative crosslinking in alkyd and oil-based systems. Battery and energy material manufacturers use it as a direct precursor to cobalt oxide and lithium cobalt oxide cathode materials.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, it appears as an intermediate in cobalt refining circuits, where pH adjustment drives selective precipitation from leach solutions. This process ensures high-quality output for industrial use.

Textile and paper processing operations use cobalt hydroxide for catalytic bleaching and as a pH buffer in specific wet-chemistry stages. It is supplied as a fine powder or wet cake for various applications.

Moisture content and cobalt assay are the primary specification parameters buyers evaluate. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically expressed as minimum cobalt content by weight.

name: Potassium titanate
description:
Potassium titanate (CAS 12673-69-7 ), also known as potassium titanium oxide, is an inorganic ceramic compound produced in fibrous or whisker form for use as a functional filler and reinforcing agent.

It is primarily sourced for its flame retardancy and rheology modification properties across demanding industrial applications. In automotive and aerospace friction materials, these whiskers replace asbestos as a reinforcing filler.

The material is used in brake pads and clutch facings, improving thermal stability and wear resistance without hazardous fiber concerns. Plastics and polymer compounders incorporate it to enhance mechanical strength.

It provides fire resistance in engineering thermoplastics used in structural components. Building and construction applications include fire-retardant coatings and boards where the fibrous morphology contributes to flame suppression.

The compound also ensures dimensional stability under heat. In textile and paper processing, it functions as a functional additive in specialty coatings that require controlled rheology and improved surface durability.

Potassium titanate is supplied as a white powder or as short-fiber material, with fiber dimensions and aspect ratios specified to suit reinforcement applications. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Purity and particle morphology are typically confirmed by supplier specification sheets. Bulk and packaged formats are available depending on downstream processing requirements for industrial manufacturing.

name: Potassium acetate
description:
Potassium acetate (CAS 127-08-2 ), also known by the E-number E261 , is an acetate salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing as a pH buffer, preservative, and processing catalyst.

It delivers precise acidity control and stabilization in formulations where sodium-based alternatives are unsuitable. In food production, it functions as an acidity regulator and preservative in pickled products, sauces, and processed foods.

This ingredient offers a potassium-based alternative for sodium-restricted formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent in injectable solutions, oral liquids, and dialysis fluids where controlled pH is critical.

In personal care, it regulates pH in creams, lotions, and hair care products while contributing mild preservation activity. Industrial and laboratory applications include its use as a catalyst in organic synthesis.

It is also utilized as a desiccant in certain chemical processes. Potassium acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, and in some cases as a concentrated aqueous solution for industrial use.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. , supporting use across regulated food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. These standards ensure high purity for sensitive manufacturing.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial and catalytic uses where pharmaceutical compliance is not required. This versatility makes it a staple chemical for diverse manufacturing sectors globally.

name: Sodium acetate
description:
Sodium acetate (CAS 127-09-3 ), also designated E262i in food applications, is an inorganic acetate salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, acidulant, and preservative in both aqueous formulations and dry processing systems.

In food production, it extends shelf life in baked goods, snack seasonings, and condiments by controlling acidity and inhibiting microbial growth. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to buffer parenteral solutions, tablet coatings, and topical formulations.

Precise pH control is critical to product stability in these medical applications. In personal care, it adjusts pH in creams, lotions, and hair care products to maintain formulation integrity across various storage conditions.

Industrial applications include use as a catalyst in certain synthesis processes and as a buffering agent in textile dyeing and effluent treatment. This versatility makes it a staple chemical for diverse manufacturing sectors.

Sodium acetate is supplied in both anhydrous powder form and as the trihydrate crystalline granules. The anhydrous grade is generally preferred for applications where moisture sensitivity is a primary concern for the manufacturer.

Standard grades include FCC food-grade, USP / BP for pharmaceutical use, and technical grade for industrial applications. These certifications ensure the material meets the rigorous safety and purity requirements of each industry.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific grade and application requirements. Our logistics network ensures consistent supply and quality control for all chemical distribution needs.

name: Pyruvic acid
description:
Pyruvic acid (CAS 127-17-3 ), also known by its FEMA 2970 designation, is a short-chain alpha-keto acid used across pharmaceutical synthesis, food flavoring, and cosmetic formulation.

It functions as a reactive intermediate, acidulant, and surface-modifying agent depending on the application. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key building block for synthesizing amino acids and vitamins.

This keto-acid scaffold is essential for active pharmaceutical ingredients where metabolic relevance is required. Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring agent, contributing subtle acidic and fruity notes to products.

In cosmetics, it is applied as a chemical exfoliant in peeling formulations. Its reactivity with skin proteins enables controlled surface renewal at lower concentrations than traditional alpha-hydroxy acids.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor and reagent in specialty organic synthesis. This is particularly useful in condensation reactions targeting fine chemical intermediates for industrial use.

The material is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically at concentrations of 98% and above. This high purity is ideal for technical and synthesis-grade applications across various sectors.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet purity requirements for regulated end uses. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums suited for industrial procurement.
