name: Tetrachloroethylene
description:
Tetrachloroethylene (CAS 127-18-4 ), commonly known as perc or PCE, is a chlorinated solvent used across industrial cleaning, degreasing, and chemical processing operations.

Its high solvency power and chemical stability make it a preferred carrier and process solvent where aqueous alternatives are impractical for specific manufacturing workflows.

In textile finishing and fabric care, perc is the dominant solvent in commercial dry-cleaning operations, effectively removing oils, greases, and soils without damaging delicate fibers.

Leather processing facilities use it for degreasing hides prior to tanning, ensuring uniform dye uptake and surface quality across the entire production batch of materials.

In the plastics and polymers sector, PCE functions as a reaction medium and carrier solvent in the production of fluoropolymers, particularly as a precursor in synthesis.

Printing and packaging operations use it as a cleaning solvent for press components and as a degreasing agent for metal substrates ahead of coating or lamination processes.

Tetrachloroethylene is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk tankers, ISO containers, and drums. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial solvent applications.

Stabilized grades are available for applications requiring extended shelf life and compatibility with sensitive process equipment used in high-precision chemical manufacturing.

name: Dimethylacetamide
description:
Dimethylacetamide ( CAS 127-19-5 ), commonly known as DMAc or DMAC, is a high-boiling polar aprotic solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, fiber production, and specialty chemical processing.

Its strong solvating power makes it the preferred choice for dissolving polymers, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and resins that resist conventional solvents. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DMAc is used as a reaction solvent.

It serves as a crystallization medium for APIs, particularly in the synthesis of antibiotics and oncology compounds where solubility and process consistency are critical. Fiber and membrane producers rely on it to dissolve polyacrylonitrile.

It is also used for aramid polymers for wet-spinning processes, including the production of carbon fiber precursors and filtration membranes. It functions as a process solvent in the manufacture of polyurethane films and coatings.

This enables uniform dispersion of high-molecular-weight resins. In agrochemical and specialty chemical synthesis, DMAc supports reactions requiring a stable, high-boiling medium that remains inert under demanding conditions.

DMAc is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for industrial use.

The material is compliant with various regulatory standards and is often categorized as an ICH Q3C Class 2 solvent. Moisture content and purity levels are typically specified to meet the requirements of regulated environments.

These specifications ensure the product meets the necessary criteria for high-stakes manufacturing. Quality control measures are strictly followed to maintain the integrity of the solvent during transport and storage.

name: Lutein
description:
Lutein (CAS 127-40-2 ), also designated E161b , is a naturally derived xanthophyll carotenoid pigment extracted primarily from marigold flowers. It functions as a yellow-to-orange colorant and antioxidant across food, supplement, and cosmetic applications.

Procurement is driven by both its coloring performance and its positioning as a functional botanical ingredient. In dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, it is formulated into softgels, tablets, and functional foods targeting eye health.

This positioning remains a major commercial driver for ingredient sourcing. Food manufacturers use it as a natural colorant in beverages, dairy products, and confectionery where synthetic dye replacement is a priority.

In personal care, it is incorporated into anti-aging creams and serums where antioxidant activity supports product claims around skin protection. Feed and aquaculture producers also source it to enhance pigmentation.

This includes the pigmentation of egg yolks and farmed fish flesh. The product is supplied as a dark viscous oleoresin, free-flowing powder, or beadlet form, with beadlets preferred for dry supplement blending.

Standard grades include food-grade and USP -compliant specifications, with concentration levels typically ranging from 5% to 20% in oleoresin and powder formats. This ensures versatility across various manufacturing processes.

Crystalline lutein is available for applications requiring higher purity, and water-dispersible forms are offered for beverage and liquid formulation use. These options allow for precise control over the final product characteristics.

name: alpha-ionone
description:
Alpha-ionone (CAS 127-41-3 ), also known by its FEMA 2594 designation, is a synthetic aroma chemical prized for its violet, woody, and orris-like scent profile. It is used across fragrance and flavor manufacturing as a key building block for fine perfumery and food flavoring systems.

In fine fragrance and personal care formulations, alpha-ionone contributes a soft violet and floral character to perfumes, body lotions, and hair care products. It blends effectively with rose, iris, and musky bases to create sophisticated olfactory profiles.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a FEMA-approved flavoring agent to impart berry, raspberry, and woody nuances in confectionery, baked goods, and beverages. It is a versatile component for creating realistic fruit profiles in various applications.

In functional flavor systems, it supports the construction of complex top and heart notes where natural orris or violet extracts would be cost-prohibitive. This makes it an essential tool for flavorists seeking high-quality results at a competitive price point.

Printing and packaging applications leverage its scent stability in scented inks and encapsulated fragrance coatings for consumer packaging. This ensures a long-lasting sensory experience for the end consumer throughout the product's shelf life.

Alpha-ionone is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in flavor-grade and fragrance-grade specifications, with FEMA 2594 status confirming its suitability for food and beverage use across global markets.

Standard packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on application volume requirements. Our supply chain ensures that the product meets rigorous quality standards for consistency and purity in every batch delivered.

It is used to standardize nutrient content in capsules, tablets, and fortified staples such as flour, milk, and infant formula. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into vitamin A deficiency treatments and multivitamin preparations where precise dosing is critical.

Regulatory compliance is ensured through adherence to USP and BP standards. In personal care, it functions as an active in anti-aging creams, serums, and moisturizers targeting skin renewal and moisture retention.

Food producers also use it to restore vitamin A levels lost during processing in margarine and cooking oils. Retinyl acetate is supplied as a crystalline powder, oily liquid, or in stabilized beadlet form for dry blending applications.

Standard grades include food-grade specifications, with potency typically expressed in International Units (IU) per gram. Beadlet formulations with varying IU concentrations are commonly available to support direct compression or powder mixing.

name: Potassium hydrogen oxalate
description:
Potassium hydrogen oxalate (CAS 127-95-7 ), also known as potassium binoxalate, is an acidic potassium salt used industrially as a pH buffer, chelating agent, and metal ion sequestrant.

It is commercially available as a stable, water-soluble solid suited for controlled-acidity processing environments. In textile and leather processing, it functions as a mordant and pH-regulating agent.

During dyeing and tanning operations, it improves dye uptake consistency. The mining and metals sector uses it to selectively precipitate or complex metal ions during ore processing and surface treatment of metals.

In paper manufacturing, it supports bleaching and pulp treatment processes where controlled acidity is critical to fiber integrity. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a reagent-grade material for analytical applications.

It also serves as an intermediate in synthesis workflows requiring precise oxalate chemistry. Potassium hydrogen oxalate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with reagent and analytical grades available for laboratory and pharmaceutical procurement. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities.

name: Ethoxylated C11-alcohol
description:
Ethoxylated C11-alcohol (CAS 127036-24-2 ), also marketed under the INCI designation Undeceth-7, is a nonionic surfactant produced by ethoxylating a C11 fatty alcohol.

It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and detergent active across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations. In household and industrial cleaning products, it delivers low-foam detergency.

It is used for grease removal in hard surface cleaners, dishwashing formulations, and institutional degreasers. Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off products where controlled foam is required.

Textile processing operations use it as a scouring and wetting agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and soil removal from fabric substrates. It is essential for high-performance textile manufacturing.

In leather and paper processing, it supports emulsification of treatment agents and improves substrate wetting during manufacturing steps. This ensures consistent quality across various industrial applications.

Ethoxylated C11-alcohol is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most buyers.

Product specifications are typically defined by HLB value, ethoxylation degree, and active matter content. Drum and IBC packaging are the most common supply formats for industrial chemical procurement.

name: 4-Nonylphenol branched ethoxylated
description:
4-Nonylphenol branched ethoxylated (CAS 127087-87-0 ) is a nonionic surfactant derived from branched nonylphenol reacted with ethylene oxide. It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and wetting agent across a broad range of industrial formulations.

In industrial and institutional cleaning, it delivers effective degreasing performance in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and heavy-duty detergent concentrates. Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent.

This chemical improves fiber penetration and process efficiency during preparation and dyeing stages. Agricultural formulators incorporate it as an emulsifier in crop protection products, helping to stabilize emulsifiable concentrates and suspension concentrates.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a dispersant and emulsification aid during resin emulsification and pigment dispersion processes. It is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid, with viscosity and HLB value varying.

The properties change according to the degree of ethoxylation. Standard ethoxylate grades range from low EO (around 4–6 moles) to higher EO variants (up to 30+ moles), covering a wide HLB range for different formulation needs.

name: Ferrocenecarboxylic acid
description:
Ferrocenecarboxylic acid (CAS 1271-42-7 ), also known as ferrocenemonocarboxylic acid, is an organometallic compound combining a ferrocene core with a carboxylic acid group.

It functions as a building block and active ingredient in pharmaceutical and specialty chemical synthesis, where its redox-active iron center and carboxylic acid handle enable controlled conjugation.

In pharmaceutical development, it serves as a key intermediate for synthesizing ferrocene-conjugated drug candidates, particularly in antimicrobial and antiparasitic research programs.

The carboxylic acid group allows direct coupling to amines, peptides, and polymers, making it valuable for producing bioactive conjugates and labeled compounds in medicinal chemistry workflows.

In personal care formulations, its biocidal and preservation properties support research into metal-based antimicrobial actives as alternatives to conventional preservative systems.

It is also used in electrochemical biosensor fabrication, where its stable redox behavior enables surface functionalization of electrode materials for various diagnostic applications.

Ferrocenecarboxylic acid is supplied as an orange to orange-brown crystalline powder. It is available primarily in research and fine chemical grades for industrial synthesis applications.

Purity specifications typically range from 97% to 99%+ for synthesis. Packaging ranges from gram-scale quantities for R&D procurement to larger lots for pilot-scale synthesis programs.

name: Sucrose benzoate
description:
Sucrose benzoate (CAS 12738-64-6 ), also marketed as Uniplex 280, is a sucrose ester resin produced by esterifying sucrose with benzoic acid. It functions as a plasticizer and rheology modifier in polymer and coating systems.

This chemical improves flow, flexibility, and compatibility with a range of resin matrices. In solvent-based and water-based coatings, it improves film formation and modifies viscosity without significantly compromising hardness.

Adhesive formulators incorporate it to adjust tack, flexibility, and open time in hot-melt and pressure-sensitive systems. It is used in printing inks to control rheology and enhance resin compatibility.

This is particularly effective in nitrocellulose and acrylic ink formulations. In plastics compounding, it acts as a secondary plasticizer or processing aid where compatibility with polar polymers is required.

The product is supplied as a pale, solid resin, typically in flake or lump form. It is available in technical grade , which is the standard specification for industrial coating, adhesive, and ink applications.

Packaging commonly ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on supplier and volume requirements. This versatile resin ensures consistent performance across various industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Diethylhexyl 2,6-naphthalate
description:
Diethylhexyl 2,6-naphthalate (CAS 127474-91-3 ), also known commercially as CORAPAN TQ, is a naphthalate-based plasticizer used in polymer processing to improve flexibility and processability.

Unlike conventional phthalate plasticizers, it offers a non-phthalate alternative for applications where regulatory compliance or migration performance is a formulation priority for manufacturers.

In flexible PVC compounding, it functions as a primary plasticizer, delivering good low-temperature flexibility and reduced volatility compared to standard phthalate esters used in the industry.

Packaging films and laminates benefit from its low migration characteristics, which help maintain seal integrity and meet food-contact or sensitive-end-use requirements for various markets.

In printing and packaging substrates, it supports ink adhesion and film performance in coated or printed flexible materials. It is also evaluated in specialty polymer blends for long-term use.

This chemical is particularly useful where long-term plasticizer retention is a key formulation criterion. It ensures that the final product maintains its physical properties over an extended period.

Diethylhexyl 2,6-naphthalate is supplied as a liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial polymer and compounding applications. Bulk and drummed packaging formats are standard.

These formats are designed for industrial procurement needs, ensuring efficient handling and storage. The product meets the necessary specifications for high-performance polymer manufacturing processes.

name: Sodium Rutin Sulfate
description:
Sodium Rutin Sulfate (CAS 12768-44-4 ), also known as Disodium Rutinyl Disulfate, is a water-soluble sulfated derivative of rutin developed to overcome poor aqueous solubility. It functions as an antioxidant and bioactive ingredient in pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications where aqueous compatibility is a requirement.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into oral and topical dosage forms targeting vascular protection and capillary fragility. Improved water solubility supports consistent dosing and bioavailability in these specialized medical applications.

Nutraceutical and dietary supplement producers use it in liquid formats including drinks, ampoules, and syrups where standard rutin cannot be adequately dispersed. This allows for more versatile delivery systems in the health and wellness sector.

Functional food and beverage formulators source it as an antioxidant ingredient for products requiring a water-miscible flavonoid with label-friendly positioning. It provides a stable solution for enhancing the nutritional profile of consumer goods.

Topical cosmeceutical preparations also incorporate it for its antioxidant activity in aqueous-based serums and creams. Its ability to remain stable in water-based formulas makes it a preferred choice for high-end skincare manufacturers.

The product is supplied as a fine powder, typically in off-white to light yellow form. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and food-grade specifications to meet the sourcing requirements of various regulated global markets.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with smaller research quantities available from specialty suppliers. Quality control ensures the material meets rigorous industry benchmarks for purity and performance in final formulations.

Isocetyl palmitate (CAS 127770-27-8 ), also supplied under trade names TEGOSOFT HP and DERMOL ICP, is a synthetic ester of isocetyl alcohol and palmitic acid used primarily as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent.

It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy feel in topical formulations and functions as a lubricant and plasticizer across several industrial applications. In personal care, it is incorporated into skin creams and lotions.

Sunscreens and color cosmetics utilize this ester to improve spreadability and provide a smooth after-feel without occlusive heaviness. Lip care and makeup products benefit from its ability to disperse pigments evenly.

The ingredient contributes significant softness to the final formula while maintaining stability. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as a base fluid or co-lubricant where a biodegradable ester is preferred.

This low-viscosity fluid is ideal for applications requiring high performance and environmental compatibility. Coatings and sealant manufacturers use it as a plasticizing component to improve flexibility and substrate wetting.

name: Sodium dimethyldithiocarbamate
description:
Sodium dimethyldithiocarbamate (CAS 128-04-1 ), commonly abbreviated as SDDC, is a dithiocarbamate salt supplied primarily as an aqueous solution. Known in rubber processing circles as Sanceler S, it functions as a biocide, fungicide, and accelerator across multiple industrial sectors.

In water treatment, SDDC acts as a broad-spectrum biocide and heavy metal precipitant, controlling microbial growth in cooling towers and industrial process water. It is highly effective at immobilizing dissolved metals ahead of effluent discharge.

Rubber manufacturers use it as an ultra-fast vulcanization accelerator, particularly in latex compounding where rapid cure at low temperatures is required. This makes it a critical component for specialized manufacturing processes.

In agriculture, it serves as an active ingredient or intermediate in the production of dithiocarbamate fungicides applied to crops. These applications help protect yields from various fungal pathogens during the growing season.

Textile and leather processing operations employ it as a preservative and antifungal agent to protect goods during storage and transit. This ensures that raw materials and finished products remain free from degradation.

Sodium dimethyldithiocarbamate is most commonly supplied as a 40% aqueous solution, though concentrations may vary by supplier and application requirement. Solid forms are available but less prevalent in commercial trade.

It is typically offered at technical grade, with specifications aligned to industrial end-use rather than food or pharmaceutical standards. This ensures the product meets the rigorous demands of heavy industrial applications.

This surfactant property helps to improve the solubility and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble compounds. Cosmetic formulators incorporate UDCA into premium skincare products for its emulsifying properties.

It is particularly useful in anti-aging and skin-barrier formulations due to its surface-modifying properties. It also serves as a chiral building block in the synthesis of steroid-based pharmaceutical intermediates.

name: Butylated hydroxytoluene
description:
Butylated hydroxytoluene (CAS 128-37-0 ), commonly known as BHT or by the trade name Ionol, is a synthetic phenolic antioxidant used across food, industrial, and personal care markets to prevent oxidative degradation.

Approved as E321 in food applications and listed under FEMA 2184 for flavoring use, it protects fats, oils, polymers, and finished formulations from rancidity and deterioration during storage and processing.

In food manufacturing, BHT is incorporated into edible oils, snack foods, and packaging materials to extend shelf life by inhibiting lipid oxidation. This ensures product freshness and quality over time.

Lubricant and fuel formulators use it to stabilize mineral oils, hydraulic fluids, and transformer oils against thermal and oxidative breakdown. This is essential for maintaining performance in high-heat environments.

Rubber and plastics processors add BHT during compounding to protect polymers from degradation caused by heat and UV exposure during service life. This prevents brittleness and discoloration in industrial materials.

In personal care, it functions as a preservative antioxidant in creams, lotions, and lip products where oil-phase stability is critical. It helps maintain the integrity of complex cosmetic formulations.

BHT is supplied as a white crystalline powder or flake. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical-grade material to serve different regulatory and application requirements.

Bulk supply is available in fiber drums and multi-wall bags. Food and pharmaceutical grades require certificate of analysis documentation aligned to relevant pharmacopoeial standards for safety and compliance.

This chemical is utilized in rinse-off and leave-on formulations targeting hygiene and brightening performance. Pharmaceutical and healthcare product developers have explored it as a disinfection and preservation active.

name: Hydroxypropyl beta cyclodextrin
description:
Hydroxypropyl beta cyclodextrin ( CAS 128446-35-5 ), also known as hydroxypropyl betadex and commonly abbreviated as HPBCD, is a modified cyclic oligosaccharide used across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Its primary commercial function is encapsulating poorly soluble or unstable active ingredients within its cavity, improving their solubility, bioavailability, and shelf stability in finished formulations.

In pharmaceutical drug formulation, HPBCD enables the development of injectable, oral, and nasal delivery systems for APIs with low aqueous solubility, a critical factor when bringing poorly bioavailable compounds to market.

Cosmetic and personal care manufacturers use it to stabilize fragrance compounds, vitamins, and botanical extracts in creams, serums, and rinse-off products, extending active ingredient performance.

In food and nutraceutical applications, it encapsulates flavors, colorants, and functional ingredients to mask off-notes or protect against oxidative degradation during processing.

Biotechnology and life sciences applications include use as a cholesterol-extracting agent in cell membrane research and as a solubilizer in assay development for various laboratory protocols.

HPBCD is supplied as a white to off-white amorphous powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications including USP , Ph. Eur. , and BP , with degree of substitution typically characterized.

name: Ascorbyl glucoside
description:
Ascorbyl glucoside (CAS 129499-78-1 ), commercially known as AA-2G, is a stable, glycosylated form of vitamin C used across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food applications. Unlike free ascorbic acid, it resists oxidative degradation under normal formulation and storage conditions.

The compound releases active vitamin C enzymatically upon skin or biological contact. This stability profile makes it a preferred vitamin C source for formulators who need reliable, long-shelf-life products for various industrial uses.

In skincare formulations, it functions as a brightening and antioxidant active in serums, creams, and toners, where conventional vitamin C would degrade before reaching the consumer. It is highly valued for its performance.

name: Macadamia oil
description:
Macadamia oil (CAS 129811-19-4 ), also known as Macadamia Nut Oil, is a premium plant-derived oil cold-pressed from the nuts of Macadamia integrifolia or M. tetraphylla. It is valued across personal care and food industries for its exceptional skin absorption and oxidative stability.

In cosmetic formulations, it functions as an emollient and moisturizing agent in facial oils, hair serums, lip balms, and skin creams. Its rapid absorption profile supports lightweight, non-greasy textures in high-end skincare applications.

Food manufacturers use it as a premium culinary oil and ingredient in specialty dressings, confectionery coatings, and functional nutrition products. It provides a rich profile while maintaining high performance in various food processing environments.

In hair care, it conditions and lubricates the hair shaft, making it a preferred base or co-ingredient in leave-in treatments and professional salon products. It helps improve manageability and shine in diverse hair types.

Coatings and sealant formulators incorporate it as a bio-based plasticizing component where renewable content and film flexibility are required. This versatility makes it a valuable raw material for sustainable industrial manufacturing.

Macadamia oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Standard market grades include cosmetic/personal care grade and food-grade variants, with refined and unrefined options available to suit different formulation requirements.

Bulk supply is typically offered in drums and IBC containers to meet industrial demand. Our product ensures consistent quality and performance across all batches for your specific manufacturing and labeling needs.

name: Pecan oil
description:
Pecan oil (CAS 129893-27-2 ), cold-pressed or expeller-pressed from Carya illinoinensis nuts, is a light culinary and cosmetic carrier oil valued for its mild flavor profile and skin-compatible fatty acid composition.

It competes directly with other premium nut oils in both food manufacturing and personal care formulation channels. In food production, it functions as a finishing oil, salad dressing base, and high-end cooking oil.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it as a carrier oil in facial serums, moisturizers, and hair conditioners. Its light skin feel supports fast absorption without heavy residue in professional skincare applications.

Industrial coatings and alkyd resin manufacturers source this oil as a drying oil component. It leverages its unsaturated fatty acid content to contribute effectively to film formation in various industrial processes.

In adhesive and sealant formulations, it can serve as a bio-based plasticizing or lubricating agent. This is particularly useful where renewable-content specifications are required for sustainable manufacturing projects.

The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications. Food-grade material is typically produced to FCC or equivalent industry standards.

Cosmetic-grade supply follows ISO 16128 natural origin criteria in many global markets. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with smaller pack sizes available for specialty formulation and pilot testing.

name: Sodium 1-naphthalenesulfonate
description:
Sodium 1-naphthalenesulfonate (CAS 130-14-3 ), also known as sodium alpha-naphthalenesulfonate, is an aromatic sulfonate salt used industrially as a dispersant and wetting agent.

It improves the distribution of pigments, dyes, and solid particles across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems. In textile processing, it acts as a leveling and dispersing agent for vat and disperse dyes.

This chemical helps achieve uniform dye uptake across fabric substrates. Ink and pigment formulators incorporate it to stabilize pigment dispersions and reduce agglomeration in printing inks and coatings.

In plastics and polymer processing, it supports the dispersion of fillers and colorants during compounding. Leather and paper manufacturers use it to improve wetting of fibrous substrates.

This enables more consistent penetration of treatment chemicals throughout the manufacturing process. Sodium 1-naphthalenesulfonate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granule.

It is available in technical grade , which covers the majority of industrial dispersant and wetting applications. Purity specifications typically range from 95% to 99% for standard use.

Packaging options are suited to both bulk industrial procurement and smaller formulation quantities. This ensures flexibility for various manufacturing scales and specific logistical requirements.

name: 1,4-naphthoquinone
description:
1,4-Naphthoquinone (CAS 130-15-4 ), also known as α-naphthoquinone, is a quinone compound used industrially as a catalyst component and chemical intermediate. It functions primarily as a polymerization modifier and oxidation catalyst.

In manufacturing processes requiring precise reaction control, it serves as a vital reagent. In rubber and polymer processing, it acts as a retarder or co-agent to regulate cure rates and crosslinking behavior in vulcanization systems.

The printing and packaging industry uses it as a photosensitizer and intermediate in the production of diazo-based coatings and photopolymer plates. Textile and leather processors apply it in dye synthesis for specialty colorants.

It is also utilized as an oxidative intermediate for producing colorants with targeted fastness properties. In paper manufacturing, it functions as a catalyst precursor in pulping chemistry where controlled oxidation is required.

This chemical improves fiber processing efficiency during the pulping stage. 1,4-Naphthoquinone is supplied as a yellow crystalline powder or flake solid, making it easy to handle in various industrial environments.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+. It is available in drum and bag packaging suited to industrial-scale procurement volumes for global distribution.

name: Menadione sodium bisulfite
description:
Menadione sodium bisulfite (CAS 130-37-0 ), also known as Vitamin K3 sodium bisulfite and commonly abbreviated as MSB, is the water-soluble bisulfite addition compound of menadione used as a source of provitamin K3 activity.

Its water solubility makes it the preferred form of menadione for aqueous formulations across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and animal feed applications. In animal feed and premix manufacturing, MSB is incorporated into poultry, swine, and aquaculture feeds.

It supports blood coagulation function, where it is dosed at established inclusion rates regulated by feed authorities. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to produce injectable and oral dosage forms requiring a stable, water-dispersible vitamin K3 source.

In veterinary nutritional supplements, MSB is blended into concentrated premixes and water-soluble powder formulations for livestock administration. It also appears in aquaculture feed concentrates where fat-soluble vitamin forms are impractical to process.

Menadione sodium bisulfite is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include feed-grade material conforming to specifications set by pharmacopoeial references such as USP and BP .

It is also available as technical-grade material for industrial premix use. Bulk supply is typically available in 25 kg bags, with activity content standardized and declared on a percentage basis for quality assurance.

name: Riboflavin sodium phosphate

Riboflavin sodium phosphate (CAS 130-40-5 ), also known as FMN and approved as E106 in the EU, is the water-soluble salt form of Vitamin B2 designed for applications where standard riboflavin's limited aqueous solubility creates formulation challenges.

Its superior solubility makes it the preferred B2 source for liquid systems, injectables, and fortified beverages where dissolution uniformity is critical. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the standard choice for parenteral nutrition solutions.

It is also used in injectable vitamin preparations, where complete solubility is a regulatory and formulation requirement. Food and beverage producers use it to fortify liquid products including energy drinks, infant formula, and dairy alternatives.

This ingredient provides consistent, measurable B2 content across various applications. As E106, it also functions as a yellow colorant in food products, delivering both nutritional value and pigmentation in a single ingredient.

In cosmetic formulations, it supports antioxidant claims and provides natural yellow coloration to serums and topical nutrient products. Riboflavin sodium phosphate is supplied as an orange-yellow crystalline powder or granules.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for pharmaceutical use, and food-grade specifications compliant with FCC standards for nutrition and food applications.

name: Quinine hydrochloride
description:
Quinine hydrochloride (CAS 130-89-2 ), also known as Quinine HCl, is the salt form of quinine derived from cinchona bark alkaloids. It is used primarily in pharmaceutical manufacturing as an active ingredient and intermediate.

Its water solubility makes it the preferred form over quinine base for oral and injectable dosage development. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Quinine HCl is formulated into tablets, capsules, and injectable solutions.

These formulations target malaria treatment and fever management across various clinical settings. The food and beverage industry sources it under FEMA 2976 as a bittering agent in tonic waters and carbonated soft drinks.

Precise dosing controls the characteristic bitter taste profile required for these beverages. It also appears in topical and oral formulations developed for nocturnal leg cramp management in select regulated markets.

Compounding pharmacies use it as a starting material when preparing customized dosage forms requiring defined quinine salt concentrations. Quinine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder in anhydrous form.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , supporting procurement for regulated pharmaceutical and food applications. Bulk quantities are available for industrial buyers and R&D customers.

name: Sodium xylenesulfonate
description:
Sodium xylenesulfonate (CAS 1300-72-7 ), commercially known as SXS or Naxonate, is an anionic hydrotrope used across detergent, personal care, and industrial cleaning formulations.

It increases the solubility of other surfactants and active ingredients in aqueous systems, allowing formulators to achieve higher active concentrations without phase separation or viscosity problems.

In liquid detergent and hard-surface cleaner manufacturing, SXS is used to boost the loading of anionic and nonionic surfactants, enabling concentrated, stable products for various markets.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and body washes to improve clarity and flowability of high-surfactant blends. This ensures a consistent user experience and product quality.

Textile and leather processing operations use SXS as a coupling agent and dispersant to ensure uniform dye penetration and consistent bath stability during the manufacturing process.

In agricultural formulations, it supports the dispersion of active ingredients in liquid concentrate products, improving homogeneity and shelf stability for long-term storage and application.

Sodium xylenesulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 40% and 45% active concentrations, and as a dry powder or granule form for applications requiring low moisture content.

Standard grades include technical and industrial, with some suppliers offering specifications aligned with detergent-industry requirements. Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers is standard.

Topical and dermatological formulations in the personal care and cosmetics space also utilize this ingredient where anti-allergic skin relief claims are pursued under applicable regulatory frameworks.

name: Bentonite
description:
Bentonite (CAS 1302-78-9 ), also known commercially as Gumbrin, Otaylite, and Wilkonite, is a naturally occurring smectite clay sourced primarily from volcanic ash deposits.

In industrial applications, it functions as a rheology modifier, binder, and flocculant across a broad range of processing and formulation environments. In water treatment, it acts as a coagulant.

It is used to remove suspended solids, turbidity, and contaminants from municipal and industrial effluents. Civil engineering projects rely on it as a slurry component in foundation drilling and tunnel boring.

It is also used in landfill liner systems where low permeability is required. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it to control viscosity, prevent sagging, and improve suspension stability.

In agriculture, it serves as a binder in granular fertilizer and animal feed pellet production. This improves pellet integrity and reduces dust during the handling and distribution process.

The material is supplied as a fine powder, granules, or coarse chips depending on the target application. Sodium and calcium are the two principal commercial grades available for purchase.

Sodium bentonite is preferred where high swelling capacity is required. Grades are available to food-grade, FCC , and technical specifications to meet various industrial requirements.

Organically modified variants are also offered for specialty coatings and rheology applications. These specialized grades ensure compatibility with a wide range of solvent- and water-based systems.

name: Borax
description:
Borax (CAS 1303-96-4 ), also marketed as E285 in food contact and preservation applications, is an inorganic sodium borate salt used across industrial and consumer formulations.

It serves as a pH buffer, corrosion inhibitor, and multifunctional processing aid. Its buffering capacity and biocidal activity make it a practical choice for formulators working across cleaning and surface treatment.

In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and anti-wear additive in cutting fluids. Coatings and adhesive manufacturers incorporate it as a crosslinking agent for polyvinyl alcohol-based systems.

This directly influences gel strength and cure behavior in various industrial applications. Textile and leather processors use it as a flame retardant treatment and pH regulator during fiber preparation and tanning.

In personal care and cleaning formulations, it acts as a buffering agent and mild preservative booster. This supports product stability across a range of pH-sensitive systems and enhances overall formulation shelf life.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with size varying by requirement. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and food-grade specifications for preservation and contact uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP standards is available for healthcare and cosmetic formulation use. These high-purity options ensure compliance with strict regulatory and safety requirements.

In polymer-based systems, it provides essential internal lubrication. In metalworking and industrial lubricant blends, it acts as a boundary lubricant additive, reducing friction between metal surfaces under moderate load conditions.

name: Laurdimonium hydroxypropyl hydrolyzed wheat protein
description:
Laurdimonium hydroxypropyl hydrolyzed wheat protein (CAS 130381-06-5 ), also referred to commercially as Laurdimonium hydroxypropyl hydrolyzed wheat, is a cationic conditioning agent derived from wheat protein hydrolysate.

It is modified with a quaternary ammonium group to combine substantivity to negatively charged surfaces with moisturizing peptide functionality. This makes it a practical ingredient for hair and skin conditioning systems.

In rinse-off and leave-in hair care formulations, it deposits on damaged or chemically treated hair to improve combability and reduce static. It helps restore a smooth surface feel in shampoos and conditioners.

Protein treatment masks use it to deliver both immediate conditioning and longer-term moisture retention through the peptide fraction. In textile processing, it functions as a fiber softener and antistatic agent.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations can incorporate it where surface wetting and mild conditioning of treated substrates are required. It is often used alongside detergency in these applications.

name: Barium peroxide

Leather processors use it during preparatory stages to achieve uniform lightening of hides before dyeing or finishing. In water treatment, it acts as a biocide and oxidant to control microbial growth in industrial effluent streams.

The compound is also used as an initiator in certain pyrotechnic and specialty chemical synthesis processes. It serves as a solid, stoichiometrically defined oxygen source required for specific chemical reactions and manufacturing needs.

Satellite electronics demand dimensional stability under extreme thermal cycling, making this material essential. Nuclear applications utilize beryllia as a neutron moderator and reflector material in reactor design.

Specialty laser and optical systems also incorporate these components where thermal management directly affects output consistency. This ensures equipment longevity in demanding industrial environments.

name: Bismuth trioxide
description:
Bismuth trioxide (CAS 1304-76-3 ), commonly referenced by its formula Bi2O3, is an inorganic bismuth compound used as a functional additive and raw material across electronics manufacturing and specialty materials production.

It serves as a key oxide source where controlled melting behavior, high refractive index contribution, or dense inorganic pigmentation is required for industrial applications and chemical synthesis.

In electronics, Bi2O3 is incorporated into low-temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC), varistors, and dielectric formulations, where it lowers sintering temperatures and modifies electrical properties in finished components.

Specialty glass manufacturers use it to produce radiation-shielding glass and optical glass with elevated density and refractive characteristics, acting as a direct substitute for lead oxide in many formulations.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a yellow-to-orange inorganic pigment in ceramic inks and decorative coatings applied to glass and ceramic substrates for high-durability finishes.

It also enters flux compositions and soldering materials where a bismuth oxide source with defined purity is required. The material is supplied as a fine yellow powder in varying particle size distributions.

Standard grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with ultra-high purity grades available for electronic and optical applications requiring compliance with ACS or USP standards.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale bags to bulk quantities depending on application volume. This ensures consistent supply for both laboratory research and large-scale industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Bismuth subnitrate
description:
Bismuth subnitrate (CAS 1304-85-4 ), also sold under the designations basic bismuth nitrate and bismuth hydroxide nitrate oxide, is an inorganic bismuth salt used across pharmaceutical and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a buffering and opacifying agent, contributing to product stability and texture in finished formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into antacid and gastrointestinal preparations.

Its buffering capacity helps neutralize excess stomach acid in solid dosage forms. Topical pharmaceutical products, including dusting powders and wound dressings, use it as an astringent and protective agent on skin and mucous membranes.

In cosmetics, it serves as an opacifier and whitening pigment in face powders, foundations, and skin-care creams where a matte or brightening finish is required for the final consumer product.

Industrial ceramic and glass applications also source this chemical as a precursor for bismuth oxide production. The material is supplied as a white, heavy powder in both pharmaceutical and technical grades.

Ph. Eur. and BP grades are the most commercially relevant, meeting purity specifications required for medicinal product manufacturing. These standards ensure the highest level of safety and efficacy.

Technical-grade material is available for non-pharmaceutical industrial uses where pharmacopoeial compliance is not required. This allows for cost-effective sourcing in large-scale manufacturing and glass production.

name: Zinc ricinoleate
description:
Zinc ricinoleate (CAS 13040-19-2 ), also known as zinc diricinoleate, is the zinc salt of ricinoleic acid derived from castor oil. It functions as a molecular odor absorber, trapping and neutralizing malodorous compounds rather than masking them with fragrance.

This mechanism makes it a sought-after active ingredient wherever durable, non-perfumed odor control is required. In personal care, it is the primary active in deodorant sticks, roll-ons, and sprays formulated as fragrance-free or clean products.

The compound binds odor molecules directly on the skin for effective results. Textile and leather processors apply it in finishing treatments to impart lasting odor control to sportswear, footwear linings, and technical fabrics.

In coatings and sealants, it functions as a surface modifier and dispersing agent, improving pigment wetting and stabilizing formulations. Adhesive and elastomer manufacturers also use it as a processing aid to influence surface tack.

The material is highly valued for its compatibility with fatty acid-based systems. Zinc ricinoleate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as a waxy solid, depending on the specific grade and processing requirements.

Standard commercial grades are available for cosmetic and industrial applications. Cosmetic-grade material typically meets purity requirements aligned with REACH and ISO 16128 natural origin criteria for global compliance.

Bulk supply is common in 25 kg bags or fiber drums to suit large-scale manufacturing. This versatile chemical remains a staple for formulators seeking natural, high-performance solutions for odor neutralization and surface modification.

name: 1,6-Hexanediol diacrylate
description:
1,6-Hexanediol diacrylate (CAS 13048-33-4 ), commonly known by its abbreviation HDDA, is a bifunctional acrylate monomer used as a reactive diluent and crosslinker in UV- and radiation-curable systems.

It reduces viscosity in formulations while contributing to network formation during cure, giving formulators control over both processability and final film properties in various industrial applications.

In UV-curable coatings and inks, HDDA lowers formulation viscosity without adding non-reactive solvent, supporting high-speed printing and packaging line requirements for modern manufacturing processes.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to tune crosslink density, balancing flexibility and cohesive strength in pressure-sensitive and structural formulations across the chemical sector.

Radiation-curable flooring, wood, and industrial coatings rely on HDDA to achieve hard, scratch-resistant surfaces with fast cure response, ensuring high durability and efficient production cycles.

In polymer synthesis, it functions as a crosslinking agent for hydrogels and specialty polymer networks where controlled mesh structure is required for specific technical performance standards.

HDDA is supplied as a low-viscosity liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport, maintaining product stability for long-term use.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly at 90% minimum. Bulk, drum, and IBC packaging are the typical supply formats for buyers.

name: Calcium hydroxide
description:
Calcium hydroxide ( CAS 1305-62-0 ), commercially known as slaked lime or hydrated lime, is a strong inorganic base used across food processing, water treatment, construction, and agriculture.

As E526 , it functions primarily as a pH regulator, firming agent, and alkali source in both industrial and food-grade applications. In food processing, it is used to nixtamalize corn for tortilla production.

It is also utilized to firm fruit and vegetable textures in pickling and canning. Water treatment plants rely on it to adjust pH, precipitate heavy metals, and soften hard water through controlled coagulation and flocculation.

In construction, it is a core component of mortars, plasters, and soil stabilization projects where controlled alkalinity improves structural binding. Pulp and paper producers use it in causticizing processes.

This process helps to regenerate sodium hydroxide from green liquor, making it integral to the kraft pulping cycle. The material is supplied as a dry white powder, with bulk availability in bags and super sacks.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E526-compliant), USP , and technical or industrial grade. Purity levels and particle size distributions vary significantly depending on the specific grade required.

Food and pharmaceutical grades are held to tighter specifications than construction or agricultural material. This ensures compliance with global safety and quality standards for sensitive manufacturing applications.

name: Calcium oxide
description:
Calcium oxide (CAS 1305-78-8 ), commonly known as quicklime and approved as food additive E529 , is a high-reactivity alkaline material produced by calcining limestone at high temperatures.

It functions as a pH regulator, desiccant, and reactive base across a broad range of industrial processes. In water and wastewater treatment, it is used to raise pH and precipitate heavy metals.

Steel and non-ferrous metal producers rely on it as a flux to remove impurities during smelting and refining operations. Pulp and paper mills use it in the kraft recovery cycle to regenerate sodium hydroxide.

This makes it integral to chemical recovery loops. In construction, it is the primary input for producing hydrated lime used in mortars, soil stabilization, and asphalt modification for infrastructure.

The material is supplied as lumps, granules, or fine powder depending on downstream processing requirements. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-calcium grades defined by CaO content.

Purity typically ranges from 90% to over 98% depending on the source. Food-grade material conforming to regulatory specifications is available for applications requiring strict compliance.

name: Calcium peroxide
description:
Calcium peroxide (CAS 1305-79-9 ), also known commercially as Calper or calcium dioxide, is a solid oxidizing agent that releases oxygen slowly in the presence of moisture.

This controlled oxygen release makes it functional across food processing, soil remediation, and industrial treatment applications. In food production, it conditions dough by strengthening gluten networks.

This process improves the machinability and volume of baked goods. Soil and groundwater remediation projects use it as an in-situ oxygen source to stimulate aerobic biodegradation of organic contaminants.

In water treatment, it acts as a biocide and oxidant to control microbial growth and reduce biological oxygen demand in effluent streams. Textile and paper processors apply it as a bleaching agent.

This allows for whitening fibers and pulp without the process complexity of chlorine-based systems. Calcium peroxide is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granule for various uses.

The active oxygen content typically ranges from 60% to 75% depending on grade. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification for dough conditioning applications.

Technical grades serve agricultural, remediation, and industrial end uses where food compliance is not required. This versatile chemical provides reliable performance across multiple sectors.

name: Hydroxylapatite
description:
Hydroxylapatite (CAS 1306-06-5 ), also known as calcium hydroxyapatite and abbreviated as HAP, is the principal mineral constituent of bone and dental enamel. It serves as the reference material for hard tissue repair and regeneration.

Its structural compatibility with natural bone drives demand across orthopedic, dental, and biomedical manufacturing sectors. In orthopedic and spinal implant manufacturing, HAP is applied as a coating on metal prostheses.

This application promotes osseointegration and long-term implant stability. Dental product formulators incorporate it into toothpastes and remineralization treatments as a functional alternative to fluoride, targeting enamel repair.

Pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers use HAP as a chromatography medium for protein and antibody purification. Its selective binding to biomolecules supports complex downstream bioprocessing workflows in modern laboratories.

In bone graft substitutes and scaffold fabrication, HAP serves as a primary structural component. It is used alone or combined with polymers to support cell attachment and tissue ingrowth during the healing process.

Hydroxylapatite is supplied as a fine white powder in varying particle size distributions. It is also available in porous granule and block forms for specialized surgical applications and medical device manufacturing.

Established grades include pharmaceutical-grade, USP -compliant, and chromatography-grade specifications. Synthetic and sintered variants are available to meet specific density and porosity requirements for industrial use.

name: Cadmium oxide
description:
Cadmium oxide (CAS 1306-19-0 ), also known as cadmium monoxide, is an inorganic compound used primarily as a precursor and catalyst in industrial chemical synthesis and electrochemical processes.

It serves as a source material for producing other cadmium compounds and functional coatings where controlled electrical or catalytic properties are required for specific manufacturing applications.

In electronics manufacturing, it is used to produce electroplating baths and conductive thin-film coatings applied to contacts and semiconductors. The compound acts as a catalyst precursor in select organic synthesis processes.

This includes the production of certain polymers and specialty chemicals. In the plastics and polymers sector, it has been used as a stabilizer component and pigment precursor for high-temperature processing.

Pulp and paper operations have historically employed cadmium compounds in specific process chemistry, though regulatory pressure has significantly narrowed this use in recent years across the global market.

The material is supplied as a brown-to-black powder in technical and high-purity grades. Purity levels typically range from 99% to 99.999% (5N), with higher-purity material directed toward electronics.

Packaging is available in small laboratory quantities through to bulk industrial quantities. All shipments are subject to applicable hazardous materials handling requirements and safety protocols.

Cadmium sulfide (CAS 1306-23-6 ), commercially recognized as Cadmium Yellow and historically marketed as Capsebon, is an inorganic pigment delivering intense yellow-to-orange hues. It offers exceptional heat and chemical stability for demanding industrial uses.

This material is used across high-performance coloring applications where organic pigments cannot withstand harsh processing conditions. In plastics and polymer compounding, it provides stable coloration in engineering resins processed at elevated temperatures.

Most organic colorants degrade under these conditions, making this inorganic compound essential for high-heat manufacturing. Coatings formulators specify it for industrial and protective finishes requiring long-term color retention.

The pigment maintains its integrity under intense UV exposure and harsh chemical environments. In the electronics sector, it functions as a photoconductive material in photoresistors and thin-film semiconductor layers.

Printing inks for specialty packaging have historically used it where opacity and color fastness are required. It is particularly effective under demanding print conditions that would compromise the quality of lesser pigments.

The product is supplied as a fine powder in pigment-grade and technical-grade forms. Pigment grades are characterized by particle size distribution and tinting strength to meet specific industrial colorant standards.

It absorbs ultraviolet radiation, offering an inorganic alternative to organic UV filters. Printing and packaging manufacturers use it as a polishing compound for optical glass and precision-coated surfaces.

This improves surface finish on print rollers and optical components. As a pigment additive, it contributes to color stability and surface uniformity in specialty coatings and ink systems.

Its biocidal and antimicrobial properties are also being leveraged in functional packaging materials. These materials are designed to extend shelf life or inhibit surface microbial growth.

name: Polyamino polyether methylene phosphonate
description:
Polyamino polyether methylene phosphonate (CAS 130668-24-5 ), commercially known as PAPEMP or Kemguard 8010, is a high-performance phosphonate chelating agent engineered for demanding water treatment and industrial process environments.

It combines sequestration and corrosion inhibition functions within a single molecule, making it effective at low dosage levels across a broad pH and temperature range. In industrial water treatment, it controls scale deposition.

This chemical prevents calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and barium sulfate in cooling water systems, boilers, and reverse osmosis membranes. Its threshold inhibition and crystal modification properties allow effective scale control.

It performs even under high hardness and high-temperature conditions where conventional phosphonates underperform. In textile processing, it sequesters heavy metal ions that would otherwise interfere with dyeing uniformity and fabric quality.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it as a chelant to prevent redeposition of hardness minerals. It also serves to stabilize active ingredients in alkaline detergent systems during the cleaning process.

Polyamino polyether methylene phosphonate is supplied as an aqueous liquid solution, typically at active concentrations around 20–30%. It is available in technical grade suitable for industrial water treatment.

This compound produces stable blue tones that withstand firing temperatures where organic pigments fail. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a drier catalyst and pigment component in industrial paints.

It is particularly useful where long-term color stability under heat or UV exposure is required. The textile and leather industries use cobalt oxide as a mordant-adjacent agent to improve dye fixation.

This application ensures surface uniformity on treated substrates. In specialty adhesives and sealants, it contributes to oxidative curing acceleration, shortening set times in oil-based formulations.

name: Dichromium trioxide
description:
Dichromium trioxide (CAS 1308-38-9 ) is a high-performance inorganic pigment valued for its exceptional heat stability and chemical resistance across demanding industrial applications. It delivers a durable, opaque green coloration that retains integrity under conditions where organic pigments would degrade.

In coatings and industrial paints, it provides permanent green pigmentation for high-temperature finishes, military coatings, and camouflage applications. This material ensures color consistency under thermal stress, which is critical for specialized surface treatments.

Rubber and tire manufacturers incorporate it to achieve stable green coloration in technical rubber compounds without compromising vulcanization chemistry. This ensures the final product maintains its physical properties while achieving the desired aesthetic.

Plastics processors use it to pigment engineering polymers that undergo high-temperature extrusion or molding. In these environments, organic alternatives would typically discolor or break down, making this inorganic pigment the preferred choice.

Printing inks for packaging and decorative laminates also rely on it for lightfast, chemically resistant green shades. Its stability ensures that printed materials remain vibrant even when exposed to harsh environmental factors or chemicals.

Dichromium trioxide is supplied as a fine, dry powder in technical and pigment grades. Standard specifications include varying particle size distributions and tinting strength classifications to match specific coating, rubber, or plastics processing requirements.

Bulk supply is available in bags and bulk containers, with pigment-grade material typically meeting established industry purity benchmarks. This ensures consistent performance across large-scale manufacturing and industrial chemical applications.

name: Pentaerythrityl distearate
description:
Pentaerythrityl distearate (CAS 13081-97-5 ), also known as Pentaerythritol Distearate, is a partial ester of pentaerythritol and stearic acid used across lubricant, polymer, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions as a plasticizer, emulsifier, and internal lubricant, helping processors and formulators improve flow, texture, and surface finish in finished products during the manufacturing process.

In plastics processing, it acts as an internal lubricant and mold release agent, reducing friction between polymer chains during extrusion and injection molding of PVC and similar resins.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into lipsticks, creams, and emollient-rich skin preparations to improve spreadability and emulsion stability in various cosmetic and topical applications.

Metalworking lubricant producers use it as a base component or additive in formulations requiring thermal stability and film-forming performance on metal surfaces for industrial use.

It also functions as a plasticizer in specialty coatings and wax blends where controlled softening and compatibility with fatty acid systems are required for high-performance results.

Pentaerythrityl distearate is typically supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid in flake or pastille form. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades for diverse industrial needs.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements for personal care applications. Standard packaging includes bags and fiber drums, with bulk supply available depending on the supplier.

name: Perlite
description:
Perlite (CAS 130885-09-5 ), also supplied under the trade designation EUROPERL-50, is a volcanic aluminosilicate mineral processed by high-temperature expansion to produce a lightweight, porous material.

Expanded perlite is a commercially established form used across construction, agriculture, and industrial sectors as a functional filler and flow modifier for various manufacturing processes.

In construction, expanded perlite is incorporated into lightweight plasters, insulation boards, and ceiling tiles to reduce density while maintaining structural integrity during application.

Horticultural and agricultural formulators blend it into growing media and soil conditioners to improve aeration and drainage in both commercial and consumer products for better plant growth.

Industrial cleaning and home care manufacturers use perlite as a mild abrasive and bulking agent in scouring powders and surface cleaning formulations to enhance mechanical cleaning action.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a low-density filler that modifies rheology and reduces resin consumption in finished parts, offering significant cost and weight savings.

Perlite is available in expanded form as a dry, free-flowing granular or fine powder material in a range of particle size grades suited to different industrial processing requirements.

Standard supply grades include filter-aid, horticultural, and industrial technical grades. Food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications are available for applications requiring regulatory compliance.

name: Iron oxide red
description:
Iron oxide red (CAS 1309-37-1 ), also sold as C.I. Pigment Red 101, red oxide, and approved as food colorant E172(ii) , is a synthetic or naturally derived inorganic pigment. It is used to impart color and corrosion resistance across a broad range of industrial and consumer applications.

Its high UV stability and opacity make it a preferred colorant where long-term color retention under outdoor exposure is a commercial requirement. In architectural and industrial coatings, red iron oxide provides both color and a passive barrier against substrate corrosion.

This pigment reduces coating system failures in marine and infrastructure environments. Concrete, paving blocks, and fiber cement products use it as a mass-toning pigment to achieve consistent, fade-resistant earth tones at scale.

Automotive OEM and refinish primers rely on its corrosion-inhibiting properties as a functional component, not just a colorant. Printing inks and packaging coatings for construction materials also incorporate it where heat-stable, non-bleeding color is required.

Iron oxide red is supplied as a dry powder in both synthetic and natural grades, with synthetic grades offering tighter particle size distribution and higher tinting strength. Standard grades include technical, construction-grade, and cosmetic/food-grade material.

Synthetic grades are also available to meet ASTM D3722 and ISO 11553 standards relevant to pigment performance benchmarking. These materials ensure high quality and consistency for demanding industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Magnesium hydroxide
description:
Magnesium hydroxide (CAS 1309-42-8 ), also recognized in food and feed applications as E528 , is an inorganic base and flame retardant used across industrial, food, and environmental sectors.

Milk of magnesia is the widely recognized pharmaceutical and consumer form, while magnesium hydrate is a term commonly encountered in water treatment and industrial procurement.

Its primary commercial roles are pH regulation, halogen-free flame retardancy, and acid neutralization. In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a smoke suppressant.

This is particularly useful in wire and cable jacketing, where regulatory pressure favors non-halogenated systems. Water treatment plants use it to neutralize acidic wastewater.

It helps stabilize pH without the overdose risk associated with stronger alkalis. In food manufacturing, it acts as an acidity regulator and firming agent in processed products.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as an active antacid ingredient and excipient in solid dosage forms. It is supplied as a dry white powder, aqueous slurry, or granules.

Standard grades include USP , FCC , Ph. Eur. , and technical grade, with flame retardant grades specified by particle size distribution and surface treatment.

Slurry concentrations for water treatment are typically supplied at around 55–63% solids. These specifications ensure compatibility across diverse polymer and chemical systems.

name: Magnesium oxide
description:
Magnesium oxide (CAS 1309-48-4 ), also known as magnesia or E530 , is a high-temperature inorganic compound sourced from the calcination of magnesite or seawater-derived magnesium hydroxide.

It functions as a pH regulator, refractory material, and nutrient source across a broad range of industrial and food-grade applications. In steelmaking and cement production, dead-burned magnesia grades line furnaces.

These grades are essential for kilns where extreme heat resistance is required. Agricultural feed producers incorporate it as a magnesium supplement to prevent grass tetany in livestock and improve animal health.

Food manufacturers use E530-grade material as an anti-caking agent and acidity regulator in processed products. Water treatment operations dose it to neutralize acidic effluents and stabilize pH levels.

This compound offers stabilization without the sharp reactivity of lime. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulators rely on USP and BP grades as an antacid active and mild abrasive in oral care products.

Magnesium oxide is supplied as a white powder in light-burned, hard-burned, and dead-burned forms. Each is calcined at different temperatures to deliver distinct reactivity and surface area profiles.

These profiles are suited to specific end uses across various sectors. Standard commercial grades include food-grade, Ph.Eur. , and technical or refractory grades for heavy industrial manufacturing.

Bulk bags, drums, and loose bulk supply are standard packaging formats across global markets. This ensures reliable logistics for large-scale chemical distribution and specialized manufacturing needs.

name: Antimony trioxide
description:
Antimony trioxide (CAS 1309-64-4 ), also known as Flowers of Antimony, is a flame retardant synergist used across plastics, textiles, and industrial materials. It does not act as a standalone flame retardant.

Instead, it amplifies the performance of halogenated flame retardant systems, allowing formulators to achieve target fire ratings at lower total additive loadings. In plastics and polymers, it is compounded with brominated or chlorinated flame retardants.

This process helps materials meet UL 94 and other flammability standards in wire insulation, connectors, and housings. Textile and fabric coatings for automotive interiors, upholstery, and protective workwear rely on it to pass certifications.

In construction materials, it is incorporated into PVC profiles, roofing membranes, and wall panels where building codes mandate flame resistance. Electronics manufacturers use it in printed circuit board laminates and encapsulant compounds.

These applications help to control flame spread in high-density assemblies. Antimony trioxide is supplied as a fine white powder in standard and high-purity grades for various industrial needs.

Technical and flame retardant grades are the most common commercial forms, with particle size specifications varying by application. Finer grades are preferred for film and fiber applications.

Bulk bags and small-pack options are standard across the supply chain. This ensures that manufacturers can source the material in the quantities required for their specific production processes.

name: Dimethyl phthalate
description:
Dimethyl phthalate (CAS 131-11-3 ), commonly sourced as DMP, is a phthalate ester plasticizer and solvent used across polymer processing, personal care manufacturing, and specialty coatings.

It functions primarily as a plasticizer for cellulose-based resins and as a carrier solvent in formulations requiring controlled evaporation and compatibility with polar substrates.

In plastics processing, DMP is used to plasticize cellulose acetate and cellulose acetate butyrate, improving flexibility in film, sheet, and molded components for industrial use.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as a solvent and fixative in nail lacquers and hair sprays, where it supports film formation and fragrance retention during application.

In printing inks and coatings, DMP acts as a solvent carrier that aids pigment dispersion and resin dissolution across nitrocellulose-based systems for high-quality finishes.

It also functions as a UV stabilizer in certain polymer formulations, helping to extend the service life of finished plastic articles exposed to light in outdoor environments.

Dimethyl phthalate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 99% or above.

Bulk tanker supply is available from major producers for high-volume industrial buyers. Our logistics network ensures timely delivery of chemical raw materials to your manufacturing facility.

name: Diallyl phthalate
description:
Diallyl phthalate (CAS 131-17-9 ), also known as DAP or by the trade names Dapon R and Dapon 35, is a reactive monomer and plasticizer used primarily in thermoset polymer systems.

It functions as a crosslinking agent and reactive diluent, enabling controlled cure profiles in molding compounds and prepregs. In plastics and composites manufacturing, DAP is used to produce stable compounds.

These thermoset molding compounds are ideal for electrical connectors, circuit boards, and aerospace components where heat and chemical resistance are critical. It improves surface hardness and reduces shrinkage.

As a crosslinker in unsaturated polyester and alkyd resin formulations, it enhances performance. In printing and packaging, DAP-based resins are used in UV-curable coatings and inks for fast cure response.

These resins provide excellent adhesion to substrates. Personal care formulators have incorporated it into nail coating systems where durable, high-gloss film formation is the target performance outcome.

Diallyl phthalate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Both monomer-grade and prepolymer grades are commercially available for various industrial applications.

Dapon-designated prepolymers are a recognized standard in the thermoset compounding market. Technical grade is the predominant specification for most industrial manufacturing requirements.

Buyers should confirm purity and residual monomer content when sourcing prepolymer forms. This ensures the material meets the specific needs of the intended chemical processing or resin formulation.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it is incorporated into PVC formulations to improve flexibility in films, sheets, and molded components for various manufacturing sectors.

Rubber and tire manufacturers use it as a processing aid and softener to improve compound workability and reduce mixing viscosity during the intensive production stages.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it acts as a plasticizing additive that helps maintain film integrity and adhesion under significant mechanical stress and pressure.

Automotive interior components, including seals and gaskets, may incorporate this chemical to achieve the required flexibility and durability specifications for long-term use.

name: n-acetylneuraminic acid

N-Acetylneuraminic acid (CAS 131-48-6 ), commercially recognized under the abbreviations NeuAc, Neu5Ac, and NANA, is the predominant sialic acid found in mammalian biology. It is a critical building block in glycan chemistry.

It is used as an analytical reference for sialylation studies, glycoprotein characterization, and enzyme assay development. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into premium skincare products for its moisture-retention properties.

It plays a vital role in supporting skin barrier function at the cellular level. In food and nutrition, it is used as a bioactive ingredient in infant formula and functional food products targeting cognitive and immune health.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a precursor in the enzymatic or chemical synthesis of sialylated oligosaccharides and therapeutic glycoconjugates. This versatile compound is essential for modern research.

N-Acetylneuraminic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research-grade and high-purity pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or above.

In coatings and industrial paints, BP-6 is incorporated to prevent yellowing and gloss loss on exterior surfaces exposed to sunlight. Plastic and polymer manufacturers use it to extend the service life of films and molded parts.

This chemical is essential for packaging materials where UV stability is a key performance requirement. In printing inks, it helps preserve color integrity and prevents substrate degradation under intense UV exposure.

Personal care formulators have evaluated BP-6 for use in sunscreen and photoprotective products. It provides broad UV absorption across both UVA and UVB ranges, ensuring comprehensive protection for sensitive formulations.

Benzophenone-6 is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in technical grade for industrial coating, polymer, and ink applications, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher.

name: Benzophenone-2
description:
Benzophenone-2 (CAS 131-55-5 ), commonly abbreviated as BP-2, is a hydroxybenzophenone-class UV absorber used to protect materials from ultraviolet-induced degradation. It functions by absorbing UV radiation across a broad spectrum.

This chemical prevents photodegradation in both finished products and their substrates. In coatings and industrial polymers, it is incorporated to extend the service life of films, lacquers, and plastic substrates exposed to outdoor weathering.

Printing inks and packaging laminates use it to prevent UV-triggered color fading and resin breakdown over shelf life. In adhesives, sealants, and elastomers, it contributes to cross-linking stability under light exposure.

This stability helps in maintaining bond integrity in demanding environments. Personal care formulators have historically used it as a sunscreen active and UV filter in topical products, though regulatory status varies by market.

Buyers should verify current compliance requirements before use. The product is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial uses.

Purity specifications are typically at 98% or above for the standard grade. Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care applications where documentation requirements are more stringent for manufacturers.
