name: 2,4-dihydroxybenzophenone
description:
2,4-Dihydroxybenzophenone (CAS 131-56-6 ), also known commercially as Uvinul 400 and abbreviated as DHBP, is a UV absorber used to protect polymers, coatings, and personal care formulations from photodegradation.

It functions by absorbing UV radiation in the 280–340 nm range, preventing premature breakdown of the host material. In coatings and industrial paints, DHBP is incorporated to extend the service life of exterior finishes.

By blocking UV-induced yellowing and chalking, it maintains the integrity of the surface. Plastics manufacturers add it to polyolefins, PVC, and engineering resins where long-term outdoor durability is a requirement.

In printing inks and packaging films, it stabilizes colorants and substrates against UV fading during storage and end use. This ensures that the visual quality of the packaging remains consistent over time.

Personal care formulators use DHBP as a UV filter in sunscreens and hair care products. It also functions as a photoinitiator and cross-linking agent in UV-curable adhesive and sealant systems.

2,4-Dihydroxybenzophenone is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white crystalline powder. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial forms, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher.

Cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant regulatory specifications is available for personal care applications. This high-purity material ensures safety and efficacy when used in consumer-facing formulations.

name: Oxybenzone
description:
Oxybenzone (CAS 131-57-7 ), also supplied under the trade name Uvinul M40 and listed in cosmetic formulations as Benzophenone-3, is a UV-absorbing compound that protects materials from photodegradation.

In sunscreen and personal care formulations, Benzophenone-3 is an established active UV filter used in lotions, creams, and lip products to meet regulatory UV protection standards for consumer safety.

Coatings and varnish manufacturers incorporate it to prevent yellowing and surface degradation in architectural and industrial finishes exposed to harsh outdoor conditions and direct sunlight.

Polymer processors add oxybenzone to plastics and elastomers during compounding to extend service life in UV-exposed end products such as films, profiles, and various molded components.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to maintain bond integrity and appearance in products subject to prolonged sunlight exposure. This ensures the long-term durability of the chemical bond.

Oxybenzone is commercially available as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is supplied in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the distinct purity and documentation requirements.

Standard packaging includes fiber drums and multi-layer bags, with bulk quantities available for industrial procurement. We ensure all batches meet rigorous quality control and safety benchmarks.

name: Inosinic acid
description:
Inosinic acid (CAS 131-99-7 ), commercially traded as inosine monophosphate (IMP) and approved as E630 , is a nucleotide used primarily as a flavor enhancer in food manufacturing.

It amplifies savory, umami taste at low use levels, typically in combination with other nucleotides or glutamates. In processed food production, IMP is combined with monosodium glutamate or disodium guanylate.

This boosts umami intensity in soups, seasonings, snack coatings, and instant noodles. The synergistic effect allows lower total additive loading for manufacturers seeking cost-effective flavor profiles.

Meat processors and bouillon manufacturers use it to reinforce broth-like depth in powdered stocks, sauces, and ready meals. In biotechnology, it serves as a biochemical reference material and substrate.

It is utilized in nucleotide metabolism research and pharmaceutical formulators source it as a precursor or active component in nucleotide-based preparations targeting metabolic support.

Inosinic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder, most commonly in the disodium salt form for food applications. Food-grade material is available meeting E630 specifications.

Technical and reagent grades are offered for industrial and research procurement. Bulk quantities are standard for food ingredient buyers, with smaller pack sizes available for laboratory use.

name: Goethite
description:
Goethite (CAS 1310-14-1 ), the naturally occurring iron oxyhydroxide mineral alpha-FeOOH, is a primary source material for iron-based pigments and a key reference compound in metallurgical and mineralogical analysis.

Its stable yellow-brown coloration and iron content make it commercially relevant across pigment production and mineral processing sectors. In pigment manufacturing, goethite serves as the base material for synthetic yellow iron oxide pigments.

These pigments are used in paints, coatings, concrete colorants, and construction materials. Cement and concrete producers use iron oxide derived from goethite to achieve consistent, lightfast coloration in architectural and infrastructure applications.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, goethite precipitation is a controlled process step for removing iron from leach solutions during zinc, copper, and nickel refining. This ensures high purity in the final metal extraction process.

Research and quality laboratories also use reference-grade goethite as a calibration standard for XRD analysis and iron speciation studies. It is essential for accurate mineralogical characterization in industrial labs.

Goethite is available as a fine powder in both natural mineral and synthetically produced forms. Synthetic grades offer tighter particle size distribution and higher purity, suited to pigment and analytical applications.

Supply specifications vary by iron content and particle morphology, with technical and reference-grade material available depending on end-use requirements. This versatility supports a wide range of industrial chemical processes.

name: Potassium hydroxide
description:
Potassium hydroxide (CAS 1310-58-3 ), also known as potash lye and sold under the designation E525 in food applications, is a strong inorganic alkali used across industrial, agricultural, and food-grade processes.

KOH functions primarily as a pH regulator, saponification agent, and chemical intermediate in manufacturing chains where sodium-based alternatives are unsuitable for the specific chemical reaction required.

In soap and detergent manufacturing, KOH is the preferred alkali for producing soft and liquid soaps, where its potassium salt chemistry delivers the required texture and solubility profile for high-end products.

Food processors use it as an approved acidity regulator in cocoa treatment, noodle production, and certain confectionery applications. Fertilizer producers rely on KOH as a potassium source in liquid nutrient formulations.

In pulp and paper, it supports fiber processing and bleaching operations, while water treatment facilities use it to correct pH and prevent pipe corrosion in distribution systems to ensure safety and longevity.

Potassium hydroxide is supplied as white flakes, pellets, or as a 45–50% aqueous solution. Standard grades include technical, food-grade ( FCC ), and pharmaceutical grades such as USP , BP , and Ph. Eur.

These grades cover the full range of industrial and regulated applications. Bulk quantities are available in drums, IBCs, and tanker deliveries depending on the physical form and volume requirements selected.

name: Lithium hydroxide
description:
Lithium hydroxide (CAS 1310-65-2 ), also known as lithium hydrate, is a strong inorganic base supplied in both anhydrous and monohydrate forms. It is used across battery manufacturing, lubricant production, and chemical synthesis as an alkalizing agent and catalyst precursor.

Demand has grown sharply with the expansion of lithium-ion battery supply chains, where it serves as a direct cathode precursor material. In electric vehicle and energy storage battery production, it is the preferred feedstock for manufacturing high-nickel NMC and NCA cathode active materials.

Lubricant manufacturers use it to saponify fatty acids, producing lithium-based greases valued for high-temperature and multi-purpose performance. In pharmaceuticals and specialty chemicals, it functions as a pH regulator and base catalyst in synthesis processes requiring precise alkalinity control.

Paper and textile processors apply it for mercerization and fiber treatment, where controlled alkaline conditions affect surface structure and dye uptake. Lithium hydroxide is available as a white powder or granules in both anhydrous and monohydrate forms.

Battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate is the dominant commercial specification, with purity typically at 56.5% LiOH minimum. It features low impurity thresholds for metals such as sodium, calcium, and sulfate to ensure high performance in electrochemical applications.

Technical and reagent grades are also available for industrial and laboratory procurement. These grades meet various industrial requirements and are often tested against rigorous quality standards such as ACS or USP depending on the specific application needs.

Lithium hydroxide monohydrate (CAS 1310-66-3 ) is a high-purity inorganic base used across battery manufacturing, industrial chemistry, and specialty lubrication. Its controlled alkalinity and reactivity profile make it a preferred source of lithium.

In processes where anhydrous forms would introduce handling or reactivity complications, this monohydrate form is preferred. In lithium-ion battery production, it serves as a precursor for cathode active materials.

name: Sodium hydroxide
description:
Sodium hydroxide (CAS 1310-73-2 ), also sold as caustic soda or lye, is a strong inorganic base used across industrial and food-grade processing to control pH and neutralize acids. As E524 , it is approved for direct food contact applications.

Demand for this versatile chemical spans water treatment, pulp and paper, textiles, and chemical manufacturing. In pulp and paper production, it breaks down lignin during the kraft process, enabling cellulose separation at scale.

Water treatment plants use it to raise pH, precipitate heavy metals, and condition water for safe distribution. Food processors apply it for curing olives, pretzel glazing, and pH adjustment in cocoa processing.

In textile and leather operations, it drives mercerization of cotton and assists in dehairing hides. These processes improve fiber uptake and surface finish, ensuring high-quality results in industrial manufacturing environments.

Sodium hydroxide is supplied as white flakes, micropearls, and solid pellets, as well as aqueous solution. The most common liquid format is the 50% concentration, which is widely used for bulk industrial applications.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical ( USP / BP / Ph. Eur. ), and technical grade for industrial use. These certifications ensure the material meets the rigorous safety requirements of each specific industry.

Membrane cell grades with low chloride content are available for applications requiring high purity. This ensures that sensitive chemical reactions and high-end manufacturing processes maintain consistent quality and performance.

name: Ammonium molybdate
description:
Ammonium molybdate (CAS 13106-76-8 ), also known as diammonium molybdate, is an inorganic molybdenum salt used across agriculture, water treatment, and industrial chemistry as a source of soluble molybdenum.

It functions primarily as a micronutrient supplier, corrosion inhibitor, and analytical reagent in commercial formulations and industrial processes. In agriculture, it is incorporated into liquid fertilizers and foliar sprays.

This product corrects molybdenum deficiency in crops, particularly for legumes and brassicas where nitrogen fixation depends on adequate molybdenum availability. Water treatment operations use it as a corrosion inhibitor.

In cooling water systems, it forms a protective film on metal surfaces to reduce pipe degradation. In analytical and laboratory chemistry, it serves as the active reagent in phosphate and silicate detection methods.

This makes it a procurement target for reagent-grade supply chains. Pharmaceutical and industrial formulators also source it as a precursor for molybdenum-based catalysts used in hydroprocessing and chemical synthesis.

Ammonium molybdate is available as a crystalline powder or granules, with purity levels ranging from technical grade to reagent grade. Established specifications include ACS reagent grade for laboratory applications.

Technical grade is also available for industrial and agricultural use. Bulk supply is standard for fertilizer and industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for analytical and pharmaceutical procurement.

name: Potassium silicate
description:
Potassium silicate (CAS 1312-76-1 ), also known commercially as Kasil and listed as E560 , is an inorganic binder and film-forming agent produced by fusing silica with potassium carbonate.

It functions as a bonding agent, corrosion inhibitor, and biocide across construction, industrial, and agricultural applications. In construction, it is the active binder in silicate paints and mineral coatings.

It reacts with masonry substrates to form a permanent, non-film-forming bond that resists weathering and biological growth. Water treatment operations use it to passivate pipe surfaces and control corrosion.

By forming a protective silicate layer on metal infrastructure, it ensures longevity. Textile and paper processing employ it as a fixative and sizing agent, improving fiber bonding and surface strength during finishing.

In industrial cleaning and detergent formulations, it acts as a builder and alkaline buffer. This enhances soil removal and prevents redeposition on hard surfaces during the cleaning process.

Potassium silicate is supplied primarily as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous solution. The solids content and silica-to-potassium ratio (SiO₂:K₂O molar ratio) vary depending on the specific grade required.

Solid forms, including powder and cullet, are available for applications requiring dry blending or controlled dissolution. Technical and industrial grades are standard for most manufacturing needs.

Food-additive grade is available in compliance with E560 specifications. Our products meet rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistent performance across all industrial and commercial sectors.

In plastics and polymer production, it initiates free-radical polymerization of vinyl and acrylic monomers, controlling molecular weight and conversion rates at mid-range processing temperatures. Rubber compounders use it to cross-link elastomers.

This chemical improves mechanical strength and heat resistance in finished seals, gaskets, and molded components. In coatings and adhesive formulations, it drives the cure of unsaturated resins, enabling controlled hardening profiles suited to industrial application windows.

Sealant and elastomer producers select it where a defined half-life temperature aligns with their processing or oven-cure conditions. This ensures consistent performance during the manufacturing of high-performance industrial materials.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically in diluted or phlegmatized form to meet transport and handling requirements for organic peroxides. Concentrations vary by supplier, with technical-grade solutions being the standard commercial offering.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on volume requirements and regional regulatory classifications. Proper storage and temperature control are essential to maintain the stability and efficacy of this reactive chemical intermediate.

name: N-oleyldiethanolamine
description:
N-Oleyldiethanolamine (CAS 13127-82-7 ), also sold under the trade name Berol 302, is a fatty amine ethoxylate derived from oleic acid used across industrial and personal care markets.

It functions as a lubricant, emulsifier, and surface-active agent, enabling stable formulations and improved substrate wetting in demanding processing environments.

In metalworking fluids and cutting oils, it provides boundary lubrication and corrosion inhibition, extending tool life and improving surface finish quality for industrial manufacturing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair conditioning and skin emollient products, where its fatty chain delivers substantivity to treated surfaces for better performance.

Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and wetting agent during fiber treatment, dyeing, and finishing operations to ensure high-quality material output.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal or external lubricant and antistatic additive, reducing friction during compounding and improving surface release properties.

N-Oleyldiethanolamine is supplied as an amber to yellow liquid at ambient conditions. It is available primarily in technical grade, suitable for industrial lubricant and polymer applications.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers, with bulk supply options available through specialty chemical distributors to meet various commercial requirements.

name: Manganese dioxide
description:
Manganese dioxide (CAS 1313-13-9 ) is an inorganic mineral compound used across coatings, printing, and personal care industries as a drying catalyst, pigment, and oxidizing agent.

It accelerates oxidative cross-linking in oil-based systems and contributes brown-black coloration in pigment applications. In alkyd and oil-based coatings, it functions as a drying agent.

The compound catalyzes the oxidative polymerization of drying oils to reduce cure times and improve film hardness. Printing ink formulators incorporate it as a black pigment and drying promoter.

This is particularly useful in oil-based ink systems for packaging applications requiring fast set times. In personal care, it is used in certain hair coloring and oxidative cosmetic formulations.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a curing accelerator in polysulfide-based systems. It drives crosslinking to achieve target mechanical properties in industrial applications.

Manganese dioxide is supplied as a fine black powder in technical and battery grades. Particle size and purity specifications vary significantly depending on the specific end-use application.

Technical grade material is standard for coatings and adhesive applications, while higher-purity grades are available for specialty formulations. Bulk supply is common in 25 kg bags.

Larger packaging options are available for industrial volumes to meet high-capacity manufacturing needs. This ensures consistent supply chains for global chemical distribution networks.

name: Molybdenum trioxide
description:
Molybdenum trioxide (CAS 1313-27-5 ), also known as molybdic anhydride, is an inorganic molybdenum compound used as a functional pigment and biocidal agent across coatings and surface treatment industries.

Its role spans corrosion-inhibiting pigmentation, antimicrobial preservation, and as a precursor in specialty chemical manufacturing. In protective coatings and primers, MoO3 acts as a corrosion-inhibiting pigment.

It is frequently used to replace chromate-based systems in metal protection applications where regulatory pressure demands safer alternatives. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a mordant and fixative.

This improves dye uptake and wash fastness in finished goods. In printing inks and packaging coatings, it contributes biocidal and preservative functionality, extending product shelf life and inhibiting microbial growth.

Adhesives and sealant formulations incorporate molybdenum trioxide where antimicrobial performance is required alongside adhesion to metal or polymer surfaces. It is supplied as a fine white-to-pale yellow powder.

The material is available in both technical and high-purity grades. Standard specifications include technical grade for industrial coating and pigment applications, with higher-purity grades for catalyst uses.

Bulk supply is typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or drums, with packaging adjusted to meet industrial procurement volumes. This ensures consistent quality for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing.

name: Sodium sulfide
description:
Sodium sulfide (CAS 1313-82-2 ), also known as disodium sulfide, is an inorganic sulfur compound supplied primarily in hydrated flake form. It functions as a reducing and precipitating agent across several heavy industrial processes.

The compound is in particular demand for leather processing, textile dyeing, and metals recovery. In leather tanning, it is the primary unhairing agent used to break down keratin bonds in hides during the beamhouse stage.

This chemical directly affects throughput and hide quality in the tanning process. Textile manufacturers use it as a reducing agent to solubilize sulfur dyes, enabling deep, wash-fast coloration on cotton and cellulosic fibers.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, it precipitates heavy metal ions from process streams and leachates. This supports both metals recovery and effluent compliance for industrial facilities and large scale mining operations.

Paper pulp operations and water treatment facilities apply it for sulfide precipitation and pH adjustment. It is particularly effective in high-alkalinity process environments where precise chemical reactions are required.

The product is commercially supplied as yellow to brick-red hydrated flakes, typically at 60% purity. This form usually contains approximately 30 to 40 percent water content to maintain stability during transport.

Technical grade is the standard market form, with purity commonly specified at 60% Na2S minimum. Anhydrous and higher-purity grades exist for specialty applications but are less common in bulk industrial trade.

name: Nickel monoxide
description:
Nickel monoxide (CAS 1313-99-1 ), commercially known as black nickel oxide, is an inorganic compound used primarily as a colorant, surface modifier, and reactive component across industrial manufacturing.

It delivers controlled coloration and chemical reactivity in high-temperature and specialty coating processes. In coatings and surface treatments, it acts as a pigment and adhesion promoter.

This compound contributes to durable, corrosion-resistant finishes on metal substrates. Printing ink formulators incorporate it to achieve stable, heat-resistant black tones in specialty packaging inks.

These inks are designed for demanding print environments where stability is key. Elastomer and sealant manufacturers use it as a curing co-agent and surface modifier to improve bonding performance.

It enhances the connection between rubber compounds and metal components. In personal care, it appears in select cosmetic formulations as a colorant where regulatory compliance is a critical consideration.

Particle consistency remains a vital sourcing factor for these applications. The product is supplied as a fine black powder in technical and industrial grades for various manufacturing needs.

Particle size distribution and purity levels are key specification parameters buyers should confirm with suppliers. These factors directly affect pigment performance and reactivity in formulation.

Standard packaging ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk containers depending on order volume. Ensuring the correct grade is essential for maintaining quality standards across all industrial sectors.

name: Nickel nitrate
description:
Nickel nitrate ( CAS 13138-45-9 ), also sold as nickelous nitrate, is an inorganic nickel salt primarily used as a precursor in catalyst manufacturing and surface treatment processes.

It delivers controlled nickel deposition across a range of industrial substrates, making it a reliable starting material where precise nickel loading is required for high-performance applications.

In catalyst production, it serves as a key precursor for supported nickel catalysts used in hydrogenation and reforming processes, where uniform metal dispersion on carriers is critical.

Electroplating and surface finishing operations use it to produce nickel coatings on metals and plastics, providing corrosion resistance and improved adhesion for subsequent layers.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a mordant, fixing dyes to fibers and hides to improve colorfastness. Mining operations also draw on it for nickel recovery.

Nickel nitrate is commercially available as a hexahydrate in crystalline or granular form, with the hexahydrate being the dominant traded specification for industrial buyers.

Technical and reagent grades are standard across the market, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+. Bulk supply is available in fiber drums or bags for logistics.

Smaller packagings are offered for laboratory and specialty formulation use. This ensures that both large-scale manufacturers and research facilities can access the material easily.

name: Zinc oxide
description:
Zinc oxide (CAS 1314-13-2 ), commonly abbreviated as ZnO, is an inorganic mineral compound used across rubber, coatings, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as an activator, pigment, and antimicrobial agent depending on the application.

Procurement teams source it across multiple grades to meet requirements ranging from industrial rubber compounding to cosmetic-grade formulations. In rubber and elastomer manufacturing, ZnO acts as a vulcanization activator.

It works alongside stearic acid to initiate and control the crosslinking process. Coatings and paint formulators incorporate it as a white pigment and mildew-resistant additive, particularly in exterior architectural and marine coatings.

In personal care, cosmetic-grade ZnO is used in sunscreens, barrier creams, and mineral foundation products. These applications require specific UV-blocking and skin-protective performance to meet consumer safety standards.

Textile and leather processors apply it as an antimicrobial surface treatment to impart preservation properties to finished goods. Zinc oxide is supplied as a white powder in a range of particle sizes, including standard and micronized grades.

Recognized specifications include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC for pharmaceutical and food-contact applications. Technical and rubber-grade designations are also available for various industrial uses.

Indirect process (French process) and direct process (American process) grades are both commercially available. The former is typically preferred for rubber and higher-purity applications requiring consistent chemical performance.

name: Strontium peroxide
description:
Strontium peroxide (CAS 1314-18-7 ), also referred to as strontium dioxide, is an inorganic oxidizing salt that releases active oxygen upon contact with moisture or acidic conditions.

This controlled oxygen release makes it commercially valuable as a bleaching agent and biocide across several industrial processing sectors. In textile and paper manufacturing, it functions as a bleaching agent.

It is used for fiber and pulp treatments where a controlled, sustained oxidation profile is required. Water treatment operations use it to deliver slow-release oxygen for biocidal action against microbial contamination.

This application is critical in process water and effluent systems. Leather processing incorporates it into hide treatment stages to achieve uniform whitening without the aggressive degradation of stronger oxidants.

In personal care formulations, it appears in hair bleaching and tooth-whitening product development as an active oxygen source. Strontium peroxide is supplied as a white to off-white powder.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with active oxygen content and purity specifications typically confirmed by certificate of analysis. Packaging is available in moisture-resistant containers.

This specialized packaging is necessary given the product's reactivity with water under storage conditions. It remains a stable and reliable source of oxygen for diverse industrial and chemical applications.

name: Zirconium dioxide
description:
Zirconium dioxide (CAS 1314-23-4 ), commercially known as zirconia, is a high-performance inorganic oxide used across coatings, ceramics, and surface treatment applications. It functions primarily as a hardening agent, opacifier, and surface modifier in industrial formulations.

In coatings and sealants, zirconia acts as a crosslinking agent and surface hardener, improving scratch resistance and adhesion durability in architectural and industrial finishes. Personal care formulators incorporate it into antiperspirant and deodorant products.

In these cosmetic applications, it serves as an active odor-control and sweat-inhibiting material. In printing and packaging, it is used to enhance the abrasion resistance and gloss retention of surface coatings applied to paper and board substrates.

Adhesive and elastomer manufacturers use zirconia-based additives to improve thermal stability and bonding performance in high-stress applications. This versatility makes it a critical component for many specialized industrial manufacturing processes.

Zirconium dioxide is supplied as a white powder in varying particle sizes, including nanoscale and micronized grades suited to different processing requirements. Standard supply grades include technical, ceramic, and cosmetic-grade material.

Purity levels typically range from 99% upward for high-specification applications. Stabilized forms, including yttria-stabilized and magnesia-stabilized variants, are available for customers requiring specific structural or thermal performance.

name: Vanadium trioxide
description:
Vanadium trioxide (CAS 1314-34-7 ), also known as vanadium(III) oxide or V2O3, is an inorganic vanadium compound used primarily as a catalyst precursor and functional material in high-temperature industrial processes.

It serves as a key intermediate in vanadium chemical production and in the manufacture of specialty electronic components. In the metallurgical industry, it is used as a feedstock for producing ferrovanadium and other vanadium alloys.

These alloys are essential for strengthening steel in construction and automotive applications. The compound functions as a catalyst precursor in chemical synthesis, where controlled reduction to active vanadium species drives selective oxidation reactions.

In electronics, V2O3 thin films and powders are used in thermistor and switching device manufacturing. This application exploits its metal-insulator transition behavior for temperature-sensitive components and advanced circuitry.

It also serves as a starting material in the preparation of higher vanadium oxides, including vanadium pentoxide, used in sulfuric acid production catalysts. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial chemical manufacturing.

Vanadium trioxide is supplied as a fine black or dark gray powder in technical and high-purity grades. Standard purity levels range from 98% to 99.9%+, with high-purity grades available for electronics and research.

Packaging is typically offered in multi-kilogram quantities up to bulk industrial supply, depending on grade and application requirements. Our logistics team ensures secure handling and delivery for all industrial chemical orders.

name: Phosphorus pentoxide
description:
Phosphorus pentoxide (CAS 1314-56-3 ), also supplied under the designation P2O5 or phosphoric anhydride, is one of the most powerful desiccating and dehydrating agents available in industrial chemistry.

It reacts aggressively with water and moisture-bearing compounds, making it a critical reagent for driving dehydration reactions and producing phosphoric acid intermediates at scale.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, P2O5 acts as a cyclization and dehydration reagent for manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients where controlled water removal is essential to reaction yield.

Semiconductor and electronics manufacturers use it as a phosphorus diffusion source to dope silicon wafers, directly influencing conductivity profiles in chip fabrication.

In agrochemical production, it serves as a precursor in synthesizing phosphate-based fertilizers and crop protection compounds for the global agricultural market.

Catalyst manufacturers also use it to prepare solid acid catalysts for petroleum refining and petrochemical processing, ensuring high efficiency in industrial chemical streams.

Phosphorus pentoxide is supplied as a white hygroscopic powder or granular solid. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial synthesis and high-purity grades.

These grades meet specific pharmaceutical and electronics specifications. Packaging is typically in moisture-sealed drums or multi-layer bags to prevent premature hydration during storage.

name: Antimony pentoxide
description:
Antimony pentoxide (CAS 1314-60-9 ), also known as antimonic oxide, is an inorganic compound used primarily as a flame retardant synergist in polymer and textile systems.

Unlike antimony trioxide, it is preferred in applications requiring a halogen-free or low-halogen approach, and in systems where coloration or surface compatibility is a concern.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a synergist alongside halogenated flame retardants to improve fire resistance ratings in wire insulation and cable jacketing.

Textile and paper manufacturers apply it in back-coating formulations to meet fire safety standards for upholstery, curtains, and industrial fabrics used in various sectors.

In electronics, it is incorporated into printed circuit board laminates and encapsulant resins where flame retardancy must meet UL 94 or IEC standards for safety.

Building and construction applications include flame-retardant coatings and sealants where low smoke generation is a critical specification requirement for modern projects.

Antimony pentoxide is supplied as a white to pale yellow powder or as a colloidal aqueous dispersion, with the colloidal form preferred for textile and coating applications.

Standard grades include technical and industrial purity levels, with particle size and dispersion stability being key specification parameters for procurement and formulation.

name: Vanadium pentoxide
description:
Vanadium pentoxide (CAS 1314-62-1 ), also referenced commercially as V2O5, is the primary industrial form of vanadium used as a catalyst and catalyst precursor. It drives large-scale oxidation reactions across chemical manufacturing.

This material is particularly vital in sulfuric acid production where it functions as the active catalytic component. In sulfuric acid plants, it catalyzes the oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide in the contact process.

This specific role makes it indispensable to fertilizer, mining, and chemical manufacturing supply chains. The electronics and energy storage sectors use it as a precursor for vanadium redox flow batteries.

Consistent purity directly affects electrolyte performance in these advanced energy systems. Metallurgical processors use V2O5 as a feedstock for producing ferrovanadium and other vanadium alloys used in high-strength steel.

It also serves as a catalyst precursor in the production of phthalic anhydride from naphthalene or o-xylene oxidation. Vanadium pentoxide is supplied as an orange-yellow powder or fused flake form.

Flakes are common in catalyst manufacturing applications. Technical and metallurgical grades are the most widely traded, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.5%+ for high-purity catalyst and battery-grade specifications.

Packaging is available in drums and bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures reliable supply for large-scale industrial operations and specialized chemical processing facilities worldwide.

name: Phosphorus pentasulfide
description:
Phosphorus pentasulfide (CAS 1314-80-3 ), also known as P4S10 and phosphorus persulfide, is a reactive inorganic compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of organosulfur compounds.

Its core industrial value lies in its ability to introduce both phosphorus and sulfur into organic molecules, making it a critical building block across agrochemical, lubricant additive, and mineral processing chemistries.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it serves as a precursor to zinc dialkyldithiophosphate (ZDDP) and related antiwear and extreme-pressure additives for high-performance applications.

Agrochemical producers use it to manufacture dithiophosphate-based pesticides and insecticides, where controlled reactivity with alcohols and amines drives active ingredient synthesis for crop protection.

In mining and flotation chemistry, dithiophosphate collectors derived from P4S10 improve selective mineral separation in sulfide ore processing, enhancing the efficiency of metal extraction operations.

It also functions as a catalyst or reagent in specialty organic synthesis, including the production of pharmaceuticals and flame retardants, providing versatile chemical pathways for manufacturers.

Phosphorus pentasulfide is supplied as a yellow-green powder or fused lump form, typically packaged under inert atmosphere due to its high moisture sensitivity and reactive nature.

name: Molybdenum disulfide
description:
Molybdenum disulfide (CAS 1317-33-5 ), commonly identified by the shorthand MoS2, is a naturally occurring inorganic sulfide mineral processed into fine powder for industrial use.

It functions as a solid-state lubricant and surface modifier, reducing friction and wear between moving metal surfaces without relying on liquid carrier systems.

In metalworking and heavy machinery, MoS2 is compounded into greases, pastes, and dry-film lubricants to protect high-load, high-temperature bearing surfaces where conventional oils fail.

Coatings formulators incorporate it into anti-friction coatings applied to fasteners, gears, and aerospace components, where bonded dry-film performance is critical for the application.

In rubber and elastomer compounding, it improves surface slip and reduces mold adhesion during processing. Cosmetic formulators use MoS2 as a pigment and slip agent in pressed powders.

In color cosmetics, its dark gray tone and platelet structure contribute to texture and coverage. Molybdenum disulfide is supplied as a fine to ultrafine black-gray powder.

Particle size is a key specification that determines suitability across lubrication, coating, and cosmetic applications. Technical and industrial grades are standard for lubricant use.

Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care applications. Purity levels and particle size distribution are the primary differentiators between commercial offerings.

name: Lead monoxide
description:
Lead monoxide (CAS 1317-36-8 ), commonly known as litharge or massicot depending on its crystalline form, is an inorganic lead compound used as a reactive oxide in industrial processing. It functions primarily as a catalyst, curing agent, and flux across rubber manufacturing and metallurgical applications.

In rubber and tire production, lead monoxide acts as a vulcanization activator and accelerator co-agent, improving cross-link density and heat resistance in specialty compounds. Metallurgical processors use it as a flux in lead refining and smelting operations.

In these smelting operations, it facilitates the separation of impurities from base metal melts. It also serves as a precursor in the production of lead-based glass formulations, contributing to refractive index and density in optical and crystal glass manufacturing.

In mining and metals processing, it functions as an intermediate in the recovery and refining of lead from ore concentrates. Lead monoxide is supplied as a fine powder or dense granules, with particle size and purity specifications varying by end-use requirement.

Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels, typically at 99% minimum lead oxide content. Both litharge (alpha-PbO) and massicot (beta-PbO) polymorphic forms are available, with litharge being the predominant commercial form.

It delivers controlled copper ion release, which underpins its function in antimicrobial and surface-active applications. In personal care and cosmetics, it is incorporated into formulations where copper-based activity supports scalp and skin preservation.

Construction and coatings manufacturers use it as a pigment to achieve stable brown-black coloration in ceramic glazes, glass, and specialty coatings. Textile and leather processors apply it in dyeing auxiliaries and finishing treatments.

These treatments are essential where surface modification and biocidal protection are required. In printing and packaging, it contributes to specialty ink formulations and functional coatings where antimicrobial performance is a specification requirement.

Copper monoxide is supplied as a fine black powder in technical and industrial grades. Particle size distribution and purity levels vary by application, with high-purity grades available for electronic and specialty chemical uses.

name: Cuprous oxide
description:
Cuprous oxide (CAS 1317-39-1 ), also known as copper(I) oxide, is an inorganic compound used industrially as a biocidal pigment and surface-active agent.

It delivers both color and antimicrobial performance in a single raw material, making it a practical choice across protective coatings and agricultural formulations.

In marine and antifouling coatings, cuprous oxide acts as the primary biocidal pigment, preventing barnacle and algae attachment on submerged surfaces.

Agricultural formulations rely on it as a copper-based fungicide and bactericide for crop protection, particularly in seed treatments and foliar sprays.

Textile and leather processing use it for imparting antimicrobial properties to finished fabrics and hides. In electronics, it functions as a conductive pigment.

Cuprous oxide is supplied as a fine red-to-brown powder in varying particle size distributions suited to coating or agricultural end uses for industrial clients.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%. Specialized grades with controlled particle size are available.

These grades are ideal for antifouling paint formulations where dispersion consistency directly affects biocidal performance and long-term surface protection.

name: Hematite
description:

In protective coatings and primers, this mineral provides passive corrosion inhibition, making it a preferred pigment in heavy-duty industrial and marine paint systems. The construction industry incorporates it into concrete and cement products.

These paving products deliver durable red-to-brown coloration that resists UV degradation and weathering. In the pulp and paper sector, it is used as a filler and colorant where inorganic mineral stability is required for the final product.

Mining and metallurgical operations source this material as a dense medium in gravity separation processes. It also serves as a primary iron ore feedstock for downstream smelting and various mineral processing applications globally.

The product is supplied as a fine powder, with particle size and surface area specifications varying by application grade. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade pigment powder and natural ore concentrate for industrial use.

Iron oxide content is typically specified by buyers for both pigment and metallurgical use to ensure performance. Synthetic iron oxide variants are available where tighter color consistency and purity are required for specific formulations.

Its magnetic properties and chemical stability make it a reliable functional ingredient in both industrial and regulated end-use markets. In pigment manufacturing, it delivers a black colorant for concrete and coatings.

Construction materials utilize this oxide where consistent color performance and UV stability are required. Electronics producers use it as a core material in magnetic recording media and ferrite components.

It is also utilized in electromagnetic shielding applications. In catalysis, it functions as an active phase or support material in chemical synthesis and gas treatment processes, including hydrogen production.

Corrosion-inhibiting primers and protective coatings for automotive and structural steel applications incorporate it to extend substrate service life. It is supplied as a fine black powder in various grades.

Food-grade material is available under the E172 designation, meeting specifications for use as a colorant in regulated applications. Technical and pigment grades are also offered for industrial use.

name: Titanium dioxide
description:
Titanium dioxide (CAS 1317-80-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TiO2, is a high-performance white pigment and UV-blocking agent used across coatings, plastics, cosmetics, and construction materials.

The rutile form dominates commercial supply due to its superior opacity and weathering resistance. Procurement is driven primarily by whiteness index, particle size, and surface treatment specifications.

In architectural and industrial coatings, TiO2 delivers hiding power and durability, directly determining the coverage rate and exterior performance of paints and primers.

Plastics and polymer compounders incorporate it to achieve opacity and UV stabilization in films, pipes, and packaging materials. Personal care formulators use it in sunscreens.

In color cosmetics, it acts as a physical UV filter and white pigment. In paper and textile manufacturing, it improves brightness and opacity for paper coatings and synthetic fiber delusterants.

TiO2 is supplied as a fine white powder in rutile and anatase crystal forms, with rutile grades accounting for the majority of industrial demand for chemical manufacturers.

Surface-treated grades coated with alumina, silica, or organic treatments are standard for coatings and plastics applications, while uncoated grades serve specialty uses.

Common specifications include technical grade, cosmetic grade, and food-contact compliant grades meeting relevant regulatory standards for global distribution and safety.

Its fluorinated structure delivers low surface tension and selective solvency, making it a candidate solvent where conventional options are unsuitable. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a reaction solvent for fluorine-containing active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis.

Its chemical inertness prevents unwanted side reactions during complex chemical processes. It has been investigated as an inhalation anesthetic agent, with historical research under the Iso-indoklon designation informing modern CNS-active compound development.

Formulators working with specialty coatings or fluoropolymer systems use it as a carrier solvent where precise solvency control is required. Its low reactivity also supports use as a cleaning and rinsing solvent in precision manufacturing environments.

This compound is particularly effective when handling sensitive pharmaceutical equipment that requires non-reactive cleaning agents. Hexafluoroisopropyl methyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in research and specialty chemical quantities.

description:
Zeolite A (CAS 1318-02-1 ), also marketed as Zeosorb, is a synthetic aluminosilicate mineral engineered for ion exchange and sequestration across industrial and consumer applications.

Its structured microporous framework selectively captures calcium and magnesium ions, making it a functional replacement for phosphate-based builders in detergent systems.

In laundry and automatic dishwashing detergents, it acts as the primary water softening builder, sequestering hardness ions to prevent soap scum and improve surfactant efficiency.

Water treatment operations use it for ammonia removal and heavy metal capture in municipal and industrial effluent streams to ensure compliance with environmental regulations.

In agriculture, it is incorporated into soil amendment blends and slow-release fertilizer carriers, improving nutrient retention in sandy or degraded soils for better crop yields.

Construction product formulators add it to cement and lightweight aggregate mixes to improve moisture management and long-term structural performance in various building projects.

The material is supplied as a fine white powder, with particle size and bulk density varying by grade. Standard commercial grades include detergent-grade, technical-grade, and agricultural-grade.

Purity levels and ion-exchange capacity are the primary specification parameters buyers use to qualify supply sources and ensure the material meets specific application requirements.

name: Kaolinite
description:
Kaolinite (CAS 1318-74-7 ) is a naturally occurring aluminosilicate clay mineral used across industrial and specialty applications as a functional filler, coating agent, and rheology modifier.

It provides opacity, viscosity control, and surface smoothness in formulated products without altering the active chemistry of the system. In paper and board manufacturing, it is applied as a coating pigment.

This mineral improves printability, brightness, and surface uniformity in paper products. Rubber compounders incorporate it as a reinforcing filler in tire sidewalls and industrial rubber goods for dimensional stability.

It contributes to processing consistency in various manufacturing environments. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in tablet formulations and topical preparations where its adsorptive capacity supports delivery.

In agriculture, these formulations are applied as particle film coatings on crops and as a carrier in pesticide products. It is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder in various grades.

Standard commercial specifications include technical grade, pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and food-grade ( FCC ) depending on the target application and the specific regulatory requirements of the industry.

In coatings and resin manufacturing, cresol dissolves epoxy, phenolic, and wire enamel resins where lower-boiling solvents lack sufficient solvency power. Pharmaceutical and veterinary disinfectant formulations rely on its biocidal activity against bacteria and fungi.

This material is particularly effective in industrial cleaning concentrates and hard-surface sanitizers. Polymer producers use cresol as a reaction solvent and chain-stopper in the synthesis of polysulfones, polyimides, and specialty engineering resins.

Adhesive and sealant formulators also incorporate it as a stabilizer to inhibit oxidative degradation during processing and storage. Cresol is supplied as a liquid in mixed isomer form, with meta/para blends being the most commercially prevalent grade.

Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial solvent and synthesis applications. Drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities are typical supply formats for industrial procurement. This versatile chemical ensures stability and performance in demanding environments.

It functions as a mild but effective surface-active agent suited to formulations where skin compatibility and process efficiency are both priorities. In personal care, it appears in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers.

These applications require controlled foam and mild cleansing without aggressive stripping of the skin barrier. Textile wet processing relies on it as an emulsifier and wetting agent during dyeing and finishing operations.

This improves liquor penetration and dye uptake uniformity across various fabric types. In leather processing, it supports degreasing and preparation steps where consistent emulsification of fats and oils is critical to hide quality.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and serums where it provides a smooth, film-forming effect. This action supports moisture retention on the skin surface, providing a silky feel that consumers value in premium cosmetic products.

In textile processing, it modifies fiber surfaces to improve softness and antistatic performance during finishing operations. This ensures that fabrics remain comfortable and easy to handle throughout the manufacturing and consumer lifecycle.

Paper and leather manufacturers apply it to alter surface wetting behavior and enhance the uniformity of coatings or treatments. This industrial application ensures consistent quality and performance across various material substrates and finishes.

name: Lauryl hydroxysultaine
description:
Lauryl hydroxysultaine (CAS 13197-76-7 ), also supplied under trade names such as ORISTAR LHS and MACKAM LHS, is an amphoteric betaine-type surfactant derived from lauryl chemistry.

It functions as a foam booster, viscosity modifier, and conditioning agent across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid hand soaps, it enhances foam density.

The surfactant stabilizes lather while reducing the irritation potential of primary surfactant systems. Conditioning and antistatic properties make it a practical inclusion in hair care rinse-off products.

This ingredient is particularly useful where mildness is a formulation requirement. In textile and leather processing, it supports emulsification and soil removal in scouring and degreasing baths.

Paper manufacturing operations use it to control foam and improve fiber dispersion in wet-end processing. This versatility makes it a staple in various industrial chemical applications.

Lauryl hydroxysultaine is commercially available as an aqueous solution, typically at 30–50% active content. It is supplied in standard industrial grades suited for personal care and industrial applications.

Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for industrial volumes. This ensures safe and efficient transport for large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Sodium ortho-phenylphenate
description:
Sodium ortho-phenylphenate (CAS 132-27-4 ), also known as sodium o-phenylphenol, is the sodium salt form of ortho-phenylphenol, offering enhanced water solubility compared to its parent phenol.

It functions as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial and preservative active across industrial, agricultural, and consumer-facing applications. In textile and leather processing, it controls microbial growth in wet-processing baths.

The compound protects hides during storage and transit. Food-contact surface sanitizers and hard-surface disinfectants in food processing facilities rely on it as the active biocidal ingredient.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it as a preservative booster in rinse-off and leave-on products where water-soluble antimicrobial actives are required for stability.

In agriculture, it is used in post-harvest treatments and storage facility disinfection to prevent fungal and bacterial contamination of produce. This ensures the longevity and safety of the food supply.

Sodium ortho-phenylphenate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution, with concentration and purity specifications varying by end-use market requirements.

Technical grade material is standard for industrial disinfection and textile applications. Purer grades meeting pesticide registration requirements are available for food-contact and agricultural end uses.

name: Dibenzofuran
description:
Dibenzofuran (CAS 132-64-9 ), also known as diphenylene oxide or DBF, is a polycyclic heterocyclic compound used as a reference material and chemical intermediate in flavor and fragrance development.

Its fused aromatic structure makes it a recognized building block in the synthesis of specialty aroma chemicals and functional organic compounds. In flavor and fragrance formulation, DBF serves as a synthetic intermediate.

It is used for producing targeted aroma compounds used in fine fragrance and flavor systems. Cosmetic formulators source it as a precursor in the development of specialty fragrance ingredients for personal care products.

It is also used as an analytical reference standard in quality control laboratories testing for polycyclic aromatic compounds in food and cosmetic matrices. This ensures compliance with rigorous safety protocols.

Research and specialty chemical applications include its use as a scaffold for synthesizing heterocyclic derivatives with defined sensory or functional profiles. This versatility makes it essential for modern labs.

Dibenzofuran is typically supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. Standard offerings include technical grade and high-purity grades suitable for research, reference standard, and synthesis applications.

Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial orders depending on the intended use. Our logistics team ensures that all shipments meet the necessary safety and handling requirements for global delivery.

name: Penicillin v potassium
description:
Penicillin V Potassium (CAS 132-98-9 ), also known as Penicillin VK and Phenoxymethylpenicillin Potassium, is the potassium salt form of the acid-stable oral penicillin antibiotic used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

Its water-soluble salt form makes it the preferred raw material for solid oral antibiotic formulations over the free acid. The primary application is in the manufacture of oral antibiotic tablets and capsules.

It serves as the API for treating bacterial infections in human medicine. In veterinary pharmaceutical production, it is incorporated into oral suspensions and bolus formulations targeting livestock and companion animals.

Pharmaceutical compounding operations source it for preparation of oral liquid suspensions, particularly pediatric formulations requiring precise dosing flexibility. This ensures accurate administration for sensitive patient groups.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it is used as a selective agent in cell culture media to control bacterial contamination during research workflows. This maintains the integrity of experimental results.

Penicillin V Potassium is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bulk quantities suited to pharmaceutical manufacturing scale. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for compliance.

The potency is typically expressed in International Units (IU) per milligram to ensure standardized efficacy. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to multi-hundred kilogram drums.

These industrial API procurement options support both small-scale research and large-scale commercial production. The material meets rigorous global quality standards for pharmaceutical distribution.

name: Hydroxyethyl urea
description:
Hydroxyethyl urea (CAS 1320-51-0 ) is a urea-based humectant used primarily in personal care formulations and industrial processing applications. It attracts and retains moisture within substrates effectively.

This chemical serves as a functional alternative to glycerin and conventional urea in leave-on and rinse-off systems. In skin and hair care, it is incorporated into moisturizers, serums, and conditioners.

The ingredient delivers sustained hydration without the tackiness associated with high-glycerin formulations. Textile processors use it as a hygroscopic finishing agent to improve fabric hand-feel and reduce static.

It is effective in synthetic and natural fiber treatments. In leather processing, it supports uniform penetration of dyes and softening agents by maintaining substrate moisture during tanning operations.

Home care formulators include it in fabric softeners and surface cleaners where controlled moisture retention improves product performance. It is typically supplied as a clear to slightly yellow aqueous solution.

The product is most commonly available at a 50% active concentration. Cosmetic-grade material is the predominant commercial specification, with quality aligned to personal care industry standards.

These standards ensure low impurity profiles for sensitive applications. Technical-grade solution is also available for textile and industrial applications where cosmetic purity requirements do not apply.

Contact us for supply of Hydroxyethyl urea

name: Dodecanol
description:
Dodecanol (CAS 1322-35-6 ), also known as lauryl alcohol, is a fatty alcohol derived from natural or synthetic sources used across personal care, cleaning, and industrial formulation.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, surfactant precursor, and carrier in finished product manufacturing. In personal care, it acts as an emollient and co-emulsifier in creams, lotions, and hair conditioners.

It contributes to texture and skin feel without adding active claims. Sulfation or ethoxylation of dodecanol produces sodium lauryl sulfate and laureth surfactants, which are key intermediates in detergent manufacturing.

Industrial cleaning formulators use it as a coupling agent and solvent carrier to improve the stability of concentrated liquid cleaners. It helps maintain consistency in various chemical formulations.

In plastics and polymer processing, it functions as a plasticizer intermediate and lubricant additive. This helps to reduce friction during extrusion and molding operations in industrial settings.

Dodecanol is supplied as a white waxy solid or liquid depending on temperature, typically available in flake, pastille, or molten bulk form. It is handled according to standard safety protocols.

Standard commercial grades include technical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications. These ensure the material meets global regulatory requirements.

Purity levels commonly range from 98% to 99%+ for high-specification applications, with technical grades available for industrial use. This ensures reliability across diverse manufacturing sectors.

Contact us for supply of Dodecanol

name: Sodium diisopropylnaphthalenesulfonate
description:
Sodium diisopropylnaphthalenesulfonate (CAS 1322-93-6 ) is an anionic surfactant used across industrial formulations for wetting, dispersing, and emulsifying applications. It delivers strong surface activity in aqueous systems, enabling uniform distribution of active ingredients.

This chemical compound facilitates improved substrate penetration and ensures the stability of complex mixtures. In agrochemical formulations, it acts as a dispersant and wetting agent in wettable powder and suspension concentrate pesticides.

By improving raindrop coverage and leaf adhesion, it enhances the efficacy of agricultural treatments. Textile and leather processors use it to enhance dye penetration and ensure level dyeing across various fiber substrates.

In paper manufacturing, it supports pulp processing and surface sizing by reducing surface tension. This promotes even coating distribution and improves the overall quality of the finished paper products during the production cycle.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it to improve soil release and substrate wetting on hard surfaces. It is highly effective in demanding environments where rapid wetting and high electrolyte tolerance are required.

The product is supplied as a powder or as an aqueous solution, with the powder form being the most common for industrial handling. Technical grade is the standard specification available for agricultural and textile applications.

Bulk supply is typically offered in bags or drums depending on the physical form and customer requirements. It remains a versatile component for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in diverse chemical processing and cleaning sectors.

name: Myristyl lactate
description:
Myristyl lactate (CAS 1323-03-1 ), also marketed under the trade name Ceraphyl 50 and known commercially as tetradecyl lactate, is an ester used in personal care formulations as an emollient, solubilizer, and skin-conditioning agent.

It improves the spreadability and sensory feel of topical products without leaving a heavy or greasy residue. In leave-on skin care, including lotions, creams, and serums, it functions as a lightweight emollient that enhances skin feel.

This ingredient aids in the uniform distribution of active ingredients across the skin surface. Color cosmetics such as foundations and lipsticks use it as a plasticizer and binder to improve texture, adhesion, and payoff.

It also acts as a solubilizer for fragrance components and oil-soluble actives in both rinse-off and leave-on systems. Hair care formulations incorporate it to condition and reduce friction without contributing to buildup.

Myristyl lactate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard for personal care applications, and is commonly evaluated against purity benchmarks.

These benchmarks are relevant to finished product compliance and safety standards. Packaging typically ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers for commercial supply volumes to meet industrial manufacturing needs.

name: Glyceryl ricinoleate
description:
Glyceryl ricinoleate (CAS 1323-38-2 ), also known commercially as glyceryl monoricinoleate, is a monoglyceride ester derived from castor oil used across personal care, food, and industrial lubrication markets.

It functions as an emulsifier, humectant, and lubricant depending on the application context. In personal care formulations, it acts as a skin-conditioning emulsifier in creams, lotions, and lip products.

This ingredient helps stabilize oil-in-water systems while supporting moisture retention. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifying agent in fat-based systems to aid dispersion of incompatible phases.

It is frequently utilized in confectionery and bakery applications. In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it serves as a bio-based lubricant additive, reducing friction in cutting fluids and forming oils.

Low toxicity and biodegradability make it a priority for procurement teams. Its compatibility with natural and synthetic waxes also makes it a functional component in stick formulations and solid emollient bases.

Glyceryl ricinoleate is typically supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid or semi-solid, depending on temperature and purity. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications.

The food-grade material conforms to FCC standards where required. Bulk supply is standard in drums or intermediate bulk containers to meet the needs of large-scale industrial manufacturing operations.

name: Propylene glycol monostearate
description:
Propylene glycol monostearate (CAS 1323-39-3 ), commonly abbreviated as PGMS and approved as E477 , is a propylene glycol ester of stearic acid used as an emulsifier and plasticizer.

It is produced from the esterification of propylene glycol with stearic acid, yielding a mono-ester with moderate hydrophilic-lipophilic balance suited to oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems.

In food manufacturing, PGMS functions as an aerating emulsifier in cake mixes, whipped toppings, and bakery shortenings, improving volume and crumb structure for better consumer appeal.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions to stabilize emulsions and modify texture, contributing to a smooth, non-greasy skin feel in various cosmetic products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a plasticizer and emulsifying agent in topical formulations and tablet coatings where controlled release and consistency are required for safety.

In plastics processing, PGMS acts as an internal lubricant and softener, reducing melt viscosity and improving surface finish in polymer extrusion and other industrial manufacturing processes.

PGMS is supplied as white to off-white flakes or a waxy solid. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and E477 specifications is the most commonly traded form for global distribution.

Typical commercial grades are characterized by their mono-ester content, acid value, and iodine value to confirm purity and performance consistency across different industrial applications.

name: Edetate sodium tetrahydrate
description:
Edetate sodium tetrahydrate (CAS 13235-36-4 ), commonly known as EDTA tetrasodium salt tetrahydrate, is a fully neutralized, water-soluble chelating agent used across industrial and consumer product manufacturing.

It binds and sequesters metal ions such as calcium, magnesium, iron, and heavy metals. This prevents them from interfering with formulation stability, process efficiency, or overall product quality during manufacturing.

In personal care and cosmetics, it stabilizes emulsions and preservative systems by deactivating trace metals. These metals would otherwise accelerate oxidation or reduce the efficacy of antimicrobial systems in the product.

Water treatment operations use it to control scale formation and remove metal deposits from process equipment. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of distribution systems in various industrial environments.

In textile and paper processing, it prevents metal-catalyzed degradation of bleaching baths and dye formulations. This improves color consistency and yield while protecting the integrity of the final materials.

Food-grade applications include sequestering metal contaminants in canned and processed foods to protect flavor and color. This helps maintain shelf life and meets the strict requirements of the food industry.

Edetate sodium tetrahydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. It is available in food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical grades to meet the specification requirements of different industries.

Bulk packaging in bags and drums is standard for this material. Industrial quantities are available for large-scale procurement to support high-volume manufacturing and chemical processing operations.

description:
Pigment Blue 1 (CAS 1325-87-7 ), also known as C.I. Pigment Blue 1, is a triarylmethane-based organic pigment delivering a bright, reddish-blue shade across a range of industrial substrates.

It is valued in colorant formulations where vivid hue intensity and tinting strength are the primary selection criteria. In printing inks, it produces high-chroma blue tones suited to packaging applications.

Visual impact drives color specification in these sectors. Coatings formulators incorporate it into architectural and industrial finishes where a clean, saturated blue is required at relatively low pigment loading.

Textile and paper dyeing operations use it to achieve consistent surface coloration, particularly in applications where cost-effective blue shading is prioritized over extreme lightfastness demands.

Plastics compounders apply it in mass coloration of polymer substrates, including packaging films and molded articles. This versatility makes it a staple in the global colorant market for various polymers.

name: Olanzapine
description:
Olanzapine (CAS 132539-06-1 ), also referenced in procurement as LY-170053, is an atypical antipsychotic active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the manufacture of finished-dose psychiatric medications.

It is the primary API in treatments targeting schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, supplied to pharmaceutical manufacturers for tablet, orally disintegrating tablet, and injectable formulations.

The largest commercial demand comes from solid oral dosage manufacturers producing conventional film-coated tablets for long-term psychiatric maintenance therapy. These formats require high-purity API.

Orally disintegrating tablet formats require tightly controlled particle size to ensure dissolution performance and dose uniformity. Injectable depot formulations represent a growing segment in the market.

These specialized grades require defined polymorphic form and impurity profiles. Contract manufacturers and generic pharmaceutical producers also source the material as an intermediate for bioequivalent products.

Olanzapine is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for regulated market supply.

ICH-compliant impurity profiling is expected for all batches. Material is typically available in kilogram and multi-kilogram quantities with GMP-certified documentation packages required for procurement.

name: Sodium arachidate
description:
Sodium arachidate (CAS 13257-34-6 ) is the sodium salt of arachidic acid, a long-chain C20 fatty acid soap used as an emulsifier and surfactant across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its high carbon chain length positions it as a structurally distinct ingredient where conventional shorter-chain fatty acid soaps fall short in performance. In personal care, it contributes to bar soap and cream formulations.

These applications require a firm texture and stable emulsion structure. Textile processing operations use it as an emulsifying agent in fiber lubricants and finishing baths where consistent dispersion is critical.

In leather treatment, it supports fat liquoring emulsions that condition and soften hides during processing. Industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it for degreasing applications where high-melting soaps are needed.

This material provides controlled foam and soil suspension in heavy-duty environments. Sodium arachidate is typically supplied as a white powder or waxy solid for ease of handling in manufacturing.

It is available in technical and cosmetic-grade specifications to meet the sourcing requirements of both industrial and personal care manufacturers. Purity levels and packaging formats vary by supplier.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial procurement to ensure supply chain efficiency. This chemical remains a vital component for specialized surfactant systems requiring long-chain fatty acid properties.

name: Aluminum calcium silicate
description:
Aluminum calcium silicate (CAS 1327-39-5 ), also designated E556 in food regulation, is a synthetic aluminosilicate mineral used commercially as an anticaking agent and flow conditioner.

It prevents clumping and moisture absorption in powdered materials across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications. In food manufacturing, E556 is incorporated into table salt and seasonings.

These dry mixes maintain free-flowing characteristics through processing and shelf life. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an excipient in tablet and powder blends where consistent flowability is required.

It is also utilized where compressibility is necessary for manufacturing. In oil and gas operations, it functions as a component in drilling fluid formulations and cement slurries for wellbore applications.

The material contributes to fluid loss control and structural integrity. Water treatment and mining operations employ it for coagulation and flocculation support, aiding in the removal of suspended solids.

Aluminum calcium silicate is supplied as a fine white powder in both food-grade and technical-grade specifications. Food and pharmaceutical supply conforms to relevant compendial requirements.

These standards include FCC and Ph. Eur. monographs where applicable. Technical-grade material is available for industrial use in bulk quantities suited to drilling and water treatment.

The product is also ideal for mineral processing operations. This versatile mineral ensures efficiency and quality across a wide range of global manufacturing and processing sectors.

name: Polyaluminum chloride
description:
Polyaluminum chloride (CAS 1327-41-9 ), commonly known as PAC or ACH, is an inorganic coagulant used across water treatment and industrial processing. It neutralizes suspended particles and colloidal matter, enabling their removal through sedimentation or filtration.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, PAC destabilizes turbidity and organic load across a wide pH range, reducing downstream chemical demand compared to alum. This efficiency makes it a preferred choice for large-scale purification systems.

Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it as a retention and drainage aid, improving filler and fiber retention on the wire while controlling pitch deposits. This process enhances the overall quality and structural integrity of the final paper product.

Textile and leather processors use PAC in effluent treatment to precipitate dyes, suspended solids, and COD before discharge. This application is critical for meeting environmental regulations and ensuring safe wastewater management practices.

In paper sizing, it acts as a precipitant for rosin-based sizing agents, anchoring them to fiber surfaces to improve water resistance. This chemical interaction is essential for producing durable paper goods used in various commercial sectors.

Polyaluminum chloride is supplied as a liquid solution and as a dry powder or granule form, with liquid grades being the dominant commercial format. Standard basicity levels and Al2O3 content vary significantly by specific application.

Water treatment grades typically conform to drinking water standards such as those found in the FCC or USP . Technical and industrial grades are available for non-potable applications in paper, textile, and effluent treatment.

name: Arsenic trioxide
description:
Arsenic trioxide (CAS 1327-53-3 ), also known as white arsenic, is an inorganic oxide sourced for pharmaceutical manufacturing and metallurgical processing. It functions as a biocidal and chemical intermediate in tightly regulated industrial and medical supply chains.

In oncology drug manufacturing, it is the active pharmaceutical ingredient in treatments for acute promyelocytic leukemia, requiring pharmaceutical-grade supply with strict purity documentation.

Non-ferrous metal refining operations use it as a byproduct intermediate in copper and gold smelting, where it must be captured, processed, and handled under controlled conditions.

Glass manufacturing historically employed it as a fining agent to remove bubbles from molten glass, and this application persists in specialty glass production for specific industrial uses.

Wood preservation formulations, particularly in chromated copper arsenate systems, represent a legacy industrial use still active in certain regulated markets across the globe today.

Arsenic trioxide is supplied as a white powder or in refined crystalline form. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and EP specifications for global distribution.

Documented purity levels are required for API supply chains. Technical-grade material is supplied for metallurgical and industrial applications, with buyers typically requiring a certificate of analysis.

Compliance documentation is essential given the substance's regulatory status. Our supply chain ensures that all safety protocols and handling requirements are met for every industrial shipment.
