name: Pigment green 7
description:
Pigment Green 7 (CAS 1328-53-6 ), commercially known as Phthalocyanine Green and sold under trade names such as Heliogen Green G and Colanyl Green GG, is a polychlorinated copper phthalocyanine pigment.

This pigment delivers intense, high-chroma green coloration across industrial applications. It is valued by formulators for its outstanding lightfastness, heat stability, and resistance to solvents and chemicals.

These properties directly determine long-term color performance in finished goods. In coatings and industrial paints, it produces deep, saturated greens with excellent exterior durability for architectural systems.

It is a preferred choice for automotive and protective coating systems. Plastics processors incorporate it into polyolefins, PVC, and engineering resins where high processing temperatures demand stability.

The pigment holds color without bleeding or migration during manufacturing. Printing ink manufacturers rely on it for packaging inks, including offset, gravure, and flexographic applications for consistency.

Color consistency across long press runs is critical for these industries. Textile and paper dyeing operations use it to achieve uniform, wash-resistant green shades in both fiber and surface coatings.

The material is supplied as a dry powder, typically in fine-milled or micronized particle grades optimized for dispersion. It is available in standard pigment grades and dispersion-ready preparations.

Masterbatch concentrates for plastics are also available. Technical-grade material is the predominant commercial form, with specific surface treatment variants offered for waterborne or solventborne systems.

name: Blonanserin
description:
Blonanserin (CAS 132810-10-7 ), also referenced under development codes AD-5423 and DSP-5423, is an atypical antipsychotic compound developed for the treatment of schizophrenia.

It functions as a dopamine D2/D3 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonist, positioning it as a key active pharmaceutical ingredient in CNS-targeted drug development pipelines.

Blonanserin is primarily sourced as an API or pharmaceutical intermediate for the manufacture of antipsychotic drug products, including tablets and transdermal patch formulations.

Contract manufacturers and generic drug developers use it as a reference standard or synthesis starting material when developing CNS formulations targeting schizophrenia.

Research organizations and CROs procure this material for receptor binding studies and comparative pharmacological profiling in psychiatric drug discovery programs.

It is also evaluated as an intermediate in the synthesis of structurally related heterocyclic compounds within medicinal chemistry workflows for new drug development.

Blonanserin is available as a white to off-white crystalline powder in research, pilot, and commercial quantities. Supply is offered under pharmaceutical-grade specifications.

High-purity material, typically ≥98% by HPLC, is suitable for API manufacturing and analytical reference use. Packaging ranges from milligram-scale to kilogram lots.

name: Diethylphenylamine-borane
description:
Diethylphenylamine-borane (CAS 13289-97-9 ), also known as N,N-diethylanilineborane, is a selective organoboron reducing agent used in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It delivers controlled hydride reduction under mild conditions.

This reagent offers greater selectivity than many conventional borohydride reagents. In pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis, it reduces imines, oximes, and carbonyl compounds with high chemoselectivity.

It supports the production of chiral amines and active pharmaceutical ingredient precursors. Industrial cleaning and surface treatment formulations use it as a catalyst or initiator in polymerization systems.

In biotechnology research, it supports reductive amination protocols for labeling, conjugation, and biomolecule modification workflows. It also functions as a catalyst precursor in organometallic chemistry.

Its amine-borane structure enables activation under specific reaction conditions. Diethylphenylamine-borane is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on purity and handling conditions.

It is available in research and commercial quantities, with technical and high-purity grades suited to pharmaceutical and specialty chemical applications. Packaging ranges from small-scale laboratory quantities.

Bulk supply is available for process-scale synthesis. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and performance in sensitive chemical transformations and industrial processes.

name: Borane dimethyl sulfide complex
description:
Borane dimethyl sulfide complex (CAS 13292-87-0 ), commonly abbreviated as BMS, is a stabilized borane reagent used as a selective reducing agent in organic synthesis. Unlike unstabilized borane, BMS offers improved handling characteristics.

These features make it practical for large-scale pharmaceutical manufacturing and complex chemical processing. BMS is the reagent of choice for reducing carboxylic acids, amides, and oximes to their corresponding alcohols and amines.

In active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) synthesis, it is used in asymmetric hydroboration reactions. It is often paired with chiral auxiliaries to produce enantiomerically enriched intermediates for various drug candidates.

In agrochemical manufacturing, BMS supports the synthesis of herbicide and fungicide intermediates where controlled selectivity is critical. This ensures high yields and purity during the production of specialized crop protection chemicals.

Biotechnology researchers also employ it in the preparation of boronated compounds for boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) research. It is further utilized in the development of labeled biochemical probes for diagnostic use.

Borane dimethyl sulfide complex is supplied as a liquid, typically as a neat reagent or in solution with tetrahydrofuran (THF). Standard concentrations of 2M and 10M in THF are commonly available for laboratory use.

Material is typically offered at reagent and synthesis grades to meet diverse industrial needs. High-purity specifications are available to meet strict pharmaceutical intermediate requirements and regulatory standards.

name: Polyquaternium 27
description:
Polyquaternium-27 (CAS 132977-85-6 ), commercially available as Mirapol 175 and Mirapol 95, is a quaternary ammonium copolymer used across personal care and industrial applications.

It functions primarily as a conditioning agent and film-former, delivering substantivity to hair and skin surfaces while contributing to rheology control in aqueous formulations.

In hair care, it deposits a conditioning film on damaged or chemically treated hair, improving combability, reducing static, and enhancing wet and dry feel in shampoos and conditioners.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and body washes where its humectant character supports moisture retention and a smooth after-feel for the end user.

In textile processing, it modifies fiber surfaces to improve softness and antistatic performance in finishing baths. Paper and leather manufacturers use it as a surface-treatment additive.

This chemical influences wetting behavior and surface uniformity across various substrates. Polyquaternium-27 is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content varying by grade.

Mirapol 95 and Mirapol 175 represent distinct commercial grades with differing molecular weight profiles suited to different application requirements and formulation viscosities.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting the purity standards expected for leave-on and rinse-off personal care formulations.

name: DL-tartaric acid
description:
DL-tartaric acid (CAS 133-37-9 ) is the racemic form of tartaric acid, produced synthetically rather than derived from wine byproducts. It functions as an acidulant, pH buffer, and stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food and beverage production, it acidifies confectionery, baked goods, and soft drinks where a clean, tart flavor profile is required. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent in effervescent tablets and oral solutions.

Controlled pH directly affects active ingredient stability and dissolution rate in these medical applications. In personal care, it adjusts pH in creams, serums, and hair treatments, contributing to product stability and skin compatibility.

It also functions as a chelating agent in formulations where metal ion control is needed to prevent oxidative degradation. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking consistent performance across diverse product lines.

DL-tartaric acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules for easy handling. Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is the most commonly sourced grade for acidulant applications in the industry.

Pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to USP and Ph.Eur. monographs is available for regulated manufacturing environments. These high-purity standards ensure the ingredient meets strict safety and quality requirements for global distribution.

name: Dichloroxylenol
description:
Dichloroxylenol (CAS 133-53-9 ), also known as DCMX and marketed under the name Decasept, is a chlorinated phenolic compound used as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial preservative and biocide.

Its activity against bacteria, fungi, and mold makes it a functional ingredient where microbial control is a formulation or process requirement across industrial and consumer-facing applications.

In personal care and cosmetics, DCMX is incorporated into antiseptic washes, medicated soaps, and topical disinfectant formulations as the active preservative agent for various product lines.

Textile and leather processors use it to prevent microbial degradation during wet processing and in finished goods requiring long-term preservation against environmental factors and decay.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it functions as an antioxidant and stabilizer, protecting materials from oxidative breakdown during processing and extending the overall service life.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers also source it as an intermediate in the synthesis of antimicrobial active ingredients. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

Technical grade is the most common commercial form, with pharmaceutical-grade material available for regulated applications requiring tighter purity specifications and adherence to strict manufacturing protocols.

Buyers typically source it in multi-kilogram bags or drum quantities depending on application volume. This ensures consistent supply chains for large-scale manufacturing and specialized chemical processing.

name: DL-alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate
description:
DL-alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate (CAS 133-80-2 ) is the synthetic ester form of Vitamin E, offering greater stability than free tocopherol for use in fortified products and formulations.

It functions as both a nutritional supplement ingredient and a formulation antioxidant across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. In food and dietary supplement manufacturing, it is used to fortify products.

This includes infant formula, meal replacements, and vitamin blends where label-declared Vitamin E content is required. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into oral capsules, softgels, and injectable preparations.

In personal care, it is added to skin creams, serums, and hair care products to deliver antioxidant protection. It also supports the shelf stability of oil-based formulations and prevents rancidity over time.

Animal feed producers use it to supplement livestock and poultry diets, where consistent potency is critical. Oxidative stability during pelleting and storage ensures the nutritional value remains intact for the animals.

DL-alpha-Tocopheryl Acetate is supplied as a clear, viscous oil or in dry, powder-dispersible forms. These formats are suitable for solid dosage and dry-blend applications across various industrial sectors.

Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications. The oil form is typically available at 1000 IU/g potency to meet specific manufacturing requirements for high-quality output.

Feed-grade material is also available, often standardized to specific IU/g activity levels for premix incorporation. This ensures precise dosing and uniform distribution within large-scale agricultural feed production.

name: Xylene
description:
Xylene (CAS 1330-20-7 ), also known as xylol, is an aromatic hydrocarbon solvent sourced as a mixed isomer blend used across coatings, adhesives, and chemical manufacturing.

It dissolves a broad range of resins, oils, and polymers that resist less aggressive solvents, making it a preferred carrier in high-performance formulations for industrial applications.

Demand is consistent across industrial cleaning, printing, and automotive sectors where solvent strength and evaporation rate are critical sourcing criteria for manufacturers and distributors.

In coatings and paints, xylene thins alkyd, epoxy, and polyurethane resins to achieve correct application viscosity for industrial and architectural finishes and protective surface layers.

Rubber compounders use it to dissolve and process natural and synthetic rubber during adhesive and sealant manufacturing. Printing ink producers rely on it as a carrier solvent.

In automotive refinishing and industrial cleaning, it cuts through grease, wax, and cured coatings to prepare metal and plastic surfaces before treatment or final finishing processes.

Xylene is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. It is available in mixed xylenes as the standard commercial form with high purity specifications.

Industrial-grade and solvent-grade designations are the most commonly traded specifications across global markets, typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ purity for various uses.

name: Sodium tetraborate
description:
Sodium tetraborate ( CAS 1330-43-4 ), also known by its E-number E285 , is the anhydrous form of borax — a mineral salt used across industrial and food-contact applications as a preservative and buffering agent.

It also functions as a flame retardant and cleaning booster. Its anhydrous form offers a higher boron content and lower moisture contribution compared to hydrated grades, which matters for formulators managing water activity.

In building and construction, it is applied to wood treatments and insulation materials to provide flame retardancy and resistance to fungal degradation. Textile and leather processors use it in bath formulations to control pH.

This chemical helps improve the uptake of dyes and finishing agents. Water treatment operations rely on it as a buffering compound to stabilize pH in industrial process water, ensuring consistent chemical reactions.

At permitted levels under the E285 designation, it functions as a preservative in certain food contact and packaging applications in regulated markets. Sodium tetraborate anhydrous is supplied as a white powder.

It is also available as fine granules. Standard commercial grades include technical and food-grade specifications, with purity typically at 99% or higher. Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities.

name: Diisooctyl maleate
description:
Diisooctyl maleate (CAS 1330-76-3 ), also supplied under trade designations such as Bisomer D10M and Octomer DIOM, is a reactive diester monomer used across polymer and lubricant manufacturing.

It functions as both a copolymerizable building block and an internal plasticizer, allowing formulators to modify flexibility and processability directly within the polymer backbone.

In plastics and polymer production, it copolymerizes with acrylates, vinyl acetate, and other monomers to produce films, coatings, and adhesives with tailored softness and elongation.

Rubber compounders incorporate it to improve flexibility and processing behavior in specialty elastomers without relying solely on external plasticizer migration during the manufacturing process.

In lubricant formulations, it contributes to viscosity modification and acts as a functional base fluid component in metalworking and industrial lubricant blends for various industrial sectors.

Coatings manufacturers use it as a reactive diluent that reduces viscosity during application while becoming chemically bound in the cured film, effectively avoiding common plasticizer bleed-out.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger procurement volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Buyers should confirm purity, acid value, and color specifications with suppliers, as these parameters directly affect copolymerization performance and the final quality of the chemical application.

name: Tricresyl phosphate
description:
Tricresyl phosphate (CAS 1330-78-5 ), also known as TCP or Kronitex, is an organophosphate ester used as a plasticizer, flame retardant, and extreme-pressure lubricant additive across demanding industrial applications.

Its combination of thermal stability and load-bearing performance makes it a preferred functional additive where both flexibility and fire resistance are required in a single component for various manufacturing processes.

In PVC and synthetic rubber compounding, TCP imparts flexibility while simultaneously reducing flammability. This dual function reduces the need for separate additive packages in polymer formulations.

Hydraulic fluids and compressor lubricants incorporate TCP as an extreme-pressure additive. It forms protective films on metal surfaces under high-load conditions to prevent wear and mechanical failure.

Aerospace and defense applications rely on TCP in aircraft hydraulic fluids and turbine engine oils. Resistance to thermal degradation at elevated operating temperatures is critical for these high-stakes environments.

Automotive transmission fluids and gear oils also use TCP to extend component life under heavy mechanical stress. It ensures smooth operation and longevity for critical vehicle drivetrain systems.

Tricresyl phosphate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical grade, with industrial-specification material being the standard commercial form for lubricant and polymer applications.

Bulk liquid supply in drums and ISO tank containers is the norm for large-volume procurement. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery of high-purity chemical additives for your specific industrial needs.

name: Polyaminopropyl biguanide
description:
Polyaminopropyl biguanide (CAS 133029-32-0 ), commonly referred to as PAPB or PHMB, is a polymeric antimicrobial agent used across industrial and personal care markets. It delivers broad-spectrum biocidal activity against bacteria, fungi, and algae.

This chemical functions as both a preservative and a surface-active disinfectant. Its polymeric structure allows effective performance at low use concentrations across diverse formulation types and industrial applications.

In personal care, PAPB is used as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products including contact lens solutions, eye drops, and skin cleansers. Low irritation potential is a key formulation requirement for these uses.

Water treatment operations use it as an algaecide and bactericide in swimming pools and cooling towers. It is often utilized as an alternative to chlorine-based systems in these specific environments.

Textile and leather processing facilities apply it as an antimicrobial finish to impart durable hygiene properties to fabrics. This treatment ensures long-lasting protection for various treated materials and industrial textiles.

In wound care and medical device cleaning formulations, it functions as a primary active biocide. It is particularly valued where residual antimicrobial action is required for safety and hygiene standards.

Polyaminopropyl biguanide is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 20% active concentration. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially available forms for industrial procurement.

Some suppliers offer material conforming to pharmacopoeial standards for healthcare applications. Bulk supply is standard in intermediate and large-volume quantities for industrial buyers and manufacturing facilities.

name: Zinc borate
description:
Zinc borate (CAS 1332-07-6 ) is an inorganic boron-zinc compound used as a flame retardant and smoke suppressant across a range of polymer and coating systems. It functions by promoting char formation and inhibiting combustion.

This chemical reduces both flame spread and afterglow in finished materials. In plastics and polymer compounding, it is incorporated into PVC, polyolefins, and engineering resins to meet fire performance standards.

It allows manufacturers to achieve safety goals without relying solely on halogenated additives. Coatings and intumescent formulations use it to enhance char yield and suppress smoke generation on treated substrates.

Common applications include structural steel and timber protection. Rubber and elastomer manufacturers add it to cable jacketing and conveyor belting where sustained flame resistance is a regulatory requirement.

In textile and paper treatments, it provides flame retardancy to coated fabrics and barrier papers. These materials are frequently used in construction and specialized industrial packaging applications.

The product is supplied as a white powder in varying particle size distributions suited to different compounding processes. It is available in technical and flame-retardant grades for industrial use.

Product specifications are typically defined by the boron-to-zinc ratio and water of crystallization content. Packaging options generally include 25 kg bags and bulk quantities for industrial procurement.

name: Pumice
description:
Pumice (CAS 1332-09-8 ), also known as pumicite in its fine powdered form, is a naturally occurring volcanic mineral sourced and processed for use across abrasive, filtration, and surface treatment applications.

Its controlled porosity and hardness make it a practical functional filler and abrasive agent in both industrial and consumer product manufacturing. In personal care and cleaning formulations, it is widely used.

Pumice powder is incorporated into hand soaps, foot scrubs, and scouring pastes where controlled mechanical exfoliation is required. The textile and denim industry uses pumice stones in garment finishing to achieve effects.

These stones help achieve stonewashed effects and surface distressing on fabric. Construction applications include use as a lightweight aggregate in concrete, plaster, and insulating blocks where reduced density is a target.

In leather processing, pumice is used for buffing and surface preparation to achieve consistent texture before finishing. Pumice is supplied as crushed stone, coarse granules, and milled powder for various uses.

Particle size is the primary specification variable across grades. Standard grades include technical and cosmetic-grade powder, with cosmetic grades subject to tighter particle size and purity controls.

Bulk supply is common for industrial buyers, with finer mesh grades available for personal care and cleaning product formulators. This ensures compatibility with a wide range of manufacturing requirements.

name: Iron oxide
description:
Iron oxide (CAS 1332-37-2 ), sold under the food and cosmetic designation E172 , is a family of inorganic pigments spanning red, yellow, black, and brown hues.

These pigments deliver stable, opaque coloration across a broad range of industrial and consumer applications where UV resistance and heat stability are procurement priorities for manufacturers.

In architectural and industrial coatings, iron oxides provide long-term color retention on exterior surfaces exposed to weathering. Concrete and paving blocks are mass-tinted using these pigments.

Roof tiles achieve consistent, fade-resistant coloration throughout the substrate. Plastics compounders incorporate them into masterbatches for automotive parts, pipes, and packaging films for performance.

Colorfast performance under high processing temperatures is required. Printing inks and packaging laminates use iron oxide pigments to meet opacity and regulatory compliance targets in various applications.

Iron oxide is supplied as dry powder, granules, and dispersed slurry or paste concentrates. Granule and low-dust forms are preferred for large-scale industrial handling and safety protocols.

Standard grades include synthetic iron oxides meeting ASTM D3722 for pigment applications, as well as food-grade material conforming to E172 specifications under EU and FCC standards.

Natural and synthetic variants are both commercially available. Synthetic grades offer tighter particle size distribution and higher tinting strength for precise industrial color matching requirements.

name: Copper oxychloride
description:
Copper oxychloride (CAS 1332-40-7 ), also sold under trade names such as Coprantol and Cuprasol, is an inorganic copper-based compound used primarily as a fungicide and bactericide across agricultural and industrial markets.

Its biocidal action against a broad range of fungal pathogens and bacteria makes it a well-established active ingredient in crop protection and industrial preservation programs. In agriculture, it is formulated into wettable powders.

These suspension concentrates are used for foliar application, controlling diseases such as downy mildew, blight, and bacterial canker on fruits, vegetables, and vines. Water treatment operations use it to suppress algal growth.

It is effective against microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water circuits. In the pulp and paper industry, it functions as a slimicide and preservative, preventing microbial contamination in process water.

It also serves as a copper supplement source in animal feed premixes where regulated copper intake supports livestock health. The compound is supplied as a green-blue powder or wettable powder concentrate.

Technical-grade material is the most common commercial form. Agricultural-grade specifications are standard, with active copper content typically expressed as metallic copper equivalent for various industrial applications.

Feed-grade material is available in select markets where regulatory approval for use in animal nutrition has been granted. This ensures the product meets necessary safety requirements for the livestock industry.

name: Kaolin
description:
Kaolin (CAS 1332-58-7 ), also known commercially as Bolus alba, is a naturally occurring hydrated aluminum silicate clay mineral processed for industrial use. It functions as a functional filler, coating pigment, and rheology modifier across a broad range of manufacturing sectors.

In pulp and paper manufacturing, kaolin is applied as a coating pigment and filler to improve printability, brightness, and surface smoothness of finished sheets. Rubber compounders incorporate it as a reinforcing filler in tire sidewalls and molded goods.

Personal care formulators use it as an absorbent and texture-modifying agent in face masks, dry shampoos, and pressed powders. In construction materials, kaolin serves as a functional extender in paints and ceramic bodies.

It is also used in cement-based products to control viscosity and reduce raw material costs. Kaolin is supplied as a dry powder in both calcined and water-washed grades, with calcined forms offering higher brightness for coatings.

Standard commercial grades include technical, ceramic, paper-coating, and rubber-grade specifications. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications are served by USP and BP -compliant grades, available in bulk bags or drums.

These high-purity grades ensure safety and efficacy in sensitive formulations. Whether for industrial coatings or personal care products, this mineral remains a versatile and cost-effective solution for modern manufacturing needs.

name: Copper oxychloride
description:
Copper oxychloride (CAS 1332-65-6 ), also known as copper chloride hydroxide, is an inorganic copper salt used commercially as a contact fungicide and bactericide. It delivers broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity across agricultural and industrial applications where copper-based protection is required.

In crop protection, this compound is formulated into wettable powders and suspension concentrates to control fungal and bacterial diseases in fruits, vegetables, vines, and cereals. This includes effective management of downy mildew, blight, and leaf spot pathogens.

Ornamental horticulture and forestry operations use it to protect nursery stock and timber against bacterial canker and fungal rots. In water treatment, it functions as an algaecide and microbial control agent in reservoirs and irrigation systems.

The material is also utilized in industrial cooling circuits to maintain system hygiene. It frequently appears in antifouling coatings and wood preservative formulations where sustained copper release is needed for long-term protection.

Copper oxychloride is supplied as a green-blue technical powder, with wettable powder and water-dispersible granule forms common in the agrochemical trade. These formats ensure ease of application and stability during storage.

Standard technical grades are specified by copper content, typically expressed as metallic copper equivalent. Buyers sourcing for formulation should confirm particle size distribution and copper assay against relevant industrial specifications.

name: Potassium tetraborate
description:
Potassium tetraborate (CAS 1332-77-0 ), also known as dipotassium tetraborate or potassium borate, is an inorganic boron salt used across industrial processing as a buffering agent, flame retardant, and preservative.

Its combination of functions makes it a practical single-source additive in formulations where pH stability and biological protection are both required. In water treatment, it acts as a pH buffer and biocide.

This chemical helps to control microbial growth in process water and cooling systems. Textile manufacturers apply it as a flame retardant finish on natural and synthetic fibers to reduce combustibility.

In leather processing, it functions as a preservative during curing and tanning, extending material stability before finishing. This ensures the leather remains durable throughout the manufacturing cycle.

Agricultural applications include use as a boron micronutrient source in fertilizer blends. This is essential for addressing boron-deficient soils that often limit crop yield and overall plant health.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications, with material specifications typically defined by purity and moisture content.

Quality is often measured by the boron oxide equivalent within the batch. Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific application volume and logistical requirements.

This process achieves deep blue shades with high fixation efficiency. Leather tanneries use it for through-dyeing and surface coloration where color fastness under wet conditions is a critical performance requirement.

In paper manufacturing, it is used for mass coloration and surface treatment of specialty papers where consistent hue and bleed resistance matter. It also serves as a substrate in biochemical assays.

It is typically provided in commercial dye concentrations standardized by dye content percentage. Technical and laboratory grades are both available depending on the specific application and purity needs.

name: Phenolsulfonic acid
description:
Phenolsulfonic acid (CAS 1333-39-7 ), also known as benzenesulfonic acid monohydrate, is a strong organic acid used industrially as a catalyst and pH-regulating agent.

Its combination of acidic and phenolic functionality makes it effective in driving reactions and controlling process chemistry across multiple manufacturing sectors and industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an acid catalyst in synthesis steps and as a counterion in salt formation for active pharmaceutical ingredients during complex chemical production.

Textile processors use it in dyeing and finishing baths to regulate pH and improve dye uptake consistency across fiber types, ensuring high-quality results in large-scale textile manufacturing.

In leather processing, it supports tanning and retanning operations where controlled acidity is critical to hide penetration and finish quality for various commercial leather goods.

Water treatment applications include use as a sulfonating agent and process chemical where precise pH control is required in industrial effluent systems and environmental management protocols.

Phenolsulfonic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging around 65% w/w, though other concentrations are available to meet specific process requirements.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available for API synthesis and regulated manufacturing environments.

name: Chromium trioxide
description:
Chromium trioxide (CAS 1333-82-0 ), also known as chromic trioxide, is a strong inorganic oxidizing agent used primarily in metal surface treatment and electroplating processes. It delivers controlled oxidation and surface activation across a range of industrial finishing operations.

In hard chrome electroplating, it forms the electrolyte bath that deposits wear-resistant chromium coatings on industrial components, tooling, and hydraulic parts. Metal surface treatment operations use it to create conversion coatings.

These coatings improve corrosion resistance and paint adhesion on aluminum and steel substrates. The leather industry applies it in chrome tanning processes, where it fixes hides and produces durable, consistent leather for footwear and upholstery.

In specialty printing and packaging, it functions as an oxidizing agent in the production of certain pigments and surface-etching applications. This chemical is supplied as dark red flakes or granules for various industrial uses.

Liquid chromic acid solutions are also available for direct process use. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher for electroplating and surface treatment applications.

Packaging is available in drums and bulk quantities, with strict regulatory compliance documentation required. This is due to its classification as a substance of very high concern under REACH regulations.

name: Sodium bifluoride

Sodium bifluoride ( CAS 1333-83-1 ), also sold as sodium acid fluoride, is an inorganic fluoride salt used industrially as a pH buffer, mild acidic flux, and surface treatment agent.

Its controlled fluoride release makes it effective for etching, cleaning, and corrosion inhibition across metal, mineral, and textile processing operations. In metal finishing and mining, it functions as a pickling agent.

The compound is essential for removing oxide scale and preparing metal surfaces prior to coating or further processing. Textile and leather processors use it to adjust bath pH and improve dye uptake uniformity.

During fabric treatment, it ensures consistency across batches. In building and construction, it is applied to concrete and masonry surfaces as a hardening and anti-efflorescence treatment for long-term durability.

Water treatment operations use it as a source of fluoride ions for controlled dosing and pH correction in industrial effluent streams. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing and environmental management.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher to meet rigorous industrial specifications.

name: Carbon black
description:
Carbon black (CAS 1333-86-4 ), also marketed as furnace black, lamp black, and thermal black depending on production method, is a fine carbon particulate produced through controlled combustion or thermal decomposition of hydrocarbons.

In industry, it functions primarily as a reinforcing agent, pigment, and UV stabilizer across rubber, plastics, and coating systems. In tire and rubber manufacturing, it reinforces elastomer matrices to improve abrasion resistance.

This mechanical durability accounts for the majority of global consumption. Plastics compounders incorporate it as a UV stabilizer and black colorant in pipe, film, and automotive components requiring long-term outdoor performance.

Printing inks and coatings rely on specific particle-size grades to achieve deep black pigmentation and controlled rheology. These are used in offset, flexographic, and industrial coating formulations to ensure consistent quality.

Sealants and adhesives use the material to modify surface wetting, improve cohesive strength, and deliver conductivity in electrically functional systems. It is supplied as a dry powder or in pelletized form for industrial use.

Pellets are often preferred for dust-controlled handling in high-volume compounding operations. Grades are differentiated by particle size, structure, and surface area, commonly designated under ASTM classifications such as N220.

Other common designations include N330 and N550 for rubber applications. Specialty grades meeting food-contact or regulatory standards, including E153 classification in certain markets, are available for specific compliance.

These specialty options ensure that manufacturers can meet strict end-use requirements. The versatility of the product makes it a cornerstone material for modern industrial manufacturing and chemical processing globally.

In personal care, it functions as a fragrance component and solvent in perfumes, lotions, and hair care products where a soft floral note is required. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a flavoring agent in baked goods, beverages, and confectionery.

This ingredient adds a subtle rose or hyacinth-type character within permitted usage levels for various food applications. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a solvent and carrier in topical preparations, where its solvency profile supports active ingredient delivery.

It also serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of fragrance compounds and pharmaceutical actives. This makes it a primary procurement target for chemical manufacturers building more complex molecules for industrial use.

name: Magnesium peroxide
description:
Magnesium peroxide (CAS 1335-26-8 ), also marketed as Peromag and Drillox M, is a solid oxidizing agent that releases oxygen slowly upon contact with moisture. This controlled oxygen release makes it effective as a soil amendment and water treatment additive.

It serves as a powerful antimicrobial agent across multiple industries. In contaminated site remediation and groundwater treatment, it delivers sustained oxygen to stimulate aerobic biodegradation of hydrocarbon pollutants.

Agricultural applications rely on its slow oxygen release to improve soil aeration and promote root development. It is also used to extend the viability of seeds in waterlogged or anaerobic conditions.

Pharmaceutical and healthcare formulators use it as a mild bleaching and antimicrobial component. It is frequently found in oral care products, wound care preparations, and various disinfectant formulations.

In oilfield drilling, it functions as an oxidizing additive to control anaerobic bacteria in drilling muds and fluid systems. This ensures the stability and safety of the fluid systems during extraction.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder, typically with active oxygen content specified as a percentage. Standard commercial grades range from approximately 15% to 50% active content.

name: Ammonium hydroxide
description:
Ammonium hydroxide (CAS 1336-21-6 ), also sold as ammonia water and designated E527 in food-grade applications, is an aqueous solution of ammonia used industrially as an alkaline reagent and pH control agent.

It functions across cleaning, processing, and treatment operations where a fast-acting, readily soluble base is required. In water treatment, it adjusts pH and supports chloramine disinfection in municipal systems.

Textile, leather, and paper processing rely on it to neutralize acids, swell fibers, and condition pulp during wet processing stages. Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it to cut through grease and protein-based soils.

In rubber compounding, it acts as a stabilizer for latex dispersions, preventing premature coagulation during transport and storage. This ensures the material remains stable during long-term industrial transport and storage.

Ammonium hydroxide is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging from 25% to 30% ammonia by weight for industrial supply. This high concentration allows for efficient dilution in various processes.

Food-grade material conforming to E527 specifications is available for permitted food processing applications. Technical-grade solutions are the standard for water treatment, cleaning, and industrial processing uses.

name: Ethylbutylamine
description:
Ethylbutylamine ( CAS 13360-63-9 ) is a secondary aliphatic amine used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical production, and polymer chemistry. N-Butylethylamine is a recognized alternative name buyers may encounter in supplier catalogs.

It functions primarily as a chemical intermediate, solvent, and reaction modifier in multi-step industrial processes. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a building block for active ingredient synthesis.

It also acts as a buffering agent to control pH in reaction sequences. Agrochemical formulators use it as an intermediate in the production of herbicides and pesticides, where controlled basicity is required.

In polymer and plastics production, it acts as a polymerization initiator or catalyst modifier. This influences chain initiation and molecular weight distribution during the manufacturing of various materials.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as a functional additive. Amine-based pH control improves formulation stability and performance in demanding industrial environments.

Ethylbutylamine is supplied as a liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging suited for industrial volumes. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification for most industrial applications.

Purity levels suitable for pharmaceutical intermediate use are available from select suppliers. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and moisture content when sourcing for GMP-regulated applications.

name: Isobutyl cyanoacetate
description:
Isobutyl cyanoacetate (CAS 13361-31-4 ) is an ester of cyanoacetic acid used as a reactive intermediate and monomer building block across specialty chemical manufacturing. Its combination of an active methylene group and a nitrile function makes it a practical starting material.

This chemical is essential for synthesizing more complex molecules in pharmaceutical and agrochemical production. In pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis, it serves as a precursor in the construction of heterocyclic compounds and active pharmaceutical ingredient scaffolds.

Agrochemical manufacturers use it to produce crop protection compounds, particularly where the cyanoacetate moiety is incorporated into herbicide or pesticide structures. It provides a reliable backbone for these specialized agricultural applications.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a monomer or co-monomer in the preparation of cyanoacrylate-type systems and specialty adhesive formulations. It also supports Knoevenagel condensation reactions at scale for industrial use.

These reactions enable the production of fine chemical intermediates for various downstream applications. Isobutyl cyanoacetate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging suitable for bulk and intermediate-volume procurement.

Technical grade is the primary commercially available specification, with purity levels typically confirmed by GC analysis. Suppliers commonly offer this product in drum quantities for diverse manufacturing needs.

Larger bulk arrangements are available through contract or toll manufacturing channels to meet high-volume demand. The material is handled according to standard industrial safety protocols for organic esters and nitriles.

name: Polyglyceryl-3 caprate
description:
Polyglyceryl-3 caprate (CAS 133654-02-1 ), also known as triglycerol caprate, is a mild, plant-derived emulsifier produced by esterifying polyglycerol with capric acid. It functions as a surfactant and emulsifier across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

This versatile ingredient enables stable oil-in-water systems at low use levels. In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetics, it emulsifies light oils and actives into water-based systems, supporting clean-label and naturally derived formulations.

Food manufacturers use it to improve fat dispersion and texture in emulsified products where a mild, non-ionic emulsifier is required. In skin care, its humectant character supports moisture retention in lotions and serums without leaving a heavy residue.

Coating and adhesive formulators apply it as a wetting and dispersing agent to improve substrate adhesion and pigment distribution. This functionality makes it a valuable component in high-performance industrial applications requiring precise surface tension control.

Polyglyceryl-3 caprate is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid or low-viscosity paste. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available to meet diverse manufacturing needs.

Material often meets COSMOS or NATRUE certification requirements for natural and organic formulations. Bulk supply is standard in drums or IBCs, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and development quantities.

name: Copper naphthenate
description:
Copper naphthenate (CAS 1338-02-9 ), also sold under the abbreviation CNC and commercially known as naphthenic acids copper salts, is an oil-soluble copper compound used across industrial preservation, coatings, and rubber processing.

It delivers broad-spectrum biocidal activity and functions as a metal catalyst in curing and cross-linking systems. In wood preservation and agricultural treatments, it protects timber, utility poles, and structural materials.

The compound prevents fungal decay and insect attack without requiring pressure treatment in all cases. Coatings and marine antifouling formulations incorporate it as a biocidal additive that remains active in oil-based systems.

This makes it ideal where water-soluble alternatives are unsuitable. Rubber and elastomer manufacturers use it as a cross-linking catalyst and adhesion promoter, particularly in bonding rubber to metal or textile substrates.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it acts as a boundary lubrication additive and corrosion inhibitor for specific metal surfaces. It is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in mineral spirits or naphtha carriers.

Copper content is commonly specified at 8% or higher concentrations depending on end-use requirements. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity and copper content verified by certificate of analysis.

Bulk supply in drums and IBCs is standard for industrial buyers, with concentration and solvent carrier confirmed per order specification. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing applications.

name: Methyl ethyl ketone peroxide
description:
Methyl ethyl ketone peroxide (CAS 1338-23-4 ), commonly known as MEKP, is an organic peroxide used as a free-radical initiator in polymer curing and crosslinking systems. Supplied as a solution rather than in pure form, it activates resin systems at room temperature without requiring elevated heat.

Formulators and compounders rely on it to control cure speed and crosslink density across a range of thermoset applications. MEKP is the standard initiator for curing unsaturated polyester and vinyl ester resins in fiberglass-reinforced composites.

This includes marine hulls, automotive panels, and construction laminates. In combination with cobalt-based accelerators, it enables ambient-temperature cure cycles that are critical for open-mold and hand lay-up fabrication.

Rubber compounders use it as a crosslinking agent to improve heat resistance and mechanical performance in elastomeric profiles and molded parts. It also initiates polymerization in gel coats and casting resins.

In these applications, cure uniformity directly affects surface quality and product yield. MEKP is supplied as a liquid solution, typically diluted in plasticizers or inert carriers to reduce reactivity hazards during handling and transport.

Standard commercial concentrations range from approximately 33% to 60% active oxygen content, with grades varying by reactivity profile to suit different resin systems and processing conditions.

Technical-grade material is the norm for most industrial uses. Buyers should confirm active oxygen percentage and dilution carrier with suppliers when qualifying for specific applications to ensure compatibility.

name: Sorbitan monododecanoate
description:
Sorbitan monododecanoate (CAS 1338-39-2 ), commercially recognized as Sorbitan monolaurate and approved as E493 , is a sorbitan ester derived from sorbitol and lauric acid.

It functions primarily as a non-ionic emulsifier and dispersing agent across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In food production, E493 stabilizes emulsions in bakery coatings and confectionery.

It is used in fat-based systems where consistent texture and shelf life are critical purchasing criteria. Pharmaceutical formulators use it to emulsify topical creams, ointments, and oral preparations.

It is often used in combination with polysorbates to achieve target HLB values. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into lotions, sunscreens, and hair conditioners for emulsion stability.

The product is valued for its mild skin compatibility. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a fiber lubricant and softening agent applied during finishing operations.

Sorbitan monolaurate is supplied as a pale yellow to amber viscous liquid or soft waxy solid depending on temperature and grade. Food-grade material conforming to E493 specifications is available.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP /NF and Ph. Eur. monographs are both commercially available. Technical grade is also offered for industrial textile and leather applications.

These industrial grades are suitable where food or pharma compliance is not required. The material remains a versatile staple for manufacturers requiring reliable emulsification properties.

name: Sorbitan monostearate
description:
Sorbitan monostearate (CAS 1338-41-6 ), commonly known as SMS or E491 , is a non-ionic emulsifier derived from sorbitol and stearic acid. Arlacel 60 is a recognized trade name buyers will encounter across supplier and formulation documentation.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier and stabilizer across food, cosmetic, and industrial manufacturing processes. In food production, SMS is used to stabilize fat-based emulsions in baked goods and confectionery coatings.

In these applications, it controls fat crystallization and improves texture consistency in products like margarine. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions as a water-in-oil emulsifier.

This provides structure and improves product spreadability for high-end topical applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use SMS as an excipient in topical ointments and tablet coatings for various medical uses.

Controlled emulsification supports uniform active ingredient distribution throughout the finished product. In textile processing, it functions as a fiber lubricant and softening agent during manufacturing.

This reduces friction during yarn and fabric production to ensure high-quality output. Sorbitan monostearate is supplied as a cream to tan-colored waxy solid, typically in flake or bead form.

Food-grade material is available meeting FCC and E491 specifications for global compliance. Pharmaceutical-grade supply conforms to USP and Ph. Eur. standards for regulated markets.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial textile and paper applications. These diverse grades ensure that the specific purity requirements of every manufacturing sector are met effectively.

name: Sorbitan monooleate
description:
Sorbitan monooleate (CAS 1338-43-8 ), commercially recognized as Span 80 and approved as E494 in food applications, is a nonionic lipophilic emulsifier derived from sorbitol and oleic acid.

It stabilizes water-in-oil emulsions and dispersions across food, cosmetic, and industrial manufacturing processes. In food production, E494 functions as an emulsifier in shortenings, margarine, and bakery fats.

This additive prevents phase separation and improves texture consistency in various food products. Personal care formulators use Span 80 to build stable water-in-oil creams, lotions, and ointment bases.

It is often paired with polysorbate 80 to fine-tune HLB balance in complex formulations. Textile and leather processing operations apply it as a wetting and softening agent for better results.

The chemical improves fiber lubrication and dye penetration during finishing stages. In agrochemical and industrial formulations, SMO acts as a dispersant and emulsifier for pesticide concentrates.

It is also utilized in metalworking fluids to ensure stability and performance. Sorbitan monooleate is supplied as an amber, oily liquid in drum and IBC quantities for large scale use.

Standard grades include food-grade meeting FCC and E494 specifications and technical-grade for industrial applications. Cosmetic-grade material is also available for specialized needs.

Material conforming to Ph.Eur. and BP specifications is available for personal care manufacturing. These high standards ensure the product meets rigorous safety and quality requirements.

name: Gypsum
description:
Gypsum (CAS 13397-24-5 ), also sold as mineral white, is a naturally occurring calcium sulfate dihydrate used across construction, agriculture, and food processing. It functions as a setting agent, soil conditioner, and rheology modifier depending on the application sector.

In food manufacturing, gypsum acts as a coagulant in tofu production and a calcium-fortifying agent in beverages and baked goods. Construction applications rely on it as the primary raw material for drywall, plaster, and cement retarders.

Controlled set time is critical to product performance in these industrial settings. Agricultural buyers source gypsum to improve soil structure in clay-heavy fields and supply calcium and sulfur to crops without altering soil pH.

In paper manufacturing, it functions as a filler and coating pigment that improves sheet brightness and printability. Gypsum is supplied as a fine powder, granules, or crushed stone depending on the specific end-use requirement.

Food-grade and FCC -compliant grades are available for direct food contact applications. Technical and agricultural grades cover construction and soil amendment uses where high purity is not the primary concern.

Purity levels and particle size distribution are the primary specification variables buyers should confirm with suppliers. This ensures the material meets the necessary standards for the intended industrial or commercial application.

name: Sodium ascorbate
description:
Sodium ascorbate (CAS 134-03-2 ), also sold under the food additive designation E301 , is the sodium salt form of ascorbic acid used commercially as an antioxidant and preservative across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Unlike ascorbic acid, it offers a neutral pH profile that makes it suitable for sensitive formulations where acidity must be controlled. In food processing, E301 prevents oxidative discoloration and rancidity in cured meats and beverages.

It often functions as a curing accelerator alongside nitrites in packaged goods. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a stable, non-acidic vitamin C source in tablet, powder, and injectable formulations where patient tolerability is a priority.

In cosmetic and personal care products, it acts as an antioxidant stabilizer in serums, creams, and topical formulations. This helps to protect active ingredients from oxidative degradation during storage and application.

The food supplement sector also uses it as a direct vitamin C source in effervescent tablets, sachets, and functional drink mixes. Sodium ascorbate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial applications.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , with pharmaceutical grades subject to stricter purity thresholds. Bulk supply is typically available in 25 kg bags or fiber drums.

name: Menthyl anthranilate
description:
Menthyl anthranilate (CAS 134-09-8 ), also known as meradimate, is an organic UV filter used in sunscreen and photoprotection formulations. It absorbs UV radiation in the UVA range, allowing formulators to build broad-spectrum protection.

When combined with other UV actives, it enhances the overall efficacy of the product. Its primary use is as a UVA filter in sunscreen products including lotions, creams, sprays, and sticks, where it contributes to SPF ratings.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into daily moisturizers and color cosmetics that require incidental sun protection without heavy mineral filter loads. This makes it a versatile choice for modern skincare applications.

In lip care products, it provides UV protection while remaining compatible with emollient and wax-based systems. This compatibility ensures a smooth application and stable shelf life for various consumer goods.

Beyond finished cosmetics, it is also evaluated as a pharmaceutical intermediate in photoprotective topical drug formulations. These applications are often subject to specific OTC monograph requirements for safety.

Menthyl anthranilate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity standards for personal care.

Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities suited to commercial sunscreen manufacturing. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale industrial production needs.

name: Diethyltoluamide
description:
Diethyltoluamide ( CAS 134-62-3 ), widely recognized by its abbreviation DEET, is the benchmark active ingredient in insect and arthropod repellent formulations. It acts by disrupting the olfactory receptors of insects, preventing them from locating a host.

This mechanism makes it the reference standard against which other repellent actives are measured. It is the primary active in consumer and professional-grade repellent products including sprays, lotions, creams, and impregnated wipes.

Concentrations typically range from 5% to 100% depending on protection duration and target market. In military and expedition-grade formulations, high-concentration products are specified for extended field use against mosquitoes and ticks.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into pump sprays and roll-ons sold through pharmacy and outdoor retail channels. It is also used to treat fabrics and gear in combination repellent systems for outdoor gear.

While fabric-specific actives such as permethrin are common, this material remains a versatile choice for many applications. It is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in bulk and drummed quantities for industrial use.

Technical-grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 95–99%. Some suppliers offer pharmaceutical or cosmetic-grade material to support regulated consumer product registration requirements.

name: 4-methylbenzophenone

In UV-curable coatings and inks, it acts as a photoinitiator that triggers polymer cross-linking upon UV exposure. This process produces hard, durable surface finishes without the need for thermal processing during the manufacturing cycle.

Printing and packaging converters use it in energy-curable ink formulations where fast cure speeds are essential. These formulations meet low migration potential requirements, which are critical process standards for modern industrial printing applications.

In adhesive and sealant systems, it supports photoinitiated bonding in specialized applications. This is particularly useful where heat-sensitive substrates rule out conventional curing methods that require high temperatures to set.

Polymer stabilizer blends also incorporate it as a UV-stabilizing component to protect plastic substrates. This protection prevents photodegradation over the service life of the material, ensuring long-term structural integrity and appearance.

4-Methylbenzophenone is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid for industrial use. It is available in technical grade for formulation, with purity specifications typically at 99% or above for photoinitiator-grade applications.

Packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for laboratory and formulation development to bulk drum supply. This flexibility supports both small-scale testing and large-scale industrial production volumes for global chemical distributors.

name: Sodium ichthyol
description:
Sodium ichthyol (CAS 1340-06-3 ), also known commercially as Ichthyol, is a sulfonated shale oil derivative used primarily for its antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties in pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations.

It is produced by the distillation and sulfonation of oil-bearing shale, yielding a dark, viscous material with broad-spectrum activity against bacteria and fungi. Procurement demand is driven largely by dermatological product manufacturers.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, this compound is the active ingredient in ointments and creams targeting acne, eczema, folliculitis, and localized skin infections. Compounding pharmacies source it to prepare customized formulations.

In personal care, it is incorporated into scalp treatments and anti-dandruff products where its antimicrobial action targets fungal overgrowth. Agricultural and veterinary applications include topical treatments for hoof conditions.

Sodium ichthyol is supplied as a dark, viscous liquid or semi-solid paste, typically in concentrations of 10% or 50% aqueous preparations, as well as in near-anhydrous form for specific industrial uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to Ph. Eur. and BP specifications is the standard for medicinal applications. Technical-grade material is available for veterinary and agricultural end uses.

Contact us for supply of Sodium ichthyol

name: Cobalamin
description:
Cobalamin (CAS 13408-78-1 ), also referenced commercially as Cbl, is the parent form of the vitamin B12 family of compounds. It functions as a biologically active cofactor essential to the production of nutritional supplements and pharmaceutical dosage forms.

The material is used extensively in fortified food and feed products across multiple regulated industries. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into injectable preparations, oral tablets, and sublingual formulations targeting deficiency treatment.

Food and beverage producers use it to fortify products such as plant-based milks, breakfast cereals, and functional beverages. This is particularly important where dietary B12 intake is a specific formulation requirement for the end consumer.

In animal nutrition, it is added to premixes and compound feed to support metabolic function in livestock and poultry. In these applications, a deficiency directly impacts production performance and overall animal health outcomes.

Nutraceutical formulators also incorporate it into multivitamin blends and specialty dietary supplements. These products often target vegan and vegetarian consumer segments who require reliable external sources of this essential vitamin.

The product is supplied as a fine crystalline powder, typically in cyanocobalamin or methylcobalamin forms depending on the application. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for high-purity requirements.

Food-grade specifications are also available for fortification use in various commercial sectors. Bulk supply is offered in quantities ranging from small technical lots to commercial-scale packaging to meet production demands.

name: Nicotinamide riboside
description:
Nicotinamide riboside (CAS 1341-23-7 ), commonly abbreviated as NR, is a naturally occurring form of vitamin B3 that functions as a direct precursor to NAD+ in cellular metabolism.

Its commercial value lies in this NAD+ precursor activity, which positions it as a premium active ingredient across nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic markets globally.

In dietary supplements, NR is formulated into capsules and tablets targeting energy metabolism and healthy aging, where it commands a distinct market segment from conventional niacin.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into anti-aging serums and moisturizers to support skin cell renewal and improve the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles in topical applications.

In pharmaceutical research and clinical nutrition, NR is evaluated in formulations addressing metabolic and neurodegenerative conditions, driving demand for high-purity, well-characterized material.

Biotechnology and life sciences applications include use as a biochemical reagent and cell culture supplement where controlled NAD+ modulation is required for experimental success.

Nicotinamide riboside is supplied primarily as a white crystalline powder. It is available in stabilized salt forms which offer improved shelf stability for commercial formulation and storage.

Grades range from research-grade material to food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with leading suppliers providing certificates of analysis aligned to USP standards.

name: Isooctyl palmitate
description:
Isooctyl palmitate (CAS 1341-38-4 ), also known commercially as palmitic acid 2-ethylhexyl ester, is a synthetic ester of palmitic acid used as an emollient, solvent, and carrier in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations.

It provides skin-conditioning and spreading properties without the heaviness associated with natural oils. In personal care, it functions as a lightweight emollient in lotions, creams, and sunscreens, improving skin feel and spreadability.

This versatile ester helps in reducing greasiness in various topical applications. Pharmaceutical topical formulations use it as a carrier solvent to enhance the delivery and dispersion of active ingredients across the skin barrier effectively.

Color cosmetics such as lipsticks and foundations incorporate it as a plasticizer and binder to improve texture and application consistency. It also serves as a solubilizer for oil-soluble actives and pigments in product formats.

The material is effective in both rinse-off and leave-on product formats for diverse consumer needs. Isooctyl palmitate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid suitable for direct incorporation into many different formulations.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of regulated end products. Bulk supply is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers for industrial logistics.

Technical-grade material is also available for non-cosmetic industrial applications requiring high performance. Our product ensures consistent quality and reliability for manufacturers across the global chemical and beauty industries.

name: Ammonium bifluoride
description:
Ammonium bifluoride (CAS 1341-49-7 ), also known as ABF, is an inorganic fluoride salt used across metal treatment, surface preparation, and industrial cleaning processes.

It delivers controlled fluoride activity in acidic conditions, making it a practical alternative to hydrofluoric acid in applications where handling pure HF is operationally difficult.

In metal processing and mining, ABF functions as a flux and etchant for removing oxide layers from aluminum, stainless steel, and other alloys prior to finishing or refining.

Electronics manufacturers use it in glass and silicon etching, where precise surface modification is required for component fabrication during the manufacturing process.

In textile and paper production, it acts as a pH buffer and flame retardant additive, contributing to fire-resistance treatments in various types of finished goods.

Building and construction applications include masonry cleaning and concrete surface treatment, where its fluoride content dissolves silicates and mineral deposits effectively.

Ammonium bifluoride is supplied as white crystalline granules or powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically at 95–98%+.

Bulk packaging in fiber drums or HDPE containers is common for industrial supply, with smaller quantities available for laboratory or specialty use in research settings.

name: Sodium selenate
description:
Sodium selenate (CAS 13410-01-0 ), also identified commercially as disodium selenate, is an inorganic selenium salt used as a controlled selenium source across agricultural, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications.

Unlike selenium-deficient formulations, it delivers a precise, water-soluble selenium dose where bioavailability and dosing accuracy are critical procurement considerations for chemical manufacturers and distributors.

In animal nutrition and feed manufacturing, this compound is incorporated into premixes and mineral supplements to correct selenium deficiency in livestock, particularly in regions with selenium-depleted soils.

Fertilizer producers use it as a foliar spray or soil amendment to fortify selenium-deficient crops, supporting food chain selenium enrichment programs and improving overall agricultural output quality.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators source it as a selenium active for tablet and solution preparations where exact elemental selenium content must meet strict regulatory specification.

In water treatment and industrial processes, it functions as a biocide component and corrosion inhibitor in specific closed-loop systems, providing stability and protection for sensitive equipment.

Sodium selenate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or anhydrous solid. Standard grades include technical, feed-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material for various industrial needs.

Pharmaceutical supply typically conforms to USP or Ph. Eur. specifications. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial orders, with concentration and purity levels specified per grade.

name: Ammonium thiolactate
description:
Ammonium thiolactate (CAS 13419-67-5 ) is the ammonium salt of thiolactic acid, used across personal care, textile, and pharmaceutical manufacturing as a reducing and buffering agent.

Its thiol-reactive chemistry makes it effective for breaking and reforming disulfide bonds in protein-based substrates, supporting both structural modification and stabilization processes.

In hair care, it functions as the active reducing agent in permanent wave and chemical straightening formulations, softening keratin bonds to allow controlled reshaping.

Leather processing operations use it to assist in depilation and fiber relaxation during hide preparation, reducing reliance on more aggressive sulfide-based chemistries.

Textile processors apply it in wool treatment to improve fiber receptivity before dyeing or finishing steps. This ensures consistent results across various industrial applications.

Pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulators also incorporate it as a pH buffer and mild antioxidant stabilizer in formulations sensitive to oxidative degradation during storage.

Ammonium thiolactate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration ranges varying by application grade to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available. Buyers should confirm active content and pH specification with suppliers, as these parameters affect performance.

name: Sunset Yellow FCF
description:
Sunset Yellow FCF (CAS 1342-61-6 ), also known as E110 and FD&C Yellow No. 6, is a synthetic azo dye approved for use in food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. It delivers a stable orange-yellow hue across a broad range of formulations.

This product is one of the most recognized certified colorants in global markets. In food manufacturing, it is used to color beverages, confectionery, snack coatings, and processed foods where a consistent orange-yellow shade is required.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers apply it to tablet coatings, capsule shells, and liquid oral preparations to aid product identification and brand differentiation. It ensures visual consistency across different production batches and global regions.

In personal care, it appears in rinse-off products such as shampoos and bath gels where color stability under varying pH conditions is a formulation priority. It is also used in pet food coloring for regulatory acceptance.

Batch-to-batch consistency and high purity are key sourcing criteria for industrial buyers. Sunset Yellow FCF is supplied as a fine orange powder, typically in both pure dye form and as a lake pigment for specific uses.

These lake pigments are ideal for applications requiring oil-dispersible or insoluble color. Standard grades include food-grade meeting FD&C, EU E110, and BP specifications to ensure global compliance.

Purity levels and certifiable lot documentation are standard requirements for food and pharmaceutical procurement channels. Our material meets rigorous quality benchmarks for safety and performance in sensitive applications.

name: Hydroxocobalamin
description:
Hydroxocobalamin (CAS 13422-51-0 ), also known as Vitamin B-12b, is a naturally occurring form of cobalamin distinguished by a hydroxyl ligand in place of the more common cyano group. OH-Cbl is the predominant cobalamin form found in food sources.

It serves as a direct precursor to the two biologically active coenzyme forms of B12. In pharmaceutical and nutritional manufacturing, it functions as both an active ingredient and a conversion intermediate for various formulations.

In injectable pharmaceutical formulations, it is the preferred B12 form for treating deficiency and cyanide poisoning. Its superior retention time over cyanocobalamin supports clinical dosing protocols in medical settings.

Nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturers use it in tablet, capsule, and sublingual formats targeting B12 repletion. Biotech and life sciences producers rely on it as a biosynthetic precursor for production.

It is used for producing adenosylcobalamin and methylcobalamin in specialized labs. In animal nutrition, it is incorporated into premixes and feed additives to support metabolic function in livestock and companion animals.

The material is supplied as a dark red to red crystalline powder for industrial use. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for global compliance.

Anhydrous and hydrated forms are both present in the market depending on the application. Bulk quantities are sourced for API manufacturing, while smaller pack sizes serve research and nutraceutical applications.

name: Methylcobalamin
description:
Methylcobalamin (CAS 13422-55-4 ), also known as MeB12, is the bioactive, coenzyme form of vitamin B12 used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in neurological and nutritional supplement formulations.

Unlike synthetic cyanocobalamin, it is the form directly utilized in human metabolism, making it the preferred choice for finished-dose manufacturers targeting premium positioning in the market.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this ingredient is formulated into oral tablets, sublingual preparations, and injectable solutions targeting peripheral neuropathy, cognitive support, and B12 deficiency indications.

Nutraceutical producers incorporate it into high-potency B-complex supplements and combination neurological formulas where bioavailability claims are a commercial differentiator for the final consumer product.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it is used in topical serums and scalp treatments where B12 activity is positioned around skin renewal and hair health for specialized beauty applications.

Contract manufacturers also source it as an intermediate for combination API blends in prescription neuropathy products. It is supplied as a dark red crystalline powder in light-protected packaging.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. , with food-grade and cosmetic-grade material also available depending on the specific application and regulatory requirements of the region.

Bulk quantities are offered in kilogram and multi-kilogram lots, with high-purity specifications commonly at 98% or above to ensure the highest quality for industrial chemical processing.

name: Potassium myristate
description:
Potassium myristate (CAS 13429-27-1 ), also known commercially as potassium tetradecanoate and marketed under the trade name Nonsoul MK 1, is a potassium soap derived from myristic acid.

It is used across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning applications. It functions primarily as a surfactant, delivering emulsification, foam generation, and degreasing performance in both formulated products.

In personal care manufacturing, it is used to build lather and emulsify oils in liquid soaps, shaving creams, and cleansing formulations where a dense, stable foam is required for the user.

Textile and leather processors use it as a scouring and degreasing agent to remove natural fats and process oils from fiber and hide surfaces prior to dyeing or finishing the materials.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface treatment and sizing processes where controlled foam and dispersing action are needed. Food-grade applications include its use as an emulsifier.

It also serves as a foam control agent in certain processed food systems. Potassium myristate is supplied as a paste or aqueous solution, with concentration and viscosity varying by grade.

Technical-grade material is standard for textile, leather, and industrial cleaning uses, while food-grade specifications are available for food and nutrition applications to meet safety needs.

Buyers should confirm active content and pH specification when sourcing for formulation-critical end uses. This ensures the chemical meets the necessary performance criteria for the final product.
