name: Cochineal
description:
Cochineal ( CAS 1343-78-8 ), also known as Natural Red 4, is a natural red colorant derived from the dried bodies of the Dactylopius coccus insect. With FEMA 2330 designation, it delivers stable, vivid crimson-to-purple hues across food, cosmetic, and textile applications.

This natural colorant is ideal for industries where synthetic dyes are undesirable or restricted. In food and beverage manufacturing, it produces consistent red and pink shades in products such as yogurts, confectionery, juices, and processed meats.

Cosmetic formulators use it to achieve rich red tones in lipsticks, blushes, and eyeshadows where natural-origin colorants are a requirement. The textile industry applies it in dyeing natural fibers, particularly wool and silk, where it produces deep reds.

These applications benefit from lightfast reds achieved through mordant fixation. Leather goods manufacturers also use it as a finishing colorant to achieve premium, natural-toned surface treatments across various high-end leather products.

The product is commercially available as a dried powder, aqueous extract, and concentrated liquid solution. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade, with supply conforming to FCC specifications for food applications.

It also meets relevant EU cosmetic regulations for personal care use. Carmine ( E120 ), the aluminum lake derivative processed from the raw extract, is a related but distinct commercial form commonly sourced alongside the primary material.

name: Magnesium silicate
description:
Magnesium silicate (CAS 1343-88-0 ), also known commercially as Ambosol and approved as E553a in food applications, is an inorganic salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an anticaking agent, adsorbent, and flow-control additive in both dry and semi-solid formulations. In food processing, it prevents clumping in powdered seasonings and salt blends.

This additive maintains free-flowing characteristics through packaging and storage. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet excipient and as an adsorbent to remove impurities and fatty acids during oil purification.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it improves powder texture and acts as a carrier for active ingredients in pressed powders, dry shampoos, and talc-alternative products for consumers.

It also functions as a thickener and suspending agent in topical creams and ointments where rheology control is required. The material is supplied as a fine white powder in varying particle size distributions.

Grades available include food-grade ( FCC compliant) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP /NF), with technical grades available for industrial purification applications. These meet strict global safety requirements.

Bulk supply is standard in bags or supersacks, with food and pharma grades requiring documented quality specifications. This ensures consistency and safety across all manufacturing and industrial supply chains.

name: Silicic acid
description:
Silicic acid (CAS 1343-98-2 ), also known as orthosilicic acid or monosilicic acid, is the soluble monomeric form of silicon that serves as the bioavailable silicon source in aqueous systems.

It functions as a stabilizer, rheology modifier, and foam control agent across water treatment, food, pharmaceutical, and personal care applications. In water treatment, it is dosed into distribution systems.

This process forms protective silicate films on pipe surfaces, reducing corrosion and scale deposition. Food and supplement manufacturers use it as a bioavailable silicon source in functional beverages.

These nutritional formulations target bone and connective tissue support. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a stabilizing agent in liquid formulations where controlled silica chemistry is required.

This prevents active ingredient degradation. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin-conditioning products and hair treatments where soluble silicon is preferred over particulate silica.

The material is supplied primarily as aqueous solution, with concentration and stabilization varying by application. Technical-grade and food-grade specifications are the most commonly sourced.

Food-grade material is subject to purity requirements aligned with FCC standards. Pharmaceutical-grade supply is available for regulated manufacturing with documentation supporting USP compliance.

Additional documentation is available for Ph. Eur. requirements. This ensures the highest quality standards are met for sensitive industrial and medical applications across global markets.

name: Aluminum zirconium trichlorohydrex gly
description:
Aluminum zirconium trichlorohydrex gly (CAS 134375-99-8 ), also marketed as aluminum zirconium octachlorohydrex gly, is an aluminum-zirconium complex used as the active antiperspirant ingredient in personal care formulations.

It functions by temporarily blocking eccrine sweat glands, reducing perspiration output at the skin surface. The primary application is in antiperspirant deodorant products such as sticks, roll-ons, aerosols, and creams.

In these applications, it delivers clinically recognized sweat reduction. Formulators select it over simpler aluminum salts when enhanced efficacy and longer-duration protection are required, particularly in clinical-strength or sport-positioned products.

It is also used in prescription-adjacent antiperspirant formulations where regulatory frameworks permit higher active concentrations. The glycine complexation improves skin compatibility, making it a preferred active in sensitive-skin lines.

This ingredient is a preferred choice where tolerability is a formulation requirement. Aluminum zirconium trichlorohydrex gly is supplied as a fine white powder or as aqueous solution concentrates, depending on the process.

Standard grades conform to USP monograph specifications, with active aluminum content and zirconium-to-aluminum ratios defined as key quality parameters. Buyers should confirm the buffered or unbuffered designation.

This designation affects pH behavior in finished formulations. Ensuring the correct grade is essential for maintaining stability and performance in high-end personal care and pharmaceutical-grade antiperspirant products.

name: Sodium aluminosilicate
description:
Sodium aluminosilicate ( CAS 1344-00-9 ), also known by its food additive designation E554 , is a synthetic inorganic salt derived from alumina and silica sources. It functions primarily as an anticaking agent in food and industrial applications.

This chemical prevents powder clumping and maintains free-flow characteristics in bulk materials. In food manufacturing, it is used in powdered products such as table salt, dried milk, and spice blends to maintain flowability through processing lines.

Water treatment operations use this compound as a coagulant and flocculant to remove suspended solids and improve clarification efficiency. In pulp and paper production, it contributes to retention and drainage control during sheet formation.

Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a stabilizer in dyeing and finishing baths. This helps to manage rheology and prevent precipitation during complex industrial manufacturing cycles.

The material is supplied as a fine white powder, with particle size specifications varying by application. Food-grade material is available to meet purity requirements under EU food additive regulations and international safety protocols.

Technical grades are also available for industrial uses in water treatment and paper manufacturing. These grades ensure consistent performance in heavy-duty applications where high-volume processing is required for operational success.

name: Sodium silicate
description:
Sodium silicate (CAS 1344-09-8 ), also known as water glass, is an inorganic alkali salt used across heavy industry as a binder, sealant, and reactive flocculant. It functions by forming a rigid silica gel network upon drying or acidification.

This mechanism enables bonding, surface hardening, and chemical stabilization across a broad range of substrates. In pulp and paper manufacturing, it stabilizes hydrogen peroxide during bleaching, preventing decomposition and improving whiteness yields.

Adhesive and board manufacturers use it as a structural binder in corrugated packaging. Its fast-set properties and compatibility with cellulose substrates reduce reliance on synthetic resins in high-volume production environments.

Water treatment facilities dose it as a corrosion inhibitor and coagulation aid. It conditions pipe surfaces and supports floc formation in clarification processes to ensure efficient removal of suspended solids from the water stream.

In construction, it penetrates concrete and masonry to densify surfaces. This improves abrasion resistance and reduces permeability without the need for topcoat systems, providing a durable and cost-effective solution for industrial flooring.

Sodium silicate is supplied as a liquid solution, most commonly in SiO2:Na2O ratios ranging from 2.0 to 3.5. Solids content typically falls between 30–50% depending on the specific viscosity requirements of the application.

Solid forms, including powder, granules, and anhydrous glass cullet, are available for applications requiring dry blending. These formats are ideal for extended shelf life and specialized manufacturing processes that avoid liquid handling.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for most chemical processes. Food-grade and water treatment-certified grades are also available for regulated end uses requiring specific purity and safety compliance.

name: Aluminium Oxide
description:
Aluminium Oxide (CAS 1344-28-1 ), commonly known as Alumina, is an inorganic mineral sourced in multiple industrial grades for use across refining, abrasive, and catalytic processes.

It functions as a catalyst support, abrasive medium, and surface treatment agent across a broad range of manufacturing and processing industries. In petroleum refining, Alumina serves as a catalyst carrier.

It is used for hydrodesulfurization and other fixed-bed reactions, where its high surface area and thermal stability determine catalyst performance. Abrasive operations rely on fused or calcined grades.

These grades help to grind, polish, and lap metals, ceramics, and composite materials to tight tolerances. In water treatment, activated Alumina removes fluoride and arsenic from drinking water.

This adsorption process helps facilities meet regulatory standards for municipal and industrial systems. Electronics manufacturers use high-purity Alumina as an insulating substrate and thermal barrier.

Consistent dielectric properties are critical to component qualification in aerospace. Aluminium Oxide is available as powder, granules, and shaped pellets, with particle size specified to requirements.

Established grades include activated, calcined, fused, and tabular forms, each targeting distinct end uses. Supply specifications include technical, refractory, and high-purity grades for industry.

Select products meet USP or Ph. Eur. standards for pharmaceutical and analytical applications. This ensures the material meets the rigorous quality benchmarks required for sensitive processes.

name: Lead sulfochromate yellow
description:
Lead sulfochromate yellow (CAS 1344-37-2 ), commercially known as Pigment Yellow 34, is a high-performance inorganic pigment delivering intense, opaque yellow coloration across demanding industrial applications.

Its exceptional heat stability and lightfastness make it a benchmark colorant where organic alternatives cannot meet performance thresholds. In plastics and polymers, it withstands high processing temperatures.

Engineering resins such as polyolefins and PVC utilize this pigment without color shift or degradation. Industrial coatings manufacturers use it to achieve durable, high-opacity finishes on heavy machinery.

It is also ideal for agricultural equipment and road-marking paints where long-term exterior exposure is a requirement. In printing inks for packaging, it provides consistent hue strength and resistance to bleed.

Rubber compounders and sealant formulators incorporate it where pigment stability under mechanical stress is a priority. It is also favored in environments where chemical exposure is a procurement concern.

Lead sulfochromate yellow is supplied as a dry powder, typically in fine-milled grades optimized for dispersion. It works effectively in solvent-borne, water-borne, and various resin systems.

The material is available in Technical-grade , with particle size distribution and oil absorption values specified to suit coatings. These specifications ensure compatibility with modern plastics processing.

Supply is subject to regulatory controls in multiple jurisdictions. Buyers should confirm all necessary compliance documentation and safety data sheets prior to final procurement for industrial use.

name: Copper chloride
description:
Copper chloride (CAS 1344-67-8 ) is an inorganic copper salt used across industrial sectors as a catalyst and biocidal agent. It functions as a reactive copper source in chemical synthesis and as a preservative in systems requiring controlled microbial suppression.

In water treatment, this compound is dosed to control algae and microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and municipal infrastructure. Mining and metallurgical operations use it as a leaching and etching agent for copper recovery.

Metal surface preparation and refining processes rely on its chemical reactivity for consistent results. Textile and leather processors apply it as a mordant to fix dyes onto fiber substrates, improving color fastness and uniformity.

Agricultural formulations incorporate it as a fungicide and micronutrient source in crop protection products and soil amendment programs. It provides essential trace elements while protecting plants from various fungal pathogens.

The material is supplied as a crystalline solid or anhydrous powder, with the dihydrate form being the most commonly traded commercial grade. Technical grade is standard across industrial applications for most manufacturing needs.

Purity specifications typically range from 97% to 99% depending on the specific requirements of the end user. Bulk quantities are available in fiber drums and big bags to accommodate large-scale industrial consumption.

Smaller packaged quantities are also offered for laboratory and specialty use where precision is required. Proper handling and storage protocols must be followed to maintain the integrity and safety of the chemical supply.

name: Calcium silicate
description:
Calcium silicate (CAS 1344-95-2 ), also designated E552 in food and pharmaceutical applications, is an inorganic mineral compound used primarily as an anticaking agent, flow aid, and functional filler across multiple industries.

Its ability to absorb moisture and oils without losing free-flowing properties makes it a preferred additive in both food processing and industrial manufacturing. In food and pharmaceutical manufacturing, it prevents caking in powdered products.

This ensures consistent dosing and packaging performance in items such as table salt, spice blends, and tablet formulations. Rubber and plastics processors use it as a reinforcing filler and processing aid for better results.

These applications improve dimensional stability and surface finish in molded components. In building and construction, it serves as a core material in fire-resistant boards, insulation panels, and ceiling tiles where thermal performance is required.

Structural integrity is a key benefit in these construction materials. Paper manufacturers incorporate it as a functional filler to improve opacity, printability, and sheet formation in various specialty paper grades.

Calcium silicate is available as a fine white powder in varying bulk densities to suit different processing and handling requirements. Supply grades include food-grade, USP , and Ph.Eur. for pharmaceutical use.

Technical grade options are also available for industrial applications. Specifications differ by surface area, oil absorption capacity, and moisture content depending on the intended end use and specific manufacturing needs.

name: Manganese chloride tetrahydrate
description:
Manganese chloride tetrahydrate (CAS 13446-34-9 ), also sold as manganous chloride tetrahydrate, is an inorganic manganese salt used across industrial, agricultural, and life science sectors. It functions primarily as a micronutrient supplement and process reagent.

In animal feed and agriculture, it supplies manganese as a trace mineral additive to support livestock nutrition. It is incorporated into premixes and compound feed at defined inclusion rates to ensure optimal animal health and growth.

Water treatment operations use it as a reagent in manganese greensand filtration systems. Here, it supports the oxidation and removal of dissolved iron and manganese from potable water supplies to meet safety standards.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as a manganese source in mineral supplement formulations. It also serves as a critical reagent in cell culture media and various biological research applications.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into select cosmetic preparations where controlled manganese ion delivery is required. This versatile chemical is essential for maintaining specific chemical balances in high-end formulations.

Manganese chloride tetrahydrate is supplied as a pink crystalline solid or granular powder. Standard commercial grades include technical, feed-grade, and reagent/ ACS grades for laboratory and industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP specifications to ensure the highest purity. Packaging typically ranges from laboratory quantities up to bulk bags for large-scale industrial supply.

name: Potassium molybdate
description:
Potassium molybdate (CAS 13446-49-6 ), also known as dipotassium molybdate, is an inorganic molybdenum salt used across industrial and agricultural sectors primarily as a corrosion inhibitor and micronutrient source.

Its solubility and molybdenum content make it a preferred form for applications requiring precise dosing in aqueous systems. In water treatment and industrial cooling systems, it functions as an anodic corrosion inhibitor.

It protects metal surfaces in recirculating water circuits where scale and oxidation control are critical. Agriculture and specialty fertilizer manufacturers use it as a molybdenum micronutrient source in foliar sprays.

Soil amendment formulations targeting molybdenum-deficient crops also utilize this salt. In mining and metals processing, it is used in flotation reagent systems and as a component in metal surface treatment chemistries.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it where corrosion protection of metal substrates during cleaning cycles is a requirement. Potassium molybdate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid.

Technical and reagent-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply, depending on the application volume.

name: Antimony trisulfide
description:
Antimony trisulfide (CAS 1345-04-6 ), also sold as antimonous sulfide or black antimony, is an inorganic sulfide compound used primarily as a flame retardant and pigment across industrial manufacturing.

Its role in combustion management and coloration makes it a recurring specification in rubber compounding, pyrotechnic formulations, and specialty coatings for various industrial sectors.

In rubber and tire manufacturing, this compound functions as both a flame retardant additive and a vulcanization modifier, improving heat resistance in finished compounds and materials.

Pyrotechnic and match manufacturing industries rely on it as a fuel component and friction-sensitive oxidizer contributor in strike surfaces and delay compositions for safety and performance.

As needle antimony, it appears in certain specialty pigment applications where its dark coloration is required in printing inks and industrial coatings for specific aesthetic and functional needs.

Mining and metallurgical processors also source it as a precursor material in antimony refining and recovery operations, ensuring a steady supply for downstream chemical production.

The material is supplied as a fine black powder, with particle size and purity specifications varying by end-use grade. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most uses.

High-purity grades are available for pyrotechnic and specialty chemical applications. Typical purity levels range from 95% to 99%+, with moisture content and heavy metal impurity limits specified.

name: Ferrous oxide
description:
Ferrous oxide (CAS 1345-25-1 ), also known as Iron oxide (FeO), is an inorganic iron compound used as a precursor and functional material in metallurgical and industrial chemical processes.

It serves as a reactive iron source in applications where a divalent iron species is required, distinguishing it from the more oxidized ferric forms found in other industrial oxides.

In metallurgy and mining, it functions as a flux and intermediate in iron and steel production, where controlled oxygen activity in smelting operations is critical for efficiency.

Pulp and paper manufacturers use it in chemical recovery processes, particularly within kraft pulping systems where iron chemistry affects liquor composition and equipment performance.

Water treatment operations employ it as a precursor in the synthesis of iron-based coagulants and reactive media for contaminant removal in large scale municipal systems.

It also serves as a pigment intermediate and raw material in the production of mixed iron oxide colorants for ceramics and specialty coatings used in the construction industry.

Ferrous oxide is supplied as a black powder, with particle size and purity varying by application grade. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form for most uses.

Purity levels are typically specified by iron content. Bulk quantities are available for industrial supply chains, with packaging options suited to moisture-sensitive handling requirements.

name: Atorvastatin
description:
Atorvastatin (CAS 134523-00-5 ), also known by the brand name Lipitor, is a synthetic HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in prescription cholesterol-lowering medications.

It is one of the most commercially significant statin APIs in global pharmaceutical manufacturing and procurement. Atorvastatin API is the core active ingredient in finished oral solid dosage forms.

Primarily film-coated tablets are manufactured for cardiovascular disease management using this material. Generic drug manufacturers source it to produce bioequivalent formulations requiring strict pharmacokinetic matching.

These formulations must match reference listed drugs. Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) use it in formulation development projects targeting lipid-lowering therapeutic categories.

It also appears in combination tablet formulations, paired with antihypertensives such as amlodipine. This requires compatibility evaluation during development to ensure stability and efficacy.

Atorvastatin is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in pharmaceutical-grade form. Standard specifications include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for global compliance.

Purity is typically at 98% or above as required for API use. Packaging is available in quantities ranging from research-scale to commercial bulk for various manufacturing needs.

Documentation including CoA, DMF references, and impurity profiles are available on request. This ensures full transparency and regulatory support for pharmaceutical procurement teams.

name: Atorvastatin calcium

Atorvastatin calcium (CAS 134523-03-8 ), also known by the trade names Tahor and CI-981, is a pharmaceutical active ingredient used in the manufacture of cholesterol-lowering medications.

It functions as an HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor and is the active salt form selected for its stability and bioavailability profile in solid dosage manufacturing for global pharmaceutical supply chains.

The primary application is in the production of oral solid dosage forms, such as tablets and film-coated tablets, for lipid management therapies where the calcium salt form supports consistent dissolution.

Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as the API for finished drug product registration across regulated markets including FDA, EMA, and WHO-prequalified supply chains for international distribution.

Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) use it in formulation development projects requiring ICH-compliant starting materials to ensure high-quality therapeutic outcomes for patients.

name: Barite
description:
Barite (CAS 13462-86-7 ), also known as heavy spar, is a naturally occurring barium sulfate mineral sourced and processed for industrial use across multiple sectors.

Its high specific gravity and chemical inertness make it a preferred functional filler and weighting agent where density and stability are critical procurement criteria for manufacturers.

In oil and gas drilling, it is the primary weighting material added to drilling fluids to control wellbore pressure and prevent blowouts. API -grade specification governs most of this demand.

Rubber and plastics compounders incorporate it as a dense inert filler to increase product weight and improve dimensional stability in automotive parts and sound-dampening panels.

Paints and coatings formulators use it as an extender pigment to improve opacity, reduce cost per unit volume, and enhance corrosion resistance in industrial primers.

Printing inks and paper coatings also rely on it to achieve the smooth, high-brightness surface finish required for quality print reproduction and high-end commercial applications.

The material is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder, with particle size distributions tailored to drilling, coating, or filler applications for various industrial processes.

Material meeting API 13A specifications is the dominant commercial standard for oilfield supply. Paint and plastics grades are available in various micronized forms for specific needs.

name: Zinc pyrithione
description:
Zinc pyrithione (CAS 13463-41-7 ), commonly abbreviated as ZPT, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent used across personal care, coatings, and industrial water treatment applications. Known also as zinc pyridinethione, it controls fungal and bacterial growth in formulated products and process systems.

In antidandruff shampoos and scalp treatments, ZPT is the active ingredient that controls Malassezia yeast, making it one of the most established actives in OTC haircare. Marine and architectural coatings rely on it as a biocidal additive.

This additive helps to prevent algae, mold, and mildew growth on exterior surfaces. Adhesives, sealants, and elastomers incorporate ZPT to extend product shelf life and resist microbial degradation in humid or outdoor environments.

Industrial water treatment systems use it to suppress microbial fouling in recirculating and process water circuits. Zinc pyrithione is supplied primarily as a white to off-white powder and as aqueous dispersions.

These dispersions are typically provided at 48% active content. Standard grades include technical and cosmetic-grade specifications, with cosmetic-grade material subject to purity requirements aligned with regional regulatory limits.

These limits apply specifically to leave-on and rinse-off formulations. Drum and IBC packaging are standard for bulk procurement, ensuring safe handling and efficient transport for large-scale industrial and manufacturing operations.

name: Ferrous sulfate monohydrate
description:
Ferrous sulfate monohydrate (CAS 13463-43-9 ) is an iron salt used across water treatment, agriculture, and metallurgical processing as a coagulant, pH modifier, and iron source.

Feromax and Fespan are recognized commercial forms of this compound found in feed and supplement supply chains. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it acts as a coagulant and flocculant.

The compound is utilized to remove phosphates and suspended solids and is used to reduce chromate in effluent streams. Agricultural applications include soil amendment to correct iron deficiency in crops.

It is also used for pH correction in alkaline soils, where it is incorporated into fertilizer blends or applied directly. In animal feed production, it supplies bioavailable iron to prevent anemia.

This essential mineral helps livestock and poultry meet nutritional fortification targets. Mining operations use it in hydrometallurgical processes, including the precipitation of metals from process liquors.

It is further utilized for pH control in acid mine drainage treatment. Ferrous sulfate monohydrate is supplied as a granular or powdered solid to meet various industrial requirements.

Standard grades include technical, feed-grade, and agricultural-grade. Feed and nutritional applications typically requiring compliance with USP or BP specifications for safety.

name: Titanium dioxide
description:
Titanium dioxide (CAS 13463-67-7 ), also known as titania and TiO2, is an inorganic white pigment used across coatings, plastics, cosmetics, and food manufacturing. As E171 in food applications, it delivers opacity and brightness that few alternatives can match at comparable cost and stability.

In architectural and industrial coatings, TiO2 is the primary opacity-building pigment, determining hiding power and tint strength in paints and primers. Plastics compounders incorporate it to achieve consistent whiteness and UV resistance in films, packaging, and molded components.

Personal care formulators rely on it in sunscreens, foundations, and pressed powders where physical UV blocking and skin-tone coverage are both required. In food manufacturing, E171 grade TiO2 is used to whiten confectionery coatings, chewing gum, and tablet coatings.

A clean, bright appearance is a product quality standard for many consumer goods. Titanium dioxide is supplied as a fine white powder in two principal crystal forms, rutile and anatase, each suited to different performance requirements across coatings, plastics, and cosmetics.

Standard grades include food-grade, cosmetic-grade, and technical-grade, with rutile dominating coatings and plastics applications. Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities, with surface-treated variants available for improved dispersibility in specific media.

The material is valued for its high refractive index and chemical inertness. These properties ensure that the pigment remains stable under various processing temperatures and environmental conditions, maintaining the aesthetic integrity of the final product over time.

name: Indium sulfate
description:
Indium sulfate (CAS 13464-82-9 ) is an inorganic indium salt used as a source compound in electronics manufacturing and catalytic processes. Diindium trisulfate is the stoichiometrically precise form most referenced in technical procurement contexts.

It provides a soluble, processable form of indium for applications where controlled deposition or chemical conversion of the metal is required. In electronics, it functions as a precursor for indium-containing thin films.

Transparent conductive oxide layers, including indium tin oxide (ITO) coatings used in displays and photovoltaic devices, rely on this compound. Electroplating and electrodeposition processes use it to deposit indium metal onto substrates.

These processes create corrosion-resistant or low-friction surface finishes for various industrial components. In catalysis research and specialty chemical synthesis, it acts as a Lewis acid catalyst for organic transformations.

Common applications include Friedel-Crafts-type reactions and ring-opening processes. Pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturers use it as a starting material for producing other indium compounds with defined purity profiles.

Indium sulfate is supplied as a crystalline powder or solid. It is available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications, with high-purity grades offered for electronics and catalyst applications.

Standard high-purity grades are typically 99%+ or 99.99% metals basis. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to kilogram-scale industrial lots depending on the specific requirements of the supplier.

name: 3-carene
description:
3-Carene (CAS 13466-78-9 ), also known as Delta-3-Carene, is a naturally occurring bicyclic monoterpene derived primarily from turpentine and conifer resins. It functions as both a specialty solvent and a fragrance ingredient.

This versatile chemical is used across personal care, food, and industrial applications. In printing and packaging, it serves as a bio-based solvent component in ink formulations, offering strong solvency for resins.

It provides a reduced reliance on petrochemical alternatives in various manufacturing processes. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into fragrance blends for its fresh, sweet, and piney character.

It contributes to perfumes, shampoos, and cosmetic products. As a FEMA 3821-listed ingredient, it is approved for use as a flavoring agent in food and beverage applications where pine profiles are required.

Its solvency profile also makes it relevant as a carrier in terpene-based cleaning and coating formulations. The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at purities ranging from 90% to 98% or higher.

Higher-purity grades are available for flavor and fragrance end uses. Food and fragrance applications generally require material meeting FCC or equivalent quality standards for safety and compliance.

Documentation is provided to support flavor-grade compliance for regulated industries. Technical-grade material is available for solvent and industrial applications where lower purity thresholds are acceptable.

name: Lamivudine

Lamivudine (CAS 134678-17-4 ), also known by the abbreviation 3TC and supplied under the trade name Heptovir, is a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient.

Lamivudine is primarily used in the manufacture of oral solid dosage forms, such as tablets and film-coated tablets, for HIV treatment regimens often combined with other antiretroviral APIs in products.

Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a key API for hepatitis B antiviral therapies, where regulatory-grade purity is a critical procurement requirement for international safety standards.

It is also used by formulators developing pediatric oral solutions, requiring specific solubility-compatible grades. Contract development and manufacturing organizations source it as a synthesis intermediate.

Lamivudine is available as a white crystalline powder in pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Recognized grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , aligning with the requirements of regulated markets.

These standards ensure compliance in North America, Europe, and beyond. Supply is typically offered in kilogram to metric-ton quantities, with documentation packages supporting GMP-compliant procurement.

name: Sodium dihydrogen phosphate dihydrate
description:
Sodium dihydrogen phosphate dihydrate (CAS 13472-35-0 ), also known as monosodium phosphate (MSP), is an inorganic phosphate salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial processing as a pH buffer and sequestrant.

Its reliable buffering capacity and chelating action make it a standard input wherever precise acidity control or metal ion management is required. In water treatment, MSP controls scale formation and corrosion.

It works by sequestering calcium and magnesium ions in boiler and cooling water systems. Food manufacturers use it as a buffering and stabilizing agent in processed cheeses, beverages, and meat products.

In these applications, consistent pH directly affects texture and shelf life. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into parenteral solutions, topical preparations, and oral dosage forms requiring buffer systems.

In industrial cleaning and surface treatment, it functions as a chelating agent to prevent metal ion interference during processing. Sodium dihydrogen phosphate dihydrate is available as a white crystalline powder.

Food-grade material is supplied to FCC specifications, while pharmaceutical-grade product meets USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards. Technical grade is also available for industrial applications.

name: Sodium pyrophosphate decahydrate
description:
Sodium pyrophosphate decahydrate (CAS 13472-36-1 ), commonly abbreviated as TSPP, is the fully hydrated crystalline form of tetrasodium pyrophosphate. It functions as a chelating agent, pH buffer, and dispersant across a broad range of industrial and food-grade applications.

Procurement teams sourcing TSPP in hydrated form should note that water content affects active concentration relative to the anhydrous grade. In food processing, TSPP acts as an emulsifying and sequestering salt in processed cheese, seafood, and cured meat products.

It is essential for controlling texture and preventing discoloration by binding metal ions. Water treatment operations use it to sequester calcium and magnesium hardness, preventing scale formation in boilers and distribution systems.

In textile and leather processing, it disperses dyes and assists in removing metal impurities during preparation stages. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a pH buffer and tartar-control agent in oral care products, particularly toothpaste.

Sodium pyrophosphate decahydrate is supplied as white crystalline granules or powder. It is available in food-grade specifications meeting FCC and technical-grade standards for industrial use.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities, with purity specifications commonly at 99% or higher on a dry basis. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing and chemical processing environments.

name: Sodium tungstate
description:
Sodium tungstate (CAS 13472-45-2 ), also sold as sodium wolframate, is an inorganic tungsten salt used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor and catalyst precursor. It delivers controlled tungsten chemistry in applications where a water-soluble tungsten source is required at scale.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a flame retardant and weighting agent, applied directly to fabric and hide treatments to meet fire resistance specifications. This ensures high performance in industrial safety applications.

Pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturers use it as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in oxidation reactions, particularly in peroxide-based synthesis routes. It provides a reliable chemical pathway for complex organic transformations.

In mining and metallurgy, it serves as a starting material for producing tungsten metal, tungsten carbide, and downstream alloy intermediates. These materials are essential for high-strength industrial tools and components.

Paper manufacturers apply it as a flame retardant additive and to improve the density and opacity of specialty paper grades. This chemical treatment enhances the physical properties and safety profile of the final paper product.

Sodium tungstate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as the dihydrate form, which is the most commercially prevalent grade. It is highly valued for its solubility and consistent performance in aqueous solutions.

Technical and reagent-grade specifications are standard across the market, with purity levels typically ranging from 99% upward for industrial and laboratory supply. These grades meet the rigorous demands of modern chemical manufacturing.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement, with smaller packaging offered for laboratory and pharmaceutical sourcing. This flexibility allows for seamless integration into both large-scale production and research environments.

name: Aluminum nitrate
description:
Aluminum nitrate (CAS 13473-90-0 ), also supplied as aluminium nitrate or aluminum trinitrate, is an inorganic aluminum salt used industrially as a coagulant, mordant, and chemical intermediate.

Its high solubility and aluminum ion availability make it effective for pH adjustment and flocculation across several process industries. In water treatment, it functions as a coagulant to destabilize suspended solids.

This supports clarification in municipal and industrial effluent systems by removing colloidal matter. Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant to fix dyes onto fiber substrates, improving color fastness.

It ensures uniformity in finished goods and is essential for high-quality textile production. In pulp and paper manufacturing, it supports retention aid programs and assists with pH regulation during wet-end chemistry.

Mining and metallurgical operations use it as a chemical intermediate in alumina processing. It also serves as a reagent in selective precipitation steps for various industrial extraction and purification processes.

Aluminum nitrate is commercially available as a crystalline solid, most commonly in the nonahydrate form. Standard supply grades include technical and industrial grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

Bulk quantities are available in bags or drums, with packaging options suited to both large-scale industrial users and laboratory or specialty buyers. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for all industrial applications.

name: Quaternium-80
description:
Quaternium-80 (CAS 134737-05-6 ), commercially available as Silquat Q 100 and Abil-Quat 3272, is a silicone-based quaternary ammonium compound used in personal care and industrial formulations.

It combines conditioning, emulsification, and surface-active properties into a single ingredient, reducing the need for multiple additives in complex formulations. In hair care, it deposits onto negatively charged hair fibers.

This action delivers detangling, softness, and frizz control in conditioners, shampoos, and leave-in treatments. Skin care formulators use it as an emulsifier and moisturizing agent in various creams and lotions.

It supports stable oil-in-water systems with a smooth skin feel. In textile processing, it functions as a softening and antistatic agent applied during finishing, improving fabric handle and reducing static buildup.

Leather treatment formulations also incorporate it to condition and uniformly coat surfaces during processing. The material is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically in neat form or as a diluted solution.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suitable for personal care applications, with technical-grade material offered for textile and leather end uses. Drum and IBC packaging are standard for industrial quantities.

name: Calcium nitrate tetrahydrate
description:
Calcium nitrate tetrahydrate (CAS 13477-34-4 ) is a water-soluble calcium and nitrogen source used across agriculture, construction, and water treatment industries. It delivers both calcium and nitrate simultaneously.

This makes it a preferred inorganic salt where dual nutrient or ionic activity is required in solution. In agriculture, it functions as a fully water-soluble fertilizer for fertigation systems and foliar sprays.

It supplies nitrate nitrogen and calcium to crops simultaneously. Concrete and construction admixture producers use it as an accelerating agent in cold-weather concreting to shorten set times.

The product supports early strength development in various building materials. In wastewater treatment, it acts as an electron acceptor to suppress hydrogen sulfide generation in anaerobic conditions.

This application is vital within sewer networks and treatment facilities. Pulp and paper operations apply it for pH regulation and as a process aid where controlled ionic activity is needed.

The chemical is supplied as white granules, prills, or flakes, with liquid solution grades also available. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and fertilizer grade for industrial use.

Purity levels typically range from 99% on a dry basis for high-quality applications. Bulk supply is common for agricultural buyers, with intermediate packaging available for specialty or laboratory use.

name: Nickel nitrate hexahydrate
description:
Nickel nitrate hexahydrate (CAS 13478-00-7 ) is a water-soluble nickel salt supplied as a crystalline solid, used industrially as a source of nickel ions in surface treatment and catalyst preparation.

Its high solubility and controlled nickel content make it a preferred precursor where precise nickel loading is required for electrochemical processes and industrial manufacturing applications.

In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as the primary nickel precursor for impregnating alumina or silica supports, producing hydrogenation and reforming catalysts used in petrochemical processing.

Electroplating and electroless nickel operations use it to formulate bath solutions that deposit uniform nickel coatings on metal and plastic substrates for various industrial components.

In electronics, it supports the production of nickel-containing electrode materials and conductive layers in printed circuit board fabrication and other high-tech hardware manufacturing.

Mining and hydrometallurgical operations use this chemical in solution chemistry for nickel recovery and refining steps, ensuring efficient processing of raw materials and metal ores.

The product is supplied as green crystalline granules or flakes, typically in technical and reagent grades. Standard concentrations are based on the hexahydrate form for consistency.

Purity specifications commonly range from technical grade to high-purity reagent grade suitable for laboratory synthesis. Bulk packaging in drums and IBCs is standard for industrial supply.

It delivers roasted, caramel-like, and nutty flavor notes that replicate or enhance the sensory profile of heat-processed foods. In baked goods and confectionery, it contributes roasted top notes.

These notes reinforce the flavor signature of cookies, pastries, and toffees. Beverage formulators incorporate it into coffee, cocoa, and malt-flavored drinks to add depth and authenticity.

It is particularly effective for thermally derived flavor profiles. Savory applications include snack seasonings and processed meat flavors, where it supports the Maillard-type character.

This compound is also used in dairy-flavored products such as butter and cream formulations to round out cooked or toasted nuances. It is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid.

The material typically features high purity levels suited for flavor use. Food-grade material meeting FEMA and FCC standards is the primary commercial form available from suppliers.

In personal care formulations such as shampoos, liquid soaps, and skin cleansers, it prevents metal ion interference that degrades fragrance stability and reduces preservative efficacy during storage.

Water treatment operations use it to control scale formation and metal deposition in cooling towers and process water circuits. It is highly effective at maintaining system efficiency over time.

In industrial and institutional cleaning concentrates, it boosts surfactant performance by softening hard water and keeping soils suspended in the wash liquor for more effective cleaning results.

name: Zinc chromate
description:
Zinc chromate (CAS 13530-65-9 ), also sold as Zinc Chrome Yellow and Buttercup Yellow, is an inorganic chromate pigment used primarily for its corrosion-inhibiting properties in protective coatings.

It functions as an active anti-corrosion pigment rather than a purely decorative one, releasing chromate ions that passivate metal substrates and suppress underfilm corrosion in various industrial applications.

In aerospace and defense, zinc chromate is specified in primer systems for aluminum and steel airframe components where long-term corrosion resistance under harsh environmental exposure is critical.

Automotive OEM and refinish coatings use it in primer formulations applied to steel bodywork and structural parts requiring durable barrier protection and high-performance chemical resistance.

Industrial maintenance coatings for bridges, pipelines, and heavy steel structures incorporate it to extend service life in aggressive outdoor or chemical environments where metal integrity is paramount.

Printing inks and specialty packaging coatings also use it as a yellow pigment where color stability and substrate adhesion are formulation priorities for high-quality industrial printing projects.

Zinc chromate is supplied as a dry powder in varying particle size distributions to suit different coating formulations. It is available in technical and industrial grades for diverse manufacturing needs.

Specifications are typically aligned to ASTM standards referenced in aerospace and defense procurement. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on specific volume requirements.

name: Sodium lauroyl lactylate
description:
Sodium lauroyl lactylate (CAS 13557-75-0 ) is an anionic surfactant and emulsifier derived from lauric acid and lactic acid. It functions as an emulsifier, conditioning agent, and rheology modifier across food manufacturing and personal care formulation.

In bakery and bread applications, it strengthens dough structure and improves crumb texture by interacting with gluten and starch networks. This interaction helps in extending shelf life in commercial production environments.

Personal care formulators use it to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions in lotions, creams, and hair conditioners. In these applications, it also delivers mild skin-conditioning properties to the final product.

In leave-on and rinse-off hair care products, it improves wet combability and the deposit of conditioning actives onto the hair shaft. This makes it a versatile ingredient for high-performance hair treatments.

Food manufacturers also incorporate it into dairy-based and plant-based products to improve fat dispersion and mouthfeel consistency. It ensures a smooth texture and uniform quality in various processed food items.

Sodium lauroyl lactylate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, supporting use as a direct food additive in regulated markets.

Cosmetic-grade material is produced to personal care industry standards and is suitable for use in certified natural and organic formulations. It remains a preferred choice for clean-label beauty products.

name: Lithium molybdate
description:
Lithium molybdate (CAS 13568-40-6 ) is an inorganic salt used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor, protecting metal surfaces in aqueous and high-temperature environments.

It functions by forming a passive protective layer on metal substrates, reducing oxidative degradation in process systems. In water treatment, it is dosed into closed-loop cooling and heating circuits.

This helps to inhibit corrosion of ferrous and non-ferrous metals, extending system service life and reducing maintenance costs. Metalworking and lubricant formulators incorporate it into cutting fluids.

It is used in metal-working concentrates where corrosion protection of tooling and workpiece surfaces is required. It is also evaluated as a component in high-performance grease and lubricant formulations.

Molybdate-based inhibition offers performance at elevated temperatures. Industrial coating and surface treatment processes use molybdate salts as non-chromate corrosion inhibitor alternatives.

This supports compliance with restrictions on hexavalent chromium compounds. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Technical and high-purity grades are available for industrial use.

These grades meet the requirements of industrial formulation and specialty chemical applications. Packaging is typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or drums for various needs.

Bulk quantities are available for large-scale industrial procurement. This ensures a steady supply for manufacturers requiring consistent chemical quality and performance in their processes.

name: N,N-Dimethyl-9-decenamide
description:
N,N-Dimethyl-9-decenamide (CAS 1356964-77-6 ) is a bio-based fatty acid amide used as a solvent, wetting agent, and degreasing component across agricultural, cleaning, and personal care formulations.

Its unsaturated C10 amide structure positions it as a functional alternative to conventional synthetic solvents in performance-driven applications. In agricultural formulations, it functions as a carrier and penetration enhancer.

This material improves the delivery of active ingredients through plant surfaces in spray concentrates and adjuvant blends. Home care and industrial cleaning products incorporate it for its degreasing and surface-wetting performance.

It is particularly effective in hard-surface cleaners and industrial degreasers where low residue and biodegradability are purchasing criteria. Personal care formulators use it as an emollient carrier and surface modifier.

In rinse-off and leave-on systems, it enhances skin feel and spreadability to affect product differentiation. Its bio-derived origin supports formulation strategies targeting renewable content claims across all three sectors.

N,N-Dimethyl-9-decenamide is supplied as a liquid. It is available in technical grade suitable for industrial and agricultural applications, with cosmetic-grade material accessible for personal care use.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers depending on order volume. This versatile chemical provides a sustainable solution for modern industrial and consumer product manufacturing requirements.

name: Dimethyldibenzylidene sorbitol
description:
Dimethyldibenzylidene sorbitol (CAS 135861-56-2 ), commercially recognized as Millad 3988, is a high-performance nucleating and clarifying agent used in polypropylene processing. It accelerates crystallization during molding and significantly improves optical clarity in finished plastic parts.

In polypropylene packaging and consumer goods, it enables processors to achieve glass-like transparency without switching to more expensive resins. Injection-molded food containers, caps, and closures benefit from faster cycle times.

Improved stiffness-to-weight ratios are achieved when this clarifier is incorporated at low loading levels. Thin-wall packaging films and sheets processed on high-speed lines use it to maintain consistent clarity across production runs.

In building and construction applications, it supports the production of transparent or translucent polypropylene components. This is essential where optical performance and structural integrity must both be met during the manufacturing process.

Dimethyldibenzylidene sorbitol is supplied as a fine white powder, suited for dry blending or masterbatch incorporation into polyolefin systems. It is available in food-contact compliant grades for various industries.

The material meets regulatory requirements for packaging applications in major markets. Technical-grade material is also available for non-food industrial applications where regulatory compliance is not a primary sourcing criterion.

name: Dodecylguanidine hydrochloride
description:
Dodecylguanidine hydrochloride (CAS 13590-97-1 ), sold commercially as Metasol DGH, is a cationic biocide with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against bacteria, fungi, and algae.

It is used across industrial and agricultural applications where microbial control in aqueous systems or on treated surfaces is required. In agriculture, it functions as an active ingredient in fungicidal formulations.

These formulations target post-harvest pathogens and soil-borne disease in crop protection programs. Water treatment operations use it to control algae and bacterial growth in cooling towers and industrial process water.

It is also effective in recirculating systems. In textile and leather processing, it is applied as a preservative treatment to inhibit microbial degradation during wet processing and storage.

Paper and pulp manufacturers incorporate it into slimicide programs to prevent biofilm formation. This prevents biofilms that cause sheet defects and equipment fouling in the manufacturing process.

Dodecylguanidine hydrochloride is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration levels varying by supplier and end-use specification. Technical grade is the standard commercial form.

Buyers should confirm active content and formulation compatibility when evaluating supply sources. Solution strength directly affects dosing calculations and handling requirements for industrial applications.

name: Zinc selenite
description:
Zinc selenite ( CAS 13597-46-1 ), also referenced by the formula ZnSeO3, is an inorganic salt supplying both zinc and selenium in a single compound. It functions as a dual-mineral source in nutritional and biological applications where controlled selenium delivery is required.

In animal feed and livestock nutrition, zinc selenite provides selenium supplementation to address deficiency-related conditions in poultry, swine, and ruminants. Precise dosing is critical for regulatory compliance in these sectors.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a selenium source in mineral supplement formulations, including tablets and premixes targeting trace element replenishment. It is a vital component for maintaining metabolic health in various populations.

In biotechnology and cell culture research, it supplies selenium to support antioxidant enzyme activity in defined growth media. This ensures the stability and health of cellular structures during complex laboratory processes.

Agricultural applications include soil amendment programs and foliar treatments designed to correct selenium-deficient soils in crop production. This helps improve the nutritional profile of the resulting harvest for consumers.

Zinc selenite is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Technical and feed-grade specifications are the most commercially available forms, with purity levels typically confirmed by assay against recognized standards.

Purity levels are often measured against recognized pharmacopoeial or feed additive standards such as USP , BP , or EP . These benchmarks ensure the material is safe for its intended industrial or nutritional use.

Buyers sourcing for pharmaceutical or nutraceutical use should confirm grade documentation, including certificate of analysis and trace metal impurity profiles, prior to procurement to ensure full compliance.

name: Phosphonic acid
description:
Phosphonic acid (CAS 13598-36-2 ) is an inorganic phosphorus-based acid used industrially as a pH regulator, reducing agent, and stabilizer across water treatment, agriculture, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its reducing character makes it effective in processes requiring controlled acidic conditions without introducing strong oxidizing byproducts. In water treatment, it functions as a pH adjustment agent and scale-inhibition precursor.

It supports corrosion control programs in industrial cooling and boiler systems. Textile and paper processors use it to manage bath acidity during dyeing and bleaching operations, where consistent pH control directly affects product quality.

In agriculture, it serves as a building block or acidulant in formulating phosphonate-based fungicides and fertilizer adjuvants. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reagent and intermediate in synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients.

These applications require controlled reducing conditions. Phosphonic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging around 50% by weight for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, though higher-purity specifications are available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements. Packaging options typically include drums and intermediate bulk containers.

name: Zinc dibutyldithiocarbamate
description:
Zinc dibutyldithiocarbamate (CAS 136-23-2 ), commonly known as ZDBC, is an organozinc compound used as a secondary accelerator in rubber vulcanization and as a stabilizer in polymer processing.

It delivers fast cure activation at moderate temperatures, making it a preferred choice for compounders seeking controlled processing windows. In rubber manufacturing, ZDBC functions as an ultra-accelerator.

This compound is essential for natural and synthetic rubber, particularly in latex goods, footwear, and industrial seals where consistent cure rates are critical for the final product quality.

Tire and technical rubber compounders use it in combination with primary accelerators such as sulfenamides to fine-tune scorch safety and crosslink density during the manufacturing process.

In plastics processing, it acts as a stabilizer and catalyst precursor in certain polymerization systems where zinc-based coordination chemistry is required for material integrity.

Personal care formulators have evaluated ZDBC as a preservation-active ingredient in specific rinse-off and leave-on systems, subject to regional regulatory compliance and safety standards.

Zinc dibutyldithiocarbamate is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder, with granule forms available for dust-reduced handling in industrial compounding environments.

Standard commercial grades are offered at high active content, typically 98% or above. Technical grade is the predominant market form, with documentation suited to industrial procurement requirements.

name: Cobalt octoate
description:
Cobalt octoate (CAS 136-52-7 ), also sold as cobalt 2-ethylhexanoate, is an oil-soluble cobalt salt used as a metal drier and curing catalyst across coatings, adhesives, and polymer manufacturing.

It accelerates oxidative crosslinking and cure reactions, making it a go-to catalyst where controlled drying speed and through-cure performance are critical sourcing criteria for industrial manufacturers.

In alkyd and oxidative-cure coatings, this material acts as a primary drier, accelerating surface dry times in architectural paints, industrial finishes, and high-performance printing inks.

Rubber and tire compounders use it to promote adhesion between steel cord and rubber compounds during vulcanization, directly affecting bond strength in finished tire construction and safety.

In unsaturated polyester resins and gel coats, it functions as a promoter alongside peroxide initiators to control cure onset and the overall processing window during the manufacturing stage.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it as a crosslinking catalyst in systems requiring fast ambient-temperature cure without the need for additional heat input or specialized equipment.

The product is supplied as a liquid solution, with cobalt metal content typically ranging from 6% to 12% in hydrocarbon or mineral spirit carriers to ensure easy integration into formulations.

Both technical and coatings-grade specifications are available to meet different purity and color requirements. Drum, IBC, and bulk liquid supply formats are standard across the global market.

name: Zinc 2-ethylhexanoate
description:
Zinc 2-ethylhexanoate (CAS 136-53-8 ) is an organozinc carboxylate salt used across coatings, rubber, and polymer industries as a catalyst and curing agent. Its oil-soluble character makes it compatible with organic systems.

In coatings and paint formulations, it functions as a drier and catalyst to accelerate oxidative crosslinking of alkyd resins. This improves through-cure and film hardness in various industrial finishes.

Rubber compounders use it as an activator and crosslinking agent in sulfur-cure and peroxide-cure systems. It is particularly effective where controlled vulcanization rates are required for manufacturing.

In adhesives and sealants, it promotes cure in moisture- or heat-activated systems. This supports bond development in structural and industrial assembly applications across multiple manufacturing sectors.

Polymer producers also employ it as a polymerization catalyst in the synthesis of certain polyesters and polyurethanes. Its chemical stability ensures consistent performance during high-temperature processing.

Zinc 2-ethylhexanoate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in mineral spirits or other hydrocarbon solvents. The zinc content is specified by weight percentage to meet precise formulation needs.

Standard concentrations vary by application, with coatings-grade material commonly characterized by defined metal content. Technical-grade product is the predominant commercial form for most industrial uses.

Specifications are strictly aligned to industrial end-use requirements to ensure compatibility. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance benchmarks for heavy-duty chemical applications.

This material improves skin feel and extends scent longevity in lotions, creams, and color cosmetics. Polymer and plastics processors use it as a carrier solvent for disperse dyes in textile finishing.

It also serves as a plasticizer auxiliary in PVC and synthetic resin systems. In printing and packaging inks, it supports resin dissolution and pigment dispersion, contributing to adhesion and film formation.

The compound functions as a catalyst solvent or reaction medium in specialty chemical synthesis where controlled ester solvency is required. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with cosmetic-grade material available for personal care and fragrance applications meeting relevant purity thresholds for industrial use.

name: Hexylresorcinol
description:
Hexylresorcinol (CAS 136-77-6 ) is a phenolic compound used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing as an antioxidant, preservative, and UV stabilizer. Its ability to inhibit enzymatic browning and microbial activity makes it a commercially significant ingredient.

In food processing, this compound is applied to crustaceans and seafood to prevent melanosis, extending shelf life and preserving commercial appearance. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin-brightening and anti-aging products.

The ingredient suppresses tyrosinase activity to reduce hyperpigmentation in various skincare applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an active ingredient in antiseptic throat lozenges and topical preparations targeting minor infections.

Polymer and plastics producers also use it as a UV stabilizer and antioxidant additive to protect against photo-degradation in finished materials. This versatility ensures its demand across diverse industrial sectors and manufacturing processes.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or solid. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with USP and BP grades commonly offered for regulated applications.

name: 2-Aminobenzothiazole
description:
2-Aminobenzothiazole (CAS 136-95-8 ), also known commercially as 2-Benzothiazolamine, is a heterocyclic aromatic compound used as a chemical intermediate and curing agent across rubber, textile, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its reactive amine group makes it a building block for accelerators, dyes, and pigment systems where precise cross-linking performance is required. In rubber and tire production, it functions as a precursor to sulfenamide-class accelerators.

These accelerators control vulcanization rate and improve finished product consistency. Textile and leather processors use it in the synthesis of azo dyes and optical brighteners, where it contributes to color fastness and substrate bonding.

Specialty pigment manufacturers incorporate it into heterocyclic chromophore systems for industrial coatings and printing inks. It also serves as an intermediate in agrochemical and pharmaceutical synthesis.

The benzothiazole scaffold is a recognized pharmacophore building block for active ingredient development. 2-Aminobenzothiazole is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for synthesis and research applications. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to multi-tonne bulk supply.

name: Sodium ferrocyanide
description:
Sodium ferrocyanide (CAS 13601-19-9 ), also known commercially as E535 and tetrasodium hexacyanoferrate, is an inorganic iron-cyanide salt used across food processing and industrial water treatment.

It functions primarily as an anti-caking agent, chelating agent, and corrosion inhibitor depending on the end-use sector. In food and salt processing, it is approved to prevent clumping in table salt.

This additive is used in mineral salts at regulated dosage levels to ensure flowability. Water treatment operations use it to sequester heavy metals and control corrosion in distribution systems and cooling circuits.

In mining and metallurgy, it supports metal separation and precipitation processes where controlled iron-cyanide chemistry is required. Textile and leather processing operations also employ it as a stabilizer.

It acts as a reducing agent in dyebath formulations and tanning auxiliaries. Sodium ferrocyanide is supplied as a yellow crystalline powder or granules, with decahydrate being the standard commercial form.

Food-grade material is available to E535 specifications and FCC standards. Technical-grade product serves industrial applications in water treatment and mining where high purity is still essential.

name: 2-isocyanatoethyl acrylate
description:
2-Isocyanatoethyl acrylate (CAS 13641-96-8 ) is a bifunctional reactive monomer combining an isocyanate group and an acrylate group within a single molecule. This dual reactivity allows formulators to introduce both UV-curable and urethane-crosslinking chemistry into the same polymer system.

In UV-curable coatings and inks, it functions as a crosslinking monomer that simultaneously builds urethane linkages. This improves adhesion, hardness, and chemical resistance in the cured film without requiring separate reactive components.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to modify acrylate backbones with isocyanate functionality. This enables moisture-cure or dual-cure mechanisms in structural and flexible bonding systems for industrial applications.

Polymer chemists incorporate it into acrylic resins to introduce pendant isocyanate groups for post-functionalization. This allows for reactive blending with various hydroxyl-bearing or amine-bearing substrates in complex formulations.

In printing and packaging applications, it supports the development of high-performance overprint varnishes. It is also used in laminating adhesives where both flexibility and high crosslink density are critical for performance.

Supplied as a liquid monomer, it is typically stabilized to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most industrial manufacturing processes.

Purity specifications are commonly at 97% or higher to ensure consistent performance in sensitive chemical reactions. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to drum-scale supply for large-scale industrial use.

name: Propylene glycol isostearate
description:
Propylene glycol isostearate (CAS 1366396-43-1 ) is an ester of propylene glycol and isostearic acid used as an emollient, emulsifier, and lubricant across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its branched fatty acid structure resists crystallization, making it effective in applications where low-temperature stability and skin-feel are purchasing priorities for manufacturers.

In cosmetics and personal care, it functions as an emollient and co-emulsifier in creams, lotions, and color cosmetics, contributing to smooth spreadability and skin conditioning without a heavy residue.

Coating and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a plasticizer and wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and film flexibility. It is highly valued for its consistent performance in diverse environments.

In lubricant and metalworking compounds, it acts as a boundary lubricant and corrosion-inhibiting carrier in cutting fluids and release agents. This ensures high efficiency in heavy industrial processes.

It also serves industrial sealant and elastomer formulations where a non-crystallizing, low-viscosity ester is required for processing compatibility. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Propylene glycol isostearate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of various end markets.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers to accommodate large-scale production needs. Our logistics team ensures timely delivery and adherence to all safety protocols.

name: Tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate
description:
Tris(2-chloroisopropyl) phosphate , identified by CAS 13674-84-5 and commonly known as TCPP, is a chlorinated organophosphate flame retardant used across rigid and flexible foam systems.

It functions as both a flame retardant and plasticizer, reducing ignition risk while maintaining processability in finished materials. This chemical is the dominant flame retardant in rigid polyurethane foam.

It is used extensively for building insulation panels, where it meets fire classification requirements without significantly disrupting foam cell structure. In flexible polyurethane foam, it reduces flammability.

For furniture and automotive seating, it preserves mechanical performance while enhancing safety. Textile backcoatings and technical fabrics incorporate this additive to achieve fire resistance standards.

These standards are required in transportation and contract furnishing markets. It is also used in unsaturated polyester resins, epoxy systems, and adhesives where halogen-based flame retardancy is specified.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk quantities, IBC containers, and drums. It is available in technical grade , which is the standard commercial specification for this product.

Purity levels and viscosity specifications vary by supplier, and buyers typically align procurement to regional fire safety standards. Common benchmarks include EN 13501 or FMVSS 302 for industrial use.

Electronics manufacturers apply it in encapsulants, coatings, and connector housings where UL flame ratings must be achieved within tight dimensional tolerances for safety.

Textile and technical fabric producers use it as a back-coating additive to impart flame retardancy to upholstery, curtains, and various types of protective workwear.

name: Calcium pantothenate
description:
Calcium pantothenate (CAS 137-08-6 ), also known commercially as Pantholin, is the calcium salt form of vitamin B5 and the standard delivery form used across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It provides a stable, bioavailable source of pantothenic acid for use in finished products where consistent potency and shelf life are critical sourcing requirements for industrial manufacturers.

In dietary supplements and multivitamin formulations, it supplies the B5 component in tablets, capsules, and powder blends where label-claim accuracy and regulatory compliance drive specification choices.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it to fortify functional foods, infant formula, and nutritional beverages to meet declared vitamin content requirements and ensure consumer health benefits.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into B-complex preparations and oral dosage forms where USP or BP grade compliance is required for safety and efficacy standards.

Personal care formulators use it in hair care products, particularly conditioners and scalp treatments, where it supports moisture retention and improves hair fiber manageability in cosmetic lines.

name: Sodium lauroyl sarcosinate
description:
Sodium lauroyl sarcosinate (CAS 137-16-6 ), also known commercially as Sarkosyl NL, is a mild amino acid-derived surfactant used across personal care and food-contact applications.

It functions as a foaming agent, emulsifier, and cleansing active, offering effective surface activity with a gentler profile than conventional sulfate surfactants in various formulations.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, facial cleansers, and toothpastes, delivering dense, stable foam while minimizing irritation to skin and mucous membranes.

Toothpaste manufacturers rely on it specifically for its compatibility with fluoride systems and its ability to reduce surface tension without disrupting active ingredient stability during the manufacturing process.

In shave gels and conditioning cleansers, it contributes to slip and emulsification, helping suspend oils and conditioning agents evenly throughout the formula for a superior consumer experience.

Food-contact and industrial cleaning applications also utilize it as a degreasing and wetting agent where low toxicity and biodegradability are procurement requirements for modern industrial standards.

Sodium lauroyl sarcosinate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow aqueous solution, typically at 30% active content, and as a dry powder or needle form for formulators requiring anhydrous processing.

Standard grades include cosmetic/personal care grade meeting industry purity benchmarks, with technical grade available for industrial cleaning uses to ensure cost-effective and high-performance results.
