name: Sodium methyl oleoyl taurate
description:
Sodium methyl oleoyl taurate (CAS 137-20-2 ), also known commercially as Hostapon T or Metaupon paste, is an anionic surfactant derived from oleic acid and taurine. It functions as a foaming agent, emulsifier, and detergent active across textile processing and personal care manufacturing.

In textile wet processing, it acts as a scouring and wetting agent, helping to remove oils, waxes, and sizing agents from fiber surfaces before dyeing or finishing. This ensures a high-quality finish for various fabric types.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into mild shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers where controlled foam and skin compatibility are formulation priorities. It is valued for its ability to provide a creamy lather without causing irritation.

In leather processing, it supports degreasing and fat-liquoring operations, ensuring uniform penetration of subsequent treatment chemicals. This leads to a more consistent texture and color in the final leather products.

Paper manufacturing uses it as a dispersing and wetting agent to improve fiber distribution and surface uniformity during sheet formation. This application is critical for maintaining the structural integrity of the paper.

Sodium methyl oleoyl taurate is commercially supplied as a paste, reflecting its typical physical form at ambient temperatures. It is available in technical grade, with active matter content commonly specified around 30–35%.

Buyers should confirm active content and sodium chloride levels when evaluating grades for sensitive formulations such as personal care products. Proper storage in a cool, dry environment is recommended to maintain the stability of the paste.

name: Tetramethylthiuram Disulfide
description:
Tetramethylthiuram Disulfide (CAS 137-26-8 ), commercially known as Thiram and abbreviated TMTD, is an organosulfur compound used as a rubber vulcanization accelerator, fungicide, and industrial biocide.

It functions across rubber processing, crop protection, and preservation applications where sulfur-donor chemistry is required. In rubber and tire manufacturing, TMTD acts as a primary or secondary vulcanization accelerator.

This chemical enables efficient crosslinking at lower temperatures and improves aging resistance in finished rubber goods. In agriculture, Thiram is an active ingredient in seed treatment and foliar fungicide formulations.

It protects crops against a broad spectrum of fungal pathogens including Botrytis and Fusarium species. Industrial formulators use it as a biocide in latex preservation and polymer stabilization for aqueous rubber dispersions.

The compound also functions as a catalyst precursor in certain specialty chemical syntheses where controlled sulfur donation is required. It is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as pre-dispersed granules.

Standard grades include technical-grade material meeting rubber industry specifications, as well as agricultural-grade material conforming to FAO/WHO pesticide standards. Purity typically ranges from 95% to 98%+.

The material is available in masterbatch forms suited for rubber compounding to ensure uniform distribution. This versatility makes it a critical component for manufacturers requiring high-performance sulfur-donor chemistry.

It protects against fungal and microbial degradation during storage and transit. In agricultural formulations, it serves as a fungicide active ingredient targeting crop pathogens, particularly in specialty products.

Paper manufacturers apply it in mill process water treatment and as a slimicide to control microbial growth. This prevents growth that would otherwise compromise pulp quality and equipment performance.

In rubber compounding, it functions as an ultra-accelerator in natural and synthetic rubber systems, particularly where fast cure rates are required. This includes applications in tire components, seals, and various molded goods requiring high durability.

name: 2-methyl-1-butanol
description:
2-Methyl-1-butanol (CAS 137-32-6 ), also known as primary active amyl alcohol, is a chiral aliphatic alcohol used across food, cosmetic, and polymer manufacturing. It functions primarily as a flavoring agent and solvent.

This chemical serves as a vital intermediate in the synthesis of esters and other derivatives. In food and beverage production, it is approved under FEMA 3998 as a flavoring ingredient for various applications.

It contributes significantly to fruit and fermented flavor profiles in finished products. Cosmetic formulators use it as a solvent and co-solvent in fragrance compounds and hair care formulations where performance is required.

The product is also utilized in topical preparations where controlled evaporation and carrier performance are essential. In polymer and plastics processing, it serves as a reactive intermediate for manufacturing.

It is used in the production of plasticizers, resins, and cross-linking agents. It also functions as a precursor to amyl esters, such as amyl acetate, used in both flavor and industrial coating applications.

The material is supplied as a clear liquid in drums and IBC containers. Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is available for flavor industry applications to ensure high quality and safety.

Technical-grade is supplied for industrial and polymer end uses where specific regulatory standards are not required. Purity levels typically range from 98% upward depending on the intended application.

Our supply chain ensures consistent availability for global manufacturers. We provide comprehensive documentation including safety data sheets and certificates of analysis for every batch delivered to our clients.

name: Sodium propionate
description:
Sodium propionate (CAS 137-40-6 ), also recognized by its food additive designation E281 , is the sodium salt of propionic acid used commercially as a preservative and pH buffering agent. It inhibits mold and bacterial growth across food, feed, pharmaceutical, and personal care applications.

Supplied in anhydrous form, it offers reliable shelf-life extension in moisture-sensitive formulations. In baked goods, E281 is applied to bread, cakes, and pastries to suppress mold development and extend retail shelf life without affecting flavor profiles.

Animal feed manufacturers incorporate it as an antifungal agent in compound feeds and grain storage to prevent spoilage during transport and storage. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent and preservative in topical preparations and oral dosage forms.

It is also utilized in ophthalmic solutions and personal care products. In personal care, it functions as a preservative booster in creams, lotions, and rinse-off products where low-pH stability is required for the final formulation.

Sodium propionate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granulated forms preferred where dust control matters in feed and industrial handling. This ensures a safer and cleaner working environment during the manufacturing process.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), feed-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) to meet regulatory requirements across industries. These quality standards ensure the product is suitable for its intended high-purity application.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on application volume. This flexibility allows for efficient logistics and storage management for both small-scale producers and large industrial manufacturers.

name: Lidocaine
description:
Lidocaine (CAS 137-58-6 ), also known by the trade name Xylocaine®, is a synthetic amino amide compound used as a local anesthetic and topical analgesic across pharmaceutical and personal care applications.

It functions by blocking nerve signal transmission, making it the active ingredient of choice in a broad range of prescription and OTC formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is formulated into injectable solutions.

These solutions are used for regional and local anesthesia in surgical, dental, and emergency care settings. Topical dosage forms including creams, gels, patches, and sprays rely on it as the active ingredient.

These products deliver surface-level pain and itch relief in both prescription and consumer OTC products. Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it into numbing creams used ahead of aesthetic procedures.

Common uses include tattooing, laser treatments, and minor dermal interventions. It also appears as an active in combination formulations targeting premature ejaculation, hemorrhoid relief, and wound care.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both free base and hydrochloride salt forms. The hydrochloride is the preferred grade for aqueous injectable and topical formulations due to its water solubility.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. , with API-grade material supported by full regulatory documentation. This ensures compliance for pharmaceutical procurement and large-scale manufacturing.

name: Ascorbyl palmitate
description:
Ascorbyl palmitate (CAS 137-66-6 ), also known by its EU food additive designation E304i , is a fat-soluble ester of vitamin C used commercially as an antioxidant and stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Unlike water-soluble ascorbic acid, its lipophilic character makes it effective at protecting oils, fats, and lipid-based systems from oxidative degradation. In food production, it is added to oils, fats, and fat-containing products.

Common applications include margarines, baked goods, and infant formula to extend shelf life by retarding rancidity. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into lipid-based drug delivery systems and soft gel formulations where oxidation-sensitive active ingredients require protection.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, including creams, serums, and sunscreens, it functions as both an antioxidant preservative and a skin-conditioning agent within emulsion systems. It also serves as a co-emulsifier in lipid dispersions.

This functionality improves the stability of oil-in-water systems in both food and topical applications. The material is supplied as a white to yellowish powder or crystalline solid for industrial use.

Standard grades include food-grade meeting FCC specifications, as well as USP and Ph.Eur. grades for pharmaceutical applications. These standards ensure the highest level of purity and safety for global distribution.

Cosmetic-grade material is also commercially available, with purity typically at or above 98%. This high concentration ensures effective performance in complex chemical formulations and sensitive manufacturing processes.

name: Sodium metavanadate
description:
Sodium metavanadate (CAS 13718-26-8 ), also referenced commercially as sodium trioxovanadate and NaVO3, is an inorganic vanadium salt used across industrial chemistry as a catalyst precursor and biocidal agent.

Its solubility in aqueous systems makes it a practical source of vanadate ions for processes where controlled vanadium delivery is required. In water treatment, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and biocide.

The compound protects industrial cooling systems and pipelines from microbial fouling and metal degradation. Mining and hydrometallurgical operations use it as a catalyst precursor in oxidation processes.

This includes the recovery and refining of non-ferrous metals. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology research relies on vanadate solutions prepared from this salt to inhibit phosphatase enzymes in cell biology assays.

It also serves catalyst manufacturing as a vanadium source in the preparation of mixed-oxide catalysts for sulfuric acid production and other oxidation reactions. This makes it vital for chemical synthesis.

Sodium metavanadate is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline powder or granular solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with higher-purity grades available for research.

Analytical applications may require specific quality standards such as ACS or USP depending on the final use. Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply.

name: Barium selenite
description:
Barium selenite (CAS 13718-59-7 ), with the formula BaSeO3, is an inorganic barium salt of selenious acid used in specialty electronics and materials manufacturing. It serves as a controlled source of both barium and selenium in high-purity synthesis and ceramic processing applications.

In electronics, this compound functions as a precursor in the production of selenium-containing compounds and doped ceramic materials where precise elemental ratios are required. It is used in the manufacture of specialty glass formulations, including optical and radiation-shielding glass.

Selenium contributes specific optical properties that influence light transmission characteristics in these glass types. Research and industrial synthesis operations use it as a starting material for preparing other barium or selenium compounds under controlled conditions.

Ceramic and phosphor material producers may incorporate it into formulations requiring a stable, low-solubility selenium source. This material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial applications.

It is available primarily in technical and research grades, with purity levels typically specified by suppliers for laboratory and industrial use. Packaging is generally offered in small to medium quantities given the specialized nature of demand.

The product meets rigorous internal specifications for consistency and performance in high-tech manufacturing environments. Suppliers ensure that the chemical properties align with the requirements of advanced material science and electronic component production.

name: Hydroxyethylnitrosourea
description:
Hydroxyethylnitrosourea (CAS 13743-07-2 ), also referenced as N-(2-hydroxyethyl)-N-nitrosourea, is a nitrosourea compound used primarily in pharmaceutical research and oncology drug development.

It functions as a DNA-alkylating reference agent and research intermediate in studies targeting cell proliferation and mutagenesis mechanisms. In pharmaceutical R&D, it serves as a reference standard.

It is used as a synthetic intermediate in the development of alkylating chemotherapeutic agents, particularly within nitrosourea-class drug programs. Biotechnology laboratories use it in controlled mutagenesis studies.

These studies investigate DNA damage response pathways and evaluate repair mechanisms in cell-based assay systems. It is also employed in preclinical screening protocols where nitrosourea-type compounds are benchmarked.

Contract research organizations sourcing nitrosourea intermediates for structure-activity relationship studies may evaluate this compound as a building block for analog synthesis in various programs.

Hydroxyethylnitrosourea is supplied as a solid, typically in small research-scale quantities reflecting its primary use in laboratory and preclinical settings. Material is available to research-grade specification.

Purity is confirmed by HPLC or NMR as standard for pharmaceutical intermediates. Buyers should confirm cold-chain and stability requirements with suppliers prior to procurement for safety.

Nitrosourea compounds require controlled storage conditions to maintain integrity. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance benchmarks required for sensitive pharmaceutical research applications.

name: Potassium ferricyanide
description:
Potassium ferricyanide (CAS 13746-66-2 ), also known commercially as red prussiate, is an oxidizing salt used across industrial processes requiring controlled redox reactions. Its selectivity as an oxidant makes it a reliable reagent in both manufacturing and laboratory-scale operations.

In metal finishing and etching, it acts as a controlled oxidizing agent for blueprint development and photographic toning. These applications require precise image contrast and surface definition to ensure high-quality results in technical imaging.

Textile and leather processors use it in discharge printing and bleaching operations to selectively remove color from dyed substrates. This process allows for intricate patterns without degrading the structural integrity of the base material.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, it functions as a leaching or selective precipitation agent during precious metal recovery. This chemical property is essential for separating valuable minerals from complex ore matrices in industrial settings.

Pharmaceutical and analytical laboratories rely on it as a reagent for colorimetric assays and as an oxidant in the synthesis of active intermediates. It is a staple in research environments where consistent chemical behavior is mandatory.

Potassium ferricyanide is supplied as a crystalline powder or granules, typically in a bright red-orange form that aids visual quality verification. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for large-scale industrial use.

High-purity reagent and ACS grades are available for laboratory and pharmaceutical procurement channels. These grades ensure compliance with strict analytical standards required for sensitive chemical testing and synthesis.

Bulk supply is common in 25 kg bags or fiber drums, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and specialty buyers. Proper storage in a cool, dry environment is recommended to maintain the stability of the crystalline structure.

description:
4-Morpholinecarbodithioic acid 4-morpholinyl ester (CAS 13752-51-7 ), also known as morpholin-4-yl morpholine-4-carbodithioate, is a sulfur-based compound used in rubber and polymer processing.

It functions as a curing and crosslinking agent by initiating and regulating vulcanization reactions. This contributes to controlled network formation in various elastomeric systems and industrial applications.

In rubber compounding, it acts as an accelerator or co-accelerator during vulcanization. This helps to establish crosslink density and improve the mechanical performance of finished rubber goods.

Tire manufacturers and industrial rubber product producers use it to fine-tune cure rates. This ensures consistent processing behavior across different compound batches during the manufacturing cycle.

In polymer systems, it supports controlled radical or ionic polymerization initiation. This makes it relevant for specialty resin and adhesive formulations requiring specific chemical properties.

It is also evaluated in heterocyclic compound research and development programs. These programs target new curing system designs to enhance the durability and stability of modern polymer materials.

This compound is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline form suited for direct weighing. It is available primarily in technical grade with purity specifications varying by supplier.

Packaging options generally range from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply depending on scale. Proper storage is required to maintain the chemical integrity of the product over time.

name: Potassium metavanadate
description:

Specialty glass and ceramic manufacturers use it to introduce vanadium as a colorant and modifier in formulations requiring controlled optical or thermal properties. It also serves as a corrosion inhibitor component.

These shells are essential for stampers for optical discs and precision aerospace components. Decorative and functional nickel plating operations use it to achieve smooth, ductile coatings on automotive parts.

It is also widely utilized for electronics connectors and industrial hardware. In the mining sector, it is used in hydrometallurgical refining processes where controlled nickel deposition is required for efficiency.

Metalworking fluids and specialty lubricant formulations incorporate the chemical as a corrosion inhibitor. This helps to protect ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces during various industrial processing stages.

Nickel sulfamate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 300 to 600 g/L, and as a crystalline solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for plating and industrial applications.

name: Ammonia borane
description:
Ammonia borane (CAS 13774-81-7 ), also known as borazane, is a solid hydrogen storage compound that releases hydrogen gas at relatively low temperatures through controlled decomposition.

It functions as a chemical hydrogen carrier and reducing agent in research, specialty synthesis, and emerging energy applications. In hydrogen storage and fuel cell development, it serves as a solid-state hydrogen source.

This material enables compact, high-capacity storage systems for aerospace and defense platforms where weight and volume constraints are critical. Pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturers use it as a selective reducing agent.

It is utilized in the synthesis of complex intermediates, particularly where milder conditions are required than conventional borohydride reagents offer. In electronics, it supports the deposition of boron-containing thin films.

The compound acts as a precursor in chemical vapor deposition processes for semiconductor fabrication. Industrial cleaning formulations targeting specialized surface treatment applications also draw on its reducing chemistry.

Ammonia borane is supplied as a white crystalline powder, typically in research and specialty quantities reflecting its current stage of commercial development. It is available in technical and high-purity grades.

name: Trisodium hexafluoroaluminate
description:
Trisodium hexafluoroaluminate (CAS 13775-53-6 ), commercially known as cryolite, is a fluoride-based inorganic salt sourced both from natural mineral deposits and synthesized as a synthetic equivalent.

In the aluminum smelting industry, it functions as the primary flux and electrolyte medium that enables the dissolution and electrochemical reduction of alumina into metallic aluminum.

In aluminum production, cryolite forms the molten bath in Hall-Héroult electrolytic cells, directly determining process efficiency and metal purity. This makes it a critical procurement input for primary aluminum smelters.

In agriculture, it is applied as a contact insecticide under the trade name Cryocide, targeting chewing insects such as grape phylloxera and citrus pests on crops where residue tolerances permit its use.

Glass and enamel manufacturers incorporate it as a fluxing agent and opacifier to lower melting temperatures and improve surface finish in specialty coatings. It also serves as a catalyst component in certain systems.

Synthetic cryolite is the dominant commercial form, available as a fine white powder or granules. It is supplied in technical and agricultural grades, with the agricultural specification subject to regional registration.

Bulk supply is standard for metallurgical buyers, while smaller packaged quantities are available for agricultural and industrial use. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols for fluoride compounds.

name: Calcium bisulfite
description:
Calcium bisulfite (CAS 13780-03-5 ), also known by its food additive designation E227 , is an inorganic sulfite salt supplied primarily as an aqueous solution. It functions as a preservative, antioxidant, and bleaching agent across food processing, pulp manufacturing, and water treatment operations.

In food and beverage production, this additive controls microbial growth and oxidative browning in products such as wines, fruit juices, and dried fruits where sulfite preservation is required. It is essential for maintaining the shelf life and color stability of sensitive food products.

Pulp and paper manufacturers use this chemical as the active cooking liquor component in the sulfite pulping process. In this application, it breaks down lignin to liberate cellulose fibers for paper production, ensuring high-quality output for industrial use.

In water treatment, it serves as a dechlorination agent, neutralizing residual chlorine in municipal and industrial effluent streams before discharge. This process is vital for environmental safety and meeting regulatory standards for wastewater management.

It also acts as a bleaching agent in the treatment of wood pulp, improving brightness without the harsher conditions required by chlorine-based alternatives. This makes it a preferred choice for manufacturers seeking efficient and controlled bleaching processes.

The product is commercially supplied as an aqueous solution, typically in concentrations ranging from 6% to 15% active SO₂ equivalent. Food-grade material is available to the required specification for use within permitted additive limits for global distribution.

Technical-grade solution is standard for pulp, paper, and water treatment applications where high purity is necessary for industrial performance. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for all large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: Calcium nitrite
description:
Calcium nitrite ( CAS 13780-06-8 ) is an inorganic calcium salt used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor and accelerating admixture in construction and infrastructure applications. It is occasionally referenced under the Caswell No. 147 designation in regulatory contexts.

Its primary commercial value lies in protecting embedded steel reinforcement from chloride-induced corrosion while simultaneously accelerating early concrete strength development. In reinforced concrete structures, it is dosed as an admixture to extend service life.

Bridges, parking decks, marine infrastructure, and below-grade foundations utilize this chemical in chloride-rich environments. Precast concrete producers use it to shorten demolding cycles by accelerating cement hydration at lower temperatures.

In oil and gas well cementing, it functions as a set accelerator under cold downhole conditions. The mining sector uses the compound in grouting operations and in corrosion protection treatments for steel ground support elements.

Calcium nitrite is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with 30% and 35% concentrations being the most commercially standard for concrete admixture use. Solid forms, including powder and granules, are available for specific applications.

These solid formats are preferred where liquid handling or freight costs are a constraint. Technical grade is the predominant specification across construction and mining end uses, ensuring reliable performance in heavy industrial settings.

name: Calcium sodium phosphate
description:
Calcium sodium phosphate (CAS 13780-17-1 ), also known commercially as Rhenanite, is an inorganic phosphate salt used as a pH buffer and mineral source across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications.

It provides controlled phosphate delivery in systems where both calcium and sodium cation balance is relevant to formulation performance. In food manufacturing, it functions as a buffering and leavening agent.

This compound is utilized in baked goods, processed cheeses, and dry-mix products where pH stability directly affects texture and shelf life. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a mineral excipient and pH-adjusting agent.

It is commonly found in tablet and powder formulations requiring controlled calcium and phosphate content. In animal feed, it serves as a bioavailable phosphorus and calcium supplement for livestock and poultry.

The material supports bone development and metabolic function in various diets. It is also evaluated in fertilizer blends where slow-release phosphate delivery to soil is a primary formulation objective.

Calcium sodium phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules depending on the intended application. Food-grade and feed-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent.

Technical-grade material is also available for agricultural and industrial use. Buyers should confirm particle size distribution and purity grade when sourcing, as these parameters vary between suppliers.

These specific factors directly affect dissolution behavior in end formulations. Ensuring the material meets necessary quality standards is essential for maintaining consistency in large-scale chemical production.

name: Valsartan
description:
Valsartan (CAS 137862-53-4 ), also known as VAL489, is an angiotensin II receptor antagonist used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in the treatment of hypertension and heart failure. It functions by selectively blocking the AT1 receptor subtype.

This makes it a core API in cardiovascular drug formulations worldwide. Valsartan is the primary active ingredient in oral solid dosage forms, such as tablets and capsules, manufactured for antihypertensive therapy.

It is often utilized in combination products alongside hydrochlorothiazide or amlodipine. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a key API for generic drug production, where it undergoes formulation development and bioequivalence testing.

The material is also essential for regulatory filing and clinical trials. Contract research organizations and formulation labs procure it for analytical reference standards and method development work to ensure product quality.

In some specialty contexts, it is evaluated within peptide-adjacent research programs targeting cardiovascular peptide pathways. Valsartan is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications conforming to USP , Ph.Eur. ( EP ), and BP monographs, supporting GMP-compliant manufacturing processes across various global regions.

name: Butyl lactate
description:
Butyl lactate (CAS 138-22-7 ), also known by its FEMA 2205 designation, is a slow-evaporating ester solvent derived from lactic acid used across industrial, cosmetic, and food applications.

It combines strong solvency with low toxicity, making it a preferred alternative to conventional petrochemical solvents in formulations requiring a more favorable regulatory and environmental profile.

In coatings, inks, and polymer processing, it dissolves resins, nitrocellulose, and cellulose acetate butyrate where controlled evaporation rate and film quality are critical for the final product.

Personal care formulators use it as a carrier solvent in nail care products, fragrances, and skin formulations where compatibility with active ingredients and low irritation potential drive solvent selection.

As a flavoring agent, it contributes buttery, creamy top notes to food and beverage products including dairy analogs, baked goods, and confectionery. It also functions as a plasticizer and coalescing agent.

Butyl lactate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for solvents.

Food and flavor grades meeting specific purity specifications are available for sensitive applications. Kosher and natural-origin certified material is available from select producers to support clean-label positioning.

name: Limonene

In industrial cleaning and printing, this compound cuts through inks, adhesives, and greases on press equipment and packaging lines, replacing harsher hydrocarbon solvents.

Food manufacturers use it as a flavoring agent to deliver citrus character in beverages, confectionery, and baked goods. Personal care formulators incorporate it into fragrance blends.

name: Calcium magnesium silicate
description:
Calcium magnesium silicate ( CAS 13813-64-4 ) is an inorganic mineral salt used across industrial sectors as a rheology modifier and functional filler. It influences flow behavior, texture, and structural consistency in formulated products.

In agriculture and animal feed, it functions as a flow agent and anti-caking additive in powdered fertilizers and feed blends. This prevents clumping during storage and handling, ensuring consistent distribution of nutrients.

Construction applications include use as a filler and rheology modifier in cementitious systems, mortars, and grouts. In these environments, it helps control workability and reduce shrinkage during the curing process.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it acts as a mineral filler that modifies melt viscosity and improves dimensional stability. This makes it a valuable component for manufacturers producing high-precision finished parts.

Specialty coating and sealant formulations also incorporate this mineral to adjust application consistency and reduce settling. It ensures that pigments and other solids remain suspended throughout the product shelf life.

The material is supplied as a fine white powder, with particle size distributions tailored to specific processing requirements. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial applications.

name: Lead fluoroborate
description:
Lead fluoroborate (CAS 13814-96-5 ), also known as lead tetrafluoroborate, is an inorganic lead salt supplied primarily as an aqueous solution for electroplating and metal finishing operations.

It delivers high-solubility lead ion concentrations that support stable, high-speed deposition baths where conventional lead salts would be impractical for industrial use.

In electroplating, it is the primary lead source in fluoborate bath formulations used to deposit lead and lead-tin alloy coatings onto copper, steel, and electronic substrates.

Printed circuit board manufacturers rely on these baths to plate solder-compatible lead-tin finishes on through-holes and surface features during the manufacturing process.

In the electronics sector, it supports the production of bearing overlays and connector coatings where controlled deposit hardness and thickness are critical to performance.

Mining and metallurgical operations use lead fluoborate baths in electrorefining processes to recover and purify lead from various types of mixed-metal feedstocks.

Lead fluoroborate is commercially available as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 50% by weight. It is supplied in technical grade for industrial plating.

Bulk quantities are available in drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to continuous plating line operations and large-scale metal refining facilities worldwide.

name: Tin(II) tetrafluoroborate

Consistent layer thickness and solderability are critical for lead frames and semiconductor packaging. The compound supports tin-lead and pure tin plating in high-speed reel-to-reel operations for the electronics industry.

In the printing industry, it serves in the production of tinned metal substrates used for packaging applications. These applications require corrosion-resistant surfaces to ensure the longevity and safety of the final products.

Mining and metals processors use it in surface finishing lines where fluoroborate-based electrolytes offer improved bath stability. These systems provide higher current density tolerance compared to traditional sulfate systems.

The product is commercially available as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations suited for direct use in plating bath formulation. It is supplied in technical grade, with specifications aligned to industry standards.

name: Potassium tripolyphosphate
description:
Potassium tripolyphosphate (CAS 13845-36-8 ), also known as KTPP or E451ii , is an inorganic polyphosphate salt used across food processing, water treatment, and industrial applications.

It functions primarily as a sequestrant, buffering agent, and dispersant. It binds metal ions and stabilizes formulations where sodium-based alternatives are unsuitable or restricted in specific chemical processes.

In food processing, KTPP is approved for use in meat and seafood products. It improves water retention and texture in processed and cured preparations, ensuring high-quality results for commercial food manufacturers.

Water treatment operations rely on it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions. This prevents scale formation in boilers, cooling towers, and distribution pipelines, maintaining the efficiency of industrial water systems.

In textile and paper manufacturing, it disperses pigments and controls hardness ions during dyeing and pulp processing. This improves process consistency and ensures uniform color application in large-scale production.

Leather processing operations use it as a buffering and softening agent during hide preparation stages. It helps manage the chemical environment to ensure the durability and quality of the final leather goods.

Potassium tripolyphosphate is supplied as a white powder or granule. Food-grade material is available to the required specification, suitable for use in regulated food and beverage applications globally.

Technical grade is also available for industrial water treatment and manufacturing end uses. This grade provides a cost-effective solution for non-food applications requiring high-performance sequestration and buffering.

name: Caprylisononyldimethylammonium chloride
description:
Caprylisononyldimethylammonium chloride (CAS 138698-36-9 ), commercially known as Bardac 2170 and Bardac 21, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as an active biocidal ingredient.

Its cationic charge enables strong adsorption onto negatively charged surfaces, supporting both antimicrobial performance and soil removal in formulated products across industrial and institutional cleaning markets.

In home care and institutional cleaning, it functions as the active quat in disinfectant concentrates, hard surface sanitizers, and no-rinse floor cleaners where microbial control is required.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into conditioning rinses and leave-on treatments where surface deposition on hair or skin is the target outcome for the final consumer product.

Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and antistatic agent applied during finishing stages to modify surface feel and reduce static charge buildup on various materials.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface sizing and wet-end chemistry where cationic charge aids fiber retention and surface treatment adhesion during the production process.

The material is supplied as an aqueous solution, with Bardac 2170 representing a 70% active concentrate. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial formulation volumes.

Supply quantities range from drums to IBC totes suited to large scale manufacturing. This chemical ensures high performance in diverse applications requiring surface-active properties.

name: Disodium disilicate
description:
Disodium disilicate (CAS 13870-28-5 ), also known as sodium disilicate, is an inorganic silicate salt used across industrial processing and formulation as a pH buffer, corrosion inhibitor, and cleaning agent.

Its controlled alkalinity and silicate content make it a functional ingredient in water treatment, surface treatment, and construction applications. In water treatment, it inhibits pipe corrosion by forming a protective silicate film.

The material simultaneously buffers pH in distribution systems to ensure stability. Textile and leather processors use it as a pretreatment and scouring aid, where its alkaline buffering supports fiber preparation and dye fixation.

In detergent and industrial cleaning formulations, it provides degreasing action and helps maintain the alkaline conditions needed for soil removal. This makes it essential for heavy-duty cleaning applications.

Construction product manufacturers incorporate it into cement-based adhesives and coatings as a binder component and setting modifier. It enhances the structural integrity and performance of various building materials.

Disodium disilicate is supplied as a white powder or granules depending on the intended application and handling requirements. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial water treatment and construction uses.

Food-contact and personal care applications may require material meeting FCC or equivalent purity specifications. We ensure our supply chain meets the rigorous demands of global industrial and specialty chemical standards.

name: Coenzyme B12
description:
Coenzyme B12 (CAS 13870-90-1 ), also known as adenosylcobalamin, is the biologically active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 used in pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic formulations.

Unlike synthetic precursor forms, it is recognized directly by cellular enzymatic pathways, making it a preferred active ingredient where bioavailability is a sourcing priority for manufacturers.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into oral supplements, sublingual tablets, and injectable preparations targeting B12 deficiency and neurological support.

Cosmetic formulators use it in anti-aging and skin-conditioning products, where its role in cellular metabolism supports claims around skin renewal and moisture retention in topical applications.

Food and beverage producers apply it in functional nutrition formats, including fortified drinks and dietary supplements, where an active cobalamin form is specified over cyanocobalamin.

It also appears in specialized clinical nutrition products where the coenzyme form is required by formulation specification. The material is supplied as a fine crystalline powder for easy blending.

Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP -aligned) and food-grade specifications to meet regulatory requirements across target markets and international safety standards.

Bulk quantities are available alongside smaller research and development quantities for formulation trials. It is typically stored in light-protected packaging due to its inherent photosensitivity.

name: Pantoprazole sodium
description:
Pantoprazole sodium (CAS 138786-67-1 ), also marketed under the brand name Protonix, is a proton pump inhibitor active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the manufacture of prescription gastrointestinal medications.

The anhydrous form is the primary commercially traded specification, distinct from the sesquihydrate salt used in some finished formulations. The API is the active component in oral tablet and intravenous formulations.

Indicated for acid-related gastrointestinal conditions, it is a core procurement target for finished dosage form manufacturers. Generic drug producers source this material as the starting material for enteric-coated tablet production.

Acid-resistant coating is critical to bioavailability in these applications. Contract manufacturing organizations handling sterile injectables require high-purity grades to meet parenteral formulation standards for patient safety.

It is also sourced by pharmaceutical reference standard suppliers and QC laboratories for analytical and method validation purposes. Pantoprazole sodium is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

It is available in API-grade specifications conforming to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. pharmacopoeial standards. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to multi-kilogram lots for manufacturing.

name: Sodium cyclamate
description:
Sodium cyclamate (CAS 139-05-9 ), also marketed as Sucaryl sodium and designated E952iv in food regulation, is a synthetic non-nutritive sweetener approximately 30–50 times sweeter than sucrose.

It is used across food, beverage, and pharmaceutical manufacturing as a cost-effective sugar substitute. It is often used in combination with other high-intensity sweeteners to achieve a balanced sweetness profile.

In beverage and tabletop sweetener production, it is blended with saccharin or acesulfame-K to mask off-notes. This reduces total sweetener cost per unit while maintaining a high quality of taste for the end consumer.

Confectionery and bakery manufacturers use it in sugar-free and reduced-calorie product lines. It is preferred where heat stability during processing is a critical formulation requirement for the production line.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a taste-masking agent in syrups, chewable tablets, and oral suspensions. Palatability in these applications directly affects patient compliance and overall product success.

In markets where it holds regulatory approval, it is also used in canned fruit, dairy desserts, and dietetic foods. It serves as a direct sucrose replacement in these various food processing applications.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter conforming to USP and Ph.Eur. standards.

Bulk supply is standard in 25 kg bags for industrial use. Documentation typically includes certificates of analysis aligned to FCC requirements to ensure full compliance with international safety standards.

name: Benzododecinium chloride
description:
Benzododecinium chloride (CAS 139-07-1 ), also identified commercially as BAC-C12 and Cequartyl A, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a cationic surfactant and broad-spectrum biocide across industrial and consumer markets.

It functions as both an antimicrobial preservative and an emulsification agent, making it relevant to formulators sourcing actives for preservation or surface-active performance in various chemical applications.

In water treatment, BAC-C12 controls microbial growth in cooling towers, industrial process water, and oilfield systems where biofilm formation is a persistent operational concern for facility managers.

Pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturers incorporate it into topical antiseptic formulations, wound care products, and hard-surface disinfectants where regulatory-grade purity is a sourcing requirement for safety.

Personal care formulators use it in conditioning shampoos, skin sanitizers, and preservative systems where cationic activity also contributes to substantivity on hair and skin for improved product performance.

It is also applied in industrial cleaning concentrates where combined surfactancy and biocidal action reduces the need for multiple active ingredients, streamlining the manufacturing process and reducing costs.

Benzododecinium chloride is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% active content, though other concentrations are available depending on specific application requirements and formulation needs.

Technical and pharmaceutical grades are the most commonly sourced, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph. Eur. specifications for use in regulated formulations and medical products.

name: Aluminum acetate

This chemical improves dye uptake and color fastness on natural fibers and hides. Water treatment operations use it to destabilize suspended particles and colloidal matter for clarification.

It facilitates sedimentation in both municipal and industrial effluent streams. In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber bonding and sizing processes, contributing to surface strength.

Pharmaceutical and topical formulation manufacturers use it as an astringent active in dermatological preparations. Its coagulating action on proteins supports wound care products.

Aluminum acetate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution. Technical grade is standard for industrial uses including water treatment and textile processing.

name: Nitrilotriacetic acid
description:
Nitrilotriacetic acid ( CAS 139-13-9 ), commonly abbreviated as NTA, is a chelating agent that binds and sequesters metal ions in aqueous systems. Triglycollamic acid and aminotriacetic acid are recognized alternative names encountered in technical sourcing.

It functions as a cost-effective alternative to EDTA across industrial processes where metal ion control is critical. In water treatment, NTA prevents scale formation and controls heavy metal precipitation in industrial cooling and process water systems.

Textile and paper manufacturers use it to deactivate trace metals that would otherwise interfere with bleaching, dyeing, and pulp processing. This improves consistency and reduces chemical waste during large-scale manufacturing operations.

In leather processing, it supports metal removal during preparatory stages, contributing to cleaner effluent profiles. Personal care formulators incorporate NTA as a sequestrant to stabilize formulations against metal-induced degradation.

This stabilization prevents discoloration and maintains the shelf life of various consumer products. Nitrilotriacetic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling and storage in industrial environments.

It is also available as the trisodium salt, which offers improved water solubility for liquid formulations and dosing systems. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for most industrial and chemical applications.

Purity levels are typically confirmed by titration or HPLC methods to meet industrial application requirements. This ensures consistent performance and reliability for manufacturers across the global chemical supply chain.

name: Disodium EDTA
description:
Disodium EDTA (CAS 139-33-3 ), also known as Na2H2EDTA and listed as E386 in food applications, is a chelating agent that binds and neutralizes metal ions in formulations and processes.

By sequestering calcium, magnesium, iron, and other trace metals, it prevents discoloration, rancidity, and scale formation across a broad range of industries and finished products.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it stabilizes emulsions and preservative systems by removing metal ions that would otherwise accelerate oxidative degradation during the shelf life.

Food manufacturers use it under the E386 designation to protect canned vegetables, dressings, and seafood products from metal-catalyzed color and flavor loss during storage and processing.

Water treatment and industrial cleaning operations rely on it to sequester hardness ions, improving detergent efficiency and preventing mineral deposits in various types of process equipment.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a stabilizer in liquid dosage forms and ophthalmic preparations where trace metal contamination must be tightly controlled for safety.

Disodium EDTA is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard grades include food-grade, USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for pharmaceutical and regulated food applications.

Technical grade is also available for industrial use. Bulk supply is available in bags and fiber drums, with packaging options suited to both formulation-scale and large industrial procurement.

name: Trihydroxystearin
description:
Trihydroxystearin (CAS 139-44-6 ), also known as Glyceryl tri(12-hydroxystearate), is a fully esterified glycerol derivative of 12-hydroxystearic acid. It is used as a rheology modifier, emulsifier, and lubricant across multiple industrial sectors.

Commercially available under the trade name CUTINA BW, it functions primarily as a structuring and thickening agent in both oil-based and wax-based systems. This versatile chemical provides essential body and texture to various formulations.

In personal care and cosmetics, it provides body and texture to lipsticks, balms, and anhydrous creams without contributing greasiness. It is highly valued for its ability to stabilize formulations while maintaining a smooth application feel.

Industrial lubricant formulators use it as a gelling agent in grease systems, where it builds a stable thixotropic network. This network effectively holds base oils under mechanical stress, ensuring long-term performance and stability.

In coatings and adhesives, it controls flow and sag resistance in high-viscosity formulations applied to vertical surfaces. This prevents dripping and ensures an even application of the product during the manufacturing or construction process.

Food-grade versions are used as a release agent and emulsifier in confectionery and bakery applications. These specialized grades ensure that food products maintain their shape and release easily from molds or processing equipment.

Trihydroxystearin is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form suited for melt-and-mix processing. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications for diverse industrial needs.

Food-grade material conforms to FCC requirements, ensuring safety for consumption. Technical-grade material is available for industrial lubricant and coatings applications where food compliance is not required.

name: Ethyldiethanolamine

Ethyldiethanolamine (CAS 139-87-7 ) is a tertiary amine-alcohol used across industrial formulations for pH buffering, corrosion inhibition, and emulsification. Its dual hydroxyl and amine functionality makes it effective at coordinating metal ions.

This chemical is highly efficient at stabilizing aqueous systems. In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it acts as a corrosion inhibitor and pH stabilizer in cutting fluids and coolant concentrates, extending fluid service life.

Textile and leather processing operations use it as a dispersing and leveling agent in dye baths. This improves dye uptake uniformity across fiber substrates, ensuring consistent quality in large-scale manufacturing environments.

Coatings and adhesive formulations incorporate it to control pH during emulsion polymerization. It is also used to improve pigment dispersion stability, which is critical for maintaining the shelf life of industrial paints.

Water treatment programs rely on it for metal chelation and scale inhibition in recirculating systems. It is particularly effective where hardness ions must be sequestered to prevent equipment fouling and maintenance issues.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. It is available in technical grade, which is the predominant commercial specification for industrial end uses.

By forming stable complexes with calcium, magnesium, iron, and heavy metals, it prevents unwanted mineral interference in formulations and process streams. In water treatment, HEDTA controls scale formation.

It keeps metal ions in solution, protecting equipment and extending system life. Personal care formulators use it to deactivate trace metals in shampoos, conditioners, and skin cleansers.

Metal contamination reduces process efficiency and damages fabric quality. In agriculture, it functions as a micronutrient carrier, chelating iron and manganese into plant-available forms.

name: Triethanolamine lauryl sulfate
description:
Triethanolamine lauryl sulfate (CAS 139-96-8 ), also known as TEA-Lauryl Sulfate and marketed under trade names such as Drene and Texapon TH, is an anionic surfactant used across personal care and cosmetic manufacturing.

It delivers foaming, emulsification, and cleansing performance in rinse-off formulations where mildness and compatibility with other ingredients are priorities. In shampoo manufacturing, it functions as the primary foaming and cleansing agent.

The compound works by solubilizing sebum and styling product residues from the scalp and hair shaft. Body washes and liquid hand soaps rely on it to generate stable, dense lather while maintaining compatibility with conditioning additives.

It is also used in fragrance systems, facial cleansers, and shaving creams, where its emulsifying action helps suspend oils and particulates for effective rinsing. This ensures a clean finish for various consumer applications.

Formulators working on specialty cleansing products use it to adjust foam profile and viscosity response. It is often used in combination with amphoteric or nonionic co-surfactants to achieve specific performance goals.

Triethanolamine lauryl sulfate is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications, with active matter concentrations commonly around 40% for industrial use.

Buyers should confirm active content and pH range with suppliers when qualifying batches for formulation consistency. Adhering to these parameters ensures the final product meets the necessary stability and performance requirements.

name: Carmine
description:
Carmine (CAS 1390-65-4 ), also known as Natural Red 4 and Crimson Lake, is a natural red pigment derived from cochineal insects. It is used across food, cosmetic, and industrial coloring applications.

Its deep crimson hue and stability under heat and light make it a preferred alternative to synthetic red dyes in regulated markets. In food manufacturing, it delivers consistent red-to-pink shades.

It is commonly used in products such as yogurts, confectionery, processed meats, and beverages where natural colorant labeling is a commercial requirement. Cosmetic formulators use it for vivid reds.

It is ideal for lipsticks, blushes, and eye shadows, where pigment intensity and skin compatibility drive colorant selection. Textile and leather processors apply it to achieve rich crimson tones.

This is particularly useful on natural fibers and hides where natural dye certification supports product positioning. Printing ink manufacturers incorporate it into specialty inks for packaging.

This is often specified by brand owners who require natural-origin pigments. The product is supplied as a fine powder, water-soluble liquid extract, or aluminum lake suspension depending on the application.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC -compliant), cosmetic-grade, and technical-grade. The carmine content is typically expressed as a percentage of carminic acid for quality control.

Concentrated liquid forms are also available for direct dosing in beverage and dairy production lines. These formats ensure ease of use and consistent color intensity across various manufacturing batches.

name: Annatto
description:
Annatto ( CAS 1393-63-1 ), also known as roucou, achiote, and commercially designated E160b or C.I. Natural Orange 4, is a natural colorant derived from the seeds of Bixa orellana. It delivers yellow-to-orange hues across food, cosmetic, and personal care formulations as a plant-based alternative to synthetic dyes.

In dairy manufacturing, annatto is the standard colorant for cheddar cheese, butter, and margarine, providing the characteristic orange tone consumers associate with these products. Snack coatings, seasonings, and processed meat products use it to achieve consistent warm color without synthetic additives.

In personal care, it is incorporated into lip products, foundations, and skin-toning cosmetics where natural-origin pigmentation is a formulation requirement. It also functions as a mild flavoring agent in certain regional food applications, contributing a subtle earthy, peppery note to spice blends and condiments.

Annatto is supplied as an oil-soluble extract, water-soluble liquid concentrate, and dry powder, with bixin content and norbixin content serving as the primary specification markers. Food-grade material is available to FCC standards, and cosmetic-grade supply aligns with relevant regional colorant regulations.

Concentration levels in commercial extracts are typically defined by percentage bixin or norbixin content, which buyers should confirm against application-specific requirements. This ensures the final product meets the desired color intensity and stability throughout its shelf life.

As a versatile natural pigment, it remains a preferred choice for manufacturers seeking clean-label solutions. Its stability in various pH environments and resistance to light degradation make it suitable for a wide range of industrial and consumer goods.

name: Aluminum triphosphate
description:
Aluminum triphosphate (CAS 13939-25-8 ) is an inorganic aluminum salt used primarily as a corrosion-inhibiting pigment and pH buffer in protective coating systems. It functions by passivating metal substrates.

This chemical slows electrochemical corrosion without relying on heavy metals such as chromate or zinc phosphate. In anticorrosive primers and industrial coatings, it acts as a non-toxic corrosion inhibitor.

It is ideal for steel and aluminum substrates, replacing chromate-based alternatives in compliance-sensitive formulations. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to improve adhesion to metal surfaces.

The compound helps maintain pH stability in the cured system. In construction materials such as cementitious coatings and waterproofing membranes, it contributes to substrate protection and long-term durability.

Water treatment formulators use it as a buffering agent to control pH in treatment compounds and mineral-based process chemicals. It is supplied as a fine white powder suited for dispersion into liquid systems.

The material is compatible with adhesive bases and dry-blended construction formulations. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with particle size distribution being a key quality parameter.

Buyers sourcing for coatings applications should confirm compatibility specifications. Performance varies with surface area and purity level for pigment-grade material in industrial manufacturing environments.

name: Potassium ferrocyanide
description:
Potassium ferrocyanide ( CAS 13943-58-3 ), also known commercially as E536 and tetrapotassium hexacyanoferrate, is an inorganic iron-cyanide salt used across food processing, metal treatment, and industrial separation processes.

It functions primarily as an anti-caking agent, chelating agent, and selective precipitant depending on the application sector. In food production, E536 is approved as an anti-caking additive in table salt and salt substitutes.

This additive prevents clumping during storage and packaging. Metal processing operations use it to selectively precipitate heavy metals, particularly copper and zinc, from process streams and wastewater, supporting both recovery and effluent compliance.

In winemaking, it is applied as a fining agent to remove excess copper and iron ions that would otherwise cause haze or off-flavors. Textile and leather dyeing processes rely on it as a reducing auxiliary and fixative.

It is also used in blue pigment formulations, including Prussian blue production. Potassium ferrocyanide is supplied as a yellow crystalline powder or granules. Food-grade material is available to E536 specification.

This material meets purity requirements for use in edible salt applications. Technical grade is supplied for industrial water treatment, mining, and dyeing applications where food compliance is not required.

name: Lauryl laurate
description:
Lauryl laurate (CAS 13945-76-1 ), also known as dodecyl dodecanoate, is a fatty acid ester derived from lauric acid and lauryl alcohol. It functions as a plasticizer, lubricant, and emollient carrier across personal care, polymer, and industrial lubrication applications.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a skin-conditioning carrier and emollient, improving spreadability and texture in creams, serums, and color cosmetics. Polymer processors use it as a plasticizer and internal lubricant to reduce melt viscosity.

This ester helps improve processing flow in PVC and similar thermoplastic compounds. In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it contributes lubricity and acts as a base fluid or functional additive in cutting oils and release agents.

It also serves as a solvent and dispersing medium for active ingredients, pigments, and waxes in both cosmetic and specialty industrial formulations. Lauryl laurate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid at ambient temperatures.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity standards relevant to personal care manufacturing. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers for industrial use.

name: Diethanolamine oleate

Diethanolamine oleate (CAS 13961-86-9 ), also referred to as oleic acid diethanolamine salt, is an amine-based surfactant produced by combining oleic acid with diethanolamine.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, lubricant, and corrosion inhibitor across several industrial sectors. In metalworking fluids and cutting oils, it provides both lubrication and corrosion protection.

This chemical helps protect ferrous metal surfaces, extending tool life and protecting workpieces between processing stages. Textile and leather processing operations use it as an emulsifier and softening agent.

It is frequently utilized in fiber lubricants, scouring baths, and finishing formulations. In coatings and adhesive systems, it aids pigment dispersion and improves substrate wetting, contributing to film uniformity.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into emulsion-based products such as creams and lotions. Its surfactant character supports stable oil-in-water systems for various cosmetic applications.

Diethanolamine oleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste, depending on concentration and temperature. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most buyers.

name: Chitin
description:
Chitin (CAS 1398-61-4 ), also referenced in technical contexts as PNAG, is a naturally derived polysaccharide obtained primarily from crustacean shells and fungal biomass. It functions as a structural biopolymer and rheology modifier across food, pharmaceutical, agricultural, and biotechnology applications.

In pharmaceutical and biomedical manufacturing, this material is processed into films, membranes, and scaffolds used in wound dressings and controlled-release delivery systems. Food and nutrition formulators incorporate it as a dietary fiber source and texture modifier in functional food products.

Agricultural applications include its use as a soil amendment and crop biostimulant, where it activates plant defense responses to improve yield resilience. In biotechnology, it serves as a chromatography matrix material and as a substrate for enzyme immobilization in bioprocessing workflows.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder, with flake and fibrous forms available depending on the source material and processing method. Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material for various industrial needs.

Purity specifications are typically defined by the degree of deacetylation and molecular weight range to ensure consistency. Shrimp-derived and squid-derived variants are the most commercially prevalent options for global manufacturers and distributors.

Fungal-sourced material is also available for applications requiring non-crustacean certification or specific vegan compliance. This versatile biopolymer continues to be a critical component in sustainable chemical development and advanced material science.

name: Pentasodium pentetate
description:
Pentasodium pentetate (CAS 140-01-2 ), commonly sourced and specified as Pentasodium DTPA, is a high-performance chelating agent used across industrial and consumer product manufacturing.

It binds and neutralizes metal ions, particularly calcium, magnesium, iron, and heavy metals, that would otherwise destabilize formulations, discolor substrates, or interfere with processing chemistry.

In personal care and cosmetics, it stabilizes bleach-based hair products and preservative systems by sequestering trace metals that catalyze oxidative degradation during the manufacturing process.

Pulp and paper processors use it to deactivate metal contaminants in bleaching baths, protecting peroxide efficiency and preventing fiber damage to ensure high-quality finished paper products.

Water treatment and industrial cleaning formulations rely on it to prevent scale formation and maintain process equipment. In textile and leather processing, it controls metal interference during dyeing.

This improves color consistency and yield across various fabric types. Pentasodium DTPA is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 40% active concentration for industrial use.

Technical-grade and industrial-grade designations are standard across the market. Specifications vary by application sector, with cosmetic-grade material available for personal care compliance requirements.

The nitrile group enables essential downstream functional group transformations. Agrochemical producers rely on it as a precursor in the synthesis of certain insecticides and herbicides for crop protection.

Flavor and fragrance chemists use it as a starting material for phenylacetic acid derivatives. These derivatives contribute rose and honey-like notes to finished fragrance compositions and consumer products.

It also functions as a specialty solvent in select chemical processes where its polarity and reactivity profile suit specific reaction conditions. The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid.

name: Estragole
description:
Estragole (CAS 140-67-0 ), also known as para-allylanisole, is a naturally occurring phenylpropanoid ether extracted from botanical sources including tarragon, basil, and fennel. It functions as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient.

This compound delivers a characteristic sweet, anise-like profile valued across food and cosmetic applications. In flavor formulation, it is used to replicate or reinforce the taste profile of tarragon and anise in seasonings and sauces.

The FEMA 2411 status supports its use in regulated flavor systems for processed food products. Fragrance compounders incorporate it into fine fragrances, personal care products, and functional cosmetics where herbal top notes are required.

It also appears in oral care formulations such as toothpaste and mouthwash, where its anise character contributes to flavor masking. These applications rely on its ability to provide consumer-preferred taste profiles.

Some antioxidant stabilizer applications in food systems leverage its phenylpropanoid structure to support shelf-life performance. This is particularly effective in fat-containing matrices where stability is a primary concern for manufacturers.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically at purities of 98% and above for flavor and fragrance use. Both natural-origin and synthetic grades are available to meet specific industry needs.

Natural grades command a premium for clean-label and botanical-positioned formulations in the current market. Buyers should confirm origin declaration and purity specification when sourcing for regulated flavor applications.

name: Ethyl acrylate
description:
Ethyl acrylate (CAS 140-88-5 ), commonly abbreviated as EA, is a reactive acrylic monomer used as a building block in polymer synthesis and as a flavoring agent in food applications.

It copolymerizes readily with other acrylates and vinyl monomers to produce resins with controlled flexibility and adhesion properties. In flavoring, it contributes pineapple and fruity notes at trace concentrations, listed under FEMA 2418 .

EA is a primary monomer in emulsion polymerization for producing acrylic coatings, pressure-sensitive adhesives, and flexible packaging films where low glass transition temperature is required.

In printing and packaging, it is incorporated into water-based inks and overprint varnishes to improve substrate adhesion and film flexibility. Textile and leather finishes use EA-based copolymers to achieve soft, durable surface coatings.

These coatings are highly resistant to cracking and environmental wear. As a flavoring ingredient, it is used at permitted trace levels in processed foods and beverages to deliver fruity top notes.

Ethyl acrylate is supplied as an inhibited liquid, typically stabilized with hydroquinone monomethyl ether to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport.

Standard commercial grades include technical and polymerization grade, with purity levels commonly at 99% or higher. Food-grade material conforming to FEMA specifications is available for flavor applications.

name: Potassium ethylxanthate
description:
Potassium ethylxanthate (CAS 140-89-6 ), commonly known as KEX, is a xanthate collector salt used primarily in mineral flotation and selective metal recovery. It functions by selectively bonding to sulfide mineral surfaces.

This chemical enables the efficient separation of minerals from gangue material in froth flotation circuits. In base metal mining, KEX is the standard collector for sulfide ores including copper, lead, zinc, and nickel concentrates.

It drives recovery efficiency in flotation cells, ensuring high yields for mining operations. Gold and silver processing operations use it to float sulfide-associated precious metals that would otherwise report to tailings.

In industrial water treatment, KEX precipitates heavy metal ions, including copper, mercury, and lead, from process effluents as insoluble xanthate complexes. This supports compliance with environmental discharge limits.

Agrochemical formulators have also employed xanthate chemistry as a dithiocarbamate precursor in certain biocidal and soil treatment applications. The product is supplied as a yellow to pale green powder or granule.

Granular forms are often preferred for handling and storage stability in mining operations. Standard commercial grades are specified by active content, typically 90% minimum purity for industrial use.

Technical-grade material is the dominant market form for this chemical. Packaging is available in moisture-resistant bags or drums given the product's sensitivity to humidity and decomposition under storage.

name: Sodium isopropyl xanthate
description:
Sodium isopropyl xanthate (CAS 140-93-2 ), also known commercially as Proxan-sodium and Aeroxanthate 343, is a selective flotation collector used in the concentration of sulfide ores.

It functions by adsorbing onto mineral surfaces, rendering them hydrophobic so they attach to air bubbles and separate from gangue material during froth flotation processes.

In copper, lead, and zinc sulfide processing, it selectively collects target minerals at relatively low dosage rates, improving concentrate grade and recovery across the circuit.

Gold and silver operations use it to float sulfide-associated precious metals where the ore body requires a short-chain xanthate collector for optimal mineral separation.

It is also applied in nickel and molybdenum circuits, where its selectivity over non-sulfide gangue reduces downstream processing costs and improves overall plant efficiency.

Blended collector formulations in complex polymetallic ores incorporate it alongside other xanthates or dithiophosphates to broaden mineral response across varying ore grades.

The product is supplied as a yellow to pale-green powder or granules, with granular form preferred for safer handling and reduced dust exposure on site during mixing.

Standard commercial purity is typically 90% or higher, with technical-grade product the norm for mining applications. Packaging is available in bags and bulk quantities.

name: Dimethylolurea
description:
Dimethylolurea (CAS 140-95-4 ), also known commercially as DMU, is a methylol-functional urea derivative used as a reactive intermediate and crosslinking agent across textile, paper, and polymer applications.

It introduces durable network structures into coatings, resins, and treated substrates by reacting with hydroxyl- and amino-functional materials under heat or acid catalysis during the manufacturing process.

In textile finishing, DMU is applied to cellulosic fabrics to impart crease resistance and dimensional stability in durable press treatments. Paper manufacturers incorporate it into wet-strength resin systems.

In these systems, it crosslinks fiber networks to improve resistance to moisture-induced degradation. Coating and adhesive formulators use DMU as a reactive monomer to build urea-formaldehyde-type resin systems.

These systems offer controlled cure profiles for various industrial uses. In polymer processing, it functions as a building block for modified resins where lower formaldehyde release is a formulation priority.

Dimethylolurea is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging from 50–60% in liquid form. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Material meeting specific textile or paper industry purity requirements is available from select producers. Buyers should confirm methylol content and free formaldehyde levels when evaluating grades for compliance.

name: Orcein
description:
Orcein (CAS 1400-62-0 ), also known commercially as orchil and approved as food colorant E182 , is a natural dye derived from lichens used to impart red-purple to violet hues across food, textile, and biological staining applications.

Its depth of color and affinity for protein-based substrates make it a recognized choice where natural origin and distinctive tone are procurement priorities. In food and beverage production, E182 is approved for use as a colorant to deliver red-violet shades.

This dye is utilized in confectionery, beverages, and specialty products where natural-origin labeling is commercially advantageous. Textile manufacturers apply orcein to wool, silk, and other protein fibers, where it bonds directly without requiring a mordant.

This direct bonding capability reduces processing steps in industrial dyeing operations. In histology and biological research, it is the active component in staining preparations used to differentiate elastic fibers and chromosomal material in tissue sections.

Leather and paper industries also use it to achieve consistent violet tones in specialty finishing and decorative applications. Orcein is supplied as a dark brown to black powder that yields characteristic red-purple color in solution.

It is available in natural and synthetic forms, with synthetic orcein commonly offered for laboratory and histological staining grades. Food-grade material conforming to E182 specifications is available for regulated colorant applications.

name: Tannic Acid
description:
Tannic Acid (CAS 1401-55-4 ), commercially sourced as tannins, is a plant-derived polyphenolic compound used across food, industrial, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a chelating agent, astringent, and protein precipitant.

This versatile compound is applicable in processes ranging from clarification and coagulation to flavor modification and surface treatment. In food and beverage production, it acts as a fining agent for wines, beers, and fruit juices.

By binding proteins and colloids, it significantly improves clarity in liquid products. Leather tanneries rely on it to cross-link collagen fibers in hides, producing firm, durable leather with consistent surface quality.

Water treatment operations use its coagulation properties to precipitate heavy metals and suspended solids from industrial effluents. This makes it an essential component for environmental management and industrial waste processing.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an excipient and active component in topical formulations targeting skin conditions requiring astringent action. It is supplied as a light yellow to tan powder for easy handling.

Liquid extract forms are also available for specific industrial applications. Standard grades include food-grade material meeting FCC specifications and pharmaceutical-grade material aligned with USP and BP standards.

Technical-grade material is available for leather processing, textile dyeing, and water treatment applications. These grades are suitable where food or pharma compliance is not required for the specific manufacturing process.
