name: Iron(III) acetylacetonate
description:
Iron(III) acetylacetonate (CAS 14024-18-1 ), also known as Iron Acetylacetonate, is an organometallic coordination compound used as a catalyst and catalyst precursor across polymer chemistry and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It delivers controlled iron-center reactivity in systems where precise metal loading and solubility in organic media are critical sourcing requirements for industrial chemical applications.

In plastics and polymer production, it functions as an initiator or co-catalyst in controlled radical and ring-opening polymerization processes, enabling targeted molecular weight distribution in engineering polymers.

Lubricant additive formulators incorporate it as a precursor for iron-based friction modifiers and extreme-pressure additive packages. In metalworking and surface treatment, it serves as a deposition source.

It is utilized in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) and metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) processes for iron-containing thin films and coatings. Biotechnology researchers use it as a defined iron source.

It is essential for nanoparticle synthesis and model reaction systems requiring soluble, organically compatible iron(III). Iron(III) acetylacetonate is supplied as a crystalline powder, typically in dark red to brown form.

It is available in technical and high-purity research grades, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 97% to 99%+. Packaging options span laboratory-scale quantities through bulk industrial supply.

These options suit both R&D procurement and production-scale requirements. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for global manufacturers requiring high-performance organometallic catalysts.

name: Zinc acetylacetonate
description:
Zinc acetylacetonate (CAS 14024-63-6 ), commonly abbreviated as Zn(acac)2, is an organozinc coordination compound used industrially as a catalyst, crosslinker, and curing agent.

It functions by delivering reactive zinc in a thermally activatable, organically soluble form. This enables controlled reactivity in polymer and coating systems where inorganic zinc salts are incompatible.

In coatings and adhesives, Zn(acac)2 acts as a latent crosslinking agent for resin systems. It improves film hardness, adhesion, and chemical resistance without premature gelation during processing.

Polymer formulators use it as a catalyst precursor in the production of polyesters, polyurethanes, and specialty elastomers. It is ideal for applications where precise cure initiation is required.

In plastics, it functions as a stabilizer and processing aid, particularly in PVC and other halogenated polymer systems. It helps maintain structural integrity during high-temperature manufacturing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it at low concentrations for its zinc-delivery and astringent functionality. It is often found in skin-conditioning and antimicrobial product lines.

Zinc acetylacetonate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications for various industrial needs.

Anhydrous and monohydrate forms are available depending on application sensitivity. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply for large operations.

description:
Copper EDTA disodium ( CAS 14025-15-1 ), also known as Cu-EDTA or copper disodium edetate, is a chelated copper complex that delivers bioavailable copper in a stable, water-soluble form.

It is used across agriculture, nutrition, and water treatment as a controlled copper source where free ionic copper would be ineffective or incompatible with the formulation matrix.

In agriculture and animal feed, Cu-EDTA supplies copper as a micronutrient in foliar sprays, fertigation programs, and premix formulations where uptake efficiency is critical for growth.

Water treatment applications use it to maintain copper activity in systems where hardness or pH would otherwise precipitate free copper salts, ensuring consistent performance in various environments.

In food and nutritional products, it functions as a copper fortification agent in mineral premixes and dietary supplements requiring chelated mineral forms for better absorption and stability.

Industrial formulations also employ it as a sequestrant to stabilize copper activity and prevent undesirable oxidation or mineral interference during complex chemical manufacturing processes.

Copper EDTA disodium is supplied as a crystalline powder or granule, typically in blue-green coloration characteristic of the copper complex, ensuring easy identification and handling.

Standard grades include technical and feed-grade specifications, with agricultural applications often requiring documentation to recognized quality standards for industrial procurement volumes.

In textile dyeing and leather finishing, it delivers rich blue shades with strong substrate adhesion, particularly in batch and continuous dyeing processes used in large-scale textile production.

Printing inks and packaging coatings rely on this pigment for its high tinting strength, allowing formulators to achieve deep color saturation at lower pigment loadings for cost-effective manufacturing.

In paper manufacturing, it is used to produce blue-toned specialty papers and to correct color balance in white paper grades, ensuring high-quality visual standards for premium paper products.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it into products such as eyeshadows and mascaras where a stable, non-bleeding blue colorant is required for long-lasting wear and safety.

name: Borane-tetrahydrofuran
description:

These transformations are difficult to achieve cleanly with conventional reducing agents. It initiates ring-opening polymerization of cyclic monomers, making it a useful catalyst precursor in specialty polymer production.

Agrochemical synthesis relies on it for constructing chiral intermediates where stereoselective hydroboration is required. Biotechnology and life sciences research also draw on it for synthesizing boron-containing building blocks.

Higher concentration solutions are available for industrial-scale processes where solvent minimization is a priority. It is sourced primarily to pharmaceutical-grade and reagent-grade specifications for various applications.

description:
4-Carboxyphenylboronic acid (CAS 14047-29-1 ), also known as 4-boronobenzoic acid, is a bifunctional arylboronic acid combining a carboxylic acid and a boronic acid group on a single benzene ring.

This dual reactivity makes it a valued building block in pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer chemistry, and specialty material development. In drug discovery, it serves as a key intermediate in Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions.

This enables the construction of biaryl scaffolds found in active pharmaceutical ingredients. Polymer chemists use it to introduce boronic acid functionality into hydrogels and responsive materials for various applications.

Reversible covalent bonding with diols enables glucose-sensing or controlled-release behavior. In personal care formulations, the boronic acid moiety supports antimicrobial and preservative activity by interacting with bacterial cell wall components.

The carboxylic acid group also allows direct conjugation to amine-bearing substrates, making it useful for surface functionalization and bioconjugate chemistry. This versatility is essential for modern chemical manufacturing.

4-Carboxyphenylboronic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram commercial lots for industrial use.

Purity grades typically range from 97% to 99%+ for synthesis-grade and high-purity pharmaceutical applications. Specification against HPLC purity standards is standard for pharma-facing supply chains.

Contact us for supply of 4-carboxyphenylboronic acid

name: Glycyrrhizin
description:
Glycyrrhizin (CAS 1405-86-3 ), also known as glycyrrhizinic acid and classified as E958 in food applications, is the principal bioactive triterpene glycoside extracted from licorice root.

It functions commercially as a natural sweetener, flavor modifier, and functional additive across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. In food and beverage production, E958 delivers intense sweetness.

The compound is approximately 50 times sweeter than sucrose while simultaneously masking bitter off-notes in functional ingredients, protein blends, and nutraceutical formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient.

It is frequently used as a flavor-masking agent in oral dosage forms including syrups, lozenges, and chewable tablets. In personal care, it is incorporated into skin-soothing serums, toners, and brightening formulations.

The ingredient supports moisture retention and helps stabilize active ingredients against oxidative degradation. Confectionery and tobacco processing also rely on it as a flavor enhancer and humectant to control texture.

Glycyrrhizin is commercially available as an ammoniated form and as the free acid, supplied in powder and granular formats. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade material.

Our supply meets USP , BP , and cosmetic-grade requirements to satisfy regulatory standards across end markets. Purity specifications typically range from 95% to 98% depending on the intended application.

name: Flavylium
description:
Flavylium (CAS 14051-53-7 ), also referenced as the flavylium cation in colorant chemistry, is the core structural scaffold underlying anthocyanin-based natural pigments. It defines the chromophore responsible for the red, purple, and blue hues found across plant-derived colorant systems.

Industrial interest centers on its role as a reference compound and synthetic intermediate for developing pH-responsive colorants and natural dye analogs. In food and nutrition, flavylium-based structures are studied and applied as the functional basis for anthocyanin colorants.

These colorants are used in beverages, confectionery, and dairy products where natural hue stability is a formulation target. Printing and packaging applications leverage its pH-sensitive color-switching behavior to develop smart inks and indicator labels.

These labels signal freshness or environmental changes. Formulators working on natural dye replacement programs use flavylium derivatives as benchmarks when screening synthetic or semi-synthetic colorant candidates. Research and QA laboratories source it as an analytical reference standard.

This standard is essential for anthocyanin quantification and colorant authentication work. Flavylium is typically available as a solid salt form, most commonly as the perchlorate or chloride salt, in research and specialty chemical quantities.

Supply is primarily positioned at laboratory and development scale rather than bulk commodity volumes. Technical and research-grade specifications are standard; food-grade supply is not a recognized commercial format for this compound.

name: Vitamin D
description:
Vitamin D (CAS 1406-16-2 ) is a fat-soluble vitamin supplied commercially as either cholecalciferol (D3) or ergocalciferol (D2), the two biologically active forms recognized across global markets.

It functions as a nutritional fortification agent in food, feed, and pharmaceutical applications, supporting calcium metabolism and bone health claims in regulated product categories.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to fortify dairy products, plant-based milks, cereals, and infant formula to meet regulatory nutrient requirements for various consumer demographics.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into tablets, capsules, and oral drops as an active ingredient in dietary supplements and prescription-grade preparations for global distribution.

In animal nutrition, it is added to poultry, swine, and aquaculture feed to support skeletal development and optimize feed conversion. Agrochemical and premix producers also use it as a component.

Vitamin D is available as an oily liquid concentrate, spray-dried powder, and beadlet form. The latter is preferred for dry blending and tableting due to improved flowability and stability.

Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications, with D3 being the dominant commercial form. Potency is expressed in International Units (IU) for accuracy.

Common concentrations range from 100,000 IU/g to 1,000,000 IU/g depending on the application. These variations allow for precise formulation in diverse industrial and nutritional settings.

Contact us for supply of Vitamin D

name: Vitamin E
description:
Vitamin E (CAS 1406-18-4 ), also known commercially as Tocopherol, is a fat-soluble antioxidant used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing to protect formulations and finished products from oxidative degradation.

It functions primarily as a stabilizer for lipid-containing systems, extending shelf life and preserving product integrity. In food and nutrition manufacturing, it protects edible oils, fats, and fortified products from rancidity.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, serums, and lip products where it stabilizes oil phases and supports moisturizing performance in skin-contact formulations. This ensures long-term stability for high-end personal care items.

Pharmaceutical producers use it as both an active nutrient ingredient and a functional antioxidant in soft gel capsules, emulsions, and topical preparations. It is essential for maintaining the potency of sensitive medicinal compounds.

In animal feed, it is added to premixes and compound feeds as a nutritional supplement supporting livestock health and product quality. Vitamin E is supplied as an oil, typically mixed tocopherols or d-alpha tocopherol concentrate.

It is also available in powder form via encapsulation or adsorption onto carriers for dry blending applications. Established grades include USP , Ph. Eur. , BP , and food-grade FCC standards.

Natural (d-alpha) and synthetic (dl-alpha) forms are available depending on application requirements. Technical grades are also available for industrial antioxidant use in various non-food applications and manufacturing processes.

Contact us for supply of Vitamin E

name: Chlorophyll
description:
Chlorophyll (CAS 1406-65-1 ), also designated E140i in food regulatory frameworks, is a natural green pigment extracted from plant material including grass, alfalfa, and nettles.

It functions as a natural colorant in food, beverage, and cosmetic formulations where synthetic dyes are undesirable or restricted. In food and beverage manufacturing, it delivers stable green coloration.

This pigment is used in products such as pasta, confectionery coatings, dairy alternatives, and soft drinks. Personal care formulators incorporate it into facial creams, serums, and cleansing products.

A natural green tint and plant-derived positioning are commercially important for these applications. In the nutraceutical and supplement sector, it is used in green powder blends and liquid drops.

It is also found in capsules targeting health-conscious consumer segments. Beverage producers working with clean-label or organic-certified product lines use it as a direct replacement for synthetic green colorants.

Chlorophyll is supplied as a liquid extract, oil-soluble concentrate, or dry powder, depending on the intended application matrix. Standard grades include food-grade meeting E140i specifications.

These grades comply with EU food additive regulations, as well as cosmetic-grade material. Purity and solvent profiles vary by supplier, so buyers should confirm extraction solvent compliance.

Always ensure that the material meets relevant regional regulations for your specific industry. This ensures the highest quality and safety standards for your final consumer products.

name: Tocopherols
description:
Tocopherols (CAS 1406-66-2 ), also sold under E306 , are a family of naturally derived fat-soluble antioxidants extracted primarily from vegetable oils. In commercial formulations, they function as oxidative stabilizers.

These compounds protect lipid-containing products from rancidity, color degradation, and shelf-life reduction. In food manufacturing, they are used to extend the shelf life of edible oils, fats, margarines, and fat-based spreads.

By retarding lipid oxidation, they ensure product quality over time. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate these antioxidants into oil-based drug formulations, softgel capsules, and nutritional supplements where stability is critical.

In animal feed production, they protect fat-soluble nutrients and feed fats from oxidation during storage and pelleting. Personal care formulators rely on them in emollient-rich creams, serums, and hair oils.

They serve both as an antioxidant preservative system and as a moisturizing active in cosmetic applications. These products are supplied as viscous oils or oil-based liquid concentrates with varying concentrations.

Mixed tocopherol concentrations typically range from 50% to 97% depending on the specific application. Food-grade and feed-grade specifications are standard across the market for industrial use.

Food applications are covered under the specific regulatory designation. USP and Ph.Eur. grades are available for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical use cases requiring documented purity and compliance.

name: Potassium tetrafluoroborate
description:
Potassium tetrafluoroborate (CAS 14075-53-7 ), also known as potassium fluoborate and abbreviated KBF4, is an inorganic fluoroborate salt used across metallurgy, electronics, and surface treatment industries.

It functions primarily as a flux agent, grain refiner, and controlled fluoride source in high-temperature processing applications. In aluminum and magnesium casting, KBF4 acts as a grain-refining additive.

This improves the mechanical properties of finished metal components. Electronics manufacturers use it as a flux component in soldering pastes and brazing alloys, where controlled fluoride release aids oxide removal.

In abrasives production, it is incorporated into grinding wheels and coated abrasives as an active filler. This reduces heat buildup and extends tool life during intensive metalworking operations.

Surface treatment and electroplating operations also draw on potassium fluoroborate as a fluoride donor. It is used in bath formulations for metal finishing processes to ensure high-quality results.

Potassium tetrafluoroborate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

High-purity grades are available for electronics and specialty metallurgical applications. Consistent fluoride content and low impurity profiles are critical to process control in these sectors.

name: Ferrous fumarate
description:
Ferrous fumarate (CAS 141-01-5 ), also sold under the trade names Feostat and Ercoferro, is an iron(II) salt used across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and feed industries as a bioavailable source of elemental iron.

Its high iron content and relatively low solubility make it a preferred choice for solid-dose iron supplementation where tolerability and stability are formulation priorities for manufacturers.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in oral iron deficiency treatments, formulated into tablets, capsules, and chewable dosage forms to ensure effective delivery.

Nutritional supplement producers use it to fortify food products such as breakfast cereals, infant formula, and meal replacement powders where iron enrichment is required for health.

Animal feed compounders incorporate it into premixes and complete feeds to address iron deficiency in livestock and companion animals, supporting overall growth and metabolic health.

In personal care, it functions as a colorant and stabilizing agent in select cosmetic formulations. The material is supplied as a fine reddish-brown powder for easy blending.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications, as well as feed-grade specifications for animal nutrition.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial and cosmetic use cases. This ensures that all regulatory and quality requirements are met across various global markets.

name: Dioctyl fumarate
description:
Dioctyl fumarate (CAS 141-02-6 ), also known as bis(2-ethylhexyl) fumarate, is a difunctional ester monomer used as both a reactive building block in polymer synthesis and a plasticizing agent across several industrial sectors.

Its dual functionality makes it relevant to formulators working at the intersection of polymerization chemistry and end-product flexibility. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it is incorporated as a copolymerizable monomer.

This material is used to modify the mechanical and thermal properties of acrylic, vinyl, and specialty polymer systems. Rubber compounders use it to improve flexibility and processing characteristics in elastomeric formulations.

It is particularly useful where reactive compatibility with the polymer matrix is required. In coatings, it contributes to film formation and flexibility when copolymerized with acrylates or other vinyl monomers.

This applies to both solvent-borne and UV-curable systems. Adhesive and sealant formulators source it as a reactive plasticizer where conventional non-reactive plasticizers would compromise bond integrity or long-term durability.

Dioctyl fumarate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available primarily in technical grade, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher depending on the specific supplier requirements.

Bulk liquid and intermediate packaging formats are standard for industrial procurement. This ensures efficient handling and integration into large-scale manufacturing processes for various chemical applications.

name: Bis(2-(2-butoxyethoxy)ethyl) adipate
description:
Bis(2-(2-butoxyethoxy)ethyl) adipate (CAS 141-17-3 ), also known commercially as Dibutoxyethoxyethyl adipate, is a specialty ester used as a plasticizer, lubricant, and solvent carrier across demanding industrial applications.

Its low-temperature performance and compatibility with a range of polymers make it a practical choice for formulators working in performance-critical environments. In plastics compounding, it functions as a primary or secondary plasticizer.

It is utilized for PVC and other polymers where flexibility at low temperatures is a formulation requirement. Lubricant formulators incorporate it into synthetic lubricant blends and metalworking fluids for film-forming characteristics.

These ester-based base stocks are preferred for their thermal stability. Aerospace and automotive sealant and coating manufacturers use it to maintain elastomer flexibility under wide temperature cycling during operation.

It also serves as a solvent carrier in specialty formulations where controlled solvency and low volatility are required. This ensures the stability of the final product in various industrial and commercial settings.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid and is available in technical grade. Supply is typically offered in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) to meet industrial volume requirements for large-scale manufacturing.

name: Diethylene glycol monolaurate
description:
Diethylene glycol monolaurate (CAS 141-20-8 ), also known commercially as Glaurin or PEG-2 Laurate, is a fatty acid ester used across personal care, food, and industrial formulations. It serves as an emulsifier, humectant, and solubilizer.

It bridges oil and water phases in complex systems where stable dispersion and controlled rheology are both required. In personal care formulations, it functions as an emulsifier and moisturizing agent in creams and lotions.

The compound is frequently used in hair conditioning products, improving texture and skin feel. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a softening and lubricating auxiliary for fiber treatment and surface finishing.

In printing inks and coatings, it acts as a carrier and rheology modifier, helping control viscosity and pigment dispersion across different substrate types. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial manufacturing.

Food-grade applications include its use as an emulsifier in processed food systems, where it supports fat dispersion and improves product consistency. It is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting paste.

Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with food-grade material meeting relevant purity standards for use in regulated applications. Bulk liquid supply is standard for industrial buyers.

The material is often distributed in drums or IBCs to meet the needs of large-scale production facilities. Its chemical stability and performance characteristics ensure reliable results across diverse chemical sectors.

name: Ricinoleic acid
description:
Ricinoleic acid (CAS 141-22-0 ), also known as ricinolic acid, is the principal fatty acid derived from castor oil, accounting for approximately 85–90% of its composition.

It functions as a reactive intermediate, emulsifier, and surface-active agent across a broad range of industrial and personal care applications. In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it acts as a base component.

Sulfated and ethoxylated derivatives improve lubricity and metal surface protection. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a reactive plasticizer and adhesion promoter, particularly in polyurethane systems.

Its hydroxyl group enables direct polymer chain incorporation. The textile and leather industries rely on it for fiber softening, fat liquoring agents, and surface conditioning treatments that improve flexibility.

In personal care, it functions as an emollient and emulsifier in lipstick bases, skin creams, and hair conditioners where its skin-compatible profile supports stable oil-in-water formulations.

Ricinoleic acid is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid, typically derived from the saponification and acidulation of castor oil. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades.

Purity levels commonly range from 80% to 95%+ depending on the application. Bulk liquid supply in drums and ISO tanks is standard for industrial procurement and large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Geranial
description:
Geranial (CAS 141-27-5 ), also known commercially as trans-citral or lemonal, is the trans-isomer of citral and the primary contributor to the intense lemon character found in citral mixtures.

It functions as a key aroma chemical and flavoring agent, and serves as a synthetic precursor in the production of vitamins, ionones, and other fragrance compounds.

In flavor formulations, geranial delivers a sharp, fresh citrus note used in beverages, confectionery, and citrus-type flavor blends where high-impact lemon character is required.

Fragrance manufacturers use it as a building block for ionones and pseudoionones, which underpin violet and woody fragrance families across fine perfumery and functional products.

In personal care, it contributes to citrus-forward scent profiles in soaps, shampoos, and lotions. The pharmaceutical and nutraceutical industries source it as an intermediate.

It is used specifically in the synthesis of Vitamin A and beta-carotene. Geranial is supplied as a pale yellow liquid, typically as part of citral mixtures or in isolated isomer form.

Standard commercial grades include technical and fragrance-grade specifications, with high-purity isolates available for pharmaceutical synthesis applications.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities suited to industrial fragrance and synthesis operations, ensuring stability and quality for diverse manufacturing needs.

Diethyl adipate ( CAS 141-28-6 ), commonly abbreviated as DEA, is a diester ester used across cosmetic, food, and industrial formulations as a solvent, plasticizer, and emollient carrier.

In personal care, DEA functions as an emollient and solvent carrier in skin creams, hair oils, and color cosmetics, improving spreadability without leaving a heavy or greasy residue on the skin.

The food industry uses it as a flavoring agent and solvent for flavor concentrates, particularly in applications requiring an ester with a mild, fruity character for specific aromatic profiles.

In lubricant formulations, it serves as a synthetic base fluid or co-solvent in metalworking fluids and light-duty lubricants where biodegradability is a primary formulation requirement for the user.

It also acts as a plasticizer solvent in specialty coatings and polymer processing where low-temperature flexibility is needed. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing.

name: Butyl acrylate
description:
Butyl acrylate (CAS 141-32-2 ), commonly abbreviated as BA, is a reactive acrylic monomer used as a foundational building block in polymer synthesis. It enables formulators to tune the flexibility, adhesion, and film-forming characteristics of the final polymer across a broad range of industrial end products.

In adhesives and pressure-sensitive labels, BA is copolymerized with other acrylates to control tack and peel strength. Coatings manufacturers incorporate it into emulsion polymers for architectural and industrial paints, where it contributes to film flexibility at low temperatures.

Sealant and elastomer producers use BA-based copolymers to achieve durable, weather-resistant joints in construction and automotive assembly. name: Monoethanolamine
description:
Monoethanolamine ( CAS 141-43-5 ), commonly abbreviated as MEA and also known as Olamine in cosmetic and pharmaceutical contexts, is a bifunctional compound combining amine and alcohol groups.

It serves as a pH regulator, surfactant intermediate, and gas treatment agent across multiple industries. Its ability to absorb acidic gases and neutralize formulations makes it a high-volume industrial chemical.

Demand is high across refining, personal care, and water treatment sectors. In natural gas and refinery operations, MEA is the active absorbent in amine gas sweetening units, selectively removing H₂S and CO₂ from process streams.

Personal care formulators use it to neutralize carbomer-based gels and adjust pH in creams, lotions, and hair products. In water treatment, MEA functions as a corrosion inhibitor and pH buffer in boiler and cooling water systems.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an alkalizing agent in topical and oral formulations, where controlled pH stability is a critical quality parameter. MEA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 99% purity.

name: Sodium ethoxide
description:
Sodium ethoxide (CAS 141-52-6 ), also sold as sodium ethylate, is a strong alkoxide base used as a catalyst and reagent across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing.

NaOEt drives condensation, cyclization, and transesterification reactions where controlled basicity and reactivity are critical to process efficiency and high-quality chemical output.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, sodium ethoxide catalyzes the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients including barbiturates, sulfonamides, and vitamin B1, where precise reaction control affects yield.

Agrochemical producers use it as a base catalyst in the synthesis of herbicides and pesticide intermediates. In biodiesel production, sodium ethylate is the preferred transesterification catalyst.

It converts triglycerides to fatty acid ethyl esters, offering faster reaction rates than sodium hydroxide in anhydrous conditions. Specialty chemical formulators also apply it in Claisen condensations.

Sodium ethoxide is supplied as a solution in ethanol, typically at 20–21% concentration, and as a dry powder for moisture-sensitive applications to ensure maximum stability and performance.

The solution grade is the most commercially prevalent form, favored for ease of handling in large-scale continuous processes. Dry powder grades are available for laboratory and pharmaceutical applications.

These powder grades are ideal for processes requiring anhydrous conditions. Our material meets rigorous industrial specifications to ensure consistent results across all manufacturing sectors.

name: Sodium formate
description:
Sodium formate (CAS 141-53-7 ), also sold as E237 , is the sodium salt of formic acid produced at industrial scale for use across chemical processing, food, and energy sectors.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, reducing agent, and preservative depending on the application. Procurement demand spans both technical and food-grade supply chains.

In oil and gas drilling, sodium formate brines are used as high-density completion and workover fluids that protect reservoir formations without solids. The leather and textile industries rely on it.

It is used as a buffering agent in chrome tanning baths and dyeing processes to control pH and improve fixation uniformity. As E237, it is approved for use in food applications as a preservative.

In pharmaceutical and chemical synthesis, it acts as a reducing agent and catalyst precursor, particularly in transfer hydrogenation reactions. Sodium formate is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade (E237-compliant), technical grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting BP or Ph. Eur. specifications for industrial use.

Bulk supply is available in bags or bulk containers, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher for industrial applications. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing sectors.

name: Ethyl acetate
description:
Ethyl acetate (CAS 141-78-6 ), commonly abbreviated as EtOAc, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across printing, pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturing. Approved as E1504 for food applications, it also functions as a flavoring agent with FEMA 2414 designation.

In flexible packaging and gravure printing, EtOAc is a primary solvent for nitrocellulose and polyurethane-based inks. Its evaporation rate directly affects print quality and line speed in high-volume industrial operations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it for API extraction, recrystallization, and tablet coating processes. It is preferred as a low-residue solvent with broad regulatory acceptance across global markets and manufacturing standards.

In food and beverage production, it contributes a characteristic fruity note to confectionery, baked goods, and alcoholic beverages. These applications require precise dosing at controlled usage levels to ensure flavor consistency.

Nail care and cosmetic formulations use it as a fast-drying carrier solvent in lacquers and polish removers. Its ability to dissolve resins quickly makes it an essential component in modern beauty and personal care products.

Ethyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tankers. Standard commercial grades include technical, food-grade ( FCC ), and pharmaceutical-grade ( BP / USP ), ensuring compliance with industry requirements.

Purity levels typically range from 99.0% to 99.9% depending on the specific needs of the client. Grade selection is driven by end-use regulatory requirements, particularly for food contact and pharmaceutical applications.

Personal care formulators use it as a pH adjuster and mild preservative-boosting agent in skin care products. Controlled acidity supports formulation stability while maintaining the efficacy of active ingredients in various cosmetic applications.

This enables ambient-cure systems in waterborne architectural and industrial coatings. Food manufacturers use it as a flavoring ingredient to impart butter, fruit, and rum-like notes in baked goods.

It is also utilized in confectionery and beverages. In personal care formulations, it contributes fragrance character to creams, lotions, and rinse-off products for various consumer applications.

Pharmaceutical and agrochemical synthesis also draws on EAA as a building block for heterocyclic intermediates and active ingredient production. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

name: Coco glucoside
description:
Coco glucoside (CAS 141464-42-8 ) is a mild, plant-derived nonionic surfactant produced from coconut fatty alcohols and glucose. Known in trade as decyl glucoside, it is a preferred ingredient in rinse-off and leave-on formulations.

This material is selected where gentle cleansing with low irritation potential is a sourcing priority. In personal care, it functions as the primary or co-surfactant in baby shampoos, facial cleansers, and body washes.

It delivers stable foam with minimal disruption to skin barrier formulations. It pairs effectively with anionic surfactants to boost foam volume and moderate harshness, a combination standard in sulfate-free shampoo development.

In household and institutional cleaning products, it contributes degreasing performance in surface sprays and hand dishwashing liquids. This is particularly useful where biodegradability is a strict formulation requirement.

Food-contact surface sanitizers and produce wash concentrates also utilize this surfactant for its cleaning efficacy. It performs well under regulatory frameworks that restrict synthetic surfactant residues in food environments.

The product is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid, typically as an aqueous solution at 50–70% active content. Technical and cosmetic grades are available to meet various industrial needs.

Cosmetic-grade material meets COSMOS and ECOCERT certification criteria relevant to natural and organic product lines. It remains a versatile choice for manufacturers seeking sustainable and effective surfactant solutions.

name: Humic acid
description:
Humic acid (CAS 1415-93-6 ), also referred to as HA, is a naturally derived organic acid extracted from leonardite, lignite, or peat. It functions as a chelating agent, pH buffer, and soil conditioner across agriculture and water treatment industries.

In crop nutrition programs, HA chelates micronutrients such as iron, zinc, and manganese, improving their uptake efficiency and reducing fertilizer lock-up in alkaline soils. Liquid and soluble powder formulations are applied as soil drenches or foliar sprays.

These applications stimulate root development and enhance nutrient retention in the rhizosphere. In water treatment, humic acid acts as a coagulation and flocculation aid, helping to aggregate suspended solids and organic matter for easier removal.

It also serves in pH regulation applications where buffering capacity is needed to stabilize process water or irrigation inputs. Humic acid is supplied as a dry powder, granules, flakes, and concentrated liquid for various industrial uses.

Standard grades include technical-grade soluble powder, typically 50 to 90 percent humic acid content, and agricultural-grade formulations optimized for fertigation or dry broadcast application. These products meet rigorous industrial requirements.

Solubility and active content vary by source material and extraction method, so buyers typically specify minimum humic acid percentage. This is often requested alongside potassium humate or sodium humate salt form where applicable.

name: Magnesium sulfate monohydrate
description:
Magnesium sulfate monohydrate (CAS 14168-73-1 ), also designated E518 , is an inorganic magnesium salt supplying both magnesium and sulfate ions across food, agricultural, and industrial applications.

It functions primarily as a mineral supplement, pH buffer, and nutrient source in formulations where controlled water content is critical compared to the heptahydrate form.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it acts as an acidity regulator and magnesium fortification agent in products such as sports drinks, infant formula, and functional foods.

Breweries use it to adjust sulfate levels in process water, directly influencing mineral profile and flavor development in finished beer. In agriculture, it supplies magnesium to correct soil deficiencies.

It is incorporated into foliar sprays and compound fertilizer blends. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient and mineral source in tablet and oral supplement formulations.

This is particularly useful where moisture-sensitive processing demands a lower-hydrate form. The product is supplied as a white powder or granule for various industrial requirements.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E518-compliant), USP / BP pharmaceutical grade, and technical grade for agricultural and industrial use.

It functions as a mild anionic surfactant, delivering cleansing, emulsification, and foam modulation across a range of finished products. In skin cleansing bars and syndet formulations, it contributes gentle lather.

This surfactant offers reduced irritation potential compared to conventional soap bases, which is a key consideration for sensitive skin product lines. Body washes and facial cleansers incorporate it to emulsify sebum.

The material effectively removes rinse-off residues while maintaining skin feel. In home care and industrial cleaning concentrates, it supports degreasing performance and dispersion of oils in aqueous systems.

Shampoo and conditioning cleanser formulators also use it to balance foam profile and improve compatibility with co-surfactant blends. It is typically supplied as a paste or liquid for easy handling.

name: Bis(2-ethylhexyl) maleate
description:
Bis(2-ethylhexyl) maleate (CAS 142-16-5 ), commonly known as dioctyl maleate or DOM, is a reactive ester monomer used across polymer and coating industries. It functions simultaneously as a copolymerizable building block and an internal plasticizer.

This dual functionality allows formulators to modify flexibility and processability directly within the polymer backbone rather than through post-blending. In acrylic and vinyl copolymer systems, DOM is incorporated to reduce glass transition temperature.

It improves film flexibility in coatings, pressure-sensitive adhesives, and sealants. Printing ink formulators use it as a reactive diluent that lowers viscosity during processing while becoming chemically bound into the final resin.

This chemical bonding avoids the migration issues associated with conventional solvents. In PVC and specialty elastomer compounding, it acts as a reactive plasticizer that resists extraction and improves long-term retention.

Adhesive manufacturers targeting demanding substrates also use DOM to tune tack and peel strength without sacrificing cohesive integrity. It is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities for industrial use.

Bulk tanker options are available for high-volume buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 98% or above to ensure consistent performance in manufacturing.

Suppliers may offer material conforming to monomer-grade specifications where low color and controlled acid value are required. These standards are essential for high-quality polymerization applications and specialty resin production.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into lotions, creams, and cleansers for its dual role as an emulsifier and skin-conditioning humectant. In cosmetic systems, it modifies surface wetting behavior, improving spreadability and texture.

description:

It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and cleaning agent, enabling stable formulations and effective soil removal across a range of process conditions for various industries.

In textile and leather processing, SOS acts as a wetting and scouring agent, improving dye penetration and removing oils or finishes from fiber surfaces before treatment.

name: Monosodium glutamate
description:
Monosodium glutamate ( CAS 142-47-2 ), commonly known as MSG or E621 , is the sodium salt of glutamic acid produced through fermentation for use as a flavor enhancer in food manufacturing.

It amplifies savory, umami taste profiles, allowing formulators to reduce sodium content while maintaining or improving perceived flavor intensity. MSG is a primary seasoning ingredient in processed foods.

It is used in instant noodles, soups, snack seasonings, sauces, and ready meals, where it boosts palatability at low use levels. In meat processing and marinades, it enhances savory depth.

It also helps mask off-notes from preservation ingredients. Personal care formulators incorporate sodium glutamate as a humectant and buffering agent in skin conditioning products.

Its moisture-retention function supports formulation stability. It also serves as a pH buffer in fermentation media and certain food processing applications requiring controlled acidity.

MSG is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules, with particle size variants available to suit different blending and dissolution requirements for various industries.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications, with purity typically at 99% or higher. Bulk supply is available in bags and supersacks.

Some suppliers offer technical-grade material for non-food industrial applications. This versatile chemical remains a staple in global food production and industrial chemical formulation.

name: Hexanoic acid
description:
Hexanoic acid (CAS 142-62-1 ), also known as caproic acid, is a short-chain fatty acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. Recognized under FEMA 2559 , it functions as a flavoring agent and pH regulator.

This versatile chemical serves as a preservative and a precursor to ester synthesis. In food and beverage production, it contributes characteristic cheesy, goat-like flavor notes and acts as an acidulant in flavor formulations.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as a starting material for synthesizing medium-chain triglycerides and capric/caprylic acid esters. It is essential for high-purity chemical synthesis and processing.

In personal care formulations, it supports emulsification and acts as a pH modifier in creams, cleansers, and conditioning products. It also serves as a catalyst precursor and ligand in organometallic chemistry.

These properties make it relevant to specialty chemical and polymer processing applications. Hexanoic acid is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities for industrial use.

Food-grade material meeting FEMA and FCC specifications is available for flavoring applications. Technical-grade material covers industrial and synthesis uses across various manufacturing sectors.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply conforming to USP or Ph.Eur. standards is also commercially available for regulated manufacturing. This ensures compliance with international quality and safety protocols.

Agricultural formulations use it as a fungicide and algaecide active ingredient, particularly in treatments targeting mold, algae, and microbial growth on surfaces or in water systems.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it into products where controlled copper ion activity supports preservation or color effects in various specialized applications.

In mining and metal processing, it acts as a reagent in electroplating baths and surface treatment processes to deposit or condition copper layers for industrial components.

The material is supplied as a blue-green crystalline powder or monohydrate crystals. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% upward.

As a catalyst precursor, it is used in polymerization and esterification reactions, particularly in the production of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and other polyesters. In food processing, it serves as an acidity regulator and mineral supplement in fortified products and functional beverages.

Magnesium acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, typically in the tetrahydrate form. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade material to suit different application requirements.

It helps reduce brittleness in films and sealant formulations. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into emollient systems, where it functions as a skin-conditioning carrier for actives and pigments.

Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and lubricating agent during fiber treatment and finishing operations. In metalworking, it serves as a base fluid or additive component.

name: Heptane
description:
Heptane (CAS 142-82-5 ), also known as n-Heptane, is a straight-chain aliphatic hydrocarbon solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, industrial processing, and laboratory applications.

Its controlled evaporation rate and low polarity make it a preferred solvent for extraction, cleaning, and reaction processes where residue-free performance is critical for high-end production.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, heptane is used as a recrystallization solvent and reaction medium for active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis, where low residual solvent limits are tightly regulated.

Rubber and polymer producers use it to dissolve and process elastomers, control polymerization reactions, and prepare adhesive formulations for various industrial and commercial bonding applications.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a fast-evaporating carrier solvent in gravure inks and surface coatings. Analytical and calibration laboratories rely on n-heptane as a primary reference standard.

It is used for octane rating tests and as a mobile phase component in normal-phase chromatography. Heptane is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities.

Established grades include technical, reagent, HPLC, and pharmaceutical-grade. High-purity anhydrous grades are available for moisture-sensitive synthesis applications and specialized chemical research.

Dipropylamine (CAS 142-84-7 ) is a secondary aliphatic amine used as a chemical intermediate and functional additive across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and industrial manufacturing. It acts as a pH regulator, corrosion inhibitor, and reactive building block in synthesis processes.

In agrochemical production, this compound serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of herbicide salts and active ingredient formulations, particularly for glyphosate-based products. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic intermediate for drug compounds.

It also serves as a buffering agent in active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) processing. In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor additive, protecting metal surfaces in cutting fluids and industrial lubricants.

Polymer and plastics processing also draws on its amine reactivity for catalyst systems and curing agent preparation. This versatility makes it an essential component in modern chemical manufacturing and material science applications.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in standard bulk packaging including drums and IBC containers, with isotank options available for larger volumes. It is commercially available in technical grade, suited to industrial synthesis.

name: Sodium decyl sulfate
description:
Sodium decyl sulfate ( CAS 142-87-0 ) is an anionic surfactant used across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning applications. It delivers controlled foaming, emulsification, and surface-active performance in formulations.

This chemical is often preferred in formulations where a mid-chain sulfate ester is required over longer-chain alternatives. In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in shampoos and body washes.

It is particularly effective in facial cleansers where a milder foam profile is required for sensitive skin. Textile processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform dye penetration.

The product is also essential for soil removal from fiber substrates during industrial manufacturing. In leather processing, it supports degreasing baths where consistent emulsification of natural fats is critical.

This ensures high-quality hide preparation for various leather goods. Paper manufacturers apply it as a dispersing agent to improve fiber distribution and surface uniformity during the pulp processing stage.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution. It is typically available at concentrations of 30 to 35 percent active matter depending on the specific application needs.

Technical and cosmetic-grade material are the most commonly traded specifications in the global market. Buyers should confirm active content and sodium sulfate levels when evaluating lots for formulation use.

It is also important to verify the pH range to ensure compatibility with other ingredients. Proper testing ensures the surfactant meets the necessary performance standards for industrial and consumer products.

name: Lauryl methacrylate
description:
Lauryl methacrylate (CAS 142-90-5 ), also known as dodecyl methacrylate and abbreviated as LMA, is a long-chain alkyl ester monomer used to build polymer systems requiring flexibility and hydrophobicity.

It functions as a reactive building block in copolymer synthesis across lubricant, personal care, and polymer manufacturing sectors. It is valued for its ability to provide low glass transition temperatures.

In lubricant additive manufacturing, LMA is copolymerized to produce viscosity index improvers and pour point depressants. These additives keep engine and industrial oils performing across wide temperature ranges.

Personal care formulators incorporate LMA-based polymers into film-forming agents for hair fixatives and skin adhesives. It is also used in water-resistant cosmetic coatings for improved durability.

In plastics and polymer production, it is used to modify acrylic copolymers, improving flexibility and surface properties. This makes it ideal for high-performance coatings, adhesives, and sealants.

Its long alkyl chain also makes it suitable for producing oil-soluble polymers used in metalworking fluid formulations. Lauryl methacrylate is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid for industrial use.

The product is typically stabilized with a polymerization inhibitor such as MEHQ for safe handling and storage. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity levels commonly at 98% or higher.

Bulk quantities are offered in drums and IBC totes, with tanker supply available for large-volume industrial buyers. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for all manufacturing needs.

Isopropyl palmitate (CAS 142-91-6 ), commonly abbreviated as IPP and sold under trade names such as Wickenol 111, Unimate IPP, and Tegosoft P, is a synthetic ester of isopropyl alcohol and palmitic acid.

It is frequently found in creams, lotions, lip products, and color cosmetics, where it improves skin feel without a greasy residue. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into topical drug delivery systems.

These applications include ointments and transdermal patches, where it acts as a carrier that enhances active penetration and formulation spreadability. In hair care, it conditions and adds gloss to treatments.

Industrial and metalworking formulators use IPP as a lubricant base and carrier in cutting fluids and release agents. It is preferred where low viscosity and good surface wetting are required for the process.

Isopropyl palmitate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter conforming to USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. standards.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with cosmetic and pharma grades being the most commercially active. This versatile ester remains a staple for formulators seeking high purity and consistent performance.

name: Hexyl acetate
description:
Hexyl acetate (CAS 142-92-7 ), also identified by FEMA 2565 , is a synthetic ester used commercially as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient. It delivers a characteristic fresh, fruity note that makes it a target compound for flavor houses.

This aroma chemical is predominantly used to replicate apple and pear notes in various industrial applications. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to build or reinforce fruit flavor profiles in confectionery and baked goods.

It is also a staple in beverages and chewing gum formulations. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into fine fragrances, body care products, and household products where a light, fresh-fruity topnote is required for the consumer experience.

In personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning emollient and carrier in formulations such as serums and leave-on treatments. Its low viscosity supports even distribution across the skin surface during application.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a crosslinker to improve flexibility and weathering resistance in structural bonds exposed to UV or moisture cycling during long-term outdoor exposure.

In composite and casting resin systems, it extends epoxy networks with reduced yellowing, particularly relevant for clear or light-colored end products requiring high aesthetic standards over time.

Building and construction applications include flooring systems and grouts where its aliphatic structure supports long-term color stability under UV exposure in commercial and residential settings.

name: Flufenacet
description:
Flufenacet (CAS 142459-58-3 ), also known by its development code FOE 5043, is a selective herbicide used in commercial agriculture to control grass and broadleaf weeds in cereal and oilseed crops.

It inhibits very-long-chain fatty acid synthesis in target plants, making it effective as a pre-emergence and early post-emergence soil treatment for various agricultural applications.

Flufenacet is primarily applied in winter wheat, winter barley, and oilseed rape to suppress problematic grass weeds such as blackgrass and ryegrass where resistance has reduced options.

In maize production, it controls annual grasses and certain broadleaf species when applied to the soil surface before crop emergence to ensure optimal yield and crop health.

Formulators combine it with partners such as diflufenican or metribuzin to broaden the weed control spectrum and reduce resistance selection pressure in intensive farming systems.

It is also registered in potato and soybean cropping systems in select markets, where soil-applied weed management is a standard agronomic practice for professional growers.

Flufenacet is supplied as a technical-grade active ingredient for formulation into suspension concentrates (SC) and oil dispersions (OD) for industrial agricultural use.

Standard technical purity typically meets requirements for commercial herbicide manufacturing. Packaged quantities range from drum to bulk supply depending on formulation volumes required.

name: Capryloyl glycine
description:
Capryloyl glycine (CAS 14246-53-8 ), also known as 2-octanamidoacetic acid, is an amino acid-derived surfactant produced by condensing caprylic acid with glycine. It functions as a mild surface-active agent with buffering and antimicrobial-boosting properties.

This makes it a preferred ingredient in rinse-off and leave-on formulations where skin compatibility is a priority. In personal care, it is used in facial cleansers, shampoos, and micellar waters to deliver gentle cleansing.

The ingredient supports the skin's natural pH balance and acts as a sebum-regulating agent in anti-acne and oily-skin formulations. It is often paired with other actives to enhance their overall efficacy in topical applications.

In deodorant and antiperspirant products, it contributes to odor control by limiting bacterial proliferation on the skin surface. Food-contact and oral care applications also utilize its buffering capacity and surface activity.

It is frequently found in toothpastes and mouthwash formulations due to its functional versatility. Capryloyl glycine is commercially supplied as a white to off-white powder for industrial and laboratory use.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at or above 98%. The material is sourced to meet the quality requirements of major regional cosmetic regulatory frameworks including EU and US markets.

name: Phosphate
description:
Phosphate (CAS 14265-44-2 ) is the trivalent anion that forms the functional basis of a broad family of inorganic phosphate salts used across food processing, agriculture, water treatment, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Supplied commercially as sodium, potassium, calcium, and ammonium salt forms, it delivers pH buffering, chelation, and stabilization functions that are specified by grade and counterion depending on the application.

In food and beverage processing, phosphate salts regulate acidity, sequester metal ions that cause oxidative rancidity, and extend shelf life in meat, dairy, and bakery products.

Fertilizer and feed manufacturers rely on phosphate compounds as the primary source of bioavailable phosphorus for crop nutrition and animal diet supplementation for various livestock.

Water treatment operations use phosphate dosing to inhibit scale formation and corrosion in distribution pipelines and industrial cooling systems to maintain infrastructure integrity.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators source specific phosphate salts as buffering agents in injectable solutions, oral dosage forms, and mineral supplement blends for patient health.

Phosphate is supplied through its salt derivatives, most commonly as powder, granule, or solution. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , Ph. Eur. , and technical grade.

The appropriate specification is determined by the counterion and end-use sector. Buyers typically source by specifying both the cation and the phosphate ratio such as mono-, di-, or tribasic.

name: Zinc glycinate
description:
Zinc glycinate (CAS 14281-83-5 ), also supplied as zinc bisglycinate, is an amino acid-chelated zinc mineral in which zinc is coordinated with glycine for enhanced bioavailability compared to inorganic zinc salts.

It is used across nutraceutical, feed, and cosmetic manufacturing where stable, bioavailable zinc delivery is a formulation priority. In dietary supplements, it is the preferred zinc source for gastrointestinal tolerability.

Absorption efficiency makes it a key product differentiator in functional foods. Animal feed producers incorporate it as an organic trace mineral to support immune function and growth performance in livestock and aquaculture species.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it functions as a skin-conditioning active and mild preservative booster. It is commonly found in creams, serums, and anti-acne products to improve skin health.

Agricultural applications include foliar sprays and soil amendments where chelated zinc corrects micronutrient deficiencies. It performs more effectively than sulfate alternatives in various environmental conditions.

Zinc glycinate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Standard grades include food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with some manufacturers offering USP or Ph. Eur. -aligned material.

Zinc content typically ranges from 20–30% in most commercial batches. Buyers should confirm the chelation ratio and elemental zinc assay when evaluating specific supplier technical data sheets.

Ethylenediaminetetra(methylenephosphonic acid) (CAS 1429-50-1 ), commonly known as EDTMP , is a phosphonate chelating agent used across industrial water treatment, oilfield chemistry, and process industries.

It binds calcium, magnesium, iron, and other metal ions to prevent scale formation and inhibit corrosion in high-temperature, high-hardness water systems. In water treatment and cooling water systems, it controls calcium carbonate scale.

The chemical effectively manages calcium sulfate scale deposition, extending equipment service life in boilers and heat exchangers. Oilfield operators use it as a scale inhibitor and corrosion control additive in injection water.

It is also utilized in produced water handling to maintain system integrity. In textile and paper processing, it sequesters hardness ions and trace metals that would otherwise interfere with bleaching and dyeing operations.

Coatings and cleaning formulations incorporate this agent to stabilize peroxide-based systems and prevent metal-catalyzed decomposition. This ensures the longevity and effectiveness of various industrial chemical formulations.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 20–50%, and is also available in solid form for applications requiring dry blending or concentrated dosing for specific needs.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to industrial water treatment and oilfield end uses. Purity and active content are the primary quality parameters buyers should confirm.

name: Potassium orthovanadate
description:
Potassium orthovanadate (CAS 14293-78-8 ), also referenced commercially as tripotassium vanadate, is an inorganic vanadium salt used primarily as a catalyst and catalyst precursor in industrial chemical processes.

It delivers a soluble, high-purity source of vanadium in applications where controlled reactivity and precise vanadium loading are required. In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for vanadium-based oxidation catalysts.

These catalysts are used in sulfuric acid production and selective catalytic reduction (SCR) systems. The mining and metals sector uses it in hydrometallurgical processing, where vanadium compounds support leaching and recovery operations.

This is particularly important for vanadium pentoxide production. Research and specialty chemical producers use it to prepare supported vanadium catalysts on oxide carriers for oxidative dehydrogenation and other gas-phase reactions.

It also appears in electrochemical research contexts, particularly in studies related to vanadium redox flow battery electrolyte development. Potassium orthovanadate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

It is available in technical and high-purity reagent grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99.9%+ depending on the intended application. Packaging is offered in laboratory-scale quantities.

Bulk industrial lots are also available for catalyst producers and chemical manufacturers. This ensures a reliable supply chain for large-scale industrial operations requiring consistent chemical performance and high purity standards.

name: Oleyl alcohol
description:
Oleyl alcohol (CAS 143-28-2 ), also supplied under trade designations such as Witcohol 85 and Witcohol 90, is a long-chain fatty alcohol derived from oleic acid. It functions primarily as an emollient, emulsifier, carrier solvent, and surface-active agent across personal care and industrial manufacturing.

In cosmetics and personal care, it conditions skin and hair in creams, lotions, and conditioning rinses by reducing moisture loss and improving spreadability. Textile processors use it as a softening and lubricating agent during fiber finishing.

This chemical improves handle and reduces friction in yarn and fabric production. In printing inks and coatings, it acts as a solvent carrier and wetting agent that aids pigment dispersion and controls viscosity for better application.

Leather treatment formulations rely on it to penetrate and soften hides, improving flexibility and surface uniformity. Oleyl alcohol is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid, suitable for various industrial and commercial processes.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial applications and cosmetic or high-purity grades meeting specifications relevant to personal care manufacturing. These grades ensure consistency across different production batches.

Typical purity specifications range from approximately 85% to 90%+ oleyl alcohol content, reflecting the Witcohol-grade designations commonly referenced in procurement. This high level of purity is essential for sensitive chemical formulations.

name: Sodium cyanide
description:
Sodium cyanide (CAS 143-33-9 ), also sold under the trade names Cymag and Cyanogran, is an inorganic salt used primarily as a chemical reagent and processing agent across mining, metal finishing, and chemical synthesis.

Its ability to form stable complexes with metals drives its role in extractive and surface treatment processes. In gold and silver mining, it is the primary lixiviant in heap leach and tank leach circuits.

It selectively dissolves precious metals from ore for downstream recovery. Electroplating and metal finishing operations use it as a complexing agent in copper, zinc, and cadmium bath formulations to control deposition quality.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a building block in synthesizing nitrile intermediates and other nitrogen-containing active pharmaceutical ingredients. In organic synthesis, it functions as a cyanide source.

It is used in nucleophilic addition reactions to produce specialty chemicals and polymer precursors. Sodium cyanide is supplied as white briquettes, granules, or pellets, with Cyanogran and Cymag representing established forms.

Technical grade is the standard for mining and industrial applications, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Packaging is available in bulk quantities suited to large-scale industrial procurement.

Handling requirements are governed by strict regulatory frameworks in most jurisdictions. This ensures safety and compliance across the global supply chain for this critical industrial chemical reagent.

name: Zinc Diethyldithiocarbamate
description:
Zinc Diethyldithiocarbamate (CAS 14324-55-1 ), commercially known as ZDEC, is a zinc-based dithiocarbamate compound used as an accelerator, biocide, and fungicide across rubber processing and agriculture.

Its dual function as both a chemical accelerator and a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent makes it relevant across several industrial supply chains and preservation applications.

In rubber and tire manufacturing, ZDEC acts as an ultra-fast vulcanization accelerator, reducing cure times and improving crosslink density in latex and dry rubber compounds.

In agriculture, it serves as an active ingredient in fungicide formulations targeting crop pathogens, particularly in foliar sprays and seed treatments for various crops.

Water treatment and industrial preservation systems use ZDEC as a biocide to control microbial growth in process water, cooling circuits, and specialized industrial coatings.

Textile and leather processing operations apply it as a preservative and antifungal agent to protect finished goods and intermediate materials during storage and transit.

ZDEC is supplied as a white to off-white powder and as a dispersion or emulsion for latex-compatible processing. Standard grades include technical-grade powder and pre-dispersed masterbatch forms.

Purity specifications typically range from 95% to 98% for technical applications, with particle size and dispersion consistency being key procurement parameters for rubber and latex end users.

name: Emtricitabine
description:
Emtricitabine (CAS 143491-57-0 ), also known by the development codes BW-524W91 and 524W91 and abbreviated as FTC, is a synthetic nucleoside analogue used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in antiviral therapy.

It functions as a reverse transcriptase inhibitor, blocking viral replication in HIV and hepatitis B treatment regimens. FTC is the primary API in several approved fixed-dose combination antiretroviral tablets.

In these formulations, it is co-formulated with tenofovir, efavirenz, or integrase inhibitors for once-daily HIV treatment. It is also incorporated into pre-exposure prophylaxis formulations targeting HIV prevention.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers source this material as a key intermediate for producing both branded and generic antiretroviral drug products. Research organizations and contract development manufacturers procure it for development.

It is frequently used for bioequivalence studies and analytical reference standard preparation. Emtricitabine is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial applications.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade quality aligned with USP and Ph. Eur. monograph specifications, supporting both clinical and commercial manufacturing requirements for global distribution.

Bulk API quantities and smaller research-grade lots are both available depending on the procurement stage. This ensures flexibility for laboratories and large-scale pharmaceutical production facilities alike.

name: Disodium lauroamphodiacetate
description:
Disodium lauroamphodiacetate (CAS 14350-97-1 ), commercially known as Miranol H 2M, is an amphoteric surfactant derived from lauric acid used across personal care formulations.

It functions as a mild cleansing, foam-boosting, and conditioning agent compatible with a broad range of ionic surfactant systems. In shampoos and body washes, it enhances foam volume and creaminess.

This surfactant reduces the irritation potential of harsher anionic surfactants like sodium lauryl sulfate. Baby care and sensitive-skin cleansers rely on it specifically for its mildness profile.

It supports effective cleansing without compromising skin or eye tolerance in delicate applications. Facial cleansers and micellar formulations use it to improve emulsification of sebum and light makeup residues.

It also appears in conditioning shampoos and 2-in-1 formats, where its amphoteric character contributes to post-rinse softness. This versatility makes it a staple in modern cosmetic chemistry.

Disodium lauroamphodiacetate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content commonly around 39–40%. It is available in cosmetic/personal care grade meeting industry standards.

Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial-scale production. This ensures reliable supply chains for large-scale manufacturing of personal care products.

name: Sodium oleoyl sarcosinate
description:
Sodium oleoyl sarcosinate (CAS 14351-62-3 ) is an amino acid-derived anionic surfactant built on a sarcosine backbone with an oleic acid chain. It delivers effective cleansing, foaming, and emulsification across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

This chemical is valued for its mildness relative to conventional sulfate-based surfactants. In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in facial cleansers, shampoos, and shaving products.

It generates a stable, dense foam while minimizing skin irritation during use. Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it as a degreasing agent in hard surface cleaners and metal treatment products.

The surfactant helps lift oils and soils from various substrates effectively. Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a wetting and dispersing agent to improve dye penetration and process uniformity.

In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber dispersion and surface treatment steps requiring controlled foaming behavior. Sodium oleoyl sarcosinate is supplied as a liquid or paste, typically at active concentrations of 30% or higher.

Solid or powder forms are available from select producers for applications requiring dry blending or concentrated formulation. Both technical-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are commercially available for industrial use.

Cosmetic grades meet purity requirements for personal care use and sensitive applications. The material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols to ensure stability and performance in final products.

name: 2,2,4-Trimethyl-1,3-pentanediol
description:
2,2,4-Trimethyl-1,3-pentanediol (CAS 144-19-4 ), commonly known as TMPD, is a specialty diol used across coatings, adhesives, and polymer systems. It functions as a coalescing solvent, plasticizer, and rheology modifier.

This chemical helps formulators balance film formation, flexibility, and flow properties in finished products. In waterborne architectural and industrial coatings, it acts as a coalescing agent that improves film formation.

It performs well at low temperatures without the regulatory burden of conventional glycol ethers. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to enhance flexibility and substrate adhesion in polyurethane and acrylic formulations.

In polyester resin synthesis, it serves as a diol monomer that introduces branching to control hardness and flexibility. This ensures compatibility with other resin components during the manufacturing process.

Cleaning product formulators use it as a carrier solvent where low volatility is required. It provides good solvency for organic soils in hard-surface and industrial cleaning concentrates for professional use.

TMPD is supplied as a white crystalline solid or low-melting flake, with liquid form available in heated bulk supply. Standard commercial grades include technical and coatings-grade material with high purity.

The purity is typically at 98% or higher to meet industrial requirements. Packaging options range from drums to bulk isotanks for high-volume coatings and resin producers requiring consistent supply chains.

name: Sodium bicarbonate
description:
Sodium bicarbonate (CAS 144-55-8 ), also known commercially as baking soda, is a mild alkali used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets to regulate pH and leaven baked goods.

It is also used to neutralize acids in process streams. NaHCO3 is one of the most broadly sourced inorganic salts, available from multiple global producers in food and technical grades.

In food manufacturing, it acts as a chemical leavening agent in baked goods, reacting with acidic ingredients to generate CO₂ and produce the desired rise and texture for the final product.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active excipient in antacid formulations and effervescent tablets, where controlled CO₂ release is critical to dosage form performance and efficacy.

In water treatment, it adjusts alkalinity and stabilizes pH in drinking water and process water systems without introducing chloride ions. Personal care formulators incorporate it into toothpastes.

It is also used in bath products and deodorants for its mild abrasive and odor-neutralizing properties. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in a range of particle sizes.

Food-grade material is available to FCC and E500(ii) specifications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is supplied to USP and Ph. Eur. standards for global compliance.

Bulk supply is typically offered in bags, supersacks, and bulk tanker quantities. This ensures that industrial and commercial users receive the appropriate volume for their specific manufacturing needs.
