name: Oxalic acid
description:
Oxalic acid (CAS 144-62-7 ) is a dicarboxylic organic acid used across industrial processing as a reducing agent, chelating agent, and pH regulator. It removes metal ions and mineral deposits from surfaces and process streams.

This chemical is a go-to reagent in cleaning, bleaching, and metal finishing operations. In water treatment and industrial cleaning, it dissolves iron oxide and rust deposits from boilers, heat exchangers, and pipework.

The acid effectively cleans systems without damaging base metals. Textile and paper manufacturers use it as a bleaching and stripping agent to remove discoloration from natural fibers and pulp during production.

Mining and hydrometallurgical operations rely on it to precipitate rare earth elements and other metals from leach solutions. This process is essential for recovering valuable materials during ore processing.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a pH adjuster and chelating agent. It is commonly found in hair bleaching and skin-lightening products to ensure stability and efficacy in the final formula.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with anhydrous and dihydrate forms available. Standard grades include technical, industrial, and pharmaceutical-grade material for various uses.

Purity levels typically range from 99% to 99.6% to meet strict industry requirements. Packaging options span from small bags to bulk quantities, supporting both laboratory-scale and large industrial supply.

name: Tosylchloramide
description:
Tosylchloramide (CAS 144-86-5 ), commercially recognized as Chloramine-T, is an active chlorine-releasing compound used as a biocide, disinfectant, and bleaching agent across industrial and institutional applications.

It delivers controlled oxidative action, making it suitable for processes where precise antimicrobial performance is required without the handling challenges of elemental chlorine. In water treatment, it is used to disinfect potable water.

It is also applied in cooling systems and process water where stable chlorine release over time is preferred to hypochlorite. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reagent for radiolabeling proteins and peptides.

This is particularly critical in iodination procedures for diagnostic compound production. In industrial and institutional cleaning, it is formulated into sanitizers and disinfectants for food-contact surface treatment.

It is also utilized for healthcare facility hygiene and veterinary disinfection. Textile and paper processors apply it as a bleaching agent where controlled whitening without fiber degradation is a requirement.

Tosylchloramide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granules. It is available in technical grade for industrial disinfection and cleaning applications for various global markets.

The material is also available as pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications for regulated manufacturing. Active chlorine content is a key specification buyers should confirm.

This specification directly affects dosing and product performance in final formulations. Proper storage in cool, dry conditions is recommended to maintain the stability and efficacy of the active chlorine content.

name: Scandium triflate
description:
Scandium triflate (CAS 144026-79-9 ), also known as scandium trifluoromethanesulfonate, is a rare earth metal salt valued primarily as a Lewis acid catalyst. It activates a broad range of organic reactions under mild conditions.

Unlike many metal catalysts, it retains activity in aqueous media. This property directly reduces solvent costs and waste in manufacturing processes, making it a sustainable choice for modern chemical production facilities.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, this compound catalyzes Friedel-Crafts alkylations, Diels-Alder cycloadditions, and Mannich reactions. It enables efficient construction of complex intermediates without requiring anhydrous conditions.

Polymer manufacturers use it to initiate ring-opening polymerizations and controlled cationic processes. This allows for precise control over molecular weight distribution in the production of specialty plastics and resins.

In textile and paper processing, it functions as a catalyst for esterification and crosslinking treatments. These applications improve fiber durability and surface performance for high-end industrial materials.

Its application in flame retardant formulation development is emerging. It acts as a catalyst in the synthesis of phosphorus- or halogen-based retardant compounds used in various safety-critical industries.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram commercial lots, with purity grades typically ranging from 95% to 99%+.

High-purity grades suited to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis are the most commercially prevalent offerings. These materials meet rigorous internal quality standards for consistency and performance in sensitive reactions.

name: Dextrose monohydrate
description:
Dextrose monohydrate (CAS 14431-43-7 ) is a hydrated crystalline glucose used as a fermentable sugar, sweetener, and energy source across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing.

Dextrose ( USP ) is the designation most commonly referenced in pharmaceutical procurement and clinical nutrition contexts. In food manufacturing, it functions as a fermentation substrate.

It is used in brewing, baking, and confectionery, where controlled sweetness and browning behavior are process requirements. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a primary excipient in oral solid dosage forms.

It serves as a diluent, binder, or coating sugar, and as the base carbohydrate in IV dextrose solutions and oral rehydration formulations. Sports nutrition producers rely on it as a fast-absorbing source.

It is found in energy drinks, recovery powders, and enteral feeding products. Fermentation industries also use it as a carbon source for antibiotic, amino acid, and enzyme production.

Dextrose monohydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard grades include food-grade, BP , and Ph. Eur. , with anhydrous dextrose available as a separate specification.

This is used where moisture content is critical. Bulk supply is typical in 25 kg bags or bulk sacks, with pharmaceutical grades requiring full documentation including COA and residual solvent profiles.

name: Sodium ferrocyanide decahydrate
description:
Sodium ferrocyanide decahydrate (CAS 14434-22-1 ) is an inorganic iron-cyanide salt supplied in its fully hydrated crystalline form. It functions as a chelating and sequestering agent across food processing, mining, and industrial manufacturing.

Its stability under normal handling conditions makes it suitable for regulated and technical applications alike. In food processing, it is approved as an anti-caking agent in salt and salt substitutes, preventing clumping during storage.

Mining operations use it in metal separation and precipitation processes, where it selectively binds heavy metal ions to aid in ore processing and effluent treatment. This ensures efficient recovery and environmental compliance.

Textile and leather industries apply it in dyeing and finishing processes, where controlled iron complexation helps stabilize color baths. This prevents unwanted oxidation and ensures consistent results across production batches.

In paper manufacturing, it supports process water treatment by sequestering metal ions that would otherwise interfere with bleaching and pulp quality. This helps maintain the brightness and structural integrity of the final paper products.

Sodium ferrocyanide decahydrate is supplied as yellow crystalline powder or granules. Food-grade material is available meeting specifications for use as a direct food additive, ensuring safety and compliance with global standards.

Technical-grade product is also supplied for industrial applications where high-volume processing is required. Buyers should confirm purity levels and moisture content when sourcing for regulated food or mining applications.

name: Trimethyl orthoacetate
description:
Trimethyl orthoacetate ( CAS 1445-45-0 ), also known as 1,1,1-trimethoxyethane and abbreviated as TMOA, is an orthoacid ester used as a reactive intermediate and protecting group reagent in organic synthesis.

In flavor chemistry, it functions as a precursor and acidulant component in controlled-release formulation work. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TMOA acts as an acetyl transfer agent and methoxylation reagent.

This chemical enables selective protection of hydroxyl and carboxyl groups during multi-step API synthesis. Flavor formulators use it to generate acetic acid esters under mild acidic conditions for food applications.

It provides controlled acidulant release in finished food and beverage applications. As a catalyst precursor, it participates in transesterification and condensation reactions where controlled hydrolysis is required.

Its role in preservation-related formulations draws on its ability to release acetic acid derivatives gradually. This process extends active compound stability in the end product for industrial users.

Trimethyl orthoacetate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in purity grades of 97–99% for synthesis applications. Technical and reagent-grade specifications are the most commonly available formats.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is offered by select suppliers to meet API manufacturing requirements. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities through to bulk drum supply for industrial users.

name: Dioleyl phosphate
description:
Dioleyl phosphate (CAS 14450-07-8 ), also known as dioleyl hydrogen phosphate, is a phosphate ester derived from oleyl alcohol used as a functional additive in industrial lubrication and surface treatment.

It combines lubricity with corrosion-inhibiting and surface-modifying properties, making it a practical choice for formulators working across metalworking, textile, and polymer processing applications.

In metalworking fluids and lubricant formulations, it acts as an extreme-pressure and anti-wear additive, forming a protective film on metal surfaces to reduce friction and inhibit corrosion.

Textile and leather processors use it as a fiber lubricant and softening agent, where its surface-active character improves processing performance and reduces fiber-to-metal friction during operations.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as an internal lubricant and processing aid, improving melt flow and reducing die buildup during the manufacturing process.

It is also incorporated into specialty grease and oil formulations where both lubricity and metal surface protection are required simultaneously for high-performance industrial equipment.

Dioleyl phosphate is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous oil. It is available in technical grade , which is the standard specification for industrial lubricant and surface treatment applications.

name: Menadione dimethylpyrimidinol bisulfite
description:
Menadione dimethylpyrimidinol bisulfite (CAS 14451-99-1 ), commercially known as Hetrazeen, is a stabilized, water-soluble form of menadione used as a source of vitamin K activity in animal nutrition and pharmaceutical applications.

Its bisulfite complex form improves handling and formulation compatibility compared to free menadione, making it a practical choice for manufacturers requiring a stable K-vitamin source.

In animal feed manufacturing, it is incorporated into premixes and complete feeds to support vitamin K supplementation in poultry, swine, and aquaculture diets for various livestock.

name: Tetrasodium iminodisuccinate
description:
Tetrasodium iminodisuccinate (CAS 144538-83-0 ), commercially known as IDS tetrasodium salt, is a biodegradable chelating agent derived from aspartic acid. It sequesters calcium, magnesium, iron, and other metal ions across a broad pH range.

This versatile chemical prevents scale formation, precipitation, and metal-catalyzed degradation in industrial and consumer formulations. In water treatment, it controls scale and corrosion in cooling towers, boilers, and process water systems.

It is particularly effective where conventional chelants face discharge restrictions. Personal care formulators use it to stabilize emulsions and protect active ingredients from metal ion interference in rinse-off and leave-on products.

Textile and leather processors rely on it to prevent metal-induced dye inconsistencies during dyeing and finishing operations. In agricultural formulations, it functions as a micronutrient carrier for various applications.

It improves the bioavailability of iron and manganese in foliar sprays and fertigation systems. Tetrasodium iminodisuccinate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 30–40% active content, and in dry powder form.

Standard commercial grades meet technical and industrial specifications. Formulation-grade material is available for personal care and agricultural applications, ensuring high performance across diverse sectors.

Buyers should confirm active content, pH, and biodegradability certification when evaluating supply options. This ensures the material meets specific regulatory and performance requirements for the intended industrial use.

name: Phosphatidylserine
description:
Phosphatidylserine (CAS 1446756-47-3 ), commonly abbreviated as PS, is a phospholipid naturally occurring in cell membranes and sourced commercially from soy or sunflower lecithin.

It functions as a bioactive lipid ingredient in nutritional and pharmaceutical formulations targeting cognitive and neurological support. PS is the primary active ingredient in cognitive health supplements.

In capsules, softgels, and functional foods, it is standardized to defined phosphatidylserine content for label claims. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into formulations.

These applications target memory, mental focus, and age-related cognitive decline. Personal care formulators use PS as a membrane-active moisturizing agent in premium skin care products.

Its phospholipid structure supports skin barrier function and ingredient delivery. Biotechnology and cell culture applications rely on PS as a membrane component in liposomal drug delivery systems.

Phosphatidylserine is supplied as a fine powder or oil-based concentrate, with powder forms being the most common for supplement manufacturing. Standard commercial grades are typically standardized.

These grades are available at 20%, 50%, or 70% PS content, derived from soy or sunflower sources. Food-grade and USP -referenced specifications are available for industrial use.

Soy-free sunflower-derived grades are increasingly sought for allergen-sensitive formulations. These high-purity options ensure compliance with modern safety and labeling requirements for global markets.

name: Olmesartan medoxomil

For the treatment of hypertension, it is formulated as a standalone or combination product, commonly paired with amlodipine or hydrochlorothiazide. Generic drug manufacturers source this API to develop bioequivalent products.

This sourcing typically follows patent expiry in key regulated markets. Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) use it in formulation development projects requiring ICH-compliant API characterization.

Stability profiling is a critical component of these projects. Pharmaceutical importers and distributors also source it for supply into regulated markets requiring DMF or CEP documentation support for their filings.

name: Dioctyl succinate
description:
Dioctyl succinate (CAS 14491-66-8 ), also known as dicapryl succinate, is a diester of succinic acid used across industrial formulations as a plasticizer, lubricant, and carrier solvent.

It functions by improving flexibility, reducing friction, or enhancing the solvency of finished formulations depending on the application context. In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a plasticizer.

This material is used to improve flexibility and workability in PVC and similar resin systems. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a carrier solvent or softening agent to adjust viscosity.

These adjustments are made to film properties without compromising adhesion performance. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it contributes lubricity and helps reduce wear at metal contact surfaces.

Automotive applications include its use in specialty lubricants and sealant compounds where ester-based fluids are preferred for thermal stability and compatibility with elastomeric components.

Dioctyl succinate is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in technical grade, suited to industrial plastics, lubricant, and coatings applications. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC totes.

name: Methacryloxypropylmethyldimethoxysilane
description:
Methacryloxypropylmethyldimethoxysilane (CAS 14513-34-9 ), also known commercially as 3-(dimethoxymethylsilyl)propyl methacrylate, is a bifunctional organosilane coupling agent that bridges organic polymer matrices with inorganic substrates.

It carries both a hydrolyzable silane group and a reactive methacrylate group, enabling simultaneous surface bonding and participation in radical polymerization networks for various industrial applications.

In coatings and adhesives, it improves adhesion to glass, metals, and mineral fillers by chemically anchoring the organic binder to the substrate surface. This reduces delamination risk in demanding service conditions.

Sealant and elastomer formulators use it as a crosslinker to build moisture-cure networks with controlled flexibility and durability. It is essential for maintaining structural integrity in harsh environments.

Electronics manufacturers apply it as a surface primer or additive in encapsulants and underfill resins where reliable interfacial adhesion to silicon or ceramic components is critical for performance.

In fiber-reinforced composites and filled polymer systems, it treats filler surfaces to improve dispersion and mechanical integration within the matrix. This leads to enhanced physical properties and stability.

Supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums. Technical-grade material is the primary commercial form, with purity specifications typically at 97% or higher.

description:
Ammonium fumarate (CAS 14548-85-7 ), also known as diammonium fumarate and approved as E368 , is the ammonium salt of fumaric acid used commercially as a pH buffer and acidulant.

It provides controlled acidity adjustment and mild preservative action across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural formulations. In food manufacturing, it functions as a buffering agent in baked goods and beverages.

Stable pH control directly affects shelf life and product consistency in processed foods. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an excipient to regulate pH in oral solid dosage forms and as a counterion in salt formation.

In animal feed applications, it acts as an acidifier to manage gastrointestinal pH, supporting feed hygiene and palatability. Agricultural formulations incorporate it as a buffering component in liquid fertilizers.

It is also used in crop protection products to stabilize solution pH during mixing and application. Ammonium fumarate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules for various industrial uses.

Food-grade material conforming to E368 specifications is the most commonly traded form. Technical-grade is available for agricultural and industrial applications where high purity is not the primary requirement.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply is sourced to meet compendial purity requirements where excipient documentation is required. This ensures the material meets the necessary safety standards for medical applications.

name: Magnesium sulphate monohydrate
description:
Magnesium sulphate monohydrate (CAS 14567-64-7 ), commercially known as Kieserite, is an inorganic magnesium salt used across agriculture and industrial processing. It delivers a concentrated, slow-releasing source of both magnesium and sulphur to crops.

This chemical is essential for industrial systems where precise nutrient or ion dosing is required. In agriculture, Kieserite is applied directly to soil or blended into compound fertilizers to correct magnesium and sulphur deficiencies.

It is commonly used for cereals, oilseed rape, sugar beet, and grassland. Its lower water content compared to heptahydrate grades makes it preferred for dry fertilizer blending where moisture-stable granules are critical.

These stable granules are essential to product shelf life and handling during transport. In water treatment, it functions as a source of magnesium ions for pH buffering and supports coagulation and flocculation processes.

It is utilized in both municipal and industrial effluent systems for effective treatment. Feed-grade applications also exist, where it supplements magnesium in compound animal feeds for livestock nutrition programs.

Magnesium sulphate monohydrate is supplied as granules or powder, with granular Kieserite being the dominant commercial form. Standard grades include technical, feed-grade, and fertilizer-grade specifications.

name: Dimethyl isophthalate
description:
Dimethyl isophthalate ( CAS 1459-93-4 ), commonly abbreviated as DMIP, is a diester monomer used as a reactive building block in the synthesis of high-performance polyesters, polyurethanes, and specialty resins.

It introduces meta-oriented ester linkages into polymer backbones, improving flexibility, thermal stability, and compatibility with downstream formulation requirements for industrial applications.

In coatings and powder coatings, DMIP is incorporated into polyester resin synthesis to balance hardness and flexibility in the final film. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a co-monomer.

This helps to tune the mechanical properties of polyester-based systems, particularly where elongation and adhesion need to be controlled. In engineering plastics and fiber production, DMIP modifies crystallinity.

It alters processing behavior in copolyester systems, offering an alternative to terephthalate-based monomers where amorphous or lower-melting profiles are required for specific manufacturing needs.

It also functions as a plasticizer intermediate in specialty elastomer compounding. Dimethyl isophthalate is supplied as a white crystalline solid or flake for easy handling in production environments.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial forms, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher. Packaging is available in bags and drums suited to bulk polymer and resin manufacturing.

name: Riboflavine monophosphate
description:
Riboflavine monophosphate (CAS 146-17-8 ), also known as Flavin mononucleotide (FMN) and designated E101a in food regulation, is the phosphorylated, water-soluble form of riboflavin used as a colorant and nutrient source.

Its superior solubility compared to riboflavin base makes it the preferred choice where consistent color performance and bioavailability in aqueous systems are required across food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology applications.

In food and beverage manufacturing, E101a delivers a stable yellow-orange hue to liquid products such as soft drinks, dairy alternatives, and sauces where riboflavin's limited solubility would otherwise cause dispersion issues.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate FMN into injectable vitamin preparations and oral supplements where a water-soluble B2 source is required for both nutrient delivery and regulatory compliance.

In clinical nutrition, it is used in parenteral and enteral formulations where precise dosing of bioavailable riboflavin is critical for patient health and therapeutic outcomes in medical settings.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a coenzyme source in cell culture media and enzymatic assay systems, supporting growth and metabolic functions in various laboratory and industrial processes.

Riboflavine monophosphate is supplied as a sodium salt in powder form, which is the commercially standard presentation for both food and pharmaceutical procurement and distribution channels.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with pharmaceutical supply typically conforming to USP or Ph. Eur. specifications. Purity levels of 98% and above are standard for regulated-market supply.

It participates in Maillard browning reactions to develop characteristic roasted and baked notes. In food production, it is used in bakery, confectionery, and savory flavor formulations where controlled browning and taste development are required.

Fermented beverage and dairy manufacturers incorporate it to influence flavor profile depth in products such as beer, wine, and aged cheeses. In personal care, it functions as a humectant in skin-conditioning formulations like moisturizers and serums.

Its water-binding capacity supports texture and hydration claims in hair care products. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement producers also source it as an active ingredient in amino acid blends targeting collagen synthesis support.

L-Proline is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade and USP / Ph.Eur. grades are the most commercially prevalent, with food-grade material meeting FCC specifications for use in flavoring and nutritional applications.

name: Silver cation
description:
Silver cation (CAS 14701-21-4 ), also referenced as Ag(1+), is the active ionic form of silver responsible for its antimicrobial and catalytic performance across industrial applications. It is generated in solution from silver salt precursors.

This species represents the functionally relevant component in systems where silver's biocidal or oxidative activity is required. In water treatment, it is incorporated into filtration media and disinfection systems to control bacterial growth.

These systems allow for effective microbial control without reliance on chlorine-based chemistries. Mining operations use it as a catalyst in hydrometallurgical processes, particularly in the oxidative leaching of ores to improve metal recovery yields.

Pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturers formulate silver cation-releasing materials into wound care products and antimicrobial coatings. These are used on medical device surfaces where sustained ion release is the primary design objective.

In biotechnology, it is used to control microbial contamination in cell culture environments. It also serves as a selective agent in certain diagnostic assay formats and specialized laboratory research applications.

Silver cation is not supplied as an isolated compound but is sourced through silver salt precursors. Most commonly, these include silver nitrate or silver sulfate, which release the active ion when introduced into a solution.

These precursors are available in technical, reagent, and pharmaceutical grades. Grade selection depends on the downstream application, with USP and Ph.Eur. specifications relevant for healthcare and biotech procurement.

name: Rosuvastatin calcium
description:
Rosuvastatin calcium (CAS 147098-20-2 ), also known by the brand reference Crestor and as rosuvastatin hemicalcium, is a synthetic statin compound used as the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) in cholesterol-lowering medications.

It functions by inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, making it the core ingredient in finished-dose cardiovascular drug products. The primary commercial application is the manufacture of oral solid dosage forms.

These include tablets and film-coated tablets targeting hypercholesterolemia and mixed dyslipidemia. Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source this API to produce bioequivalent formulations following patent expiry of the originator product.

Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) also use it in early-phase and commercial-scale formulation development. Regulatory drug product filings across major markets require API sourced to documented standards.

These markets include FDA, EMA, and ICH-aligned jurisdictions. Rosuvastatin calcium is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications aligned with USP and Ph. Eur.

It is also available in EP and in-house monographs accepted by major regulatory agencies. Standard commercial supply includes defined particle size distributions to support manufacturing processes.

These processes include direct compression or wet granulation. The material is handled according to strict quality protocols to ensure stability and efficacy in the final pharmaceutical application.

name: Zinc dibenzyldithiocarbamate
description:
Zinc dibenzyldithiocarbamate (CAS 14726-36-4 ), commercially known as ZBEC, is a zinc dithiocarbamate accelerator used in rubber vulcanization. It drives efficient sulfur crosslinking at processing temperatures while offering low nitrosamine generation.

This factor is increasingly driving purchasing decisions in rubber compounding. ZBEC is a primary or secondary accelerator in sulfur-cured rubber compounds, including natural rubber, SBR, and EPDM systems used in seals and gaskets.

It is also widely utilized in automotive components. In latex applications, it supports room-temperature or low-temperature vulcanization where conventional thiuram accelerators raise regulatory concerns for manufacturers.

Tire manufacturers and technical rubber goods producers use ZBEC in formulations requiring a cleaner toxicological profile without sacrificing cure rate. It is also used as a secondary accelerator alongside sulfenamides.

This combination helps to boost crosslink density in mechanical rubber goods. Zinc dibenzyldithiocarbamate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Technical and rubber-grade specifications are standard across the market.

Purity levels are typically confirmed by active content assay and melting point. Pre-dispersed masterbatch forms are available from some suppliers to improve handling and dispersion in rubber mixing operations.

name: Polyquaternium 30
description:
Polyquaternium-30 (CAS 147398-77-4 ), commercially available as Mexomere PX, is a cationic conditioning polymer used in rinse-off and leave-on personal care formulations. It delivers film-forming, moisturizing, and rheology-modifying performance across a range of aqueous systems.

In hair care, it deposits a conditioning film on the hair shaft during rinsing, improving combability, softness, and frizz control in shampoos and conditioners. Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and serums where it contributes to a smooth skin feel.

The polymer supports moisture retention and enhances the overall sensory profile of cosmetic products. In textile processing, it modifies fiber surface properties to improve softness and handle during finishing operations.

Paper and leather treatments also utilize its surface-modifying properties to enhance substrate feel and coating adhesion. Polyquaternium-30 is typically supplied as an aqueous solution or liquid dispersion suited for direct incorporation into water-based formulations.

Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to personal care industry requirements. Bulk supply is available in drums and IBCs for industrial-scale procurement and manufacturing needs.

The material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols to ensure stability and performance. Its versatile nature makes it a staple for formulators seeking reliable conditioning and film-forming properties in diverse applications.

name: Azilsartan
description:
Azilsartan (CAS 147403-03-0 ), also referenced under the development code TAK-536, is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the treatment of hypertension.

It serves as the free acid form of the prodrug azilsartan medoxomil, and its role in the pharmaceutical supply chain centers on API manufacturing and finished dosage form development.

Azilsartan is primarily sourced by pharmaceutical manufacturers producing antihypertensive tablet formulations, where it functions as the core active ingredient for various therapeutic applications.

Contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) use it as a reference standard or synthetic intermediate when developing generic equivalents of branded ARB products.

Regulatory submissions for generic antihypertensive drugs require characterized API material, making azilsartan relevant to analytical and QA workflows for global compliance.

Research institutions also procure it for pharmacological studies comparing ARB receptor selectivity and binding profiles to better understand the mechanism of action in patients.

Azilsartan is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade quality aligned with in-house or customer-specified specifications for manufacturing.

The material is typically offered at research, pilot, and commercial scale to support different stages of drug development and large-scale production requirements for the industry.

name: m-xylylenediamine
description:
m-Xylylenediamine (CAS 1477-55-0 ), commercially known as MXDA, is an aromatic diamine used as a reactive building block in polymer synthesis and curing systems. Its two primary amine groups enable it to form durable, high-performance polymer networks.

MXDA is a key monomer in the production of polyamide MXD6, a high-barrier resin used in food packaging films and multilayer bottles where oxygen transmission must be minimized. This makes it essential for modern packaging solutions.

In epoxy systems, it functions as a room-temperature curing agent, producing coatings and adhesives with strong chemical resistance. These are ideal for industrial flooring, pipelines, and protective linings in harsh environments.

The compound also serves as a chain extender and crosslinker in polyurethane and isocyanate-based formulations. These applications target structural adhesives and composite materials requiring high mechanical strength.

In specialty gas barrier packaging, MXDA-based polymers are compounded into blends that extend shelf life. This is particularly important for oxygen-sensitive food and beverage products in the global supply chain.

m-Xylylenediamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard commercial and technical grades. Packaging options typically include drums and IBC containers suited to bulk industrial procurement needs.

Material is available to specifications aligned with polymer-grade and epoxy-grade purity requirements. This ensures consistent performance depending on the specific end application and industrial manufacturing standards.

name: Magnesium glycinate
description:
Magnesium glycinate (CAS 14783-68-7 ), also known as magnesium diglycinate, is a chelated mineral salt combining magnesium with the amino acid glycine. It is used across nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing where enhanced bioavailability and formulation stability are commercial priorities.

In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is a preferred magnesium source for tablets, capsules, and powdered drink mixes where tolerability and absorption profile influence product positioning. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering and stabilizing agent in oral dosage forms sensitive to pH variation.

In food and functional nutrition products, it serves as a mineral fortification ingredient where clean-label amino acid chelate forms are specified. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing serums and skin conditioning products.

Its humectant properties support water retention in the finished formulation, making it a versatile additive for topical applications. Magnesium glycinate is supplied as a white to off-white powder that integrates easily into various production workflows.

Standard grades include food-grade and USP -compliant specifications, with Ph.Eur. -aligned material available for pharmaceutical applications. Bulk quantities are typically offered in fiber drums or multi-layer bags for industrial use.

name: Sodium diethyldithiocarbamate
description:
Sodium diethyldithiocarbamate (CAS 148-18-5 ) is a metal chelating and complexing agent used across water treatment, agriculture, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It binds heavy metal ions with high selectivity, enabling their removal, detection, or controlled use in catalytic systems.

In industrial water treatment, this compound precipitates heavy metals such as copper, nickel, and lead from effluent streams, supporting compliance with discharge limits. Agricultural formulators use it as a precursor or stabilizer in dithiocarbamate-based fungicide systems.

These systems target soil-borne and foliar pathogens effectively. In catalyst preparation, it functions as a metal-complexing ligand to produce well-defined metal sulfide catalysts and nanoparticle precursors for research and specialty chemical production.

Pharmaceutical and biotechnology applications include its use as a chelating reference compound in metal ion studies. It also serves as an active component in experimental antidote formulations for specialized medical research and development.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution, depending on the application and supplier. Standard grades include technical and reagent-grade specifications for various industrial needs.

High-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical and analytical use, often meeting ACS or USP standards. Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply to meet diverse customer requirements.

name: Thiabendazole
description:
Thiabendazole (CAS 148-79-8 ), commonly abbreviated as TBZ and approved as food additive E233 , is a broad-spectrum antifungal agent used across food preservation, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and agricultural crop protection.

It controls mold, rot, and fungal pathogens at low effective concentrations, making it a practical active ingredient for both surface treatments and formulated products in various industrial sectors.

In post-harvest food handling, TBZ is applied as a surface treatment on citrus fruits, bananas, and potatoes to suppress mold and extend shelf life during storage and transit across global supply chains.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in anthelmintic formulations targeting parasitic worm infections in human and veterinary medicine, adhering to strict USP quality standards.

In agriculture, it functions as a systemic fungicide incorporated into seed treatments and turf management programs to protect against soil-borne and foliar fungal diseases throughout the growing season.

TBZ also serves as a catalyst precursor in certain polymerization and polymer stabilization processes, particularly in PVC production, where it enhances the durability and chemical resistance of the final material.

Thiabendazole is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade, pharmaceutical, and technical grades to meet the distinct purity requirements of food and chemical processing.

Bulk supply is standard, with packaging options ranging from kilogram-scale to multi-tonne quantities depending on the specific grade and the logistical requirements of the purchasing organization.

name: Talc
description:

It functions primarily as a filler, lubricant, anti-caking agent, and surface modifier in solid and semi-solid formulations across multiple sectors. In pharmaceuticals, it acts as a glidant and lubricant.

This material improves powder flow and prevents die sticking during tablet compression. Personal care and cosmetics formulators incorporate it into pressed powders and foundations to control texture and absorb moisture.

It is also used to improve slip in body powders. Plastics processors use it as a mineral filler to increase stiffness, reduce cycle times, and lower raw material costs in polypropylene compounds.

In food production, it is approved as an anti-caking agent for coating chewing gum, rice, and dried goods. This prevents clumping during storage and handling while maintaining product integrity.

The product is supplied as a fine white powder in a range of particle sizes and surface treatments. Established grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , Ph. Eur. , and technical grades.

name: Quartz
description:
Quartz (CAS 14808-60-7 ), also sold as Silicon Dioxide or E551 in food-contact and industrial contexts, is a naturally occurring crystalline mineral processed for use across construction and electronics.

It functions primarily as a functional filler, abrasive, and rheology modifier in solid and composite systems. In building and construction, it is compounded into mortars, grouts, and engineered stone slabs.

These applications help to control hardness, dimensional stability, and surface texture. Electronics manufacturers rely on high-purity quartz as a raw material for silicon wafer production and as a filler.

It is frequently used in epoxy encapsulants for semiconductor packaging. Foundry and refractory applications use quartz sand as a mold medium and heat-resistant aggregate in furnace linings.

In plastics and polymer compounding, milled quartz improves scratch resistance and reduces shrinkage in thermoset and thermoplastic systems. It is supplied as mined sand, crushed stone, and milled powder.

The material is available across a broad particle size range, from coarse aggregates to sub-micron grades. Standard commercial grades include technical, foundry, and high-purity electronic grades.

Purity levels are typically specified by SiO2 content. Surface-treated variants are available for polymer compounding applications where improved matrix adhesion is required for the final product.

name: Sulfate ion
description:
Sulfate ion (CAS 14808-79-8 ), also referenced as SO4²⁻, is the dissociated anion present across a broad range of inorganic sulfate salts used in industrial processing. It functions as a reactive species in pH buffering and coagulation chemistry.

These salts are selected based on the cation required for a given process, such as ammonium sulfate for specific applications. In water treatment, sulfate-bearing coagulants drive suspended solids removal and clarification.

These compounds are essential for municipal and industrial effluent systems to ensure effective purification. Mining operations rely on sulfate chemistry for leaching, metal precipitation, and tailings management across various sites.

In agriculture, sulfate salts deliver bioavailable sulfur to crops and are incorporated into fertilizer blends. These blends are specifically designed for targeting sulfur-deficient soils to improve overall crop yields and health.

Food-grade sulfate compounds serve as mineral supplements and processing aids in regulated food and feed formulations. Sulfate ion is not supplied as an isolated species; procurement is always through a specific salt form.

Available formats include powder, granule, crystal, or liquid solution depending on the industrial need. Grades available across sulfate salts include technical, food-grade ( FCC ), and feed-grade, depending on the salt selected.

Buyers should specify both the desired cation and the required grade when sourcing these chemical products. This ensures the material meets the necessary specifications for the intended industrial or food-related application.

Calcium acid pyrophosphate (CAS 14866-19-4 ), commonly abbreviated as CAPP and also known as calcium dihydrogen pyrophosphate, is an inorganic phosphate salt used in food manufacturing and industrial processing.

This provides controlled gas release during baking to achieve consistent crumb structure in breads, cakes, and self-rising flours. Meat processors use it to bind moisture, improve texture, and stabilize color.

In pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing, it serves as a calcium source and excipient where controlled pH and mineral supplementation are required. Agricultural and feed applications utilize CAPP as a bioavailable source.

It delivers broad-spectrum antimicrobial performance while offering a more environmentally favorable counterion profile compared to conventional quat chloride salts in industrial formulations.

name: Bismuth subsalicylate

Bismuth subsalicylate (CAS 14882-18-9 ), also known as pink bismuth and commonly abbreviated as BSS, is an inorganic bismuth salt used across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an antimicrobial and preservative agent, with established use in gastrointestinal formulations and topical applications. BSS is the active pharmaceutical ingredient in over-the-counter remedies.

It is formulated into oral suspensions and chewable tablets at defined dosage strengths. In personal care, it is incorporated into cosmetic formulations such as lip products and skin preparations for its properties.

Its antimicrobial and mild astringent properties make it a versatile additive. Pharmaceutical manufacturers also use it as an intermediate in the production of other bismuth-based compounds for various uses.

Its biocidal activity supports preservation in topical creams and ointments where alternative preservatives face regulatory restrictions. Bismuth subsalicylate is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder.

name: HATU
description:
HATU (CAS 148893-10-1 ), also known as N-HATU, is a high-efficiency peptide coupling reagent used extensively in solid-phase and solution-phase peptide synthesis. It activates carboxylic acids toward amide bond formation.

This reagent enables rapid, high-yield couplings that are critical in API and peptide drug manufacturing. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it enables the assembly of complex peptide APIs including GLP-1 analogs and cyclic peptides.

Coupling efficiency directly impacts yield and purity at scale. Biotech and contract manufacturing organizations rely on it for synthesizing peptide libraries used in drug discovery screening campaigns for new medicines.

It supports the preparation of protected amino acid fragments in convergent synthesis strategies, reducing racemization compared to older reagent classes. This makes it a preferred choice for modern laboratories.

Research institutions also use this activator in the synthesis of peptidomimetics and conjugates where difficult sequences or sterically hindered residues require a high-performance activator for successful results.

The product is supplied as a crystalline powder, typically at purities of ≥98% by HPLC. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for GMP manufacturing environments across the globe.

Specifications vary by supplier, with GMP-grade material supported by full analytical documentation. This includes a CoA, residual solvent data, and batch traceability to ensure the highest quality standards are met.

name: 2-mercaptobenzothiazole
description:
2-Mercaptobenzothiazole (CAS 149-30-4 ), commonly known as MBT or Captax, is a primary accelerator and intermediate used across rubber processing, industrial preservation, and specialty chemical synthesis.

It activates sulfur vulcanization in elastomers and functions as a biocide and corrosion inhibitor in industrial fluid systems. In rubber and tire manufacturing, MBT accelerates sulfur crosslinking.

This improves cure efficiency and mechanical performance in finished goods for natural and synthetic elastomers. Industrial metalworking fluids and cooling water systems use it as a copper corrosion inhibitor.

It forms a protective complex on metal surfaces to extend fluid service life. As a biocide, it controls microbial growth in cutting fluids, adhesives, and polymer dispersions where biological fouling occurs.

MBT also serves as a key synthesis intermediate for benzothiazole-based accelerator derivatives, including MBTS and CBS. These are produced at scale for the global rubber chemicals market.

The product is supplied as a yellow to tan powder or as a sodium salt solution for fluid-system applications. Standard commercial grades include technical and rubber-grade specifications.

Purity typically ranges from 95% to 98% or higher depending on the specific application. Bulk supply is available in bags or drums, with technical-grade product being the dominant form traded.

name: Erythritol

Erythritol (CAS 149-32-6 ), also known by the food additive designation E968 , is a naturally derived sugar alcohol used primarily as a low-calorie sweetener and humectant.

It is utilized across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It delivers sweetness at approximately 70% the intensity of sucrose while contributing negligible caloric value to the final product.

This makes it a preferred ingredient in reduced-sugar and diabetic-friendly formulations. In food and beverage production, it is used to bulk out tabletop sweetener blends and sugar-free confectionery.

In low-calorie baked goods, it helps control moisture migration and extend shelf life. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it as a tablet excipient and coating agent for solid dosage forms.

Its low hygroscopicity supports stable formulations, while in personal care, it functions as a humectant in skin creams and serums. It also serves as a reactive polyol in specialty resin applications.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in granular form suited to direct compression. Standard grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications for global distribution.

name: Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate
description:
Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate (CAS 149-44-0 ), also sold under trade names Aldanil, Discolite, and Formopan, is a reducing agent and bleaching compound used across textile, paper, and water treatment industries.

Commonly abbreviated as SFS, it functions as a chemical reductant capable of stripping color and neutralizing oxidizing agents in industrial processes. In textile dyeing and finishing, it is used as a discharge agent.

This compound allows manufacturers to selectively remove or reduce dye from fabric, enabling precise pattern bleaching without damaging fiber structure. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it to brighten pulp and reduce residual color.

In leather processing, it serves as a reducing bleach to even out hide coloration prior to dyeing. Water treatment operations use SFS to neutralize excess chlorine and other oxidants in effluent streams before discharge.

Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial bleaching and reduction applications.

Supply is typically offered in moisture-resistant packaging due to the compound's sensitivity to humid storage conditions, with bulk and drummed formats available for industrial procurement.

name: 2-ethylhexanoic acid
description:
2-Ethylhexanoic acid (CAS 149-57-5 ), also known as 2-EHA, is a branched-chain fatty acid used primarily as a building block for metal salt synthesis and as a ligand in catalyst systems.

Its branched structure makes it commercially valuable for producing metal carboxylates that would otherwise be difficult to formulate with straight-chain acids. In coatings and adhesives, it is reacted with metals.

Metals such as cobalt, zinc, and zirconium are used to produce driers and crosslinking agents that accelerate oxidative cure in alkyd and oil-based systems. Catalyst manufacturers use it to prepare metal 2-ethylhexanoates.

These serve as precursors for polyurethane, silicone, and esterification catalysts. In sealants and elastomers, the resulting metal salts function as adhesion promoters and cure accelerators across a range of polymer systems.

Flavor and fragrance producers use 2-EHA at low concentrations to contribute fatty, waxy top notes in certain formulations. 2-Ethylhexanoic acid is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

Bulk tanker supply is available for high-volume industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, covering the majority of coatings and catalyst applications for industrial users.

name: Trimethyl orthoformate
description:
Trimethyl orthoformate ( CAS 149-73-5 ), commonly abbreviated as TMOF and also known as methyl orthoformate, is a reactive orthoacid ester used as a protecting group reagent and synthetic building block.

It serves as a vital solvent across pharmaceutical and specialty chemical manufacturing. Its primary commercial role is enabling controlled reactions in sensitive synthesis environments where conventional reagents would cause unwanted side reactions.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, TMOF acts as a methoxymethylating agent and carbonyl-protecting reagent. This enables the construction of complex active pharmaceutical ingredient intermediates with high selectivity during the manufacturing process.

Agrochemical and fine chemical producers use it as a formylation reagent to introduce formate functionality into target molecules under mild conditions. This versatility makes it a staple in modern industrial chemistry.

In flavor and fragrance manufacturing, it functions as a precursor to orthoester-based aroma compounds. It also serves as a stabilizing carrier solvent for sensitive fragrance ingredients that require specific chemical environments.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a low-water solvent medium for enzymatic reactions. This is particularly useful where aqueous conditions would compromise yield or selectivity in delicate biological processes.

The product is supplied as a colorless liquid in standard packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drum shipments. Technical and synthesis-grade specifications are the most commonly available for industrial use.

Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher for pharmaceutical and fine chemical applications. High-purity reagent-grade material is also available to meet the stricter quality requirements of API synthesis and analytical workflows.

name: Gallic acid
description:
Gallic acid (CAS 149-91-7 ) is a natural polyphenolic organic acid derived primarily from tannin-rich plant sources such as gallnuts and tea. It functions as an antioxidant, antimicrobial agent, and UV stabilizer across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Pyrogallol-5-carboxylic acid is an alternative name occasionally encountered in technical literature. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of trimethoprim and propyl gallate.

The latter is a widely regulated antioxidant for fats and oils. Food producers use it to extend the shelf life of lipid-containing products by inhibiting oxidative rancidity in edible oils, packaged snacks, and meat-based formulations.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into sunscreen and anti-aging products. Its UV-absorbing and antioxidant activity helps protect both the formulation and the end user's skin from oxidative degradation.

It also functions as a preservative and astringent active in topical preparations targeting skin tone and texture. This versatile compound is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. These grades often meet rigorous quality standards such as USP , FCC , or Ph.Eur. requirements.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial applications such as ink manufacturing and tanning processes. This ensures that manufacturers can select the appropriate purity level for their specific production needs and regulatory environments.

name: Menthol
description:
Menthol (CAS 1490-04-6 ), also identified by FEMA 2665 , is a naturally derived or synthetically produced cyclic alcohol extracted primarily from peppermint and cornmint oils. It delivers a characteristic cooling sensation without a temperature change.

This unique property makes it a high-demand active in flavoring, fragrance, and pharmaceutical applications. In oral care and confectionery, it provides the cooling and flavor profile expected in toothpastes and mouthwashes.

It is also essential for chewing gums and mint-flavored candies. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into topical analgesics, throat lozenges, nasal decongestants, and cough suppressant formulations as a functional cooling agent.

Personal care producers use it in shaving products, lip balms, and skin cooling gels where the sensory effect is a primary performance attribute. It serves as a critical ingredient for products requiring a refreshing feel.

Tobacco and e-liquid blending represents a significant industrial volume application. In these sectors, it is used to modify harshness and deliver a distinctive flavor character that consumers expect from mentholated products.

The product is supplied as colorless to white crystals or flakes, with natural and synthetic variants available. Established grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , as well as food-grade specifications.

Natural l-menthol often commands a premium over racemic synthetic material in the global market. Bulk supply is available in fiber drums or cartons, with purity typically at 99% or above for pharmaceutical and flavor-grade material.

It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel in cosmetic applications while providing effective lubrication and surface conditioning in technical uses. In skin care and color cosmetics, it acts as an emollient carrier.

This ingredient improves spreadability and texture in creams, foundations, and lip products without leaving heavy residue. Sunscreen and SPF formulations use it to disperse UV filters evenly while maintaining a cosmetically elegant finish.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it supports emulsification of oils and soils, improving rinse-off performance in hard surface cleaners and degreasers. This versatility makes it a staple for diverse chemical manufacturing.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it as a base fluid or additive where low viscosity, good film formation, and compatibility with synthetic systems are required. It offers excellent stability across various temperature ranges.

name: Copper pyrithione

Copper pyrithione (CAS 14915-37-8 ), also known as Copper Omadine and abbreviated as CuPT, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial compound used across industrial and personal care markets.

It functions as a biocide and preservative, controlling bacterial, fungal, and algal growth in formulated products and treated materials. In antifouling and protective coatings, CuPT is incorporated as a biocidal active.

This prevents microbial and algal fouling on marine and architectural surfaces. Personal care formulators use it in anti-dandruff shampoos and scalp treatments as an alternative to zinc pyrithione.

It offers comparable efficacy with distinct formulation compatibility. Textile, leather, and paper manufacturers apply CuPT to impart durable antimicrobial protection to finished goods and processing substrates.

name: Magnesium trisilicate
description:
Magnesium trisilicate (CAS 14987-04-3 ) is an inorganic magnesium silicate compound used across pharmaceutical, food, and industrial manufacturing. It functions primarily as an antacid, anticaking agent, and adsorbent.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used as an active antacid ingredient in tablet and suspension formulations. Here, it neutralizes excess gastric acid and adsorbs pepsin to provide relief for patients.

Food producers incorporate it as an anticaking agent in powdered and granulated products. This prevents clumping during processing and storage, ensuring a free-flowing consistency for the end consumer.

In polymer and plastics processing, it acts as a catalyst support and stabilizer. This improves thermal resistance and processing consistency in certain resin systems during high-temperature manufacturing cycles.

Refiners and chemical processors also use it as an adsorbent to remove impurities. It is particularly effective at removing pigments and free fatty acids from oils and various organic streams.

The material is supplied as a fine white powder in both hydrated and anhydrous grades. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for regulated drug products.

Food-grade supply is also established for anticaking applications in the global market. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and catalyst-related uses where high purity is required.

name: D-glucosamine sulfate
description:
D-glucosamine sulfate (CAS 14999-43-0 ) is an amino monosaccharide salt used primarily as an active pharmaceutical ingredient and nutraceutical compound. It is the sulfated form of glucosamine, recognized in dietary supplement markets under the abbreviation GS.

Commercially, it functions as a joint-support active in finished dosage forms and as a bioactive ingredient in functional food and cosmetic formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, GS is the preferred active ingredient in oral solid dosage forms.

These tablets and capsules target joint health and cartilage support. Nutraceutical formulators use it in combination products alongside chondroitin sulfate or MSM for branded joint-care supplements to enhance efficacy.

In functional food and beverage development, it is incorporated into fortified products where a bioactive amino sugar is required. Personal care formulators apply it in topical skin-conditioning products for specific applications.

These amino sugar actives are specified for anti-aging or moisturizing claims in high-end cosmetic lines. D-glucosamine sulfate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for easy handling during production.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , BP ) and food-grade ( FCC ) specifications to meet regulatory requirements across different global markets and ensure high purity levels.

Stabilized potassium chloride (2KCl) and sodium chloride (NaCl) salt complexes are standard commercial forms. These are used to improve hygroscopic stability in finished formulations and extend the shelf life of the product.

name: 4-aminobenzoic acid
description:
4-Aminobenzoic acid (CAS 150-13-0 ), commonly known as PABA or para-aminobenzoic acid, is an aromatic amino acid derivative used as a key building block in pharmaceutical synthesis.

Its bifunctional structure, carrying both an amine and a carboxylic acid group, makes it a reactive intermediate for producing dyes, UV absorbers, and active pharmaceutical ingredients.

In pharmaceuticals, PABA serves as a precursor in the synthesis of local anesthetics such as benzocaine and procaine, as well as folate-class compounds for various medical uses.

Textile and leather processors use it as an intermediate in azo dye production, where it contributes to colorfast, high-affinity dye systems for natural and synthetic fibers.

In sunscreen and personal care formulations, PABA derivatives function as UV-B absorbing agents, though demand has shifted toward its ester forms in recent years.

It also acts as a crosslinking and surface-modifying agent in specialty polymer and coating applications, providing versatility across multiple industrial chemical sectors.

4-Aminobenzoic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material for diverse needs.

The pharmaceutical supply conforms to USP and BP specifications. Bulk quantities are available for industrial synthesis, with smaller quantities offered for R&D use.

name: Trisodium EDTA
description:
Trisodium EDTA (CAS 150-38-9 ) is a water-soluble chelating agent that binds and neutralizes metal ions in aqueous systems. It prevents them from interfering with formulation stability or process efficiency.

It is the trisodium salt form of EDTA, offering a moderately alkaline pH profile. This suits applications where the tetrasodium form would be too basic for the specific chemical environment.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it sequesters calcium and magnesium ions in hard water. This protects preservative systems and maintains product clarity in various consumer goods.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to stabilize liquid preparations by deactivating trace metals. This prevents metals from catalyzing oxidative degradation, ensuring the longevity of the final product.

Water treatment operations rely on it to control scale formation and metal ion interference in process water. In textile and paper processing, it prevents metal-catalyzed discoloration during bleaching.

This chemical improves batch consistency and end-product quality in industrial dyeing operations. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution at 40–50% concentrations.

Grades available include technical, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers and specialty use.

Smaller packaging is also available for laboratory and specialty formulation requirements. This ensures that the product meets the diverse needs of both large-scale and niche manufacturers.

name: Hydroxyethylethylenediaminetriacetic acid
description:
Hydroxyethylethylenediaminetriacetic acid (CAS 150-39-0 ), commonly known as HEDTA, is a chelating agent used across industrial and personal care applications. It binds and sequesters metal ions, particularly calcium, magnesium, iron, and heavy metals.

By sequestering these ions, it prevents them from interfering with formulation performance or process chemistry. In personal care formulations, HEDTA stabilizes products by deactivating trace metal ions that would otherwise degrade active ingredients.

This stabilization prevents discoloration and maintains the integrity of the final product. Water treatment operations use it to control scale formation and metal ion interference in process water and cooling systems.

Textile and paper processing rely on HEDTA to sequester hardness ions during bleaching and dyeing. This process improves consistency and reduces chemical waste across large-scale manufacturing operations.

In cleaning formulations, it enhances detergent performance by keeping calcium and magnesium ions from reducing surfactant efficiency. This ensures that cleaning agents remain effective even in hard water conditions.

HEDTA is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with concentration levels varying by grade and supplier specification. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial applications including water treatment.

Personal care applications may require grades meeting cosmetic or purity specifications aligned with industry standards. These high-purity options ensure compatibility with sensitive skin and hair care formulations.

name: Dibenzyl disulfide
description:
Dibenzyl disulfide (CAS 150-60-7 ), also known as DBDS, is an organosulfur compound used as a flavoring agent, antioxidant, and catalyst precursor across food, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

Assigned FEMA 3617 , it is recognized as a flavor ingredient in regulated food and fragrance contexts. In food and beverage flavoring, DBDS contributes characteristic savory, roasted, and sulfurous notes.

It is used in meat, coffee, and processed food formulations at trace concentrations. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it as an antioxidant stabilizer to extend the shelf life of lipid-containing products.

This includes applications such as creams and balms. In catalyst chemistry, it functions as a sulfur-donor precursor for generating metal sulfide catalysts used in hydroprocessing and organic synthesis.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers also evaluate it as an intermediate or stabilizing additive in select formulation development programs. Dibenzyl disulfide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid or powder.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade material meeting FEMA specifications and technical-grade product for industrial and catalyst applications. Packaging is typically available in kilogram quantities.

This allows for laboratory and pilot use, scaling to bulk drum supply for industrial procurement. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure stability and purity during transport.

name: 4-methoxyphenol
description:
4-Methoxyphenol (CAS 150-76-5 ), also known commercially as mequinol and 4-hydroxyanisole, functions as a polymerization inhibitor and antioxidant in industrial chemical processing.

It prevents premature crosslinking and radical chain reactions in reactive monomer systems, protecting product integrity during storage and transport across various supply chains.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it stabilizes vinyl and acrylic monomers against unwanted polymerization during bulk storage. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to extend shelf life.

It is particularly effective in UV-curable and reactive resin systems where premature gelation is a critical quality risk. As a pharmaceutical intermediate, mequinol is a direct active ingredient.

It is used in topical depigmentation formulations and as a building block for synthesizing complex API structures. In personal care, it is incorporated into skin-lightening products.

Regulatory-grade purity is a procurement requirement for these applications. 4-Methoxyphenol is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid or flake for industrial use.

Technical grade is standard for industrial inhibitor applications, while pharmaceutical and cosmetic buyers typically source material meeting BP or USP specifications.

Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale bags to bulk drum quantities depending on application volume. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale labs and large manufacturing plants.

name: Disodium succinate
description:
Disodium succinate (CAS 150-90-3 ), also known by FEMA 3277 , is the sodium salt of succinic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer and flavor enhancer.

This versatile ingredient stabilizes formulations and contributes a mild, characteristic taste profile to finished products. In food and beverage production, it acts as a flavor potentiator and acidulant, particularly in savory seasonings and soups.

It is frequently utilized in processed foods where it enhances umami character. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent in oral and injectable formulations, helping maintain target pH ranges throughout shelf life.

In personal care, it supports pH regulation in rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos, conditioners, and skin creams. It also appears as an intermediate in the synthesis of specialty chemicals and polymers.

The compound is essential for the production of biodegradable polymers and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Disodium succinate is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both anhydrous and hexahydrate forms.

Buyers should confirm which hydration state is required before sourcing, as they differ in active content. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the most commonly traded grade for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. standards is available for regulated applications. These high-purity grades ensure compliance with international safety and quality protocols for medicine.

name: Polyquaternium-44
description:
Polyquaternium-44 (CAS 150599-70-5 ) is a cationic conditioning polymer used primarily in rinse-off and leave-on personal care formulations. It deposits onto hair and skin surfaces to improve texture and reduce static.

This versatile polymer enhances the sensory profile of finished products by creating a smooth protective layer. In shampoos and conditioners, it provides detangling and smoothing benefits by adsorbing onto negatively charged hair fibers.

It improves combability without heavy buildup, making it ideal for daily use products. Leave-on styling products rely on it for light hold and frizz control while maintaining a non-tacky feel for the consumer.

Skin care formulations incorporate it as a film-forming humectant that helps retain moisture at the surface. This action helps to maintain skin hydration and improves the overall tactile experience of lotions and creams.

In fabric care and hard surface cleaners, it contributes antistatic and soil-release properties to rinse-off systems. This makes it a valuable additive for industrial and institutional cleaning applications requiring surface modification.

Polyquaternium-44 is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 20 to 30 percent active content. It is available in cosmetic grade suitable for a wide range of personal care applications.

The supply conforms to standard industry specifications for cationic polymers to ensure consistent performance. Packaging is typically in drums or IBCs for bulk procurement to meet large scale manufacturing needs.

1,2-Ethanediamine, N1,N2-bis[[4-(2-thiazolyl)phenyl]methyl]- (CAS 1507370-40-2 ), also known commercially as Tionsil 1258 , is a specialized diamine compound combining thiazole and phenyl moieties within a symmetrical ethylenediamine backbone.

It functions as a pharmaceutical intermediate and research building block in the synthesis of biologically active molecules targeting specific biochemical pathways. In pharmaceutical development, it serves as a key structural intermediate.

It is used for synthesizing candidate compounds in antimicrobial and antiparasitic drug discovery programs. Medicinal chemistry teams use its bis-thiazolylbenzyl architecture to construct libraries of heterocyclic amines for high-throughput screening.

These libraries are tested against disease-relevant targets. Biotechnology researchers incorporate it into probe molecule synthesis where the thiazole units contribute to selective binding profiles in target-engagement studies.

Contract research organizations sourcing building blocks for small-molecule drug programs evaluate it for multi-step synthesis routes. These routes require a defined, bifunctional diamine scaffold for complex chemical reactions.

Tionsil 1258 is supplied as a solid, typically as a powder or crystalline material, in research and development quantities. These range from milligram to multi-gram scale depending on the specific project requirements.

It is available under research-grade specifications, with purity confirmed by HPLC and NMR characterization data. Custom batch production for preclinical supply can be arranged through specialist fine chemical and API intermediate manufacturers.

description:
2',4',5',7'-Tetrabromofluorescein (CAS 15086-94-9 ), commercially recognized as D&C Red #21, is a brominated xanthene dye approved for use in cosmetic and personal care formulations.

In cosmetics, D&C Red #21 delivers a distinctive pink-to-red fluorescent tone in lip products, blushes, and nail preparations, where its color-shift behavior on skin is a valued attribute.

Polymer compounders incorporate it into plastics where both coloration and halogen-based flame retardancy are specified in a single additive for industrial manufacturing.

Textile and paper processors use it as a surface-active colorant, where its wetting behavior supports even dye distribution across various substrates and fiber types.

In printing and packaging inks, it contributes vivid fluorescent hues to specialty formulations targeting high-visibility or decorative end uses for consumer goods.

2',4',5',7'-Tetrabromofluorescein is supplied as a fine powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade quality meeting D&C colorant specifications as regulated by the FDA.

description:
3-Benzylidene camphor (CAS 15087-24-8 ) is an organic UV filter used in sunscreen and cosmetic formulations to absorb ultraviolet radiation in the UVB range. It belongs to the camphor-derived UV absorber class.

The material is evaluated for inclusion in regulated cosmetic ingredient lists across multiple markets. In sunscreen development, it functions as a UVB-absorbing active that can be combined with other UV filters.

This combination helps achieve broad-spectrum protection profiles required by modern sun care standards. Formulators incorporate it into leave-on products such as sun lotions, day creams, and facial SPF products.

Photostability and filter compatibility are key selection criteria for these applications. It also appears in color cosmetics and foundations where incidental UV protection is built into the formulation matrix.

3-Benzylidene camphor is supplied as a solid powder or crystalline material suitable for incorporation into oil-phase cosmetic systems. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification for global use.

name: Cryolite
description:
Cryolite (CAS 15096-52-3 ), also sold under the trade name Cryocide, is a synthetic sodium aluminum fluoride mineral used primarily as a flux and electrolyte medium in industrial processing.

Commercially produced to replace the now-depleted natural mineral deposits, it is a critical input in aluminum smelting and select agrochemical and abrasive applications.

In primary aluminum production, cryolite functions as the molten bath electrolyte in Hall-Héroult cells, dissolving alumina at high temperatures to enable electrochemical reduction into metal.

This functionality makes it indispensable to smelter operations. Abrasive product manufacturers incorporate it as a filler and grinding aid in resin-bonded grinding wheels and coated abrasives.

In these applications, it improves cut rate and extends wheel life. In the pulp and paper industry, it is used as an opacifying agent and filler to improve sheet brightness and printability.

Historically applied as an insecticide under the Cryocide trade name, it remains a registered pesticide active ingredient in certain markets for control of chewing insects on crops.

Cryolite is supplied as a fine white powder in bulk, supersacks, and bagged formats. Technical and metallurgical grades are the most common, with purity specifications typically aligned to industry standards.

Pesticide-grade material is available in select markets where regulatory approvals are maintained. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for large-scale industrial requirements.
