name: L-Malic acid-13C4
description:
L-Malic acid-13C4 (CAS 150992-96-4 ) is a stable isotope-labeled form of L-malic acid in which all four carbon atoms are replaced with carbon-13. It is used primarily as an analytical reference standard and metabolic tracer.

This compound enables precise quantification and tracking of malic acid in complex biological and chemical matrices. In pharmaceutical and bioanalytical research, it serves as an internal standard for LC-MS/MS and GC-MS methods.

The use of this labeled standard improves accuracy when quantifying malic acid in drug formulations or biological fluids. Metabolic flux analysis in biotechnology relies on 13C-labeled organic acids to map carbon flow.

Researchers utilize this compound to track movement through the TCA cycle and related pathways. Food science researchers use it to authenticate natural malic acid content and detect adulteration in fruit-based products.

It is also applied in juices and acidulant systems to ensure product integrity. Isotope tracer studies in nutrition research apply this compound to investigate malic acid absorption and metabolism in vivo.

L-Malic acid-13C4 is supplied as a solid powder in research-scale quantities, typically ranging from milligrams to low-gram amounts. It is available at high isotopic purity, commonly ≥99 atom % 13C.

The chemical purity specifications are suited to reference standard applications. Packaging is designed for long-term stability under controlled storage conditions to maintain the integrity of the labeled material.

name: Sodium lauryl sulfate
description:
Sodium lauryl sulfate (CAS 151-21-3 ), commonly abbreviated as SLS and designated E487 , is an anionic surfactant used across personal care, food, and industrial manufacturing.

It delivers reliable foaming, emulsification, and detergency across a broad range of formulated products. In personal care, SLS is the primary foaming and cleansing agent in toothpastes and shampoos.

It is also used in body washes, where consistent lather and soil removal are formulation requirements. Food-grade applications include use as an emulsifier and whipping aid in egg-white products.

It is used in marshmallow confections under the E487 designation. Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to improve dye penetration and remove surface contaminants.

In industrial cleaning and printing, it functions as a dispersant and degreaser in press-wash compounds and hard-surface cleaners. SLS is supplied as a white to off-white powder or needle.

Flake, liquid, and paste forms are also available for specific processing requirements. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC for pharmaceutical and food applications.

Technical grade is also available for industrial use. Concentration in liquid or paste form typically ranges from 28% to 35% active content, ensuring high performance in diverse chemical formulations.

name: Potassium cyanide
description:
Potassium cyanide (CAS 151-50-8 ), commonly referenced as KCN in industrial procurement, is an inorganic salt used primarily as a complexing and leaching agent in metal processing and surface finishing operations.

Its ability to form stable metal-cyanide complexes drives its demand across electroplating and precious metal recovery sectors. In electroplating, KCN functions as the primary electrolyte carrier for depositing gold and silver.

It is also used for copper and zinc coatings onto metal substrates, producing uniform, adherent finishes for electronics connectors and decorative hardware. Precious metal mining operations rely on cyanide leaching processes.

In these processes, KCN solubilizes gold and silver from low-grade ores, enabling cost-effective recovery at scale. In electronics manufacturing, it supports selective metal deposition on printed circuit boards.

It is also utilized for semiconductor components where precise surface conductivity is required. Jewelry finishing operations also use KCN-based baths for bright gold and silver plating on consumer goods.

Potassium cyanide is supplied as white granules or lumps, with solution forms available for specific industrial applications. Standard commercial grades are offered at 98% minimum purity for industrial use.

Technical grade is the predominant specification in mining and electroplating supply chains. Packaging and handling requirements are subject to strict regulatory controls and safety protocols.

Procurement typically requires end-use documentation and licensed handling facilities to ensure compliance. This ensures the material is managed safely throughout the entire global chemical supply chain.

name: Hydrolyzed oat protein
description:
Hydrolyzed oat protein (CAS 151661-87-9 ) is derived from oat grain through enzymatic or chemical hydrolysis, yielding a mixture of peptides and amino acids. It functions as a film-forming humectant and surface-conditioning agent across personal care, food, and pharmaceutical applications.

In hair and skin care formulations, it deposits a protective peptide film that reduces moisture loss and improves surface texture in conditioners, serums, and leave-on treatments. Shampoos and styling products incorporate it to enhance wet combability and reduce breakage by binding to damaged hair fiber.

In food and nutritional products, it contributes plant-based protein fortification to beverages, bars, and functional supplements where clean-label oat-derived ingredients are preferred. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use it as a functional excipient in topical preparations.

These oral delivery systems require biocompatible protein fractions to ensure safety and efficacy. Hydrolyzed oat protein is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with dry powder forms available for applications requiring lower water activity or extended shelf stability.

Standard grades include cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications, with concentration levels in liquid form typically ranging from 25% to 50% active solids. Buyers should confirm molecular weight distribution and degree of hydrolysis against specification sheets.

These parameters directly affect film-forming performance and solubility in finished formulations. The material is highly valued for its versatility and compatibility with a wide range of surfactants and emulsifiers in industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Araldite PT 910
description:
Araldite PT 910 (CAS 152042-34-7 ) is a multifunctional epoxy resin hardener used to cure and crosslink epoxy systems in high-performance industrial applications. It is recognized in the market as a solid curing agent that delivers elevated thermal and chemical resistance.

In electronics, this material is used to formulate encapsulants, potting compounds, and underfill materials where cured systems must maintain dimensional stability under thermal cycling. These applications require high reliability in demanding end-use environments.

Aerospace and automotive structural adhesives rely on this hardener to achieve high glass transition temperatures and mechanical strength in bonded assemblies. It ensures that structural components remain secure under significant physical stress.

Coating formulators incorporate the product into powder coating systems and high-build protective coatings where resistance to aggressive chemical exposure is required. This makes it ideal for industrial surfaces and heavy-duty machinery protection.

Sealant and elastomer manufacturers use it to control rheology and crosslink density in epoxy-based sealant formulations for industrial joints and assemblies. This control is vital for maintaining the integrity of seals over long periods.

The product is supplied as a solid, typically in powder or granule form suited for dry-blending with epoxy resins. It is available in technical grade for industrial and specialty formulation use across various manufacturing sectors.

Packaging options generally range from kilogram-scale bags to bulk quantities depending on volume requirements. This flexibility allows for both small-scale specialty production and large-scale industrial manufacturing processes.

Contact us for supply of Araldite PT 910

name: 2-Acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid
description:
2-Acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid (CAS 15214-89-8 ), commercially known as AMPS, is a reactive sulfonic acid monomer used to engineer performance polymers across industrial and specialty chemical markets.

Its strong anionic character makes it a preferred building block for water-soluble and hydrogel polymer systems where charge density and hydrolytic stability are critical sourcing considerations for manufacturers.

In water treatment, AMPS is copolymerized into scale inhibitors and dispersants that control mineral deposition in cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems to maintain operational efficiency.

Personal care formulators incorporate AMPS-based polymers as rheology modifiers and film formers in styling gels, skin creams, and sunscreen carriers to enhance product texture and application performance.

Textile and paper processing operations use AMPS copolymers for surface sizing, wet-strength improvement, and dye fixation, ensuring high-quality finishes and durability in the final consumer products.

In oilfield applications, AMPS serves as a key monomer in fluid loss control additives and friction reducers used in drilling and enhanced oil recovery formulations for demanding environments.

AMPS is supplied as a white crystalline powder and as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% concentration. Standard grades include technical and industrial purity levels suited for polymer synthesis.

Specialty grades meeting higher purity thresholds are available for personal care and cosmetic polymer applications, ensuring compliance with rigorous industry safety and performance requirements.

name: Sodium benzotriazole
description:
Sodium benzotriazole (CAS 15217-42-2 ), also known commercially as sodium benzotriazolide, is a water-soluble corrosion inhibitor and metal deactivator used across industrial and specialty chemical applications.

It functions by forming a stable protective complex on copper, brass, and other non-ferrous metal surfaces, preventing oxidation and degradation in aggressive environments.

In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it is incorporated into cutting fluids, hydraulic oils, and rust-preventive formulations to protect copper alloy components during machining and storage.

Water treatment programs use it to inhibit copper corrosion in cooling tower circuits and closed-loop systems, where uncontrolled metal ion release would compromise system integrity.

Electronics manufacturing relies on it as a surface passivation agent during PCB processing and metal finishing, preventing tarnish on copper traces and contacts.

Automotive antifreeze and coolant formulations include it to protect brass and copper radiator components under high-temperature operating conditions.

Sodium benzotriazole is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically ranging from 40% to 50%.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, though high-purity grades are available for electronics and precision industrial applications. It is commonly packaged in drums or IBCs.

name: Ferric sulfate hydrate
description:
Ferric sulfate hydrate (CAS 15244-10-7 ), also known as Iron(III) sulfate hydrate, is an iron-based inorganic salt used industrially as a coagulant, flocculant, and pH-regulating agent.

It delivers reliable performance across water treatment, mineral processing, and pulp and paper operations where controlled iron chemistry is required. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it acts as a primary coagulant.

The product effectively removes suspended solids, phosphates, and turbidity from effluent streams. Mineral processing operations use it as a leaching agent and oxidant in hydrometallurgical circuits for metal recovery.

It is particularly useful for recovering copper and other base metals from sulfide ores. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it in effluent treatment to precipitate lignin and color bodies before discharge.

It also supports pH adjustment and sludge conditioning in wastewater systems where iron-based chemistry is preferred over aluminum alternatives. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial processing.

Ferric sulfate hydrate is supplied as a granular solid or powder, with bulk quantities available for industrial procurement. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for water treatment and mining.

Purity levels and hydration state should be confirmed with the supplier, as iron content and soluble fraction directly affect dosing calculations. Proper storage is required to maintain the integrity of the hydrate.

name: Lead styphnate
description:
Lead styphnate (CAS 15245-44-0 ), also known as lead trinitroresorcinate, is a primary explosive compound used as an initiating agent in energetic systems. It reliably converts a low-energy stimulus into a detonation signal.

This material reacts to friction, heat, or electrostatic discharge, making it a foundational component in primer and ignition train design. In small arms and artillery ammunition, it is the active initiating compound in primer compositions.

The compound generates the initial deflagration that ignites propellant charges. Defense and aerospace pyrotechnic assemblies rely on it within multi-component ignition trains to ensure consistent, low-threshold initiation across various conditions.

In commercial and industrial detonators used in mining and demolition, it functions as the primary charge. It bridges the gap between an electrical or percussion stimulus and the secondary explosive for reliable performance.

It is also incorporated into specialty squib and initiator devices used in aerospace safety systems, including ejection seats and airbag inflators. This versatility makes it essential for high-reliability safety and defense applications.

Lead styphnate is supplied as a wetted powder or paste to reduce sensitivity during handling and transport. Normal lead styphnate and basic lead styphnate are the two commercially recognized forms available for industrial use.

Each form has distinct initiation characteristics suited to different primer formulations. Material is typically produced and supplied to military specification grades and is subject to strict regulatory controls governing quantity and packaging.

All shipments must comply with end-use authorization requirements. Our supply chain ensures that these energetic materials meet the highest safety and performance standards required for critical defense and industrial operations.

name: N-Boc-O-benzyl-L-threonine
description:
N-Boc-O-benzyl-L-threonine , also known as Boc-Thr(Bzl)-OH with CAS 15260-10-3 , is a dual-protected threonine derivative used in solid-phase and solution-phase peptide synthesis.

The Boc group shields the alpha-amine while the benzyl group protects the hydroxyl side chain, enabling selective deprotection during multi-step assembly of complex peptide sequences.

The primary application is as a building block in the synthesis of pharmaceutical peptides, where orthogonal protection strategies are required to construct threonine-containing sequences.

This prevents side-chain racemization or unwanted cyclization during the manufacturing of peptide-based active pharmaceutical ingredients, including research compounds and GMP intermediates.

Biotechnology researchers incorporate it into custom peptide libraries for receptor binding studies and enzyme substrate profiling to ensure high-fidelity sequence construction.

Cosmetic peptide formulators sourcing actives for anti-aging or skin-conditioning products may also specify this building block when the target peptide sequence contains threonine residues.

Boc-Thr(Bzl)-OH is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder and is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for process-scale synthesis.

Purity specifications typically range from 98% to 99%+ by HPLC, with optical purity confirmed by specific rotation to meet rigorous industrial and laboratory requirements.

name: Rutin
description:
Rutin (CAS 153-18-4 ), also known commercially as Venoruton, Tanrutin, and Sophorin, is a bioflavonoid glycoside sourced primarily from buckwheat and sophora japonica buds. In industry, it functions as an antioxidant and stabilizing agent across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic formulations.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is a primary active ingredient in venous insufficiency treatments, capillary-strengthening tablets, and circulatory support supplements. Food and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into functional beverages and dietary capsules.

It is frequently used in fortified foods where antioxidant protection and label-friendly botanical positioning are priorities. In cosmetic formulations, it is used in serums, creams, and eye-area products for formula stabilization.

The compound also functions as an oxidation inhibitor in food systems to extend the shelf life of fat-containing products. It provides skin-conditioning performance and antioxidant protection required for high-end personal care applications.

The material is supplied as a fine yellow to yellow-green powder in standard commercial quantities. Established grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to ensure compliance with global industry requirements.

Purity levels are commonly available at 95% and 98% as determined by HPLC. Both natural-extract and standardized botanical-source variants are available to meet different regulatory and labeling requirements across international markets.

name: Meadowfoam seed oil
description:
Meadowfoam seed oil (CAS 153065-40-8 ), also marketed as meadowfoam oil, is a cold-pressed vegetable oil derived from the seeds of Limnanthes alba. Its unusually high content of long-chain fatty acids gives it exceptional oxidative stability.

This stability makes it a preferred base oil where shelf life and performance consistency matter to formulators and buyers alike. In personal care, it functions as an emollient and moisturizer in skin creams and hair conditioners.

It is also used in lip products, where its low grease feel and strong spreadability improve finished product texture. Industrial lubricant manufacturers use it as a bio-based base fluid or additive for specific needs.

This is particularly useful where biodegradability is a procurement requirement. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it to improve flexibility and film formation in specialty coatings and various industrial applications.

Its natural emulsification behavior also supports use in dispersions and blended formulations requiring a stable, plant-derived carrier oil. The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for easy handling.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications, with cosmetic-grade being the dominant commercial form for personal care supply chains. Standard packaging ranges from small drums to bulk totes.

Refined and cold-pressed variants are available depending on application requirements. The oil maintains its integrity under high heat and pressure, ensuring reliable performance across diverse manufacturing environments.

name: Fexofenadine hydrochloride
description:
Fexofenadine hydrochloride (CAS 153439-40-8 ), marketed under the brand name Allegra, is a second-generation antihistamine active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the manufacture of prescription and OTC allergy relief products.

It targets peripheral H1 receptors without significant CNS penetration, making it a preferred API for non-sedating antihistamine formulations. The primary use is in finished oral dosage forms such as tablets and capsules.

These products are indicated for seasonal allergic rhinitis and chronic idiopathic urticaria. Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers source it as the active ingredient in branded and private-label antihistamine products.

In personal care, it is evaluated for inclusion in topical formulations targeting skin hypersensitivity and allergic dermatitis responses. Pharmaceutical formulators also utilize it in pediatric oral suspension development.

Precise particle size and solubility profiles influence grade selection for these liquid applications. Fexofenadine hydrochloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. compendial grades to meet regulatory requirements across major markets. Bulk quantities are typically offered for large scale pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Micronized grades are available to support specific dissolution and bioavailability targets. This ensures the API meets the rigorous standards required for modern drug delivery systems and patient safety protocols.

name: Thiamin Diphosphate
description:
Thiamin Diphosphate (CAS 154-87-0 ), also known as Cocarboxylase and abbreviated as TPP, is the biologically active coenzyme form of Vitamin B1. Unlike standard thiamine salts, it is supplied in its phosphorylated form.

This makes it the preferred starting material for enzyme-dependent biochemical applications where the coenzyme must be present in ready-to-use form. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, TPP is used as an active ingredient.

It is commonly found in injectable formulations and specialty supplements targeting metabolic support indications. Biotechnology and life sciences buyers source it as a cofactor in enzymatic assay systems and cell culture media.

It is also utilized in in vitro diagnostic reagents where direct coenzyme activity is required. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin-conditioning preparations where the phosphorylated B1 form is preferred for bioavailability.

The material also functions as a reference standard and process reagent in enzyme kinetics research and fermentation process development. Thiamin Diphosphate is supplied as a crystalline powder, typically as the chloride salt form.

Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications. We also provide research-grade material for laboratory and biotechnology use to meet diverse industrial needs.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial pharmaceutical production alongside smaller pack sizes for laboratory procurement. This ensures a reliable supply chain for both large-scale manufacturing and specialized research projects.

name: Potassium ascorbate
description:
Potassium ascorbate (CAS 15421-15-5 ), also known by its food additive designation E303 , is the potassium salt form of vitamin C used as an antioxidant and preservative across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications.

Unlike ascorbic acid, it delivers vitamin C activity in a neutralized, lower-acidity form suited to pH-sensitive formulations. In food and beverage manufacturing, it protects against oxidative degradation in products where acidic ingredients are undesirable.

This includes certain dairy-based and neutral-pH formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a vitamin C source in effervescent tablets, oral solutions, and dietary supplements targeting consumers who require a gentler gastric profile.

In agriculture and animal feed, it functions as a stabilized antioxidant nutrient added to premixes and feed concentrates. This supports animal health during production stress and ensures the stability of the nutritional profile over time.

Cosmetic and nutraceutical formulators also incorporate it into topical and ingestible products where combined potassium and ascorbate delivery is a formulation objective. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

Food-grade material conforming to E303 specifications is the most commonly traded form. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to USP and Ph. Eur. standards to meet strict regulatory requirements for global distribution.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags or fiber drums to ensure safe transport and storage. This versatile chemical remains a staple for manufacturers seeking a stable, non-acidic source of essential vitamin C.

name: Sodium antimonate
description:
Sodium antimonate (CAS 15432-85-6 ) is an inorganic antimony salt used primarily as a flame retardant and synergist in polymer and coating systems. Unlike antimony trioxide, it offers lower volatility and improved compatibility.

This material is ideal for high-temperature processing environments, making it the preferred antimony source for specific formulation requirements. In plastics and polymer compounding, it acts as a halogen synergist.

It boosts the flame-retardant efficiency of brominated or chlorinated systems in PET, nylon, and engineering resins. The electronics industry uses it in flame-retardant coatings and laminates where stability is critical.

Processing stability at elevated temperatures is essential for these applications. Textile and paper manufacturers apply it in back-coating formulations to meet fire safety standards for upholstery and curtains.

It is also used for industrial fabrics and automotive components. Aerospace producers incorporate it into intumescent or halogenated flame-retardant compounds for interior parts subject to strict fire performance.

The product is supplied as a white powder in technical and industrial grades. Particle size distribution is a key procurement parameter, as finer grades improve dispersion in polymer matrices and coatings.

Standard packaging includes 25 kg bags, with bulk quantities available depending on supplier capability. This ensures consistent quality and handling for large-scale industrial manufacturing and chemical processing.

name: Bromochlorophen
description:
Bromochlorophen (CAS 15435-29-7 ) is a halogenated bisphenol antimicrobial active used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and water treatment applications. It delivers broad-spectrum biocidal activity against bacteria and fungi.

This chemical serves as a reliable preservative and disinfectant ingredient in various formulated products. In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated to protect creams, lotions, and cleansing preparations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an antimicrobial active in topical preparations and as an intermediate in the synthesis of more complex active compounds. It ensures product stability and safety during storage.

Water treatment operations employ it for its biocidal properties in controlling microbial growth in industrial water systems and process fluids. It is highly effective in maintaining hygiene in large-scale industrial environments.

It also functions as an antimicrobial agent in industrial cleaning and disinfection formulations where halogenated phenolic actives are specified. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy-duty sanitation protocols.

Bromochlorophen is typically supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical and pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet the purity requirements of different end-use sectors across the globe.

name: Zinc pidolate
description:
Zinc pidolate (CAS 15454-75-8 ), also known as Zinc PCA and zinc pyroglutamate, is the zinc salt of pyroglutamic acid. It is a naturally occurring amino acid derivative found in skin and used across personal care and pharmaceutical formulations.

Its affinity for keratin supports targeted delivery in oily-skin treatments. Hair care formulators incorporate it into scalp serums and anti-dandruff products to control sebaceous secretion and support scalp condition.

Oral supplement manufacturers use it as a well-tolerated, bioavailable zinc source in tablets and capsules. It is preferred where gastrointestinal compatibility is a formulation priority for the end consumer.

name: Diethylhexyl butamido triazone
description:
Diethylhexyl butamido triazone (CAS 154702-15-5 ), sold under the trade name Uvasorb HEB, is an oil-soluble UVB filter used in sunscreen and photoprotection formulations. It delivers high molar absorptivity in the UVB range.

This characteristic allows formulators to achieve effective sun protection at relatively low use concentrations. In sunscreen products, it is used as a primary UVB-absorbing active for high performance.

It is often combined with UVA filters to achieve broad-spectrum SPF performance. Its oil solubility makes it suitable for anhydrous formulations, emollients, and W/O emulsions where water-soluble filters are not compatible.

Formulators in color cosmetics incorporate it into tinted moisturizers and foundations where daily UV protection is required. This is achieved without compromising the final skin feel of the cosmetic product.

It is also used in hair care products such as leave-on treatments where UV-induced color fade needs to be controlled. This helps prevent protein degradation caused by environmental exposure to the sun.

Diethylhexyl butamido triazone is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard for personal care applications, with purity levels typically confirmed by HPLC.

Packaging options commonly include kilogram-scale bags and drum quantities suited to industrial formulation batches. This ensures reliable supply chains for large-scale manufacturing of sun care and beauty products.

name: Zinc mercaptobenzothiazole
description:
Zinc mercaptobenzothiazole ( CAS 155-04-4 ), commonly abbreviated as ZMBT and also marketed under the trade name Bantex, is an organozinc compound used as a primary accelerator and stabilizer in rubber vulcanization.

It delivers controlled cure rates and oxidative protection across a broad range of elastomer systems. In rubber compounding, ZMBT accelerates sulfur vulcanization in natural and synthetic rubbers, including NR, SBR, and NBR.

This chemical produces consistent cure profiles suited to mechanical goods, seals, and gaskets. Tire manufacturers incorporate it into tread and sidewall compounds where predictable scorch safety and aging resistance are critical.

In plastics processing, it functions as a stabilizer to inhibit thermal degradation during extrusion and molding of polymer components. It also sees use as a secondary accelerator in latex systems.

The compound improves crosslink density in dipped goods and coated fabrics. ZMBT is supplied as a fine off-white to pale yellow powder. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade material meeting industry specifications.

Purity levels are typically at 95% or above for standard applications. It is available in bulk bags and smaller packaged units to suit both large-scale compounders and specialty formulators for various industrial needs.

name: Stannous pyrophosphate
description:
Stannous pyrophosphate (CAS 15578-26-4 ), also known as ditin pyrophosphate, is an inorganic tin salt used as a stabilizer and buffering agent in food and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily to inhibit oxidative degradation and control pH in finished formulations, extending product shelf life and maintaining quality consistency across various industrial applications.

In canned seafood and meat products, it prevents struvite crystal formation and controls discoloration caused by metal-catalyzed oxidation during the preservation and storage process.

Oral care formulators incorporate it into toothpaste and mouthwash systems where it acts as a tartar-control agent, helping to inhibit calcium phosphate deposition on tooth surfaces effectively.

In beverage and food processing, it serves as a sequestrant to protect flavor stability against oxidative changes during storage. Personal care manufacturers also use it in stain-prevention formulations.

This material is utilized where controlled tin ion release is required. The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder available in food-grade specifications aligned with FCC standards.

It is also available as technical-grade material for industrial applications. Packaging is typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or drums to meet both small-batch and bulk procurement requirements.

name: L-arginine hydrochloride
description:

These applications require precise pH control and amino acid delivery. Nutritional supplement producers incorporate it into sports nutrition powders, capsules, and functional beverages targeting amino acid fortification.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a pH adjuster and conditioning agent in hair care and skin care products. Feed and agricultural applications include its use as a dietary amino acid supplement.

It is used in animal nutrition programs to support protein metabolism in livestock and poultry. L-Arginine Hydrochloride is available as a white crystalline powder in bulk and packaged formats for global distribution.

Established grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade FCC specifications to meet pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and food industry requirements.

Technical grade is also available for feed and non-regulated industrial applications. Our material ensures high purity and consistency for demanding manufacturing processes across multiple sectors.

name: Phenylpyruvic acid
description:
Phenylpyruvic acid (CAS 156-06-9 ), also known as phenylpyroracemic acid, is an aromatic keto acid used as a building block and intermediate in pharmaceutical and biotechnology synthesis.

It serves as a precursor in the production of amino acids, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and specialty biochemicals. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key intermediate.

It is used in the enzymatic or chemical synthesis of L-phenylalanine, a commercially significant amino acid used in drug formulations and nutritional products for various industries.

Biotechnology researchers use it as a substrate in transamination studies and enzyme screening assays, where its reactivity with aminotransferases makes it relevant for bioprocess development.

It also appears in the synthesis of phenylpyruvate-derived compounds investigated as scaffolds for CNS-related drug candidates. As a polymerization initiator, it supports specialty polymer systems.

Phenylpyruvic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available primarily in research and pharmaceutical-intermediate grades for industrial applications.

Purity specifications are typically at 98% or higher to meet synthetic and analytical requirements. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk orders for process-scale procurement.

name: 4-nitrosodiphenylamine
description:
4-Nitrosodiphenylamine (CAS 156-10-5 ), also known as p-Nitrosodiphenylamine, is an aromatic amine compound used primarily as a stabilizer and antidegradant in polymer and rubber processing.

It functions by inhibiting oxidative degradation, extending the service life of finished materials under heat and mechanical stress. In rubber compounding, it acts as a prevulcanization inhibitor and antidegradant.

This chemical helps processors control cure onset timing while protecting the compound during mixing and storage. Tire manufacturers incorporate it into tread and sidewall formulations where oxidative breakdown must be minimized.

In plastics processing, it is used to stabilize polymer intermediates and finished articles exposed to elevated temperatures during extrusion or molding. It also serves as a building block in the synthesis of additives.

These complex antioxidant and antiozonant additives are used across rubber goods production. 4-Nitrosodiphenylamine is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline material for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial rubber and polymer applications. It is available in bulk quantities suited to compounding operations for various manufacturing needs.

name: Cysteamine hydrochloride
description:
Cysteamine hydrochloride (CAS 156-57-0 ), also sold as mercaptamine hydrochloride or cysteamine HCl, is a stable salt form of the aminothiol cysteamine used across pharmaceutical, agricultural, and industrial processing applications.

Its thiol and amine functional groups make it a reactive intermediate and active agent in synthesis, formulation, and surface treatment processes. In pharmaceuticals, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients.

It is the basis for cystinosis treatment formulations, making it a high-value procurement target for API manufacturers. Textile and leather processors use it as a reducing agent in wool and hair fiber treatments.

This enables controlled disulfide bond cleavage for permanent waving, softening, and depilation products. In agriculture and animal feed, it functions as a growth-promoting additive and antioxidant stabilizer in premix formulations.

Food manufacturers source it as a flavoring agent and dough conditioner, where its reducing action on gluten disulfide bonds improves dough extensibility in baked goods. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

Standard commercial grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications, as well as technical-grade product for industrial and agricultural use.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to bulk drum supply depending on application requirements. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale laboratory use and large-scale industrial manufacturing.

name: trans-1,2-dichloroethylene
description:
Trans-1,2-dichloroethylene (CAS 156-60-5 ), also known as trans-acetylene dichloride, is a chlorinated solvent used primarily for precision cleaning and degreasing in industrial settings. Its relatively low boiling point and strong solvency make it a practical choice for removing oils and greases.

This chemical is highly effective at removing flux residues from sensitive substrates without aggressive chemical attack. In electronics manufacturing, it is used to clean printed circuit boards and precision components where residue-free surfaces are critical to performance.

Metalworking operations use it as a degreasing solvent to prepare parts prior to coating, plating, or assembly. Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it as a carrier solvent to improve the penetration and evaporation profile of cleaning concentrates.

It also appears in specialty lubricant formulations as a solvent carrier for active ingredients applied to tight-tolerance mechanical components. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance maintenance and repair operations across various sectors.

Trans-1,2-dichloroethylene is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification available for industrial solvent applications, ensuring consistent performance in large-scale manufacturing environments.

Purity levels typically range from 97% upward, with high-purity grades available for electronics and precision cleaning end uses. These specifications ensure that the solvent meets the rigorous demands of modern industrial cleaning and chemical processing standards.

name: Calcium cyanamide
description:
Calcium cyanamide (CAS 156-62-7 ), commercially known as nitrolime or lime nitrogen, is a nitrogen-containing inorganic compound used as a slow-release nitrogen fertilizer and soil-conditioning agent in agriculture.

In industrial contexts, it functions as a chemical intermediate and biocidal agent across several processing applications. In agriculture, it is applied directly to soil as a combined fertilizer and herbicide.

The compound releases nitrogen gradually while suppressing weeds, moss, and certain soil-borne pathogens, reducing the need for separate crop protection treatments. The steel and metallurgical industries use calcium carbimide as a desulfurization agent.

In iron and steel production, it reacts with sulfur impurities in molten metal to improve final product quality. It also serves as a precursor in the synthesis of dicyandiamide and other nitrogen-based chemicals.

These chemicals are used in resin and flame retardant manufacturing. In mining operations, it is used as a flotation reagent to selectively depress certain sulfide minerals during ore separation processes.

Calcium cyanamide is supplied as a granular or powdered solid, typically with a dark grey appearance due to carbon content from the production process. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade material.

Nitrogen content specifications commonly range around 19–21% N. Agricultural-grade formulations are available with added granulation for controlled soil application to ensure consistent nutrient delivery.

name: Sodium lauroamphoacetate
description:
Sodium lauroamphoacetate (CAS 156028-14-7 ), also known by the trade name Miranol HMA, is an amphoteric surfactant derived from lauric acid. It functions as a mild cleansing, foaming, and conditioning agent.

This chemical is highly valued in personal care formulations for its compatibility with both anionic and cationic systems. In shampoos and body washes, it boosts foam density and improves lather quality.

When combined with primary anionic surfactants such as SLES or SLS, it helps in reducing overall irritation potential. Facial cleansers and baby care products use it as a secondary surfactant where mildness is a priority.

It also performs as an emulsifier and dispersant in leave-on and rinse-off conditioning products. This helps stabilize complex surfactant blends while maintaining the desired viscosity and performance of the final product.

Micellar waters and cleansing foams rely on its low irritancy profile to meet sensitive-skin positioning requirements. It is a versatile ingredient that supports the development of high-performance cosmetic formulations.

Sodium lauroamphoacetate is typically supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous solution. The active matter content is commonly around 30–40% depending on the specific requirements of the manufacturer.

It is available in personal care and cosmetic grades, with buyers evaluating conformance to standard industry specifications. Packaging options generally include drums and IBCs for industrial-scale procurement.

name: Sodium methallylsulfonate
description:
Sodium methallylsulfonate (CAS 1561-92-8 ), commonly abbreviated as SMAS, is a reactive sulfonate monomer used as a functional comonomer in polymer synthesis. It introduces anionic sulfonate groups into polymer backbones.

This chemical enables targeted performance modifications in industrial formulations. In water treatment, SMAS is copolymerized into scale inhibitors and dispersants that prevent mineral deposition in cooling towers.

These industrial water systems benefit from the enhanced stability provided by the monomer. Textile and paper processing operations use SMAS-based polymers to improve dye uptake and fiber affinity.

The monomer also improves surface sizing performance in paper manufacturing. In the plastics and polymers sector, it is incorporated into acrylic and vinyl copolymers to enhance colloidal stability.

This improves electrolyte tolerance in emulsion systems during production. Leather processing also employs SMAS-derived polymers as retanning and dispersing agents for better results.

These agents improve the penetration and uniformity of treatment across the material. Sodium methallylsulfonate is typically supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution.

Standard concentrations are available, and the Technical grade is the primary commercial specification for industrial buyers. It is offered in bulk quantities suited to polymer manufacturing.

Packaging options range from bags to intermediate bulk containers to meet logistics needs. This versatile monomer remains a critical component for high-performance anionic polymer production.

Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier in fat-based systems and confectionery coatings, where it supports uniform dispersion and texture consistency. It ensures that ingredients remain well-blended during the manufacturing process.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it acts as a surface modifier and wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and coating uniformity. This improves the overall performance and durability of the industrial application.

Its compatibility with natural and organic formulation standards makes it a preferred emulsifier in certified clean-label and natural cosmetic product lines. It meets the growing demand for sustainable chemical solutions.

name: Sodium isethionate
description:
Sodium isethionate (CAS 1562-00-1 ) is a mild sulfonate salt used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and specialty chemical applications. As a key intermediate and functional ingredient, it enables the synthesis of acyl isethionate surfactants.

These surfactants form the basis of some of the mildest cleansing systems in commercial formulation. In personal care manufacturing, it serves as the direct precursor to sodium cocoyl isethionate and related acyl isethionates.

These are the active cleansing agents in syndet bars, baby washes, and sensitive-skin products. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering and stabilizing component in topical preparations where skin compatibility is required.

Low irritation potential drives ingredient selection in these medical applications. In cosmetic emulsions and liquid cleansers, it contributes to pH regulation and helps maintain formulation stability across a range of electrolyte conditions.

Some industrial applications also leverage its hydroxyethylsulfonate structure for surface-active and dispersing functions in specialty chemical processes. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution, with concentration and purity varying by application. Technical and cosmetic-grade material is the most common commercial form available.

High-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical use, often meeting stringent internal specifications. Buyers should confirm moisture content and active assay when specifying for acyl isethionate synthesis or regulated formulations.

name: Trimethylolpropane triacrylate
description:
Trimethylolpropane triacrylate , widely recognized in the industry as TMPTA, is a trifunctional acrylate monomer used as a reactive crosslinker and diluent in UV- and EB-curable systems.

Its three acrylate groups enable rapid network formation, making it a standard building block in radiation-curable formulations across coatings, adhesives, and inks. The CAS 15625-89-5 material is essential for high-performance applications.

In UV-curable coatings for automotive and industrial substrates, it increases crosslink density, improving scratch resistance and chemical durability of the cured film. Printing ink formulators use it as a reactive diluent.

This allows for precise control of viscosity without sacrificing cure speed or print resolution in energy-curable offset and flexographic inks. In adhesives and sealants, it contributes to cohesive strength and dimensional stability.

Electronics manufacturers incorporate it into conformal coatings and encapsulants where fast cure and thermal resistance are process requirements. It is supplied as a low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

The product is available in standard technical and industrial grades, with some suppliers offering low-skin-sensitization variants. Specifications are generally aligned with reactive monomer industry standards.

Material is commonly evaluated against viscosity, acid value, and inhibitor content to ensure consistency. It meets rigorous industrial requirements for high-speed manufacturing and durable end-use performance.

name: Sodium percarbonate
description:
Sodium percarbonate (CAS 15630-89-4 ), also known by the abbreviation SPC, is an adduct of sodium carbonate and hydrogen peroxide that releases active oxygen upon dissolution in water.

It functions as a solid, free-flowing oxygen bleach and oxidizing agent across cleaning, textile, and water treatment applications. In laundry and household cleaning formulations, SPC delivers bleaching performance.

It serves as a direct alternative to liquid hydrogen peroxide, with the handling advantage of a dry solid. Textile processors use it to bleach natural fibers such as cotton and linen without fiber degradation.

This avoids the issues associated with chlorine-based systems. Water treatment operations apply it as a biocide and oxidant to control biofilm, algae, and organic contaminants in municipal and industrial systems.

In personal care, it is incorporated into tooth-whitening powders and effervescent bath products where controlled oxygen release is the functional mechanism. It is supplied as a white, free-flowing granular powder.

The product typically features an active oxygen content of around 13–14% or expressed as 30% equivalent hydrogen peroxide. Standard commercial grades include technical and detergent grades for various uses.

Coated variants are available to improve storage stability and moisture resistance in finished formulations. Bulk supply is available in bags and big bags for large-scale industrial manufacturing requirements.

Food-contact and high-purity grades are offered for regulated applications. Our material meets rigorous industry specifications to ensure consistent performance and safety across all global supply chains.

name: Polyglyceryl dipolyhydroxystearate
description:
Polyglyceryl dipolyhydroxystearate (CAS 156531-21-4 ), also marketed as Polyglyceryl-2 Dipolyhydroxystearate, is a polyglycerol ester of polyhydroxystearic acid used primarily as a water-in-oil emulsifier and rheology modifier.

It stabilizes emulsions and controls viscosity across cosmetic, food, and industrial formulations. In personal care, it anchors water-in-oil emulsions in sunscreens, foundations, and long-wear skin creams.

This ingredient delivers stable, non-greasy textures that hold up under high pigment or UV-filter loads. Food manufacturers use it as a dispersing and emulsifying agent in chocolate coatings and fat-based confectionery systems.

In these food applications, it reduces viscosity and improves flow during processing. In color cosmetics, it suspends and disperses pigments uniformly within anhydrous or low-water formulations, preventing separation over shelf life.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to stabilize pigment dispersions and modify the rheological profile of oil-based systems. Polyglyceryl dipolyhydroxystearate is supplied as a viscous liquid or soft paste.

The physical state depends on the specific grade and temperature. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are available, with cosmetic grades commonly meeting COSMOS or Ecocert certification requirements.

It is typically offered in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial-scale formulation. This versatile ester provides reliable performance across a wide range of temperature and pH conditions in diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Hydrolyzed rice protein
description:
Hydrolyzed rice protein (CAS 156715-40-1 ), also marketed under trade names such as Gluadin R and Colhibin, is derived from rice endosperm protein broken down into peptides and amino acids through enzymatic or chemical hydrolysis.

In personal care and food applications, it functions as a film-forming humectant and surface-conditioning agent that binds to hair, skin, or food matrices to improve texture and moisture retention.

In hair care formulations, including shampoos, conditioners, and leave-in treatments, it adsorbs onto damaged keratin surfaces to reduce breakage and improve combability. This makes it a versatile ingredient for restorative products.

Skin care manufacturers incorporate it into serums and moisturizers where its low molecular weight peptide fractions support hydration and surface smoothing without leaving an occlusive residue on the skin.

In food and nutrition, it serves as a plant-based protein supplement and flavor precursor in savory applications, including broths, seasonings, and protein-enriched beverages. It is highly valued for its nutritional profile.

Pharmaceutical formulators also use it as a clean-label excipient in oral nutritional products targeting allergen-sensitive populations. It is supplied as a liquid concentrate or spray-dried powder for various uses.

The powder form is preferred for dry blending and capsule applications. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, with some suppliers offering defined molecular weight fractions for specific targets.

Organic-certified and allergen-free variants are available for clean-label and hypoallergenic product lines. These options ensure compliance with modern consumer demands for high-quality, sustainable ingredients.

name: Monoammonium glutamate
description:
Monoammonium glutamate (CAS 15673-81-1 ), also known by its food additive designation E624 , is the ammonium salt form of glutamic acid used primarily as a flavor enhancer in food manufacturing.

It delivers umami taste characteristics at reduced sodium levels, making it a functional alternative to monosodium glutamate in sodium-reduction applications. In processed and savory food production, it is used to boost umami intensity.

This additive is frequently utilized in soups, sauces, seasonings, and snack coatings where sodium content must be controlled. Formulators in meat processing and ready meals incorporate it to maintain flavor depth.

This is particularly useful when reducing salt levels across reformulated products. In agricultural and feed applications, it functions as a palatability enhancer and amino acid supplement in compound animal feeds.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers also use it as a buffering agent in formulations requiring controlled pH stability. Monoammonium glutamate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the standard commercial form for flavor and feed applications. Technical-grade material is available for non-food industrial uses as well.

Buyers should confirm purity levels and DL- versus L-form designation when sourcing for specific formulation requirements. This ensures the material meets the necessary standards for the intended application.

name: Ibuprofen
description:
Ibuprofen (CAS 15687-27-1 ) is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory active pharmaceutical ingredient used across prescription and OTC drug manufacturing globally. Sourced in bulk API form, it functions as the primary analgesic agent.

The largest commercial demand comes from OTC tablet and capsule production, where it is the active ingredient in pain relief and fever reduction products. Liquid suspension manufacturing represents a distinct high-volume segment.

These pediatric formulations require specific particle size and solubility profiles to ensure efficacy. Topical pharmaceutical products, including gels and creams for localized pain, rely on defined concentrations for transdermal delivery.

Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers also source this material as a starting material or intermediate. It is frequently used in the synthesis of ibuprofen lysinate and other specialized salt-form derivatives.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bulk quantities, typically ranging from kilogram to multi-tonne lots. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph.Eur. , and JP for global compliance.

Grade selection is driven by the target market's regulatory requirements and specific formulation needs. Micronized grades are available for applications where enhanced dissolution rate or suspension uniformity is a priority.

Flexographic and gravure ink formulators use it to control drying speed and maintain pigment dispersion stability on press. This ensures high-quality results during the printing process across various industrial substrates.

Industrial and institutional cleaning products rely on it as an active solvent for cutting through grease, oils, and soils on hard surfaces. It provides the necessary strength for heavy-duty degreasing applications.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust open time and improve substrate wetting in solvent-borne formulations. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing and product development.

The material is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity typically at 99% or above for most industrial uses.

name: Lead octoate
description:
Lead octoate (CAS 15696-43-2 ), also supplied under trade designations such as Pb-Novosik and Nikka Octhix Lead, is an organolead carboxylate used industrially as a catalyst and curing co-agent.

It accelerates crosslinking and polymerization reactions in rubber and polymer processing, where reaction rate and cure efficiency are the primary sourcing drivers for industrial manufacturers.

In rubber compounding, lead octoate functions as a vulcanization accelerator and co-catalyst, improving cure speed and crosslink density in technical rubber goods and specialized components.

Polymer and PVC processors use it as a heat stabilizer co-component and catalytic additive in resin systems requiring controlled gelation and specific thermal stability profiles during production.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it contributes to extreme-pressure additive packages where metal-reactive organometallic compounds are specified for high-performance applications.

Specialty coating and alkyd resin manufacturers also employ it as a drier catalyst to promote oxidative curing in industrial finishes, ensuring proper film formation and durability.

Lead octoate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in mineral spirits or naphtha carriers, at varying metal content concentrations commonly expressed as percentage lead by weight.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial applications. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers, with concentration and carrier solvent confirmed against requirements.

name: Ferric sodium EDTA
description:
Ferric sodium EDTA (CAS 15708-41-5 ), also known as NaFeEDTA and sodium ironedetate, is a chelated iron compound used across food, pharmaceutical, agricultural, and personal care markets.

It delivers bioavailable iron in a stable, water-soluble form that remains active across a wide pH range. This is a critical factor for formulators working with complex matrices where conventional iron salts would precipitate.

In food fortification, NaFeEDTA is added to staple foods such as flour, rice, and condiments to deliver iron with higher absorption rates than inorganic iron salts, particularly in populations with inhibitor-rich diets.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use sodium ironedetate as the active iron source in oral iron-deficiency preparations, including syrups and drops, where tolerability and stability are formulation priorities.

In agriculture, it functions as a foliar or soil-applied iron chelate to correct iron chlorosis in crops grown in high-pH soils where iron availability is limited for the plants.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a chelating agent to sequester trace metals in rinse-off and leave-on products, protecting fragrance and active ingredient stability over time.

Ferric sodium EDTA is supplied as a water-soluble powder or granule. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter meeting USP and BP standards.

Agricultural grades are also commercially available for fertilizer and crop nutrition applications. These various grades ensure the product meets the specific purity requirements of each industrial sector.

In cosmetics and topical pharmaceutical products, it functions as a preservative in creams, lotions, and ointments, controlling microbial growth across both gram-positive bacteria and fungi.

Industrial cleaning and disinfectant manufacturers incorporate it into hard-surface sanitizers and instrument disinfection products where reliable bactericidal performance is required for safety.

Water treatment applications use it as a biocide to control microbial fouling in process water and cooling systems. Personal care formulators also select it for preservation of various products.

It is particularly effective for rinse-off and leave-on products where the neutral-to-alkaline pH range aligns with its optimal activity window for maximum antimicrobial efficacy and stability.

Sodium p-chloro-m-cresol is supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid. It is available in technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of markets.

It delivers reliable surface-active performance across cleaning, emulsification, and dispersion applications in both industrial and consumer formulations. In home care and industrial cleaning, it functions as the primary surfactant.

It is used in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and all-purpose concentrates, providing low-foam or controlled-foam profiles depending on the degree of ethoxylation. Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off products.

It is also used in emulsified systems where stable oil-in-water emulsions are required. Textile processing operations use it as a scouring and wetting agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and soil removal.

In paper and leather processing, it supports emulsification of treatment baths and improves surface wetting during coating or finishing steps. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

It functions as a broad-spectrum biocide and preservative, targeting microbial contamination in finished products and manufacturing environments. In topical pharmaceutical preparations, it is incorporated to maintain sterility.

Personal care manufacturers use it in rinse-off and leave-on products, including shampoos, conditioners, and skin cleansers, where microbial control is a formulation requirement for safety.

It is also evaluated for use in antiseptic preparations where surface-active biocidal performance is needed alongside acceptable skin compatibility. This makes it versatile for various hygiene applications.

name: Sodium dodecylmonooxyethylene sulfate
description:
Sodium dodecylmonooxyethylene sulfate ( CAS 15826-16-1 ), also known as sodium lauryl ether sulfate, is an anionic surfactant used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

It delivers effective foaming, emulsification, and soil removal at competitive use levels. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid hand soaps, it functions as the primary cleansing and lather-generating agent.

name: Diethylenetriamine pentamethylene phosphonic acid
description:
Diethylenetriamine pentamethylene phosphonic acid , commonly known as DTPMP, is a high-performance phosphonate chelating agent used across water treatment, energy, and industrial processing sectors.

It binds metal ions and inhibits scale formation, keeping process systems clean and operational under demanding conditions. This chemical is identified by CAS 15827-60-8 .

In water treatment, DTPMP is dosed into cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems to prevent calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and barium sulfate scale deposits.

Oil and gas operators use it in injection water and produced water handling to control mineral scaling in pipelines and downhole equipment. It is essential for maintaining flow efficiency.

Textile and paper mills apply it to sequester hardness ions in process water, protecting equipment and improving the consistency of bleaching and dyeing operations.

Its phosphonate structure also supports corrosion inhibition in closed-loop systems, where metal ion stabilization reduces oxidative degradation of system components.

DTPMP is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 50% active content, though higher-concentration grades are available for specific industrial applications.

The Technical grade is the standard market offering, formulated for industrial dosing systems. Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers is the conventional format for procurement.

name: Desmorapid
description:

This catalyst gives formulators precise control over the reaction profile and processing window. In flexible and rigid polyurethane foam production, it promotes the isocyanate-water reaction, enabling consistent cell structure and rise times.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to shorten open time and improve green strength in one- and two-component PU systems. In coatings, it supports crosslink density development in moisture-cure and two-pack urethane formulations.

These formulations are commonly applied to industrial substrates for enhanced durability. Industrial cleaning and surface treatment products incorporate it as a pH buffer and process aid where controlled alkalinity is required.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically handled in drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial-scale dosing. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for polyurethane catalyst applications.

name: Glucono Delta Lactone
description:
Glucono Delta Lactone (CAS 15892-28-1 ), commonly abbreviated as GDL, is a naturally derived cyclic ester of gluconic acid used as a slow-release acidulant in food and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Unlike mineral acids, it hydrolyzes gradually in aqueous environments, enabling controlled pH reduction without sharp acidic shock. This makes it a preferred choice where gentle, time-dependent acidification is a formulation requirement.

In food manufacturing, GDL is used to set tofu and fresh cheeses by triggering protein coagulation through gradual acidification, giving processors precise control over texture and yield.

Meat processors incorporate it into cured products such as salami and frankfurters to accelerate fermentation and improve color stability without relying solely on bacterial cultures.

Bakers use GDL as a leavening acid in combination with sodium bicarbonate, particularly in dry mixes where reaction timing must be delayed until baking.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications, it functions as a pH modifier and excipient in tablet formulations and effervescent systems.

GDL is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade is the primary commercial specification, with material commonly meeting FCC and E575 standards for food additive use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting BP or Ph. Eur. specifications is available for regulated manufacturing applications.

name: Calcium stearate
description:
Calcium stearate (CAS 1592-23-0 ), also known as calcium distearate, is a calcium soap of stearic acid used across plastics, rubber, pharmaceuticals, and construction materials.

It functions primarily as a lubricant, release agent, and stabilizer, preventing adhesion, reducing friction, and controlling flow in solid processing systems.

In PVC and polymer compounding, it acts as an internal and external lubricant, improving melt flow and preventing die buildup during extrusion and calendering.

Pharmaceutical tablet manufacturers use it as a die lubricant and anti-caking agent to ensure consistent tablet weight and clean press release during the manufacturing process.

In concrete and building products, it waterproofs cement mixes and improves workability without compromising structural integrity. Rubber processors incorporate it as a mold release agent.

It also serves as a dispersing aid for fillers, reducing cycle times and improving surface finish on molded parts. Calcium stearate is supplied as a fine white powder.

Particle size and bulk density vary by grade to suit different processing requirements. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications.

Technical-grade product is standard for plastics, rubber, and construction applications, where purity thresholds are less stringent for industrial manufacturing needs.

name: 1-Docosene
description:
1-Docosene (CAS 1599-67-3 ) is a long-chain linear alpha-olefin used as a monomer and chemical building block in polymer synthesis and specialty lubricant formulations.

Its 22-carbon terminal double bond makes it a reactive intermediate for producing high-molecular-weight polymers and functionalized derivatives sought by formulators working at the heavier end of the olefin spectrum.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, 1-Docosene is incorporated as a comonomer or homopolymer feedstock to modify chain length, crystallinity, and melt behavior in polyolefin systems.

Lubricant formulators use it as a base material or co-reactant for producing synthetic base oils and viscosity-modifying additives suited to high-temperature or heavy-duty applications.

Its reactivity at the terminal double bond supports the synthesis of detergent-range intermediates, waxes, and surface-active compounds in oleochemical processing.

Metalworking fluid producers may also draw on its lubricity contribution when blending specialty cutting or forming fluids targeting extreme-pressure conditions.

1-Docosene is supplied as a liquid at elevated temperatures or as a waxy solid at ambient conditions, depending on purity and handling setup for industrial use.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically confirmed by GC analysis. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers.

name: Zinc lactate
description:
Zinc lactate (CAS 16039-53-5 ), also referred to as zinc dilactate, is an organic zinc salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It delivers bioavailable zinc in a form that integrates cleanly into aqueous formulations.

Clean label and taste neutrality are priorities for these food applications. In pharmaceutical tablet and capsule formulations, it supplies zinc as a mineral supplement with favorable gastrointestinal tolerability.

Polyglyceryl-4 Caprate (CAS 160391-93-5 ), also marketed as Tegosoft PC 41 and known in formulation as Tetraglycerol Monocaprate, is a mild, plant-derived emulsifier and wetting agent used across personal care, food, and industrial applications.

Food manufacturers use it to stabilize emulsions and improve texture in fat-based systems, benefiting from its compatibility with natural and organic labeling requirements across global markets today.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a dispersing and wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and pigment distribution. It also supports humectancy in leave-on cosmetic formats for moisture.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with material often meeting FCC and EU cosmetic regulatory requirements. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers.

description:
Butyl 3-mercaptopropionate (CAS 16215-21-7 ) is a thiol-functional ester used as a reactive building block and performance additive across polymer chemistry and industrial lubrication.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it into metalworking fluids and gear oils where sulfur-containing additives reduce friction and protect metal surfaces under extreme pressure conditions.

It also serves as a reactive intermediate in synthesizing polythiol crosslinkers, which are used to produce fast-curing coatings and sealants with controlled network density.

Plastics compounders may use it as a processing stabilizer or co-agent in systems where thiol reactivity improves compatibility between polymer phases during the manufacturing process.

Butyl 3-mercaptopropionate is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purity levels, typically 95% or higher. It is available in technical grade for industrial and polymer applications.

Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to drum-scale supply for industrial buyers, ensuring flexible procurement options for diverse manufacturing requirements and scales.

name: Zinc myristate
description:
Zinc myristate (CAS 16260-27-8 ), also known as zinc tetradecanoate, is a zinc salt of myristic acid used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and polymer manufacturing. It functions primarily as a lubricant, flow modifier, and surface treatment agent in solid and semi-solid systems.

In cosmetics and personal care, it acts as a slip agent and texture modifier in pressed powders, foundations, and dry skincare formulations. These properties help in improving spreadability and skin adhesion for high-end consumer products.

Pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing uses it as a lubricant to reduce die friction and improve ejection performance in direct compression processes. This ensures consistent dosage forms and prevents sticking during high-speed production cycles.

In plastics and polymer processing, it functions as an internal and external lubricant, aiding mold release and reducing surface defects. It is particularly effective in PVC and other thermoplastic compounds requiring high thermal stability.

It also serves surface treatment applications where hydrophobic coating of mineral fillers or pigments is required. This process is essential to improve dispersion in polymer matrices and enhance the final physical properties of the material.

Zinc myristate is supplied as a fine white powder. Technical and cosmetic-grade material are the most commonly available specifications, with particle size distribution being a key quality parameter for powder-based formulations.

Buyers sourcing for pharmaceutical applications should confirm compliance with relevant pharmacopeial standards such as USP , BP , or EP . Adherence to excipient GMP requirements is also critical for regulatory approval in medical applications.

name: Zinc salicylate
description:
Zinc salicylate (CAS 16283-36-6 ), also known as zinc disalicylate, is the zinc salt of salicylic acid used across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing. It combines the keratolytic and antimicrobial activity of salicylate with the skin-conditioning and astringent properties of zinc.

This combination makes it highly relevant to formulators targeting both therapeutic and cosmetic endpoints. In topical pharmaceutical formulations, it is used in creams and ointments targeting acne, seborrheic conditions, and hyperkeratotic skin disorders.

These applications are ideal where controlled exfoliation and antimicrobial action are required. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into anti-dandruff shampoos, foot care products, and deodorant formulations for enhanced performance.

Both zinc and salicylate activity contribute to the finished product's performance profile in these settings. It also appears in medicated powders and dusting formulations designed for moisture control and mild antiseptic protection.

Oral care applications include its use as an active component in certain astringent mouthwashes and gum-care preparations. Zinc salicylate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet purity requirements aligned with USP and BP standards. Technical-grade supply is also sourced for industrial personal care manufacturing and large-scale production needs.

Packaging is typically offered in kilogram quantities through to bulk drums depending on application requirements. This ensures flexibility for both research-scale development and full-scale commercial manufacturing processes.

description:
Bis-aminopropyl diglycol dimaleate (CAS 1629579-82-3 ) is a specialty diamine crosslinker used in personal care formulations to modify and strengthen hair fiber surfaces.

By forming covalent bonds with keratin proteins, it improves the structural integrity of chemically treated or damaged hair. It is primarily used in bond-building hair treatments and salon-grade repair systems.

The compound works alongside bleaching or coloring processes to reduce breakage and improve elasticity. In leave-on and rinse-off conditioning formulations, it deposits onto the hair shaft to reinforce weakened disulfide bonds.

Retail bond-repair product lines, including pre-treatment boosters and in-salon additives, rely on this ingredient to deliver measurable improvements in tensile strength for various hair types.

It is also incorporated into at-home treatment masks and serums targeting chemically processed or heat-damaged hair. This versatile ingredient ensures long-lasting results for professional hair care applications.

Bis-aminopropyl diglycol dimaleate is supplied as a liquid, typically as an aqueous solution. It is available in cosmetic-grade quality suitable for direct incorporation into personal care formulations.

name: Strontium carbonate
description:
Strontium carbonate (CAS 1633-05-2 ), also identified under the colorant index reference CI 77837, is an inorganic mineral salt used across ceramics, electronics, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a strontium source in high-temperature processing and as a stabilizing or buffering agent in formulated systems. In the electronics industry, it is a key raw material for producing cathode ray tube glass.

Ferrite components also utilize this material, where controlled strontium content directly affects dielectric performance. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a corrosion-inhibiting pigment in anti-rust primers.

In these applications, it neutralizes acidic byproducts and passivates metal substrates. In plastics and polymer compounding, it acts as a heat and light stabilizer, extending service life in PVC and related systems.

Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical producers also use it as a catalyst precursor and pH-buffering agent. It is essential in various synthesis and processing applications requiring high chemical stability.

Strontium carbonate is supplied as a fine white powder in technical and high-purity grades. Particle size distribution varies by grade, with finer cuts available for electronic and coating applications.

Surface coverage and reactivity are critical factors in these specialized sectors. Standard packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities to suit both laboratory-scale and industrial procurement needs.
