name: Methyl tert-butyl ether
description:
Methyl tert-butyl ether (CAS 1634-04-4 ), commonly known as MTBE, is an ether-based solvent used across chemical processing and specialty formulation industries. It offers fast evaporation and strong solvency for a range of organic compounds.

This material is a practical choice where clean solvent recovery is a priority. In personal care and cosmetics manufacturing, it functions as a process solvent for extracting and purifying fragrance ingredients and active compounds.

Its low residue profile suits applications where solvent carryover into finished formulations must be minimized. In laboratory and analytical settings, it is a standard extraction solvent for isolating non-polar compounds from aqueous matrices.

Flavor and fragrance producers also use it as a carrier solvent during intermediate synthesis steps. In these environments, controlled evaporation aids in precise concentration management during the production cycle.

The product is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), and drums. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for industrial use and large-scale processing.

High-purity grades are available for analytical and specialty synthesis applications. Buyers should confirm purity thresholds and peroxide content specifications when sourcing for sensitive extraction or formulation processes.

name: N-Propylethanolamine
description:
N-Propylethanolamine (CAS 16369-21-4 ), also referred to commercially as PMEA or mono-n-propyl monoethanolamine, is a bifunctional amino alcohol combining both amine and hydroxyl reactivity in a single molecule.

It functions as a pH buffer, corrosion inhibitor, and emulsifier across industrial and personal care formulations. In metalworking fluids and lubricant concentrates, it provides corrosion protection for ferrous and non-ferrous metals.

The chemical stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions at working concentrations. Coatings and resin systems use it as a neutralizing agent for acid-functional resins, improving dispersion stability and film formation in waterborne systems.

In adhesives and sealants, it acts as a reactive intermediate or curing modifier where controlled amine functionality is required. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a pH adjuster in emulsion-based products.

This moderate, less volatile amine is often preferred over triethanolamine in specific formulations. N-Propylethanolamine is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes.

It is available in technical grade, which covers the majority of industrial applications in lubricants, coatings, and adhesives. Buyers sourcing for personal care applications should confirm purity specifications.

name: Dolomite
description:
Dolomite (CAS 16389-88-1 ), a naturally occurring calcium magnesium carbonate mineral, is used across industrial and agricultural sectors primarily as a pH-adjusting and buffering agent.

Its dual calcium and magnesium content makes it a preferred choice over single-element neutralizers where soil or process chemistry demands both nutrients simultaneously.

In agriculture, dolomite is applied to acidic soils to raise pH and correct magnesium deficiency, directly improving crop yields in magnesium-sensitive crops such as cereals and potatoes.

Water treatment facilities use it to remineralize soft or desalinated water, restoring alkalinity and hardness to meet drinking water standards for municipal and industrial use.

In construction, it serves as a filler and aggregate in asphalt, concrete, and road base materials, where consistent particle size and carbonate content are critical to specification compliance.

Metallurgical operations use dolomite as a flux in steel and iron production to remove impurities during smelting. It is supplied as crushed stone, ground powder, and micronized grades.

Particle size ranges vary from coarse agricultural lime to fine industrial powders. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are available, with purity levels defined by CaCO3 and MgCO3 content.

Agricultural grades are commonly sold by mesh size, while industrial grades may be specified by reactivity or neutralizing value to ensure performance in chemical processes.

name: Sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate
description:
Sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate (CAS 1639-66-3 ), also known as sodium diethylhexyl sulfosuccinate, is an anionic surfactant used across industrial and specialty formulations.

It functions primarily as a wetting agent, emulsifier, and dispersant, enabling uniform mixing of oil and water phases in systems where conventional surfactants underperform.

In agricultural formulations, it improves the spreading and penetration of pesticide and herbicide concentrates, ensuring even coverage on treated surfaces during application.

Personal care and cosmetic manufacturers incorporate it into cleansing products and emulsions where controlled foam and stable dispersion are required for high-quality results.

Textile and leather processing operations use it to enhance dye penetration and improve wetting of fiber substrates during treatment baths to ensure consistent color and finish.

In printing and packaging, it acts as a dispersant and wetting agent in ink and coating formulations to promote substrate adhesion and pigment uniformity across various materials.

Sodium dioctyl sulfosuccinate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at concentrations of 70–75% active content, though solid forms are available for specific industrial applications.

Technical and food-grade specifications are the most commonly sourced, with food-grade material meeting FCC standards for use in regulated applications and sensitive formulations.

name: Geraniol acetate
description:
Geraniol acetate (CAS 16409-44-2 ) is a naturally occurring ester used as a fragrance and flavoring ingredient across personal care, food, and industrial applications. It delivers a fresh, floral-rosy character with fruity nuances.

This versatile chemical is a recognized building block in perfumery and flavor formulation. In fine fragrance and personal care products, including soaps and lotions, it contributes a clean floral top note that blends well with citrus accords.

Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it as a flavoring agent in fruit preparations and confectionery. It is often utilized where a rose-like or peach-adjacent profile is desired, carrying FEMA code 2509 and E number E1518 status.

Coatings and printing ink formulators use it as a fragrance modifier to mask solvent odors. This application helps improve the scent profile of finished products, ensuring a more pleasant experience for the end user in industrial settings.

Adhesive and sealant applications also draw on its ester character to contribute mild, pleasant odor correction. This is particularly useful in consumer-facing formats where chemical odors must be minimized through effective masking agents.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid and is available in various specifications. Flavor-grade options typically meet FCC standards for food use, ensuring high purity and safety for consumption in regulated markets.

name: Hexadecyltrimethoxysilane
description:
Hexadecyltrimethoxysilane (CAS 16415-12-6 ), also known as Cetyl trimethoxysilane, is a long-chain alkylsilane used to chemically modify inorganic surfaces and impart hydrophobicity.

It bonds covalently to mineral substrates, enabling durable water repellency and improved compatibility between inorganic fillers and organic matrices. In coatings and sealants, it treats mineral fillers.

Commonly treated fillers include silica, calcium carbonate, and talc to improve dispersion and reduce moisture uptake in the final formulation. Adhesive and elastomer manufacturers use it as a coupling agent.

This silane strengthens the interface between polymer matrices and glass or silica-based reinforcements. In plastics compounding, surface-treated fillers processed with this silane deliver better mechanical performance.

The material also helps in reducing agglomeration during processing. Personal care formulators apply it to powder pigments and mineral actives to convert hydrophilic surfaces to hydrophobic ones.

This application improves skin feel and water resistance in color cosmetics. The product is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid and is available in technical grade with purity levels at 95% or higher.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk IBC containers, depending on supplier and volume requirements. This versatile chemical ensures high performance across various industrial and consumer applications.

description:
Erythrosine (CAS 16423-68-0 ), also known as E127 and erythrosine sodium anhydrous, is a synthetic red dye derived from fluorone. It delivers a bright cherry-pink to red coloration across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications.

It is one of the few certified red colorants approved for specific food uses in multiple regulatory markets. This makes it a reliable option for formulators working within defined compliance frameworks and strict safety guidelines.

In food manufacturing, it is used to color maraschino cherries, candied fruits, and certain confectionery products where a vivid red shade is required. Pharmaceutical tablet coatings and oral dosage forms use it for product identification.

In printing inks and packaging, it contributes to red and pink tones in water-based ink formulations. The textile and paper industries apply it as a dye for specialty coloring processes where its fluorescent properties support visual effects.

The product is supplied as a fine red powder or water-soluble granules. It is available in food-grade specifications certified to FCC and E127 standards, ensuring high purity for human consumption and safety.

Its oxidative stability and clean sensory profile make it a preferred alternative to conventional sunflower oil across food, personal care, and industrial applications for various manufacturers.

In food manufacturing, it is used as a frying and cooking oil where extended shelf life and heat stability reduce oil turnover costs in commercial kitchens and snack production lines.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, lotions, and hair conditioners as an emollient that absorbs readily without leaving a heavy residue on the skin or hair.

In industrial lubricants and metalworking fluids, its stability under thermal stress supports longer fluid service life compared to standard vegetable oils used in similar mechanical processes.

Coatings and alkyd resin manufacturers also use it as a bio-based raw material where controlled drying behavior is required for high-performance industrial finishes and protective layers.

It functions as a natural antimicrobial and antioxidant agent across cosmetic, nutraceutical, and pharmaceutical formulations. In personal care, it is incorporated into facial serums, toners, and acne-targeting treatments.

Natural preservation and skin-calming activity are required alongside synthetic or clean-label preservative systems. Pharmaceutical and healthcare product manufacturers use it in topical preparations and herbal remedy formulations.

These applications target antimicrobial efficacy in various medical contexts. In functional food and nutraceutical applications, it appears in botanical supplement blends and health beverages positioned around traditional herbal use.

name: Tetrabutylammonium bromide
description:
Tetrabutylammonium bromide (CAS 1643-19-2 ), commonly sourced under the abbreviation TBAB, is a quaternary ammonium salt used primarily as a phase-transfer catalyst and reagent in chemical synthesis.

Its ability to shuttle anions between immiscible phases makes it a practical tool for improving reaction efficiency and yield in multi-step manufacturing processes across various industrial sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TBAB accelerates nucleophilic substitution and alkylation reactions, reducing processing time and solvent consumption in active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) synthesis.

Personal care formulators use it as a conditioning and antimicrobial agent in rinse-off and leave-on products where quaternary ammonium activity is required for the final formulation.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor in polymer and specialty chemical production, where controlled ionic transfer between organic and aqueous phases is critical to process consistency.

In research and fine chemical synthesis, TBAB supports the preparation of ionic liquids and serves as a co-catalyst in carbon dioxide fixation reactions for sustainable chemistry.

Tetrabutylammonium bromide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid. It is available in technical and high-purity reagent grades for diverse laboratory and industrial uses.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meets specifications relevant to API and excipient manufacturing. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial lots.

name: Trisodium dicarboxymethyl alaninate
description:
Trisodium dicarboxymethyl alaninate (CAS 164462-16-2 ), also known as DL-Alanine-N,N-diacetic acid trisodium salt, is a biodegradable aminopolycarboxylate chelating agent derived from alanine.

It sequesters calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions across a broad pH range, enabling formulators to replace conventional chelants such as EDTA in environmentally sensitive applications.

In personal care, it stabilizes formulations by deactivating trace metals that would otherwise degrade active ingredients or cause discoloration in shampoos, lotions, and liquid soaps.

Home care and industrial cleaning products rely on it to prevent limescale redeposition and boost surfactant performance in hard-water conditions during various cleaning cycles.

Water treatment applications use it to control metal ion interference in process water and cooling systems where biodegradability is a regulatory or operational requirement for the facility.

Its compatibility with alkaline cleaning systems also makes it suitable for CIP formulations in food processing environments where high performance and safety are essential for operations.

Trisodium dicarboxymethyl alaninate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations commonly available in the 30 to 40 percent range for industrial use.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering, with product specifications aligned to chelant performance parameters such as active content, pH, and iron content limits.

name: Sodium ferric EDDHA
description:
Sodium ferric EDDHA (CAS 16455-61-1 ), commonly supplied and sourced as Fe-EDDHA or EDDHA Iron Chelate, is a chelated iron micronutrient used to correct and prevent iron deficiency in crops.

Unlike simpler iron salts, it maintains iron availability across a wide soil pH range, making it the preferred choice for alkaline and calcareous soils where other iron sources fail to perform.

Fe-EDDHA is the standard corrective treatment for iron chlorosis in high-value crops including citrus, grapevines, stone fruits, and ornamentals, applied via soil drench or fertigation systems.

In greenhouse and hydroponic production, it supplies stable, plant-available iron throughout the growth cycle without precipitation at elevated pH levels during the cultivation process.

Turf management programs use it to maintain color and density in alkaline-soil sports fields and golf courses. Formulators of soluble fertilizer blends incorporate it as the primary iron source.

This is especially critical where soil pH or water hardness would compromise alternative chelates. Sodium ferric EDDHA is supplied as a dark red-brown granular or microgranular solid material.

Iron content is typically expressed as a percentage of total and ortho-ortho chelated iron fraction. Standard commercial grades are defined by total Fe% and solubility specifications.

These grades are aligned with EU fertilizer regulations. Technical and agronomic grades are available, with ortho-ortho fractions ranging from 1.6% to 6% Fe depending on application requirements.

name: Pantoprazole sodium sesquihydrate
description:
Pantoprazole sodium sesquihydrate (CAS 164579-32-2 ), also marketed under the brand name Pantosec, is the stable hydrated sodium salt form of pantoprazole used as the active pharmaceutical ingredient in proton pump inhibitor drug products.

It is the commercially preferred form for solid and injectable dosage manufacturing due to its defined hydration state and improved handling characteristics. The primary application is in the manufacture of enteric-coated tablets.

It is also used for delayed-release capsules for the treatment of acid-related gastrointestinal conditions. It is formulated into lyophilized powders for intravenous injection, where the sodium salt form supports aqueous solubility requirements.

Generic drug manufacturers source this API to produce finished dose forms targeting hospital and retail pharmacy supply chains. Formulators working on bioequivalence studies or line extensions also procure it as a reference-grade material.

Pantoprazole sodium sesquihydrate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications conforming to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. monographs for global compliance.

The material is provided with documentation packages including CoA, DMF references, and ICH-compliant impurity profiles. Packaging typically ranges from small quantities for R&D use to bulk quantities for commercial manufacturing.

name: DL-panthenol
description:
DL-Panthenol (CAS 16485-10-2 ), also known as pantothenol, is the racemic form of the provitamin B5 alcohol used as a humectant, moisturizing agent, and film-forming conditioner across personal care, pharmaceutical, and polymer applications.

Unlike the D-isomer, the DL form is positioned primarily for topical and industrial use where biological activity of the pure enantiomer is not required. In personal care formulations, it is incorporated into shampoos and conditioners.

It is also used in skin creams and lotions to improve moisture retention and surface feel in the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it in topical preparations such as wound gels, nasal sprays, and eye drops.

In these medical applications, its humectant function supports tissue hydration. In polyurethane and polymer systems, it functions as a reactive diol, participating in cross-linking and chain extension to modify flexibility.

This chemical helps modify mechanical properties in industrial systems. Cosmetic formulators also use it in leave-on hair treatments, where it penetrates the hair shaft and reduces brittleness for better hair health.

DL-Panthenol is supplied as a clear, viscous liquid. Standard commercial grades include cosmetic/personal care grade and pharmaceutical grade, with the latter typically conforming to USP or Ph.Eur. specifications.

Bulk supply is available in drums and IBCs, with concentrations commonly at 75% or 50% aqueous solution alongside neat material. This ensures versatility for various manufacturing scales and formulation requirements.

name: Neotame
description:
Neotame (CAS 165450-17-9 ), also identified by its EU designation E961 , is a high-intensity artificial sweetener derived from aspartame chemistry but engineered for significantly greater potency.

At 7,000–13,000 times the sweetness of sucrose, it allows formulators to achieve target sweetness profiles at extremely low inclusion rates, reducing ingredient cost per unit and simplifying label declarations.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to sweeten reduced-calorie and sugar-free products including carbonated drinks, dairy desserts, baked goods, and confectionery where heat and pH stability are required.

Tabletop sweetener blends and flavor-masking applications benefit from its ability to suppress bitter off-notes at sub-threshold concentrations. In oral care products it delivers sweetness without fermentable sugars.

This supports non-cariogenic formulation claims in products such as toothpaste and mouthwash. Personal care formulators also incorporate it into lip care and cosmetic products where a mild sweet sensory profile is desirable.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade material meeting FCC and regulatory specifications aligned with FDA and EFSA approvals is the standard commercial form.

Packaging typically ranges from small quantities for R&D use up to bulk quantities for industrial-scale production. This ensures versatility for both laboratory testing and large manufacturing requirements.

name: Sodium methyl siliconate
description:

It functions as both a surface modifier and a corrosion inhibitor across construction, textile, and industrial treatment processes. In building and construction, it is applied to concrete, brick, and masonry surfaces.

This application reduces water absorption and slows corrosion of embedded reinforcement. Textile and leather processors use it to treat fabrics and hides, improving moisture resistance without altering hand feel.

In paper manufacturing, it modifies surface energy to control water penetration and improve dimensional stability of finished sheets. This ensures the material remains durable under various environmental conditions.

Water treatment and industrial maintenance applications use it as a corrosion inhibitor in metal-contact systems. The siliconate film formation provides protective barrier properties for critical pipework.

The product is typically supplied as an aqueous alkaline solution, with active content concentrations commonly in the range of 30–50%. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for these uses.

Bulk supply in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) is the norm for industrial procurement volumes. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and construction projects.

Diisononyl hexahydrophthalate (CAS 166412-78-8 ), commercially known as DINCH, is a non-phthalate plasticizer developed as a high-purity alternative for sensitive-end-use PVC applications.

It delivers flexibility and durability to polymer formulations where regulatory compliance and low migration are procurement priorities. In medical devices and food-contact materials, DINCH meets stringent extraction thresholds.

It is ideal for PVC tubing, blood bags, and packaging films. Automotive interior components, including instrument panel skins and door liners, use DINCH-plasticized PVC to meet low-fogging and low-emission specifications.

These materials often must comply with standards such as VDA 278. Flexible packaging and printing substrates benefit from its compatibility with inks and coatings where odor neutrality is a critical requirement.

Toy and childcare article manufacturers specify DINCH to satisfy REACH restrictions on conventional phthalate plasticizers in consumer goods. It ensures safety and compliance for products intended for children.

In biotechnology and molecular biology, it is used in enzyme reaction buffers and nucleic acid precipitation protocols where precise magnesium ion concentration is critical. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a pH-buffering excipient in parenteral and topical preparations.

These preparations often require controlled ionic strength for stability. In personal care, it supports moisture retention in skin-conditioning formulations and helps stabilize product pH across a range of cosmetic systems.

Food-grade material is used as a magnesium source and acidity regulator in functional food and dietary supplement manufacturing. This versatile compound is available as a white crystalline powder or granule depending on the specific industrial need.

name: Triethanolamine lauroylsarcosinate
description:
Triethanolamine lauroylsarcosinate (CAS 16693-53-1 ), also known as lauroylsarcosine triethanolamine, is a mild anionic surfactant used in personal care and cosmetic formulations.

It delivers cleansing, foam generation, and emulsification performance while maintaining compatibility with sensitive skin systems. In facial cleansers and body washes, it provides effective soil and sebum removal.

The material offers a controlled, stable foam profile suited to mild formulations. Shampoo and conditioner manufacturers use it to balance cleansing efficacy with scalp compatibility, often in combination with other surfactant systems.

It functions as an emulsifier and dispersant in leave-on and rinse-off products where uniform distribution of active ingredients across the formulation is required for performance.

Toothpaste and oral care formulators also incorporate it as a secondary surfactant to support cleaning action and foam texture without the harshness associated with conventional sulfate-based systems.

Triethanolamine lauroylsarcosinate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution. It is available in cosmetic and personal care grade specifications, with purity and active content levels aligned to industry requirements.

name: Sodium hydrosulfide
description:
Sodium hydrosulfide ( CAS 16721-80-5 ), also known as sodium sulfhydrate and commonly abbreviated as NaHS, is an inorganic sulfide salt used across heavy industry as a reactive sulfur source and chemical intermediate.

It functions primarily as a reducing agent, precipitant, and flotation reagent in processes where controlled sulfide chemistry is required. In mining and metals processing, NaHS is used as a selective flotation depressant.

It acts as a metal sulfide precipitant to recover copper, zinc, and other non-ferrous metals from ore slurries. Pulp and paper manufacturers use it in kraft cooking liquor to improve pulping efficiency and delignification rates.

Leather processors apply it as a depilatory agent to remove hair from hides during the beamhouse stage, a step critical to tannery throughput. In wastewater treatment, it precipitates heavy metals from industrial effluent streams.

This process creates insoluble sulfides, supporting compliance with discharge limits. Sodium hydrosulfide is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 45% NaHS, and in solid flake form.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification across most industrial applications. Solution grades are common for continuous-process industries due to handling and dosing convenience.

name: 3-propoxypropylamine
description:
3-Propoxypropylamine (CAS 16728-59-9 ) is a primary amine with an ether-linked propoxy group, used across industrial formulations as a reactive intermediate and functional additive.

Its combination of amine reactivity and ether solubility character positions it for corrosion inhibition, pH control, and emulsification duties in demanding process environments.

In oil, gas, and water treatment systems, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and pH buffer, protecting metal infrastructure in aggressive aqueous or hydrocarbon media.

Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a curing agent or reactive diluent, where the primary amine group drives crosslinking with epoxy resins.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers use it to stabilize emulsions and maintain pH balance under high-load operating conditions for industrial machinery.

Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical producers source it as a synthetic building block for active ingredients and functional intermediates requiring an ether-amine scaffold.

3-Propoxypropylamine is supplied as a liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial and formulation applications across various manufacturing sectors.

name: Potassium metabisulfite
description:
Potassium metabisulfite (CAS 16731-55-8 ), also sold as potassium pyrosulfite and approved as E224 , is an inorganic sulfite salt used industrially as a preservative, antioxidant, and reducing agent.

It releases sulfur dioxide upon contact with moisture or acids, making it effective for microbial control and oxidation prevention across food, beverage, and industrial applications.

In winemaking and brewing, it is the standard choice for sanitizing equipment, inhibiting wild yeast, and protecting finished products from oxidative spoilage during storage.

Food manufacturers use it to prevent enzymatic browning in dried fruits, potato products, and seafood processing. Water treatment operations rely on it to dechlorinate potable water.

It is also used for process streams before discharge or further treatment. In textile and leather processing, it functions as a bleaching and reducing agent during fabric preparation.

Potassium metabisulfite is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , BP ), and technical-grade.

Purity levels typically range from 97% to 99%, with food and pharma grades carrying tighter sulfur dioxide content specifications to ensure safety and compliance for global distribution.

Its emulsifying properties support stable oil-in-water systems in leave-on and rinse-off cosmetic formats, including lightweight lotions and various types of conditioning treatments.

In home care and institutional cleaning products, it contributes to degreasing and wetting performance in formulations targeting specific biodegradability requirements and environmental standards.

The surfactant also functions as a co-emulsifier alongside conventional surfactants, allowing formulators to reduce harsher ingredients without sacrificing overall product performance or stability.

The ingredient provides these benefits without occlusive heaviness. Nutraceutical producers blend it with other omega fatty acid concentrates to differentiate premium pine nut oil extracts for the health food market.

Pharmaceutical researchers also evaluate it as a lipid excipient or active ingredient in topical and oral delivery systems targeting inflammatory pathways. It is supplied as a liquid oil, either as a concentrated free fatty acid fraction.

name: Potassium fluorosilicate

Potassium fluorosilicate (CAS 16871-90-2 ), also known as potassium hexafluorosilicate and potassium silicofluoride, is an inorganic salt used across industrial processing and surface treatment applications.

It functions primarily as a curing agent, flux, and biocidal component in formulations where controlled fluoride release and silicate reactivity are required for specific chemical processes.

name: Tetrafluoroboric acid
description:
Tetrafluoroboric acid (CAS 16872-11-0 ), commonly referenced by its formula HBF4, is a strong inorganic acid supplied primarily as an aqueous solution. It functions as a catalyst and electrolyte component.

The material serves as a surface treatment agent across electroplating, electronics manufacturing, and specialty chemical synthesis. In metal finishing, it serves as the primary electrolyte acid for tin and lead.

It is used in tin-lead alloy plating baths, where it maintains bath stability and deposit quality. Electronics manufacturers use it in PCB surface treatment and flux formulations to prepare metal surfaces.

The acid is essential for soldering and bonding processes. As a catalyst in polymer and resin production, it promotes condensation and cyclization reactions where conventional mineral acids are unsuitable.

In mining and metals processing, it is used in pickling and etching operations to selectively remove oxides from reactive metal surfaces. This ensures high-quality finishes on various industrial components.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 48–50% concentration being the most commercially standard grade. Technical grade is the predominant specification available at industrial scale.

High-purity electronic grade material is offered for semiconductor and precision plating applications. Bulk supply is available in drums and IBC containers for large-scale manufacturing requirements.

Smaller packaging options are also available for laboratory and specialty use. This ensures that the chemical meets the diverse needs of both research facilities and heavy industrial operations.

name: Sodium fluorosilicate
description:
Sodium fluorosilicate (CAS 16893-85-9 ), also known as sodium hexafluorosilicate or sodium fluosilicate, is an inorganic fluoride salt used industrially as a biocide, curing agent, and surface-hardening additive.

In building and construction, it functions as a concrete densifier and hardener, reacting with surface calcium compounds to improve wear resistance in industrial flooring and cement-based coatings.

Water treatment operations use it as a fluoridation source, dosing municipal supplies where silicofluoride compounds are the preferred fluoride carrier for public health initiatives.

Textile and leather processing incorporates it as a preservative and mothproofing agent, protecting finished goods during storage and transit from biological degradation and pests.

In agriculture, it serves as an active ingredient in pesticide formulations targeting wood-boring insects and soil pests, providing effective protection for crops and timber products.

Sodium fluorosilicate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial and agricultural use, with purity levels typically specified at 98–99%.

Water treatment applications may require grades meeting specific national or regional drinking water standards to ensure safety and compliance with local environmental regulations.

name: Ammonium fluorosilicate
description:
Ammonium fluorosilicate (CAS 16919-19-0 ), also sold as ammonium silicofluoride and ammonium hexafluorosilicate, is an inorganic fluorine salt used industrially for surface modification and hardening.

Its dual fluoride and silicate activity makes it effective where both surface chemistry and corrosion resistance are required simultaneously across multiple manufacturing sectors and industrial processes.

In building and construction, it functions as a concrete hardener and densifier, reacting with surface substrates to improve wear resistance and reduce porosity in industrial flooring and masonry treatments.

Textile and leather processors use it as a fixing and surface-treatment agent, improving fiber or hide resistance to degradation during finishing operations for high-quality material production.

In mining and metallurgy, it serves in ore flotation processes and metal surface treatments where controlled fluoride release is critical to process efficiency and chemical stability.

Water treatment applications utilize it as a fluoridation source, and it also appears in wood preservation formulations targeting fungal and insect resistance for long-term protection.

Ammonium fluorosilicate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ on a dry basis.

Bulk quantities are available in bags or supersacks, with smaller packaged quantities offered for laboratory and specialty formulation use to meet diverse industrial and research requirements.

Potassium fluorozirconate (CAS 16923-95-8 ), also known as potassium hexafluorozirconate or zirconium potassium fluoride, is an inorganic zirconium salt used across metal treatment and surface finishing.

It functions primarily as a corrosion inhibitor and biocide in industrial process formulations and specialty chemical manufacturing. In metal surface treatment, it serves as a flux and grain refiner in aluminum processing.

The compound improves adhesion for downstream coating and anodizing operations in magnesium alloy processing. The mining and metals sector uses it in zirconium refining and as a fluoride source in electrolytic processes.

Textile and leather processors incorporate it into treatment baths where controlled fluoride release supports fiber fixation. This application also provides essential preservation against microbial degradation during the manufacturing cycle.

In personal care manufacturing, it appears in formulations requiring zirconium-based antiperspirant or preservation activity. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling in industrial settings.

name: Sodium borohydride
description:
Sodium borohydride (CAS 16940-66-2 ), commonly abbreviated as NaBH4, is a selective reducing agent used across chemical manufacturing, precious metals recovery, and industrial processing. It delivers controlled reduction reactions under mild conditions.

This makes it a preferred reagent where selectivity and process efficiency are critical procurement considerations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, NaBH4 reduces ketones and aldehydes to alcohols in active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis.

It offers a safer and more scalable alternative to other hydride reagents. Precious metals recovery operations use it to precipitate gold, silver, and platinum-group metals from leach solutions, improving yield in mining and refining circuits.

Pulp and paper producers apply it as a bleaching stabilizer to protect brightness gains during hydrogen peroxide bleaching stages. Textile and leather processors use NaBH4 in reductive finishing baths to fix dyes.

This helps reduce residual chromium in effluent and meet discharge compliance targets. Sodium borohydride is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in stabilized aqueous solution, with concentrations ranging from 12% to 40%.

Standard grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with pharmaceutical supply aligned to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications. Bulk powder is available in drums and fiber packs.

Solution grades are typically shipped in IBCs or isotanks. This versatile chemical remains a staple for industrial applications requiring high-purity reduction and efficient metal recovery processes globally.

This versatile ester delivers a smooth, non-greasy skin feel in cosmetics and reduces friction in mechanical applications. In personal care, it is used in skin creams, sunscreens, and color cosmetics to improve spreadability.

It provides a lightweight, silky texture without heaviness, making it ideal for high-end skincare. Coating and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a plasticizer to enhance film flexibility and substrate adhesion.

In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it acts as a base fluid or additive to reduce surface friction. This improves processing performance and extends the lifespan of mechanical components in various systems.

It also functions as a dispersing aid in pigment concentrates, helping achieve uniform color distribution. This is critical for both cosmetic and coating systems where consistency and visual appeal are paramount for the end user.

Octyl palmitate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications, with cosmetic-grade material commonly meeting purity standards for manufacturing.

These baths deposit conductive gold layers on printed circuit boards, connectors, and semiconductor contacts. Catalyst producers use it to prepare supported gold nanoparticle catalysts for various industrial uses.

Precise gold loading on oxide supports determines activity in oxidation and hydrogenation reactions. In mining and precious metals refining, it functions as a reference standard and analytical reagent.

It is essential for gold assay and recovery process development. Specialty chemical manufacturers also use it to produce other gold compounds and colloidal gold dispersions for diagnostic and research applications.

name: Pyridinium
description:
Pyridinium (CAS 16969-45-2 ) is the protonated form of pyridine, generated when pyridine accepts a proton to form a positively charged nitrogen-containing ring. It functions as a reactive intermediate and ionic species in synthesis and catalysis.

This chemical is essential for the preparation of quaternary ammonium-type compounds across multiple industrial sectors. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, these intermediates are used in the synthesis of active ingredients where a charged nitrogen center is required.

Agricultural chemical producers rely on this chemistry to build herbicide and pesticide structures, particularly in the development of bipyridylium-class compounds. It is a critical building block for modern crop protection solutions.

Polymer chemists employ these reagents as initiators or coupling agents in controlled polymerization processes. This allows for precise control over chain architecture and the incorporation of specific functional groups into the polymer matrix.

Waterborne coatings and latex systems use it as a neutralizing amine to adjust pH and stabilize dispersions, improving shelf life and application performance during storage.

In personal care, it is incorporated into skin-conditioning emulsions and barrier-repair formulations where its moisturizing and stabilizing properties support lipid-layer restoration.

name: Barium hydroxide
description:
Barium hydroxide (CAS 17194-00-2 ), also known as caustic baryta, is a strong inorganic base used across industrial processes requiring precise alkalinity control and barium ion delivery.

In water treatment, this compound precipitates sulfate and carbonate impurities from process streams, producing effluents that meet discharge specifications for environmental compliance.

Plastics and polymer manufacturers use it as a catalyst and stabilizer precursor in PVC formulations, where it contributes to heat stability and flame retardancy performance.

In mining and metals processing, it conditions leach solutions and adjusts pH in barium-sensitive precipitation circuits to ensure high-quality mineral recovery and processing efficiency.

Pulp and paper operations apply it in causticizing steps and as a pH regulator in specialty chemical recovery processes, ensuring consistent output in large-scale manufacturing environments.

The product is supplied as a white powder or as the octahydrate form, with the monohydrate and anhydrous grades also available depending on specific application requirements.

Standard commercial grades include technical and reagent-grade specifications. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities, with purity levels commonly specified at 95–99%.

name: L-mandelic acid
description:
L-mandelic acid (CAS 17199-29-0 ), also known as (S)-mandelic acid, is a chiral alpha-hydroxy acid used as a stereospecific building block and active ingredient across pharmaceutical and cosmetic manufacturing.

Its defined stereochemistry makes it a preferred starting material where enantiomeric purity is a critical specification. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a chiral intermediate for producing antibiotics.

It is also used for antispasmodics and other APIs where a single enantiomer is required for regulatory compliance. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into chemical exfoliant products such as peels, serums, and toners.

In these applications, it provides keratolytic action with a gentler skin tolerance profile than glycolic acid. In topical antimicrobial formulations, its preservative and biocidal properties support product stability.

It also functions as a pH buffer and stabilizer in specialty formulations where controlled acidity is needed without introducing racemic impurities. L-mandelic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications, with enantiomeric excess (ee%) a standard quality parameter for pharma procurement.

Cosmetic and technical grades are also commercially available for buyers with less stringent stereochemical requirements. This ensures versatility across various industrial and laboratory applications.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it functions as a selective reducing agent and hydroboration reagent for producing chiral intermediates and active pharmaceutical ingredients where precise stereochemical control is required.

Polymer manufacturers use it as a radical polymerization initiator, particularly for initiating polymerization of acrylates and other vinyl monomers under mild conditions for specialized material production.

In electronics, it supports the production of boron-containing specialty materials and surface modification processes relevant to semiconductor fabrication and advanced component manufacturing.

Biotechnology applications include its use in nucleotide chemistry and oligonucleotide synthesis, where controlled borane transfer is needed without side reactions from more reactive boron sources.

description:
Disodium azelate (CAS 17265-13-3 ), the disodium salt of azelaic acid, is a water-soluble buffering agent used in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations. It provides pH stabilization in aqueous systems where the free acid form presents solubility challenges.

In topical pharmaceutical formulations, it functions as a buffering component in creams and gels targeting skin conditions where azelaic acid is the active ingredient. This improves the deliverable form's stability profile during long-term storage.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into serums and emulsions to maintain target pH ranges while contributing the recognized skin-conditioning benefits associated with the azelate anion. It is highly effective in aqueous-based systems.

It also serves pharmaceutical manufacturers as an intermediate in synthesis workflows requiring a neutralized, salt-form dicarboxylate starting material. This allows for more efficient processing in complex chemical reactions.

Aqueous-based personal care systems, particularly those sensitive to acidic excipients, benefit from its buffering capacity without the low-pH handling concerns of the parent acid. This makes it a versatile choice for modern formulations.

name: Behentrimonium chloride

description:
Dimethyl dodecanedioate (CAS 1731-79-9 ), also known as dimethyl 1,12-dodecanedioate, is the methyl diester of dodecanedioic acid used as a reactive intermediate and functional additive across polymer and lubricant manufacturing.

It enables controlled chain-building in polyester and polyamide synthesis while also contributing lubricity in specialty formulations. In plastics and polymer production, it serves as a monomer for synthesizing long-chain polyesters.

These materials are ideal for applications where flexibility and low-temperature performance are required end-product targets. As a plasticizer, it is incorporated into polymer matrices to reduce brittleness in films and coatings.

It is also used in molded components without migrating as readily as shorter-chain alternatives. In lubricant formulations, its ester structure delivers boundary lubrication properties suited to metalworking fluids and synthetic base stocks.

The compound also functions as a chain extender or crosslinking precursor in specialty resin systems. This is particularly useful where precise molecular weight control is a formulation requirement for industrial chemical processes.

name: Hydroquinone monosulfate
description:
Hydroquinone monosulfate (CAS 17438-29-8 ), also referred to as quinol sulfate, is a sulfate ester derivative of hydroquinone used as a stabilizing intermediate and antioxidant precursor in specialty chemical synthesis.

It functions primarily as a controlled-release or masked form of hydroquinone, enabling formulators to work with reduced reactivity while retaining the core functional activity of the parent compound.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a synthetic intermediate in the preparation of hydroquinone-based active ingredients where controlled oxidation potential is required for the final product.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin-tone-modulating preparations where a stabilized hydroquinone source is preferred over the free diol form to ensure long-term stability and efficacy.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it is used in biochemical assay development and enzyme substrate research where precise redox behavior must be maintained across various experimental conditions.

It also supports pH-buffering roles in specialty formulations requiring antioxidant activity alongside acid-base regulation, making it a versatile component in complex chemical systems.

Hydroquinone monosulfate is typically supplied as a solid powder and is available primarily in pharmaceutical-grade and research-grade specifications with high purity levels.

These grades are suited to USP and BP standards for GMP-compliant manufacturing. Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D use to bulk quantities for industrial-scale synthesis.

name: Hexafluorotitanic acid
description:
Hexafluorotitanic acid (CAS 17439-11-1 ) is an inorganic fluorotitanate compound supplied as an aqueous solution, used industrially to deposit titanium-fluoride conversion coatings on metal and non-metal substrates.

It functions as both a surface activator and mild etchant, enabling adhesion promotion and corrosion protection without heavy-metal chemistry. In metal pretreatment and coil coating lines, it forms thin titanium-based conversion layers.

These layers are applied on aluminum, steel, and galvanized surfaces as a chromate-free alternative prior to painting or powder coating. The construction sector uses it in concrete densifiers and facade treatments.

In these applications, it reacts with substrate minerals to harden and seal surfaces. Textile and paper processors apply it to modify fiber or sheet surfaces, improving dye uptake or coating adhesion in continuous processing lines.

Water treatment operations use it at controlled dosing rates for pH adjustment and as a fluoride-source reagent in specific process streams. Hexafluorotitanic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution for industrial use.

Concentrations typically around 50% are standard in commercial trade. Technical grade is the primary market offering, with specifications aligned to metal finishing and surface treatment industry requirements.

Packaging ranges from intermediate bulk containers to drums, depending on volume requirements. This chemical provides a versatile solution for modern manufacturing and surface engineering across multiple global sectors.

name: Triethylammonium
description:
Triethylammonium (CAS 17440-81-2 ) is the protonated form of triethylamine, existing as a cationic species in solution and commonly encountered as a counterion in salt formulations and buffer systems.

Known in analytical and biotech contexts as TEAH, it functions primarily as a pH-regulating agent and ionic pairing component across several industrial sectors. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, salts are used as ion-pair reagents.

These reagents are essential in HPLC method development, enabling the separation of polar and ionizable drug compounds. Biotech and life sciences workflows rely on triethylammonium acetate buffers for oligonucleotide purification.

These buffers are also critical for the chromatographic analysis of nucleic acids. In agrochemical formulations, the cation serves as a counterion in herbicide and pesticide salt forms, influencing solubility.

This influence extends to the bioavailability of active ingredients in various crops. Water treatment applications utilize triethylammonium-based compounds for pH adjustment and corrosion inhibition in industrial cooling systems.

The chemical is supplied commercially as salts rather than the free cation, most commonly as triethylammonium acetate or triethylammonium bicarbonate in liquid or solid form for diverse industrial uses.

Analytical-grade and HPLC-grade specifications are standard for life sciences procurement. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and agrochemical applications requiring bulk chemical supplies.

name: Aluminum zirconium octachlorohydrex gly
description:
Aluminum zirconium octachlorohydrex gly (CAS 174514-58-0 ) is a high-efficacy antiperspirant active used in personal care formulations to reduce sweat output by temporarily blocking eccrine sweat ducts.

It belongs to the aluminum-zirconium chlorohydrate family and is distinguished by its glycine-complexed form, which improves skin compatibility and formulation stability during the manufacturing process.

It is the primary active ingredient in clinical-strength and prescription-strength antiperspirant products, where higher active concentrations are required to meet specific efficacy thresholds.

Stick, soft-solid, and invisible-solid antiperspirant formats rely on this grade for its favorable rheological behavior and compatibility with various wax and emollient systems used in production.

Roll-on and aerosol antiperspirant formulations also incorporate it where enhanced sweat reduction performance is the key commercial differentiator for the end-user market.

Contract manufacturers and brand formulators sourcing for clinical or dermatologist-recommended product lines specifically seek this grade over standard aluminum chlorohydrate alternatives for better results.

Aluminum zirconium octachlorohydrex gly is supplied as a fine white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, with active content typically expressed as a percentage of anhydrous complex.

Buyers should confirm compliance with relevant pharmacopeial or OTC monograph requirements, particularly for markets where antiperspirant actives are regulated as over-the-counter drug ingredients.

name: Gamma cyclodextrin
description:
Gamma cyclodextrin (CAS 17465-86-0 ), also identified as γ-CD, Ringdex C, and approved food additive E458 , is a cyclic oligosaccharide derived from starch. It features a toroidal molecular structure that enables it to encapsulate guest molecules within its cavity.

This encapsulation function drives its commercial value across pharmaceuticals, food, and personal care. It is primarily used for improving the stability, solubility, and controlled release of various active ingredients in industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical formulations, γ-CD encapsulates poorly soluble active compounds to enhance bioavailability. It is also frequently utilized to mask undesirable tastes or odors in oral dosage forms to improve patient compliance.

Food manufacturers use it under E458 approval to stabilize volatile flavor compounds and extend the shelf life of sensitive ingredients. It can also be used to reduce fat perception in various reduced-calorie products.

In personal care, it encapsulates fragrance molecules and actives in skin and hair care formulations. This process enables controlled release and improved product longevity for high-end cosmetic applications.

Its chelating capacity also allows it to sequester metal ions in formulations where oxidative stability is a concern. Gamma cyclodextrin is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling and processing.

It is available in food-grade specification compliant with E458 regulatory requirements. We also offer pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and Ph.Eur. standards for regulated medical applications.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial encapsulation applications where high purity is required. Our product ensures consistent performance across all manufacturing and formulation sectors.

name: Polyquaternium 46
description:
Polyquaternium-46 (CAS 174761-16-1 ) is a cationic conditioning polymer used primarily in hair care formulations. It delivers film-forming and fixative performance across rinse-off and leave-on systems.

This versatile ingredient is a go-to for formulators targeting hold, conditioning, and manageability in a single polymer. In hair styling products such as gels, mousses, and sprays, it provides strong hold.

The polymer offers excellent humidity resistance while maintaining a non-tacky feel on the hair shaft. Shampoo and conditioner formulators incorporate it to deposit a conditioning film that improves combability.

It effectively reduces static after rinsing, enhancing the overall sensory profile of hair care products. In textile finishing, it modifies fiber surfaces to improve softness and antistatic performance.

The chemical is utilized in fabric treatment baths and paper processing operations for surface modification. Its cationic charge aids in uniform coating adhesion and surface uniformity for leather processing.

Polyquaternium-46 is supplied as an aqueous solution with active polymer content standardized for direct use. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification suitable for high-end personal care applications.

Industrial grades for textile and paper processing are also sourced to meet specific manufacturing needs. Supply volumes range from standard drum quantities to bulk IBC formats for large-scale production.

name: Calcium malate
description:
Calcium malate (CAS 17482-42-7 ), also identified as E352 , is the calcium salt of malic acid used in food and pharmaceutical manufacturing as an acidulant, buffering agent, and mineral supplement source.

It delivers both pH control and bioavailable calcium in a single ingredient, reducing the need for separate additives. In food and beverage production, it functions as an acidulant and flavor enhancer.

It is frequently used in fruit-based products, confectionery, and soft drinks where a clean, mild tartness is required. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a calcium source in dietary supplements and mineral tablets.

This is particularly effective where malic acid co-administration supports absorption. It also acts as a stabilizer and buffering agent in processed foods, helping maintain target pH through thermal processing.

In functional food development, it appears in calcium-fortified products targeting bone health positioning. It provides these benefits without the chalkiness associated with carbonate-based calcium sources.

Calcium malate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with compliance to FCC and Ph. Eur. standards commonly referenced.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags for industrial use. Smaller packaging options are also available for specialized pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications to meet specific client needs.

name: Ammonium propionate
description:
Ammonium propionate (CAS 17496-08-1 ) is the ammonium salt of propionic acid, commercially recognized as ammonium propanoate. It functions as a mold inhibitor and preservative in food and agricultural feed applications.

In these industries, controlled microbial activity is the primary requirement for product stability. In baked goods and processed foods, it extends shelf life by inhibiting mold and rope-forming bacteria.

This additive works without significantly affecting yeast activity, making it suitable for bread and bakery formulations. Animal feed manufacturers apply it as an antifungal treatment in grain storage and compound feeds.

This application protects nutritional integrity during storage and transit. It also functions as a flavoring agent and acidulant in food systems where a mild, slightly acidic profile is required for the final product.

In silage treatment, it supports fermentation control and reduces spoilage losses in forage preservation. The chemical is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in aqueous solution form, depending on requirements.

Food-grade specifications, often meeting FCC standards, are the most commonly traded. Technical-grade material is also available for specific agricultural and feed use where high purity is less critical.

Formulators targeting hyperpigmentation from UV exposure or post-inflammatory sources use it alongside other actives such as niacinamide or vitamin C. This allows for the creation of multi-mechanism brightening systems.

Its lipophilic profile supports stable incorporation into oil-in-water and anhydrous emulsion systems. This is a practical consideration during formulation development for chemists working with complex cosmetic bases.

Undecylenoyl phenylalanine is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, with Sepiwhite MSH and Sepiwhite MSH QD representing distinct commercial grades for the industry.

name: Lead methanesulfonate
description:
Lead methanesulfonate (CAS 17570-76-2 ) is a lead salt of methanesulfonic acid used primarily as a soluble lead source in electroplating baths and specialty metal finishing processes. Unlike traditional lead compounds, it offers high solubility in aqueous systems.

It is also utilized for connectors and semiconductor components where precise layer control is required. Metalworking operations use this chemical as an additive in extreme-pressure lubricant formulations for industrial use.

In these lubricant applications, it contributes to surface protection under high-load conditions. It also functions as a corrosion inhibitor component in specific industrial fluids where lead-based chemistry is specified for performance.

Automotive parts finishing, particularly for bearing surfaces and bushing coatings, represents another established end-use. This application relies on the chemical for controlled lead deposition required in high-performance parts.

name: Thiourea dioxide
description:
Thiourea dioxide (CAS 1758-73-2 ), also known as formamidinesulfinic acid and abbreviated as TDO, is a reductive bleaching and reducing agent used across textile, paper, and leather processing industries.

It acts as a controlled source of reducing power under alkaline and elevated-temperature conditions, enabling selective bleaching and color stripping without the aggressive fiber damage associated with oxidative systems.

In textile processing, TDO is used for reductive clearing after dyeing with disperse dyes on polyester, removing unfixed surface dye to improve wash fastness and color brightness.

Pulp and paper producers apply it for bleaching mechanical and chemical pulps, particularly where brightness reversion needs to be minimized during the manufacturing process.

Leather processors use it to achieve uniform whitening of hides prior to dyeing, ensuring consistent color uptake across the finished material and improving the final aesthetic quality.

In water treatment and industrial effluent applications, it functions as a reducing agent to neutralize residual oxidants such as chlorine and chromate compounds found in waste streams.

Thiourea dioxide is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial processing applications, with purity typically specified at 98% or higher.

Packaging is commonly available in 25 kg bags or drums suited to bulk industrial procurement. This ensures safe handling and stability during transport and long-term storage in warehouse facilities.

Dioctyltin diacetate (CAS 17586-94-6 ), also known as Bis(n-octyl)tin diacetate, is an organotin compound used industrially as a catalyst and curing agent across polymer and coating systems.

It accelerates condensation reactions and crosslinking processes, enabling controlled cure rates in demanding manufacturing environments. In silicone sealants and elastomers, it functions as a room-temperature vulcanization catalyst.

This material drives crosslink formation in one- and two-component systems used in construction and industrial assembly. PVC stabilization compounding relies on organotin chemistry to manage thermal degradation during processing.

Dioctyltin compounds offer compatibility with flexible formulations in these applications. Polyurethane and adhesive formulators use it to initiate and regulate polymerization, controlling open time and final bond strength.

In structural applications, coatings manufacturers incorporate it into moisture-cure systems. Precise catalytic activity determines film formation speed and surface quality in these specialized industrial coatings.

Dioctyltin diacetate is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial concentrations, suitable for direct incorporation into formulation processes. This ensures ease of use during large scale chemical manufacturing.

name: Hexyldecyl stearate
description:
Hexyldecyl stearate (CAS 17618-45-0 ), commercially known as Eutanol G 16S, is a branched-chain ester derived from stearic acid used across personal care, industrial lubrication, and polymer applications.

Its branched molecular structure resists crystallization at low temperatures, keeping formulations fluid and spreadable across a wide working range. Formulators select it primarily as an emollient, lubricant, and plasticizing agent.

In skin care and color cosmetics, it functions as a non-greasy emollient that improves slip and skin feel in creams, lotions, and foundations without leaving a heavy residue.

Sunscreen and SPF formulations benefit from its ability to disperse UV filters evenly while maintaining a lightweight sensory profile. This makes it a versatile choice for modern sun care products.

In industrial lubricants and metalworking fluids, it acts as a base fluid or additive that reduces friction and improves surface glide on metal substrates. It provides excellent stability under mechanical stress.

Polymer and elastomer compounders use it as a plasticizer to enhance flexibility and processing flow in PVC and rubber compounds. This improves the overall durability and handling of the final materials.

Hexyldecyl stearate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the distinct purity requirements of personal care versus industrial end uses.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with cosmetic-grade material typically conforming to established supplier specifications aligned with ISO and COSMOS-compatible sourcing requirements.

name: Ammonium thiocyanate
description:
Ammonium thiocyanate (CAS 1762-95-4 ), also known commercially as Trans-aid and by the abbreviation NH4SCN, is an inorganic salt sourced for its flame retardant properties.

It functions as a reactive auxiliary in wet-process industries, delivering nitrogen- and sulfur-based chemistry that interrupts combustion pathways in polymer and fiber systems.

In textile processing, it acts as a dyeing auxiliary and anti-felting agent for wool, improving fiber receptivity and dimensional stability in finished fabrics during production.

Leather and paper manufacturers use it as a processing aid to modify surface characteristics and control shrinkage during treatment, ensuring high-quality material outputs for industrial use.

In plastics and polymer formulations, it contributes flame retardant performance, particularly in systems where halogen-free solutions are required to meet modern fire safety specifications.

Building and construction applications include incorporation into construction adhesives and cementitious formulations where controlled set modification and flame retardancy are both required.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline solid, typically in powder or granular form. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial applications with high purity levels.

Purity levels commonly range from 97% to 99%. It is packaged in moisture-resistant bags or drums given its hygroscopic behavior in standard warehouse storage conditions.

name: Myristyl stearate
description:
Myristyl stearate (CAS 17661-50-6 ), also known as tetradecyl stearate, is a fatty acid ester derived from myristic alcohol and stearic acid. It functions as a lubricant, emollient, and rheology modifier across personal care and industrial formulations.

Solid at room temperature, it contributes waxy texture, slip, and consistency to a broad range of end products. In personal care, it is used to build structure and improve skin feel in stick formulations and pressed powders.

It is frequently utilized in cream-based cosmetics where a smooth, non-greasy payoff is required. Lip balms, solid perfumes, and deodorant sticks rely on its waxy binding properties to achieve the desired hardness and application texture.

In lubricant and metalworking applications, it acts as a solid lubricant additive, reducing friction in formulations where controlled viscosity and film-forming behavior are priorities for the manufacturing process.

It also functions as a dispersing aid in pigment-loaded systems, improving homogeneity in wax blends and color cosmetics. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for formulators seeking consistent performance.

Myristyl stearate is supplied as a white to off-white solid, typically in flake or pastille form. Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to personal care industry requirements.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial and lubricant applications. Our product ensures high purity and stability for demanding chemical processes and high-end consumer goods manufacturing.

name: Behenyl behenate
description:
Behenyl behenate (CAS 17671-27-1 ), also known as docosyl docosanoate, is a long-chain wax ester derived from behenic acid and behenyl alcohol. It functions as a plasticizer, emulsifier, and rheology modifier.

This material is ideal for formulations where high-melting, structurally stable wax components are required. In personal care, it is used to build body and texture in lipsticks, balms, and solid emulsions.

It provides a smooth, non-greasy skin feel without compromising structural integrity. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into topical creams and ointments where controlled consistency is critical.

Emulsion stability across temperature ranges is essential to product performance. It also serves as a plasticizing component in film coatings and sustained-release tablet formulations for drug delivery.

Its high melting point supports controlled delivery profiles. In color cosmetics, it contributes to pigment dispersion and helps stabilize anhydrous systems such as pressed powders and stick formats.

Behenyl behenate is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for regulated formulations.

These grades meet the purity requirements of USP and Ph.Eur. standards. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial applications where pharmacopeial compliance is not required.

name: Oleyl erucate
description:
Oleyl erucate (CAS 17673-56-2 ), also marketed under the trade name TEGOSOFT OER, is a fatty acid ester derived from erucic acid and oleyl alcohol. It functions as a lubricant, plasticizer, and emollient across industrial and personal care applications.

This chemical offers low-viscosity performance with high thermal stability for demanding environments. In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it is used as a base fluid or additive in cutting oils and forming lubricants.

Its ester structure provides essential film-forming protection under pressure during heavy manufacturing. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, hair conditioners, and color cosmetics as a lightweight emollient.

The product spreads evenly without leaving a greasy residue on the skin or hair. In plastics processing, it acts as an internal or external plasticizer and slip agent in polymer films and compounds, improving flexibility.

It also enhances surface release and supports emulsification in formulated lubricant concentrates. This is particularly useful in metalworking fluids where stable oil-in-water dispersion is required for cooling and lubrication.

Oleyl erucate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for various industrial uses. It is available in technical grade for industrial lubrication and polymer applications to ensure consistent performance.

It is also offered in cosmetic grade meeting purity standards required by personal care manufacturers. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with smaller packaging available for specialty formulators and laboratories.

name: Ethyltriacetoxysilane
description:
Ethyltriacetoxysilane (CAS 17689-77-9 ), also known commercially as Dynasylan ETAC, is an acetoxy-functional silane used as a crosslinker and surface modifier in moisture-curing polymer systems.

It releases acetic acid upon hydrolysis, enabling rapid cure at ambient conditions without requiring a catalyst in many formulations. In silicone sealants and elastomers, it acts as a crosslinking agent.

This chemical controls cure speed and final mechanical properties, making it a standard component in one-part RTV systems for construction and automotive assembly. Adhesive formulators use it to improve substrate adhesion.

It is particularly effective for glass, metals, and plastics where bond durability under moisture exposure is critical. In coatings, it functions as a surface coupling agent that promotes adhesion between substrates.

This promotes bonding between inorganic substrates and organic binder systems. Building and construction applications include structural glazing compounds and facade sealants where weathering resistance is required.

It is also utilized where long-term flexibility is essential for the final product. Ethyltriacetoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial use.

This is the standard specification for industrial sealant and coating applications. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers, suited to both formulators and larger-volume industrial users.

name: Sodium trithiocyanurate
description:
Sodium trithiocyanurate (CAS 17766-26-6 ), commercially known as TMT, is the trisodium salt of trithiocyanuric acid used to precipitate and immobilize heavy metal ions in industrial processes.

It reacts selectively with dissolved metals to form stable, insoluble complexes that can be separated from liquid streams. In industrial wastewater treatment, TMT precipitates heavy metals such as mercury and lead.

It also targets cadmium and copper from effluent streams, enabling compliance with discharge limits. Mining and mineral processing operations use it to remove residual metal contaminants from process water.

It is frequently applied to tailings pond runoff and electroplating wastewater where conventional hydroxide precipitation alone fails to meet regulatory thresholds. This ensures safer environmental discharge.

Metal smelting and refining facilities use TMT as a polishing agent in final effluent treatment. This process captures trace dissolved metals that resist other common treatment methods effectively.

Sodium trithiocyanurate is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 15% concentration. This is the standard commercial form for dosing systems in large scale industrial facilities.

Dry powder form is available for applications requiring concentrated stock preparation or extended shelf storage. Technical grade is the primary specification offered for these industrial uses.

Product quality is typically characterized by active content and heavy metal precipitation efficacy. This ensures the chemical meets the necessary performance standards for heavy metal remediation.

name: 2,4-dichlorobenzyl alcohol
description:
2,4-Dichlorobenzyl alcohol (CAS 1777-82-8 ), also known commercially as Dybenal, is an aromatic chlorinated alcohol used primarily as an antimicrobial and preservative agent across industrial and consumer product sectors.

It delivers broad-spectrum activity against bacteria and fungi, making it a functional ingredient where microbial control is a formulation requirement in various manufacturing processes.

In pharmaceutical and healthcare products, it is a recognized active ingredient in throat lozenges and topical antiseptic formulations, where it provides localized antimicrobial action for patients.

Personal care and cosmetic manufacturers incorporate it as a preservative booster in rinse-off and leave-on products requiring protection against microbial contamination during their shelf life.

Industrial applications include its use as a biocide in textile processing and leather treatment, where it controls microbial degradation during critical wet processing stages in the factory.

Its chlorinated aromatic structure also supports flame retardant applications in construction materials and polymer systems, providing essential safety characteristics to the final industrial products.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or solid. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications, including BP and Ph. Eur. compliance for regulated uses.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial biocide and flame retardant end uses, ensuring that manufacturers have the appropriate quality for their specific application needs.

name: Dihomo-gamma-Linolenic Acid
description:
Dihomo-gamma-Linolenic Acid (CAS 1783-84-2 ), also known commercially as Eicosatrienoic acid, is a 20-carbon polyunsaturated omega-6 fatty acid occurring naturally in human tissue and select botanical oils.

It functions as a bioactive lipid precursor and skin-conditioning agent across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and cosmetic applications. In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into moisturizers and barrier repair products.

Its skin-conditioning properties support lipid replenishment in the stratum corneum. Nutritional supplement manufacturers use it as a functional fatty acid ingredient in softgel and oil-based formats targeting omega-6 fatty acid profiling.

Pharmaceutical researchers source it as a reference standard or active ingredient in investigational lipid-based formulations. In specialty food and nutraceutical products, it contributes to targeted fatty acid enrichment.

This occurs where precise omega-6 composition is a formulation requirement. Dihomo-gamma-Linolenic Acid is supplied as a neat liquid oil or in solution, depending on concentration and intended use.

It is available in research-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, with purity levels typically confirmed by GC analysis. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory and formulation development.

Larger volumes are available for commercial production runs. This ensures that manufacturers can scale their operations from initial research phases through to full market distribution and supply chain management.
