name: Calcium disodium edetate hydrate
description:
Calcium disodium edetate hydrate (CAS 23411-34-9 ) is the hydrated crystalline form of calcium disodium EDTA, a chelating agent used across food and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It works by binding free metal ions that would otherwise catalyze oxidative degradation.

In food processing, it is incorporated into canned vegetables, legumes, mayonnaise, and salad dressings to prevent metal-catalyzed discoloration and rancidity. This extends shelf life without altering the flavor profile of the finished product.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it to stabilize liquid drug products, ophthalmic solutions, and topical preparations where trace metal contamination threatens active ingredient integrity. It ensures the long-term stability of sensitive medicinal compounds.

It also functions as a sequestrant in personal care formulations, preventing soap scum formation and improving preservative efficacy. It achieves this by stripping metal cofactors from microbial cell walls during the preservation process.

Industrial cleaning and water treatment applications rely on it to control scale-forming metal ions in process systems. This prevents the buildup of mineral deposits that can damage equipment or reduce the efficiency of industrial operations.

Calcium disodium edetate hydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the pharmaceutical form commonly meeting USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards.

Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial volumes depending on the grade and supplier. This versatility allows for its use in both small-scale research and large-scale manufacturing environments across various sectors.

name: Alpha-naphthol orange
description:
Alpha-naphthol orange (CAS 2347-72-0 ), also known as E111 and Orange GGN, is a synthetic azo dye approved for use as a colorant in regulated food and non-food applications.

It imparts a characteristic orange hue to finished products across food manufacturing, cosmetics, and industrial dyeing processes. In food and beverage production, E111 is used to achieve consistent orange coloration.

This dye is utilized where permitted under regional regulatory frameworks. Textile processors apply it in dyebath formulations to color natural and synthetic fibers, where batch-to-batch shade consistency is a key consideration.

In leather finishing, it contributes to surface colorants and topcoat formulations requiring durable, uniform tone. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into cosmetic preparations such as soaps and bath products.

The material is valued for colorant stability under alkaline conditions. Alpha-naphthol orange is typically supplied as a powder or granule to meet various industrial and commercial manufacturing requirements.

Food-grade material meeting E111 specifications is available for regulated applications, while technical-grade material is sourced for textile, leather, and industrial use for global supply chains.

name: Phenoxyethyl caprylate
description:
Phenoxyethyl caprylate (CAS 23511-73-1 ), also marketed as Tegosoft XC, is a synthetic ester used as an emollient, solvent, and carrier in cosmetic and industrial formulations.

It combines the sensory properties of a light skin-feel ester with strong solvency for actives, pigments, and UV filters. In personal care, it functions as a spreading agent and solvent.

It is used in sunscreens, color cosmetics, and skin care products to dissolve organic UV filters and disperse pigments that are difficult to incorporate into standard emollient bases.

Its low viscosity and compatibility with silicones make it a preferred carrier in foundation formulas and pressed powders where texture and payoff are critical for the end user.

In industrial and metalworking applications, it serves as a base fluid or co-solvent in lubricant formulations where a synthetic ester with good film-forming characteristics is required.

It also finds use as a solvent carrier for fragrance and active delivery systems in leave-on formulations. Phenoxyethyl caprylate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid.

It is available in cosmetic-grade quality meeting standard personal care specifications. Supply is typically provided in drums and IBCs for commercial quantities and bulk orders.

name: Hexyl nicotinate
description:
Hexyl nicotinate (CAS 23597-82-2 ), also known as nicotinic acid hexyl ester, is an ester of nicotinic acid used as a penetration enhancer and carrier in topical formulations.

It promotes localized vasodilation at the skin surface, making it a functional active in cosmetic and pharmaceutical products targeting circulation and warmth response for various applications.

In topical pharmaceutical formulations, it is incorporated into creams and gels designed to produce a warming or flushing sensation, commonly used in muscle rub and sports recovery products.

Cosmetic formulators use it in anti-cellulite creams and body contouring products where visible skin redness and improved microcirculation are desired endpoints for the end user.

It also functions as a carrier and penetration enhancer, improving transdermal delivery of co-formulated actives through the skin barrier to ensure maximum efficacy of the final product.

In pharmaceutical intermediate applications, it serves as a building block for synthesizing nicotinic acid derivatives and related heterocyclic compounds used in advanced chemical synthesis.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical and cosmetic-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher confirmed by GC analysis.

name: Hexanediaminetetra(methylenephosphonic acid)
description:
Hexanediaminetetra(methylenephosphonic acid) , also known as CAS 23605-74-5 , is a phosphonate chelating agent used to control scale formation and metal ion interference. It is highly effective in industrial water systems and process fluids.

Its strong calcium and heavy metal binding capacity makes it a preferred choice where conventional chelants underperform. It remains stable and effective even at elevated temperatures or under high hardness conditions.

In industrial water treatment, it inhibits calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and barium sulfate scale deposition. This is critical for the maintenance of cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems.

Oil and gas producers use it in injection water and produced water handling to prevent mineral scaling. This protection extends to pipelines and downhole equipment, ensuring efficient extraction and transport.

Textile and leather processing operations rely on it to sequester hardness ions during dyeing and finishing. This process protects colorant consistency and maintains the overall stability of the chemical bath.

In paper manufacturing, it controls metal ions that would otherwise catalyze peroxide decomposition during bleaching sequences. This ensures the efficiency of the bleaching process and the quality of the final product.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 30–40% active content. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications requiring high-performance sequestration.

Bulk supply is standard in intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) and drums for easy handling. Larger quantities are available in isotanks for high-volume industrial procurement and global logistics needs.

name: Heneicosanoic acid
description:
Heneicosanoic acid (CAS 2363-71-5 ) is a saturated C21 straight-chain fatty acid used as a reference standard, specialty emulsifier, and functional lubricant component across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

Its odd-chain carbon structure makes it commercially distinct from even-chain fatty acids, supporting specific analytical and formulation roles that even-chain alternatives cannot fulfill in various applications.

In food and nutrition research, it serves as an internal standard for fatty acid profiling by GC analysis, where its odd-chain status ensures it does not interfere with naturally occurring even-chain lipid peaks.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into emollient systems and wax blends to modify texture, spreadability, and film-forming behavior in skin-care and hair-care products for improved performance.

In lubricant formulations, it functions as a boundary lubricant additive or base component in specialty greases where controlled chain length and saturation are required for industrial machinery.

It also supports lipid metabolism research as a biochemical tracer, giving it a niche but consistent demand in life science supply chains and specialized laboratory environments worldwide.

Heneicosanoic acid is supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid. It is available primarily in research-grade and high-purity analytical grades, with purity specifications typically at 98% or above.

Its combination of a C12 hydrophobic tail and multiple amine groups positions it as a functional ingredient for emulsification, biocidal activity, and corrosion control in various applications.

In water treatment, it acts as a biocide and corrosion inhibitor, protecting metal surfaces in cooling towers and industrial water systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into conditioning systems.

It improves wet combability and substantivity in rinse-off hair products. Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and finishing agent, helping fibers retain flexibility and resist microbial degradation.

In industrial cleaning formulations, its dual amine functionality supports degreasing performance on metal and hard surfaces where both surfactancy and antimicrobial action are required for effective results.

Laurylamine dipropylenediamine is typically supplied as an amber to yellow liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly in the 95–99% range.

Drum and IBC packaging are standard for industrial volumes. This chemical intermediate is valued for its stability and versatility across diverse manufacturing sectors and specialized chemical processes.

name: Dioctyl sulfosuccinate
description:
Dioctyl sulfosuccinate (CAS 2373-23-1 ) is an anionic surfactant used across industrial and consumer formulations as a wetting agent, emulsifier, and dispersant. It lowers surface tension effectively at low concentrations.

This chemical enables uniform distribution of active ingredients and improves substrate penetration in aqueous systems. In personal care, it functions as a wetting and emulsifying agent in cleansers and shampoos.

It is also utilized in skin conditioning products where consistent texture and ingredient dispersion are required. Food-grade applications include its use as an emulsifier and wetting agent in food processing.

This is particularly useful where controlled dispersion of fats or solids is needed. Textile and leather processors use it to improve dye bath penetration and fiber wetting, reducing processing time.

It improves color uniformity in manufacturing. In water treatment, it supports dispersion of particulates and aids in defoaming and surface-active control within various treatment circuits.

Dioctyl sulfosuccinate is typically supplied as a liquid or solution, with concentration levels varying by grade. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commercially common.

Food-grade material is produced to meet relevant regulatory standards for use in food contact applications. Buyers should confirm purity, active content percentage, and solvent carrier composition.

Evaluating supplier specifications ensures the material meets the necessary requirements for the intended application. This surfactant remains a versatile component in modern chemical manufacturing.

name: Ureidopropyltriethoxysilane
description:
Ureidopropyltriethoxysilane (CAS 23779-32-0 ), also known commercially as 3-Ureidopropyltriethoxysilane, is an organosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices.

It improves adhesion at interfaces where standard silanes underperform, particularly with polar resins and moisture-exposed systems. In glass fiber-reinforced composites and filled plastics, it bonds mineral fillers.

This material is used with polyamide, epoxy, and polyurethane matrices, improving mechanical retention under humid conditions. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a primer or additive to enhance substrate adhesion.

It is effective on glass, metal, and concrete surfaces where long-term durability is required. In electronics encapsulants and underfill resins, it promotes interfacial adhesion between inorganic substrates and polar thermoset systems.

This supports reliability under thermal cycling. Automotive coatings and structural bonding applications use it to improve wet adhesion performance on treated metal and composite surfaces for industrial use.

Ureidopropyltriethoxysilane is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid. It is available in technical grade, with purity typically specified at 95% or higher for various manufacturing requirements.

Packaging ranges from small drums for laboratory and formulation use to bulk quantities for industrial-scale production. The product is handled according to standard chemical safety and storage protocols.

name: Hydroxyphosphonoacetic acid
description:
Hydroxyphosphonoacetic acid ( CAS 23783-26-8 ), commonly sourced and specified as HPAA, is an organophosphonic acid used across water treatment and industrial formulations as a chelating and scale-inhibiting agent.

It binds metal ions and disrupts mineral crystal growth, preventing scale deposition and corrosion in process water systems. In cooling water and boiler systems, HPAA controls calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate.

It also manages calcium phosphate scale at low dosage levels, making it a preferred choice for high-hardness water circuits. Formulators incorporate it into corrosion inhibitor blends where both metal chelation and threshold inhibition are required.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it functions as a dispersant and adhesion promoter, improving pigment stability and substrate bonding on metal surfaces. This versatility makes it essential for industrial manufacturing.

Personal care manufacturers use it as a chelating preservative booster, sequestering trace metals that would otherwise degrade product stability or reduce biocide efficacy. It ensures long-term shelf life and performance.

HPAA is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 50% active content being the most commonly traded concentration. Technical grade is the standard specification for industrial water treatment and coating applications.

Food-contact and personal care applications typically require documentation confirming purity and absence of heavy metal contaminants. Reputable suppliers provide these alongside standard TDS and COA documents.

name: Tetraethylene glycol monomethyl ether
description:
Tetraethylene glycol monomethyl ether (CAS 23783-42-8 ) is a polyethylene glycol-based ether solvent and humectant used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulation.

Its combination of hygroscopic retention and solvent capacity makes it a practical choice for formulators working with polar and semi-polar actives in various chemical applications.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a humectant and solubilizer in skin creams, serums, and hair care products where moisture retention and ingredient compatibility are both required.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a carrier solvent in topical and semi-solid dosage forms, helping to dissolve active ingredients and improve skin penetration without aggressive solvency.

Printing ink formulators incorporate it to control viscosity and drying behavior in water-based and specialty ink systems to ensure consistent performance during the application process.

In metalworking and lubricant applications, it serves as a coupling agent and co-solvent in water-miscible cutting fluids and corrosion-inhibiting formulations for industrial machinery.

Tetraethylene glycol monomethyl ether is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in technical and high-purity grades suited to industrial and personal care applications.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers, with smaller quantities available for laboratory and development use to meet specific manufacturing and research requirements.

name: DC Red No 30
description:

It is also utilized in pressed powders where strong tint strength and skin-contact compliance are required. Printing ink manufacturers incorporate it into packaging inks where consistent hue and substrate adhesion are priorities.

Coatings and industrial paint formulators use it to achieve saturated red shades in solvent-based and specialty systems. Textile and paper dyeing operations also draw on this pigment for surface coloration.

This pigment is ideal where surface coloration rather than fiber penetration is the target outcome. It is supplied as a fine dry powder to ensure easy dispersion within various manufacturing processes.

Cosmetic-grade material is available meeting D&C specifications applicable to externally applied products. Technical-grade material serves industrial coatings and printing ink applications for diverse sectors.

name: 3-Ureidopropyltrimethoxysilane
description:
3-Ureidopropyltrimethoxysilane (CAS 23843-64-3 ), also known commercially as Ureidopropyltrimethoxysilane, is an organosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices.

It improves adhesion at mineral or glass interfaces by forming covalent bonds on both sides of the interface, reducing delamination and improving composite durability across various industrial applications.

In glass fiber-reinforced composites and filled polymer systems, it improves fiber-to-matrix adhesion, directly affecting mechanical performance and moisture resistance of the finished part for long-term use.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a primer or additive to improve bonding to glass, concrete, and metal substrates, particularly in construction and automotive assembly projects.

In coatings for electronics, it promotes adhesion of encapsulants and conformal coatings to circuit board substrates where long-term humidity resistance is critical for maintaining device integrity.

It also functions as a crosslinker in moisture-cure systems, contributing to network formation in silane-modified polymer sealants used in high-performance industrial and commercial sealing applications.

3-Ureidopropyltrimethoxysilane is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity grades suitable for industrial compounding and specialty formulation where consistent chemical performance is required.

Technical grade is the standard offering across most suppliers, with high-purity grades available for electronics and precision adhesive applications. Packaging ranges from small drums to IBC quantities.

name: Butyltin tris(2-ethylhexanoate)
description:
Butyltin tris(2-ethylhexanoate) (CAS 23850-94-4 ), sold commercially as Fascat 4102 and Fascat 9201, is an organotin catalyst used across coatings, adhesives, sealants, and polymer systems.

It accelerates curing and cross-linking reactions, enabling manufacturers to achieve controlled network formation at defined processing conditions. In moisture-cure and two-component polyurethane sealants, it promotes tin-catalyzed urethane bond formation.

This directly influences open time and final mechanical properties. Silicone elastomer producers use it to drive condensation cross-linking, where catalyst loading determines cure depth and surface tack-free time.

These are critical parameters for quality control. In industrial coatings, it supports isocyanate-based systems where cure speed and film hardness must meet tight application specifications.

Adhesive formulators working with reactive hot melts or structural bonding systems select it when precise pot life management and bond strength development are required.

Butyltin tris(2-ethylhexanoate) is supplied as a liquid, typically at high tin-content concentrations suited for direct addition to formulations or dilution into solvent-based systems.

It is available in technical grade , the standard for industrial catalyst applications in coatings and sealants. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers.

This reflects typical industrial procurement volumes. The product ensures consistent performance across a wide range of temperature and humidity conditions during the manufacturing process.

name: 2,2'-Dithiodi(ethylammonium) bis(dibenzyldithiocarbamate)
description:
2,2'-Dithiodi(ethylammonium) bis(dibenzyldithiocarbamate) (CAS 239446-62-9 ) is a dithiocarbamate salt used as a vulcanization accelerator and stabilizer in rubber and polymer processing. Its dual functional structure supports both crosslinking activity and antioxidant protection within a single compound.

In rubber and tire manufacturing, it accelerates sulfur vulcanization while contributing to long-term oxidative stability in the cured compound. Polymer formulators incorporate it where a combined curing and stabilization effect reduces the need for separate additive packages.

Its dithiocarbamate chemistry also positions it as a candidate for agricultural biocide formulations, where this compound class is established for fungicidal and preservation activity. Industrial buyers in plastics processing evaluate it for stabilizer applications.

This material is particularly useful in polymer systems requiring protection against degradation during high-temperature processing. This compound is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline material for industrial use.

It is available primarily at technical and research grades, with supply sourced through specialty chemical distributors serving rubber, polymer, and agrochemical markets. Packaging is generally offered in small laboratory quantities.

Suppliers also provide kilogram-scale industrial lots depending on the specific requirements of the buyer. The material is handled according to standard industrial protocols for specialty dithiocarbamate salts and chemical additives.

name: 2-chloro-5-methoxyaniline
description:
2-Chloro-5-methoxyaniline (CAS 2401-24-3 ), also known commercially as 6-chloro-m-anisidine, is an aromatic amine intermediate used in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty agrochemicals.

Its dual functional groups, a reactive amine and a chloro substituent, make it a building block for constructing complex heterocyclic and azo-based target molecules for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a key starting material for manufacturing drug candidates, particularly in programs targeting kinase inhibitors and other small-molecule therapeutics where precise substitution patterns are required.

Agrochemical manufacturers use it in the production of herbicide and fungicide active ingredients, where the chloro and methoxy groups direct selective reactivity during coupling steps in the manufacturing process.

Dye and pigment producers incorporate it into azo dye synthesis, where the aniline nitrogen undergoes diazotization to generate stable colorant intermediates for textile and industrial coatings.

It also appears in polymer research as a co-monomer or initiator component in specialty polymerization systems. This versatile chemical is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid for easy handling.

It is available in technical grade for industrial synthesis and in higher-purity grades suited to pharmaceutical intermediate applications. Packaging ranges from small research quantities to bulk drum supply.

name: Conjugated linoleic acid
description:
Conjugated linoleic acid ( CAS 2420-56-6 ), commonly abbreviated as CLA, is a naturally occurring fatty acid isomer produced commercially for use across food, feed, and pharmaceutical applications.

The specific isomer 10,12-CLA is the primary form of commercial interest, distinguishing it from the broader CLA family. It functions as a bioactive lipid ingredient targeting body composition and immune modulation.

In functional food and dietary supplement manufacturing, 10,12-CLA is incorporated into softgel capsules, fortified dairy products, and sports nutrition formulations targeting fat metabolism support.

Animal feed producers use it as a performance additive in ruminant and swine diets to influence milk fat composition and lean mass ratios. It is also used in lipid-based delivery systems.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators source it as an active ingredient where antioxidant stabilization is required. Food manufacturers apply it in fat blends and emulsified products.

CLA is supplied as a free fatty acid oil, typically in liquid form at room temperature, and as triglyceride or glyceride-esterified variants depending on specific application requirements.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with some producers offering material compliant with USP or FCC standards for high-purity applications.

Bulk supply is available in drums and IBCs, with isomer purity and total CLA content specified on certificates of analysis to ensure consistent quality for industrial manufacturing processes.

name: 2-hexyl-1-decanol
description:
2-Hexyl-1-decanol (CAS 2425-77-6 ), commercially available as Guerbitol 16 and Isofol 16, is a branched-chain fatty alcohol used across lubricant, polymer, and personal care manufacturing.

Its branched structure resists crystallization at low temperatures, making it a reliable base material where linear alcohols would solidify and disrupt processing during industrial applications.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it functions as a base fluid component and lubricity additive in synthetic esters and cutting fluids. It provides excellent thermal stability and performance.

Plastics processors use it as a plasticizer and processing aid in PVC and other polymer systems, improving flexibility and workability without the volatility concerns associated with shorter-chain alcohols.

In personal care, it acts as an emollient carrier and co-emulsifier in creams, lotions, and color cosmetics, contributing to skin feel and formulation stability for high-end consumer products.

It also serves as a solvent and carrier for active ingredients in industrial and specialty chemical formulations where low polarity and good solvency are required for effective chemical delivery.

2-Hexyl-1-decanol is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in technical grade for industrial lubricant and polymer applications, with cosmetic-grade material meeting high purity standards.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to meet the needs of large-scale manufacturing. Our material ensures consistent quality and performance across all specified industrial sectors.

name: 1,4-butanediol diglycidyl ether
description:
1,4-Butanediol diglycidyl ether (CAS 2425-79-8 ), commonly abbreviated as BDDGE, is a bifunctional epoxy reactive diluent and crosslinker used across adhesive, coating, and polymer systems.

It reduces viscosity in epoxy formulations while contributing to the final crosslink density of the cured network. In epoxy coatings and flooring systems, BDDGE lowers formulation viscosity without sacrificing cure performance.

This allows for higher filler loading and improved substrate wetting during application. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a reactive diluent to extend pot life and improve flexibility in cured bond lines.

In polymer and elastomer production, it functions as a crosslinking agent for hydroxyl- or amine-terminated systems. This includes applications in hydrogels and various surface-modified materials for industrial use.

Printing ink formulators incorporate BDDGE to adjust flow properties in UV-curable and solvent-based systems. This ensures the maintenance of film integrity and durability after the curing process is complete.

BDDGE is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid for industrial applications. Standard commercial grades are available at purities of 95% and above to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

Technical and high-purity grades are offered depending on the specific end-use requirements of the client. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers for bulk industrial supply and logistics.

name: Mepiquat chloride
description:
Mepiquat chloride (CAS 24307-26-4 ), also known commercially as BAS-083, is a plant growth regulator used primarily in cotton production to control excessive vegetative growth. By inhibiting gibberellin biosynthesis, it compacts plant architecture.

This chemical redirects energy toward boll development rather than canopy expansion. In cotton cultivation, it is applied as a foliar treatment to shorten internode length, reduce lodging risk, and improve harvestability.

This is particularly effective in high-yield, irrigated production systems. It is also used in wheat and barley to reduce stem elongation and prevent lodging under high-nitrogen fertility programs for modern agriculture.

Formulators incorporate it as the active ingredient in liquid suspension concentrates and soluble concentrate formulations for commercial herbicide and PGR products. Some programs combine it with cyclanilide or other actives.

These combinations broaden its agronomic effect on cotton maturity and fiber quality. The material is supplied as a technical-grade solid or as pre-formulated aqueous concentrates for various industrial applications.

Active ingredient concentrations typically range from 37% to 42% in commercial liquid products. Technical material is available for formulators requiring custom concentration or combination products for specific needs.

Supply is offered in bulk drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to agrochemical manufacturing volumes. This ensures efficient distribution and handling for large-scale agricultural chemical production facilities.

SAM chloride is used in finished dosage forms including tablets, enteric-coated formulations, and injectables. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement producers use it as the active ingredient in joint support and cognitive health products.

Stable salt forms are preferred over free-base material for processing in these industries. Biotechnology researchers rely on it as a cofactor and reagent in methyltransferase assays and epigenetic research workflows.

Food-grade applications include functional food fortification where methyl donor supplementation is a defined formulation objective. It is supplied as a crystalline powder, typically in stabilized salt form to maintain activity.

name: Triheptadecanoin
description:
Triheptadecanoin (CAS 2438-40-6 ), also known as glycerol triheptadecanoate, is a synthetic odd-chain triglyceride used as a reference standard and functional lipid ingredient across food and cosmetic applications.

Its defined, uniform fatty acid composition makes it a reliable tool for analytical calibration and a controlled-purity emollient base where consistency is critical for high-end manufacturing processes.

In food and nutrition research, it is used as an internal standard for quantifying triglyceride content in lipid profiling and fatty acid analysis by GC and HPLC. This ensures precision in complex testing.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into emollient systems where a structurally defined triglyceride is required to benchmark performance or support stability testing. It provides a consistent baseline for new products.

As a functional lipid, it contributes moisturizing and skin-conditioning properties in creams and lotions, acting as an emollient carrier within oil phases. It integrates seamlessly into various topical formulations.

Its odd-chain structure distinguishes it from naturally occurring triglycerides, making it traceable in biological and formulation matrices. This unique chemical signature is highly valued in specialized research.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white solid or waxy powder. It is available primarily in high-purity analytical and research grades, with purity specifications typically at 99% or above for accuracy.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade material is also available for formulators requiring larger quantities beyond laboratory scale. These batches meet rigorous industry requirements for safety and performance.

name: Drometrizole
description:
Drometrizole (CAS 2440-22-4 ), commonly known in the industry as UV-P, is a benzotriazole-class UV absorber used to protect organic substrates from photodegradation. It absorbs UV radiation in the 300–385 nm range, preventing yellowing and color fade.

This chemical prevents mechanical degradation in light-exposed materials. In plastics and polymer compounding, UV-P is incorporated into polyolefins, PVC, and engineering resins to extend service life in outdoor or UV-exposed end products.

Coatings formulators use it in industrial and architectural finishes where long-term gloss retention and substrate protection are required. Adhesives and sealant manufacturers add it to formulations where UV exposure would cause embrittlement.

In personal care, this compound is used as a UV filter in cosmetic formulations including sunscreens and leave-on products. It provides broad UV-A/UV-B protection and ensures the stability of the final consumer product.

The material is supplied as a white to light yellow crystalline powder. It is available in technical grade for industrial polymer and coatings applications, as well as cosmetic grade meeting high purity standards.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to multi-hundred kilogram drums to suit both development-scale and commercial production volumes. Our material meets rigorous quality control protocols for consistency.

name: Palmitoyl glycine
description:
Palmitoyl glycine (CAS 2441-41-0 ) is a fatty acid-amino acid conjugate derived from palmitic acid and glycine, used in personal care formulations as a mild surfactant and skin-conditioning agent.

Its acyl amino acid structure positions it as a functional ingredient where both surface activity and compatibility with biological substrates are required for high-performance cosmetic applications.

In cleansing formulations such as facial washes, shampoos, and body cleansers, this ingredient delivers effective degreasing with a gentler profile than conventional sulfate surfactants, supporting low-irritation products.

It acts as an emulsifier in leave-on and rinse-off systems, helping stabilize oil-in-water emulsions in creams and lotions. Its surface-modifying properties improve wetting and spreadability across the skin.

Formulators also incorporate it into premium cleansing bars and syndet products where amino acid-based surfactants are a key differentiator for brands focusing on mildness and skin health.

This chemical is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, with purity levels commonly at or above 98% as assessed by HPLC analysis.

name: di-tert-butyl dicarbonate
description:
Di-tert-butyl dicarbonate (CAS 24424-99-5 ), commonly known as Boc₂O or BOC-anhydride, is a reagent used across pharmaceutical synthesis and biotechnology to introduce the tert-butoxycarbonyl protecting group onto amines.

This function is central to controlled peptide assembly and API manufacturing, where selective protection of reactive sites determines synthetic yield and product purity in complex chemical processes.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Boc₂O is used to protect amine groups during multi-step synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, preventing unwanted side reactions at critical stages of development.

Peptide synthesis relies heavily on Boc chemistry, particularly in solid-phase and solution-phase processes producing therapeutic peptides and amino acid derivatives for various medical applications.

Biotechnology workflows use it to modify proteins, linkers, and bioconjugates where reversible amine protection is required. It also appears in agrochemical and specialty chemical synthesis for clean transformations.

Di-tert-butyl dicarbonate is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, with liquid form being the standard commercial presentation for bulk handling and efficient industrial processing.

It is available in reagent-grade and high-purity pharmaceutical-grade specifications suited to GMP manufacturing environments. Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities up to drum-scale supply for operations.

name: Bryonolic acid
description:
Bryonolic acid (CAS 24480-44-2 ), also known as bryononic acid, is a naturally derived triterpenoid organic acid isolated primarily from plants of the Cucurbitaceae family. In pharmaceutical and biotechnology research, it functions as a bioactive reference compound.

This material serves as a tool for investigating anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory pathways at the cellular level. In pharmaceutical R&D, it is used as an analytical reference standard for identifying and quantifying triterpenoid constituents.

Biotechnology researchers source it as a biochemical probe to study macrophage activation and cytokine signaling in preclinical assay systems. It also supports the development and quality control of plant-derived active pharmaceutical ingredients.

Triterpenoid profiling is often required for regulatory submissions and standardized botanical extracts. Formulators use this compound to establish validated marker compound specifications for various herbal formulations and botanical products.

The product is supplied as a dry solid powder, typically at high purity levels suited to research and reference standard applications. Common grades include HPLC-grade and research-grade material for laboratory use.

name: Triglycidyl isocyanurate
description:
Triglycidyl isocyanurate (CAS 2451-62-9 ), commercially known as TGIC, is a trifunctional epoxy compound used as a crosslinker and curing agent in thermosetting polymer systems.

It reacts with carboxyl-functional resins to build durable, chemically resistant networks, making it a standard component in high-performance coating formulations for industrial use.

TGIC is the primary crosslinker in polyester-based powder coatings, where it delivers superior outdoor durability, UV resistance, and mechanical strength in architectural finishing applications.

In the electronics industry, it contributes to epoxy encapsulants and printed circuit board laminates that require tight dimensional stability under thermal cycling and stress.

Aerospace and defense manufacturers use TGIC-cured systems in structural adhesives and composite matrices where resistance to elevated temperatures and aggressive environments is critical.

Flexible packaging printers also incorporate it into ink and coating formulations that demand strong substrate adhesion and chemical resistance across various commercial printing platforms.

TGIC is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades are available at purities of 98% and above, serving the coatings and composites sectors.

name: Zinc laurate
description:
Zinc laurate (CAS 2452-01-9 ), also known as zinc dilaurate, is a zinc soap derived from lauric acid used as a functional additive across rubber, plastics, and personal care manufacturing.

It acts as a lubricant, release agent, and surface modifier, reducing friction and improving processing behavior in solid-form applications. In rubber and tire compounding, it functions as an internal lubricant.

This additive serves as a mold release agent, reducing die swell and improving surface finish on extruded profiles. Plastics processors incorporate it into PVC and polyolefin formulations to reduce equipment wear.

It is also used to improve flow during extrusion or calendering. In personal care, it is used in pressed powder cosmetics and dry formulations to improve slip, binding, and texture uniformity.

Metalworking applications use it as a solid lubricant component in drawing compounds and stamping aids where oil-based lubricants are impractical. The material is supplied as a fine white powder.

It is available in technical grade for industrial processing applications, and in cosmetic-grade specifications for personal care formulators requiring tighter purity and particle size control.

Packaging typically ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk quantities depending on application volume. This versatile chemical ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing sectors and industrial processes.

name: Dioctyltin carboxylate
description:
Dioctyltin carboxylate (CAS 24577-34-2 ) is an organotin compound used as a catalyst in polymer and elastomer processing. It promotes curing, crosslinking, and polymerization reactions across a range of industrial formulations where controlled tin-based catalysis is required.

In PVC stabilization and polyurethane systems, it functions as a condensation catalyst, accelerating urethane bond formation in foam and elastomer production. Silicone sealant and RTV rubber manufacturers use it to drive room-temperature vulcanization.

This catalyst is essential for controlling the cure rate and final mechanical properties of the material. Coating formulators incorporate it into moisture-cure systems where precise catalytic activity at low loading levels is commercially important.

Adhesive and sealant producers working with tin-catalyzed crosslinking systems select it for applications requiring a balance between pot life and cure speed. It ensures consistent performance across various chemical environments and processing temperatures.

Dioctyltin carboxylate is supplied as a liquid, typically at high active-tin concentrations suited for direct addition or dilution into formulations. This versatility makes it a preferred choice for large-scale industrial manufacturing.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to industrial catalyst applications. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers depending on volume requirements for the specific facility.

Biotechnology laboratories use it as an analytical reference standard for HPLC method validation and peptide quantification assays. In food and nutrition research, it is evaluated as a functional peptide component in studies examining bioavailability.

Coating formulators use it as a crosslinking intermediate in polyester and alkyd resin systems where precise functionality is required. Low volatility and specific process requirements make it an ideal choice for these industrial applications.

In adhesive and sealant formulations, it contributes to polymer backbone construction where thermal stability is a qualification criterion. It ensures durability under prolonged service conditions for high-performance bonding agents.

It delivers cerium in an oil-soluble, organically compatible form, enabling its use across coating, polymer, and lubricant systems where inorganic cerium salts would be incompatible.

In coating formulations, it functions as a drier and oxidative cure promoter, accelerating cross-linking in alkyd and air-drying resin systems for industrial applications.

Polymer producers use it as a polymerization catalyst and co-catalyst, particularly in processes requiring rare earth metal activation to achieve specific material properties.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it acts as an additive precursor where controlled metal content supports performance at elevated temperatures and pressures.

Sealant and elastomer manufacturers incorporate it to promote cross-linking and improve cure response in specialty rubber compounds used in demanding environments.

In industrial coatings and flooring systems, EHGE lowers epoxy resin viscosity to improve substrate wetting and application at ambient temperatures for better surface coverage.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a reactive flexibilizer, where it participates in the cure network to reduce brittleness in structural bonds and joints.

Automotive and industrial coating formulators use it in solvent-free primer and topcoat systems to achieve low-VOC compliance while maintaining a workable pot life during application.

In epoxy-based inks for printing and packaging, it functions as a reactive carrier that improves pigment dispersion and film flexibility across various industrial substrates.

This stability is essential for active ingredients. In water treatment, it chelates calcium and magnesium ions to prevent scale formation in industrial cooling and distribution systems.

It also acts as a sequestrant in emulsified and dairy-based products, preventing discoloration and texture degradation caused by trace metal contamination during the manufacturing process.

name: 3-Isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane
description:
3-Isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane (CAS 24801-88-5 ), also known as ICPTES, is a bifunctional silane coupling agent combining an isocyanate group with an alkoxysilane anchor. It bonds organic polymer matrices to inorganic substrates by reacting at both the organic and inorganic interface simultaneously.

This versatile chemical is used for glass, metals, and mineral fillers. In adhesives, sealants, and structural bonding formulations, it improves adhesion to glass and metal substrates where moisture resistance is critical for long-term performance.

Coatings manufacturers use it to crosslink polyurethane systems onto treated surfaces, improving durability and intercoat adhesion on automotive and industrial parts. It ensures a robust chemical bond between the coating and the underlying material.

In filled polymer compounds, it functions as a surface modifier for silica and glass fiber, improving stress transfer between filler and matrix in reinforced plastics. This leads to enhanced mechanical properties and structural integrity.

Electronics encapsulants and underfill resins incorporate it to enhance interfacial adhesion between polymer and substrate under thermal cycling conditions. This prevents delamination and protects sensitive electronic components from environmental stress.

Supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard packaging from small laboratory quantities up to bulk drums and IBC containers. Technical grade is the primary commercial offering, with purity typically at 95% or higher.

Moisture-sensitive handling requirements influence packaging specifications, and nitrogen-blanketed containers are standard for bulk shipments. Proper storage is essential to maintain the chemical stability and reactivity of the isocyanate functional group.

name: Docosapentaenoic acid
description:
Docosapentaenoic acid (CAS 24880-45-3 ), commonly known as Clupanodonic acid or DPA n-3, is a long-chain omega-3 fatty acid naturally occurring in marine oils and certain algal sources.

It occupies a distinct metabolic position between EPA and DHA, making it a target ingredient for formulators developing advanced omega-3 products for the global market.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, DPA n-3 is incorporated into omega-3 concentrates where its role in supporting EPA-to-DHA conversion pathways differentiates it from standard fish oil fractions.

Marine-derived feed ingredients for aquaculture and livestock nutrition utilize Clupanodonic acid to enrich fatty acid profiles in farmed species. Pharmaceutical-grade omega-3 formulations increasingly specify it.

These formulations targeting cardiovascular and metabolic indications often include DPA n-3 as a discrete active alongside EPA and DHA to ensure a complete marine omega-3 spectrum for consumers.

Functional food producers also incorporate it into fortified oils and emulsified products. Docosapentaenoic acid is supplied as a refined liquid oil, typically as a triglyceride or ethyl ester concentrate.

Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels commonly ranging from concentrated blends to high-purity isolates that meet USP and Ph.Eur. standards.

Bulk supply is available in drum and IBC quantities, with cold-chain handling required to maintain oxidative stability. Our material complies with FCC and BP requirements for industrial use.

name: Zinc formaldehyde sulfoxylate
description:
Zinc formaldehyde sulfoxylate ( CAS 24887-06-7 ), also known as zinc bis(hydroxymethanesulphinate), is an inorganic reducing salt used industrially as a bleaching and stripping agent. It functions by releasing active reducing species under heat or alkaline conditions.

This chemical enables controlled decolorization and whitening in various wet processing operations. In textile dyeing and finishing, it serves as a discharge agent to selectively remove or reduce dye from fabric, enabling resist and discharge printing effects.

Leather processing operations use it to bleach hides and control oxidative discoloration during tanning. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it to brighten mechanical pulps and reduce yellowing in finished paper grades to improve final product quality.

Water treatment applications use it as a reducing agent to neutralize residual oxidants such as chlorine and chromate compounds in industrial effluent streams. This ensures that wastewater meets environmental standards before discharge into local systems.

Zinc formaldehyde sulfoxylate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or granular solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 90% to 98% active content for industrial use.

Packaging is generally available in 25 kg bags or bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. The material should be stored in a cool, dry place to maintain its chemical stability and effectiveness over long periods of time.

name: Sodium 2-mercaptobenzothiazole
description:
Sodium 2-mercaptobenzothiazole (CAS 2492-26-4 ), commonly referenced as Sodium MBT or Na-MBT, is the water-soluble sodium salt form of mercaptobenzothiazole used across industrial sectors as a corrosion inhibitor and biocide.

Unlike its parent compound, it dissolves readily in aqueous systems, making it the preferred form for liquid formulations requiring metal protection or microbial control in various manufacturing environments.

In metalworking and cutting fluid formulations, Na-MBT protects non-ferrous metals, particularly copper and brass, from corrosion during machining and storage. This ensures the integrity of the finished metal parts.

Water treatment systems use it to inhibit metal corrosion in cooling towers and closed-loop circuits where copper alloy components are present. It provides a protective layer that prevents oxidative damage to the system.

Automotive antifreeze and coolant manufacturers incorporate it as a copper and brass corrosion inhibitor to extend system component life. This application is critical for maintaining the efficiency of vehicle cooling systems.

It also functions as a preservative and biocide in industrial fluids, rubber latex processing, and coating systems where microbial growth would degrade product quality. This helps maintain the shelf life of the fluids.

Sodium MBT is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% concentration. Standard grades include technical grade for industrial applications and higher-purity grades for specialty formulations.

Packaging ranges from bags and drums to intermediate bulk containers depending on volume requirements. These options allow for flexible logistics and storage solutions for chemical distributors and end-users alike.

name: 4-bromophenyl isocyanate
description:
4-Bromophenyl isocyanate (CAS 2493-02-9 ), also known as p-bromophenyl isocyanate, is a reactive aryl isocyanate used as a building block in organic synthesis and polymer chemistry.

The bromine substituent provides a handle for further functionalization, making it a practical intermediate for constructing complex molecular architectures in pharmaceutical and specialty chemical workflows.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a key intermediate for preparing urea-containing drug candidates and bioactive compounds where the bromine atom enables downstream cross-coupling reactions.

Agrochemical and fine chemical manufacturers use it to introduce the bromophenyl-urea motif into active ingredient scaffolds. In polymer research, it functions as a monomer for producing specialty polyureas.

Biotechnology researchers also employ it in the preparation of labeled probes and derivatization reagents for analytical applications. It is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid in high-purity grades.

Standard offerings include reagent-grade and synthesis-grade material, with purity specifications commonly at 97% or higher by GC. Packaging ranges from small quantities to bulk quantities for industrial use.

name: Polyvinylidene fluoride
description:
Polyvinylidene fluoride (CAS 24937-79-9 ), commonly known as PVDF, is a high-performance fluoropolymer resin used across demanding industrial applications where chemical resistance and thermal stability are non-negotiable sourcing criteria.

It functions as a structural and functional material in environments where conventional polymers fail. This material enables long service life in aggressive chemical, electrical, and outdoor exposure conditions for global manufacturers.

In the electronics and battery industries, PVDF serves as the primary binder material for lithium-ion battery electrode coatings. This application directly influences cell performance and cycle life in modern energy storage systems.

Piping systems, pumps, valves, and tank linings for chemical processing rely on PVDF where resistance to acids, solvents, and halogens is required. It provides a robust solution for high-purity fluid handling and transport.

Architectural coatings and building facade systems use PVDF-based formulations to deliver weathering resistance and color retention over decades. These coatings protect structures from UV degradation and harsh environmental pollutants.

In filtration membranes for water treatment and pharmaceutical processing, PVDF is the base polymer of choice. It is favored due to its ability to be cast into microporous structures with controlled pore geometry.

PVDF is supplied as powder, pellets, and solution-grade dispersions depending on the processing method. Injection molding, extrusion, or coating applications each require distinct forms to ensure optimal manufacturing results.

Standard grades include homopolymer and copolymer variants, with battery-grade and membrane-grade specifications available. Purity and molecular weight specifications vary by end-use, with binder grades subject to tight quality controls.

name: Polyethylene adipate
description:
Polyethylene adipate (CAS 24938-37-2 ) is a polyester polyol produced by condensing ethylene glycol with adipic acid. It functions as a base polymer and plasticizing component across multiple industrial sectors.

This material provides essential flexibility, compatibility, and chain-extension capability in various polymer systems. In polyurethane manufacturing, it serves as a polyol building block for producing flexible foams and elastomers.

It is also used for cast parts where controlled molecular weight determines final mechanical performance. Coatings formulators incorporate it into two-component polyurethane systems to improve film flexibility and adhesion.

The product ensures superior performance on metal and plastic substrates. In adhesives and sealants, it contributes significantly to peel strength and elongation in structural bonding applications across the industry.

Lubricant manufacturers use polyester-based fluids derived from this material where thermal stability is required. It is particularly effective in metalworking and gear oil formulations due to its low volatility.

Polyethylene adipate is supplied as a waxy solid or viscous liquid depending on molecular weight grade. Typical melt points vary across commercial ranges to meet specific industrial processing requirements.

Standard supply forms include technical-grade material in drums or bulk containers. Molecular weight specifications commonly range from low to high MW variants tailored to specific application requirements.

Hydroxyl value and acid value are the primary specification parameters buyers use to qualify grades. These metrics are essential for qualifying the material for polyurethane or coating applications.

name: Tridecyl ethyleneglycol monoether
description:
Tridecyl ethyleneglycol monoether (CAS 24938-91-8 ), also marketed as Trideceth and classified under E1300 , is a nonionic surfactant derived from tridecyl alcohol and ethylene oxide.

It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and cleaning agent across industrial and personal care formulations, with performance tunable by varying the degree of ethoxylation.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a scouring and degreasing agent, removing oils and contaminants from fiber and hide surfaces prior to dyeing or finishing.

Personal care formulators use it to stabilize emulsions in creams, lotions, and cleansing products, where it also contributes to foam modulation for better performance.

In industrial cleaning concentrates, it improves soil dispersion and rinsability across hard-surface and equipment cleaning applications. Paper processing operations use it as a dispersant.

It serves as a process aid to control pitch deposits and improve coating uniformity. Tridecyl ethyleneglycol monoether is supplied as a liquid or paste depending on the ethoxylation degree.

Low-EO grades typically present as liquids and higher-EO grades as waxy solids or pastes. It is available in technical and industrial grades with specific ethoxylate chain lengths.

Common variants like Trideceth-6 or Trideceth-10 are selected based on HLB requirements of the target formulation to ensure optimal stability and performance in various chemical systems.

name: Sodium allylsulfonate
description:
Sodium allylsulfonate (CAS 2495-39-8 ), commonly abbreviated as SAS, is a reactive sulfonate monomer used across polymer chemistry and surface treatment industries. It introduces permanent sulfonate functionality into polymer backbones.

This enables controlled modification of surface charge, hydrophilicity, and ionic character in finished materials. In electroplating and metal finishing, SAS is incorporated into nickel and chrome bath formulations.

It acts as a brightening and leveling co-monomer, improving deposit uniformity and surface quality. Textile and leather processors use it to graft sulfonate groups onto fiber surfaces, enhancing dye uptake.

This process improves wet fastness in synthetic fabrics. In polymer manufacturing, SAS copolymerizes with acrylic acid, acrylamide, or vinyl acetate to produce scale inhibitors and dispersants for water systems.

These are used for industrial water treatment systems. Paper manufacturers apply SAS-based copolymers as retention aids and surface sizing agents to improve sheet formation and ink receptivity.

Sodium allylsulfonate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution. Solution concentrations are typically around 40–50% w/w for most industrial and technical applications.

Standard commercial grades are available with purity specifications commonly at 98% or higher for solid forms. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities to suit both laboratory and high-volume producers.

name: Acrylamide-styrene copolymer
description:
Acrylamide-styrene copolymer (CAS 24981-13-3 ), also referred to as styrene/acrylamide copolymer, is a synthetic polymer used across industrial processing sectors for rheology control, flocculation, and surface modification.

Its balance of hydrophilic and hydrophobic character makes it effective in both aqueous and mixed-phase systems where conventional homopolymers underperform. In water treatment, it functions as a flocculant to aggregate suspended solids.

This material improves clarification efficiency in municipal and industrial effluent streams by aggregating colloidal particles. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it as a wet-strength or retention aid during sheet formation.

The polymer improves fiber bonding and filler retention, which is critical for high-quality paper production. In textile and leather processing, it modifies surface properties of substrates to improve coating adhesion.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it as a rheology modifier to control viscosity. It ensures suspension stability in liquid detergent systems, preventing the separation of active ingredients during storage.

Acrylamide-styrene copolymer is supplied as an aqueous dispersion or solution, with dry powder forms available for applications requiring extended shelf life. Molecular weight and charge density vary by grade.

Suppliers typically offer technical-grade material tailored to specific processing conditions. Buyers should confirm solid content, ionic character, and viscosity specifications against their process requirements before procurement.

name: Polyethylene glycol diamine
description:
Polyethylene glycol diamine (CAS 24991-53-5 ), commonly abbreviated as PEG diamine, is a difunctional amine-terminated polyether used to introduce flexible, hydrophilic segments into polymer networks.

Its terminal amine groups enable direct reaction with epoxies, isocyanates, and anhydrides, making it a practical building block for controlled crosslinking and chain extension in various systems.

In epoxy coating and adhesive systems, this material acts as a flexible curing agent, reducing brittleness in cured films while maintaining adhesion to demanding substrates during the curing process.

Polyurethane and polyurea formulators incorporate it as a soft-segment extender to tune elasticity and moisture response in sealants and elastomeric components for industrial and commercial use.

Surface modification of textiles and technical fibers relies on its amine reactivity to graft hydrophilic functionality, improving wettability and dye uptake across different fiber types.

In industrial cleaning and home care formulations, it contributes to rheology adjustment and surface-active behavior in polymer-based systems, enhancing the performance of the final product.

The product is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid across a range of molecular weights, typically from 400 to 4000 g/mol, with MW directly influencing flexibility and density.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity and amine value specified per lot. Bulk and drum quantities are the typical supply formats for industrial procurement needs.

name: Polyethylene glycol dimethyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol dimethyl ether (CAS 24991-55-7 ), commonly abbreviated as PEGDME and known commercially as Selexol, is a series of end-capped polyethylene glycol oligomers.

It functions as a high-boiling polar solvent, plasticizer, and humectant across industrial and consumer formulation markets. In industrial gas treatment, Selexol is the active solvent.

It is used in physical absorption processes for removing CO2, H2S, and other acid gases from natural gas and syngas streams. Personal care formulators use PEGDME as a humectant.

It acts as an emollient carrier in skin creams, hair conditioners, and leave-on treatments where low volatility and skin compatibility are priorities. In polymer processing, it acts as a plasticizer.

It improves flexibility and workability in PVC compounds and adhesive formulations. Cleaning and industrial solvent applications also draw on its capacity to dissolve a broad range of soils.

PEGDME is supplied as a clear liquid, with viscosity and molecular weight varying by grade. Typical commercial grades range from PEGDME 250 to PEGDME 2000, reflecting average molecular weight.

Technical and industrial grades are the most commonly traded. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available for select molecular weight cuts meeting relevant compendial standards.

name: Vinyl toluene
description:
Vinyl toluene (CAS 25013-15-4 ) is a reactive monomer used as a building block in polymer synthesis and resin production. It functions as a crosslinking and copolymerization agent, enabling formulators to modify the performance characteristics of polymer systems.

This versatile chemical is utilized across coatings, adhesives, and plastics applications. In unsaturated polyester and alkyd resin systems, it acts as a reactive diluent and crosslinker, replacing styrene where lower volatility is required.

Coatings manufacturers use it to produce harder, faster-curing films in industrial and architectural finishes. In printing inks, it contributes to resin binders that require controlled drying speed and adhesion to various substrates.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it into copolymer backbones to tune flexibility, tack, and cohesive strength. This is particularly useful in pressure-sensitive and structural formulations requiring specific mechanical properties.

The product is supplied as a liquid monomer, typically inhibited with a polymerization inhibitor to maintain stability during storage and transport. This ensures the material remains reactive only when intended during the manufacturing process.

It is available in technical grade , which is the standard specification for industrial polymer and resin applications. Bulk liquid supply in drums, IBCs, and isotanks is the conventional commercial format for this product.

name: Butylated Hydroxyanisole
description:
Butylated Hydroxyanisole ( CAS 25013-16-5 ), commonly known as BHA or E320 , is a synthetic phenolic antioxidant used across food, cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications.

It prevents oxidative degradation in fats, oils, and lipid-containing formulations, extending shelf life and maintaining product integrity. In food manufacturing, BHA is approved under E320 and FEMA 2183 .

It is used in edible fats, oils, snack foods, and packaging materials where fat oxidation is a primary spoilage concern. Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions.

These products stabilize oil-phase ingredients against rancidity. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to protect lipid excipients and active ingredients in oral and topical dosage forms to ensure stability.

In plastics, rubber, and lubricant production, BHA functions as a processing stabilizer. It protects polymer matrices and petroleum-based fluids from oxidative breakdown during manufacturing and storage.

BHA is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or powder form. It is available in food-grade specifications conforming to FCC , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards.

Technical grade options are also available for industrial applications. Purity levels of 98.5% and above are standard for regulated food and pharmaceutical supply chains to ensure high performance.

name: Pinacolborane

Pinacolborane (CAS 25015-63-8 ), commonly abbreviated as HBpin, is a selective hydroboration reagent used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. It delivers boron functionality to unsaturated substrates under mild, controllable conditions.

This reagent enables efficient access to organoboron intermediates that would otherwise require multi-step routes. In pharmaceutical and API synthesis, HBpin is the reagent of choice for catalytic hydroboration of alkenes and alkynes.

In specialty monomer production, it supports the synthesis of boron-functionalized monomers for controlled polymerization platforms. Pinacolborane is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically at purities of 95% and above.

High-purity grades are available for sensitive synthetic applications. It is offered in research quantities through to multi-kilogram industrial packaging to meet various production scales.

Moisture-sensitive handling requirements are reflected in inert-atmosphere packaging formats. Technical and synthesis-grade specifications are standard across the market for this versatile chemical intermediate.

description:
Butyl acrylate-methacrylic acid-methyl methacrylate copolymer (CAS 25035-69-2 ) is an acrylic terpolymer combining soft butyl acrylate segments with methacrylic acid and methyl methacrylate.

This combination delivers tunable film-forming and adhesion properties across industrial formulations. Buyers source this resin where controlled flexibility, surface adhesion, and rheological behavior must be balanced.

In architectural and industrial coatings, the terpolymer functions as a film-forming binder that controls viscosity build. It improves substrate adhesion on metal, plastic, and wood surfaces for long-term durability.

Pressure-sensitive adhesive formulators use it to achieve the peel strength and tack balance required for labels, tapes, and protective films. It is essential for high-performance bonding applications.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it contributes to gloss retention and ink holdout on both porous and non-porous substrates. Plastic compounders incorporate it as a surface modifier for adhesion.

This copolymer is typically supplied as an aqueous dispersion or emulsion, with solids content varying by grade. Solution grades in organic solvents are available for applications where water sensitivity is a constraint.

Grades are generally offered to technical specifications, with molecular weight and acid value being the primary parameters. These factors are used to differentiate product performance tiers for industrial use.

name: Ethylene glycol-MDI copolymer
description:
Ethylene glycol-MDI copolymer (CAS 25036-33-3 ), also referenced commercially as Polyurethane y-304 and Polyurethane-39, is a urethane-based polymer formed from the reaction of ethylene glycol with methylene diphenyl diisocyanate.

It functions as a structural resin and crosslinking matrix in polymer systems requiring controlled rigidity, adhesion, and network density. In coatings and adhesive formulations, it contributes crosslink density and substrate bonding performance.

The material provides excellent adhesion across metal, plastic, and composite surfaces. Automotive OEM and refinish applications use it in structural adhesives and underbody sealants where dimensional stability under thermal cycling is required.

Rubber compounding and tire manufacturing incorporate it as a processing aid to modify rheological behavior. It is specifically utilized to improve green strength before vulcanization in various industrial rubber applications.

In rigid and semi-rigid plastic components, it supports network formation that determines final hardness and load-bearing characteristics. This makes it a vital component for manufacturers focusing on high-durability plastic parts.

Ethylene glycol-MDI copolymer is typically supplied as a solid or dispersed resin, depending on the intended processing route. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most industrial uses.

Specifications are strictly aligned to end-use performance requirements in industrial polymer processing. Packaging is generally available in bulk quantities suited to industrial compounding and formulation operations.

name: Isoprene-styrene copolymer
description:
Isoprene-styrene copolymer (CAS 25038-32-8 ), commercially recognized as Styrene Isoprene Styrene (SIS), is a thermoplastic elastomer block copolymer used across adhesive, sealant, and rubber compounding applications.

It delivers elastic recovery and melt processability without requiring vulcanization, making it a preferred base polymer for hot-melt and pressure-sensitive systems. SIS is the primary base polymer in hot-melt pressure-sensitive adhesives.

These adhesives are used for labels, tapes, and hygiene product construction, where its natural tack and cohesive strength determine bond performance. In roofing and waterproofing membranes, it modifies bitumen to improve low-temperature flexibility.

The material also provides resistance to thermal creep in construction applications. Rubber compounders incorporate it to adjust hardness and elastic recovery in molded and extruded profiles, ensuring high performance in industrial settings.

In household and industrial contact adhesives, SIS contributes to open-time control and peel strength across a range of substrates. Isoprene-styrene copolymer is supplied as pellets, crumbs, or blocks depending on the grade.

Styrene content and diblock ratio are the key specification variables that differentiate commercial grades, with typical styrene content ranging from 14% to 30%. Technical grades are standard for most industrial uses.

Food-contact compliance varies by grade and should be confirmed against applicable regulations. Manufacturers ensure consistency by adhering to strict production protocols to meet specific industrial requirements and performance benchmarks.

name: Ethylene propylene diene terpolymer
description:
Ethylene propylene diene terpolymer ( CAS 25038-36-2 ), commonly known as EPDM, is a synthetic elastomer produced from ethylene, propylene, and a diene monomer. It is used across rubber compounding, sealing, and insulation applications.

This material is preferred where long-term resistance to heat, ozone, and weathering is a commercial requirement. In automotive manufacturing, EPDM is the primary material for door seals, window gaskets, and under-hood hoses.

Dimensional stability under thermal cycling is critical for these automotive components. Roofing membrane producers rely on EPDM sheeting as a durable waterproofing layer for flat and low-slope commercial roofing systems.

Wire and cable manufacturers use it as an insulating jacket material in medium-voltage applications requiring flexibility at low temperatures. In polymer blending, EPDM functions as an impact modifier and rheology modifier.

When used in polypropylene compounds, it improves toughness in injection-molded automotive and appliance components. EPDM is supplied as bales, granules, or pellets depending on Mooney viscosity grade and diene content.

Grades are differentiated by ethylene content, ENB (5-ethylidene-2-norbornene) or DCPD diene type, and oil-extended versus non-extended formulations. Both peroxide-curable and sulfur-curable grades are available.

These various formulations allow manufacturers to match specific compounding requirements for diverse industrial needs. The material remains a versatile choice for high-performance rubber applications globally.

name: Polycaprolactam
description:
Polycaprolactam (CAS 25038-54-4 ), commercially known as Nylon 6, is a synthetic polyamide produced through ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam. It is a foundational engineering polymer used across textile, automotive, and industrial manufacturing.

In textile manufacturing, Nylon 6 is extruded into continuous filament and staple fiber for apparel, hosiery, and technical fabrics where durability and elasticity are critical. Automotive suppliers compound it into under-hood components.

These structural brackets and cable management systems must perform under thermal and mechanical stress. Industrial applications include injection-molded gears, bearings, and conveyor parts where load-bearing performance is required.

Material selection is driven by the need for extended service life in demanding environments. In film and packaging, it is processed into barrier layers for food-contact flexible packaging requiring puncture resistance.

This material provides necessary oxygen impermeability for sensitive goods. Polycaprolactam is supplied as pellets or granules, the standard form for compounding and injection molding operations across the global supply chain.

Fiber-grade and film-grade variants are available, along with reinforced compounds incorporating glass fiber at defined loading levels. Material is offered to industrial specifications for various manufacturing needs.

Food-contact compliant grades are available for packaging applications requiring specific safety certifications. This ensures the polymer meets the rigorous demands of modern industrial and consumer-facing production standards.

name: Polyethylene terephthalate
description:
Polyethylene terephthalate (CAS 25038-59-9 ), commercially known as Terylene or by the trade name Rynite, is a thermoplastic polyester resin used across packaging, textile, and industrial manufacturing.

Approved as E1512 for food-contact applications, it delivers high mechanical strength, dimensional stability, and barrier performance that procurement teams across multiple sectors rely on for their production needs.

In packaging, PET is the dominant material for blow-molded beverage bottles, food trays, and flexible films requiring moisture and gas barrier properties. Textile manufacturers use it to produce polyester fiber and filament yarn.

This resin serves as the base material for apparel, upholstery, and technical fabrics. In printing and packaging converting, biaxially oriented PET film serves as a substrate for lamination, metallization, and flexible printed electronics.

Engineering-grade compounds are also injection-molded into precision components such as connectors, housings, and structural parts in automotive and electrical applications. PET is supplied as pellets, chips, or flakes for industrial use.

Resin grades are differentiated by intrinsic viscosity (IV) to suit bottle, fiber, film, or engineering applications. Food-contact and beverage-grade material is available meeting FDA and EU food safety regulations.

Recycled PET (rPET) flake and pellet are also commercially available for buyers with sustainability or regulatory mandates. These materials ensure high performance while meeting modern environmental standards for global supply chains.
