name: Poly(vinylsulfonic acid) sodium salt
description:
Poly(vinylsulfonic acid) sodium salt (CAS 25053-27-4 ), also known as sodium poly(ethylenesulfonate), is a water-soluble anionic polyelectrolyte used across industrial processing and formulation.

It functions as a dispersant, scale inhibitor, and surface modifier in aqueous systems where charge-based stabilization is required. In water treatment, it inhibits scale formation and disperses particles.

The compound is highly effective in cooling water circuits and industrial effluent systems. Textile and paper manufacturers apply it as a surface modifier to improve wettability and dye uptake on substrates.

In leather processing, it aids tanning bath dispersion and controls the rheology of processing liquors. Home care and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it to prevent soil redeposition.

The additive helps stabilize surfactant systems at varying pH levels. Poly(vinylsulfonic acid) sodium salt is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging from 25% to 35% by weight.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with molecular weight variants available to suit specific viscosity and charge density requirements for diverse industrial applications.

Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers for industrial supply volumes. This ensures safe handling and efficient transport for large-scale manufacturing operations.

name: Polyvinylcarbazole
description:
Polyvinylcarbazole (CAS 25067-59-8 ), also known as PVK, is a photoconductive polymer derived from N-vinylcarbazole monomer. It is used across electronics, specialty coatings, and imaging applications where controlled charge transport and film-forming properties are required.

In organic electronics, PVK functions as a hole-transport layer in OLEDs, organic photovoltaics, and photodetectors, where it supports charge carrier mobility in thin-film device stacks.

Electrophotographic and laser printing systems use it as a photoconductor in drum coatings, enabling the charge-discharge cycle that defines image resolution for high-performance printing.

Specialty optical coatings and photoresist formulations incorporate PVK to achieve UV-sensitive layers in lithographic and imaging processes. This ensures precision in advanced manufacturing.

Research and development applications in organic semiconductors rely on it as a matrix material for phosphorescent dopants and light-emitting composites. It is a staple in modern material science.

Polyvinylcarbazole is supplied as a fine powder or granules, with molecular weight grades ranging from low to high MW to suit different processing and film-formation requirements.

Technical and research-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically confirmed by GPC and spectroscopic analysis to ensure consistent performance.

Packaging is available in quantities from laboratory-scale to bulk industrial supply. Our logistics network ensures that high-purity polymers are delivered safely to your facility for immediate use.

name: Bisphenol a epoxy resin
description:
Bisphenol A epoxy resin (CAS 25068-38-6 ), also designated E828 in food contact applications, is a thermosetting polymer formed by reacting bisphenol A with epichlorohydrin. It functions as a reactive matrix resin and adhesive binder across structural, protective, and electronic applications.

The resin cures with a range of hardeners to form chemically resistant, high-strength materials. In protective coatings, it forms the backbone of corrosion-resistant systems for industrial infrastructure, marine vessels, and concrete flooring.

Structural adhesive formulations rely on it to bond metals, composites, and substrates in automotive assemblies and aerospace components. Joint integrity under mechanical stress is critical in these high-performance environments.

In electronics, it is used to encapsulate components and manufacture printed circuit board laminates. Dimensional stability and electrical insulation after cure are procurement priorities for these technical applications.

Building and construction applications include grout systems, anchoring mortars, and waterproofing membranes. Chemical and moisture resistance determine product performance in these demanding infrastructure projects.

Supplied as a liquid resin at varying viscosities or as a solid at higher molecular weights, it is typically shipped in drums, IBCs, or bulk. Standard grades are defined by epoxide equivalent weight (EEW).

Low-viscosity liquid grades and solid flake grades are both commercially available to meet specific manufacturing needs. Food-contact grades compliant with the E828 designation are available for internal coatings of cans and packaging.

name: PVP/VA copolymer
description:
PVP/VA copolymer (CAS 25086-89-9 ) is a film-forming polymer produced from vinylpyrrolidone and vinyl acetate monomers in varying ratios. It delivers controlled film formation, adhesion, and moisture resistance across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial coating applications.

These properties provide performance benefits that pure PVP alone cannot achieve. In hair care, it functions as the primary fixative in styling sprays, mousses, and gels, where the VA content controls hold strength and humidity resistance relative to the VP ratio.

Pharmaceutical tablet coating and transdermal patch formulations use it as a film former and adhesion promoter. Grade selection is typically driven by the specific VP:VA ratio required for the final drug delivery system or coating thickness.

In printing inks and overprint varnishes, it improves substrate adhesion and surface gloss on both porous and non-porous substrates. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance industrial coatings and specialized packaging applications.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into long-wear foundations and sunscreens to extend wear and improve water resistance. Its ability to form a flexible, breathable film ensures comfort while maintaining the integrity of the cosmetic product on the skin.

PVP/VA copolymer is supplied as an aqueous solution or anhydrous ethanol solution, with dry powder forms available for specific applications. The VP:VA ratio, commonly 60:40 or 70:30, is the primary specification buyers use to match performance.

Cosmetic and pharmaceutical grades are the standard market offerings for this material. Pharmaceutical-grade material is manufactured to meet USP /NF monograph requirements, ensuring high purity and consistency for sensitive medical applications.

name: Isooctyl thioglycolate
description:
Isooctyl thioglycolate (CAS 25103-09-7 ), also known as isooctyl mercaptoacetate, is a sulfur-containing ester used as a reactive intermediate and functional additive across polymer, rubber, and lubricant applications.

It acts as a chain transfer agent, plasticizer, and stabilizer component depending on the formulation system. In PVC and polymer processing, it functions as a co-stabilizer component and plasticizing modifier.

This chemical improves flexibility and thermal processing performance in finished compounds. Rubber formulators use it to influence vulcanization chemistry and as a softening agent in specialty elastomer blends.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it contributes sulfur-active functionality relevant to extreme-pressure and boundary lubrication performance. It also serves as a monomer or chain transfer agent.

This is particularly useful in free-radical polymerization, where controlled molecular weight distribution is a process requirement. Isooctyl thioglycolate is supplied as a liquid for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically confirmed by GC analysis. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers to suit bulk industrial procurement needs.

name: Tert-dodecylmercaptan
description:

It is particularly vital for styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) and acrylonitrile-butadiene-styrene (ABS), where it regulates polymer chain length to achieve target mechanical properties. This ensures consistency in industrial manufacturing.

In emulsion polymerization for latex coatings and adhesives, it controls viscosity and film-forming characteristics of the final product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use TDM as a reagent and intermediate in synthesis processes.

These processes often require controlled thiol reactivity for precise chemical outcomes. At trace concentrations, it also functions as a flavoring agent in food applications, where sulfur-containing compounds contribute to savory profiles.

In personal care, it appears in rinse-off and leave-on product formulations such as shampoos, body washes, and lotions where a light fruity top note is desired. Its stability in finished formulations also makes it suitable for use in scented household and air care products.

Ethyl 2-cyclohexylpropionate is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in flavor and fragrance grade, meeting purity standards appropriate for use in food-contact and cosmetic applications. Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on the supplier.

Acrylates Copolymer (CAS 25133-97-5 ) is a synthetic acrylic polymer derived from ethyl acrylate, methyl methacrylate, and methacrylic acid monomers. It functions as a film-former, rheology modifier, and dispersant across personal care, coatings, and industrial applications.

In cosmetic formulations, it builds viscosity and stabilizes emulsions in products such as foundations, sunscreens, and hair styling gels. It delivers controlled texture and suspension of pigments or actives for high-performance beauty products.

Coating formulators use it to improve film integrity and adhesion on substrates including metal, plastic, and wood. Consistent rheology during application is a key processing requirement for these industrial coating systems.

In textile and paper processing, it acts as a binder and surface modifier, improving coating uniformity and durability of functional finishes. This ensures that the final treated materials maintain their structural integrity over time.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust tack, cohesion, and flow behavior in pressure-sensitive and structural formulations. This versatility makes it a staple component in modern chemical manufacturing and assembly.

name: Methyl nadic anhydride
description:
Methyl nadic anhydride ( CAS 25134-21-8 ), also known as nadic methyl anhydride or MNA, is a cycloaliphatic anhydride used as a curing agent and reactive intermediate in high-performance polymer systems.

It delivers thermally stable, chemically resistant cured networks suited to demanding structural and electrical applications. In epoxy resin formulations for aerospace and automotive composites, MNA produces cured systems.

These systems feature high glass transition temperatures and long pot life, which are critical for large-part processing. Electronics manufacturers use it to encapsulate and pot components where dimensional stability is required.

In electrical laminates and printed circuit board resins, MNA contributes to low dielectric loss and resistance to moisture uptake. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it into systems requiring flexibility.

This is particularly useful where cycloaliphatic chemistry improves UV stability over aromatic alternatives. Methyl nadic anhydride is supplied as a low-viscosity liquid, facilitating direct blending with liquid epoxy systems.

It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity levels typically specified at 95% or higher. Standard packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers for high-volume compounders.

Polyquaternium-39 (CAS 25136-75-8 ), also identified in formulation literature as AA/DMDAAC/AM copolymer, is a cationic conditioning polymer used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

In hair care, it deposits a conditioning film on the fiber surface during rinsing, improving detangling, softness, and wet combability in shampoos and conditioners for professional use.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and gels where it contributes moisture retention and a smooth skin feel without leaving a heavy or greasy residue on the surface.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it modifies solution viscosity and improves surface wetting, supporting more uniform coverage on various hard surfaces and substrates.

It is also used in leave-on hair styling products where controlled film deposition aids hold and manageability, making it a versatile ingredient for modern cosmetic manufacturing.

Nonylphenol (CAS 25154-52-3 ), commonly abbreviated as NP, is an alkylphenol intermediate used across industrial manufacturing as a precursor to surfactants, antioxidants, and polymer stabilizers.

It serves as a foundational building block for ethoxylated derivatives and other downstream chemical products rather than as a finished formulation ingredient for consumer applications.

In textile and leather processing, NP is reacted with ethylene oxide to produce nonylphenol ethoxylates, which function as emulsifiers and wetting agents in dyeing and finishing baths.

Plastics and rubber manufacturers use NP-derived antioxidants to protect polymer compounds from thermal and oxidative degradation during processing and end-use applications.

In metalworking and lubricant formulations, NP-based additives contribute to emulsion stability in cutting fluids and corrosion-inhibiting packages for industrial machinery.

Printing and packaging operations rely on NP derivatives as dispersants and emulsifiers in ink and coating systems to ensure consistent application and durability.

Nonylphenol is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions and is available in bulk quantities including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats for global distribution.

name: Poly(vinyl chloride-co-isobutyl vinyl ether)
description:
Poly(vinyl chloride-co-isobutyl vinyl ether) (CAS 25154-85-2 ), also known as vinyl chloride-vinyl isobutyl ether copolymer, is a thermoplastic resin produced by copolymerizing vinyl chloride with isobutyl vinyl ether.

The isobutyl vinyl ether component acts as an internal plasticizer, improving flexibility and processability without requiring separate plasticizer additions. In coatings formulations, this copolymer improves film flexibility and adhesion.

It provides excellent adhesion to difficult substrates including metals and plastics, making it suitable for industrial protective and decorative finishes. Printing ink manufacturers use it as a binder resin where controlled viscosity is critical.

Substrate wetting is essential to print quality on flexible packaging films. In adhesive and sealant systems, it contributes cohesive strength while maintaining the soft, conformable character needed for applications.

It is ideal for pressure-sensitive and heat-seal applications. Plastics compounders incorporate it to modify the rheological profile of PVC-based compounds, easing processing at lower temperatures during manufacturing.

This copolymer is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granules, with particle size and molecular weight varying by grade. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for industrial use.

Grades are differentiated by viscosity or K-value to match specific processing requirements. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities for industrial buyers seeking high-volume chemical supplies.

name: Sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate
description:
Sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate ( CAS 25155-30-0 ), commonly identified in trade as SDBS, is an anionic surfactant derived from the neutralization of dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid with sodium hydroxide.

It delivers strong detergency, emulsification, and foam generation across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations. In household and industrial cleaning products, SDBS functions as the primary active surfactant.

It is used in liquid detergents, dishwashing formulations, and hard-surface cleaners, where it breaks down grease and oils effectively at low concentrations. Textile processors rely on it as a scouring and wetting agent.

It helps to remove sizing agents, oils, and contaminants from fiber surfaces prior to dyeing. In water treatment, it supports the dispersion of suspended solids and acts as an emulsifier in effluent treatment processes.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and body washes where controlled foaming and cleansing performance are required. Sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate is supplied as a white to light yellow powder.

It is also available as a viscous liquid slurry, with active matter content typically ranging from 90% in powder form to 30–60% in aqueous paste or slurry grades. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

Detergent-grade material meeting defined active content thresholds is available for formulation use. Packaging options commonly include 25 kg bags for powder and IBC totes or drums for liquid grades.

name: 3-methoxybutanol
description:
3-Methoxybutanol (CAS 2517-43-3 ) is a glycol ether-type solvent used across industrial cleaning, coating, and personal care formulations. Its slow evaporation profile and miscibility with both water and organic solvents make it a practical choice.

Formulators utilize this chemical for managing solvent balance and substrate compatibility. In metalworking and industrial cleaning, it functions as a co-solvent in degreasing compounds and aqueous cleaning concentrates where controlled evaporation is required.

Printing and packaging formulators incorporate it into ink systems to improve flow, open time, and adhesion on difficult substrates. This versatility allows for high-performance results in demanding industrial environments.

In personal care, it acts as a carrier solvent in formulations such as hair care products and skin cleansers. It is often preferred over more aggressive alternatives when a mild, slow-evaporating solvent is necessary for the application.

Coating manufacturers also use it to optimize viscosity and film formation in waterborne and solvent-borne systems. This ensures a consistent finish and reliable performance across various surface types and application methods.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. It is available in technical grade for industrial and coating applications requiring high-volume supply.

Purity specifications generally range from 98% upward to meet strict manufacturing requirements. Documentation packages including COA and SDS are available for regulatory and QA review to ensure compliance with safety standards.

name: Polyvinylcaprolactam
description:
Polyvinylcaprolactam (CAS 25189-83-7 ), commercially known as PVCL, is a water-soluble thermoresponsive polymer used across personal care and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It exhibits a lower critical solution temperature that formulators exploit to control viscosity.

This unique property allows for precise control over film formation and moisture retention in finished products. In hair care and skin care formulations, PVCL functions as a rheology modifier and film-forming agent.

It contributes significantly to hold, texture, and the controlled release of active ingredients. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a matrix polymer in drug delivery systems where temperature-sensitive solubility is required.

Its application supports controlled-release tablet and hydrogel formats effectively. Textile and leather processors apply it as a surface modifier to improve wettability, handle, and coating adhesion on treated substrates.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface sizing and coating formulations where moisture management is essential. Film integrity is critical to end-product performance in these industrial applications.

Polyvinylcaprolactam is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with molecular weight ranges selected to match specific viscosity and film-forming performance targets.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is sourced to meet relevant purity specifications required for excipient qualification. This ensures the material meets the rigorous demands of modern chemical manufacturing and formulation.

name: Brilliant Black BN
description:
Brilliant Black BN ( CAS 2519-30-4 ), also known as Black PN and approved as E151 , is a synthetic azo dye used to impart deep black and dark brown-black coloration across food, textile, and leather applications.

It functions as a colorant in both aqueous and formulated systems, delivering strong tinctorial strength at low use levels. In food manufacturing, it is approved for use in products such as confectionery and sauces.

This additive is frequently utilized in fish roe analogues and soft drinks where a true black or near-black appearance is required. Textile processors apply it to dye wool, silk, and nylon substrates specifically.

It is particularly effective where uniform dark shades and acceptable wash fastness are specified. Leather finishers use it in dyeing and coating formulations to achieve consistent black tones on finished hides.

Paper manufacturers incorporate it into specialty colored paper grades where deep black coloration is part of the product specification. The material is supplied as a dark powder or granule for industrial use.

Its water solubility makes it suitable for liquid concentrate preparation. Food-grade material is available meeting E151 specifications under EU colorant regulations, ensuring high safety and quality standards.

Purity requirements govern subsidiary dyes and heavy metal limits for these applications. Technical grades are also available for textile and leather end uses where food compliance is not required for the process.

name: Polytetrahydrofuran
description:
Polytetrahydrofuran (CAS 25190-06-1 ), commercially known as PTMEG or Polytetramethylene Ether Glycol, is a difunctional polyether diol used as a building block in high-performance polymer synthesis.

It provides the soft-segment component in polyurethane and elastomer systems, directly influencing flexibility, elongation, and low-temperature performance in finished materials.

In polyurethane manufacturing, PTMEG reacts with diisocyanates to produce elastic fibers such as spandex and Lycra, where its molecular weight grade determines the stretch-recovery characteristics.

Thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) producers use it to engineer elastomers for automotive seals, hoses, and flexible tubing that must retain performance across a wide temperature range.

In the textile and apparel sector, PTMEG-based polyurethane urea is the standard intermediate for high-elasticity fabrics used in activewear and hosiery applications worldwide.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it as a plasticizing and carrier component in specialty greases and metalworking fluids where controlled viscosity and compatibility are required.

PTMEG is supplied as a waxy solid or viscous liquid depending on molecular weight, with common commercial grades at 650, 1000, 1800, and 2000 g/mol for industrial use.

Technical and industrial grades are standard; higher-purity grades are available for fiber and medical-grade polyurethane applications. Bulk supply is typically offered in heated drums.

name: Polyphenylene sulfide
description:
Polyphenylene sulfide (CAS 25212-74-2 ), commonly abbreviated as PPS, is a high-performance engineering thermoplastic used across demanding industrial sectors. Poly(thio-1,4-phenylene) is a recognized alternative designation in technical and polymer literature.

It delivers exceptional chemical resistance and dimensional stability under continuous high-temperature service conditions. This makes it a preferred matrix resin for precision-engineered components in various heavy industries.

In automotive manufacturing, PPS is compounded into glass- or mineral-filled grades for fuel system components and pump housings. These under-hood parts must withstand aggressive fluids and elevated temperatures consistently.

Electronics manufacturers rely on it for connector housings, relay components, and SMT-compatible parts. In these applications, tight dimensional tolerances and flame resistance are critical for safety and performance.

Aerospace and defense applications include structural brackets, fluid handling components, and radomes. These parts require low weight combined with extreme thermal and chemical durability in harsh environments.

It is also processed into films, fibers, and coatings for industrial filtration membranes and specialty textile applications. PPS is supplied as pellets or granules, with compounded grades available for specific targets.

Standard commercial grades are differentiated by melt flow, crosslink level, and filler content rather than pharmacopeial specifications. Technical-grade material is the primary market form for most industrial users.

Specialty grades are available for injection molding, extrusion, and compression molding processes. These materials ensure high performance across a wide range of manufacturing techniques and final product requirements.

name: Ethyl acrylate-methacrylic acid copolymer
description:
Ethyl acrylate-methacrylic acid copolymer (CAS 25212-88-8 ) is an acrylic copolymer resin used across coatings, adhesives, and specialty finishing systems. It functions as a rheology modifier, binder, and surface-active agent.

This material gives formulators control over film formation, adhesion, and cross-linking response in aqueous and solvent-based systems. In architectural and industrial coatings, it acts as a binder and rheology modifier.

The copolymer improves film build, leveling, and substrate adhesion on metal, plastic, and wood surfaces. Pressure-sensitive adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to tune tack, cohesive strength, and cure response.

It is effective in both waterborne and solvent-borne formulations. Textile and paper finishers apply it as a surface modifier to improve coating holdout, printability, and resistance to abrasion during processing.

In flexographic and gravure printing inks, it contributes to pigment binding and controls ink viscosity. This ensures consistent transfer across high-speed packaging lines for various commercial printing applications.

Ethyl acrylate-methacrylic acid copolymer is supplied as aqueous dispersions or emulsions, and in some grades as solution polymer or dried powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Specific solids content, pH, and viscosity profiles are defined by individual product grades. Specifications vary by supplier and are typically aligned to end-use performance requirements in coatings or adhesives.

name: Vinyl acetate-vinyl alcohol copolymer
description:
Vinyl acetate-vinyl alcohol copolymer (CAS 25213-24-5 ) is a partially hydrolyzed polyvinyl acetate that bridges the performance gap between fully hydrolyzed polyvinyl alcohol and standard polyvinyl acetate resins.

By controlling the degree of hydrolysis, manufacturers can tune water solubility, adhesion strength, and film flexibility to meet specific processing requirements across multiple industrial sectors.

In textile sizing, the copolymer coats warp yarns to reduce breakage during high-speed weaving, improving throughput and fabric quality. Paper and board manufacturers use it as a surface sizing agent.

It acts as a binder to enhance printability, surface strength, and ink holdout. In construction adhesives and tile-setting formulations, it contributes to bond strength and open time control on porous substrates.

Packaging and printing applications rely on it as a film-forming binder in water-based coatings and laminating adhesives. Controlled rheology and substrate wetting are critical to coating uniformity.

Vinyl acetate-vinyl alcohol copolymer is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granules, with solution grades available at defined solid content levels for various industrial processes.

Key specification parameters include degree of hydrolysis and viscosity grade, which together define suitability for a given application. Technical and industrial grades are standard for most uses.

description:
PPG 15 Stearyl Ether (CAS 25231-21-4 ) is a propoxylated fatty alcohol ether used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations as an emollient, solvent carrier, and lubricant.

It bridges the gap between oil-soluble and polar ingredients, giving formulators control over texture, spreadability, and ingredient delivery. In skin and hair care, it functions as a lightweight emollient.

It is used in serums, conditioners, and leave-on treatments to improve skin feel without the heaviness of conventional oils. Pharmaceutical topical formulations use it as a carrier to enhance active penetration.

This ensures uniform distribution across creams and ointments. In color cosmetics, it aids pigment dispersion and contributes to smooth, even application in foundations and lip products for better performance.

Industrial and metalworking lubricant formulators incorporate it for its film-forming and load-bearing properties. It is frequently utilized in cutting fluids and release agents for various manufacturing processes.

name: Dipropylene glycol

In personal care and cosmetics, DPG is a primary carrier for fragrance compounds and active ingredients. It improves spreadability and skin feel in lotions, creams, and deodorants while maintaining stability.

Polymer and resin manufacturers use it as a plasticizer and reactive intermediate in the production of polyurethane foams. It is also essential for the manufacturing of unsaturated polyester resins.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it acts as a slow-evaporating solvent that controls viscosity. This property improves substrate adhesion and ensures consistent application during the printing process.

Lubricant and metalworking formulators incorporate DPG as a base fluid and coupling agent. It is frequently used in cutting fluids and hydraulic formulations to enhance performance and stability.

description:
Glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (CAS 2530-83-8 ), also marketed as Silane A-187 and KBM-403 and abbreviated GPTMS, is an epoxy-functional silane coupling agent used to chemically bridge inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices.

name: 3-chloropropyltriethoxysilane
description:
3-Chloropropyltriethoxysilane (CAS 2530-87-2 ), also supplied as (3-chloropropyl)trimethoxysilane, is an organosilane coupling agent used to chemically bridge inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices.

The reactive chloropropyl group serves as a precursor for further functionalization, enabling manufacturers to tailor surface chemistry for specific bonding or crosslinking requirements.

Electronics manufacturers use it to treat substrate surfaces and encapsulant formulations where moisture resistance and dielectric stability are procurement priorities for high-performance components.

name: Methylhexahydrophthalic anhydride
description:
Methylhexahydrophthalic anhydride ( CAS 25550-51-0 ), commonly known as MHHPA, is a liquid cycloaliphatic anhydride used as a curing agent and reactive intermediate in epoxy resin systems.

Its low viscosity and long pot life make it a preferred hardener where processing conditions demand extended working time and consistent cure performance across various industrial applications.

In electronics manufacturing, MHHPA is the primary hardener for epoxy encapsulants, LED lens compounds, and semiconductor packaging resins, where optical clarity and thermal stability after cure are critical.

Coatings formulators use it to produce high-gloss, chemically resistant finishes for industrial and automotive substrates. In structural adhesives and composite systems, it crosslinks epoxy matrices effectively.

This material delivers mechanical strength and dimensional stability under thermal cycling. Electrical insulation components, including cast transformers and switchgear potting compounds, rely on these cured epoxies.

MHHPA-cured systems are valued for their dielectric performance and long-term reliability. The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically in drums and IBC totes for bulk procurement.

It is available in standard technical and electronic grades, with electronic-grade material meeting tighter purity and color specifications for optical and semiconductor applications.

Accelerator-blended formulations are also offered commercially for buyers requiring ready-to-use hardener systems. This ensures versatility for manufacturers across the chemical and electronics sectors.

description:
Agitan 260 (CAS 255719-70-1 ), also supplied under the designation AGITAN P 803, is a silicone-free defoamer and wetting agent used across water-based industrial formulations.

It controls foam build-up during production and application while improving substrate wetting, helping formulators maintain process efficiency and end-product quality.

In architectural and industrial coatings, Agitan 260 suppresses foam generated during high-speed dispersion and application, preventing surface defects such as craters and pinholes.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to eliminate entrapped air during mixing and coating operations where foam causes bond inconsistencies in the final product.

In industrial and institutional cleaning concentrates, it controls foam in spray and mechanical wash systems where excess lather reduces overall cleaning performance.

Textile processing operations use it to manage foam in padding, dyeing, and finishing baths where foam interference disrupts liquor circulation and fabric treatment uniformity.

Agitan 260 is supplied as a liquid, suitable for direct addition or dilution into water-based systems. It is available in standard industrial packaging including drums and IBCs.

name: Potassium polyacrylate
description:
Potassium polyacrylate (CAS 25608-12-2 ) is a water-soluble superabsorbent polymer used across agriculture, water treatment, and personal care manufacturing. It absorbs and retains large volumes of water relative to its own weight.

This makes it a functional material for moisture management and rheology control in both industrial and consumer formulations. In agriculture, it is incorporated into soil conditioning products and slow-release fertilizer carriers.

These applications help to reduce irrigation frequency by retaining moisture in the root zone. Water treatment operations use it as a flocculant and scale inhibitor in cooling water systems and industrial effluent processing.

Personal care formulators add it to gels, creams, and lotions where it functions as a thickener and humectant. This contributes to texture and moisture retention in the finished product for various consumer uses.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it supports suspension stability and controls viscosity in liquid detergent formulations. This ensures that active ingredients remain evenly distributed throughout the shelf life.

Potassium polyacrylate is supplied as a white powder or granule, with particle size and molecular weight varying by application grade. Agricultural and horticultural grades are the most common types available.

These specific grades are specified by absorbency capacity and gel strength to meet farming requirements. Technical and industrial grades are available for water treatment and cleaning applications with high performance.

Purity and viscosity specifications differ accordingly to ensure compatibility with industrial processes. Our material meets rigorous internal quality controls to ensure consistent performance across all manufacturing sectors.

name: Polyaspartic acid
description:
Polyaspartic acid (CAS 25608-40-6 ), also referred to as PAA, is a biodegradable polyamino acid polymer used across industrial and agricultural sectors. It functions primarily as a scale inhibitor and dispersant.

This versatile chelating agent prevents mineral deposits from forming on surfaces and equipment in contact with hard water or process fluids. In water treatment, it inhibits calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate scales.

It is frequently used in cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems, replacing conventional phosphonate-based chemistries where environmental compliance is required. This makes it a sustainable choice for modern facilities.

Agricultural formulators incorporate it into fertilizer blends to enhance nutrient uptake efficiency. It is particularly effective for micronutrients like zinc and iron in various soil applications to improve crop yields.

In personal care, it functions as a conditioning polymer and dispersant in rinse-off products where biodegradability is a requirement. Household cleaners use it to sequester hardness ions for better performance.

By improving surfactant performance in hard water conditions, it ensures cleaner surfaces. Polyaspartic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 40% or 50% active content.

It is commonly provided in sodium salt form, though dry powder grades are available for applications requiring solid formulations. Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for most buyers.

Documentation typically includes heavy metal limits and molecular weight specifications relevant to scale inhibition performance. These standards ensure the material meets the necessary requirements for industrial use.

name: Barium dinonylnaphthalenesulfonate
description:
Barium dinonylnaphthalenesulfonate (CAS 25619-56-1 ) is an oil-soluble barium salt used as a corrosion inhibitor, antioxidant, and detergent additive in petroleum-based formulations.

It belongs to the dinonylnaphthalenesulfonate family of overbased or neutral sulfonates that protect metal surfaces in aggressive service environments during industrial operations.

In lubricant and grease formulations, it neutralizes acidic by-products of oxidation, extending service life in high-temperature and high-load applications for machinery.

Metalworking fluids rely on it to prevent rust and corrosion on ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces during cutting, forming, and storage of various industrial parts.

Fuel system additives and engine oils incorporate it as a detergent-dispersant, keeping metal components clean under thermal stress and preventing the buildup of sludge.

It also functions as a rust-preventive component in preservation oils and protective coatings applied to steel parts during shipping and long-term storage across the globe.

Barium dinonylnaphthalenesulfonate is supplied as a viscous liquid or dissolved in hydrocarbon solvent at varying active-content concentrations for specific manufacturing needs.

Both neutral and overbased grades are available, with the overbased form carrying higher total base number for acid-neutralizing applications in Technical grade specifications.

name: Glyceryl dioleate
description:
Glyceryl dioleate (CAS 25637-84-7 ), also known as Diolein, is a diester of glycerol and oleic acid used across personal care, food, and industrial formulations. It functions primarily as an emulsifier, skin-conditioning agent, and lubricant.

This versatile compound bridges oil and water phases or reduces friction in mechanical systems. In personal care formulations, it stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions in creams, lotions, and serums.

The ingredient delivers a smooth, non-greasy skin feel to cosmetic products. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier in fat-based products, bakery fillings, and confectionery coatings where consistency is required.

It is particularly effective where controlled crystallization and texture consistency are required. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, its oleic acid backbone provides essential boundary lubrication.

This reduces wear on metal surfaces during cutting and forming operations. It also acts as a dispersing agent in pigment concentrates and oleophilic systems where uniform distribution of components is critical.

Glyceryl dioleate is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid at ambient temperature. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade ( FCC ) specifications, with purity levels defined by specific ratios.

The quality is typically defined by monoglyceride/diglyceride ratio and acid value. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial lubricant and metalworking applications to meet diverse industrial needs.

name: Hexabromocyclododecane
description:
Hexabromocyclododecane (CAS 25637-99-4 ), commercially known as HBCD, is an additive flame retardant used primarily in thermoplastic and foam-based materials. It functions by interrupting combustion cycles in polymer matrices.

This additive reduces flammability in finished products without requiring chemical bonding to the substrate. In building and construction, HBCD is incorporated into expanded and extruded polystyrene insulation boards.

These boards meet fire performance standards required in wall, roof, and floor assemblies. Textile and upholstery manufacturers apply it to back-coatings on fabrics where flame resistance is a regulatory requirement.

This is essential for commercial interiors and transportation seating. Electronics producers use it in housings and enclosures where UL 94 or equivalent fire ratings must be achieved in plastic components.

These components are typically injection-molded or extruded. Paper and board laminates used in construction packaging also utilize HBCD to comply with specific fire classification requirements for safety.

Hexabromocyclododecane is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granule, with the mixed isomers form being the standard commercial specification for industrial applications and chemical processing.

Technical-grade material is the predominant offering, typically characterized by bromine content and thermal stability parameters relevant to polymer processing and high-temperature manufacturing environments.

It is available in bulk bags and drummed packaging suited to industrial compounding and coating operations. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and distribution needs.

Povidone-iodine (CAS 25655-41-8 ), commonly abbreviated as PVP-I, is a stable iodine complex used as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active in pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing.

Unlike free iodine, it releases active iodine in a controlled manner, making it suitable for formulations requiring sustained efficacy with reduced irritation for various medical applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, PVP-I is the active ingredient in surgical scrubs, wound care solutions, and pre-operative skin antiseptics. Topical antiseptic creams and gels rely on it for infection control.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into antiseptic mouthwashes, throat sprays, and medicated skin cleansers where regulatory-grade antimicrobial performance is required for consumer safety and health.

In food processing environments, it is used in surface disinfection and equipment sanitization protocols where iodine-based biocides are specified to maintain high hygiene standards during production.

Povidone-iodine is supplied as a dark brown powder or as aqueous solutions at standardized iodine concentrations. Recognized grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for global compliance.

Iodine content and available iodine specifications are defined within each pharmacopoeia. Buyers should confirm the available iodine percentage and polymer molecular weight range for their specific needs.

Both factors affect formulation performance and regulatory compliance. Ensuring these standards are met is critical for the successful manufacturing of high-quality antimicrobial products in the industry.

name: Butyl acrylate-styrene copolymer
description:
Butyl acrylate-styrene copolymer (CAS 25767-47-9 ) is a synthetic resin produced by copolymerizing butyl acrylate with styrene to deliver a controlled balance of flexibility and hardness in polymer systems.

It functions primarily as a film-forming binder and rheology modifier across coatings, adhesives, and packaging applications. In architectural and industrial coatings, it serves as the primary binder.

It is used in water-based and solvent-borne formulations, controlling film hardness, gloss, and outdoor durability. Pressure-sensitive adhesives and laminating adhesives rely on this copolymer to tune tack.

It allows for the adjustment of peel strength without compromising cohesive integrity. In printing inks and overprint varnishes, it provides adhesion to difficult substrates including films and foils.

The resin supports fast drying in various printing applications. Sealant and elastomeric compound formulators use it to adjust elongation and cross-link density when combined with curing agents.

Butyl acrylate-styrene copolymer is supplied as aqueous emulsions and as solvent-borne resin solutions. The solids content typically ranges from 40% to 60% in standard emulsion form.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering for this material. Specific grades vary by molecular weight distribution, glass transition temperature, and monomer ratio.

These parameters are critical for buyers to confirm against formulation targets when sourcing. Proper selection ensures the desired performance in the final chemical application or product.

It is frequently utilized in crosslinking systems where dual reactivity is required for complex chemical structures. In textile and fiber processing, it functions as a reactive crosslinker for various cellulosic substrates.

This enables durable chemical bonding between fiber and finishing agents during manufacturing. Polymer chemists incorporate it into specialty resin formulations where the amine group participates in curing reactions.

The vinyl sulfone group drives chain extension or network formation in these systems. In leather treatment and paper chemistry, it supports the development of crosslinked coatings that improve wet strength.

The compound also serves as a monomer in synthesizing functional polymers with pendant sulfonyl-aniline units. These are highly relevant to ion-exchange materials and specialty membrane research applications.

It is used for synthesizing triazines, guanazoles, and other nitrogen-heterocyclic compounds used in active ingredient development. Polymer manufacturers use it as a stabilizer and antioxidant precursor.

In polyurethane and resin systems, it helps inhibit oxidative degradation during processing. In agrochemical formulations, it contributes to preservative and biocidal activity in various products.

In pharmaceutical intermediate manufacturing, it is used alongside carbodiimide reagents such as EDC or DCC to improve coupling efficiency. This process helps reduce epimerization in complex molecule assembly during API production.

Contract research and development organizations rely on HOBt for small-scale synthesis of peptide-based drug candidates. Stereochemical integrity is a critical quality parameter that this reagent helps maintain throughout the process.

This additive helps to reduce friction during extrusion and molding of PVC and other thermoplastics, improving surface finish and mold release. In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it acts as a slip and anti-friction additive.

This material accelerates suspended solids separation in clarification and sludge dewatering processes. Detergent and industrial cleaning formulations use it as an anti-redeposition agent and scale inhibitor.

It prevents mineral buildup on surfaces and equipment during wash cycles. Textile and paper manufacturers apply it to control viscosity in coating and sizing operations, improving process consistency.

In agriculture, it functions as a soil conditioner and water-retention aid in irrigation systems. This reduces runoff and improves moisture availability to crops across various soil types.

name: Dimethylamine-epichlorohydrin copolymer
description:
Dimethylamine-epichlorohydrin copolymer (CAS 25988-97-0 ), approved as E1063 , is a cationic polyelectrolyte used across water treatment and process industries to destabilize suspended particles and facilitate their removal.

Its positive charge density makes it effective as a primary coagulant or coagulant aid in clarification processes. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it coagulates colloidal solids, turbidity, and negatively charged contaminants.

This process significantly reduces downstream filtration load. Pulp and paper producers apply it for retention aid and drainage improvement during sheet formation, directly impacting production efficiency and fiber recovery.

Textile and dyehouse effluent treatment relies on it to precipitate reactive and disperse dyes from wastewater before discharge. In leather processing, it supports chrome and tannin removal from tannery effluents.

name: Cetyl myristate
description:

This chemical delivers a smooth texture and surface conditioning without leaving a heavy residue. In cosmetic formulations, it is used in skin creams, lotions, and lip products to improve spreadability and provide a non-greasy, silky skin feel.

Hair care manufacturers incorporate it into conditioners and styling products where it softens the hair shaft and aids in detangling. In lubricant and metalworking applications, it acts as a solid-film lubricant and friction modifier.

It is utilized in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. Its reactive phenolic hydroxyl group makes it a sought-after intermediate for constructing complex molecular architectures.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, this compound serves as a key intermediate for active pharmaceutical ingredient development. Its benzoxazine scaffold supports the construction of targeted small-molecule candidates.

The compound's hydroxyl functionality enables conjugation and derivatization steps critical to medicinal chemistry workflows. It is essential for researchers working on drug development pipelines.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a polymerization initiator, particularly in ring-opening systems where controlled initiation is required. This allows for precise chemical engineering.

Biotechnology researchers also employ it in the preparation of probe molecules and ligand scaffolds for receptor binding studies. This versatility makes it a valuable asset in various labs.

Both the amine and borate components contribute to metal protection and formulation stability. In metalworking fluids, it protects ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces from corrosion while maintaining the alkaline pH range.

This stability is required for cutting and grinding operations. Water treatment formulations use it to buffer system pH and inhibit corrosion in recirculating cooling and process water circuits.

In waterborne coatings and primers, it supports flash rust inhibition on metal substrates during application and drying. Adhesive and sealant systems benefit from its buffering capacity during the manufacturing process.

Controlled pH stability influences cure behavior and substrate compatibility. Monoethanolammonium borate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration varying by producer and application requirement.

description:
Bis(2-ethylhexyl) tetrabromophthalate (CAS 26040-51-7 ), also known commercially as TBPH or BEH-TEBP, is a brominated additive that delivers both flame retardancy and plasticizing performance within a single component.

It is essential where UL flame ratings must be maintained in flexible substrates. Automotive and aerospace interior components, including seating foams, gaskets, and panel linings, rely on it to meet fire performance specifications.

These applications require retaining mechanical flexibility under various conditions. Building and construction applications include flame-retardant sealants, adhesives, and flexible roofing membranes for long-term performance.

It functions as both a polymerization precursor and a plasticizing agent in polymer systems designed for sustainable material applications. In plastics and packaging, it serves as the structural monomer for PHB-based biopolymers.

This material enables the production of compostable films, rigid containers, and biodegradable packaging materials. Biotechnology manufacturers use it as a fermentation-derived intermediate for scaling microbial polyester production.

name: Syndiotactic polypropylene
description:
Syndiotactic polypropylene (CAS 26063-22-9 ), commonly abbreviated as sPP, is a stereoregular form of polypropylene distinguished by its alternating monomer orientation along the polymer chain.

Unlike isotactic grades, sPP delivers superior flexibility, optical clarity, and impact resistance, making it a preferred base resin where standard polypropylene falls short on performance.

In packaging films and flexible containers, sPP provides enhanced transparency and puncture resistance compared to conventional polypropylene grades for industrial and consumer use.

Automotive interior components, including soft-touch panels and under-hood parts, use sPP to meet flexibility and low-temperature impact requirements in demanding environments.

In building and construction, it functions as a rheology modifier and plasticizing component in bitumen blends and waterproofing membranes, improving low-temperature crack resistance.

Printing and labeling substrates benefit from sPP's surface characteristics, which support ink adhesion and film processability on high-speed converting lines for commercial labeling.

Syndiotactic polypropylene is supplied as pellets or granules, with melt flow index variants available to suit extrusion, injection molding, and film casting processes.

Technical and polymer-grade specifications are standard across the market. Buyers typically source sPP in bulk bags or octabins, with specific MFI and tacticity specifications confirmed.

It functions primarily as a scale inhibitor, dispersant, and corrosion inhibitor in aqueous systems where mineral deposit control is critical. In cooling water and boiler systems, PMA prevents calcium carbonate scale formation.

It also inhibits calcium sulfate and calcium phosphate scale, extending equipment service life and reducing maintenance downtime. Textile and paper processors use it as a dispersant and sequestrant to improve dye uptake.

This chemical prevents mineral interference during wet processing and ensures uniformity. In construction chemistry, it acts as a retarder and dispersant in cement and gypsum-based formulations, influencing set time and workability.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate PMA to sequester hardness ions and prevent redeposition of soils onto treated surfaces. This ensures high performance in various commercial cleaning applications.

In agriculture, it functions as a dispersant and suspending agent in liquid fertilizer concentrates and agrochemical suspension formulations for improved stability.

Its rheology-modifying behavior also supports use in specialty coating and pigment dispersion applications where controlled viscosity and high performance are required.

This material serves as a sustainable alternative to conventional petroleum-based plastics. In packaging, PLA is processed into films, trays, cups, and rigid containers where end-of-life compostability is a requirement.

Medical device and pharmaceutical manufacturers use PLA to produce resorbable sutures, drug delivery matrices, and implantable scaffolds. These components degrade predictably in biological environments during use.

In 3D printing, PLA filament is one of the most commercially dominant materials for FDM and FFF processes. This is due to its processing ease and high dimensional stability during the cooling phase.

In agrochemical formulations, it functions as an emulsifier and wetting agent in emulsifiable concentrate pesticides. This improves active ingredient dispersion in water for better agricultural performance.

Coatings and adhesive manufacturers use it to stabilize pigment dispersions and improve substrate wetting on low-energy surfaces. It ensures a more uniform application and better adhesion for industrial coatings.

In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it acts as an emulsifier in soluble cutting oils and corrosion-inhibiting fluids. This helps maintain the stability of the oil-in-water emulsions during heavy machining.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a wetting and penetration agent in dyebath and finishing operations. It assists in the even distribution of dyes and treatments throughout the material fibers.

The product is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste with active content commonly ranging around 70 percent. This concentration is reflected in the designation of several common trade-name products.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering with specifications aligned to agrochemical and industrial surfactant requirements. Drum and IBC packaging are the norm for bulk industrial supply chains.

name: Sodium methylnaphthalene sulfonate
description:
Sodium methylnaphthalene sulfonate (CAS 26264-58-4 ) is an anionic surfactant used across industrial processing and formulation as a dispersant and wetting agent. It improves the distribution of solids in liquid systems.

This reduces uneven coloration in batch and continuous dyeing operations. Cement and concrete admixture formulators use it as a dispersant to improve workability and reduce water demand in applications.

In industrial and institutional cleaning products, it boosts soil release and surface wetting on hard surfaces and process equipment. Leather and paper manufacturers incorporate it into processing baths.

Consistent dispersion of treatment agents directly affects product quality and yield. Sodium methylnaphthalene sulfonate is supplied as a powder or as an aqueous solution for various industrial uses.

Powder is the more common form for dry-blended formulations and admixture manufacturing. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for most industrial applications and processes.

name: Sorbitan monopalmitate

Formulators select it for its mid-range HLB value, which positions it between shorter and longer-chain sorbitan esters for targeted emulsion control. In food production, E495 functions as an emulsifier in bakery shortenings and margarine.

It is also used in confectionery coatings to improve texture consistency and shelf stability. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into topical creams and ointment bases where controlled water-oil balance is critical to product performance.

Personal care formulators use it to stabilize lotions and conditioning treatments, particularly where a waxy, skin-feel emulsifier is preferred over lighter alternatives. In textile and fiber processing, it acts as a lubricating agent.

It serves as a dispersing agent applied during fiber finishing operations. Sorbitan monopalmitate is supplied as a cream to tan-colored waxy solid, typically in flake or bead form for easy handling in industrial settings.

It is available in food-grade (E495-compliant) and pharmaceutical-grade specifications meeting USP and Ph. Eur. standards. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial textile and paper applications.

name: Hexamethyldisiloxane
description:
Hexamethyldisiloxane (CAS 26298-61-3 ), also known as Cosmetic Fluid 8108-OH, is a low-molecular-weight silicone fluid used across personal care, industrial, and polymer manufacturing sectors.

It functions as a foam suppressant, lubricant, and surface modifier, delivering consistent performance in both formulated products and process applications. In personal care formulations, it acts as a lightweight carrier.

It serves as a skin-feel modifier in serums, primers, and color cosmetics, leaving no greasy residue. Industrial cleaning and metalworking operations use it to control foam in cutting fluids and process baths.

Uncontrolled foam disrupts throughput in these environments. Polymer and resin manufacturers incorporate it as a processing aid and mold release component, improving surface finish and reducing cycle times.

In lubricant formulations, it provides a stable, low-viscosity base layer for precision applications where conventional mineral oils introduce contamination risk. This ensures high performance in sensitive systems.

Hexamethyldisiloxane is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet various purity requirements.

description:
Ethylenediamine ethoxylated propoxylated polymer (CAS 26316-40-5 ) is a block copolymer surfactant built on an ethylenediamine core extended with ethylene oxide and propylene oxide chains.

The balance of hydrophilic and hydrophobic segments can be tuned during synthesis, producing a range of products with distinct HLB values suited to different formulation requirements.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, dispersant, and rheology modifier across industrial cleaning, coatings, and water treatment applications. In industrial and institutional cleaning formulations, it delivers performance.

It provides low-foam or controlled-foam degreasing, particularly in spray wash and CIP systems where foam management is critical. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to stabilize pigment dispersions.

It also improves substrate wetting, reducing the need for additional co-solvents. In textile and leather processing, it aids in dye leveling and fiber lubrication during wet processing stages.

Water treatment programs incorporate it as a dispersant to inhibit scale deposition and keep particulates suspended for removal. This polymer is supplied as a liquid, typically ranging from low-viscosity fluids.

It can also be supplied as more viscous pastes depending on the EO/PO ratio and molecular weight. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most industrial applications.

Specific grades are differentiated by HLB value, molecular weight, and ethylene oxide content to match application requirements. This ensures optimal performance across various chemical formulations.

name: Benzisothiazolinone
description:
Benzisothiazolinone (CAS 2634-33-5 ), commonly abbreviated as BIT, is a broad-spectrum biocide used to prevent microbial degradation in industrial formulations and manufactured goods.

It targets bacteria, fungi, and yeast across a wide range of pH conditions, making it a practical preservation solution for both aqueous and semi-aqueous systems.

In paints, coatings, and adhesives, BIT functions as an in-can preservative, protecting formulations from spoilage during storage and extending shelf life for various industrial applications.

Metalworking fluids and lubricants incorporate BIT to control bacterial growth that would otherwise cause fluid breakdown and corrosion in machining operations and heavy equipment maintenance.

Leather, textile, and paper manufacturers use it to protect materials during processing and in finished goods where microbial attack poses a significant quality risk to the final product.

Water treatment programs and cooling systems also rely on BIT as a biostatic agent to limit biofilm formation in recirculating systems and industrial water circuits across many sectors.

BIT is supplied as a crystalline powder and in liquid solution form, with concentration levels varying by application requirement and the specific needs of the manufacturing process.

Standard technical-grade material is the most common commercial form, though formulated blends with complementary biocides are available for enhanced efficacy and documentation is standard for procurement.

description:
Ethylhexyl oleate (CAS 26399-02-0 ), also known by the trade name SABODERM EO, is an ester of oleic acid and 2-ethylhexanol used across personal care, lubricant, and polymer industries.

It is frequently found in lotions, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, where it delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel. Industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it into metalworking fluids and cutting oils.

It serves as a base fluid or co-lubricant, where its ester structure provides good boundary lubrication on metal surfaces. In plastics processing, it acts as a plasticizer and softener for PVC and other polymer systems.

This material improves flexibility without significant migration. It also functions as a solvent and carrier for active ingredients, pigments, and UV filters in both cosmetic and industrial coating formulations.

Ethylhexyl oleate is supplied as a clear, pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity standards suitable for personal care manufacturing.

Rubber compounders use it to improve processing and flexibility in seals, gaskets, and extruded profiles. In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it serves as a base fluid or functional additive for high thermal stability.

It is also evaluated in specialty lubricant blends for applications where conventional mineral oils present compatibility or volatility concerns. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance industrial chemical procurement.

Diisotridecyl adipate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically confirmed by ester content and acid value testing protocols.

name: Glyceryl caprate
description:
Glyceryl caprate (CAS 26402-22-2 ), also known as 1-decanoylglycerol, is a monoglyceride ester of capric acid used as an emulsifier and moisturizing agent across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

This ingredient helps to bind water and oil phases while improving skin feel. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in topical and semi-solid dosage forms where controlled emulsification is required.

It is also utilized where skin penetration support is necessary. In food-grade applications, it functions as an emulsifying agent in fat-based systems, contributing to texture and shelf stability in processed food products.

Its mild surfactant profile also makes it suitable for rinse-off personal care formats such as gentle cleansers and baby care products. Glyceryl caprate is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid.

The physical state depends on purity and processing. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications, with some suppliers offering material compliant with FCC or Ph. Eur. standards.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for formulators and R&D procurement. This versatile ester remains a staple for manufacturers seeking reliable emulsification properties.

name: Cresyl diphenyl phosphate

name: Toluene diisocyanate

description:
Hexane, 1,6-diisocyanato-, homopolymer, 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate-blocked , identified by CAS 264888-31-5 , is a multifunctional urethane acrylate oligomer. It is used as a reactive building block in UV/EB-curable systems.

This chemical delivers high crosslinking density, surface hardness, and scratch resistance in radiation-cured formulations. In UV-curable coatings for wood, plastic, and metal substrates, it contributes to high-gloss, abrasion-resistant topcoats.

Cure speed and film integrity are critical performance factors for this material. Printing and packaging applications rely on it for radiation-curable inks and overprint varnishes that require flexibility alongside surface durability.

In adhesive and sealant formulations, the aliphatic HDI backbone provides excellent weathering and yellowing resistance. This makes it highly suitable for outdoor applications and specialized optical bonding requirements.

Plastics processors use it in UV-curable hardcoats for polycarbonate and other transparent substrates. It is particularly effective where optical clarity must be maintained over the lifespan of the finished product.

The product is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically requiring moderate warming for handling and blending. It is available in a quality consistent with industrial radiation-cure raw material specifications.

name: Nonylphenyl phosphite
description:
Nonylphenyl phosphite (CAS 26523-78-4 ), commercially known as TNPP, is a phosphite ester antioxidant and stabilizer used across polymer processing, rubber manufacturing, and lubricant formulation.

It functions primarily as a secondary antioxidant, decomposing hydroperoxides formed during thermal processing to prevent degradation of the base material during high-temperature manufacturing cycles.

In plastics processing, TNPP is incorporated into polyolefins, PVC, and styrenic polymers to protect against color development and molecular weight loss during high-temperature extrusion or molding processes.

Rubber compounders use it in tire and industrial rubber goods to extend service life by inhibiting oxidative breakdown during both the initial processing stages and the final end-use applications.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it acts as an antioxidant and mild extreme-pressure additive, helping maintain fluid stability under significant thermal stress and mechanical pressure.

It also functions as a plasticizer in certain flexible PVC applications, contributing to processing efficiency alongside its stabilizing role to ensure the longevity and durability of the finished product.

Nonylphenyl phosphite is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature, facilitating direct metering into continuous mixing or compounding lines for efficient industrial scale production and handling.

Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and technical applications. Buyers should confirm phosphorus content, acid value, and color specifications when evaluating lots for sensitive polymer uses.

name: Octhilinone
description:
Octhilinone (CAS 26530-20-1 ), commonly abbreviated as OIT and also known as 2-Octyl-4-isothiazolin-3-one, is a broad-spectrum biocide used to prevent microbial degradation.

Its activity targets bacteria, fungi, and algae, making it a standard preservation choice across coatings, personal care, and industrial process fluids for long-term stability.

In architectural and industrial coatings, OIT is incorporated as a dry-film preservative to protect cured paint surfaces from fungal and algal growth over an extended service life.

Adhesives, sealants, and elastomers rely on OIT to prevent microbial attack during storage and in-service exposure to humid environments, ensuring product integrity and performance.

In textile, leather, and paper processing, it controls spoilage organisms in aqueous process baths and finished goods, preventing discoloration and structural degradation of the materials.

Metalworking fluids and lubricants use OIT to extend fluid service life by suppressing bacterial contamination that causes emulsion breakdown and unpleasant odors in industrial settings.

Octhilinone is supplied as a liquid concentrate, typically as a solution in carrier solvents or water at active concentrations of 45% or higher for easy formulation integration.

The Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial applications. Personal care applications may require material meeting specific purity thresholds for safety.

name: 4-Isononylphenol
description:
4-Isononylphenol (CAS 26543-97-5 ) is an alkylphenol intermediate used in the production of nonionic surfactants, particularly ethoxylated derivatives that drive emulsification and wetting performance.

It functions primarily as a building block rather than a finished surfactant, making it a procurement target for formulators producing cleaning agents, emulsifiers, and surface-active systems.

In home care and industrial cleaning, it serves as a precursor to ethoxylates used in heavy-duty degreasers and hard-surface cleaners where robust soil removal is required for industrial applications.

Textile and leather processors rely on ethoxylated derivatives produced from this compound for scouring, dyeing auxiliaries, and finishing baths to ensure high-quality material processing and consistency.

In coatings and adhesives, it contributes to emulsifier systems that stabilize resin dispersions and improve substrate wetting. Polymer manufacturers use it as a reactive intermediate or modifier.

This chemical is essential where controlled surface activity is needed in the production process. 4-Isononylphenol is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions for ease of handling and storage.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically ranging from 95% upward depending on the intended downstream synthesis and specific industrial requirements.

Bulk quantities are available in drums and IBC containers, with packaging suited to industrial-scale formulation and chemical synthesis operations across various global manufacturing sectors.

name: Disodium methylenebisnaphthalenesulfonate
description:
Disodium methylenebisnaphthalenesulfonate (CAS 26545-58-4 ), commercially known as sodium methylenebis(naphthalenesulfonate), is an anionic dispersant used across industrial formulations to stabilize suspensions.

It functions primarily as a dispersing and wetting agent where uniform distribution of solids is critical to end-product performance. In textile dyeing and finishing, it disperses dye particles evenly across fiber substrates.

This prevents agglomeration that causes uneven coloration. Concrete admixture manufacturers use it as a plasticizer component to improve workability and reduce water demand in cement slurries without compromising set strength.

Agricultural formulators incorporate it into suspension concentrates and wettable powder pesticide formulations. This ensures stable dispersion of active ingredients during dilution and application in the field.

In pulp and paper processing, it improves the distribution of sizing agents and pigments across fiber matrices. This supports consistent sheet formation and high coating quality during the manufacturing process.

The product is supplied as a brown to dark-brown powder or as an aqueous solution. Active content typically ranges from 85–95% for powder grades, meeting the requirements for Technical grade specifications.

Buyers should confirm active content, sodium sulfate levels, and compatibility with specific formulation pH ranges. Evaluating these parameters ensures the material meets the necessary standards for industrial applications.

name: Ethoxylated stearylamine
description:
Ethoxylated stearylamine (CAS 26635-92-7 ), also supplied under the designation RY 130T2, is a cationic surfactant derived from the ethoxylation of stearylamine. It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and rheology modifier across textile, agricultural, and cleaning applications.

In textile processing, it acts as a softening and antistatic agent, improving fabric handle and reducing static charge buildup during finishing. Agricultural formulations rely on it as an adjuvant in herbicide and pesticide concentrates.

This chemical improves droplet adhesion and active ingredient dispersion on leaf surfaces. Industrial and institutional cleaning products use it for degreasing and soil dispersion, particularly in formulations targeting hard surfaces and metal parts.

In personal care and cosmetics, it supports emulsion stability and conditioning performance in rinse-off products. Ethoxylated stearylamine is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation.

Grades vary by ethylene oxide content, commonly expressed as moles of EO per mole of amine, which directly determines HLB value and application suitability. It is available in technical grade for industrial use.

Standard packaging for bulk procurement includes drum and IBC options. The material meets rigorous industrial specifications to ensure consistent performance across diverse manufacturing sectors and chemical processing environments.

name: Ethoxylated oleylamine
description:
Ethoxylated oleylamine (CAS 26635-93-8 ) is a nonionic/cationic surfactant derived from oleylamine reacted with ethylene oxide. It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and surface modifier across industrial and agricultural formulations.

In agrochemical formulations, it improves the dispersibility and leaf adhesion of herbicide and pesticide concentrates. This directly affects field efficacy and product stability during long-term storage and application.

Water treatment programs use it as a corrosion inhibitor and dispersant for scale-forming particles in industrial cooling systems. It is also effective in process water systems where mineral buildup must be managed.

Textile and leather processing operations apply it as a softening agent and antistatic additive. This improves fabric handle and reduces static buildup during high-speed fiber processing and manufacturing stages.

In metalworking fluids and lubricant concentrates, it acts as an emulsifier that stabilizes oil-in-water systems. It maintains performance even under high-shear conditions common in industrial machining and metal fabrication.

Ethoxylated oleylamine is supplied as an amber to yellow viscous liquid for industrial use. It is available in technical grade, with the ethoxylation degree varying by supplier to meet specific formulation needs.

Common grades range from 2 to 15 moles EO, which determines the HLB value and application fit. Bulk supply is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for large-scale chemical manufacturing.
