name: Polyoxyethylene behenyl ether
description:
Polyoxyethylene behenyl ether (CAS 26636-40-8 ), commercially known as Beheneth, is a long-chain ethoxylated fatty alcohol derived from behenic acid. It functions as a nonionic surfactant and emulsifier across personal care, cleaning, and industrial formulations.

In cosmetic formulations, it stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions in creams, lotions, and conditioners while contributing a smooth skin feel that supports moisturizing performance. This ingredient is valued for its high stability and compatibility.

Hair care manufacturers use it as a conditioning agent and emulsion stabilizer in rinse-off and leave-in products. The C22 chain length delivers substantivity to the hair shaft, improving manageability and texture in professional hair treatments.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it acts as a wetting and dispersing agent. It improves soil removal in hard surface cleaners and detergent concentrates, ensuring effective performance in various aqueous environments.

Textile and leather processing operations use it to modify fiber surface tension during dyeing and finishing. This ensures even dye uptake and consistent coating adhesion, which are critical for high-quality industrial textile production.

Polyoxyethylene behenyl ether is supplied as a waxy solid, flakes, or paste depending on the degree of ethoxylation. Common commercial grades are designated by ethylene oxide chain length, such as Beheneth-5, Beheneth-10, and Beheneth-20.

Each grade targets different HLB requirements for specific formulation needs. Cosmetic-grade material conforming to standard industry purity specifications is the most commonly traded form for global manufacturing and distribution.

name: Disodium 4-(undecylenic monoethanolamide) sulfosuccinate
description:
Disodium 4-(undecylenic monoethanolamide) sulfosuccinate (CAS 26650-05-5 ) is an anionic surfactant derived from undecylenic acid, a naturally sourced fatty acid with recognized antifungal properties.

It functions as a mild cleansing, foaming, and emulsifying agent suited to both personal care and cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers, it delivers effective cleansing.

The foam profile is highly compatible with sensitive-skin positioning. Its undecylenic acid origin makes it a preferred choice in antifungal foot care products, dandruff treatments, and scalp formulations.

In these applications, the active component adds functional value beyond simple surfactancy. In home care and industrial cleaning products, it contributes to emulsification and soil dispersion in liquid systems.

It also serves as a co-surfactant in specialty formulations where formulators need to balance mildness with cleaning performance. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing.

The product is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active matter content commonly in the range of 30–35%. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades to meet various requirements.

name: Dipalmitin
description:
Dipalmitin (CAS 26657-95-4 ), also known as Glyceryl Dipalmitate, is a diglyceride ester of palmitic acid used as an emulsifier and moisturizing agent across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It provides controlled fat crystallization and interfacial stabilization in complex formulations where pure monoglycerides or triglycerides alone are insufficient for the desired chemical stability.

In food manufacturing, it functions as a structuring agent and emulsifier in shortenings, margarine, and baked goods, improving texture consistency and shelf stability for commercial distribution.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and lip products where it contributes emollient properties and helps stabilize oil-water interfaces without leaving a heavy or greasy residue.

In pharmaceutical solid dosage forms, it acts as a lipid excipient in controlled-release matrices and lipid-based drug delivery systems. It also appears in specialty confectionery coatings for fat bloom control.

Dipalmitin is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms for industrial chemical procurement.

Some suppliers offer material meeting FCC or Ph.Eur. purity standards. Packaging is available in kilogram-scale bags through to bulk quantities depending on the specific application volume.

name: Monopalmitin
description:
Monopalmitin (CAS 26657-96-5 ), also known as 1-Palmitoylglycerol, is a monoglyceride derived from palmitic acid used as an emulsifier and humectant across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It stabilizes oil-water interfaces and helps retain moisture in finished formulations. In food processing, it functions as an emulsifier in bakery products, margarines, and shortenings to improve texture.

This ingredient improves consistency and extends shelf stability in various food applications. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and lip products where it supports emulsion structure.

It contributes significantly to skin-feel and moisture retention in personal care items. In pharmaceutical solid dosage manufacturing, it acts as a lipid-based excipient in controlled-release formulations.

The compound is also utilized in lipid matrix systems and nutraceutical encapsulation. This helps to improve the delivery and bioavailability of fat-soluble active ingredients in specialized supplements.

The material is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, meeting FCC or USP standards where required.

Purity levels are commonly at 90% or higher for technical applications and ≥99% for reference use. Bulk supply is standard, with smaller quantities available for formulation development and quality testing.

name: Sorbitan tristearate
description:
Sorbitan tristearate (CAS 26658-19-5 ), also known commercially as E492 , is a lipophilic emulsifier derived from sorbitol and stearic acid. It functions primarily as a water-in-oil emulsifier, crystal modifier, and stabilizer across food, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

In food manufacturing, E492 controls fat crystal structure in chocolate and compound coatings, preventing bloom and improving texture stability during temperature cycling. Personal care formulators use it to stabilize water-in-oil creams and lotions.

Its low HLB value supports stable emulsion architecture in rich, occlusive formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it as an emulsifying and suspending agent in topical preparations and oral dosage forms.

In plastics processing, it acts as an antistatic agent and lubricant additive, improving surface properties and processing behavior in polyolefin systems. This versatility makes it a staple in various manufacturing sectors.

Sorbitan tristearate is supplied as a cream to tan-colored waxy solid, typically in flake or bead form. Food-grade material is available to E492 specification, while cosmetic and pharmaceutical grades are supplied to meet relevant standards.

These grades are manufactured to meet relevant compendial or industry standards. Technical-grade material is also available for polymer and industrial applications, ensuring performance across diverse technical requirements.

name: Acrylic acid-maleic anhydride copolymer
description:
Acrylic acid-maleic anhydride copolymer (CAS 26677-99-6 ) is a synthetic polymer used across water treatment, construction, and industrial process chemistry. It functions as a scale inhibitor, dispersant, and corrosion inhibitor in systems where mineral deposits must be controlled.

In water treatment, it prevents calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and other mineral scales from forming on heat exchanger surfaces and cooling tower equipment. This ensures optimal thermal efficiency and prevents costly downtime in industrial cooling systems.

Textile and paper processing operations use it to sequester hardness ions and improve process water quality. This reduces interference with dyes and sizing agents, leading to more consistent product quality and reduced chemical waste during manufacturing.

In construction chemistry, it modifies the rheology of cementitious formulations, controlling workability and retarding premature stiffening. This allows for better handling of concrete and mortar in various environmental conditions and complex builds.

Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations incorporate it as a corrosion inhibitor and dispersant. It keeps metal fines and contaminants suspended rather than depositing on equipment surfaces, extending the life of machinery and tools.

The copolymer is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations commonly ranging from 40% to 50%. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial and water treatment applications.

Packaging is generally available in drums and IBC totes suited to bulk industrial procurement. These formats ensure safe transport and easy integration into automated dosing systems used in large-scale chemical processing facilities.

2,4-Toluene diisocyanate dimer (CAS 26747-90-0 ) is a solid, low-vapor-pressure blocked isocyanate derived from TDI, designed to release reactive isocyanate groups upon thermal activation.

Unlike monomeric TDI, the dimerized form offers significantly reduced volatility, making it a preferred building block where handling safety and formulation stability are procurement priorities.

In powder coatings and one-component polyurethane systems, it functions as a latent crosslinker that activates during cure cycles, enabling stable pre-mixed formulations with extended shelf life.

Rubber and tire compounders incorporate it as a curative to improve adhesion between rubber substrates and reinforcing materials, particularly in belt and hose constructions.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to introduce controlled crosslink density in polyurethane systems without the handling complications associated with free TDI.

In thermoplastic polyurethane and elastomer production, it serves as a reactive monomer contributing to hard-segment formation and mechanical performance.

2,4-Toluene diisocyanate dimer is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically confirmed by NCO content titration.

In wire and cable insulation, DIDP delivers the thermal stability and low migration needed for long-service electrical applications. Automotive interior components rely on DIDP for heat resistance and reduced fogging.

name: Diaminotoluene
description:
Diaminotoluene (CAS 26764-44-3 ), also referred to as toluenediamine or TDA, is an aromatic diamine used as a reactive building block in polymer chemistry. It functions primarily as a curing agent and chain extender.

This chemical is essential in the production of polyurethanes, epoxy systems, and specialty resins. In polyurethane manufacturing, TDA serves as a chain extender in the synthesis of rigid and flexible foams and elastomers.

It is also utilized in cast systems where precise crosslink density is required. Epoxy formulators use it as a hardener in high-performance coatings, adhesives, and structural laminates where thermal resistance is demanded.

In rubber compounding and tire manufacturing, it contributes to vulcanization systems and antiozonant precursor chemistry. Adhesive and sealant producers incorporate it into two-component systems for industrial bonding.

These applications target environments with demanding mechanical performance requirements. Diaminotoluene is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid depending on isomer composition, with various grades available.

name: 1,2-dihydro-2,2,4-trimethyl quinoline, polymer
description:
1,2-Dihydro-2,2,4-trimethyl quinoline, polymer (CAS 26780-96-1 ), commonly known as TMQ, is a polymerized quinoline antioxidant used to protect rubber compounds from oxidative and thermal degradation.

It extends service life in both natural and synthetic rubber systems by inhibiting aging caused by heat, oxygen, and flex fatigue. This chemical is a primary antioxidant in tire manufacturing processes.

It protects carcass compounds, sidewalls, and tread formulations during both vulcanization and long-term service. In industrial rubber goods, it prevents hardening and cracking under elevated temperature conditions.

Common applications include belts, hoses, and seals. Automotive rubber components such as engine mounts and vibration dampeners rely on TMQ to maintain mechanical integrity across wide temperature ranges.

It is also incorporated into plastic and polymer blends where long-term thermal stability is a processing or end-product requirement. TMQ is supplied as a dark brown to amber flake or granule.

Flake is the most common commercial form for rubber compounding. Standard grades include technical-grade material meeting typical rubber industry specifications for antioxidant content and softening point.

Bulk and bagged packaging options are available to suit both large-scale compounders and specialty formulators. This ensures the material remains stable and easy to handle during the manufacturing process.

name: Amoxicillin
description:
Amoxicillin (CAS 26787-78-0 ) is a broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic supplied as an active pharmaceutical ingredient for human and veterinary drug manufacturing. It targets a wide range of gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial pathogens.

This material is one of the highest-volume antibiotic APIs in global procurement. Wymox is among the recognized brand formulations built on this API for various clinical applications and therapeutic uses.

In human pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the primary API in oral solid dosage forms such as capsules, tablets, and pediatric suspensions. These are produced at commercial scale worldwide for healthcare providers.

Veterinary drug manufacturers use it to produce injectable and oral formulations under brands such as Vetremox. These products target livestock and companion animal indications across the global agricultural sector.

It is also combined with beta-lactamase inhibitors such as clavulanic acid to produce co-formulated antibiotic products. These address resistant bacterial strains in both human and animal health markets.

Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers source it as a starting material for finished dose production. All manufacturing is conducted under strict GMP-controlled conditions to ensure high purity levels.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in both trihydrate and anhydrous forms. Standard specifications include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. to support regulatory submissions.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial API procurement with micronized grades offered for specific formulation requirements. This ensures compatibility with various manufacturing processes and delivery systems.

name: Methylisothiazolinone
description:
Methylisothiazolinone (CAS 2682-20-4 ), commonly abbreviated as MIT, is a broad-spectrum biocide used to control microbial growth in aqueous industrial and consumer formulations. It targets bacteria, fungi, and algae at low concentrations.

This makes it a cost-effective preservation solution across multiple sectors. In coatings, paints, and adhesives, MIT is used as an in-can preservative to prevent spoilage during storage and extend shelf life.

Water treatment facilities apply it to control biofouling in cooling towers, industrial water systems, and paper mill process water. In personal care, MIT appears in rinse-off products such as shampoos and liquid soaps.

In these applications, it prevents microbial contamination throughout the product's use cycle. Textile and leather processing operations use it to protect wet-processed materials and finished goods from degradation.

This protection is vital against bacterial and fungal degradation during production and transit. MIT is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 9.5% or 14% for various uses.

Higher-concentration formulations are available for industrial use. It is commonly offered in technical grade for industrial applications and in cosmetic-grade specifications meeting relevant regulatory standards.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on volume requirements. This versatile biocide remains a staple for manufacturers requiring reliable microbial control in diverse liquid environments.

name: 2-Thiazolidinone
description:
2-Thiazolidinone (CAS 2682-49-7 ) is a sulfur-nitrogen heterocyclic building block used in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. Oxothiazolidine is a recognized alternative name encountered in research and procurement contexts.

Its primary commercial role is as a reactive intermediate and polymerization initiator in the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and advanced materials. In pharmaceutical development, it serves as a key scaffold for synthesizing biologically active compounds.

This includes antimicrobial and enzyme-inhibitor candidates at the API intermediate stage. Medicinal chemistry programs use it to construct thiazolidinone-based drug candidates, where the ring system is incorporated directly into the final molecular structure.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a polymerization initiator, enabling controlled synthesis of specialty polymers used in biomedical and industrial applications. Biotechnology researchers also employ it as a synthetic precursor in the preparation of reagents.

2-Thiazolidinone is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram commercial lots, with purity grades typically ranging from 97% to 99%+ to meet fine chemical requirements.

name: Disodium lauryl sulfosuccinate
description:
Disodium lauryl sulfosuccinate (CAS 26838-05-1 ) is a mild anionic surfactant used across personal care and cleaning formulations. Derived from succinic acid and lauryl alcohol, it delivers effective cleansing and foaming.

It offers a lower irritation profile than conventional sulfate surfactants, which is a key consideration for formulators targeting sensitive-skin positioning. In personal care, it functions as the primary or co-surfactant.

It is commonly found in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers where mildness is a formulation requirement. Baby care and dermatologically tested products rely on it to maintain cleansing performance.

The surfactant helps products meet low-irritation benchmarks while ensuring high performance. In household and industrial cleaning, it contributes to foam stability and soil removal in liquid detergents.

It is also utilized in hard-surface cleaners for its effective properties. Textile and leather processing applications use it as a wetting and dispersing agent to improve substrate penetration during wet processing.

Disodium lauryl sulfosuccinate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous paste. The active content typically ranges from 30% to 40% in paste form for various industrial uses.

Cosmetic-grade material conforming to standard purity specifications is the predominant commercial offering. Technical-grade variants are available for industrial cleaning and textile applications as needed.

description:
Disodium cetyl sulfosuccinate (CAS 26838-10-8 ) is an anionic surfactant derived from a C16 fatty alcohol and sulfosuccinic acid. It functions as an emulsifier and cleansing agent in formulations where mildness and foam quality are priorities.

In personal care, it is used in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers to improve foam texture and support emulsification of conditioning actives. Home care and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it where low irritation potential is required.

Textile processing operations use it as a wetting and dispersing agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and substrate coverage. In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports emulsification during wet processing stages.

Consistent surface treatment is critical to end-product quality in these industrial sectors. Disodium cetyl sulfosuccinate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with active matter content commonly ranging around 30–35%.

name: Glycerol monolactate
description:
Glycerol monolactate (CAS 26855-41-4 ), also known as glyceryl lactate, is an ester formed from glycerol and lactic acid used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a humectant, mild acidulant, and carrier solvent in finished formulations.

In food production, it acts as a moisture-retaining agent and mild flavoring component in baked goods, dairy products, and processed foods where controlled acidity and texture stability are required. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin care preparations.

These preparations include creams, lotions, and serums where its humectant properties help bind moisture to the skin matrix and improve product spreadability. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a solvent and carrier for active ingredients.

It is utilized in topical and oral formulations, offering compatibility with both aqueous and lipid-based systems. Its dual alcohol-acid functionality also makes it useful as a co-solvent in flavor delivery systems and encapsulation applications.

Glycerol monolactate is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with material sourced to meet relevant purity standards for each application sector.

The material is manufactured to meet high quality standards such as FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , or ACS depending on the specific grade required. Packaging options generally range from drums to intermediate bulk containers.

name: Triglycerol monostearate
description:
Triglycerol monostearate (CAS 26855-43-6 ), also known as triglycerol stearate, is a polyglycerol ester derived from stearic acid used as an emulsifier and rheology modifier across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

DERMOFEEL PS is a recognized trade form supplying this ester to personal care formulators. Its ability to stabilize oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems makes it a practical choice for manufacturers managing emulsion consistency.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier in baked goods, margarine, and dairy-based products to improve texture and extend shelf stability. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and skin conditioning products.

These formulations benefit from both emulsification and moisturizing performance. Pharmaceutical topical preparations use it to control viscosity and ensure uniform active ingredient distribution across semi-solid dosage forms.

In personal care, it supports water-binding in leave-on skin formulations, reducing the need for heavier occlusive agents. Triglycerol monostearate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or flake for easy handling.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with technical-grade material also offered for industrial applications. Purity levels and ester content vary by supplier for specific needs.

N-Octyl Pyrrolidone (CAS 2687-94-7 ), commonly abbreviated as NOP, is a high-boiling, low-volatility pyrrolidone solvent used across pharmaceutical, coatings, and personal care manufacturing.

This enables more uniform film formation on difficult surfaces including plastics and metals. Personal care formulators use it as a solvent and penetration enhancer in topical products such as hair treatments.

In skin conditioners, it aids active ingredient delivery. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it supports drug solubilization and membrane permeation in transdermal and topical dosage forms.

Industrial cleaning and agrochemical formulations rely on NOP's emulsification and surface-modification properties. These characteristics improve active distribution and contact efficiency across various applications.

name: Neodecanoic acid
description:
Neodecanoic acid (CAS 26896-20-8 ), also sold under the trade names Wiltz 65 and Topper 5E, is a highly branched C10 synthetic carboxylic acid used across coatings, lubricants, and polymer systems.

Its branched structure drives performance in metal salt synthesis, surface treatment, and corrosion protection applications. In coatings, it is reacted with metal oxides to produce metal neodecanoates.

These driers and catalysts are used in alkyd and industrial coating formulations. Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers use it as a corrosion inhibitor and as a building block for synthetic ester base fluids.

These fluids provide strong oxidative stability in demanding environments. In plastics and polymer processing, it functions as a surface modifier and compatibilizer, improving adhesion between dissimilar substrates.

This is particularly useful in adhesive and sealant systems. It is also used to produce neodecanoate metal soaps applied as stabilizers and crosslinking agents in elastomer compounding for industrial use.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

name: Behenyl betaine
description:
Behenyl betaine (CAS 26920-62-7 ) is a zwitterionic surfactant derived from behenic acid, offering a longer carbon chain than conventional betaines such as cocamidopropyl betaine.

This extended chain profile makes it particularly effective in conditioning and foam-modifying applications across personal care and cleaning formulations. In hair care, it functions as a conditioning co-surfactant.

It improves wet combability and reduces static while contributing mild cleansing in shampoos and conditioners. Skin cleansing products incorporate it to moderate foam texture and reduce the harshness of anionic systems.

Facial washes and body bars benefit from its mildness. In home care formulations such as fabric softeners and rinse aids, it supports emulsification of actives and improves deposition on treated surfaces.

Industrial and institutional cleaning concentrates use it to stabilize foam profiles and boost degreasing performance across a range of pH conditions. It is a versatile component for high-performance cleaners.

Behenyl betaine is commercially supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at around 40% active content. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades suited to both personal care and industrial cleaning end uses.

name: Hexadecene
description:
Hexadecene (CAS 26952-14-7 ), also known commercially as cetene, is a long-chain alpha-olefin used as a reactive monomer and chemical intermediate across polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its 16-carbon chain length positions it in a specific performance window for applications requiring higher molecular weight contributions than shorter alpha-olefins can deliver to the final product.

In polyolefin production, hexadecene serves as a comonomer to modify the density, flexibility, and processing characteristics of polyethylene and related polymers during the manufacturing process.

Lubricant formulators use it as a building block for synthesizing poly-alpha-olefin (PAO) base oils, where the chain length directly influences viscosity index and thermal stability of the finished lubricant.

In oilfield chemistry, it contributes to the synthesis of viscosity modifiers and pour point depressants used in drilling and completion fluids for demanding industrial environments.

Specialty surfactant and detergent manufacturers also draw on it as a feedstock for producing long-chain alkyl derivatives, providing essential properties for various cleaning and industrial formulations.

Hexadecene is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, with drum and ISO tank packaging available for industrial procurement. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most uses.

Controlled branching in this chemical improves performance over linear-chain alternatives in various industrial applications. In plasticizers and polymer processing, it is reacted with phthalic or adipic acid anhydrides to produce ester plasticizers.

name: Isocyanuric acid
description:
Isocyanuric acid (CAS 27026-93-3 ) is a triazine-based compound used industrially as a chlorine stabilizer and biocide carrier in water treatment and sanitization systems. It functions by binding free chlorine in solution, slowing photodegradation and extending the effective life of disinfectant residuals.

Procurement teams also recognize it as a precursor platform for chlorinated isocyanurate derivatives used across cleaning and polymer applications. In swimming pool and recreational water treatment, it stabilizes chlorine against UV degradation, reducing chlorine consumption and reapplication frequency.

Trichloroisocyanuric acid (TCCA) and sodium dichloroisocyanurate (NaDCC) — both derived from isocyanuric acid — are the active disinfectants in tablet and granule sanitizer formulations for pools, potable water, and surface disinfection.

In industrial and institutional cleaning products, it serves as a buffering and stabilizing component in chlorine-releasing tablet systems. The plastics industry uses it as a crosslinking agent and UV stabilizer precursor in polymer processing.

This compound is particularly valuable in polyurethane and epoxy formulations. Isocyanuric acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and industrial grade, with purity levels typically at 98–99%+.

name: Poly(hexamethylenebicyanoguanide-hexamethylenediamine) hydrochloride
description:
Poly(hexamethylenebicyanoguanide-hexamethylenediamine) hydrochloride ( CAS 27083-27-8 ), commercially recognized as Polyhexamethylene biguanide hydrochloride — or PHMB — is a polymeric antimicrobial agent effective against a broad spectrum of bacteria, fungi, and algae.

It functions as a preservative and biocide across industrial, personal care, and healthcare applications. In water treatment, PHMB controls microbial growth in swimming pools, cooling towers, and industrial process water as an alternative to chlorine-based systems.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos, skin cleansers, and contact lens solutions. In wound care and surgical preparation, it is used in antiseptic irrigations and antimicrobial dressings.

These medical applications are particularly valued where residual activity is required. Textile and leather processors apply it to impart durable antimicrobial finishes to fabrics and treated surfaces, ensuring long-term protection against microbial degradation.

PHMB is most commonly supplied as an aqueous solution, with 20% concentration being the standard commercial form. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are available to meet the requirements of industrial versus personal care end uses.

Bulk supply is typically offered in drums or IBC containers suited to high-volume industrial procurement. Our material meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure consistency and efficacy across all specialized manufacturing sectors and global distribution channels.

name: Botryodiplodin
description:
Botryodiplodin (CAS 27098-03-9 ) is a sesquiterpene aldehyde produced by the fungus Botryodiplodia theobromae. It is primarily sourced as a pharmaceutical research intermediate and bioactive compound for agrochemical studies.

In pharmaceutical research, botryodiplodin is investigated for its antimicrobial and cytotoxic properties against various cell lines. Agrochemical researchers evaluate it as a potential lead compound for crop protection formulations.

These formulations specifically target various fungal pathogens in agricultural settings. Analytical laboratories use it as a reference standard for mycotoxin detection and quantification in food safety testing protocols.

Botryodiplodin is supplied as a high-purity solid, typically in milligram to gram quantities for research use. Research-grade and analytical reference standard specifications are available for procurement.

name: Phosphatidylcholine
description:
Phosphatidylcholine (CAS 27098-24-4 ), commonly sourced as a soy or sunflower lecithin fraction, is a phospholipid used across pharmaceutical, food, and biotech manufacturing as a natural emulsifier and membrane-forming agent.

Its ability to form stable bilayers and liposomal structures makes it a critical functional ingredient in drug delivery and specialty nutrition systems. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to construct liposomes and lipid nanoparticles.

These structures are essential for encapsulating active compounds, improving bioavailability and controlled release profiles. Food and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into emulsified systems including infant formula and functional beverages.

It is also used in dietary supplements where clean-label emulsification is a formulation requirement. Biotech and cell culture applications rely on it as a membrane lipid component in research reagents and in vitro assay systems.

Cosmetic formulators also use it to build lamellar emulsions and liposomal delivery vehicles for topical actives. The material is available as a liquid, gel, or powder depending on purity level and carrier format.

High-purity grades (90%+ PC content) are supplied for pharmaceutical and liposomal applications. Lower-concentration lecithin fractions serve food and industrial uses to provide cost-effective emulsification solutions.

Suppliers offer both soy-derived and sunflower-derived material, with non-GMO and organic certifications available. These options ensure the product meets specific market requirements and regulatory standards for global distribution.

name: Chromium formate
description:
Chromium formate (CAS 27115-36-2 ), also known as chromic formate, is an organochromium salt used across metal treatment, textile processing, and leather manufacturing.

It functions as a surface modifier, corrosion inhibitor, and catalyst precursor in industrial process chemistry. In leather tanning, it acts as a masking agent and auxiliary tanning salt.

This chemical improves chrome uptake and produces uniform, well-penetrated leathers. Textile dyeing operations use it as a mordant and fixative to enhance dye adhesion on wool and other protein fibers.

In metalworking and surface treatment, it is applied in passivation baths and corrosion-inhibiting coatings where controlled chromium deposition is required for industrial protection.

Mining and hydrometallurgical processes also employ it as a catalyst component or complexing agent in selective metal recovery circuits to ensure efficient chemical reactions.

Chromium formate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution or crystalline solid, with concentration and purity specifications varying by end-use sector and specific application.

Technical grade is the most common commercial form, with specifications aligned to industrial tanning and metalworking requirements for large-scale manufacturing and processing.

Buyers sourcing for specialty applications should confirm chromium content, pH range, and solution stability with the supplier prior to procurement to ensure compatibility with systems.

name: Polyacrylamidomethylpropane sulfonic acid
description:
Polyacrylamidomethylpropane sulfonic acid ( CAS 27119-07-9 ), commonly abbreviated as PAMPS, is a high-performance anionic polymer used across industrial and personal care markets.

It functions as a rheology modifier, dispersant, and scale inhibitor, delivering performance stability across a broad range of pH and temperature conditions that matter to formulators.

In water treatment, PAMPS inhibits scale formation and disperses mineral deposits in cooling towers, boilers, and industrial water circuits to maintain system efficiency and longevity.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into gels, lotions, and styling products where it provides thickening and suspension without compromising clarity or skin feel for consumers.

Textile and paper processing operations use it as a dispersant and retention aid, improving pigment distribution and reducing chemical waste in various wet-end manufacturing processes.

In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, it stabilizes surfactant systems and prevents redeposition of soils onto treated surfaces during the washing or rinsing cycles.

PAMPS is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations typically ranging from 15% to 50%, depending on the grade and the specific intended industrial application.

Technical and industrial grades are the most commonly available, with molecular weight variants available to match specific viscosity or performance targets across different end-use formulations.

name: Dipropylene glycol dibenzoate
description:
Dipropylene glycol dibenzoate (CAS 27138-31-4 ), commonly abbreviated as DPGDB, is a benzoate ester plasticizer and coalescing solvent used across polymer-based formulations and industrial coatings.

It functions as both a plasticizer and a rheology modifier, improving film formation, flow, and flexibility in finished products. In coatings and adhesives, DPGDB acts as a coalescing agent.

This chemical lowers the minimum film formation temperature, enabling uniform film development in waterborne systems. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to improve tack and flexibility.

It also enhances substrate adhesion in pressure-sensitive and construction-grade products. In PVC and other polymer compounding, it functions as a secondary plasticizer that enhances processing.

This additive reduces brittleness in finished parts. Printing ink manufacturers use it as a solvent-carrier to control viscosity and improve pigment wetting across solvent-borne and UV-curable ink systems.

Dipropylene glycol dibenzoate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in technical grade, the standard specification for industrial coatings, adhesives, and plastics applications.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC totes, with bulk quantities available for large-scale industrial procurement. This versatile ester ensures high performance in diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Triethanolamine oleate
description:
Triethanolamine oleate (CAS 2717-15-9 ), also known as TEA-Oleate or Triethanolammonium oleate, is an anionic surfactant formed from the salt of triethanolamine and oleic acid.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, lubricant, and cleaning agent across industrial and personal care manufacturing. In metalworking fluids, it stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions and provides lubrication.

This chemical is essential in cutting, grinding, and rolling operations, reducing tool wear and improving surface finish. Textile processors use it as a softening and lubricating agent during fiber treatment.

Consistent emulsion stability is critical to process performance during fabric finishing. In leather processing, it supports fat liquoring and degreasing steps, helping to distribute conditioning agents evenly.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions as an emulsifying agent. It is particularly useful in formulations where a mild anionic surfactant is preferred over more aggressive alternatives.

Triethanolamine oleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste, depending on concentration and temperature. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications including metalworking.

name: Dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid
description:
Dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid (CAS 27176-87-0 ), commonly known as DDBSA or laurylbenzenesulfonic acid, is a high-performance anionic surfactant and acid catalyst used across cleaning, agricultural, and industrial processing applications.

It functions primarily as a surfactant precursor, emulsifier, and pH-active ingredient in formulated products. In household and industrial cleaning formulations, it is neutralized on-site to produce linear alkylbenzene sulfonate.

This derivative serves as the active detergent component in liquid dish soaps, hard surface cleaners, and degreasers. Agricultural formulations use it as an emulsifier and dispersant in pesticide and herbicide concentrates.

These applications improve active ingredient delivery and tank-mix stability. Textile and leather processors apply it as a wetting and penetration agent during dyeing, tanning, and finishing operations.

In industrial contexts, it also acts as an acid catalyst in alkylation and esterification processes. The product is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically at 96–97% active content for industrial use.

Technical grade is the predominant market form, with hard and soft acid variants available depending on the linear or branched alkyl chain composition. Drum and IBC packaging are standard for most orders.

name: Diisodecyl adipate
description:
Diisodecyl adipate (CAS 27178-16-1 ), commonly abbreviated as DIDA, is a high-molecular-weight ester plasticizer and lubricant base fluid derived from adipic acid. It is used across plastics processing, rubber compounding, and industrial lubrication.

This chemical is essential where low-temperature flexibility and high-temperature stability are both required in the finished product. In PVC and flexible polymer formulations, DIDA functions as a primary or secondary plasticizer.

It improves cold-temperature performance in cable jacketing, automotive interior components, and sealing profiles. Rubber compounders use it to soften and process compounds destined for automotive seals, gaskets, and tire components.

Low-volatility is a critical processing requirement for these applications. As a synthetic base fluid or co-fluid in lubricant blends, DIDA delivers stable viscosity across a wide service temperature range for industrial use.

This makes it suitable for compressor oils, gear lubricants, and metalworking fluids. It also acts as a carrier or solvent in specialty coating and adhesive formulations where compatibility with polymer matrices is a priority.

Diisodecyl adipate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Bulk tanker options are available for high-volume buyers seeking efficient logistics for large manufacturing operations.

Standard commercial grades meet technical and industrial specifications for global trade. Plasticizer-grade material is the most commonly traded form in polymer and rubber markets for various industrial applications.

name: Potassium amyl xanthate
description:
Potassium amyl xanthate (CAS 2720-73-2 ), commonly abbreviated as PAX, is a xanthate collector salt used in the froth flotation of sulfide ores. It selectively binds to mineral surfaces, enabling the separation and concentration of target metals from gangue material.

PAX is primarily used as a collector in the flotation of copper, lead, zinc, and nickel sulfide ores. Its longer carbon chain provides stronger hydrophobicity than shorter-chain xanthates, improving recovery rates for finely disseminated minerals.

In gold and silver processing, it promotes flotation of sulfide-associated precious metals that are difficult to recover by conventional cyanidation alone. Its selectivity profile makes it suitable for complex polymetallic ores.

Differential flotation circuits require precise collector choice to ensure efficiency. Concentrators processing coarser feed or lower-grade sulfide deposits often specify PAX over shorter-chain alternatives to achieve target concentrate grades.

Potassium amyl xanthate is supplied as a yellow to pale-yellow powder or granules. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically ranging from 90% to 95% active content.

Bulk supply in bags or drums is standard for mining operations, with packaging options scaled to site consumption volumes. This ensures consistent performance across large-scale mineral processing and extraction facilities.

name: Calcium glycerophosphate
description:
Calcium glycerophosphate (CAS 27214-00-2 ), also known as beta-glycerophosphoric acid calcium salt, is an organic calcium and phosphorus salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It delivers both mineral nutrients in a single compound, making it a preferred source for calcium and phosphorus fortification where solubility and tolerability matter for the final product.

In oral care formulations, it is incorporated into toothpastes and mouth rinses as a remineralizing agent that helps restore enamel mineral content. This makes it a versatile ingredient for dental health.

Food and supplement manufacturers use it to fortify products such as infant formula, nutritional beverages, and dietary supplements where a bioavailable calcium-phosphorus source is required for health.

Pharmaceutical formulators select it as an excipient and active mineral source in tablet and liquid dosage forms. In cosmetic products, it functions as a stabilizer and pH buffer in skin-contact formulations.

Calcium glycerophosphate is supplied as a white powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with compliance to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. monographs.

These monographs are commonly referenced by buyers to ensure safety. FCC -grade material is also available for food and supplement applications requiring documented purity standards for production.

description:
Monomyristin (CAS 27214-38-6 ), also known as glyceryl myristate and commercially available as Grindtek MM 90, is a monoglyceride ester of myristic acid used as an emulsifier.

It acts as a rheology modifier across food and personal care manufacturing. It controls texture and stabilizes emulsions in finished formulations where precise consistency and phase compatibility are critical.

In personal care, it functions as a structuring agent and emulsifier in creams, lotions, and stick formulations. This helps to build viscosity and stabilize oil-water systems during the production process.

Food manufacturers use it to control fat crystallization and improve texture in bakery fats, margarine, and confectionery coatings. It also acts as a co-emulsifier in complex lipid systems for rheological behavior.

Formulators select it for applications requiring a C14 fatty acid profile, which influences crystal habit and melting characteristics. These traits are highly relevant to specific industrial processing temperatures.

Monomyristin is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the standard commercial forms for high-volume industrial procurement.

Purity grades are commonly at 90% monoglyceride content or above, as reflected in the Grindtek MM 90 designation. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric ton quantities depending on scale.

These formulations benefit as it simultaneously stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions and contributes moisture retention to the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a functional excipient in topical formulations for various applications.

name: Polyethylene glycol tetradecyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol tetradecyl ether (CAS 27306-79-2 ), commercially recognized as Myreth, is a nonionic surfactant produced by ethoxylating tetradecyl alcohol. It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and detergent across personal care, cleaning, and industrial processing applications.

In cosmetic formulations, Myreth grades are used to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions in lotions, creams, and conditioning products. The ethoxylation degree is carefully selected to match the required HLB value for specific stability needs.

Household and industrial cleaners rely on this chemical to reduce surface tension and improve soil removal from hard surfaces and fabrics. It is highly effective in removing grease and organic residues in various cleaning environments.

Textile processors apply it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and fiber preparation. This ensures that the final textile products maintain consistent color and quality throughout the manufacturing cycle.

In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports surface modification and dispersing functions during wet processing stages. These applications benefit from the surfactant's ability to manage interface interactions between different materials.

Polyethylene glycol tetradecyl ether is supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation. Lower EO variants tend toward waxy solids while higher EO grades remain fluid at ambient temperature.

Common commercial grades are differentiated by the number of ethylene oxide units, typically ranging from Myreth-3 to Myreth-10. The EO count is always specified in the technical product documentation for precise formulation.

Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available to meet personal care and industrial sourcing requirements. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking reliable surfactant performance.

name: Laureth-7 carboxylic acid
description:
Laureth-7 carboxylic acid (CAS 27306-90-7 ), also marketed as Rlm 45, is an ethoxylated fatty acid surfactant used in personal care and cosmetic formulations.

It combines mild cleansing action with emulsification and pH-buffering capability in a single ingredient, reducing the need for multiple additives in complex chemical systems.

In facial and body cleansers, it delivers effective soil removal while maintaining compatibility with sensitive skin formulations, a key consideration for mild or low-irritation product lines.

It functions as an emulsifier in cream and lotion systems, stabilizing oil-in-water emulsions across a range of pH conditions for consistent shelf-life and texture.

Formulators also use it in shampoos and conditioning products where it contributes to foam quality and helps buffer the system toward a specific target pH level.

Its cleaning and degreasing performance makes it relevant in rinse-off formats where residue-free results are required for high-performance consumer applications.

Laureth-7 carboxylic acid is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste, depending on temperature and concentration, and is available in cosmetic-grade quality.

Buyers should confirm active content and pH range with the supplier, as these parameters vary between commercial grades and specific manufacturing batches.

name: Choleth-10
description:
Choleth-10 (CAS 27321-96-6 ) is an ethoxylated cholesterol derivative used as an emulsifier and humectant in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations. Recognized in trade under the designation Cl-4494, it bridges the gap between lipid-phase components and aqueous systems.

This chemical enables stable emulsion formation in skin-contact products. In topical cosmetic formulations, including creams, lotions, and serums, it stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions while supporting moisture retention at the skin surface.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it to solubilize and disperse active ingredients in semi-solid preparations such as ointments and dermal delivery systems. It is highly effective in maintaining the consistency of complex medicinal mixtures.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it functions as a membrane-compatible surfactant in liposomal and lipid-based delivery systems. Its cholesterol backbone supports bilayer integration, making it essential for advanced research applications.

Hair care products, particularly conditioning treatments, incorporate it to improve ingredient dispersion and deposit uniformity on the hair shaft. This ensures that active conditioning agents are distributed evenly across the surface.

The material is supplied as a waxy solid or viscous paste depending on temperature and processing conditions. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet various formulator requirements.

These grades ensure compliance across regulated and non-regulated markets globally. Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial drums for commercial-scale production and manufacturing needs.

name: Fluorescent Brightener 230
description:
Fluorescent Brightener 230 (CAS 27344-06-5 ), also referred to commercially as Fluorescent Brightener, is a stilbene-based optical brightening agent that absorbs ultraviolet light and re-emits it as visible blue-white fluorescence.

Applied to substrates that appear yellowed or dull, it corrects perceived color without bleaching, delivering a measurable whiteness improvement across textile, paper, and leather processing industries worldwide.

In textile finishing, it is applied to cotton, linen, and blended fabrics during dyeing or padding operations to achieve high whiteness indices required by apparel and home textile buyers.

Paper and pulp manufacturers incorporate it into surface sizing or coating formulations to meet brightness specifications for printing and writing grades. This ensures a high-quality finish for commercial paper products.

Leather processors use it in finishing baths to enhance the visual brightness of white and light-colored hides destined for footwear and upholstery markets. It provides a clean, professional aesthetic to the final leather goods.

It also performs in detergent formulations where fabric whitening during laundering is a required end-product claim. This versatility makes it a staple component in many industrial and consumer cleaning products.

Fluorescent Brightener 230 is supplied as a liquid solution or powder, with liquid concentrations being the most common commercial form for ease of dosing in continuous processing lines.

Standard supply grades are aligned with textile and industrial specifications, with purity levels and active content documented for quality assurance. Packaging is typically available in drums or IBCs for bulk procurement.

Contact us for supply of Fluorescent Brightener 230

name: Disodium distyrylbiphenyl disulfonate
description:
Disodium distyrylbiphenyl disulfonate (CAS 27344-41-8 ), commercially known as Brightener BR 49 , is a stilbene-based optical brightening agent used to enhance the perceived whiteness and brightness of substrates.

By absorbing UV light and re-emitting it as visible blue fluorescence, it counteracts yellowing in treated materials without adding pigment. This mechanism is essential for maintaining high visual standards in industrial applications.

In pulp and paper manufacturing, it is applied during wet-end processing or surface sizing to boost sheet brightness and meet commercial print quality standards. This ensures a professional finish for high-end paper products.

Textile finishing operations use it in padding baths to achieve durable optical brightening on cotton and blended fabrics. It provides a consistent, brilliant white appearance that remains stable throughout the manufacturing process.

In packaging production, it improves the visual appeal of white paperboard and coated substrates where brand presentation is critical. This makes it a vital component for consumer-facing goods and luxury packaging solutions.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into detergent and fabric care products to deliver a brightening effect on laundered textiles. It helps maintain the original brightness of clothing over multiple wash cycles.

Disodium distyrylbiphenyl disulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations ranging from 15% to 40% active content. Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for these sectors.

Specifications are aligned to paper, textile, and detergent end-use requirements. Packaging options commonly include drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes and logistics.

name: Catecholborane
description:
Catecholborane (CAS 274-07-7 ) is a cyclic organoboron reagent used as a selective hydroboration agent in synthetic chemistry. It delivers controlled boron addition to unsaturated substrates, enabling the preparation of boronate esters.

These boronate esters are essential chiral intermediates that downstream processes require for complex molecular construction. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is used to produce enantiomerically enriched boronic acid derivatives.

These derivatives serve as building blocks for active pharmaceutical ingredients, including protease inhibitors and antifungal compounds. Asymmetric hydroboration with chiral rhodium or iridium catalysts relies on this boron source.

This process allows for the generation of stereocenters with high selectivity during drug development. In agrochemical development, it supports the synthesis of boron-containing crop protection compounds at the research stage.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor and initiator in certain boron-mediated polymerization processes within specialty materials research. The reagent is supplied as a liquid, typically handled under an inert atmosphere.

Due to its moisture sensitivity, it is available in research quantities and in larger volumes for process chemistry and scale-up applications. Standard offerings include technical and high-purity grades for various uses.

Purity specifications are commonly confirmed by NMR or GC analysis to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements. This ensures the material meets the rigorous standards necessary for sensitive chemical transformations and manufacturing.

name: Isotridecanol
description:
Isotridecanol (CAS 27458-92-0 ), also known as isotridecyl alcohol, is a branched-chain fatty alcohol used as a functional base in surfactant synthesis, plasticizer production, and specialty formulation work.

It acts as a building block for ethoxylated nonionic surfactants and as a carrier or co-solvent in industrial formulations where controlled solvency and low volatility are required for the process.

In personal care and cosmetics, it serves as an emollient carrier and solvent base in formulating skin creams, hair products, and color cosmetics. Textile and leather processors use it as a lubricant.

It is a softening agent in fiber finishing baths and leather fatliquoring compounds. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it functions as a plasticizer intermediate and processing aid that improves flexibility.

Metalworking and lubricant formulators incorporate it into cutting fluids and rolling oils where its lubricity and compatibility with mineral oil systems reduce friction and tool wear during manufacturing.

Isotridecanol is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial applications.

Purity specifications commonly range from 99% and above to ensure consistent performance. Bulk tank delivery is available from major producers for high-volume procurement and large scale operations.

name: Isostearyl alcohol
description:
Isostearyl alcohol (CAS 27458-93-1 ) is a branched-chain fatty alcohol derived from isostearic acid, valued across personal care and industrial markets for its emollient, lubricating, and solubilizing performance.

Its branched structure prevents the waxy solidification typical of linear C18 alcohols, keeping it liquid at room temperature and easy to process. This characteristic drives its selection in formulations where spreadability is a priority.

In personal care, it functions as an emollient and carrier in lip products, foundations, and skin creams. It delivers a non-greasy, smooth application without the drag of solid waxes often found in traditional formulations.

Sunscreen and color cosmetic formulators use it to dissolve UV filters and pigment dispersants that require a liquid fatty alcohol base. This ensures a consistent texture and effective distribution of active ingredients.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as a base fluid or co-solvent where low pour point and oxidative stability matter. It provides reliable performance in demanding industrial environments.

Automotive and industrial grease manufacturers also incorporate it as a plasticizer and viscosity modifier in specialty lubricant blends. This versatility makes it a staple for high-performance mechanical applications.

Isostearyl alcohol is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Standard commercial grades include cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material, with cosmetic supply typically meeting purity specifications for the industry.

It is available in drums and IBC quantities for both personal care and industrial procurement. Our logistics team ensures that all shipments meet the necessary handling and storage requirements for bulk chemical supply.

name: Isononyl alcohol
description:
Isononyl alcohol (CAS 27458-94-2 ), also known as Isononanol, is a branched-chain fatty alcohol used as a chemical intermediate and functional solvent across multiple industrial sectors.

Its primary commercial role is as a precursor in plasticizer synthesis and as a processing solvent where controlled solvency and low volatility are required for manufacturing.

The largest volume use is in the production of diisononyl phthalate (DINP) and other phthalate-free plasticizers, which are compounded into flexible PVC for cables and flooring.

In coatings and printing inks, it functions as a slow-evaporating solvent that aids film formation and reduces viscosity without compromising adhesion or final product quality.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it as a reactive diluent or processing aid to improve workability and substrate wetting during the application process.

Personal care manufacturers use it as an emollient carrier in skin-conditioning formulations where a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel is required for the end consumer.

Isononyl alcohol is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity typically at 99% or above.

Food-contact and cosmetic-grade material is available from select producers where downstream application compliance requires tighter quality documentation and safety standards.

name: Quaternium 14
description:
Quaternium 14 (CAS 27479-28-3 ), also known commercially as Dodecyl(ethylbenzyl)dimethylammonium chloride, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a cationic surfactant in personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

It functions primarily as a conditioning agent, emulsifier, and surface modifier, delivering substantivity to hair and skin substrates while improving wetting and dispersion performance across various applications.

In hair care, it deposits onto negatively charged hair fibers to reduce static, improve combability, and enhance the sensory feel of conditioners and rinse-off treatments. Fabric softeners use it to modify surface charge.

These rinse-aid formulations improve softness and reduce static cling on textile fibers. In industrial and institutional cleaning products, it supports emulsification of oils and soils, aiding soil release from hard surfaces.

Personal care formulators also incorporate it into leave-on skin conditioning products where controlled deposition and wetting behavior are required. It is typically supplied as an aqueous solution with varying active content.

Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available to meet the requirements of personal care and industrial cleaning applications respectively. Buyers should confirm active content percentage and counterion purity.

When evaluating batches for formulation use, ensure the material meets necessary industry specifications. This versatile surfactant remains a staple for manufacturers seeking reliable conditioning and emulsification properties.

name: Phenylbenzimidazole sulfonic acid
description:
Phenylbenzimidazole sulfonic acid ( CAS 27503-81-7 ), commonly abbreviated as PBSA, is a water-soluble UV filter used primarily in sun care and personal care formulations. Unlike oil-soluble UV absorbers, its water solubility makes it suitable for aqueous and hydrophilic systems.

This chemical is ideal for applications where broad-spectrum UVB protection is required. PBSA is a regulated UVB-filtering active in sunscreens, functioning across lotions, sprays, and gel formulations where water-phase UV protection is needed.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it provides photostabilization to light-sensitive active ingredients, extending product shelf life and efficacy. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into daily moisturizers and after-sun products.

These formulations deliver UVB protection without compromising texture or transparency. It also appears in combination UV filter systems alongside UVA absorbers, where its water solubility complements oil-phase actives to achieve full-spectrum coverage.

PBSA is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher to meet regulatory requirements in sun care markets.

Suppliers commonly offer it in compliance with EU Cosmetics Regulation and equivalent international standards governing UV filter actives. The material is often tested against USP and Ph.Eur. standards to ensure safety and performance.

name: Trimethylsilyl triflate
description:
Trimethylsilyl triflate ( CAS 27607-77-8 ), commonly abbreviated as TMSOTf, is a highly reactive silylating agent used across synthetic chemistry and specialty chemical manufacturing. It transfers trimethylsilyl groups to nucleophilic substrates under mild conditions.

This reagent enables selective protection and activation steps that less reactive silylating agents cannot achieve efficiently. In pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, it is used to install TMS-protecting groups on alcohols and amines.

It is also utilized for carbonyl compounds during multi-step API manufacturing. It activates glycosyl donors in carbohydrate chemistry, making it a standard reagent in oligosaccharide and glycoconjugate synthesis processes.

In polymer and materials chemistry, it initiates cationic polymerization and surface silylation processes where controlled reactivity is critical. This ensures product consistency across various industrial applications.

Personal care ingredient manufacturers use it in the synthesis of silicone-modified actives and surface-treated powders. This is particularly useful where conventional silylation routes are too slow or lack the necessary selectivity.

TMSOTf is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically in moisture-sealed packaging to preserve reactivity. Standard commercial concentrations are neat with a purity of at least 98 percent for industrial use.

Anhydrous solvent solutions are also available, suited for direct use in synthesis. Technical and high-purity reagent grades are offered, with the latter meeting specifications required for pharmaceutical intermediate production.

name: Glyceryl dilaurate
description:
Glyceryl dilaurate (CAS 27638-00-2 ), also known as Dilauroyl-rac-glycerol, is a glycerol diester of lauric acid used as an emulsifier and carrier in pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic formulations.

It enables stable oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems where controlled lipid composition is required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a lipid excipient in self-emulsifying drug delivery systems.

This material improves the oral bioavailability of poorly soluble active ingredients. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and skin conditioning products where a medium-chain lipid emulsifier is needed.

It stabilizes the emulsion matrix effectively across various personal care applications. In food applications, it acts as an emulsifying agent in fat-based systems, contributing to texture and phase stability.

The compound is also used as a carrier in lipid-based encapsulation systems for nutraceutical and functional ingredient delivery. It is typically supplied as a solid waxy material or flakes for industrial use.

It is available in technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of different regulated industries. Buyers should confirm compliance with relevant pharmacopeial or food additive standards.

Quality standards such as USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , or FCC may apply depending on the specific grade and intended application. This ensures the material meets the necessary safety and performance criteria.

name: Ponceau 6R
description:
Ponceau 6R (CAS 2766-77-0 ), also known as Acid Red 44 and formerly designated E126 , is a synthetic azo dye used to impart red coloration across textile, food, and industrial applications.

Its strong dyeing affinity and vivid red hue make it a recognized colorant in both regulated and industrial supply chains. In textile processing, it is applied to wool, silk, and nylon fabrics using acid dyeing methods.

These methods achieve bright, durable red shades across various fiber types. Leather manufacturers use it in finishing baths where consistent color uptake on protein-based substrates is required for high-quality results.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a colorant in inks where red tones must meet specific hue and fastness targets. Historically supplied under the E126 designation, it has also appeared in food colorant formulations.

Regulatory status for food use varies significantly by market and should be confirmed before procurement. Ponceau 6R is typically available as a red to dark red powder or granule for industrial handling.

It is supplied in technical and dye-grade specifications, with purity levels commonly expressed as dye content percentage. Packaging is generally offered in fiber drums or multi-wall bags suited to bulk procurement.

name: Vinyltrimethoxysilane
description:
Vinyltrimethoxysilane (CAS 2768-02-7 ), commonly abbreviated as VTMS, is a bifunctional organosilane monomer used to chemically bridge inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices.

It provides covalent bonding between mineral fillers, glass fibers, or metal surfaces and surrounding resin systems, improving composite performance and adhesion durability across various industries.

In polyolefin cable and pipe manufacturing, VTMS enables moisture-cure crosslinking of polyethylene, producing XLPE compounds with improved thermal and mechanical resistance for demanding environments.

It functions as a coupling agent in glass fiber-reinforced composites, bonding the silica surface to epoxy, polyester, or polyurethane resins to increase tensile strength and reduce delamination.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use VTMS as an adhesion promoter on glass, aluminum, and mineral substrates, particularly in automotive glazing sealants and structural bonding applications.

In electronics, it supports surface treatment of silica fillers used in encapsulants and underfill compounds, improving filler dispersion and moisture resistance in cured systems.

Vinyltrimethoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers requiring consistent supply chains.

Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels, typically specified at ≥97% or ≥98% purity. Specialty grades are available for high-performance polymer applications.

name: Vanadyl sulfate
description:
Vanadyl sulfate (CAS 27774-13-6 ), also sold as VOSO4, is an inorganic vanadium(IV) salt used as a catalyst precursor and active vanadium source across industrial and specialty chemical applications.

It delivers a stable, water-soluble form of vanadium that can be incorporated into catalyst systems, electrochemical processes, and specialty formulations without the handling complexity of other vanadium compounds.

In catalyst manufacturing, vanadyl sulfate serves as a precursor for preparing supported vanadium oxide catalysts used in oxidation and sulfuric acid production processes.

Vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB) electrolyte preparation represents a growing procurement segment, where VOSO4 is used to produce or condition the vanadium electrolyte solution.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, it appears in vanadium recovery and refining workflows as a process intermediate. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers also source this compound.

It is used as the active ingredient in vanadium-based dietary supplement formulations targeting metabolic support research. Vanadyl sulfate is available as a blue crystalline powder or as a hydrated solid.

It is most commonly found in the pentahydrate form (VOSO4·5H2O). Technical and reagent grades are standard across the market, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical and battery electrolyte applications.

Bulk quantities are supplied in fiber drums or bags, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and specialty use. This ensures flexibility for both large-scale industrial use and research development.

name: Isononylamine
description:
Isononylamine (CAS 27775-00-4 ) is a branched-chain aliphatic primary amine used as a reactive building block and functional additive across industrial chemical manufacturing.

Its primary amine group enables covalent bonding in curing systems, corrosion-inhibiting formulations, and surface-active chemistries for various industrial applications.

In epoxy coating and adhesive systems, it acts as a curing agent or co-curing component, contributing to crosslink density and adhesion to metal substrates.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as a corrosion inhibitor precursor, where it reacts with fatty acids to form protective amine salts.

In polymer and elastomer production, it serves as a reactive modifier for adjusting surface wettability or as an intermediate in synthesizing coupling agents.

Coatings manufacturers also use it to prepare imidazoline or amide derivatives that function as film-forming corrosion inhibitors in industrial maintenance products.

This chemical is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels suited for industrial synthesis and formulation work, meeting Technical grade standards.

Purity specifications are commonly in the 98–99% range, and it is available in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk supply options for high-volume industrial users.

name: Stearyl stearate
description:
Stearyl stearate (CAS 2778-96-3 ), also known as octadecyl stearate, is a waxy ester derived from stearic acid and stearyl alcohol used across personal care, industrial lubricant, and polymer processing applications.

It functions as a lubricant, plasticizer, and consistency agent, providing controlled slip, texture modification, and processing efficiency depending on the specific formulation requirements of the end user.

In personal care, it is incorporated into lipsticks, creams, and solid emulsions to build structure, improve spreadability, and modify skin feel without adding any unwanted greasiness to the final product.

Polymer and rubber compounders use it as an internal or external lubricant to reduce melt viscosity and prevent die buildup during extrusion and calendering processes for various industrial materials.

In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it functions as a solid lubricant component in greases and release agents where high-temperature stability and low migration are considered top priorities.

Textile and leather finishing operations apply it as a softening agent to improve hand feel and surface slip on treated substrates, ensuring a high-quality finish for consumer and industrial goods.

Stearyl stearate is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form suited for melt blending and direct weighing in large scale manufacturing environments.

Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly available, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care formulations. Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers.

name: Hydroxypropyl methacrylate
description:
Hydroxypropyl methacrylate (CAS 27813-02-1 ), commonly abbreviated as HPMA and also marketed as Rocryl 410, is a reactive monomer used to build functional acrylic polymer systems.

It introduces hydroxyl groups into polymer backbones, enabling controlled crosslinking, adhesion tuning, and surface reactivity across a broad range of industrial formulations.

In automotive and industrial coatings, HPMA reacts with isocyanates or melamine resins to produce two-component polyurethane and acrylic topcoats with defined cure profiles and film hardness.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to improve substrate bonding and cohesive strength in structural and pressure-sensitive systems for various industrial applications.

In UV-curable printing inks and packaging coatings, it functions as a reactive diluent that reduces viscosity while contributing to crosslink density after the curing process is complete.

Electronics manufacturers use HPMA-based polymers in conformal coatings and encapsulants where controlled hydroxyl functionality supports adhesion to sensitive substrates and components.

Hydroxypropyl methacrylate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically as a mixture of the 2-hydroxypropyl and 1-methyl-2-hydroxyethyl isomers for standard industrial use.

Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering, with inhibitor content specified to ensure storage stability. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers with 97% purity.

name: Dichloroisocyanurate
description:
Dichloroisocyanurate (CAS 2782-57-2 ), commonly supplied as its sodium or potassium salt, is a chlorine-releasing compound used across water treatment, sanitation, and cleaning applications.

It delivers controlled, stabilized active chlorine that disinfects, bleaches, and controls microbial growth across a broad range of industrial and consumer end uses.

In water treatment, it serves as the active disinfectant in swimming pool and potable water systems, where its slow chlorine release maintains residual sanitizer levels more effectively.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulators incorporate it into dishwashing powders, surface sanitizers, and hard-surface disinfectants targeting bacteria, fungi, and algae.

Laundry and textile bleaching products rely on it to deliver oxidative whitening without the handling risks associated with liquid hypochlorite in various industrial settings.

In personal care, it is used at low concentrations in denture-cleaning tablets and wound-care formulations requiring controlled antimicrobial action for safety and efficacy.

Dichloroisocyanurate is commercially available as a dry, free-flowing powder or in tablet and granule form, most commonly as the sodium salt (NaDCC) or potassium salt.

Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and potable water treatment specifications, with active chlorine content typically confirmed against recognized standards like FCC .
