name: Sunset yellow fcf
description:
Sunset Yellow FCF (CAS 2783-94-0 ), also known as FD&C Yellow 6, Orange Yellow S, and E110 , is a synthetic azo dye that imparts a characteristic orange-yellow hue to food, beverage, and industrial products.

C.I. Food Yellow 3 is the colorimetric designation used in technical and regulatory documentation. It is approved across major regulatory frameworks and widely specified by formulators requiring consistent, heat-stable orange coloration.

In food and beverage manufacturing, E110 is used to color soft drinks, confectionery, snack coatings, and processed foods where a bright orange-yellow appearance is required for consumer appeal.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into tablet coatings, capsule shells, and liquid preparations to achieve uniform color for product identification and branding purposes.

In the textile and leather industries, it is applied in dyebath processes to achieve orange shades on natural and synthetic substrates. Printing ink formulators also use it as a colorant in packaging inks.

Sunset Yellow FCF is supplied as a fine orange-red powder, typically in sodium salt form. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade for industrial dyeing applications.

Purity specifications for food and pharma grades generally require a minimum dye content of 85%, with low-heavy-metal and low-subsidiary-dye specifications to ensure safety and performance.

name: Pigment red 170
description:
Pigment Red 170 (CAS 2786-76-7 ), also sold under trade names such as Permanent Red F 3RK70 and Sunbrite Red 170, is a high-performance azo pigment delivering a clean, saturated red shade.

This pigment is used across a broad range of industrial colorant applications. Its strong tinting strength and resistance to migration make it a preferred red pigment for demanding end-use markets.

In coatings and industrial paints, it provides excellent lightfastness and weather resistance. This supports exterior architectural and automotive refinish formulations where durability is a primary requirement.

Printing ink manufacturers use it in packaging inks where color intensity and resistance to overprint varnishes are critical. It ensures that the final printed product maintains its visual appeal.

Plastics processors incorporate it into polyolefin and PVC compounds for consumer goods and packaging film. It is ideal for molded parts requiring stable, heat-resistant coloration during processing.

In textile and paper applications, it is used to produce vivid red shades in surface coatings. It is also a key component in pigment printing pastes for various fabric types and finishes.

The product is supplied as a dry powder, with press cake forms available for certain ink and coating applications. Standard commercial grades vary in particle size distribution and surface treatment.

These variations suit solvent-borne, water-borne, or plastics end uses. Technical-grade material is the predominant market offering, with specialty dispersions available for specific formulation requirements.

Contact us for supply of Pigment red 170

name: Crocetin
description:
Crocetin (CAS 27876-94-4 ) is a natural carotenoid dicarboxylic acid derived primarily from saffron and gardenia fruit, where it occurs as the aglycone core of crocin pigments.

In commercial applications, it functions as a natural colorant and antioxidant active across food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic formulations for global manufacturers and distributors.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, this compound is incorporated into capsules and softgels targeting cognitive support and sleep quality positioning for consumers.

Food and beverage producers use it as a natural yellow-to-orange colorant in products where synthetic dye replacement is a primary formulation priority for clean-label initiatives.

Cosmetic formulators source this ingredient for inclusion in premium skincare serums and creams, where its antioxidant activity supports anti-aging product claims and efficacy.

Pharmaceutical researchers and specialty ingredient buyers also evaluate it as an active botanical extract for investigational oral and topical preparations in clinical settings.

The material is supplied as a fine crystalline or amorphous powder, typically in standardized extract form with defined purity levels ranging from around 90% to 98%+ by HPLC.

It is available in both synthetic and natural grades, with specification documentation commonly including heavy metal testing and residual solvent data to support regulatory submissions.

name: Polyhydroxystearic acid
description:
Polyhydroxystearic acid (CAS 27924-99-8 ), also known as Poly(12-hydroxystearic acid), is a polymeric fatty acid derivative used primarily as a dispersant and rheology modifier in pigment and filler systems.

It functions by anchoring to particle surfaces and providing steric stabilization, preventing agglomeration in non-aqueous formulations. In coatings and inks, it disperses inorganic pigments and extenders.

This material is highly effective in solvent-borne and high-solids systems, improving color development and reducing viscosity. Plastics compounders use it to treat mineral fillers such as calcium carbonate.

By treating titanium dioxide with this polymer, manufacturers enable higher filler loadings without sacrificing processability. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it acts as a surface-active component.

The additive improves wetting of metal surfaces and enhances additive compatibility. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to stabilize filled systems and control application rheology during use.

Polyhydroxystearic acid is supplied as a viscous liquid or low-melting solid, depending on molecular weight and grade. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial use.

Purity and acid value specifications vary by supplier, ensuring the material meets specific formulation needs. It is available in bulk quantities and is commonly offered as a neat material for production.

The product can also be found as a component in pre-formulated dispersant blends. This versatility makes it a staple for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in complex chemical systems.

name: 1,1,1-tris(p-hydroxyphenyl)ethane
description:
1,1,1-Tris(p-hydroxyphenyl)ethane , also known as THPE, is a trifunctional phenolic monomer used as a branching agent and crosslinker in polymer systems. Its three reactive hydroxyl groups allow formulators to build controlled network structures.

This chemical, identified by CAS 27955-94-8 , is essential for epoxy, polycarbonate, and specialty coating resins. In epoxy coating and powder coating formulations, it introduces branching points that improve crosslink density.

These additions enhance the chemical resistance and thermal performance of the cured film. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to tune mechanical properties and increase cohesive strength in structural systems.

Polycarbonate producers use it as a chain-branching comonomer to achieve high-melt-strength grades. These grades are particularly suited for demanding blow molding and extrusion applications in industrial manufacturing.

In rubber compounding and elastomer systems, it functions as a phenolic curative and stabilizer. This contributes to long-term oxidative stability and durability in various harsh environmental conditions.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for easy handling. Technical and high-purity grades are available, with purity specifications typically at 98% or above for processing.

These specifications ensure the material meets rigorous polymer-grade requirements. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale bags for laboratory use to bulk quantities for large-scale industrial polymer production.

name: Triethylenediamine
description:
Triethylenediamine (CAS 280-57-9 ), commercially known as DABCO, is a bicyclic diamine used primarily as a tertiary amine catalyst in polyurethane manufacturing. It accelerates the reaction between isocyanates and polyols.

This chemical controls foam formation and cure rates across a broad range of formulations. In flexible and rigid polyurethane foam production, it drives the gelling and blowing reactions that determine cell structure.

The catalyst is essential for managing density and mechanical performance in industrial applications. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to accelerate cure in two-component polyurethane and epoxy systems.

By reducing open time and improving bond development, it enhances manufacturing efficiency. In coatings, it functions as a crosslinking catalyst for moisture-cure and two-part urethane systems applied to substrates.

Life science and biotechnology applications include its use as an antifade mounting medium component. In this role, it inhibits photobleaching in fluorescence microscopy preparations for laboratory research.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline solid, typically in powder or granule form. It is also available as pre-dissolved solutions in glycols such as dipropylene glycol for easier handling.

Standard commercial grades are available at high purity levels suitable for catalyst applications. Solution concentrations are commonly at 33% active content in glycol carriers for precise dosing.

Technical grade is the primary market specification for industrial use. Supply is typically managed in bags, drums, and IBCs to meet the logistical needs of large-scale chemical manufacturing facilities.

name: 9-Borabicyclononane
description:
9-Borabicyclononane (CAS 280-64-8 ), commercially supplied as its stable dimer 9-borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane dimer, is a selective hydroboration reagent used in synthetic chemistry.

It enables precise, stereoselective addition of boron to alkenes, making it a preferred reagent for building chiral intermediates in complex molecule synthesis for various industries.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to produce enantiomerically enriched intermediates for active pharmaceutical ingredients where stereochemical control is critical for the final product.

Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling reactions rely on it as a boron source to form carbon–carbon bonds in the synthesis of drug candidates and fine chemicals for global distribution.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers use it in the preparation of labeled compounds and probe molecules for biological assays and advanced diagnostic testing procedures.

Industrial cleaning and specialty chemical formulators source it as a catalyst precursor in boron-mediated reaction sequences requiring high regioselectivity and consistent chemical performance.

9-Borabicyclononane is supplied as a solid dimer or as stabilized solutions in tetrahydrofuran or other anhydrous solvents. Standard concentrations for solution grades are typically 0.5 M and 1.0 M.

Material is available at research, pilot, and commercial scale, with specifications aligned to pharmaceutical-grade synthetic reagent requirements and rigorous quality control protocols.

name: Phenol polymer with formaldehyde glycidyl ether
description:
Phenol polymer with formaldehyde glycidyl ether (CAS 28064-14-4 ), commercially recognized as polyglycidyl ether of phenolic novolac, is a multifunctional epoxy resin derived from novolac chemistry.

With three or more epoxide groups per molecule, it delivers higher cross-link density than standard diglycidyl ether resins. This makes it the preferred choice where elevated thermal resistance and chemical durability are required.

In protective coatings, it is formulated into high-performance tank linings, pipe coatings, and industrial floor systems. These systems must withstand aggressive solvents and elevated service temperatures during operation.

Structural adhesives and composite matrices for automotive and aerospace components rely on its dense cure network. This allows manufacturers to meet demanding mechanical performance specifications in critical applications.

In electrical laminates and encapsulants, it provides the dimensional stability and dielectric performance required. This is essential for modern printed circuit boards and semiconductor packaging technologies.

Building and construction sealants and grouts use it as a reactive binder where chemical resistance is a qualification requirement. It is particularly effective against exposure to various acids and alkalis.

Supplied as a semi-solid to viscous liquid resin, the viscosity and epoxide equivalent weight (EEW) vary by grade. This variety allows the material to suit specific processing requirements across different industries.

Standard technical and industrial grades are the norm for this polymer. Buyers should confirm EEW, functionality, and softening point against their cure system and application specifications before procurement.

name: Ethylene glycol monopropyl ether
description:
Ethylene glycol monopropyl ether (CAS 2807-30-9 ), also known commercially as Propyl Cellosolve, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings, printing, and personal care manufacturing.

Its controlled evaporation rate supports film formation and flow in solvent-based systems where faster solvents cause surface defects. In architectural and industrial coatings, it improves flow and leveling.

This solvent is effective in alkyd and waterborne formulations, reducing brush marks and orange peel in the final film. Printing ink manufacturers use it to control drying speed and maintain viscosity stability.

It is particularly useful for packaging inks on flexible substrates. In personal care, it functions as a carrier solvent in hair care and skin formulations where uniform ingredient dispersion is required.

Adhesive and sealant producers incorporate it as a coalescing or coupling solvent to improve substrate wetting and bond development. This ensures high performance across various industrial bonding applications.

Ethylene glycol monopropyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

High-purity grades are available for personal care and specialty formulation use where tighter quality specifications are required. We ensure all shipments meet rigorous industrial and safety standards.

name: Potassium cumene sulfonate
description:
Potassium cumene sulfonate (CAS 28085-69-0 ) is an aromatic sulfonate salt used primarily as a hydrotrope in aqueous formulations. It improves the solubility of surfactants and other poorly water-soluble ingredients.

This chemical enables stable, high-active liquid concentrates that would otherwise separate or cloud. In home care and industrial cleaning, it allows formulators to produce high-concentration liquid detergents.

Common applications include hard surface cleaners, dishwashing liquids, and degreasers without phase separation. Textile processing operations use it to boost the compatibility of dye auxiliaries and finishing agents.

It improves bath stability and process consistency in aqueous baths. In industrial and institutional cleaning concentrates, it functions as a viscosity modifier, helping formulators hit target rheology profiles.

This is achieved without adding thickeners that reduce clarity. Coatings and adhesive systems that require water-based carrier fluids benefit from its ability to keep active components in stable solution.

Potassium cumene sulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 45% active concentration being the most common commercial form. Dry powder and granule forms are available for specific applications.

These forms are used where water content must be minimized or shipping weight is a constraint. It is typically offered at technical grade, with product specifications covering active content and pH.

Sodium chloride levels are also monitored as they are relevant to formulation performance. The material ensures long-term stability during storage and application across various industrial sectors.

name: Etidronic acid
description:
Etidronic acid (CAS 2809-21-4 ), commonly known as HEDP or Oxyethylidenediphosphonic acid, is a phosphonate chelating agent used across water treatment, industrial cleaning, and personal care manufacturing.

It binds metal ions and inhibits scale formation, preventing corrosion and deposit buildup in process systems and formulated products. In water treatment and oilfield operations, HEDP controls calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate scale.

This chemical is essential for cooling towers, boilers, and injection systems, effectively extending equipment service life. Personal care formulators use it as a stabilizer in oxidative hair color and bleaching products.

It sequesters trace metals that would otherwise degrade peroxide systems, ensuring product stability. Textile and paper processors apply it to prevent metal-catalyzed degradation during bleaching and dyeing processes.

This application protects fiber quality and ensures process consistency across manufacturing lines. In industrial cleaning and detergent formulations, it disperses iron and hardness ions to improve wash performance.

The agent prevents redeposition of minerals on surfaces during the cleaning cycle. Etidronic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at sixty percent active content for industrial use.

While other concentrations are available for specific applications, Technical grade is the standard for water treatment. Higher-purity grades serve personal care and specialty formulation markets globally.

Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or drums is the typical commercial format for this product. We ensure all shipments meet rigorous industrial specifications for consistency and performance in your applications.

name: Pigment red 4
description:
Pigment Red 4 (CAS 2814-77-9 ), also known as D&C Red No. 36, is an azo-based organic pigment delivering a bright, clean red shade across a range of industrial coloring applications.

It is used to impart color in plastics, surface coatings, printing inks, and textile substrates where consistent hue and process compatibility are the primary sourcing criteria for manufacturers.

In plastics and polymer processing, it is incorporated into masterbatches and compound colorants for consumer and packaging goods requiring vivid red tones and reliable dispersion during production.

Coatings formulators use it in solvent-based and industrial paints where strong tinting strength and surface uniformity are required to meet specific aesthetic and performance standards in the field.

In printing and packaging, it is selected for gravure and flexographic ink systems targeting high-impact red reproduction on paper and film substrates for various commercial branding needs.

Textile and leather processors apply it in dyeing and finishing operations where surface coloration of synthetic and natural materials is needed to achieve specific seasonal or industrial colors.

The product is supplied as a dry powder, the standard commercial form for dispersion into resin, solvent, or aqueous systems. Technical grade is the primary market offering available.

Product specifications are typically defined by color strength, purity, and particle size distribution. Packaging is available in fiber drums or bags suited to bulk industrial procurement and logistics.

name: Vinylpyrrolidone-vinylamine copolymer
description:
Vinylpyrrolidone-vinylamine copolymer (CAS 28158-56-7 ) is a synthetic cationic polymer combining the film-forming characteristics of vinylpyrrolidone with the reactive amine functionality of vinylamine.

It is used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial sectors primarily for rheology modification, surface conditioning, and flocculation. In personal care formulations, the polymer functions as a conditioning agent.

It acts as a film-forming agent in hair care products, improving wet combability and surface adhesion of actives. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a binder or coating aid where controlled surface interaction is required.

Adhesion to substrates is a key benefit in these applications. In water treatment, its cationic amine groups support coagulation and flocculation of suspended particles, making it relevant for industrial effluent processing.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it to modify rheology and improve surface wetting performance on hard surfaces. This versatility makes it a valuable component in diverse chemical systems.

Vinylpyrrolidone-vinylamine copolymer is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with solids content varying by grade and supplier. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available.

Selection is driven by amine content, molecular weight range, and intended application. Buyers should confirm charge density and viscosity profile against their formulation requirements when evaluating supply options.

name: Irgarol
description:
Irgarol (CAS 28159-98-0 ), also marketed as Irgarol 1051 and known by the common name Cybutryne, is a triazine-based biocide used to inhibit algae and microbial growth in protective coating systems.

It functions as an antifouling agent, preventing biological colonization on submerged and exposed surfaces. In marine and industrial antifouling paints, Irgarol 1051 is incorporated as a co-biocide.

It is used alongside copper compounds to broaden the spectrum of protection against algae and slime-forming organisms. Coating formulators use it in hull paints, dock coatings, and offshore structure treatments.

These applications are essential where long-term biostatic performance is required. In architectural and industrial coatings, it protects exterior surfaces from algal discoloration, extending the service life.

Sealants and elastomers for outdoor construction applications also incorporate Irgarol to prevent surface biofilm development. This is particularly effective in high-humidity environments for industrial use.

Irgarol is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in technical grade, with purity specifications typically at 97% or higher, suitable for direct use in coating formulations.

Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale quantities to bulk industrial supply depending on application volume requirements. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale testing and large-scale manufacturing.

name: Calcium L-lactate
description:
Calcium L-lactate (CAS 28305-25-1 ), also known as calcium lactate, is a calcium salt of lactic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It delivers bioavailable calcium while functioning as a buffering agent, acidulant, and stabilizer in finished formulations.

In food production, it extends shelf life in baked goods and fresh-cut produce by controlling pH and inhibiting microbial growth without imparting strong acidic flavor. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a calcium supplement active in tablets and chewables.

Its high solubility supports consistent dosing and good patient palatability in medical applications. In personal care formulations, it acts as a pH buffer and mild astringent in oral care products, including toothpastes and mouthwashes.

Food processors also use it as a firming agent in canned vegetables and as a mineral fortifier in dairy alternatives and infant nutrition products. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking functional mineral enrichment.

Calcium L-lactate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granulated forms preferred for direct compression in tablet manufacturing. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and Ph. Eur. , covering both food and pharmaceutical requirements.

Anhydrous and pentahydrate forms are available, with the pentahydrate being the most commonly traded specification. These high-purity grades ensure compliance with international safety standards for global distribution and industrial use.

name: Pinanyl hydroperoxide
description:
Pinanyl hydroperoxide (CAS 28324-52-9 ), also known as Pinane hydroperoxide, is an organic peroxide used as a radical source in polymer manufacturing and curing systems. Derived from the oxidation of pinane, it delivers controlled radical generation suited to demanding industrial polymerization processes.

In rubber and tire manufacturing, it functions as a polymerization initiator for emulsion and solution polymerization of synthetic rubbers, including SBR and other diene-based elastomers. This chemical is essential for high-performance rubber production.

Coatings formulators use it in redox initiator systems where low-temperature cure initiation is required, enabling film formation under conditions where thermal initiators are ineffective. This allows for greater flexibility in industrial coating applications.

In adhesives and sealant production, it supports cross-linking and curing of elastomeric bases, contributing to final bond strength and heat resistance. Plastics processors also employ it to initiate controlled radical polymerization in specialty resin systems.

Pinanyl hydroperoxide is supplied as a liquid, typically as a solution or at defined active-oxygen concentrations to meet handling and stability requirements. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial polymerization and curing applications.

Buyers should confirm active-oxygen content and concentration specifications directly with suppliers, as these vary across producers and determine initiator efficiency in process design. Proper storage and handling are critical for maintaining product stability.

name: Sodium isopropylbenzenesulfonate
description:
Sodium isopropylbenzenesulfonate ( CAS 28348-53-0 ), commercially known as sodium cumene sulfonate, is an aromatic sulfonate salt used primarily as a hydrotrope and coupling agent in liquid formulations.

It improves the solubility and stability of surfactant systems, allowing formulators to build higher-active, clear liquid products without phase separation in various industrial environments.

In household and industrial cleaners, sodium cumene sulfonate enables the formulation of concentrated, water-clear detergents by keeping surfactant blends homogeneous at elevated active levels.

Textile and leather processing operations use it to improve dye bath stability and ensure even distribution of processing agents across fiber substrates during the manufacturing cycle.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as a dispersing aid that helps maintain emulsion stability during manufacture and storage, preventing unwanted sedimentation or separation.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into liquid soaps and shampoos as a viscosity modifier and solubilizer for fragrance and active ingredients to ensure product clarity and performance.

Sodium isopropylbenzenesulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 40% active concentration, and as a dry powder or granule form for applications requiring low moisture content.

Standard supply grades include technical and industrial-grade specifications. Food-contact and cosmetic-grade documentation is available from select suppliers to support regulatory compliance.

name: Sodium glycolate
description:
Sodium glycolate (CAS 2836-32-0 ), also known as sodium 2-hydroxyacetate, is the sodium salt of glycolic acid used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food applications as a buffering agent, chelant, and humectant.

Its ability to regulate pH and bind metal ions makes it a functional ingredient in formulations where stability and moisture retention are critical procurement considerations for industrial manufacturers.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, sodium glycolate is used as a buffering excipient in topical and injectable formulations, helping maintain pH stability throughout the entirety of the product shelf life.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin care products, particularly exfoliating serums, moisturizers, and cleansers, where it supports moisture retention and enhances the performance of active ingredients.

In industrial and personal care cleaning formulations, it acts as a chelating agent to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, improving surfactant efficiency in hard water conditions for better results.

Food-grade applications include its use as an acidity regulator in processed food systems requiring precise pH control. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution.

Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade material, with the latter conforming to USP or Ph. Eur. specifications where required for high-purity compliance.

Packaging is typically available in kilogram quantities for laboratory and formulation use, scaling to bulk supply for industrial buyers seeking consistent quality and reliable chemical distribution.

name: Diisononylamine
description:
Diisononylamine (CAS 28454-70-8 ) is a branched secondary amine used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor and surface-active agent. Its secondary amine structure makes it effective for metal protection and interfacial modification.

In metalworking fluids and lubricant additives, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor, forming protective layers on ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces to extend component service life across demanding industrial formulations.

Coatings formulators incorporate it as a surface modifier to improve substrate adhesion and wetting on difficult surfaces. In adhesive and sealant systems, it acts as a reactive intermediate or cure promoter.

This chemical contributes significantly to bond performance in polymer-based formulations. Plastics and polymer processors use it as a processing aid or functional additive where controlled surface chemistry is required.

Diisononylamine is supplied as a liquid, typical for secondary amines in this molecular weight range. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications aligned to industrial end-use requirements.

Buyers sourcing for lubricant or coatings applications should confirm amine content and isomer distribution. Branching profiles can vary between producers, impacting the final performance of the chemical in specific applications.

name: Tributylphenol
description:
Tributylphenol (CAS 28471-16-1 ), commercially recognized as 2,4,6-Tributylphenol, is a hindered phenolic compound used across plastics, rubber, and energy sectors as an antioxidant stabilizer.

Its bulky alkyl substitution pattern makes it effective at inhibiting oxidative degradation in demanding industrial formulations, acting as a plasticizer and process solvent for various applications.

In plastics and polymer processing, it functions as a stabilizer that protects resins and compounded materials from thermal oxidation during high-temperature manufacturing and extrusion processes.

Rubber and tire formulators incorporate it to extend service life by suppressing oxidative breakdown in vulcanized compounds, ensuring durability and performance in harsh environmental conditions.

In oil and gas applications, it is used as an additive in lubricants, process oils, and drilling fluids where oxidative stability under elevated temperatures is a primary formulation requirement.

It also serves as a carrier solvent in specialty industrial formulations where compatibility with hydrocarbon-based systems is a key selection criterion for chemical manufacturers and blenders.

Tributylphenol is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, with bulk and drummed packaging available for industrial procurement. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and isomeric profile when evaluating supplier documentation for formulation-critical applications to ensure the highest performance in their final products.

name: Neopentyl glycol diethylhexanoate
description:
Neopentyl glycol diethylhexanoate (CAS 28510-23-8 ), also known commercially as neopentyl glycol dioctanoate, is a synthetic diester ester fluid used across lubrication, personal care, and industrial formulation.

It functions as a lubricant base fluid, plasticizer, and emollient carrier depending on the application segment. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it serves as a high-performance synthetic base fluid or co-fluid.

The material offers thermal stability across demanding operating conditions, which is a key factor for automotive and industrial gear oils. Personal care formulators use it as a lightweight emollient and carrier oil.

It is frequently found in skin creams, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, where its low greasiness supports elegant skin feel without compromising active delivery. As a plasticizer, it improves flexibility and processing.

The compound is utilized in polymer and coating systems to enhance performance. Its solvency profile also supports pigment dispersion in industrial coatings and specialty ink formulations for various manufacturing needs.

Neopentyl glycol diethylhexanoate is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements relevant to personal care manufacturing.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC totes for bulk procurement. This versatile ester provides reliable performance across diverse chemical sectors, ensuring stability and efficiency in final product formulations.

name: Isophorone diamine
description:
Isophorone diamine (CAS 2855-13-2 ), commonly known as IPDA, is a cycloaliphatic diamine used as a curing agent and building block in high-performance polymer systems.

Its low reactivity at ambient temperatures combined with rapid cure at elevated temperatures makes it a controlled, reliable hardener for demanding formulations across various industries.

In epoxy coatings for automotive and aerospace substrates, IPDA delivers cured films with strong UV stability and chemical resistance, which is critical for exterior and underbody protection.

Structural adhesives and sealants in construction and transportation rely on IPDA-cured systems where flexibility and long-term durability under mechanical stress are required for safety.

As a monomer in polyurea and polyurethane synthesis, IPDA contributes to elastomers and casting compounds used in industrial flooring, protective linings, and electronic encapsulation.

Printing and packaging applications use IPDA-based systems in laminating adhesives where low yellowing and adhesion to film substrates are key selection criteria for manufacturers.

IPDA is supplied as a clear to slightly yellowish liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging. Technical and industrial grades are the primary commercial forms available for purchase.

Purity is typically specified at 99% or higher. Some suppliers offer low-color or low-viscosity variants tailored for coating and adhesive formulations with strict appearance requirements.

Diisononyl phthalate ( CAS 28553-12-0 ), commonly known as DINP, is a high-molecular-weight phthalate plasticizer used across PVC and polymer processing industries. It improves flexibility and workability in rigid formulations.

This chemical serves as a standard choice where durability and low volatility are procurement priorities. In building and construction, it is used in PVC flooring, roofing membranes, and window profiles.

These applications require long-term flexibility under mechanical stress. Automotive manufacturers specify it in interior trim, underbody coatings, and cable insulation due to its resistance to heat aging.

Wire and cable producers rely on this plasticizer to meet electrical insulation performance requirements across a range of operating temperatures. It ensures stability in demanding environments.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a plasticizer in inks and coatings applied to flexible PVC substrates. This versatility makes it a staple in modern industrial manufacturing processes.

The product is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk quantities including ISO tank, flexi-tank, and drum formats. It is available in technical grade for industrial use.

name: Bromotrimethylsilane
description:
Bromotrimethylsilane ( CAS 2857-97-8 ), commonly abbreviated as TMSBr, is a reactive organosilicon reagent used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a silylating agent and Lewis acid activator.

This versatile compound enables selective protection and deprotection of functional groups in complex molecule construction. In pharmaceutical API synthesis, TMSBr converts phosphonate esters to phosphonic acids for drug manufacturing.

This specific transformation is central to antiviral and nucleotide analog drug manufacturing processes. Polymer chemists use it to introduce trimethylsilyl groups onto polymer backbones, modifying surface adhesion and compatibility.

These modifications are essential for specialty coatings and adhesives used in industrial applications. In fine chemical and agrochemical synthesis, it activates esters and ethers under mild conditions, reducing harsh catalysts.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators apply it in silicone-based systems where controlled surface modification is required. TMSBr is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels of 97% or greater.

Anhydrous grades are standard given the compound's sensitivity to moisture. Packaging ranges from small reagent quantities to multi-kilogram drums for industrial synthesis to meet various production demands.

Technical and synthesis-grade specifications are the most commonly available across the market. The reagent remains a critical component for laboratories focusing on advanced organic synthesis and material science.

name: Dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate
description:
Dimethylaminoethyl methacrylate (CAS 2867-47-2 ), commercially known as DMAEMA, is a reactive amino-functional monomer used in the synthesis of specialty polymers and copolymers. Its tertiary amine group enables pH-responsive behavior and cationic character in finished polymer systems.

This makes it a preferred building block for performance-driven formulations across coatings, adhesives, and textile treatment chemistries. In coatings and adhesives, DMAEMA is copolymerized to introduce adhesion-promoting and crosslinkable functionality.

It is frequently utilized in waterborne and UV-curable systems to enhance overall durability. The textile and leather industries use DMAEMA-based polymers as fixatives and softening agents, where cationic charge improves fiber affinity and treatment longevity.

In paper manufacturing, it contributes to wet-strength resins and retention aid formulations that enhance process efficiency and end-product performance. Printing and packaging applications rely on these copolymers in inkjet coatings and binder systems.

These systems require controlled surface interaction and ink receptivity for high-quality results. DMAEMA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically stabilized with a polymerization inhibitor to ensure safe handling and storage during transit.

name: Cyclopentane
description:
Cyclopentane (CAS 287-92-3 ) is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon used primarily as a blowing agent and specialty solvent across several industrial sectors. Its low boiling point and high purity availability make it a preferred choice where controlled volatility is a process requirement.

In rigid polyurethane foam manufacturing, it is the dominant blowing agent for producing insulation panels used in refrigerators, freezers, and cold-chain equipment. It serves as a critical replacement for older HFC-based alternatives under modern environmental regulations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reaction solvent and extraction medium in API synthesis where a non-polar, low-residue solvent profile is required. It ensures high efficiency in chemical processing while maintaining the integrity of sensitive molecular structures.

In specialty fragrance and flavor formulations, it functions as a carrier solvent for delivering volatile aroma compounds at controlled evaporation rates. Lubricant formulators also use it as a process solvent during synthesis and blending of cycloparaffinic base stocks.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities to meet various industrial scales. Standard commercial grades include high-purity technical grade (95%+) and polyurethane foam-grade with tightly controlled purity specifications.

These specifications are designed to meet specific blowing agent performance requirements and thermal conductivity standards. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to buyers requiring documentation aligned with ICH solvent guidelines for manufacturing.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale industrial applications. We provide comprehensive technical data sheets and safety documentation to support the integration of this hydrocarbon into your specific production workflows.

name: Diacetone acrylamide
description:
Diacetone acrylamide (CAS 2873-97-4 ), commercially known as DAAM, is a functional acrylamide monomer used to introduce reactive ketone groups into polymer backbones.

These pendant ketone groups enable post-polymerization crosslinking through reaction with dihydrazide compounds, giving formulators precise control over cure timing and network density.

In waterborne coatings and adhesives, DAAM is copolymerized into acrylic emulsions to enable ambient-temperature crosslinking without external catalysts, improving film hardness and solvent resistance.

Textile and paper treatment formulations use DAAM-based polymers to deliver durable surface finishes that withstand repeated washing or mechanical stress during industrial processing.

Printing and packaging applications benefit from DAAM's ability to enhance ink adhesion and coating cohesion on difficult substrates, ensuring high-quality finishes for commercial use.

Personal care formulators incorporate DAAM copolymers into film-forming systems where controlled crosslink density affects hold strength and flexibility in various cosmetic applications.

Diacetone acrylamide is supplied as a white crystalline solid. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with purity levels typically at 98% or above.

Quality is confirmed by GC or HPLC analysis. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities, and temperature-controlled storage is standard practice to maintain monomer stability.

name: Polyhexamethylene biguanide
description:
Polyhexamethylene biguanide (CAS 28757-47-3 ), commonly known as PHMB, is a polymeric antimicrobial agent used across industrial and consumer markets to control bacterial, fungal, and algal contamination.

It functions as a broad-spectrum biocide effective at low concentrations, making it a preferred active ingredient where persistent antimicrobial performance is required for various industrial applications.

In water treatment, PHMB is used as an alternative to chlorine-based biocides in swimming pools, cooling towers, and process water systems where chlorine compatibility is a concern for operators.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products including contact lens solutions, wound cleansing preparations, and skin antiseptics for consumer safety.

The textile and leather industries apply PHMB to impart durable antimicrobial finishes to fabrics, nonwovens, and treated surfaces to prevent the growth of odor-causing bacteria and mold.

In industrial and institutional cleaning, it is formulated into hard surface disinfectants and sanitizers targeting healthcare, food processing, and veterinary environments requiring high hygiene standards.

PHMB is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 20% active concentration. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are available depending on the specific requirements of the end application.

Buyers should confirm active content and compliance with relevant regional regulatory listings, including EU Biocidal Products Regulation, when evaluating supply sources for their manufacturing needs.

name: 4-propylbenzaldehyde
description:
4-Propylbenzaldehyde (CAS 28785-06-0 ) is an aromatic aldehyde used as a building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and fragrance formulation. Its para-substituted benzaldehyde structure makes it a recognized intermediate for constructing more complex active compounds.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key synthetic intermediate for preparing APIs and specialty compounds where a propyl-substituted aromatic aldehyde scaffold is required. This material is essential for high-precision chemical engineering.

Fragrance chemists incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional fragrance formulations to contribute aldehydic, floral-green character to finished compositions. It provides a unique olfactory profile for premium consumer products.

It also supports the synthesis of liquid crystal compounds, where para-alkyl benzaldehyde derivatives are established structural components. These applications are critical for the development of modern display technologies and electronics.

Specialty chemical producers use it as a precursor in condensation and reductive amination reactions targeting novel molecular architectures. Its reactivity makes it a versatile tool for research and development laboratories.

4-Propylbenzaldehyde is supplied as a liquid, typically offered at high purity levels suited for pharmaceutical intermediate and research-grade applications. The material maintains stability under standard industrial storage conditions.

Standard packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities through to bulk drum supply, depending on the supplier's production scale. Technical-grade material is the most commonly traded specification in the global chemical market.

name: Imidazole
description:
Imidazole (CAS 288-32-4 ) is a five-membered nitrogen-containing heterocycle used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer chemistry, and industrial processing. Its primary commercial value lies in its dual function as a synthetic building block and a buffering agent.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of antifungal agents, antihistamines, and a broad range of active pharmaceutical ingredients. It is essential for creating molecules containing the imidazole ring structure.

Epoxy resin formulators use it as a curing agent and cure accelerator, particularly in electronics-grade laminates and adhesive systems. This allows for controlled crosslinking and improved thermal stability in high-performance materials.

In water treatment and industrial processes, it functions as a pH buffer and corrosion inhibitor precursor. These applications rely on its chemical stability and ability to maintain specific environmental conditions during processing.

Agricultural chemical producers also incorporate it as an intermediate in the synthesis of imidazole-based fungicides and plant growth regulators. This versatility makes it a staple chemical for large-scale agrochemical manufacturing.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline solid or flake. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial applications and high-purity grades meeting USP and Ph. Eur. specifications for pharmaceutical use.

Bulk quantities are available in fiber drums or bags, with reagent-grade material offered for laboratory and research procurement. We ensure consistent quality and supply chain reliability for all industrial and life science applications.

name: 1H-Tetrazole
description:
1H-Tetrazole (CAS 288-94-8 ), also referred to as 1,2,3,4-tetrazole, is a nitrogen-rich heterocyclic building block used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical development, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its high nitrogen content and bioisosteric properties make it a target intermediate for drug discovery programs and crop protection research. In pharmaceutical development, it functions as a carboxylic acid bioisostere.

This enables medicinal chemists to modify drug candidates for improved metabolic stability and membrane permeability without altering core pharmacological activity. Agrochemical formulators incorporate it as a synthetic intermediate.

It is used in the production of fungicides and herbicides where specific heterocyclic scaffolds are required. In polymer chemistry, tetrazole derivatives act as photoactivatable crosslinkers and polymerization initiators.

These derivatives support the production of specialty polymers and photoresist materials. Biotechnology researchers also use it as a coupling reagent in oligonucleotide synthesis for automated DNA/RNA assembly.

It activates phosphoramidite monomers during the assembly process. 1H-Tetrazole is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder and is available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications.

High-purity lots (≥98–99%) are commonly offered to meet pharmaceutical intermediate and synthesis requirements. Packaging ranges from gram-scale quantities for laboratory use to kilogram batches for procurement.

name: Sodium polyglutamate
description:
Sodium polyglutamate (CAS 28829-38-1 ), commonly abbreviated as NaPGA, is a naturally derived polyamino acid produced through microbial fermentation of glutamic acid. It functions as a high-performance humectant, film-former, and chelating agent across food, cosmetic, and industrial markets.

In skincare and haircare formulations, NaPGA outperforms hyaluronic acid in moisture retention at equivalent concentrations, making it a premium ingredient in serums, moisturizers, and conditioning treatments.

Food manufacturers use it as a flavor enhancer and texture modifier in soups, sauces, and fermented products, where it also reduces sodium content without compromising taste profile.

In agriculture, it improves nutrient uptake efficiency by chelating micronutrients in liquid fertilizer formulations, reducing fertilizer loss through leaching. This makes it a sustainable choice for modern farming.

Water treatment applications leverage its chelating capacity to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, controlling scale formation in industrial cooling and process water systems. This ensures equipment longevity and efficiency.

Sodium polyglutamate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution at varying concentrations. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent.

Fermentation-derived material remains the market standard for high-purity applications. Technical-grade material is also available for agricultural and water treatment applications to meet specific industrial needs.

name: Sodium Pidolate
description:
Sodium Pidolate (CAS 28874-51-3 ), also known as Sodium Pyroglutamate, is the sodium salt of pyroglutamic acid and a naturally occurring component of the skin's natural moisturizing factor (NMF).

It functions as a humectant and moisture-retention agent across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications. In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into moisturizers, serums, and hair conditioners.

The material binds water within the skin or hair matrix, improving hydration performance. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a stabilizing excipient in topical preparations and oral formulations where moisture regulation affects shelf life.

In food and nutrition applications, it acts as a flavor enhancer and stabilizer in processed foods, functional beverages, and nutritional supplements. It also appears in professional skincare actives and amino acid-based treatments.

These products target dry or compromised skin conditions effectively. Sodium Pidolate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in aqueous solution at various concentrations to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

Standard grades include cosmetic/personal care grade and pharmaceutical grade, with material typically conforming to USP or in-house specifications depending on the intended application for the final product.

Food-grade material is available for nutrition and flavoring uses. Buyers should confirm grade-specific documentation, including CoA and residual solvent data, at the sourcing stage to ensure compliance with all safety standards.

name: Adrenic acid
description:
Adrenic acid (CAS 28874-58-0 ) is a 22-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid naturally occurring in adrenal gland tissue and recognized as a key elongation product of arachidonic acid.

It functions as a biochemical reference standard, a nutritional lipid ingredient, and a bioactive component in specialty formulations targeting skin barrier and cellular function.

In pharmaceutical and biotechnology research, it is used as a certified reference standard for lipidomics, eicosanoid pathway studies, and fatty acid profiling assays.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into premium skin care products where it supports moisture retention and reinforces the lipid barrier of the stratum corneum.

In nutritional science, it is used in fatty acid composition studies and as a tracer compound in metabolic research involving omega-6 elongation pathways.

Food and supplement manufacturers source it for use in reference materials and in the development of structured lipid formulations for various industrial applications.

The product is supplied as a neat liquid or dissolved in organic solvent, typically at high purity levels suited to research and analytical applications.

It is available in research-grade and high-purity grades, commonly packaged in small quantities under inert atmosphere to preserve integrity. Bulk quantities are available on request.

name: Sodium dichloroisocyanurate
description:
Sodium dichloroisocyanurate (CAS 2893-78-9 ), commonly known as NaDCC or troclosene sodium, is a chlorine-releasing compound used across industrial and municipal sectors as a disinfectant, biocide, and bleaching agent.

It delivers controlled, stable active chlorine in solid form, making it a practical alternative to liquid chlorine systems where handling and dosing precision matter for large-scale operations.

In water treatment, NaDCC is used to disinfect drinking water, swimming pools, and wastewater streams, where its consistent chlorine release allows accurate dosing at scale for safety and compliance.

Food processing facilities rely on it for surface sanitation and equipment disinfection, meeting hygiene standards without the corrosion risks associated with traditional hypochlorite solutions.

In textile and paper manufacturing, it functions as a bleaching agent to whiten fibers and pulp without the process instability of gaseous chlorine, ensuring a more controlled production environment.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into effervescent disinfectant tablets and antiseptic products where a stable, dry chlorine source is required for long-term shelf stability and efficacy.

Sodium dichloroisocyanurate is supplied as a white powder, granules, or compressed tablets, with granule size and tablet weight customized to specific industrial application requirements.

Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and potable water treatment specifications, with active chlorine content typically around 60–62% for bulk bags, drums, and smaller packaged formats.

Ethoxylated trimethylolpropane triacrylate (CAS 28961-43-5 ), commonly abbreviated as EO-TMPTA, is a trifunctional acrylate monomer used as a reactive diluent and crosslinker in UV- and EB-curable systems.

The ethoxylation distinguishes it from standard TMPTA by reducing skin sensitization potential and improving flexibility in cured films. These factors significantly influence formulator and procurement decisions.

In UV-curable coatings and varnishes, this monomer controls crosslink density while maintaining surface hardness. It is a standard component in wood, plastic, and paper coatings for industrial use.

Printing ink formulators use it to achieve fast cure response and adhesion on flexible substrates. It is particularly effective in flexographic and offset UV inks for high-speed production lines.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to tune elongation and peel strength in radiation-cured systems. It supports high-gloss, scratch-resistant surfaces with reduced shrinkage stress.

Compared to non-ethoxylated alternatives, it is ideal for plastic part finishing and optical coatings. The chemical is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for various industrial applications.

It is available in technical and industrial grades, with ethoxylation levels typically specified by moles of ethylene oxide per hydroxyl group. This is a key parameter buyers should confirm with suppliers.

Bulk, IBC, and drum packaging are standard supply formats for this chemical. Proper handling and storage are required to maintain the stability and performance of the monomer over time.

description:
Glycidoxypropylmethyldiethoxysilane (CAS 2897-60-1 ), also known as 3-Glycidoxypropylmethyldiethoxysilane, is an epoxy-functional organosilane used to bond organic polymer matrices to inorganic substrates.

It acts as a coupling agent, crosslinker, and surface modifier across demanding industrial applications where adhesion durability is critical. In electronics, it improves adhesion between epoxy encapsulants and semiconductor substrates.

This reduces delamination risk in printed circuit boards and chip packaging. Coatings formulators use it to enhance wet adhesion and chemical resistance on glass, metal, and mineral surfaces for long-term protection.

In adhesives and sealants, it functions as a crosslinking agent that strengthens bonds between silicone or epoxy systems and difficult substrates including aluminum and ceramics. This ensures structural integrity.

Fiber-reinforced composites for automotive and aerospace applications rely on it as a sizing or primer component. It improves interfacial strength between glass fibers and polymer resins in high-stress environments.

The material is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from kilogram quantities to bulk drums. It is available in technical and high-purity grades to meet the requirements of electronics applications.

name: Glucosamine sulfate
description:
Glucosamine sulfate (CAS 29031-19-4 ) is an amino sugar salt sourced primarily from shellfish chitin or produced via fermentation for non-animal supply chains. Glucosamine sulphate is the preferred spelling in several European markets.

This makes it a distinct commercial search term for importers and formulators. It is used across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing as a bioactive ingredient and humectant for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in oral dosage forms such as tablets, capsules, and sachets targeting joint health. Personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing creams and serums.

Its humectant properties support skin hydration and barrier function in cosmetic products. It also appears in topical formulations where pH buffering is required to maintain product stability across a defined range.

Nutraceutical producers use it in combination products alongside chondroitin or collagen for joint-support supplement lines. Glucosamine sulfate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for easy processing.

name: Sorbitan dioleate
description:
Sorbitan dioleate (CAS 29116-98-1 ) is a non-ionic emulsifier derived from sorbitol and oleic acid, positioned between the mono- and trioleate members of the sorbitan ester family.

It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and moisturizing additive across personal care, food-adjacent, and industrial formulations. In personal care, it stabilizes water-in-oil emulsions.

This ingredient is used in creams and lotions while contributing skin-conditioning properties to the finished product. Food-contact and industrial lubricant formulations use it to control interfacial tension.

It is particularly effective where a mid-range HLB emulsifier is required. Textile and leather processing operations apply it as a fiber lubricant and surface wetting agent to improve processing.

This helps to ensure uniformity and reduce friction during manufacturing. In industrial cleaning concentrates, it supports emulsification of oils and greases into aqueous systems for better performance.

Sorbitan dioleate is supplied as an amber to yellow viscous liquid. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity specifications typically confirmed by rigorous laboratory testing.

name: Triisopropylbenzene polycarbodiimide
description:
Triisopropylbenzene polycarbodiimide (CAS 29117-01-9 ), commercially known as Stabaxol P 100, is a polymeric carbodiimide stabilizer used to protect hydrolysis-sensitive polymers from acid-catalyzed degradation.

It reacts with carboxylic acid end groups generated during polymer hydrolysis, extending the service life of engineering plastics, elastomers, and coatings in demanding environments.

In polyester and polyurethane compounding, it functions as a hydrolysis stabilizer that scavenges free acid groups, preventing molecular weight loss during processing or long-term use.

Rubber and elastomer formulators incorporate it into thermoplastic polyurethane and polylactic acid compounds where moisture exposure would otherwise accelerate chain scission.

Coating and adhesive manufacturers use it as a crosslinker for waterborne systems containing carboxyl-functional resins, improving film durability and chemical resistance.

It is also used in fiber and film production where maintaining mechanical performance under humid or elevated-temperature conditions is a processing requirement.

Triisopropylbenzene polycarbodiimide is supplied as a solid, typically in granule or flake form, suited for melt compounding and masterbatch preparation.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications typically defined by carbodiimide equivalent weight and residual isocyanate content.

It bridges oil and water phases in complex formulations while improving spreadability and surface coverage. In personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning emollient and co-solvent in serums and lotions.

This ingredient helps to solubilize active ingredients and fragrance components without leaving a greasy residue. Coating and adhesive formulators use it to improve substrate wetting and dispersion of pigments.

It is particularly effective on low-energy surfaces for resins. In textile and leather processing, it aids in the uniform penetration of dyes and finishing agents, improving treatment consistency across fiber surfaces.

It also serves as a carrier solvent in sealant and elastomer systems where controlled evaporation is required. This ensures compatibility with polymer matrices during the manufacturing and application processes.

name: Dioctyl maleate

Dioctyl maleate ( CAS 2915-53-9 ), also known as DOM, is a reactive diester monomer used as both a plasticizer and a copolymerizable building block in polymer systems.

Unlike conventional plasticizers, it can be chemically incorporated into polymer backbones, reducing migration and improving long-term performance in finished materials.

In coatings and adhesives, DOM is copolymerized with acrylates, vinyl acetate, or styrene to modify film flexibility and adhesion characteristics without sacrificing durability.

Sealant and elastomer formulators use it to improve elongation and low-temperature compliance in cured systems. In PVC and other thermoplastic compounds, it functions as a reactive plasticizer.

Printing ink and packaging adhesive manufacturers incorporate it into emulsion polymerization processes to control rheology and substrate bonding in flexible laminate constructions.

Dodecyl benzoate (CAS 2915-72-2 ), also known as lauryl benzoate, is an ester used across personal care, lubricant, and polymer applications. It functions as a carrier, plasticizer, and lubricating agent.

Water treatment programs rely on it to inhibit calcium carbonate and calcium phosphate scale in cooling towers, boilers, and process water circuits. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of industrial equipment.

In textile and paper processing, it prevents metal-catalyzed degradation of bleaching baths and dye liquors, protecting product consistency. This is vital for maintaining high-quality standards in manufacturing.

It dissolves hair at or below the skin surface without mechanical action. Textile processors use it to chemically modify wool fiber structure, enabling controlled shrink-proofing treatments.

This chemical also improves dye uptake uniformity in various textile applications. In leather processing, it supports unhairing and fiber relaxation during beam house operations.

Using this agent helps in reducing reliance on sulfide-based alternatives in industrial settings. Paper and specialty fiber applications use it as a reducing agent for protein-containing substrates.

Calcium Thioglycolate Trihydrate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications for formulators.

These grades meet the requirements of personal care formulators and industrial processors respectively. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to bulk industrial quantities.

name: Polyglycerol polyricinoleate
description:
Polyglycerol polyricinoleate (CAS 29894-35-7 ), commonly identified as PGPR or E476 , is a food-grade emulsifier derived from polyglycerol esters of polycondensed fatty acids from castor oil.

It reduces viscosity in fat-based systems and controls the interaction between water droplets and continuous fat phases. These functions directly affect processing efficiency and end-product texture.

In chocolate and compound coatings, PGPR reduces flow resistance during enrobing and moulding. This allows manufacturers to lower cocoa butter content without sacrificing coverage quality.

Confectionery fillings and fat-based spreads use it to stabilize water-in-oil emulsions and prevent phase separation. In bakery applications, it improves the workability of fat-based icings.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a lipophilic emulsifier and rheology modifier in anhydrous systems. It is frequently used in low-water products such as lip products and skin balms.

PGPR is supplied as a viscous amber liquid or semi-solid, depending on temperature and formulation. Food-grade material is available to FCC and E476 specifications for global use.

Purity and acid value parameters are aligned to regulatory requirements in the EU, US, and Codex Alimentarius markets. Technical-grade material is available for non-food industrial applications.

name: Ferrous gluconate
description:
Ferrous gluconate (CAS 299-29-6 ), also known as E579 and marketed historically under the name Cerevon, is an iron(II) salt of gluconic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

This prevents oxidative discoloration during canning and packaging. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a bioavailable iron supplement active in oral dosage forms including tablets, capsules, and liquid tonics.

These products typically target iron-deficiency indications. In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it acts as a chelating agent to sequester trace metals that would otherwise destabilize emulsions.

This prevents the acceleration of rancidity in various topical products. Food and beverage producers also apply it as a pH buffer and mineral fortification ingredient in functional drinks and enriched products.

Ferrous gluconate is supplied as a fine yellowish-grey powder or granules. Established grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , with food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications being the most prevalent.

name: Phenyltrimethoxysilane
description:

In adhesives and sealants, it functions as a crosslinking agent that enhances bond durability to glass, metal, and ceramic surfaces. This versatility allows for stronger structural integrity in demanding environmental conditions.

Plastics compounders incorporate it as a coupling agent to improve filler-matrix adhesion in reinforced polymer systems. This process optimizes the mechanical properties and chemical resistance of the final composite materials.

The product is supplied as a liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial synthesis and surface treatment applications. It is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols for organosilicon compounds.

name: Lead(II) 2-ethylhexanoate
description:
Lead(II) 2-ethylhexanoate (CAS 301-08-6 ), also known as Lead Octoate, is an organolead carboxylate used industrially as a catalyst, plasticizer, and lubrication additive.

It delivers controlled metal content in organic matrices, making it a functional component in polymer processing and surface coating systems for various industrial applications.

In coatings and resin systems, Lead Octoate acts as a drier catalyst, accelerating oxidative crosslinking in alkyd and oil-based formulations to achieve faster film cure and durability.

Polymer processors use it as a heat stabilizer and plasticizer in PVC compounding, where it improves thermal processing tolerance and flexibility in finished profiles and sheeting.

In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it functions as an extreme-pressure additive, reducing metal-on-metal wear under high-load conditions for heavy machinery.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it into curing systems where controlled lead content supports polymerization rate and bond development across different substrates.

Lead(II) 2-ethylhexanoate is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically in concentrations ranging from 24% to 36% lead content by weight with the Pb-36 designation indicating 36% lead.

The product is available in Technical grade as the standard commercial specification. Packaging is available in drums and intermediate bulk containers for industrial procurement.

name: Stannous octoate
description:
Stannous octoate (CAS 301-10-0 ), also known as stannous 2-ethylhexanoate, is an organotin compound used as a catalyst across polyurethane, silicone, and polymer manufacturing.

It accelerates curing and polymerization reactions, enabling controlled chain growth and cross-linking in industrial production processes. In polyurethane foam and elastomer manufacturing, it catalyzes the reaction between polyols and isocyanates.

This material controls gel time and cell structure in both flexible and rigid foam systems. Silicone rubber producers rely on it to cure RTV formulations, where reaction rate and final mechanical properties depend on catalyst selection.

In polylactic acid (PLA) and other biodegradable polymer synthesis, it initiates ring-opening polymerization of lactide monomers. This makes it a standard catalyst choice for modern bioplastics production and development.

Coatings and sealant formulators use it to tune pot life and through-cure speed in moisture-cure and two-component systems. It is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid, typically at concentrations of 95% and above.

It is available in technical grade , with purity and tin content specified as primary quality parameters. Packaging ranges from small drums to IBC containers to suit both laboratory-scale and bulk industrial procurement.

name: Diammonium citrate
description:
Diammonium citrate (CAS 3012-65-5 ), also known as dibasic ammonium citrate, is a water-soluble ammonium salt of citric acid used across food, personal care, and industrial applications. It serves as a buffering agent, chelator, and pH regulator.

This chemical controls acidity in formulations and binds metal ions that would otherwise destabilize finished products. In food and beverage production, it functions as an acidulant and buffering salt to maintain target pH ranges during processing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products where metal ion sequestration prevents discoloration and preservative degradation. This ensures the long-term stability and aesthetic quality of cosmetic formulations.

Water treatment applications rely on its chelating action to complex calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions. This process significantly improves the overall performance and efficiency of various industrial treatment chemicals.

It also appears in fertilizer formulations as a soluble nitrogen and citrate source compatible with micronutrient blends. This versatility makes it a valuable component in modern agricultural and horticultural nutrient management systems.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, while technical-grade product is offered for industrial and agricultural use to meet specific requirements.

Bulk supply is standard in 25 kg bags, with larger packaging available for industrial volumes. We ensure consistent quality and reliable logistics for all global shipments of this essential chemical compound.

Plastics processors incorporate it into polyolefins and engineering polymers where high processing temperatures would degrade conventional yellow pigments. Printing ink formulators use it in packaging inks, particularly solvent-based and UV-curable systems.

name: Potassium cocoyl glycinate
description:
Potassium cocoyl glycinate (CAS 301341-58-2 ) is an amino acid-based surfactant derived from glycine and coconut fatty acids. It functions as a mild cleansing and foaming agent, favored in personal care formulations where skin compatibility and low irritation potential drive ingredient selection.

In facial cleansers and foaming washes, it delivers effective cleansing with a dense, stable foam profile suited to sensitive and compromised skin formulations. Shampoos and scalp care products use it to balance cleansing performance with scalp tolerance.

This ingredient is often used in combination with other sulfate-free surfactants to enhance performance. It also supports emulsification and dispersion in leave-on and rinse-off formulations where uniform ingredient distribution is required.

Body washes and baby care products rely on it as a primary or co-surfactant to meet low-irritancy positioning claims. Its gentle nature makes it a preferred choice for high-end dermatological applications and premium consumer goods.

Potassium cocoyl glycinate is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content typically in the 30–40% range. It is available in cosmetic-grade quality aligned with personal care industry standards for safety and efficacy.

The material ensures compliance with major international cosmetic ingredient regulations for global distribution. Packaging is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for commercial supply volumes and industrial use.

name: Hydrazine
description:
Hydrazine (CAS 302-01-2 ), also referred to commercially as N2H4, is a reactive inorganic base and reducing agent used across chemical synthesis, energy, and industrial process industries.

It functions primarily as a chemical building block, corrosion inhibitor, and oxygen scavenger in demanding industrial environments. In pharmaceutical and agrochemical manufacturing, it is a critical intermediate.

This compound is essential in the synthesis of active ingredients, including antituberculosis drugs, herbicides, and plant growth regulators. Boiler and feedwater treatment operations rely on it as an oxygen scavenger.

It is used to prevent corrosion in high-pressure steam systems across power generation and oil and gas facilities. Textile and paper processing industries use it as a reducing agent in dye synthesis and bleaching.

It also serves as a polymerization initiator and chain extender in the production of specialty polymers and foaming agents such as azodicarbonamide. Hydrazine is supplied commercially as an aqueous solution.

Hydrazine hydrate, at approximately 64% and 80% concentrations, represents the most widely traded forms. Anhydrous hydrazine is available for specialized industrial and aerospace applications where water content is minimized.

Technical and industrial grades are standard for most applications. Buyers in pharmaceutical synthesis typically require documentation supporting manufacturing that is compliant with USP or Ph.Eur. standards.

Quality assurance is vital for these high-purity applications. Suppliers ensure that the material meets the rigorous specifications required for complex chemical synthesis and large-scale industrial utility.

name: DL-alanine
description:
DL-Alanine (CAS 302-72-7 ), the racemic form of alanine, is a non-essential amino acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, flavor modifier, and moisturizing agent in finished formulations.

In food and beverage production, this amino acid improves taste profile by moderating bitterness and enhancing savory notes in seasonings, sauces, and processed foods. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a buffering agent in parenteral solutions.

Stable pH control is critical to product integrity in oral dosage forms. In personal care, it is used in skin-conditioning formulations, particularly moisturizers and hair care products, where its humectant properties support water retention.

It also appears in peptide synthesis as a building block where stereoselectivity is not required, reducing input costs compared to enantiopure grades. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for diverse industrial applications.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) specifications, with selection driven by the regulatory requirements of the target application.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement, with smaller packaging options for R&D and specialty formulation use. This ensures that manufacturers can source the material according to their specific production scale and needs.

description:
Diethylamino hydroxybenzoyl hexyl benzoate (CAS 302776-68-7 ), widely recognized in the industry by its abbreviation DHHB, is an oil-soluble UVA filter used in sunscreen and cosmetic formulations.

It helps meet regulatory SPF and UVA protection requirements in leave-on products such as sunscreens, day creams, and foundations. Its oil solubility makes it suitable for anhydrous and emulsion systems.

In plastics and polymer applications, it functions as a light stabilizer to prevent UV-induced degradation in films, coatings, and molded parts. This ensures long-term durability for industrial materials.

Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate it to extend the service life of UV-sensitive substrates exposed to outdoor weathering. This prevents yellowing and structural failure in various applications.

The product is supplied as a pale yellow to yellow powder or as a solution pre-dispersed in cosmetic-grade emollients for easier incorporation. It is available in cosmetic-grade purity, typically at ≥98%.
