It serves as a consumer-facing differentiator in eye contour products. Pharmaceutical-grade material is used in adjunct therapy formulations, particularly in oral dosage forms where precise potency drives sourcing.

Food and supplement manufacturers also use solubilized forms such as Q-Gel to improve bioavailability. This is essential in finished products where absorption performance is a primary formulation requirement.

name: Pentamethyldiethylenetriamine
description:
Pentamethyldiethylenetriamine (CAS 3030-47-5 ), commonly abbreviated as PMDETA, is a tertiary triamine used primarily as a ligand and catalyst in controlled radical polymerization and polyurethane systems.

Its ability to coordinate with metal centers makes it a key enabler in atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) processes and amine-catalyzed cure reactions in various industrial sectors.

In polymer manufacturing, PMDETA functions as a ligand for copper catalysts in ATRP, enabling precise molecular weight control in the production of specialty acrylates, methacrylates, and block copolymers.

Polyurethane formulators use it as a tertiary amine catalyst to balance gel and blow reactions in flexible and rigid foam systems, as well as in coatings and adhesives for construction.

In epoxy and sealant formulations, it accelerates cure at ambient or elevated temperatures, supporting faster line speeds in industrial bonding applications and high-performance manufacturing environments.

Water treatment chemical producers also employ it as a building block in the synthesis of chelating agents and corrosion inhibitors, expanding its utility beyond traditional polymer science.

PMDETA is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purity levels, typically 98% or higher. Technical grade is the predominant specification available in the market, supplied in drums or IBCs.

It is not commonly offered in food or pharmaceutical grades, and sourcing is primarily directed toward industrial and research applications requiring high-performance chemical intermediates.

description:
2,4-Decadienoic acid (CAS 30361-33-2 ) is a straight-chain unsaturated fatty acid used as a flavoring agent in food and fragrance applications. It contributes characteristic fatty, waxy, and citrus-like notes that replicate natural flavor profiles.

In food manufacturing, it is used to build or reinforce citrus, orange peel, and fatty top notes in beverages, confectionery, and savory flavor systems. Flavor houses incorporate it into reconstituted natural flavor blends where authentic fruit character is required.

It also finds use in fragrance compounding, where its waxy-green profile supports citrus and floral accords in fine fragrance and functional fragrance applications. This versatile ingredient is essential for creating complex aromatic structures.

As an acidulant with flavor-active properties, it can serve a dual role in formulations requiring both pH contribution and sensory impact. This makes it a valuable tool for product developers seeking multi-functional chemical components.

2,4-Decadienoic acid is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on purity and storage conditions. It is available in flavor and fragrance grade suitable for use in food-contact applications.

name: Sodium myristoyl sarcosinate
description:
Sodium myristoyl sarcosinate (CAS 30364-51-3 ) is a mild amino acid-derived surfactant used in personal care and cosmetic formulations. Based on the sarcosine backbone with a C14 fatty acid chain, it delivers cleansing and foaming performance.

This ingredient remains compatible with sensitive-skin positioning while providing conditioning benefits. Formulators value it for its low irritation profile relative to conventional sulfate surfactants used in the industry.

In facial and body cleansers, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant, generating a dense, stable foam while conditioning the skin during rinse-off. It helps maintain the skin barrier during the cleaning process.

Toothpaste and oral care products use it as a foaming and cleansing agent. Its compatibility with fluoride systems and low bitterness make it a preferred alternative to sodium lauryl sulfate in many dental applications.

Shampoos and scalp treatments incorporate it to boost lather and improve wet-combing feel without stripping natural oils. It also appears in shaving preparations where mildness and emulsification must be balanced.

Sodium myristoyl sarcosinate is commercially supplied as a powder or as an aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically around 30%. Standard grades include cosmetic/personal care grade for topical use.

name: Sodium vinylsulfonate
description:
Sodium vinylsulfonate (CAS 3039-83-6 ), commonly abbreviated as SVS, is a reactive monomer used as a building block in polymer synthesis and surface modification chemistry.

It introduces permanent sulfonate functionality into polymer chains, enabling performance characteristics that drive demand across water treatment, textile processing, and specialty coatings.

In water treatment, SVS is copolymerized into scale inhibitors and dispersants that prevent mineral deposit buildup in industrial cooling systems and boilers.

Textile and paper processors incorporate SVS-based polymers to improve dye uptake uniformity and wet fastness on fiber surfaces during the manufacturing process.

In the plastics and polymer industry, it functions as a comonomer in the production of ion-exchange resins, antistatic coatings, and hydrophilic membrane materials.

Leather finishing formulations use SVS copolymers to achieve durable surface treatments with improved adhesion and water resistance for high-quality consumer goods.

Sodium vinylsulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 25% or 30% active content, which is the standard commercial form for handling and direct use.

Technical grade is the predominant specification available in the market. It is packaged in drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes.

name: Potassium sodium tartrate
description:
Potassium sodium tartrate (CAS 304-59-6 ), commercially known as Rochelle salt or E337 , is a double salt of tartaric acid used primarily as a buffering agent and sequestrant.

Its ability to stabilize pH and chelate metal ions makes it a functional ingredient in formulations where consistency and shelf stability are critical across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food production, E337 functions as a stabilizer and emulsifying salt in processed cheese, where it controls texture and prevents fat separation during the manufacturing process.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent in oral solutions and effervescent formulations to maintain target pH ranges and ensure the stability of active ingredients.

In personal care, it appears in creams and lotions as a chelating agent, neutralizing trace metals that would otherwise accelerate oxidative degradation of the final product.

It also serves as a laxative active in certain over-the-counter preparations, where regulatory-grade purity is a sourcing requirement for manufacturers and compounding pharmacies.

Potassium sodium tartrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. It is available in food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and BP / Ph.Eur. grades to meet compliance requirements.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags, with documentation packages supporting food and pharmaceutical applications to ensure full traceability and quality assurance.

name: L-Carnosine
description:
L-Carnosine (CAS 305-84-0 ), also marketed under the trade name Dragosine, is a naturally occurring dipeptide used as an antioxidant and stabilizing agent across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic formulations.

It protects sensitive ingredients and biological tissues from oxidative degradation, making it a valued functional ingredient where shelf-life extension and cellular protection are formulation priorities.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it is incorporated into capsules, tablets, and functional beverages targeting cognitive and muscle health positioning for various consumer markets.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it to stabilize active compounds against oxidative and carbonyl stress in both oral and topical drug products, ensuring long-term stability and efficacy of the final product.

In personal care, Dragosine is used in anti-aging skin care formulations for its ability to suppress glycation-related degradation of skin proteins, supporting high-performance product efficacy claims.

Food producers apply it as an antioxidant in processed and functional food products where clean-label, naturally derived stabilizers are preferred for modern consumer demands and regulatory compliance.

L-Carnosine is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with USP and Ph.Eur. grades accessible for regulated applications.

Purity levels of 98% and above are standard for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical procurement, meeting the rigorous quality requirements of global chemical distribution and manufacturing standards.

name: Zidovudine
description:
Zidovudine (CAS 30516-87-1 ), also known as AZT and marketed under the brand name Retrovir®, is an antiretroviral nucleoside analogue used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in HIV treatment formulations.

It functions as a reverse transcriptase inhibitor, blocking viral replication at the enzymatic level and forming the basis of combination antiretroviral therapy regimens for patients worldwide.

The primary application is as an API in oral solid and liquid dosage forms, including tablets, capsules, and syrups, manufactured for HIV/AIDS treatment protocols in the pharmaceutical industry.

Zidovudine is also incorporated into fixed-dose combination products alongside other antiretrovirals, requiring precise blending and compatibility assessment during the formulation development process.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers sourcing it as an intermediate use it in the synthesis of combination drug substances subject to stringent regulatory review and high quality control standards.

Research institutions and generic drug developers procure it as a reference standard or starting material for bioequivalence and stability studies to ensure therapeutic efficacy and safety.

Zidovudine is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades to meet the documentation requirements of regulated markets.

Quantities range from research-scale to commercial bulk, with full batch documentation typically required by regulated-market buyers to ensure compliance with international manufacturing guidelines.

name: Paraformaldehyde
description:
Paraformaldehyde (CAS 30525-89-4 ), also known commercially as Paraform, PFA, and Aldacide, is the solid polymerized form of formaldehyde used as a controlled-release formaldehyde source in industrial synthesis and preservation.

It functions as a cross-linking agent, curing component, and biocide across a broad range of manufacturing processes. In plastics and resins manufacturing, PFA is a key raw material for producing phenol-formaldehyde resins.

These are used in urea-formaldehyde and melamine-formaldehyde resins for adhesives, laminates, and molding compounds. Agricultural formulators use it as a soil and seed disinfectant for effective antimicrobial action.

Its slow formaldehyde release provides protection without rapid volatilization. In textile and leather processing, it cross-links fibers and tanning agents to improve dimensional stability and durability of finished goods.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on PFA as a synthesis intermediate and laboratory fixative. Precise formaldehyde delivery is critical to process consistency and meeting high-quality USP or Ph.Eur. standards.

Paraformaldehyde is supplied as a white powder or granules, with granular forms preferred for handling and dust reduction. Standard commercial grades include 91–93% and 95–96% purity levels for various uses.

Technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet different regulatory requirements. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities for high-volume industrial procurement needs.

name: Triethylene glycol monododecyl ether
description:

It is frequently used in degreasers and laundry products where low-foam or controlled-foam profiles are required. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as an emulsifier and solubilizer in creams and lotions.

The compound is also utilized in rinse-off products for its gentle properties. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a wetting and scouring agent to improve substrate penetration during preparation.

It is highly effective during dyeing stages to ensure even color distribution. In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a dispersing aid and wetting agent to improve pigment distribution and adhesion.

Triethylene glycol monododecyl ether is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste depending on temperature and concentration. It is available in technical grade for industrial and cleaning applications.

The material is also offered as cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care use. Bulk supply is standard in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for large scale manufacturing.

name: Glyceryl monothioglycolate

Its free sulfhydryl group enables controlled disulfide bond cleavage, making it the active component in permanent wave and hair relaxer formulations as well as fiber and substrate treatment processes.

In professional and retail hair care, it is the primary active in acid-wave permanent waving systems, where it breaks and reforms keratin disulfide bonds to reshape hair structure.

Textile processors apply it to wool and protein fibers to improve dye uptake and surface uniformity during wet finishing. In leather processing, it functions as a depilatory and fiber-opening agent.

This chemical supports consistent hide preparation ahead of tanning. Paper and specialty substrate treatments use it to modify surface chemistry for improved adhesion or coating receptivity.

This versatile chemical enables stable blending of oil and water phases in complex formulations. In food manufacturing, it controls starch retrogradation in baked goods and improves texture consistency in margarine and ice cream.

name: Polydioxanone
description:
Polydioxanone (CAS 31621-87-1 ), also referenced commercially as Resomer X 210 and Resomer X 206S, is a biodegradable, absorbable polyester polymer used across medical device manufacturing and pharmaceutical applications.

It degrades predictably in biological environments through hydrolysis, making it a controlled-release and structural material of choice where temporary implantation is required for patients.

Polydioxanone is the base material for absorbable monofilament sutures, where its flexibility and sustained tensile strength retention over several weeks meet the mechanical demands of soft tissue approximation.

In drug delivery, it is processed into fibers, films, and microspheres designed to release active pharmaceutical ingredients over defined timeframes without requiring surgical removal of the device.

Medical device manufacturers use it to produce bone fixation pins, cardiovascular stents, and scaffolds for tissue engineering applications. Biotechnology researchers also select it as a matrix polymer.

It is frequently used for electrospun membranes in wound care and regenerative medicine platforms. Polydioxanone is supplied as a solid polymer, typically in pellet or powder form for industrial use.

It occurs naturally as a byproduct of wine production and is also produced synthetically for commercial supply. In food processing, it functions as an acidity regulator in beverages and confectionery.

It is widely used in baked goods where controlled tartness and stable pH are required. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in tablet formulations to maintain active ingredient stability.

Its buffering capacity is essential for high-quality medicinal products. It also serves as a calcium fortification source in functional food and nutraceutical products targeting mineral supplementation.

In winemaking, calcium tartrate is recovered and refined as a raw material feedstock for tartaric acid production. This versatile compound is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the most commonly traded form. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to BP or Ph. Eur. standards for regulated applications.

It functions as a reactive metal carboxylate capable of delivering potassium ions in solution-phase reactions and formulation systems. In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a catalyst or co-catalyst in polyurethane systems.

This film reduces friction, improves combability, and enhances shine in conditioners, serums, and leave-on treatments. Textile and leather finishers apply it to impart soft hand feel and water repellency.

In automotive and industrial coatings, it functions as a surface leveling and wetting agent, reducing surface tension to prevent cratering and improve film uniformity across various substrates.

Sealant and elastomer manufacturers incorporate it as a reactive intermediate or plasticizer where terminal hydroxyl groups enable crosslinking with silicone networks for enhanced durability.

This material improves the spreadability of creams, lotions, and serums. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solubilizing carrier for active ingredients in topical and semi-solid dosage forms.

It improves API dispersion without the need for harsh solvents. In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a reactive diluent and rheology modifier, adjusting viscosity and improving substrate wetting.

name: Thiencarbazone-methyl
description:
Thiencarbazone-methyl (CAS 317815-83-1 ) is a selective herbicide active ingredient belonging to the triketone and sulfonylaminocarbonyl-triazolinone chemical classes.

It is registered under the ISO common name and marketed under trade names including Velocity and Capreno. It controls a broad spectrum of grass and broadleaf weeds in cereal crops.

The compound works by inhibiting acetolactate synthase (ALS), disrupting amino acid biosynthesis in target plants. It is primarily used in winter and spring wheat, barley, and corn production.

This active ingredient provides post-emergence control of economically damaging weeds such as blackgrass, ryegrass, and volunteer cereals. In corn herbicide formulations, it is often combined with isoxaflutole.

Formulators and registrants source the technical active ingredient for development of suspension concentrate (SC) and water-dispersible granule (WG) herbicide products for global distribution.

Its ALS-inhibitor mode of action makes it relevant for resistance management programs where rotation of herbicide classes is required by modern agronomic protocols and safety standards.

Thiencarbazone-methyl is supplied as a technical-grade active ingredient, typically as a solid powder or crystalline material meeting agreed specification sheets for industrial formulation use.

Personal care formulators incorporate aminofunctional silanes into hair treatment systems to modify surface wetting and improve substantivity on damaged fiber. This application helps in creating more effective and long-lasting cosmetic products.

Aminopropylmethyldiethoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to IBC containers. Technical grade is the primary commercial form, with purity specifications typically at 97% or higher.

name: Polyhexamethylene guanidine
description:
Polyhexamethylene guanidine (CAS 31961-54-3 ), also known commercially as Polisept, is a cationic polymeric biocide effective against a broad spectrum of bacteria, fungi, and algae.

It functions as both a preservative and a coagulant-flocculant, giving formulators and process engineers a single active ingredient that addresses microbial control and particle aggregation simultaneously.

In water treatment, it is dosed to disinfect potable and process water while simultaneously flocculating suspended solids, reducing the need for separate treatment chemicals.

Personal care and cosmetics manufacturers incorporate it as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on formulations where low irritation potential is a key selection criterion for the industry.

Textile and leather processors apply it to impart durable antimicrobial finishes to fabrics and hides, extending product shelf life and meeting hygiene standards across various global markets.

Industrial and household cleaning products use it as the active biocidal component in surface disinfectants and sanitizing concentrates for both commercial and residential maintenance applications.

The product is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations typically ranging from 20% to 25% depending on the specific requirements of the end user.

Technical and industrial grades are the most commonly traded forms. Buyers sourcing for personal care or pharmaceutical end uses should confirm grade documentation and impurity profiles with the supplier.

Contact us for supply of Polyhexamethylene guanidine

name: Sodium cumenesulfonate
description:
Sodium cumenesulfonate (CAS 32073-22-6 ), also known as sodium p-cumenesulphonate, is a hydrotrope used across detergent, personal care, and industrial cleaning formulations.

It increases the solubility of other surfactants and active ingredients in aqueous systems, allowing formulators to achieve higher active concentrations without phase separation.

In liquid detergent manufacturing, it enables high-surfactant-load formulations to remain stable and pourable at elevated concentrations. This ensures product consistency during storage.

Personal care producers incorporate it into shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps to improve clarity and reduce viscosity at high surfactant levels for better performance.

In textile and leather processing, it supports the dispersion of dyes, finishing agents, and cleaning auxiliaries in aqueous baths. This improves the efficiency of the treatment.

Agricultural formulations use it as a carrier and dispersant to improve the solubility and stability of active ingredients in liquid crop protection products for better field results.

Sodium cumenesulfonate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 40% or 45% active content, and in dry powder or granule form for applications requiring low moisture content.

Standard grades include technical and industrial-grade material. Food-contact and cosmetic-grade material is available where formulation compliance requires tighter purity specifications.

name: 5-chlorosalicylic acid
description:
5-Chlorosalicylic acid (CAS 321-14-2 ), also referenced in procurement as 5-CSA, is an organochlorine derivative of salicylic acid used as a building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and as a functional additive in industrial formulations.

Its combination of phenolic and carboxylic acid groups makes it a reactive intermediate for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty performance chemicals. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, 5-CSA serves as a key intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory APIs, where controlled chlorination and hydroxyl positioning are critical to the final molecule's activity. Coating and resin formulators incorporate it as a UV stabilizer.

It also acts as an antioxidant to extend the service life of protective coatings exposed to outdoor weathering. In adhesive and sealant systems, it contributes biocidal and preservation properties that inhibit microbial degradation.

These properties help maintain the product's shelf life. Personal care formulators also evaluate it as a preservative-boosting component in leave-on and rinse-off products where broad-spectrum efficacy is required.

5-Chlorosalicylic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with pharmaceutical-grade product typically meeting defined purity thresholds.

This grade is suitable for API intermediate use. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk drum supply for industrial procurement, ensuring flexibility for various manufacturing scales and requirements.

name: L-selenomethionine
description:
L-Selenomethionine (CAS 3211-76-5 ) is the bioavailable, organically bound form of selenium used across nutritional, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. As Seleno-L-methionine, it is the preferred selenium source in dietary supplements.

It is widely used in functional food fortification due to its superior absorption compared to inorganic selenium salts. In dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, it serves as the primary active ingredient in selenium fortification products.

The compound is essential for targeting antioxidant support formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as the selenium source in micronutrient preparations, including tablets, capsules, and infusion solutions where precise dosing is critical.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it functions as an antioxidant and moisturizing agent in anti-aging creams and serums. Biotechnology and cell culture applications rely on it as a selenium supplement in growth media.

It is particularly useful where organic selenium is required for protein expression studies. L-Selenomethionine is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications.

The USP and Ph.Eur. grades are commonly sourced for regulated applications. Bulk quantities are offered for industrial formulators, with smaller research quantities available for biotechnology and laboratory use.

name: Polyoxyethylene octyldodecyl ether
description:
Polyoxyethylene octyldodecyl ether (CAS 32128-65-7 ) is a nonionic ethoxylated fatty alcohol surfactant used across personal care, cleaning, and industrial formulation.

It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and humectant, enabling stable oil-in-water systems and effective surface-active performance across a range of formulation types.

In personal care, it emulsifies oils and actives into creams, lotions, and leave-on skin formulations, contributing to smooth texture and skin feel for the end user.

Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it as a degreasing surfactant where low irritation potential and compatibility with sensitive substrates matter most.

Textile and leather processing applies it as a dispersant and wetting agent during dyeing, finishing, and treatment stages to ensure uniform application of chemicals.

In agricultural formulations, it supports emulsifiable concentrate and suspension concentrate systems where stable dispersion of active ingredients is critical for efficacy.

Polyoxyethylene octyldodecyl ether is supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation and the specific requirements of the manufacturing process.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications. Different ethoxylation levels are offered to adjust HLB values for specific formulation targets.

name: Polyethylene glycol 2-aminoethyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol 2-aminoethyl ether (CAS 32130-27-1 ) is a PEG-based amine that combines a reactive primary amine terminus with a hydroxyl-capped polyethylene oxide chain.

This dual-functional structure makes it a reactive building block for surface modification, polymer conjugation, and formulation design across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning markets.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a conditioning and moisturizing agent, improving substrate adhesion and water retention in leave-on and rinse-off products.

Textile and leather processors use it to modify fiber surfaces, enhancing dye uptake, softness, and wetting performance in finishing baths for various industrial applications.

The primary amine group enables covalent attachment to substrates or reactive intermediates, making it a functional linker in polymer crosslinking and surface grafting processes.

In industrial and household cleaning formulations, it contributes to soil dispersion and surface wetting, particularly on hard-to-wet synthetic substrates and materials.

Polyethylene glycol 2-aminoethyl ether is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous solution, with molecular weight variants available to suit different application requirements.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, though higher-purity grades are available for specialty formulation and research use in drum or IBC quantities.

name: Golpanol BEO
description:
Golpanol BEO (CAS 32167-31-0 ), also known as hydroxyethylated 2-butyne-1,4-diol, is an acetylenic diol ethoxylate supplying reactive hydroxyl functionality for polymer and coating systems.

It functions as both a crosslinker and a rheology modifier, giving formulators control over network density and flow behavior in a single building block for various industrial applications.

In polyurethane and epoxy coatings, this chemical acts as a chain extender or crosslinking diol, contributing to film hardness and chemical resistance without requiring additional rheology additives.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to tune cure density and improve substrate adhesion in structural and elastic bond lines across diverse manufacturing sectors.

In industrial cleaning formulations, its surfactant-compatible structure supports wetting and leveling performance across hard-surface products, ensuring consistent results in commercial cleaning environments.

Polymer producers also use it as a reactive monomer to introduce acetylenic backbone segments that modify flexibility and crosslink spacing in specialty elastomers and high-performance materials.

The product is supplied as a liquid and is available in technical grade, suited for industrial coating, adhesive, and polymer manufacturing processes requiring reliable chemical inputs.

Bulk and intermediate packaging options are standard across the supply chain to meet the logistical needs of large-scale chemical distributors and industrial end-users globally.

name: 4-biphenylaldehyde
description:
4-Biphenylaldehyde (CAS 3218-36-8 ), also known as 4-biphenylcarboxaldehyde, is an aromatic aldehyde used as a synthetic building block in specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its biphenyl-aldehyde structure makes it a valued intermediate for constructing complex organic molecules across polymer, fragrance, and fine chemical applications.

In polymer and materials chemistry, it serves as a monomer or crosslinking intermediate for engineering specialty resins and liquid crystal polymers where rigid aromatic backbones are required.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into fine fragrance and cosmetic compositions for its floral-aldehyde character, particularly in applications targeting premium personal care products.

In pharmaceutical and agrochemical synthesis, it functions as a key intermediate for constructing biphenyl-containing active compounds for various industrial research purposes.

Printing and packaging chemists also utilize it in the development of photoinitiator systems and UV-curable ink formulations to enhance performance in specialized coating applications.

4-Biphenylaldehyde is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is commercially available at 99% purity, which is the standard specification for synthesis-grade procurement.

Packaging is typically offered in gram to kilogram quantities, reflecting its primary positioning as a fine chemical intermediate rather than a bulk commodity for industrial use.

name: Monosodium glutamate
description:
Monosodium glutamate (CAS 32221-81-1 ), commonly known as MSG, is the sodium salt form of glutamic acid used as a flavor enhancer in food manufacturing. It amplifies savory, umami taste profiles, allowing formulators to reduce sodium content.

This versatile ingredient enhances palatability without altering base formulations. In processed food manufacturing, MSG is incorporated into soups, sauces, seasonings, and snack coatings to intensify savory flavor at low use levels.

Ready meals and meat processors apply it in marinades, cured products, and seasoning blends. This ensures consistent flavor delivery across batch production, which is critical for maintaining high industrial standards and consumer satisfaction.

In pharmaceutical applications, it functions as a buffering and taste-masking agent in oral formulations. This is particularly useful where palatability affects patient compliance and the overall effectiveness of the medicinal delivery system.

Culinary ingredient suppliers also package it as a standalone seasoning component for foodservice and retail distribution. MSG is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules with various particle size grades available.

These grades are designed to suit direct blending or specific coating applications. Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is the standard commercial form, with USP -grade available for specialized pharmaceutical use.

Bulk supply is typically offered in 25 kg bags to ensure ease of handling and storage. Larger quantities are also available in supersacks for industrial buyers requiring high-volume logistics and efficient manufacturing throughput.

name: Polyhexamethylene biguanide
description:
Polyhexamethylene biguanide (CAS 32289-58-0 ), commonly known as PHMB or polyhexanide, is a polymeric antimicrobial agent used across industrial, healthcare, and consumer applications.

It functions as a broad-spectrum biocide and preservative, effective against bacteria, fungi, and certain viruses at low use concentrations. Poly(hexamethylenebiguanide) hydrochloride is the most commercially distributed salt form.

In wound care and medical device manufacturing, polyhexanide is the active ingredient in antiseptic irrigations, wound dressings, and contact lens solutions. These applications rely on its high efficacy.

Personal care formulators incorporate PHMB as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos, wipes, and skin cleansers. It ensures product stability and consumer safety during use.

Textile and leather processors apply it to impart durable antimicrobial protection to fabrics, nonwovens, and treated surfaces. This prevents odor and degradation caused by microbial growth in materials.

Water treatment operations use PHMB to control microbial growth in swimming pools, cooling towers, and industrial process water. It serves as a stable and effective alternative to chlorine-based biocides.

Polyhexamethylene biguanide is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 20% active concentration. Grades include technical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical quality for various industrial requirements.

Buyers should confirm active content, molecular weight distribution, and regulatory compliance when sourcing. This includes checking biocidal product regulations and cosmetic approvals for regulated end uses.

name: Ornithine aspartate
description:
Ornithine aspartate (CAS 3230-94-2 ), also known as LOLA and marketed under names such as Hepamerz, is a salt formed from two amino acids used primarily in pharmaceutical manufacturing and clinical nutrition.

It functions as a metabolic agent supporting ammonia detoxification pathways, making it a target active ingredient for hepatology-focused drug development and formulation for global suppliers.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, LOLA is the active substance in infusion solutions and oral granules indicated for hepatic encephalopathy and liver dysfunction, where reducing elevated blood ammonia levels is the primary goal.

Contract formulators and API suppliers source it for finished dosage form development, including sachets, injectables, and oral liquid preparations to meet specific patient needs in clinical settings.

In clinical nutrition products, it is incorporated into specialized medical foods targeting patients with compromised liver function. Cosmetic formulators have also evaluated it as a humectant and pH-buffering agent.

While it is used in skin-conditioning formulations, pharmaceutical applications represent the dominant commercial demand. Ornithine aspartate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications aligned with in-house or compendial standards, with purity levels typically at 98% or above to meet API requirements and USP or EP quality.

Bulk quantities are offered for industrial manufacturing, with smaller research-grade quantities available for formulation development. This ensures consistency across various production scales and applications.

name: Myristyl myristate
description:
Myristyl myristate (CAS 3234-85-3 ), also known as tetradecyl tetradecanoate, is a saturated fatty acid ester derived from myristic acid and myristyl alcohol. It functions as an emollient, texture modifier, and carrier in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations.

This versatile ingredient contributes a dry, non-greasy skin feel that distinguishes it from heavier ester alternatives. In skin and body care products, including lotions and creams, it improves spreadability and delivers a smooth, velvety after-feel.

Color cosmetics manufacturers use it as a binder and texture agent in lipsticks, foundations, and eyeshadow compacts. In these applications, it helps control hardness and pigment dispersion while ensuring a consistent application for the end user.

Solid and semi-solid pharmaceutical topical formulations incorporate it as a carrier to adjust consistency and support active ingredient delivery. It also appears in hair care products such as conditioners and styling waxes to aid slip.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid or flake. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter meeting USP or Ph.Eur. standards where required by the manufacturer.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale bags to bulk pallet quantities to suit both development and commercial production volumes. This ensures flexibility for companies operating at various stages of the product lifecycle.

name: Decyldimethyloctylammonium chloride
description:
Decyldimethyloctylammonium chloride (CAS 32426-11-2 ), also known commercially as Quaternium-24, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a biocidal active and conditioning surfactant across personal care, cleaning, and industrial applications.

Its cationic charge drives both antimicrobial performance and surface substantivity, making it a functional ingredient where dual-action formulation efficiency matters. In home care and institutional cleaning products, it delivers broad-spectrum bactericidal activity.

It provides fungicidal activity in surface disinfectants, sanitizing sprays, and hard-surface cleaners. Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products, particularly conditioning treatments and scalp-care formulations.

In these applications, antimicrobial preservation and hair substantivity are required simultaneously. Water treatment applications leverage its biocidal properties to control microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water circuits.

It also appears in industrial disinfectant concentrates where compatibility with other quaternary ammonium actives allows blended formulations to meet broader efficacy standards. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Decyldimethyloctylammonium chloride is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations commonly ranging around 50% or 80%. Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for most buyers.

Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care applications requiring specific purity. Packaging options generally include drums and IBCs to support both formulation-scale and bulk procurement needs for global distribution.

name: Bis(2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl) phosphate
description:
Bis(2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl) phosphate (CAS 32435-46-4 ) is a bifunctional phosphate monomer combining a reactive methacrylate group with a pendant phosphate moiety. It is recognized in procurement as bis(methacryloyloxyethyl) hydrogen phosphate.

The phosphate functionality delivers flame retardancy and surface adhesion promotion directly within a polymerizable matrix. This eliminates the need for separate additive packages in many industrial formulations.

In UV- and thermally-cured coatings, it acts as a reactive flame-retardant monomer that becomes chemically bound into the polymer network. This prevents plasticizer-style migration losses over time in the finished product.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to improve bonding to metal and mineral substrates. The phosphate group coordinates with surface oxides to enhance adhesion without the requirement of a separate primer layer.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it supports substrate wetting and anchorage on difficult surfaces. This is particularly effective for applications involving aluminum foil and various treated films.

Polymer compounders incorporate it as a co-monomer to introduce inherent flame retardancy into acrylic systems. These materials are frequently targeted at demanding electronics and construction applications.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically with an inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial users.

Purity specifications are commonly confirmed by acid value and phosphorus content assays. Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D sampling to bulk drum supply for large-scale industrial formulation.

Glucuronolactone (CAS 32449-92-6 ), also known as D-Glucurono-6,3-lactone and D-Glucurone, is a naturally occurring compound derived from glucose metabolism. It is used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing as a functional ingredient.

The compound offers antioxidant, moisturizing, and surface-active properties for various industrial applications. In energy drinks and functional beverages, it is included as an active nutritional ingredient often alongside taurine and caffeine.

These formulations target cognitive and physical performance claims for the consumer market. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a detoxification-support compound in tablet and capsule products for liver health categories.

Its role in glucuronidation pathways supports specific product positioning in the health supplement sector. In cosmetic formulations, it functions as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in serums, creams, and toners.

Its ability to attract and retain moisture improves skin feel and overall product stability. It also appears in topical formulations requiring mild surface-wetting behavior to improve ingredient distribution across the skin.

name: Copper nitrate
description:
Copper nitrate (CAS 3251-23-8 ), also sold as cupric nitrate, is an inorganic copper salt used industrially as an oxidizing agent, catalyst precursor, and biocidal active.

It delivers soluble copper ion in concentrated, reactive form across a broad range of manufacturing and treatment processes. In water treatment, it functions as a biocide and algaecide.

It is used for controlling microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water circuits. Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant and surface treatment agent.

This helps to fix dyes and impart antimicrobial finishes to finished goods. In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as a copper precursor for preparing supported metal oxide catalysts.

These catalysts are used in chemical synthesis and emissions control. Agriculture applications include its use as a micronutrient copper source in foliar sprays and soil correction.

These programs target copper-deficient crops. Copper nitrate is supplied as blue crystalline trihydrate or hexahydrate solids, with the trihydrate being the most prevalent form.

Technical grade is standard for industrial and agricultural supply, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%. Bulk quantities are available in bags or drums.

name: Dipotassium guanylate
description:
Dipotassium guanylate (CAS 3254-39-5 ), also designated E628 , is the dipotassium salt of guanylic acid used as a flavor enhancer in food manufacturing. It amplifies savory, umami taste profiles, typically in combination with other nucleotides.

This additive works with glutamates to achieve synergistic flavor intensification at low use levels. In processed food production, E628 is incorporated into soups, broths, seasonings, and snack coatings to boost umami depth without increasing sodium content.

Instant noodle and bouillon manufacturers use it alongside monosodium glutamate or disodium inosinate to deliver consistent flavor profiles at reduced additive loads. This efficiency makes it a preferred choice for large-scale industrial food production.

In meat processing, it supports flavor retention in cured and restructured products where taste consistency across batches is a formulation priority. It ensures that the savory profile remains stable throughout the shelf life of the product.

Pharmaceutical applications include use as a nucleotide source in specialized nutritional preparations and oral formulations where palatability enhancement is required. It helps mask bitter notes and improves the overall patient experience with oral medications.

Dipotassium guanylate is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade material conforming to E628 purity specifications is the standard commercial form available to food manufacturers and formulators globally.

It is typically offered in bulk quantities suited to industrial seasoning and flavor blending operations. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure it meets the necessary regulatory requirements for food and pharma use.

name: Ammonium laureth sulfate
description:
Ammonium laureth sulfate (CAS 32612-48-9 ), commonly abbreviated as ALES, is an ethoxylated anionic surfactant used as a primary cleansing and foaming agent in personal care formulations.

It delivers effective soil and sebum removal while producing a dense, stable lather that consumers associate with product performance. In shampoos and body washes, ALES functions as the primary surfactant.

It generates the foam volume and cleansing action required in rinse-off formats. Its ethoxylated structure makes it milder than non-ethoxylated alternatives, positioning it for sensitive-skin and mild-formula product lines.

It is also incorporated into liquid hand soaps and facial cleansers where compatibility with secondary surfactants and conditioning agents is a formulation priority for the manufacturer.

In light-duty household cleaning liquids, ALES contributes both degreasing performance and emulsification of oily soils. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient in many industrial cleaning applications.

Ammonium laureth sulfate is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous solution, typically at 25–30% active matter concentration. Standard commercial grades are available for personal care and cosmetic applications.

Suppliers commonly offer material conforming to cosmetic-grade specifications. Buyers should confirm ethoxylation degree and active content when evaluating lots for their specific production needs.

These parameters directly affect formulation performance and cost-in-use. Proper storage in a cool, dry place is recommended to maintain the stability and efficacy of the surfactant over time.

name: Potassium propionate
description:
Potassium propionate (CAS 327-62-8 ), also known by its food additive designation E283 , is the potassium salt of propionic acid used as a preservative in food and agricultural applications.

It inhibits mold and bacterial growth, extending shelf life across a range of perishable products without the sodium load associated with sodium propionate alternatives.

In baked goods, E283 is applied to bread, cakes, and pastries to suppress mold development and extend retail shelf life. Feed manufacturers incorporate it into animal nutrition products.

This is particularly useful in poultry and swine feeds to control microbial contamination during storage and transport. Food processors handling dairy-adjacent products use it as a mold inhibitor.

It is ideal for processed cheese formulations where sodium content must be minimized. It also functions as a grain preservative in agricultural storage, protecting harvested crops from fungal spoilage.

Potassium propionate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granular forms preferred in feed applications for ease of blending during the manufacturing process.

Standard grades include food-grade specifications aligned with FCC and E283 regulatory requirements. Technical-grade material is available for agricultural and non-food preservation uses.

name: Bromochlorodimethylhydantoin
description:
Bromochlorodimethylhydantoin ( CAS 32718-18-6 ), commonly known as BCDMH, is a halogen-release biocide used to control microbial growth in water systems and formulated products.

It delivers both bromine and chlorine upon dissolution, providing broad-spectrum disinfection across a range of pH conditions. In water treatment, it is the active disinfectant in cooling towers.

Swimming pools and spa systems utilize this compound where controlled halogen release maintains effective sanitization without the handling risks of liquid chlorine or other volatile gases.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative in rinse-off products such as shampoos and body washes. Its dual-halogen activity targets bacteria and fungi at low use concentrations.

Industrial and institutional cleaning products use it as a bleaching and sanitizing agent in hard surface disinfectants and laundry formulations to ensure high hygiene standards.

In healthcare settings, it is used in instrument disinfection and surface sanitization applications requiring reliable broad-spectrum efficacy and consistent performance in various environments.

BCDMH is supplied as compressed tablets, granules, and powder to suit different dosing equipment. Standard grades include technical and water treatment grades for industrial use.

Tablet forms are commonly available in various sizes for automated feeders. Purity specifications typically range from 96% to 99% active content depending on the intended application.

name: Pivaloyl chloride
description:
Pivaloyl chloride (CAS 3282-30-2 ), also known as trimethylacetyl chloride, is a reactive acylating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

It introduces the pivaloyl protecting group or activates carboxylic acid derivatives for downstream coupling reactions. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it activates amino acids and carboxylic acids to form mixed anhydrides.

This process enables efficient peptide bond formation and API synthesis. Agrochemical producers use it to manufacture herbicide and pesticide esters, where the bulky pivaloyl group improves hydrolytic stability.

The compound functions as a catalyst precursor in Ziegler-Natta polymerization systems. In these applications, pivaloyl-based compounds influence catalyst activity and polymer tacticity during the manufacturing process.

Contract synthesis and fine chemical operations also rely on it for acylation steps in multi-stage routes to complex intermediates. It is a versatile building block for high-value chemical production.

Pivaloyl chloride is supplied as a liquid in standard packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums. Technical and synthesis-grade material is the primary commercial form available.

Purity specifications are typically at 98% or higher for industrial use. Buyers should confirm moisture-controlled packaging requirements, as the product is sensitive to hydrolysis during storage and transit.

name: Cholesteryl dichlorobenzoate
description:
Cholesteryl dichlorobenzoate (CAS 32832-01-2 ) is a cholesterol ester derivative used as a specialty intermediate in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research. It functions as a liquid crystal-forming compound and a structural building block in the synthesis of cholesterol-based materials.

In pharmaceutical research, it serves as an intermediate in the development of cholesterol-conjugated drug delivery systems, where controlled esterification chemistry is required. Liquid crystal research relies on this compound to produce thermotropic cholesteric phases.

These phases are evaluated for use in optical and sensing applications. Biotechnology workflows use cholesteryl esters of this type as reference standards or model compounds when studying membrane interactions and lipid-based formulation behavior.

It also appears in the preparation of functionalized cholesterol derivatives for use in nucleic acid delivery and liposomal system development. This material is essential for researchers focusing on advanced delivery mechanisms.

Cholesteryl dichlorobenzoate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available primarily in research and specialty quantities, with purity grades typically at 97% or higher to meet laboratory and synthesis requirements.

Packaging is generally offered in gram to multi-gram scales suited to pharmaceutical research and development procurement. This ensures that the material meets the specific needs of high-precision laboratory environments and pilot studies.

name: Trimethylolpropane trimethacrylate
description:
Trimethylolpropane trimethacrylate ( CAS 3290-92-4 ), commonly identified as TMPTMA or by trade names such as Acryester TMP, is a trifunctional methacrylate monomer used as a crosslinking agent.

It is utilized in radiation-curable and peroxide-cured polymer systems. Its three reactive methacrylate groups enable rapid network formation, making it a standard building block in high-performance formulations.

In UV- and EB-curable coatings, TMPTMA functions as a reactive diluent and crosslinker, improving hardness, chemical resistance, and cure speed in wood, plastic, and metal finishes.

Rubber and tire compounders use it as a co-agent in peroxide vulcanization to increase modulus and heat resistance without compromising elasticity in demanding industrial environments.

In adhesives and sealants, it contributes to cohesive strength and dimensional stability under thermal cycling. Printing ink formulators incorporate it to achieve fast cure response.

The monomer provides improved abrasion resistance in packaging applications. TMPTMA is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid and is available in technical and industrial grades.

Inhibited versions containing polymerization inhibitors are available for storage stability. Bulk, IBC, and drum packaging are standard supply formats for industrial buyers and manufacturers.

name: Dibromoneopentyl glycol
description:
Dibromoneopentyl glycol (CAS 3296-90-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DBNPG and also known by the trade reference Pentaerythritol dibromide, is a reactive brominated diol used as a flame retardant intermediate.

Unlike additive flame retardants, it chemically incorporates into the polymer backbone, delivering durable fire resistance without migration or blooming across various polymer and coating systems.

In polyurethane foams and rigid panels for construction, DBNPG is reacted into the polyol component to meet building fire safety standards without compromising structural integrity.

Unsaturated polyester resins used in composite panels and laminates incorporate it to achieve UL or EN flame classification requirements for industrial and commercial applications.

Textile and leather finishing formulations use DBNPG as a reactive component in back-coating systems where wash-durable flame retardancy is required for high-performance materials.

In adhesives, sealants, and epoxy systems, it functions as a co-monomer that imparts flame retardant performance directly into the cured network for long-term stability.

Dibromoneopentyl glycol is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Quality is confirmed by GC or titration to ensure consistency. Packaging is available in 25 kg bags, with bulk options for high-volume polymer and resin producers.

name: Diuron
description:
Diuron (CAS 330-54-1 ), also sold under the trade name Karmex and referenced in research contexts as DCMU, is a substituted urea herbicide used for broad-spectrum weed and algae control.

It functions by inhibiting photosynthesis in target plants, making it effective across both agricultural and industrial settings. In agriculture, it is applied as a pre- and post-emergent herbicide.

It is used on crops such as cotton, sugarcane, and fruit orchards to suppress grassy and broadleaf weeds. Industrial and non-crop uses include total vegetation control on railways, roadsides, and industrial sites.

This chemical is preferred where long-residual activity is required. In antifouling and preservation applications, it acts as a biocide in coatings for marine surfaces, textiles, and paper to inhibit growth.

It is effective at stopping algal and microbial growth in these environments. Polymer and flame-retardant formulations also incorporate this substance as a functional additive for specialty material performance.

The photosynthesis-inhibiting mechanism is leveraged for these specific industrial applications. The product is available as a wettable powder (WP), suspension concentrate (SC), and technical-grade solid.

Standard agricultural formulations are supplied at 80% WP and 50% SC concentrations. Technical-grade material is the primary form sourced by formulators and industrial buyers producing downstream products.

name: Trioleyl phosphate
description:
Trioleyl phosphate (CAS 3305-68-8 ), commercially available as Hostaphat KO 300 and NIKKOL TOP-0, is a phosphate ester derived from oleyl alcohol used across industrial lubrication, polymer processing, and rubber compounding.

Its primary function is to reduce friction and wear in metal-on-metal contact while also acting as a plasticizer and flame retardant in polymer systems. In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it functions as an extreme-pressure additive.

It serves as an anti-wear additive in cutting fluids, gear oils, and hydraulic formulations where metal surface protection is critical. Polymer formulators incorporate it as a plasticizer and flame-retardant additive in PVC and other thermoplastics.

description:
Sodium laureth carboxylate (CAS 33939-64-9 ) is an ether carboxylate surfactant derived from ethoxylated lauryl alcohol. It delivers effective cleansing, foaming, and emulsification performance across personal care formulations.

This versatile ingredient offers mildness profiles that suit sensitive-skin product lines. In shampoos and body washes, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant, generating stable foam while maintaining compatibility with skin and hair proteins.

Facial cleansers and micellar formulations use it to emulsify sebum and cosmetic residues without the harshness associated with conventional sulfate surfactants. It also performs well in conditioning rinse-off products.

In these applications, controlled foam and low irritation potential are formulation priorities. Liquid hand soaps and baby care products rely on it for degreasing efficacy combined with a gentler cleansing profile.

This profile is particularly suited to frequent use and delicate skin types. Sodium laureth carboxylate is typically supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous liquid for easy handling in manufacturing.

Standard active concentrations in commercial grades are commonly around 25–30% active matter. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade designations are available depending on the specific industrial or personal care application.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements relevant to personal care finished goods. This ensures the final product maintains high quality and safety standards for consumer use in various global markets.

name: Polyglyceryl-3 oleate
description:
Polyglyceryl-3 oleate (CAS 33940-98-6 ), also known commercially as CAPROL 3GO and Triglycerol monooleate, is a polyglycerol ester of oleic acid used as an emulsifier and rheology modifier.

It is utilized across food, personal care, and industrial applications. This versatile chemical stabilizes oil-water systems and controls flow behavior in complex formulations for various manufacturing sectors.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier in fat-based systems such as chocolate, compound coatings, and bakery margarines. It reduces viscosity and improves processing efficiency during production.

Personal care formulators use it to build stable water-in-oil emulsions in skin creams, sunscreens, and color cosmetics. It provides a smooth, non-greasy skin feel that supports consumer-acceptable textures.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a dispersant and wetting agent. This improves pigment distribution and substrate adhesion, ensuring a high-quality finish and durable bond in industrial settings.

Sealant and elastomer compounders incorporate it as a processing aid to optimize flow during mixing and application. This ensures the material remains workable and consistent throughout the manufacturing process.

Polyglyceryl-3 oleate is supplied as an amber to yellow viscous liquid. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available for purchase by professional manufacturers.

Food-grade material typically meets FCC or EU food additive standards. Industrial technical grades are also offered for coatings and adhesive applications where food compliance is not required.

name: Decaglyceryl dioleate
description:
Decaglyceryl dioleate (CAS 33940-99-7 ) is a polyglycerol ester of oleic acid used as a non-ionic emulsifier and carrier in food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations.

It belongs to the polyglycerol ester family, a class recognized for stabilizing oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems across a broad range of processing conditions.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier in dressings, spreads, and low-fat products where stable oil-water interfaces are required at low use levels.

Cosmetic formulators use it to build stable emulsions in creams and lotions, particularly where a mild, skin-compatible emulsifier is needed to replace more irritating alternatives.

In pharmaceutical applications, it acts as a solubilizer and carrier for lipophilic active ingredients in oral and topical delivery systems for various formulations.

It is also used in bakery and confectionery processing to improve fat dispersion and extend product shelf life by maintaining consistent texture and moisture levels.

Decaglyceryl dioleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste at ambient temperature. Food-grade material is the most common commercial specification available.

Some suppliers offer material compliant with FCC or regional food additive standards. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and cosmetic applications.

name: Stearoyl glutamic acid
description:
Stearoyl glutamic acid (CAS 3397-16-8 ), commercially known as Amisoft HA, is an N-acyl amino acid derived from stearic acid and glutamic acid. It functions as a mild surfactant and emulsifier across personal care and food applications.

This material is highly valued for its skin compatibility and multifunctional formulation performance. In skincare and cleansing formulations, it acts as a gentle surfactant that produces a creamy lather while maintaining skin barrier integrity.

This makes it a preferred choice in premium facial cleansers and sensitive-skin products. It contributes to rheology modification in emulsions, helping stabilize creams and lotions without requiring heavy thickener loads.

In hair care, it improves conditioning and foam texture in shampoos and scalp treatments. Food-grade applications include use as an emulsifier and dough conditioner in baked goods where it supports fat dispersion.

It is also used to ensure crumb structure consistency in various industrial food processes. Stearoyl glutamic acid is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake for easy handling and processing.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications, with food-grade material conforming to relevant purity standards for use as a food additive. This ensures safety and compliance across different global markets.

Packaging options commonly include bags and fiber drums suited to both small-batch formulators and larger manufacturing operations. These formats ensure the stability and integrity of the product during transport and storage.

name: Lauroyl Glutamic Acid
description:
Lauroyl Glutamic Acid (CAS 3397-65-7 ) is an N-acyl amino acid produced by condensing lauric acid with glutamic acid. It functions as a mild surfactant, emulsifier, and conditioning agent across personal care and food-related applications.

In skin and hair care formulations, it acts as a gentle cleansing and conditioning agent compatible with sensitive-skin products such as facial cleansers, shampoos, and body washes. Its emulsifying and wetting properties support stable oil-in-water emulsions.

In creams and lotions, it helps to disperse active ingredients evenly across the formulation. Food-grade material is evaluated as an emulsifier and surface modifier in certain processed food systems where amino acid-derived ingredients are preferred.

In functional cosmetic formulations, it contributes to pH buffering, helping formulators maintain target pH ranges without additional acidulants. This versatility makes it a valuable component for high-performance personal care products.

name: Oxaceprol
description:
Oxaceprol (CAS 33996-33-7 ), also known by the trade name Jonctum and commercially as acetyl hydroxyproline, is a modified amino acid derivative used in pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations.

It functions as a humectant, antioxidant stabilizer, and pH-buffering agent, supporting both skin conditioning and active ingredient performance in finished products for various industries.

In pharmaceutical preparations, it has been developed as an active ingredient in anti-inflammatory and joint-support formulations, particularly for oral and topical dosage forms targeting connective tissue.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into premium skincare products, such as serums, creams, and masks, where its moisture-retention capacity supports essential skin hydration claims.

Its buffering behavior helps stabilize pH-sensitive formulations, making it relevant for developers working with peptide-based or enzyme-active systems in modern laboratory settings.

The compound also appears in functional topical preparations where collagen-pathway support is a desired positioning attribute for high-end personal care and dermatological brands.

This material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications suited to drug product manufacturing and cosmetic-grade material.

name: Phenyltris(butanoxime)silane
description:
Phenyltris(butanoxime)silane (CAS 34036-80-1 ), also known as Phenyltris(methylethylketoximio)silane, is an oxime-functional silane crosslinker used in room-temperature vulcanizing (RTV) silicone systems.

It releases butanone oxime during cure, enabling moisture-triggered crosslinking without requiring elevated temperatures. In one-component RTV silicone sealants, it controls cure speed and network density.

This makes it a standard crosslinker for construction, glazing, and automotive sealing applications. Silicone adhesives for electronics and industrial assembly rely on it to achieve cohesive, flexible bonds.

The material provides good adhesion to glass, metal, and plastics. Formulators of silicone coatings use it to tune film hardness and surface properties in protective and release coating systems.

It also functions as a reactive modifier in silicone elastomer compounding, where it influences rheology during processing before final cure. This versatility is essential for high-performance industrial applications.

Phenyltris(butanoxime)silane is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or IBC containers suited for industrial-scale sealant and adhesive manufacturing. It is available in technical grade for various uses.

Purity specifications are commonly confirmed by GC analysis to ensure consistent performance. Buyers should verify oxime content and moisture sensitivity controls when evaluating supply chain suitability.

name: Glucosamine
description:
Glucosamine (CAS 3416-24-8 ), also known as D-glucosamine, is an amino monosaccharide derived from chitin that serves as a foundational building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and nutraceutical manufacturing.

It functions as a precursor to glycosaminoglycans and is a primary active ingredient in joint health formulations sold globally. In nutraceuticals and dietary supplements, it is the active compound in joint support products.

These products target cartilage maintenance and are often combined with chondroitin or MSM. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing more complex glycoconjugates and as a starting material for drug development.

In cosmetic formulations, it acts as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in anti-aging creams and serums. Its moisture-retention profile supports product performance claims in high-end skincare applications.

Food-grade applications include functional food enrichment targeting mobility and joint wellness in aging consumer demographics. Glucosamine is commercially available as a white crystalline powder in its free base form.

The hydrochloride and sulfate salt forms are more common in finished product manufacturing. Standard grades include USP , BP , and food-grade specifications to meet regulatory requirements across global supply chains.

These standards ensure compliance across pharmaceutical, supplement, and cosmetic industries. Bulk supply is typically offered in kilogram to metric ton quantities, with documentation supporting GMP-compliant sourcing.

name: Tetra-(methylethylketoxime)silane
description:
Tetra-(methylethylketoxime)silane (CAS 34206-40-1 ), commonly referred to in the silicone industry as TMEKS or ketoxime silane, is a tetrafunctional silane crosslinker used to cure silicone-based systems at room temperature.

It functions as the reactive core component in oxime-cure silicone formulations, releasing butanone oxime upon moisture exposure to initiate network formation. Its primary use is as a crosslinker in one-component room-temperature vulcanizing silicone sealants.

In these systems, it governs cure speed, mechanical strength, and adhesion to substrates such as glass, metal, and plastics. In construction and glazing applications, it is incorporated into neutral-cure silicone sealants for curtain wall systems.

It is also utilized for window sealing and sanitary joints. Silicone coating formulations for industrial and protective applications use it to build crosslink density and improve surface durability across various substrates.

The product is also used in silicone adhesive systems where controlled cure kinetics and compatibility with silicone polymer blends are required. This ensures high performance in demanding industrial environments and bonding applications.

Tetra-(methylethylketoxime)silane is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drums or IBC containers suited to moisture-sensitive handling requirements. Packaging under inert atmosphere is standard practice to preserve reactivity.

name: Hexyl laurate
description:
Hexyl laurate (CAS 34316-64-8 ), also known as hexyl dodecanoate, is a synthetic ester used as an emollient, solvent, and carrier in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations. It provides a light, non-greasy skin feel while improving the spreadability and texture of finished products.

In cosmetic formulations, this ester functions as an emollient and texture modifier in skin creams, lotions, and color cosmetics. It effectively reduces the heavy or tacky feel often associated with heavier oils in complex mixtures.

It acts as a solvent and carrier for active ingredients, pigments, and UV filters in sunscreen and foundation formulations where uniform dispersion is critical. This ensures a consistent application and performance across various skin types.

Pharmaceutical topical preparations use it as a plasticizer and penetration-enhancing carrier to improve the delivery and skin compatibility of active compounds. Its low viscosity makes it suitable as a dispersing medium in lip care products.

The material is also utilized in hair conditioning products to enhance shine and manageability without leaving a heavy residue. Its versatile nature allows it to be integrated into a wide range of high-performance beauty and health care solutions.

Hexyl laurate is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial-scale formulation. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for diverse manufacturing needs.

Purity levels typically meet requirements for use in regulated personal care and topical drug products. Suppliers commonly offer technical-grade material for non-regulated industrial applications requiring consistent chemical properties.

name: Ceramide 3
description:
Ceramide 3 (CAS 34354-88-6 ), also marketed under the trade name Cellapy A Repair, is a synthetic sphingolipid that mirrors the ceramides naturally present in the skin's stratum corneum.

It functions as a barrier-reinforcing and moisture-retention agent in topical formulations, helping to restore lipid structure in compromised or aging skin. In premium skincare, it is incorporated into moisturizers and serums.

These products replenish depleted intercellular lipids and reduce transepidermal water loss. It is used in dermocosmetic formulations targeting eczema-prone, sensitive, or post-procedure skin for optimal recovery.

Formulators often combine it with cholesterol and fatty acids to replicate the natural lamellar bilayer. Hair care formulators use it in conditioning treatments and leave-on products to smooth the cuticle.

This ingredient improves fiber integrity and overall hair health. Pharmaceutical topical preparations also incorporate it where skin barrier restoration is a documented clinical endpoint for patient care.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher for use.

name: Bismuth neodecanoate
description:
Bismuth neodecanoate (CAS 34364-26-6 ) is an organobismuth compound used as a metal catalyst in polyurethane and polymer curing systems. It offers a non-tin, non-mercury pathway for catalyzing urethane reactions.

This chemical addresses increasingly strict regulatory requirements around heavy metal content in finished products. In polyurethane foam, elastomer, and coating formulations, it catalyzes the isocyanate-hydroxyl reaction.

This enables gel and cure without organotin compounds such as DBTDL. Sealant and adhesive manufacturers use it to achieve controlled open times and through-cure in one- and two-component systems.

In industrial coatings, it supports crosslinking of polyurethane and alkyd systems while meeting VOC and heavy metal compliance targets. This is essential for architectural and automotive end markets.

Lubricant and metalworking formulators also evaluate it as a bismuth-based EP additive precursor and functional component. It is supplied as a liquid, typically in solution form with varying bismuth metal content.

The product is available in technical grade, with specifications defined by bismuth assay and viscosity parameters relevant to catalyst dosing. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers suited to industrial volumes.

name: Glyceryl 2-myristate
description:
Glyceryl 2-myristate (CAS 3443-83-2 ) is a monoglyceride ester of myristic acid in which the fatty acid is positioned at the sn-2 carbon of the glycerol backbone. It functions as an emulsifier, moisturizing agent, and lubricant across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

name: 2-oleoylglycerol
description:
2-Oleoylglycerol (CAS 3443-84-3 ) is a monoglyceride formed from glycerol and oleic acid, functioning as an emulsifier, carrier, and humectant across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic applications.

It is structurally distinct from the more common 1-oleoylglycerol isomer, making it relevant in research-grade and specialty formulation contexts where positional specificity matters for the final product.

In pharmaceutical formulation, it acts as a lipid-based carrier in drug delivery systems, improving solubilization and absorption of poorly water-soluble active ingredients during the manufacturing process.

Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier to stabilize fat-in-water systems in processed foods, spreads, and bakery products. It provides consistent texture and shelf stability in various food matrices.

In personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning emollient and co-emulsifier in creams and lotions, supporting moisture retention. This makes it a versatile ingredient for high-end cosmetic formulations.
