name: Potassium thioglycolate
description:
Potassium thioglycolate (CAS 34452-51-2 ), commonly abbreviated as K-TGA, is the potassium salt form of thioglycolic acid used across cosmetic and industrial processing applications. It functions as a reducing agent and keratin-disulfide bond disruptor.

This chemical enables the modification of protein-based substrates. Procurement teams source it as a more pH-compatible alternative to ammonium thioglycolate in formulations requiring tighter alkalinity control.

In professional hair depilation and chemical straightening products, K-TGA breaks disulfide bonds in hair keratin to reshape or remove the fiber structure. This makes it a critical component in salon-grade hair treatments.

Leather processing operations use it as a depilatory agent to remove hair from hides during the beamhouse stage. This application helps in reducing the industrial reliance on traditional sulfide-based chemistries.

Textile processing applications include wool fiber modification, where controlled reduction of cystine linkages alters shrink resistance and surface texture. It also functions as a chelating agent in specific formulations.

The product is utilized where sequestration of metal ions is needed to stabilize the active system. Potassium thioglycolate is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically ranging around 40–50% active content.

Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available. Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements aligned with personal care manufacturing standards for safety and performance.

Bulk liquid supply in drums or IBC containers is the standard commercial format for industrial buyers. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and processing facilities.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, it is formulated into capsules, tablets, and powders targeting urinary tract health, which is one of its most commercially established end uses.

Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it as a low-glycemic sweetener and nutrient additive in health-oriented products. Personal care formulators use it as a humectant in skin creams.

Its moisture-binding capacity supports product performance claims in serums and hair care products. Pharmaceutical manufacturers also use it as an excipient and active ingredient in specialized medical nutrition.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder and is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Recognized grades include USP and FCC standards.

name: Triammonium citrate
description:
Triammonium citrate (CAS 3458-72-8 ), also known by its food additive designation E380 , is the fully neutralized ammonium salt of citric acid used across food, personal care, and industrial water treatment applications.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, chelating agent, and stabilizer, controlling acidity and sequestering metal ions in formulated products. In food and beverage manufacturing, it acts as an acidity regulator and sequestrant.

This prevents metal-catalyzed oxidation that degrades flavor and color in processed products. Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and hair care products to buffer pH and stabilize active ingredients.

In water treatment, it chelates calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions to prevent scale formation and protect process equipment. It also functions as a preservative-supporting agent in formulations where metal ion control is critical.

Triammonium citrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, supporting use in regulated food and beverage applications.

Technical-grade product is also offered for industrial water treatment and non-food formulation use. This versatile chemical ensures stability and performance across a wide range of demanding industrial and consumer sectors.

In architectural and industrial coatings, DPGME functions as a coalescing agent and flow promoter, improving film formation in waterborne latex systems. Electronics manufacturers use it in flux formulations and PCB cleaning processes.

The solvent is particularly valued in electronics where residue-free evaporation is critical. In printing inks and packaging coatings, it supports pigment dispersion and controls drying speed across flexographic and gravure applications.

Adhesive and sealant producers incorporate it as a carrier solvent to adjust viscosity and open time in both water-based and reactive formulations. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

DPGME is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels, with high-purity grades available for electronics and specialty cleaning applications.

Specifications typically align with established industry standards for glycol ether solvents, including purity, water content, and color limits. This ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Ethyl Glucoside
description:
Ethyl Glucoside (CAS 34625-23-5 ) is a mild, sugar-derived glycoside produced by combining glucose with ethanol. It functions as a humectant, emulsifier, and solvent carrier across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

Buyers source it as a multifunctional ingredient that reduces formulation complexity without compromising performance. In cosmetic formulations, it acts as a skin-conditioning humectant in creams, serums, and cleansers.

This ingredient helps retain moisture at the surface level for improved hydration. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solubilizing carrier for active ingredients in topical and oral preparations where a biocompatible vehicle is required.

It serves as a low-irritation option for sensitive applications. In food-grade applications, it functions as a dispersing and carrying agent for flavors and bioactives, improving homogeneity in liquid systems.

Personal care formulators also incorporate it into hair care products to improve texture. It enhances ingredient compatibility across water- and oil-based systems, making it a versatile choice for complex mixtures.

The product is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or as a clear aqueous solution, depending on concentration. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent.

name: Bis(hexamethylenetriaminepenta(methylenephosphonic acid))
description:
Bis(hexamethylenetriaminepenta(methylenephosphonic acid)) , identified by CAS 34690-00-1 , is a high-performance phosphonate chelating agent used in industrial water and process fluid management.

It controls scale deposition and inhibits corrosion by sequestering calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions under demanding conditions. In oilfield and gas processing, it is dosed into injection water systems.

This prevents carbonate and sulfate scale from fouling pipelines and downhole equipment. Water treatment plants use it in cooling tower and boiler circuits, where it stabilizes hardness ions and suppresses metal corrosion.

Mining operations apply it in mineral processing circuits to control scale buildup on heat exchangers and process vessels exposed to high-hardness brines. Its stability across a broad pH range is notable.

This characteristic also suits it for use in industrial cleaning formulations targeting mineral deposits. The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 30–40% active content.

name: Zinc carbonate
description:
Zinc carbonate (CAS 3486-35-9 ), also known as Zincspar, is an inorganic zinc salt used across coatings, rubber, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer and catalyst precursor.

This versatile chemical acts as a mild biocide in both wet and dry formulation systems. In coatings and anticorrosive primers, it acts as a zinc source that stabilizes pH and contributes to substrate protection.

Rubber and elastomer compounders use it as a zinc oxide precursor. By calcining it in-process, they generate active ZnO for vulcanization without the need for handling the oxide directly during the initial stages.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it provides mild astringency and odor control. It is frequently utilized in powders, creams, and topical products to enhance the overall stability and performance of the formula.

Water treatment and mining operations use it to adjust pH in process streams and precipitate interfering metal ions. This ensures that industrial processes remain efficient and meet environmental safety requirements.

Zinc carbonate is supplied as a white powder in technical and pharmaceutical grades. USP and BP grades are available for healthcare and personal care applications to ensure high purity.

Technical grade serves industrial coatings, rubber, and mining end uses. Standard packaging ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk quantities, with purity levels typically specified at 57–60% ZnO equivalent.

It contributes fresh, fatty, and slightly floral character to finished scent profiles, making it a functional building block for perfumers and flavorists. In personal care, it is used in fine fragrances and body washes.

Its multiple amine groups enable both surface bonding and cross-linking functions within a single molecule, making it a preferred choice where standard monoamine silanes fall short.

In adhesives, sealants, and epoxy systems, it improves adhesion to glass, metals, and mineral fillers by chemically linking the substrate to the polymer network.

Electronics manufacturers use it as a surface primer on circuit board laminates and encapsulant interfaces to improve moisture resistance and bond durability.

In coatings for automotive and aerospace components, it acts as an adhesion promoter on metal and composite surfaces, reducing delamination under thermal cycling.

Plastics compounders incorporate it as a coupling agent for glass fiber-reinforced systems, improving mechanical strength retention in demanding structural applications.

name: Propylparaben sodium
description:
Propylparaben sodium (CAS 35285-69-9 ), also known as E217 , is the water-soluble sodium salt form of propylparaben, developed specifically to overcome the limited aqueous solubility of its parent ester.

It functions as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial preservative across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it protects oral suspensions, syrups, and topical formulations.

This is particularly useful in formulations where high water content would otherwise limit standard propylparaben use. Food and beverage producers apply E217 in aqueous-based products including sauces and beverages.

It is also used in bakery fillings where direct incorporation of a water-soluble preservative is required. Personal care formulators use it in lotions, shampoos, and liquid cosmetics to extend shelf life.

The ingredient helps maintain product clarity and stability during storage. It is often combined with methylparaben or other paraben salts to achieve broader antimicrobial coverage across a wider range of organisms.

Propylparaben sodium is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter conforming to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards.

Packaging is typically offered in kilogram bags through to bulk quantities suitable for industrial-scale production. This ensures consistent quality and reliability for large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: Acid Blue 3
description:
Acid Blue 3 (CAS 3536-49-0 ), commercially recognized as Patent Blue V and approved as E131 , is a synthetic triarylmethane dye used to impart vivid blue coloration across food, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

Regulatory approval in multiple jurisdictions makes it a primary consideration for formulators requiring a certified blue colorant. In food and beverage production, it is used to color confectionery, soft drinks, and ice cream.

This dye is preferred where a bright, stable blue shade is required. Cosmetic and personal care manufacturers incorporate it into rinse-off products such as shampoos, bath products, and toothpaste to achieve consistent blue tones.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a dye component in water-based inks where color intensity and substrate adhesion are critical to print quality. Textile and leather processors use it in aqueous dyebaths.

The product is used to dye protein-based fibers and finished leather goods. It is supplied as a powder or granule, with liquid concentrations available for direct dosing in various industrial processes.

Food and cosmetic grades conforming to E131 specifications are the most commonly sourced, with purity requirements aligned to regional regulatory standards including EU and Codex Alimentarius frameworks.

Technical grade material is available for non-consumable applications such as textile dyeing and ink formulation. This ensures versatility for manufacturers across different sectors requiring high-performance colorants.

Contact us for supply of Acid Blue 3

name: Hexadecyl phosphate
description:
Hexadecyl phosphate (CAS 3539-43-3 ), also known as cetyl phosphate, is a phosphate ester of cetyl alcohol used as an anionic surfactant and emulsifier across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations.

It functions primarily to stabilize emulsions, modify surface wetting, and control rheological behavior in finished products. In cosmetic and topical pharmaceutical formulations, it acts as an emulsifying agent.

This material provides stable oil-in-water systems with a smooth skin feel in creams and lotions. Formulators in the pharmaceutical sector use it as an excipient in semi-solid dosage forms for performance.

Controlled viscosity and emulsion stability are critical to product performance in these applications. In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as a surface modifier and wetting agent for the user.

It improves substrate adhesion and pigment dispersion in various industrial settings. Personal care manufacturers also incorporate it into conditioning treatments and sunscreen bases for long-term stability.

This stability is maintained under varying pH conditions, which is a common formulation requirement. Hexadecyl phosphate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid material.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of regulated end markets. Bulk quantities are generally offered in fiber drums or multi-layer bags.

These packaging options are suited to standard warehouse handling and long-term storage. The product ensures consistent quality for manufacturers requiring reliable anionic surfactants in their supply chain.

name: Polyquaternium-32
description:
Polyquaternium-32 (CAS 35429-19-7 ), also referred to by the broader class name Polyquaternium, is a cationic conditioning polymer used across personal care and industrial formulations. It functions as both a rheology modifier and a surface-active agent.

This versatile chemical provides film formation, conditioning, and viscosity control in aqueous systems. In hair care and skin care formulations, it deposits a conditioning film on the substrate, improving combability and softness.

It enhances moisture retention without heavy buildup in various cosmetic applications. Shampoos, conditioners, body washes, and leave-in treatments rely on it to deliver sensory performance alongside thickening properties.

In textile processing, it modifies fiber surfaces to improve softness and antistatic behavior during finishing operations. Home care and industrial cleaning products incorporate it to adjust viscosity and enhance surface wetting.

The polymer is effective on hard surfaces and provides consistent performance across different pH levels. Polyquaternium-32 is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations suited for direct incorporation into water-based formulations.

It is available in cosmetic-grade quality meeting the requirements of major personal care ingredient standards. Industrial-grade supply is also available for textile and cleaning applications where cosmetic specification is not required.

Contact us for supply of Polyquaternium-32

name: beta-Naphthoxyethanol
description:
Beta-Naphthoxyethanol (CAS 35545-57-4 ) is a naphthol-derived ethoxylate used as a surface-active building block and functional additive across specialty chemical formulations. It acts as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and dispersion aid in systems where controlled interfacial activity is required.

In textile processing, it supports dye leveling and fiber wetting, improving dye uptake uniformity across synthetic and blended fabrics. Coating and ink formulations use it to modify surface tension and enhance pigment dispersion.

These properties contribute to improved film formation and print quality in various industrial applications. In adhesive and sealant systems, it functions as a rheology modifier, helping to control flow behavior and substrate wetting during application.

Leather and paper treatment processes also employ it to achieve consistent surface penetration and finish uniformity. This versatility makes it a valuable component for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in complex chemical systems.

Beta-Naphthoxyethanol is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity melt, depending on ethoxylation degree and purity specification. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most industrial users.

Purity levels are commonly specified by the supplier to meet industrial formulation requirements and ensure batch consistency. Packaging is available in drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes.

Contact us for supply of beta-Naphthoxyethanol

name: Murumuru butter
description:
Murumuru butter (CAS 356065-49-1 ), also traded as Astrocaryum murumuru and known in Turkish markets as Kati Murumuru Yağı, is a tropical seed fat derived from the murumuru palm native to the Amazon basin.

It functions as an emollient and emulsifier across personal care formulations and specialty food applications. In cosmetics, it is used as a base ingredient in hair conditioners, lip balms, and body butters.

Its high lauric and myristic acid content supports moisture retention and smooth spreadability on skin and hair. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a cocoa butter alternative or extender in confectionery coatings.

Its melting profile suits solid chocolate and compound coating production. In adhesives and sealant formulations, it serves as a bio-based plasticizing component where renewable raw material sourcing is required.

The product is supplied as a solid ivory-to-white fat, typically available in block, pellet, or flake form for ease of handling. Standard commercial grades include cosmetic and food-grade options.

Specifications are aligned to FCC standards where applicable. Refined and crude variants are both available on the market, with refined grades preferred for applications requiring low odor and color.

Contact us for supply of Murumuru butter

name: Brazil nut oil
description:
Brazil nut oil (CAS 356065-50-4 ), also marketed as Fats and Glyceridic oils, brazil nut, is a cold-pressed or expeller-pressed vegetable oil sourced from the seeds of Bertholletia excelsa.

It is valued across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulation for its high unsaturated fatty acid content and skin-conditioning performance. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as an emollient.

It is used as a moisturizing base in creams, serums, hair oils, and lip care products, where it supports skin barrier conditioning without heavy residue. Food manufacturers use it as a premium edible oil.

It is found in specialty nutrition products, gourmet dressings, and functional food formulations. In coatings and sealants, its fatty acid profile supports lubrication and film-forming properties in specialty resin systems.

It also serves as a carrier or base oil in nutraceutical softgel and topical supplement formulations. Brazil nut oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, available in both refined and unrefined grades.

Standard supply formats include drums and IBCs for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for cosmetic formulators. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly traded.

Refined grades offer improved color and odor stability for sensitive formulations. This versatile oil meets various industry requirements for purity and performance across global manufacturing sectors.

Contact us for supply of Brazil nut oil

name: Bis(hexamethylene)triaminopenta(methylene-phosphonic acid)
description:
Bis(hexamethylene)triaminopenta(methylene-phosphonic acid) , also known as BHMTPMPA or BHMT, is a high-performance phosphonate chelating agent. It is identified by CAS 35657-77-3 and is widely used in industrial water and process chemical applications.

The compound functions by sequestering metal ions and inhibiting scale formation and corrosion in aggressive aqueous systems. Its sodium salt form is also commercially traded and sourced for formulated products requiring enhanced solubility.

In industrial water treatment, BHMT is formulated into scale and corrosion inhibitor packages for cooling water and boiler water. It is essential for oilfield injection systems where calcium carbonate and other mineral deposits are a persistent concern.

Oil and gas producers use it in produced water treatment and downhole chemical programs to prevent mineral scaling. This ensures the integrity of pipelines and wellbore equipment during demanding extraction and transport operations.

Textile and leather processors incorporate it into pretreatment baths to deactivate hardness ions. This prevents interference with dyeing uniformity and chemical uptake, ensuring high-quality finished goods in manufacturing cycles.

In paper manufacturing, it controls metal ion interference during pulp bleaching and process water recycling. This application helps maintain brightness and prevents the degradation of chemical additives during the production process.

BHMT is supplied as an aqueous solution, with the sodium salt form available for applications requiring improved handling. This version is preferred for solubility at neutral to alkaline pH levels in various industrial formulations.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial end uses. Bulk supply is typical for water treatment chemical formulators and industrial blenders looking for reliable performance in large-scale systems.

Contact us for supply of Bis(hexamethylene)triaminopenta(methylene-phosphonic acid)

name: Acid red 33
description:
Acid Red 33 (CAS 3567-66-6 ), also known as CI 17200, Azo Fuchsine, and D&C Red No. 33, is a synthetic azo dye approved for use across food, cosmetic, and industrial coloring applications.

It delivers a bright, bluish-red hue with strong tinctorial strength, making it a reliable option for formulators and buyers seeking consistent batch-to-batch color performance in various manufacturing sectors.

In personal care and cosmetics, D&C Red No. 33 is used to color hair dyes, lipsticks, and rinse-off products where regulatory approval for skin contact is required for consumer safety and compliance.

Food-grade applications include coloring confectionery, beverages, and maraschino cherries in markets where the dye holds regulatory clearance. Textile and leather processors use CI 17200 to dye protein-based fibers.

This includes materials such as wool and silk, where its acid dye chemistry bonds effectively under low-pH dyebath conditions. Paper manufacturers apply it for decorative and specialty paper coloring.

Surface uniformity and shade consistency are critical in these applications. Acid Red 33 is supplied as a powder or granule, with water-soluble formulations available for liquid concentrate preparation.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially relevant, with purity levels typically meeting FD&C or D&C certification standards depending on the target market and intended use.

Technical grade is available for textile and industrial use. Our product ensures high stability and meets rigorous quality benchmarks for global distribution and industrial chemical processing requirements.

name: Carmoisine
description:
Carmoisine (CAS 3567-69-9 ), also known as E122 , Food Red 3, and C.I. Acid Red 14, is a synthetic azo dye producing a deep red to maroon shade across food and industrial applications.

It functions as a colorant in both consumable products and industrial substrates, offering strong tinctorial strength and reliable batch-to-batch color consistency for various manufacturing processes.

In food and beverage manufacturing, E122 is used to color confectionery, soft drinks, dessert mixes, and jams to achieve consistent red and burgundy tones within strict regulatory limits.

Textile processors apply it to wool, silk, and nylon dyeing under acid conditions, where it delivers strong fiber uptake and good wash fastness for high-quality fabric production.

In leather finishing, it contributes to surface coloration of hides where a vivid red tone is specified. Printing ink formulators also incorporate it into water-based inks for packaging applications.

These applications require food-contact-compliant colorants to ensure safety. Carmoisine is supplied as a fine powder or granule, typically as the disodium salt form for easy solubility.

It is available in food-grade specification meeting E122 purity requirements under EU and Codex Alimentarius standards, as well as technical grade for textile and industrial use.

Buyers should confirm dye content percentage, which commonly ranges from 85% upward depending on grade. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance criteria for the intended use.

name: Methyldibromo glutaronitrile
description:
Methyldibromo glutaronitrile (CAS 35691-65-7 ), commonly referred to as MDBGN, is a broad-spectrum biocide used to control microbial growth in industrial and consumer formulations.

It delivers effective preservation against bacteria, fungi, and yeast at low use concentrations across a range of product types. In water treatment and industrial process fluids, it controls microbial contamination.

This chemical is essential for cooling water systems, paper mill circuits, and metalworking fluids. Coatings, adhesives, and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as an in-can preservative to extend shelf life.

It prevents spoilage during storage and distribution. The textile, leather, and pulp and paper industries rely on it to protect wet-process materials and finished goods from microbial degradation.

It has also been used in personal care formulations as a preservation booster, though regulatory restrictions in cosmetics vary by market and must be verified before sourcing for that application.

MDBGN is available as a solid crystalline powder and in liquid solution blends, often combined with other biocidal actives such as phenoxyethanol for broader-spectrum performance.

The technical grade is the standard supply form for industrial applications. Buyers should confirm regional regulatory status, particularly for cosmetic end uses, prior to procurement.

Approved concentrations differ across jurisdictions. Ensuring compliance with local safety standards is necessary when integrating this biocide into diverse manufacturing processes and product lines.

name: Fmoc-L-tryptophan
description:
Fmoc-L-tryptophan (CAS 35737-15-6 ), commonly referenced as Fmoc-Trp-OH, is a protected amino acid building block used in solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS).

The Fmoc protecting group allows sequential, controlled chain assembly under mild deprotection conditions, making this compound a standard reagent in peptide manufacturing workflows.

In pharmaceutical peptide production, Fmoc-Trp-OH is incorporated into therapeutic peptide sequences where tryptophan residues are required for biological activity or structural integrity.

Research and contract synthesis organizations use it to produce peptide APIs, peptide libraries, and reference standards at both discovery and scale.

In biotechnology, it supports the synthesis of peptide-based probes, linkers, and conjugates used in diagnostic and analytical applications for various industries.

Academic and industrial peptide chemists also rely on it for custom sequence development during early-stage drug candidate screening and development processes.

Fmoc-Trp-OH is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots to support scale-up.

Common grades include synthesis-grade for research use and higher-purity specifications aligned with requirements for commercial peptide manufacturing and production.

name: Trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride
description:
Trifluoromethanesulfonic anhydride (CAS 358-23-6 ), commercially known as triflic anhydride or Tf₂O, is one of the most powerful electrophilic triflating agents available for synthetic chemistry.

It activates hydroxyl groups and other nucleophilic sites for downstream coupling and functionalization steps that milder reagents cannot achieve efficiently. In pharmaceutical synthesis, Tf₂O converts phenols and enols into vinyl triflates.

These are key intermediates in palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions used to build complex active pharmaceutical ingredients. Polymer chemists use it to initiate cationic polymerization of cyclic monomers.

This enables precise molecular weight control in specialty polymer production. It also functions as an activating agent in the synthesis of glycosyl triflates, supporting carbohydrate-based drug and excipient manufacturing.

In fine chemical production, Tf₂O generates highly reactive triflate intermediates that allow selective C–O and C–N bond formation under conditions where conventional sulfonating agents fail.

Triflic anhydride is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically in sealed, moisture-protected packaging due to its reactivity with atmospheric moisture.

It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for process-scale synthesis. Standard commercial offerings are high-purity technical and synthesis grades.

Purity specifications are commonly at 99% or above as confirmed by GC or titration methods, ensuring reliability for sensitive industrial applications and laboratory research.

name: Dimethylol glycol
description:
Dimethylol glycol (CAS 3586-55-8 ), also known as ethylene glycol bis(semiformal), is a difunctional hydroxymethyl compound used as a reactive building block and crosslinking agent in polymer and resin systems.

Its dual hydroxymethyl groups make it effective for controlled network formation in thermosetting formulations. In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a crosslinker that improves film cohesion and adhesion strength.

This compound also enhances resistance to solvents and humidity in various industrial applications. Textile and leather finishing operations use it to impart dimensional stability and wrinkle resistance to treated fabrics and hides.

Paper and pulp processors incorporate it into wet-strength resin formulations where controlled crosslink density directly affects end-product performance. Polymer formulators also evaluate it as a plasticizing comonomer.

This application is particularly useful where flexibility and compatibility with hydroxyl-functional resins are required. Dimethylol glycol is typically supplied as a liquid at standard commercial concentrations for ease of use.

Technical-grade material is the primary market form, with specifications aligned to industrial end-use requirements in coatings, textile, and paper applications. Buyers should confirm purity and active content directly.

Stability parameters should also be verified with the supplier, as these vary between producers. This ensures the material meets the specific needs of the intended chemical manufacturing or processing application.

name: Pigment brown 23
description:
Pigment Brown 23 (CAS 35869-64-8 ), also marketed as Cromophtal Brown 5R, is a high-performance azo condensation pigment used to deliver warm brown shades. It provides strong heat and lightfastness across demanding industrial colorant applications.

It is favored where color durability under processing stress is a primary sourcing requirement. In plastics and polymer compounding, it withstands high processing temperatures, making it suitable for engineering resins.

This pigment is ideal for masterbatch production where color integrity must survive extrusion or injection molding. Coatings formulators incorporate it into industrial and automotive finishes for outdoor exposure.

The material offers high resistance to UV degradation and color shift in harsh environments. In printing inks, it performs reliably in packaging applications subject to heat-sealing or lamination processes.

Textile and leather dyeing operations use it where a stable, warm brown tone is required. It is compatible across synthetic fiber and surface coating systems for consistent results in manufacturing.

Pigment Brown 23 is supplied as a dry powder, the standard commercial form for pigment dispersion. It is available in technical grade, with some suppliers offering press cake or predispersed forms.

These specialized forms are suited to specific ink or coating manufacturing processes. Buyers should confirm tinting strength, oil absorption, and particle size specifications against their formulation requirements.

Careful evaluation of supplier lots ensures the pigment meets the necessary performance criteria. This high-performance brown remains a staple for durable industrial and commercial coloring solutions.

name: Muconic Acid
description:
Muconic acid (CAS 3588-17-8 ), also referred to as trans,trans-Muconic acid, is a linear unsaturated dicarboxylic acid produced through both chemical synthesis and bio-based fermentation routes.

It functions as a platform chemical and pH-regulating agent in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and agrochemical development pipelines. In pharmaceutical research and synthesis, it serves as a precursor and intermediate.

This material is used in the preparation of specialty compounds, including adipic acid analogues explored for bio-based polymer development. Biotechnology applications center on its role as a fermentation-derived building block.

It is frequently evaluated in metabolic engineering programs targeting renewable chemical production. In agrochemical formulations, its acidic functionality supports pH buffering and contributes preservative activity.

This is particularly useful in formulation systems requiring microbial control. It is also used as a reference standard and analytical reagent in life sciences research, specifically for monitoring benzene metabolite exposure.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available primarily in research and technical grades, with high-purity specifications of 98% or higher as the standard for procurement.

These specifications meet the rigorous needs of pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk volumes depending on specific industrial application requirements.

name: Calcium glycinate
description:
Calcium glycinate (CAS 35947-07-0 ), also known as calcium bisglycinate, is an amino acid-chelated mineral in which calcium is bound to glycine for enhanced bioavailability compared to inorganic calcium salts.

It functions as a bioavailable calcium source across nutritional, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications. In dietary supplements and functional foods, it delivers calcium with improved gastrointestinal tolerance.

This makes it a preferred choice for high-potency tablet, capsule, and powder formulations. Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it into fortified products including dairy alternatives and infant nutrition.

It is also used in sports nutrition formats where clean-label mineral delivery is a formulation priority. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an active mineral ingredient in bone health preparations.

The material is frequently used in prenatal preparations where the absorption profile influences product positioning. Animal feed producers use it to supply bioavailable calcium in premixes and compound feeds.

This is particularly effective where digestive efficiency in monogastric animals is a key performance target. Calcium glycinate is supplied as a white to off-white powder available in food-grade and feed-grade.

Some suppliers offer material compliant with USP or Ph. Eur. standards for specialized applications. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers with various packaging options.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities to metric ton volumes to suit different manufacturing scales. This ensures a reliable supply chain for large-scale production requirements globally.

name: Citranaxanthin
description:
Citranaxanthin (CAS 3604-90-8 ), also designated E161i , is a synthetic carotenoid pigment used to impart yellow-to-orange coloration in food, feed, and cosmetic applications.

It functions as both a colorant and an antioxidant stabilizer across regulated product categories. In poultry and aquaculture feed, it is incorporated to achieve consistent pigmentation in egg yolks and broiler skin.

This pigment is a key quality driver for commercial producers in farmed fish flesh. Food manufacturers use it to standardize color in processed products where natural pigment variability would otherwise affect batch consistency.

In cosmetic formulations, it provides stable warm-toned coloration in products such as self-tanners, color cosmetics, and skin-care preparations. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators source it for antioxidant-positioned dietary supplements.

These supplements often target carotenoid intake for specific health applications. Citranaxanthin is typically supplied as a powder or in oil-suspension and beadlet forms suited to feed and food processing lines.

It is available in feed-grade and food-grade specifications, with product quality aligned to regional regulatory requirements including EU authorization. Concentration levels in commercial preparations vary by supplier.

Buyers should confirm specification sheets against their formulation targets before procurement. The material ensures high stability and uniform distribution within various industrial manufacturing environments and complex matrices.

name: Alpinetin
description:
Alpinetin (CAS 36052-37-6 ) is a naturally occurring flavanone extracted primarily from Alpinia katsumadai and related botanical sources. It functions as a bioactive antioxidant ingredient used across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and life sciences applications.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulations, this compound is incorporated as an active botanical ingredient in capsules, tablets, and standardized herbal extracts. These applications typically target antioxidant support and metabolic health.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers source it as a reference standard or tool compound for in vitro assay work and mechanistic studies. It is essential for laboratories requiring high-purity plant-derived phenolic compounds for testing.

Food and beverage formulators apply it in functional product development where plant-derived antioxidant actives are required. This helps manufacturers meet clean-label or botanical positioning requirements for modern consumer markets.

It is also evaluated in cosmetic-adjacent formulations where oxidative stability from a natural phenolic source is a formulation requirement. The compound provides a stable, plant-based alternative to synthetic antioxidants in topical applications.

name: PEG-6 caprylic/capric glycerides
description:
PEG-6 caprylic/capric glycerides (CAS 361459-38-3 ) is an ethoxylated medium-chain glyceride derived from coconut or palm kernel oil fractions. It functions as an emulsifier, solubilizer, and carrier across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food-grade formulation systems.

In pharmaceutical drug delivery, it solubilizes poorly water-soluble active ingredients, improving bioavailability in soft gel capsules and self-emulsifying drug delivery systems. This makes it a critical component for modern medicine delivery.

Cosmetic formulators use it to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions in creams, lotions, and leave-on skin care products. Its humectant character supports moisture retention in the finished formula, providing a smooth and hydrated skin feel.

In nutraceutical and functional food applications, it enables lipophilic vitamin and omega fatty acid dispersions in liquid and encapsulated formats. This ensures consistent dosing and stability for various health supplements.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it as a low-irritation surfactant component in mild cleansing concentrates. Its gentle nature makes it suitable for products designed for sensitive environments and applications.

PEG-6 caprylic/capric glycerides is typically supplied as a liquid or semi-solid at room temperature, available in bulk drums and intermediate bulk containers. This allows for flexible storage and handling in large-scale production.

name: n-butylbenzenesulfonamide

It functions as a low-volatility softening agent that improves flexibility and processability in demanding formulations. BBSA is primarily used to plasticize polyamide resins, where it reduces melt viscosity.

It improves flexibility in extruded and injection-molded parts such as films, fibers, and engineering components. In hot-melt adhesives and coatings, it acts as a reactive or non-reactive plasticizer.

This chemical helps to control flow and adhesion properties in various industrial settings. Personal care formulators incorporate it into nail lacquers and film-forming systems to enhance flexibility.

It improves the wear resistance of the dried film in cosmetic applications. It also functions as a catalyst or co-catalyst in certain polyurethane and resin cure systems for manufacturing.

The sulfonamide group participates in the reaction network to ensure stability. BBSA is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial polymer applications.

Select suppliers offer purity specifications suited to personal care end uses. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to meet the high volume demands of global chemical manufacturing.

name: Isocetyl alcohol
description:
Isocetyl alcohol (CAS 36311-34-9 ) is a branched-chain fatty alcohol used primarily in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations as an emollient, emulsifier, and texture modifier.

Its branched structure prevents the waxy, heavy feel associated with straight-chain fatty alcohols, making it a preferred choice where a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel is the formulation target.

In skincare and color cosmetics, it functions as an emollient and rheology modifier, contributing to spreadability and a smooth after-feel in creams, lotions, and foundations.

Hair care formulators incorporate it into conditioners and styling products where it aids in detangling and improves product slip without excessive buildup for the end user.

Pharmaceutical topical formulations use it as a carrier and co-emulsifier in ointments and creams, supporting active ingredient delivery across the skin barrier effectively.

It also serves as a solvent and dispersant in pigment-based systems, improving pigment wetting and stability in color cosmetic manufacturing and various industrial applications.

Isocetyl alcohol is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid at room temperature. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for diverse needs.

The latter typically conforms to relevant pharmacopeial standards. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with technical-grade material also available for industrial applications.

name: Magnesium gluconate
description:
Magnesium gluconate (CAS 3632-91-5 ) is an organic magnesium salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing as a bioavailable magnesium source and pH buffer.

Its high gastrointestinal tolerance relative to inorganic magnesium salts makes it a preferred choice for supplement formulators and functional food producers seeking high-quality ingredients.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, it serves as an elemental magnesium carrier in tablets, capsules, and fortified beverages where tolerability and label-friendly positioning matter.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into oral rehydration formulas and magnesium-deficiency therapeutics where consistent purity and controlled release profiles are required for safety.

In food processing, it functions as a pH regulator and stabilizer in dairy analogues, infant nutrition, and processed foods requiring mineral fortification without flavor interference.

Personal care formulators use it as a chelating and buffering agent in skin-conditioning products and mineral-enriched topical preparations to enhance product stability and performance.

Magnesium gluconate is supplied as a white crystalline powder, available in both anhydrous and hydrated forms. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and BP / Ph. Eur.

Food and beverage producers incorporate it into functional foods and fortified products where zinc labeling claims are required without the metallic off-notes associated with inorganic sources.

name: Tribromoneopentyl alcohol

Tribromoneopentyl alcohol (CAS 36483-57-5 ), commonly known as TBNPA, is a brominated aliphatic alcohol used as a reactive flame retardant intermediate. Unlike additive flame retardants, it chemically bonds into polymer matrices.

Unsaturated polyester resins used in construction panels and composite materials rely on TBNPA to achieve halogen-based fire performance ratings. This ensures structural integrity and safety in high-risk environments.

Paper and leather finishing treatments also employ it where substrate-bound flame retardancy is specified by end-use safety requirements. It provides a reliable solution for specialized industrial coatings and finishes.

name: Thymidine monophosphate

Thymidine monophosphate (CAS 365-07-1 ), also known as dTMP or 5'-thymidylic acid, is a nucleotide monophosphate used as a biochemical building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and life science research.

description:
Hexaglycerol (CAS 36675-34-0 ), also supplied under the designation PCB 06, is a polyglycerol produced by the condensation of six glycerol units. It functions as a humectant, emulsifier, and carrier across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food processing, hexaglycerol acts as a base for polyglycerol esters of fatty acids, where it enables emulsification in bakery fats, margarines, and confectionery coatings. This versatile ingredient helps stabilize complex mixtures.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing creams and serums for its hygroscopic character. This supports water retention in the finished product and reduces the need for additional humectants in the formulation.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solvent and carrier in topical and oral formulations. It is particularly useful where a high-boiling, water-miscible polyol is required for stability and delivery of active ingredients.

It also functions as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of specialty surfactants and polyglycerol-based esters. These are used extensively for industrial and cosmetic applications requiring specific surface-active properties.

Hexaglycerol is typically supplied as a viscous liquid. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of different regulated markets and specific industrial standards.

Buyers should confirm purity profiles and polyglycerol distribution data before purchase. The degree of polymerization can vary between production batches and suppliers, affecting the performance of the final product.

name: L-carnitine L-tartrate
description:
L-Carnitine L-Tartrate (CAS 36687-82-8 ), commonly abbreviated as LCLT and marketed under the trade name L-Carnipure, is a salt form of L-carnitine combined with tartaric acid.

It delivers the metabolic activity of L-carnitine with improved stability and faster dissolution compared to free-form carnitine. Procurement teams in sports nutrition and pharmaceutical sectors source it for formulations.

LCLT is the preferred carnitine form in sports nutrition supplements, including protein powders, ready-to-drink beverages, and capsules, where rapid absorption and clean label positioning are priorities.

In pharmaceutical applications, it serves as the active ingredient in oral solid dosage forms targeting carnitine deficiency or metabolic support. Functional food manufacturers incorporate it into energy bars.

The ingredient is used in fortified beverages where its buffering capacity also supports pH stability in the final product. Personal care formulators use it in skin-conditioning products for moisture retention.

L-Carnitine L-Tartrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with material meeting USP and EP standards.

These quality benchmarks are commonly requested by regulated-market buyers. Bulk supply is standard in kilogram and metric ton quantities to meet the demands of large-scale industrial manufacturing.

name: Sodium thioglycolate
description:
Sodium thioglycolate (CAS 367-51-1 ), commonly abbreviated as NATG, is the sodium salt form of thioglycolic acid used across personal care, textile, and industrial processing markets.

It functions primarily as a reducing agent and depilatory active, breaking disulfide bonds in keratin-containing substrates to enable chemical modification of hair and wool fibers.

In personal care manufacturing, NATG is the active ingredient in chemical depilatory creams and cold wave permanent solutions, where it disrupts the protein structure of hair.

Leather processors use it during the unhairing stage to remove hair from hides without mechanical damage, improving throughput and hide quality for various industrial applications.

Textile producers apply it in wool treatment processes to reduce fiber stiffness and improve dye uptake. In analytical and industrial chemistry, it acts as a stabilizing agent.

It also serves as a metal chelator in formulations requiring control of oxidative degradation. Sodium thioglycolate is supplied as an aqueous solution with concentrations from 40% to 58%.

Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commercially available, with cosmetic-grade material subject to purity thresholds aligned with regional regulatory requirements.

Bulk liquid supply in drums or IBCs is standard for industrial buyers. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing facilities.

name: 4-methylbenzylidene camphor
description:
4-Methylbenzylidene camphor (CAS 36861-47-9 ), also known as 4-MBC and Enzacamene, is an organic UV filter used in sunscreen and cosmetic formulations. It absorbs UV-B radiation, protecting both the skin and the integrity of cosmetic products from photodegradation.

Its primary use is in sunscreen products such as creams, lotions, and sprays where it functions as a UV-B filter. It is typically combined with other UV actives to achieve broad-spectrum protection for the end user.

In color cosmetics and daily moisturizers with SPF claims, it contributes to the required sun protection factor. This is achieved without significantly affecting product aesthetics or the final texture of the formulation.

Formulators also incorporate it into hair care products such as leave-in conditioners and styling preparations. This application helps to prevent UV-induced color fading and protects the hair fiber from environmental damage.

4-Methylbenzylidene camphor is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, with purity levels typically at or above 98% for high-quality manufacturing.

The material is commonly evaluated against Ph.Eur. or in-house supplier monographs to ensure consistency. Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale quantities for development use to bulk drums for commercial production.

name: Decyl oleate
description:
Decyl oleate (CAS 3687-46-5 ) is a fatty acid ester derived from oleic acid and decanol, used across personal care and industrial formulations as an emollient, carrier, and lubricant.

It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel in cosmetic applications while providing effective lubricity in industrial systems. In personal care, it functions as an emollient and solvent carrier.

It is commonly used in skin creams, lotions, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, where it improves spreadability and active ingredient delivery. Industrial lubricant formulators use it as a bio-based base fluid.

It serves as an additive in metalworking fluids, where its ester structure provides boundary lubrication and reduces friction on metal surfaces. It also acts as a plasticizer and softening agent.

In polymer and coating formulations requiring improved flexibility, it provides essential performance. As a solvent carrier, it dissolves oil-soluble actives and pigments in various dispersion systems.

Decyl oleate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications, with cosmetic grades typically conforming to standards such as Ph.Eur.

These purity benchmarks are relevant to personal care sourcing. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with packaging options suited to both cosmetic and industrial procurement volumes.

name: Chlorhexidine dihydrochloride
description:
Chlorhexidine dihydrochloride (CAS 3697-42-5 ), also known as chlorhexidine hydrochloride, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial applications.

It delivers effective bactericidal and fungicidal action against a wide range of gram-positive and gram-negative organisms. Procurement teams source it as a primary biocidal ingredient where water-soluble salt forms are required.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is formulated into antiseptic wound washes, surgical scrubs, and mucous membrane disinfectants. A water-soluble salt form is often preferred over the diacetate or digluconate versions.

Personal care producers incorporate it into antibacterial hand washes, medicated shampoos, and oral rinse concentrates targeting microbial control. It functions as a preservative active in various topical formulations.

Industrial water treatment operations use it as a biocide to control microbial growth in cooling systems and process water. It is highly effective where regulatory specifications call for a defined chlorhexidine salt.

Chlorhexidine dihydrochloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to BP and Ph. Eur. specifications for global compliance.

Technical grade is also available for industrial and water treatment end uses. Packaging is typically offered in kilogram quantities up to bulk drum supply to suit both formulation-scale and large-volume procurement needs.

name: Hydroxyethyl imidazolidinone
description:
Hydroxyethyl imidazolidinone (CAS 3699-54-5 ) is a cyclic urea derivative used as a humectant and moisture-retention agent across textile, personal care, and paper processing industries.

Its ability to bind and regulate moisture in treated substrates makes it a functional ingredient in both wet-process formulations and finished product applications for various industrial sectors.

In textile finishing, it is incorporated into crease-resistance and durable press formulations, helping fabrics maintain dimensional stability after washing and improving the overall hand feel.

Personal care formulators use it in leave-on and rinse-off products where sustained hydration of the skin or hair substrate is required to maintain health and appearance over time.

In paper and leather processing, it supports moisture management during treatment stages, contributing to flexibility and surface quality in the finished material during the manufacturing cycle.

It also appears in specialty coating formulations where controlled hygroscopicity of the substrate needs to be maintained through processing to ensure consistent application and drying results.

Hydroxyethyl imidazolidinone is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration levels varying by supplier and end-use specification to meet specific formulation requirements.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial textile and paper applications. Personal care grades with appropriate purity documentation are available for cosmetic formulation use.

name: Diethylhydroxylamine
description:
Diethylhydroxylamine , also known as CAS 3710-84-7 , is a versatile hydroxylamine derivative used industrially as an oxygen scavenger, antioxidant, and polymerization inhibitor. It intercepts free radicals and dissolved oxygen in process streams.

This chemical protects equipment and materials from oxidative degradation across various industrial sectors. In boiler feedwater and steam systems, it scavenges dissolved oxygen to prevent corrosion in pipework and heat exchangers.

The compound also acts as a metal passivator to ensure long-term system integrity. Polymer and monomer producers utilize it to inhibit premature polymerization during the storage and transport of vinyl and acrylic monomers.

In oil and gas processing, it stabilizes hydrocarbon streams and protects refinery equipment from oxidative fouling. This ensures that process efficiency is maintained and downtime caused by equipment failure is minimized.

Rubber and latex formulations incorporate this additive as an antioxidant to extend shelf life. It helps maintain product integrity through rigorous processing and long-term storage conditions in global supply chains.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically as an aqueous solution at concentrations of 85% and 100%. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications aligned to industrial requirements.

Packaging options for this chemical range from standard drums to IBC totes and bulk tanker quantities. This flexibility allows for efficient logistics and handling depending on the specific volume requirements of the facility.

name: Olealkonium chloride
description:
Olealkonium chloride (CAS 37139-99-4 ), also supplied under the trade names Rhodaquat 7LUF and Cycloton 7LUF and recognized commercially as Benzyldimethyloleylammonium chloride, is a quaternary ammonium compound used across personal care, cleaning, and industrial markets.

Its primary functions are antimicrobial preservation, surface modification, and emulsification in formulated products. In personal care, it acts as a conditioning agent and preservative booster in rinse-off and leave-on formulations.

It is particularly effective in hair conditioners and skin creams. Industrial and institutional cleaning products rely on it as an active biocide against bacteria and fungi, where it delivers broad-spectrum efficacy at low use levels.

Textile processors apply it as a softening and antistatic agent during fiber finishing, improving handle and reducing static charge in synthetic fabrics. This versatility makes it a staple in large-scale manufacturing environments.

In leather and paper manufacturing, it functions as a surface-active treatment agent to improve wetting, penetration, and uniformity of processing baths. This ensures consistent quality across various industrial substrates and materials.

Olealkonium chloride is typically supplied as a liquid solution, with active content concentrations commonly ranging from 50% to 80%. Technical-grade material is the standard offering for industrial and cleaning applications.

Personal care grades are available to meet cosmetic formulation requirements and safety standards. Packaging is available in drums and IBC containers suited to bulk procurement for global distribution and logistics.

name: Potassium polysulfide
description:
Potassium polysulfide (CAS 37199-66-9 ) is an inorganic sulfur-potassium salt used industrially as a biocide and chemical treatment agent across water management, mining, and agricultural applications.

Its sulfide chemistry enables targeted precipitation, microbial control, and soil amendment functions that drive demand across multiple regulated sectors. In water treatment, it precipitates heavy metals from industrial effluent streams.

This supports compliance with discharge limits for lead, mercury, and cadmium. Mining operations use it for selective sulfidization of oxidized copper and gold ores ahead of flotation, improving mineral recovery from refractory feed materials.

In agriculture, it functions as a registered pesticide for controlling fungal pathogens and mite populations on crops. It is typically applied as a foliar spray in approved programs to ensure crop health and yield.

Industrial pH buffering applications also employ it where alkaline sulfide chemistry is needed to condition process streams before downstream treatment. Potassium polysulfide is supplied as an aqueous solution for ease of use.

Concentration and polysulfide chain length vary by grade and intended use. Agricultural and pesticide-grade material is formulated to meet EPA registration requirements, while technical-grade solution is available for mining.

Water treatment procurement also utilizes technical-grade solutions for large-scale operations. Packaging typically ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) depending on specific volume requirements.

name: L-citrulline
description:
L-Citrulline (CAS 372-75-8 ) is a non-essential amino acid naturally occurring in watermelon and produced endogenously in the urea cycle. In commercial applications, it functions as a precursor to L-arginine.

It supports nitric oxide pathway activity that underpins its use across sports nutrition, pharmaceutical, and personal care formulations. In sports nutrition, it is a primary active ingredient in pre-workout powders.

These capsules target exercise performance and muscle recovery. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active or supporting ingredient in formulations addressing urea cycle disorders and cardiovascular-related indications.

In functional food and beverage development, it is incorporated into fortified drinks and nutritional bars where amino acid enrichment is a label claim. Personal care formulators include it in topical products.

It is used for its moisture-retention contribution and its role in supporting skin barrier function. This product is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial and commercial applications.

Food-grade and USP -grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms. Food-grade material meets FCC standards for use in ingestible products and dietary supplement manufacturing.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial formulation. Pharmaceutical-grade material is subject to tighter purity and testing requirements to ensure compliance with global regulatory standards for safety.

name: Konjac glucomannan
description:
Konjac glucomannan ( CAS 37220-17-0 ), also supplied as konjac flour and konjac powder, is a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide extracted from the tuber of Amorphophallus konjac.

Approved as E425 in the EU, KGM functions as a gelling agent, thickener, and film-former across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing sectors.

In food production, KGM is used to build gel structures in low-calorie noodles, vegan meat analogues, and restructured seafood products where it replaces gelatin or starch.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into controlled-release tablet matrices and capsule coatings, where its swelling behavior regulates active ingredient delivery.

In personal care, KGM is used in facial masks, moisturizing creams, and cleansing sponges, where its film-forming capacity supports moisture retention on the skin surface.

It also functions as a stabilizer in dairy alternatives and plant-based beverages, preventing phase separation during shelf life and improving overall texture.

Konjac glucomannan is available as an off-white to cream-colored powder in varying particle sizes. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC -compliant) and pharmaceutical-grade material.

Glucomannan content is typically specified at 60–90% or higher for premium grades. Bulk supply is standard in 25 kg bags, with moisture and viscosity specifications declared on data sheets.

name: Potassium peroxymonosulfate
description:
Potassium peroxymonosulfate ( CAS 37222-66-5 ), also known as potassium caroate or KMPS, is an active oxygen-releasing compound supplied commercially as a triple salt. It functions as a non-chlorine oxidizer across disinfection, bleaching, and surface activation applications.

Buyers source it where chlorine-free oxidation is required without sacrificing performance. In water treatment, KMPS serves as a shock oxidizer for swimming pools and aquaculture systems, breaking down organic contaminants.

It is highly effective at controlling biofilm without raising chlorine levels. Personal care formulators use it as the active oxidant in hair color activators and denture cleaning tablets, where controlled peroxide release is critical.

This stability is essential for product shelf life and consumer safety. Pulp and paper producers apply it for bleaching and brightness retention in chlorine-free processing lines to meet environmental standards.

In textile and leather finishing, it functions as a pre-treatment oxidant to improve dye uptake and surface uniformity. This ensures consistent color application and high-quality finishes across various industrial materials.

Potassium monopersulfate is supplied as a white granular or powder solid. Standard commercial grades include technical and pool/spa grades, with active oxygen content typically specified at around 4.5% for most uses.

Industrial and specialty formulation grades are available for personal care and water treatment end uses. These grades ensure the material meets specific purity requirements for sensitive manufacturing environments and applications.

name: Crotonic acid
description:
Crotonic acid (CAS 3724-65-0 ), also known as beta-methylacrylic acid, is an unsaturated monocarboxylic acid used primarily as a reactive monomer and chemical intermediate across polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its conjugated double bond makes it a functional building block for synthesizing resins, coatings, and copolymers with targeted performance characteristics. In polymer chemistry, it is copolymerized with vinyl acetate.

This process produces hair-fixative resins used in aerosol sprays and styling formulations. Agricultural chemical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing crop protection actives and adjuvant systems.

In food and flavor applications, it functions as a flavoring agent and acidulant in approved formulations, particularly where a mild acidity profile is required for specific end products.

Pharmaceutical producers also source it as a synthetic intermediate for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid for industrial use.

Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with purity levels typically ranging from 99% upward for high-specification applications. Packaging is available in small drums through to bulk quantities.

Triton H 66 (CAS 37281-48-4 ) is an anionic surfactant used across industrial formulation and process chemistry. It delivers effective emulsification, dispersion, and degreasing performance in demanding aqueous systems.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a wetting and scouring agent, improving penetration of treatment baths and ensuring uniform fiber or hide processing. This ensures high-quality results in manufacturing.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations use it to emulsify oils and lift soils from hard surfaces, equipment, and process lines. It is highly effective for heavy-duty degreasing and maintenance tasks.

Coatings and adhesive manufacturers incorporate it as a dispersant to stabilize pigment and filler suspensions. This improves product consistency and shelf stability for long-term storage and application.

In paper manufacturing, it supports sizing and surface treatment processes where controlled wetting and dispersion are critical to sheet quality. It helps maintain uniformity across large production runs.

Triton H 66 is typically supplied as a liquid, suited for direct incorporation into aqueous formulations or dilution into process baths. This allows for easy handling and precise dosing in industrial settings.

It is available in technical grade, the standard specification for industrial cleaning, textile, and coatings applications. This grade meets the rigorous requirements of most large-scale chemical processes.

name: Calcium polystyrene sulfonate
description:
Calcium polystyrene sulfonate (CAS 37286-92-3 ), commonly abbreviated as CPS, is a cation-exchange resin used in pharmaceutical manufacturing and clinical formulation. It functions by exchanging calcium ions for potassium ions in the gastrointestinal tract.

This mechanism makes it the active basis for oral and rectal hyperkalemia treatments. CPS is the active pharmaceutical ingredient in finished-dose products designed to reduce elevated potassium levels in patients with renal impairment.

It is formulated into oral suspensions, powders for reconstitution, and rectal enema preparations for hospital and outpatient use. Contract manufacturers and pharmaceutical formulators source CPS as a bulk API for both branded and generic drug products.

Specialty compounding pharmacies also procure CPS to prepare patient-specific dosage forms where commercial products are unavailable or unsuitable. Calcium polystyrene sulfonate is supplied as a fine, cream to buff-colored powder in bulk quantities.

The material is suited to pharmaceutical manufacturing scale and is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Material is typically characterized by defined exchange capacity, particle size distribution, and moisture content to meet API requirements.

Suppliers commonly provide documentation supporting GMP-compliant sourcing for industrial buyers. This includes certificates of analysis and pharmacopoeial alignment with international standards such as USP , BP , or EP guidelines.

name: Palmitoleic acid
description:
Palmitoleic acid (CAS 373-49-9 ), also known as zoomeric acid, is a monounsaturated omega-7 fatty acid sourced primarily from sea buckthorn, macadamia oil, and marine lipids.

It functions as a bioactive lipid ingredient in nutritional, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations where fatty acid profile and skin-compatibility are key sourcing criteria for manufacturers.

In personal care, it is incorporated into facial creams, serums, and barrier-repair products where its structural similarity to skin sebum supports emollient performance and formulation stability.

Nutraceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in omega-7 supplements targeting metabolic and cardiovascular health positioning. Food formulators source it to enrich functional lipid blends.

Pharmaceutical researchers also use it as a reference standard or active component in lipid-based drug delivery systems. It is available as a liquid oil or in concentrated free fatty acid form.

Purity grades typically range from technical to high-purity for specialty applications. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms in the chemical market.

It is also available as a standardized extract within sea buckthorn oil fractions, depending on the intended application. Quality is maintained according to industry standards for lipid purity.

name: Polydecene
description:
Polydecene (CAS 37309-58-3 ), also referred to commercially as decene homopolymer, is a synthetic hydrocarbon polymer used as a base fluid and viscosity modifier in lubricant formulations. Its controlled molecular weight distribution makes it a functional building block for high-performance lubricant systems.

This material is highly valued where thermal stability and low volatility are procurement priorities. In automotive and industrial lubricant blending, it serves as a base stock component in gear oils, compressor oils, and engine oil formulations requiring consistent viscometric performance.

Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it into cutting and forming lubricants where film strength and oxidative stability directly affect tool life and surface finish quality. It provides reliable performance across a wide range of temperature conditions.

In the oil and gas sector, it is used in drilling fluid additives and downhole lubricants where synthetic hydrocarbon base fluids outperform mineral oil under high-pressure conditions. These applications rely on the polymer's inherent chemical stability.

Rheology modifiers based on this polymer are also blended into grease formulations to control consistency and flow behavior. This ensures that the final product maintains its structural integrity during heavy-duty industrial operations and mechanical stress.

The product is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid, with commercial grades differentiated primarily by viscosity grade. Technical-grade material is the standard offering, with viscosity specifications typically ranging to suit light through heavy applications.

Bulk liquid and intermediate bulk container (IBC) supply formats are standard for industrial buyers. This ensures efficient logistics and handling for large-scale manufacturing facilities and chemical blending plants worldwide.

Contact us for supply of Polydecene

name: Potassium lignosulfonate
description:
Potassium lignosulfonate (CAS 37314-65-1 ), also sold as potassium ligninsulfonate, is a water-soluble anionic polymer derived from sulfite pulping of wood. It functions as a dispersant, plasticizer, and binder across a broad range of industrial processes.

In these applications, controlling flow behavior or particle suspension is commercially critical. In concrete and cement production, it acts as a water-reducing admixture, improving workability and compressive strength without increasing water content.

Agricultural formulators use it as a dispersant and binder in wettable powder pesticides and granular fertilizers. This ensures uniform particle distribution and dust suppression during handling and application in the field.

In leather tanning and textile dyeing, it disperses tannins and dyes evenly across substrates. This improves process consistency and reduces chemical waste, making it a valuable additive for large-scale manufacturing operations.

Water treatment operations use it as a sequestrant to inhibit scale formation. It helps keep mineral deposits in suspension within industrial cooling systems, preventing buildup that can lead to equipment inefficiency or failure.

Potassium lignosulfonate is supplied as a brown powder or spray-dried granules, with liquid concentrate forms also available for bulk industrial use. Standard grades include technical and agriculture-grade for various needs.

Purity and lignosulfonate content are typically specified by dry solids content and sulfonate group density. Buyers should confirm compatibility requirements, as molecular weight distribution varies between production sources.

These variations significantly affect performance in concrete versus agricultural applications. Ensuring the correct grade is selected is essential for achieving the desired chemical stability and performance in the final product.

name: Cardanol
description:
Cardanol (CAS 37330-39-5 ) is a phenolic lipid derived from cashew nut shell liquid (CNSL), offering a bio-based alternative to petroleum-derived phenols in reactive polymer systems.

It functions as a reactive diluent, plasticizer, and surface-active modifier across coatings, adhesives, and polymer formulations. In epoxy coatings and anticorrosion primers, cardanol-based hardeners improve film flexibility.

This material maintains chemical resistance, which is a key performance balance for marine and industrial protective coatings. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to reduce viscosity and enhance substrate wetting.

It achieves these properties without sacrificing cure performance. In phenolic resins and friction materials, it acts as a plasticizing co-monomer that reduces brittleness in brake pads and clutch facings.

Lubricant additive producers also incorporate it as a bio-derived base for metalworking fluids. Its phenolic structure contributes to boundary lubrication and surface interaction during industrial processes.

The product is supplied as a dark amber to brown viscous liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically defined by hydroxyl value and unsaturation content.

These specifications are highly relevant to reactive applications. Refined and distilled grades with tighter color and composition profiles are available for demanding coating and polymer applications.
