name: Nonacosanoic acid
description:
Nonacosanoic acid (CAS 4250-38-8 ) is a long-chain saturated fatty acid with 29 carbon atoms, occurring naturally in plant waxes and certain biological matrices. In industry, it functions as a rheology modifier and lubricant.

It also serves as a surface-active agent across personal care, food, and coating applications. In personal care formulations, it contributes to texture control and film-forming properties in creams, balms, and waxy solid formats.

Coating and adhesive manufacturers incorporate it to modify surface wetting behavior and improve substrate adhesion in specialty formulations. As a lubricant component, it is evaluated in systems requiring high-melting chemistry.

This low-migration fatty acid is essential for specific industrial processes. Food-grade applications include its use as a processing aid or surface modifier where long-chain fatty acid functionality is required under regulatory frameworks.

Nonacosanoic acid is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. It is available in research-grade and technical-grade quantities, with supply predominantly through specialty chemical and fine chemical distributors.

description:
Methyltriacetoxysilane ( CAS 4253-34-3 ), commonly abbreviated as MTAS, is an acetoxy-functional silane used as a crosslinker and curing agent across adhesive, sealant, and coating systems.

It releases acetic acid upon moisture exposure, triggering condensation cure in silicone-based formulations. MTAS is a primary crosslinker in one-component acetoxy-cure silicone sealants.

This includes construction, glazing, and sanitary grades where fast surface cure and strong substrate adhesion are required. In industrial coatings, it functions as a surface modifier to improve adhesion.

It is effective for glass, metals, and mineral substrates. Silicone elastomer compounders use it to control network density and mechanical properties in RTV systems for various industrial applications.

Personal care formulators apply it in film-forming and conditioning systems where silicone crosslinking at ambient conditions is needed without heat activation or specialized equipment.

Methyltriacetoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most manufacturing needs.

name: Polyoxyethylene lauryl ether sodium phosphate

Polyoxyethylene lauryl ether sodium phosphate (CAS 42612-52-2 ) is an anionic surfactant combining ethoxylated lauryl alcohol with a phosphate ester sodium salt structure. It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and detergent active across personal care, cleaning, and industrial processing applications.

In shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers, it delivers mild foaming and emulsification while remaining compatible with sensitive skin formulations. Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it as a degreasing active where low irritation is required.

Good hard-surface wetting is provided alongside detergency for various maintenance tasks. Textile processors apply it during scouring, dyeing, and finishing operations to improve fiber wetting and dye penetration uniformity across the fabric.

Leather and paper manufacturing operations use it to control surface tension and aid dispersion of processing agents across substrates. Polyoxyethylene lauryl ether sodium phosphate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste at varying ethoxylation degrees.

The specific ethoxylation levels determine the HLB value and application fit for the final product. Buyers should confirm the EO chain length when sourcing to ensure the surfactant meets the specific technical requirements of their formulation.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material suitable for rinse-off and leave-on personal care product registration. Packaging is commonly offered in drums and IBC totes for industrial volumes to facilitate transport.

name: Dimethylamine-epichlorohydrin-ethylenediamine copolymer
description:
Dimethylamine-epichlorohydrin-ethylenediamine copolymer (CAS 42751-79-1 ) is a cationic polyelectrolyte used across water treatment and process industries to destabilize suspended particles and facilitate their removal.

Its quaternary amine functionality delivers a strong positive charge across a broad pH range, making it effective where consistent coagulation performance is required for industrial applications.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, it functions as a primary coagulant or coagulant aid, reducing turbidity and suspended solids load ahead of filtration or sedimentation stages.

Pulp and paper producers apply it for retention and drainage improvement on the wet end, helping fine fibers and fillers bind to the sheet rather than pass through the wire during production.

In textile processing, it supports dye fixation and effluent treatment, reducing color in discharge water to meet regulatory limits. Leather and tannery operations use it to coagulate protein-rich streams.

This copolymer is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations ranging from 40% to 50% active content. Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or tankers is the norm for buyers.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with product performance characterized by charge density and molecular weight rather than specific pharmacopeial standards like USP or Ph.Eur.

The material is also evaluated against BP , EP , and ACS benchmarks when required for specific high-purity industrial processes or specialized chemical manufacturing applications.

name: Lauramidopropylbetaine
description:
Lauramidopropylbetaine (CAS 4292-10-8 ) is an amphoteric surfactant derived from lauric acid, used across personal care and cosmetic formulations for its foam-boosting, conditioning, and mildness-enhancing properties.

It is closely related to cocamidopropyl betaine but based on a defined C12 lauric acid chain, offering formulators a more consistent fatty acid profile for high-performance applications.

Procurement teams source it primarily as a liquid concentrate for rinse-off and leave-on product manufacturing. In shampoos and body washes, it boosts and stabilizes foam generated by primary anionic surfactants.

It reduces overall formulation irritation potential when used with sodium lauryl sulfate. Facial cleansers and baby wash products incorporate it where mildness is a priority for sensitive skin types.

It helps moderate the aggressiveness of stronger surfactants in the blend. It functions as a secondary surfactant in conditioning shampoos and two-in-one formulations, contributing to wet-comb feel.

Mild liquid hand soaps and intimate hygiene products also use it to balance cleansing performance with skin compatibility. Lauramidopropylbetaine is supplied as an aqueous liquid, typically at 30–35% active content.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and COSMOS-approved variants to meet clean beauty and certified natural formulation requirements. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers.

name: Octadecyltrimethylammonium iodide
description:
Octadecyltrimethylammonium iodide (CAS 4292-25-5 ) is a quaternary ammonium salt used industrially as a cationic surfactant. It modifies surface charge and controls rheology.

This chemical enables stable emulsification across a range of formulation and process applications. In textile and leather processing, it conditions fiber surfaces and improves dye uptake by altering substrate charge.

Water treatment operations use it to disperse suspended solids and modify the wetting behavior of treatment media. It is an essential component for managing complex industrial fluid systems.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into conditioning systems where controlled viscosity and emulsion stability are required. It provides reliable performance in diverse cosmetic and hygiene products.

In paper manufacturing, it functions as a surface-active agent to improve sheet formation and coating adhesion. This helps maintain high quality and consistency during large-scale production runs.

Octadecyltrimethylammonium iodide is typically supplied as a solid powder or crystalline material. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial surface modification.

This grade is suitable for dispersion and process chemistry applications. Purity specifications vary by supplier, with high-purity grades available for research and specialty formulation use.

name: Tripropylene glycol diacrylate
description:
Tripropylene glycol diacrylate , commonly abbreviated as TPGDA , is a difunctional acrylate monomer used as a reactive diluent and crosslinker in UV- and EB-curable systems. It reduces viscosity in formulations while contributing to the cured polymer network.

This chemical, identified by CAS 42978-66-5 , offers formulators a balance between processing ease and final film performance. In UV-curable coatings and inks, it lowers formulation viscosity without the need for solvent addition.

This functionality enables faster cure speeds and cleaner processing on high-speed printing lines. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a crosslinking monomer to improve cohesive strength and flexibility in various systems.

It is particularly effective in pressure-sensitive and structural adhesive systems. Electronics producers use it in conformal coatings and encapsulants where controlled crosslink density is critical to substrate adhesion and dielectric performance.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a reactive plasticizer that integrates into the polymer matrix during cure rather than migrating over time. This ensures long-term stability and performance in the finished product.

The product is supplied as a clear liquid, typically available in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. It is predominantly offered in technical and industrial grades, with specifications aligned to monomer purity standards.

These standards are relevant to coatings and adhesives manufacturing. Some suppliers offer inhibited grades with controlled hydroquinone monomethyl ether levels to ensure storage stability during transport and long-term warehouse storage.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a dispersing and stabilizing agent in topical and oral preparations where natural-origin excipients are preferred. It meets various industrial requirements for consistency and performance in complex mixtures.

In textile and paper processing, it acts as a sizing and dispersion aid, helping to control coating rheology and improve substrate adhesion. This versatility makes it a valuable component in high-performance manufacturing environments.

Food-grade applications include its use as a stabilizer and texture modifier in functional food systems. It is often evaluated against standards such as FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , or ACS depending on the specific regional regulatory requirements.

Sodium carboxymethyl inulin is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in technical and cosmetic-grade specifications, with degree of substitution and molecular weight being the primary parameters that differentiate commercial grades.

Packaging options generally range from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply. This ensures that both research facilities and large-scale production plants can access the material in the necessary volumes for their specific operations.

In food and beverage manufacturing, diacetyl ( FEMA 2370 ) is used to impart butter, cream, and caramel notes in margarines, dairy analogs, and microwave popcorn coatings.

Flavor houses use it as a building block in complex flavor compositions where low-level dosing achieves high aromatic impact in confectionery products and baked goods.

In personal care, it contributes to fragrance blends targeting warm, gourmand, or dairy-inspired scent profiles. Its reactive diketone functionality also supports cross-linking applications.

In these oral care applications, it helps maintain pH consistency in toothpaste and mouthwash formulations. In cosmetic systems, it contributes moisturizing properties that support skin conditioning in leave-on and rinse-off products.

Food-grade applications include use as a processing aid and buffering agent in select formulations where amino acid-derived additives are required. This versatile chemical is often utilized for its high purity and compatibility with various ingredients.

name: n-formylmorpholine
description:
N-Formylmorpholine (CAS 4394-85-8 ), commonly abbreviated as NFM, is a polar aprotic solvent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer processing, and industrial cleaning applications.

Its high solvating power and thermal stability make it a preferred alternative to more regulated solvents in demanding process environments. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, NFM functions as a reaction solvent.

It is used as a carrier in active ingredient synthesis, particularly where low volatility and chemical inertness are process requirements. Polymer processors use it to dissolve and spin aromatic polyamides.

This material is ideal for creams, lotions, and rinse-off cleansing products where controlled foam and skin compatibility are priorities. Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations rely on it for hard-surface degreasing.

name: Carnauba wax
description:
Carnauba wax (CAS 442682-58-8 ) is a natural plant-derived wax extracted from the leaves of the Brazilian palm Copernicia prunifera. It functions as a hardening agent, lubricant, and rheology modifier across food, cosmetic, and industrial coating applications.

In food manufacturing, it is applied as a surface coating on confectionery, fruits, and pharmaceutical tablets to provide gloss and reduce moisture transfer. This prevents sticking during processing and ensures a professional finish for consumer goods.

Cosmetic formulators use it to build structure in lipsticks, solid balms, and pressed powders. Its high melting point delivers heat stability and firm texture, making it an essential ingredient for high-quality personal care products.

Industrial coatings and polishes, including automotive, furniture, and floor care products, rely on it to deliver a hard, durable finish. It is prized for creating a characteristic high-gloss surface that resists wear and environmental damage.

In adhesives and sealant formulations, it acts as a processing aid and release modifier. This improves slip and reduces tack at elevated temperatures, facilitating more efficient manufacturing and application processes for industrial users.

The material is supplied as hard, brittle flakes or powder in yellow to light brown grades. Standard commercial grades include T1, T3, and T4, reflecting refinement level and color, with T1 being the most refined grade available.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet FCC and BP specifications. These quality standards ensure the product is suitable for sensitive applications in the global food and healthcare industries.

name: Metronidazole

Topical formulations such as gels and creams are produced for dermatological indications, including rosacea management. Here, the active is incorporated at defined concentrations into semi-solid bases for targeted delivery.

Veterinary drug manufacturers use the compound in oral and injectable preparations targeting gastrointestinal anaerobic infections. These applications are common in both companion animals and livestock health management.

It also acts as a stabilizer and release agent in rubber and polymer compounding. Lithium stearate is supplied as a white powder or fine granules for various manufacturing processes.

name: Dimethyl dicarbonate
description:
Dimethyl dicarbonate ( CAS 4525-33-1 ), commercially known as DMDC and approved as E242 , is a cold-sterilization agent used to eliminate spoilage microorganisms in beverages without heat treatment.

It reacts rapidly with microbial enzymes and decomposes into trace carbon dioxide and methanol, leaving no functional residue in the finished product. DMDC is the standard antimicrobial treatment for still and sparkling wines.

This allows producers to stabilize product without altering flavor profiles through thermal processing. In ready-to-drink teas, juices, and isotonic sports beverages, it controls yeast and mold at dosage levels compliant with regulatory limits.

Craft brewers and commercial breweries use it to treat non-alcoholic and low-alcohol beers where conventional pasteurization would compromise sensory quality. In biotechnology, DMDC functions as a nuclease inhibitor in RNA extraction workflows.

It protects RNA integrity during sample processing. Dimethyl dicarbonate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in small sealed containers for laboratory use and in larger drums or intermediate bulk containers for production.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the primary commercial grade, with purity levels generally at or above 99%. Technical-grade material is available for non-food biotechnology and research applications.

Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as both a corrosion inhibitor and lubricity additive in cutting and grinding fluids. It ensures smooth skin feel in cosmetics and high performance in industrial fluids.

In coatings and adhesives, it acts as a dispersant and emulsifying agent for pigment pastes and water-based systems. Textile and leather processing operations use it to prepare emulsified lubricants.

These softening agents are applied during fiber and hide treatment to improve texture and durability. Triethanolamine stearate is typically supplied as a paste or waxy solid depending on the specific grade.

Appearance and consistency vary by the stearic acid ratio used during production. Technical-grade material is the standard offering for industrial applications including metalworking fluids and coatings.

Cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity specifications is available for personal care formulations. Our product ensures consistent quality for manufacturers requiring reliable emulsification and surface activity.

name: Coniferyl alcohol

Biotechnology and life sciences laboratories source it as a high-purity reference compound for enzyme activity assays. These assays particularly involve peroxidases and laccases involved in lignocellulosic biomass conversion for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical researchers use it as a synthetic intermediate in the preparation of bioactive phenylpropanoid derivatives. It also serves as a model substrate in studies targeting lignin valorization for bio-based material development.

Confectionery and ready meals often utilize this ingredient to achieve vibrant hues without synthetic dyes. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it into capsules, tablets, and functional supplements.

name: Dicyandiamide
description:
Dicyandiamide (CAS 461-58-5 ), commonly abbreviated as DICY and also known as cyanoguanidine, is a crystalline solid used as a latent curing agent and cross-linking compound across multiple industrial sectors.

Its low reactivity at ambient temperatures makes it practical for formulating one-component systems with extended shelf life. In epoxy resin systems, DICY functions as a latent hardener for structural adhesives.

It is also utilized in powder coatings and printed circuit board laminates, activating only at elevated cure temperatures. Textile and paper processors use it to produce crease-resistant and wet-strength treatments.

In these applications, it reacts with other finishing agents to build durable cross-linked networks on fiber substrates. In leather processing, it acts as a retanning auxiliary that improves fiber structure and fullness.

Flame-retardant formulations for plastics and coatings also incorporate DICY as a reactive nitrogen-containing component. This specific chemical property contributes to char formation during combustion processes.

Dicyandiamide is supplied as a white crystalline powder in a range of particle sizes. Fine-milled grades are available for epoxy applications requiring uniform dispersion and high performance.

name: Hydantoin
description:
Hydantoin (CAS 461-72-3 ), also known as 2,4-imidazolidinedione, is a five-membered heterocyclic compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate and stabilizer across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing.

Its core ring structure serves as the synthetic scaffold for a broad range of active ingredients, preservatives, and specialty chemicals. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is a key precursor for producing amino acids.

The material is utilized via the Bucherer-Bergs reaction, as well as for anticonvulsant drug intermediates such as phenytoin. Personal care formulators use hydantoin-derived compounds as formaldehyde-releasing preservatives.

These derivatives are common in shampoos, conditioners, and skin creams. It also functions as a buffering and stabilizing agent in formulations where controlled pH maintenance extends shelf life or protects sensitive actives.

Industrial chemical producers use it as a building block for specialty agrochemicals and hydantoin-based biocides. These are applied in water treatment and industrial disinfection processes across various sectors.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP standards for regulated supply chains.

name: tert-butylaminoethanol

In water treatment and metalworking fluids, it provides corrosion inhibition by neutralizing acidic species and forming protective complexes on metal surfaces. This dual functionality makes it a versatile component for complex chemical systems.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a neutralizing amine to adjust pH in waterborne resin systems, improving stability and film formation. This ensures that the final product maintains its integrity and performance over time.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into emulsion systems where controlled alkalinity and compatibility with surfactant blends are required. Its unique structure allows for precise control over the chemical environment of the formulation.

In lubricant formulations, it acts as a functional additive that combines buffering capacity with surface-active behavior to extend fluid service life. This helps in maintaining the efficiency of machinery and reducing maintenance costs.

Tert-butylaminoethanol is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging suited to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures that large-scale operations can maintain a steady supply of this essential chemical intermediate.

In functional food and dietary supplement production, ALA is incorporated into fortified oils, capsules, and nutritional blends to deliver plant-sourced omega-3 content to finished products.

Personal care formulators use it in facial oils, moisturizers, and hair treatments, where its skin-barrier-supporting properties justify premium positioning in naturals-oriented product lines.

In specialty emulsion formulations, it contributes to dispersion stability in products where polyunsaturated fatty acid composition is a labeled or regulated specification.

name: Carbonic acid
description:
Carbonic acid (CAS 463-79-6 ) is a weak inorganic acid formed when carbon dioxide dissolves in water, existing in equilibrium with dissolved CO2 in aqueous systems.

In industrial and commercial contexts, it functions primarily as a pH-regulating agent and mild acidulant across water treatment, food processing, and pharmaceutical applications.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, it is used to adjust alkalinity and control scaling in distribution systems without introducing chloride or sulfate ions.

Carbonated beverage production relies on dissolved CO2/carbonic acid equilibrium to deliver consistent acidity and preservation in soft drinks, sparkling water, and beer.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, buffered carbonic acid systems support pH stabilization in parenteral formulations and effervescent tablet chemistry for various products.

Agricultural irrigation systems use carbonic acid dosing to lower the pH of alkaline water, improving nutrient availability and preventing mineral deposits in drip lines.

Carbonic acid is not isolable as a stable pure compound and is supplied commercially as CO2 gas or carbonated aqueous solutions for direct application in many industries.

Food-grade and technical-grade CO2 are the standard supply forms, with food-grade material meeting specifications under FCC and relevant pharmacopeial standards.

name: Eucalyptol
description:
Eucalyptol (CAS 470-82-6 ), also known commercially as cineole, is a naturally derived cyclic ether extracted primarily from eucalyptus oil. It functions as both a flavoring agent and a functional solvent across food, fragrance, and personal care manufacturing.

In oral care formulations, such as toothpastes, mouthwashes, and breath fresheners, it delivers a characteristic cool, camphoraceous flavor profile recognized under FEMA 2465 . Fragrance compounders use it as a top-note ingredient in fine fragrances and air care products.

It is frequently utilized in functional perfumery where a fresh, medicinal character is required. In personal care, it acts as a penetration-enhancing carrier in topical formulations, improving the delivery of active ingredients through the skin barrier.

Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it at controlled use levels to impart minty, herbal notes in confectionery, baked goods, and liqueurs. This versatile compound is essential for creating complex flavor profiles in the food industry.

The material is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers. It is available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications to meet various regulatory requirements.

High-purity grades commonly exceed 99% eucalyptol content for flavor and fragrance applications. Natural and synthetic sourcing options exist, with natural-origin material derived from eucalyptus or rosemary oil commanding preference.

These natural options are particularly favored in clean-label formulations. The product maintains high quality standards to ensure consistency across large-scale manufacturing batches and diverse industrial applications.

Contact us for supply of Eucalyptol

name: Potassium lauryl sulfate
description:
Potassium lauryl sulfate (CAS 4706-78-9 ), also known as potassium dodecyl sulfate, is an anionic surfactant used across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning applications. It delivers reliable foaming, emulsification, and detergency across a broad range of formulation types.

In personal care, it functions as the primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers where a potassium-based salt is preferred over sodium alternatives for specific texture or solubility profiles.

Textile processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to remove oils, sizing agents, and contaminants from fiber and fabric prior to dyeing or finishing. This ensures high-quality results during the manufacturing process.

In leather processing, it supports degreasing and preparation steps where consistent emulsification of natural fats is required. This helps maintain the integrity and quality of the leather throughout the treatment stages.

Paper and pulp operations employ it as a dispersing agent to control fiber distribution and improve sheet formation. This application is critical for achieving uniform thickness and strength in various paper products.

Potassium lauryl sulfate is supplied as a powder or as an aqueous solution, with active content typically ranging from 30% to 95% depending on the grade. This flexibility allows for use in diverse industrial settings.

Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly available, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity standards suitable for personal care formulations. These grades ensure safety and efficacy in consumer-facing products.

Packaging options generally include drums and bulk quantities to serve both formulators and industrial users. This variety in logistics supports both small-scale laboratory testing and large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Calcium carbonate
description:
Calcium carbonate (CAS 471-34-1 ), also known as E 170 and supplied under grades such as Aeromatt, is a mineral-based ingredient used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a filler, pH buffer, coating agent, and calcium source depending on the application sector. In plastics and rubber compounding, it acts as a functional filler that reduces raw material costs.

This versatile mineral improves stiffness and dimensional stability in finished parts. Food and pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a calcium fortification agent, acidity regulator, and tablet excipient in solid dosage forms.

Paper producers apply it as a coating pigment and filler to improve brightness, opacity, and printability in fine paper grades. In construction, it is a core raw material in cement and lime mortars.

Dry-mix formulations benefit from controlled alkalinity which supports setting and durability. Calcium carbonate is available as ground (GCC) and precipitated (PCC) grades, each offering distinct particle size distributions.

These variations are suited to different processing requirements. Standard supply forms include fine powder, ultrafine powder, and coated variants for polymer applications. Recognized grades include food-grade, FCC , and USP .

Additional quality standards available for procurement include Ph. Eur. and technical grade for industrial use. This ensures compliance across various global regulatory frameworks and manufacturing specifications.

name: Oxamide
description:
Oxamide (CAS 471-46-5 ), also known as oxalamide, is the diamide form of oxalic acid used industrially as a slow-release nitrogen source and pH buffer. Its low solubility and controlled hydrolysis rate make it a functional alternative to conventional urea-based nitrogen carriers.

In agriculture, this compound is formulated into slow-release fertilizers where its gradual soil hydrolysis delivers nitrogen over extended periods. This process significantly reduces leaching losses compared to fast-release alternatives used in large-scale farming.

The pulp and paper industry uses it as a buffering agent to stabilize process pH during chemical pulping and bleaching stages. This ensures that the chemical reactions remain consistent throughout the manufacturing cycle for better paper quality.

In textile and leather processing, it supports pH regulation in dyebath and tanning formulations. This helps maintain consistent bath chemistry across production runs, preventing fluctuations that could damage delicate fabrics or hides during treatment.

Specialty resin and polymer formulators also incorporate this chemical as a stabilizer or co-reactant. It is particularly useful in applications where controlled nitrogen release or specific buffering capacity is required for the final product.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in technical grade , which covers the majority of industrial and agrochemical applications. Standard packaging includes 25 kg bags, with bulk quantities available for large buyers.

Purity specifications typically range from 98% to 99%+ on a dry basis, with the technical grade being the predominant commercial form. This high level of purity ensures reliable performance in both agricultural and industrial chemical processes.

name: Glycyrrhetinic acid
description:
Glycyrrhetinic acid (CAS 471-53-4 ), also known as uralenic acid, is a pentacyclic triterpenoid derived from licorice root extract. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a skin-conditioning active.

In flavoring applications, it contributes to the characteristic licorice taste profile of finished products. In cosmetic formulations, it is used in anti-inflammatory creams, serums, and spot-treatment products.

Formulators incorporate it into whitening and brightening preparations where it acts as a tyrosinase modulator. This helps to reduce the appearance of hyperpigmentation and redness in various skin types.

In the flavor industry, it is used as a flavoring agent and acidulant in confectionery and oral care products. It is also utilized in tobacco flavoring systems where a licorice character is required.

It appears in topical pharmaceutical preparations as a functional active in formulations addressing minor skin irritation. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 98% by HPLC. These standards ensure high performance in sensitive applications.

Bulk quantities are offered in kilogram and multi-kilogram packaging to suit both development-scale and commercial production requirements. We ensure consistent quality for all global manufacturing needs.

name: Stachydrine
description:
Stachydrine (CAS 471-87-4 ) is a naturally occurring proline betaine found in plants such as Leonurus japonicus and citrus species. It is the primary bioactive marker used to standardize botanical extracts for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications.

In pharmaceutical development, this compound serves as the reference standard and active constituent in standardized extracts used in cardiovascular and women's health formulations. Nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it into dietary supplements where extract potency must be verified.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers source it as an analytical reference material for HPLC method development and bioavailability studies. Food and functional beverage formulators use standardized botanical extracts where label claims require quantified active content.

The material is available as a white crystalline powder in both high-purity reference-grade and bulk active ingredient formats. Common specifications include ≥98% purity by HPLC, suitable for use as an analytical standard or as an active in finished formulations.

Botanical extract forms standardized to a defined content are also commercially available for direct use in supplement manufacturing. This ensures consistency across production batches and meets the rigorous requirements of modern quality control protocols.

Our supply chain ensures that the material meets international quality standards for purity and stability. We provide comprehensive documentation including certificates of analysis and safety data sheets to support your regulatory compliance needs.

Contact us for supply of Stachydrine

name: tris(N-hydroxyethyl) hexahydrotriazine
description:
Tris(N-hydroxyethyl) hexahydrotriazine (CAS 4719-04-4 ) is a triazine-based biocide and corrosion inhibitor used across industrial preservation and fluid protection applications. It controls microbial growth and prevents metal degradation in water-containing systems.

This chemical serves as a practical active ingredient where both antimicrobial and anti-corrosive functions are required simultaneously. In metalworking and cutting fluids, it suppresses bacterial and fungal contamination that shortens fluid service life.

It effectively prevents odor and corrosion in sumps caused by microbial activity. Water treatment programs use it to control sulfate-reducing bacteria and biofilm formation in cooling towers and industrial water circuits.

In oil and gas operations, it is dosed into injection water and produced water systems. This application helps to inhibit microbial-induced corrosion in pipelines and downhole equipment during extraction and transport.

Coatings and adhesive formulations incorporate it as an in-can preservative to extend shelf life. This protects the final products against microbial spoilage during storage and distribution to end users.

Tris(N-hydroxyethyl) hexahydrotriazine is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 78–80% active content. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for these industrial applications.

The product is suited for industrial biocide and corrosion inhibition programs. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers, reflecting its use in bulk industrial dosing programs across various manufacturing sectors.

name: Astaxanthin
description:
Astaxanthin (CAS 472-61-7 ), also marketed under the trade names Natupink and Lucantin Pink and designated E161j in the EU, is a ketocarotenoid pigment sourced from microalgae, yeast fermentation, or chemical synthesis.

It functions as a high-performance antioxidant and colorant across feed, food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications. In aquaculture feed, it is the primary pigmenting agent responsible for the characteristic pink-red coloration of farmed salmon and trout flesh.

This directly affects product marketability and consumer acceptance in the global seafood industry. Poultry feed manufacturers incorporate it to enhance yolk and skin pigmentation in egg and broiler production to meet specific market demands.

In nutraceutical and functional food formulations, it is used as an antioxidant active at concentrations where most carotenoids are ineffective. This unique property supports premium supplement positioning for various health and wellness brands.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into anti-aging creams and serums where its antioxidant activity supports product claims around skin protection. It is highly valued for its ability to improve the overall appearance and health of the skin.

The product is supplied as a synthetic oleoresin, microalgae-derived extract, or encapsulated powder. Oil suspensions and water-dispersible beadlet forms are also available for specialized feed and supplement manufacturing processes.

Standard commercial concentrations include 1%, 2.5%, 5%, and 10% in oil or beadlet form. Recognized grades include feed-grade, food-grade, and USP -grade for dietary supplement applications requiring high purity levels.

name: Cryptoxanthin
description:
Cryptoxanthin (CAS 472-70-8 ), also known as E161c , is a naturally occurring carotenoid pigment derived primarily from sources such as paprika and citrus fruits. It functions as a yellow-to-orange colorant and antioxidant across food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications.

In food and beverage manufacturing, E161c is approved for use as a natural colorant, delivering warm yellow and orange hues to products such as juices, dairy items, and confectionery. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement formulators incorporate it as a provitamin A source.

This positioning allows finished products to sit within the carotenoid supplement category. In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it is used to impart color and antioxidant activity in skin creams, serums, and color cosmetics.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers also evaluate it as a natural pigment for soft gel capsules and coating systems where synthetic dye alternatives are required. This versatility makes it a valuable ingredient for manufacturers seeking clean-label solutions.

Cryptoxanthin is supplied as a powder or oil suspension, with concentration and carrier varying by application. Food and supplement grades conforming to E161c specifications are the most commonly traded forms in the global market.

Buyers should confirm source material, extraction method, and carotenoid content with suppliers. These factors directly affect regulatory acceptance and formulation performance across different industrial sectors and geographic regions.

name: Delta-carotene
description:
Delta-carotene (CAS 472-92-4 ) is a naturally occurring carotenoid pigment found in plant sources, functioning as a precursor to vitamin A and a source of orange-yellow coloration in food and feed applications.

It belongs to the broader carotene family and is evaluated for use across nutrition, agriculture, and cosmetic formulation contexts. In animal feed, delta-carotene contributes to yolk and skin pigmentation in poultry.

It also supports provitamin A nutrition in livestock diets. Food manufacturers incorporate carotenoid blends into beverages, dairy analogs, and fat-based products where natural coloration and antioxidant stabilization are required.

In personal care, it is used in skin-conditioning formulations where carotenoid-derived color and antioxidant activity support product positioning in natural and clean-label lines for various consumer markets.

Agricultural supplement programs targeting provitamin A enrichment in animal nutrition represent a further procurement channel. Delta-carotene is typically available as a crystalline powder or in oil-suspension forms.

Emulsified forms are also suited to different formulation matrices. Supply is generally sourced as part of mixed natural carotene extracts rather than as an isolated single-isomer material for industrial use.

Buyers should confirm these details at the specification stage. Technical and food-grade designations apply depending on the intended end use and regional regulatory requirements for the specific application.

Contact us for supply of Delta-carotene

name: gamma-carotene
description:
Gamma-carotene (CAS 472-93-5 ), also referenced as beta,psi-Carotene in technical literature, is a naturally occurring carotenoid pigment that functions as both a colorant and antioxidant precursor.

It is used in food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. Unlike the more prevalent beta-carotene, it offers a distinct carotenoid profile that appeals to formulators seeking broader spectrum carotenoid sourcing.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it contributes orange-yellow coloration to products such as beverages, dairy analogs, and functional foods where natural pigment sourcing is a formulation requirement.

Nutraceutical and dietary supplement producers incorporate it as part of mixed carotenoid blends, where the combination of provitamin A activity and antioxidant function supports product positioning.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it in skin care preparations where carotenoid-based antioxidant activity is a stated ingredient benefit for high-end topical formulations.

Pharmaceutical researchers also evaluate it within carotenoid ingredient matrices for encapsulated or softgel delivery formats, ensuring compliance with USP or FCC standards where applicable.

Gamma-carotene is typically supplied as a crystalline powder or in oil suspension form, depending on the intended application and delivery system requirements for the manufacturer.

It is available in food-grade and research-grade specifications, with purity levels commonly confirmed by HPLC. Due to its relative scarcity, it is sourced through specialty carotenoid suppliers.

name: Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate
description:
Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate (CAS 4722-98-9 ), also known as MEA-Lauryl Sulfate, is an anionic surfactant derived from lauryl alcohol and monoethanolamine. It functions as a primary surfactant delivering foaming, cleansing, and emulsification performance.

This versatile chemical is used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. In shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps, it generates dense, stable foam while effectively removing oils and residues from hair and skin.

Home care formulators incorporate it into hard surface cleaners and dishwashing liquids. It is valued where consistent degreasing performance and compatibility with other surfactant blends are required for high-quality results.

Textile and leather processors use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils and sizing agents. It is also effective at removing contaminants during various pre-treatment stages in industrial manufacturing.

In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber dispersion and surface treatment processes. This is particularly useful where controlled foaming and emulsification are operationally critical for the final product quality.

Monoethanolamine lauryl sulfate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste. The active matter content commonly ranges around 30–35% aqueous solution, providing a stable base for a wide variety of formulations.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care versus industrial end uses. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs for industrial buyers worldwide.

name: Glycerol formal
description:
Glycerol formal (CAS 4740-78-7 ), also known as 1,3-Dioxan-5-ol, is a cyclic acetal solvent derived from glycerol that combines low volatility with strong solvency across polar and non-polar systems.

It functions as a solvent, humectant, and plasticizer in formulations where conventional glycols or standard solvents fall short on performance or regulatory fit. In coatings and adhesives, it improves resin compatibility.

This versatile chemical enhances film formation while reducing the need for more aggressive solvents. Personal care formulators use it as a humectant and carrier in skin and hair products for better results.

Its glycerol origin supports mild, skin-compatible positioning in various cosmetic applications. In industrial and household cleaning concentrates, it acts as a co-solvent that boosts active ingredient solubility.

This material ensures stability without compromising the integrity of the final formulation. Polymer and elastomer compounders incorporate it as a plasticizer to improve flexibility and processability in finished materials.

Glycerol formal is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at high purity levels suited for both industrial and cosmetic-grade applications. Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly available options.

Specifications vary by supplier based on purity, water content, and residual acetal profile. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on order volume and specific logistical requirements for the client.

name: Irgacure 127
description:
Irgacure 127 (CAS 474510-57-1 ), also known as Bis(4-(2-hydroxy-2-methylpropionyl)phenyl)methane, is a high-performance alpha-hydroxy ketone photoinitiator designed for UV-curable systems.

It generates free radicals upon UV exposure, triggering rapid polymerization and crosslinking in formulated products. Its low volatility and high molecular weight make it a preferred choice for compliance.

In UV-curable coatings for wood, plastic, and metal substrates, this photoinitiator delivers fast surface cure with minimal yellowing. This characteristic supports high-throughput production lines effectively.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to achieve controlled cure depth and bond strength in structural applications. It is also utilized in pressure-sensitive applications for consistent performance.

In energy-curable printing inks, including offset, flexo, and screen, it supports cure performance across pigmented and clear systems. It is highly valued for its versatility in various ink formulations.

It is also specified in photopolymer formulations for electronics and optical applications. This is particularly important where low extractable content is a strict regulatory requirement for the industry.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity specifications typically reaching levels at or above 98%.

Standard packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for laboratory and development use to bulk quantities for commercial formulation. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale testing and large-scale manufacturing.

description:
1,2-Cyclohexanedicarboxylic acid diisononyl ester (CAS 474919-59-0 ), commercially known as Hexamoll DINCH, is a non-phthalate plasticizer developed as a safer alternative to conventional phthalate-based softeners.

It functions as a primary plasticizer, imparting flexibility and durability to PVC and other polymer systems across demanding applications. In sensitive-contact applications it replaces phthalate plasticizers.

These applications include medical devices, food packaging films, and children's toys where regulatory compliance and low migration are procurement priorities. Automotive interior components also utilize this material.

Dashboards, door panels, and seating materials use it to meet strict VOC emission standards and long-term heat stability requirements. In building and construction, it is specified for flexible PVC flooring.

It is also used for roofing membranes and wall coverings where UV resistance and low fogging are critical. Rubber compounders incorporate it into seals and gaskets requiring flexibility and compliance.

These components often must meet food-contact or potable-water regulations. The product is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options for high-volume procurement.

It is available to technical and food-contact grades, with documentation supporting compliance under REACH, EU food contact regulations, and FDA requirements. Specifications are typically aligned with major OEM frameworks.

This alignment with regulatory approval frameworks makes grade verification a standard part of sourcing qualification. The material offers a reliable solution for manufacturers seeking high-performance alternatives.

name: Acusol op 301
description:
Acusol OP 301 (CAS 475673-75-7 ), also known as OP 301, is an alkali-swellable acrylic polymer emulsion designed for rheology modification and stabilization in aqueous formulations.

It thickens and suspends at elevated pH, giving formulators precise control over viscosity and flow behavior across a range of end products. In personal care, it builds viscosity in shampoos and body washes.

The polymer is ideal for conditioning systems where clarity and skin compatibility are priorities. Coatings formulators use it to control sag resistance and improve pigment suspension in waterborne paints.

It is highly effective in architectural and industrial paints. In adhesives and sealants, it contributes to open-time management and application rheology in water-based systems for industrial use.

Water treatment applications rely on its dispersing function to stabilize suspensions. This prevents particle settling in treatment chemical formulations, ensuring consistent performance in various environments.

Acusol OP 301 is supplied as an aqueous polymer emulsion, typically in liquid form suitable for direct incorporation. It is available in technical grade for manufacturing needs.

The product meets the performance requirements of industrial and personal care manufacturing. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for industrial-scale procurement.

name: Ellagic acid
description:
Ellagic acid (CAS 476-66-4 ) is a naturally derived polyphenol extracted primarily from pomegranate, oak galls, and other tannin-rich plant sources. In food and cosmetic manufacturing, it functions as an antioxidant and skin-brightening active.

This versatile compound protects formulations and finished products from oxidative degradation. In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into serums, creams, and spot-treatment products targeting hyperpigmentation.

The ingredient inhibits melanin synthesis to deliver a measurable brightening effect. Food manufacturers use it as a natural antioxidant to extend shelf life in functional beverages, nutraceutical supplements, and fortified food products.

In dietary supplement production, it is supplied as a standardized botanical extract. It is positioned as a premium plant-based antioxidant ingredient for capsule and tablet formats to meet consumer demand for natural labels.

Cosmetic formulators also apply it in anti-aging product lines where oxidative stress protection is a key performance claim. The material is available as a fine yellow powder, typically supplied as a standardized extract.

Defined polyphenol content ranges from 40% to 98% purity depending on the application. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent for industrial use and product development.

High-purity grades are suitable for nutraceutical and premium skincare applications. Bulk quantities are available for industrial formulators, with smaller quantities offered for R&D and pilot-scale production needs.

name: Tetrabutyl orthosilicate
description:

It hydrolyzes under moisture to form silica networks, enabling durable bonding and surface consolidation in demanding industrial applications. In protective coatings and sealants, it functions as a crosslinking agent.

This material builds chemical resistance and improves adhesion to mineral and glass substrates. The construction industry uses it as a stone and concrete consolidant for various projects.

Controlled hydrolysis reinforces porous surfaces without altering appearance. In silicone elastomer formulations, it acts as a curing agent and chain extender, influencing network density and mechanical performance.

Adhesive formulators incorporate it to improve substrate wetting and promote chemical bonding at interfaces. This occurs between organic and inorganic materials to ensure long-term stability.

Tetrabutyl orthosilicate is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in technical grade, with purity levels typically at 97–99% for industrial use and large scale manufacturing.

Standard packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers, with bulk supply available for high-volume coating. It is ideal for construction chemical manufacturers requiring consistent quality.

name: Dimethylolpropionic acid
description:
Dimethylolpropionic acid ( CAS 4767-03-7 ), commonly known as DMPA, is a bifunctional monomer carrying both hydroxyl and carboxylic acid groups. It is used primarily to introduce ionic or hydrophilic character into polyurethane and polyester systems.

This unique chemical structure enables water dispersibility without the need for external emulsifiers. In waterborne polyurethane dispersions, DMPA acts as an internal emulsifier where its carboxylic acid group is neutralized.

This process creates stable, solvent-free coatings for wood, leather, and plastic substrates. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it into polyurethane prepolymers where controlled crosslink density and substrate adhesion are required.

In polyester and alkyd resin synthesis, it functions as a chain extender that improves water compatibility for industrial and architectural coating systems. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing.

Personal care formulators use DMPA-based polyurethane polymers as film-forming agents in hair fixatives and skin-feel modifiers. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling and processing.

Standard commercial grades are available at purities of 98% and above, with technical and high-purity variants offered depending on end-use requirements. It is commonly packaged in 25 kg bags for industrial use.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement to meet large-scale production needs. The product maintains high stability when stored under proper conditions, ensuring consistent performance in various chemical applications.

name: Rhein
description:
Rhein (CAS 478-43-3 ), also known as Cassic acid and Rhubarb Yellow, is an anthraquinone compound derived from rhubarb root and related botanical sources. It functions as a natural colorant, antioxidant, and UV-stabilizing agent across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial applications.

In personal care formulations, it is incorporated as a natural yellow pigment and antioxidant active, particularly in products targeting skin tone evenness and photoprotection. The textile and leather industries use it as a natural dye capable of imparting yellow to orange hues.

This compound is applied to protein-based and cellulosic fibers, often in combination with mordants to improve wash fastness. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a reference standard and active ingredient in preparations derived from traditional botanical extracts.

It contributes to the documented bioactivity of rhubarb-based formulations in various medicinal contexts. In paper processing, it is evaluated as a surface-modifying agent that influences substrate wettability and coating adhesion for specialized industrial uses.

The material is supplied as a yellow to orange crystalline powder for ease of handling. It is available in research-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 95% to 98%+ by HPLC analysis.

name: Fulvic acid
description:
Fulvic acid ( CAS 479-66-3 ), also marketed as Fulvic Minerals and abbreviated FA, is a low-molecular-weight humic fraction extracted from leonardite, shale, or composted organic matter.

It functions as a natural chelating agent and biostimulant, improving nutrient availability and uptake in both agricultural and industrial applications. In crop production, FA chelates micronutrients.

These include iron, zinc, and manganese, keeping them soluble and plant-available in soil and foliar spray formulations. Fertilizer manufacturers incorporate it into liquid NPK blends and micronutrient concentrates.

This helps to prevent nutrient lockout and improve field performance. In water treatment, FA is applied as a natural complexing agent to bind heavy metals and reduce their bioavailability in effluent streams.

Animal feed producers also use FA as a supplement additive, where its chelating capacity supports mineral absorption in livestock nutrition programs. Fulvic acid is supplied as a dry powder or water-soluble flakes.

It is also available as a concentrated liquid solution. Common commercial specifications include potassium fulvate powder, typically featuring 50 to 80 percent FA content, and liquid concentrates standardized by weight.

Technical and agricultural grades are the most prevalent, with product quality often verified against humic substance standards such as those defined by the International Humic Substances Society.

name: Pentaethylene glycol
description:
Pentaethylene glycol (CAS 4792-15-8 ), also abbreviated as PEG-5, is a mid-chain polyethylene glycol diol used as a humectant, plasticizer, and solvent across pharmaceutical, industrial, and polymer applications.

Its defined five-unit ethylene oxide chain makes it a well-characterized building block for formulators requiring a specific molecular weight fraction within the PEG family.

In pharmaceutical formulations, PEG-5 functions as a solvent and carrier for active ingredients in topical and semi-solid dosage forms. Polymer and plastics manufacturers incorporate it as a plasticizer.

This additive helps to improve flexibility and processability in films and coatings. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a softening agent and humectant to maintain substrate moisture balance.

Metalworking fluid formulators include it as a lubricant component and carrier in water-miscible cutting and grinding fluid systems. Pentaethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, viscous liquid.

It is available in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. It is available in technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for various buyers.

Buyers typically source against defined purity thresholds relevant to their regulatory requirements. Specification alignment with USP or Ph.Eur. PEG monographs should be confirmed.

name: Ethyl lauroyl arginate
description:
Ethyl lauroyl arginate ( CAS 48076-74-0 ), also known as lauric arginate ethyl ester, is a cationic surfactant derived from lauric acid and the amino acid arginine. It functions as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical preservation systems.

In food manufacturing, it is approved as a surface antimicrobial for processed meats, poultry, and ready-to-eat products. It controls Listeria, E. coli, and other spoilage organisms without affecting sensory attributes.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products such as shampoos, conditioners, and skin creams. Its cationic charge provides both preservation and surface-conditioning effects on hair and skin substrates.

In oral care, it is used in mouthwashes and toothpastes as an antimicrobial active targeting biofilm-forming bacteria. This makes it a versatile ingredient for maintaining hygiene in various consumer health applications.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers apply it as a preservative in topical formulations where conventional parabens or phenoxyethanol are restricted. This is often driven by regulatory requirements or specific consumer preference constraints.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as a liquid concentrate, depending on the grade and intended application. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent.

Purity levels are typically at or above 95% for standard industrial batches. Buyers should confirm grade suitability against regional regulatory approvals, as permitted use levels and applications vary between markets.

name: Stearyl acrylate
description:
Stearyl acrylate (CAS 4813-57-4 ), also known commercially as octadecyl acrylate, is a long-chain alkyl ester monomer used to introduce hydrophobic character and flexibility into polymer systems.

Its C18 fatty chain makes it a practical building block for tailoring surface properties, film formation, and lubricity in finished materials. In coatings and adhesives, it is copolymerized with acrylic monomers.

This process improves water resistance, substrate adhesion, and low-temperature flexibility in pressure-sensitive and structural formulations. Personal care formulators incorporate it into film-forming polymers for hair fixatives.

It is also utilized for skin-feel modifiers and water-repellent emulsion systems. In lubricant additive chemistry, polymerized stearyl acrylate contributes to viscosity modification and boundary lubrication performance.

These applications are vital in metalworking and industrial fluids. It also functions as a surface-modifying comonomer in specialty plastics and elastomers where controlled hydrophobicity is required.

The material is effective for applications needing reduced surface energy. Stearyl acrylate is supplied as a low-melting solid or liquid depending on temperature, typically available in technical and monomer grades.

Inhibited grades containing polymerization inhibitors such as MEHQ are standard for safe storage and transport. Bulk and drum packaging are the common supply formats for industrial buyers globally.

name: Phenoxyethyl acrylate
description:
Phenoxyethyl acrylate ( CAS 48145-04-6 ), also known commercially as 2-phenoxyethyl acrylate, is a reactive monomer used in UV-curable and radiation-curable systems.

It functions as both a reactive diluent and a plasticizing co-monomer, reducing viscosity in formulations while contributing to the final polymer network during the curing process.

In UV-curable inks and coatings for printing and packaging, it lowers formulation viscosity without sacrificing cure speed or film hardness. This makes it ideal for high-speed production lines.

Radiation-curable adhesives and pressure-sensitive adhesive formulations incorporate it to improve flexibility and substrate adhesion in the cured matrix, ensuring long-lasting performance.

Coatings manufacturers use it in wood, plastic, and metal finishing systems where a balance of hardness and elongation is required for durable and aesthetic surface protection.

In polymer synthesis, it serves as a building block for specialty acrylate resins where aromatic character and controlled glass transition properties are specifically targeted by chemists.

Phenoxyethyl acrylate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. It is available in technical grade.

name: Indigo
description:
Indigo (CAS 482-89-3 ), also recognized commercially as FD&C Blue No. 2 and sold under the E132 designation as Indigo Carmine, is one of the oldest and most established blue colorants in industrial use.

It delivers a deep, characteristic blue hue across textile, food-contact, and printing applications where consistent color performance and regulatory acceptance are required for global distribution and manufacturing.

In textile manufacturing, indigo is the defining colorant for denim production, applied through vat dyeing processes to achieve the characteristic fading profile demanded by apparel brands and high-end fashion retailers.

Leather and paper producers use it to achieve uniform blue tones in both decorative and functional grades of finished material. In printing and packaging, it functions as a base pigment in ink formulations.

Deep blue shades and batch-to-batch consistency are critical to brand color standards. The water-soluble sulfonated form, Indigo Carmine, is used as a food and pharmaceutical colorant in tablets and capsules.

These ingestible products are manufactured under FD&C and E132 approvals to ensure safety. Indigo is available as a powder and in pre-reduced liquid vat form for direct textile processing and industrial dyeing.

Food and pharmaceutical grades conforming to FD&C, E132, and USP specifications are supplied as fine powder. Technical-grade material is offered for industrial ink and pigment applications across various sectors.

Its combination of hydroxyl and carboxyl groups makes it a practical monomer for producing specialty polyesters and alkyd resins. Oxypivalic acid is an alternative name occasionally encountered in trade.

In coatings, HPA is used to synthesize hydroxyl-functional polyester resins that crosslink with isocyanates or melamines, delivering improved hardness and weatherability in automotive and industrial finishes.

Alkyd resin producers incorporate it to control molecular weight and introduce branching, directly influencing viscosity and drying performance in the final coating applications.

In adhesives and sealants, HPA-derived polyesters contribute flexibility and adhesion to demanding bonding applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a chiral intermediate for synthesis.

description:

This potent ingredient allows manufacturers to reduce sugar or other flavouring inputs without sacrificing the overall taste profile. In confectionery, bakery, and soft drink production, it boosts perceived sweetness and extends flavour longevity at use levels typically below 50 ppm.

Tobacco manufacturers incorporate it to smooth harshness and add a sweet, creamy character to blended products. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a fragrance modifier that enhances vanilla, fruity, and gourmand scent profiles in perfumes and lotions.

The compound is also utilized in lip products to improve the sensory experience. Its chelating behaviour supports oxidative stability in fat-containing formulations, effectively reducing the development of rancidity during the product shelf life.

This chemical is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy integration into various production processes. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and purity specifications is the standard commercial form for flavour and food applications.

Technical-grade material is available for non-food industrial use where high purity is not the primary requirement. Bulk supply is typically offered in fibre drums or multi-layer bags to ensure product integrity during transport and storage.

name: Pigment red 149
description:
Pigment Red 149 (CAS 4948-15-6 ) is a high-performance perylene pigment delivering deep, bluish-red shades with outstanding heat stability and lightfastness. It belongs to the perylene diimide class, a group recognized by formulators for durability in demanding colorant applications.

In plastics, it withstands processing temperatures required for engineering polymers, making it a reliable choice for coloring polyolefins, PVC, and high-temperature thermoplastics without shade shift. This stability ensures consistent color quality during manufacturing.

Coatings formulators select it for automotive and industrial finishes where long-term exterior durability and resistance to weathering are critical performance requirements. It maintains its integrity even when exposed to harsh environmental conditions over time.

Printing ink manufacturers use it in high-quality packaging inks where color strength and resistance to migration into adjacent substrates must meet strict compliance standards. This makes it ideal for premium branding and packaging solutions.

It also performs in rubber compounding and elastomer applications where pigment stability under mechanical stress and heat exposure is a procurement priority. The pigment ensures that the final rubber products retain their aesthetic appeal and structural properties.

The product is supplied as a dry powder, typically in press cake or finished pigment form depending on the downstream application. Standard commercial grades are available as crude pigment or surface-treated variants optimized for specific dispersion systems.

These variants are suitable for solventborne, waterborne, or plastics applications. Technical-grade specifications are the norm, with particle size distribution and tinting strength documented per batch for quality assurance purposes.

name: Fenofibrate
description:
Fenofibrate (CAS 49562-28-9 ) is a fibric acid derivative active pharmaceutical ingredient used primarily in lipid-regulating drug formulations. As a pharmaceutical intermediate and finished API, it enables the production of oral dosage forms.

These forms target dyslipidemia management across global generic and branded drug markets. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is processed into tablets, capsules, and nanoparticle formulations where particle size engineering affects bioavailability.

Generic drug manufacturers source it as a key API for cholesterol and triglyceride-lowering products sold across regulated markets including the US, EU, and Asia-Pacific. This ensures high-quality therapeutic options for patients worldwide.

Formulators working on lipid-modifying combination therapies incorporate it alongside statins, requiring consistent purity and polymorphic form control. Contract development organizations also use it as a reference compound in dissolution testing.

This material is essential for formulation development benchmarking and comparative studies. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in quantities ranging from research-scale to multi-tonne commercial volumes.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications, with purity typically at 99% or above to meet pharmacopoeial requirements. This ensures the highest level of safety and efficacy for pharmaceutical use.

Certificate of Analysis documentation, ICH-compliant impurity profiling, and DMF support are standard expectations when sourcing from established API suppliers. These documents provide the necessary transparency for regulatory submissions.

name: Carbohydrazide
description:
Carbohydrazide (CAS 497-18-7 ), also known as N,N'-diaminourea, is an oxygen scavenger and corrosion inhibitor used across industrial water treatment and energy systems. It removes dissolved oxygen from process water and boiler systems, protecting metal surfaces from oxidative corrosion.

In boiler feedwater treatment, this compound replaces hydrazine as a safer oxygen scavenger, reacting with dissolved oxygen to prevent pitting and corrosion in steam generation systems. This application is critical for maintaining the integrity of high-pressure equipment.

Refineries and oil and gas facilities use it to protect pipelines and heat exchangers operating under high-temperature conditions. Its ability to passivate metal surfaces makes it an essential component in heavy industrial maintenance and protection protocols.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a cross-linking and curing agent for polyurethane and epoxy systems. This application improves the mechanical performance and chemical resistance of the final material, ensuring durability in demanding environments.

It also serves as a catalyst precursor in the synthesis of specialty chemicals and pharmaceutical intermediates. Its versatile chemical structure allows for precise reactions in complex organic synthesis and specialized manufacturing processes.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder to meet various industrial requirements. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

Quality control ensures the material meets rigorous industrial benchmarks for consistency and performance. Packaging is available in bags and drums suited to industrial procurement volumes, ensuring safe transport and storage for large-scale operations.

name: Sodium carbonate
description:
Sodium carbonate (CAS 497-19-8 ), commonly known as soda ash or washing soda, is an inorganic alkali supplied across industrial, food, and pharmaceutical markets. As E500 , it functions as an acidity regulator and raising agent in food manufacturing.

Across broader industry, it serves as a pH control agent, flux, and processing alkali in applications ranging from glass production to water treatment. In glass manufacturing, it lowers the melting point of silica, reducing energy costs in furnace operations.

This makes it one of the highest-volume industrial uses globally. Pulp and paper producers use it to regulate pH during chemical pulping and bleaching stages. In water treatment, it adjusts alkalinity to prevent pipe corrosion and support downstream coagulation processes.

Food and pharmaceutical formulators use it as a leavening component, buffering agent, and pH modifier in both solid and liquid systems. Sodium carbonate is available as a dense or light powder, granules, and anhydrous flakes, with particle size and bulk density varying by grade.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / Ph. Eur. ), and technical-grade for industrial use. Soda ash dense and soda ash light are the two primary industrial forms, differing in bulk density and handling characteristics.

The material is also available in compliance with BP , EP , and ACS standards for laboratory and specialized manufacturing. These high-purity grades ensure consistent performance in sensitive chemical reactions and pharmaceutical formulations.

name: Arbutin
description:
Arbutin (CAS 497-76-7 ), also known as alpha-arbutin in its synthetic isomeric form, is a naturally derived glycoside used primarily as a skin-brightening and hyperpigmentation-correcting active in cosmetic formulations.

It functions by inhibiting melanin synthesis, making it a sought-after alternative to hydroquinone in regulated markets. In skincare, it is formulated into serums, creams, and spot treatments targeting uneven skin tone and age spots.

Toners and essence products across the Asian personal care market rely on this ingredient as a primary brightening active, often at concentrations between 1–5%. Pharmaceutical-grade material is used in topical dermatological preparations.

These preparations require documented efficacy and purity documentation for regulatory submission. It also appears in color cosmetics and UV-care products where a secondary brightening benefit is commercially positioned alongside sun protection.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both natural (beta) and synthetic (alpha) forms. Alpha-arbutin commands a premium due to greater stability and potency at lower concentrations compared to the beta form.

Standard grades include cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with the latter requiring tighter purity specifications. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and multi-kilogram quantities for industrial manufacturing needs.

High-purity grades are typically specified at ≥98% by HPLC to ensure maximum efficacy. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for manufacturers requiring reliable active ingredients for high-end personal care and dermatological lines.

name: Triethanolamine palmitate
description:
Triethanolamine palmitate (CAS 49719-60-0 ), also known as TEA-Palmitate, is an amine salt of palmitic acid used as an emulsifier and surfactant across personal care and industrial formulations.

It enables stable oil-in-water emulsions and improves wetting and dispersion in complex systems. In personal care, it functions as an emulsifying agent in creams, lotions, and cleansing formulations.

The fatty acid-amine salt chemistry delivers smooth, stable textures. Coatings and adhesive manufacturers use it to improve pigment dispersion and substrate wetting, supporting uniform film formation.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a softening and wetting aid, helping active ingredients penetrate fiber and hide surfaces more effectively for better processing results.

Corrosion inhibitor formulations in industrial fluids also incorporate it to protect metal surfaces through surface-active adsorption. This provides a protective layer against environmental degradation.

Triethanolamine palmitate is typically supplied as a paste or waxy solid, depending on grade and processing. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available to serve buyers.

Specifications are generally aligned to application requirements rather than pharmacopeial standards like USP , FCC , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , or ACS .

Buyers should confirm purity and acid value with suppliers when qualifying for formulation use. This ensures the material meets the specific performance criteria for the intended industrial application.

name: N,N-dicyclohexyl-2-benzothiazolesulfenamide
description:
N,N-Dicyclohexyl-2-benzothiazolesulfenamide (CAS 4979-32-2 ), commonly known as DCBS, is a delayed-action sulfenamide accelerator used in rubber vulcanization. It controls the onset and rate of cure, giving processors a longer scorch safety window before crosslinking begins.

DCBS is the preferred accelerator in tire manufacturing, where it enables safe processing of thick-section components such as sidewalls, treads, and bead fillers without premature cure.

In industrial rubber goods, such as conveyor belts, hoses, and seals, it supports consistent crosslink density across heavy-gauge profiles. Formulators combine it with secondary accelerators to fine-tune cure speed.

Commonly paired with DPG or TBBS, it helps achieve specific modulus development in demanding compound specifications. Its delayed onset also makes it suitable for injection-molded and transfer-molded rubber parts.

This is particularly critical where extended flow time is required before cure initiates. DCBS is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or granules, with granular form preferred for dust-controlled handling.

The material is available in technical rubber grade, the standard specification for this accelerator class. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities for industrial use.

Active content specifications are confirmed by melting point and assay testing per supplier certificates of analysis. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing batches and applications.
