name: L-cysteic acid
description:
L-Cysteic acid (CAS 498-40-8 ), also known as Cysteinesulfonic Acid, is a naturally occurring sulfonic amino acid derivative found in oxidized cysteine pathways. In industry, it functions as a flavoring agent and acidulant.

It serves as a biochemical building block across food, pharmaceutical, and life science applications. In food and flavor systems, it contributes acidic and savory taste profiles, particularly in processed foods.

Flavor enhancer formulations targeting umami-adjacent sensory characteristics often utilize this compound. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of taurine and other sulfur-containing amino acid derivatives.

In peptide chemistry and biochemical research, it serves as a reference standard and building block for synthesizing sulfonic acid-bearing peptides. These are used extensively in proteomics and enzyme studies.

Life science suppliers also source it for use in cell culture media development and metabolic pathway research. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is produced to meet purity thresholds suitable for API intermediate use. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory procurement to bulk quantities for industrial synthesis applications.

name: Dipicolinic acid
description:
Dipicolinic acid (CAS 499-83-2 ), commonly abbreviated as DPA, is a pyridine-based dicarboxylic acid used across food, cosmetic, and industrial chemistry applications. It functions primarily as a chelating agent, catalyst precursor, and preservation-active compound in formulated systems.

In food and flavoring applications, DPA acts as an acidulant and flavor modifier in processed formulations where precise pH control and taste profile adjustment are required. Its strong metal-chelating capacity makes it a valued precursor in catalyst preparation.

This material is particularly useful for coordination complexes used in organic synthesis and polymerization processes. In personal care and cosmetic formulations, DPA contributes to preservation systems by disrupting microbial activity.

By reducing reliance on conventional biocides, it offers a versatile solution for modern formulators. Industrial buyers also source it for use in analytical chemistry and as a reference standard for spore detection assays.

DPA is a recognized biomarker for bacterial endospores, making it essential for specialized laboratory testing. Dipicolinic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial needs.

It is available in technical grade for industrial and catalytic applications, as well as high-purity grades suited to analytical, food, and cosmetic end uses. Standard packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to bulk orders.

name: 4-Phenylcyclohexene
description:
4-Phenylcyclohexene (CAS 4994-16-5 ) is a cyclic olefin compound used as a chemical building block and specialty solvent in pharmaceutical synthesis and polymer chemistry. Its reactive double bond makes it a functional intermediate for constructing complex ring-containing molecular frameworks.

In pharmaceutical and biotech research, it serves as a synthetic intermediate for producing cyclohexane-based active pharmaceutical ingredients and chiral building blocks requiring defined ring geometry.

Polymer chemists use it as a monomer in specialty polymerization processes, where the pendant phenyl group and olefinic functionality allow incorporation into structured polymer backbones.

It also functions as a carrier solvent in formulation development where aromatic-aliphatic character improves compatibility with specific resin or polymer matrices in various industrial applications.

In life sciences research settings, it supports the preparation of reference standards and structurally defined intermediates for screening libraries and other analytical testing procedures.

4-Phenylcyclohexene is supplied as a clear liquid in research and commercial quantities. It is available primarily at technical and high-purity grades for diverse laboratory requirements.

Purity specifications typically range from 97% to 99%+ for synthesis and reference applications. Packaging options generally scale from small laboratory quantities to bulk volumes depending on supplier capability.

name: Nickel octanoate
description:
Nickel octanoate (CAS 4995-91-9 ), also known as nickel dioctanoate, is an organometallic nickel salt used as a catalyst and catalyst precursor across polymer, rubber, and coatings industries.

Its oil-soluble character makes it compatible with organic processing systems where inorganic nickel salts cannot be readily dispersed. In polymer and rubber processing, it functions as a catalyst precursor.

It is utilized for Ziegler-Natta and related polymerization systems, influencing chain growth and molecular weight distribution in polyolefin and synthetic rubber production for industrial applications.

Coatings and resin formulators use it as a curing and cross-linking agent, particularly in systems requiring controlled metal-catalyzed oxidative cure to ensure proper material performance.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it serves as an additive precursor where nickel-based organometallics contribute to extreme-pressure and anti-wear performance in heavy machinery.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it into elastomeric systems to promote cross-link density and improve long-term cohesive strength for various construction and automotive uses.

Nickel octanoate is supplied as a liquid or viscous solution, typically in hydrocarbon or mineral oil carriers at defined nickel metal content to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with concentration specified by percentage nickel content. Bulk and drum quantities are the typical supply formats for industrial buyers.

name: Formaldehyde
description:
Formaldehyde (CAS 50-00-0 ), also known commercially as Paraform in its solid polymerized form and listed as E240 in food-related contexts, is a high-demand chemical intermediate.

It is a biocidal agent used across industrial manufacturing and preservation applications. It functions primarily as a crosslinking agent, disinfectant, and reactive monomer in the production of resins and polymers.

In chemical manufacturing, it is the foundational building block for urea-formaldehyde and phenol-formaldehyde resins used in adhesives, laminates, and molded components for various industrial sectors.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a crosslinking agent to impart wrinkle resistance, dimensional stability, and wet strength to finished goods during the manufacturing process.

Water treatment operations use it as a biocide to control microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water. In personal care, it functions as a preservative in low-concentration formulations.

Pharmaceutical producers rely on it for equipment sterilization and vaccine inactivation processes. Formaldehyde is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 37% concentration known as formalin.

It is also available in solid polymerized form as paraformaldehyde powder or prills. Technical and industrial grades are standard for resin and chemical synthesis applications across the global market.

Pharmaceutical and reagent grades are available for controlled manufacturing environments requiring tighter purity specifications. These grades ensure compliance with rigorous safety and quality protocols.

name: Guanidine hydrochloride
description:
Guanidine hydrochloride (CAS 50-01-1 ), also known as guanidinium chloride or GuHCl, is a strong protein denaturant and chaotropic salt used across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and life science manufacturing.

It disrupts hydrogen bonding and hydrophobic interactions in proteins, making it a critical reagent wherever controlled protein unfolding or solubilization is required for industrial processes.

In biopharmaceutical manufacturing, GuHCl is used to solubilize inclusion bodies during recombinant protein production, enabling downstream refolding into active drug substances for therapeutic use.

Protein denaturation studies and urea-alternative unfolding assays rely on concentrated GuHCl solutions as the standard chaotropic agent. In nucleic acid extraction workflows, it lyses cells and inactivates RNases.

This protects RNA and DNA integrity during isolation procedures. Cosmetic formulators use it at low concentrations as a conditioning and preservation-supporting agent in hair and scalp treatments.

Guanidine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include high-purity reagent-grade and molecular biology-grade specifications suited to sensitive bioprocessing.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. standards is available for GMP-regulated manufacturing environments. These high-quality standards ensure consistency and safety in production.

name: Lactic acid
description:
Lactic acid ( CAS 50-21-5 ), also known as milk acid and listed as E270 in food additive regulations, is an organic acid produced through fermentation or chemical synthesis. It functions as an acidulant, preservative, and pH regulator across food, pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial manufacturing.

In food and beverage production, E270 acidifies and preserves products including dairy, pickled vegetables, meat preparations, and ready-to-eat meals. This process extends shelf life while contributing a mild, clean sour note to the final product.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a pH-adjusting agent in topical formulations, oral solutions, and vaginal preparations. Precise buffering is critical to product stability and efficacy in these specialized medical applications.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into exfoliating creams, toners, and moisturizers. Its humectant action supports skin hydration and its acidifying effect helps maintain scalp and skin pH levels effectively.

In leather tanning and textile processing, lactic acid controls bath acidity and aids in deliming hides. It often replaces stronger mineral acids where a milder, more controllable chemical process is required for quality results.

Lactic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 80% and 88% concentrations being the most commercially standard. Food-grade, USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades are available to meet regulatory requirements across different end markets.

Technical grade is also offered for industrial applications such as water treatment and textile processing. These various grades ensure that the specific purity needs of each unique industrial or commercial sector are met.

name: D-ribose
description:
D-Ribose (CAS 50-69-1 ) is a naturally occurring pentose sugar used across food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology sectors. As a FEMA 3793 -listed ingredient, it is recognized as a flavoring substance and functional nutrient.

In formulation and manufacturing, it acts primarily as a biochemical substrate, humectant, and energy-support ingredient. In food and nutraceutical products, it is incorporated into sports nutrition supplements and energy drinks.

Functional foods targeting cellular energy replenishment frequently utilize this sugar. Pharmaceutical and healthcare formulators use it as a precursor in the biosynthesis of nucleotides, coenzymes, and active pharmaceutical ingredients.

This includes the production of various antiviral compounds. Biotechnology and life sciences manufacturers rely on it as a carbon source and substrate in fermentation media, cell culture systems, and enzymatic assay reagents.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a humectant and Maillard reaction participant. This contributes to skin-conditioning effects in select cosmetic applications where cellular energy support is a primary goal.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade and USP -grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms, with food-grade material frequently meeting FCC standards for use in dietary supplements.

name: Sorbitol
description:
Sorbitol (CAS 50-70-4 ), also known by the E-number E420 , is a polyol humectant and sweetener used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It retains moisture in finished products and acts as a chelating agent to stabilize formulations against metal-ion degradation. In food production, it functions as a bulk sweetener and humectant.

It is used in sugar-free confectionery, baked goods, and chewing gum, where it controls water activity and extends shelf life. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in tablet coatings.

It is also found in liquid oral preparations and sugar-free syrups, where its moisture-retention properties support product stability. Personal care formulators incorporate it into toothpastes.

It is used in skin creams and hair care products to prevent drying and maintain texture over the product's shelf life. Its chelating capacity makes it useful in formulations where trace metal ions must be sequestered.

This prevents oxidative degradation in sensitive chemical mixtures. Sorbitol is supplied as a 70% aqueous solution or as a crystalline powder, with the liquid form being the most common in industrial supply chains.

Recognized grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , supporting use across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic applications. Specialty grades are available for specific processing requirements.

name: Acetylsalicylic acid
description:
Acetylsalicylic acid (CAS 50-78-2 ) is a synthetic salicylate derivative used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, personal care formulation, and specialty chemical applications. It functions primarily as an active pharmaceutical ingredient and chemical intermediate.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, ASA is the active ingredient in analgesic, antipyretic, and antiplatelet solid dosage forms. These include tablets, effervescent formulations, and coated pellets for various medical applications.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a keratolytic and preservation-supporting agent in exfoliating creams and scalp treatments. It is also frequently utilized in the production of anti-dandruff products and skin care solutions.

As a chemical intermediate, it serves in the synthesis of salicylate-based compounds where controlled acetylation is required. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial chemical synthesis and laboratory research.

In food-contact and specialty applications, its antioxidant and mild acidulant properties support stabilization in defined regulatory frameworks. It plays secondary roles in preservation and pH-related formulation work across industries.

Acetylsalicylic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder in pharmaceutical and technical grades. USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. specifications are standard for pharmaceutical procurement and quality assurance.

name: Glucose
description:
Glucose (CAS 50-99-7 ), commercially known as dextrose, is a simple monosaccharide sugar sourced primarily from corn or wheat starch hydrolysis. It functions as a fermentable sugar, sweetener, and humectant.

This versatile ingredient serves as an energy substrate across food manufacturing, pharmaceutical production, and personal care formulation. In food and beverage manufacturing, it provides fermentable sugar for baked goods and brewing.

The product contributes significantly to browning, texture, and shelf life in confectionery. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use dextrose as an IV infusion base, tablet excipient, and diluent in oral solid dosage forms.

Grade compliance and endotoxin control are critical procurement considerations for medical applications. In personal care formulations, it acts as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in moisturizers and cleansers.

Fermentation industries rely on it as a primary carbon source for producing amino acids and organic acids. It is also used for bioethanol production at an industrial scale to ensure high yields.

The material is supplied as anhydrous powder, monohydrate powder, and liquid syrup. Monohydrate is the most common solid form in commercial trade for various industrial and laboratory applications.

Recognized grades include USP , BP , Ph.Eur. , and FCC for pharmaceutical and food applications. Technical grade is also available for industrial fermentation use where high purity is less critical.

Bulk quantities are typically available in 25 kg bags or bulk tanker shipments for liquid grades. These logistics options ensure efficient supply chain management for large-scale manufacturing facilities.

name: Cyclopentadecanone
description:
Cyclopentadecanone (CAS 502-72-7 ), commercially known as Exaltone, is a macrocyclic musk ketone used as a fragrance raw material in perfumery and flavor applications. Normuscon is another recognized trade name encountered in supplier and formulation contexts.

It delivers a clean, animalic musk character that anchors and extends fragrance compositions across a range of finished products. In fine fragrance and prestige perfumery, Exaltone functions as a base note fixative.

This material improves longevity and blending cohesion in eau de parfum and eau de toilette formulations. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skin creams, body lotions, and hair care products where sustained musk diffusion is a target.

Adhesive and sealant producers use macrocyclic musks to mask processing odors and impart a neutral-to-pleasant residual scent in consumer-facing products. This ensures a better experience for the end user during application.

Coatings and printing ink formulators apply it at low concentrations to manage solvent-associated off-notes in the finished film. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial chemical inventories for odor management.

Cyclopentadecanone is supplied as a solid, typically in flake or crystalline form, reflecting its waxy character at ambient temperature. It is available in fragrance-grade and flavor-grade specifications for global trade.

Documentation is aligned to industry standards expected by cosmetic and flavor buyers. Minimum order quantities and pack sizes vary by supplier, with bulk quantities available for industrial fragrance blending operations.

name: Sodium methylparaben
description:
Sodium methylparaben (CAS 5026-62-0 ), also known by its EU food additive designation E219 , is the sodium salt form of methylparaben used as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial preservative.

Its water-soluble nature makes it the preferred paraben variant for aqueous-based formulations across pharmaceuticals, personal care, and food applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it protects liquid oral preparations.

It is also utilized in topical creams and injectable formulations against microbial contamination throughout shelf life. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, lotions, and wet wipes where water activity creates spoilage risk.

As E219, it is permitted in select food categories to extend product stability, particularly in processed foods and beverages where alternative preservatives may affect taste or regulatory standing.

Coating and adhesive systems with aqueous carrier phases also use it to prevent in-can microbial growth during storage and distribution. Sodium methylparaben is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for pharmaceutical and personal care applications. Food-grade material meeting E219 specifications is also available for regulated food use.

Technical grade is also available for industrial coating and adhesive applications. This ensures compatibility across a wide range of manufacturing requirements and global regulatory standards for chemical safety.

name: Methacrylatoethyl trimethyl ammonium chloride
description:
Methacrylatoethyl trimethyl ammonium chloride (CAS 5039-78-1 ), commercially known as METAC, is a cationic quaternary ammonium monomer used as a reactive building block in polymer synthesis.

It introduces permanent positive charge into polymer chains, enabling the production of cationic polyelectrolytes and functional coatings across multiple industrial sectors.

In paper manufacturing, METAC-based polymers function as retention aids and wet-strength additives, improving fiber bonding and filler retention during sheet formation.

Textile processors use cationic polymers derived from METAC to improve dye uptake and substrate adhesion on negatively charged fibers during the manufacturing process.

In leather processing, it contributes to the formulation of cationic fixatives and surface treatment agents that enhance finish durability and overall product quality.

The plastics and polymers sector uses METAC as a comonomer in superabsorbent polymer networks and antistatic coatings where its quaternary nitrogen group provides permanent charge.

METAC is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 75–80% active content. It is available in technical grade for industrial polymerization applications.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes, suited to bulk procurement requirements in polymer manufacturing operations and large scale chemical distribution networks.

name: Glyceryl distearate
description:
Glyceryl distearate (CAS 504-40-5 ), also known as Glyceryl 1,3-distearate, is a diester of glycerol and stearic acid used across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions as an emulsifier, rheology modifier, and softening agent in solid and semi-solid formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a lipid-based excipient for controlled-release solid dosage forms.

It is frequently utilized in matrix tablets, where it regulates drug release profiles. Personal care formulators use it to build viscosity and improve texture in creams, lotions, and stick formulations.

In food applications, it functions as an emulsifier to stabilize fat-based systems such as margarines, shortenings, and confectionery coatings. It provides excellent stability and texture to these products.

As a plasticizer in film coatings and waxy matrices, it improves flexibility and processability during manufacturing. This makes it a versatile component for various industrial coating processes.

Glyceryl distearate is supplied as a white to off-white powder, flakes, or waxy solid. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications, supporting use in regulated drug products.

Food-grade supply is also available for applications requiring compliance with food additive standards. This ensures the material meets the necessary safety and purity requirements for global distribution.

name: 1,3-propanediol
description:
1,3-Propanediol (CAS 504-63-2 ), also known as trimethylene glycol or PDO, is a bifunctional diol used as a monomer, solvent, and humectant across polymer, personal care, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Its two terminal hydroxyl groups make it a reactive building block for polyesters and polyurethanes, while its solvent and moisture-retention properties support formulation work across multiple sectors.

In polymer production, PDO is the key monomer for polytrimethylene terephthalate (PTT), a polyester used in carpet fiber, apparel, and engineering plastics. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a humectant.

It is used in skin creams, serums, and hair conditioners, where it supports moisture retention and helps dissolve active ingredients. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use PDO as a carrier solvent in topical and oral formulations.

It is valued for its compatibility with a broad range of actives. In industrial coatings and adhesives, it functions as a cross-linking agent and reactive intermediate in polyurethane and UV-curable resin systems.

1,3-Propanediol is supplied as a clear, colorless liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options for large-volume buyers. It is available in technical grade for polymer and industrial applications.

High-purity grades meeting USP and pharmaceutical specifications are also available. Bio-based PDO, produced via fermentation, is commercially available and increasingly specified in sustainable formulation programs.

name: Imidazolidine
description:
Imidazolidine (CAS 504-74-5 ) is a saturated five-membered heterocyclic amine used as a building block and functional intermediate across chemical synthesis and formulation.

Its buffering capacity and solvent behavior make it relevant to manufacturing processes where pH control and carrier performance are required for industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a synthetic intermediate in the preparation of active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty heterocyclic compounds for various uses.

Agrochemical producers use it in the synthesis of crop protection agents, where its cyclic amine structure contributes to the construction of biologically active molecules.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a pH-regulating agent within treatment baths and finishing formulations to ensure consistent quality and performance.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into product systems where buffering and carrier properties are needed to stabilize active ingredients during the manufacturing process.

The material is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, available in technical and research grades depending on specific application requirements and standards.

Pharmaceutical-intermediate applications generally require higher purity specifications, and material is available to support API synthesis workflows and bulk industrial supply.

name: Isorhamnetin 3-O-glucoside
description:
Isorhamnetin 3-O-glucoside (CAS 5041-82-7 ), also referred to commercially as isorhamnetin-3-Glu, is a naturally occurring flavonoid glycoside isolated primarily from plant sources such as sea buckthorn and onion.

It functions as a bioactive antioxidant ingredient in nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and research-grade formulations. In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is incorporated into capsule and tablet formulations.

These applications target antioxidant and cardiovascular health positioning. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical developers use it as a reference standard or active botanical ingredient in standardized plant extracts.

Biotechnology and life sciences laboratories source it as an analytical reference compound for HPLC method development, metabolite profiling, and in vitro bioactivity screening for various research projects.

Food and functional beverage formulators apply it in products where polyphenol content is a measurable quality or marketing parameter. It is supplied as a fine powder, typically at purity levels of 95% or 98%.

Purity is confirmed by HPLC, and it is available in research quantities for laboratory use and in larger batch sizes for industrial or clinical supply. Both standard-grade and high-purity reference-grade material are offered.

name: trans-5-hydroxy-L-pipecolic acid
description:
Trans-5-hydroxy-L-pipecolic acid (CAS 50439-45-7 ) is a hydroxylated cyclic amino acid used as a reference standard and building block in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research. It supports pH regulation and buffering in specialized formulations where precise chemical characterization is required.

In pharmaceutical development, it serves as an analytical reference standard for method validation, impurity profiling, and quality control of amino acid-related drug substances. Peptide chemists use it as a chiral building block in the synthesis of constrained peptidomimetics.

The compound is essential for the development of bioactive cyclic peptide scaffolds. Biotechnology researchers employ it in metabolic studies and biosynthetic pathway investigations, particularly in work related to natural product biosynthesis.

Its defined stereochemistry makes it a preferred reagent for asymmetric synthesis programs requiring enantiomerically pure cyclic amino acid inputs. This ensures high precision in complex chemical reactions and research applications.

Trans-5-hydroxy-L-pipecolic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available primarily in research and catalog quantities, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher by HPLC analysis.

Supply is sourced through fine chemical and specialty amino acid suppliers catering to pharmaceutical and life sciences procurement. The material meets rigorous internal quality benchmarks to ensure consistency across various laboratory and industrial batches.

name: Tridecanedioic acid
description:
Tridecanedioic acid (CAS 505-52-2 ), also known commercially as brassylic acid, is a long-chain aliphatic dicarboxylic acid used as a monomer and functional ingredient across polymer, lubricant, and personal care manufacturing.

Its 13-carbon diacid structure makes it a sought-after building block where chain length directly influences end-product flexibility and performance. In polymer synthesis, it serves as a monomer for producing polyamides.

These polyesters offer enhanced flexibility and low-temperature performance, which is particularly relevant for specialty nylon grades and hot-melt adhesives. Lubricant formulators use it to produce diester base fluids.

These additive components are essential where thermal stability and film strength are required. In personal care, brassylic acid derivatives appear in emollient esters and conditioning agents targeted at skin and hair formulations.

Printing and packaging applications include its use in alkyd resin modification and ink binder systems requiring improved adhesion and substrate compatibility. This chemical is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity variants, with some suppliers offering material meeting polymer-grade specifications for monomer applications. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale bags to bulk quantities.

name: Hexadecanedioic acid
description:
Hexadecanedioic acid (CAS 505-54-4 ), also known as thapsic acid, is a long-chain dicarboxylic acid used as a functional building block across specialty chemical formulations. Its bifunctional acid structure makes it a reactive intermediate for polymer synthesis.

This versatile chemical is essential for creating ester-based lubricants and advanced emulsifier systems. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it serves as a precursor to complex ester base fluids that deliver high-temperature stability.

These fluids are valued for providing low-friction performance in demanding industrial environments. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into wax esters and emollient systems where controlled spreading and surface modification are required.

Food-grade ester derivatives produced from this acid are used as emulsifiers and release agents in processed food applications. In polymer chemistry, it functions as a diacid monomer for nylon and polyester synthesis.

The material contributes to the development of high-performance materials with defined chain length and thermal properties. Hexadecanedioic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or flake for easy handling.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Food-grade and high-purity grades are available for applications requiring tighter specification compliance for global markets.

name: Muconic acid
description:
Muconic acid (CAS 505-70-4 ) is a dicarboxylic acid produced through both synthetic and bio-based fermentation routes, positioning it as a platform chemical at the intersection of green chemistry and industrial manufacturing.

It functions as a precursor in the synthesis of high-value polymers, pharmaceuticals, and specialty chemicals, with growing commercial interest driven by its bio-renewable production pathways.

Its primary industrial role is as a chemical intermediate for producing adipic acid and terephthalic acid, which are key monomers in nylon and PET production, making it a target material for bio-based polymer supply chains.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, this compound serves as a building block for active ingredient intermediates requiring controlled dicarboxylic acid functionality and high chemical stability during the reaction process.

Agricultural formulation developers evaluate it for pH buffering in liquid crop protection products where acid stability across dilution is a critical formulation requirement for effective field application.

Biotechnology researchers also source it as a reference standard or fermentation process benchmark when developing microbial production platforms for sustainable chemical manufacturing and green engineering.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in research-grade and technical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+ depending on intended use.

Packaging options range from small laboratory quantities to bulk orders supporting pilot-scale and commercial production. All batches are tested to ensure they meet rigorous industrial and laboratory requirements.

name: Heptadecanoic acid
description:
Heptadecanoic acid (CAS 506-12-7 ), also known as margaric acid, is a saturated odd-chain fatty acid used as a reference standard, emulsifier, and surface-active agent across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

Its odd-carbon structure makes it a reliable analytical marker and functional ingredient where even-chain fatty acids are unsuitable. In food and nutrition, it serves primarily as a certified reference standard for fatty acid profiling.

This material is essential for lipid analysis in quality control laboratories. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, balms, and waxy emulsions where it contributes to texture, emulsion stability, and skin-feel.

It provides these benefits without the melting-point limitations of shorter-chain acids. In lubricant and metalworking applications, it functions as a boundary lubricant and surface modifier, reducing friction on metal substrates.

It is frequently utilized in cutting fluids and specialty grease formulations. Its surface-active character also supports emulsification and dispersion tasks in industrial processing where precise fatty acid chain length is required.

Heptadecanoic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or flake. It is available in high-purity analytical grades suited for reference standard and laboratory use, as well as technical grades for industrial applications.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory procurement to bulk quantities for manufacturing-scale sourcing. The product meets rigorous internal specifications to ensure consistency across various batch sizes and applications.

name: Arachidic acid
description:
Arachidic acid (CAS 506-30-9 ), also known as eicosanoic acid, is a saturated C20 fatty acid derived primarily from peanut oil, fish oil, and other natural fats. It functions as a stabilizer, emulsifier, and surface-active agent across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

In personal care, this fatty acid is used to adjust the texture and consistency of creams, lotions, and lip products, contributing to a smooth, stable emulsion structure. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a stabilizer and antioxidant component in fat-based systems.

In these systems, oxidative stability and shelf life are procurement priorities. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as a boundary lubricant and surface modifier, improving film adhesion on metal substrates for industrial processes.

Surfactant producers also use it as a fatty acid feedstock for the synthesis of soaps, esters, and amide-based emulsifiers. This versatile chemical intermediate is essential for creating high-performance surfactants used in various cleaning and processing agents.

Arachidic acid is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake solid. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications and in higher-purity grades suitable for cosmetic and food-contact formulations to meet specific safety requirements.

Standard specifications align with GC purity requirements, with typical commercial offerings ranging from 90% to 99%+ purity depending on end-use requirements. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for large-scale manufacturing and specialized laboratory applications.

description:
Arachidonic acid (CAS 506-32-1 ), commonly abbreviated as ARA, is a long-chain polyunsaturated omega-6 fatty acid sourced primarily from animal and fungal lipid fractions.

It functions as a bioactive lipid ingredient in nutritional, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic formulations where specific fatty acid composition is a formulation requirement.

In infant formula, ARA is added alongside DHA to meet regulatory standards for essential fatty acid content in early-life nutrition products for global distribution.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reference standard and active ingredient in prostaglandin and eicosanoid research, as well as in lipid-based drug delivery systems.

Sports nutrition and dietary supplement producers incorporate ARA to support muscle protein synthesis pathways in performance-focused products and specialized health supplements.

In cosmetic formulations, it is used in skin barrier repair creams and serums where targeted fatty acid delivery to the stratum corneum is required for efficacy.

Arachidonic acid is supplied as a liquid oil or in encapsulated powder form, with encapsulation commonly used to improve oxidative stability for food and supplement applications.

It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 40% to >98% depending on the intended use and industry.

Its long-chain fatty acid profile contributes to emollient performance and film formation on the skin surface. In lubricant formulations, it functions as a boundary lubricant additive or surface modifier in metalworking fluids.

name: Pentacosanoic acid
description:
Pentacosanoic acid (CAS 506-38-7 ), also known as hyenic acid, is a saturated C25 fatty acid used as a reference standard and functional ingredient in food, nutrition, and personal care formulations.

Its odd-chain fatty acid structure makes it a sought-after material for analytical calibration and biomarker research, as well as a functional component in emulsification and rheology systems.

In food and nutrition research, this acid serves as a certified reference standard for quantifying odd-chain fatty acids in plasma, dairy, and tissue samples. This is a growing area of interest in nutritional biomarker studies.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into emollient systems and wax blends where controlled melting behavior and film-forming consistency are required for high-end cosmetic products.

Its emulsifying properties support the stabilization of water-in-oil systems in topical creams and balms. In rheology modification, it contributes to the structural integrity of anhydrous formulations.

Common applications include lipsticks and solid serums where stability is paramount. The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid for easy handling.

It is available in high-purity research and reference-grade specifications, typically at ≥98% or ≥99% purity. These grades are suited for both analytical and formulation use in various industries.

name: L-hydroxyproline
description:
L-Hydroxyproline (CAS 51-35-4 ), commonly abbreviated as Hyp, is a non-essential amino acid derived primarily from collagen hydrolysis. It functions as a biochemical marker for collagen content and serves as a building block in peptide synthesis.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Hyp is used as a reference standard and synthetic intermediate in the production of collagen-related peptides and drug compounds targeting connective tissue. It is essential for nutraceutical formulations and cosmetic actives development.

Food and nutrition manufacturers incorporate it into collagen-based supplements, functional protein blends, and hydrolyzed collagen products where amino acid profile verification is required. This ensures high-quality standards for consumer health products.

Personal care formulators use it as a moisturizing and stabilizing agent in anti-aging creams, serums, and skin-conditioning treatments where collagen support claims are commercially relevant. It helps maintain the structural integrity of topical applications.

It also serves as an analytical reagent in quality control laboratories for quantifying collagen content in raw materials and finished products. This application is vital for maintaining consistency across various industrial manufacturing processes.

L-Hydroxyproline is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in USP , FCC , and reagent-grade specifications to meet the sourcing requirements of pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturers.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with smaller quantities available for R&D and QC applications. Our supply chain ensures that all technical requirements and quality benchmarks are met for every shipment.

name: Vinyl neodecanoate
description:
Vinyl neodecanoate (CAS 51000-52-3 ) is a branched-chain vinyl ester monomer used to build flexibility, hydrophobicity, and adhesion into polymer systems. It functions as a reactive building block in emulsion and solution polymerization.

This monomer modifies the performance profile of the resulting resin without requiring post-processing steps. In architectural and industrial coatings, it is copolymerized with vinyl acetate or acrylic monomers to improve water resistance.

The chemical is highly effective at reducing film brittleness in various coating applications. Pressure-sensitive adhesives and laminating adhesives incorporate it to tune tack and peel strength across a range of substrates.

Sealant and elastomer formulations benefit from its contribution to low-temperature flexibility and long-term weatherability. In printing and packaging, it supports the development of emulsion polymers used in barrier coatings.

The product is also utilized in ink-receptive layers to enhance performance. Vinyl neodecanoate is supplied as a clear liquid monomer and is available in technical grade for industrial polymerization applications.

Standard inhibitor packages are included to ensure storage stability over time. Bulk and intermediate container formats are typical for industrial procurement volumes to meet large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: Pigment yellow 13
description:
Pigment Yellow 13 (CAS 5102-83-0 ), also known as Diarylide Yellow and abbreviated as PY13, is a high-performance organic pigment used to deliver bright, opaque yellow coloration across a broad range of industrial substrates.

Commercially available under trade names such as Monolite Yellow GL and Helio Fast Yellow GRF, it is a benchmark yellow pigment valued for its strong tinting strength and cost-effective performance in demanding production environments.

In printing inks, PY13 is a standard choice for offset and flexographic formulations where high color strength and good transparency are required for process yellow applications.

Plastic compounders incorporate it into polyolefins, PVC, and engineering resins to achieve consistent yellow shades in finished consumer and industrial goods.

Coatings manufacturers use it in industrial and decorative paints where opacity and batch-to-batch color consistency are critical for high-volume manufacturing.

In paper and textile applications, it delivers uniform surface coloration in coated papers and pigment-printed fabrics, ensuring a high-quality finish across various materials.

PY13 is supplied as a dry powder, with press cake forms available from select manufacturers for direct dispersion into liquid systems. It is offered in technical and industrial grades.

Specific formulations are optimized for either solvent-based or water-based systems. Particle size and surface treatment variants are available to meet the dispersion requirements of different end-use applications.

name: Triglycerin monolaurate
description:
Triglycerin monolaurate (CAS 51033-31-9 ) is a polyglycerol ester of lauric acid used as a mild, non-ionic emulsifier and humectant across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations.

Its polyglycerol backbone provides a higher hydrophilic character than conventional monoglycerides, making it effective at stabilizing oil-in-water systems at relatively low use levels.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier in bakery products, dairy alternatives, and low-fat spreads where stable emulsion structure and moisture retention are both required.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and leave-on skin care products where it contributes both emulsification and surface moisturization without heavy residue.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it supports uniform active ingredient distribution within emulsion-based carriers and is evaluated in nutraceutical encapsulation systems.

Triglycerin monolaurate is typically supplied as a liquid or semi-solid paste, depending on temperature and formulation grade for industrial applications.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with some suppliers offering material aligned to FCC or Ph. Eur. excipient standards.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller quantities available for formulation development to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

name: Decaglyceryl monocaprylate
description:
Decaglyceryl monocaprylate (CAS 51033-41-1 ), also marketed as MCA 750 and sold under the INCI designation Polyglyceryl-10 caprylate, is a polyglycerol ester of caprylic acid.

It is used as a mild, water-soluble emulsifier and humectant across personal care, food, and cleaning applications. Its high hydrophilicity makes it effective at stabilizing oil-in-water systems.

This ingredient improves skin feel in leave-on and rinse-off formulations. In cosmetic formulations, it functions as a primary or co-emulsifier in lightweight lotions, serums, and micellar products.

It is often preferred where a clean-label, non-ethoxylated surfactant is required. Food manufacturers use it to stabilize emulsions and improve texture in low-fat and functional food products.

Polyglycerol esters are accepted under applicable regulations for food use. In home care and industrial cleaning concentrates, it supports wetting and dispersion of active ingredients.

It is particularly useful in mild or naturally derived formulation platforms. It also acts as a solubilizer for fragrance and lipophilic actives in aqueous systems for various industries.

Decaglyceryl monocaprylate is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available for industrial use.

Food-grade material generally conforms to applicable purity standards for polyglycerol esters. Bulk supply is standard in drums or IBCs, with sample quantities available for development.

name: Totarol
description:
Totarol (CAS 511-15-9 ) is a naturally derived diterpenoid phenol extracted primarily from the heartwood of Podocarpus totara. It functions as a potent antimicrobial and antioxidant active.

This compound is used in preservation systems and bioactive formulations across personal care and pharmaceutical development. In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated as a natural preservative booster.

It is effective against gram-positive bacteria and offers an alternative to synthetic biocides in clean-label product lines. Skincare brands use it in creams, serums, and deodorant formulations.

It is ideal where broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity is required alongside antioxidant protection. Pharmaceutical researchers apply it in topical and oral care preparations targeting bacterial biofilm disruption.

It is particularly useful in anti-acne and anti-plaque product development. Its antioxidant capacity also supports stability in lipid-rich formulations, helping extend shelf life in oil-based personal care products.

The product is typically supplied as a fine powder or resinous solid, with purity grades commonly ranging from 95% upward for cosmetic and research applications. Standardized botanical extracts are also available.

These extracts contain defined concentrations for formulators seeking a diluted, easier-to-handle format. Buyers should confirm specification documentation, including HPLC-verified purity and botanical sourcing details.

This is essential when evaluating suppliers for regulated end-use applications. Quality control ensures the material meets the rigorous demands of the global chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

name: Methyl diisopropyl propionamide
description:
Methyl diisopropyl propionamide (CAS 51115-67-4 ), widely recognized in the flavor and personal care industries as WS-23 , is a synthetic cooling agent that delivers a clean sensation.

It provides a non-menthol cooling effect without the associated taste or odor. Registered under FEMA 3804 , it is used across food, beverage, oral care, and cosmetic applications.

In flavored products including chewing gum, mints, and confectionery, it provides intense cooling at low use levels. This allows formulators to reduce or replace menthol entirely in their recipes.

Oral care manufacturers incorporate it into toothpastes, mouthwashes, and breath strips. It is preferred where a clean cooling effect is desired over a traditional mint flavor profile.

In personal care, it is used in lip balms, skin gels, and after-sun products. It delivers a sensory cooling effect that enhances the consumer perception of freshness and relief.

Home care formulators also use it in surface sprays and fabric conditioners. It adds a cooling freshness cue to the product experience, improving the overall brand perception for users.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in liquid carrier solutions. It is available in food-grade quality conforming to FEMA specifications for various industries.

Technical grades are also offered for non-ingestible applications. Typical supply formats include bulk powder and pre-diluted concentrates for ease of handling in manufacturing facilities.

description:
Glycerin monostearate polyethylene glycol ether (CAS 51158-08-8 ), commonly sourced under the designation PEG-20 glyceryl stearate, is a nonionic surfactant and emulsifier derived from glyceryl stearate and polyethylene glycol.

It stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions and improves skin feel in finished formulations, making it a practical choice for formulators balancing performance with mildness in various applications.

In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-emulsifier in lotions, creams, and moisturizers, contributing both emulsion stability and a humectant effect on the skin surface.

Shampoos and conditioning rinses use it to solubilize oils and improve spreadability without disrupting foam profiles. It is highly valued for its versatility across different cosmetic formats.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it acts as a wetting and dispersing agent in liquid detergent systems. It helps maintain consistency and performance in complex chemical mixtures.

Textile processing operations apply it as a softening and surface-conditioning agent during finishing treatments to improve fabric handle and uniformity across various fiber types.

Glycerin monostearate polyethylene glycol ether is typically supplied as a paste or waxy solid, with liquid forms available depending on PEG chain length and specific formulation needs.

name: Octaethylene glycol
description:
Octaethylene glycol (CAS 5117-19-1 ), commonly abbreviated as PEG-8, is a mid-chain polyethylene glycol used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations. It functions as a solvent, humectant, and emulsifier, bridging water-soluble and lipophilic components in complex systems.

In personal care formulations, PEG-8 acts as a humectant and carrier, improving moisture retention and enhancing the spreadability of creams, lotions, and serums. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solubilizer and vehicle for active ingredients.

In topical and oral preparations, consistent molecular weight distribution is critical for dosing accuracy. In printing inks and coatings, it improves pigment dispersion and controls viscosity to meet specific substrate adhesion requirements.

Metalworking and industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it into water-based cutting fluids and process lubricants to reduce friction and improve tool life. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing processes.

Octaethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, viscous liquid. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications including USP and BP , as well as cosmetic-grade and technical-grade options depending on purity requirements.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers, with high-purity grades supplied for regulated pharmaceutical and personal care applications. Proper storage ensures the stability and longevity of the chemical profile.

name: Trimethyl phosphate
description:
Trimethyl phosphate (CAS 512-56-1 ), also known as TMP and trimethyl orthophosphate, is an organophosphate ester used industrially as a flame retardant additive and pH buffering agent.

Its low volatility and thermal stability make it a practical processing aid across polymer, textile, and cleaning formulations. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, TMP functions as a flame retardant plasticizer.

It is incorporated into resins and coatings to meet fire performance specifications. Textile processors use it as a finishing agent where controlled phosphate release contributes to flame resistance in treated fabrics.

In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, TMP acts as a pH buffer and sequestrant to stabilize active ingredients across varying water hardness conditions. This ensures product stability and performance.

The leather and paper industries apply it during processing stages where controlled acidity and surface treatment consistency are required. It is a versatile chemical for diverse industrial manufacturing needs.

Trimethyl phosphate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger procurement volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher for industrial applications. Buyers sourcing for specialty polymer or electronics applications should confirm specification sheets against process-specific purity requirements.

name: Ascaridole
description:
Ascaridole (CAS 512-85-6 ) is a naturally occurring bicyclic monoterpene endoperoxide isolated primarily from chenopodium oil, where it constitutes the majority of the active fraction. Historically significant as one of the first natural compounds with confirmed antiparasitic activity, it serves as a reference compound.

It is utilized as a synthetic intermediate in pharmaceutical and agrochemical research programs. In pharmaceutical development, it is used as a starting material or structural reference for synthesizing novel antiparasitic and antimicrobial candidates.

This is particularly relevant where endoperoxide pharmacophores are under investigation. Agrochemical researchers evaluate it as a biocidal active in formulations targeting soil-borne pathogens and certain pest species, drawing on its documented activity.

Its endoperoxide bridge makes it a relevant model compound in oxidative chemistry studies aimed at developing new crop protection actives. Specialty chemical suppliers also offer it to academic and industrial laboratories conducting natural product synthesis.

It is frequently used for comparative bioactivity screening in various laboratory settings. The product is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity grades suited to research and pharmaceutical intermediate applications.

It is available in small to moderate quantities through specialty fine chemical and reference standard suppliers, reflecting its niche positioning outside bulk commodity markets. This ensures high quality for specialized industrial needs.

Certificate of Analysis documentation with purity confirmation by GC or HPLC is standard for procurement at research and pharmaceutical grades. This documentation ensures the material meets the rigorous requirements of modern chemical manufacturing and testing.

name: 4,4-dimethyloxazolidine
description:
4,4-Dimethyloxazolidine (CAS 51200-87-4 ) is a cyclic amine biocide and preservative used across industrial and personal care applications. It functions by releasing formaldehyde under aqueous conditions, delivering broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity.

This chemical provides effective control against bacteria, fungi, and yeast in various environments. In metalworking and industrial lubricants, it controls microbial contamination in water-miscible cutting fluids and coolants, extending fluid service life.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative booster in rinse-off and leave-on products. This is particularly common where formaldehyde-donor preservation systems are specified for product stability and safety.

In oilfield and water treatment operations, it is used to prevent biofouling and microbiologically influenced corrosion. It is frequently applied in injection water systems and process pipelines to maintain operational integrity.

The compound also functions as a corrosion inhibitor in industrial fluid formulations where microbial-driven degradation accelerates metal attack. This dual-action capability makes it a versatile additive for complex industrial systems.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically as a concentrated aqueous or neat solution. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial applications, while cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care use.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes depending on volume requirements and logistical needs. It is handled according to standard industrial safety protocols to ensure stability and efficacy during storage and transport.

name: Chloroallyl methenamine chloride
description:
Chloroallyl methenamine chloride (CAS 51229-78-8 ), commercially recognized as the cis-form of Quaternium-15, is a formaldehyde-releasing biocide used to control microbial growth in water-based industrial and personal care formulations.

It functions by generating controlled levels of formaldehyde in situ, providing broad-spectrum preservation against bacteria, yeasts, and molds. In coatings and adhesives, it protects water-based systems from microbial spoilage.

This includes latex paints and construction adhesives during storage and in-can use. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products such as shampoos, conditioners, and lotions.

Consistent antimicrobial efficacy across a broad pH range is a key selection criterion for these applications. Sealant and elastomer manufacturers use it to extend the shelf life of aqueous dispersions susceptible to bacterial contamination.

It also finds use in metalworking fluids and industrial water treatment where microbial control directly impacts process integrity. The chemical is supplied as an aqueous solution with active concentrations typically in the range of 96–98%.

It is available in solid form or as diluted liquid grades to suit various manufacturing needs. The product is offered in technical and cosmetic-grade specifications to meet the requirements of both industrial and personal care end markets.

In architectural coatings and construction materials, including concrete and paving products, it provides consistent earth-tone yellows that resist UV fading and weathering.

Plastics compounders incorporate it into masterbatches for packaging films and molded parts where processing temperatures would degrade organic alternatives.

Food manufacturers use the E172iii-grade to color confectionery coatings, bakery products, and dietary supplements within permitted limits for safe consumption.

Printing inks and industrial sealants also rely on this pigment for opacity and color consistency in high-volume production runs across various global markets.

name: Polyepoxysuccinic acid
description:
Polyepoxysuccinic acid (CAS 51274-37-4 ), also marketed as PESA, is a biodegradable polymeric chelating agent used in industrial water and process systems. It controls scale deposition and inhibits corrosion by sequestering hardness ions.

This chemical effectively manages calcium, magnesium, and barium before they precipitate on equipment surfaces. In cooling water and boiler systems, PESA prevents calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate scale from forming on heat transfer surfaces.

By maintaining thermal efficiency and reducing downtime, it serves as a critical component in industrial maintenance. Oil and gas operators use it in produced water treatment and injection water conditioning for flow assurance.

Mineral scale in pipelines and wellbores causes significant problems that this agent helps mitigate. Desalination and reverse osmosis plants apply it as an antiscalant to extend membrane service life significantly.

It keeps sparingly soluble salts in solution to prevent fouling. Its environmental profile makes it a preferred substitute for phosphonate-based scale inhibitors in regions with strict phosphorus discharge limits.

Polyepoxysuccinic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 40% active content. It is available in technical grade for industrial water treatment applications across various sectors.

Bulk supply is standard in IBC totes and drummed quantities for large-scale operations. Documentation typically includes COA, MSDS, and biodegradability test data to support regulatory compliance in sensitive environments.

In hair care formulations, it deposits onto negatively charged hair fibers to deliver detangling, softness, and static control in conditioners, masks, and leave-in treatments. Fabric softeners and textile finishing compounds rely on it to improve fiber hand feel.

This chemical helps reduce static buildup during processing and is essential for high-performance textile manufacturing. In leather treatment, it acts as a surface modifier that enhances uniformity of finish coats and improves substrate wetting.

Paper manufacturing uses it as a softening and conditioning additive to modify surface properties of tissue and specialty paper grades. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking reliable surface modification properties.

Electronics producers use it as a raw material for barium titanate synthesis, a key dielectric compound in capacitors and piezoelectric components. In glass and specialty optical formulations, it modifies refractive index and improves durability.

name: Cadmium carbonate
description:
Cadmium carbonate (CAS 513-78-0 ), also referenced in some supplier catalogues as Kalcit or Chemcarb, is an inorganic cadmium salt used primarily as a precursor and catalyst component in industrial chemical processes.

It serves as a controlled source of cadmium ion in applications where direct use of more soluble cadmium compounds would complicate processing or handling. In electronics manufacturing, it acts as a starting material.

This compound is essential for producing cadmium-based pigments, phosphors, and semiconductor compounds used in specialty components. The mining and metals sector uses it as an intermediate in cadmium refining workflows.

Controlled decomposition yields cadmium oxide for further downstream processing. It also functions as a catalyst precursor in select organic synthesis reactions where thermal conversion to the oxide is part of the design.

Formulators working with cadmium-based stabilizers for PVC and specialty coatings may also source it as a raw material input. The material is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder for industrial use.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically expressed as minimum assay by metal content. This ensures consistency across various manufacturing and chemical synthesis applications.

Packaging is available in small laboratory quantities through to bulk industrial quantities. All shipments are subject to applicable regulatory requirements governing cadmium compounds in the buyer's jurisdiction.

name: Cobalt carbonate
description:
Cobalt carbonate (CAS 513-79-1 ), also known as cobaltous carbonate, is an inorganic cobalt salt used across metallurgical, catalytic, and coating applications. It functions primarily as a cobalt source in processes where controlled reactivity is required.

In the mining and metals industry, it serves as a precursor for producing cobalt oxides, cobalt powders, and hard metal alloys used in cutting tools. These materials are essential for manufacturing wear-resistant components and industrial machinery.

Coatings and pigment manufacturers use it to introduce cobalt into ceramic glazes, glass colorants, and drying agents for alkyd-based paints. This ensures consistent coloration and improved drying times in various industrial finishing processes.

As a catalyst precursor, it is calcined or reduced to generate active cobalt species for hydroprocessing and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis. This makes it a vital component in modern petrochemical and fuel production technologies.

Water treatment applications utilize its pH-buffering capacity to stabilize process streams where cobalt dosing is required. This application is critical for maintaining chemical balance in specialized industrial water systems.

The product is supplied as a fine pink to violet powder in both technical and reagent grades. Purity specifications typically range from 99% for laboratory uses down to technical grades suited for metallurgical processing.

Our material meets rigorous quality benchmarks, including USP and ACS standards where applicable for high-purity requirements. Packaging is available in small drums through to bulk quantities depending on your specific needs.

name: Propylene glycol n-butyl ether
description:
Propylene glycol n-butyl ether (CAS 5131-66-8 ), commonly abbreviated as PnB and also marketed as 1-Butoxy-2-propanol, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent used across coatings and industrial formulations.

Its controlled evaporation rate and compatibility with both water-based and solvent-based systems make it a preferred choice for formulators managing film formation and flow in various chemical applications.

In architectural and industrial coatings, PnB functions as a coalescing aid and flow promoter, improving film leveling in waterborne latex systems. It is essential for achieving high-quality surface finishes.

Automotive refinish and OEM coating formulators use it to extend open time and reduce surface defects in spray-applied finishes. This ensures a smooth application process and durable final product results.

In printing inks for packaging applications, it supports pigment dispersion and press stability across flexographic and gravure processes. This versatility makes it a staple in the modern printing industry.

Hard-surface cleaners and industrial degreasers incorporate PnB to solubilize oils and greases while remaining compatible with water-dilutable concentrate formats for efficient cleaning performance.

Propylene glycol n-butyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging including drums and IBC totes. Bulk liquid is also available for high-volume procurement and large-scale manufacturing.

Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, meeting purity requirements for coatings. Solvent-grade material is commonly evaluated against established benchmarks for purity and water content.

name: Sulfosuccinic acid
description:
Sulfosuccinic acid (CAS 5138-18-1 ) is a bifunctional organic acid carrying both carboxylic and sulfonic acid groups, used industrially as a surface-active intermediate and wetting agent.

It serves primarily as a building block for ester-based surfactants, particularly dialkyl sulfosuccinates, that appear across personal care, textile, and industrial cleaning formulations.

In textile and leather processing, sulfosuccinic acid derivatives improve fiber wetting and dye penetration, enabling more uniform treatment across various substrates and materials.

Personal care formulators use it as a precursor to mild surfactant esters found in shampoos, cleansers, and foam-based products where low irritation is a high formulation priority.

In printing and packaging, sulfosuccinate-based surfactants derived from this acid act as dispersants and wetting agents in specialized ink and coating systems for industrial use.

Industrial cleaning formulations rely on its esterified derivatives for degreasing and emulsification of oils and soils on hard surfaces in commercial and manufacturing environments.

Sulfosuccinic acid is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration varying by supplier. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for these applications.

Buyers sourcing for personal care or cosmetic end products should confirm grade suitability and purity specifications with the supplier prior to procurement to ensure compliance.

name: Abietic acid
description:
Abietic acid (CAS 514-10-3 ), also known commercially as Sylvic acid, is the primary resin acid derived from pine rosin and serves as a foundational raw material across adhesive, coating, and surface treatment applications.

It functions as a tackifier, emulsifier, and film-forming agent, giving formulators a bio-based building block with strong substrate adhesion characteristics. In adhesives and sealants, it is used to build tack and cohesive strength.

Pressure-sensitive and hot-melt formulations benefit from its inclusion. Printing ink manufacturers rely on it as a resin component that controls viscosity, pigment dispersion, and ink adhesion to paper and packaging substrates.

In surface coatings, it contributes to film formation and acts as a wetting agent that improves substrate coverage in alkyd and varnish systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into cosmetic bases for texture modification.

This material is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or crystalline solid. It is available in technical grade, which covers the majority of industrial adhesive, ink, and coating applications.

Rosin-derived grades vary in purity and acid value, and buyers should confirm specification sheets against their formulation requirements. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance standards for the end product.

name: Canthaxanthin
description:
Canthaxanthin (CAS 514-78-3 ), also sold under the trade names Carophyll Red and Orobronze, and designated E161g in the EU, is a red-orange ketocarotenoid pigment used to deliver and stabilize color in food and feed applications.

It functions as both a colorant and an antioxidant, making it a dual-purpose ingredient for formulators working across nutrition and pigmentation categories. In aquaculture and poultry feed, it is used to achieve consistent flesh and egg yolk pigmentation.

This directly influences the visual quality that drives consumer purchasing decisions. Salmon and trout producers rely on it as a primary pigmentation agent to meet market color specifications. In food manufacturing, it is approved for specific product categories.

These categories include certain cheeses, sausage casings, and decorative confectionery coatings. It also appears in dietary supplement formulations targeting carotenoid intake, where its antioxidant activity supports product positioning.

The product is supplied as a fine crystalline powder and in stabilized beadlet or dispersion forms designed for feed and food processing compatibility. Standard commercial grades include feed-grade and food-grade specifications.

The beadlet form is commonly used to improve handling and dispersibility in premix and dry blend applications. Purity levels and carrier systems vary by grade and intended regulatory market to ensure compliance with global standards.

name: Acid green 5
description:
Acid Green 5 (CAS 5141-20-8 ), also known commercially as Light Green SF Yellowish and AF Green No. 2, is a synthetic triarylmethane acid dye used to impart bright yellow-green shades to a range of substrates.

It bonds effectively to protein and polyamide fibers under acidic conditions, making it a reliable colorant choice for industries requiring consistent, reproducible hues for their specific manufacturing needs.

In textile dyeing, this chemical is applied to wool, silk, and nylon fabrics where it delivers strong color yield and good leveling properties under standard acid bath conditions for high-quality results.

Leather finishers use it to achieve uniform surface coloration in both drum dyeing and spray application processes. In paper manufacturing, it is used to produce colored printing and packaging grades.

Ink formulators also incorporate it into water-based printing inks for packaging applications requiring bright, defined green shades. This versatility makes it a staple in various industrial coloring processes.

The product is supplied as a powder, typically in technical and dyestuff grades meeting standard colorimetric specifications. Purity and dye content are commonly expressed as a percentage of active colorant.

Commercial grades generally range from 60% to 85% dye content depending on the specific application. Bulk quantities are available for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging options for laboratory use.

name: Bisabolol
description:
Bisabolol (CAS 515-69-5 ), also known as α-Bisabolol, is a naturally derived monocyclic sesquiterpene alcohol originally sourced from German chamomile. It is now predominantly produced synthetically or from candeia tree oil for industrial use.

It functions as a skin-conditioning agent and active carrier in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations. This ingredient is highly valued for its ability to enhance the penetration of other actives into the skin layers.

In skincare formulations, it is used as a primary soothing and moisturizing agent in creams, serums, and lotions. These products typically target sensitive or reactive skin types requiring gentle care.

Its carrier properties make it a preferred solvent for active ingredients in topical pharmaceutical preparations. This includes wound-care products and medicated creams where high purity and efficacy are essential.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it as a fixative and mild floral base note in fine fragrances and functional perfumery. It also appears in after-sun products, baby care lines, and anti-aging formulations.

The material is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid. Standard commercial grades include natural and synthetic variants, with natural-origin material often certified to differentiate supply chains.

Cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are both available to meet industry needs. Natural grades are commonly accompanied by optical purity data confirming the specific enantiomer content.

name: Ammonium lactate
description:
Ammonium lactate (CAS 515-98-0 ), also known commercially as Lac-Hydrin, is the ammonium salt of lactic acid used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, humectant, and mild preservative.

This versatile compound is highly relevant to formulators working across multiple regulated categories. In pharmaceutical topical formulations, it delivers moisturization and mild keratolytic activity for skin health.

It is a standard active in prescription and OTC dry skin lotions. Food manufacturers use it as a pH regulator and buffering agent in processed and fermented products where lactic acid alone may be too aggressive.

In personal care, it appears in body lotions, creams, and scalp treatments where controlled moisture retention is required. Mild acidification is another key benefit provided by this ingredient in cosmetic applications.

Preservation-boosting systems in cosmetic formulations also incorporate it to support antimicrobial efficacy at specific pH ranges. This ensures product stability and safety throughout the shelf life of the formulation.

Ammonium lactate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 60% concentration, though other concentrations are available. Pharmaceutical-grade material is produced to USP specifications for high purity.

Food-grade product meets FCC standards to ensure safety in edible applications. Technical-grade solution is also available for industrial pH control and various non-regulated manufacturing applications.

name: Butyltin oxide
description:
Butyltin oxide (CAS 51590-67-1 ), also known as Monobutyltin oxide and commercially as Tegokat 256, is an organotin compound used as a catalyst and functional additive across polymer and industrial coating systems.

It drives esterification, transesterification, and condensation reactions where precise reaction control and thermal stability are required. In plastics and polymer processing, it catalyzes the production of polyesters and polyurethanes.

This material enables consistent molecular weight distribution in industrial-scale synthesis. PVC stabilization systems use it as a precursor to produce organotin heat stabilizers that protect against thermal degradation during extrusion.

Building and construction applications include its use in curing silicone sealants and coatings. It accelerates crosslinking without compromising adhesion to substrates in various architectural and industrial environments.

Textile and leather finishing operations employ it in flame-retardant treatments and surface coatings. These applications require durable chemical bonding to fiber or hide substrates for long-term performance and stability.

Butyltin oxide is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in technical grade, with purity specifications typically ranging from 95% to 98%+ depending on the intended industrial application.

Packaging options generally follow standard industrial formats, including fiber drums and multi-wall bags suited for bulk procurement. This ensures safe handling and storage for large-scale chemical manufacturing facilities.
