name: Sodium acryloyldimethyltaurate
description:
Sodium acryloyldimethyltaurate , also known as Sodium AMPS, is a reactive monomer used as a building block in the synthesis of specialty polymers and copolymers. It is primarily valued for its role in producing materials that control rheology.

This chemical, identified by CAS 5165-97-9 , helps modify surfaces and stabilize emulsions across demanding industrial and personal care applications. In personal care, it is polymerized into thickening and stabilizing agents.

These agents are used in creams, lotions, and sunscreens where conventional thickeners underperform at extreme pH or electrolyte levels. Oil and gas producers incorporate these polymers into drilling fluids and recovery formulations.

These formulations maintain viscosity under high-temperature and high-salinity conditions. Water treatment programs use its derived polymers as scale inhibitors and dispersants in cooling towers and industrial water systems.

In textile and paper processing, it contributes to surface modification coatings that improve wet strength, dye uptake, and fiber adhesion. This versatility makes it a critical component for many specialized manufacturing sectors.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% active content, though solid forms are available. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial offering for most large-scale applications.

name: Ethoxylated pentaerythritol tetraacrylate
description:
Ethoxylated pentaerythritol tetraacrylate (CAS 51728-26-8 ), also sold under the designation RP 1040, is a multifunctional acrylate monomer used as a reactive crosslinker and diluent in UV- and EB-curable systems.

The ethoxylation imparts flexibility and reduced skin sensitization potential compared to non-ethoxylated counterparts. This makes it a preferred crosslinker where film toughness and substrate adhesion must be balanced.

In UV-curable coatings, it crosslinks the polymer network to deliver hard, scratch-resistant films on wood, plastic, and metal substrates. Radiation-curable adhesives and sealants use it to control cure speed.

In printing inks, particularly energy-curable offset and flexo formulations, it improves ink film cohesion and reduces oxygen inhibition. This ensures a more efficient curing process and higher quality finish.

Plastic substrate coatings benefit from its ethoxylated backbone, which enhances adhesion to low-surface-energy materials without requiring primer layers. This simplifies the application process for industrial users.

Supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, it is typically available in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial formulation volumes. Standard commercial grades are characterized by acrylate functionality.

Viscosity and acid value are key metrics, with technical-grade specifications being the norm for this product class. Some suppliers offer low-color or low-odor variants targeting high-quality graphic arts.

These specialized versions are ideal for optical coating applications where clarity is paramount. The material remains a versatile staple for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in radiation-cured systems.

name: Quaternium-22

The ingredient provides substantive moisturization across various cosmetic platforms. Its mildness profile makes it suitable for baby care and sensitive-skin product lines where conventional quats would be too harsh for the end user.

name: Sodium methanethiolate
description:
Sodium methanethiolate (CAS 5188-07-8 ), also known as sodium thiomethylate, is a reactive organosulfur nucleophile used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and polymer chemistry.

SMM functions primarily as a methylthiolation reagent, introducing the methylthio group into target molecules under controlled reaction conditions. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is a key intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients where selective sulfur alkylation is required, including certain antibiotics and cardiovascular compounds. Agrochemical producers use it for functionality.

It introduces methylthio functionality into herbicide and pesticide molecules during multi-step synthesis. In polymer and plastics processing, it acts as a catalyst or chain-transfer agent to control weight.

It is used to modify end-group chemistry in various materials. The oil and gas sector applies sodium thiomethylate in scavenger formulations and as a pH-regulating additive in refinery process streams.

Sodium methanethiolate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in aqueous or methanolic form, with concentration ranges commonly between 20% and 40% by weight for industrial use.

Technical and synthesis grades are the standard commercial offerings, with pharmaceutical-grade material available from select manufacturers to meet API intermediate specifications for high purity.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes depending on volume requirements. This ensures safe handling and transport of the chemical across global supply chains for diverse manufacturing needs.

name: Matrine

It functions as a bioactive agent with preservation, stabilization, and UV-protective properties across multiple formulated product categories. In agricultural formulations, it is used as a botanical biopesticide.

It is incorporated into crop protection products where synthetic chemical restrictions apply or where organic certification is required. Personal care formulators incorporate it into UV-protective and antioxidant products.

This is particularly common in markets where plant-derived actives are preferred over synthetic stabilizers. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical development, it serves as a reference compound and active ingredient.

It is a candidate in finished dosage form research. Agricultural feed applications also utilize matrine-based preparations as a natural preservative component to extend product stability and shelf life.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in varying purity grades, with high-purity specifications commonly used in pharmaceutical and research applications.

Lower-purity technical grades serve agricultural and industrial formulation needs. Packaging options typically range from small research quantities to bulk kilogram-scale orders depending on requirements.

name: Triethylene glycol monochlorohydrin
description:
Triethylene glycol monochlorohydrin (CAS 5197-62-6 ), also marketed as Provichem 0333, is a chlorinated glycol ether functioning as a reactive intermediate and solvent in specialty chemical synthesis.

Its terminal chlorine group and free hydroxyl make it a practical building block for introducing polyether segments into target molecules. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as an alkylating agent.

It is used for constructing PEGylated intermediates and ether-linked drug conjugates requiring precise chain length control. Agricultural chemical manufacturers use it to synthesize herbicide and pesticide intermediates.

This occurs where a short ethylene oxide chain with a reactive chloride terminus is specified. In polymer chemistry, it acts as a chain-end functionalization agent and initiator for ring-opening polymerization.

This enables controlled incorporation of hydrophilic segments into polyurethane and polyether systems. Specialty surfactant producers also employ it as a precursor for nonionic and cationic amphiphile synthesis.

Triethylene glycol monochlorohydrin is supplied as a liquid in bulk and drum quantities. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications typically confirmed by GC assay.

name: Mono-2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl maleate
description:
Mono-2-(methacryloyloxy)ethyl maleate (CAS 51978-15-5 ), also known as HEMA maleate, is a bifunctional reactive monomer carrying both a methacrylate and a maleic acid half-ester group.

This dual reactivity allows it to participate in free-radical polymerization while introducing pendant carboxylic acid functionality into polymer backbones. This combination drives adhesion and surface compatibility.

In electronics, it is incorporated into photoresist formulations and adhesion-promoting coatings where carboxylic acid groups improve substrate bonding to metals and inorganic surfaces.

UV-curable inks and overprint varnishes in printing and packaging use it to enhance adhesion to low-energy substrates while maintaining cure speed and overall performance.

Structural and pressure-sensitive adhesive formulations benefit from its ability to introduce crosslinkable acid sites that improve cohesive strength and peel resistance in various environments.

In polymer modification, it functions as a reactive compatibilizer, grafting onto polymer chains to improve interfacial adhesion in composite and laminate systems for industrial use.

The product is supplied as a liquid monomer, typically with an inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transit. It is available in technical grade for coatings.

Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk drum supply depending on application scale. Proper storage conditions are required to maintain the stability of this reactive monomer.

name: Tetrasodium glutamate diacetate
description:
Tetrasodium glutamate diacetate , also identified by CAS 51981-21-6 , is a biodegradable chelating agent derived from glutamic acid. It binds and sequesters metal ions such as calcium, magnesium, iron, and manganese to prevent interference in formulations.

Buyers in personal care, cleaning, and water treatment source it as a more sustainable alternative to EDTA and NTA. In personal care formulations, it stabilizes product performance by deactivating trace metals that would otherwise degrade active ingredients.

Industrial and institutional cleaning products use it to boost surfactant efficiency and prevent mineral scale redeposition on surfaces. Water treatment applications rely on it to control metal ion concentrations and inhibit scale formation.

In food-contact and agricultural cleaning, its biodegradability profile supports compliance with stricter environmental regulations. It maintains high chelation performance while meeting modern ecological standards for industrial chemical use.

The product is typically supplied as a liquid solution at 47% active content, which is the standard commercial concentration. Technical and industrial grades are the most common market forms available for bulk procurement.

description:

It is frequently utilized in cooling towers and process water circuits to maintain system efficiency. Oilfield and metalworking operations use it to prevent microbial-induced corrosion and spoilage in drilling fluids and cutting fluid emulsions.

Pulp, paper, and textile processing also employ it to control slime-forming bacteria that degrade product quality and clog equipment. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial manufacturing environments.

It also serves as a precursor in the synthesis of N-acetylcysteine and other sulfur-containing actives. In personal care, it is the active ingredient in professional hair-straightening treatments.

Controlled reduction of keratin disulfide bonds reshapes hair structure effectively. Food and beverage producers also incorporate it as an antioxidant to prevent browning in fruit-based products.

This versatile compound provides essential support for vascular and cellular protection in various finished products. In dietary supplements and functional foods, it is formulated into capsules, tablets, and fortified beverages.

These applications typically target circulatory health and general antioxidant support for consumers. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into veinotonic preparations and combination products alongside diosmin for standardized profiles.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it in serums and creams to stabilize formulations against oxidative degradation. It also supports skin-conditioning claims while enhancing the overall stability of the topical product.

In nutraceutical blends, it is commonly paired with vitamin C to enhance bioavailability and broaden the antioxidant profile. This synergy is highly valued in the production of high-quality health and wellness supplements.

The material is supplied as a fine yellow to off-white powder, with purity grades typically ranging from 90% to 98% by HPLC. Standard commercial grades conform to USP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications.

High-purity pharmaceutical grades are available for regulated drug product manufacturing. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric ton quantities, standardized from sweet orange or bitter orange sources.

It also appears in the development of stability-indicating methods, where its selective reactivity with amine groups helps identify degradation products in drug formulations.

description:

It functions as a colorant, antioxidant, and UV-stabilizing agent across cosmetic and industrial formulations. In personal care and cosmetics, it is incorporated into formulations where botanical-origin pigmentation is required.

description:
Propylene glycol monoethyl ether (CAS 52125-53-8 ), also known commercially as PE-P and 1(or 2)-ethoxypropanol, is a glycol ether solvent used across industrial and consumer formulations.

Its slow-to-moderate evaporation rate and compatibility with both water-based and solvent-based systems make it a practical choice for formulators managing film formation and substrate wetting.

In coatings and paints, it functions as a coalescing agent and flow promoter, improving surface leveling in architectural and industrial finishes for various applications.

Cleaning product manufacturers incorporate it into hard surface cleaners and degreasers where controlled evaporation and soil solubilization are required for effective performance.

In printing inks, it supports pigment dispersion and press stability across flexographic and gravure processes, ensuring consistent quality during high-speed production runs.

Metalworking fluid formulators use it as a coupling solvent to maintain emulsion stability and improve lubricity in water-miscible cutting fluids used in heavy machinery.

Propylene glycol monoethyl ether is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for high-volume industrial buyers.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this compound is the active ingredient in lozenges, throat sprays, and buccal tablets targeting oral and throat infections for patients.

Vaginal tablets and pessaries represent a significant dosage form, where it functions as the primary antifungal and antibacterial agent for local gynecological treatment.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into antiseptic mouthwashes and medicated skincare products where preservative and antimicrobial efficacy is required for the product.

It also appears in medicated wound dressings and topical preparations where surface disinfection of skin or mucous membranes is the target outcome for the user.

Dequalinium chloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to Ph. Eur. specifications is the standard commercial form.

Technical-grade material is available for non-pharmaceutical antiseptic and preservative applications in personal care and other industrial disinfection processes.

In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a skin-conditioning antioxidant in creams, serums, and sunscreens, where it protects both the formulation and the skin surface from oxidative degradation.

Its compatibility with emulsion systems also makes it suitable for slow-release or encapsulated delivery formats in both personal and environmental protection products.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulators incorporate it into polymer systems that improve suspension stability and surface wetting in liquid detergents and hard-surface cleaners.

Textile and paper processors use copolymers derived from this monomer to modify fiber surface properties, improving softness, water repellency, or dye uptake depending on the co-monomer system.

Its ethoxylate segment also contributes emulsification performance in emulsion polymerization processes where surfactant-monomers are required to stabilize the latex particle interface.

Steareth-20 methacrylate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or viscous paste, with handling characteristics dependent on temperature. It is available in technical grade for industrial use.

Dipotassium azelate (CAS 52457-54-2 ), the dipotassium salt of azelaic acid, is a water-soluble organic salt used in personal care, pharmaceutical, and specialty formulations.

Myristoyl sarcosine (CAS 52558-73-3 ), also known commercially as Hamposyl M, is an N-acyl sarcosine derivative used as a mild anionic surfactant across personal care and industrial cleaning markets.

It combines surfactant activity with corrosion-inhibiting properties, making it a functional ingredient where both cleaning performance and substrate protection are required for various applications.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a foam booster and mild cleansing agent in shampoos, facial cleansers, and toothpastes, where its low irritation profile suits sensitive-skin products.

name: Gluconic acid
description:
Gluconic acid ( CAS 526-95-4 ), also identified as E574 in food additive classifications, is a mild organic acid produced by the oxidation of glucose. It functions primarily as a chelating agent, acidulant, and pH buffer across food, pharmaceutical, industrial, and personal care markets.

In water treatment, it sequesters calcium, magnesium, and iron ions to prevent scale formation and improve the performance of cleaning and concrete admixture formulations. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as an acidulant where a smooth, non-astringent sourness is required.

This is particularly useful in dairy products, baked goods, and mineral-fortified drinks. Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it to produce mineral gluconate salts, where controlled bioavailability of calcium, iron, or zinc is a formulation priority.

In personal care, it acts as a chelating agent and mild exfoliant in rinse-off and leave-on skin formulations targeting sensitive skin. Gluconic acid is supplied as a 50% aqueous solution, which is the dominant commercial form for industrial and food-grade applications.

Solid forms are available but less common in bulk trade. Grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP ), and technical-grade to meet the sourcing requirements of different regulated markets.

name: Permethrin

It functions as a rheology modifier and moisturizing agent across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In functional food and nutraceutical products, it is incorporated into beverages and cereals.

The material contributes to texture and consumer-facing nutritional positioning in dietary supplements. Cosmetic formulators use it in serums, creams, and masks to improve skin hydration and film-forming performance.

In pharmaceutical and biotech applications, it is used as an excipient and as an active component in immune-modulating formulations. It is also utilized in research reagents and specialized medical applications.

Animal feed producers incorporate it into feed premixes targeting gut health and performance outcomes in poultry and swine. Beta Glucan is supplied as a fine powder or as a liquid dispersion, depending on source.

Common grades include food-grade and USP -compliant specifications, with purity levels typically defined by beta glucan content percentage. These levels commonly range from 70% to 95%+ for concentrated extracts.

Yeast-derived and oat-derived variants are the most commercially prevalent and are often specified separately by buyers. This is due to differing regulatory and application requirements across global chemical markets.

name: Sodium ethanesulfonate
description:
Sodium ethanesulfonate (CAS 5324-47-0 ) is an aliphatic sulfonate salt used industrially as a wetting agent and dispersant. Its sulfonate group provides strong surface activity, supporting emulsification and surface modification across several manufacturing processes.

In textile processing, it improves dye bath penetration and fiber wetting, enabling more uniform coloration across synthetic and natural substrates. Leather finishing operations use it to aid dispersion of treatment agents.

This ensures consistent surface coverage during tanning and coating steps. In paper manufacturing, it supports sizing formulations and surface treatment processes where controlled wetting is critical to sheet quality.

Plastics and polymer processing applications include its use as a dispersant in compounding and coating formulations. This is essential where uniform distribution of additives is required for material integrity.

Sodium ethanesulfonate is typically supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution. Technical grade is the most commonly available specification for industrial processing applications.

It is suited to the textile, leather, and paper sectors. Packaging is generally offered in bags or drums, with bulk quantities available for high-volume industrial procurement and supply chain needs.

This is particularly useful in pharmaceutical quality control workflows. Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and penetration agent to improve dye uptake and chemical treatment uniformity across fiber substrates.

In industrial and institutional cleaning formulations, it contributes to emulsification and soil release on hard surfaces and equipment. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into select rinse-off formulations.

These applications often require controlled foaming and surfactant mildness as process requirements. Sodium octanesulfonate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution, depending on the supplier.

Standard grades include high-purity reagent and HPLC-grade material for analytical use, as well as technical grade for industrial cleaning and textile processing. Packaging ranges from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial volumes.

name: Pinaverium bromide
description:
Pinaverium bromide (CAS 53251-94-8 ), also marketed as Dicetel, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as an antispasmodic active pharmaceutical ingredient targeting gastrointestinal smooth muscle.

It is the active substance in finished dosage forms prescribed for irritable bowel syndrome and other functional bowel disorders. As an API, it is the core ingredient in oral solid dosage manufacturing.

This compound is primarily used in film-coated tablets formulated for gastrointestinal indications. Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers source it to develop bioequivalent products where the reference listed drug contains Dicetel.

Formulators working in regulated markets across Latin America, Europe, and Asia procure it under strict pharmacopoeial-aligned specifications to meet registration requirements. It is also relevant to research organizations.

These organizations conduct GI motility studies requiring a characterized reference standard. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder available in pharmaceutical-grade quality.

The product is aligned with in-house or customer-specific specifications, as no widely adopted compendial monograph ( USP / Ph.Eur. ) is broadly published for this specific compound.

Packaging is typically offered in kilogram-scale quantities suited to clinical batch manufacturing and commercial API supply chains. This ensures reliable delivery for large-scale pharmaceutical production needs.

name: Sulfamic acid
description:
Sulfamic acid (CAS 5329-14-6 ), also known as sulphamic acid or sulfaminic acid, is a dry, stable inorganic acid used across industrial cleaning, descaling, and pH control applications.

Unlike liquid mineral acids, it handles and doses easily in solid form, making it a practical choice for formulators and industrial buyers managing acid-based processes in various facilities.

In industrial and institutional cleaning, it is the active descaling agent in boiler cleaners, heat exchanger treatments, and hard surface descalers, where it dissolves calcium and iron deposits.

It performs these tasks without the fuming hazards of hydrochloric acid. Water treatment operations use it to control pH and neutralize excess chlorine in municipal and process water systems.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a dye-bath acidifier and pH buffer, ensuring consistent uptake and finish quality. In pulp and paper manufacturing, it functions as a bleach stabilizer.

It also acts as a pH regulator during chemical pulping and brightening stages. Sulfamic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granule grades preferred for dust control.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and industrial grade, with purity levels typically at 99% or above. Bulk supply in bags, supersacks, and drums is standard for industrial volumes.

name: Di-2-propylheptyl phthalate
description:
Di-2-propylheptyl phthalate (CAS 53306-54-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DPHP, is a high-molecular-weight phthalate plasticizer used primarily in PVC compounding.

It functions as a primary plasticizer, imparting flexibility and processability to rigid polymer systems across demanding industrial applications. In PVC formulations, DPHP delivers low volatility and strong permanence.

This makes it a preferred choice for wire and cable insulation where long-term performance under elevated temperatures is required. Flooring materials and roofing membranes rely on DPHP-plasticized PVC for durability.

Wall coverings in the building and construction sector also benefit from its dimensional stability. Rubber compounders use it to improve flexibility in seals, gaskets, and technical profiles where resistance to migration is critical.

Its high boiling point also suits it for automotive interior components and industrial sheeting. These materials must maintain flexibility across a broad service temperature range to ensure long-term structural integrity.

Di-2-propylheptyl phthalate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats. It is available in technical grade for industrial PVC and rubber processing.

Purity levels typically meet or exceed 99%, with product conforming to established industrial plasticizer specifications. This ensures consistent performance and reliability for large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: 3-Bromoquinoline
description:
3-Bromoquinoline (CAS 5332-24-1 ) is a halogenated heterocyclic building block used primarily in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. The bromine substituent at the 3-position makes it a reactive intermediate for cross-coupling reactions.

This functionality enables the efficient construction of more complex quinoline-based structures. In pharmaceutical development, it serves as a key intermediate for synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug candidates.

This is particularly relevant where quinoline scaffolds are required for biological activity. Polymer and plastics manufacturers incorporate brominated quinoline derivatives into flame retardant formulations for industrial use.

In these applications, the halogen content contributes to combustion suppression in finished materials. In textile and paper treatment chemistries, it functions as a precursor to preservation and stabilization compounds.

These compounds protect substrates from degradation over time. Research and fine chemical producers also source it for producing ligands, dyes, and specialty reagents where a functionalized quinoline core is the starting point.

3-Bromoquinoline is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, typically at purities of 97% or higher for synthetic and research applications. Technical and high-purity grades are available to meet specific requirements.

These grades support pharmaceutical intermediates manufacturing and specialty chemical production. Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D use to bulk quantities for industrial-scale synthesis programs.

This chemical contributes to controlled cure rates and improved film flexibility in various industrial applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a key intermediate in synthesizing APIs and agrochemical compounds.

It is particularly useful where a primary amine with an ether spacer is required for molecular architecture. In personal care formulations, it functions as a pH buffer and stabilizer in rinse-off and leave-on products.

description:
Octyldodecanol (CAS 5333-42-6 ) is a long-chain fatty alcohol used as an emollient and solvent carrier in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations. It delivers a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel that makes it a preferred base ingredient in premium personal care products.

In skincare and color cosmetics, it functions as an emollient base and spreading agent in creams, foundations, lipsticks, and sunscreens, improving texture and skin adhesion. Formulators use it as a solvent for oil-soluble actives, pigments, and UV filters.

This material is highly valued where clarity and compatibility with silicones or esters are required. In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it acts as a carrier for active ingredients in ointments and dermal delivery systems.

Its low viscosity and oxidative stability also make it a functional component in fragrance concentrates and perfume oil dilutions. This versatility ensures its use across a wide range of high-performance industrial applications.

The product is supplied as a clear, liquid alcohol suitable for direct incorporation into formulations without further processing. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications for global distribution.

name: Sodium diisobutyl dithiophosphate
description:
Sodium diisobutyl dithiophosphate (CAS 53378-51-1 ) is an organosulfur salt used primarily as a collector and surface-active agent in mineral processing and as a functional additive in metalworking formulations.

Its affinity for metal sulfide surfaces and reactive metal interfaces makes it a targeted choice for selective mineral recovery and metal protection applications. In froth flotation, it acts as a selective collector for copper, lead, and zinc sulfide ores.

This chemical improves concentrate grades while reducing reagent consumption versus less selective alternatives. Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as an extreme-pressure and anti-wear additive for high-load conditions.

It forms protective films on metal surfaces during cutting and grinding. It also functions as a corrosion inhibitor in industrial lubricants and hydraulic fluids, chelating dissolved metal ions that would otherwise accelerate oxidative degradation.

In mixed-sulfide ore circuits, its selectivity over iron sulfides allows processors to improve downstream metallurgical performance. This product is typically supplied as an aqueous solution with concentration ranges around 25–40% active content.

Higher-concentration grades are available depending on the supplier. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for both mining reagent and lubricant additive applications, ensuring consistent performance in industrial settings.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes and bulk tanker supply for large-volume mining operations. This versatility in logistics ensures that the product can be integrated into various industrial workflows and large-scale processing plants.

Pharmaceutical producers use it as an excipient in tablet and capsule production, where controlled pH and mineral content are critical to formulation stability. It ensures consistent quality in medicinal products.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, humectant, and solubilizer, helping to stabilize oil-in-water systems and retain moisture in finished products. In personal care formulations, it acts as an emulsifier and humectant.

It is commonly used in creams, lotions, and serums, improving skin feel and extending product shelf stability. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a carrier and solubilizing agent in topical preparations.

This ingredient is essential where consistent active ingredient dispersion is required. Textile and leather processors incorporate it into finishing baths and softening formulations to improve fiber lubrication and surface uniformity.

In industrial and household cleaning products, it supports emulsification of oils and greases, contributing to detergent performance across a range of pH conditions. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Ethoxylated sorbitol is typically supplied as a viscous liquid. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with grade selection driven by application requirements and regional regulatory compliance.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with intermediate packaging available for formulators requiring smaller volumes. This ensures flexibility for both large-scale production and specialized laboratory testing.

name: Polyquaternium-22
description:
Polyquaternium-22 (CAS 53694-17-0 ) is a cationic copolymer used across personal care and industrial formulations for conditioning, film formation, and rheology control. It is commercially recognized under the DADMAC/acrylic acid copolymer designation in technical procurement contexts.

Its cationic charge density makes it effective at binding to negatively charged surfaces, enabling durable deposition in rinse-off and leave-on systems. In hair care, it deposits a conditioning film on the hair shaft during shampooing.

This film improves wet combability and reduces static in finished products. Skin care formulators incorporate it as a moisturizing and film-forming agent in lotions, gels, and toners where it supports humectancy alongside texture modification.

In textile processing, it functions as a surface modifier to improve fiber feel and antistatic performance in finishing baths. Paper and leather manufacturers use it to enhance surface adhesion and modify substrate charge.

These applications occur during wet-end or coating operations to ensure uniform distribution. Polyquaternium-22 is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active polymer content typically ranging around 35–40% for ease of handling.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications meeting the requirements of personal care industry standards. Technical grades are also provided for industrial textile and paper applications requiring high-performance surface modification.

name: Trilinolenin
description:
Trilinolenin (CAS 537-40-6 ), also known as Trilinolein, is the triglyceride form of linoleic acid, a naturally occurring lipid found in plant-derived oils. It functions as an emollient, carrier, and emulsifier across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

In personal care formulations, it supports skin barrier function and acts as a lightweight carrier for active ingredients in serums, creams, and oils. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a lipid excipient in soft gel encapsulation.

It is frequently utilized in lipid-based drug delivery systems where controlled release and biocompatibility are priorities. In food applications, it serves as a reference standard and functional lipid component in nutritional research.

The material is also used in specialty fat formulations. Cosmetic chemists incorporate it into emulsified systems where a linoleic-rich triglyceride profile is required for specific formulation differentiation and performance.

Trilinolenin is typically supplied as a liquid oil at ambient temperature. It is available in research-grade and high-purity analytical grades, commonly used as a reference standard in lipid profiling and quality control workflows.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade material is sourced in bulk for formulators requiring defined fatty acid triglyceride composition. This ensures consistency across various industrial applications and high-volume manufacturing processes.

name: n-acetyl-L-tyrosine
description:
N-Acetyl-L-Tyrosine (CAS 537-55-3 ), commonly abbreviated as NALT, is the acetylated derivative of L-tyrosine offering significantly improved water solubility compared to the free amino acid.

This property makes it the preferred form for parenteral nutrition formulations and high-load aqueous systems where standard tyrosine would be impractical to dose. It functions as a bioavailable amino acid source.

It also acts as an antioxidant stabilizer across pharmaceutical and cosmetic manufacturing. In clinical and parenteral nutrition, NALT is incorporated into intravenous amino acid solutions where its enhanced solubility allows delivery.

Therapeutic tyrosine levels can be delivered without precipitation. Cosmetic formulators use it as an antioxidant and UV-stabilizing agent in serums, creams, and photoprotective products to protect skin from oxidative stress.

It also appears in oral dietary supplement capsules and powders targeting cognitive support, where the acetylated form is marketed for its absorption profile. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a stabilizing excipient.

This is particularly useful in sensitive peptide-based drug formulations. N-Acetyl-L-Tyrosine is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , and food-grade specifications.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is the most commercially prevalent. Bulk quantities are available for industrial formulation, with smaller quantities offered for R&D and quality testing purposes.

Tricaprylin (CAS 538-23-8 ), also known as tricaprylyl glycerol, is a triglyceride ester of glycerol and caprylic acid used as a carrier, emollient, and solubilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It delivers stable, lipid-based dispersion for active ingredients that require an inert, non-aqueous medium. In pharmaceutical formulations, it functions as a lipophilic carrier for poorly water-soluble APIs in soft gel capsules.

This material is essential for oral lipid-based drug delivery systems and injectable preparations. Food manufacturers use it as a fat replacer and carrier for fat-soluble vitamins, flavors, and nutraceutical actives in encapsulated products.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, serums, and sunscreens where a lightweight, non-greasy emollient is required. It also serves as a reference standard and excipient in lipid nanoparticle research.

The product is supplied as a clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid. Pharmaceutical and food-grade material is available to USP , FCC , and Ph. Eur. specifications, supporting regulatory compliance across multiple markets.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial and research applications. This versatile triglyceride ensures high stability and performance in diverse chemical formulations and high-purity manufacturing environments.

description:
Butyl cinnamate (CAS 538-65-8 ), also known commercially as Eliminoxy, is an ester used as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient across food and personal care applications.

In food and beverage flavoring, it contributes balsamic and fruity nuances to confectionery, baked goods, and fruit flavor compositions. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products.

This includes skin creams, lotions, and hair care formulations where it functions as a scent modifier and fixative. It is also used in fine fragrance blending to add depth to oriental and floral accords.

Flavor houses sourcing for FEMA-listed ingredients include it in flavor systems targeting tropical and exotic fruit profiles. It is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for industrial use.

It is available in flavor and fragrance grade, with specifications aligned to FEMA and industry purity standards. Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities up to drum volumes.

These volumes are suitable for commercial flavor and fragrance production. The material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols to ensure high quality and consistency for buyers.

name: Dicyclohexylcarbodiimide
description:
Dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (CAS 538-75-0 ), commonly known as DCC, is a coupling reagent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, peptide chemistry, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It activates carboxylic acids for condensation reactions, enabling the formation of amide, ester, and peptide bonds under mild conditions for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical API synthesis, DCC drives amide bond formation in the production of active ingredients where selectivity and yield are critical procurement considerations.

Peptide manufacturers rely on it as a standard coupling agent in both solution-phase and solid-phase peptide synthesis workflows for high-efficiency chemical production.

In flavor and fragrance chemistry, DCC facilitates ester synthesis for aroma compound production where conventional acid-catalyzed routes are unsuitable for the final product.

Cosmetic formulators use it in the synthesis of specialty esters and functional ingredients requiring controlled reaction conditions to ensure the stability of the formulation.

DCC is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is available in technical and high-purity reagent grades, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting specifications.

The material is suitable for GMP synthesis environments. Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to bulk supply for large-scale industrial synthesis operations.

name: Thaumatin
description:
Thaumatin (CAS 53850-34-3 ), approved as E957 , is a natural protein sweetener extracted from the West African katemfe fruit. At roughly 2,000 to 3,000 times the sweetness of sucrose by weight, it functions primarily as a high-intensity sweetener.

This ingredient acts as a powerful flavor modifier at very low use levels. In food and beverage formulations, it masks bitter and astringent off-notes from ingredients such as caffeine and steviol glycosides.

It allows formulators to reduce or replace less clean-tasting alternatives effectively. Confectionery, chewing gum, and tabletop sweetener manufacturers use it to round out sweetness profiles without adding calories.

In pharmaceutical oral dosage forms like tablets, syrups, and lozenges, it suppresses the bitterness of active ingredients. This improves patient compliance and overall product palatability for the end user.

Personal care applications include use in oral hygiene products such as toothpaste and mouthwash. In these applications, it significantly improves flavor perception and masks the taste of functional additives.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder, typically standardized to minimum 16% or higher protein content. It is available in food-grade specifications compliant with FEMA 3732 designations.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting additional purity requirements is available for oral healthcare and drug formulation use. This ensures the highest quality standards for sensitive medical and health applications.

name: Citral
description:
Citral (CAS 5392-40-5 ), also marketed under the trade name Lemsyn GB, is a naturally derived aldehyde used as a primary flavoring and fragrance ingredient. It delivers an intense lemon-citrus character and serves as a key synthetic precursor for ionones and vitamin A.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used at low concentrations to impart or reinforce lemon, lime, and verbena flavor profiles in beverages and confectionery. It carries FEMA 2303 status for use as a flavoring agent in commercial production.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine perfumes, functional fragrances, and household products where fresh citrus top notes are required. In personal care formulations, it contributes scent to shampoos, body washes, and skin creams.

Concentration limits apply under IFRA guidelines for topical applications. It also functions as a chemical intermediate in the industrial synthesis of aroma compounds including citronellol, geraniol derivatives, and beta-ionone.

The material is supplied as a pale yellow liquid, typically in concentrations of 95% or higher for commercial fragrance and flavor use. Natural-derived and synthetic grades are both available to meet specific formulation needs.

Natural citral is commonly sourced from lemongrass or Litsea cubeba oils. Food-grade material is supplied in compliance with FCC and FEMA specifications to ensure the highest safety and quality standards for global distribution.

This ingredient is used in confectionery, tobacco flavorings, and functional beverages. The FEMA 2528 designation supports its use as a recognized flavor ingredient for various industrial applications.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a buffering and stabilizing agent in oral preparations. It helps maintain product integrity across varying pH conditions during the manufacturing and storage process.

In personal care, it is used in skin-soothing formulations such as creams, serums, and toners. Its ability to retain moisture and reduce irritation supports specific product performance claims for sensitive skin.

Oral care products, including toothpastes and mouthwashes, also use it for flavor enhancement and mild antimicrobial support. Ammonium glycyrrhizate is supplied as a white to off-white powder for easy blending.

It is available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher. Pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to USP or BP standards is also commercially available.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of cephalosporin antibiotics and related beta-lactam compounds, where the aminothiazole moiety is a structurally critical fragment.

Medicinal chemistry programs use it in the construction of heterocyclic libraries for drug discovery, particularly in campaigns targeting antimicrobial and antifungal candidates.

Contract manufacturers and API producers source it as a building block for regulated synthesis workflows requiring documented purity and traceability for high-quality chemical production.

Specialty chemical formulators also evaluate it within heterocyclic compound programs for fine chemical and agrochemical research applications across various industrial sectors.

Ethyl 2-aminothiazole-4-carboxylate is supplied as a solid powder, typically off-white to pale yellow in appearance. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram commercial lots.

Formulators working on generic drug development use it as a comparator substance. This application is critical during formulation optimization and stability testing protocols to ensure product efficacy and safety.

name: gamma-tocopherol
description:
Gamma-tocopherol (CAS 54-28-4 ), also recognized as E308 and D-gamma-tocopherol, is a naturally occurring member of the vitamin E family sourced primarily from soybean and corn oils.

It functions as a lipid-soluble antioxidant and stabilizer, protecting oils, fats, and active ingredients from oxidative degradation across food, feed, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications.

In food and nutraceutical manufacturing, E308 is used to extend the shelf life of edible oils, fat-based spreads, and encapsulated supplement blends where oxidative rancidity is a primary quality concern.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, serums, and lip products to protect lipid-rich bases and deliver moisturizing benefits to finished formulations for consumers.

In animal feed and agricultural premixes, it supports oxidative stability in fat-supplemented feed compounds and contributes to vitamin E nutritional profiles for livestock and pets.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an antioxidant excipient in soft gel capsules and oil-based drug delivery systems. It is supplied as a viscous amber oil or as part of mixed tocopherol concentrates.

Standard grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications, with USP and technical grades available depending on the intended application and regulatory requirements.

This material is utilized across human and veterinary pharmaceutical markets. Furosemide is the primary API in oral tablet formulations, where it is manufactured at standardized strengths for prescription drug products.

Injectable solution manufacturing represents a distinct supply channel, requiring high-purity pharmaceutical-grade material compatible with parenteral processing standards. This ensures safety and efficacy in clinical settings.

The compound also serves as a reference standard and analytical reagent in QC laboratories. These facilities use it for validating diuretic drug products and ensuring consistent manufacturing quality.

name: Cetyl palmitate
description:
Cetyl palmitate (CAS 540-10-3 ), also known as palmitic acid cetyl ester, is a natural wax ester derived from palmitic acid and cetyl alcohol. Found natively in spermaceti and plant-based wax fractions, it functions as an emollient and emulsifier.

This versatile compound serves as a lubricant across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations. In cosmetics and skincare, it provides a smooth, non-greasy skin feel in creams, lotions, and lip products.

The compound ensures shelf life and ingredient compatibility in various cosmetic applications. It is supplied as a white crystalline solid, typically in powder or granular form for easy handling and processing.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reagent and intermediate where controlled barium content is required in API synthesis workflows to ensure consistent chemical reactions and outcomes.

In laboratory and analytical settings, it functions as a pH buffer and precipitation agent for sulfate detection and gravimetric analysis, providing reliable results for researchers.

Specialty chemical formulators also draw on it for the preparation of barium-based compounds where acetate acts as a reactive leaving group during thermal decomposition or calcination.

Barium acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid. It is available in technical and reagent grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

name: Tetrazene
description:
Tetrazene (CAS 54410-57-0 ), also referenced in some technical catalogues as Tetraaz-1-ene, is a high-nitrogen heterocyclic compound used as a sensitizer and polymerization initiator in energetic material formulations.

Its primary commercial role is in primer and ignition compositions where reliable, low-energy initiation is required. In defense and aerospace propulsion, it is incorporated into percussion primer mixes.

This chemical serves to lower the activation threshold of primary explosive compositions. Mining and blasting operations use it in detonator and initiator assemblies where consistent sensitivity is critical.

It functions as a co-sensitizer alongside lead styphnate or diazodinitrophenol in small-arms and pyrotechnic primer formulations. Research programs evaluate it as a candidate to replace legacy heavy-metal compounds.

The material is supplied as a dry powder, typically handled and shipped in desensitized or wetted form to meet transport regulations. Material is generally offered to technical-grade specifications.

Purity and particle size characterization are provided on a lot-specific basis. Supply is restricted to qualified buyers operating under appropriate explosive handling licenses and end-use certifications.

name: Hexyl glucoside
description:
Hexyl glucoside (CAS 54549-24-5 ) is a short-chain alkyl polyglucoside surfactant derived from glucose and hexanol. It functions as a mild emulsifier, foam booster, and cleansing agent across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic formulations, this ingredient improves skin compatibility while contributing to emulsification and sensory profile. Home care and industrial cleaning products incorporate it as a co-surfactant.

These applications enhance degreasing performance and stabilize foam systems. Its low irritation profile makes it a preferred choice in baby care, sensitive skin cleansers, and mild shampoo bases where surfactant mildness is a sourcing criterion.

Food-contact and specialty cleaning applications also draw on its biodegradable character. This supports formulations where environmental compliance is a procurement requirement for modern industrial standards.

The product is typically supplied as a liquid or aqueous solution, with active content concentrations commonly in the 50–60% range. Technical and cosmetic grades are the standard market offerings for global distribution.

This surfactant remains highly compatible with sensitive formulation environments. In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in facial cleansers, shampoos, and body washes where low irritation potential is a priority.

It supports stable foam generation and soil removal in rinse-off products targeting sensitive skin or baby care lines. In food-contact and food processing contexts, it is evaluated as a cleaning and degreasing agent.

It is particularly useful in heavy-duty degreasers where high-flash-point formulations are preferred over sodium-neutralized alternatives. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and body washes for better performance.

In these cosmetic applications, the amine-neutralized form contributes to viscosity response and mildness balance. Textile processing operations use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils and sizing agents from fabric.

It is one of the most established actives in this segment. Dietary supplements and functional foods use it as a zinc source with favorable absorption characteristics compared to inorganic zinc salts.

In pharmaceutical tablet and capsule formulations, it serves as a mineral supplement active where controlled zinc delivery is required. Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it into deodorants.

It is also used in skin preparations for its antimicrobial and astringent properties. The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder, typically in anhydrous or trihydrate form for various uses.

The trihydrate is the more common commercial grade. Standard grades include food-grade and USP / BP -compliant specifications to meet pharmaceutical and nutraceutical requirements for global markets.

name: Titanium isopropoxide
description:
Titanium isopropoxide (CAS 546-68-9 ), commonly abbreviated as TTIP and also known as tetraisopropyl orthotitanate, is a reactive organotitanium compound used as a catalyst precursor.

It functions as a sol-gel processing agent across specialty chemical manufacturing. It enables controlled deposition of titanium dioxide coatings and serves as a crosslinking agent in polymer systems.

In sol-gel and thin-film processes, TTIP is hydrolyzed to deposit TiO₂ layers on glass, metal, and plastic substrates for photocatalytic, anti-reflective, or barrier coating applications.

Polymer manufacturers use it as a crosslinker for polyesters and alkyd resins, improving adhesion and film integrity in coatings and adhesives for industrial use.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it functions as a surface-modification agent for treating pigment particles, particularly titanium dioxide used in sunscreens and color cosmetics.

Pharmaceutical and biotech applications include its use as a catalyst in stereoselective synthesis, notably in asymmetric epoxidation reactions for high-purity chemical production.

TTIP is supplied as a moisture-sensitive liquid, typically at 97% or higher purity. Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available for industrial procurement.

Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums under inert atmosphere. Handling and storage requirements under dry, inert conditions are standard for this material.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering component in drug synthesis and as a lithium source in active pharmaceutical ingredient manufacturing. In personal care formulations, it contributes to pH stabilization in products where conventional buffers may interfere.

Industrial catalysis processes also employ LiOAc as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in organic synthesis reactions, including esterification. Lithium acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, available in both anhydrous and dihydrate forms.

Buyers should confirm the hydration state, as it affects lithium content and formulation calculations. Standard grades include reagent-grade and ACS -grade for laboratory and life science procurement, with technical-grade material available for industrial applications.

name: Magnesium carbonate
description:
Magnesium carbonate (CAS 546-93-0 ), also known commercially as Magnesite and designated E504 in food applications, is an inorganic mineral salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an acidity regulator, anti-caking agent, and processing aid, keeping bulk powders free-flowing and stabilizing pH in formulated products. In food manufacturing, it prevents clumping in powdered products.

This includes table salt, flour, and dry mixes, maintaining consistent flowability through packaging and processing lines. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet excipient and antacid active ingredient.

Its buffering capacity supports both formulation stability and gastric pH regulation. In personal care, it acts as a bulking and absorbency agent in dry cosmetic formulations including pressed powders and dry shampoos.

It is also utilized in talc-free body powders. Plastics processors incorporate it as a filler and acid scavenger during polymer compounding, neutralizing residual catalyst acids that would otherwise degrade the material.

Magnesium carbonate is supplied as a white powder in both light and heavy bulk density grades, with particle size selected to match specific processing requirements. Recognized grades include FCC and USP .

In personal care formulations, it acts as a mild surfactant and co-emulsifier in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers where reduced irritation is a priority for the consumer.

Home care and industrial cleaning products use it to boost degreasing performance and improve soil dispersion on hard surfaces. Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a wetting agent.

Ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate ( CAS 5466-77-3 ), commonly abbreviated as OMC, is a UV-B absorbing ester used as the active sunscreen ingredient in cosmetic and personal care formulations.

It absorbs ultraviolet radiation in the 280–320 nm range, protecting both the skin and the stability of light-sensitive formulations. OMC is the primary UV filter in sunscreen lotions and SPF-rated moisturizers.

In daily-wear foundations, it delivers broad UV-B protection at concentrations typically between 2–10%. In hair care, it is incorporated into leave-on conditioners and styling products to prevent UV-induced color fade.

It also prevents protein degradation in hair fibers. Lip care products, including SPF lip balms and glosses, rely on OMC for photostability in thin-film applications across various cosmetic lines.

Pharmaceutical topical preparations also use it to protect active ingredients from photodegradation during shelf life. This ensures the efficacy of the medication remains intact throughout its storage period.

The product is supplied as a clear, pale yellow oily liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, which is the standard for personal care applications and industrial manufacturing.

name: Citrulline malate
description:

In sports nutrition, this compound is a primary active ingredient in pre-workout powders, capsules, and energy drinks targeting endurance and muscle recovery for professional athletes and hobbyists.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it in oral solutions and tablets for fatigue-related indications, particularly in markets where Stimol has established clinical recognition and widespread consumer trust.

Food and nutraceutical formulators incorporate it into functional beverages and chewable formats where mild acidulant properties contribute to flavor balance alongside its active metabolic function.

It also appears in amino acid blends and recovery formulas where malic acid's role as a metabolic intermediate adds formulation rationale for specific label claims and nutritional profiles.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in standard 2:1 ratio, the form most commonly specified by buyers. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available for order.

name: Ethylene dodecanedioate
description:
Ethylene dodecanedioate (CAS 54982-83-1 ), also known commercially as Zenolide and by the ring descriptor 1,4-dioxacyclohexadecane-5,16-dione, is a macrocyclic musk compound used as a fragrance ingredient.

It delivers a clean, musky scent profile that positions it as a synthetic alternative to animal-derived musks in finished fragrance formulations. In fine fragrance and personal care, it functions as a base-note musk.

This compound contributes depth and longevity to eau de parfum, body lotions, and skin care products. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into leave-on and rinse-off products where substantivity on skin or hair is required.

Beyond personal care, it is evaluated for use in scented coatings, adhesives, and packaging applications. These uses are ideal where controlled fragrance release is part of the technical product specification.

Ethylene dodecanedioate is typically supplied as a solid, either crystalline powder or flakes. This physical form is suited for weighing and blending into fragrance concentrates or direct formulation processes.

It is available at fragrance-grade purity, with documentation aligned to IFRA compliance requirements that procurement teams routinely request. Bulk and smaller lot sizes are generally offered to serve industrial compounders.

The material meets high industry benchmarks for stability and performance in diverse chemical environments. Specialty fragrance houses utilize this musk for its reliable olfactory profile and consistent quality standards.

name: p-Methylaminophenol sulfate
description:
p-Methylaminophenol sulfate (CAS 55-55-0 ), commercially known as Metol, is a photographic developing agent and reducing compound used across imaging and specialty chemical applications.

It functions as a primary electron donor in developer formulations, enabling controlled silver halide reduction in photographic and radiographic processing. In photographic and X-ray film processing, Metol is a core component of developer baths.

It is typically combined with hydroquinone to produce fine-grain, high-acutance image development. Printing plate and graphic arts workflows use Metol-based developers where precise tonal gradation and developer activity control are critical.

In hair dye formulations, it acts as a coupler or oxidation base, contributing to color development in permanent colorant systems. Specialty industrial imaging processes, including document archiving, also rely on Metol.

Micrographic film development utilizes this compound for its consistent reducing performance across a range of pH and temperature conditions. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

Technical and photographic grades are the most commonly traded forms, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+. Packaging is available in kilogram-scale bags through to bulk quantities.

These bulk quantities are suited for industrial developer concentrate manufacturing. The compound remains a standard in the chemical industry for high-precision imaging and specialized oxidation reactions.

name: Chlorhexidine
description:
Chlorhexidine (CAS 55-56-1 ), commonly abbreviated as CHX, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and healthcare manufacturing. It disrupts microbial cell membranes at low concentrations.

This characteristic makes it a go-to active ingredient for preservation and surface disinfection in regulated formulations. In pharmaceutical and healthcare products, CHX is the active ingredient in surgical scrubs and wound irrigation solutions.

It is also utilized in catheter care protocols where sustained antimicrobial activity is required. Oral care manufacturers incorporate it into prescription-grade mouthwashes and gels targeting periodontal bacteria.

In these applications, it remains the clinical benchmark for plaque control. Personal care formulators use it as a preservative and antimicrobial booster in skin cleansers, hand sanitizers, and topical preparations.

Water treatment and industrial hygiene applications rely on CHX-based formulations for equipment sanitation. These solutions are essential for surface disinfection in controlled environments and industrial settings.

Chlorhexidine is supplied in several salt forms, most commonly as chlorhexidine digluconate, chlorhexidine diacetate, and chlorhexidine dihydrochloride. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP specifications.

The material is also available according to BP and Ph. Eur. standards, with digluconate solutions typically offered at 20% concentration. Technical-grade supply is also available for industrial and veterinary applications.

name: D-psicose
description:
D-Psicose , also known commercially as Allulose, is a rare low-calorie monosaccharide approved as a sweetener in food and beverage applications. It delivers approximately 70% of the sweetness of sucrose while contributing negligible metabolizable calories.

This makes it a sought-after sucrose replacement in reduced-calorie and functional food formulations. The chemical is identified by CAS 551-68-8 and is utilized globally for its unique metabolic profile and functional properties.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to replace sucrose in products such as soft drinks, yogurts, baked goods, and confectionery where caloric reduction is a labeling priority. It participates in Maillard browning reactions effectively.

This allows bakers and confectioners to achieve comparable color and texture development without the caloric load of conventional sugar. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators incorporate it as an excipient in dietary supplements.

These supplements often target blood glucose management and metabolic health. Biotechnology researchers also use it as a substrate in enzymatic synthesis studies and rare sugar production process development for industrial scaling.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in aqueous solution form. Food-grade is the primary commercial grade, with supply conforming to purity specifications typically above 98% on a dry basis for manufacturing.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial food processing, with smaller research-grade quantities accessible for laboratory use. Quality standards ensure compliance with FCC and other international food safety regulations for global distribution.

name: 2-nitrobenzoic acid
description:
2-Nitrobenzoic acid (CAS 552-16-9 ), also known as o-nitrobenzoic acid, is an aromatic nitro compound used as a key building block in the synthesis of pharmaceutical intermediates and specialty chemicals.

Its reactive carboxyl and nitro groups make it a practical starting material for multi-step organic synthesis across several industrial sectors. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a precursor.

It is used in the production of anthranilic acid derivatives, dyes, and active pharmaceutical ingredients requiring ortho-substituted benzoic acid frameworks. Pigment and colorant producers use it as an intermediate.

This chemical is essential in synthesizing azo dyes and other chromophoric structures for textile and industrial coating applications. In personal care formulations, it contributes to preservation systems.

It is also utilized for pH buffering where aromatic acid chemistry is required. Specialty chemical manufacturers apply it in surface modification agents and wetting formulations where controlled acidity is needed.

The aromatic character of this compound influences substrate interaction significantly. 2-Nitrobenzoic acid is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with pharmaceutical-grade material available for regulated synthesis applications. Bulk quantities are typically offered in fiber drums or multi-layer bags.

Smaller packaging is available for laboratory and pilot-scale procurement. This ensures flexibility for both large-scale manufacturing and specialized research and development projects within the industry.

name: Trimellitic anhydride
description:
Trimellitic anhydride (CAS 552-30-7 ), commonly abbreviated as TMA, is a reactive aromatic anhydride used as a monomer and curing agent across polymer and coating systems. It introduces carboxylic acid functionality into resin backbones, enabling cross-linking, chain extension, and surface-reactive formulations.

In high-performance coatings, TMA is reacted with polyols or amines to produce polyimide and polyester resins that withstand elevated temperatures and chemical exposure. These specialized resins are essential for industrial applications requiring durability.

The plastics industry uses it to manufacture plasticizers, particularly trimellitate esters, for flexible PVC in wire and cable insulation. These materials require low volatility at high operating temperatures to ensure safety and longevity.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate TMA as a cross-linking monomer to improve heat resistance and adhesion to metal substrates. This chemical property makes it a vital component in demanding structural bonding applications.

In pigment and dye manufacturing, it acts as an intermediate in the synthesis of reactive dyes and color developers. Its unique structure allows for the creation of stable and vibrant colorants used in various industrial sectors.

Trimellitic anhydride is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder or flake. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically at 98–99%+ by GC, ensuring consistent performance in chemical synthesis.

Packaging ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk supersacks to meet diverse logistical needs. Storage requirements for moisture-sensitive handling are strictly communicated in product documentation to maintain material integrity.

It delivers effective emulsification, detergency, and foam-generating performance across a range of industrial and personal care formulations. In home care and industrial cleaning products, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant.

It is used in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and heavy-duty detergent concentrates where soil removal and emulsification of oils are required. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and cleansing systems.

In these systems, controlled foaming and emulsification of conditioning agents are process priorities. Textile processing operations use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils, waxes, and sizing agents.

This occurs from fiber substrates prior to dyeing or finishing. In leather and paper processing, it supports uniform dispersion of treatment chemicals and improves substrate penetration during wet processing stages.

This product is typically supplied as an aqueous liquid solution. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with concentration and active content specifications confirmed against data sheets.

name: Dioctyldimethylammonium chloride
description:
Dioctyldimethylammonium chloride (CAS 5538-94-3 ), also known as DODAC or Dioctyldimonium chloride, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a cationic surfactant and biocide across personal care, industrial cleaning, and water treatment sectors.

Its cationic charge drives adsorption onto negatively charged surfaces, enabling effective antimicrobial action and surface conditioning in a single active ingredient. In water treatment, DODAC functions as a biocidal agent controlling microbial growth.

It is widely utilized in cooling towers, industrial process water, and swimming pool systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair conditioners and rinse-off treatments, where it deposits on hair fiber to reduce static.

This chemical helps to improve combability in hair care applications. Textile and leather processors apply it as a softening and antistatic agent during finishing operations, improving handle and reducing friction in finished goods.

In industrial and institutional cleaning formulations, it contributes both surfactant and disinfectant activity. This reduces the need for separate actives in hard-surface sanitizers and specialized cleaning solutions for commercial use.

Dioctyldimethylammonium chloride is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active concentrations typically ranging from 50% to 80%. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial forms for most global buyers.

It is commonly available under trade designations including Querton 28CL and Dodigen 2617, which buyers may encounter as distinct product references from different manufacturers. The material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols.

name: Lithium carbonate
description:
Lithium carbonate (CAS 554-13-2 ), also referred to commercially as Li2CO3, is an inorganic lithium salt used across battery manufacturing, ceramics, and pharmaceutical production. It functions primarily as a lithium source, flux agent, and pH buffer depending on the processing environment.

In lithium-ion battery manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for cathode active materials such as lithium iron phosphate and lithium cobalt oxide. This makes it a critical input for EV and energy storage supply chains globally.

Ceramic and glass producers use it to lower melting temperatures and improve thermal stability in specialty frits, glazes, and glass-ceramics. These properties are essential for high-performance industrial glass applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active substance in mood-stabilizing formulations for bipolar disorder treatment. The material is processed under strict pharmacopeial controls to ensure patient safety and efficacy.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it into lithium-based greases, where it reacts with fatty acids to form the thickener structure. This structure determines grease performance across various industrial temperature ranges.

Lithium carbonate is supplied as a white powder in technical, battery, and pharmaceutical grades. Battery-grade material is produced to tight purity specifications, typically exceeding 99.5 percent purity levels.

The production process includes controlled limits on sodium, calcium, and sulfate impurities to ensure stability. Pharmaceutical-grade supply conforms to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. monographs for global compliance.

name: Triethylamine hydrochloride
description:
Triethylamine hydrochloride (CAS 554-68-7 ), also known as triethylammonium chloride and commonly abbreviated as TEA·HCl, is the stable salt form of triethylamine produced by neutralization with hydrochloric acid.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, reaction intermediate, and auxiliary agent across pharmaceutical synthesis, textile processing, and specialty chemical manufacturing for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TEA·HCl acts as a buffering agent and counterion source in API synthesis, where controlled pH and stable amine delivery are critical to reaction yield and purity.

Textile and leather processors use it as an auxiliary in dyebath formulations, improving dye uptake and fixation on fiber substrates. In paper treatment, it supports surface chemistry modifications.

This occurs where controlled charge interaction between fiber and coating agents is required. It also serves as a synthetic intermediate in the preparation of quaternary ammonium compounds.

These compounds and other specialty amines are used in preservation and biocide formulations. Triethylamine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid for easy handling.

name: Aluminum benzoate
description:
Aluminum benzoate ( CAS 555-32-8 ), also known as aluminium tribenzoate, is an organometallic compound used industrially as a rheology modifier and cross-linking agent.

It functions by coordinating with polymer chains and binder systems to control flow behavior and build structural integrity in coatings and specialty formulations.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it acts as a gelling agent to adjust viscosity and prevent pigment settling during production and storage. This ensures consistent application.

Plastics and polymer compounders use it as a cross-linking promoter to improve dimensional stability and mechanical performance in finished parts. It is essential for high-performance materials.

In textile and leather finishing, it contributes to binder cross-linking, helping fix coatings and treatments that must withstand mechanical stress and washing over time.

Paper treatment processes also employ it where controlled rheology in coating slurries is critical to uniform surface coverage. This allows for high-quality finishes in paper production.

Aluminum benzoate is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available primarily in technical grade, suited for industrial coating, ink, and polymer processing applications.

Packaging options generally range from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial quantities depending on supplier. This flexibility supports both research and large-scale manufacturing.
