name: Glyceryl Tristearate
description:
Glyceryl Tristearate (CAS 555-43-1 ), also known as Tristearin, is a fully saturated triglyceride derived from glycerol and stearic acid. It functions as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and lubricant across food, pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial applications.

Its high melting point and solid waxy form make it a preferred structuring and release-control agent in solid-format products. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a matrix-forming excipient in sustained-release tablets.

It is utilized in lipid-based drug delivery systems, controlling active ingredient release rates. Confectionery and food producers use it as a bloom inhibitor and texture modifier in chocolate and fat-based coatings, improving shelf stability.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into stick formats such as lip balms, deodorants, and solid lotions. In these applications, it provides structural rigidity and a smooth skin feel for the end consumer.

In industrial lubricants and metalworking compounds, it serves as a base component or additive. It is particularly useful where a solid, high-melting fat with low reactivity is required for specific manufacturing processes.

Glyceryl Tristearate is supplied as a white to off-white powder, flakes, or waxy solid. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with pharmaceutical supply conforming to USP and Ph.Eur. specifications.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial lubricant and coating applications. This ensures that the product meets the diverse requirements of various global manufacturing sectors and quality protocols.

name: Tripalmitin
description:
Tripalmitin (CAS 555-44-2 ), also referred to as palmitic triglyceride, is a saturated triglyceride composed entirely of palmitic acid chains. It functions as a structuring agent, emollient base, and lipid excipient across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing applications.

In cosmetics and skincare, tripalmitin is used to build solid or semi-solid textures in balms, sticks, and cream formulations. It provides a smooth skin feel without relying on synthetic waxes, making it a versatile choice for natural product lines.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it as a lipid matrix component in solid lipid nanoparticles and controlled-release dosage forms. Its defined melting behavior supports consistent drug encapsulation and delivery in various therapeutic applications.

In food processing, it functions as a structuring fat in confectionery coatings and specialty fat blends. This is particularly useful where a high palmitic acid profile is required for precise tempering and texture control in finished goods.

It also serves as a reference standard and model compound in lipid research and quality testing of fat-based raw materials. This allows laboratories to maintain high accuracy when analyzing complex lipid profiles in industrial settings.

Tripalmitin is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake solid. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available, with the latter typically conforming to USP or Ph.Eur. standards for global compliance.

High-purity research grades are also offered for analytical and formulation development use. These materials ensure that manufacturers meet the rigorous demands of modern chemical processing and high-end product development cycles.

name: Trimyristin
description:
Trimyristin (CAS 555-45-3 ) is a naturally occurring triglyceride derived primarily from nutmeg kernel fat, where it constitutes the dominant lipid fraction. In industry, it functions as a structuring agent, carrier lipid, and emollient base.

This versatile compound is utilized across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food manufacturing applications. In pharmaceutical solid dosage development, it is used as a lipid matrix former in sustained-release suppositories.

The material is essential for lipid-based drug delivery systems, where its defined melting behavior supports controlled API release. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it as an occlusive emollient and texturizer in stick formats.

It is frequently found in body butters and skin conditioning bases to improve texture. In food manufacturing, it serves as a cocoa butter analog and structuring fat in confectionery coatings where precise melting is required.

The product is also used as a carrier matrix in lipid nanoparticle systems for encapsulation. This applies to active ingredients in both nutraceutical and topical formulations requiring high stability and bioavailability.

Trimyristin is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flakes at room temperature. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications to meet various industrial requirements.

name: Disodium guanylate
description:
Disodium guanylate (CAS 5550-12-9 ), also known as E627 and GMP-Na2, is a nucleotide-based flavor enhancer derived from guanosine 5'-monophosphate. It amplifies savory, umami taste perception at low use levels.

This ingredient functions synergistically with glutamates to boost overall flavor intensity in processed food formulations. In the food industry, it is combined with disodium inosinate and monosodium glutamate.

These blended flavor enhancer systems are used in soups, snacks, instant noodles, sauces, and seasoning mixes. It allows formulators to reduce total glutamate content while maintaining perceived flavor strength.

This reduction is a key cost and label consideration for manufacturers. In savory snack coatings and dry seasoning blends, small concentrations deliver significant taste-boosting effects for the user.

These effects improve product palatability without masking other flavor notes. Personal care formulators have also explored nucleotide ingredients for skin-conditioning applications in various cosmetic products.

However, food flavoring remains the primary commercial demand driver for this chemical. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder, typically in food-grade quality meeting FCC purity specifications.

The material is available in standard packaging formats suited to industrial food production, including bulk bags. Smaller quantities are also available for R&D use and laboratory testing purposes.

Blended nucleotide products combining GMP-Na2 with IMP are also commercially available for direct use. These blends are specifically designed for immediate application in seasoning and snack formulations.

name: Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium sulfate
description:
Tetrakis(hydroxymethyl)phosphonium sulfate (CAS 55566-30-8 ), commonly known as THPS, is a water-soluble organophosphorus biocide and flame retardant used across industrial and specialty chemical markets.

Supplied under trade names such as Retardol S and Pyroset TKO, it delivers broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity alongside durable flame retardancy in treated substrates for various sectors.

In water treatment, THPS controls sulfate-reducing bacteria and biofilm formation in oilfield injection systems, cooling towers, and industrial process water systems to maintain operational efficiency.

Textile and nonwoven manufacturers apply it as a durable flame retardant finish for cotton and cellulosic fabrics, where it bonds to fiber during curing to meet fire performance standards.

In leather processing, it functions as a biocide during hide preservation and wet-end operations to prevent microbial degradation. This ensures the quality and longevity of the leather materials.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it at low concentrations as a preservative active against a broad range of bacteria and fungi, ensuring product safety and shelf stability.

THPS is commercially available as an aqueous solution, typically at 75% active content. It is supplied in technical grade for industrial water treatment and textile applications.

Select grades meet specifications for cosmetic preservation use. Packaging options generally include drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) to suit varying procurement volumes and logistics.

This agent is effective on cotton, viscose, and blended fabrics without altering the base color. Paper manufacturers incorporate it into pulp slurries or surface sizing to meet brightness specifications required for printing and packaging grades.

name: Zinc cyanide
description:
Zinc cyanide (CAS 557-21-1 ) is an inorganic salt used primarily as a source of both zinc and cyanide ions in controlled industrial processes. It functions as a plating reagent and synthesis intermediate across electrochemical and chemical manufacturing operations.

In electroplating, this compound is a key bath constituent for depositing uniform, corrosion-resistant zinc coatings on steel and iron components. This is particularly useful where alkaline cyanide bath chemistry is specified for complex geometries.

The mining and metals sector uses it in hydrometallurgical processing, where controlled cyanide chemistry is required for metal recovery and refining operations. It ensures precision in the extraction and purification of various metallic elements.

In polymer and plastics manufacturing, it serves as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in select polymerization reactions. This includes the production of certain polyols used in polyurethane systems for industrial applications.

Specialty chemical synthesis also draws on this material as a reagent for introducing nitrile functionality into organic intermediates. Its reactivity makes it a valuable tool for complex molecular construction in laboratory settings.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications typically ranging from 96% to 99%+ to meet rigorous industrial requirements.

Packaging is available in drums and bulk quantities, with handling requirements reflecting its classification as a highly toxic material. Strict safety protocols must be followed during transport and storage of this chemical.

name: Zinc acetate

It functions as a preservative, pH buffer, and catalyst precursor depending on the application context. In food and nutraceutical products, it serves as a zinc fortification agent and approved preservative.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an active ingredient in throat lozenges and oral zinc supplements targeting zinc deficiency. In polymer and plastics manufacturing, it acts as a catalyst or catalyst precursor.

It is used in the production of polyesters and polylactic acid resins. Personal care formulators incorporate it into oral care products and topical preparations where antimicrobial activity and astringency are required.

Zinc acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, typically as the dihydrate form. Standard grades include USP , BP , and food-grade specifications for regulated applications.

These standards ensure high purity for sensitive industries, alongside technical grade for industrial use. Packaging ranges from small quantities for pharmaceutical compounding to bulk bags for manufacturing volumes.

In coatings and adhesives, it acts as a curing and cross-linking agent, contributing to polymer network formation and improving film durability. Textile and leather processors use it as a preservation agent.

It serves as a biocide agent, helping protect treated materials during processing and in finished goods. Plastics and polymer formulators incorporate it as a stabilizer to extend material service life.

This chemical helps materials withstand thermal or oxidative stress. It also functions as a flame retardancy additive in polymer systems where nitrogen-based compounds are specified for halogen-free formulations.

Ethylamine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications, with material typically assayed at 98% or higher.

name: Acrylic acid-hydroxypropyl acrylate copolymer
description:
Acrylic acid-hydroxypropyl acrylate copolymer (CAS 55719-33-0 ), also referenced commercially as AA/HPA, is a water-soluble anionic polymer used across industrial water management and process chemistry.

It functions as a scale inhibitor, dispersant, and corrosion control agent in systems handling hard water, mineral slurries, and process fluids. In oilfield and industrial water treatment, it inhibits calcium carbonate.

It also prevents calcium sulfate and other mineral scale deposits in cooling towers, boilers, and injection water systems. Textile and paper processing operations use it to disperse pigments and control rheology.

These applications in coating formulations improve uniformity and reduce equipment fouling. Mining and mineral processing applications rely on it as a flocculant aid to accelerate solid-liquid separation.

This is particularly effective in tailings and ore slurry circuits. It also functions as a threshold inhibitor in low-dose antiscalant programs where conventional precipitation-based treatments are impractical.

Acrylic acid-hydroxypropyl acrylate copolymer is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 40–50% active content. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

The product is formulated to meet industrial water treatment and process chemistry specifications. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes and bulk tanker supply depending on volume requirements.

name: Glyceryl stearate citrate
description:
Glyceryl stearate citrate (CAS 55840-13-6 ), also known as stearyl monoglyceridyl citrate or monostearin citrate, is a citric acid ester of glyceryl monostearate used as an emulsifier and stabilizer across food and personal care manufacturing.

It combines the lipophilic character of stearic acid with the hydrophilic contribution of citrate, enabling stable oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems without synthetic co-emulsifiers.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier and mild acidulant in fat-based systems such as margarines, shortenings, and processed dairy products, improving texture consistency and shelf stability.

Bakery formulators use it to condition dough and extend crumb softness in breads and cakes by moderating fat crystal interactions. In personal care, it acts as an emulsifying agent in creams and lotions.

This ingredient supports uniform dispersion of oils and actives across a range of skin-feel profiles. It also appears in flavor delivery systems where its amphiphilic structure helps encapsulate and stabilize lipophilic flavor compounds.

Glyceryl stearate citrate is typically supplied as a waxy solid, flake, or powder depending on the manufacturer's processing method. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially available.

Purity and acid value parameters vary by supplier. Buyers should confirm grade suitability against relevant regional food additive regulations before procurement to ensure compliance with industry standards.

Its dual halogen substitution makes it a selective alkylating agent for synthesis and analytical workflows. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a building block for active pharmaceutical ingredient development.

Controlled halogen reactivity enables targeted bond formation in multi-step processes. Water treatment research uses it as a reference standard for monitoring disinfection byproducts formed during chlorination.

This monitoring is essential for drinking water supplies. In biotechnology and life sciences, it is employed in protein modification studies and enzyme inhibition assays requiring precise alkylating agents.

Formulation chemists and analytical labs also use it to prepare calibration standards for regulatory compliance testing. This includes testing under EPA and WHO drinking water guidelines for safety.

In plastics, it withstands the high processing temperatures of engineering polymers such as polyamide and polypropylene, maintaining hue integrity where lower-grade yellows fail.

Coatings formulators use it in industrial and automotive finishes where exterior durability and resistance to UV degradation are critical to long-term product performance.

In printing inks, particularly high-end packaging and specialty gravure applications, it delivers sharp, reproducible yellow tones with strong substrate adhesion and clarity.

Rubber and elastomer compounders select it for coloring profiles, seals, and technical parts that undergo prolonged outdoor or thermal exposure during their service life.

description:

In hair care, it is incorporated into leave-on scalp serums, anti-hair loss treatments, and trichological formulations where oxidative damage to the follicle environment is a primary concern. Cosmetic formulators use it alongside other actives in premium scalp care lines.

These formulations often target thinning hair and age-related follicle decline. In pharmaceutical-adjacent topical preparations, it is evaluated for its capacity to support scalp health through antioxidant stabilization mechanisms during the application process.

Its compatibility with aqueous and emulsion-based systems makes it a practical choice for rinse-off and leave-on formats alike. This versatility allows manufacturers to integrate the compound into a wide variety of existing product bases without stability issues.

It is used particularly in the manufacture of polyesters and alkyd resins. Coating formulators use it as a crosslinking agent for silicone and organic coatings, improving adhesion and cure performance on metal and glass substrates.

In sol-gel chemistry, it serves as a titanium dioxide precursor for producing thin films, ceramics, and functional coatings with controlled optical or barrier properties. This makes it essential for high-performance materials.

This chemical improves film leveling and reduces surface defects in waterborne systems. Printing ink formulators use it to control viscosity and drying profiles in packaging inks, particularly where extended open time is required.

Formulators of plating electrolytes incorporate it to control grain structure and surface smoothness in printed circuit board manufacturing. This ensures high-quality finishes for sensitive components.

In polymer chemistry, the reactive alkyne group supports its use as a building block for sulfonate-functionalized polymers and surface-modification coatings for various industrial applications.

Mining and metals processors may also evaluate it as a functional additive where controlled surface interaction during metal recovery or treatment is required for efficient processing.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional fragrance compositions where warm, floral-spicy base notes are required. Its versatility allows for seamless integration into complex aromatic profiles.

Frozen and retort food producers rely on it to maintain gel structure and prevent syneresis through repeated freeze-thaw cycles. This ensures product quality over long periods.

Bakery and dairy formulators incorporate it to improve mouthfeel and extend shelf life in products such as yogurts, puddings, and cream fillings for better consumer appeal.

Methylchloroisothiazolinone/methylisothiazolinone (CAS 55965-84-9 ), commonly identified as CMIT/MIT, is a broad-spectrum biocide active against bacteria, fungi, and algae across a wide range of industrial systems.

In water treatment and cooling tower systems, CMIT/MIT controls microbial growth that would otherwise cause biofouling, corrosion, and process inefficiency. This ensures long-term operational stability.

Oilfield and gas operations use it as an injection biocide to suppress sulfate-reducing bacteria in produced water and pipeline systems. This prevents the degradation of critical infrastructure.

Pulp and paper mills apply it to process water and slurries to prevent slime formation that disrupts production and contaminates finished product. It is essential for maintaining high output quality.

In rinse-off personal care formulations and industrial coatings, it functions as an in-can and in-process preservative. This protects the integrity of the product against spoilage during storage.

description:

Its three reactive amine groups make it a functional starting material for constructing more complex molecular architectures in drug development and bioconjugation workflows.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, this compound serves as an intermediate for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients and drug candidates requiring polyamine scaffolds.

Biotech and life science researchers use it in linker chemistry and conjugation platforms, where controlled amine reactivity is critical to payload attachment or crosslinking efficiency.

It also finds use in the preparation of chelating agents and polyamine derivatives applied in diagnostic and therapeutic research contexts for various medical applications.

Specialty chemical manufacturers utilize it as a precursor for curing agents, epoxy hardeners, and nitrogen-rich polymer additives in adjacent industrial applications.

The material is available as a liquid at standard commercial purities, with high-purity grades supplied for pharmaceutical and research applications for global clients.

name: Tributyltin oxide
description:
Tributyltin oxide (CAS 56-35-9 ), commercially known as TBTO or Butinox, is an organotin biocide used across industrial preservation applications. It functions as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial agent.

This chemical is highly effective at controlling fungi, bacteria, and marine fouling organisms in demanding environments. In textile and leather processing, it is applied as an antifungal treatment.

The treatment helps to prevent mold and mildew degradation during storage and transit. Pulp and paper manufacturing uses it as a slimicide to inhibit microbial growth in process water and on finished materials.

In building and construction, it serves as a wood preservative, protecting structural timber and joinery against fungal decay and insect attack. This ensures the longevity of structural components.

Marine and industrial coatings have historically incorporated this compound as an antifouling agent. It is used to prevent biofouling on submerged surfaces and various types of industrial equipment.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically as a clear to pale yellow oily fluid. It is available in technical grade, with concentration specifications commonly expressed as percentage active ingredient.

Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers. Supply quantities are suited to industrial-scale formulation and treatment operations for global manufacturing requirements.

description:
Glycine (CAS 56-40-6 ), abbreviated Gly and designated E640 , is the simplest amino acid and a high-volume industrial ingredient. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, humectant, and flavor modifier across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this amino acid acts as a buffering agent in parenteral formulations and a stabilizer in lyophilized protein and vaccine products. Food producers use it as a flavor modifier and mild sweetness enhancer in seasonings and processed foods.

The ingredient is frequently utilized in beverages, where its regulatory designation supports EU-compliant labeling. In personal care formulations, it improves moisture retention in skin creams, serums, and hair care products, reducing the need for higher-cost humectants.

It also serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals, and chelating agents such as glyphosate and EDTA derivatives. This versatility makes it a staple for chemical synthesis and industrial manufacturing.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bulk bags, drums, and fiber containers. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph.Eur. , and FCC , covering both pharmaceutical and food-grade procurement requirements.

name: Adenosine triphosphate
description:
Adenosine triphosphate (CAS 56-65-5 ), commonly abbreviated as ATP, is a nucleotide used across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology applications as an active functional ingredient.

Known commercially as Striadyne and Triadenyl in pharmaceutical contexts, it supports cellular energy transfer processes that formulators leverage for skin conditioning and bioactive formulations.

In cosmetic formulations, ATP is incorporated into anti-aging and moisturizing products where it supports skin hydration and cellular renewal at the ingredient level for high-end skincare.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it in injectable preparations and clinical formulations targeting cardiovascular and metabolic indications, ensuring high efficacy and safety in medical applications.

Biotechnology and life sciences applications rely on ATP as a substrate and reagent in enzymatic assays, cell culture media, and diagnostic test systems for precise laboratory results.

It also functions as a stabilizing co-factor in bioluminescence-based detection kits and ATP-quantification assays used in microbial contamination testing across various industrial sectors.

ATP is supplied as a white to off-white lyophilized powder or crystalline solid, with disodium salt form being the most commercially prevalent for global distribution and manufacturing.

Grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications, as well as research and reagent grades for biotechnology use and industrial laboratory procurement.

name: PEG-3 isostearate
description:

In personal care formulations, it functions as an emulsifier and moisturizing co-emulsifier in creams, lotions, and conditioning products, helping stabilize oil phases while contributing to skin feel.

Textile processing operations use it as a fiber lubricant and wetting agent, improving dye penetration and reducing surface tension during finishing treatments to ensure consistent quality across batches.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a dispersant and surface modifier, aiding pigment wetting and substrate adhesion. Leather treatment formulations also incorporate it to improve fat liquoring distribution.

PEG-3 Isostearate is typically supplied as a liquid or semi-liquid at ambient temperature. Cosmetic-grade material meeting standard industry purity requirements is the most common commercial form available.

name: Sucralose
description:
Sucralose (CAS 56038-13-2 ), also marketed under the brand name Splenda and listed as E955 in the EU, is a high-intensity chlorinated sugar derivative used as a non-caloric sweetener in food, beverage, and personal care applications.

It delivers approximately 600 times the sweetness of sucrose with no caloric contribution, making it a preferred choice for sugar-reduced and diabetic-friendly product development in various industrial sectors.

In food and beverage manufacturing, this ingredient is used to replace sugar in low-calorie soft drinks, dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery where heat stability across processing temperatures is required.

Tabletop sweetener blends and single-serve sachets rely on this compound as the active sweetening agent, typically bulked with maltodextrin or dextrose to provide the necessary volume for consumer use.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use it to mask bitterness in oral syrups, chewable tablets, and dietary supplements. In personal care, it functions as a flavoring and mild humectant in toothpastes and mouthwashes.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Standard grades conform to FCC , USP , and Ph. Eur. monographs, with purity typically at 98% or above.

Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric ton quantities, with packaging ranging from foil-lined bags to fiber drums. We ensure all shipments meet rigorous quality control standards for global distribution.

In cosmetic and skincare formulations, it retains moisture in the skin barrier and improves the spreadability of emulsions, serums, and cleansing products. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier and humectant in baked goods.

It is frequently utilized in confectionery coatings and fat-based fillings where moisture retention and texture stability are priorities. In coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a reactive diluent or plasticizing carrier.

This material improves flow and substrate compatibility in water-based formulations. Its low viscosity and hygroscopic character also make it a preferred co-solvent in sealant and elastomer systems requiring controlled flexibility.

Polyglycerin-3 is supplied as a clear, viscous liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent for global distribution and manufacturing needs.

name: Selenium sulfide
description:

This material is a recognized active ingredient in regulated topical products. In medicated shampoos and scalp treatments, it functions as the active ingredient at concentrations typically ranging from 1% to 2.5%.

Higher concentrations are reserved for prescription-grade products. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into topical lotions and creams formulated for dermatological conditions requiring antifungal efficacy.

In agricultural contexts, it has been evaluated as a biocidal agent in crop protection and pest management applications. Specialty formulators also reference it in antimicrobial preservation systems.

Fungal control is a primary formulation requirement for these systems. Selenium sulfide is supplied as a fine powder in both pharmaceutical and technical grades to meet diverse industry needs.

USP and BP grades are available to support regulated drug product manufacturing. These grades come with documentation packages suitable for regulatory submissions and quality assurance.

Technical-grade material serves non-pharmaceutical industrial applications where compendial specifications are not required. This ensures flexibility for manufacturers across different sectors and use cases.

name: Heptaethylene glycol
description:
Heptaethylene glycol (CAS 5617-32-3 ) is a mid-chain polyethylene glycol diol used as a solvent, humectant, and functional intermediate across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

Its defined chain length and dual hydroxyl end groups make it a precise building block where molecular uniformity matters for performance or regulatory purposes in various chemical processes.

In pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations, it functions as a carrier and humectant, helping to solubilize active ingredients and retain moisture in topical products for better skin absorption.

Printing ink and packaging manufacturers use it as a plasticizer and dispersing aid to improve film flexibility and pigment compatibility across different substrate types and printing methods.

Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a softening agent and processing solvent to modify substrate feel and improve dye uptake during the manufacturing stages.

Lubricant and metalworking formulators apply it as a base component or additive where water-soluble, low-volatility glycol chemistry is required for high-performance industrial applications.

Heptaethylene glycol is supplied as a clear viscous liquid. It is available primarily at high-purity grades suited to pharmaceutical research, specialty chemical synthesis, and performance formulation.

Packaging typically ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to drum volumes, reflecting its positioning as a specialty intermediate rather than a commodity glycol for large scale use.

name: Dimorpholinomethane
description:
Dimorpholinomethane (CAS 5625-90-1 ), also known as 4,4-Methylenedimorpholine, is a morpholine-derived amine used industrially as a biocide and corrosion inhibitor. It functions by releasing formaldehyde slowly under use conditions.

This mechanism provides controlled antimicrobial and metal-protection activity across various aqueous systems. In metalworking fluids, it acts as a formaldehyde-releaser biocide to control bacterial and fungal growth.

It is commonly used in water-miscible cutting and grinding fluids to extend fluid service life. Water treatment formulations incorporate it to suppress microbial fouling in recirculating cooling systems and process water.

Coatings, adhesives, and sealant systems use it as a preservation agent to prevent microbial degradation during storage. This helps avoid in-can spoilage and maintains the integrity of the chemical formulations.

Textile processing and leather finishing operations also rely on it for antimicrobial protection. It is effective in aqueous process baths and for the long-term protection of finished industrial goods.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically at concentrations around 80% active content in aqueous solution. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial biocide requirements.

It is aligned with metalworking fluid formulation standards and industrial safety protocols. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers, reflecting its primary use in large-volume applications.

It improves dimensional stability and wet strength for cellulose-based substrates. Water treatment applications rely on its chelating capacity to sequester metal ions effectively.

Tridecethcarboxylic acid (CAS 56388-96-6 ), also known commercially as an ether carboxylate surfactant, is a nonionic-anionic hybrid surface-active agent derived from tridecyl alcohol ethoxylates.

It delivers effective emulsification, mild cleansing, and degreasing performance across a broad pH range. This makes it a preferred choice where compatibility with sensitive substrates or formulation stability is critical.

In personal care, it functions as a mild primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, facial cleansers, and body washes. It is ideal where low irritation potential is a primary formulation requirement for the manufacturer.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulators use it to build hard-surface cleaners and degreasers. These products must perform reliably in both alkaline and acidic conditions to ensure effective results.

Textile processing operations apply it as an emulsifier and wetting agent in scouring and dyeing auxiliaries. It is also utilized in fiber preparation baths to enhance the overall quality of the textile treatment.

In leather and paper processing, it supports uniform dispersion of treatment chemicals and improves substrate penetration. This ensures that the chemical additives are distributed evenly throughout the material.

Tridecethcarboxylic acid is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste, depending on the degree of ethoxylation. It is available in technical and industrial grades with varying EO chain lengths for specific needs.

Water treatment and aquaculture industries have historically used it as an antifungal and antiparasitic agent in process water. However, regulatory status varies significantly by region and specific application.

name: Cetrimonium bromide
description:
Cetrimonium bromide (CAS 57-09-0 ), commonly known as CTAB, is a quaternary ammonium surfactant used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial applications. It functions primarily as a cationic surfactant and conditioning agent.

This material acts as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial, making it a go-to ingredient where surface activity and biocidal performance are required together. In hair care formulations, CTAB conditions and detangles fibers.

By adsorbing onto negatively charged hair, it reduces static and improves combability. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a preservative and solubilizer in topical preparations to support product stability.

name: Urea
description:
Urea (CAS 57-13-6 ), also known as carbamide, is one of the most commercially significant nitrogen compounds in global trade, supplying high-concentration nitrogen to agricultural and industrial markets alike.

In agriculture, urea is the dominant solid nitrogen fertilizer, applied directly to soil or converted into liquid UAN solutions for crop nutrition programs. It remains a staple for global food production.

Cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a keratolytic humectant in topical creams, lotions, and medicated skin preparations where controlled moisture retention and skin-softening action are required.

Urea-formaldehyde resins, produced using urea as a primary feedstock, are the basis for adhesives, laminates, and particleboard binders in the wood panel industry. This makes it vital for construction.

In textiles and paper processing, it acts as a solubilizing and wetting agent during reactive dyeing and coating operations. This versatility ensures its use in diverse manufacturing environments.

Urea is supplied as white prilled or granular solid, with granular grades preferred for bulk agricultural handling and prills used in blended fertilizer applications. The physical form is optimized for use.

In personal care, its humectant behavior supports moisture retention in leave-on skin and hair products, including various creams, serums, and conditioners for consumer use.

The product ensures a smooth application without leaving a heavy or greasy residue. Formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and serums where both moisturizing performance and emulsification support are required.

It is particularly effective in polymer-based compounds where durability and flexibility are essential. The substance is supplied as a clear liquid suitable for direct incorporation into both aqueous and oil-phase systems.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care and industrial buyers respectively. Standard packaging includes drums and IBCs for various logistics needs.

name: Methyltin mercaptide
description:
Methyltin mercaptide (CAS 57583-35-4 ), also known commercially as dimethyltin carboxylate, is an organotin compound used primarily as a heat stabilizer and processing aid in PVC and related polymer systems.

It protects polymer chains from thermal degradation during high-temperature processing, enabling consistent output quality in demanding extrusion and molding operations for industrial manufacturers.

In rigid PVC processing, it functions as a thermal stabilizer that suppresses discoloration and chain scission during extrusion of pipes, profiles, and window frames where clarity is critical.

Transparent PVC packaging and sheeting benefit from its ability to maintain optical clarity under processing heat without introducing haze or color shift during the manufacturing cycle.

It also supports cross-linking and curing processes in specialty rubber and polymer compounding where controlled reactivity under heat is required for high-performance material applications.

Formulators working with tin-catalyzed polymerization systems use it as a catalyst precursor to initiate or regulate reaction kinetics in polyester and polyurethane production workflows.

Methyltin mercaptide is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial concentrations, typically blended or compounded for direct addition to polymer processing lines in various facilities.

It is available in technical grade, with supply quantities ranging from drum to bulk IBC formats suited to industrial-scale stabilizer formulations and large-scale chemical procurement needs.

name: Resorcinol bis(diphenyl phosphate)
description:
Resorcinol bis(diphenyl phosphate) (CAS 57583-54-7 ) is a halogen-free organophosphate flame retardant used across engineering plastics and polymer blends. It combines flame suppression with plasticizing action.

This makes it the retardant of choice for housings in consumer electronics, IT equipment, and office devices. Automotive interior components benefit from its low volatility and thermal stability.

These properties support compliance with vehicle flammability requirements. Aerospace and defense applications use RDP in structural polymer composites where halogen-free certification is a requirement.

It also functions as a reactive plasticizer in flexible polyurethane and epoxy systems. This improves flow during processing while contributing to the fire performance of the cured part.

Resorcinol bis(diphenyl phosphate) is supplied as a viscous liquid at ambient temperature. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form for most industrial applications.

Purity specifications for this chemical are typically at 97% or higher. Bulk liquid supply in drums and IBC containers is the norm for industrial procurement and large-scale manufacturing.

name: Oleth-3 carboxylic acid
description:
Oleth-3 carboxylic acid (CAS 57635-48-0 ), also marketed as PEG-3 oleyl ether carboxylic acid, is an ether carboxylate surfactant derived from oleyl alcohol and ethylene oxide. It combines anionic and nonionic character to deliver effective emulsification and wetting.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulators use it to boost wetting and soil removal in hard surface cleaners and degreasers. It is particularly effective in alkaline systems where ether carboxylates outperform conventional anionics.

Textile processors incorporate it as a wetting and scouring agent during fiber preparation and dyeing. Consistent surface penetration directly affects process yield and the overall quality of the finished textile products.

In leather processing, it supports fat-liquoring and finishing steps by stabilizing emulsions under varying pH conditions. This stability ensures uniform application and performance during the intensive manufacturing stages of leather goods.

Oleth-3 carboxylic acid is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste, depending on the specific grade and concentration required. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications meeting standard industry requirements for personal care.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial cleaning and textile end uses. These grades ensure that formulators have the appropriate chemical profile for diverse industrial applications and large-scale manufacturing processes.

name: Trimethylolpropane trioleate
description:
Trimethylolpropane trioleate (CAS 57675-44-2 ), also marketed as Nissan Unister H-381, is a synthetic ester derived from trimethylolpropane and oleic acid. It functions as a base fluid and lubricity additive in high-performance lubricant formulations.

This chemical offers strong oxidative stability and low-temperature fluidity that are critical for demanding industrial and automotive applications. In fully synthetic and semi-synthetic lubricants, it serves as a base oil component for compressor oils.

It is frequently utilized in gear oils and hydraulic fluids where extended service intervals are required. Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it to improve lubricity in cutting and forming operations, reducing tool wear in precision machining.

The product is also used as a plasticizer in specialty polymer and rubber compounding where compatibility with oleate-based systems is a formulation requirement. In the energy sector, it appears in turbine and circulating oil formulations.

These formulations are specifically designed to meet demanding thermal and oxidative stability specifications. Trimethylolpropane trioleate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid for various industrial uses.

It is available in technical and lubricant grades, with packaging typically ranging from drums to intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for industrial supply volumes. Specifications are generally aligned with technical-grade purity standards.

These standards are appropriate for lubricant and industrial fluid applications across the global manufacturing sector. The material ensures consistent performance in high-pressure environments and specialized chemical processing tasks.

name: Docusate sodium
description:
Docusate sodium (CAS 577-11-7 ), also known as DSS and approved as E480 in food applications, is an anionic surfactant used across pharmaceutical, food, and industrial sectors.

Its primary function is to lower surface and interfacial tension, enabling emulsification, wetting, and dispersing in formulations where conventional surfactants underperform in various environments.

In pharmaceuticals, DSS is the active ingredient in stool softener laxatives and is incorporated into tablet and capsule formulations as a wetting agent to improve drug dissolution rates.

Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier and dispersing aid in products such as gelled desserts, cocoa-based mixes, and sugar confectionery under its specific food additive designation.

In textile and paper processing, it acts as a penetrant and wetting agent, ensuring uniform dye uptake and consistent fiber saturation during the manufacturing and finishing stages.

Industrial cleaning and degreasing formulations rely on DSS for its ability to emulsify oils and reduce foam in process water systems, providing high efficiency in technical applications.

Docusate sodium is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at 70% active content in water or ethanol, and as a dry powder or granule form for solid dosage manufacturing.

Recognized grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical procurement, as well as food-grade material meeting specific safety standards for industrial and textile applications.

name: Acridone
description:

Its light-absorbing characteristics make it a valued intermediate in colorant chemistry and polymer stabilization systems. In plastics and polymer formulations, acridone derivatives function as UV absorbers and antioxidants.

These derivatives protect finished materials from photodegradation during outdoor or high-exposure use. The printing and packaging industry relies on acridone-based pigments for their strong color strength and lightfastness.

These pigments are used in inks applied to flexible packaging and commercial print substrates. Textile and paper dyeing processes use acridone intermediates to produce fluorescent and high-chroma colorants.

These colorants offer good wash and light fastness performance. In personal care formulations, acridone derivatives contribute UV-filtering functionality in products where photostability is a requirement.

Acridone is supplied as a yellow crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity typically specified at 98% or higher by HPLC for industrial applications.

Packaging ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial volumes depending on supplier. This ensures flexibility for both research and development and large-scale manufacturing needs.

description:

This process occurs during vulcanization, improving reinforcement efficiency and reducing rolling resistance. Electronics manufacturers apply it as a surface primer on glass and ceramic substrates to promote adhesion.

It is frequently used for encapsulants and conformal coatings. In plastics compounding, it modifies mineral filler surfaces, including silica and glass fiber, to improve dispersion and interfacial strength in various systems.

This applies to both thermoplastic and thermoset systems. The terminal alkene also supports co-polymerization and cross-linking reactions in specialty silicone formulations and UV-curable systems for industrial use.

3-Butenyltriethoxysilane is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or intermediate bulk containers for industrial volumes. Smaller quantities are also available for R&D use and laboratory testing.

name: Pyridoxine hydrochloride
description:
Pyridoxine hydrochloride (CAS 58-56-0 ), commonly sourced under the name vitamin B6 hydrochloride, is the stable salt form of vitamin B6 used across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions as a bioavailable B-vitamin source in finished products requiring precise, measurable dosing of B6 activity. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is formulated into tablets, capsules, and injectable solutions.

These formulations target B-vitamin deficiency indications. Nutraceutical producers incorporate it into multivitamin blends, prenatal supplements, and functional food fortification programs where label-declared B6 content must meet specifications.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it is used in scalp treatments, anti-hair loss serums, and conditioning products. Here, B6 activity supports scalp and follicle health claims for consumers.

Food manufacturers apply it as a nutrient fortifier in breakfast cereals, infant formula, and meal replacement products. Pyridoxine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications to meet the compliance requirements of pharmaceutical, dietary supplement, and food applications.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with smaller quantities available for R&D and quality control purposes. This ensures consistent supply chains for large-scale manufacturing and laboratory testing.

name: Adenosine
description:
Adenosine (CAS 58-61-7 ), also known by the trade name Boniton, is a naturally occurring nucleoside used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biotechnology applications. In topical formulations, it functions as a humectant and antioxidant stabilizer.

This material helps to maintain moisture retention and ingredient integrity. Procurement demand spans both high-purity synthesis-grade material and cosmetic-grade specifications for various industrial manufacturing needs.

In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into anti-aging creams and serums, where it supports skin smoothing and moisture-binding performance. It does not require active pharmaceutical classification in most markets.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient and biochemical intermediate in cardiovascular drug synthesis and injectable formulations. In biotechnology, it serves as a critical building block for nucleotide synthesis.

It is also used for cell culture media supplementation and enzymatic assay development. Research-scale buyers source it for use in molecular biology workflows, including ATP pathway studies and receptor binding research.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications, with cosmetic-grade material available for personal care use.

Research and reagent grades are also offered for life sciences procurement. These typically feature defined purity thresholds of 98% or higher by HPLC to ensure consistent performance in laboratory environments.

name: Inosine
description:
Inosine (CAS 58-63-9 ), also known commercially as Selfer and Pantholic-L, is a naturally occurring purine nucleoside used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biotechnology applications.

As a biochemical building block and metabolic intermediate, it supports cell culture processes, active ingredient formulation, and skin conditioning systems for various industrial sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this compound is incorporated into injectable preparations and oral dosage forms targeting cellular energy metabolism support and therapeutic development.

Cosmetic formulators use it as a humectant and antioxidant stabilizer in anti-aging creams, serums, and moisturizing treatments where it helps retain moisture and protect formulation integrity.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it serves as a nucleoside supplement in cell culture media, supporting cell viability and growth in complex bioproduction workflows and laboratory research.

It also functions as a reference standard and reagent in analytical and research settings, where high purity and batch consistency are critical procurement considerations for global suppliers.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder and is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications including USP and BP , as well as research-grade and technical-grade options.

Bulk quantities are standard for pharmaceutical and biotech procurement, with smaller packaging available for quality control and formulation development use in specialized manufacturing facilities.

name: Biotin
description:
Biotin (CAS 58-85-5 ), commonly known as Vitamin B7 or Vitamin H, is a water-soluble B-complex vitamin that functions as a coenzyme in carboxylation reactions critical to metabolism.

In commercial supply, it is sourced as a pure active ingredient for use across nutritional, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and biotechnology manufacturing sectors worldwide.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, it is incorporated into capsules, tablets, and fortified products targeting hair, skin, and nail health claims for consumers.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in prescription and OTC formulations, requiring documented purity and traceability to meet strict regulatory standards.

In personal care, it is added to shampoos, conditioners, and topical serums where label claims around hair and nail strength drive significant consumer demand in the market.

Biotechnology applications rely on its strong affinity for streptavidin and avidin, making it a standard reagent in assay development, diagnostic kits, and cell culture media.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications.

Feed-grade material is available for animal nutrition. Pre-diluted blends at 1% or 2% concentrations in carriers such as dextrose or starch are also available for easier handling.

name: D-xylose
description:
D-xylose (CAS 58-86-6 ), also known as wood sugar, is a naturally occurring pentose monosaccharide derived primarily from hemicellulose hydrolysis of plant materials such as corncobs and birch wood.

In industry, it functions as a reducing sugar, humectant, and Maillard reaction precursor across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. In food production, it is used to generate brown color.

It creates roasted flavor notes in baked goods, confectionery, and savory products through controlled Maillard reactions with amino acids. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in oral formulations.

It also serves as a diagnostic reference standard for intestinal absorption testing. In cosmetic formulations, it acts as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in moisturizers and serums.

Its water-binding capacity supports product stability and skin feel. It also serves as a fermentation substrate in biotechnology processes for producing xylitol and other bio-based compounds.

D-xylose is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the most commonly traded form for industrial use.

USP and BP grades are available for pharmaceutical applications. Bulk quantities are typically offered in 25 kg bags, with high-purity grades exceeding 99% for analytical use.

name: Hydrochlorothiazide
description:
Hydrochlorothiazide (CAS 58-93-5 ), commonly abbreviated as HCTZ, is a thiazide diuretic active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the treatment of hypertension and edema.

It is one of the most established antihypertensive APIs in global pharmaceutical manufacturing, appearing in both standalone formulations and fixed-dose combinations.

HCTZ is a primary active ingredient in oral solid dosage forms, such as tablets and capsules, targeting cardiovascular and renal indications for patients worldwide.

Fixed-dose combination products pairing HCTZ with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or beta-blockers represent a major share of its commercial demand in the pharmaceutical sector.

Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a finished API for direct compression or wet granulation processes to ensure efficient production cycles.

Contract formulators also use it as a reference standard component in bioequivalence and analytical method development for various regulatory submission requirements.

Hydrochlorothiazide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. compendial grades to meet global standards.

Micronized grades are available where particle size control is critical to dissolution performance and content uniformity in finished dosage forms for high-quality manufacturing.

name: Tocopheryl acetate
description:
Tocopheryl acetate (CAS 58-95-7 ), also known as Vitamin E acetate, is the esterified, shelf-stable form of Vitamin E used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Unlike free tocopherol, the acetate ester resists oxidation during processing and storage, making it the preferred supply form for formulators requiring consistent potency and long-term stability.

It functions as both a nutritional supplement ingredient and an antioxidant stabilizer in finished products. In dietary supplements, it delivers Vitamin E activity in softgel capsules and fortified oils.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into injectable formulations and oral dosage forms requiring a standardized, pharmacopeial-grade active. It is also used in vitamin blends for clinical applications.

In personal care, it protects emulsions and skin-conditioning products from lipid oxidation. Food producers use it to fortify infant formula and cereal products to meet regulatory enrichment requirements.

Tocopheryl acetate is supplied as a clear, viscous oil, with natural-source and synthetic versions available. Recognized specifications include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade FCC .

Concentration variants such as 50% and 70% dilutions in carrier oils are also standard for premix and feed applications. These formats ensure easy handling and precise dosing during large-scale production.

name: Quaternium-52
description:
Quaternium-52 (CAS 58069-11-7 ), commercially available as Dehyquart SP, is a cationic quaternary ammonium compound used across personal care and industrial formulations. It functions primarily as an emulsifier, conditioning agent, and surface modifier.

This versatile chemical delivers substantivity to hair, fiber, and hard surfaces. In hair care, it deposits onto negatively charged hair surfaces to improve combability, reduce static, and provide conditioning in rinse-off and leave-on products.

Textile and leather processors use it to apply softening and antistatic finishes to fabric and hide during wet processing. In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, it modifies surface wetting behavior to improve product performance.

Paper manufacturers apply it as a surface treatment agent to influence sheet properties such as softness and charge balance. Quaternium-52 is typically supplied as a liquid or aqueous solution, suited for direct incorporation into formulations.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for use in leave-on and rinse-off personal care products. Packaging options generally range from drums to IBC containers for industrial volumes.

name: Potassium benzoate
description:
Potassium benzoate (CAS 582-25-2 ), also known as E212 , is the potassium salt form of benzoic acid used as a broad-spectrum preservative across food, beverage, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications.

It inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria, extending shelf life in acidic formulations where microbial control is critical. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to preserve acidic products.

Common applications include carbonated drinks, fruit juices, condiments, and pickled goods, where it is preferred over sodium benzoate for its lower sodium contribution to the final product formulation.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products, including shampoos, lotions, and wipes, as a preservative active often in combination with other antimicrobials for efficacy.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a preservative in oral liquid formulations and topical preparations where pH conditions support its antimicrobial activity. It also functions as a buffering agent.

This material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade for industrial applications.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on grade and application requirements. It provides reliable stability and performance in formulations requiring mild pH stabilization.

name: Triton DF 16
description:
Triton DF 16 (CAS 58229-81-5 ) is a low-foaming nonionic surfactant designed for applications where controlled foam profiles and strong surface activity are critical. It delivers effective wetting, emulsification, and degreasing performance across a range of industrial formulations.

In home care and industrial cleaning, this surfactant is used in hard surface cleaners, machine dishwashing formulations, and CIP systems where foam suppression is a process requirement.

Textile processors incorporate it into scouring and dyeing auxiliaries to improve fiber wetting and dye penetration without generating disruptive foam during the manufacturing process.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a wetting and dispersing agent to improve substrate adhesion and pigment distribution in waterborne systems for better finish quality.

Leather and paper manufacturers apply it to ensure uniform treatment liquor penetration during processing, which enhances the overall consistency and durability of the final material.

Triton DF 16 is supplied as a liquid, suitable for direct incorporation into aqueous formulations or dilution systems. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for industrial applications.

Packaging typically includes drums and IBC totes to support both mid-scale and bulk procurement requirements. This ensures efficient logistics and handling for various industrial and institutional cleaning facilities.

name: Dipotassium oxalate
description:
Dipotassium oxalate (CAS 583-52-8 ), also known as potassium oxalate, is the dipotassium salt of oxalic acid used industrially as a chelating and sequestering agent. It binds and immobilizes metal ions in solution.

This chemical enables effective cleaning, precipitation, and process control across mineral processing, textile, and water treatment operations. In mining and metal processing, it precipitates calcium and heavy metal ions from process streams.

This functionality supports ore separation and effluent control. Textile manufacturers apply it as a reducing and cleaning agent during fabric preparation, helping to remove metal impurities that would otherwise interfere with dyeing uniformity.

In leather processing and paper manufacturing, it functions as a sequestrant to control calcium hardness in process water. This protects equipment and improves product consistency across various manufacturing stages.

Water treatment operations use it to complex interfering metal ions before downstream chemical dosing steps. This ensures that the treatment process remains efficient and free from unwanted mineral interference.

Dipotassium oxalate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications, with monohydrate form being the standard commercial specification for most buyers.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on application volume. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for large-scale industrial requirements.

name: Potassium carbonate
description:
Potassium carbonate (CAS 584-08-7 ), also known historically as pearl ash and commercially listed as E501i , is an inorganic alkali used across food, industrial, and chemical manufacturing sectors.

It functions primarily as a pH regulator, buffering agent, and reaction catalyst in a broad range of formulations and processes. In food production, it acts as a leavening agent and pH modifier.

This compound is essential in cocoa processing, noodle manufacturing, and confectionery, where controlled alkalinity directly affects texture and color. Glass and ceramic manufacturers rely on it as a flux.

It is used to lower melting points in specialty glass formulations. In textile and leather processing, it serves as a scouring and dyeing auxiliary, helping to fix dyes and regulate bath pH during finishing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair care and skin preparations as an alkalizing agent to adjust product pH within target ranges. It is supplied as a white granular powder or fine powder.

Granule grades are often preferred in industrial settings for reduced dust handling. Standard market grades include food-grade (E501i compliant), USP , and technical grade for various applications.

name: Toluene 2,4-diisocyanate
description:
Toluene 2,4-diisocyanate (CAS 584-84-9 ), commonly abbreviated as TDI, is a reactive diisocyanate monomer used as a core building block in polyurethane synthesis. It reacts with polyols to form urethane linkages.

This chemical enables the production of flexible foams, coatings, adhesives, and elastomers across multiple industrial sectors. TDI is the primary isocyanate used in flexible polyurethane foam manufacturing processes.

Common applications include automotive seating, furniture cushioning, and mattress production. In coatings and lacquers, it functions as a crosslinker that improves hardness, chemical resistance, and adhesion to various substrates.

It is particularly effective on metal and wood surfaces. Adhesive and sealant formulators use TDI-based prepolymers to achieve high-strength, flexible bonds in construction and automotive assembly projects.

Elastomer producers also rely on TDI to cure cast polyurethane parts requiring abrasion resistance. This is essential for industrial rollers and seals that must withstand significant mechanical stress during operation.

TDI is supplied as a liquid, typically as an 80/20 isomer blend of the 2,4- and 2,6-isomers (TDI-80). The pure 2,4-isomer (TDI-100) is available for applications requiring controlled reactivity.

The material is offered as technical grade , which is the standard commercial specification. Bulk supply is common in ISO tank containers and drums for large-scale industrial manufacturing requirements.

Purity is typically at 99% or above for technical-grade material. This ensures consistent performance and reliable chemical reactions when formulating high-quality polyurethane systems for global distribution.

description:
3-Phenolsulfonic acid (CAS 585-38-6 ) is an aromatic sulfonic acid combining a hydroxyl and sulfonic acid group on the same benzene ring. In industrial settings, it functions as a catalyst, pH buffer, and surface-active agent across chemical processing and treatment applications.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a wetting and penetration aid, improving dye uptake and surface uniformity on fibrous substrates. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to modify surface energy and promote substrate adhesion in aqueous systems.

Water treatment programs incorporate it as a buffering agent where controlled pH and mild surface activity are required simultaneously. In paper manufacturing, it supports surface sizing and coating formulations where consistent pH regulation directly affects product quality.

3-Phenolsulfonic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration levels varying by supplier and end-use requirement. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial applications.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes, suited to bulk procurement in manufacturing environments. This chemical intermediate is valued for its dual functionality in complex formulations requiring both acidity and surface modification.

The compound's stability and solubility make it a versatile choice for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in aqueous environments. It remains a staple component in specialized chemical synthesis and industrial surface treatments.

name: Lactitol
description:
Lactitol (CAS 585-86-4 ), also known commercially as Importal and classified as E966 , is a sugar alcohol derived from lactose used primarily as a reduced-calorie bulk sweetener.

It serves as a humectant across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care markets. Its low glycemic response and prebiotic activity make it a functional ingredient beyond simple sweetening applications.

In food manufacturing, it replaces sucrose in sugar-free confectionery, baked goods, and chocolate. It delivers comparable bulk and texture at roughly half the caloric value of traditional sugar.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as an excipient in tablet manufacturing and as an active osmotic laxative ingredient. It is commonly found in oral powder and syrup preparations for patients.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skincare and oral care formulations for its humectant properties. This helps retain moisture in various creams, lotions, and toothpastes.

It also functions as a prebiotic in functional food and dietary supplement products targeting gut health. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in monohydrate form.

The monohydrate is the most commercially prevalent version. Standard grades include food-grade material and pharmaceutical-grade material compliant with Ph. Eur. and USP monographs.

Bulk supply is available in multi-kilogram bags through to pallet quantities depending on application requirements. This ensures consistent availability for large-scale industrial manufacturing needs.

Contact us for supply of Lactitol

name: Maltitol
description:
Maltitol ( CAS 585-88-6 ), also known by its food additive designation E965 , is a sugar alcohol derived from maltose used as a reduced-calorie bulk sweetener in food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It delivers sweetness close to sucrose while supporting sugar-free and diabetic-friendly product claims without the aftertaste associated with high-intensity sweeteners. In confectionery and baked goods, it replaces sucrose in sugar-free chocolates.

Hard candies and chewing gum benefit from its comparable bulk and mouthfeel. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet excipient and coating agent in sugar-free formulations where controlled glycemic response is a labeling requirement.

With zero caloric contribution, it is a primary ingredient of interest for sugar reduction programs across food, beverage, and pharmaceutical applications. In beverage formulation, it replaces sucrose and high-fructose corn syrup in carbonated drinks.

It is also used in flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas while meeting clean-label consumer expectations. Dairy and bakery manufacturers incorporate it into yogurts, ice creams, and reduced-sugar baked goods where caloric targets must be met.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical producers use it to mask bitterness and improve palatability in oral dosage forms, syrups, and dietary supplements. It also appears in tabletop sweetener blends, often combined with erythritol or inulin.

Rebaudioside A is supplied as a white to off-white powder in varying purity grades, typically ranging from 60% to 99% content on a dry basis. Food-grade material is available to FCC and JECFA specifications.

The compound is particularly useful where steric bulk at the alpha-carbon is required. Fragrance and flavor chemists use it to prepare ester and amide derivatives with specific branched-chain profiles suited to fine fragrance and aroma formulations.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers employ it in the preparation of prodrugs, enzyme substrates, and biochemical probes. These applications often require controlled lipophilicity and hydrolytic stability as primary design criteria.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor component in select organometallic and coordination chemistry applications. The material is supplied as a liquid, typically in reagent or synthesis grade for industrial and laboratory use.

Printing ink manufacturers rely on Pigment Red 57 for offset and gravure inks, particularly in packaging applications demanding consistent, high-density color reproduction and reliable performance on various substrates.

In rinse-off personal care products like shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant, generating stable foam while maintaining skin and scalp tolerance.

Baby care formulations rely on it specifically because it meets the mildness requirements that harsher sulfate-based surfactants cannot, ensuring safety for sensitive skin applications.

In household and industrial cleaning concentrates, it contributes degreasing and emulsification performance in formulations targeting sensitive surface or skin-contact applications.

name: DL-methionine
description:
DL-Methionine (CAS 59-51-8 ), also referred to as Hmet, is the racemic synthetic form of the essential sulfur-containing amino acid methionine. It functions as a nutritional supplement and precursor compound across feed, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Controlled methionine supply is critical to formulation performance and biological efficacy in these industries. In animal nutrition, it is a primary feed additive for poultry, swine, and aquaculture, correcting deficiency in cereal-based diets.

This additive supports growth performance and feed conversion in livestock. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient or excipient in tablet and infusion formulations targeting liver support and amino acid therapy.

In food fortification, it is incorporated into protein supplements, clinical nutrition products, and functional foods. These applications ensure amino acid profiling meets defined dietary standards for human consumption.

Personal care formulators apply it as an antioxidant and conditioning agent in hair and skin preparations. It helps protect formulations from oxidative degradation, maintaining product stability and efficacy over time.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or free-flowing granule. Granulated forms are often preferred for feed premix blending due to improved handling characteristics and reduced dust during processing.

Standard grades include feed-grade, USP , and food-grade ( FCC ). These quality standards ensure the material is suitable for its intended application in highly regulated global markets.

Bulk supply is available in 25 kg bags or bulk containers depending on specific application requirements. This flexibility allows for efficient logistics and storage across various manufacturing scales and industrial sectors.

name: Nicotinic acid
description:
Nicotinic acid (CAS 59-67-6 ), also known commercially as E375 and Niacin, is a water-soluble B-vitamin (B3) used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions as a nutrient fortifier, acidulant, and catalyst precursor depending on the application sector.

In food and beverage manufacturing, nicotinic acid is approved for flour and cereal fortification, restoring B-vitamin content lost during processing. Pharmaceutical producers use it as an active ingredient in vitamin B3 supplements and as a precursor in the synthesis of nicotinamide.

In personal care formulations, it supports skin-conditioning actives, particularly in products targeting uneven tone and barrier function. Specialty chemical manufacturers also employ it as a ligand or precursor in catalyst systems for organic synthesis processes.

Nicotinic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications, with food-grade material conforming to purity requirements for direct food contact applications.

FCC -grade material is available for North American food and dietary supplement markets. This ensures compliance with strict safety standards across various global jurisdictions and industrial requirements for high-purity chemical sourcing.

The material is also available in EP and Ph.Eur. compliant forms to meet European pharmaceutical standards. These certifications guarantee the chemical integrity and consistency required for sensitive manufacturing environments and large-scale production.

name: Butyl propionate
description:
Butyl propionate (CAS 590-01-2 ), also identified under FEMA 2211 , is an ester solvent and flavoring agent used across food, fragrance, and industrial coating applications. It delivers a fruity, apple-like aroma profile that makes it commercially relevant to flavor houses and fragrance blenders.

In industrial settings, it functions as a medium-evaporation solvent for resins and surface coatings. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used as a flavoring ingredient to impart fruity top notes in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products, including lotions, shampoos, and fine fragrances, where its pleasant ester character contributes to top-note compositions. In the printing and packaging industry, it acts as a carrier solvent for inks and coatings.

This chemical supports resin dissolution and controlled evaporation rates on press. It also appears in nail care formulations and cosmetic solvents where moderate evaporation speed is a specific formulation requirement for the end product.

Butyl propionate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. Food-grade material is available in compliance with the FEMA 2211 designation for flavoring use in various food systems.

Technical-grade supply is standard for solvent and coating applications. This material meets the rigorous demands of industrial manufacturing while maintaining consistent purity levels for high-performance chemical processing and formulation needs.

name: Potassium formate
description:
Potassium formate (CAS 590-29-4 ), also referred to as potassium formiate, is the potassium salt of formic acid used across oil field operations, food processing, and de-icing applications.

It functions primarily as a high-density brine fluid, buffering agent, and preservation aid depending on the industry context. In oil and gas drilling, it serves as a completion and workover fluid.

Its high density and low solids content help protect reservoir formations during well interventions. Food manufacturers use it as a pH regulator and preservative in processed products.

In these applications, it controls microbial activity and stabilizes formulations. In agriculture, it is incorporated into feed preservation and silage treatments to inhibit spoilage organisms.

This helps extend shelf life for various agricultural products. Personal care formulators use it as a buffering agent in rinse-off and leave-on products to maintain target pH ranges.

Potassium formate is supplied as a clear aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 75–80%, and as a dry crystalline solid. Standard grades include food-grade and technical-grade.

The food-grade material is produced in compliance with FCC specifications. Industrial grades are available in bulk liquid totes or drums suited for oilfield and de-icing end uses.
