name: Betaine hydrochloride
description:
Betaine hydrochloride (CAS 590-46-5 ) is the acidic salt form of betaine, supplying hydrochloric acid upon dissolution in water. It is used across pharmaceutical, nutritional supplement, and food processing applications as a controlled acidulant.

Buyers sourcing this material should note that it is distinct from anhydrous betaine and delivers measurable acidity alongside the betaine molecule itself. In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in stomach acid support capsules.

Precise HCl delivery per dose is a key formulation requirement for these products. Food processors use it as an acidulant and buffering agent in products where controlled, gradual acidification is preferred over mineral acids.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into solid dosage forms requiring both pH adjustment and osmolyte activity within the same excipient. This dual functionality makes it a versatile choice for complex chemical formulations.

Personal care manufacturers apply it in scalp and skin formulations where its hygroscopic character supports moisture retention. It helps in maintaining a mildly acidic environment necessary for certain topical applications.

Betaine hydrochloride is commercially available as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , FCC , and technical-grade material, with the food-grade variant being most common for supplement applications.

In food and beverage formulation, it contributes to the development of roasted, malty, and chocolate flavor profiles in confectionery, baked goods, and dairy products.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrance and personal care formulations where green, fruity, or aldehydic top notes are required for the final scent profile.

It also functions as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of more complex aroma compounds, supporting flavor ingredient manufacturers upstream in the supply chain.

Cosmetic formulators use it in shampoos, conditioners, and skin care products where a defined scent profile is part of the product brief and consumer experience.

name: Ferrous lactate

Ferrous lactate (CAS 5905-52-2 ), also known by its food additive designation E585 , is an iron(II) salt of lactic acid used as a bioavailable iron source and color stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications.

Its relatively mild gastric profile supports patient compliance in liquid tonics. In animal feed and premix production, it functions as a bioavailable iron source for livestock and poultry nutrition programs to ensure health.

Food and beverage producers also apply it as a mineral fortification ingredient in functional drinks, infant formulas, and fortified cereals. It is supplied as a greenish-white to off-white crystalline powder for easy blending.

It is used in synthesizing azo and mordant dyes that bond directly to fiber substrates. Personal care manufacturers use it as an oxidative hair dye coupler, where it reacts with primary developers to produce tones.

In polymer and resin systems, it acts as a curing agent and cross-linker, contributing to epoxy and urethane network formation. Pharmaceutical and agrochemical producers also rely on it as a synthetic intermediate.

name: 1,4-Pentanediamine
description:
1,4-Pentanediamine (CAS 591-77-5 ), also known as 1,4-diaminopentane, is a branched-chain aliphatic diamine used as a building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its asymmetric structure makes it a sought-after intermediate where standard linear diamines are unsuitable. In pharmaceutical development, it serves as a chiral intermediate for synthesizing active pharmaceutical ingredients.

These applications require defined stereochemical configurations for optimal efficacy. Biotechnology researchers use it in the preparation of polyamine analogs and conjugates for drug delivery and nucleic acid binding studies.

It also functions as a linker or spacer molecule in the construction of peptidomimetics and other bioactive scaffolds. Specialty polymer chemists evaluate it for producing polyamides and polyureas with modified chain geometry.

This provides unique properties compared to standard linear diamine feedstocks. 1,4-Pentanediamine is typically supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, available in research and development quantities through to multi-kilogram lots.

It is primarily sourced to pharmaceutical and biotechnology specifications, with purity grades commonly ranging from 95% to 98%+ for synthetic applications. Packaging is generally offered in sealed glass or HDPE containers.

These storage solutions maintain product integrity during storage and transit. Our supply chain ensures that all materials meet rigorous internal quality standards for consistency and performance in sensitive chemical processes.

name: Diglycerin
description:
Diglycerin (CAS 59113-36-9 ) is a polyol dimer of glycerol used across cosmetic, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing as a humectant, emulsifier, and solvent carrier. Its moisture-retaining and surface-active properties make it a functional ingredient.

This material is often preferred where standard glycerol or propylene glycol falls short in performance or regulatory fit. In personal care formulations, it acts as a humectant and co-emulsifier in skin creams, serums, and hair conditioners.

The compound improves moisture retention and texture stability in various cosmetic applications. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier and carrier in fat-based systems, including confectionery coatings and bakery shortenings.

In these food applications, it supports the uniform dispersion of ingredients throughout the mixture. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a solvent and plasticizer in topical preparations and soft capsule shells.

Its low volatility and compatibility with active ingredients are operationally relevant for drug delivery. In polymer and resin processing, it functions as a plasticizer and softening agent for industrial use.

It is particularly useful in applications requiring a bio-based polyol alternative. The product is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically at purities ranging from 90% to 99%+ depending on the specific grade.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly traded, with technical-grade material available. It can be manufactured to meet FCC or USP standards depending on the end-use requirements.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on volume requirements for global shipping. This versatile polyol remains a staple for manufacturers seeking high-performance humectancy and stability.

Formulators in the baby care segment rely on it to replace harsher sulfate-based surfactants without sacrificing lather or rinse-off clarity. It provides a gentle alternative that meets modern consumer demands for mildness.

In household and institutional cleaning products, it contributes degreasing and soil dispersion in surface cleaners and dishwashing liquids. It is also highly effective in all-purpose concentrates and industrial detergents.

Its compatibility with a broad range of co-surfactants and active ingredients makes it a practical choice for natural product lines. This is especially useful where ingredient restrictions limit formulation options for chemists.

name: Sodium cetearyl sulfate
description:
Sodium cetearyl sulfate (CAS 59186-41-3 ) is an anionic surfactant derived from a blend of cetyl and stearyl alcohols, supplied as a sodium salt of the mixed sulfate esters. It functions as an emulsifier and cleansing agent across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations.

In cosmetic emulsions, such as creams, lotions, and hair conditioners, it stabilizes oil-in-water systems and contributes to a smooth, spreadable texture. Formulators target this ingredient for both leave-on and rinse-off products to ensure consistency.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an emulsifying excipient in topical preparations such as creams and ointments. In these applications, consistent droplet size and formulation stability are critical to the overall performance of the medicinal product.

In shampoos and body washes, it delivers foam generation and surface wetting alongside primary surfactants. This synergy improves overall cleansing efficiency and enhances the sensory experience for the end user during application.

name: Triphenyl phosphorothionate
description:
Triphenyl phosphorothionate (CAS 597-82-0 ), also known as triphenyl phosphorothioate, is an organophosphorus ester used primarily as a synergist and stabilizer in agrochemical formulations.

It functions by enhancing the efficacy of active ingredients and improving the oxidative stability of formulated products. In pesticide formulations, it acts as a synergist to boost performance.

This additive is particularly effective with pyrethroid and organophosphate insecticides, allowing formulators to reduce active ingredient loading while maintaining high levels of efficacy.

It is incorporated into emulsifiable concentrates and wettable powder formulations where oxidative degradation of the active substance is a concern for long-term storage and use.

Agricultural chemical manufacturers also use it as a co-formulant in products targeting stored grain pests and crop protection applications across various global markets.

Its compatibility with a range of carrier solvents makes it a practical additive in technical-grade insecticide blends destined for both professional and agricultural sectors.

Triphenyl phosphorothionate is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, typically available in technical grade. It is commonly offered in drum and IBC quantities for manufacturing.

In pharmaceuticals, it is used as an active ingredient in zinc deficiency treatments and as an excipient in topical formulations where controlled zinc release is required for therapeutic efficacy.

Food and feed manufacturers use it as a zinc fortification agent in nutritional products, dietary supplements, and animal feed premixes to ensure proper mineral intake and health maintenance.

In polymer and plastics processing, it acts as a catalyst precursor for polymerization reactions and as a stabilizer component to improve the durability and performance of synthetic materials.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into oral care products and astringent preparations where its buffering and mild preservative properties support product stability and user safety.

Zinc acetate dihydrate is available as a white crystalline powder or granules. Recognized grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , FCC , and technical grade for diverse sourcing needs.

name: Manganese carbonate

This supplement helps to meet nutritional specifications for livestock and poultry. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as a mineral source in tablet and capsule formulations where controlled manganese content is required.

In ceramics and pigment production, it acts as a colorant and flux precursor, contributing to specific fired-color outcomes. Industrial catalyst producers use it as a starting material for manganese oxide catalysts.

name: N,n-dimethylurea
description:
N,N-Dimethylurea (CAS 598-94-7 ), also recognized commercially as 1,1-dimethylurea and asym-Dimethylurea, is a substituted urea derivative used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical production, and polymer chemistry.

It functions primarily as a solvent, reaction intermediate, and plasticizing agent in industrial formulations. In pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturing, it serves as a solvent and carrier in synthesis routes.

This compound is preferred where standard urea would introduce unwanted reactivity. Agrochemical formulators use it as a building block in the production of herbicides and plant growth regulators, particularly within the phenylurea class.

In polymer and resin systems, it acts as a plasticizer and softener, improving flexibility and processability in certain thermoset formulations. It also finds use in buffering and pH-control applications.

These applications are common within biological media and research-grade formulations. The product is supplied as a white crystalline solid or powder, ensuring ease of handling during the manufacturing process.

Technical and research grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ for synthesis and laboratory applications. This ensures high performance in sensitive chemical reactions.

name: Glabridin
description:
Glabridin (CAS 59870-68-7 ) is the primary bioactive isoflavonoid extracted from licorice root, where it occurs as the dominant polyphenol in the hydrophobic fraction. In commercial formulation, it functions as a skin-brightening active and antioxidant.

This compound serves as a UV-stabilizing ingredient across cosmetic and pharmaceutical product lines. In topical skincare, it is formulated into serums, creams, and spot-treatment products targeting hyperpigmentation and uneven skin tone.

The ingredient inhibits melanin synthesis pathways relevant to cosmetic efficacy claims. Suncare formulators incorporate it as a secondary UV-stabilizing component alongside primary filters to improve photostability of finished SPF products.

In functional food and nutraceutical applications, it is used in antioxidant-positioned supplements and standardized licorice extracts. Buyers require documented polyphenol content for these specific health and wellness applications.

Pharmaceutical researchers and contract manufacturers source it as a reference standard or active ingredient for topical dermatological preparations. It is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder for various industrial uses.

The material is typically standardized to 90%, 95%, or 98% purity by HPLC. It is available in both cosmetic-grade and research-grade specifications, with documentation suited to EU cosmetic regulation dossiers or pharmaceutical development files.

name: Phosphonomethyliminodiacetic acid
description:
Phosphonomethyliminodiacetic acid (CAS 5994-61-6 ), commonly abbreviated as PMIDA, is a phosphonate-based chelating agent used across industrial water treatment, agriculture, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its primary commercial role is sequestering metal ions and inhibiting scale and corrosion in process systems. PMIDA is also a key intermediate in the synthesis of glyphosate herbicide, giving it significant relevance.

In agrochemical manufacturing, PMIDA serves as the direct precursor to glyphosate, making it a critical raw material for herbicide producers operating at scale. It is essential for high-volume production lines.

Water treatment formulators incorporate it into corrosion and scale inhibitor blends for cooling towers, boilers, and oilfield injection systems where metal ion control is critical for maintaining equipment integrity.

In textile and paper processing, it sequesters calcium and magnesium ions to prevent interference during bleaching and dyeing operations. This ensures consistent quality and color uniformity in the final products.

Oil and gas operators use PMIDA-based formulations to control mineral scale deposition in pipelines and production equipment. This application is vital for preventing flow restrictions and maintaining operational efficiency.

PMIDA is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically specified at 98% or higher for agrochemical intermediate use.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial procurement, with packaging options ranging from multi-layer bags to IBC containers depending on volume requirements and logistical needs for global distribution.

description:
2-Hydroxyethyliminodimethanephosphonic acid ( CAS 5995-42-6 ), commonly referred to as HEIDP, is a phosphonate chelating agent used to control scale formation and metal ion interference in industrial water systems.

It binds calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions, preventing precipitation and deposit buildup in process equipment. In industrial water treatment, HEIDP is formulated into scale and corrosion inhibitor blends.

These blends are used for cooling water circuits, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems. Home care and institutional cleaning products use it to sequester hardness ions, improving surfactant performance and preventing redeposition.

In textile processing, it controls metal ion interference during dyeing and bleaching, protecting color consistency and fabric quality. Paper and leather manufacturing incorporate it into process water treatment.

This prevents mineral scaling on equipment and improves overall process efficiency. HEIDP is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 30–50% for various industrial applications.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for water treatment and industrial cleaning applications. Buyers specifying phosphonate content should request lot-specific assay data for their records.

name: Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid
description:
Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (CAS 60-00-4 ), commercially known as EDTA or Versene Acid, is a synthetic aminopolycarboxylic acid used across industrial and consumer markets as a chelating and sequestering agent.

By binding free metal ions in solution, it prevents unwanted oxidation, discoloration, and mineral interference in formulations and process streams. In food manufacturing, EDTA is used as a preservative and stabilizer.

It is approved in products such as canned legumes, mayonnaise, and soft drinks to inhibit metal-catalyzed rancidity and color degradation. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it to stabilize active ingredients against trace metal contamination.

It is also used to enhance preservative efficacy in ophthalmic and injectable preparations. Personal care manufacturers rely on EDTA to sequester calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, improving surfactant performance.

This improves the quality of shampoos, creams, and liquid soaps. In water treatment and industrial cleaning, it removes scale-forming metal deposits from boilers, heat exchangers, and textile processing equipment.

EDTA is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both free acid and salt forms, with the disodium and tetrasodium salts being the most commercially traded variants. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ).

Other available quality standards include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for regulated applications. Technical grade options are also available for various industrial use cases.

It acts as a broad-spectrum preservative in lotions, shampoos, and liquid soaps, where it inhibits bacterial and yeast growth. Food and beverage manufacturers incorporate it as a FEMA-approved flavoring.

This ingredient is used to impart floral rose notes in confectionery, baked goods, and beverages. Printing and packaging operations use it as a solvent and additive in flexographic and gravure inks.

In these industrial settings, it supports controlled drying and ink stability. It also functions as an intermediate in the synthesis of fragrance compounds and phenethyl esters used in fine fragrance production.

2-Phenylethanol is supplied as a clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, with FCC and natural-origin grades commonly stocked.

name: 2-mercaptoethanol
description:
2-Mercaptoethanol (CAS 60-24-2 ), commonly referred to as β-mercaptoethanol or BME, is a thiol-functional reducing agent used across industrial and research-grade applications. It breaks disulfide bonds in proteins and polymers, enabling controlled denaturation.

Fiber modification and chemical synthesis are primary uses for this versatile compound. Procurement demand spans biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and personal care manufacturing sectors globally. It is essential for various industrial processes.

In biotechnology and protein biochemistry, BME is a standard reagent for denaturing proteins prior to gel electrophoresis. It is also used for maintaining reduced thiol states in cell culture and buffer systems for research.

Textile and leather processors use it to cleave disulfide linkages in keratin fibers. This enables permanent wave treatments, fiber softening, and chemical modification of wool during the manufacturing and treatment stages.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it functions as an intermediate in the production of thiol-containing active compounds. It also serves as a stabilizer in certain formulations to ensure product longevity and chemical integrity.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into depilatory and hair-relaxing formulations where controlled keratin disruption is required. This application relies on the specific chemical properties of the thiol group.

2-Mercaptoethanol is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 98–99% purity for technical and laboratory-grade applications. Reagent-grade and molecular biology-grade specifications are available to meet strict quality requirements.

Bulk quantities are offered for industrial users, with smaller pack sizes standard for research and QC laboratory supply. The product is handled according to rigorous safety protocols to ensure consistent performance.

name: Diethyl ether
description:
Diethyl ether (CAS 60-29-7 ), also sold as ethyl ether or solvent ether, is a low-boiling organic solvent with exceptionally strong solvating power for nonpolar and moderately polar compounds. It is a standard extraction and reaction medium across pharmaceutical manufacturing and specialty chemical processing.

In pharmaceutical production, it serves as a primary solvent for alkaloid extraction, active ingredient isolation, and recrystallization processes where high purity and clean solvent removal are required. Industrial and laboratory cleaning applications rely on it to dissolve greases and resins.

It is frequently used to remove polymer residues from precision equipment and tooling surfaces. In plastics and polymer research, it is used as a reaction solvent and polymer precipitation medium, particularly where rapid evaporation and low residue are critical to product quality.

Analytical laboratories use it as a reference extraction solvent in lipid determination, pesticide residue testing, and standardized sample preparation protocols. It is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in a range of pack sizes from small containers to bulk drums.

Anhydrous and stabilized grades are standard, with anhydrous variants used where moisture interference affects reaction outcomes. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications for regulated manufacturing environments.

In food production, it acts as an acidulant and flavoring component, contributing to the characteristic taste profiles of fats and oils. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams and serums to support emulsion stability.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a functional excipient in lipid-based drug delivery systems. Its emulsification properties improve the bioavailability of poorly soluble active ingredients in various medical formulations.

In industrial oleochemical processing, it serves as a feedstock for the production of conjugated linoleic acid and other derivative compounds. It is also utilized as a pH regulator across several manufacturing sectors.

The product is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid, typically in bulk or drummed formats suited to industrial processing volumes. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications for global distribution.

Personal care formulators use it as a humectant and surface-modifying agent in skin conditioning products, where it supports moisture retention at the formulation level for high-quality cosmetic goods.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a buffering component and nitrogen source in microbial culture media and biochemical assay systems used for research and development purposes.

In specialty chemical synthesis, it functions as a catalyst precursor and pH-regulating agent in controlled reaction environments to ensure consistent results across different manufacturing batches.

name: Methimazole
description:
Methimazole (CAS 60-56-0 ), also known by the trade name Tapazole and abbreviated as MMI, is an active pharmaceutical ingredient and synthesis intermediate used across pharmaceutical manufacturing and select industrial processes.

It functions as a thyroid hormone synthesis inhibitor in drug formulations and as a stabilizing agent in industrial chemical applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, MMI is the active substance in antithyroid drug products.

This makes it a direct procurement target for API suppliers and finished-dose formulators. Textile and leather processors source it as a corrosion inhibitor and stabilizing additive in processing baths where metal ion control is critical.

In paper manufacturing, it is applied as a biocide and preservation agent to extend the service life of process fluids. MMI also serves as a building block in heterocyclic synthesis for chemical production.

Its reactive thione group supports the production of more complex pharmaceutical intermediates. Methimazole is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bulk quantities suited to both pharmaceutical and industrial procurement.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP specifications, supporting API and formulation manufacturing requirements. Technical-grade material is available for industrial applications.

name: 2-Methylbutanoic acid
description:
2-Methylbutanoic acid (CAS 600-07-7 ), also known as 2-methylbutyric acid, is a short-chain branched fatty acid used primarily as a flavoring agent and fragrance ingredient.

It delivers characteristic cheesy, fruity, and rancid-dairy notes that are difficult to replicate with simpler acid structures. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a flavoring component.

It is used in dairy-type flavors, cheese seasonings, and processed snack coatings where authentic fermented notes are required. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into compositions targeting earthy profiles.

These compositions often target animal or aged-dairy olfactory profiles for personal care and household products. In crop protection and agrochemical formulations, it serves as an intermediate or acidulant.

It also finds use in feed flavoring applications, where palatability enhancement of animal nutrition products is the target outcome. The substance is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid.

It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications, with food-grade material typically meeting FCC or flavor-industry purity standards relevant for direct use in consumable formulations.

Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on application volume requirements. This versatile chemical is essential for achieving specific aromatic profiles in industrial applications.

name: Glycine hydrochloride
description:
Glycine hydrochloride (CAS 6000-43-7 ), also known as aminoacetic acid hydrochloride, is the hydrochloride salt form of glycine used across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer and acidulant in formulations where precise, stable acidic conditions are required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a buffering agent in parenteral formulations.

This material is essential for lyophilized drug products and API synthesis where controlled pH is critical to product stability. Food and nutrition producers use it to adjust acidity in functional food systems.

It also acts as a preservation aid where mild antimicrobial activity is needed at low pH. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin-conditioning products to support moisture retention.

Its hygroscopic character is beneficial in both leave-on and rinse-off formats. It also appears in peptide synthesis workflows as a protected amino acid precursor for specialty chemical and biotech procurement.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP specifications, supporting regulated drug product manufacturing requirements.

Technical and reagent grades are also commercially available for industrial synthesis and laboratory applications. This ensures versatility across various industrial sectors and research environments globally.

name: Sodium glycinate
description:
Sodium glycinate (CAS 6000-44-8 ), also sold as sodium aminoacetate, is the monosodium salt of glycine used across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, humectant, and stabilizer in formulations where controlled acidity and moisture retention are critical to product performance.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it buffers injectable solutions, oral liquids, and topical formulations to maintain stable pH across storage conditions for long-term stability.

Food and beverage producers use it as a flavor modifier and buffering agent in processed foods, where it also contributes mild antioxidant stabilization to extend shelf life.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin care products and cleansing systems to regulate pH while supporting moisture retention in the final product for consumers.

It also appears in amino acid-based nutritional supplements and clinical nutrition products as a bioavailable glycine source for various health and wellness applications.

Sodium glycinate is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available, with pharmaceutical supply typically conforming to USP or BP specifications.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for formulators and R&D applications to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

name: Cetylpyridinium chloride monohydrate
description:
Cetylpyridinium chloride monohydrate (CAS 6004-24-6 ), commonly abbreviated as CPC, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as an antimicrobial active and preservative across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing.

It delivers broad-spectrum biocidal activity against bacteria, fungi, and some viruses, making it a go-to active ingredient where surface-active preservation is required for high-performance formulations.

In oral care, CPC is the active ingredient in antiseptic mouthwashes, throat lozenges, and medicated sprays targeting plaque-forming bacteria and oral pathogens. These applications rely on its efficacy.

Topical pharmaceutical formulations, including wound rinses and antiseptic creams, rely on it for preservative efficacy at low use concentrations. It is highly effective in maintaining product stability.

In personal care, it functions as both a conditioning agent and antimicrobial in shampoos and skin cleansers, where its cationic surfactant character aids substantivity to hair and skin surfaces.

It also appears in nasal sprays and respiratory hygiene products as an antiviral adjunct active. This versatile compound is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for pharmaceutical applications, as well as cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity specifications for personal care use.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk bags for industrial formulation. This ensures flexibility for manufacturers across different sectors and production scales.

name: Gabapentin
description:
Gabapentin (CAS 60142-96-3 ), also known under the brand name Neurontin®, is a gamma-aminobutyric acid analogue used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient in finished dosage form manufacturing.

It functions as the primary API in anticonvulsant and neuropathic pain formulations supplied to pharmaceutical manufacturers and contract packagers worldwide for various clinical applications.

Gabapentin is the core API in oral solid dosage forms, such as capsules and tablets, manufactured for epilepsy and nerve pain indications, making it a high-volume procurement target.

Generic drug producers and contract manufacturers sourcing for regulated markets require material that meets strict pharmacopoeial specifications for potency and impurity profiling during production.

In API synthesis pipelines, it also serves as a reference standard or intermediate for structurally related compounds under development by research and development laboratories globally.

Some specialty formulators evaluate gabapentin in topical compounding applications, where it is incorporated into creams for localized pain management and specialized patient care solutions.

Gabapentin is supplied as a white crystalline powder in quantities ranging from kilogram lots to multi-tonne commercial volumes. It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades.

These grades support regulatory submissions across major markets. Certificates of Analysis, DMF references, and GMP documentation are standard requirements buyers should confirm with suppliers.

name: Sorbitan monocaprylate
description:
Sorbitan monocaprylate (CAS 60177-36-8 ), also known as sorbitan caprylate, is a sorbitan ester derived from sorbitol and caprylic acid used as a non-ionic emulsifier and wetting agent across food and industrial applications.

Its relatively short C8 fatty acid chain gives it an HLB profile suited to water-in-oil emulsion systems and surface modification tasks where lighter esters are preferred for specific formulation needs.

In food manufacturing, it functions as an emulsifier to stabilize fat-in-water systems and improve texture consistency in processed products. It helps maintain a uniform distribution of ingredients during storage.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions where it contributes both emulsification and moisturizing performance. This dual functionality often reduces the need for additional humectants in recipes.

Industrial and home care cleaning formulations use it as a wetting agent to improve substrate penetration and surface coverage. It is highly effective at lowering surface tension in various liquid systems.

In textile and leather processing, it supports surface modification during finishing stages, improving uniformity of treatment across fiber and hide substrates. This ensures a high-quality finish for the end product.

Sorbitan monocaprylate is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity oily substance. It is available in food-grade and technical-grade specifications depending on the target application and regulatory needs.

Buyers sourcing for food or cosmetic use should confirm compliance with relevant regional purity standards before procurement. Proper storage in a cool, dry environment is recommended to maintain chemical stability.

name: Nickel acetate tetrahydrate
description:
Nickel acetate tetrahydrate (CAS 6018-89-9 ) is a water-soluble nickel salt used as a catalyst precursor and surface treatment agent across several industrial sectors. It delivers controlled nickel ion release in solution.

This chemical is suitable for processes where precise metal deposition or activation is required. In textile and leather finishing, it functions as a mordant and fixative, improving dye uptake and wash fastness on treated substrates.

Electroplating and anodizing operations use it as a sealing agent for anodized aluminum, closing surface pores to enhance corrosion resistance. This ensures long-term durability for metal components in harsh environments.

As a catalyst precursor in polymer and specialty chemical synthesis, it is calcined or reduced to generate active nickel species. These species are essential for hydrogenation and related chemical reactions in manufacturing.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a reagent and process chemical where nickel-mediated catalysis is required at laboratory or pilot scale. Its consistent performance makes it a reliable choice for R&D.

Nickel acetate tetrahydrate is supplied as a green crystalline solid or powder. It is available in technical and reagent grades, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ depending on the application.

Packaging options generally range from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply. This flexibility allows manufacturers to source the exact volume needed for their specific production or research requirements.

name: Creatine monohydrate
description:
Creatine monohydrate (CAS 6020-87-7 ) is a naturally occurring nitrogenous compound used as a performance and energy-support ingredient across sports nutrition, pharmaceutical, and functional food markets.

Creapure is a recognized trade name for high-purity creatine monohydrate produced under controlled manufacturing standards, often specified by formulators seeking a premium-grade source.

It functions primarily as an energy substrate replenisher in muscle tissue, driving demand across both finished product manufacturing and bulk ingredient supply chains globally.

In sports nutrition, it is the active ingredient in pre-workout powders, capsules, and ready-to-mix formulations targeting strength and endurance. Functional food manufacturers incorporate it into protein bars.

Fortified drinks and meal replacement products utilize it where performance-oriented labeling is a commercial differentiator. Pharmaceutical producers use it in tablet formats for clinical nutrition applications.

Nutraceutical producers target neuromuscular conditions, while cosmetic formulators have adopted it in topical skin-firming and anti-aging products to support cellular energy metabolism in dermal tissue.

Creatine monohydrate is supplied as a white, fine-to-coarse crystalline powder in bulk bags and drums. Food-grade and USP specifications are standard for most industrial applications.

Creapure-branded material carries additional third-party certification relevant to sports nutrition compliance. Micronized grades are available for applications requiring faster dissolution or improved blendability.

name: Behenamidopropyl dimethylamine
description:
Behenamidopropyl dimethylamine (CAS 60270-33-9 ), also known commercially as Amidet, is a long-chain fatty amide amine derived from behenic acid used as a conditioning and functional intermediate.

It acts as a precursor to quaternary ammonium compounds and betaines, and delivers surface-active, emulsifying, and rheology-modifying performance in its own right for personal care formulations.

In hair care, it is used to produce conditioning agents that deposit on hair fiber to reduce static and improve combability. Shampoos and conditioner formulations incorporate it directly for viscosity.

It has the ability to adjust viscosity and stabilize emulsions at low use levels. Skin care and leave-on products use it to modify surface wetting and improve the spreadability of emollient systems.

It also functions as a pH buffer in rinse-off formulations, helping maintain system stability across processing and storage conditions. This ensures the longevity and performance of the final product.

Behenamidopropyl dimethylamine is supplied as a solid waxy flake or paste, depending on grade and processing. Technical and cosmetic grades are the standard commercial offerings for industrial use.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements suited for personal care end products. Packaging typically ranges from fiber drums to bulk quantities for industrial formulators and large scale production.

name: Triphenylphosphine
description:
Triphenylphosphine (CAS 603-35-0 ), commonly abbreviated as TPP, is a phosphorus-based ligand and reagent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer stabilization, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a catalyst component, reducing agent, and stabilizer precursor in demanding industrial processes. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TPP is a key reagent in Mitsunobu and Wittig reactions.

This material enables stereoselective synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients at scale. Polymer producers incorporate it as a processing stabilizer and catalyst precursor in polyester and polyurethane systems.

In these applications, it controls oxidative degradation during high-temperature compounding. Printing ink and packaging formulators use TPP-derived systems as photoinitiator components and stabilizers.

These additives extend the service life of UV-curable coatings. In specialty catalyst systems, it acts as a ligand for palladium, rhodium, and other transition metals, supporting cross-coupling reactions.

Such reactions are critical to fine chemical production. Triphenylphosphine is supplied as a white crystalline powder and is available in technical grade for industrial catalyst and polymer applications.

It is also offered in high-purity grades meeting pharmaceutical manufacturing requirements. Packaging options typically range from kilogram-scale bags to bulk drum quantities to suit various needs.

These formats support both R&D and production-scale procurement. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery of this essential phosphorus-based reagent for your specific industrial requirements.

name: Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate dihydrate

Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate dihydrate (CAS 6035-47-8 ), commonly known as SFS, is a reducing agent used industrially for bleaching and stripping color from substrates.

Rongalite is a recognized trade name under which this product is frequently sourced in textile and paper markets. In textile processing, SFS is used as a discharge agent to remove dye.

This enables precise pattern creation without damaging fiber structure. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it as a bleaching agent to brighten mechanical and chemical pulps where milder conditions are required.

Leather processors use SFS to achieve uniform whitening of hides prior to dyeing, improving final color consistency. It also functions as a reductive stripping agent in vat and sulfur dye systems.

This allows for color correction and re-dyeing of off-shade goods. Sodium formaldehyde sulfoxylate dihydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules for various industrial uses.

Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and technical applications, with purity specifications typically ranging from 95% to 98% active content for high performance.

name: Ethyl lauroyl arginate hydrochloride
description:
Ethyl lauroyl arginate hydrochloride (CAS 60372-77-2 ), commercially known as LAE or Cytoguard LA and approved as E243 in the EU, is a cationic antimicrobial derived from natural amino acid and fatty acid precursors.

It functions as a broad-spectrum preservative and surface-active biocide across food, personal care, and pharmaceutical applications. In food manufacturing, E243 is approved for use in processed meats and certain bakery products.

This ingredient inhibits bacterial and yeast growth, extending shelf life without synthetic preservative blends. Personal care formulators incorporate LAE into rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos and conditioners.

In these applications, it delivers both antimicrobial preservation and conditioning activity on hair and skin surfaces. In pharmaceutical topical formulations, it functions as a preservative system component where low-toxicity actives are preferred.

Home care and surface disinfection products use LAE for its rapid bactericidal action against Gram-positive and Gram-negative organisms. It remains effective at low use concentrations across various industrial formulations.

Ethyl lauroyl arginate hydrochloride is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as aqueous solution concentrates. Food-grade material is available meeting E243 regulatory specifications for global distribution.

name: alpha-D-glucose pentaacetate
description:
Alpha-D-glucose pentaacetate (CAS 604-68-2 ), also known as pentaacetyl-alpha-D-glucose, is a fully acetylated glucose derivative used primarily as a pharmaceutical intermediate and specialty chemical in fine chemical synthesis.

It serves as a protected glucose building block, enabling selective glycosylation reactions without the need for additional protection steps. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key starting material for synthesis.

This compound is used for synthesizing nucleoside analogues, glycosylated drug compounds, and other carbohydrate-based active pharmaceutical ingredients. Its well-defined anomeric configuration makes it the preferred precursor for stereoselective glycosylation.

This precision is critical to API purity and regulatory compliance. In personal care formulations, it is evaluated as a stabilizing and moisturizing agent where controlled release of glucose moieties supports skin conditioning performance.

Research and specialty chemical producers also use it as a reference standard or reagent-grade intermediate in carbohydrate chemistry workflows. It is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various uses.

It is available in reagent-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of API synthesis and GMP-compliant manufacturing environments. Packaging typically ranges from laboratory-scale quantities up to bulk orders.

name: Dipentaerythritol pentaacrylate
description:
Dipentaerythritol pentaacrylate (CAS 60506-81-2 ), commercially available as SR 399 and Miramer M500, is a high-functionality multiacrylate monomer used to achieve rapid UV/EB cure.

It is utilized to create dense crosslink networks in radiation-curable systems. Its five reactive acrylate groups deliver high crosslink density, making it a go-to building block for formulations.

This monomer is ideal where cure speed, hardness, and chemical resistance are primary targets. In UV-curable coatings, it builds scratch-resistant, hard surface finishes for wood, plastic, and metal substrates.

Printed electronics and conformal coatings rely on it to achieve tight network formation. This protects circuit boards from moisture and chemical exposure during their operational lifespan.

Radiation-curable inks for packaging benefit from its fast cure response on high-speed press lines. This reduces energy consumption while maintaining excellent adhesion to various packaging materials.

In adhesive and sealant formulations, it functions as a reactive crosslinker. It improves cohesive strength and solvent resistance in the cured film, ensuring long-term durability in harsh environments.

The product is supplied as a viscous liquid in technical and industrial grades. Specifications are typically aligned to monomer purity, viscosity, and acid value parameters relevant to UV/EB formulation.

Inhibited grades containing MEHQ are commonly available to ensure storage stability. This prevents premature polymerization during transport and warehousing, maintaining the integrity of the chemical supply.

name: Benzyl PCA
description:
Benzyl PCA (CAS 60555-57-9 ) is a pyrrolidone carboxylic acid ester used in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent. It combines the moisture-binding properties of PCA with enhanced lipophilicity.

This unique chemical structure improves compatibility with oil-phase systems and emollient-rich formulations. In skincare, it is incorporated into moisturizing creams, serums, and lotions where it supports water retention in the stratum corneum.

The ingredient contributes to a smooth skin feel and its oil-phase compatibility makes it suitable for anhydrous formulations. This includes balms, facial oils, and waterless skincare products where conventional humectants often underperform.

Formulators in hair care use it in conditioning treatments and leave-on products targeting hydration and cuticle smoothness. It provides a versatile solution for maintaining moisture balance in diverse cosmetic applications.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it functions as a conditioning excipient in creams and ointments requiring mild humectant activity. It is particularly useful in systems that require performance without water-phase dependency.

The product is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid or low-viscosity oil. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, suitable for use in both leave-on and rinse-off personal care products.

Packaging options commonly include drums and smaller quantities for laboratory or pilot-scale formulation development. This ensures flexibility for manufacturers ranging from boutique brands to large-scale industrial producers.

Disodium NADH (CAS 606-68-8 ), commonly abbreviated as NADH, is the stabilized disodium salt form of the reduced coenzyme nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide. It functions as a bioactive coenzyme and antioxidant active across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, NADH is formulated into oral supplements and clinical preparations targeting cognitive function, fatigue management, and neurological support. These applications focus on cellular energy metabolism support as the target outcome.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into anti-aging serums and moisturizing treatments. Its antioxidant activity helps protect against oxidative stress at the cellular level, making it a valuable ingredient for high-end skincare formulations.

Biotechnology and life sciences operations use NADH as a cofactor in enzymatic assays and biosensor development. It is also essential in in vitro diagnostic reagent production and serves as a pharmaceutical intermediate for complex coenzyme-based active ingredients.

Disodium NADH is supplied as a lyophilized powder or fine crystalline solid, typically requiring cold-chain handling to maintain stability. Standard grades include research-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material to meet industry requirements.

Purity specifications are commonly at 95% or higher by HPLC to ensure efficacy in sensitive applications. Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory and R&D procurement to bulk quantities for commercial formulation and large-scale manufacturing.

name: n-hydroxysuccinimide
description:
N-Hydroxysuccinimide (CAS 6066-82-6 ), commonly abbreviated as NHS, is a key reagent in bioconjugation chemistry used to activate carboxylic acid groups for stable amide bond formation.

It enables efficient coupling of proteins, peptides, antibodies, and other biomolecules to surfaces, linkers, or drug payloads. NHS is extensively used in the synthesis of NHS esters.

These are reactive intermediates for antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) manufacturing and targeted therapeutic development. In diagnostic kit production, it enables immobilization of biomolecules onto solid supports.

Common supports include beads, membranes, and microplates. Peptide synthesis and PEGylation workflows rely on NHS-activated intermediates to achieve controlled, site-specific conjugation under mild aqueous conditions.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators also use NHS-based crosslinking chemistry in the development of hyaluronic acid derivatives and biomaterial scaffolds for various medical and aesthetic applications.

N-Hydroxysuccinimide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and research-grade specifications for diverse industrial and laboratory needs.

High-purity grades (≥98%, ≥99%) are commonly required for GMP bioconjugation and API intermediate applications. Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to bulk industrial supply.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to build thixotropy in polyurethane, epoxy, and silicone systems without compromising optical clarity or adhesion. It provides structural stability while ensuring the product remains easy to apply.

Its hydrophobic surface treatment makes it effective as an anti-caking and flow aid in moisture-sensitive polymer powders and rubber compounding. This ensures that raw materials remain free-flowing during storage and processing stages.

In construction sealants and elastomeric systems, it reinforces the matrix and stabilizes paste viscosity across temperature fluctuations. This durability is essential for materials exposed to varying environmental conditions over time.

The product offers effective wetting and interfacial activity at moderate use levels. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a scouring and wetting agent, improving penetration of dye baths and finishing liquors into fiber substrates.

Its dual functional groups make it effective in applications requiring simultaneous acidification and surface modification within a single compound. In water treatment, it functions as a pH regulator and scale-control additive.

Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and penetration agent to improve dye uptake and surface uniformity on fiber and hide substrates. It is essential for achieving consistent results in large-scale manufacturing.

Potassium tetroxalate dihydrate (CAS 6100-20-5 ) is an acidic potassium oxalate salt used industrially as a pH buffer, chelating agent, and cleaning active. Its strongly acidic character in solution makes it effective for removing mineral deposits.

This chemical is highly efficient at removing metal ions and oxidation products across multiple process industries. In textile and leather processing, it removes iron stains and rust from fabrics and hides without damaging fiber structure.

Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it to dissolve limescale, metal oxides, and tannin-based stains from hard surfaces. It provides a reliable solution for maintaining equipment and surface integrity in harsh environments.

name: Phenacetin

It functions as an antioxidant stabilizer and processing aid in polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing. In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a stabilizer to inhibit oxidative degradation during high-temperature compounding.

The pharmaceutical and fine chemical industries source it as an intermediate for synthesizing active compounds and research-grade formulations. In textile and leather processing, it is used as a surface modifier and auxiliary agent.

These applications help to improve dye uptake and substrate compatibility. Personal care formulators have historically incorporated it into preservation and stabilization systems within cosmetic manufacturing processes.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Standard grades include USP and BP , with pharmaceutical-grade material subject to tighter purity thresholds.

These thresholds are typically above 99% for high-purity applications. Bulk quantities are available in multi-kilogram and metric-ton packaging, with smaller quantities offered for laboratory and formulation development use.

name: Choline
description:
Choline (CAS 62-49-7 ) is a water-soluble nutrient compound classified within the B-vitamin family, supplied commercially in its stabilized salt form, choline chloride. It functions as a methyl donor and lipid transport agent across food, feed, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In animal feed production, choline chloride is incorporated into poultry, swine, and aquaculture premixes to support liver function and prevent fatty liver syndrome. This directly impacts livestock yield and feed efficiency across global agricultural supply chains.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a nutritional fortifier in infant formula, sports nutrition products, and functional beverages targeting cognitive health positioning. These applications require high purity levels to ensure consumer safety and product stability.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into dietary supplements and nutraceutical capsules where label claims around brain health and prenatal nutrition drive product differentiation. It is a critical component in modern wellness and medical nutrition portfolios.

In personal care, it appears in scalp treatments and conditioning formulations where its role in membrane integrity supports moisturization claims. Its versatile chemical properties allow for seamless integration into various cosmetic delivery systems.

Choline chloride is the dominant commercial form, available as a 70–75% aqueous solution or as a dry powder adsorbed onto silica or corn cob carriers at 50–60% active content. This variety allows for flexibility in different manufacturing environments.

Feed-grade material is the highest-volume specification, while food-grade and USP -grade variants serve nutritional supplement and pharmaceutical applications. These standards ensure the material meets rigorous global regulatory requirements.

Packaging ranges from drums and IBCs for liquid grades to bulk bags for dry carrier-based forms. Proper storage and handling are essential to maintain the integrity of the compound during transport and long-term storage.

name: Aniline
description:
Aniline (CAS 62-53-3 ), also known historically as Kyanol, is a primary aromatic amine that serves as a foundational building block across dye manufacturing, polymer chemistry, and rubber processing.

Its reactivity toward electrophiles and isocyanates makes it a critical intermediate in producing finished industrial materials rather than an end product in itself. In polyurethane production, aniline reacts with formaldehyde to form MDA.

This serves as the precursor to MDI, one of the highest-volume isocyanates used in rigid foam and elastomer manufacturing. Textile and leather processors rely on aniline-derived dyes and azo pigments for stable coloration.

These pigments achieve deep, stable coloration on synthetic and natural fibers. Rubber compounders use aniline-based antioxidants and accelerators to extend service life in tires and industrial belts for heavy machinery.

In flame retardant formulations, aniline derivatives are incorporated into polymer matrices for wire, cable, and construction applications requiring fire performance compliance. This ensures safety across various industrial sectors.

Aniline is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in bulk quantities, typically in drums, IBCs, and ISO tank containers. Technical grade is the dominant commercial specification for most buyers.

Purity levels are generally at 99% or higher for standard industrial use. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available where aniline is required as a specified impurity reference standard for laboratory testing.

name: Calcium acetate
description:
Calcium acetate (CAS 62-54-4 ), also known by the E-number E263 , is an inorganic calcium salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as a preservative, pH buffer, and sequestrant in formulated products.

In food production, E263 controls acidity and extends shelf life in baked goods, confectionery, and processed foods where microbial stability is a formulation priority. This additive is essential for maintaining product integrity over time.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active excipient in phosphate-binding preparations, including branded products such as Phoslyra and PhosLo, targeting renal patient formulations. It is a critical component in specialized medical treatments.

In personal care, it acts as a buffering agent and firming component in creams, gels, and topical formulations requiring controlled pH. These properties ensure the stability and efficacy of various cosmetic and dermatological products.

Industrial applications include its use as a catalyst precursor in acetone production and as a setting agent in textile and paper processing. Its versatility makes it a valuable chemical across multiple manufacturing sectors.

Calcium acetate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with monohydrate being the most commercially prevalent form. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and BP specifications for global supply chains.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial use, with pharmaceutical-grade material subject to stricter purity and documentation requirements. This ensures that all regulatory standards are met for sensitive applications in healthcare.

name: Thiourea
description:
Thiourea (CAS 62-56-6 ) is an organosulfur compound used across chemical synthesis, surface treatment, and industrial processing as a reducing agent, complexing agent, and reaction intermediate.

It functions as a catalyst precursor and auxiliary chemical in processes where controlled sulfur donation or metal ion sequestration is required for specific chemical transformations.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this compound serves as a key intermediate in synthesizing active compounds, including certain antithyroid drugs and antimicrobial agents for medical use.

The printing and packaging industry uses it in photographic fixing baths and toning solutions, where its metal-complexing behavior controls image development chemistry and stability.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a reducing agent for bleaching and surface preparation. It also functions as a catalyst precursor in hydrothermal synthesis routes.

These routes are essential for sulfide-based nanomaterials and pigments. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules available in technical grade for industrial applications.

Higher-purity grades are available meeting pharmaceutical or reagent specifications. Standard packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to bulk industrial quantities.

Purity is typically specified at 99% or above for most commercial grades. This ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing and laboratory environments worldwide.

name: n-nitrosodimethylamine
description:
N-Nitrosodimethylamine (CAS 62-75-9 ), commonly abbreviated as NDMA, is a nitrosamine compound used as a reference standard and analytical reagent in pharmaceutical and life sciences research.

Its primary commercial role is as a certified impurity standard for method development, validation, and quality control testing in drug manufacturing processes across the global industry.

Pharmaceutical QA laboratories use NDMA as a reference standard to detect and quantify nitrosamine impurities in active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished drug products for safety compliance.

This testing is performed in compliance with ICH M7 and regulatory guidance from FDA and EMA. Analytical method development teams rely on it to validate HPLC, GC-MS, and LC-MS/MS procedures.

In biotechnology and life sciences research, it serves as a positive control in genotoxicity and mutagenicity assays, including Ames tests and various in vitro studies for safety profiles.

Contract testing laboratories sourcing NDMA require certified reference materials with traceable purity documentation to meet rigorous regulatory submission standards and audit requirements.

NDMA is supplied as a certified reference standard, typically as a neat liquid or in solution form at defined concentrations in appropriate solvents for laboratory applications.

Material is available under strict regulatory frameworks, with certificates of analysis confirming purity. Supply is restricted to qualified pharmaceutical and research buyers with authorization.

name: Triheptanoin
description:
Triheptanoin (CAS 620-67-7 ), also known as glycerol triheptanoate, is a synthetic triglyceride composed of three heptanoic acid chains esterified to a glycerol backbone. It functions as an emollient, skin-conditioning agent, and carrier in formulations where controlled lipid delivery and oxidative stability are priorities.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it provides a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel in serums, sunscreens, and color cosmetics. It also acts as a solvent for UV filters and oil-soluble actives, offering a high-performance alternative to conventional plant-derived oils.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a carrier oil in topical drug delivery systems and as a medium-chain triglyceride alternative in oral and parenteral nutrition research applications. Its unique structure allows for precise metabolic targeting in clinical settings.

In food and nutraceutical contexts, it serves as a structured lipid for metabolic studies and specialized clinical nutrition products. Its oxidative stability relative to unsaturated oils makes it a preferred carrier in sensitive formulations with long shelf-life requirements.

The material is supplied as a clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical supply typically aligned to GMP manufacturing standards.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D use to bulk drums for commercial production. This versatility ensures that both laboratory-scale development and large-scale industrial manufacturing needs are met with consistent quality and reliable supply chains.

This chemical protects sensitive materials and chemical processes from premature degradation or uncontrolled reaction. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a process stabilizer and inhibitor.

It is highly effective at preventing unwanted polymerization during monomer storage and transport. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate and stabilizer in active ingredient synthesis.

Controlled radical chemistry is critical to product integrity in these applications. In flavor and fragrance formulation, it contributes to oxidative stability of finished blends and aromatic compounds.

Personal care formulators apply it in products requiring antioxidant protection. It helps maintain formulation performance over time and extends the shelf life of sensitive aromatic compounds.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is available in technical and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of industrial applications.

name: Ammonium acryloyldimethyl Taurate homopolymer
description:
Ammonium acryloyldimethyl taurate homopolymer (CAS 62152-14-1 ), also known as ammonium polyacryloyldimethyl taurate, is a synthetic anionic polymer used primarily as a rheology modifier and thickener across aqueous formulation systems.

Its sulfonate functionality delivers effective viscosity control and suspension stability in both electrolyte-sensitive and surfactant-rich environments. In personal care and cosmetics, it thickens lotions, creams, and gels without requiring neutralization.

This makes it compatible with a broad range of pH conditions and ionic systems. Water treatment operations use it as a flocculant to aggregate suspended solids and improve clarification efficiency in industrial effluent processing.

Textile and paper manufacturers apply it as a surface modifier to improve coating adhesion and substrate uniformity during finishing processes. In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, it stabilizes emulsions.

It also suspends active ingredients in liquid detergents and hard-surface cleaners. The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous dispersion, depending on the grade and intended application.

Standard grades are available for cosmetic and industrial use, with cosmetic-grade material commonly evaluated against supplier-specific specifications for viscosity and active content. Packaging is typically offered in bags or drums.

name: Docosahexaenoic acid
description:
Docosahexaenoic acid (CAS 6217-54-5 ), commonly known as DHA, is a long-chain omega-3 fatty acid sourced from marine oils and microalgae. It functions as a bioactive nutritional ingredient in food and pharmaceutical formulations.

In infant formula and functional foods, DHA is incorporated to meet regulatory omega-3 content requirements and support nutritional labeling claims. It is essential for products where omega-3 enrichment is the primary objective.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in softgel capsules and prescription omega-3 concentrates. These products typically target cardiovascular and metabolic health markets requiring high-purity ingredients.

In personal care, DHA is formulated into skin-conditioning products where its fatty acid profile supports barrier repair. It is frequently used in emollient-rich creams and serums to enhance moisturization properties.

Food producers also use it to enrich dairy products, beverages, and fortified snacks. These applications often require encapsulated forms to manage oxidative stability and minimize any potential flavor impact on the final product.

DHA is available as a liquid oil and in microencapsulated powder form. The encapsulated grade is preferred for dry food applications where oxidation control is critical for maintaining shelf life and quality.

Standard supply grades include food-grade, USP , and pharmaceutical-grade concentrations. These typically range from 40% to over 90% DHA content in either ethyl ester or triglyceride forms for various industrial uses.

Algal-derived DHA is also available for vegetarian and vegan-certified supply chains. This ensures that manufacturers can meet specific consumer dietary requirements while maintaining high nutritional standards in their formulations.

name: Benzyloxyethanol
description:
Benzyloxyethanol ( CAS 622-08-2 ), also known as ethylene glycol monobenzyl ether, is a glycol ether solvent used across coatings, personal care, and specialty chemical formulations.

It combines slow evaporation with good solvency, making it effective as a carrier and coalescing agent in systems where controlled drying is commercially important for industrial processes.

In coatings and printing inks, it functions as a high-boiling solvent that improves flow, leveling, and film formation in both waterborne and solvent-based systems for professional use.

Personal care formulators use it as a solvent and carrier in fragrance compositions, emollients, and preservation systems where it supports active delivery and formulation stability across various product lines.

In adhesives and sealants, it aids resin dissolution and controls open time, particularly in systems requiring extended workability during the application phase of construction or manufacturing.

It also appears in UV-stabilizer formulations as a carrier solvent, helping to disperse stabilizing actives uniformly within the final product to ensure long-term durability and performance.

This chemical is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial form, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care applications where tighter impurity profiles are required to meet specific safety and regulatory standards within the global beauty industry.

Myristyl propionate (CAS 6221-95-0 ), also known as tetradecyl propionate, is a fatty acid ester used across personal care and industrial formulations as an emollient and lubricant.

In cosmetics and skincare, it functions as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent in lotions, creams, lip products, and color cosmetics, contributing to smooth application and improved skin feel.

Sunscreen and color cosmetic formulators use it to enhance pigment dispersion and adjust the sensory profile of finished products. It is highly valued for its consistent chemical stability.

name: Terephthalaldehyde

Its two aldehyde groups enable controlled condensation and crosslinking reactions that underpin a range of advanced material and formulation processes. In polymer and materials science, it functions as a monomer for synthesizing polyimines.

It is also utilized for covalent organic frameworks and high-performance resins where precise crosslink density is required. Pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers use it as an intermediate in active ingredient synthesis.

Ethyl methyl carbonate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities. Battery-grade and high-purity electronic grades are the most commercially prominent specifications for industrial use.

These grades feature defined water content and metal ion limits critical for electrolyte applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available from select suppliers where process purity documentation is required.

Biotechnology and fermentation applications also employ DMDS as a sulfur source in microbial culture media. This is particularly useful where controlled sulfur supplementation is required for specific growth.

Dimethyl disulfide is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Food-grade material is available meeting strict industry specifications for safety.

description:
4-Chlorobutanoic acid (CAS 627-00-9 ), also known as 4-chlorobutyric acid and gammachlorobutyric acid, is a halogenated organic acid used primarily as a building block in pharmaceutical synthesis.

This is particularly useful where a four-carbon chain with terminal halogenation is required for cyclization or chain extension reactions. Biotechnology and life sciences researchers use it in the preparation of labeled compounds.

It is also utilized for linkers and probe molecules for drug discovery workflows. The compound also supports agrochemical synthesis, where halogenated acid intermediates are used to produce herbicide and pesticide active substances.

Its chloro group enables nucleophilic substitution reactions that are central to constructing gamma-lactam and pyrrolidone ring systems. These systems are found in several drug scaffolds across the medical industry.

4-Chlorobutanoic acid is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid depending on purity and storage conditions. It is available in technical and high-purity grades suited to pharmaceutical intermediate and research applications.

name: Dibenzoyl-L-tartaric acid monohydrate
description:
Dibenzoyl-L-tartaric acid monohydrate (CAS 62708-56-9 ), commonly abbreviated as L-DBTA, is a chiral resolving agent derived from L-tartaric acid. It is used primarily in pharmaceutical manufacturing to separate racemic mixtures.

The separation occurs through diastereomeric salt formation, allowing for the isolation of enantiomerically pure compounds. L-DBTA is most extensively used in the resolution of chiral amines, amino acids, and alkaloid-type APIs.

This process is essential where a single enantiomer is required for regulatory approval. In active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis, it enables the isolation of target enantiomers at pilot and commercial scale.

By utilizing this resolving agent, manufacturers can avoid the high costs and complexity of chiral chromatography. Biotechnology processes also employ it in the production of chiral building blocks for peptide drug candidates.

It is equally effective for small-molecule drug candidates during the development phase. In specialty chemical manufacturing, it also functions as a chiral catalyst precursor in various asymmetric synthesis workflows.

Dibenzoyl-L-tartaric acid monohydrate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and reagent-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of API manufacturing.

The material is produced to meet rigorous quality standards for research applications. Packaging is typically offered in laboratory quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for process-scale use in industrial facilities.

name: Magnesium laureth sulfate
description:

In shampoos, shower gels, and liquid hand soaps, it produces a dense, stable lather while remaining milder on skin than conventional sodium lauryl sulfate. Formulators use it in baby care and sensitive-skin products where a lower irritation profile is a key selection criterion.

In household and industrial cleaning concentrates, it contributes to soil removal and emulsification of oily residues on hard surfaces. Its compatibility with amphoteric and nonionic co-surfactants also makes it a practical choice for high-active liquid detergent bases.

Magnesium laureth sulfate is typically supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous liquid. Standard active concentrations in the market are 26–28% and around 70%, with the higher-active grade suited to formulators managing transport and storage costs.

The material is valued for its versatility in diverse formulations ranging from high-end cosmetics to industrial degreasers. It maintains performance across a wide pH range and exhibits excellent stability in various aqueous systems.

This compound is essential in the synthesis of nicotinic acid derivatives and fluoride-containing drug candidates. Biotechnology and life sciences laboratories source it as an analytical reagent for assay development and compound screening workflows.

Its buffering capacity makes it suitable for use in formulation research where precise pH control influences active ingredient stability. Contract research organizations and API manufacturers also use it as a building block.

The material is frequently utilized in heterocyclic compound synthesis programs. Nicotinyl alcohol hydrofluoride is typically supplied as a crystalline solid or powder to ensure ease of handling in laboratory settings.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and research-grade specifications to meet the purity requirements of API development and analytical applications. These standards ensure consistency across various manufacturing processes.

name: Amyl acetate
description:
Amyl acetate ( CAS 628-63-7 ), also known as pentyl ethanoate, is an ester solvent and flavoring agent with a characteristic banana-like odor recognized across multiple industries.

It functions primarily as a solvent for coatings, lacquers, and resins, and as a flavoring ingredient in food and fragrance applications. In coatings and lacquer manufacturing, it dissolves nitrocellulose.

This makes it a standard solvent choice for wood finishes and industrial surface coatings. Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring agent to deliver banana, pear, and tropical fruit notes.

It is frequently utilized in confectionery, beverages, and baked goods. In personal care formulations, it functions as a solvent and carrier in nail lacquers and hair products, where its evaporation rate supports film formation.

Metalworking and lubricant formulators also employ it as a carrier solvent in cleaning and surface preparation compounds. Amyl acetate is available as a clear liquid in both technical and food-grade specifications.

Food-grade material is supplied to meet FCC standards, supporting its use in flavor and fragrance applications. It is typically offered in drums and intermediate bulk containers.

Purity levels are commonly at 98% or higher depending on the intended application. This versatile chemical remains a staple for manufacturers requiring reliable solvent performance and specific aromatic profiles.
