It is valued primarily for its ability to modify flow behavior in non-aqueous systems and improve surface release in processing applications. In paints and coatings, it thickens solvent-based formulations and prevents pigment settling.

This additive extends shelf stability without the need for complex reformulation. Plastics processors use it as an internal and external lubricant to reduce friction during extrusion and molding, improving throughput and surface finish.

In grease and lubricant manufacturing, it builds gel structure in hydrocarbon-based systems, controlling consistency and thermal resistance. This ensures high performance in demanding industrial environments and mechanical systems.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into stick products, pressed powders, and anhydrous creams. It provides body and improves texture without the need for water-based emulsification, maintaining product integrity.

The material is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity and metal content specifications varying by application to meet specific manufacturing needs.

Lubricant and coatings grades are the most commonly stocked varieties for industrial use. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific requirements of the supplier and the end user.

name: Ethyl tert-butyl ether
description:
Ethyl tert-butyl ether (CAS 637-92-3 ), commonly known as ETBE, is a fuel oxygenate and blending component produced from bioethanol and isobutylene. It is used primarily to raise the octane rating of gasoline and reduce tailpipe emissions.

In fuel blending, ETBE is incorporated into gasoline at regulated concentrations to meet octane specifications and comply with clean fuel mandates across European and Asian markets. Refiners favor it over MTBE in regions where bio-derived content requirements apply.

Its bioethanol origin supports renewable fuel obligations. In solvent applications, it functions as a low-polarity carrier in specialty coatings, extraction processes, and chemical synthesis where controlled evaporation rate and miscibility are relevant.

Its low water solubility compared to ethanol also reduces groundwater contamination risk. This is a key procurement consideration in environmentally regulated markets where strict safety and environmental standards are enforced for chemical handling.

ETBE is supplied as a liquid in bulk tanker, ISO container, and drummed formats suited to fuel-grade logistics. Fuel-grade is the primary commercial specification, with purity typically at 99%+ for blending applications.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial solvent use, with supply volumes generally tied to refinery or petrochemical production schedules. This ensures a consistent supply chain for large-scale industrial and energy sector operations.

name: Polyglyceryl diisostearate
description:
Polyglyceryl diisostearate (CAS 63705-03-3 ), also marketed as Dehymuls B and Polyglycerol diisostearate, is a polyglycerol ester of isostearic acid used as a lipophilic emulsifier and rheology modifier.

It stabilizes water-in-oil emulsions and controls texture across cosmetic, food, and industrial formulations. In skin care and color cosmetics, it functions as the primary emulsifier in W/O creams and foundations.

It is also utilized in sunscreens, delivering stable emulsions with a smooth, non-greasy skin feel. Lip care and color formulations rely on it for its ability to disperse pigments uniformly while maintaining product consistency.

In food applications, it acts as an emulsifier and dispersing agent in fat-based systems such as chocolate coatings and compound confectionery. This ensures a smooth texture and prevents separation in various food products.

Coatings and adhesive formulations use it to improve dispersion of solid components and adjust flow behavior in oil-continuous systems. This versatility makes it a valuable additive for industrial manufacturing processes.

Polyglyceryl diisostearate is supplied as a viscous liquid or paste at ambient temperature. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available for global distribution and manufacturing.

Cosmetic grades typically meeting requirements for use in regulated personal care markets are standard. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers depending on specific volume requirements for the client.

name: Sodium dipropionate
description:
Sodium dipropionate (CAS 63785-15-9 ), also known as sodium propionate, is the sodium salt of propionic acid used as an antimicrobial preservative and pH buffer across food, feed, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It inhibits mold and bacterial growth in finished products and during processing, extending shelf life without synthetic preservative blends. In baked goods, tortillas, and packaged bread, it controls mold and rope-forming bacteria.

This allows manufacturers to meet commercial shelf-life targets without refrigeration. Animal feed producers incorporate it into grain and compound feeds to suppress fungal contamination during storage and transit.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent and mild preservative in topical preparations and oral solid dosage forms. Food-grade applications also include dairy products and processed meats.

In these sectors, it functions as a secondary hurdle against spoilage organisms. Sodium dipropionate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule, with granulated forms preferred where dust control matters.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and feed-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to USP or BP standards. These ensure compliance with global safety regulations.

Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities suited to industrial-scale procurement. This versatility makes it a staple for large-scale chemical distribution and manufacturing operations worldwide.

name: Acetylated distarch adipate
description:
Acetylated distarch adipate (CAS 63798-35-6 ), also identified as E1422 , is a chemically modified starch produced by dual treatment with acetic anhydride and adipic anhydride.

This dual modification delivers superior freeze-thaw stability and resistance to retrogradation compared to native starches, making it a reliable thickener and stabilizer across demanding food processing environments.

In processed foods, E1422 maintains consistent texture and viscosity in sauces, dressings, soups, and fruit pie fillings that undergo freeze-thaw cycles or high-temperature processing.

Dairy applications such as yogurts, cream-based desserts, and processed cheese benefit from its emulsification and water-binding capacity, which prevents syneresis and phase separation during shelf life.

In the paper and pulp industry, it functions as a surface sizing and coating agent, improving paper strength and printability. Textile manufacturers apply it as a warp sizing agent to reduce yarn breakage.

Acetylated distarch adipate is supplied as a white to off-white powder in food-grade and technical grades. The food-grade specification conforms to FCC and E1422 regulatory standards.

Defined substitution levels govern the acetyl and adipate content within the chemical structure. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on specific application requirements.

name: Manganese diacetate
description:
Manganese diacetate (CAS 638-38-0 ), also known as manganous acetate, is an inorganic manganese salt used across industrial chemistry primarily as a catalyst and metal ion source.

It delivers controlled manganese content in formulations and process baths where precise metal dosing determines product quality. In textile dyeing and leather finishing, it acts as a mordant and oxidation catalyst.

This chemical improves dye fixation and surface uniformity in various industrial applications. Coatings and paint manufacturers use it as a drier catalyst to accelerate oxidative curing in alkyd and oil-based systems.

In agriculture, it supplies manganese as a micronutrient in fertilizer formulations and foliar spray concentrates. This is particularly effective where manganese deficiency correction is the primary target outcome.

Polymer and plastics producers incorporate it as a catalyst in polymerization and condensation reactions. This is essential in processes where transition metal activation is required for high-quality material production.

Manganese diacetate is supplied as a crystalline powder or granules, with tetrahydrate form being the most commercially prevalent. Standard grades include technical and reagent-grade specifications for processing.

Purity levels typically range from technical grade through high-purity grades suited for pharmaceutical and biotechnology use. These products are manufactured to meet rigorous industrial and laboratory standards.

name: Sepiolite
description:
Sepiolite (CAS 63800-37-3 ), also known by the food additive designation E562 , is a naturally occurring fibrous magnesium silicate clay mineral. It functions as a rheology modifier and anti-caking agent across a broad range of industrial and agricultural applications.

In building and construction, sepiolite is incorporated into mortars, renders, and joint compounds to control sag resistance and improve workability without excessive water demand. These properties ensure consistent application and durability in structural finishes.

Agricultural formulators use it as a carrier and flow conditioner for granular pesticides and fertilizers, improving handling and preventing clumping during storage. This ensures that active ingredients remain evenly distributed throughout the application process.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it thickens liquid formulations and suspends active ingredients, maintaining product stability on shelf. This prevents sedimentation and ensures that the product remains effective over its entire lifecycle.

Rubber compounders incorporate sepiolite as a reinforcing filler and processing aid, contributing to dimensional stability in extruded and molded profiles. This improves the mechanical properties and longevity of the final rubber components.

Sepiolite is supplied as a fine powder or micronized powder, with particle size and surface treatment varying by application grade. Technical and industrial grades are the most common commercial forms for large scale manufacturing.

Food-grade material is available under the E562 designation for use in feed and food-contact applications. These grades meet specific purity requirements to ensure safety and compliance with international regulatory frameworks.

Rheological performance grades, including surface-modified variants sold under trade names such as PANGEL, are available for demanding suspension and thickening applications. These specialized grades offer superior performance in complex chemical environments.

name: Potassium sodium tartrate tetrahydrate
description:
Potassium sodium tartrate tetrahydrate (CAS 6381-59-5 ), also known as Rochelle salt and approved as E337 , is a double salt of tartaric acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a buffering agent, chelating agent, and stabilizer in formulated products. In food processing, E337 buffers pH in confectionery, dairy, and baked goods while sequestering metal ions.

These metal ions would otherwise accelerate oxidative spoilage. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient in effervescent formulations and laxative preparations, where its buffering capacity supports product stability.

In personal care, it chelates trace metals in creams and lotions, protecting active ingredients from degradation during shelf life. It also serves as a complexing agent in electroplating baths and analytical reagent applications.

Consistent purity is critical for these industrial uses. Potassium sodium tartrate tetrahydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification.

Pharmaceutical supply meets USP and BP / Ph. Eur. standards. Technical grade is also available for industrial and laboratory use, ensuring versatility across various manufacturing sectors.

name: Sodium erythorbate
description:
Sodium erythorbate (CAS 6381-77-7 ), also sold as sodium isoascorbate and labeled E316 in food applications, is an antioxidant used across food processing and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an oxygen scavenger, preventing oxidative discoloration and rancidity in finished products. In cured and processed meats, it accelerates the color-fixing reaction of nitrites.

This ensures consistent pink coloration and extending shelf life in products like hot dogs, bacon, and deli slices. Beverage manufacturers use it to protect flavor integrity and prevent browning.

It is commonly applied in fruit juices, soft drinks, and canned goods. In frozen seafood and fish processing, it inhibits oxidative spoilage during cold storage and transport for global distribution.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into topical products as an antioxidant stabilizer to protect active ingredients and extend product shelf life in various cosmetic and skincare applications.

Sodium erythorbate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Standard commercial grades include food-grade meeting FCC and BP specifications, with purity typically at 99% or higher.

Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities suited to industrial food processing operations. This versatile chemical remains a staple for maintaining quality and safety in modern manufacturing.

name: Potassium carbonate sesquihydrate

It functions as an alkali and pH buffer across food, agricultural, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications. In food production, it adjusts dough pH in cocoa processing and acts as a leavening agent.

This compound is particularly useful in baked goods where sodium-free formulations are required. Water treatment operations use it to raise pH and reduce corrosivity in distribution systems and boiler feed water.

Agrochemical formulators incorporate it as a potassium source in fertilizer blends and as a buffering agent in crop protection product concentrates. It ensures stability and efficacy in various agricultural settings.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it controls alkalinity during resin synthesis and improves adhesion performance on specific substrates. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial chemical manufacturing.

name: Disodium EDTA dihydrate
description:
Disodium EDTA dihydrate (CAS 6381-92-6 ) is the dihydrate form of the disodium salt of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid, commonly sourced under the abbreviation EDTA disodium. It functions as a chelating and sequestering agent.

By binding metal ions, it prevents oxidation, discoloration, and microbial activity across a broad range of industrial and consumer product applications. In personal care and cosmetics, it stabilizes formulations by deactivating trace metals.

This prevents the degradation of preservatives or the development of rancidity in creams, shampoos, and lotions. Food and beverage manufacturers use it to prevent metal-catalyzed oxidation in canned goods and dressings.

It is particularly effective in seafood products where color and shelf life are critical quality parameters. Water treatment operations deploy it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, controlling scale formation in industrial systems.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it enhances preservative efficacy in ophthalmic and injectable formulations. It achieves this by chelating metal cofactors that support microbial growth in sensitive medical products.

Disodium EDTA dihydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , supporting procurement across various highly regulated industries.

Technical grade is also available for industrial applications such as textile processing and leather treatment. It is widely used in water treatment where specific pharmacopeial certification is not strictly required.

Methyl di-t-butyl hydroxyhydrocinnamate (CAS 6386-38-5 ), commercially known as Irganox 3114's methyl ester counterpart and often sold under the designation Antioxidant 3114M, is a hindered phenolic antioxidant.

It is used to protect polymers, lubricants, and industrial materials from oxidative degradation during processing and end-use. It functions by scavenging free radicals generated by heat and oxygen exposure.

This process extends the service life of finished products. In plastics and polymer processing, it stabilizes polyolefins, engineering resins, and rubber compounds against thermal oxidation during high-temperature extrusion.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it to prevent oxidative breakdown in base oils and synthetic lubricant packages. Coatings and adhesive manufacturers use it to maintain color stability.

It also prevents embrittlement in finished films and bonded assemblies. In printing inks and packaging materials, it guards against oxidative yellowing that would compromise print quality or food-contact compliance.

Methyl di-t-butyl hydroxyhydrocinnamate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid. It is available in technical grade, with purity specifications typically at 98% or above.

name: Artemisinin
description:
Artemisinin (CAS 63968-64-9 ), also known as Qinghaosu or QHS, is a naturally derived sesquiterpene lactone endoperoxide extracted from Artemisia annua. It serves as the foundational starting material for a class of semi-synthetic derivatives.

These derivatives are among the most commercially significant active pharmaceutical ingredients in the antimalarial drug supply chain. The primary commercial demand for this compound is as a pharmaceutical intermediate for chemical conversion.

It is converted into derivatives such as artesunate, artemether, and dihydroartemisinin for inclusion in artemisinin-based combination therapies. Contract manufacturers and API producers source bulk material to feed downstream synthesis pipelines.

These pipelines supply regulated pharmaceutical markets globally. In personal care formulations, it is evaluated as a botanical active in anti-inflammatory and skin-clarifying products targeting oxidative stress pathways.

Fragrance and flavor researchers have also explored its use as a minor ingredient, though pharmaceutical intermediates represent the dominant procurement driver. The material is supplied as an off-white to white crystalline powder.

Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or in-house specifications, with purity levels typically cited at 98% or above by HPLC. This ensures high quality for industrial applications.

Supply is sourced primarily from cultivated Artemisia annua crops, with China and East Africa representing the principal production regions. This geographic diversity helps stabilize the global supply chain for manufacturers.

Water treatment operations use it to control metal ion concentrations and inhibit scale formation in process systems. Pharmaceutical manufacturing employs it as a chelating preservative aid, extending product stability.

This is particularly important in topical and injectable formulations where metal contamination must be tightly controlled. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder and as aqueous solutions, typically at 40% concentration.

name: Formic acid
description:
Formic acid (CAS 64-18-6 ), also known by its E-number E236 , is the simplest carboxylic acid and a commercially significant organic acid used across industrial, agricultural, and food applications.

It functions as a pH regulator, preservative, and processing aid depending on the sector, and its reducing character makes it useful in catalytic and chemical synthesis contexts.

In leather and textile processing, formic acid controls bath pH during dyeing and tanning, directly affecting color uptake and hide quality. This ensures consistent results in large-scale manufacturing.

Silage preservation and animal feed acidification represent major agricultural volume, where it inhibits microbial spoilage and extends shelf life without requiring heat treatment or complex additives.

Food and beverage producers use it as an approved acidulant and preservative, particularly in baked goods, beverages, and dairy applications. It is a versatile tool for maintaining product stability.

In pharmaceuticals and water treatment, it serves as a pH-adjusting agent and intermediate in synthesis. Its chelating capacity supports scale and metal ion control in process water systems.

Formic acid is supplied as an aqueous liquid, with 85% and 94% concentrations being the most commercially standard. Food-grade material is available to FCC and E236 specifications.

Technical-grade product covers industrial and agricultural end uses where high purity is less critical. Bulk supply is typical in IBC containers and road tankers for efficient logistics.

name: Acetic acid
description:
Acetic acid (CAS 64-19-7 ), commercially recognized as E260 , is the primary organic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing. It functions as an acidulant, pH regulator, preservative, and solvent carrier depending on the application sector.

Glacial acetic acid, the concentrated and anhydrous form, is a distinct grade relevant to industrial and synthesis buyers. In food and beverage production, E260 controls pH and acts as a preservative and flavoring agent in condiments, pickles, and sauces.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent in formulations and as a reagent or solvent in active ingredient synthesis. In textile and leather processing, it regulates dye bath pH to improve fiber uptake and fixation.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair rinses and toners where controlled acidity affects cuticle conditioning and product stability. Acetic acid is supplied as a liquid in concentrations typically ranging from 56% to 99.5%.

Recognized grades include Food Grade ( FCC ), USP / BP for pharmaceutical use, and technical grade for industrial applications. Bulk supply is standard in IBC containers and road tankers for large scale operations.

name: Diethyl sulfate
description:
Diethyl sulfate ( CAS 64-67-5 ), also known as DES, is a reactive diethyl ester of sulfuric acid used industrially as an ethylating agent. It transfers ethyl groups to amines, alcohols, and other nucleophiles.

This functionality enables the synthesis of ethylated intermediates across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and specialty chemical manufacturing. In pharmaceutical synthesis, DES alkylates active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates.

It is particularly useful where controlled ethylation is required at scale. Agrochemical producers use it to manufacture ethylated herbicide and pesticide intermediates, especially where other agents present disadvantages.

In personal care chemistry, DES supports the production of ethylated surfactants and conditioning agents used in finished formulations. It also functions as a solvent and carrier in select chemical processes.

The reactivity profile of this compound must be compatible with the target substrate for optimal results. Diethyl sulfate is supplied as a liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial consumption.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly at 99% minimum. Buyers sourcing for pharmaceutical intermediate production should confirm supplier documentation carefully.

Ensure all materials meet applicable regulatory requirements for your specific jurisdiction. This product is a critical component for high-volume chemical synthesis and industrial manufacturing applications worldwide.

name: Lactose monohydrate
description:
Lactose monohydrate (CAS 64044-51-5 ) is a natural milk-derived sugar supplied as a crystalline powder across food and pharmaceutical markets. Grades such as Pharmatose DCL 11 and Pharmatose 90M are recognized specifications in tablet manufacturing.

Zeparox designates a specific milling grade for dry powder inhalation. Its primary industrial role is as a carrier, diluent, and mild sweetener rather than a primary flavoring agent in most commercial applications.

In solid dose pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a tablet filler and binder, providing compressibility and flow properties that support high-speed tableting lines. These features are essential for modern production.

Inhalation-grade variants are used in dry powder inhalers as a carrier particle to deliver active pharmaceutical ingredients to the lungs. In food production, it acts as a mild sweetener and bulking agent.

Common food uses include infant formula, confectionery coatings, and dairy-based products. Nutraceutical and supplement manufacturers use it as a diluent in capsule and sachet formulations where a clean flavor profile is required.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in a range of particle size distributions tailored to end-use requirements. Established quality standards include Ph. Eur. , USP /NF, BP , and FCC .

These certifications cover both pharmaceutical and food applications globally. Inhalation-specific and direct-compression grades are available for specialized manufacturing processes to ensure consistent performance and safety.

name: Aminotrimethylene phosphonic acid
description:
Aminotrimethylene phosphonic acid (CAS 6419-19-8 ), commercially known as ATMP, is a phosphonate chelating agent used across industrial water and process chemistry. It controls scale deposition and inhibits corrosion in systems where mineral buildup and metal degradation are operational concerns.

In water treatment, ATMP prevents calcium carbonate, calcium sulfate, and barium sulfate scale in cooling towers, boilers, and reverse osmosis systems by threshold inhibition and crystal modification.

Oil and gas operations rely on it as a scale inhibitor in oilfield injection water and produced water handling, where mineral precipitation can block pipelines and reduce flow efficiency.

Textile and paper processing use ATMP to sequester hardness ions in process water, preventing interference with dyeing, bleaching, and pulp treatment chemistry in various industrial environments.

In metalworking and mining, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and chelating agent in circulating water systems and mineral processing circuits to ensure long-term equipment durability and performance.

ATMP is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at 50% active content, and as a solid crystalline powder for applications requiring concentrated or dry formulations for specific manufacturing needs.

Technical grade is the standard offering across most industrial segments. Specifications are typically aligned with industry performance benchmarks rather than pharmacopeial standards like USP or FCC .

Given its primarily industrial end-use profile, the material is handled according to standard chemical safety protocols to maintain high efficiency in large-scale cooling and heating applications.

name: Dioctyl terephthalate
description:
Dioctyl terephthalate ( CAS 6422-86-2 ), commercially known as DOTP and also marketed as Di-(2-ethylhexyl) terephthalate or DEHT, is a non-phthalate plasticizer used across PVC compounding and polymer processing.

It delivers flexibility and durability to finished materials while meeting increasingly strict regulatory requirements for phthalate-free formulations. In PVC compounding, DOTP is the primary alternative to DEHP.

It is used in flexible films, cables, flooring, and medical-grade tubing where phthalate restrictions apply. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to improve elongation and low-temperature performance.

These applications are common in construction and automotive assembly. Coatings manufacturers use it as a plasticizing modifier to reduce brittleness in industrial and protective coatings without compromising film integrity.

Personal care formulators apply it as a solvent and plasticizer in nail lacquers and film-forming cosmetic products. DOTP is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in bulk, IBC, and drum packaging.

It is available in technical and industrial grades, with select suppliers offering material conforming to REACH compliance documentation and RoHS requirements. Specifications typically align with established plasticizer purity standards.

Purity levels are commonly at 99% or higher. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing sectors requiring high-quality chemical inputs for their specialized production processes.

name: Sodium isostearate
description:
Sodium isostearate (CAS 64248-79-9 ), also known as sodium isooctadecanoate, is the sodium salt of isostearic acid, a branched-chain fatty acid derivative. It functions as an emulsifier, surfactant, and skin-conditioning agent across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its branched structure prevents the crystallization issues common with straight-chain fatty acid soaps, giving formulators greater flexibility in texture and stability. In personal care, it is used to build bar soaps, stick deodorants, and anhydrous formulations.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into emollient creams and color cosmetics to improve spreadability and skin feel without the drag associated with saturated soap bases. It is ideal for products where a non-waxy, pliable consistency is required.

In coatings and sealant systems, it functions as a dispersant and wetting agent for pigments and fillers, improving substrate adhesion and coating uniformity. This ensures a more consistent application and finish across various industrial surfaces.

Textile and leather processing operations use it as a softening and surface-modification agent to enhance material hand and finish quality. Its chemical properties allow for deep penetration and lasting softness in high-end fabric treatments.

Sodium isostearate is typically supplied as a paste or soft solid, reflecting the liquid nature of its parent isostearic acid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of diverse buyers.

Packaging is commonly offered in drums or totes suited to mid- to large-volume procurement. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for manufacturers requiring reliable surfactant and emulsification solutions.

name: Dimorpholinodiethyl ether
description:
Dimorpholinodiethyl ether (CAS 6425-39-4 ), commonly known by its abbreviation DMDEE, is a tertiary amine compound used as a reactive catalyst in polyurethane and polymer systems.

It accelerates curing reactions, particularly in moisture-triggered and one-component formulations, without requiring post-cure removal. This makes it a primary catalyst choice in one-component polyurethane sealants.

In these applications, it drives moisture-cure reactions at ambient temperature to achieve fast skin formation and through-cure. In construction and building products, it enables reliable cure performance.

This includes roofing membranes, joint sealants, and gap fillers across variable humidity conditions. Polyurethane foam systems, including spray foam insulation, use it to balance gel and blow reactions.

This gives formulators control over cell structure and rise time. Its reactivity profile also suits crosslinking applications in elastomers and coatings where controlled cure onset is a requirement.

The product is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purity levels, typically 98% or higher. It is available in technical grade, the standard specification for industrial catalyst applications.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes, with bulk options available depending on volume requirements. This ensures flexibility for various manufacturing scales and logistical needs in the chemical industry.

name: Phthalaldehyde
description:
o-Phthalaldehyde (CAS 643-79-8 ), commonly abbreviated as OPA, is an aromatic dialdehyde used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a high-level disinfectant and chemical intermediate.

This material is highly valued for its reactivity with amine-containing compounds. In healthcare settings, OPA is the active biocidal agent in cold sterilization solutions for heat-sensitive medical instruments, particularly endoscopes.

It often outperforms glutaraldehyde in speed and efficacy for clinical applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic building block in the production of APIs and heterocyclic compounds where dual aldehyde groups enable reactions.

These dual groups allow for controlled condensation reactions during synthesis. In analytical chemistry and diagnostics, OPA serves as a fluorometric reagent for detecting primary amines and amino acids in HPLC workflows.

Personal care formulators have explored its antimicrobial properties in preservation systems for rinse-off and professional-use products. OPA is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid for various industrial uses.

Liquid solution forms are also available for ready-to-use disinfectant applications. Standard commercial grades include high-purity synthesis-grade material suitable for pharmaceutical intermediates and solution concentrates.

These concentrates are formulated to defined active concentrations for medical device disinfection. Buyers should confirm purity specifications against USP or equivalent compendial standards depending on requirements.

name: Activated carbon
description:
Activated carbon (CAS 64365-11-3 ), also sold as activated charcoal and carrying the food colorant designation E153 , is a high-surface-area adsorbent material produced from carbonaceous sources.

It is manufactured from coal, coconut shell, or wood to capture contaminants, odors, colors, and dissolved organics across a broad range of industrial processes and purification systems.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, it removes chlorine, chloramines, pesticides, and trace organic compounds from drinking water and process streams to ensure safety and compliance.

Food and beverage producers use it to decolorize sugar syrups, edible oils, and fermentation liquors, meeting strict purity targets before final processing and distribution to consumers.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it for API purification, solvent recovery, and removal of color bodies or impurities from intermediates during the complex chemical synthesis stages.

In mining, it is central to gold recovery via carbon-in-pulp and carbon-in-leach circuits, where it adsorbs dissolved gold from cyanide leach solutions for efficient extraction.

Activated carbon is supplied as granular activated carbon (GAC), powdered activated carbon (PAC), and extruded or pelletized forms. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E153-compliant).

Other available standards include USP / BP pharmaceutical grade and technical grade. Coconut shell, coal, and wood variants are available to meet specific pore structure requirements.

It prevents spoilage during storage and transport for water-based paints, sealants, and latex systems. These systems incorporate DMDMH to protect against bacterial and fungal degradation that would compromise viscosity.

It is also used in wet-state preservation of adhesive and elastomer compounds where conventional biocides lack sufficient water compatibility. This ensures long-term stability in complex chemical mixtures.

name: Histidine monohydrochloride
description:
Histidine monohydrochloride (CAS 645-35-2 ), also marketed as Histidine HCl, is the hydrochloride salt form of the essential amino acid L-histidine. Its salt form offers improved solubility and stability compared to the free base.

This makes it the preferred form for pharmaceutical manufacturing and precision nutrition applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Histidine HCl is used as a buffering agent in biologic drug formulations.

It is particularly useful for monoclonal antibodies and protein-based injectables, where it stabilizes pH and protects active compounds during storage. Parenteral nutrition solutions incorporate it as a source of this amino acid.

It is also used in combination vitamin preparations targeting deficiency treatment and prophylaxis. Nutritional supplement and functional food producers incorporate it into multivitamin blends and fortified cereals.

It is found in infant formula and sports nutrition products to meet declared B6 label claims. Cosmetic formulators use it in scalp treatments and anti-hair loss serums where B6 activity supports keratinocyte function.

The material also serves as a pharmaceutical intermediate in the synthesis of Pyridoxal-5-Phosphate, the active coenzyme form. It is commercially supplied as a white crystalline powder, most commonly as Pyridoxine Hydrochloride.

This salt form is preferred for its improved stability and water solubility in finished dosage forms. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , covering pharmaceutical and food-grade requirements.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial-scale manufacturing, with fine particle specifications offered for direct compression. These grades ensure compliance with global quality standards for diverse industrial applications.

name: Benzoic acid
description:
Benzoic acid (CAS 65-85-0 ), also designated E210 in food and beverage applications, is a naturally occurring organic acid used commercially as a preservative and pH regulator.

Its antimicrobial action against yeasts, moulds, and bacteria makes it a standard functional ingredient across food, personal care, and industrial formulations worldwide.

In food and beverage production, E210 controls microbial growth in acidic products such as soft drinks, fruit juices, and condiments, where it is effective at low concentrations.

Personal care formulators use it as a preservative and pH adjuster in rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos, lotions, and liquid soaps for consumer safety.

Coatings and resin manufacturers use benzoic acid as a chain-stopper and catalyst component in alkyd resin production, influencing molecular weight and drying performance.

In pharmaceuticals, it functions as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients and as a preservative in topical preparations for various medical applications.

Benzoic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or flake. Commercially available grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , BP , Ph.Eur. ).

Technical-grade options are available for industrial applications. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities, supported by full compliance documentation for all sectors.

name: Quaternium-82
description:
Quaternium-82 (CAS 65059-61-2 ) is a quaternary ammonium compound used in personal care formulations as a conditioning and surface-modifying agent. It functions by adsorbing onto negatively charged surfaces.

This chemical improves wettability, spreadability, and emulsion stability in finished products. In hair care, it is used in conditioners and leave-in treatments to deposit a conditioning film on the hair shaft.

The compound is effective at reducing static and improving combability for various hair types. Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and creams where controlled emulsification is required.

It ensures uniform ingredient dispersion throughout the formulation. It also functions as a wetting agent in rinse-off systems, helping active ingredients contact the skin or scalp surface more effectively.

Specialty formulations such as styling products and treatment serums use it to modify surface tension. This modification helps to improve the overall product feel during and after application.

The material is typically supplied as a liquid or solution, with concentration and carrier solvent varying by manufacturer. It is available in cosmetic-grade quality aligned with industry standards.

Buyers should confirm active content percentage and recommended use levels directly with the supplier. Commercial specifications can differ across sources depending on the specific production method.

name: Cetrimonium methosulfate
description:
Cetrimonium methosulfate (CAS 65060-02-8 ), also known commercially as CRODAZOSOFT DBQ, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a conditioning agent and emulsifier across personal care and industrial formulations.

It deposits onto negatively charged surfaces such as hair, skin, and fibers to reduce static, improve softness, and stabilize emulsions. In hair care, it is the active conditioning agent in rinse-off conditioners and shampoos.

It is frequently used in treatment masks where it smooths the cuticle and reduces combing friction. Fabric softeners and textile finishing formulations use it to impart softness and antistatic properties to synthetic and natural fibers.

In skin care, it functions as an emulsifier and stabilizer in creams and lotions, helping maintain emulsion integrity over shelf life. Leather and paper processing operations apply it as a surface modifier.

These industrial applications help to improve feel, flexibility, and surface uniformity across various substrates. Cetrimonium methosulfate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on concentration and formulation.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements suitable for leave-on and rinse-off personal care products. Standard packaging includes drums and IBC containers for bulk procurement.

name: Casein hydrolyzate
description:
Casein hydrolyzate (CAS 65072-00-6 ), also marketed under the trade name N-Z Amine, is produced by enzymatic or acid hydrolysis of casein protein. This process yields a mixture of peptides and free amino acids.

It functions as a bioavailable nitrogen source and flavor contributor across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications. In food manufacturing, it delivers savory, umami-forward flavor profiles to soups and sauces.

It is frequently used in seasonings and processed meat products where clean-label protein hydrolysates are specified. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use it as a nitrogen source in culture media.

It also serves as a peptide ingredient in clinical nutrition products targeting protein supplementation. In animal feed and agricultural fermentation, it supports microbial growth as a readily metabolized nitrogen substrate.

It is used in fermentation broths and starter culture media. Infant formula and sports nutrition manufacturers source it as a partially hydrolyzed protein fraction to improve digestibility and reduce allergenicity.

Casein hydrolyzate is supplied as a cream to tan-colored powder, with particle size and solubility profiles varying by manufacturer. Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications.

Select suppliers offer USP or FCC -compliant material. Degree of hydrolysis and nitrogen content are key specification parameters buyers should confirm when evaluating lots for fermentation use.

These parameters are also critical for clinical nutrition applications. Proper sourcing ensures the material meets the necessary requirements for high-performance industrial and nutritional formulations.

name: Calcium thioglycolate trihydrate
description:
Calcium thioglycolate trihydrate (CAS 65208-41-5 ), also known as thioglycolic acid calcium salt trihydrate, is an inorganic salt used as a reducing and depilatory active in personal care and pharmaceutical formulations.

It disrupts disulfide bonds in keratin, enabling hair removal and protein modification at controlled pH levels. In depilatory creams and lotions, it functions as the primary active ingredient.

The compound breaks down the structural integrity of hair at the skin surface for chemical removal without mechanical action. Pharmaceutical formulators use it where controlled keratin-disrupting activity is required in topical preparations.

It also appears in professional cosmetic treatments targeting hair restructuring, where precise bond reduction is needed before neutralization. Cold wave and permanent wave formulations represent another documented end-use.

In professional salon products, bond reduction must be consistent across hair types. Calcium thioglycolate trihydrate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with purity specifications typically aligned to personal care manufacturing requirements. Packaging is offered in kilogram-scale quantities suited to procurement.

name: Pigment yellow 65
description:
Pigment Yellow 65 (CAS 6528-34-3 ) is a monoazo yellow pigment used to deliver bright, warm yellow hues across a range of industrial colorant systems. Known in trade as PY65, it belongs to the acetoacetarylide class.

It is valued for its clean masstone and reliable color strength in demanding manufacturing processes. In plastics and polymer compounding, PY65 provides consistent yellow coloration in rigid and flexible substrates.

Processing temperatures require reasonable heat stability for these applications. Coatings formulators incorporate it into industrial paints and decorative finishes where a reddish-yellow tone and good hiding power are priorities.

Printing ink manufacturers use it in packaging inks, particularly solvent-based and offset systems, where color reproducibility across print runs is critical. This ensures high quality and consistency for large scale production.

Textile and paper dyeing operations also draw on PY65 for surface coloration and pigment-printed fabric applications. It offers versatility across multiple sectors requiring durable and vibrant yellow pigments for various materials.

Pigment Yellow 65 is supplied as a dry powder, typically in press cake or flushed paste form depending on the downstream application. Standard commercial grades are available for plastics, coatings, and ink use.

name: 1-(1-naphthylmethyl)quinolinium chloride
description:
1-(1-Naphthylmethyl)quinolinium chloride (CAS 65322-65-8 ) is a quaternary ammonium salt used as a specialty reagent in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research. It functions as a charged heterocyclic building block and ionic species capable of pH-modulating activity in controlled research environments.

In pharmaceutical research, it serves as a reference compound or synthetic intermediate in the development of quinolinium-based active pharmaceutical ingredients. Biotechnology laboratories use it in assay development and biochemical screening where structurally defined quaternary nitrogen compounds are required.

Its well-defined ionic character makes it applicable in buffer system studies where cationic species influence solution pH behavior at the research scale. It also appears in the synthesis of novel heterocyclic libraries targeting receptor binding studies.

1-(1-Naphthylmethyl)quinolinium chloride is supplied as a solid powder, typically in high-purity research grades suited to laboratory and pharmaceutical development use. Standard offerings are positioned at ≥97% or ≥98% purity, consistent with pharmaceutical reference and synthetic intermediate applications.

Packaging is generally available in small quantities ranging from milligram to multi-gram scale, reflecting its primary use in R&D rather than bulk industrial production. This chemical is handled according to standard laboratory safety protocols for quaternary ammonium compounds.

The compound is valued for its stability and predictable behavior in organic synthesis and analytical chemistry. Researchers utilize its unique naphthylmethyl substitution to explore specific molecular interactions within complex biological or chemical systems.

name: Pigment red 112
description:
Pigment Red 112 (CAS 6535-46-2 ), also marketed as Permanent Red FGR, Naphthol Red FGR, and Luconyl Red 3855, is a high-performance azo pigment delivering strong red coloration across a broad range of industrial substrates.

It is valued in demanding applications for its color strength, heat stability, and resistance to migration. In coatings and industrial paints, it produces vivid, opaque red shades with good lightfastness suitable for both solvent-borne and water-borne systems.

Plastics processors incorporate it into polyolefins, PVC, and engineering polymers where consistent color development and thermal stability during processing are critical. Printing ink manufacturers use it in packaging inks, particularly for flexible packaging.

This pigment is ideal where sharp hue and printability on film substrates are required. Textile and leather finishers apply it in pigment printing pastes and surface coatings to achieve uniform, durable red tones across various materials.

Pigment Red 112 is supplied as a dry powder, and press cake forms are available from select producers for wet-process ink and coating applications. This versatility allows for seamless integration into different manufacturing workflows.

description:
Glyceryl caprylate caprate (CAS 65381-09-1 ), commonly sourced and traded as MCT, is a mixed ester of glycerol with caprylic and capric fatty acids derived primarily from coconut or palm kernel oil.

It functions as a carrier, emollient, and solubilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In nutritional supplements, MCT serves as a calorie-dense carrier oil for fat-soluble vitamins.

It is also used for flavors and active ingredients requiring efficient dispersion. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a lipid vehicle in soft-gel capsules, oral solutions, and topical drug delivery systems.

This is particularly useful where a non-aqueous solvent with low viscosity is required. In personal care, it acts as a lightweight skin-conditioning base in serums, creams, and color cosmetics.

It provides excellent spreadability without greasiness. Industrial lubricant applications include biodegradable base fluids and release agents where low toxicity and oxidative stability are procurement priorities.

Glyceryl caprylate caprate is supplied as a clear, odorless liquid. Standard market grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP /NF and Ph. Eur. ), and cosmetic or technical grades.

name: Polyethylene glycol lauryl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol lauryl ether (CAS 6540-99-4 ) is a nonionic surfactant used across industrial and personal care formulations for emulsification, foam control, and cleaning. It functions as both a surface-active agent and a carrier solvent.

This versatile chemical enables the stable dispersion of oils, pigments, and actives in aqueous systems. In personal care and cosmetics, it emulsifies oil-in-water systems in creams, lotions, and cleansing products.

The compound contributes significantly to texture and ingredient compatibility in high-end formulations. Textile and leather processing operations use it to improve dye penetration and as a scouring agent to remove oils.

It effectively removes contaminants from fiber surfaces during industrial manufacturing. In printing and packaging, it supports ink dispersion and acts as a defoamer in coating formulations where foam buildup disrupts quality.

Water treatment applications rely on it as a defoaming and dispersing agent in process water circuits. Polyethylene glycol lauryl ether is supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on the ethoxylation degree.

name: Polacrilin potassium
description:
Polacrilin potassium (CAS 65405-55-2 ) is a crosslinked potassium salt of methacrylic acid copolymerized with divinylbenzene. It is used in pharmaceutical manufacturing as a tablet disintegrant and ion exchange resin.

Sold under the trade name Amberlite IRP88, it is a recognized excipient in solid dosage form development. In tablet and capsule manufacturing, it functions as a superdisintegrant by absorbing water rapidly.

This action promotes tablet breakup and improves active ingredient release. Formulators use it in chewable tablets and orally disintegrating tablet formats where fast disintegration without excessive swelling is required.

It also serves in drug purification and controlled-release systems as a cation exchange resin. It binds basic drug molecules to modify release profiles in various pharmaceutical applications.

Pediatric and veterinary oral solid formulations use it where taste masking is a goal. It provides reliable disintegration while ensuring the final product meets specific patient compliance standards.

The material is supplied as a fine, off-white to cream-colored powder. It is available in USP /NF and Ph. Eur. compendial grades, which are the standard specifications demanded by procurement.

These quality standards ensure the material is suitable for regulated pharmaceutical environments. Packaging is typically offered in fiber drums suited to GMP manufacturing environments and long-term storage.

description:
Sitagliptin phosphate (CAS 654671-78-0 ) is the phosphate salt form of sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor active pharmaceutical ingredient developed for the management of type 2 diabetes.

Sitagliptin phosphate monohydrate is the primary commercially distributed hydrate form, while the anhydrous grade serves distinct formulation requirements for pharmaceutical manufacturers.

Both forms are sourced by pharmaceutical manufacturers and API importers as the basis for finished oral dosage production. The compound is the active ingredient in oral antidiabetic tablet formulations.

It functions as the DPP-4 enzyme inhibitor delivering the therapeutic effect. Contract manufacturers and generic drug producers source it to develop bioequivalent products following patent expiry.

It is also used in fixed-dose combination tablets paired with metformin, requiring compatibility evaluation. Analytical and QA laboratories procure reference-grade material for method validation.

Sitagliptin phosphate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder in both monohydrate and anhydrous forms. Standard grades include API-grade material manufactured under ICH Q7 GMP guidelines.

description:
Guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride (CAS 65497-29-2 ) is a cationic guar derivative used across personal care and industrial markets. It deposits a conditioning film on negatively charged surfaces through electrostatic attraction.

This mechanism drives its use as a conditioning and rheology-modifying agent in rinse-off and leave-on formulations. In shampoos and conditioners, it reduces combing friction and improves wet detangling without weighing hair down.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and cleansers where it provides moisturization and a smooth after-feel. In textile processing, it functions as a softening and antistatic agent applied during finishing.

The chemical improves fabric handle and is also utilized by paper and leather manufacturers. These industries use it to modify surface charge and improve wet strength or binding performance in their respective processing steps.

Guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride is supplied as a free-flowing off-white to cream powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suitable for personal care formulations with varying charge densities.

name: Glyceryl monoundecylenate
description:
Glyceryl monoundecylenate (CAS 65684-27-7 ), also known as glyceryl 10-undecenoate, is a monoester of glycerol and undecylenic acid used across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

It functions as an emulsifier, humectant, and lubricant, derived from a naturally sourced fatty acid with a reactive unsaturated chain that supports further chemical modification for various industrial uses.

In personal care, it is incorporated into skin creams, lotions, and leave-on treatments where it contributes both emulsification and moisture retention to the finished formula for better skin feel.

Food-grade applications include use as an emulsifying agent in fat-based systems and confectionery coatings where controlled texture and stability are required for high-quality food production.

In lubricant and metalworking formulations, its ester structure provides boundary lubrication and surface adhesion on metal substrates, ensuring high performance in demanding mechanical environments.

The reactive double bond also makes it a functional building block in coatings, adhesives, and sealant systems where crosslinkable bio-based intermediates are specified for sustainable manufacturing.

Glyceryl monoundecylenate is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting paste depending on purity and temperature conditions. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications.

Industrial technical grades are also offered for coatings and lubricant applications where food or cosmetic compliance is not required, meeting formulator requirements across all regulated markets.

description:
L-Lysine monohydrochloride (CAS 657-27-2 ), commonly sourced as L-Lysine hydrochloride, is the stabilized salt form of the essential amino acid lysine. It offers improved handling and solubility over the free base form.

It functions as a nutritional supplement, feed additive, and bioactive ingredient across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural markets. In animal feed, it corrects lysine deficiency in cereal-based diets for swine and poultry.

This directly improves feed conversion ratios and protein utilization. Food and beverage manufacturers use it to fortify protein-enriched products, meal replacements, and functional nutrition formulations where lysine is the first limiting amino acid.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as an active or excipient in tablet and oral solution manufacturing. This is particularly useful where controlled pH buffering of the final dosage form is required for stability.

In personal care, it appears in topical formulations and hair care products as a conditioning agent and moisture-retention support ingredient. L-Lysine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

name: Sodium p-toluenesulfonate
description:
Sodium p-toluenesulfonate (CAS 657-84-1 ), also known as sodium tosylate, is an aromatic sulfonate salt used across industrial and specialty chemical applications. It functions primarily as a hydrotrope, coupling agent, and catalyst precursor in aqueous and solvent-based systems.

In textile and leather processing, it improves dye solubility and penetration, enabling more uniform color uptake across fiber substrates. Coatings and ink formulations use it as a hydrotrope to stabilize pigment dispersions and prevent phase separation.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into surfactant blends to adjust viscosity and enhance the solubility of active ingredients in cleansing and conditioning products. It also serves as a precursor or co-catalyst in synthesis processes where a stable source is required.

Sodium p-toluenesulfonate is available as a white crystalline powder or granule, with both anhydrous and hydrate forms supplied commercially. Standard grades include technical and high-purity specifications for various industrial needs.

As a versatile chemical intermediate, it supports the production of diverse specialty chemicals. Its role as a hydrotrope ensures that complex formulations remain homogeneous under varying temperature and concentration conditions during storage and use.

name: Hexamidine diisethionate
description:
Hexamidine diisethionate (CAS 659-40-5 ), also sold as hexamidine isethionate, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used in pharmaceutical and cosmetic formulations. It targets bacteria, fungi, and protozoa, making it a reliable preservative and biocide.

In topical products where microbial control is a formulation requirement, this compound provides consistent efficacy. In cosmetics, it functions as a preservative in rinse-off and leave-on products including shampoos and facial cleansers.

It is frequently utilized as a paraben-free alternative in moisturizers and other personal care items. Topical pharmaceutical preparations, such as antiseptic creams and eye drops, use it as the primary antimicrobial active at low effective concentrations.

name: Oxidized starch
description:
Oxidized starch (CAS 65996-62-5 ) is a chemically modified starch produced by treating native starch with oxidizing agents to introduce carbonyl and carboxyl groups into the polymer chain.

The modification reduces viscosity, improves film-forming capacity, and increases paste clarity compared to native starch. These properties make it a functional binder and coating agent across paper, textile, food, and construction applications.

In paper manufacturing, it is applied at the size press or in surface coating formulations to improve paper smoothness, ink holdout, and surface strength. Textile mills use it as a warp sizing agent for efficient yarn coating.

Its lower viscosity at higher solids content allows for effective processing without excessive stiffening. In food production, it functions as a thickener and stabilizer in sauces, puddings, and various processed foods.

It is particularly useful where a clean, low-viscosity paste is required. Construction adhesives and gypsum board formulations incorporate it as a binder to control rheology and improve adhesion to mineral substrates.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder derived from corn, potato, tapioca, or wheat starch bases. Food-grade material is available meeting FCC specifications for global compliance.

Technical grades are supplied for industrial paper and textile applications. Degree of oxidation and viscosity grade vary by application, and suppliers typically offer multiple viscosity profiles to match specific process requirements.

name: Calcined phosphate rock
description:
Calcined phosphate rock (CAS 65996-94-3 ), also known commercially as Phospal and Calciphos, is a thermally processed mineral used as a slow-release phosphorus source and soil pH corrective in agricultural markets.

The calcination process converts raw phosphorite into a more reactive form, improving phosphorus availability to crops without the rapid leaching associated with soluble fertilizers.

In crop nutrition programs, it functions as a direct-application phosphate fertilizer for acidic soils, supplying phosphorus and calcium over extended growing cycles for various crops.

Animal feed manufacturers incorporate it as a mineral supplement to meet phosphorus and calcium requirements in livestock and poultry diets, ensuring proper bone development and health.

Water treatment operations use it in pH adjustment and phosphate dosing applications, particularly where controlled, gradual release is preferred over soluble phosphate salts in the system.

It also serves as a raw material input for downstream phosphate chemical production where a calcined, low-organic mineral source is specified for high-purity industrial manufacturing processes.

Calcined phosphate rock is supplied as a fine to medium powder, with particle size typically tailored to application requirements. Feed-grade and fertilizer-grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms.

P2O5 content and heavy metal limits define grade boundaries for procurement. Technical-grade material is available for industrial and water treatment procurement to meet specific operational needs.

name: Hydrogenated Rosin
description:
Hydrogenated Rosin (CAS 65997-06-0 ) is a chemically stabilized resin derived from pine-sourced gum or wood rosin through catalytic hydrogenation. This process significantly reduces the acid value variability and oxidative instability of natural rosin.

The resulting resin offers consistent performance across demanding formulation environments. It functions primarily as a tackifier, plasticizer, and rheology modifier in adhesive, coating, and rubber compounding systems.

In pressure-sensitive and hot-melt adhesives, it improves tack and peel strength while offering better color stability and aging resistance than unmodified rosin grades. This makes it ideal for long-term applications.

Rubber compounders incorporate it as a softener and processing aid in tire and mechanical goods manufacturing. Controlled viscosity and compatibility with elastomer matrices are critical factors in these industrial processes.

In printing inks and overprint varnishes, it contributes to film formation, gloss, and substrate adhesion across paper and packaging substrates. It ensures high-quality finishes and durable bonding for various media.

Textile sizing and paper coating formulations also use it to modify surface properties and improve fiber or substrate bonding. Its versatility allows for precise adjustments in specialized manufacturing sectors.

The material is supplied as a pale yellow to water-white solid, typically in flake or block form. It is available in technical and food-contact grades, with specifications aligned to FCC and USP standards.

Acid value and softening point are the primary grade-defining parameters buyers should confirm against application requirements. These technical specifications ensure the product meets the necessary performance criteria.

name: Glyceryl rosinate
description:
Glyceryl rosinate (CAS 65997-13-9 ) is a hydrogenated rosin ester produced by reacting glycerol with refined rosin acids, resulting in a pale, thermally stable resin. It functions as a tackifier, plasticizer, and emulsifier across adhesive, cosmetic, and rubber compounding applications.

In personal care, it anchors pigments and waxes in lip products, mascaras, and depilatory waxes, improving adhesion to skin and hair. Rubber compounders incorporate it to improve tack and processing flow in tire and technical rubber formulations.

Printing ink manufacturers use it as a resin binder and film-forming component in solvent-based and heat-set ink systems. In pressure-sensitive adhesives and hot-melt formulations, it improves bond strength and compatibility with polymer matrices.

The material is highly compatible with polymers such as SIS and EVA, making it a versatile choice for industrial bonding. It provides excellent thermal stability and resistance to oxidation during high-temperature processing cycles.

Glyceryl rosinate is supplied as pale yellow to amber solid flakes, pellets, or blocks. Technical and cosmetic-grade material is available, with cosmetic-grade product meeting purity requirements relevant to personal care formulation standards.

name: Hexanal
description:
Hexanal (CAS 66-25-1 ), also known as n-Caproaldehyde and carrying FEMA number 2557 , is a short-chain aliphatic aldehyde used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient.

It delivers a characteristic fresh, green, grassy note that underpins a broad range of consumer product formulations. In food and beverage flavoring, it contributes to the fresh, cut-grass character of fruit flavors.

This is particularly useful in apple, citrus, and tomato profiles where it is used at trace concentrations to enhance naturalness. Fragrance compounders incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional fragrance bases.

It adds green top-note lift, especially in floral and chypre compositions. In personal care, it appears in shampoos, body washes, and household cleaners where a fresh, natural-green olfactive character is required.

It also serves as a reference standard and process marker in food quality research. Hexanal concentration is monitored as an indicator of lipid oxidation in packaged foods to ensure product stability.

The material is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in flavor and fragrance grades, with purity typically at 98% or higher for demanding compounding applications.

name: Pyridoxal
description:
Pyridoxal (CAS 66-72-8 ), also known as Piridoxal, is one of the three primary forms of vitamin B6 alongside pyridoxine and pyridoxamine. It functions as a biochemically active aldehyde form of B6.

This compound serves as a direct precursor to pyridoxal-5-phosphate (PLP), the coenzyme involved in a broad range of enzymatic reactions. Demand is driven primarily by pharmaceutical synthesis and nutritional supplementation.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used as a starting material or reference standard in the production of B6-related active pharmaceutical ingredients. It is also essential for creating various coenzyme derivatives.

Nutritional supplement formulators source it where a more bioavailable or reactive B6 form is required compared to pyridoxine hydrochloride. It is a critical component for high-end health and wellness formulations.

In biotechnology and cell biology research, it is used to study transaminase activity, enzyme kinetics, and cofactor-dependent metabolic pathways. It is a staple reagent in modern life sciences research.

Animal feed and veterinary nutrition applications also utilize this material where specific B6 form differentiation is required. This is particularly important in the development of specialized feed premixes.

The product is supplied as a crystalline powder and is available in research-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. These grades meet the purity requirements of laboratory and API synthesis applications.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory use to bulk quantities for industrial procurement. We ensure all batches meet rigorous quality standards for consistency and performance in industrial processes.

name: Glucosamine hydrochloride
description:

It is used across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing as a bioactive ingredient targeting joint health support and skin hydration in various industrial applications.

In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is the preferred form of glucosamine for tablet and capsule formulations due to its higher nitrogen content and lower molecular weight compared to the sulfate salt.

This allows more active substance per dose. Pharmaceutical producers use it as an active ingredient in OTC joint health products and as an intermediate in the synthesis of more complex compounds.

In functional food and beverage applications, it is incorporated into fortified products positioned for mobility and joint wellness. Cosmetic formulators use it in moisturizing creams and serums.

It supports skin barrier function and acts as a humectant in leave-on formulations. Glucosamine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy processing and blending.

Stearyl heptanoate (CAS 66009-41-4 ), also known as octadecyl heptanoate, is a synthetic ester of stearyl alcohol and heptanoic acid used across personal care and industrial formulations.

It functions primarily as an emollient, lubricant, and skin-conditioning agent, delivering a lightweight, non-greasy feel in finished products. In cosmetics and personal care, it is used in skin creams and lotions.

Lip products and color cosmetics utilize this ester to improve spreadability and provide a smooth after-feel without heavy occlusion. Sunscreen and foundation formulations incorporate it to enhance pigment dispersion.

This ingredient helps optimize texture on the skin for various beauty applications. In lubricant and metalworking applications, it contributes to boundary lubrication in light-duty formulations where ester-based fluids are preferred.

It supports a smooth, even texture without a heavy feel in various topical applications. Sunscreen and color cosmetic manufacturers use it to disperse pigments and UV filters uniformly within emollient bases for better coverage.

name: C12-13 pareth
description:
C12-13 Pareth (CAS 66455-14-9 ), also marketed as Neodol 23-3, is a nonionic ethoxylated alcohol surfactant derived from a C12–C13 fatty alcohol blend.

It delivers reliable emulsification and detergency across a broad range of formulation types, making it a go-to building block for formulators balancing performance with compatibility.

In household and industrial cleaning, it functions as the primary surfactant in liquid detergents, hard surface cleaners, and degreasers, providing low-foam or controlled-foam profiles.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off products such as body washes and shampoos where stable emulsification and skin-compatible cleansing are required.

In textile processing, it supports scouring and wetting operations, helping to remove oils and sizing agents from fiber substrates ahead of dyeing and finishing.

Industrial and institutional cleaning concentrates also rely on it for emulsifying hydrocarbon soils in alkaline formulations, ensuring high efficiency in heavy-duty applications.

The material is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste, with the ethoxylation degree varying by grade to suit specific HLB requirements for different chemical systems.

Technical and industrial grades are standard across the market, with packaging typically ranging from drums to IBC totes and bulk tanker quantities for large-scale manufacturing.

name: C9-11 alcohols
description:
C9-11 Alcohols (CAS 66455-17-2 ), commercially available under the trade name Linevol 911, are a blend of synthetic, linear primary alcohols in the C9 to C11 carbon chain range. They function as mid-chain fatty alcohols used across cleaning, personal care, and industrial formulations.

These alcohols are primarily utilized as solvents, carriers, and emulsification aids. In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, they act as hydrotropes and co-solvents that improve the solubility of surfactant systems and boost cleaning performance.

They are particularly effective in hard surface cleaners and degreasers. Personal care formulators use them as carrier solvents in fragrance delivery systems and as emollient components in rinse-off products where a light skin feel is required.

In metalworking and lubricant applications, they serve as base fluids or co-solvents in cutting fluids and rust-preventive formulations. They are also used as intermediates in the production of ethoxylated alcohol surfactants and sulfate esters.

C9-11 Alcohols are supplied as a clear liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial and cleaning applications.

Purity and composition specifications typically follow supplier-defined standards aligned with oleochemical and petrochemical industry norms. This ensures consistent performance across various manufacturing and chemical processing environments.

name: Panthenyl ethyl ether
description:
Panthenyl ethyl ether (CAS 667-83-4 ) is a lipophilic derivative of provitamin B5, modified to improve skin penetration compared to standard panthenol. It functions as a moisturizing and conditioning active in cosmetic and pharmaceutical topical formulations.

In leave-on skincare products such as serums, creams, and lotions, it delivers sustained hydration while supporting the skin barrier. This makes it particularly suitable for sensitive and dry skin formulations.

Hair care formulators use it in conditioners and styling products where its enhanced lipophilicity improves deposition on the hair shaft. This characteristic helps to significantly reduce moisture loss in hair treatments.

It is incorporated into topical pharmaceutical preparations requiring a provitamin B5 source with improved penetration through lipid-rich skin layers. This ensures the active reaches deeper layers of the dermis effectively.

Suncare and after-sun products also use it for its moisture-retention profile alongside UV-protective actives. It helps soothe the skin and restore hydration levels after exposure to environmental stressors.

Panthenyl ethyl ether is supplied as a clear to slightly yellowish liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard form for personal care and topical pharmaceutical applications.

Packaging typically ranges from small drums to bulk quantities suited to industrial formulation volumes. This ensures flexibility for both boutique manufacturers and large-scale industrial production facilities.

name: Pentaerythritol tetrakis(3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-hydroxyhydrocinnamate)
description:
Pentaerythritol tetrakis(3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-hydroxyhydrocinnamate) (CAS 6683-19-8 ) is a hindered phenolic primary antioxidant used to protect polymers, lubricants, and industrial formulations from oxidative degradation.

It functions by scavenging free radicals generated by heat and oxygen exposure, extending the functional lifespan of finished materials during processing and long-term service.

In plastics and polymer processing, it stabilizes polyolefins, engineering thermoplastics, and elastomers against thermal oxidation during high-temperature extrusion and molding.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it into synthetic and mineral base oils to prevent viscosity breakdown and deposit formation under sustained operating conditions.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to maintain bond integrity and prevent discoloration in heat-cured systems. Coating and packaging applications rely on it to protect film substrates.

It protects printed surfaces from oxidative yellowing throughout the product shelf life. The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granules for industrial use.

Standard grades include technical, food-contact compliant, and polymer-grade specifications meeting requirements under FDA and EU regulatory frameworks for safety and performance.

It is available in both standard and low-dust granule forms to support handling in industrial compounding environments, ensuring efficient integration into various manufacturing workflows.
