name: Sodium isostearoyl lactylate
description:
Sodium isostearoyl lactylate (CAS 66988-04-3 ), commercially known as PATIONIC ISL, is a lactylate-based anionic surfactant derived from isostearic acid and lactic acid. It functions as an emulsifier and rheology modifier across food processing and personal care manufacturing.

This versatile ingredient helps stabilize oil-in-water systems and condition interfacial films in complex formulations. In baked goods and dough systems, it strengthens gluten networks and improves dough machinability, contributing to consistent crumb structure.

The additive also helps extend shelf life by maintaining moisture and texture integrity over time. Personal care formulators use it to stabilize emulsions in creams and lotions where conventional surfactants may compromise skin feel or formulation mildness.

In conditioning hair care products, it supports uniform distribution of actives and improves the sensory profile of rinse-off formats. Food manufacturers also incorporate it into whipped toppings and dairy analog products to control aeration.

By preventing phase separation during processing, it ensures a high-quality final product for the consumer. Sodium isostearoyl lactylate is typically supplied as a paste or soft solid, reflecting the branched-chain fatty acid profile of isostearic acid.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the standard commercial offerings for industrial use. Food-grade material is produced to meet applicable purity and additive regulations to ensure safety and compliance across global markets.

Packaging is commonly available in drums or totes suited to industrial-scale procurement and logistics. This ensures that manufacturers can maintain consistent supply chains for large-scale production of food and cosmetic goods.

name: Thiamine hydrochloride
description:
Thiamine hydrochloride (CAS 67-03-8 ), also known by its FEMA 3322 designation, is the stable salt form of vitamin B1 used across pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions as a nutritional fortifier and process stabilizer, enabling manufacturers to deliver consistent B1 potency in finished products. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the preferred active ingredient.

This compound is used in oral tablets, injectables, and multivitamin formulations due to its high water solubility and stable shelf life. Food and beverage producers use it to fortify breakfast cereals and flour.

It is also essential for infant formula and energy drinks to meet regulatory nutritional labeling requirements. In flavor applications, it serves as a precursor in Maillard reaction systems.

This process generates meat-like and savory flavor profiles in processed food production. Personal care formulators incorporate it into scalp treatments and hair care products targeting enrichment claims.

Thiamine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder in packaging ranging from kilogram bags to bulk metric ton quantities. It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications.

These grades meet the compliance requirements of different regulated markets. FCC -grade material is standard for food and beverage fortification applications to ensure high safety standards.

name: Choline chloride
description:
Choline chloride (CAS 67-48-1 ), also sold under the names Lipotril and Paresan, is a quaternary ammonium salt classified as a B-complex vitamin essential to animal metabolism. Approved as food additive E1001(iii) , it functions as a nutrient supplement, humectant, and processing aid across feed, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

In animal feed production, it is the primary source of dietary choline for poultry, swine, and aquaculture, where deficiency directly impacts liver function and growth performance. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a nutrient fortifier in functional foods, infant formula, and dietary supplements.

These supplements often target cognitive and metabolic health. In pharmaceutical formulations, it serves as an active ingredient in lipotropic preparations and as a buffering agent in liquid dosage forms. Personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing products where its hygroscopic character supports water retention.

Choline chloride is supplied as a dry corn cob or silica carrier-based powder, typically containing fifty to seventy percent active content, for feed applications. It is also available as an aqueous solution, commonly seventy to seventy-five percent, for liquid feed and industrial use.

Anhydrous crystalline grades are available for pharmaceutical and food applications meeting USP and FCC specifications. These high-purity grades ensure compliance with international safety standards for human consumption and medical use.

The material is highly hygroscopic and must be stored in a cool, dry environment to prevent clumping. Proper handling ensures the stability of the compound across various industrial applications, from large-scale agriculture to specialized laboratory settings.

name: 3,5-dimethylpyrazole
description:
3,5-Dimethylpyrazole (CAS 67-51-6 ), commonly abbreviated as DMP, is a nitrogen-containing heterocyclic compound used primarily as a nitrification inhibitor in agricultural and industrial applications.

By blocking the enzymatic conversion of ammonium to nitrate in soil, it extends the availability of nitrogen fertilizers and reduces nitrous oxide emissions. In agriculture, DMP is the active component in formulations.

These formulations are applied alongside urea and ammonium-based fertilizers to improve nitrogen use efficiency in crops. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a building block for synthesizing pyrazole-containing APIs.

Its reactive NH group enables controlled derivatization for various intermediates. In water treatment, DMP-based formulations help manage nitrification in wastewater systems and cooling towers during processing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into select preservation and stabilization systems where heterocyclic nitrogen chemistry is required. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid.

It is typically available in powder or flake form. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 98% to 99%+ as confirmed by GC or HPLC analysis.

Packaging is available in kilogram-scale quantities for laboratory and development use. This scales to bulk drum supply for industrial and agrochemical production to meet high-volume manufacturing requirements.

name: Methanol
description:
Methanol (CAS 67-56-1 ), also known as wood alcohol or wood naphtha, is a primary alcohol produced at industrial scale and used as a solvent, chemical feedstock, and fuel component across multiple sectors.

Its role spans from direct process solvent applications to serving as the foundational building block for downstream chemical synthesis. In the petrochemical and energy sectors, it is blended into fuel formulations.

Methanol is used as a feedstock for producing dimethyl ether and other fuel additives. Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a process solvent for API synthesis, extraction, and chromatography-scale purification.

In plastics and polymers, it drives the production of formaldehyde, acetic acid, and methyl methacrylate. These intermediates feed directly into resin and polymer manufacturing for various industrial applications.

Printing and packaging operations use methanol-based solvent systems in ink formulations where fast evaporation and resin compatibility are process requirements. This ensures high efficiency in high-speed production lines.

Methanol is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk tanker, IBC, and drum formats. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and refined grades meeting ASTM D1152 specifications for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP standards for regulated manufacturing environments. These quality benchmarks ensure the material is suitable for sensitive chemical processes.

name: Isopropyl alcohol
description:
Isopropyl alcohol (CAS 67-63-0 ), commonly known as IPA, is a fast-evaporating solvent used across cleaning, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It dissolves a broad range of oils, resins, and active ingredients without leaving residue.

This is a critical factor for processes where surface cleanliness or formulation clarity is required. In electronics manufacturing, IPA removes flux residues, fingerprints, and particulate contamination from PCBs and precision components.

It performs these tasks without damaging sensitive substrates. Pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturers rely on it as a disinfectant and process solvent in tablet coatings, topical formulations, and cleanroom surface sanitation.

In personal care, IPA functions as a solvent and preservative in antiperspirants, hand sanitizers, and skin toners. Its rapid evaporation supports consumer-acceptable dry-down in these various cosmetic applications.

Printing and packaging operations use it as a fountain solution additive and ink solvent to control viscosity and improve plate wetting. IPA is supplied as a liquid in concentrations typically ranging from 70% to 99%+ anhydrous grades.

Standard specifications include USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. for pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications. It is also available in technical grade for industrial cleaning and general solvent use.

Acetone (CAS 67-64-1 ), also known by its FEMA 3326 designation in flavour applications, is one of the most commercially traded ketone solvents in the global chemical market.

It dissolves a broad range of resins, oils, waxes, and synthetic polymers, making it a primary solvent choice across manufacturing, formulation, and cleaning operations.

In plastics and polymer processing, it is used to dissolve and thin cellulose acetate, polyester resins, and epoxy systems during fabrication and surface preparation.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a process solvent for active ingredient extraction, recrystallisation, and equipment cleaning where residue-free evaporation is critical.

Printing and packaging operations use acetone-based formulations to clean ink systems and prepare substrates for adhesion to ensure high quality results.

In metalworking and precision manufacturing, it removes machining oils, flux residues, and contaminants from metal surfaces prior to coating or assembly.

Acetone is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) specifications.

name: Chloroform
description:
Chloroform (CAS 67-66-3 ) is a halogenated solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, biotechnology research, and polymer processing. It dissolves a broad range of organic compounds and is valued for its density and selectivity in liquid-liquid extraction workflows.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used as a process solvent for active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) synthesis and purification, where its extraction efficiency reduces downstream processing steps.

Biotechnology and life sciences laboratories rely on it for nucleic acid extraction protocols, including the Chomczynski-Sacchi RNA isolation method, where phase separation from aqueous samples is critical.

Polymer processors use this solvent to dissolve and cast films from materials such as polystyrene and polycarbonate, enabling controlled thickness and surface uniformity in specialty film production.

It also functions as a reaction medium in the synthesis of fluorocarbon intermediates and other halogenated compounds. The material is supplied as a liquid, typically stabilized with a small amount of ethanol or amylene.

This stabilization is necessary to prevent phosgene formation during storage. Standard commercial grades include technical, reagent, HPLC, and ACS grades, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to USP and BP specifications.

Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale bottles to bulk drum quantities for industrial procurement. Our supply chain ensures consistent purity and compliance with international safety and handling regulations for hazardous materials.

Biotech and life sciences operations rely on it for cryopreservation of cell lines and as a carrier solvent in compound libraries. It is also approved as a flavoring agent ( FEMA 3875 ).

name: Cholecalciferol
description:
Cholecalciferol (CAS 67-97-0 ), also known as Vitamin D3, is the animal-derived form of vitamin D used across food fortification, dietary supplements, animal feed, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It supports calcium and phosphorus metabolism regulation, making it a critical active ingredient for bone health and nutritional product development in various industrial applications.

In food and beverage manufacturing, cholecalciferol is used to fortify dairy products, plant-based milks, cereals, and infant formula to meet established nutritional labeling standards.

Premix and supplement manufacturers incorporate it into softgels, tablets, and powdered blends where precise dosing and stability in oil-based carriers are required for the final product.

Animal feed producers use it to support skeletal development and egg production performance in poultry, swine, and aquaculture operations to ensure optimal livestock health and yield.

Pharmaceutical-grade cholecalciferol is also used as the active in prescription and OTC vitamin D3 formulations, including drops and oral solutions targeting deficiency treatment.

Cholecalciferol is supplied as an oily liquid concentrate, dry powder, or microencapsulated beadlet form to suit different manufacturing processes and stability requirements.

Recognized grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade specifications to meet regulatory requirements across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and feed markets.

name: Dequalinium
description:
Dequalinium (CAS 6707-58-0 ), commonly supplied as dequalinium chloride, is a quaternary ammonium bisquinolinium compound used as an antimicrobial active in pharmaceutical and personal care formulations.

It functions as a broad-spectrum biocide effective against bacteria, fungi, and certain protozoa at low concentrations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, dequalinium chloride is the active ingredient in topical antiseptic lozenges.

It is also used in throat sprays and oral rinses targeting oropharyngeal infections. It is formulated into vaginal tablets and pessaries for the treatment of bacterial vaginosis and mixed vaginal infections.

In these applications, it acts as a local antimicrobial agent. Personal care formulators incorporate it into antiseptic mouthwashes and medicated skin preparations requiring preservative-level antimicrobial activity.

In research and specialty chemical contexts, it is used as a mitochondria-targeting agent in experimental drug delivery systems. Dequalinium is commercially available primarily as dequalinium chloride.

It is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP , BP , or Ph. Eur. specifications for industrial use.

High-purity grades are available for API and finished dosage form manufacturing. Packaging is typically offered in small quantities for R&D through to kilogram-scale lots for commercial production.

name: Tetramethyldipropylenetriamine
description:
Tetramethyldipropylenetriamine (CAS 6711-48-4 ) is a tertiary triamine used as a catalyst and curing agent in polyurethane and epoxy systems. Its balanced amine functionality supports controlled reactivity across a range of polymer formulations.

This chemical is a practical choice for formulators managing cure speed and crosslink density. In polyurethane foam and elastomer production, it acts as a blowing and gelling catalyst, influencing cell structure and mechanical properties.

Epoxy formulators use it as a curing agent or co-curing agent where extended pot life and moderate cure temperatures are required. In adhesive and sealant systems, it supports crosslinking in two-component formulations targeting structural bonding.

The product is also suitable for flexible sealing applications. Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers use amine-based catalysts of this type as corrosion inhibitor intermediates or additive precursors for specialized industrial fluids.

Tetramethyldipropylenetriamine is supplied as a liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically specified at 98% or higher for catalyst applications to ensure consistent performance.

Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes depending on order volume. This material should be handled according to standard safety protocols for industrial amines, ensuring proper storage in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated facility.

name: Diethanolisopropanolamine
description:
Diethanolisopropanolamine (CAS 6712-98-7 ), commonly known by its abbreviation DEIPA, is a tertiary alkanolamine combining hydroxyl and amine functionality in a single molecule.

It functions as a pH regulator, corrosion inhibitor, and dispersing agent across industrial and personal care formulations. In cement and concrete grinding aids, DEIPA improves particle dispersion.

It enhances mill efficiency, reducing energy consumption during clinker processing, which is one of its most commercially significant uses. Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as a corrosion inhibitor.

It acts as a pH buffer, extending fluid service life and protecting ferrous and non-ferrous surfaces. In personal care products such as lotions and creams, DEIPA neutralizes acidic polymers.

It works with fatty acids to stabilize emulsions and adjust final pH. Water treatment formulations use it as a chelating agent to sequester hardness ions and prevent scale deposition.

This prevents buildup in industrial cooling systems. DEIPA is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow viscous liquid, typically at 85% and 100% active concentrations for various applications.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with bulk liquid supply in drums, IBCs, and isotanks being the norm for industrial buyers. No food or pharmaceutical grades are recognized.

name: N,N-Bis(3-dimethylaminopropyl)isopropanolamine
description:
N,N-Bis(3-dimethylaminopropyl)isopropanolamine (CAS 67151-63-7 ) is a tertiary amine compound used as a reactive catalyst and crosslinker in polyurethane and polymer systems. Its combination of amine and hydroxyl functionality allows it to participate directly in the polymer network.

This unique structure allows the compound to accelerate cure rather than acting as a purely fugitive catalyst. In polyurethane foam and elastomer production, it functions as a balanced blow and gel catalyst for industrial use.

The chemical helps control cell structure and the processing window in flexible and rigid foam formulations. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to accelerate cure in two-component polyurethane systems where migration must be minimized.

In coatings, its reactive hydroxyl group allows incorporation into the crosslinked matrix, reducing volatile amine content in the cured film. Polymer compounders also evaluate it as a building block for specialty polyols.

It is frequently utilized as an amine-functional intermediate in custom resin synthesis. The product is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, typically in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial formulation volumes.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for polyurethane and coatings applications. Specification alignment with major polyurethane raw material standards is common for global distribution and manufacturing.

Buyers should confirm amine value and hydroxyl number against their specific formulation requirements. This ensures the material meets the necessary performance criteria for high-quality polymer and resin production cycles.

name: Trans-2-hexenal
description:
Trans-2-hexenal (CAS 6728-26-3 ), also known by its FEMA 2560 designation, is an aldehyde-based aroma chemical used across flavor and fragrance manufacturing.

It delivers a fresh, green, apple-like character that perfumers and flavorists rely on to replicate natural fruit and botanical profiles in various industrial applications.

In food flavoring, it is used at low concentrations to build green apple, tomato, and fresh herb notes in beverages, confectionery, and savory products for global markets.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine perfumery and functional fragrance blends where fresh-cut green or leafy top notes are required for high-end consumer goods.

In personal care formulations, it contributes to shampoos, body washes, and skincare products targeting fresh fruit or botanical scent profiles for a natural experience.

It also appears in flavor reconstruction work, where matching the volatile profile of fresh produce demands precise inclusion of this compound to ensure sensory accuracy.

The material is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels. Food-grade material conforming to FCC standards is the most commercially common specification available.

Buyers should confirm purity grade and isomeric composition when sourcing, as the trans-isomer content is critical to achieving the intended sensory profile in final products.

name: Propyldiethanolamine
description:
Propyldiethanolamine (CAS 6735-35-9 ) is a tertiary alkanolamine combining both amine and hydroxyl functionality, making it effective as a pH buffer, corrosion inhibitor, and emulsifier across industrial formulations.

N-Propyldiethanolamine is the recognized alternative designation buyers encounter in technical literature and supplier documentation. In metalworking fluids and cutting coolants, it buffers pH and inhibits ferrous and non-ferrous metal corrosion.

This chemical helps in extending fluid service life in various mechanical applications. Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations use it to emulsify oils and disperse soils while maintaining alkaline stability under dilution.

Water treatment programs incorporate it as a corrosion inhibitor and chelating agent to control scale and metal ion interference in recirculating systems. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of industrial water infrastructure.

Coatings and adhesive formulations employ it as a neutralizing amine for acid-functional resins. This application improves dispersion stability and substrate adhesion in modern waterborne systems used in manufacturing.

Propyldiethanolamine is supplied as a liquid, typically at high purity levels suited for industrial and specialty chemical applications. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most buyers.

Purity specifications are commonly in the 98–99%+ range depending on the specific supplier requirements. Packaging ranges from drums to intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) for large industrial volumes.

name: Sodium malate
description:
Sodium malate (CAS 676-46-0 ), also known by its food additive designation E350i , is the disodium salt of malic acid used commercially as a pH buffer and acidulant.

It delivers a mild, smooth tartness without the sharp acidity of mineral acids, making it a preferred choice in food and pharmaceutical formulations where precise pH control is required.

In food and beverage manufacturing, sodium malate regulates acidity in fruit-based products, confectionery, and soft drinks where a rounded, fruit-forward flavor profile is desired.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a buffering agent in oral liquid preparations and effervescent tablets to stabilize active ingredients across a defined pH range.

It functions as a flavor enhancer and acidity moderator in low-sodium seasoning blends and processed foods, where direct acidulants would be too aggressive.

In nutraceutical applications, it appears in mineral supplement formulations as a well-tolerated carrier salt. Sodium malate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules.

Food-grade material conforming to E350i specifications is the standard commercial form, with FCC -grade product available for applications requiring documented purity standards.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply meeting USP or Ph.Eur. specifications is available for regulated drug product manufacturing and high-purity industrial applications.

name: Allyl isoamyl glycolate
description:
Allyl isoamyl glycolate (CAS 67634-00-8 ), also known as allyl (3-methylbutoxy)acetate, is a specialty ester used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient in food and cosmetic applications.

It delivers a fruity, green, and slightly tropical character that makes it a valued building block in flavor and fragrance compositions. In food flavoring, it contributes fresh, fruity top notes to confectionery.

It is frequently utilized in beverages and chewing gum formulations where a tropical or green fruit profile is desired. Fragrance houses incorporate it into fine fragrance and functional fragrance blends.

This ingredient adds light, diffusive top notes with a natural fruit character to various products. In personal care, it appears in scented rinse-off and leave-on formulations including shampoos and body washes.

It is also found in lotions where a fresh, fruity signature is required. Its ester structure supports use as a modifier in complex flavor systems, helping to round and lift other aromatic components.

Allyl isoamyl glycolate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging suitable for flavor and fragrance manufacturing. It is available at flavor-grade and fragrance-grade purity levels.

Specifications are aligned to industry quality standards for aroma chemicals. Drum and smaller quantity packaging options are typical for this type of specialty aroma ester used in global manufacturing.

name: C12-18 carboxylic acids
description:
C12-18 Carboxylic Acids (CAS 67701-01-3 ), also marketed as Fatty Acids C12-18, are a mid-chain fatty acid blend derived from vegetable oils including coconut. Across multiple industries, they function as emulsifiers, lubricants, and surface-active agents.

In personal care, they are used to build bar soap structure, condition skin creams, and control emulsion texture in lotions and cleansers. These acids provide essential stability and consistency to various cosmetic formulations.

Coatings and adhesives formulators incorporate them as surface modifiers to improve substrate wetting and pigment dispersion. They are effective in both solvent-based and water-based systems for industrial applications.

In rubber compounding and tire manufacturing, they act as processing aids and internal lubricants. These components reduce friction between polymer chains during the intensive mixing and extrusion processes.

Metalworking fluid formulators use them as base components for cutting oils and corrosion-inhibiting lubricants. They are applied to both ferrous and non-ferrous metals to ensure protection and performance.

C12-18 Carboxylic Acids are supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid or semi-solid, depending on composition. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial applications.

Cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity specifications is available for personal care use. Bulk supply is typically managed in drums and ISO tanks to meet the high-volume needs of global manufacturers.

name: Fatty acids, C16-18
description:
Fatty acids, C16-18 (CAS 67701-03-5 ) is a mixed-chain fatty acid blend derived from vegetable or animal fats, combining palmitic and stearic acid fractions in commercially relevant ratios. It functions as a lubricant and surface modifier.

Sold under trade designations such as Emersol stearic acid 120 and Emersol stearic acid 132, it acts as a rheology modifier across a broad range of industrial and consumer product manufacturing sectors globally.

In personal care, it acts as an emulsifier and consistency agent in creams, lotions, and bar soaps, contributing to texture and skin feel without requiring additional thickeners or stabilizers in the formula.

Rubber and tire compounders use it as an activator and internal lubricant during vulcanization, improving processing efficiency and compound flow. This ensures high-quality output during the manufacturing of rubber goods.

Plastics processors incorporate it as a mold release agent and processing aid in PVC and polyolefin systems, reducing die buildup and improving surface finish. It is essential for maintaining high production speeds.

In coatings and adhesives, it modifies surface tension and improves substrate wetting, directly affecting adhesion performance and film formation. This makes it a versatile additive for various industrial coating applications.

Supplied as flakes, pastilles, or a solid waxy mass, with liquid form available for bulk industrial supply. Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and cosmetic-grade specifications for diverse industrial needs.

Purity levels are typically defined by iodine value and acid value. Buyers should confirm the palmitic-to-stearic ratio, as this varies by grade and affects performance in specific end-use formulations and products.

name: Distilled Coco Oil Acid
description:
Distilled Coco Oil Acid (CAS 67701-05-7 ) is a refined mixture of C8–C18 fatty acids derived from coconut oil through distillation. It functions as a surface-active raw material used across personal care, cleaning, coatings, and lubricant formulations.

This versatile chemical enables essential processes such as emulsification, wetting, and lubrication in various industrial settings. In personal care, it acts as a precursor for soap bases, emulsifiers, and surfactant esters used in skin cleansers.

It is also a key component in shampoos and conditioning products. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a reactive intermediate or surface modifier to improve substrate adhesion and the dispersion of pigments and fillers.

In industrial and household cleaning products, it is saponified or neutralized to produce fatty acid salts. These salts deliver necessary detergency and foam control for high-performance cleaning solutions across multiple sectors.

Metalworking and lubricant applications rely on it as a base component for cutting fluids. It is also utilized in corrosion-inhibiting formulations where controlled lubricity is required for mechanical efficiency and protection.

Distilled Coco Oil Acid is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on temperature and fatty acid profile. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with quality typically characterized by acid value and color.

The material is also evaluated based on iodine value and specific color specifications to ensure consistency. Bulk liquid supply and intermediate packaging formats are standard for industrial procurement and large-scale manufacturing.

name: Tallow oleic acid
description:
Tallow oleic acid (CAS 67701-08-0 ), also supplied under trade names Emersol 110 and Priolene 6900, is a mixed C16-C18 fatty acid fraction derived from animal tallow. It features a high proportion of unsaturated content and functions as a lubricant and surface modifier.

This versatile chemical acts as a rheology modifier across a wide range of industrial manufacturing processes. In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it serves as a base component or additive that reduces friction and improves surface film performance.

Coatings and adhesive manufacturers utilize this fatty acid to modify rheology and enhance substrate wetting in solvent-based and reactive systems. It ensures consistent performance and improved application characteristics for various industrial coatings.

Rubber and tire compounders incorporate it as a processing aid and internal lubricant. This application helps to improve the dispersion of fillers and significantly reduces mill sticking during the manufacturing of rubber components.

In textile and leather processing, it supports fiber lubrication and surface conditioning during wet finishing operations. Its chemical properties allow for better penetration and more uniform treatment of natural and synthetic fibers.

Tallow oleic acid is supplied as an amber to yellow liquid at ambient temperatures. Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and technical applications, with specifications typically defined by acid value, iodine value, and titer.

Supply is available in bulk liquid, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), and drum quantities to meet diverse production needs. Our logistics team ensures reliable delivery of high-quality fatty acids for your specific industrial requirements.

name: glycerides C14-18 mono- and di-
description:
Glycerides C14-18 mono- and di- (CAS 67701-33-1 ) is a mixed partial glyceride fraction derived from C14–C18 fatty acids. It is used commercially as an emulsifier and plasticizer across food, personal care, and polymer applications.

Known in food manufacturing as E471 , it stabilizes oil-water systems and modifies texture in finished products. In baked goods and margarine, it controls fat crystallization and extends shelf life by maintaining emulsion stability.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions as an emulsifier and co-emulsifier. This improves skin feel and product consistency while ensuring the stability of the formulation throughout its shelf life.

In plastics processing, it functions as a plasticizer and lubricant for PVC and other polymer systems. It reduces melt viscosity and improves the surface finish in various extruded or calendered products.

It also finds use in bread improvers and shortening blends, where it conditions dough and optimizes crumb structure. This versatile ingredient is essential for achieving specific textural properties in industrial food production.

Supplied as a cream to off-white waxy solid, it is typically available in flake, bead, or pastille form for ease of handling. Food-grade material is manufactured to meet FCC and USP quality standards.

Technical-grade options are also available for polymer and industrial applications. Drum and bulk packaging are standard, with kosher and halal certifications commonly available depending on the specific feedstock origin.

name: C12-18 alcohols
description:
C12-18 Alcohols (CAS 67762-25-8 ), also supplied under trade names such as Alfol 1218 and Lorol, are a blend of saturated fatty alcohols derived from natural or synthetic feedstocks.

In formulation and industrial manufacturing, they function as emulsifiers, emollients, and rheology modifiers across a broad range of finished products. In personal care, they are used to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions.

These alcohols are found in lotions, creams, and conditioners, contributing body and texture to the finished formula. Household and industrial cleaning products use them as co-emulsifiers and foam stabilizers.

They are frequently utilized in liquid detergents and fabric softeners. In lubricant manufacturing, they serve as intermediates for producing ester-based lubricants and metalworking fluids where controlled viscosity is required.

They are also used in the production of ethoxylated alcohol surfactants, making them a key petrochemical and oleochemical processing input. C12-18 Alcohols are typically supplied as white to off-white waxy flakes.

Pellets are also common, with liquid form available at elevated temperatures. Standard grades include technical and cosmetic quality, with the latter meeting specifications relevant to personal care manufacturing.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems while contributing body and texture to finished formulations. In cosmetic manufacturing, it functions as the structural backbone of creams and lotions.

name: Stearyl dimethicone
description:
Stearyl dimethicone (CAS 67762-83-8 ) is a silicone polymer modified with stearyl (C18) alkyl groups, combining the surface-slip characteristics of silicone with the emollient behavior of long-chain fatty chemistry.

It functions as an emulsifier, conditioning agent, and surface modifier across personal care and industrial applications. In skin and hair care formulations, it provides a smooth, non-greasy skin feel while improving spreadability.

This material is widely used in creams, lotions, and leave-on conditioners. Color cosmetics manufacturers use it to enhance pigment dispersion and achieve uniform coverage in foundations and pressed powders.

In textile finishing, it imparts soft-hand effects and improves fabric slip without compromising breathability. Coatings and sealant formulators incorporate it as a surface-active modifier to improve substrate wetting.

It is also used to reduce surface tension in silicone-based systems. Stearyl dimethicone is typically supplied as a waxy solid or high-viscosity paste, depending on molecular weight and alkyl substitution level.

Cosmetic-grade material is the dominant commercial form, with supply conforming to standard industry purity expectations for personal care use. Technical-grade variants are available for industrial coating and textile applications.

name: Methylated silica
description:
Methylated silica (CAS 67762-90-7 ), also known as dimethyl silicone polymer with silica, is a surface-treated amorphous silica in which silanol groups are replaced with hydrophobic methyl groups.

This modification converts standard hydrophilic silica into a material that controls flow, suppresses foam, and modifies surface behavior across a broad range of non-aqueous and aqueous systems.

In coatings and sealants, it functions as a thixotropic agent, preventing sagging in applied films while maintaining workability during mixing and application for industrial users.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into anhydrous systems such as color cosmetics and sunscreens to improve texture, control oil absorption, and modify skin feel for consumers.

Industrial and household cleaning products use it as a defoamer component, particularly in concentrated liquid formulations where foam suppression must persist under high-shear conditions.

In silicone elastomers and polymer compounding, it reinforces the matrix while contributing to hydrophobic surface characteristics that resist moisture uptake and environmental degradation.

Methylated silica is supplied as a fine white powder with varying degrees of surface treatment and particle size distribution. It is available in technical grade for various uses.

Specific BET surface area and carbon content specifications determine performance in a given application. Packaging typically ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk containers depending on volume.

name: Diisostearyl malate
description:
Diisostearyl malate (CAS 67763-18-2 ) is a diester of malic acid and isostearyl alcohol, supplied commercially under trade names including Pelemol DISM, Creaester IM, and Haimalate DIS.

In personal care manufacturing, it functions as an emollient and plasticizer, delivering a smooth, non-greasy skin feel while improving the flexibility and payoff of cosmetic formulations.

Lip color formulations including lipsticks, lip glosses, and liquid lips use this ingredient as a primary emollient base because it enhances pigment dispersion and contributes a comfortable, non-tacky texture.

In color cosmetics such as eyeshadow sticks and pressed powders, it acts as a binder and softener, improving product cohesion and skin adhesion for better application and wear.

Skincare formulators incorporate it into anhydrous balms and body butters where its moisturizing properties support long-wear hydration without the drawback of occlusive heaviness on the skin.

It also functions as a plasticizer in mascara and eyeliner formulas, reducing brittleness and improving film flexibility on application to ensure a smooth and lasting finish for the user.

The material is supplied as a viscous liquid or semi-solid depending on temperature. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard for personal care and color cosmetic applications.

Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBCs for bulk procurement. This ensures that manufacturers can source the material efficiently for large-scale production of various beauty and skincare products.

name: Soybean oil methyl ester
description:
Soybean oil methyl ester (CAS 67784-80-9 ) is produced by transesterification of soybean oil and functions as a bio-based solvent, lubricant base, and plasticizer across multiple industrial sectors.

Derived from a renewable feedstock, it offers formulators a plant-derived alternative to petroleum-based functional fluids and carriers. In industrial and household cleaning formulations, it acts as a solvent carrier.

It is used for degreasers, paint strippers, and hard-surface cleaners where low toxicity and good solvency are procurement priorities. Metalworking fluid manufacturers incorporate it as a base stock or co-solvent.

It is utilized in cutting, grinding, and forming lubricants, where its film-forming character supports metal protection during processing. In plastics compounding, it functions as a plasticizer and processing aid.

This is particularly useful in PVC and flexible polymer systems where bio-content is a formulation requirement. It also serves as a biodiesel blend component and carrier fluid in agricultural chemical formulations.

Soybean oil methyl ester is supplied as an amber to pale yellow liquid in bulk, IBC, and drum formats. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial applications.

Refined grades are available for applications requiring lower color and reduced impurity profiles. Specifications typically align with ASTM D6751 parameters where biodiesel-grade material is required.

name: PEG-200 hydrogenated glyceryl palmate
description:
PEG-200 hydrogenated glyceryl palmate (CAS 67784-88-7 ), also recognized commercially as palm-oil glycerides hydrogenated ethoxylated, is a polyethylene glycol ester derived from hydrogenated palm oil glycerides.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier and rheology modifier across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations. In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic formulations, it stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions.

This ingredient contributes a smooth, moisturizing skin feel, making it a practical dual-function ingredient in creams, lotions, and cleansers. Pharmaceutical topical preparations use it to ensure uniform dispersion.

It helps maintain active ingredients within emollient bases for consistent delivery. In textile processing, it acts as a fiber lubricant and softening emulsifier, improving fabric handle during finishing operations.

Paper and leather processing operations also use it to control surface rheology and improve treatment uniformity. PEG-200 hydrogenated glyceryl palmate is typically supplied as a paste or waxy solid.

Myristamidopropylamine oxide (CAS 67806-10-4 ) is an amphoteric surfactant derived from myristic acid, functioning as a foam booster, viscosity modifier, and mild cleansing agent in personal care formulations.

It performs effectively across a broad pH range, making it compatible with both anionic and cationic systems without destabilizing the formulation. In shampoos and liquid cleansers, it enhances foam volume and stability.

This surfactant contributes to a smooth, conditioning rinse feel in various hair care products. Body washes and facial cleansers incorporate it to boost mildness and improve the sensory profile without sacrificing cleaning performance.

It is used in conditioning treatments and rinse-off hair products to support emulsification of oils and actives. Household and personal care liquid detergents also use it as a foam stabilizer and viscosity builder.

The chemical is effective in both sulfate-based or sulfate-free systems, providing versatility for formulators. Myristamidopropylamine oxide is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content commonly in the 30–35% range.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades suited for rinse-off and leave-on personal care applications. Packaging options generally include drums and IBCs for bulk procurement to meet industrial manufacturing needs.

name: Bismuth tris(2-ethylhexanoate)
description:
Bismuth tris(2-ethylhexanoate) (CAS 67874-71-9 ), also supplied under trade designations such as Pucat 25, Neostann U 600, and KK 348, is an organo-bismuth compound used as a metal catalyst.

It functions as a non-tin, non-mercury alternative for accelerating reactions in polyurethane and polymer formulations. In polyurethane systems, it catalyzes the isocyanate-polyol reaction effectively.

This makes it a drop-in replacement for organotin catalysts in foam, elastomer, and coating formulations where regulatory pressure limits tin use. Sealant and adhesive manufacturers use it to control cure speed.

It is ideal for managing open time in one- and two-component systems. In industrial coatings, it promotes cross-linking in moisture-cure and two-pack urethane topcoats applied to metal and wood substrates.

Lubricant formulators also employ it as a precursor for bismuth-based extreme-pressure additive packages. Bismuth tris(2-ethylhexanoate) is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically in solution with organic solvents.

This allows for the adjustment of bismuth metal content and handling viscosity. Standard commercial grades are characterized by bismuth content and are available at technical grade .

Packaging ranges from drums to IBCs for bulk industrial supply. This material provides a high-performance solution for manufacturers seeking environmentally compliant catalytic alternatives in modern chemical processing.

Its low viscosity and skin-compatible profile make it a preferred alternative to heavier mineral oil-based ingredients in cosmetic formulations. In personal care, it functions as a lightweight emollient and spreading agent.

It is commonly used in skin creams, lotions, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, improving texture and skin feel without greasiness. Lubricant and metalworking formulators incorporate it into cutting fluids and release agents.

This material is ideal where biodegradable, bio-based ester chemistry is a sourcing priority. Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and conditioning agent applied during finishing to improve flexibility.

It also serves as a plasticizer in specialty coatings and paper treatments where improved substrate flexibility is required. Isodecyl oleate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for various uses.

name: Tetrapotassium etidronate
description:
Tetrapotassium etidronate (CAS 67953-76-8 ) is the fully neutralized potassium salt of etidronic acid, supplied as a ready-to-use alkaline solution for industrial and personal care applications.

It functions as a chelating agent and corrosion inhibitor, sequestering calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions that would otherwise interfere with formulation stability or process efficiency.

In personal care formulations, it stabilizes hydrogen peroxide-based products such as hair colorants and bleaching creams by binding trace metals that catalyze decomposition.

Water treatment and industrial cleaning operations use it to prevent scale formation and protect metal surfaces from corrosion in alkaline process conditions.

Textile and leather processing facilities apply it to control hardness ions during dyeing and finishing, improving dye uptake consistency across various production batches.

In oilfield chemistry, it is incorporated into scale inhibitor packages to protect pipelines and downhole equipment from mineral deposit buildup in harsh environments.

Tetrapotassium etidronate is commercially available primarily as an aqueous solution, with 35–40% active content being the most commonly traded concentration range.

name: Trisodium citrate
description:
Trisodium citrate (CAS 68-04-2 ), also known as TSC and classified as E331iii in food applications, is the trisodium salt of citric acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, chelating agent, and stabilizer, controlling acidity and sequestering metal ions in finished formulations. In food and beverage production, TSC acts as an acidity regulator and emulsifying salt.

This is critical in processed cheese manufacturing to prevent fat separation and improve texture. Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it to buffer oral solutions, effervescent tablets, and anticoagulant blood collection systems.

Precise pH control is non-negotiable in these medical applications. In personal care, it adjusts the pH of creams, shampoos, and cleansing products while chelating trace metals that would otherwise destabilize the formula.

Water treatment applications use TSC as a sequestrant to control scale-forming calcium and magnesium ions in industrial process water. Trisodium citrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

The anhydrous form and the dihydrate are the two commercially standard variants. Recognized grades include FCC (food-grade), USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , covering pharmaceutical and food compliance requirements.

Technical grade is available for industrial and water treatment applications where food or pharma certification is not required. This versatile chemical ensures stability and performance across diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Thioglycolic acid
description:
Thioglycolic acid (CAS 68-11-1 ), also known as mercaptoacetic acid and commonly abbreviated as TGA, is an organosulfur acid used across industrial and consumer-facing manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a reducing agent, stabilizer, and chemical intermediate in processes requiring controlled thiol reactivity. In personal care, TGA is the active ingredient in permanent wave solutions.

It is used in depilatory creams, where it breaks disulfide bonds in keratin to reshape or dissolve hair. PVC stabilizer production relies on TGA as a key building block for tin and lead mercaptide heat stabilizers.

These stabilizers prevent polymer degradation during processing. Leather processing uses TGA to assist in depilation and hide preparation, reducing reliance on sulfide-based alternatives in the tanning industry.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of active compounds. It also acts as a reagent in analytical testing for metal ion detection and laboratory research applications.

Thioglycolic acid is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically at concentrations of 70%, 80%, and 99%+ for technical and high-purity grades. This ensures versatility for various industrial needs.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP specifications for regulated manufacturing environments. This high level of purity is essential for sensitive chemical synthesis.

Technical-grade material is the standard for polymer stabilizer production and industrial leather processing. We provide consistent quality across all grades to meet specific manufacturing requirements.

Dimethylformamide ( CAS 68-12-2 ), commercially known as DMF, is a high-boiling polar aprotic solvent used across chemical manufacturing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and industrial processing.

Its ability to dissolve a broad range of organic and inorganic compounds makes it a preferred solvent where water-miscible, low-volatility performance is required for complex reactions.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DMF serves as a reaction solvent and purification medium for active pharmaceutical ingredients, where controlled solvation and high purity grades are critical.

Acrylic fiber and synthetic leather production rely on DMF to dissolve and process polyacrylonitrile and polyurethane resins into spinnable or coatable forms for industrial use.

Electronics manufacturers use it to strip and clean photoresist layers during PCB and semiconductor fabrication. In agrochemical synthesis, DMF functions as both a solvent and a catalyst precursor.

DMF is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-purity pharmaceutical grade for various needs.

Specifications are aligned to USP and Ph. Eur. pharmacopeial standards where API manufacturing requires it. Low-water and anhydrous variants are available for moisture-sensitive synthesis.

name: Cyanocobalamin
description:
Cyanocobalamin (CAS 68-19-9 ), commonly known as Vitamin B12, is the synthetic, stable form of cobalamin used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions as a bioactive nutrient supplement.

This ingredient enables producers to fortify finished products with a measurable, shelf-stable B12 source. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in injectable formulations, oral tablets, and sublingual preparations.

Food and beverage producers use it to fortify plant-based milks, breakfast cereals, and nutritional supplements. These are categories where B12 is often absent from natural ingredients, making fortification essential for consumers.

In clinical nutrition, it is incorporated into enteral and parenteral nutrition products. Precise dosing and stability under various processing conditions are critical factors for these specialized medical applications.

Cosmetic formulators add it to serums and hair care products positioned around scalp health and skin radiance claims. It is supplied as a fine crystalline powder, typically in diluted trituration blends at concentrations of 0.1% or 1%.

These blends use carriers such as mannitol or starch, allowing accurate dosing at low inclusion rates. Pure form is available for specialized applications requiring high potency and minimal additives.

It is also utilized in infant formula and cooking oils, restoring vitamin content lost during processing. Pharmaceutical-grade retinol enters topical drug formulations and compounded preparations targeting dermatological indications.

Retinol is supplied as a crystalline powder or stabilized oil solution, with oil-based forms common for easier handling and formulation incorporation. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur.

name: Butylated melamine formaldehyde resin
description:
Butylated melamine formaldehyde resin (CAS 68002-25-5 ) is a thermosetting crosslinker used to cure hydroxyl-, carboxyl-, and amino-functional resins in industrial coating and polymer systems.

It delivers durable, chemically resistant networks upon heat activation, making it a core component in high-performance finish formulations for various industrial sectors.

In automotive and industrial coatings, it crosslinks polyester, alkyd, and acrylic binders to produce hard, scratch-resistant topcoats with excellent gloss retention and durability.

Textile and leather finishers apply it to impart crease resistance, dimensional stability, and improved surface durability to treated fabrics and hides during the finishing process.

In paper manufacturing, it functions as a wet-strength and surface-sizing agent, improving resistance to moisture and mechanical stress during high-speed industrial processing.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to increase cohesive strength and thermal resistance in structural bonding applications across the construction and assembly industries.

This resin is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in butanol or xylene-based carriers, at varying solids concentrations suited to coating and adhesive manufacturing requirements.

The Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with specifications defined by solids content, viscosity, and free formaldehyde levels for industrial use.

description:
Cocotrimonium methosulfate (CAS 68002-60-8 ) is a cationic quaternary ammonium surfactant derived from coconut fatty acids. It functions as a conditioning agent, emulsifier, and antistatic in formulations where substantivity to negatively charged surfaces is required.

In hair care, it deposits onto the hair shaft to deliver detangling, softness, and static control in conditioners, rinse-off treatments, and leave-in sprays. Fabric softeners and rinse conditioners rely on it to impart a smooth hand feel.

This chemical helps reduce static cling on textile fibers during the laundering process. In industrial and institutional cleaning, it acts as a surface-active agent in formulations targeting hard surfaces where its cationic charge aids adsorption.

The material provides a residual effect that is highly valued in professional cleaning applications. Textile and leather processing operations use it as an antistatic finish and softening agent applied during various wet processing stages.

Cocotrimonium methosulfate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution for ease of handling. Active content concentrations commonly range from 50% to 75% depending on the specific requirements of the industrial application.

These containers are suited to industrial procurement volumes and ensure safe transport. The product remains stable under standard storage conditions and is a versatile component for formulators seeking reliable cationic performance.

name: Cetearyltrimonium chloride
description:
Cetearyltrimonium chloride (CAS 68002-62-0 ), also marketed as ceteartrimonium chloride, is a mixed C16-C18 quaternary ammonium salt used as a conditioning and emulsifying agent across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its cationic charge drives adsorption onto negatively charged surfaces such as hair, fibers, and skin. This delivers a level of substantivity that neutral or anionic surfactants simply cannot achieve in these applications.

In hair care, it functions as the primary conditioning active in rinse-off conditioners, conditioning shampoos, and hair masks. It is highly effective at reducing static and improving both wet and dry combability.

Textile and fabric softener manufacturers use it to coat fiber surfaces during finishing. This imparts softness and reduces friction in both rinse-cycle consumer products and various industrial fabric treatments.

In skin care and emulsion systems, it stabilizes oil-in-water creams and lotions while providing a smooth skin feel. Paper and leather processing operations apply it as a surface-conditioning agent to modify charge.

These applications improve the handling characteristics of treated substrates significantly. Cetearyltrimonium chloride is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 25 to 30 percent active content.

Cosmetic-grade material conforming to standard industry purity requirements is the most common commercial form. Technical-grade solutions are available for textile, paper, and industrial cleaning applications.

description:

name: Dibutyltin dichloride
description:
Dibutyltin dichloride (CAS 683-18-1 ), also known as dibutyltin chloride, is an organotin compound used industrially as a catalyst and stabilizer precursor across polymer and coating systems.

It functions primarily as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of other dibutyltin derivatives and as a direct catalyst in condensation and polymerization processes for various industrial applications.

In PVC and polymer processing, it serves as a precursor to heat stabilizer packages that prevent thermal degradation during compounding and extrusion, ensuring material integrity during high-heat manufacturing.

Coating formulators use it as a catalyst in moisture-cure urethane and silicone systems, where it accelerates crosslinking at ambient conditions to improve the efficiency of the curing process.

In adhesive and sealant manufacturing, it promotes cure in tin-catalyzed RTV silicone formulations, directly affecting open time and bond development for high-performance industrial bonding solutions.

Printing and packaging applications rely on it within specialty ink and lacquer systems requiring controlled polymerization initiation to achieve specific finish and durability requirements for the end user.

Dibutyltin dichloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is available in technical grade, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher depending on the specific supplier specification.

Packaging is offered in drum and bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures a reliable supply chain for large-scale manufacturing operations requiring consistent chemical inputs.

name: Soybean meal
description:
Soybean meal (CAS 68308-36-1 ), also marketed as soy flour, is the protein-rich co-product recovered after oil extraction from soybeans. It functions as a primary protein and amino acid source across animal feed manufacturing and food ingredient applications.

In commercial livestock and aquaculture feed production, soybean meal serves as the dominant plant-based protein ingredient. It supplies the essential amino acid profile required for growth performance in poultry, swine, and fish diets.

Food manufacturers incorporate soy flour into baked goods, meat analogues, and extruded snack products to boost protein content and improve texture. In pet food formulation, it provides a cost-effective protein matrix that complements animal-derived ingredients.

Specialty food processors also use it as a functional binder and protein fortifier in high-protein nutritional products and infant formula blends. This versatility makes it a staple in modern food science and industrial processing.

Soybean meal is supplied in bulk powder and pellet form, with solvent-extracted and expeller-pressed variants available to suit different processing and residue requirements. These options ensure compatibility with various manufacturing systems.

Standard grades include food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with protein content typically declared at 44% or 48% crude protein for feed applications. Quality control ensures consistency across large-scale industrial batches.

Defatted soy flour for food use is available in full-fat, low-fat, and defatted forms. Toasted and non-toasted options are provided depending on specific enzyme activity requirements for the final product formulation.

description:
Cottonseed fatty acids (CAS 68308-51-0 ), also marketed as Emery Vegetable Fatty Acid 600, are a mixed-chain fatty acid blend derived from refined cottonseed oil. They function as surface-active intermediates and lubricating agents across a range of industrial manufacturing processes.

In coatings and alkyd resin production, cottonseed fatty acids serve as reactive raw materials that contribute drying characteristics and film flexibility to finished coatings. Textile and leather processors use them as fiber lubricants and softening agents.

These fatty acids improve handle and reduce friction during mechanical processing. In metalworking fluids and rolling oils, they provide boundary lubrication under moderate load conditions, reducing tool wear and surface defects during production.

Rubber compounders incorporate them as processing aids and internal lubricants to improve flow and mold release during vulcanization. This ensures a more efficient manufacturing cycle and higher quality finished rubber components.

Cottonseed fatty acids are supplied as an amber to yellow liquid at ambient temperatures. Standard commercial grades are available to technical specifications, with quality parameters typically covering acid value, iodine value, color, and moisture content.

Supply is available in drum and bulk quantities, with consistency tied to cottonseed oil crop cycles and regional sourcing. Our products are manufactured to meet rigorous industrial requirements and maintain high performance standards.

name: Soya fatty acids
description:
Soya fatty acids (CAS 68308-53-2 ), also supplied under the designation soybean-oil fatty acids, are a mixed-chain fatty acid blend derived from refined soybean oil. They function as reactive intermediates, surface modifiers, and plasticizing agents across coatings, polymer, and lubricant manufacturing.

In alkyd resin production, soya fatty acids are esterified with polyols to produce semi-drying coatings with controlled flexibility and adhesion for architectural and industrial paints. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate them to improve substrate wetting and adjust tack.

These fatty acids are utilized in both solvent-borne and reactive systems to enhance performance. In plastics and rubber compounding, they act as internal lubricants and softeners, reducing processing torque and improving surface release in finished articles.

Metalworking fluid manufacturers use them as bio-based lubricity additives in cutting and forming fluids. These applications are critical where reduced friction and metal surface conditioning are required for high-performance industrial operations.

Soya fatty acids are supplied as an amber to yellow liquid at ambient temperatures. Standard commercial grades include technical and refined qualities, with distilled grades available for applications requiring tighter acid value and color specifications.

name: Quaternary ammonium ethosulfate
description:
Quaternary ammonium ethosulfate (CAS 68308-64-5 ) is a cationic surfactant derived from coconut oil fatty chains, used across personal care, cleaning, and industrial processing for its conditioning and emulsifying properties.

Its cationic charge makes it effective for modifying substrate surfaces, dispersing actives, and stabilizing formulations where anionic surfactants are unsuitable for the specific chemical environment.

In personal care, it functions as a conditioning agent and emulsifier in hair rinses, conditioners, and skin creams, helping to deposit actives uniformly onto hair and skin surfaces for better results.

Textile and leather processors use it as a softening and antistatic treatment, improving handle and reducing static buildup in finished fabrics during the manufacturing and finishing stages of production.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it for its wetting and dispersion performance, particularly in hard surface cleaners and fabric softeners designed for commercial use.

Water treatment applications leverage its surface-active behavior to aid in dispersion and stabilization of treatment chemical blends, ensuring consistent performance in various aqueous systems.

This material is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with active content concentrations commonly ranging from 50% to 80% in aqueous solution. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Buyers should confirm active content, pH range, and compatibility requirements with the supplier prior to procurement to ensure the material meets the specific needs of their industrial application.

name: Pigment Red 81
description:
Pigment Red 81 (CAS 68310-07-6 ), also supplied as Pigment Red 81:3, is a rhodamine-based fluorescent organic pigment used to produce vivid, high-chroma red and pink colorations across a range of industrial substrates.

Its fluorescent character delivers brightness levels that conventional non-fluorescent pigments cannot match, making it a preferred choice where visual impact is a primary specification requirement.

In printing and packaging, it is used in offset, gravure, and flexographic inks where intense pink-to-red hues are required for labels, folding cartons, and promotional materials.

Textile and paper manufacturers apply it to achieve fluorescent effects in specialty coated papers, cardstock, and dyed fabrics where daylight fluorescence is a defined end-product requirement.

In plastics and polymer systems, it is incorporated into masterbatches for consumer goods, toys, and packaging films requiring bright red or magenta shading for the consumer market.

Coatings formulators use it in solvent-based and UV-curable systems for decorative and industrial surface applications. It provides excellent dispersibility and color strength in these specialized systems.

Pigment Red 81 is supplied as a fine dry powder, typically in press cake or flushed paste form for ink manufacturing. It is available in technical and commercial ink grades for various uses.

Particle size and dispersibility specifications vary by application. Packaging is commonly offered in fiber drums or multi-wall bags for bulk procurement and long-term storage in industrial facilities.

name: Propylene glycol caprylate
description:
Propylene glycol caprylate (CAS 68332-79-6 ), also known as 2-hydroxypropyl octanoate, is an ester of propylene glycol and caprylic acid used as an emollient and solubilizer.

It serves as a carrier across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and food applications. It combines the skin-conditioning profile of a medium-chain fatty ester with the solvent capacity of a glycol derivative.

This makes it a practical multifunctional ingredient for formulators. In personal care, it functions as an emollient and co-emulsifier in skin creams, lotions, and hair conditioners.

It improves spreadability and moisture retention without a heavy feel. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a solubilizing carrier for lipophilic active ingredients in topical and oral preparations.

In food-grade applications, it acts as a flavor carrier and dispersing agent in encapsulated systems. Coatings and adhesive formulations incorporate it as a plasticizing solvent for film flexibility.

Propylene glycol caprylate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications for various industrial and commercial requirements.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meets USP or Ph.Eur. compendial standards where required. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs for large scale manufacturing needs.

name: Ammonium polyphosphate
description:
Ammonium polyphosphate ( CAS 68333-79-9 ), commonly abbreviated as APP, is an inorganic salt used primarily as a flame retardant and intumescent agent across a broad range of industrial materials.

Approved as E545 for certain applications, it functions by releasing ammonia and phosphoric acid under heat, forming a protective char layer that limits flame spread and combustion.

In plastics and polymer compounding, APP is incorporated into polyolefins, polyurethanes, and epoxy systems to meet UL 94 and other fire safety standards without halogenated additives.

Intumescent coatings and fireproofing paints for steel structures rely on APP as the acid source in the intumescent system, activating expansion under fire conditions.

Textile and paper manufacturers apply APP-based treatments to achieve flame-retardant certification for technical fabrics, upholstery, and packaging materials.

In agriculture, it also functions as a concentrated phosphorus and nitrogen fertilizer source, applied in liquid fertilizer blends and foliar formulations.

APP is supplied as a white powder in two principal crystal forms, Phase I and Phase II, with Phase II preferred for most flame retardant applications due to its thermal stability.

Standard grades include uncoated and microencapsulated variants, the latter offering improved compatibility in polymer matrices. Technical and industrial grades are the most commercially prevalent.

These alcohols are used in creams, lotions, and conditioners, contributing to texture and product structure. Home care formulators incorporate them into liquid detergents and fabric softeners to control foam.

They improve surfactant system performance in various household applications. In industrial and institutional cleaning products, they support degreasing efficiency when blended with anionic or nonionic surfactant systems.

It functions as a foam booster, viscosity builder, and emulsifier, helping formulators achieve stable, aesthetically consistent products. In shampoos and liquid hand soaps, it thickens the base effectively.

This ingredient enhances foam volume and creaminess without requiring high loading levels. It stabilizes emulsions in conditioning rinses and cream-based cleansers, improving product texture and shelf stability.

description:
Hydrogenated vegetable oil (CAS 68334-28-1 ) is produced by catalytic hydrogenation of plant-derived oils, converting liquid unsaturated fats into semi-solid or solid fats with improved oxidative stability and extended shelf life.

It functions as a structuring agent, lubricant, and texture modifier across food manufacturing, personal care, and industrial applications. In food production, it provides the solid fat structure required in shortenings and margarines.

Confectionery coatings and filled biscuits utilize this material where controlled melting behavior is critical to end-product texture. Personal care formulators use it to build body and consistency in lip balms and stick deodorants.

Its semi-solid character helps stabilize the finished form in emollient creams. Industrial lubricant manufacturers incorporate it as a base component or additive in metalworking fluids and release agents to reduce friction.

Its film-forming properties are highly effective on metal surfaces. It also functions as a processing aid and mold-release agent in rubber and plastics manufacturing, ensuring efficient production cycles and high-quality finishes.

name: Sodium metasilicate
description:
Sodium metasilicate (CAS 6834-92-0 ), also sold under the E-number E550 , is an inorganic alkali salt used across industrial cleaning, water treatment, and surface processing operations.

It functions primarily as a builder, pH regulator, and corrosion inhibitor in formulated products and process chemicals. In industrial and institutional cleaning, it acts as a detergent builder.

This chemical boosts alkalinity, sequesters hardness ions, and improves soil removal in heavy-duty formulations. Textile and leather processors use it to prepare fiber surfaces and control bath pH.

It is also utilized during scouring and dyeing to improve dye uptake consistency. Water treatment operations apply it as a corrosion inhibitor for metal pipelines to protect iron and steel surfaces.

The compound forms a protective silicate film on these surfaces to prevent degradation. Pulp and paper producers incorporate it into bleaching and sizing processes to stabilize peroxide bleach.

It is also used to control effluent pH in paper manufacturing. Sodium metasilicate is supplied as an anhydrous powder or pentahydrate granules, with the pentahydrate form being the most common.

Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial use, with food-grade material available under the E550 designation for indirect contact or food-processing applications.

Dimethyltin dineodecanoate (CAS 68928-76-7 ) is an organotin compound used as a heat stabilizer and catalyst in polymer processing. It protects PVC and related thermoplastics from thermal degradation during high-temperature compounding and extrusion.

In rigid and flexible PVC formulations, it prevents discoloration and chain degradation during processing, supporting consistent output quality in pipe, profile, and film production.

It also functions as a catalyst in polyurethane and silicone systems, accelerating cure rates in industrial coating and sealant manufacturing. Rubber compounders use it to improve processing stability.

This chemical helps extend service life in finished elastomeric components. In specialty polymer applications, it contributes to long-term stabilization against oxidative and thermal breakdown in demanding environments.

Dimethyltin dineodecanoate is supplied as a liquid, typically in bulk drums or intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial-scale consumption. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering.

Purity specifications are aligned to polymer and rubber processing requirements. Buyers sourcing for sensitive or regulated applications should confirm tin content and compatibility with their specific formulation system.

name: Methyl glucose sesquistearate
description:
Methyl glucose sesquistearate (CAS 68936-95-8 ), commercially known as Glucate SS or Grillocose PS, is a mild, sugar-derived emulsifier used across personal care and industrial formulations.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions while simultaneously providing moisturizing benefits to the skin. In skin care formulations it functions as a primary or co-emulsifier.

This ingredient delivers stable emulsions with a smooth, non-greasy skin feel in creams, lotions, and body butters. Hair care manufacturers incorporate it into conditioning treatments and styling products.

In these applications, it improves spreadability and moisture retention. In home care and industrial cleaning products, it acts as a wetting and dispersing agent, improving surface contact.

It also enhances soil removal efficiency in various cleaning solutions. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it to modify surface tension and support uniform dispersion of pigments or active components.

The material is typically supplied as a waxy solid or flake form, with a melt point suitable for hot-process manufacturing. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification for various uses.

This ensures it meets the quality requirements expected for leave-on and rinse-off personal care applications. Technical-grade material is also available for industrial cleaning and coatings end uses.

name: Hydrogenated polyisobutene
description:
Hydrogenated polyisobutene (CAS 68937-10-0 ) is a fully saturated synthetic hydrocarbon polymer produced by hydrogenating polyisobutene to eliminate residual unsaturation. In personal care and industrial markets, it functions as an emollient, plasticizer, and lubricant base.

This material offers oxidative stability that unsaturated alternatives cannot match. In cosmetics and personal care, it is used as a skin-conditioning emollient in lip products, color cosmetics, and skin creams.

Its non-greasy, spreadable texture improves sensory performance and formula stability. Industrial lubricant formulators incorporate it as a base fluid or additive in gear oils, compressor fluids, and metalworking compounds.

Thermal and oxidative resistance are critical to service life in these industrial applications. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a plasticizer to control tack, flexibility, and low-temperature performance.

It is highly effective in hot-melt and pressure-sensitive systems. In plastics compounding, it acts as a processing aid and softener that improves flexibility without migrating out of the finished part.

Hydrogenated polyisobutene is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid. Viscosity grades range from low to high molecular weight to suit different application requirements across various sectors.

Cosmetic-grade material is available meeting standard purity expectations for personal care use. Technical grades serve industrial lubricant and polymer applications where high performance is required.
