name: Triisobutylenated triphenyl phosphate
description:
Triisobutylenated triphenyl phosphate (CAS 68937-40-6 ), commercially known as DISFLAMOLL 51092, is an organophosphate compound used as a combined flame retardant and plasticizer in polymer systems.

Its dual functionality allows formulators to reduce flammability while maintaining or improving the flexibility of finished materials. In PVC and engineering thermoplastics, it delivers flame retardancy without the need for separate plasticizer additions.

This simplifies formulation and reduces raw material complexity. Building and construction applications include wire and cable jacketing, flooring, and wall coverings where fire performance standards must be met.

Automotive and aerospace interior components rely on it to achieve UL or FAR flammability ratings in flexible and semi-rigid polymer parts. In electronics, it is used in connector housings and enclosures.

It is also utilized in potting compounds where both flame resistance and dimensional stability under thermal stress are required. The product is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions for easy handling.

This makes it suitable for direct blending into polymer matrices or solvent-based systems. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for industrial and polymer processing applications.

Bulk and intermediate packaging options are typical for industrial supply, with drum and IBC formats commonly offered. This ensures efficient logistics and storage for large-scale manufacturing operations.

name: Isopropylphenyl phosphate
description:
Isopropylphenyl phosphate ( CAS 68937-41-7 ), commercially known as IPPP or isopropylated triphenyl phosphate, is an organophosphate ester used as both a flame retardant and plasticizer in demanding industrial applications.

It delivers fire resistance and flexibility simultaneously, reducing the need for multiple additive systems in a single formulation. In plastics and polymer compounding, IPPP functions as a reactive flame retardant-plasticizer.

It is used in PVC, polyurethane foams, and engineering resins, improving processability while meeting flammability standards. Hydraulic fluids and fire-resistant lubricants for aerospace and industrial machinery incorporate IPPP.

This helps to maintain lubrication performance under high-temperature conditions where conventional mineral oils present ignition risk. Automotive interior components use IPPP to satisfy OEM flame retardancy specifications.

These components include wire and cable insulation, seating foams, and under-hood parts. It also appears in metalworking fluids where fire resistance at elevated operating temperatures is a formulation requirement.

IPPP is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically in bulk drums or IBC containers suited to industrial-scale procurement. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for this material.

Specifications are aligned to phosphorus content, viscosity, and acid value as key quality parameters. Buyers should confirm purity and isomer distribution with suppliers as these affect flame retardant efficiency.

These factors also impact compatibility with target polymer systems. Proper handling and storage are essential to maintain the chemical stability and performance characteristics of the product over its shelf life.

name: Silicone polyether
description:
Silicone polyether (CAS 68937-55-3 ), also supplied under designations such as Y-10734 and XF-J 2557, is a silicone-based surfactant that combines the surface-active properties of polyether with the film-forming characteristics of silicone.

It functions as a wetting agent, emulsifier, and foam modifier across a broad range of formulated products. In personal care, it conditions skin and hair by improving spreadability and providing a smooth, non-greasy feel.

This material is frequently used in lotions, serums, and leave-on treatments to enhance texture. Textile and leather processing operations use it to achieve uniform dye penetration and surface leveling during finishing stages.

In agricultural formulations, it lowers surface tension in spray concentrates, improving droplet spread and active ingredient coverage on leaf surfaces. This ensures more efficient delivery of crop protection products.

Household and industrial cleaners incorporate it to control foam levels while maintaining detergency. It remains effective in both low- and high-temperature wash processes, making it a versatile additive for detergents.

Silicone polyether is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid, typically at varying viscosity grades suited to different formulation requirements. Standard supply options include technical and cosmetic-grade specifications.

Selection is driven by the target application and regional regulatory requirements. Bulk supply is available in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) to meet the needs of large-scale industrial manufacturing.

name: Caprylic/Capric Acid
description:
Caprylic/Capric Acid (CAS 68937-75-7 ) is a mixed medium-chain fatty acid blend derived primarily from coconut or palm kernel oil. It functions as an emulsifier, lubricant, and flavoring agent across food and industrial applications.

In food manufacturing, it acts as a flavoring agent and acidulant in dairy products, baked goods, and flavor concentrates where medium-chain character contributes a mild, characteristic fatty note.

Personal care formulators use it as an emollient and emulsifier base in skin creams, cleansers, and hair care products, often as a precursor to caprylic/capric triglyceride esters for topical use.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into lipid-based drug delivery systems and excipient blends where controlled solubilization of active ingredients is required for effective delivery.

In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it provides boundary lubrication and acts as a functional additive in cutting fluids and release agents for various manufacturing processes.

Caprylic/Capric Acid is supplied as a liquid at ambient-to-moderate temperatures, with specific C8:C10 ratio profiles available to meet different formulation requirements and performance needs.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade and technical-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to USP and Ph. Eur. standards for regulated industries.

Bulk supply is typically offered in drums and ISO tank quantities to ensure efficient logistics and consistent supply chain management for large-scale industrial and chemical operations.

name: Trimer fatty acids
description:
Trimer fatty acids (CAS 68937-90-6 ), also supplied under the trade name Empol 1041, are high-molecular-weight polymerized fatty acids produced by trimerizing C18 unsaturated fatty acids.

They function as reactive building blocks and functional additives across coatings, adhesives, and polymer systems where controlled viscosity and flexible chain structure are commercially valuable.

In polyamide and polyurethane resin synthesis, trimer fatty acids contribute chain flexibility and impact resistance to hot-melt adhesives and structural bonding formulations.

Coatings manufacturers use them to modify rheology and improve film flexibility in alkyd and epoxy-based systems. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, their high molecular weight supports boundary lubrication.

These acids ensure film persistence under load. Plasticizer applications leverage their compatibility with polymer matrices to reduce brittleness in sealants and elastomeric compounds without migrating from the substrate.

Trimer fatty acids are supplied as a viscous liquid, typically amber to dark brown in color, in bulk, IBC, and drum formats. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

name: Sunflower seed wax
description:
Sunflower seed wax (CAS 68937-99-5 ) is a natural plant-derived wax obtained from sunflower oil refining, valued across personal care and industrial markets for its structuring and rheology-modifying performance.

It provides firm, stable texture in formulations where synthetic waxes or animal-derived alternatives are being replaced. In cosmetics, it functions as a primary structurant in lip balms, solid sticks, and anhydrous creams.

The wax delivers a clean, non-greasy skin feel that formulators target in natural and clean-label product lines. Coating formulators use it to improve surface hardness and slip resistance in protective coatings.

These coatings are used for paper, packaging, and wood substrates. In lubricant applications, it contributes dry lubrication and release properties in solid lubricant blends and mold-release formulations.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to adjust viscosity and open time in hot-melt systems. Sunflower seed wax is supplied as a solid, typically in flake or pastille form, suited for bulk handling.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with natural and organic-certified grades offered to meet clean-label sourcing requirements for global manufacturers.

name: PEG-10 methyl ether dimethicone
description:
PEG-10 methyl ether dimethicone (CAS 68938-54-5 ), commercially known as Tego Wet 270, is a silicone-based polyether surfactant that bridges the performance gap between silicone and aqueous systems.

It functions as a wetting agent, emulsifier, and surface modifier across personal care, cleaning, and industrial coating applications. In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic formulations, it enables stable silicone-in-water emulsions.

This material contributes a smooth, conditioning skin feel without heavy residue. In textile and fiber processing, it improves substrate wetting and ensures uniform distribution of treatment liquids across hydrophobic surfaces.

Industrial and household cleaning formulations use it to reduce surface tension and enhance spreading on hard-to-wet substrates. In waterborne coatings and adhesive systems, it acts as a substrate wetting agent.

name: Ethoxylated alcohols, C14-15
description:
Ethoxylated alcohols, C14-15 (CAS 68951-67-7 ), also marketed as C14-15 Pareth-7, is a nonionic surfactant derived from fatty alcohols in the C14–C15 chain range. It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and detergent across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations.

In home care and industrial cleaning, it is formulated into hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and laundry detergents where low-foam or controlled-foam profiles are required. These applications benefit from its high efficiency in removing oils.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into rinse-off products such as body washes and shampoos to support emulsification and skin-compatible cleansing. Its mild nature makes it suitable for various cosmetic formulations.

Textile processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to improve fiber penetration during dyeing and finishing operations. This ensures uniform color distribution and high-quality results in textile manufacturing processes.

In industrial settings, it also functions as a dispersant in emulsion polymerization and agricultural formulations. It helps stabilize mixtures and ensures the active ingredients are distributed evenly throughout the solution.

name: Quaternium-18 bentonite
description:
Quaternium-18 bentonite (CAS 68953-58-2 ), also known commercially as Bentone 120, is an organically modified clay produced by treating bentonite with a quaternary ammonium compound.

This material functions as a rheology modifier in non-aqueous systems, controlling viscosity and preventing settling. It builds a stable gel structure in oil-based formulations for industrial use.

In personal care, it thickens and stabilizes anhydrous products such as lipsticks and mascaras. It provides the smooth, non-greasy texture that high-end cosmetic formulations require for performance.

Coatings manufacturers use it to prevent pigment settling and sagging in solvent-borne paints. This is particularly critical for maintaining anti-settling performance during long-term storage of industrial coatings.

In adhesives and sealants, it builds thixotropic body in solvent-based systems. This allows for controlled application without slump or flow, ensuring the material stays exactly where it is applied.

It also functions as a suspending agent in oil-phase systems where uniform dispersion is needed. This ensures that active ingredients or fillers remain evenly distributed throughout the product shelf life.

The product is supplied as a fine, off-white to cream-colored powder. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with the latter meeting strict purity requirements for personal care applications.

Identified by CAS 68954-97-2 , this versatile ingredient is essential for creating stable mixtures. In personal care, it solubilizes fragrance oils, essential oils, and lipophilic actives into aqueous systems effectively.

This capability enables the production of clear gel formulations, micellar waters, and rinse-off products without cloudiness. Pharmaceutical formulators use it to improve the oral bioavailability of poorly water-soluble APIs.

It is particularly effective in self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDS) and soft gel capsules. In food and nutraceutical applications, it supports the encapsulation and emulsification of fat-soluble vitamins and flavor compounds.

Coating and adhesive formulators use it as a plasticizing carrier and dispersant for pigment and resin systems. These applications require low-viscosity, hydrophilic-compatible processing to ensure high-quality finished products.

name: Sodium C12-18 alkyl sulfate

In personal care, it functions as the primary cleansing agent in shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps, producing stable lather at moderate use levels. Home care and industrial cleaning products rely on it for grease and soil removal.

It is frequently utilized in hard surface cleaners, laundry detergents, and industrial degreasers. Textile processors use it as a scouring and wetting agent to strip oils and sizing agents from fabric prior to dyeing or finishing.

In paper and leather manufacturing, it supports emulsification and dispersion of processing aids throughout wet-end operations. This versatile surfactant ensures consistent performance in diverse industrial environments and chemical processes.

name: Potassium polyphosphate
description:
Potassium polyphosphate (CAS 68956-75-2 ), also known commercially as Rapisol, is an inorganic polyphosphate salt used across water treatment, food processing, and agricultural applications.

It functions primarily as a sequestrant and dispersing agent, binding metal ions and preventing scale formation or unwanted precipitation in complex formulations and industrial systems.

In water treatment, it inhibits scale deposition and controls corrosion in distribution systems by sequestering calcium and magnesium ions before they can precipitate.

Food processors use it as a sequestrant and stabilizer in processed meats, dairy products, and beverages, where it controls mineral activity and improves texture retention.

In agriculture, it serves as a soluble potassium and phosphorus source in liquid fertilizer formulations, delivering nutrients in a form that remains stable in concentrated solutions.

Industrial cleaning and detergent formulators incorporate it for its ability to disperse hardness ions and improve the performance of active ingredients in hard water conditions.

Potassium polyphosphate is typically supplied as a white powder or granule. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms.

name: Triisopalmitin
description:
Triisopalmitin (CAS 68957-79-9 ), also known as Glycerol Triisopalmitate, is a triglyceride ester of isopalmitic acid and glycerol used across personal care, food, and industrial formulations.

It functions primarily as an emollient, lubricant, and emulsifier, providing skin-conditioning and texture-modifying performance in finished products. In personal care, it is used in skin creams and lotions.

It is also used in color cosmetics to deliver a smooth, non-greasy skin feel while improving spreadability and formulation stability. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a fat component or emulsifier.

This is particularly useful in specialty fat blends where controlled crystallization and texture are required. In lubricant formulations, its ester structure supports film formation and friction reduction.

This performance is ideal for light-duty or biodegradable lubricant systems. It also functions as a humectant carrier in leave-on cosmetic formats, helping to retain moisture at the skin surface.

Triisopalmitin is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity oil at ambient temperature, suitable for direct incorporation into oil phases. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specs.

name: Glyoxal-hydroxyethyl cellulose copolymer
description:

The crosslinking imparts controlled water solubility and thickening behavior that standard hydroxyethyl cellulose cannot achieve, making it a distinct choice for formulators requiring modified rheological profiles.

In architectural and industrial coatings, it functions as a rheology modifier that resists sagging while maintaining open time and brush drag characteristics during the application process.

Textile and paper processors use it as a sizing and finishing agent where controlled film formation and moisture retention are required for high-quality industrial manufacturing and processing.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products to build viscosity and stabilize emulsions without excessive tackiness, ensuring a smooth and consistent final texture.

In construction materials such as tile adhesives and joint compounds, it supports water retention and workability during application, providing essential structural integrity for building projects.

name: Monoglycerides

Monoglycerides (CAS 68990-53-4 ) are partial glycerol esters derived from C14–C22 fatty acids, functioning as food-grade emulsifiers and industrial plasticizers across multiple manufacturing sectors.

Dandelion extract (CAS 68990-74-9 ), also known as Taraxacum officinale extract, is a botanical ingredient derived from the dandelion plant. It is used across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical manufacturing as a natural flavoring agent and antioxidant.

This bioactive additive is essential for finished formulations requiring natural sourcing. In food and beverage production, it delivers a characteristic bitter note to herbal teas and soft drinks. Its FEMA 2358 status supports its use as a recognized flavoring ingredient.

Functional food producers and nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it into capsules, tablets, and liquid formulations. These products often target digestive and liver health positioning within the global health and wellness market segments.

In personal care, it is used in topical creams, serums, and cleansing products. Formulation priorities in these applications typically focus on antioxidant activity and the benefits of botanical sourcing for high-end skincare lines.

Agricultural and feed applications include its use as a natural preservative or bioactive additive. It is frequently found in specialty feed blends designed for specific nutritional requirements in the livestock and pet food industries.

The material is supplied as a dry powder, liquid extract, or spray-dried concentrate. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, ensuring compliance with various industrial safety and quality protocols.

Standardized extracts are available at defined ratios or active compound concentrations to meet specific formulation needs. Organic-certified material is also commercially available for suppliers serving clean-label and natural product markets.

Quality control ensures the extract meets rigorous industry benchmarks for purity and potency. Manufacturers can select from various concentrations to achieve the desired functional properties in their final commercial products.

name: Mannitol
description:
Mannitol (CAS 69-65-8 ), also known by the food additive designation E421 , is a sugar alcohol sourced primarily from natural origins and used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions as a low-calorie bulk sweetener, humectant, and excipient. It is valued for its non-hygroscopic character in solid dosage forms and its clean, mild sweetness in food applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is a preferred filler and diluent for tablets and capsules, particularly in direct compression and freeze-drying processes where moisture uptake must be minimized.

Confectionery and chewing gum producers use it as a dusting agent and sweetener that resists sticking and delivers a cooling mouthfeel. It provides a stable texture in various food products.

Parenteral formulations rely on this ingredient as an osmotic agent in intravenous solutions, where precise tonicity control is critical for patient safety and product efficacy during medical use.

In personal care, it acts as a humectant and chelating agent in skincare formulations, helping to stabilize active ingredients and retain moisture in the product matrix for better performance.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Recognized quality standards include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , covering both pharmaceutical and food-grade requirements.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for specialty or R&D applications. Granulated forms are often preferred for direct compression tableting processes.

name: Salicylic acid
description:
Salicylic acid (CAS 69-72-7 ) is an organic acid used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food applications primarily for its preservative, keratolytic, and stabilizing functions. FEMA 3985 status supports its use as a flavoring agent in regulated food contexts.

Procurement interest centers on its dual role as both an active ingredient and a functional additive. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of aspirin and as an active in topical acne treatments.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into exfoliating cleansers, anti-dandruff shampoos, and peeling agents where controlled keratolytic action is required. It is valued for its ability to penetrate pores and improve skin texture effectively.

Food and beverage producers reference its flavoring designation for applications, particularly in small-quantity use within regulated formulations. It also functions as a preservative in certain topical and industrial preparations where microbial control is needed.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both pharmaceutical and technical grades. USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades are standard for regulated pharmaceutical and cosmetic applications to ensure purity.

Technical grade is available for industrial and intermediate synthesis use where compendial certification is not required. This grade offers a cost-effective solution for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing requirements.

name: Isotridecanol ethoxylated
description:
Isotridecanol ethoxylated (CAS 69011-36-5 ), also known as Trideceth (branched), is a nonionic surfactant produced by ethoxylating branched isotridecanol to varying degrees.

It delivers low-foam emulsification, wetting, and detergency across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations. In household and industrial cleaning products, it functions as the primary surfactant.

It is used in hard-surface cleaners, degreasers, and all-purpose concentrates where controlled foam and strong soil removal are required. Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off products.

In shampoos and body washes, its mildness and emulsifying efficiency support stable formulation at moderate use levels. Textile processing relies on it as a wetting and scouring agent for uniform dye penetration.

It ensures effective removal of oils and sizing agents from fabric. In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports degreasing baths and process chemical dispersions where surface activity is critical.

Isotridecanol ethoxylated is supplied as a liquid or paste depending on the degree of ethoxylation, with ethoxylate chain lengths typically ranging from 3 to 20 EO units for various needs.

Technical-grade material is the standard market offering, with specific grades selected by EO content to match HLB requirements for a given application. Bulk liquid supply is the common format.

The product is typically distributed in drums and IBCs. This versatile chemical ensures consistent performance across diverse industrial sectors while meeting rigorous technical specifications for global trade.

name: Silica fume
description:
Silica fume (CAS 69012-64-2 ) is an ultrafine industrial byproduct collected during silicon and ferrosilicon alloy production. It functions as a pozzolanic binder and rheology modifier in cementitious systems.

The material reacts with calcium hydroxide to densify matrix microstructure in various applications. In high-performance concrete, it is incorporated to reduce permeability and increase compressive strength.

This makes it the material of choice for bridges, marine structures, and tunnel linings. Refractory manufacturers use it to improve castable flow and sintered density in furnace linings and ladles.

These components operate under extreme thermal conditions in industrial settings. In mining, it is added to shotcrete mixes to accelerate early strength gain and reduce rebound loss in underground support.

Pulp and paper facilities use the product in cementitious flooring and containment structures. This is particularly useful where chemical resistance and durability are critical for long-term operations.

The product is supplied as a dry densified powder or undensified powder. Densified grades are often preferred for bulk handling and reduced dusting during the manufacturing and mixing process.

It is also available as a slurry for direct addition to ready-mix concrete operations. Standard grades conform to ASTM C1240 and EN 13263 specifications for industrial use.

These standards define minimum SiO₂ content and physical requirements for use in concrete applications. This ensures consistent performance and quality across various construction and refractory projects.

Contact us for supply of Silica fume

physicalProperties.Appearance: Amorphous silica, the noncrystalline form of SiO2, is a transparent to gray, odorless, amorphous powder
physicalProperties.Form: Fine white powder with particle sizes generally below 1mm. This is not the same as the commercial products “fumes silica,” “silica gel,” “precipitated silica,” or “fused silica.” It is formed during the electric arc production of elemental silicon from quartz, which is reduced to silicon monoxide, escaping from the furnace and oxidized by air to silicon dioxide. This condenses to form spherical particles. For the production of ferrosilicon, iron metal is added to the charge; during charging there is also exposure to crystalline silica.

name: Ethoxylated propoxylated C8-18 alcohols
description:
Ethoxylated propoxylated C8-18 alcohols (CAS 69013-18-9 ), commercially known as Imbentin PPF, is a nonionic surfactant produced by sequential ethoxylation and propoxylation of medium-to-long chain fatty alcohols.

It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and cleaning agent across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations. In home care and industrial cleaning, it delivers effective degreasing and soil removal.

This versatile chemical is used in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and industrial detergent concentrates. Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products where controlled emulsification is required.

The surfactant provides mild moisturizing properties for cosmetic applications. Textile processing operations use it as a wetting and scouring agent to improve fiber penetration and soil release during fabric preparation.

In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports uniform dispersion of treatment agents. It also improves substrate wettability during various processing stages to ensure high-quality finished goods for manufacturers.

Ethoxylated propoxylated C8-18 alcohols are typically supplied as a liquid. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial and cleaning applications, while cosmetic-grade material is available for personal care.

Drum and IBC packaging are the most common supply formats for bulk procurement. This product meets rigorous industrial specifications to ensure consistent performance across diverse manufacturing and cleaning sectors.

name: Hydroxy-terminated polybutadiene
description:
Hydroxy-terminated polybutadiene (CAS 69102-90-5 ), commonly known as HTPB, is a liquid reactive oligomer with hydroxyl end groups that allow it to be cured into flexible elastomeric networks.

It functions as a reactive binder, plasticizer, and crosslinkable base polymer across demanding industrial applications where low-temperature flexibility and chemical resistance are required for the final product.

In solid rocket propellant and explosive formulations, HTPB acts as the primary binder matrix, holding energetic fillers in a processable, castable composite for aerospace and defense sectors.

Polyurethane sealants and elastomers use HTPB as a soft-segment diol, reacting with isocyanates to produce systems with outstanding low-temperature performance for aerospace and construction joints.

In coatings and corrosion-resistant linings, it contributes flexibility and adhesion to substrates exposed to harsh chemical environments, ensuring long-term durability and structural integrity.

Adhesive formulators incorporate HTPB into structural and pressure-sensitive systems where elongation and impact resistance are critical performance requirements for industrial bonding applications.

HTPB is supplied as a viscous liquid at ambient temperature, typically in drum and IBC packaging. Standard commercial grades are characterized by hydroxyl functionality and molecular weight.

Both industrial and aerospace-qualified grades are available, with buyers typically referencing specifications such as R-45M or equivalent for propellant and high-performance elastomer applications.

name: Malic acid
description:
Malic acid (CAS 6915-15-7 ), also known as E296 , is a dicarboxylic hydroxy acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as an acidulant, pH regulator, and flavor enhancer.

This chemical delivers a smooth, tart taste profile preferred over citric acid in many formulations. In food and beverage production, it acidifies confectionery, fruit-flavored drinks, and low-calorie products while extending shelf life.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to adjust pH in oral solutions, effervescent tablets, and chewable formulations where taste masking is a priority. It is essential for maintaining stability in complex medicinal mixtures.

In personal care, it acts as a buffering agent in leave-on and rinse-off products such as toners, shampoos, and chemical exfoliants. It also functions as a synergist with other preservative systems in cosmetic formulations.

This synergy improves antimicrobial efficacy at controlled pH ranges, ensuring product safety. Malic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule, with granulated forms preferred for direct compression in tablet manufacturing.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical grade for industrial applications. Both L-malic acid and DL-malic acid are commercially available for various industrial needs.

Buyers specify chirality based on application and regulatory requirements for their specific region. The material is highly soluble and integrates easily into aqueous solutions for consistent manufacturing results.

Inositol (CAS 6917-35-7 ), also known as myo-inositol, is a naturally occurring sugar alcohol used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a humectant, nutrient supplement, and stabilizing agent in finished formulations.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, inositol is formulated into capsules, powders, and fortified beverages targeting metabolic and reproductive health support. Feed manufacturers incorporate it into premixes and animal nutrition products.

In these applications, it contributes to lipid metabolism and liver function in livestock and aquaculture species. Personal care formulators use it in skin creams and serums for its moisture-retention properties.

It is particularly effective in products positioned around skin barrier support. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an excipient and active ingredient in tablet and powder formulations for various therapeutic uses.

In personal care, it functions as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent in moisturizers, serums, and sunscreens, while also enhancing the efficacy of preservation systems.

The compound stabilizes foam generated by primary surfactants such as sodium lauryl sulfate. Home care and industrial cleaners rely on it to boost detergency and maintain foam structure across a range of pH conditions.

name: 7-Methyloctanoic acid
description:
7-Methyloctanoic acid (CAS 693-19-6 ), also known commercially as isopelargonic acid, is a branched-chain fatty acid used across industrial formulation chemistry.

Its branched structure resists oxidation and crystallization, making it a preferred building block for esters, metallic soaps, and specialty intermediates where straight-chain acids underperform.

In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor and lubricity additive, particularly in formulations requiring oxidative stability under high-temperature conditions.

Personal care manufacturers use it to produce ester derivatives, such as isononyl esters, that deliver lightweight emolliency in skin and hair products for various applications.

In plastics and polymer processing, it serves as a precursor to plasticizers and metal soap stabilizers that improve flexibility and processing behavior in PVC and related systems.

Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate its metallic salt forms as driers or adhesion-promoting components in solvent-borne systems to enhance overall product performance.

7-Methyloctanoic acid is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity typically specified at 98% or higher.

description:
Dodecanedioic acid (CAS 693-23-2 ), commonly abbreviated as DDDA, is a long-chain dicarboxylic acid used as a building block in polymer synthesis and a functional acid in lubricant formulations.

It bridges specialty chemical and commodity markets, with demand driven primarily by nylon and corrosion inhibitor production. It also serves as a surface-active agent in personal care and industrial applications.

In plastics and polymers, DDDA is a key monomer in the production of Nylon 6,12 and Nylon 12,12. Its longer carbon chain delivers improved flexibility and lower moisture absorption compared to shorter-chain diacids.

The material provides better chemical resistance for high-performance polymers. Lubricant and metalworking formulators use it to produce diester base fluids and corrosion inhibitors suited for biodegradable lubricant systems.

In personal care, it functions as an emulsifier and texture modifier in creams and rinse-off products. Its surface-modifying behavior supports formulation stability across various cosmetic and industrial applications.

Food-contact and flavor-adjacent applications also draw on DDDA as an acidulant and processing aid in approved formulations. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy handling and processing.

Standard commercial grades include technical and polymer-grade specifications. Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher to meet monomer-grade requirements for sensitive chemical synthesis and manufacturing.

description:
Ethyl hydrogen sebacate (CAS 693-55-0 ), also known as monoethyl sebacate, is a half-ester of sebacic acid used as a reactive intermediate and functional additive across polymer and lubricant formulations.

It provides one free carboxylic acid group and one ethyl ester group, giving formulators a chemically addressable building block for controlled crosslinking, plasticization, and surface protection.

In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a plasticizer and softener, improving flexibility in PVC and specialty polymer compounds without the volatility concerns of shorter-chain esters.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it for its corrosion-inhibiting properties, particularly in metalworking fluids where protection of ferrous and non-ferrous surfaces is a qualification requirement.

Coating and adhesive manufacturers use it as a reactive modifier to tune adhesion, flexibility, and film integrity in alkyd and polyurethane systems during the manufacturing process.

It also serves as a synthesis intermediate for producing diester lubricant base stocks and sebacate-based plasticizers at commercial scale for various industrial applications.

name: 2-methylimidazole

This chemical enables manufacturers to achieve controlled cure profiles across a range of thermoset formulations. In electronics manufacturing, 2-MZ is a standard curing agent for epoxy-based printed circuit board laminates.

It is also utilized in underfill compounds and encapsulants where precise Tg control is critical. Powder coating formulators use it to catalyze epoxy-polyester hybrid systems, adjusting cure speed and flow characteristics.

It combines carboxymethyl and hydroxypropyl functionalities with crosslinking to deliver thickening and binding performance across demanding industrial systems. In construction, it functions as a rheology modifier.

It is used in tile adhesives, joint compounds, and cement-based mortars, improving workability and reducing slump. Pulp and paper manufacturers use it as a wet-end additive and surface sizing agent.

name: Polysiloxanes di-Me hydroxy-terminated
description:
Polysiloxanes di-Me hydroxy-terminated (CAS 70131-67-8 ), commercially known as hydroxy-terminated polydimethylsiloxane or PDMS-OH, is a reactive silicone polymer used as a building block and functional additive across silicone-based manufacturing.

The terminal hydroxyl groups enable direct participation in crosslinking and condensation cure reactions, making it a primary raw material rather than a passive additive in industrial formulations.

In sealant and elastomer production, it serves as the base polymer for room-temperature vulcanizing (RTV) silicone systems, where the hydroxyl end groups react with crosslinkers to form durable, flexible networks.

Coatings and release liner formulations use it to control surface energy and improve substrate wetting without compromising film integrity. In rubber compounding and tire manufacturing, it functions as a processing aid.

It acts as a reactive modifier that adjusts flow behavior and final mechanical properties. Textile and paper treatment processes apply it to impart softness, water repellency, and controlled slip to finished surfaces.

Supplied as a clear to slightly hazy viscous liquid, it is available across a broad viscosity range, typically from low-viscosity fluids to high-viscosity gums, to suit different processing requirements.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with viscosity specifications used as the primary quality parameter for grade differentiation. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC containers depending on volume.

name: Polyethylene glycol-30 dipolyhydroxystearate
description:
Polyethylene glycol-30 dipolyhydroxystearate (CAS 70142-34-6 ), also known commercially as Polyethylene glycol-15-hydroxystearate, is a polymeric emulsifier derived from hydroxystearic acid and polyethylene glycol.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations where conventional emulsifiers fall short. In cosmetic formulations, it enables stable emulsions in sunscreens and lotions.

This is particularly useful where high oil-phase loads or UV filters are difficult to suspend. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to solubilize and disperse poorly water-soluble active ingredients in topical and oral dosage forms.

In textile processing, it functions as a wetting and dispersing agent that improves dye penetration and surface uniformity on synthetic fibers. Food-contact and industrial applications leverage its emulsifying performance.

The material maintains stability in systems requiring compatibility across a broad range of pH and temperature conditions. Polyethylene glycol-30 dipolyhydroxystearate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or paste.

Handling characteristics vary by temperature, and it is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. The latter often aligns to excipient standards relevant to topical and oral formulations.

Bulk supply is standard in drum or container quantities, with smaller packaging available for formulation development. This versatile emulsifier ensures long-term stability and performance in complex chemical systems.

name: Sodium hydroxymethylglycinate

Sodium hydroxymethylglycinate (CAS 70161-44-3 ) is a formaldehyde-releasing preservative used across personal care and industrial formulations. It controls microbial growth in water-based systems, extending shelf life and protecting product integrity.

In personal care, it preserves rinse-off and leave-on formulations including shampoos, conditioners, lotions, and liquid soaps. It is often used in combination with other preservatives to broaden the antimicrobial spectrum.

Water-based coatings and architectural paints rely on it as an in-can preservative to prevent bacterial and fungal contamination. This ensures stability during storage and application for various decorative and protective finishes.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it into water-borne systems where microbial degradation would otherwise compromise viscosity. Maintaining bond performance is critical for these industrial applications over time.

Its compatibility with a wide pH range also makes it a practical choice for preserving emulsified systems. This versatility is particularly valuable in the production of industrial cleaning products and detergents.

Sodium hydroxymethylglycinate is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at concentrations around 50%. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades to meet specific purity requirements for different sectors.

Cosmetic-grade material meets the necessary standards for use in personal care formulations. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers suited to industrial procurement volumes and logistics.

name: Pigment Red 48
description:
Pigment Red 48 (CAS 7023-61-2 ), commercially designated PR48:2, is an azo-based calcium lake pigment delivering strong, bluish-red hues across a broad range of industrial substrates.

It is produced as a metal salt complex that provides good tinctorial strength and resistance properties suited to demanding coloration applications in various manufacturing sectors.

In printing inks, particularly offset, flexographic, and publication gravure, PR48:2 is valued for its clean masstone and acceptable lightfastness in short-run and packaging formats.

Plastic coloration of polyolefins and PVC uses this pigment to achieve consistent red shades in consumer goods, films, and molded components across the global supply chain.

Coatings formulators incorporate it into decorative and industrial paints where a cost-effective, bright red with reasonable alkali resistance is required for long-term stability.

Paper dyeing and textile printing operations also draw on PR48:2 for surface coloration where substrate penetration is limited and surface deposit is the primary mechanism.

Pigment Red 48 is supplied as a dry powder, typically in press cake form or as a flushed paste for direct ink incorporation into existing production lines and workflows.

name: Lanolin oil
description:
Lanolin oil (CAS 70321-63-0 ), the liquid fraction of wool wax, is a refined emollient and lubricant used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications. Unlike solid lanolin, its low-viscosity form integrates readily into formulations without contributing waxy texture or opacity.

Liquid lanolin oil delivers moisture retention, surface conditioning, and lubrication in a single raw material. In cosmetics and skincare, it functions as an emollient in lip balms, hand creams, and hair conditioners, improving skin feel and reducing transepidermal water loss.

This material provides effective hydration without occlusive heaviness. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into topical ointments and barrier creams where controlled moisturization and compatibility with active ingredients are required for the final product.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a fiber lubricant and conditioning agent, reducing friction during processing and improving finished material suppleness. It is highly valued for its ability to penetrate fibers and provide long-lasting protection.

In industrial coatings and sealant systems, it acts as a plasticizer and rheology modifier, improving spreadability and substrate adhesion. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers looking to enhance the physical properties of their chemical blends.

Lanolin oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. Standard grades include cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with pharmaceutical supply typically conforming to USP or BP specifications for safety and purity.

Technical-grade material is available for textile and industrial applications where purity thresholds are less stringent. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality across all batches to meet the rigorous demands of global manufacturing and formulation standards.

name: Benzotriazole BT
description:
Benzotriazole BT (CAS 70321-86-7 ) is a high-performance UV absorber used to protect polymer systems and coatings from photodegradation. Commercially recognized under the trade name Tinuvin 234, it intercepts UV radiation before it can initiate chain scission.

This chemical prevents color shift in finished materials and is essential for maintaining structural integrity. In industrial and automotive coatings, it prevents yellowing and gloss loss in clear coats and pigmented topcoats.

These coatings are often exposed to prolonged outdoor weathering and require robust protection. Plastics processors incorporate it into polycarbonate, PET, and engineering thermoplastics where long-term transparency is critical.

Mechanical retention is also a key benefit for these materials during their lifecycle. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to extend service life in construction and transportation assemblies subject to UV exposure.

Printing and packaging applications rely on it to protect UV-curable inks and laminate films from fading. This is particularly important during outdoor display or storage where light exposure is constant and intense.

Benzotriazole BT is supplied as a white to off-white powder for easy handling. It is available in technical grade for industrial polymer and coatings applications, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher.

Packaging options generally range from kilogram-scale bags to bulk quantities suited for large-volume compounding operations. This ensures flexibility for both small-scale testing and full industrial production requirements.

name: Avobenzone
description:
Avobenzone (CAS 70356-09-1 ), also marketed as Parsol 1789 and Escalol 517, is a UVA-absorbing active used across suncare, personal care, and industrial UV protection applications.

It provides broad-spectrum UVA coverage in the 320–400 nm range, making it one of the most specified UVA filters in regulated markets globally for various consumer and industrial goods.

In sunscreen and daily-wear cosmetic formulations, it is the primary UVA active, often combined with UVB filters to achieve broad-spectrum compliance under FDA OTC monograph or EU cosmetic regulations.

Coatings and polymer formulators incorporate it to protect substrates, including plastics, adhesives, and sealants, from UVA-induced degradation and discoloration during outdoor exposure and high UV stress.

In personal care beyond suncare, it appears in moisturizers, lip products, and foundations where incidental UVA protection is a formulation requirement for daily skin health and product stability.

Stabilizer packages frequently pair it with photostabilizers such as Tinosorb S or octocrylene to counter its known photodegradation in finished products and ensure long-lasting efficacy for the user.

In cosmetics and personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning humectant and deodorant active, appearing in creams, lotions, and underarm products where it disrupts microbial cell membranes.

Paired with phenoxyethanol or other preservative systems, it extends antimicrobial coverage and supports clean-label formulation strategies increasingly demanded by modern brand owners.

description:
L-Cysteine Hydrochloride Monohydrate (CAS 7048-04-6 ), also known as L-Cys HCl and listed as E920 in food applications, is the stabilized salt form of the amino acid L-cysteine. In commercial baking, E920 reduces mixing time and improves dough extensibility in bread, crackers, and pizza bases by cleaving disulfide bonds in gluten networks. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a precursor in amino acid infusion formulations and as a stabilizing agent in peptide synthesis.

In personal care, it is the active ingredient in professional hair relaxing and waving treatments, where it modifies keratin structure without the harshness of thioglycolate systems. Food and nutraceutical producers also incorporate it into flavor development applications.

In these savory applications, it acts as a precursor to meat-like aroma compounds in processed products. L-Cysteine Hydrochloride Monohydrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder that is highly soluble in water. It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades for pharmaceutical use.

Tetraethylene glycol diheptanoate (CAS 70729-68-9 ), also referred to as TEGDH, is a synthetic diester built from tetraethylene glycol and heptanoic acid. It functions as a lubricant base fluid and plasticizer.

name: Trideceth-8 carboxylic acid
description:
Trideceth-8 carboxylic acid (CAS 70750-17-3 ) is a nonionic-anionic ethoxylated carboxylic acid surfactant derived from C12-13 fatty alcohols. It combines the mildness of ethoxylated nonionics with the anionic character of a carboxylate group.

This unique chemical structure makes it effective across a broad pH range for emulsification, wetting, and cleaning applications. In personal care formulations, it functions as a mild emulsifier and cleansing agent.

It is frequently utilized in shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers where low irritation potential is a priority. Industrial and institutional cleaning products use it as a low-foaming detergent component.

The surfactant is particularly effective for hard surface cleaners and degreasers, especially in alkaline systems. Textile processing benefits from its wetting and scouring performance during fiber preparation.

It is also used in dyeing auxiliaries where consistent surface penetration is critical for quality results. In leather and paper processing, it supports emulsification of treatment baths and improves uniformity.

This chemical helps achieve surface consistency during finishing operations in various manufacturing sectors. Trideceth-8 carboxylic acid is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity paste for easy handling.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades, with cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity standards for personal care use. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers for industrial scale.

name: Alcohols, C12-13, ethoxylated propoxylated
description:
Alcohols, C12-13, ethoxylated propoxylated (CAS 70750-27-5 ), commercially available as Noigen DL 0415 and NTD 02, is a nonionic surfactant built on a C12-13 fatty alcohol backbone.

This chemical is modified with both ethylene oxide and propylene oxide blocks. This dual-alkoxylation structure delivers a tunable hydrophilic-lipophilic balance for various industrial uses.

It is effective across emulsification, degreasing, and dispersion applications in industrial and consumer formulations. In home care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant to solubilize oils.

Its low-foaming behavior is ideally suited to machine-wash and spray systems. Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform dye penetration.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it stabilizes pigment dispersions and improves substrate wetting. Personal care formulators incorporate it as an emulsifier and mild moisturizing agent.

It is used in rinse-off and leave-on systems where mildness to skin is a priority. The material is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature, typically in drum and IBC quantities.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with specific mole ratios varying by product. Buyers should confirm HLB value and EO/PO ratio with the supplier to match the application.

name: Octenidine dihydrochloride
description:
Octenidine dihydrochloride (CAS 70775-75-6 ), also marketed as Octenidine HCl, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used in pharmaceutical and personal care formulations. It delivers effective bactericidal and fungicidal action at low concentrations.

This makes it a preferred preservative and antiseptic ingredient for topical and mucosal applications. In pharmaceutical wound care, it is the active ingredient in antiseptic wound gels, rinses, and impregnated dressings.

These applications are ideal where alcohol-free, tissue-compatible disinfection is required. Oral care products such as antiseptic mouthwashes and throat sprays rely on it for plaque-reducing and antimicrobial efficacy.

In personal care, it functions as a preservative and antimicrobial booster in leave-on and rinse-off formulations. This includes intimate hygiene products and skin cleansers where gentle yet effective action is needed.

It is also used in catheter care solutions and surgical site preparation products within hospital-grade antiseptic lines. The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications suited for topical and mucosal drug product manufacturing. Bulk quantities are typically offered for direct formulation use with full documentation packages.

These packages support procurement processes that must remain GMP -compliant. The high purity of the compound ensures stability and performance across a wide range of medical and cosmetic applications.

name: Chloramine-T trihydrate

Chloramine-T trihydrate (CAS 7080-50-4 ), also known as Sodium p-toluenesulfonchloramide, is an active chlorine-releasing compound used commercially as a biocide, disinfectant, and oxidizing agent.

It delivers controlled antimicrobial action across regulated industries where precise, stable halogen release is required. In water treatment, it functions as a disinfection agent for potable water systems and process water.

Its slower chlorine release reduces disinfection byproduct formation compared to free chlorine. Pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturers use it to sanitize equipment, surfaces, and production environments under validated cleaning protocols.

In food processing facilities, it serves as a surface disinfectant for food-contact materials, helping meet hygiene compliance requirements. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a preservative and bleaching agent.

This chemical is utilized in select topical and oral hygiene product lines. The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder with standardized active chlorine content, typically around 25%.

It is available in technical and pharmaceutical grades, with pharmaceutical-grade material commonly meeting BP or Ph. Eur. specifications. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial formats.

name: Troxerutin
description:
Troxerutin (CAS 7085-55-4 ), also marketed as Venoruton P4 and known in some markets as Vitamin P4, is a semi-synthetic flavonoid derivative of rutin used as an active pharmaceutical ingredient and cosmetic active.

It functions primarily as an antioxidant and vascular-protective agent across pharmaceutical and personal care formulations. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in oral and topical products.

These products target chronic venous insufficiency, hemorrhoids, and capillary fragility, appearing in tablets, capsules, and gels. Topical gel and cream formulations leverage its antioxidant activity to reduce puffiness.

It supports microcirculation in dermocosmetic products and is incorporated into eye contour creams and anti-fatigue serums. In these applications, reducing periorbital edema is a primary claim for the formulation.

Its humectant behavior also supports moisture retention in leave-on skin formulations, improving texture alongside the active benefit. The material is supplied as a yellow to yellowish-brown crystalline powder.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with purity typically ≥95% or ≥98% by HPLC, conforming to pharmacopoeial standards including those referenced in Chinese Pharmacopoeia and EP monographs.

Cosmetic-grade supply is also available for personal care applications where full pharmaceutical specification is not required. This ensures versatility for manufacturers across different regulatory environments and product types.

This versatile ingredient bridges oil and water phases while supporting moisture retention in finished products. In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetics, including lotions, creams, and hair conditioners, it stabilizes emulsions effectively.

It improves skin feel without leaving heavy residue, making it ideal for high-end formulations. Formulators incorporate it into cleansing systems such as body washes and facial cleansers to enhance wetting and solubilize oils.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it supports soil removal by improving surface wetting. It is particularly effective at dispersing oily soils across hard surfaces in various commercial and residential environments.

Cucumber Seed Oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, typically in bulk drums or intermediate bulk containers. It is available in cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications to meet diverse industry requirements.

Coatings formulators use it as a coalescing solvent and plasticizing component in industrial and decorative systems to improve film formation and flexibility across various substrates.

name: L-histidine
description:
L-Histidine (CAS 71-00-1 ), commonly abbreviated as His, is a proteinogenic amino acid sourced for use across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as a buffering agent, stabilizer, and nutritional building block in finished formulations.

In biopharmaceutical manufacturing, His is the preferred buffering agent in monoclonal antibody and protein drug formulations, where it maintains pH stability and protects against aggregation during storage.

Nutritional supplement producers use it as an active ingredient in amino acid blends, sports nutrition products, and clinical nutrition formulas targeting muscle recovery and metabolic support.

Food manufacturers apply it as a flavor precursor — FEMA 3694 — where it contributes to savory and meat-like taste profiles in processed and seasoned products.

In cosmetic formulations, it functions as a humectant and antioxidant stabilizer in skin care products, helping to protect active ingredients from oxidative degradation.

L-Histidine is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both free base and monohydrochloride salt forms. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade FCC .

The pharmaceutical grades are the most commonly specified for injectable and parenteral applications. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric ton quantities to meet both development-scale and commercial production requirements.

name: Benzene
description:
Benzene (CAS 71-43-2 ) is a foundational aromatic hydrocarbon used as a chemical intermediate and solvent across petrochemical and industrial manufacturing. It serves as a primary building block for producing a broad range of downstream chemicals at industrial scale.

The largest commercial use of benzene is in the production of ethylbenzene, cumene, and cyclohexane. These intermediates feed into styrene, phenol, and nylon supply chains respectively, supporting global manufacturing sectors.

In the pharmaceutical sector, it functions as a process solvent and precursor in the synthesis of active ingredients and fine chemicals. Dye and pigment manufacturers rely on benzene-derived intermediates to produce colorants.

These colorants are used extensively in printing inks and packaging materials. It also underpins the production of detergent alkylates and rubber processing chemicals used across personal care and industrial formulations.

Benzene is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, typically via tanker or ISO container for large-volume industrial buyers. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade and nitration-grade for various applications.

Purity specifications are commonly at 99.9% or higher to meet rigorous industrial requirements. Procurement is generally handled through petrochemical distributors or direct refinery supply agreements given the volume requirements.

name: Cobalt acetate
description:
Cobalt acetate (CAS 71-48-7 ), also sold as cobaltous diacetate, is an organometallic cobalt salt used primarily as a catalyst and metal source across chemical manufacturing and surface treatment industries.

It delivers reactive cobalt in a soluble, processable form that integrates readily into industrial formulations and process baths. In polymer and plastics manufacturing, it functions as a catalyst or co-catalyst.

It is used in PET polymerization and oxidation reactions, influencing color and molecular weight outcomes. Textile and leather processors use it in dyeing and finishing baths to promote dye fixation and surface uniformity.

In coatings and printing inks, it acts as a drier catalyst, accelerating oxidative cure in alkyd-based systems. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology applications draw on it as a cobalt precursor in synthesis processes.

It also serves as a trace metal supplement in fermentation media. The product is available as a pink to violet crystalline powder and in solution form, with the tetrahydrate being the most prevalent grade.

Technical and reagent-grade specifications are standard across the market. Bulk supply is typically offered in fiber drums or intermediate bulk containers, with smaller packaging available for laboratory use.

name: Iron lactate
description:
Iron lactate (CAS 7100-07-4 ), also designated E585 , is the iron salt of lactic acid used as a mineral source and color stabilizer in food and pharmaceutical applications. It delivers bioavailable iron in a form that integrates readily into fortified products and functional formulations.

In food manufacturing, E585 functions as a color-retention agent in olives and certain preserved vegetables, maintaining a consistent dark appearance through processing. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as an iron source in oral iron supplementation products.

This compound is particularly valued where tolerability and solubility are priorities for the end user. In animal feed and agricultural nutrition, it serves as a supplemental iron compound to address deficiency in livestock and poultry diets.

Fortified food producers also incorporate it into infant formulas and functional beverages where an organic iron salt is preferred over inorganic alternatives. It is typically supplied as a greenish-white to pale powder for industrial use.

Food-grade material conforming to E585 specifications is the most commonly traded form. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available for nutraceutical and supplement applications requiring higher purity standards like USP or FCC .

Buyers should confirm purity levels and iron content specifications with suppliers, as these vary by grade and intended regulatory market. Proper documentation ensures the material meets the specific requirements for food or medical applications.

name: Gellan gum
description:
Gellan gum (CAS 71010-52-1 ), also identified by E418 , is a microbial polysaccharide produced by fermentation and used commercially as a gelling, thickening, and stabilizing agent.

At low concentrations it forms firm, clear gels, making it a cost-effective alternative to agar and carrageenan across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing sectors.

In food production, this ingredient suspends particulates in beverages, stabilizes dairy alternatives, and provides the gel structure in low-sugar confectionery and desserts.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a controlled-release matrix in oral solid dosage forms and as a gelling agent in ophthalmic drops, where its ion-triggered gelation activates on contact.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into clear gels, lotions, and serums to build viscosity and suspend active ingredients without clouding the formula during production.

In microbiology and plant tissue culture, Gelrite gellan gum serves as a transparent agar substitute in growth media, enabling better visualization of colonies for researchers.

The product is supplied as a cream to off-white free-flowing powder. Two primary commercial forms are available: low-acyl gellan, which produces firm, brittle gels, and high-acyl gellan.

Recognized grades include food-grade, FCC , and USP , with Gelrite representing a purified grade used in specialized microbiological and pharmaceutical applications.

name: Equisetum arvense extract
description:
Equisetum arvense extract (CAS 71011-23-9 ), also marketed as horsetail extract, is a botanical ingredient derived from the field horsetail plant. It is used across personal care, nutraceutical, and pharmaceutical applications for its antioxidant activity and moisture-retention properties.

In cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into hair care products such as shampoos, conditioners, and scalp treatments. Its silica-rich profile supports claims around hair strength and shine in various professional beauty applications.

Skincare formulators use it in serums, creams, and toners targeting antioxidant protection and skin-conditioning benefits. In nutraceuticals and dietary supplements, it appears in capsule and tablet formats positioned around connective tissue support.

The extract is also utilized for mineral supplementation in health products. Pharmaceutical and herbal medicine manufacturers source it as an active botanical component in standardized herbal preparations for global distribution.

Equisetum arvense extract is supplied as a dry powder or liquid extract, with dry forms being the most common for supplement and cosmetic manufacturing. Standardized grades are available, typically defined by silica or flavonoid content.

Food-grade or cosmetic-grade specifications can be requested depending on the intended application. Organic-certified material is available from select suppliers to meet clean-label and natural formulation requirements for modern brands.

name: Polyglyceryl-2 oleyl ether
description:
Polyglyceryl-2 Oleyl Ether (CAS 71032-90-1 ) is a polyglycerol-based nonionic surfactant derived from diglycerol and oleyl alcohol. It functions as an emulsifier, humectant, and wetting agent across personal care, cleaning, and industrial applications.

In cosmetic formulations, it stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions in creams, lotions, and serums. It contributes moisturizing properties to the finished product while maintaining a smooth texture and consistent application.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it to improve substrate wetting and boost the dispersibility of active ingredients. It is frequently found in liquid detergents and surface cleaners to enhance overall performance.

Textile processing operations apply it as a wetting and softening agent during fiber treatment, dyeing, and finishing stages. This ensures that dyes and treatments are absorbed evenly throughout the fabric during the manufacturing process.

In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports surface modification by improving the uniform distribution of treatment agents across substrates. This leads to higher quality finishes and more durable end products for industrial use.

Polyglyceryl-2 Oleyl Ether is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous paste, depending on concentration and formulation. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet various requirements.

These specifications ensure the product meets the needs of personal care manufacturers and industrial processors respectively. Standard packaging includes drums and IBCs for bulk procurement and efficient logistics management.

Contact us for supply of Polyglyceryl-2 oleyl ether

name: Hypromellose acetate succinate
description:
Hypromellose acetate succinate (CAS 71138-97-1 ), commonly abbreviated as HPMCAS, is a cellulose-based enteric polymer used in pharmaceutical manufacturing to control drug release and improve oral bioavailability.

It functions as a pH-dependent solubilizer and film-former, enabling formulation strategies that would otherwise be limited by poor drug solubility. HPMCAS is the polymer of choice in amorphous solid dispersion formulations.

In these applications, it stabilizes poorly soluble APIs in a supersaturated state to enhance absorption. In enteric coating applications, it forms a protective film that resists gastric acid while dissolving at targeted intestinal pH levels.

Hot-melt extrusion and spray-drying processes both rely on HPMCAS as a matrix carrier, making it central to modern oral solid dosage development. It is also used in controlled-release capsule and tablet systems.

These systems allow for precise gastrointestinal delivery timing where it is a formulation requirement. HPMCAS is supplied as a white to off-white powder in multiple grades differentiated by substitution level.

The material is available in solubility pH thresholds typically designated as LF, MF, and HF grades. NF grade is the standard specification recognized for pharmaceutical use in these applications.

Bulk quantities are available for commercial manufacturing, with smaller quantities offered for formulation development and clinical trial supply. This ensures consistent quality across all stages of production.

name: Synthetic beeswax
description:
Synthetic beeswax ( CAS 71243-51-1 ) is a petroleum-derived wax engineered to replicate the functional profile of natural beeswax without reliance on animal-sourced raw materials. Produced through Fischer-Tropsch synthesis or ester-based processes, it delivers consistent rheology modification.

This material provides excellent lubrication performance across demanding formulation and industrial environments. In personal care, it structures lip balms, lipsticks, and solid emulsions where batch-to-batch consistency and vegan positioning are procurement priorities.

Coatings formulators use it as a slip and scratch-resistance additive in industrial and decorative surface finishes. In adhesives and sealants, it controls viscosity and open time, improving processability in hot-melt systems.

Metalworking lubricants incorporate it as a solid lubricant component where controlled release and thermal stability under mechanical load are required. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing and product design.

Synthetic beeswax is supplied as pellets, pastilles, or flakes, with some suppliers offering powdered grades for dry-blend applications. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications for various industries.

Cosmetic grades typically meet purity requirements aligned with Ph. Eur. or USP monographs for waxes. These standards ensure the material is suitable for sensitive applications in the beauty and pharmaceutical sectors.

Packing is commonly offered in 25 kg cartons or bags, with bulk options available for industrial volumes. This ensures efficient logistics and handling for both small-scale laboratories and large-scale production facilities.

Contact us for supply of Synthetic beeswax

name: Fenoxaprop-p-ethyl
description:
Fenoxaprop-p-ethyl (CAS 71283-80-2 ) is a selective post-emergent herbicide active ingredient used in crop protection to control grass weeds in broadleaf crops. It belongs to the aryloxyphenoxypropionate chemical class and acts by inhibiting acetyl-CoA carboxylase in target grasses.

Procurement is driven by demand from agrochemical formulators, generic manufacturers, and registrants developing herbicide products for global markets. It is the primary active ingredient in formulated herbicides targeting annual and perennial grass weeds.

Targeted species include wild oat, blackgrass, and ryegrass in wheat, barley, rice, and soybean crops. Formulators incorporate it into emulsifiable concentrate and oil dispersion products, often combined with safeners to broaden crop tolerance.

Contract manufacturers source it as a technical-grade active for generic herbicide registration under FAO /WHO specifications. It is also used in turf and non-crop applications where selective grass control is required.

This chemical allows for effective management without damaging broadleaf vegetation in diverse agricultural settings. Fenoxaprop-p-ethyl is supplied as a technical-grade solid or concentrated liquid for industrial use.

Purity levels are typically at 93% or above for formulation use, ensuring high efficacy in final products. It is available under international agrochemical registration standards to meet global regulatory needs.

Packaging ranges from drum quantities to bulk supply depending on formulation-scale requirements. This flexibility supports both large-scale manufacturing and specialized agricultural chemical production facilities.

name: Hydroxypropyl guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride
description:
Hydroxypropyl guar hydroxypropyltrimonium chloride (CAS 71329-50-5 ), commercially known as Jaguar C 162 or Jaguar C 16, is a cationic guar derivative used across personal care and industrial markets.

It deposits a conditioning film on negatively charged surfaces such as hair, skin, and fibers through electrostatic attraction, delivering substantivity that non-ionic polymers cannot match.

In shampoos, conditioners, and body washes, it reduces combing friction and improves wet detangling without weighing hair down. Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and cleansers.

It builds a moisturizing, film-forming layer that persists after rinsing. Textile processors apply it as a softening and antistatic agent during finishing treatments for natural and synthetic fabrics.

In paper manufacturing, it functions as a wet-end additive that improves fiber retention and surface charge management. This versatile polymer is supplied as a free-flowing off-white to cream powder.

Grades vary by degree of substitution and charge density, which directly affects performance in low-pH or high-surfactant formulations. This is a key selection factor for chemical formulators.

Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial form, with technical grades available for textile and paper applications. It remains a staple for achieving superior sensory profiles in formulations.

name: Heptacosanoic acid
description:
Heptacosanoic acid ( CAS 7138-40-1 ), also known as carboceric acid or C27:0, is a saturated very-long-chain fatty acid used as a functional ingredient in food and personal care formulations.

It serves as an emulsifier and moisturizing agent, contributing to texture, stability, and skin-conditioning performance in finished products. In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it functions as an emollient.

It is used in creams, lotions, and lip products, helping to stabilize oil-in-water systems and improve skin feel. Food manufacturers use it as a reference standard and minor functional lipid component.

It is utilized in fat-based systems where precise fatty acid profiling is required. Its role in nutritional research and biomarker studies makes it a sought-after material for producing certified reference materials.

Formulators working with wax-based systems, such as solid lipstick bases or barrier creams, source it for its contribution to structural rigidity and moisture retention in various industrial applications.

Heptacosanoic acid is supplied as a white to off-white powder or solid at room temperature. It is available in research-grade and high-purity analytical grades, with purity levels typically at 98% or above.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are available from select suppliers depending on intended application and regional regulatory requirements for global distribution and manufacturing standards.

name: Triethylhexyl citrate
description:
Triethylhexyl citrate (CAS 7147-34-4 ), also known as tris(2-ethylhexyl) citrate, is a citrate-based ester plasticizer derived from citric acid. It functions as a non-phthalate plasticizer and emollient across polymer processing and personal care formulation.

This versatile chemical offers manufacturers a bio-based alternative to conventional plasticizers. In PVC and polymer compounding, it improves flexibility and processability in films, tubing, and molded parts where phthalate-free compliance is required.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into color cosmetics, skin creams, and sunscreen products. It acts as an emollient and skin-feel modifier that also helps disperse pigments effectively within various cosmetic bases.

In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a plasticizing additive to improve substrate adhesion and film flexibility. This is achieved without compromising the overall coating integrity or the durability of the finished product.

Rubber and sealant manufacturers use it to adjust compound softness and extend service life in flexible sealing applications. Its chemical stability makes it a reliable choice for demanding industrial environments and long-term use.

Triethylhexyl citrate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly available for industrial and commercial procurement needs.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements for personal care end-use applications. Specifications vary by supplier, and buyers should confirm grade suitability against their specific regulatory and formulation requirements.
