name: Ethylhexyl isononanate
description:
Ethylhexyl isononanate (CAS 71566-49-9 ), also known commercially as 2-ethylhexyl isononanoate, is a branched-chain ester used across personal care and industrial formulations as an emollient and plasticizer.

Its low viscosity and excellent spreadability make it a preferred ingredient where skin feel, lubricity, or substrate wetting determines formulation performance in various commercial applications.

In personal care, it functions as a lightweight emollient in skin creams, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, delivering a non-greasy skin feel while improving pigment dispersion for better coverage.

Coating and adhesive formulators use it as a plasticizer to enhance flexibility and adhesion in films and sealant systems. It acts as a base fluid or additive carrier in lubricant applications.

In metalworking, it is utilized where low volatility and good lubricity on metal surfaces are required. It also serves as a solvent or dispersing medium for resins and active ingredients.

This chemical is highly valued in industrial formulations where compatibility with organic systems is a primary selection criterion. It is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

name: Amiloxate
description:
Amiloxate (CAS 71617-10-2 ), also known as isoamyl p-methoxycinnamate, is an organic UV filter used in sun care and cosmetic formulations. It absorbs UVB radiation, protecting both the skin and the stability of light-sensitive formulations from solar degradation.

Amiloxate is primarily used in sunscreens, where it functions as a UVB-absorbing active at concentrations permitted under regional cosmetic regulations. In daily-wear cosmetics such as moisturizers and foundations, it provides incidental UV protection.

This ingredient offers protection without contributing to heavy or greasy textures. Its oil-soluble nature makes it compatible with emollient systems, allowing formulators to incorporate it directly into the oil phase of emulsions.

It also appears in lip care and hair protection products where UVB defense is required alongside aesthetic elegance. Amiloxate is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid, suitable for direct blending into oil-phase systems.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, and suppliers typically align documentation to INCI and regional regulatory requirements. This includes compliance with the EU Cosmetics Regulation and relevant positive lists.

Packaging is generally offered in drums or intermediate bulk containers for commercial quantities. This ensures the material remains stable and easy to handle during large-scale manufacturing processes for personal care products.

name: Didecyldimethylammonium chloride
description:
Didecyldimethylammonium chloride ( CAS 7173-51-5 ), commonly known as DDAC, is a quaternary ammonium compound used as a broad-spectrum biocide and disinfectant across industrial and institutional markets.

It delivers effective antimicrobial action against bacteria, fungi, and enveloped viruses at low use concentrations. In food processing and beverage facilities, DDAC is formulated into no-rinse sanitizers.

These surface disinfectants are approved for use on food-contact surfaces. Water treatment programs use it to control microbial growth in cooling towers, industrial water systems, and swimming pools.

In healthcare and institutional cleaning, it is a primary active ingredient in hospital-grade disinfectant concentrates and wipes formulations. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into preservative systems.

These systems are used for rinse-off and leave-on products where broad-spectrum protection is required. DDAC is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 50% and 80% active concentrations.

Technical grade is the standard for industrial disinfection and water treatment applications. Higher-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical and personal care formulations to meet specific needs.

name: Oleyl propylene diamine
description:
Oleyl propylene diamine (CAS 7173-62-8 ), commercially recognized under the trade name Duomeen, is a fatty diamine derived from oleic acid used across industrial sectors as a corrosion inhibitor and emulsifier.

Its dual amine functionality allows it to bond to both metal surfaces and acidic or anionic substrates, making it effective across a broad range of formulation and process chemistry applications.

In oil, gas, and pipeline operations, it functions as a corrosion inhibitor in acidic and saline environments, protecting metal infrastructure from electrochemical degradation during transport.

Mining operations use it as a flotation collector and ore beneficiation agent, where it selectively adsorbs onto mineral surfaces to improve separation efficiency and recovery rates.

name: L-tryptophan
description:
L-Tryptophan (CAS 73-22-3 ) is an essential amino acid that the human body cannot synthesize, making dietary and supplemental sourcing critical for both food and pharmaceutical manufacturers.

Known by the abbreviation L-Trp, it functions as a precursor to serotonin and melatonin in biological systems and serves as a nutritional fortification agent across multiple industries.

In dietary supplements and functional foods, L-Trp is formulated into capsules, tablets, and fortified beverages targeting sleep support and mood-related nutrition products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient or excipient in amino acid infusion solutions and parenteral nutrition formulations for clinical healthcare settings.

Animal feed producers incorporate it to correct tryptophan-deficient diets in swine and poultry, improving feed efficiency and growth performance in commercial livestock operations.

In personal care, it is used in amino acid-based moisturizing formulations where its humectant properties support skin conditioning claims and cosmetic product stability.

L-Tryptophan is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and pharmaceutical-grade specifications to meet compliance requirements.

Bulk supply is standard for feed and food applications, with pharmaceutical-grade material available in smaller, documented quantities for GMP manufacturing and laboratory use.

L-Isoleucine (CAS 73-32-5 ) is an essential branched-chain amino acid that the human body cannot synthesize, making dietary or supplemental sourcing necessary. In industry, it functions as a nutritional active and a fermentation building block.

It also serves as a pharmaceutical excipient or active ingredient across multiple formulation types. In sports nutrition and clinical nutrition, it is formulated into BCAA blends, protein powders, and medical foods targeting muscle metabolism.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in amino acid infusion solutions and parenteral nutrition products. Precise purity and endotoxin control are critical sourcing criteria for these specific medical applications.

Food and beverage producers incorporate it into functional drinks, meal replacements, and fortified foods to meet amino acid profile requirements. It is also used in cosmetic formulations for skin-conditioning and hair care preparations.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade ( FCC ), ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements for safety and quality.

Pharmaceutical grades are subject to additional specifications for residual solvents and microbial limits. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric-ton quantities to serve both industrial formulators and smaller-scale manufacturers.

name: Guanine
description:
Guanine (CAS 73-40-5 ), also known commercially as Pearl Essence and Natural White 1, is a naturally occurring purine base sourced primarily from fish scales. It is used across cosmetics, biotechnology, and pharmaceutical applications.

Its crystalline platelet structure produces a distinctive iridescent optical effect, making it a sought-after ingredient in pearlescent formulations. In life sciences, it functions as a biochemical reference material and nucleotide synthesis building block.

In personal care manufacturing, guanine is incorporated into nail polishes, lipsticks, eyeshadows, and shampoos to deliver pearl-like shimmer and light diffusion. Cosmetic formulators value it as a natural-origin alternative to synthetic mica.

In pharmaceutical and biotechnology research, it serves as a precursor and reference standard in nucleoside and nucleotide synthesis workflows. Diagnostic reagent producers also source it as a high-purity analytical standard for assay development.

Guanine is supplied as a fine crystalline powder, typically in natural or synthetic origin grades depending on the application. Cosmetic-grade material is available to meet INCI-compliant formulation requirements for global distribution.

Pharmaceutical and biotech buyers source USP or research-grade specifications with defined purity thresholds. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial volumes to meet diverse manufacturing needs.

name: Lidocaine hydrochloride

Lidocaine hydrochloride (CAS 73-78-9 ) is the water-soluble salt form of lidocaine, the benchmark local anesthetic active used across injectable, topical, and dental pharmaceutical formulations.

It is a regulated active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) sourced by formulators, contract manufacturers, and pharmaceutical importers operating under strict pharmacopoeial standards.

In injectable pharmaceuticals, it is formulated into nerve block and epidural anesthetic solutions, requiring high-purity API meeting injectable-grade specifications for safety and efficacy.

Topical formulations, including creams, gels, patches, and sprays, use it as the primary anesthetic active for pain and itch relief in OTC and prescription products across global markets.

Dental cartridge manufacturers incorporate it into lidocaine-epinephrine combination solutions for procedural anesthesia. In cosmetic products, it appears in formulations targeting minor skin discomfort.

Regulatory classification for these applications varies by market and concentration. Lidocaine hydrochloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder for easy integration into various bases.

It is available in USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. grades to meet injectable and oral pharmaceutical requirements, with technical grade available for non-pharmaceutical applications.

name: Isotridecyl alcohol ethoxylate phosphate ester
description:
Isotridecyl alcohol ethoxylate phosphate ester (CAS 73038-25-2 ), also referenced commercially as Ester phosphorique, is an anionic surfactant derived from the phosphation of ethoxylated isotridecyl alcohol.

It delivers emulsification, detergency, lubrication, and corrosion inhibition across a broad range of industrial formulations. In metalworking and industrial cleaning, it functions as both a lubricity additive and a corrosion inhibitor.

It is commonly used in aqueous cutting fluids and metal cleaning concentrates. Textile processors use it as an emulsifier and wetting agent in fiber preparation baths, scouring formulations, and dyeing auxiliaries.

These applications are ideal where controlled foam and substrate compatibility are required. Water treatment formulators incorporate it for its dispersing and emulsifying performance in process water and industrial effluent.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it stabilizes emulsion polymerization processes and improves pigment dispersion in waterborne formulations. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical manufacturing.

Isotridecyl alcohol ethoxylate phosphate ester is typically supplied as a liquid or viscous paste. The ethoxylation degree varies across commercial grades to tune HLB and the specific performance profile.

It is available in technical grade , with acid and salt forms offered depending on the target application. Drum and IBC packaging are standard for industrial supply volumes to ensure safe transport.

name: Butylene Glycol Cocoate
description:
Butylene Glycol Cocoate (CAS 73138-39-3 ) is an ester derived from coconut fatty acids and 1,3-butanediol, functioning as an emollient, emulsifier, and wetting agent across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its coconut-derived fatty acid profile positions it as a mild, skin-compatible ingredient with broad formulation compatibility. In skincare and hair care products, it conditions the skin and hair surface while supporting emulsion stability.

This versatile ester is frequently utilized in lotions, creams, and serums to enhance texture. Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it to improve substrate wetting and aid in dispersing actives across surfaces.

Textile processors apply it as a softening and wetting agent during fiber treatment and finishing operations. In leather processing, it supports surface conditioning and lubricant formulations where controlled moisture retention is required.

The chemical is typically supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care manufacturers and industrial users respectively.

Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers, with supply volumes suited to both formulation-scale and industrial-scale procurement. This ensures reliable delivery for diverse manufacturing needs.

name: Bispinacolatodiborane
description:
Bispinacolatodiborane (CAS 73183-34-3 ), also known as B2pin2, is a diboron reagent used as a key borylation source in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It delivers two pinacolboronate ester units in a single reagent, enabling efficient introduction of boronic ester groups into organic molecules without requiring air-sensitive handling.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, B2pin2 is the preferred reagent for palladium-catalyzed Miyaura borylation, converting aryl and vinyl halides into pinacol boronate esters.

These serve as intermediates for Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling in active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) production. Specialty polymer manufacturers use it to introduce boron-functional groups.

This enables controlled crosslinking and stimuli-responsive material design. In fine chemical and agrochemical synthesis, it supports the preparation of borylated building blocks.

Research-scale and contract manufacturing operations in the textile and paper sectors also employ it for surface-functionalizing agents derived from boronate chemistry.

Bispinacolatodiborane is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots for industrial use.

Purity grades typically range from 97% to 99%+ to meet pharmaceutical intermediate and fine chemical manufacturing requirements for high-performance applications.

name: Lead(2+) octanoate
description:
Lead(2+) octanoate ( CAS 7319-86-0 ), commercially known as lead octoate, is an organolead carboxylate used as a metal catalyst and drier in industrial processing. It delivers controlled reactivity in curing, cross-linking, and polymerization systems where precise metal coordination is required.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, lead octoate functions as a stabilizer and catalyst precursor in PVC compounding and resin cure systems. The rubber and tire industry uses it as a vulcanization accelerator and cross-linking agent.

It promotes sulfur-based cure networks in technical rubber compounds. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as an extreme-pressure additive precursor and boundary lubrication component in grease and cutting fluid systems.

It also serves as a drier catalyst in alkyd-based industrial coatings, accelerating oxidative cure of oil-modified resin films. Lead octoate is supplied as a liquid solution, with the 36% concentration being the most recognized commercial grade.

This material is available in technical grade, suitable for catalyst and industrial processing applications. Bulk supply is standard in drums or IBC containers aligned with hazardous materials handling requirements for heavy metal compounds.

name: Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate
description:
Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate (CAS 7320-34-5 ), commonly abbreviated as TKPP and listed as E450(v) in food applications, is an inorganic potassium salt used across industrial and food-grade processes.

It functions primarily as a chelating agent, buffering agent, and dispersant, enabling formulators to control pH, sequester metal ions, and stabilize complex systems in various environments.

In food processing, TKPP acts as an emulsifying salt and moisture-retention agent in processed cheese, seafood, and cured meat products to maintain texture and quality during storage.

Industrial cleaning and textile processing rely on it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions in hard water, improving detergent efficiency and ensuring dye uptake uniformity across fabrics.

In water treatment formulations, it prevents scale formation and controls corrosion by binding interfering metal ions, protecting infrastructure and maintaining flow efficiency in industrial systems.

Building and construction applications use TKPP as a dispersant in cementitious and ceramic systems, improving workability and pigment distribution for more consistent and durable finished materials.

Tetrapotassium pyrophosphate is supplied as a white powder or granule. Food-grade material is available to FCC and E450(v) specifications, while technical-grade product serves industrial applications.

Standard commercial concentrations are typically offered at ≥95% or ≥98% purity depending on grade, ensuring reliable performance for cleaning, ceramics, and specialized water treatment needs.

name: 2-(2-ethoxyethoxy)ethyl acrylate
description:
2-(2-Ethoxyethoxy)ethyl acrylate (CAS 7328-17-8 ), commercially known as Carbitol acrylate or DEGA, is a reactive monomer used in UV/EB-curable systems to control film flexibility and reduce brittleness in cured coatings.

Its ether-chain structure delivers plasticizing character directly into the polymer network during polymerization, eliminating the need for separate plasticizer addition in the formulation process.

In UV-curable coatings and inks, DEGA functions as a reactive diluent that lowers viscosity for press or coating application while contributing to a softer, more flexible cured film.

Packaging and label printing formulators use it to improve substrate adhesion and reduce cracking on flexible substrates. In radiation-curable adhesives and sealants, it extends the polymer backbone.

This extension improves elongation and peel resistance in the final bond. Plastics and polymer manufacturers incorporate it as a co-monomer in acrylate-based systems where controlled softness is required.

Compatibility with polar substrates are key formulation targets for this monomer. It is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC quantities for large scale manufacturing.

Technical grade is the primary commercial specification, with inhibited grades available to ensure storage stability during transport and warehousing. Purity levels of 98% and above are standard.

These purity levels are ideal for reactive monomer applications. The product meets rigorous industrial requirements for consistency and performance in high-speed curing environments.

It delivers foaming, cleaning, and emulsification performance across a broad range of formulated products. In personal care, it functions as the primary surfactant in shampoos, body washes, and liquid hand soaps.

The material is effective at generating dense foam while removing oils and soils from skin and hair. Home care formulators use it in hard surface cleaners, dishwashing liquids, and laundry detergents where consistent lather is required.

Textile processing operations apply it as a scouring and wetting agent to strip natural oils and sizing agents from fiber before dyeing. In paper manufacturing, it supports pulp dispersion and surface treatment processes.

Sodium C12-16 alkyl sulfate is supplied as a liquid paste or aqueous solution, typically at active matter concentrations in the 28–30% range. Technical and cosmetic grades are available for various industrial needs.

description:
Mate extract (CAS 73296-98-7 ), also referenced commercially as Yerba mate cellular extract, is derived from the dried leaves of Ilex paraguariensis and standardized for use across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical manufacturing.

It delivers antioxidant activity and characteristic flavor notes sourced from a single botanical origin, giving formulators a dual-function ingredient in one input for various industrial applications.

In food and beverage production, it functions as a natural flavoring agent in energy drinks, teas, and functional nutrition products where a distinctly herbal, slightly bitter profile is required.

Nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it into dietary supplements targeting antioxidant support, where its polyphenol content justifies label claims and differentiates finished products in the market.

name: Sodium carbomer
description:
Sodium carbomer (CAS 73298-57-4 ), also known by the E-number E1210 , is a pre-neutralized polyacrylic acid polymer used as a rheology modifier and stabilizer across personal care, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations.

Unlike standard carbomers that require in-process neutralization, the sodium salt form disperses readily in aqueous systems, streamlining manufacturing workflows for formulators and reducing production time.

In personal care, it builds viscosity and suspends actives in gels, lotions, and cleansers without requiring a separate neutralization step. This efficiency makes it a preferred choice for modern cosmetic labs.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a thickener and binder in topical gels and ophthalmic formulations where consistent rheological performance is critical to product approval and patient safety.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as a thickening and stabilizing agent for water-based dispersions, helping control flow and application properties for industrial-scale manufacturing processes.

It also supports emulsion stability in leave-on and rinse-off cosmetic products where long shelf-life is a procurement requirement. This ensures that the final product remains stable under various conditions.

Sodium carbomer is supplied as a fine white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter conforming to Ph. Eur. and USP monograph requirements.

description:
Decanoyl- and octanoyl glycerides ( CAS 73398-61-5 ), commercially recognized as caprylic/capric triglyceride, are fractionated coconut oil-derived esters used as carrier oils and emollients.

Produced from medium-chain fatty acids, they deliver a lightweight, skin-compatible base that supports active ingredient delivery without the heaviness of conventional vegetable oils.

In cosmetic formulations, these glycerides function as an emollient and carrier for lipophilic actives in serums, sunscreens, and moisturizers, improving spreadability and skin feel.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solvent and excipient for lipid-based drug delivery systems, including soft gel capsules and various topical preparations.

In food applications, it acts as a carrier for fat-soluble vitamins, flavors, and nutraceutical ingredients requiring a stable, neutral-tasting lipid base for the final product.

Coating and adhesive formulators incorporate it as a plasticizer and processing aid where a low-viscosity, oxidation-stable oil is required for industrial performance.

description:
Phenyl trimethicone (CAS 73559-47-4 ), also known commercially as FT 8, is a phenyl-modified silicone fluid used across personal care and industrial applications. It provides a lightweight, non-greasy conditioning effect on skin and hair.

The material delivers surface lubrication and wetting performance in technical processes. In hair care formulations, it deposits a refractive film on the hair shaft that enhances shine and reduces frizz without weighing the hair down.

Skin care and color cosmetic formulators incorporate it to improve spreadability and deliver a silky after-feel in serums, foundations, and sunscreens. In textile finishing, it functions as a lubricating agent.

This silicone reduces fiber-to-fiber friction during processing and improves the hand feel of finished fabrics. Leather treatment compounds use it to condition surfaces and improve water repellency without altering the material.

Phenyl trimethicone is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid suitable for direct incorporation into emulsions and anhydrous systems. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications meeting industry standards.

name: Menadione nicotinamide bisulfite
description:
Menadione nicotinamide bisulfite (CAS 73581-79-0 ) is a water-soluble complex of menadione and nicotinamide, formulated to deliver stable vitamin K3 activity in aqueous systems. Its bisulfite complexation resolves the handling and solubility limitations of menadione.

This chemical structure makes it highly practical for liquid and feed premix manufacturing where the parent compound alone would be unsuitable. In animal nutrition, it serves as the primary source of supplemental vitamin K3 in poultry and swine.

It is also essential for aquaculture feed premixes, where water solubility is critical for uniform dosing. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into injectable and oral liquid formulations requiring a stabilized, water-compatible vitamin K source.

In food and nutrition applications, it functions as a vitamin K3 fortification agent in products where dry menadione would present processing challenges. Its antioxidant properties support stability in multi-vitamin concentrate blends.

The compound is also valued for its preservative properties across feed and nutraceutical production. Menadione nicotinamide bisulfite is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for various industrial applications.

name: Omeprazole
description:
Omeprazole (CAS 73590-58-6 ), also marketed under the brand names Losec and Prilosec, is a proton pump inhibitor active pharmaceutical ingredient used in the treatment of acid-related gastrointestinal conditions.

As a finished API, it is sourced by pharmaceutical manufacturers and contract formulators for integration into oral solid dosage forms. Omeprazole is the core active in delayed-release capsule and tablet formulations.

These formulations target gastroesophageal reflux disease, peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Formulators working with enteric-coated pellet systems rely on this API to ensure acid-stable delivery to the small intestine.

It is also incorporated into combination drug products, such as fixed-dose formulations paired with antibiotics for H. pylori eradication regimens. Veterinary pharmaceutical manufacturers source the material for animal treatments.

name: Succinoglycan
description:
Succinoglycan (CAS 73667-50-2 ) is a high-molecular-weight exopolysaccharide produced by bacterial fermentation, primarily from Agrobacterium tumefaciens. It functions as a rheology modifier and stabilizer, delivering viscosity control and gel-forming behavior in aqueous systems.

This versatile biopolymer is utilized across food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology applications. In food formulations, it acts as a thickener and texture stabilizer in sauces, dressings, and dairy-based products where consistent viscosity is required.

It maintains performance under varying temperature and shear conditions, ensuring product stability. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a matrix-forming agent in controlled-release tablet formulations and as a suspending agent in liquid dosage forms.

In biotechnology, it is applied as a functional biopolymer in microbial culture media and biofilm-related research. Its interaction with biological systems is commercially relevant for specialized laboratory and industrial processes.

The moisture-retention behavior of this material also supports use in topical formulation bases requiring sustained hydration performance. It is typically supplied as an off-white to cream-colored powder for easy integration into various manufacturing workflows.

The product is available in food-grade and research-grade specifications, with purity and molecular weight profiles varying by intended application. Quality control ensures the material meets necessary industrial requirements for consistency.

Packaging ranges from small quantities for laboratory and formulation development use to bulk quantities for industrial-scale production. This ensures flexibility for both research institutions and large-scale chemical manufacturers.

name: Dimethyloctylamine
description:
Dimethyloctylamine (CAS 7378-99-6 ), also known as DMOA, is a tertiary aliphatic amine used across cleaning, personal care, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH regulator and surface-active intermediate.

This versatile chemical enables formulators to control alkalinity and modify surface behavior in finished products. In industrial and household cleaning formulations, DMOA acts as a neutralizing agent for anionic surfactants.

It improves detergent stability and performance at target pH ranges. Personal care manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of quaternary ammonium compounds and amine oxides, which appear in conditioning products.

These compounds are also found in mild cleansing products. In textile and leather processing, it supports wetting and penetration of treatment baths, helping dyes and finishing agents distribute evenly across substrates.

Paper chemical producers also incorporate it into sizing and surface treatment formulations where controlled alkalinity is required. Dimethyloctylamine is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for various uses.

It is available in technical grade, which covers the majority of industrial and formulation applications. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with quantities suited to both development and production.

name: Palm kernel diethanolamide
description:
Palm kernel diethanolamide ( CAS 73807-15-5 ), also supplied under trade names such as Aminon PK 02S and Amisol KD 3, is a fatty acid alkanolamide derived from palm kernel oil. It functions as a foam booster, viscosity builder, and emulsifier across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

In shampoos, body washes, and liquid soaps, it enhances foam stability and thickens surfactant systems, reducing the need for additional rheology modifiers. Industrial and household cleaning products use it to boost detergency and improve grease dispersion in alkaline formulations.

Textile processing operations apply it as an emulsifier and softening aid in fiber treatment baths. In leather processing, it supports fat liquoring emulsification and improves the uniformity of surface treatments across various manufacturing stages.

Palm kernel diethanolamide is typically supplied as an amber to yellow viscous liquid. It is available in technical grade, which is the standard specification for industrial cleaning and textile applications, as well as cosmetic-grade material for personal care.

The material meets high purity requirements for use in professional formulations. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to ensure efficient logistics and handling for large-scale manufacturing operations and chemical distribution networks.

name: Sodium lauroyl isethionate
description:
Sodium lauroyl isethionate (CAS 7381-01-3 ), also known commercially as Igepon A, is an anionic surfactant derived from lauric acid and isethionic acid. It delivers effective cleansing, foam generation, and emulsification across personal care and industrial formulations.

In bar soap and syndet formulations, it produces a dense, stable lather while remaining mild enough for sensitive skin products. This is a key factor for formulators targeting premium cleansing bars and specialty soaps.

Body washes, facial cleansers, and shampoos incorporate it to balance foam performance with low irritation profiles. It is highly valued for its ability to maintain skin moisture while providing a thorough clean.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as an emulsifier and dispersing agent. This improves pigment distribution and helps in stabilizing aqueous emulsion systems during the manufacturing process.

Industrial cleaning formulations use it where controlled degreasing and foam management are required in process environments. Its versatility makes it a staple in various heavy-duty and specialty cleaning applications.

The product is supplied primarily as a white to off-white powder or flake. Granulated forms are also available for easier handling in solid formulation processes, reducing dust and improving flowability.

Cosmetic-grade material is the most common commercial specification, typically meeting purity requirements aligned with personal care industry standards. This ensures safety and consistency for high-end consumer goods.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial surfactant and coating applications where cosmetic compliance is not required. This provides a cost-effective solution for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing.

name: Propylene glycol dicaprylate
description:
Propylene glycol dicaprylate ( CAS 7384-98-7 ), also known as propylene glycol dioctanoate and 1,2-Dicaprylin, is a diester of propylene glycol and caprylic acid. It is used as a solvent, carrier, and emollient across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

Its FEMA 4471 designation supports its use in flavoring applications. Low viscosity and good lipid solubility make it a practical vehicle for active ingredient delivery in various industrial processes.

In pharmaceutical formulations, it functions as a carrier for lipophilic actives in softgel capsules and oral lipid-based drug delivery systems. It is also utilized in topical preparations to enhance the delivery of active compounds.

Food manufacturers use it as a flavor carrier and dispersant, particularly in emulsified flavor systems. This ensures the uniform distribution of oil-soluble compounds required for consistent product quality and taste profiles.

In personal care, it acts as an emollient and spreading agent in skin creams, serums, and sunscreen formulations. It improves texture without a heavy or greasy feel, making it ideal for high-end cosmetic applications.

It also serves as a plasticizer in film coatings for tablets and functional food products. This versatility allows manufacturers to achieve specific structural properties in finished solid dosage forms and nutritional supplements.

Propylene glycol dicaprylate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with the latter typically conforming to Ph.Eur. monographs for excipient use.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers for industrial scale. Kosher and halal certifications are commonly available to meet the specific regulatory requirements of food and nutraceutical applications worldwide.

name: Addovate ThermoStab
description:
Addovate ThermoStab (CAS 73912-21-7 ) is a phosphorus-based antioxidant and thermal stabilizer used to protect polymers and lubricant systems from oxidative and heat-induced degradation during processing and service life.

It functions as a hydroxy-functional phosphite, intercepting peroxy radicals and decomposing hydroperoxides before they cause molecular chain breakdown. In plastics processing, it is incorporated into polyolefins and resins.

It is used in engineering thermoplastics and compounded resins to prevent discoloration and molecular weight loss during high-temperature extrusion or injection molding. This ensures the structural integrity of the final product.

Lubricant formulators use it to extend the oxidative stability of industrial and automotive gear oils, hydraulic fluids, and greases operating under elevated thermal loads. This helps maintain performance in harsh environments.

Automotive component manufacturers specify it in underhood plastic parts and rubber-polymer blends where sustained heat exposure is a design requirement. It provides long-term durability for critical vehicle systems.

It is also evaluated in masterbatch and concentrate production, where stabilizer loading must remain effective through multiple processing passes. This makes it a versatile choice for complex manufacturing workflows.

Addovate ThermoStab is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or solid. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications aligned to polymer and lubricant additive industry requirements.

Packaging is generally available in bags or drums suited to industrial-scale procurement volumes. This ensures efficient handling and storage for large-scale chemical manufacturing and distribution operations.

name: Didecylmethylamine
description:
Didecylmethylamine (CAS 7396-58-9 ), sold commercially as Radiamine 6310, is a tertiary fatty amine used as a chemical intermediate and functional additive across industrial formulation. It serves primarily as a building block for quaternary ammonium compounds.

The product acts as a direct-acting surfactant in cleaning, lubrication, and surface treatment applications. In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, it is quaternized to produce biocidal quats used in disinfectants.

These quats are essential for hard surface cleaners and sanitizing concentrates. Metalworking fluid formulators use it as a corrosion inhibitor and emulsifier, where it helps stabilize oil-in-water systems effectively.

The chemical protects ferrous and non-ferrous metal surfaces during machining processes. In textile and leather processing, it functions as a softening and surface-modification agent, improving substrate feel and water interaction.

It is also utilized during finishing stages to enhance material properties. Paper industry applications include its use as a dispersant and wet-strength additive precursor, ensuring high performance in manufacturing.

Didecylmethylamine is supplied as a liquid at ambient temperature for easy handling. It is available in technical grade, which is the standard specification for industrial and formulation use across various sectors.

Bulk supply is typical in drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs). Tanker quantities are also available for larger procurement volumes to meet the demands of high-capacity industrial manufacturing facilities.

name: Butyl glycolate
description:
Butyl glycolate (CAS 7397-62-8 ), also known as butyl hydroxyacetate, is a glycolic acid ester used as a solvent and surface-active agent across coatings, adhesives, and personal care formulations.

It combines moderate polarity with good solvency, making it effective for dissolving resins and modifying surface behavior in industrial systems. In coatings and printing inks, it functions as a coalescing solvent.

This material acts as a wetting agent, improving film formation and substrate adhesion on difficult surfaces. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to adjust viscosity and enhance bonding performance.

In personal care, it is used as a carrier solvent in leave-on and rinse-off formulations where controlled delivery of active ingredients is required. Packaging ink manufacturers also use it to improve pigment dispersion.

The compound helps ensure high print quality on plastic substrates. It is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial packaging, including drums and IBC containers for bulk distribution.

Technical grade is the primary commercial specification available for industrial and coatings applications. Personal care and cosmetic applications typically require material meeting higher purity standards.

Buyers should confirm grade suitability with the supplier prior to procurement. The product is handled according to standard safety protocols for industrial esters to ensure stability and performance.

name: Diallyldimethylammonium chloride
description:
Diallyldimethylammonium chloride (CAS 7398-69-8 ), commonly abbreviated as DADMAC, is a quaternary ammonium monomer used primarily as a building block for cationic polyelectrolytes.

These polymers carry a permanent positive charge that enables charge-based interactions with negatively charged substrates, driving its adoption across water treatment, paper manufacturing, and personal care.

In water treatment, DADMAC-derived poly-DADMAC functions as a primary coagulant and flocculant, destabilizing suspended solids and colloidal particles in municipal and industrial effluent streams.

Paper and pulp producers use cationic polyelectrolytes built from DADMAC as retention aids and drainage aids, improving fiber retention and sheet formation efficiency during the manufacturing process.

In personal care, it polymerizes into conditioning agents that deposit on hair and skin, reducing static and improving combability in various rinse-off and leave-on formulations for consumers.

Textile and leather processors apply DADMAC-based polymers as fixatives to improve dye uptake and reduce effluent color load, ensuring more sustainable and efficient production cycles in these industries.

DADMAC is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 60–65% active content. Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial polymerization and water treatment applications worldwide.

Specifications are typically defined by active monomer content, residual impurity limits, and viscosity parameters relevant to polymerization performance and final product quality in chemical synthesis.

name: L-arginine
description:
L-Arginine (CAS 74-79-3 ), commonly abbreviated as L-Arg, is a conditionally essential amino acid sourced for use across pharmaceutical, nutritional, and cosmetic manufacturing.

It functions as a pH buffer, stabilizer, and bioavailable nitrogen source in a broad range of formulated products. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to solubilize poorly water-soluble active ingredients.

It also stabilizes protein-based drug formulations, including injectables and biologics. Sports nutrition and dietary supplement producers incorporate it into pre-workout powders, capsules, and functional beverages.

Food manufacturers apply it as a flavor precursor — FEMA 3819 — in processed and heat-treated products where controlled Maillard reaction development is required for the final product.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a pH adjuster and humectant in skin creams, hair conditioners, and scalp treatments, where its buffering capacity helps maintain formula stability.

L-Arginine is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both free base and hydrochloride salt forms. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade ( FCC ).

The hydrochloride form is commonly preferred for pharmaceutical applications requiring precise pH control. Bulk supply is available in kilogram and metric ton quantities to meet industrial production requirements.

name: Methane
description:
Methane (CAS 74-82-8 ) is the primary component of natural gas and one of the most important energy feedstocks in global industry. Known commercially as CH₄, it underpins fuel supply chains, chemical manufacturing, and large-scale hydrogen production.

In the oil and gas sector, methane serves as the dominant fuel source for power generation, industrial heating, and pipeline gas distribution. Steam methane reforming (SMR) converts it into hydrogen and synthesis gas.

This process feeds ammonia and methanol production at scale. As a chemical feedstock, it is the starting material for acetylene, chloromethanes, and other downstream intermediates used across the petrochemical chain.

Liquefied as LNG, it enables long-distance energy transport where pipeline infrastructure is unavailable. Methane is supplied as a compressed gas in cylinders and tube trailers for various industrial uses.

It is also available as liquefied natural gas (LNG) in cryogenic bulk tankers. Pipeline-grade natural gas, which is predominantly methane, is available under standard transmission specifications.

These specifications govern BTU content and impurity limits to ensure consistent performance. High-purity methane grades are available for laboratory, calibration, and specialty industrial applications.

description:
Methyl chloride (CAS 74-87-3 ), also known as R-40, is a compressed liquefied gas used as a methylating agent and chemical intermediate across multiple industrial sectors. It serves as a key building block in the synthesis of silicones and agricultural chemicals.

In polymer manufacturing, it is the primary methylating agent in the production of methylcellulose and other cellulose ethers. These materials are used as thickeners, binders, and film formers in various industrial applications.

The silicone industry relies on this chemical to produce chlorosilane intermediates. This represents the foundational step in manufacturing silicone fluids, resins, and elastomers used in global manufacturing and construction.

In agrochemical synthesis, it functions as a methylating reagent for producing herbicides and plant growth regulators. Pharmaceutical manufacturers also use it as a reaction solvent and intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients.

Methyl chloride is supplied as a liquefied gas under pressure, typically in cylinders, drums, or ISO tank containers for bulk orders. It is available in technical and high-purity grades to meet specific requirements.

These grades are designed for both industrial synthesis and more demanding pharmaceutical or specialty chemical applications. Purity specifications and packaging configurations vary by supplier and specific end-use requirement.

Methylamine (CAS 74-89-5 ), also referenced industrially as MeNH2, is a primary aliphatic amine supplied as a compressed gas or aqueous solution. It functions as a reactive building block and chemical intermediate across pharmaceutical synthesis.

This versatile chemical is essential for agrochemical production and polymer manufacturing. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is a critical precursor for active ingredients including analgesics, antivirals, and central nervous system compounds.

Agrochemical producers use it to synthesize herbicides, fungicides, and pesticide intermediates at commercial scale. In polymer and resin chemistry, it acts as a chain initiator and modifier for industrial processes.

The compound contributes to the production of ion exchange resins and specialty coatings. Textile and leather processing operations use methylamine-based formulations for pH regulation and as a carrier in dyeing and tanning processes.

Methylamine is commercially available as an anhydrous liquefied gas in pressurized cylinders and as aqueous solutions, typically at 40% concentration. Technical grade is the standard for industrial synthesis applications.

name: Dimethylamine borane
description:
Dimethylamine borane ( CAS 74-94-2 ), commonly abbreviated as DMAB, is a stable borane complex used industrially as a selective reducing agent and electroless plating initiator.

Its controlled reactivity makes it a preferred alternative to sodium borohydride in processes requiring milder, more manageable reduction conditions for industrial chemical synthesis.

In electroless nickel and cobalt plating, DMAB functions as the reducing agent that drives metal deposition onto non-conductive substrates, including plastics and printed circuit boards.

The electronics industry relies on it for metallization steps where precise deposit quality and bath stability are critical procurement considerations for high-end manufacturing.

Pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturers use DMAB for reductive amination and selective carbonyl reduction where sodium borohydride would be too aggressive for the solvent system.

It also appears in specialty polymer and adhesive formulations as a curing initiator. DMAB is supplied as a white crystalline solid, typically in powder or granule form.

Material is packaged under inert conditions to preserve stability during storage and transit. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial applications.

High-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical synthesis and electronics. Bulk quantities are available in multi-kilogram drums for laboratory and development-scale procurement.

name: Ethyl bromide
description:
Ethyl bromide (CAS 74-96-4 ), also known as bromic ether, is a low-boiling alkylating and brominating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

Its reactivity as an ethylating agent makes it a preferred building block where controlled carbon-chain extension is required at industrial scale. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a key intermediate.

It is particularly useful where N- or O-ethylation reactions are required. Agrochemical producers use it to prepare herbicide and pesticide intermediates, where precise alkylation chemistry determines efficacy.

In plastics and polymer processing, it contributes to flame retardant formulations, helping compounders meet fire-resistance specifications in finished materials. This ensures safety in various industrial applications.

Textile and leather processors have historically employed it as a solvent carrier in specialty treatment baths. This is especially true where controlled evaporation rates are operationally critical for the process.

Ethyl bromide is supplied as a liquid in drums and ISO tank containers, with quantities ranging from laboratory to bulk industrial volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most users.

High-purity grades are available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate specifications. Buyers should confirm purity thresholds and stabilizer content with suppliers, as these vary by the intended downstream application.

name: Propane
description:
Propane (CAS 74-98-6 ), also supplied under the refrigerant designation R-290 and approved as food propellant E944 , is a liquefied hydrocarbon gas sourced for use as a solvent.

It functions as an aerosol propellant and fuel across multiple industrial sectors. In the oil and gas industry, propane serves as a solvent in deasphalting processes for lubricant base stocks.

It selectively separates heavy residual oils to produce cleaner refinery streams. Food-grade propane is used as a propellant in aerosol food products, dispensing whipped creams and cooking sprays.

This application ensures products are dispensed without leaving residue or affecting flavor. In automotive and energy markets, it functions as a liquefied petroleum gas fuel for fleet vehicles.

It is also utilized for industrial burners and portable heating equipment. As a refrigerant, R-290 is increasingly adopted in commercial refrigeration systems as a low-GWP alternative to synthetic refrigerants.

Propane is supplied as a compressed liquefied gas in cylinders, bulk tanks, and ISO containers. Food-grade and aerosol-grade propane is available to FCC specification for regulated use.

These grades are suitable for use in various food and cosmetic applications. Technical-grade supply is standard for fuel, refrigeration, and industrial solvent applications across the global market.

name: p-coumaric acid
description:
p-Coumaric acid (CAS 7400-08-0 ), also recognized commercially as p-hydroxycinnamic acid, is a naturally occurring hydroxycinnamic acid sourced from plant extracts or produced synthetically for industrial supply.

It functions primarily as an antioxidant, UV-absorbing agent, and bioactive intermediate across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a key intermediate.

This material is used in the production of active compounds, including resveratrol analogs and other polyphenolic APIs. Nutraceutical and functional food formulators incorporate it as a plant-derived antioxidant.

It is frequently found in dietary supplements, botanical extracts, and standardized herbal preparations. In cosmetic formulations, its UV-absorbing and antioxidant properties make it relevant for inclusion.

Common applications include sunscreen actives, anti-aging serums, and skin-brightening products. Food manufacturers also evaluate it as a natural antioxidant stabilizer in specialty food and beverage applications.

The product is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder. It is available in technical grade for industrial synthesis and in higher-purity grades for specialized manufacturing.

These include USP -aligned and research-grade specifications for pharmaceutical and nutraceutical applications. Packaging typically ranges from small quantities for development to bulk quantities.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for commercial-scale production. We provide comprehensive documentation to support regulatory compliance and formulation stability across all industrial sectors.

name: Etidronate disodium
description:
Etidronate disodium (CAS 7414-83-7 ), also known as HEDP disodium, is the disodium salt form of hydroxyethylidene diphosphonic acid used commercially as a chelating and sequestering agent.

It binds metal ions, particularly calcium and heavy metals, to prevent scale formation, oxidative degradation, and microbial activity across industrial and formulated product applications.

In water treatment, it controls calcium carbonate and metal oxide scale in cooling towers, boilers, and process water systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and creams.

It is used in rinse-off products to sequester trace metals that would otherwise destabilize peroxide-based systems or accelerate rancidity. Textile and leather processing operations use it to deactivate hardness ions.

This improves process consistency and color yield in dye baths and bleaching liquors. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a stabilizing excipient in liquid formulations where oxidation must be controlled.

Etidronate disodium is supplied as a white crystalline powder and as aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically around 30–40%. Standard grades include technical and pharmaceutical specifications.

Material is available to meet USP and BP standards, with food-contact and cosmetic-grade material available to meet purity requirements for various regulated applications.

name: Betaine aldehyde
description:
Betaine aldehyde (CAS 7418-61-3 ) is the direct biosynthetic precursor to betaine, the well-characterized osmoprotectant and methyl donor used across pharmaceutical and nutritional applications. In research and industrial synthesis, it functions as a key intermediate in choline oxidation pathways.

This compound bridges choline and betaine in enzymatic and chemical processes, serving as a vital component in metabolic studies. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is used as a building block for producing betaine and related quaternary ammonium compounds in active ingredient manufacturing.

Biotechnology and life sciences researchers employ it as a substrate for betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase (BADH) enzyme studies. This makes it a critical reference compound in metabolic pathway research and the development of specialized biochemical assays.

In nutritional ingredient production, it supports the synthesis of betaine used in feed additives and dietary supplement formulations. It also serves as a biochemical tool in oxidative stress and methylation research where controlled intermediate availability is critical.

Betaine aldehyde is typically supplied as a solution or salt form, most commonly as the chloride salt, reflecting its stability profile in commercial handling. It is available primarily in research and specialty chemical quantities for industrial buyers.

Material is supplied to pharmaceutical and biotechnology buyers under documented purity specifications to ensure consistency. Certificates of analysis with HPLC purity data are standard for procurement in regulated research environments and manufacturing sites.

The product meets rigorous internal benchmarks and is handled according to industry-standard safety protocols. Suppliers ensure that each batch aligns with the technical requirements necessary for high-stakes laboratory and industrial synthesis applications.

name: Ethylhexyl ethylhexanoate
description:
Ethylhexyl ethylhexanoate (CAS 7425-14-1 ) is a branched-chain ester used as an emollient, carrier solvent, and plasticizer across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its low viscosity and strong compatibility with oils and actives make it a practical base fluid for formulators working across multiple end markets and diverse chemical systems.

In cosmetics and personal care, it functions as a skin-conditioning emollient and carrier in serums, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, delivering a lightweight, non-greasy skin feel.

Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a plasticizing solvent to improve flexibility and film formation in specialty resin systems and high-performance industrial coatings.

In lubricant and metalworking applications, it serves as a synthetic base fluid or co-solvent where low volatility and good lubricity are required for mechanical performance.

It also acts as a dispersing medium for pigments and active ingredients in formulations where water-free processing is preferred to maintain stability and product shelf life.

Ethylhexyl ethylhexanoate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Cosmetic-grade material is the most commonly traded specification for global buyers.

Technical-grade is available for industrial coatings and lubricant applications. Purity levels of 99% and above are standard for personal care supply chains and high-end manufacturing.

name: Aluminum
description:
Aluminum (CAS 7429-90-5 ), also known as aluminium, is a lightweight metal supplied in processed forms for industrial manufacturing and surface treatment applications. It functions as a structural material, conductive substrate, and reflective pigment across a broad range of fabricated products and coatings systems.

In coatings and printing, aluminum powder and paste deliver metallic finish, opacity, and corrosion-barrier performance in architectural, automotive, and industrial paints. The electronics industry relies on high-purity aluminum foil and sheet as a conductive substrate for capacitors and battery current collectors.

Aerospace and automotive manufacturers use aluminum alloy stock for lightweight structural components where strength-to-weight ratio drives material selection. In packaging, aluminum foil provides the hermetic barrier layer in flexible laminates, blister packs, and food-grade wrapping applications.

Aluminum is available as powder, paste, flake, foil, sheet, rod, and granule, with particle size and surface treatment tailored to the end application. Standard grades include technical, aerospace-specification alloy series, and food-contact compliant forms meeting FCC and EU regulatory requirements.

Purity levels range from standard commercial grades to 99.99% high-purity material for electronics and specialty applications. This versatile metal is essential for modern manufacturing, offering a unique combination of low density, high conductivity, and excellent corrosion resistance.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality across all formats, supporting high-volume industrial processes and specialized technical requirements. Whether for structural engineering or decorative finishes, our aluminum products meet rigorous industry standards for performance and reliability.

name: Cerium octoate
description:
Cerium octoate (CAS 7435-02-1 ), also supplied under the trade name Tib Kat 812, is a cerium-based metal carboxylate used as a drier, catalyst, and stabilizer in industrial formulations.

It promotes oxidative crosslinking and polymer curing, reducing process times in coating and resin systems. In alkyd and air-drying coatings, it functions as a through-drying drier.

This material improves film hardness and reduces surface wrinkling compared to conventional cobalt-based systems. Printing ink formulators use it to accelerate oxidative drying in oil-based inks.

This support for faster press speeds and cleaner print definition is essential for high-volume production. In polymer and elastomer compounding, it acts as a crosslinking catalyst and thermal stabilizer.

It extends service life in rubber and sealant formulations. Mining and metals processing applications include its use as a catalyst precursor in hydrocarbon processing and surface treatment chemistries.

Cerium octoate is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in mineral spirits or aliphatic hydrocarbon carriers. The cerium metal content varies by grade to meet specific industrial requirements.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with cerium concentration commonly specified as a percentage of active metal. Drum and IBC packaging is typical for industrial volumes.

name: Lead

Manganese (CAS 7439-96-5 ), abbreviated Mn and commercially known under the trade name Cutaval, is a transition metal supplied in refined elemental form for industrial and specialty applications.

It functions primarily as an alloying agent, catalyst precursor, and micronutrient source across metallurgical, agricultural, and chemical manufacturing sectors. In steelmaking and alloy production, Mn is added to control sulfur content.

This process improves hardness, making it indispensable in producing structural steel, stainless steel, and high-strength alloys. Agricultural feed and fertilizer formulators use manganese as a micronutrient additive.

These additives correct soil and animal deficiencies that affect crop yield and livestock health. Water treatment operations deploy manganese-based systems to oxidize dissolved iron and control biological fouling.

This application is critical in municipal and industrial water supplies. In personal care and pigment manufacturing, it serves as a colorant precursor and catalyst component in oxidative formulations.

Manganese is supplied as metal flakes, powder, and briquettes, with purity grades typically ranging from technical to high-purity electrolytic grades. Electrolytic manganese metal is the most traded form.

This refined material meets specifications required for steel and battery-grade applications. Feed and agricultural grades are available as elemental powder conforming to recognized nutritional and quality standards.

name: Molybdenum
description:
Molybdenum (CAS 7439-98-7 ), commonly referenced by its symbol Mo, is a refractory transition metal sourced and traded as a primary alloying and catalytic material across industrial supply chains.

In metallurgy and chemical processing, it functions as a high-performance strengthener in steel alloys and as a catalytically active component in refining and synthesis operations.

In petroleum refining, Mo-based catalysts are used in hydrodesulfurization units to remove sulfur from crude fractions, meeting fuel quality specifications for global distribution.

Steel and superalloy manufacturers incorporate molybdenum to improve high-temperature strength and corrosion resistance in structural components, tooling, and aerospace parts for extreme environments.

In the chemical industry, molybdenum compounds derived from elemental Mo serve as precursors for oxidation and ammoxidation catalysts used in producing acrylonitrile and formaldehyde.

Pigment producers also use molybdenum as a precursor for molybdate-based colorants applied in coatings and plastics, ensuring high durability and color stability in industrial applications.

Molybdenum is commercially available as powder, rod, sheet, wire, and sintered parts, with powder being the most common traded form for chemical and metallurgical processing.

Standard grades include technical-grade and high-purity specifications, with purity levels typically ranging from 99.9% to 99.99% depending on specific end-use requirements.

name: Nickel
description:
Nickel (CAS 7440-02-0 ) is a transition metal supplied in elemental form for industrial metallurgical and chemical applications. It is a foundational alloying component in stainless steel, superalloys, and specialty metals production.

In chemical processing, it functions as a catalyst base and corrosion-resistant material across demanding industrial environments. In steelmaking and alloy production, nickel is incorporated into austenitic stainless steels.

High-performance superalloys are used in turbine blades, exhaust systems, and structural aerospace components. Battery and electronics manufacturers use nickel in electrode materials, conductive coatings, and electroplating processes.

These applications improve surface durability and conductivity. Nickel-based catalysts are employed in hydrogenation reactions, including edible oil processing and petrochemical refining, where the metal provides active sites.

This allows for selective chemical conversion in various processes. In automotive and industrial applications, nickel alloys are specified for components requiring resistance to high-temperature oxidation and mechanical fatigue.

Nickel is commercially available as powder, pellets, rounds, briquettes, and foil, with particle size and purity tailored to end-use requirements. Standard grades include electrolytic nickel and carbonyl nickel powder.

Reduced nickel is also available, with each meeting different purity thresholds for metallurgical or catalytic use. Technical and high-purity grades are available for specific industrial needs.

Specifications are aligned to ASTM and industry standards depending on the application. This ensures that the material meets the rigorous demands of modern manufacturing and chemical engineering sectors.

name: Potassium
description:
Potassium (CAS 7440-09-7 ), also known as Kalium, is an alkali metal supplied industrially in refined elemental form for use as a reactive reducing agent and chemical intermediate. In food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural contexts, it functions primarily as a source of potassium ion activity.

This material supports nutrient fortification, electrolyte balance, and crop nutrition programs across various sectors. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, elemental potassium serves as a precursor in synthesizing potassium-based active ingredients and excipients where controlled reactivity is required.

Food and nutrition producers use potassium-derived compounds for mineral fortification in functional foods, dietary supplements, and electrolyte formulations targeting potassium intake. These applications ensure that essential mineral levels are maintained in consumer products.

In agriculture, it underpins the production of potassium fertilizers that correct soil deficiencies and support yield in potassium-sensitive crops. Industrial chemical synthesis also draws on elemental potassium as a strong reducing agent in specialty organic reactions.

Elemental potassium is supplied as a metal in sealed, inert-atmosphere packaging due to its high reactivity with moisture and air. It is typically provided as ingots, lumps, or dispersions in mineral oil to ensure safe handling and storage.

Technical and reagent grades are the standard commercial forms available for industrial procurement. Purity specifications vary by application, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical use to meet rigorous industry requirements.

name: Silicon
description:
Silicon (CAS 7440-21-3 ), commonly traded as silicon metal or Si, is a high-purity elemental material refined from quartz and used as a foundational raw material across metallurgical, chemical, and electronic manufacturing supply chains.

It functions primarily as a precursor for producing silicones, semiconductors, and aluminum alloys rather than as a finished additive. In the plastics and polymer industry, silicon metal is the primary feedstock for manufacturing silicone polymers.

These include silicone fluids, elastomers, and sealants used in automotive and construction applications. Automotive manufacturers rely on aluminum-silicon alloys produced with metallurgical-grade silicon to achieve lightweight, high-strength castings.

These castings are essential for engine components and structural parts. In electronics, ultra-high-purity silicon is processed into wafers that form the substrate for semiconductors, solar cells, and integrated circuits.

Chemical producers also use it as a starting material for synthesizing chlorosilanes and other organosilicon intermediates. Silicon metal is supplied as chunks, granules, or powder, with particle size and purity grade selected based on end-use requirements.

Metallurgical grade (typically 98–99% Si) covers alloy and chemical synthesis applications, while semiconductor and solar grades are held to significantly tighter purity thresholds. Standard packaging ranges from bulk bags to drums.

name: Silver
description:
Silver (CAS 7440-22-4 ), also designated E174 as a food-contact and cosmetic colorant, is a precious metal sourced in refined elemental form for industrial, decorative, and antimicrobial applications.

Argentum is the historical designation still referenced in pharmaceutical and laboratory contexts. Demand spans sectors where conductivity, catalytic activity, or controlled microbial suppression are procurement priorities.

In personal care and cosmetics, E174 silver is used as a surface colorant in decorative products such as nail preparations and body decoration, where regulatory compliance with approved colorant status drives sourcing decisions.

Water treatment systems incorporate silver-dosed media and coatings to inhibit biofilm formation in filtration units and storage vessels. Printed electronics and conductive ink formulations rely on silver particles or flakes.

These materials produce conductive traces on flexible substrates. In biotechnology and pharmaceutical manufacturing, silver-based surface treatments are applied to equipment and wound-contact materials to reduce microbial load.

Silver is supplied as powder, flakes, granules, colloidal dispersions, and foil, with particle size and morphology specified to application requirements. Grades include technical, pharmaceutical-grade, and cosmetic-grade material.

Colloidal silver concentrations and powder mesh sizes vary by end-use, and buyers typically specify purity at 99.9% or higher for electronics and pharmaceutical applications to ensure performance and safety.

name: Sodium
description:
Sodium (CAS 7440-23-5 ), also known commercially as Natrium, is a reactive alkali metal supplied in elemental form for industrial reduction and catalytic processes. It functions as a powerful reducing agent and chemical initiator in synthesis and metallurgical operations.

In water treatment, elemental sodium is used to generate sodium amalgam and other reactive intermediates for dechlorination and chemical reduction of process streams. In metals processing, it serves as a reductant in the production of reactive metals.

This includes the production of titanium and zirconium through reduction of their halide salts. Sodium also acts as a catalyst initiator in certain polymerization reactions, particularly in the production of synthetic rubber and specialty polymers.

In mining operations, it supports hydrometallurgical reduction steps where strong electron donors are required to precipitate target metals from solution. This makes it an essential component for high-purity metal extraction processes.

Elemental sodium is supplied as metallic ingots, blocks, or dispersions in mineral oil to prevent oxidative degradation during transport and storage. This ensures the material remains stable and reactive for industrial use.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with purity levels typically specified at 99% or higher depending on the application. Specialized dispersion grades are available for catalyst and synthesis applications.

These dispersions are ideal for scenarios where fine particle distribution is required for rapid reaction kinetics. The material is handled under strict safety protocols to maintain its integrity and performance in chemical manufacturing.

name: Tin
description:
Tin (CAS 7440-31-5 ) is a base metal supplied in refined elemental form, used across metallurgy, chemical synthesis, and industrial manufacturing. It serves as a foundational raw material for producing alloys and inorganic tin compounds.

Procurement demand spans solder production, chemical manufacturing, and surface coating applications. In electronics and automotive manufacturing, tin is the primary constituent of lead-free solder alloys used in PCB assembly.

Tin compounds derived from the refined metal function as catalysts in polyurethane and silicone curing systems, making it a direct precursor for catalyst manufacturers. This metal is essential for high-performance industrial systems.

In plastics processing, tin-based stabilizers produced from elemental tin provide heat and UV resistance in PVC formulations. The metal also feeds into the production of tin oxide and organotin biocides used in coatings.

Refined tin is supplied as ingots, bars, granules, and shot, with purity levels typically ranging from 99.85% to 99.99%. Standard commercial grades conform to LME specifications for global trade.

Higher-purity electronic and chemical grades are available for sensitive synthesis applications. Packaging is offered in bulk metric-ton quantities as well as smaller lot sizes for laboratory and specialty chemical use.

name: Argon
description:
Argon (CAS 7440-37-1 ), also supplied under food-grade designation E938 , is a chemically inert noble gas used across industrial and specialty applications as a protective and carrier medium.

Its inertness makes it the preferred choice wherever oxidation, contamination, or reactive atmospheres must be eliminated during processing or storage. In electronics manufacturing, argon provides the inert atmosphere required.

This gas is essential for semiconductor fabrication, plasma etching, and sputter deposition of thin films. Automotive and aerospace welding operations rely on argon as a shielding gas to protect weld pools.

By preventing atmospheric contamination, it directly influences joint integrity and finish quality. Food and beverage producers use E938-grade argon to blanket packaged products and displace oxygen effectively.

This process extends shelf life without chemical additives. In industrial cleaning, argon serves as a carrier gas in plasma surface treatment systems used to prepare substrates before coating or bonding.

Argon is supplied as a compressed gas in high-pressure cylinders, dewars, and bulk liquid form via cryogenic tankers for large-volume industrial users. Standard grades include industrial and welding specifications.

High-purity (99.999%) options meet the differing requirements of electronics fabrication versus general manufacturing. Food-contact applications require E938-certified supply with documented purity and compliance.

name: Arsenic
description:
Arsenic (CAS 7440-38-2 ) is a metalloid element sourced for industrial and specialty applications where controlled introduction of element 33 into alloys, semiconductors, or catalytic systems is required.

It functions as a dopant, alloying agent, and catalyst component across electronics manufacturing and metallurgical processing. In semiconductor fabrication, it is used as an n-type dopant to modify electrical conductivity.

This process directly influences device performance in transistors and diodes by modifying silicon and germanium wafers. The metallurgical industry incorporates it into lead and copper alloys to improve hardness.

These enhancements are critical for high-temperature strength in battery grids and ammunition. In compound semiconductor production, it is a primary feedstock for gallium arsenide wafers used in high-frequency devices.

Optoelectronic devices also rely on this material for efficient operation. Certain heterogeneous catalytic processes employ arsenic-containing compounds derived from elemental arsenic as precursor material for chemical synthesis.

The product is supplied as a solid in lump, shot, or powder form, with purity grades ranging from technical to high-purity for electronics-grade applications. Standard commercial grades are available for metallurgical use.

Semiconductor and compound semiconductor manufacturers typically require certified high-purity material. These materials must meet tightly controlled trace metal specifications to ensure consistent performance in sensitive electronic components.

name: Carbon
description:
Carbon (CAS 7440-44-0 ) is a foundational industrial element supplied primarily as activated carbon, a processed form engineered for high surface area adsorption. It functions as a purification agent.

This material is essential for filtration across water treatment, food processing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and industrial cleaning applications. It is highly effective at removing unwanted compounds from various streams.

In water treatment, activated carbon removes chlorine, organic contaminants, and taste-and-odor compounds from municipal supplies. It ensures that industrial water meets the necessary safety and quality standards.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to decolorize and purify active ingredient streams. This process helps in meeting strict purity thresholds required for finished dosage forms and USP quality standards.

In food and beverage production, it clarifies liquids such as edible oils, sugars, and alcohols. It works by adsorbing color bodies and impurities to ensure a clear and consistent final product for consumers.

Mining operations apply carbon in gold recovery circuits to capture dissolved gold from cyanide leach solutions. This occurs during carbon-in-pulp and carbon-in-leach processes used in large-scale metal extraction.

Activated carbon is available in powdered, granular, and pelletized forms to suit different filtration systems. Standard grades include food-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet diverse regulatory needs.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for laboratory procurement. These options ensure that both large-scale plants and research facilities can access high-quality carbon.
