name: Chromium
description:
Chromium (CAS 7440-47-3 ), also commercially referenced as Chrome, is a hard transition metal sourced primarily through ferrochrome production and used across metallurgy, surface finishing, and catalysis.

Its exceptional hardness and corrosion resistance make it a foundational input in alloy manufacturing and industrial coating processes. In steelmaking, chromium is alloyed to produce stainless and tool steels.

This metal determines corrosion resistance thresholds and mechanical performance grades. Electroplating operations deposit chromium onto metal and plastic substrates to deliver hard, wear-resistant surfaces for hardware.

These applications are vital for automotive, aerospace, and industrial components. In catalysis, chromium-based compounds derived from elemental chromium function as precursors for polymerization and dehydrogenation catalysts.

These catalysts are used extensively in petrochemical processing. Chromium also enters pigment manufacturing as a feedstock for chromium oxide and chromate-based colorants used in coatings and ceramics.

Specialty inks also utilize these pigments for high-performance applications. Chromium is supplied as electrolytic flakes, lumps, or powder, with purity levels ranging from technical grade to high-purity grades.

Material exceeding 99.5% Cr is available for specialized needs. Aluminothermic and electrolytic production routes yield material suited to different downstream specifications for sensitive alloy applications.

These include low-iron and low-sulfur variants. Bulk quantities are standard for metallurgical buyers, with smaller packaging available for catalyst and chemical synthesis applications.

name: Cobalt
description:
Cobalt (CAS 7440-48-4 ), commonly abbreviated as Co, is a transition metal supplied in elemental form for use across catalyst manufacturing and pigment production. It functions as a foundational raw material in processes requiring controlled oxidation states.

This versatile metal is essential for applications involving magnetic properties or colorant precursors. In catalyst manufacturing, elemental cobalt serves as a precursor for Fischer-Tropsch synthesis catalysts used in gas-to-liquid fuel conversion.

It is also utilized in hydroprocessing and various industrial chemical reactions. Pigment producers use cobalt to produce cobalt blue and cobalt violet colorants for cosmetic formulations, ceramics, and artist-grade materials.

In personal care, cobalt-derived compounds contribute to preservative and antimicrobial systems in certain formulations. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use cobalt as a starting material for synthesizing cobalt-containing active compounds.

These materials are also vital for micronutrient preparations and specialized medical applications. Elemental cobalt is available as powder, granules, pellets, and cathode or briquette forms to suit different downstream processing requirements.

Standard purity grades range from technical to high-purity (99.8%+), with battery-grade and catalyst-grade specifications available for demanding applications. Quality control ensures consistency across various industrial batches.

Powder particle size distributions are typically specified to match sintering, alloying, or dispersion requirements in end-use processes. This ensures optimal performance in metallurgical and chemical manufacturing environments.

name: Copper
description:
Copper (CAS 7440-50-8 ), abbreviated Cu and approved as food colorant E115 , is a base metal supplied in refined elemental form for industrial, agricultural, and chemical processing applications.

It functions as a biocide, catalyst, and conductive material across a broad range of manufacturing and treatment processes. In water treatment, copper is used in algaecide and antifouling systems.

These systems control microbial growth in cooling towers, reservoirs, and distribution infrastructure. Agriculture relies on copper-based formulations, including fungicides and soil amendments, to manage crop disease.

It is also used to correct mineral deficiencies in livestock feed. Electronics and surface finishing industries consume refined copper for electroplating, conductive coatings, and printed circuit board fabrication.

In chemical processing, copper serves as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in hydrogenation, oxidation, and organic synthesis reactions. Copper is supplied as cathode sheets, powder, granules, wire, and flakes.

Purity grades range from standard technical to high-purity electrolytic (99.99%). Powder grades are available in varying mesh sizes to suit catalyst preparation, pigment blending, or metallurgical applications.

Recognized commercial grades include electrolytic tough pitch (ETP) and oxygen-free (OF) copper for electrical and precision uses. This material meets rigorous industrial and chemical specifications.

name: Helium
description:
Helium (CAS 7440-59-7 ), also identified as E939 in food-grade applications, is a chemically inert noble gas supplied industrially for its unique carrier and purging properties.

Its non-reactive nature makes it the preferred choice where contamination from reactive gases would compromise process integrity or product quality in sensitive manufacturing environments.

In semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, helium is used as a carrier gas in chemical vapor deposition and as a cooling medium during wafer fabrication processes.

Chromatography laboratories rely on it as the dominant carrier gas in GC systems, where its low molecular weight delivers sharper peak resolution and faster analysis times than alternative gases.

Aerospace and defense applications use helium to purge fuel systems and pressurize rocket propellants, where zero reactivity is a non-negotiable process requirement for safety.

As a food additive, it functions as a propellant gas in food-grade aerosol packaging where inert atmosphere protection is required to maintain the shelf life of the product.

Helium is supplied as a compressed gas in high-pressure cylinders, tube trailers, and bulk liquid dewars for large-volume industrial users across various sectors.

Standard grades include research-purity, industrial-grade, and food-grade specifications. Liquid helium is available for cryogenic applications, including MRI cooling and superconducting magnet systems.

name: Vanadium
description:
Vanadium (CAS 7440-62-2 ) is a transition metal supplied in elemental form for use across metallurgical, catalytic, and energy storage applications. It functions primarily as an alloying agent and catalyst component.

Its addition modifies the performance characteristics of end materials at relatively low concentrations. In steel and titanium alloy production, it increases hardness and tensile strength for industrial use.

This makes it a critical input for high-strength structural steels used in automotive frames, pipelines, and aerospace components. Refineries use vanadium-based catalysts in fluid catalytic cracking.

It also supports sulfuric acid production, where it drives key oxidation reactions at industrial scale. Vanadium redox flow batteries depend on elemental vanadium as the primary feedstock for electrolyte.

These batteries are increasingly deployed in grid-scale energy storage. In polymerization processes, it functions as a catalyst precursor for producing ethylene-propylene rubbers and other specialty polymers.

The material is supplied as powder, flakes, and solid pieces, with purity grades ranging from technical to high-purity (99.5%+) for demanding catalytic and battery applications.

Standard specifications include technical grade for metallurgical use and high-purity grades for chemical and energy storage applications. Packaging is typically offered in sealed containers.

These specialized containers prevent oxidation during storage and transit. This ensures the material maintains its integrity for sensitive chemical reactions and high-performance alloy manufacturing.

name: Zinc

Zinc (CAS 7440-66-6 ) is a base metal supplied in refined form for industrial processing, alloying, and chemical synthesis. It serves as the foundational raw material for a broad range of downstream zinc compounds.

These coatings and alloys are used across heavy industry and manufacturing. In galvanizing, zinc is applied as a protective coating on steel structures, automotive components, and construction materials to prevent corrosion.

This ensures an extended service life for critical infrastructure. Brass and die-casting alloys consume significant zinc volumes in automotive and electronics manufacturing, where dimensional precision and conductivity are critical.

Chemical producers use refined zinc as a feedstock for synthesizing zinc oxide, zinc sulfate, and other compounds. These are used in agriculture, rubber vulcanization, and water treatment processes.

In electroplating and metalworking, zinc anodes and zinc-based lubricant additives provide both surface protection and process stability. Zinc is commercially available as ingots, slabs, granules, powder, and dust.

Purity grades range from standard SHG (Special High Grade, 99.995%) to high-grade and prime western grades. Zinc powder and dust are supplied in technical and refined grades tailored for chemical synthesis.

It functions as a low-toxicity alternative to lead and other heavy metals in applications where regulatory pressure or end-product safety requirements demand cleaner substitutes.

In pharmaceuticals, elemental bismuth serves as a precursor to active bismuth salts and compounds used in gastrointestinal formulations and antimicrobial preparations.

Polymer manufacturers incorporate it into flame-retardant systems where halogen-free compliance is required, particularly in wire, cable, and electronic component housings.

Bismuth is also used as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in oxidation and condensation reactions within specialty chemical production for various industrial sectors.

In metallurgy, it acts as a lead replacement in free-machining alloys and low-melting fusible alloys used in safety devices and precision casting applications.

Bismuth is supplied as ingots, shots, granules, and high-purity pellets to suit different downstream processing requirements and specific manufacturing workflows.

name: Calcium
description:
Calcium (CAS 7440-70-2 ) is a reactive alkaline earth metal supplied in elemental form for industrial reduction, alloying, and chemical synthesis applications. As a powerful reducing agent and desulfurization reagent, it drives critical metallurgical processes.

In steelmaking and non-ferrous metallurgy, elemental calcium is used for desulfurization, deoxidation, and inclusion modification. This directly improves the mechanical properties and cleanliness of finished metal products across various industrial sectors.

The nuclear and specialty metals industry uses it as a reduction agent to produce high-purity titanium, uranium, and rare earth metals. This is achieved via metallothermic reduction, where high reactivity is essential for success.

In the chemical industry, it serves as a precursor for calcium hydride and other reactive calcium compounds used in organic synthesis. It is also frequently utilized in the production of specialized industrial desiccants.

Battery and energy storage research also draws on elemental calcium as an anode material in next-generation calcium-ion cell development. This emerging field relies on the specific electrochemical properties of the metal.

Elemental calcium is supplied as granules, lumps, turnings, and shot, with particle size selected to match handling requirements. Technical and high-purity grades are available, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.5%+.

Material is generally packaged under inert atmosphere or in sealed containers to preserve reactivity during storage and transit. This ensures the chemical integrity of the product remains intact until it reaches the final application.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it meets the heat resistance requirements of engineering resins and polyolefin processing, where many organic yellows fail to maintain their color integrity.

Printing ink formulators select it for packaging applications requiring sharp color strength and resistance to bleed and migration into adjacent substrates during the manufacturing process.

Coatings manufacturers incorporate it into industrial and decorative finishes where outdoor exposure demands sustained color integrity and resistance to environmental degradation over long periods.

Textile and leather finishing operations use it in pigment printing pastes and surface coatings where fastness to washing and rubbing is a key performance criterion for the final product.

The pigment is supplied as a dry powder, with press cake and dispersion forms available for wet-process applications. Standard grades are offered for plastics, coatings, and ink end uses.

name: Tellurium dioxide
description:
Tellurium dioxide (CAS 7446-07-3 ), also abbreviated as TeO2, is an inorganic oxide of tellurium used primarily in electronics and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions as a catalyst and optical material, enabling precise control in acousto-optical and electrochemical processes. In acousto-optic devices, TeO2 crystals are used to manufacture deflectors.

These crystals are also used for modulators and tunable filters for laser systems and telecommunications equipment. The compound serves as a precursor in the production of tellurite glass.

This glass is incorporated into fiber optic amplifiers and infrared-transmitting optical components. In catalysis, it supports selective oxidation reactions in specialty chemical synthesis.

This includes the production of fine chemicals and pharmaceutical intermediates. Thin-film deposition processes in semiconductor fabrication also consume TeO2 as a sputtering target material.

It is used for phase-change memory applications. Tellurium dioxide is supplied as a white crystalline powder in technical and high-purity grades for electronic and optical applications.

Purity levels commonly range from 99% to 99.999% (5N). High-purity sputtering targets are available as pressed and sintered forms to meet semiconductor-grade specifications.

Packaging is typically offered in small laboratory quantities through to kilogram-scale lots depending on purity grade. This ensures flexibility for both research and industrial production.

description:
Selenium dioxide (CAS 7446-08-4 ), also known as selenious anhydride, is an inorganic oxidizing agent used primarily as a catalyst and reagent in chemical synthesis and industrial refining.

SeO2 enables selective oxidation reactions that are difficult to achieve with conventional oxidants, making it a targeted choice for specialty chemical production and advanced manufacturing.

In organic synthesis, it is the reagent of choice for allylic and benzylic oxidations, converting methylene groups to carbonyl compounds in pharmaceutical and fine chemical intermediates.

The electronics industry relies on it as a component in glass and ceramic formulations where controlled selenium incorporation modifies optical and electrical properties for high-tech use.

In metallurgy and mining, it functions as a refining agent for copper and other non-ferrous metals, removing impurities during electrorefining processes to ensure high metal purity.

It also serves as a precursor in the production of other selenium compounds used across pigment and catalyst manufacturing, supporting a wide range of industrial chemical applications.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Technical and reagent grades are the standard market offerings, with purity levels typically ranging from 99% upward for use.

Packaging is available in small quantities for research use through to bulk quantities for industrial procurement, with handling requirements reflecting its oxidizing classification.

name: Sulfur dioxide
description:
Sulfur dioxide (CAS 7446-09-5 ), commonly referenced as SO2 or E220 , is an inorganic gas used across food processing, industrial manufacturing, and water treatment. It serves as a preservative, antioxidant, and reducing agent.

Its dual role in microbial control and oxidation prevention makes it a procurement staple across multiple regulated industries. In food and beverage production, SO2 is applied to wines, dried fruits, and fruit juices.

This chemical is essential to inhibit microbial growth and prevent browning during storage and processing. Pulp and paper manufacturers use it to bleach cellulose fibers and neutralize excess chlorine in effluent streams.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, sulfur dioxide reduces hexavalent chromium and precipitates metals from process liquors during ore refining. Water treatment facilities apply it for dechlorination of potable and wastewater streams.

name: Aluminum chloride
description:
Aluminum chloride anhydrous (CAS 7446-70-0 ), also known as aluminum trichloride, is a high-activity Lewis acid catalyst and inorganic salt used across chemical synthesis, water treatment, and industrial processing.

Its strong electrophilic character makes it a preferred reagent wherever controlled catalytic activity or coagulation is required at scale. In petrochemical and organic synthesis, it drives Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation reactions.

This chemical forms the basis for producing dyes, pharmaceuticals, and specialty chemicals. Water treatment facilities use it as a coagulant to aggregate suspended solids and colloidal matter, improving clarification efficiency.

It is effective in both municipal and industrial effluent systems. The textile and leather industries apply it as a preservative and mordant, fixing dyes to fiber substrates and extending material durability.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a catalyst intermediate in active ingredient synthesis where precise Lewis acid reactivity is required. This ensures high yields and purity in complex chemical reactions.

Aluminum chloride anhydrous is supplied as a granular or lumpy crystalline solid, with powder forms available for specific process requirements. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial catalysis.

Handling and packaging specifications typically account for its moisture sensitivity. Supply is provided in sealed, inert-atmosphere containers ranging from drum to bulk quantities to maintain product integrity during transport.

name: Sodium acrylate
description:
Sodium acrylate (CAS 7446-81-3 ) is the sodium salt of acrylic acid, used primarily as a monomer in the synthesis of superabsorbent and water-soluble polymers. Its ability to polymerize into high-molecular-weight chains makes it a foundational building block.

This chemical is essential for products that require controlled water absorption or viscosity management across multiple industries. In water treatment, sodium acrylate-based polymers function as flocculants and coagulants for efficient separation.

These polymers bind suspended solids in municipal and industrial effluent systems. Personal care formulators incorporate polymerized sodium acrylate as a rheology modifier in gels, creams, and thickened lotions where stable texture is required.

Superabsorbent polymers derived from this monomer are the core functional material in hygiene products such as diapers and adult incontinence pads. It provides the necessary capacity for moisture retention in these consumer goods.

In textile and paper processing, it is used to modify surface properties and improve wet-strength or fiber bonding in finished materials. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial manufacturing and material science.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution, with concentration and purity varying by application. Technical grade is the most common commercial form for large-scale operations.

Higher-purity specifications are available for polymer synthesis applications requiring consistent monomer quality. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial production, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and specialty use.

name: Cupric chloride
description:
Cupric chloride (CAS 7447-39-4 ), also known commercially as CuCl2, is an inorganic copper salt used across industrial chemistry as a catalyst, biocide, and metal surface treatment agent.

Its reactivity with organic and inorganic substrates makes it a practical choice across multiple manufacturing sectors. In chemical synthesis and petrochemical processing, it functions as a catalyst or catalyst precursor.

It is frequently utilized in chlorination reactions and oxidative coupling processes. Textile and leather manufacturers use it as a mordant to fix dyes onto fiber substrates, improving color fastness in finished goods.

Water treatment operations employ it as a biocidal agent to control algae and microbial growth in industrial water systems. In mining and hydrometallurgy, it serves in copper etching and metal recovery processes.

It is particularly useful in printed circuit board manufacturing where controlled copper dissolution is required. The material is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as the dihydrate form in crystalline or granular format.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and reagent grade, with anhydrous and dihydrate variants available depending on application requirements. Quality is maintained according to ACS standards.

Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply in fiber drums or supersacks. This ensures safe transport and storage for various industrial and laboratory environments.

name: Potassium chloride
description:
Potassium chloride (CAS 7447-40-7 ), commercially known as muriate of potash or by its designation E508 , is a mineral salt sourced from natural evaporite deposits and produced synthetically for industrial use.

It functions as a potassium source, electrolyte replenisher, flavor enhancer, and processing aid across food, pharmaceutical, agricultural, and water treatment applications. In food manufacturing, it replaces or extends sodium chloride.

This ingredient is used in reduced-sodium products, delivering saltiness without increasing sodium content in processed meats, dairy, and snack formulations. Agricultural buyers source it as a primary potassium fertilizer.

It supplies the nutrient directly to soil or as a component in blended NPK fertilizers for crop production. Pharmaceutical and IV solution manufacturers use it as an electrolyte active in oral rehydration salts.

It is also utilized in dialysis fluids and parenteral preparations. Water treatment facilities apply it in ion exchange softening systems as a sodium-free regenerant for resin beds to maintain water quality.

Potassium chloride is available as white crystalline granules, coarse crystals, or fine powder depending on the intended application. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E508) and USP / BP for pharmaceutical use.

It is also available in technical or agricultural grade for industrial and fertilizer applications. Bulk supply is common for agricultural and industrial buyers, with smaller packaged formats available for procurement.

name: Lithium chloride
description:
Lithium chloride (CAS 7447-41-8 ), commonly abbreviated as LiCl, is an inorganic salt sourced for its hygroscopic properties and ionic reactivity across industrial and specialty chemical markets.

It functions as a desiccant, catalyst component, flame retardant additive, and reference electrolyte depending on the application sector. In textile processing, LiCl is used as a solvent additive to dissolve cellulose and aramid fibers.

This enables the production of high-performance technical fabrics and fiber spinning solutions. Polymer manufacturers use it as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in polycondensation reactions, particularly in the production of polyamides.

In pharmaceutical and biotechnology workflows, LiCl serves as a selective precipitation agent for RNA isolation. This makes it a standard reagent in nucleic acid purification protocols for laboratory and industrial use.

Water treatment and industrial humidification systems use LiCl-based solutions for moisture control and humidity regulation in closed-loop environments. The compound is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in anhydrous granule form.

Anhydrous purity is the most commercially traded specification for this material. Standard grades include technical, pharmaceutical, and reagent-grade, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.9%.

Packaging is available in moisture-resistant containers due to the compound's strong affinity for atmospheric water. This ensures the product maintains its integrity and flowability during transport and storage.

name: Ethyl 2-methylbutyrate
description:
Ethyl 2-methylbutyrate (CAS 7452-79-1 ), also known by its FEMA 2443 designation, is a synthetic flavor and fragrance ester used to impart fresh apple, fruity, and green top notes in consumer products.

It is a recognized flavoring substance approved for use in food and beverage applications across major regulatory frameworks. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to build or enhance apple, pear, and tropical fruit flavor profiles.

Common applications include confectionery, beverages, dairy products, and baked goods. Fragrance formulators incorporate it into personal care products including shampoos, body lotions, and fine fragrances where fresh green-fruity character is required.

It is also used in tobacco flavoring and functional food formulations where natural fruit character needs to be replicated or reinforced at low use levels. Flavor houses frequently blend it with other esters and aldehydes.

This blending helps to construct complex top-note profiles for finished flavor compounds. Ethyl 2-methylbutyrate is supplied as a clear mobile liquid, typically in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers.

Smaller pack sizes are available for flavor and fragrance laboratories. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and FEMA specifications is the standard commercial offering for global distribution.

Purity is generally 98% or higher for flavor-grade material. This high level of purity ensures consistent performance in sensitive formulations across the food, beverage, and cosmetic industries.

name: Tylosin tartrate
description:
Tylosin tartrate (CAS 74610-55-2 ), also marketed under the trade names Pharmasin, Tylan Soluble, and Tylan Injectable, is the tartrate salt form of the macrolide antibiotic tylosin.

It is used in veterinary medicine and animal production as an antimicrobial agent to control bacterial infections and support growth performance in livestock across various agricultural sectors.

In swine and poultry production, this compound is incorporated into medicated feed and drinking water formulations to treat and prevent respiratory and enteric infections caused by Mycoplasma.

Cattle and sheep producers use injectable formulations to manage pneumonia and soft tissue infections in individual animals. The compound also serves as a reference standard and active pharmaceutical ingredient.

Consistent potency and purity are critical for batch release in veterinary drug manufacturing. Research applications include use as a positive control in antimicrobial susceptibility testing protocols for laboratories.

The product is supplied as a water-soluble powder, suited for both oral solution and premix manufacturing. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and veterinary-grade specifications for industrial use.

Potency is typically expressed in units per milligram against established reference standards. Bulk quantities are standard for feed additive manufacturers, while smaller packaging supports compounding pharmacies.

name: Diaminopyrimidine oxide
description:
Diaminopyrimidine oxide (CAS 74638-76-9 ), commercially recognized as Aminexil and Kopexil, is an active ingredient used in topical scalp and hair care formulations.

It targets the perifollicular collagen structure to help maintain hair anchoring, making it a sought-after functional ingredient for anti-hair loss product development.

Aminexil is the primary active in leave-on scalp serums, ampoules, and treatment lotions designed to address hair thinning and premature hair loss.

Formulators incorporate it into professional salon treatments and retail anti-hair loss ranges, often in combination with other actives such as minoxidil or niacinamide.

Kopexil is also used in shampoo and conditioner formats where a scalp-conditioning benefit claim is required for the specific product line.

Cosmetic brands targeting the dermocosmetic and trichology segments source this ingredient to substantiate clinical efficacy claims on finished products.

Diaminopyrimidine oxide is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or as a pre-dispersed solution for ease of formulation in industrial settings.

Cosmetic-grade material is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels commonly at 99% or higher for bulk quantities and research samples.

name: Benzoyl isopropanol
description:
Benzoyl isopropanol (CAS 7473-98-5 ), commercially recognized as HMPP and 2-Hydroxy-2-methylpropiophenone, is a photoinitiator that triggers free-radical polymerization upon UV exposure.

It is used across coatings, adhesives, and printing to enable rapid, solvent-free cure cycles. In UV-curable coatings and industrial varnishes, HMPP initiates crosslinking under UV light.

This enables high-throughput production lines with minimal thermal input. Printing ink formulators rely on it for fast-cure flexographic and screen-printing systems where sharp cure response is critical.

Low yellowing properties are essential for these applications. In adhesive and sealant formulations, it supports UV-cure processes for optical, electronics, and label applications.

Bond integrity and cure speed are production priorities in these sectors. Personal care formulators also incorporate it into UV-curable nail gel systems for performance.

Controlled cure depth and compatibility with acrylate monomers determine its effectiveness. Benzoyl isopropanol is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid for industrial use.

It is available in technical and photoinitiator-grade specifications suited to industrial coating, ink, and adhesive applications. Packaging typically ranges from drum quantities to IBC.

Bulk procurement options are standard, with smaller quantities available for formulation development. This material meets rigorous industrial standards for consistency and reactivity.

name: Croscarmellose sodium
description:
Croscarmellose sodium (CAS 74811-65-7 ), also known as E468 , is a cross-linked polymer of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose used as a superdisintegrant in solid dosage form manufacturing.

It rapidly absorbs water and swells, breaking apart compressed tablets and capsule fills to release the active ingredient. In oral solid dosage manufacturing, it is incorporated into tablet formulations.

Both direct compression and wet granulation methods utilize this material to meet dissolution specifications for immediate-release products. Generic and branded pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it for rapid disintegration.

It is commonly used in standard tablets, orally disintegrating tablets, and chewable formats. Nutraceutical and dietary supplement producers use it in compressed supplement tablets where fast breakdown is required.

This ensures products meet label claims effectively. It also appears in veterinary tablet formulations where consistent disintegration performance across varying moisture conditions is a procurement requirement.

Croscarmellose sodium is supplied as a white to off-white free-flowing powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications including USP /NF, Ph. Eur. , and BP .

name: Disodium adipate
description:
Disodium adipate (CAS 7486-38-6 ), also designated E356 , is the disodium salt of adipic acid used commercially as a pH buffer and acidulant. It provides mild, controlled acidification and buffering capacity.

This chemical is utilized in food, personal care, and pharmaceutical formulations where precise pH management is required. In processed foods and beverages, it functions as a buffering agent and flavor modifier.

It contributes a clean, mild tartness without the sharpness associated with citric or phosphoric acid. Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and cleansing products to stabilize pH levels.

This stabilization is essential for skin compatibility and preservative efficacy. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering excipient in oral and topical formulations where consistent pH is critical.

Maintaining pH is vital to active ingredient stability. It also appears in specialty food applications such as gelatin desserts and powdered drink mixes where controlled acidity release is a requirement.

Disodium adipate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Food-grade material conforming to E356 specifications is the primary commercial form, with supply aligned to FCC standards.

The material also meets EU food additive standards for global distribution. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. excipient requirements is available for regulated applications.

name: Magnesium sulfate

It functions primarily as a nutrient source, processing aid, and stabilizer depending on the application sector. In agriculture, it corrects magnesium and sulfur deficiencies in soil and foliar spray programs.

This directly improves crop yield and quality for commodity growers. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a firming agent and magnesium fortification source in products such as tofu and brewing water adjustment.

It is also utilized in mineral-enriched beverages. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators incorporate it as an active ingredient in laxative preparations and electrolyte formulations for various medical uses.

In personal care, it is a functional bath soak ingredient and also used in cosmetic formulations where ionic mineral content affects texture and stability. Magnesium sulfate is supplied as anhydrous powder or crystals.

name: Alpha-Carotene
description:
Alpha-Carotene (CAS 7488-99-5 ) is a naturally occurring carotenoid pigment found primarily in carrots, pumpkin, and other orange-yellow produce. It functions as a provitamin A precursor and antioxidant across food, nutraceutical, and cosmetic applications.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used as a natural colorant to achieve orange-yellow hues in juices, dairy products, and processed foods without synthetic dyes. This makes it a preferred choice for clean-label formulations.

Nutraceutical and dietary supplement formulators incorporate it into softgels and capsules targeting provitamin A delivery. It is often used alongside beta-carotene to provide a broader carotenoid profile for consumer health products.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it is used in skin-tone products, serums, and anti-aging creams. The carotenoid antioxidant activity supports product positioning in the high-end skincare market.

Pharmaceutical researchers also use it as a reference standard or active ingredient in carotenoid-based formulations under clinical investigation. It meets rigorous testing requirements for specialized laboratory applications.

Alpha-Carotene is available as a crystalline powder or in oil suspension, with oil-dispersed forms preferred for encapsulation. Supply is offered in natural-source extracts, often standardized to defined concentrations.

Food-grade and research-grade specifications are the most commonly sourced, with documentation typically including HPLC purity data. These standards ensure the material meets the necessary safety and quality benchmarks.

name: Polyquaternium 69
description:
Polyquaternium-69 (CAS 748809-45-2 ), commercially available as Aquastyle 300 and Aquastyle 300AF, is a cationic conditioning polymer used in personal care and home care formulations.

It delivers simultaneous moisturization, rheology control, and surface modification within a single ingredient, reducing the need for multiple additives in complex chemical formulations.

In hair care, it deposits on the hair surface to improve combability, reduce frizz, and enhance conditioning performance in shampoos, conditioners, and leave-in treatments.

Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and serums where it builds a moisture-retaining film while adjusting product texture and flow for better application.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, its surface-modifying properties improve substrate wetting and aid in uniform product distribution across various surfaces.

It is also used in rinse-off formulations where substantivity to hair or skin must be maintained despite dilution, ensuring long-lasting benefits for the end user.

Polyquaternium-69 is supplied as an aqueous solution and is available in cosmetic-grade specification suitable for high-performance personal care applications.

Packaging options typically include drums and IBCs for industrial-scale procurement, ensuring efficient logistics and storage for large manufacturing facilities.

Contact us for supply of Polyquaternium 69

name: Calcium sorbate
description:
Calcium sorbate (CAS 7492-55-9 ), also designated E203 , is the calcium salt form of sorbic acid used as a broad-spectrum preservative across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications.

It inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria, extending shelf life in moisture-sensitive and pH-neutral formulations where potassium sorbate may be less suitable for the specific application.

In food manufacturing, E203 is used to preserve baked goods, dairy products, and processed foods where a lower-sodium or lower-potassium preservative profile is required for the final product.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and personal care products as a mild antimicrobial agent compatible with a range of pH levels and various chemical ingredients.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to protect topical preparations, oral suspensions, and semi-solid dosage forms against microbial contamination during storage and distribution cycles.

Its reduced hygroscopicity compared to potassium sorbate also makes it a practical choice for dry-blend and powder-based formulations, ensuring stability and ease of handling during production.

Calcium sorbate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and E203 specifications is the most commonly traded form for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to BP and Ph. Eur. standards for regulated applications, ensuring high purity and compliance with international safety requirements.

Contact us for supply of Calcium sorbate

name: Vinyl chloride
description:
Vinyl chloride (CAS 75-01-4 ), also known as vinyl chloride monomer (VCM), is the primary feedstock for polyvinyl chloride (PVC) production. It is one of the world's highest-volume thermoplastics.

It functions as a reactive monomer that undergoes polymerization to form the polymer backbone used across construction, packaging, and industrial manufacturing. The dominant use is suspension and emulsion polymerization.

This process produces PVC resin, which is then compounded into rigid profiles, pipes, fittings, and window frames. Flexible PVC applications include wire insulation, flooring, and medical tubing.

These applications rely on plasticized grades derived from VCM polymerization. Copolymerization with vinyl acetate or vinylidene chloride produces specialty resins used in coatings and adhesives.

These resins are also utilized in barrier packaging films. In industrial settings, VCM serves as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of chlorinated solvents and other downstream chlorine-based compounds.

Vinyl chloride monomer is supplied as a liquefied gas under pressure, typically in bulk quantities via pipeline, rail tanker, or pressurized ISO containers. It is a large-volume commodity chemical.

Traded at industrial/technical grade, purity specifications are generally at 99.9% or higher as standard for polymerization-grade supply. Procurement is handled through long-term offtake agreements.

These agreements or spot contracts are established with petrochemical producers. The material requires specialized handling and storage infrastructure due to its physical properties and industrial scale.

name: Ethylamine
description:
Ethylamine (CAS 75-04-7 ), also recognized by its FEMA 4236 designation in flavor applications, is a primary aliphatic amine supplied as an aqueous solution or anhydrous gas.

It functions as a reactive intermediate and pH modifier across pharmaceutical synthesis, polymer processing, and food flavoring. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a building block for active ingredients.

It acts as a neutralizing agent during API synthesis. Polymer producers use it as a curing and cross-linking agent in resin systems, including flame-retardant formulations where nitrogen content contributes to char-forming mechanisms.

In food and flavor applications, ethylamine is approved as a flavoring agent, contributing to characteristic notes in processed food systems. It also functions as a stabilizer and pH buffer in specialty chemical formulations.

Controlled basicity is required during production for these specialty chemicals. Ethylamine is commercially available as an anhydrous liquefied gas and as aqueous solutions, typically at 70% concentration.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is supplied to meet USP and BP specifications, while technical-grade product serves industrial polymer and chemical synthesis applications.

Packaging ranges from cylinders and ISO tanks for anhydrous material to drums and IBCs for aqueous grades. This ensures safe transport and storage for various industrial and laboratory requirements.

name: Acetonitrile
description:
Acetonitrile (CAS 75-05-8 ), also known commercially as ACN or methyl cyanide, is a high-purity polar aprotic solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, analytical chemistry, and industrial synthesis.

Its low viscosity and miscibility with water make it the dominant solvent choice in HPLC and LC-MS workflows globally. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, ACN serves as a reaction solvent and purification medium.

It is used for active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly in peptide synthesis and chromatographic separation at scale. Life science and biotech laboratories rely on it as the primary mobile phase solvent.

In reversed-phase HPLC, consistent purity directly impacts analytical reproducibility and regulatory compliance. Agrochemical producers use ACN as a solvent in the synthesis and formulation of pesticide intermediates.

Its solvating power supports high-yield reaction conditions. In printing and packaging, it functions as a solvent carrier in specialty ink and dye formulations requiring fast evaporation and clean substrate adhesion.

Acetonitrile is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. HPLC-grade and LC-MS-grade are the most commercially demanded specifications for high-end laboratory use.

Technical-grade is available for industrial synthesis applications. Gradient-grade variants meeting stringent UV absorbance cutoffs are standard for analytical supply channels and quality control.

name: Acetaldehyde
description:
Acetaldehyde (CAS 75-07-0 ), also known as ethyl aldehyde and acetic aldehyde, is a short-chain aldehyde used primarily as a chemical intermediate and flavoring agent across food, fragrance, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Its reactive carbonyl group makes it a building block for synthesizing a broad range of downstream compounds at industrial scale. In food and beverage production, this compound contributes fresh, fruity, and ethereal notes.

Known by FEMA 2003 , it is essential to flavor formulations, particularly in dairy, fruit, and alcoholic beverage profiles. Fragrance manufacturers use it as an intermediate in aldehyde-based perfume accords.

It supports the characteristic clean, soapy top notes found in classic fine fragrance compositions. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it functions as a precursor in the production of acetic acid and pyridine derivatives.

The material is also used for other active pharmaceutical intermediates. It sees use as a preservative intermediate in certain industrial applications where controlled antimicrobial action is required during processing.

The product is supplied as a liquefied, low-boiling liquid, typically handled and shipped under refrigeration or pressure. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is available for flavor applications.

Technical-grade material is supplied for industrial synthesis and chemical manufacturing use. This ensures high purity and reliability for large-scale production requirements across various global industrial sectors.

name: Dichloromethane
description:
Dichloromethane (CAS 75-09-2 ), also known as DCM, R 30, and Salesthin, is a fast-evaporating chlorinated solvent used across pharmaceutical manufacturing, industrial processing, and polymer applications.

Its high solvency power and low boiling point make it a preferred extraction and process solvent where rapid solvent removal is commercially critical for high-volume production lines.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DCM serves as a process solvent for active ingredient extraction, recrystallization, and film coating of tablets and capsules to ensure product stability.

Printing and packaging operations use it in solvent-based adhesives and as a component in paint strippers for equipment maintenance and surface preparation across various industrial facilities.

Polymer processors rely on it to dissolve and weld polycarbonate and other engineering plastics, enabling precision bonding in fabricated components for the automotive and electronics sectors.

It also functions as a blowing agent carrier and processing aid in certain foam and polymer formulations, providing consistent results in specialized manufacturing and molding processes.

Dichloromethane is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications.

These grades are suitable for regulated manufacturing environments. Technical-grade DCM remains the standard supply form for general industrial solvent and processing applications worldwide.

name: Formamide
description:
Formamide (CAS 75-12-7 ) is a primary amide solvent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, electronics manufacturing, and specialty chemical processing. It functions both as a high-polarity solvent and as a chemical intermediate in the production of active ingredients and industrial compounds.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, this compound serves as a reaction medium and building block for synthesizing purines, vitamins, and other heterocyclic compounds. The electronics industry relies on it as a solvent in the production of electrolytic capacitors.

It is also utilized as a processing aid for certain polymer films. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a softening and conditioning agent, improving flexibility and workability of treated materials during the manufacturing process.

Agrochemical producers also use this substance as an intermediate in the synthesis of pesticide and herbicide active substances. It is supplied as a clear, water-miscible liquid in standard bulk and drummed quantities for industrial use.

Technical grade is the most common commercial specification, with high-purity grades available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements. Suppliers typically offer material with defined purity thresholds, commonly 99% and above.

The material is supported by relevant analytical documentation for regulated industries. This ensures that the product meets the necessary safety and quality benchmarks required for complex chemical synthesis and large-scale industrial applications.

name: Carbon disulfide
description:
Carbon disulfide (CAS 75-15-0 ), also known as CS2 and carbon bisulphide, is a high-purity industrial solvent used across chemical manufacturing and analytical processes.

Its exceptional solvating power for sulfur, phosphorus, and halogen compounds makes it a preferred extraction and reaction medium in specialty chemical production.

In agrochemical manufacturing, CS2 serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of xanthates, dithiocarbamates, and thiuram-based fungicides and accelerators.

Flavor and fragrance laboratories use it as a solvent for GC/MS headspace analysis and aroma extraction, enabling accurate identification of trace volatile compounds in food matrices.

In viscose rayon and cellophane production, it reacts with cellulose and sodium hydroxide to form cellulose xanthate, the basis of the wet-spinning process.

Rubber processing operations also rely on CS2 as a solvent for sulfur compounds and accelerator blends during compounding and quality control testing.

Carbon disulfide is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial uses.

High-purity and reagent-grade specifications are available for analytical applications. Buyers should confirm purity thresholds and stabilizer content before purchase.

name: Ethylene oxide
description:
Ethylene oxide (CAS 75-21-8 ), also known by the abbreviation ETO and the chemical name Oxirane, is a high-volume reactive monomer and sterilizing agent central to multiple industrial supply chains.

It functions as a building block for polymerization reactions, a sterilant for heat-sensitive materials, and a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of downstream derivatives for various sectors.

In plastics and polymers, ETO is the primary monomer for producing ethylene glycols, polyethylene glycols, and ethoxylated surfactants used across detergent, textile, and personal care manufacturing.

Pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers rely on ETO gas sterilization to process single-use equipment, packaging, and instruments that cannot withstand heat or radiation during production.

In agriculture, ETO serves as a fumigant and sterilant for spices, herbs, and certain grain products where microbial load control is required before final processing and distribution to consumers.

Biotechnology and life sciences operations use ETO to sterilize laboratory consumables and culture media components at scale, ensuring the integrity of sensitive research and development environments.

Ethylene oxide is supplied as a liquefied gas under pressure, typically in cylinders, drums, or bulk tank quantities. It is available in technical and pharmaceutical grades for diverse needs.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meets USP and EP specifications for sterilization applications. Grade selection is a critical procurement decision given the regulatory requirements tied to each sector.

name: Bromoform
description:
Bromoform (CAS 75-25-2 ), also known as methyl tribromide, is a dense, halogenated solvent used across industrial processing and specialty chemical manufacturing. Its high bromine content makes it effective as a flame retardant intermediate.

It is also utilized as a heavy-medium separation agent in mineral and materials processing. In textile and leather processing, it functions as a solvent and density separation medium for fiber and material grading.

Building and construction applications utilize it as a flame retardant component, where its bromine loading contributes to fire suppression in treated materials. This makes it a vital component for safety standards.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing uses this chemical as a synthesis intermediate and, in controlled formulations, as a preservative or biocide active. It is essential for various specialized chemical reactions.

Paper production processes have employed it for foam control and as a processing solvent where halogenated media are specified. It ensures consistency and quality during the manufacturing of paper products.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or bulk containers suited to halogenated solvent handling requirements. Technical grade is the most common commercial specification for these applications.

Purity levels are generally at 99% or higher for industrial and synthesis applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP or equivalent specifications for regulated manufacturing use.

name: 2-bromopropane
description:
2-Bromopropane (CAS 75-26-3 ), commercially known as isopropyl bromide, is an alkyl halide used as a reactive intermediate in organic synthesis and as a specialty solvent in industrial processing.

It functions primarily as an alkylating agent, introducing isopropyl groups into target molecules across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and polymer manufacturing workflows. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a key building block.

This chemical is essential for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates where selective isopropylation is required. Agrochemical manufacturers use it in the synthesis of herbicide and pesticide compounds.

Controlled alkylation determines the efficacy profile of the final active ingredient in these agricultural applications. In plastics and polymer chemistry, it contributes to flame retardant formulations and specialty polymer modifications.

Textile and leather processing operations use isopropyl bromide as a solvent and chemical intermediate in dyeing auxiliaries and pigment-related formulations. It is supplied as a clear liquid, typically available in technical and reagent grades.

These grades meet the purity requirements of industrial and synthesis-scale buyers. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical intermediate applications.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and stabilizer content when sourcing for sensitive synthesis processes. This ensures the material meets the specific demands of high-precision chemical manufacturing and laboratory research.

name: Isobutane
description:
Isobutane (CAS 75-28-5 ), also recognized in refrigerant markets as R600a and in food applications as E943b , is a liquefied hydrocarbon gas used as a propellant and solvent carrier.

Its low boiling point and clean vaporization profile make it a practical choice where residue-free delivery or efficient heat transfer is required across multiple industrial sectors.

In food and aerosol manufacturing, E943b functions as a propellant in spray products, delivering controlled pressure without leaving residue in the final product for consumers.

Refrigeration systems, particularly domestic appliances and light commercial units, use R600a as a natural refrigerant with low global warming potential as a preferred alternative to synthetic HFCs.

In the oil and gas sector, isobutane is used as a blending component in alkylation processes to produce high-octane gasoline fractions for the automotive and energy industries.

Aerosol personal care and household product manufacturers also rely on it as a solvent carrier to dissolve and uniformly disperse active ingredients in various formulations.

Isobutane is supplied as a liquefied gas in pressurized cylinders, ISO tanks, and bulk transport vessels. Refrigerant-grade R600a is available to high purity specifications.

Food-grade supply conforming to E943b specifications is available for aerosol and propellant use in regulated food contact applications and meets necessary safety requirements.

name: Isopropylamine
description:
Isopropylamine (CAS 75-31-0 ), also known as MIPA, is a primary aliphatic amine used as a reactive building block and functional intermediate across chemical manufacturing. It acts as a curing agent, pH modifier, and flavoring precursor depending on the end application.

In coatings and adhesives, MIPA functions as a crosslinking agent and curing catalyst, improving film hardness and adhesion in epoxy and polyurethane systems. Polymer manufacturers incorporate it into flame retardant formulations.

These formulations contribute nitrogen-based char-forming chemistry to reduce combustibility in finished plastics. In food and flavor production, it is approved under FEMA 4238 as a flavoring agent for industrial use.

It is used at trace levels to develop characteristic taste profiles in processed food applications. It also serves as an intermediate in synthesizing agrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, and rubber accelerators.

This versatility makes it a recurring procurement target across multiple chemical supply chains. Isopropylamine is supplied as a low-boiling liquid, typically in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels commonly at 99% or higher. Food-grade supply aligned with FEMA-listed status is available from select manufacturers for flavor industry use.

name: Acetyl chloride
description:
Acetyl chloride (CAS 75-36-5 ), also known as acetic chloride, is a highly reactive acylating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing. It introduces acetyl groups into organic molecules, enabling the construction of active pharmaceutical ingredients and chemical intermediates at scale.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, acetyl chloride acetylates amines, alcohols, and phenols to produce APIs and protected intermediates where precise reaction control is critical. Cosmetic ingredient synthesis relies on it to produce acetylated derivatives.

Fatty alcohols and other actives are modified to improve stability or skin-feel performance in finished formulations. It also functions as a catalyst activator and reagent in the preparation of anhydrides and other acylating agents used upstream in fine chemical production.

Contract manufacturers and formulators processing complex multi-step syntheses source it as a key reagent where high purity and consistent reactivity directly affect yield. This ensures that the final chemical products meet rigorous industrial requirements.

Acetyl chloride is supplied as a colorless fuming liquid, typically in drums or ISO tanks suited for moisture-sensitive materials. Technical and high-purity reagent grades are the standard commercial offerings for industrial applications.

Purity specifications are commonly at 98% and above to ensure optimal performance in sensitive reactions. Packaging configurations are selected to maintain anhydrous conditions throughout storage and transport to prevent degradation.

name: Vinylidene fluoride
description:
Vinylidene fluoride (CAS 75-38-7 ), also known as Halocarbon 1132A, is a gaseous fluorinated monomer used as the primary building block in the production of high-performance fluoropolymers.

It is the key feedstock for polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and a range of fluoroelastomers that require chemical resistance, thermal stability, and durability in demanding environments.

In the plastics and polymer industry, it is polymerized to produce PVDF resin, which is processed into pipes, films, coatings, and membranes for chemical processing and semiconductor applications.

Copolymerization with hexafluoropropylene yields fluoroelastomers such as FKM and Viton-type compounds, used in seals, gaskets, and O-rings for automotive and aerospace assemblies.

Battery manufacturers use PVDF derived from this monomer as a binder material in lithium-ion electrode fabrication. In the rubber and specialty compounding sector, it contributes to fluoroelastomer compounds.

These compounds are engineered for fuel system components and high-temperature hose applications. Vinylidene fluoride is supplied as a liquefied compressed gas in cylinders or bulk containers.

This delivery method is consistent with its handling requirements as a low-boiling gaseous monomer. It is available in polymerization-grade purity, with specifications controlled for inhibitor content.

Moisture levels are also strictly monitored, as they are critical to downstream fluoropolymer production. Our material meets rigorous industrial quality standards for consistent chemical manufacturing.

name: Trimethylamine
description:
Trimethylamine (CAS 75-50-3 ), commonly abbreviated as TMA, is a tertiary amine supplied primarily in anhydrous form for industrial and specialty chemical applications. It functions as a key intermediate and reactant across pharmaceutical synthesis and food-grade flavoring.

Its strong fishy odor profile is both a target compound and a process marker in various manufacturing sectors. FEMA 3241 status confirms its recognized standing as a flavoring substance in regulated food applications.

In food and flavor manufacturing, TMA is used as a reference and active flavoring agent in seafood-type flavor systems. In these environments, its characteristic odor must be precisely controlled or replicated for consistency.

Pharmaceutical producers use it as a building block in the synthesis of choline salts and quaternary ammonium compounds. Both of these appear frequently in finished drug formulations and nutritional supplements.

It also functions as a catalyst and intermediate in the production of ion exchange resins and specialty chemicals. In preservation-related applications, TMA derivatives contribute to biocidal formulations targeting microbial control.

Trimethylamine is supplied as a compressed anhydrous gas or as aqueous solution, typically at concentrations of 30 to 45 percent in water. Food-grade and technical-grade designations are the most commonly available specifications.

Packaging ranges from pressurized cylinders for anhydrous supply to drum quantities for aqueous grades. This ensures safe handling and transport according to the specific requirements of the industrial or laboratory facility.

name: Nitromethane
description:
Nitromethane (CAS 75-52-5 ), also referenced in shorthand as MeNO2, is a high-polarity solvent and reactive chemical intermediate used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty fuel applications.

Its ability to dissolve a broad range of organic and inorganic compounds makes it a preferred solvent where conventional options fall short in industrial processes and chemical manufacturing.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a reaction solvent and building block in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly where nitroalkane chemistry is required.

The polymer and plastics industry uses it as a solvent for cellulose esters and as a reactive monomer precursor in specialty formulations for various high-performance materials and coatings.

In motorsport, aerospace, and defense sectors, high-purity nitromethane is a primary fuel component and oxidizer in high-performance combustion systems and specialized propulsion technologies.

Metalworking and lubricant formulators use it as a solvent carrier for cleaning agents and surface treatment preparations to ensure high-quality finishes and effective industrial maintenance.

Nitromethane is supplied as a clear liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk tanker quantities. Technical grade is the most common supply form, with high-purity grades available for specialty synthesis.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications, typically 95% to 99%+, based on end-use requirements, as fuel-grade and synthesis-grade material are not always interchangeable for all applications.

name: Propylene oxide
description:
Propylene oxide (CAS 75-56-9 ), commonly abbreviated as PO, is a reactive epoxide monomer and industrial solvent used across polymer manufacturing, sterilization, and chemical synthesis.

Methyl oxirane is the form referenced in many technical and regulatory contexts as a distinct search term. Its primary commercial role is as a building block for polyols and propylene glycols.

PO is the key feedstock for polyether polyols used in polyurethane foam production. This covers rigid insulation panels, flexible seating, and various automotive interiors for industrial manufacturing.

In food and pharmaceutical processing, it functions as a fumigant and sterilizing agent for spices and cocoa. It is also used for medical equipment where heat sterilization is not viable.

Propylene glycol, produced by hydration of PO, feeds into food-grade humectants and cosmetic carriers. It is also a primary component in modern antifreeze formulations and industrial coolants.

In biotechnology, PO is used as a fixative and dehydration agent in electron microscopy sample preparation. It is supplied as a liquid in bulk quantities, typically via ISO tank containers.

Standard commercial grades include polymer-grade and technical-grade specifications. Purity levels are commonly at 99.5% or higher for polyol synthesis applications and chemical manufacturing.

Buyers sourcing for food or pharmaceutical sterilization applications should confirm compliance with regional regulatory standards. Proper handling is required due to its low boiling point and volatility.

name: Tetramethylammonium chloride
description:
Tetramethylammonium chloride ( CAS 75-57-0 ), commonly abbreviated as TMAC, is a quaternary ammonium salt used as a phase-transfer catalyst and reagent across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and polymer manufacturing sectors.

It enables reactions between compounds in incompatible phases, improving yields and reducing processing complexity in synthetic workflows. In pharmaceutical synthesis, TMAC acts as a phase-transfer catalyst to facilitate alkylation.

It supports nucleophilic substitution reactions and the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients. Biotechnology applications include its use in DNA hybridization assays, where it equalizes melting temperatures.

This process stabilizes AT- and GC-rich sequences to improve probe specificity. In polymer and plastics manufacturing, TMAC functions as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in polymerization processes.

Common industrial uses include the production of epoxy resins and specialty polymers. It also serves as a nitrogen source and templating agent in the synthesis of zeolites and other porous materials.

These materials are essential for various catalytic applications. Tetramethylammonium chloride is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, available in technical grade for industrial catalysis.

High-purity grades are also available, meeting reagent or analytical specifications for pharmaceutical and life sciences use. Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities to bulk industrial supply.

name: Tetramethylammonium hydroxide
description:
Tetramethylammonium hydroxide ( CAS 75-59-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TMAH, is a quaternary ammonium base used across semiconductor manufacturing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and analytical chemistry.

It functions as a strong, metal-free alkali, making it the preferred choice where inorganic base contamination is unacceptable. In semiconductor and flat-panel display manufacturing, it is the standard developer.

TMAH is used for photoresist stripping and patterning, where its metal-free profile prevents ionic contamination of wafer surfaces. Pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers use it as a catalyst and pH-adjusting agent.

It is ideal for synthesis steps that require a clean base without introducing sodium or potassium ions. In analytical laboratories, it is used as a quaternizing agent for GC sample preparation.

This enables direct injection of fatty acid and biological samples. It also supports etching of silicon wafers in MEMS fabrication, where precise anisotropic etch rates are critical to device geometry.

TMAH is supplied as aqueous solution, most commonly at 25% concentration, with lower concentrations such as 5% and 10% available for specific process requirements. Pentahydrate solid form is also available.

Electronic-grade and reagent-grade specifications are the primary market grades. Electronic-grade material is held to strict metal impurity limits suited for semiconductor process environments.

name: tert-butylamine
description:
Tert-butylamine (CAS 75-64-9 ), also known as t-Butylamine or Erbumine, is a primary aliphatic amine used as a chemical building block and pH-regulating agent across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and industrial manufacturing processes.

Its role as a reactive intermediate drives demand from formulators and synthesis chemists sourcing for multi-step production chains. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it forms salt complexes with active ingredients.

Perindopril erbumine is a prominent example where it directly influences the final drug's stability and bioavailability profile. Agrochemical producers use it as a key intermediate in the synthesis of herbicides and fungicides.

It is particularly useful for sulfonamide-class compounds. In polymer chemistry, it functions as a polymerization initiator and chain-transfer agent, influencing molecular weight distribution in specialty plastics production.

Water treatment formulators incorporate it for pH buffering in process water systems where controlled alkalinity is required. The chemical is supplied as a liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk isotanks.

This reflects its low boiling point and specific handling requirements. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for pharmaceutical intermediate applications.

Buyers sourcing for regulated end uses typically require documentation supporting GMP -aligned quality standards. This ensures the material meets the rigorous demands of global chemical supply chains.

name: tert-Butanol
description:
tert-Butanol (CAS 75-65-0 ), also known as tert-butyl alcohol or TBA, is a tertiary alcohol used across chemical manufacturing, personal care, and food-related applications.

It functions primarily as a solvent, process aid, and flavoring agent depending on the grade and end-use sector. In flavor manufacturing, TBA acts as a carrier solvent for flavor concentrates.

It is used as a synthetic flavoring substance in food products at controlled levels. Personal care formulators use it as a solvent and viscosity modifier in aerosol systems and deodorants.

It is also utilized in topical formulations where controlled evaporation is required. In polymer and chemical synthesis, it serves as a reaction solvent and intermediate in producing isobutylene.

It also functions as a denaturant for ethanol in industrial and cosmetic applications, offering a recognized alternative to less palatable denaturants for various manufacturing processes.

tert-Butanol is supplied as a liquid above its melting point or as a crystalline solid at ambient temperatures. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade.

Available quality standards include USP and BP , alongside technical-grade for industrial processing. Bulk liquid supply in drums and ISO tanks is standard for high-volume buyers.

name: 2-methylpropane-2-thiol
description:
2-Methylpropane-2-thiol (CAS 75-66-1 ), commercially known as tert-butyl mercaptan, is a synthetic sulfur compound used as a potent flavoring agent and odorant across food and industrial applications.

Its intense, characteristic sulfurous odor makes it effective at trace concentrations, supporting both flavor creation and gas detection functions. In the flavor and fragrance industry, it is used at very low levels.

This compound helps replicate roasted, savory, and sulfurous top notes in processed food formulations. Natural gas and LPG suppliers use it as an odorant additive, blending it into fuel gas streams for safety.

This provides a detectable warning odor for leak detection compliance. Petroleum refiners and petrochemical processors also use it as a reference compound and intermediate in sulfur chemistry research and calibration standards.

In beverage and food flavor houses, it contributes to coffee, meat, and onion flavor profiles where authentic sulfur character is required. It is available in food-grade quality meeting FEMA standards.

The product is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, typically in small packaging formats suited to flavor and odorant applications. It also meets various flavor industry purity standards for global use.

Technical grade options are available for gas odorant and industrial use. Packaging ranges from laboratory-scale quantities up to drum volumes for industrial odorant blending operations and large scale manufacturing.

name: Dichlorodifluoromethane
description:
Dichlorodifluoromethane (CAS 75-71-8 ), commercially known as R-12 or Refrigerant 12, is a chlorofluorocarbon compound used historically as a refrigerant, aerosol propellant, and solvent carrier across industrial and specialty applications.

Regulatory restrictions under the Montreal Protocol have significantly shaped its current supply landscape, making sourcing and compliance verification critical considerations for buyers in the global chemical market.

In aerospace and defense, R-12 has been used as a solvent carrier in specialized cleaning and surface preparation processes where legacy equipment specifications require CFC-based formulations for operational integrity.

Automotive applications center on legacy vehicle air conditioning systems, where R-12 remains the original-spec refrigerant for pre-1994 vehicles that have not been retrofitted to alternative refrigerants or modern cooling systems.

Controlled quantities are also sourced for calibration equipment, reference standards, and maintenance of older refrigeration systems still operating under original design parameters to ensure continued functionality.

Procurement is typically driven by service and maintenance demand rather than new manufacturing integration. Dichlorodifluoromethane is supplied as a liquefied gas under pressure, available in cylinders and drums sized for industrial use.

Supply is subject to national and regional regulatory controls, with recovered and reclaimed grades being the predominant market form in most jurisdictions. Technical-grade material is the standard specification encountered.

Compliance with environmental protocols is essential for all transactions involving this substance. Buyers must ensure that all documentation and handling procedures meet the rigorous standards required for controlled chemical substances.

name: Carbon tetrafluoride
description:
Carbon tetrafluoride (CAS 75-73-0 ), also supplied under the designations PFC-14 and Freon 14, is a fluorinated gas used primarily as a plasma etching and cleaning agent in semiconductor and electronics manufacturing.

Its chemical stability under extreme conditions makes it a process gas of choice where precision and consistency are non-negotiable. In semiconductor fabrication, it functions as a plasma etch gas for silicon dioxide and silicon nitride layers.

This gas enables precise patterning in integrated circuit production. Electronics manufacturers also use it for chamber cleaning in CVD equipment, removing deposited residues without damaging sensitive components.

In aerospace and defense applications, it serves as a reference gas and dielectric medium in specialized testing and calibration environments. Cryogenic and atmospheric research programs source it as a tracer gas.

This is due to its long atmospheric residence time and measurable background concentration. The product is supplied as a compressed gas in high-pressure cylinders and tube trailers, with purity grades ranging from industrial to high-purity.

Electronic-grade specifications, typically 99.9% purity and above, are standard requirements for semiconductor process applications. Specialty gas suppliers offer certified reference mixtures for calibration and analytical use.

name: Methanesulfonic acid
description:
Methanesulfonic acid (CAS 75-75-2 ), commonly abbreviated as MSA, is a strong organic acid used across industrial and specialty chemical sectors. Unlike mineral acids, it combines high acidity with biodegradability and low oxidizing potential.

This unique profile makes it a preferred acid catalyst and pH-regulating agent in demanding process environments. In pharmaceuticals, MSA is used to form mesylate salts of active pharmaceutical ingredients, improving solubility and bioavailability.

These salts are essential for solid dosage formulations. Electronics manufacturers rely on it as an electrolyte component in tin, lead, and copper electroplating baths, where it delivers stable, high-purity metal deposits.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a catalyst in UV-curable coatings and as an etching agent for circuit board production. Water treatment operations use MSA for pH adjustment and as a descaling agent.

Its biodegradable profile offers a regulatory advantage over hydrochloric or sulfuric acid. Methanesulfonic acid is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid, typically at 70% and 99%+ (anhydrous) concentrations.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet USP and Ph. Eur. specifications. Technical-grade product serves industrial electroplating and catalysis applications, ensuring high performance across sectors.

Bulk supply is standard in IBC containers and drummed quantities to meet global logistics needs. This versatile chemical remains a cornerstone for modern industrial synthesis and high-tech manufacturing processes.

name: Methyltrichlorosilane
description:
Methyltrichlorosilane (CAS 75-79-6 ), commonly abbreviated as MTS, is a reactive chlorosilane monomer used as a fundamental building block in silicone polymer synthesis and surface treatment chemistry.

It functions as a trifunctional crosslinker and surface modifier, enabling the formation of durable siloxane networks across a range of industrial processes. In silicone manufacturing, MTS serves as a key precursor.

It is used for producing methylsilicone resins, fluids, and elastomers through controlled hydrolysis and condensation reactions. The electronics industry relies on it for chemical vapor deposition of silicon carbide coatings.

It also acts as a surface passivation agent on semiconductor substrates. In building and construction, it is applied to mineral substrates such as concrete, stone, and masonry to impart water repellency.

This is achieved through covalent bonding to surface hydroxyl groups. Textile and paper processing operations use MTS-derived treatments to achieve release coatings and hydrophobic finishes on fiber and sheet materials.

Methyltrichlorosilane is supplied as a colorless, fuming liquid in standard industrial packaging including drums and ISO tank containers for bulk procurement. It is available in technical grade for synthesis.

Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher as standard for industrial applications. Buyers should confirm moisture-controlled packaging requirements, as the product reacts with atmospheric humidity during storage.
