It functions primarily as a stabilizer, curing co-agent, and flavoring ingredient depending on the application sector. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, TAA acts as a stabilizer and cross-linking agent.

In peroxide-cured systems, it improves process consistency and end-product integrity. Food and beverage producers use it as a flavoring ingredient, where it contributes characteristic notes to finished products at regulated usage levels.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a solvent and co-solvent that aids ingredient compatibility and helps control viscosity in topical products. It also serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of tert-amyl methyl ether.

name: tert-butyl hydroperoxide
description:
Tert-butyl hydroperoxide (CAS 75-91-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TBHP, is an organic peroxide used industrially as a radical source for initiating polymerization and driving oxidation reactions.

Its controlled reactivity makes it a preferred alternative to inorganic peroxides where selectivity and handling convenience matter. In plastics manufacturing, it initiates free-radical polymerization and crosslinking.

This chemical is essential in the production of acrylics, polyethylene, and rubber compounds. Lubricant formulators use it as an oxidation catalyst to modify base oils and synthesize sulfoxide or epoxide intermediates.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it serves as a reference oxidant in cellular stress assays and enzyme activity studies. It is used where reproducible oxidative challenge is required for research.

It also functions as a bleaching agent in textile and pulp processing. This application is ideal where peroxide-based whitening must be applied under mild conditions to protect the substrate integrity.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 70% concentration. Anhydrous and higher-concentration grades are available for specific industrial applications requiring low water content.

Technical grade is the standard for polymer and lubricant applications. Handling and storage specifications vary by concentration, and buyers typically source it in drums or IBC containers for bulk use.

name: Acetylglucosamine
description:
Acetylglucosamine (CAS 7512-17-6 ), commonly abbreviated as GlcNAc, is an amino sugar derivative used as a functional ingredient across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and nutritional applications. It supports skin hydration and hyaluronic acid synthesis.

In skincare formulations, GlcNAc is incorporated into serums, moisturizers, and brightening products where it supports hyaluronic acid precursor activity and helps address uneven skin tone. It is a versatile additive for modern beauty products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a building block in research-grade and nutraceutical preparations targeting joint health and mucosal support. It plays a critical role in cellular signaling pathways relevant to formulation performance.

In functional food and dietary supplement production, it is formulated into capsules and powders marketed for connective tissue and gut lining support. This makes it a staple for manufacturers focusing on holistic wellness.

Cosmetic formulators also use it as a humectant in combination with peptide systems, where its moisture-binding capacity contributes to product stability and skin feel. It integrates seamlessly into various aqueous systems.

Acetylglucosamine is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP standards where required for compliance.

Bulk quantities are typically offered alongside smaller packaging options suited to formulation development and QA sampling. This ensures that both large-scale production and laboratory testing needs are met efficiently.

Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and purity for all industrial applications. We provide comprehensive documentation to support regulatory requirements and technical specifications for global distribution.

name: Acrylamide-acrylamidopropyltrimethylammonium chloride copolymer
description:
Acrylamide-acrylamidopropyltrimethylammonium chloride copolymer (CAS 75150-29-7 ), also marketed as Praestol 611, is a cationic polyacrylamide used across water treatment and industrial processing. It functions as a flocculant and rheology modifier, enabling efficient separation of suspended solids.

This chemical enables superior viscosity control in aqueous systems. In municipal and industrial water treatment, it destabilizes negatively charged colloidal particles, accelerating sedimentation and improving clarification in effluent and sludge dewatering operations.

Paper manufacturers apply it as a retention and drainage aid, helping fine particles and fillers bind to fiber during sheet formation. This process is essential for maintaining high production speeds and ensuring consistent paper quality across various grades.

In textile and leather processing, it supports wastewater remediation by aggregating dye particles and suspended matter before discharge. This helps facilities meet environmental regulations and reduces the overall chemical load in industrial waste streams.

Personal care formulators incorporate it under the INCI designation Acrylamidopropyltrimonium Chloride/Acrylamide to build viscosity. It is used to improve conditioning performance in both rinse-off and leave-on products for hair and skin care.

This copolymer is supplied as a dry powder or as an aqueous emulsion, with dry forms typically preferred for large-scale water treatment dosing. Molecular weight and charge density vary across grades to match specific application requirements.

Buyers should specify these parameters to ensure optimal performance in their systems. Technical and industrial grades are standard; personal care grades are available with documentation supporting cosmetic compliance for global markets.

name: Riboflavin tetrabutyrate
description:
Riboflavin tetrabutyrate (CAS 752-56-7 ), also known as Vitamin B2 tetrabutyrate and marketed under the trade name Hibon, is a lipophilic ester form of riboflavin developed to overcome poor oil solubility.

This specialized compound addresses the light sensitivity that limits standard riboflavin in certain delivery systems. Its fat-soluble profile makes it suitable for formulations where conventional riboflavin cannot be effectively incorporated.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is used in oil-based capsule formulations and lipid delivery systems. This is particularly useful where enhanced bioavailability of B2 is a primary formulation objective.

Feed premix producers use it to fortify fat-soluble vitamin blends for livestock and aquaculture. It remains stable through pelleting and extrusion processes, ensuring nutritional integrity in the final feed product.

In food applications, it functions as an antioxidant and stabilizer in fat-containing matrices such as edible oils and fat-based spreads. Cosmetic formulators also incorporate it into oil-phase systems.

The product provides a stable, non-discoloring B2 source for topical applications. Riboflavin tetrabutyrate is supplied as a yellow to orange powder or crystalline solid for various industrial uses.

It is available in pharmaceutical-grade and feed-grade specifications, with purity typically confirmed against reference standards by HPLC. Packaging ranges from small quantities for R&D use to bulk quantities.

Industrial formulation requirements are met through various supply options. Quality is maintained through rigorous testing to ensure the material meets the necessary performance criteria for global distribution.

name: n-methylmorpholine n-oxide
description:
N-Methylmorpholine N-oxide (CAS 7529-22-8 ), commonly known as NMO, is a stable, recyclable oxidant used across chemical synthesis and industrial processing. It functions primarily as a co-oxidant in catalytic oxidation reactions.

The compound also serves as a cellulose dissolution agent in fiber production. In textile and pulp manufacturing, NMO is the solvent system of choice for dissolving cellulose in the Lyocell process.

This application enables the production of fibers such as Tencel. Synthetic chemists rely on NMO as the stoichiometric co-oxidant in Sharpless dihydroxylation and Ley oxidation protocols.

In these processes, it regenerates osmium tetroxide or TPAP catalysts in situ. In biotechnology and life sciences, NMO supports selective oxidation steps in the synthesis of complex molecules.

This includes the production of carbohydrates and pharmaceutical intermediates. Water treatment applications utilize NMO-based oxidation systems for degrading recalcitrant organic compounds.

NMO is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 50% concentration, and as a monohydrate powder for applications requiring precise stoichiometry for chemical reactions.

Technical and reagent grades are available to serve both industrial-scale fiber processing and laboratory synthesis demands. Packaging ranges from small quantities to bulk drum supply.

These options support research use as well as continuous manufacturing operations. Our product meets rigorous industry requirements for purity and performance in diverse chemical environments.

name: Isobornyl methacrylate
description:
Isobornyl methacrylate (CAS 7534-94-3 ), commercially known as IBOMA and supplied under trade names such as Ageflex IBOMA and NK Ester IB, is a specialty acrylic monomer used to modify the performance characteristics of UV-curable and thermoplastic polymer systems.

Its primary function is to adjust hardness, adhesion, and shrinkage in polymerizable formulations without compromising cure speed or film integrity. In UV-curable inks and coatings for printing and packaging, IBOMA acts as a reactive diluent that reduces viscosity.

This monomer contributes to a hard, scratch-resistant surface after cure. Nail gel and UV-cured cosmetic coating formulators incorporate it to achieve durable, high-gloss films with controlled flexibility. In adhesive and sealant systems, it improves substrate adhesion.

It also raises the glass transition temperature of the cured polymer. Optical and electronic component manufacturers use IBOMA in specialty resins where dimensional stability and low shrinkage during polymerization are critical for high-performance applications.

Isobornyl methacrylate is supplied as a clear to slightly yellow liquid, typically with an inhibitor added for storage stability. Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and specialty coating applications with high purity levels.

Purity specifications are commonly at 98% or higher for most industrial uses. It is offered in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker supply available from major producers to meet large-scale manufacturing requirements across various sectors.

name: Polyquaternium-1
description:
Polyquaternium-1 (CAS 75345-27-6 ), also known as Polidronium chloride, is a cationic polymer used across personal care, water treatment, and industrial applications. It functions primarily as a preservative, conditioning agent, and surface modifier.

The compound delivers antimicrobial activity and substantivity to treated substrates. In ophthalmic and contact lens care formulations, it acts as a preservative at low concentrations, offering broad-spectrum antimicrobial efficacy with good ocular tolerance.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos and conditioners where it deposits onto hair and skin to improve texture and reduce static. In water treatment, it supports microbial control and aids in surface modification of process equipment.

Textile and leather processors use it to modify fiber surfaces, improving dye uptake and imparting antistatic or softening effects to finished goods. This versatility makes it a staple in various chemical manufacturing sectors.

Polyquaternium-1 is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations varying by grade and supplier specification. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available to meet specific requirements.

Buyers should confirm active polymer content, counterion specification, and viscosity range when evaluating lots for formulation compatibility. Ensuring these parameters meet your internal standards is critical for consistent product performance.

name: Diethyl toluene diamine
description:
Diethyl toluene diamine ( CAS 75389-89-8 ), commonly known as DETDA, is an aromatic diamine curative used to crosslink epoxy resins and polyurethane systems. It controls cure rate, pot life, and final mechanical performance in demanding polymer applications.

In high-performance epoxy formulations, DETDA acts as a chain extender and crosslinker, producing cured systems with elevated heat resistance and chemical durability suited for industrial coatings and structural composites.

Polyurethane elastomers, particularly cast and RIM systems, rely on DETDA to achieve tight hardness control and improved abrasion resistance in end products such as rollers, wheels, and seals.

Protective coatings for pipelines, marine structures, and industrial flooring use DETDA-cured epoxies where long-term chemical exposure resistance is a primary specification requirement.

In adhesive and sealant formulations, it supports fast-developing green strength while maintaining flexibility across a broad service temperature range for various industrial environments.

DETDA is supplied as an amber to light yellow liquid. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity specifications typically at 98% or higher depending on the specific supplier.

Packaging options generally include drums and IBC containers to suit both development-scale and bulk production requirements, ensuring safe handling and transport for all global logistics needs.

name: Lithium bromide
description:
Lithium bromide (CAS 7550-35-8 ), commonly abbreviated as LiBr, is an inorganic salt used across industrial refrigeration, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and life sciences. It functions primarily as an absorption refrigerant and a desiccant in gas drying systems.

In commercial HVAC and industrial cooling, LiBr serves as the absorbent fluid in absorption chiller systems. Its strong affinity for water vapor drives the refrigeration cycle without mechanical compression, making it a reagent in specialized chemical synthesis.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reagent in synthesis and as a buffering agent in select formulations requiring controlled ionic conditions. In biotechnology and life sciences, LiBr solutions are used to precipitate and purify RNA.

These solutions enable downstream molecular biology workflows and critical research processes. Water treatment operations apply it in specific biocide and pH-regulation contexts where lithium-based chemistry is specified for industrial systems.

Lithium bromide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or in concentrated aqueous solution. Solution concentrations are commonly at 55% for absorption chiller applications to ensure maximum efficiency in large-scale cooling operations.

Standard grades include technical, pharmaceutical ( USP ), and high-purity laboratory grades to meet the distinct requirements of industrial, compendial, and research procurement. This ensures compliance with global manufacturing standards.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial refrigeration supply chains, with smaller packagings offered for pharmaceutical and laboratory use. We provide consistent quality and reliable logistics for all industrial and research applications.

name: Titanium tetrachloride
description:
Titanium tetrachloride (CAS 7550-45-0 ), commonly referenced as TiCl4, is a high-purity inorganic compound used primarily as a catalyst precursor and chemical intermediate across several industrial sectors.

Its reactivity with moisture and oxygen makes it a critical building block for producing titanium-based compounds at scale. In polyolefin manufacturing, TiCl4 is a core component in Ziegler-Natta catalyst systems.

These systems are used to produce polypropylene and polyethylene, directly influencing polymer stereoregularity and molecular weight distribution. Textile and paper processors use it as a surface treatment agent.

This application improves mordanting, fiber adhesion, and coating receptivity. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it functions as a Lewis acid catalyst enabling stereoselective reactions and chiral intermediate production.

Personal care and cosmetics manufacturers use TiCl4 as a precursor to synthetic titanium dioxide pigments. These pigments are applied in sunscreens, foundations, and various opacifying formulations.

Titanium tetrachloride is supplied as a fuming liquid, typically in stabilized, moisture-protected packaging such as sealed drums or ISO containers. It is available in technical and high-purity catalyst grades.

Specifications are tailored to polymerization catalyst production or chemical synthesis requirements. Buyers should confirm purity thresholds and metal impurity limits based on end-use sensitivity.

This is particularly important for pharmaceutical or catalyst applications where strict quality control is required. Proper handling protocols must be maintained to ensure the stability of the chemical compound.

description:
Iodine (CAS 7553-56-2 ), also known as molecular iodine, is a halogen element supplied in solid form for industrial and pharmaceutical use. It functions primarily as a biocide and chemical intermediate.

This material acts as a disinfectant across a broad range of manufacturing and treatment processes. In water treatment, it is used as an active disinfectant to eliminate bacteria, viruses, and protozoa.

It is essential for potable water systems and emergency purification applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a key starting material for producing iodine-based antiseptics and contrast media.

It is also utilized for thyroid-related active ingredients. In personal care formulations, it contributes antimicrobial activity to topical antiseptic products including wound care solutions and surgical scrubs.

The substance also serves as a reagent and oxidizing agent in specialty chemical synthesis and analytical laboratory processes. It is supplied as dark grey-black crystalline flakes or granules.

name: Disodium phosphate
description:
Disodium phosphate (CAS 7558-79-4 ), also known as DSP and classified as E339(ii) in food applications, is an inorganic phosphate salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial water treatment sectors.

Its primary commercial functions are pH buffering, sequestration of metal ions, and stabilization of formulations where consistent acidity control is critical. In food manufacturing, DSP acts as an emulsifying salt and pH regulator.

It is used in processed cheese, instant noodles, and canned products where texture and shelf stability depend on controlled buffering. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to prepare buffer solutions for injectable formulations.

It is also utilized in oral liquids and tablet coatings where precise pH maintenance affects drug stability and bioavailability. Water treatment operations rely on DSP to prevent scale formation and corrosion.

It protects boiler systems and cooling towers by sequestering calcium and magnesium ions. It also functions as a dispersing and deflocculating agent in ceramic slips and detergent formulations.

Disodium phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, in both anhydrous and hydrated forms. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP / BP for pharmaceutical use, and technical grade.

The product is also available in Ph.Eur. , EP , and ACS standards depending on the specific industrial requirement. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on grade and application.

name: Perfluoro(2-methyl-3-pentanone)
description:
Perfluoro(2-methyl-3-pentanone) (CAS 756-13-8 ), commercially known as Novec 649 and classified under the fluid designation FK-5-1-12 , is a fully fluorinated ketone solvent used in precision cleaning and fire suppression applications.

Its low global warming potential relative to legacy fluorinated solvents has made it a preferred alternative in industries transitioning away from older halon and HFC-based chemistries.

In electronics manufacturing, it is used as a cleaning and defluxing solvent for PCBs, semiconductor components, and precision assemblies where residue-free performance is critical.

Industrial cleaning operations deploy it for degreasing metal parts and optical components where hydrocarbon or aqueous systems are unsuitable for the specific application.

It also functions as a heat transfer fluid and dielectric coolant in immersion cooling systems for data center hardware, providing efficient thermal management for high-density servers.

In fire suppression, FK-5-1-12 is the active agent in clean agent systems designed to protect sensitive equipment without leaving conductive or corrosive residues after discharge.

Perfluoro(2-methyl-3-pentanone) is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drums and bulk containers sized for industrial consumption and large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: Pigment Red 81
description:
Pigment Red 81 (CAS 75627-12-2 ), also supplied as Pigment Red 81:2, is a fluorescent xanthene-based organic pigment that delivers intense, bright red-to-pink coloration across a range of industrial substrates.

Its high tinctorial strength and fluorescent character make it a preferred choice where visual impact and color brilliance are primary formulation targets for manufacturers and chemical processors.

In printing inks, particularly offset and packaging inks, this pigment produces vivid, eye-catching hues suited to consumer-facing printed materials where color saturation drives shelf appeal.

Plastic coloration applications use it to achieve bright pink and red shades in films, molded articles, and packaging components. Textile and paper dyeing operations incorporate it for fluorescent brightness.

Coatings and adhesive formulations targeting decorative or specialty end uses also draw on its strong color yield to minimize pigment loading while maintaining the target shade and performance.

The material is supplied as a dry powder, typically in fine-milled form to support dispersion into liquid systems. It is available in technical and commercial grades for various industrial needs.

name: Ethyl acrylate-methacrylic acid-polyethylene glycol stearyl ether methacrylate copolymer
description:
Ethyl acrylate-methacrylic acid-polyethylene glycol stearyl ether methacrylate copolymer (CAS 75760-37-1 ) is an associative acrylic copolymer designed to control flow behavior and stabilize emulsions across aqueous formulation systems.

Its hydrophobically modified backbone allows it to build viscosity and structure in water-based systems without relying on high polymer loading. In personal care, it thickens and stabilizes lotions, creams, and leave-on treatments.

The polymer contributes to a smooth, non-tacky skin feel that formulators target in premium emulsions. Architectural and industrial coating manufacturers use it to prevent sagging and improve leveling in waterborne paint systems.

In household and institutional cleaning products, it suspends actives and particulates, maintaining product homogeneity through storage and use cycles. This ensures consistent performance for the end user over time.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to adjust open time and application rheology in water-based systems. This copolymer is typically supplied as an aqueous dispersion or liquid emulsion, with solids content varying by grade.

Both neutralized and unneutralized forms are available, with the rheological response activated upon pH adjustment in formulation. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly encountered in the market.

name: C12-13 alcohols
description:
C12-13 Alcohols (CAS 75782-86-4 ), commercially available as Oxocol 1213 and Neodol 23, are a narrow-cut blend of synthetic fatty alcohols derived from oxo synthesis. They function primarily as intermediates for ethoxylation and sulfation.

These processes produce nonionic and anionic surfactants used across cleaning, personal care, and industrial formulations. In home care and industrial cleaning, these alcohols are ethoxylated to produce alcohol ethoxylates.

These derivatives serve as the primary surfactant in laundry detergents, hard surface cleaners, and degreasers. Personal care formulators use ethoxylated and sulfated derivatives as foam boosters and emulsifiers in shampoos.

They are also utilized in body washes and liquid soaps. In metalworking fluids, they contribute to emulsification of oil-water systems, improving lubricity and coolant stability in machining operations.

They also function as wetting agents and emulsifiers in agricultural formulations and industrial process chemicals. These alcohols are supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid, typically in bulk tankers, IBCs, and drums.

Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for surfactant and industrial applications. Buyers should confirm chain length distribution and oxo-derived purity when qualifying for ethoxylation processes.

name: C14-15 alcohols
description:
C14-15 Alcohols (CAS 75782-87-5 ), commercially available as Oxocol 1415 and Dobanol 45, are synthetic fatty alcohol blends derived from oxo synthesis. They function as emulsifiers, rheology modifiers, and carrier solvents across personal care, cleaning, and industrial formulations.

In personal care, they serve as co-emulsifiers and consistency agents in creams, lotions, and conditioners. They contribute to emulsion stability and skin feel without contributing active function to the final product.

In surfactant manufacturing, they are ethoxylated to produce nonionic surfactants used in household and industrial cleaning products. Metalworking and lubricant formulators incorporate them as carrier components in cutting fluids.

These alcohols are used in emulsifiable oils where controlled viscosity and blending compatibility with mineral oils matter. They also act as solvent carriers in fragrance and active delivery systems within cosmetic formats.

C14-15 Alcohols are supplied as a liquid at ambient-to-warm temperatures, typically handled and stored in heated tanks or drums. This ensures the material remains in a workable state for manufacturing processes.

Standard commercial grades meet technical and cosmetic-grade specifications, with select grades conforming to requirements relevant to personal care and home care formulation. Quality control ensures consistency across batches.

Supply is available in intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) and bulk tanker quantities to suit both mid-scale formulators and large industrial buyers. This flexibility allows for efficient logistics and storage management.

name: Beta cyclodextrin
description:
Beta cyclodextrin (CAS 7585-39-9 ), also known as Betadex and approved as E459 , is a cyclic oligosaccharide derived from starch that encapsulates guest molecules within its hydrophobic cavity.

This inclusion complex formation allows formulators to stabilize volatile, light-sensitive, or poorly soluble actives. It improves shelf life, bioavailability, and controlled release across multiple industries.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, β-CD is used to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble APIs. This enables more consistent drug delivery in oral and topical formulations.

Food producers use it under E459 approval to protect flavors and aromas from oxidation and volatilization. This extends the effective shelf life of seasonings, encapsulated flavors, and functional food ingredients.

Personal care formulators incorporate it to stabilize fragrance compounds and active ingredients in creams, deodorants, and hair care products. This reduces degradation during storage and use.

It also functions as a chelating agent in formulations where metal ion sequestration is needed. This prevents rancidity or discoloration in sensitive chemical and cosmetic mixtures.

Beta cyclodextrin is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include food-grade (E459/ FCC ) and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , Ph. Eur. , BP ).

Technical-grade is also available for industrial encapsulation applications. Bulk supply is available in multi-kilogram and metric ton quantities to support development-scale and commercial production.

name: Pigment Red 48
description:
Pigment Red 48 (CAS 7585-41-3 ), also supplied as Pigment Red 48:1 in its barium salt form, is an azo pigment delivering strong red hues across a broad range of industrial substrates.

It is valued in coatings, plastics, and printing applications where consistent color strength and process compatibility are the primary sourcing criteria for chemical procurement and manufacturing.

In printing inks, Pigment Red 48:1 is used in offset, flexographic, and gravure formulations where high tinting strength and sharp red tones are required on paper and packaging substrates.

Plastic compounders incorporate it into polyolefins and PVC to achieve vivid red coloration in consumer and industrial goods. Surface coatings manufacturers use it in solvent-based and water-based systems.

In textile and paper applications, it supports surface dyeing and pigment printing where opacity and batch-to-batch color consistency are critical procurement requirements for global supply chains.

Pigment Red 48 is supplied as a dry powder, typically in press cake or flushed paste form depending on the end-use process. Standard grades are differentiated by salt form for specific uses.

The barium lake variant (PR 48:1) is the most commercially prevalent. Technical and ink-grade specifications are available, with particle size distribution and oil absorption values provided for screening.

Quality control ensures that all batches meet rigorous industrial benchmarks. Detailed technical data sheets are available to assist formulators in achieving optimal dispersion and stability.

name: 2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide
description:
2,4,6-Trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide , commonly known as TPO, is a monoacylphosphine oxide photoinitiator that triggers free-radical polymerization upon UV or visible light exposure. It is used across UV-curable systems to initiate rapid crosslinking and curing without thermal activation.

In UV-curable coatings for wood, metal, and plastic substrates, TPO delivers fast surface cure and low yellowing, making it a preferred choice for clear and pigmented finishes. This chemical, identified by CAS 75980-60-8 , is essential for modern industrial coating processes.

Printing inks, particularly LED-UV and broad-spectrum UV inkjet and offset formulations, rely on TPO for its strong absorption in the 380–420 nm range. This specific absorption profile enables high-speed curing on press, which is vital for high-volume commercial printing operations.

In adhesives and sealants, it supports through-cure in acrylate-based systems where depth of cure and bond strength are critical performance requirements. This ensures that the structural integrity of the bond is maintained even in thick layers or opaque formulations.

Dental composites and optical fiber coatings also use TPO where controlled, rapid photopolymerization is required in precision applications. Its ability to cure effectively under visible light makes it a versatile component in medical and telecommunications manufacturing.

TPO is supplied as a light yellow to yellow crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades are available at high purity, typically ≥98–99%, for industrial and specialty applications requiring consistent chemical performance and stability.

It is commonly offered in technical and photoinitiator-grade specifications to meet various industrial needs. Packaging options range from kilogram quantities to bulk drums suited for large-scale formulation operations and global supply chain requirements.

name: Trichloroacetic acid
description:
Trichloroacetic acid ( CAS 76-03-9 ), commonly abbreviated as TCA, is a strong chlorinated organic acid used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial processing applications. It functions primarily as a protein precipitant and chemical denaturant.

This chemical enables controlled tissue destruction, protein removal, and surface treatment in manufacturing workflows. In pharmaceutical and laboratory settings, TCA is used to precipitate proteins from biological samples for analysis.

It serves as a standard reagent in analytical and quality control procedures. The cosmetic industry applies it in controlled chemical peel formulations, where it removes damaged or keratinized skin layers at defined concentrations.

Textile and leather processors use TCA as a chemical treatment agent to modify fiber surfaces and support dyeing or finishing operations. It also functions as a biocide and preservation agent in industrial formulations.

This versatile acid is essential where microbial control is required. Trichloroacetic acid is supplied as a crystalline solid or in aqueous solution at various concentrations, with high-concentration solutions common for industrial use.

Established grades include pharmaceutical-grade and reagent-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications. Technical-grade material is available for industrial processing applications where pharmacopeial compliance is not required.

name: Trifluoroacetic acid
description:
Trifluoroacetic acid (CAS 76-05-1 ), commonly abbreviated as TFA, is a strong fluorinated organic acid used across pharmaceutical synthesis, analytical chemistry, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a reaction catalyst, ion-pairing reagent, and deprotection agent in complex chemical processes. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, TFA is the standard reagent for Boc-group removal.

This makes it indispensable to API production workflows. Analytical laboratories rely on TFA as an HPLC mobile phase additive, where it improves peak resolution and retention of basic compounds.

In reversed-phase chromatography, it ensures high precision. In textile and leather processing, it supports pH regulation and acts as a catalyst in dyeing and finishing baths where acid control is vital.

Precise control determines color uptake and substrate integrity. Specialty chemical producers also use TFA as a solvent and activating agent in the synthesis of fluorinated intermediates and agrochemicals.

Trifluoroacetic acid is supplied as a colorless liquid, typically at 99%+ purity for pharmaceutical and analytical applications. Reagent-grade and HPLC-grade specifications are the most commonly sourced.

HPLC-grade material is held to strict UV transparency and water content limits. Bulk quantities are available for industrial synthesis, with smaller packaging formats standard for laboratory procurement.

name: Chloropicrin
description:
Chloropicrin (CAS 76-06-2 ), also known as trichloro(nitro)methane, is a halogenated fumigant used in agriculture to control soil-borne pathogens, nematodes, fungi, and weed seeds ahead of planting.

Tri-clor 99.6 designates the high-purity commercial grade commonly specified in procurement and application contracts. Pre-plant soil fumigation is the primary use for this chemical agent.

The product is injected into the soil to eliminate fungal pathogens such as Fusarium and Verticillium that threaten high-value crops including strawberries, tomatoes, and peppers.

It is frequently blended with methyl bromide alternatives or other fumigants to broaden the spectrum of control against nematodes and soil insects in commodity vegetable and fruit production.

In post-harvest and storage facility treatment, chloropicrin controls insects and mold in grain storage structures and processing equipment. Turf and ornamental growers also apply it for soil sterilization.

This application is common in nursery beds and greenhouse substrates prior to transplanting. Chloropicrin is supplied as a liquid under pressure, typically in cylinders, drums, or bulk containers.

These containers are suited for field injection equipment. The Tri-clor 99.6 grade reflects a minimum 99.6% purity specification standard in commercial agricultural supply chains.

Technical-grade material is the dominant form in the market, with purity and stabilizer content specified per regional regulatory requirements to ensure consistent performance in the field.

name: Camphor
description:
Camphor (CAS 76-22-2 ), also known as laurel camphor, is a bicyclic ketone derived from the wood of Cinnamomum camphora or produced synthetically. It functions as a flavoring agent, fragrance fixative, and active ingredient across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food applications.

In topical pharmaceutical formulations, camphor acts as a counterirritant and penetration modifier in creams, liniments, and medicated patches targeting muscle and joint discomfort. Fragrance compounders use it as a fixative and character note in perfumes and incense.

It is frequently utilized in scented personal care products where a clean, medicinal profile is required. Oral care manufacturers incorporate it into toothpastes and mouthwashes for its cooling sensation and flavoring contribution.

At regulated concentrations, it is also approved as a flavoring agent in food products, where it delivers a characteristic herbal, minty note. Camphor is supplied as white crystalline powder, pressed blocks, or sublimed flakes depending on requirements.

Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications, as well as technical grade for industrial fragrance and manufacturing use. These quality standards ensure consistency across global supply chains.

Natural (d-camphor) and synthetic (racemic) variants are both commercially available for various industrial needs. Natural-origin material often commands preference in premium fragrance and clean-label formulations due to its botanical source.

name: Bornyl acetate
description:
Bornyl acetate (CAS 76-49-3 ) is a naturally occurring ester used as a fragrance and flavoring ingredient across food, cosmetic, and personal care applications. Known in the flavor industry under FEMA 2159 , it delivers a fresh, pine-like, camphoraceous character that defines its commercial value.

L-bornyl acetate and (-)-borneol acetate are recognized forms traded for their specific optical activity in fine fragrance and flavor work. In flavor formulations, it contributes conifer, herbal, and forest-type profiles to confectionery, beverages, and savory products.

Fragrance compounders use it to build top and middle notes in fine perfumes, functional fragrances, and air care products where a natural, woody-green character is required. In personal care, it appears in shampoos, shower gels, and skincare formulations targeting fresh or botanical scent profiles.

It also functions as a supporting ingredient in aromatherapy-positioned products and spa-grade cosmetics. Bornyl acetate is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in natural and synthetic grades, with natural-origin material commanding preference.

This material is often utilized in clean-label food and premium fragrance applications. Standard supply conforms to FCC specifications for food-grade use, with fragrance-grade material assessed against purity benchmarks typical for flavor and fragrance raw materials.

name: Triphenyltin hydroxide
description:
Triphenyltin hydroxide (CAS 76-87-9 ), commercially known as fentin hydroxide, is an organotin biocide used in agricultural crop protection. It acts as a fungicide and algaecide, controlling fungal pathogens and algae in targeted field applications.

Fentin hydroxide is registered for use against late blight and Cercospora leaf spot in potato and sugar beet crops. It is formulated into wettable powder or suspension concentrate sprays to ensure effective coverage and disease management.

It also controls algae in rice paddy cultivation, applied directly to flooded fields to suppress aquatic weed competition. In specialty crop programs, it has been used as a tank-mix partner with other fungicides to broaden disease control spectrums.

Industrial antifouling formulations have historically incorporated organotin compounds of this class to prevent biofouling on marine surfaces. This application helps maintain the integrity of submerged structures and vessel hulls over time.

Triphenyltin hydroxide is supplied as a technical-grade solid, typically as a white to off-white powder or crystalline material. It is available in formulated end-use products such as wettable powders and suspension concentrates for agricultural use.

Technical-grade material is sourced for formulation manufacturing, with purity specifications varying by supplier and regional registration requirements. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality for industrial and agricultural applications globally.

name: Benzilic acid
description:
Benzilic acid (CAS 76-93-7 ), also known as diphenylglycolic acid, is an aromatic hydroxy acid used as a chemical intermediate in pharmaceutical synthesis and polymer chemistry.

Its reactive hydroxyl and carboxyl groups make it a practical building block for producing esters, salts, and more complex molecular structures at industrial scale for various applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a precursor to anticholinergic active ingredients, including compounds used in antispasmodic drug formulations and other therapeutic agents.

Polymer and specialty chemical producers use it as a polymerization initiator and co-monomer to introduce defined structural features into polyester and polycarbonate systems during production.

It is also used in the synthesis of benzilic acid esters, which function as plasticizers and chemical intermediates in their own right for diverse industrial and laboratory processes.

Research-scale and fine chemical operations source it for asymmetric synthesis and chiral resolution processes where the diphenyl-substituted scaffold is a required starting point for chemists.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+.

Packaging options generally range from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to multi-hundred kilogram bulk orders for industrial users requiring consistent supply and high-quality material.

name: Methacrylic anhydride
description:
Methacrylic anhydride (CAS 760-93-0 ), also known as methacryloyl anhydride, is a reactive acylating agent used to introduce methacryloyl functional groups onto hydroxyl- or amine-bearing substrates.

It enables the synthesis of polymerizable macromonomers and modified polymers across specialty chemical manufacturing. In polymer chemistry, it is used to functionalize natural and synthetic backbones.

This includes cellulose, chitosan, and polyols, creating UV-curable or thermally crosslinkable materials for coatings, hydrogels, and resins. Personal care formulators use methacrylated intermediates derived from this reagent.

These intermediates help build film-forming polymers and crosslinked networks in hair fixatives and skin-contact materials. In dental and biomedical polymer applications, it serves as a key reagent.

It is used for producing methacrylated monomers used in adhesive and matrix formulations. Specialty flavor and fragrance synthesis also draws on its acylating reactivity to produce ester intermediates.

These processes occur at both laboratory and pilot scale. The product is supplied as a liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport.

Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels generally ranging from 94% to 99%+. Packaging options typically include drums and intermediate bulk containers.

Industrial quantities are standard, with smaller laboratory-scale packaging available from fine chemical suppliers. This ensures flexibility for various manufacturing and research requirements.

description:
Trisodium phosphate (CAS 7601-54-9 ), commonly abbreviated as TSP and approved as food additive E339iii , is an inorganic phosphate salt used across industrial and food-grade applications for pH control and sequestration.

Tribasic sodium phosphate is the recognized alternative name buyers encounter in technical specifications and regulatory documents. In industrial cleaning, TSP functions as a heavy-duty degreaser for metal and concrete surfaces.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a buffering and sequestering agent in processed cheeses, cured meats, and cereal products. It helps to control acidity and bind metal ions that would otherwise accelerate spoilage.

Water treatment facilities dose TSP to adjust pH and inhibit scale formation in boiler and cooling water systems. In textile and paper processing, it acts as a scouring aid and assists in flame-retardant formulations.

Trisodium phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with anhydrous and dodecahydrate forms both available commercially. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), technical grade, and USP .

Food-grade material meets purity thresholds required for direct food contact applications. Bulk supply is typical for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for laboratory or specialty formulation use.

name: Sodium perchlorate
description:
Sodium perchlorate (CAS 7601-89-0 ), also known commercially as perchloric acid sodium salt, is a highly soluble inorganic oxidizer sourced for applications where strong oxidizing capacity must be managed. It is a primary raw material in energetic material synthesis and specialty electrochemical systems.

In aerospace and defense, this chemical serves as a precursor in the production of ammonium perchlorate, the dominant oxidizer in solid rocket propellants and pyrotechnic compositions. Electronics manufacturers use it in electrolyte formulations for lithium battery research.

Its high ionic conductivity in solution is the deciding factor for electrochemical testing. It also appears in airbag inflator chemistry and other gas-generating systems requiring a reliable, fast-reacting oxidant for safety mechanisms.

Specialty chemical producers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing other perchlorate salts for analytical and industrial applications. Sodium perchlorate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an anhydrous solid depending on requirements.

The monohydrate form is also available depending on specific processing needs. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher for industrial use across various sectors.

As a regulated oxidizer classified under UN1502, it is handled and shipped under hazardous goods protocols. This ensures safety and compliance during the transport of these high-purity crystalline materials to global manufacturing facilities.

name: Perchloric acid
description:
Perchloric acid (CAS 7601-90-3 ), commonly referenced by its formula HClO4, is a strong inorganic acid and powerful oxidizing agent used across analytical, industrial, and electrochemical processes.

It is valued for its ability to dissolve resistant metal matrices and drive specific oxidation reactions under controlled conditions. In mining and metals processing, it is used for digesting refractory ores.

This enables accurate elemental analysis in quality control workflows for complex alloy samples. Electronics manufacturers apply it in etching and surface preparation processes where precise metal removal is required.

Surface activation is another key application in the electronics sector. Pharmaceutical and chemical laboratories use it as an ion-pairing reagent in HPLC methods and as a catalyst in organic synthesis.

Water treatment operations employ it in pH adjustment and in the preparation of perchlorate-based reference standards. These standards are essential for the calibration of various analytical instrumentation.

Perchloric acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 70% and 60% concentrations being the most commercially standard. Technical and reagent grades are available for diverse industrial needs.

High-purity analytical grades meeting specifications for laboratory and pharmaceutical use are also provided. Packaging typically ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk drums for large operations.

Availability depends on the specific grade and regional regulatory requirements. Our supply chain ensures that all products meet rigorous safety and handling protocols for chemical distribution.

name: Trisodium aminotris(methylenephosphonate)
description:
Trisodium aminotris(methylenephosphonate) (CAS 7611-50-9 ), the trisodium salt form of ATMP, is a phosphonate chelating agent used across water treatment and industrial cleaning applications.

It controls scale deposition and inhibits corrosion by sequestering calcium, magnesium, and heavy metal ions in aqueous systems. In industrial water treatment, it is dosed into cooling water circuits.

It is also used in boiler systems to prevent calcium carbonate and calcium sulfate scale buildup on heat exchange surfaces. Cleaning and detergent formulators incorporate it to sequester hardness ions.

This improves surfactant performance and prevents redeposition of soil in industrial and institutional formulations. In textile processing, it stabilizes peroxide bleach baths by chelating trace metal ions.

These ions would otherwise catalyze premature decomposition. Paper and leather processing operations use it to control metal ion interference during bleaching and tanning stages.

Trisodium aminotris(methylenephosphonate) is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration typically around 40–50% active content. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification.

This specification is ideal for water treatment and industrial applications. Packaging options commonly include drums and IBC totes suited to bulk industrial procurement needs.

name: Propargyl butylcarbamate
description:
Propargyl butylcarbamate (CAS 76114-73-3 ), also known as N-Butyl propargyl carbamate, is a broad-spectrum biocide used to protect industrial materials from microbial degradation.

It delivers fungicidal and bactericidal activity across a range of wet and dry formulation types, making it a reliable preservation option for demanding industrial applications.

In coatings and adhesives, it is incorporated to prevent mold, mildew, and bacterial growth during storage and on dried film surfaces. This ensures long-term stability and performance.

Textile and leather processors use it in finishing treatments to protect goods from fungal attack during transit and warehousing. It is essential for maintaining the integrity of these materials.

Water treatment formulations rely on it as an active biocide to control microbial fouling in industrial process water and cooling systems. This helps maintain efficiency in large-scale operations.

In agrochemical products, it functions as a preservative component in formulated crop protection products where microbial contamination of the formulation itself must be controlled.

Propargyl butylcarbamate is typically supplied as a liquid, often in solvent-based solutions at defined active concentrations suited to direct blending into end formulations.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for industrial preservation applications. Buyers should confirm active content percentage and solvent carrier with suppliers.

name: Diethyl phosphite
description:
Diethyl phosphite ( CAS 762-04-9 ), also referred to commercially as diethyl phosphonate or DEP, is a reactive organophosphorus compound used as a chemical intermediate and functional additive across multiple industrial sectors.

It acts as a building block for synthesizing phosphorus-containing compounds and delivers antioxidant, stabilizing, and lubrication functions in finished formulations. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, DEP functions as an extreme-pressure additive.

It serves as an antiwear agent, reducing metal surface degradation under high-load conditions. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly antiviral and antiparasitic compounds.

In agrochemical production, it serves as a precursor in the manufacture of organophosphate pesticides and herbicides. Polymer and plastics processors incorporate DEP as a flame retardant additive and stabilizer.

This helps to meet flammability and thermal performance requirements in end products. Diethyl phosphite is supplied as a clear, colorless to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker supply available.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher. Pharmaceutical-intermediate-grade material with controlled impurity profiles is available from select manufacturers.

This material is designed to support API synthesis qualification requirements. The product is handled according to strict industrial safety protocols to ensure consistent quality and performance across all applications.

name: Decanoyl peroxide
description:
Decanoyl peroxide (CAS 762-12-9 ), also known as didecanoyl peroxide, is an organic peroxide used as a free-radical source in polymer manufacturing and curing processes. It decomposes at controlled temperatures to generate radicals that initiate polymerization or drive cross-linking reactions.

In plastics and polymer production, it initiates free-radical polymerization of vinyl and acrylic monomers, allowing processors to control molecular weight and reaction rate. Rubber compounders use it as a curing agent to cross-link elastomers.

This chemical improves mechanical strength and heat resistance in finished rubber goods. In coatings formulations, it functions as a hardener or initiator in peroxide-cured systems where thermal activation is required for the application.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it into peroxide-cured systems where controlled gel time and bond strength are critical processing parameters. This ensures that the final product meets the necessary industrial performance standards.

Decanoyl peroxide is supplied as a white powder or paste, with concentration and diluent type varying by grade to manage handling safety and reactivity. This versatility allows it to be used across various manufacturing environments.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, with active oxygen content used as the primary specification for quality control. It is typically packaged and stored under temperature-controlled conditions to maintain stability.

Suppliers commonly offer it in formulated blends to suit specific cure profiles. These specialized formulations help manufacturers achieve consistent results during the polymerization and cross-linking stages of production.

name: Ethyl 3-ethoxypropionate
description:
Ethyl 3-ethoxypropionate (CAS 763-69-9 ), commonly known by the abbreviation EEP, is a slow-evaporating ester solvent used across coatings, personal care, and specialty chemical formulations.

Its controlled evaporation rate and strong solvency make it a preferred choice for applications requiring extended open time and clean substrate wetting during the application process.

In coatings and ink formulations, EEP improves flow and leveling in high-solids and waterborne systems, helping formulators meet VOC targets without sacrificing film quality or performance.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as a carrier solvent in nail lacquers, hair care products, and skin formulations where a slow-drying, low-odor profile is required for the consumer.

In industrial cleaning and surface preparation, EEP dissolves resins, adhesives, and polymer residues where faster solvents would evaporate before adequate penetration into the substrate occurs.

It also appears in flavor and fragrance applications as a minor component contributing ester character to finished compositions, ensuring a balanced profile in the final aromatic product.

Ethyl 3-ethoxypropionate is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger procurement volumes to meet industrial demand.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available to meet formulation-specific requirements in personal care and fragrance end uses globally.

name: Silica
description:
Silica (CAS 7631-86-9 ), also known as silicon dioxide or SiO2, is a high-purity amorphous mineral used across industrial and consumer product manufacturing. As E551 in food-contact and additive applications, it functions primarily as an anticaking agent.

It serves as a flow aid and rheology modifier in powder and liquid systems. In personal care, silica controls texture and oil absorption in pressed powders, dry shampoos, and skincare formulations where sensory performance and spreadability are critical.

Rubber and tire compounding relies on precipitated silica as a reinforcing filler that improves rolling resistance and wet grip performance in high-performance tire compounds. Plastics and polymer processing uses fumed silica to modify viscosity.

This application is vital in adhesives, sealants, and coatings, preventing sagging and improving shelf stability. In printing and packaging, silica acts as a matting agent and anti-slip additive in inks and surface coatings.

Silica is supplied as fumed silica, precipitated silica, and colloidal silica dispersions, each suited to different processing requirements. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E551) and pharmaceutical-grade options.

These pharmaceutical grades meet USP and Ph. Eur. standards, alongside technical-grade for industrial applications. Particle size, surface area, and surface treatment vary by grade and determine suitability.

Hydrophilic or hydrophobic treatments are available depending on specific formulation or processing conditions. This versatility ensures that the material meets the rigorous demands of diverse global manufacturing sectors.

name: Sodium bisulfite
description:
Sodium bisulfite (CAS 7631-90-5 ), also sold as sodium bisulphite and designated E222 in food applications, is an inorganic sulfite salt used commercially as a reducing agent, preservative, and oxygen scavenger across multiple industries.

SBS delivers reliable antioxidant and antimicrobial action at relatively low use concentrations, making it a cost-effective functional ingredient for formulators and process engineers in various sectors.

In food and beverage production, E222 prevents oxidative browning and microbial spoilage in fruit products, wines, dried foods, and seafood processing. Water treatment operations rely on sodium bisulfite to dechlorinate potable water.

It is used for treating boiler feedwater, neutralizing residual chlorine before downstream processing or discharge. Textile and paper manufacturers apply it as a bleaching and reducing agent for pulp brightening and dye stripping.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an antioxidant stabilizer in injectable formulations and oral liquid preparations where oxygen-sensitive active ingredients require protection from degradation.

Sodium bisulfite is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granules, with liquid solution forms also available for industrial water treatment applications. Standard commercial grades include food-grade material.

These grades are FCC and E222-compliant, with purity levels typically ranging from 58% to 65% active SO₂ equivalent. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. specifications is also available.

These high-purity options are specifically designed for regulated manufacturing environments. The material remains a versatile chemical essential for maintaining product stability and process efficiency globally.

name: Sodium molybdate
description:
Sodium molybdate (CAS 7631-95-0 ) is an inorganic molybdenum salt used across industrial and agricultural sectors primarily as a corrosion inhibitor, micronutrient source, and catalyst component.

The anhydrous form is distinguished from the common dihydrate in procurement contexts, with buyers sourcing each for different formulation requirements in various manufacturing processes.

In water treatment and closed-loop cooling systems, it functions as a non-chromate corrosion inhibitor, protecting metal surfaces in recirculating water circuits where regulatory pressure has phased out chromate alternatives.

Coatings and anticorrosive primer formulations incorporate it as a pigment extender and passivating agent, particularly in industrial protective coatings for steel substrates and heavy machinery.

In agriculture and animal feed, it supplies molybdenum as a trace element, which is critical for nitrogen fixation in legume crops and enzyme function in livestock nutrition and health.

Metalworking lubricants and extreme-pressure fluid formulations use it to reduce friction and surface wear under high-load conditions, ensuring the longevity of industrial equipment and tools.

Sodium molybdate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule, most commonly as the dihydrate form. Standard commercial grades include technical, feed-grade, and reagent-grade options.

Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5%+. Packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on the specific grade and the intended industrial or agricultural application.

name: Sodium monofluorophosphate

Sodium monofluorophosphate (CAS 7631-97-2 ) is an inorganic fluoride salt used as an active ingredient in dental care products and pharmaceutical formulations. It delivers controlled fluoride release to support enamel remineralization.

These formulations are designed for markets including the EU, US, and Japan. Pharmaceutical-grade applications include fluoride supplement tablets and dental treatment preparations where precise dosing and purity documentation are required.

It offers a formulation advantage over alternative fluoride salts due to its compatibility with abrasive or peroxide-containing bases. Sodium monofluorophosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for industrial use.

Packaging options typically range from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk metric-ton supply. This ensures reliable availability for industrial toothpaste manufacturing and large-scale pharmaceutical production needs.

name: Sodium lauryl sarcosinate
description:
Sodium lauryl sarcosinate ( CAS 7631-98-3 ), also known as sodium lauroyl sarcosinate, is a mild amino acid-derived anionic surfactant used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

It delivers effective foaming, cleansing, and emulsification while being considered gentler on skin than conventional sulfate surfactants. This factor directly influences formulation choices in sensitive-skin product lines.

In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, facial cleansers, toothpastes, and shaving foams. Its low irritation profile supports sulfate-free positioning in premium consumer goods.

Home care and industrial cleaning products use it to boost foam stability and improve soil removal in liquid detergents. It is also highly effective for use in various hard surface cleaners and degreasers.

Textile and leather processing operations incorporate it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure even penetration of treatment baths. In paper manufacturing, it supports fiber dispersion and surface treatment processes.

name: Sodium nitrate

Sodium nitrate (CAS 7631-99-4 ), also known as Chile saltpeter or E251 , is an inorganic salt used across food preservation, agriculture, and industrial oxidation processes. It functions as a curing agent, fertilizer feedstock, and oxidizing agent depending on the application sector.

In food processing, E251 is used to cure processed meats such as bacon, ham, and deli products, inhibiting microbial growth and stabilizing color during shelf life. This ensures product safety and maintains visual appeal for consumers.

In agriculture, it serves as a fast-acting nitrogen source in straight and compound fertilizers, particularly for crops requiring rapid nutrient uptake. This allows for efficient growth cycles and improved yields in various soil conditions.

The mining industry uses sodium nitrate as an oxidizer component in blasting agents and explosive formulations where controlled reactivity is required. Its stability makes it a preferred choice for specialized industrial blasting applications.

In pulp and paper manufacturing, it supports chemical pulping processes and acts as an oxidizing agent in bleaching and delignification operations. This helps in achieving the desired brightness and strength in the final paper products.

Sodium nitrate is supplied as white crystalline granules or prills, with powder forms available for specific industrial applications. Food and feed-compliant material is available to E251 specification and FCC grade.

description:
Sodium nitrite (CAS 7632-00-0 ), also recognized in food labeling as E250 , is an inorganic salt used industrially as a curing agent, preservative, and color fixative.

It controls microbial growth and stabilizes the characteristic pink color in processed meat products, while also serving preservation functions in pharmaceutical and industrial contexts.

In meat processing, sodium nitrite is the active curing agent in products such as bacon, ham, hot dogs, and deli meats, inhibiting Clostridium botulinum growth while fixing myoglobin.

This process delivers the cured color consumers expect. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate and active ingredient in certain antidote formulations for medical applications.

In food production more broadly, it functions as an antioxidant to retard rancidity and extend shelf life in cured and preserved products. This ensures product stability over time.

Industrial applications include its use as a corrosion inhibitor in metalworking fluids and heat transfer systems, though food and pharma remain the primary commercial demand drivers.

Sodium nitrite is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline powder or granules. Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade meeting USP and BP standards.

Technical-grade material is available for industrial end uses, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+ depending on the specific requirements of the application.

name: Sodium perborate
description:
Sodium perborate (CAS 7632-04-4 ), also known as sodium peroxometaborate, is an oxidizing salt that releases active oxygen upon dissolution in water. This controlled oxygen release makes it effective as a bleaching agent and disinfectant.

It serves as a cleaning booster across multiple industrial sectors. In detergent and laundry formulations, it acts as an oxygen bleach that removes stains and whitens fabrics without the fiber damage associated with chlorine-based alternatives.

Pulp and paper manufacturers use it to bleach cellulose fibers, achieving brightness targets while maintaining fiber integrity. In personal care, it is incorporated into tooth-whitening products and denture cleansers.

It is also used in hair bleaching formulations where controlled peroxide delivery is required. Water treatment and textile processing operations rely on it as a biocide and oxidative cleaning agent for effluent treatment.

Sodium perborate is supplied in two primary commercial forms: monohydrate and tetrahydrate. The monohydrate is preferred where lower moisture content and higher active oxygen content are priorities for the manufacturer.

Standard grades include technical and detergent-grade specifications. Particle size and active oxygen content are the key quality parameters buyers typically specify when sourcing this material for industrial use.

Bulk and bagged supply options are available to suit both large-scale industrial and mid-volume procurement requirements. This ensures flexibility for various supply chain needs and storage capacities across different regions.

name: N,n-dimethylglucamine
description:
N,N-Dimethylglucamine (CAS 76326-99-3 ) is a sugar-derived amino alcohol used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and industrial water treatment applications. It functions as a pH buffer, chelating agent, and solubilizing carrier.

This versatile compound enables the formulation of otherwise difficult-to-process active compounds. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to form salt forms of acidic APIs, improving solubility and bioavailability.

These properties are particularly beneficial in injectable and oral dosage forms. Personal care formulators incorporate it as a buffering and chelating agent in skin-conditioning products to stabilize formulations.

It helps sequester metal ions that would otherwise degrade actives in cosmetic products. Water treatment applications rely on its chelation capacity to control scale-forming metal ions in process water systems.

It also serves as a solubilizing carrier in contrast media and diagnostic formulations. In these applications, controlled pH and metal coordination are critical to ensuring consistent product performance.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to meet the purity requirements of regulated drug manufacturing and USP standards.

Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial water treatment use. Packaging is typically available in kilogram quantities through to bulk drum supply to meet diverse manufacturing needs.

name: Potassium caprylate
description:
Potassium caprylate (CAS 764-71-6 ), also known commercially as potassium octanoate, is the potassium salt of caprylic acid used across personal care, food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural formulations.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, surfactant, and antimicrobial agent, enabling formulators to stabilize oil-in-water systems while simultaneously controlling microbial growth in various applications.

In personal care formulations, it acts as a soap-forming emulsifier in liquid cleansers, shampoos, and skin creams, contributing to lather quality and emulsion stability for high-end cosmetic products.

Food manufacturers use it as a preservative and emulsifying salt in processed products where caprylic acid-based antimicrobial activity is required without acidifying the system during production.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a stabilizer and antimicrobial excipient in injectable formulations and protein-based biologics where tight microbial control is critical for safety.

Agricultural formulators incorporate it into crop protection products as a wetting and dispersing agent to improve active ingredient coverage on plant surfaces and enhance overall efficacy.

Potassium caprylate is typically supplied as a liquid solution or white to off-white powder. Food-grade and technical-grade specifications are the most commonly available for industrial use.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is produced to USP or Ph. Eur. standards for excipient applications. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial buyers, with concentration and purity confirmed against COA.

name: Sodium hydride
description:
Sodium hydride (CAS 7646-69-7 ), commonly abbreviated as NaH, is a strong inorganic base used across chemical synthesis and industrial processing. It functions primarily as a deprotonating agent and catalyst.

This chemical enables reactions that require highly basic conditions. Pharmaceutical manufacturers, polymer chemists, and specialty chemical producers rely on it to drive alkylation, condensation, and cyclization reactions.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, NaH deprotonates active pharmaceutical ingredient precursors to facilitate N- and O-alkylation steps. These steps are often difficult to achieve with milder bases.

Polymer and rubber producers use it to initiate anionic polymerization and to synthesize flame-retardant intermediates. These intermediates are then incorporated into various finished materials.

Biotechnology and fine chemical workflows depend on NaH for generating reactive carbanions and enolates in multi-step synthetic routes. It is essential for complex molecular construction.

It also functions as a catalyst precursor in reactions where a highly reactive, non-nucleophilic base is required. This allows for substrate activation without competing side reactions.

Sodium hydride is most commonly supplied as a dispersion in mineral oil. The 60% NaH concentration is the standard commercial form that balances handling safety with reactivity.

Pure, dry NaH is available for specialized laboratory and industrial applications requiring solvent-free conditions. Supply is offered in technical grade, with packaging options ranging from small quantities to bulk drums.

name: Stannic chloride
description:
Stannic chloride (CAS 7646-78-8 ), also known as tin tetrachloride or SnCl4, is an inorganic tin compound supplied primarily as a fuming liquid or in hydrated form. It functions as a Lewis acid catalyst and tin source across chemical synthesis and polymer production.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a catalyst and stabilizer precursor in the production of PVC and other tin-stabilized formulations. This helps control degradation during processing and ensures the durability of the final material.

Pharmaceutical synthesis relies on it as a Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel-Crafts reactions and other electrophilic processes. Controlled reactivity is critical to yield and purity in these complex chemical transformations.

It is also used in the production of indium tin oxide (ITO) coatings and conductive thin films. In these applications, it serves as a tin precursor deposited onto glass or plastic substrates for electronics.

In specialty chemical manufacturing, it functions as an intermediate for producing organotin compounds. These compounds are frequently used as biocides and stabilizers in various industrial formulations and coatings.

Stannic chloride is available as an anhydrous liquid and as the pentahydrate solid, with the hydrated form preferred where moisture sensitivity is less critical. Standard supply grades include technical and reagent-grade specifications.

Bulk quantities are typically packaged in drums or IBCs to ensure safe transport and storage. Smaller quantities are also available for specialized laboratory and pharmaceutical applications requiring precise measurements.

name: Cobalt chloride
description:
Cobalt chloride (CAS 7646-79-9 ), also sold as cobaltous chloride anhydrous or CoCl2, is an inorganic cobalt salt used across chemical manufacturing, agriculture, and industrial processing.

It functions primarily as a catalyst precursor, colorant, and source of bioavailable cobalt in trace mineral applications. In agriculture and animal feed, it corrects cobalt deficiencies in livestock.

The material is frequently incorporated into mineral premixes and fertilizer formulations. Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant to fix dyes and improve color fastness on treated substrates.

In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for hydrodesulfurization and Fischer-Tropsch catalysts used in refinery and petrochemical operations. This makes it vital for energy sector applications.

The compound also functions as a humidity indicator in desiccant systems and silica gel products. Its color-change behavior drives procurement in packaging and electronics protection industries worldwide.

Cobalt chloride is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as the hexahydrate form, with the hexahydrate being the more common commercial grade. It meets high industrial quality standards.

Standard specifications include technical grade and reagent grade, with purity levels typically ranging from 97% to 99%+. Packaging is available in drums and bulk quantities for industrial use.

name: Zinc chloride
description:
Zinc chloride (CAS 7646-85-7 ) is an inorganic salt used across industrial manufacturing as a flux agent, catalyst, and antimicrobial preservative. Its high solubility and reactivity with metal oxides make it a practical choice for processes requiring surface activation.

In textile and paper manufacturing, these solutions are used to activate and mercerize fibers, improving dye uptake and dimensional stability in finished goods. It functions as a Lewis acid catalyst in organic synthesis, facilitating Friedel-Crafts alkylations.

This chemical is essential in reactions where a strong electrophilic promoter is required. Water treatment operations use it as a coagulation aid and biocide to control microbial growth in industrial cooling systems and process water.

In leather processing, it serves as a preservative and tanning auxiliary, helping to stabilize hides during intermediate processing stages. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial applications and specialized chemical manufacturing.

The product is supplied as anhydrous powder, granules, and concentrated aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically ranging from 50% to 70% by weight. This variety allows for precise dosing in diverse manufacturing environments.

Standard grades include technical, pharmaceutical ( USP / BP ), and reagent-grade material to meet the specifications of different end markets. These quality standards ensure the material is suitable for its intended industrial or medical use.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial buyers, with smaller packaged formats supplied for laboratory and pharmaceutical procurement. We ensure consistent supply chains for all grades of this essential inorganic compound.
