name: Hydrochloric acid
description:
Hydrochloric acid (CAS 7647-01-0 ), also known as HCl and listed as E507 in food applications, is a strong inorganic acid supplied as an aqueous solution. It is used for industrial-scale pH control, metal processing, and chemical synthesis.

Its aggressive reactivity with oxides, carbonates, and alkaline compounds makes it a primary reagent across a broad range of manufacturing and treatment processes. In steel and metal fabrication, HCl is used to pickle and descale surfaces.

This process occurs before galvanizing, electroplating, or coating, removing iron oxides without damaging the base metal. Food and beverage producers use E507-grade acid to regulate pH in starch hydrolysis and gelatin production.

It is also essential in the manufacture of food additives. Water treatment facilities dose hydrochloric acid to correct alkalinity and maintain optimal pH in both potable water systems and industrial effluent streams.

Leather tanneries and textile processors apply it in deliming, dyeing preparation, and fiber treatment stages. In these applications, precise acidity control determines the final product quality and consistency.

Hydrochloric acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 30–33% and 35–37% concentrations being the most common commercial grades. Food-grade (E507/ FCC ) and technical-grade specifications are both available.

Food and pharma applications require compliance to BP or Ph. Eur. standards to ensure safety and purity. Bulk liquid supply in tankers and IBCs are standard formats for industrial procurement.

name: Palladium Chloride
description:
Palladium Chloride (CAS 7647-10-1 ), commonly referenced as PdCl2, is an inorganic palladium salt used primarily as a catalyst precursor and analytical reagent across chemical manufacturing and industrial processing.

It serves as the entry-point compound for producing a broad range of palladium-based catalysts deployed in high-value synthesis and surface treatment applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is used to prepare catalysts for cross-coupling reactions.

These reactions, including Suzuki, Heck, and Sonogashira, are essential for building complex active pharmaceutical ingredients. Printed circuit board and electronics manufacturers use it as a sensitizing agent in electroless plating baths.

This application enables copper deposition onto non-conductive substrates. In mining and hydrometallurgy, it functions as a reference material and selective precipitant in precious metal refining and assay processes.

Antimicrobial and biocide formulations in industrial water treatment and preservation also draw on its activity against microbial contamination. Palladium Chloride is supplied as a dark brown to red crystalline powder.

It is also available as an aqueous hydrochloric acid solution. Standard commercial grades include anhydrous and dihydrate forms, with purity levels ranging from technical grade to high-purity specifications.

These grades meet research and catalyst manufacturing requirements. Packaging is typically offered in small quantities due to the material's high unit value and specialized industrial handling needs.

name: Sodium chloride

Sodium chloride (CAS 7647-14-5 ), commonly known as salt or NaCl, is one of the most broadly sourced inorganic compounds in industrial and food supply chains. It functions as a preservative and flavor enhancer.

This versatile compound also acts as a processing aid and chemical feedstock across a wide range of manufacturing sectors. In food processing, NaCl controls water activity to extend shelf life and delivers taste.

It provides the primary savory taste profile in cured meats, cheeses, snacks, and condiments. Textile and leather manufacturers rely on it to fix dyes to fiber substrates and to cure hides during preservation.

Water treatment facilities use sodium chloride to regenerate ion exchange resins in softening systems. This process maintains consistent water quality for industrial and municipal supply chains globally.

In chemical manufacturing, it serves as a primary feedstock for chlor-alkali production. This process generates chlorine and caustic soda at an industrial scale for various downstream applications.

Sodium chloride is supplied as fine powder, coarse granules, flakes, and vacuum-evaporated crystals. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical use.

name: Sodium bromide
description:
Sodium bromide (CAS 7647-15-6 ), commonly referenced as NaBr, is an inorganic bromide salt used across industrial and pharmaceutical sectors. It functions primarily as a bromide ion source, enabling its use in completion fluids and synthesis intermediates.

In oil and gas, NaBr is a key component of high-density clear brine fluids used in wellbore completion and workover operations. Precise density control is critical in these applications to ensure safety and efficiency during drilling.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients and sedative-class compounds. This is particularly important where a bromide counterion is required for the final chemical structure.

In industrial water treatment and pool sanitation, it activates oxidizing biocides to control microbial growth in recirculating systems. This ensures that water remains clean and free from harmful biological contaminants.

Flame retardant formulations for plastics and polymers incorporate NaBr as a bromine source. It acts as a precursor or synergist in halogenated retardant systems to improve the fire safety of various materials.

Sodium bromide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, and also in liquid solution form. These solutions are available at various concentrations suited specifically to oilfield brine applications.

Its flexible glycol backbone makes it effective as a reactive plasticizer in polymer networks where brittleness must be controlled without sacrificing cure performance. This ensures high-quality results in various industrial settings.

Sealant and elastomer manufacturers incorporate it to improve substrate wetting and compliance in cured formulations. This versatility makes it a staple component for modern chemical manufacturing and material science.

name: Cyclopropylamine
description:
Cyclopropylamine (CAS 765-30-0 ) is a strained-ring primary amine used as a reactive building block in pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty polymer chemistry. The abbreviation CPA appears in procurement and research contexts as a recognized shorthand.

Its combination of amine reactivity and ring strain makes it a valued intermediate for constructing complex molecular architectures at scale. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into active pharmaceutical ingredient synthesis.

This chemical is particularly useful in the preparation of kinase inhibitors, antidepressants, and other small-molecule drug candidates where the cyclopropyl motif improves metabolic stability. Polymer chemists use it as a curing agent.

It acts as a cross-linker in epoxy and specialty resin systems, where controlled amine reactivity influences final network density and mechanical performance. In agrochemical development, it serves as a key intermediate for herbicide synthesis.

Biotech research applications include its use as a building block for probe compounds and enzyme inhibitors in target-based drug discovery programs. It is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in various packaging.

Options range from small research quantities to bulk drums and IBC containers. Technical and high-purity grades are available, with purity specifications typically from 98% up to 99%+ for pharmaceutical intermediate use.

Certificate of Analysis documentation aligned with GMP procurement requirements is standard for pharma-grade supply. This ensures the material meets the rigorous demands of modern chemical manufacturing and laboratory research.

name: Stearamidopropyl dimethylamine
description:
Stearamidopropyl dimethylamine (CAS 7651-02-7 ) is a fatty amidoamine used across personal care and industrial formulations as a conditioning agent, emulsifier, and rheology modifier. It functions primarily by adsorbing onto negatively charged surfaces to deliver softness and slip.

In hair care, it is protonated with acid to form a mild cationic conditioning active used in conditioners, detanglers, and conditioning shampoos. This process reduces combing friction and improves manageability for various hair types.

Textile and fiber processing operations use it as a softening and antistatic finish on synthetic and natural fabrics. In leather treatment, it improves surface feel and aids uniform dye dispersion across the substrate during manufacturing.

Paper manufacturers apply it as a surface modifier to improve wet strength additive compatibility and sheet handling properties. Its versatile chemical structure allows for effective performance across multiple industrial substrates and applications.

The material is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white waxy solid or low-melting flake. Technical and cosmetic grades are the standard commercial forms, with cosmetic-grade material meeting purity requirements for personal care products.

Typical active content is specified at 95% or higher depending on grade and supplier specification. This high purity ensures consistent performance in sensitive formulations and demanding industrial processes where quality is paramount.

name: Lexidronam pentasodium
description:
Lexidronam pentasodium (CAS 7651-99-2 ), also known as EDTMP pentasodium salt, is a phosphonate-based chelating agent used across industrial and specialty chemical sectors. It binds and sequesters metal ions to prevent scale formation.

This chemical is particularly effective at managing calcium, magnesium, and heavy metals to prevent discoloration and process interference in aqueous systems. It is a vital component for maintaining efficiency in high-volume industrial operations.

In water treatment, it controls scale deposition in cooling towers, boilers, and industrial water circuits by sequestering hardness ions before they precipitate. This action extends the lifespan of expensive machinery and piping systems.

Pulp and paper manufacturers use it to stabilize peroxide bleaching baths, preventing metal-catalyzed decomposition that would reduce whitening efficiency. This ensures a consistent and high-quality output during the manufacturing process.

Textile and leather processors incorporate it into pretreatment and dyeing formulations to deactivate trace metals. This prevents uneven color uptake or fabric damage that can occur when metallic impurities are present in the water.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a chelant to protect product stability and enhance the performance of preservative and bleaching systems. It ensures that consumer products remain effective and visually appealing over time.

Lexidronam pentasodium is supplied as an aqueous solution, with active content concentrations typically around 40–50%. Technical grade is the standard offering across most global industrial supply channels and distribution networks.

Specifications vary by supplier, and buyers should confirm active content, pH range, and phosphonate content against their process requirements. Proper documentation ensures the material meets the specific needs of the intended application.

name: 2-ethylhexyl thioglycolate
description:
2-Ethylhexyl thioglycolate (CAS 7659-86-1 ), commonly abbreviated as EHTG and also known commercially as 2-ethylhexyl mercaptoacetate, is a sulfur-functional ester used as a reactive intermediate.

It serves as a processing aid across polymer and rubber manufacturing. Its thiol group enables controlled reactivity in curing, chain transfer, and stabilization processes for various industrial applications.

In PVC and vinyl polymer processing, EHTG functions as a co-stabilizer component and plasticizing modifier. This helps formulators balance flexibility and thermal stability in finished compounds.

Rubber compounders use it as a crosslinking agent and vulcanization modifier. It is particularly useful where precise control over cure rate and network density is required for the material.

In polymer synthesis, EHTG acts as a chain transfer agent. This allows manufacturers to regulate molecular weight distribution during free-radical polymerization to meet specific performance criteria.

Metalworking and lubricant formulators incorporate it as a reactive sulfur additive. It is commonly found in extreme-pressure and anti-wear packages for high-performance industrial lubricants.

2-Ethylhexyl thioglycolate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial specification available to industrial buyers.

Purity levels typically range from 95% to 99% for this chemical. Documentation including COA and purity assay results are standard for procurement and quality assurance purposes.

name: Betanin
description:
Betanin (CAS 7659-95-2 ), also known as beetroot red or E162 , is a natural red-violet pigment extracted from red beetroot. It is used commercially as a plant-based colorant in food and beverage manufacturing.

Synthetic dye replacement and clean-label positioning drive demand for this ingredient. In dairy and plant-based products, including yogurts and ice creams, it delivers stable pink-to-red hues without synthetic additives.

Beverage formulators use it to color fruit drinks, smoothies, and functional beverages where natural sourcing is a label requirement. Confectionery and bakery applications include sugar coatings, frostings, and fillings.

A vivid red tone is achieved at low usage levels in these applications. Processed meat and meat-alternative producers also incorporate it to achieve or enhance red coloration in finished products.

The ingredient is supplied as a liquid concentrate, spray-dried powder, or paste, depending on the processing requirements of the end application. Standard grades include food-grade and FCC -compliant specifications.

Color strength is typically expressed as betanin content or absorbance units. Stability-optimized formulations with encapsulation or pH-buffering are available for applications requiring extended shelf life.

name: Phosphoric acid
description:
Phosphoric acid (CAS 7664-38-2 ), also known as orthophosphoric acid and designated E338 in food applications, is a mineral acid used across industrial, food, and pharmaceutical sectors.

It functions primarily as a pH regulator, acidulant, chelating agent, and surface treatment chemical depending on the application. In food and beverage production, it acidifies carbonated soft drinks and acts as a flavor modifier.

The FEMA 2902 recognition supports its use in flavoring systems. Metal surface treatment relies on phosphoric acid for rust conversion and phosphate coating prior to painting or galvanizing.

Water treatment facilities use it to dose phosphate for corrosion inhibition in distribution pipelines. Pharmaceutical and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it for pH adjustment and as a sequestrant.

These formulations stabilize active ingredients against metal ion interference. Phosphoric acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 75%, 80%, and 85% concentrations being the most commercially standard.

Food-grade material is available to FCC and E338 specifications, while pharmaceutical-grade supply meets USP and Ph. Eur. requirements for various manufacturing needs.

Technical-grade solutions are used in industrial processing where food or pharma compliance is not required. This versatile chemical remains a cornerstone for acidity control and surface preparation globally.

name: Hydrofluoric acid
description:
Hydrofluoric acid (CAS 7664-39-3 ), also supplied as anhydrous hydrogen fluoride (HF), is an inorganic acid with exceptional ability to dissolve silica, oxides, and mineral scales that resist other acids.

This property drives its use across electronics fabrication, metal surface treatment, and chemical synthesis at industrial scale. In semiconductor and flat-panel display manufacturing, HF etches silicon dioxide layers.

It cleans wafer surfaces with precision tolerances that other acids cannot achieve. Metal processing operations use it to pickle stainless steel and titanium, removing oxide scale and activating surfaces ahead of finishing.

Fluorochemical synthesis relies on HF as a primary fluorinating agent in the production of refrigerants, fluoropolymers, and pharmaceutical intermediates. In mining and hydrometallurgy, it dissolves silicate gangue minerals.

The acid assists in uranium conversion processes during ore processing. Hydrofluoric acid is supplied as aqueous solution, with 40%, 49%, and 70% concentrations being the most commercially standard grades.

Anhydrous hydrogen fluoride is available for industrial fluorination processes where water content must be minimized. Grades include technical, electronic, and reagent specifications for various industrial needs.

Electronic-grade material is subject to strict trace metal and particle limits. Our supply meets rigorous quality standards to ensure performance in high-precision manufacturing and chemical synthesis applications.

name: Ammonia
description:
Ammonia (CAS 7664-41-7 ), also supplied as anhydrous ammonia, is one of the highest-volume industrial chemicals in global trade. It functions primarily as a nitrogen source, alkalizing agent, and chemical intermediate across agriculture, manufacturing, and water treatment sectors.

In agriculture, it is applied directly as a soil fertilizer and used as a feedstock for producing urea, ammonium nitrate, and other nitrogen-based fertilizers. Water treatment facilities use it to form chloramines during disinfection.

This process provides longer-lasting residual protection in municipal distribution systems. Textile and pulp and paper operations rely on it for pH regulation during fiber processing, bleaching, and dyeing stages.

In oil refining and gas processing, it neutralizes acidic byproducts in process streams, protecting equipment from corrosion and maintaining stable operating conditions. Ammonia is supplied as a compressed liquefied gas in cylinders.

It is also available in ISO tanks and bulk pressurized vessels, with anhydrous grades being the most common commercial form. Aqueous ammonia solutions typically range from 25% to 30% concentration for various uses.

These solutions are available for applications where handling liquefied gas is impractical. Grades include technical, industrial, and refrigeration-quality specifications, with purity levels and moisture content defined per application requirements.

name: Sulfuric acid
description:
Sulfuric acid (CAS 7664-93-9 ), also known historically as oil of vitriol and approved as E513 in food-grade applications, is one of the most produced industrial chemicals globally.

It functions as a strong mineral acid used across manufacturing, processing, and treatment operations where acidification, catalysis, or chemical synthesis is required for various industrial outputs.

In fertilizer production, it converts phosphate rock into superphosphate and reacts with ammonia to produce ammonium sulfate, making it the backbone of agricultural chemical manufacturing.

Petroleum refining operations rely on it to alkylate hydrocarbons and remove impurities from fuels and lubricants. Metal processing and mining use it for ore leaching and pickling steel surfaces.

Electroplating baths require precise acid concentration to determine process yield. Water treatment and pH regulation applications consume significant volumes for neutralizing alkaline effluents.

Sulfuric acid is supplied as a liquid in concentrations typically ranging from 93% to 98% for industrial use, with dilute grades available for specific process requirements in manufacturing.

Standard commercial grades include technical, battery, and reagent specifications, alongside food-grade E513 for permitted food processing uses across the global supply chain.

It is transported in bulk tankers, intermediate bulk containers (IBCs), and drums depending on volume and concentration requirements to ensure safe delivery to industrial facilities.

name: Benzophenone-9
description:
Benzophenone-9 (CAS 76656-36-5 ) is a water-soluble UV absorber that protects formulations and substrates from UV-induced degradation. Its water solubility distinguishes it from most benzophenone-class absorbers.

This unique property makes it suitable for aqueous systems where oil-soluble alternatives cannot be used. In personal care and cosmetics, it functions as a UV filter in water-based sunscreens, lotions, and hair care products.

It is particularly effective where broad-spectrum UVA protection is required. Coatings and ink formulators incorporate it into aqueous coating systems and printing inks to prevent photodegradation of colorants and binders.

This is especially useful in packaging applications where light exposure is a concern. Water-based adhesives and sealants benefit from its stabilizing effect, extending the service life of bonded substrates.

These materials are often exposed to outdoor or fluorescent light during use. It is also used in textile treatment formulations to protect dyed fabrics from UV fading and maintain color integrity over time.

The product is supplied as a powder or as a concentrated aqueous solution, depending on the supplier and application requirements. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications for personal care.

These grades meet regulatory requirements for use across major global markets. Technical-grade material is sourced for industrial coating, ink, and adhesive applications requiring high performance and stability.

name: Potassium iodide
description:
Potassium iodide (CAS 7681-11-0 ), commonly abbreviated as KI, is an inorganic iodine salt supplied across pharmaceutical, food, and industrial markets. It functions primarily as an iodine source and a catalyst precursor.

This versatile chemical serves as a stabilizing agent in formulations where controlled iodide delivery is required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, KI is used to compound thyroid-blocking preparations and expectorant syrups.

It appears in branded formulations such as Thyro-Block and Pima. Food and nutrition producers use it to fortify table salt and dietary supplements, meeting iodine supplementation requirements in regulated markets.

In chemical synthesis and catalysis, KI acts as a halide catalyst or reagent precursor in organic reactions. It is particularly useful in nucleophilic substitution processes and various industrial chemical syntheses.

Agricultural and feed applications include its use as a trace mineral supplement in animal feed formulations. This helps to correct iodine deficiencies in livestock and supports overall animal health and growth.

Potassium iodide is available as a white crystalline powder or granule. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade ( FCC ), ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is subject to strict purity and heavy metal limits. Technical-grade material is also supplied for industrial and catalytic applications where compendial certification is not required.

name: Sodium bisulfate
description:
Sodium bisulfate (CAS 7681-38-1 ), also sold as sodium acid sulfate, is a dry acid used across industrial and food-grade applications to lower pH and adjust acidity. It serves as a reliable replacement for liquid mineral acids in solid handling processes.

Its solid form makes it a practical alternative to sulfuric acid where liquid acids present handling or logistics challenges. In food processing, it functions as an acidulant and pH regulator in meat products and potato-based foods.

It is also utilized in dry blends where precise acidity control is required. Water treatment operations use it to reduce alkalinity and adjust pH in pools, municipal systems, and industrial effluent streams for better safety.

Metal finishing and mining operations apply it to pickle metal surfaces and dissolve oxide layers. It is also used to condition process water ahead of downstream treatment to ensure optimal chemical reactions and efficiency.

In cleaning formulations, it provides the acidic backbone for descalers, toilet bowl cleaners, and hard surface products. These applications specifically target mineral scale and rust deposits in industrial and domestic settings.

Sodium bisulfate is supplied as a dry granule or powder, with granular form preferred for bulk handling. This form helps in reducing dust exposure during dosing and ensures more consistent application in large-scale systems.

Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, supporting direct food contact applications. Technical grade is the standard for industrial cleaning, water treatment, and metal processing end uses across the globe.

name: Sodium fluoride
description:
Sodium fluoride (CAS 7681-49-4 ), also sold under the name Floridine, is an inorganic salt sourced for its biocidal, flux, and fluoridating properties across industrial and pharmaceutical supply chains.

NaF functions as a preservative, pH buffer, and fluoride source in applications ranging from water treatment to pharmaceutical manufacturing. In water treatment, NaF is dosed as a fluoridation agent.

This chemical is used to adjust fluoride levels in municipal drinking water systems. Pharmaceutical and oral care formulators use it as the active fluoride source in toothpaste, mouth rinse, and topical dental preparations.

In the textile, leather, and paper industries, it acts as a preservative and biocide to prevent microbial degradation during processing and storage. This ensures long-term stability for various raw materials.

Building and construction applications include its use as a flame retardant additive and wood preservative treatment against fungi and insects. It provides essential protection for structural components.

Sodium fluoride is available as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard supply grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications, alongside technical grade for industrial use.

Purity levels typically range from 97% technical grade up to 99%+ for pharmaceutical-grade material. These high standards ensure the product meets the rigorous demands of global chemical manufacturing.

name: Sodium hypochlorite
description:
Sodium hypochlorite (CAS 7681-52-9 ), commonly referenced as NaOCl or sodium oxychloride, is an inorganic oxidizing agent used across industrial, municipal, and institutional markets. It delivers broad-spectrum antimicrobial action and oxidative bleaching through controlled chlorine release in aqueous solution.

In water treatment, NaOCl is dosed into municipal and industrial systems to disinfect potable water, control biofilm in cooling towers, and sanitize wastewater effluent. Pulp and paper producers use it to bleach cellulose fibers, replacing or supplementing elemental chlorine.

These applications often utilize ECF and TCF bleaching sequences to ensure high-quality output. Food processing facilities apply it as a surface sanitizer and equipment disinfectant, where it meets food-contact safety requirements at regulated concentrations.

Textile and laundry operations rely on it to remove color from natural fibers and to formulate industrial-strength bleaching liquors. Sodium hypochlorite is supplied as an aqueous solution, with commercial concentrations typically ranging from 5% to 15% available chlorine.

The 12–15% range is considered the standard for industrial supply across most chemical sectors. Dilute 5% solutions are common in food-grade and institutional cleaning applications where lower concentrations are preferred for safety and handling.

Technical and food-grade designations are available, with product specifications aligned to standards such as ANSI/AWWA B300 for water treatment applications. This ensures the chemical meets rigorous safety and performance benchmarks for municipal use.

The material is also manufactured to meet various international quality standards including FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , and ACS where applicable. These certifications guarantee the purity and consistency required for sensitive industrial processes.

name: Sodium hypophosphite
description:
Sodium hypophosphite (CAS 7681-53-0 ), commercially abbreviated as SHP and also known as sodium phosphinate, is an inorganic phosphorus salt used industrially as a reducing agent and catalyst.

It is essential in electroless metal plating and polymer stabilization. Its reducing capacity drives controlled chemical reactions across multiple manufacturing sectors, ensuring high-performance results in industrial settings.

In electroless nickel plating, SHP acts as the primary reducing agent, enabling uniform metal deposition on complex or non-conductive substrates without an external electrical current. This is a critical process in electronics.

Automotive and aerospace component manufacturing also rely on this technology. Polymer producers use SHP as a catalyst and stabilizer in the production of polyamides, where it controls molecular weight and prevents discoloration.

In water treatment, it functions as a sequestrant to inhibit scale formation and metal ion interference in industrial cooling and boiler systems. This helps maintain the efficiency and longevity of heavy machinery.

Pharmaceutical and food-grade applications include its use as an antioxidant and preservative in formulations where phosphorus-based reduction chemistry is required. It ensures stability and safety in sensitive products.

Sodium hypophosphite is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as an aqueous solution, typically at 50% concentration. Recognized grades include technical, food-grade meeting FCC specifications, and pharmaceutical-grade.

These pharmaceutical grades often meet USP or BP standards. Bulk quantities are available in bags or drums, with solution grades commonly shipped in IBC containers for industrial logistics.

name: Sodium metabisulfite
description:
Sodium metabisulfite (CAS 7681-57-4 ), also known as sodium pyrosulfite and sold under the abbreviation SMBS, is an inorganic sulfite salt used across food, industrial, and water treatment sectors. It serves as a preservative, antioxidant, and reducing agent.

As E223 , it is a regulated food additive recognized in major international markets. Its ability to release sulfur dioxide under controlled conditions underpins its function across multiple industries and specialized chemical processes.

In food and beverage production, E223 prevents oxidative browning and microbial spoilage in dried fruits, wines, seafood, and fruit juices. This ensures product longevity and maintains the aesthetic quality of processed goods.

Water treatment plants use SMBS to neutralize residual chlorine in municipal and industrial effluent streams before discharge or further processing. This step is critical for environmental safety and protecting downstream equipment.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a bleaching and reducing agent in dye stripping and chrome tanning operations. It provides consistent results in heavy industrial manufacturing environments requiring high-purity chemical inputs.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an antioxidant stabilizer in injectable formulations and oral solutions. This is essential where oxygen-sensitive active ingredients require protection to maintain their therapeutic efficacy.

Sodium metabisulfite is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC -compliant), USP / BP pharmaceutical grade, and technical grade for industrial applications.

Bulk supply is available in 25 kg bags, with food and pharma grades accompanied by full compliance documentation. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery for large-scale manufacturing and chemical processing facilities worldwide.

name: Cuprous iodide
description:
Cuprous iodide (CAS 7681-65-4 ), also known as CuI and commercially as Marshite, is an inorganic copper salt used across pharmaceutical synthesis, catalysis, and antimicrobial applications.

Hydro-Giene is a recognized trade designation in hygiene and textile treatment contexts. Procurement demand spans multiple sectors where controlled copper(I) chemistry is required for industrial processes.

In pharmaceutical and fine chemical manufacturing, CuI is a primary catalyst and co-catalyst in Ullmann coupling reactions and Sonogashira cross-coupling. This enables the construction of complex organic molecules at scale.

Textile and technical fabric producers apply it as an antimicrobial agent, imparting durable biocidal properties to fibers and coatings. In personal care formulations, it functions as a surface-active antimicrobial component.

It is utilized in hygiene products where sustained microbial control is required. Salt iodization and nutritional fortification programs also source CuI as a stabilized iodine carrier in certain food-grade and feed applications.

Cuprous iodide is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical, reagent, and pharmaceutical-grade material, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.5%+.

Packaging is available in small laboratory quantities through to bulk industrial formats. Moisture-controlled packaging is standard due to light and humidity sensitivity to ensure the stability of the chemical compound.

name: Sodium iodide
description:
Sodium iodide (CAS 7681-82-5 ), commonly referenced as NaI, is an inorganic iodine salt used as an iodine source across pharmaceutical manufacturing, nutritional supplementation, and chemical synthesis.

It delivers bioavailable iodine in dosage forms and acts as a catalyst or reagent in organic reactions requiring halide exchange. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, NaI is used to produce iodine-containing active ingredients.

It serves as a source compound in thyroid-related drug formulations. The Finkelstein reaction, a standard halide exchange process in organic synthesis, relies on NaI to convert alkyl chlorides or bromides into alkyl iodides.

This makes it a routine reagent in fine chemical and API production. In animal feed and agricultural nutrition products, it functions as an iodine fortification agent to address iodine deficiency in livestock.

Food-grade NaI also serves as an iodine source in salt iodization programs and dietary supplement formulations targeting human nutritional requirements. Sodium iodide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules.

Recognized grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications, as well as food-grade specifications for nutritional and feed uses. Technical grade is available for industrial and synthesis applications.

name: Natamycin
description:
Natamycin (CAS 7681-93-8 ), also known as E235 , is a naturally derived antifungal agent produced by fermentation of Streptomyces natalensis. It is used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries primarily to inhibit mold and yeast growth.

This versatile compound works effectively without affecting bacteria or altering the sensory characteristics of the end product. In food manufacturing, it is applied as a surface treatment on hard and semi-hard cheeses and dry-cured meats.

It is also utilized in bakery products to extend shelf life by preventing fungal spoilage. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate the material into ophthalmic suspensions for the treatment of fungal keratitis, where it functions as the active ingredient.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it serves as a preservation booster, replacing or reducing synthetic preservatives in products such as creams and lotions. Beverage producers also use it to control yeast contamination in wine.

This application is particularly useful in fruit-based drinks as it does not impact fermentation profiles. The product is supplied as a fine white to cream-colored powder, typically in concentrations of 50 percent active content.

The material is often blended with lactose or glucose as a carrier for ease of use. Food-grade material is available to FCC specifications, ensuring high purity and safety for various industrial applications and consumer goods.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meets USP and Ph.Eur. standards for specialized medical use. Both grades are offered in bulk and smaller packaged formats to suit industrial and specialty formulation requirements for global clients.

name: Nitric acid
description:
Nitric acid (CAS 7697-37-2 ), also known as spirit of niter, is a strong inorganic acid and powerful oxidizing agent used across industrial chemistry for acidification and metal processing.

Its reactivity with metals and organic substrates makes it a primary feedstock in manufacturing rather than a specialty additive. In agriculture, it serves as a direct input for producing ammonium nitrate.

This links bulk acid procurement directly to crop nutrition supply chains. Metal finishing and electronics manufacturers use it to etch, passivate, and clean copper, stainless steel, and semiconductor substrates.

Pharmaceutical and fine chemical producers rely on the acid for nitration reactions that introduce nitro groups into active pharmaceutical intermediates. It is essential for complex chemical synthesis.

In mining and hydrometallurgy, it dissolves base and precious metals during leaching and refining operations. This versatility makes it a staple in heavy industrial and metallurgical processing facilities.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentrations of 68% and 98–100% being the most commercially traded grades. Technical grade is standard for most industrial use cases.

Higher-purity electronic and reagent grades are available for semiconductor and analytical applications. Bulk liquid delivery in tankers and IBC containers is the norm for industrial buyers.

name: Zinc bromide
description:
Zinc bromide (CAS 7699-45-8 ), commonly abbreviated as ZnBr2, is an inorganic salt sourced for its utility as a catalyst, electrolyte component, and high-density completion fluid across industrial and specialty chemical markets.

Buyers in pharmaceuticals, oil field services, and specialty synthesis recognize it as a distinct procurement item from other zinc halides. In oil and gas well completion, ZnBr2 solutions are formulated into high-density clear brine fluids.

These fluids are used to control wellbore pressure without solids. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a precursor or reagent in active ingredient synthesis where a soluble zinc salt is required for specific chemical reactions.

In organic synthesis and catalysis, it acts as a Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel-Crafts reactions and other electrophilic processes. Personal care and biocide formulators also incorporate it for preservation and surface-active functions.

These functions are essential in specific antimicrobial formulations. Zinc bromide is supplied as a white crystalline powder or as concentrated aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically ranging to meet oilfield brine density specifications.

Standard grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with the latter conforming to USP or BP specifications. Packaging options range from laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply depending on the application grade.

name: Gibberellic acid
description:
Gibberellic acid ( CAS 77-06-5 ), also known as GA3 or Gibberellin A3, is a plant growth regulator used commercially to control flowering, fruit development, and stem elongation in cultivated crops.

Sold under trade names such as Berelex and Brellin, it is one of the most widely sourced gibberellins in agricultural supply chains. In fruit production, GA3 is applied to table grapes to increase berry size.

It is also used to improve cluster looseness, directly affecting marketable yield and pack-out grades. Citrus growers use it to delay rind senescence, extending the post-harvest window for export markets.

Seed companies and cereal producers apply it to promote uniform germination and accelerate malting in barley processing. In specialty horticulture, it is used to break dormancy in ornamental bulbs.

It is also utilized to regulate flowering timing for commercial cut flower schedules. Gibberellic acid is supplied as a technical powder, water-soluble tablets, and concentrated liquid formulations.

Standard commercial grades include 90% technical powder and lower-concentration soluble granules formulated for direct field application. Purity specifications vary by intended use for the product.

Higher-purity grades are available for research and regulated agricultural programs. This chemical remains a staple for industrial agricultural suppliers and large-scale commercial farming operations globally.

name: Phenolphthalein
description:
Phenolphthalein (CAS 77-09-8 ) is a pH-sensitive indicator compound that transitions from colorless to vivid pink-red under alkaline conditions. This makes it a standard tool in titration and analytical chemistry.

In industrial settings, it functions as a colorimetric marker for detecting alkalinity in substrates, coatings, and treated surfaces. In the printing and packaging industry, indicator solutions are used to test paper substrates.

These tests ensure compatibility with inks and adhesives during the manufacturing process. Textile and leather processors apply it to verify the pH of dye baths, wash liquors, and various finishing treatments.

This verification is critical where residual alkali affects product quality. In concrete and construction material testing, it is the standard reagent for carbonation depth assessment on cut surfaces.

Sprayed solutions reveal the boundary between carbonated and uncarbonated zones. Personal care formulators use it as a bench-level QC tool to confirm the alkalinity of cream, soap, and hair relaxer formulations.

This ensures safety and consistency during development and production. The product is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline powder available in reagent-grade and ACS -grade specifications.

These grades are suited to laboratory and analytical applications, as well as technical grade for industrial process use. Pre-prepared indicator solutions at standard concentrations are also commercially available.

name: Ursolic acid
description:
Ursolic acid (CAS 77-52-1 ), also known as urson, prunol, and malol, is a pentacyclic triterpenoid acid extracted primarily from apple peel, rosemary, and holy basil. It functions as a bioactive ingredient and antioxidant stabilizer across pharmaceutical formulations and personal care products.

In topical cosmetic formulations, it is incorporated into anti-aging creams and serums where its antioxidant activity helps protect against oxidative degradation of the finished product. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reference compound and active botanical ingredient.

It is frequently utilized in standardized herbal extracts and nutraceutical capsules. In personal care, it acts as a surface-modifying agent in scalp treatments and conditioning formulations, where it influences film-forming behavior on skin and hair.

As a natural acidulant, it supports pH buffering in botanical-based emulsions requiring mild acid stabilization. This versatile compound is essential for manufacturers seeking high-performance natural additives for complex chemical systems.

Ursolic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in multiple purity grades, including 25%, 50%, 90%, and 98%+ HPLC-grade specifications, with higher purities targeting pharmaceutical and analytical applications.

Standard packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for formulators to bulk supply for industrial extraction and processing operations. Our material meets rigorous internal quality standards to ensure consistency across every batch delivered to your facility.

name: Dibutyltin dilaurate
description:
Dibutyltin dilaurate ( CAS 77-58-7 ), commonly abbreviated as DBTL and sold under trade names including Davainex and Tinostat, is an organotin compound used industrially as a catalyst and stabilizer.

It accelerates curing and crosslinking reactions in polymer systems while also providing thermal and oxidative stabilization during processing. In polyurethane manufacturing, DBTL catalyzes the isocyanate-hydroxyl reaction.

This process controls foam rise and gel times in flexible and rigid foam production. Silicone sealant and RTV formulations rely on it to achieve consistent cure rates at room temperature.

This makes it a standard catalyst choice for construction and automotive sealants. PVC compounders use it as a heat stabilizer to prevent degradation during extrusion and calendering of flexible profiles.

It is also utilized for films and wire coatings. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it functions as an antioxidant additive to extend fluid service life under high-temperature operating conditions.

Dibutyltin dilaurate is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically specified at 95% or higher for industrial use.

It is available in drum and IBC quantities, with specifications aligned to industrial polymer and coatings applications rather than food or pharmaceutical use cases.

name: Dimethylhydantoin
description:
Dimethylhydantoin ( CAS 77-71-4 ), commercially known as DMH or Dantoin DMH, is a cyclic urea derivative used across pharmaceutical, personal care, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a building block for active intermediates.

The compound acts as a buffering agent and a precursor in biocide synthesis. In personal care formulations, DMH is the backbone of DMDM hydantoin, a widely produced preservative system used in shampoos and skin care products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing hydantoin-derived APIs, where its ring structure enables controlled chemical modification. This versatility makes it essential for various medical applications.

In industrial water treatment and antimicrobial formulations, DMH serves as a precursor to halogenated hydantoins. These are chlorine- and bromine-releasing biocides used in cooling towers and pool sanitation systems.

Specialty chemical producers also use it as a pH buffer in reaction systems requiring stable mildly acidic conditions. This ensures consistent results during complex chemical manufacturing processes and industrial reactions.

Dimethylhydantoin is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with pharmaceutical-grade material available for API synthesis and regulated applications requiring high purity.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or fiber drums. Smaller packaging is also available for laboratory and development use to meet the specific needs of research facilities and small-scale production.

name: Dicyclopentadiene
description:
Dicyclopentadiene (CAS 77-73-6 ) is a cyclic diene monomer derived from the dimerization of cyclopentadiene. It serves as a reactive building block in resin and polymer synthesis across several industrial sectors.

In unsaturated polyester resins, DCPD is incorporated to reduce styrene content, improve surface quality, and lower resin cost. This makes it a standard raw material for fiberglass composites used in automotive and construction panels.

Hydrocarbon resin manufacturers use DCPD as a primary feedstock to produce C5/C9 resins applied in hot-melt adhesives, road-marking paints, and printing inks. These resins provide excellent tack and stability.

In the coatings and ink industry, DCPD-based resins contribute to fast-drying, high-gloss formulations for publication and packaging printing. It also functions as a monomer in ring-opening metathesis polymerization.

This process produces polydicyclopentadiene, a high-impact engineering material used in structural and industrial molded parts. The material is valued for its durability and resistance to chemical degradation.

DCPD is supplied as a liquid or solid depending on purity grade, with high-purity grades typically 95% and 99% available for polymer and specialty resin applications. Technical-grade material is standard for large-volume use.

It is commonly traded in bulk quantities, with drum and ISO tank packaging available for industrial buyers. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for all manufacturing requirements.

name: 2,2-dimethoxypropane

2,2-Dimethoxypropane (CAS 77-76-9 ), commonly known as DMP or acetone dimethyl acetal, is a reactive solvent and dehydrating agent used across pharmaceutical, biotech, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

name: Dimethyl sulfate
description:

Agrochemical producers rely on it to produce herbicides and pesticides where N- or O-methylation is a critical synthetic step. In the dye and textile industry, it methylates intermediates used in the production of cationic and reactive dyes.

Specialty chemical formulators also use DMS to produce quaternary ammonium compounds and methyl esters for use in surfactant and fragrance synthesis. This versatility makes it a staple reagent for complex organic synthesis and large-scale chemical production.

Dimethyl sulfate is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities suited to industrial consumption. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity typically at 99% or above for most industrial applications.

name: Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane
description:
Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane (CAS 77-86-1 ), commonly known as Tris or Tromethamine, is an organic amine base used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and life science manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffering and neutralizing agent.

This versatile compound maintains stable pH conditions in formulations and biological systems where precise control is critical. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Tromethamine is used to neutralize acidic drug substances and as a buffering agent.

It is frequently utilized in injectable formulations, ophthalmic solutions, and topical preparations. Cosmetic formulators use Tris to adjust and stabilize pH in creams, gels, and emulsions, particularly where carbomer polymers require neutralization.

Biotechnology and life science applications rely on Tris buffers, most notably Tris-HCl, as the standard medium for DNA/RNA electrophoresis. It is also essential for protein extraction and cell lysis protocols in laboratory settings.

The material functions as a preservative booster in certain personal care systems, enhancing the efficacy of primary preservatives at controlled pH ranges. This makes it a valuable additive for long-term product stability.

Tris(hydroxymethyl)aminomethane is supplied as a white crystalline powder. It is available in USP , Ph.Eur. , and BP grades for pharmaceutical use, as well as high-purity molecular biology grades for research.

These specialized grades meet specific electrophoresis and buffer preparation standards. Technical grade is also available for industrial pH adjustment applications where high-purity pharmaceutical standards are not required.

name: Citric acid

Citric acid (CAS 77-92-9 ), also designated E330 in food and beverage applications, is a multi-functional organic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial sectors.

Water treatment operations use it to sequester calcium and heavy metal ions. This prevents scale formation in industrial systems and cleaning-in-place circuits, ensuring efficient maintenance of high-value equipment.

description:
Trimethylolpropane ( CAS 77-99-6 ), commonly abbreviated as TMP, is a trifunctional aliphatic alcohol used as a building block in polymer synthesis and resin manufacturing.

Its three hydroxyl groups enable controlled cross-linking and branching, making it a core raw material for producing durable, high-performance polymer networks across coatings and adhesives.

In coatings, TMP reacts with isocyanates or melamine resins to produce polyurethane and alkyd systems with improved hardness, flexibility, and chemical resistance for industrial use.

Adhesive and sealant formulators use it to build polyurethane prepolymers where controlled cross-link density directly affects bond strength and elasticity in various applications.

In plastics, TMP serves as a branching agent in polyester and polycarbonate production, influencing molecular weight distribution and end-product mechanical performance for manufacturers.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a humectant and stabilizer in emollient systems and film-forming preparations to ensure product stability and performance in consumer goods.

TMP is supplied as white crystalline flakes or powder, with molten liquid form available for bulk industrial supply. Standard commercial grades include technical and industrial purity levels.

These grades are typically at 99%+ purity. Specialty grades meeting stricter quality specifications are available for cosmetic and high-performance polymer applications in the global market.

name: Phenoxyisopropanol
description:
Phenoxyisopropanol (CAS 770-35-4 ), also sold as Propylene Glycol Phenyl Ether, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether solvent with broad utility across coatings, personal care, and adhesive formulations.

Its low volatility and coupling efficiency make it a practical choice for formulators managing solvent balance and preservation performance simultaneously. In waterborne coatings and architectural paints, it functions as a coalescing aid.

It acts as a coupling solvent, improving film formation without the regulatory burden of conventional glycol ethers. Personal care formulators incorporate it as both a solvent carrier and a preservative booster.

This is particularly useful in rinse-off and leave-on products where broad-spectrum antimicrobial support is required. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to adjust viscosity and improve substrate wetting in water-based systems.

It also serves as a co-solvent in industrial cleaning formulations where controlled evaporation rate and compatibility with surfactant systems are priorities. The material is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the sourcing requirements of both personal care and industrial buyers. Purity levels are typically 99% or higher for cosmetic applications.

name: Sulfur
description:
Sulfur (CAS 7704-34-9 ), also known historically as brimstone or sulphur, is a naturally occurring non-metallic element supplied in refined form for industrial and agricultural use.

It functions as a vulcanizing agent, fungicide, and chemical intermediate across a broad range of manufacturing and crop protection applications. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it is the primary cross-linking agent.

During vulcanization, it forms the polymer bridges that give rubber its mechanical strength and elasticity. Agricultural formulators use it as a contact fungicide and acaricide in crop protection products.

These products target powdery mildew and mite infestations. In mining and metallurgy, it is a feedstock for sulfuric acid production, which drives ore leaching and metal refining operations.

Textile and leather processors use sulfur-based compounds for fiber bleaching, hide preservation, and wastewater treatment. It is available as bright yellow powder, prilled granules, and crushed lump forms.

Each form is suited to different handling and dosing requirements. Standard grades include agricultural-grade, rubber-grade, and technical-grade, with refined grades meeting pharmaceutical specifications.

Purity levels typically range from 90% agricultural grade up to 99.9%+ for refined industrial and pharmaceutical applications. This ensures high performance across diverse chemical synthesis processes.

name: Erythromycin thiocyanate
description:
Erythromycin thiocyanate (CAS 7704-67-8 ), also marketed under the trade name ERYTROVET, is the thiocyanate salt form of the macrolide antibiotic erythromycin. It is used across pharmaceutical, veterinary, and agricultural sectors primarily for its antibacterial activity.

The compound is effective against gram-positive organisms and select gram-negative pathogens. In veterinary medicine, it is formulated into oral and injectable preparations for the treatment of bacterial infections in livestock and poultry.

These applications include the management of respiratory and enteric diseases. Agricultural feed manufacturers incorporate it as an antimicrobial feed additive to control bacterial disease burden in commercial poultry and swine operations.

Pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis or salt-screening stages of erythromycin-based drug development. It also serves research and fermentation process applications where a stable salt form is required.

This material is essential for microbiological assay work and specialized laboratory studies. Erythromycin thiocyanate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder available in technical and veterinary-grade specifications.

Purity levels are typically confirmed by HPLC to ensure compliance with industrial requirements. Bulk quantities are standard for feed additive and pharmaceutical intermediate procurement for large-scale manufacturing needs.

Smaller research quantities are also available for biotech and laboratory applications. The product maintains stability and efficacy when stored under appropriate conditions according to standard chemical handling protocols.

name: Potassium fumarate
description:
Potassium fumarate ( CAS 7704-72-5 ), also known by its food additive designation E366 , is the potassium salt of fumaric acid used commercially as a pH buffer and acidulant. Dipotassium fumarate offers a milder acidic profile than free fumaric acid.

This makes it suitable for applications where controlled acidity and potassium fortification are both priorities. In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as an acidulant and pH regulator in soft drinks and powdered drink mixes.

It is also used in fruit-flavored products where tartness control is critical. Bakery and confectionery producers use it to adjust dough pH and improve texture consistency in finished products to ensure high quality standards.

In pharmaceutical formulations, potassium fumarate serves as a buffering agent in oral solid dosage forms and effervescent preparations. These applications require stable pH and potassium content as essential formulation requirements.

It also appears in dietary supplement blends as a potassium source combined with fumarate anion delivery. Potassium fumarate is typically supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial and commercial uses.

Food-grade material conforming to E366 specifications is the most commonly traded form. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available to USP or BP standards for highly regulated applications and manufacturing processes.

Bulk supply is standard for industrial buyers, with smaller packaging available for formulation and QA sampling purposes. This ensures that manufacturers can meet their specific production needs while maintaining strict quality control.

name: Sodium fumarate
description:
Sodium fumarate (CAS 7704-73-6 ), also known by the E-number E365 , is the disodium salt of fumaric acid used commercially as an acidulant and pH buffering agent. It delivers controlled acidity and flavor modification across food and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

This compound provides effective results without the handling concerns associated with free organic acids. In food production, it functions as an acidulant and flavor enhancer in dry beverage mixes and bakery products.

It is particularly useful in processed foods where precise pH control affects shelf life and taste profile. It is also used in pharmaceutical formulations as a buffering agent to stabilize active ingredients and maintain target pH ranges.

The compound appears in oral rehydration and electrolyte formulations, where its salt form supports palatability and ionic balance. Mafusol-based clinical fluid formulations have historically referenced it as a functional component.

Sodium fumarate is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial uses. Food-grade material is available to E365 specification for use in regulated food applications, ensuring safety and compliance.

Pharmaceutical-grade supply meets USP and Ph. Eur. standards where required for medical applications. Bulk quantities are standard for industrial procurement, with packaging options ranging from bags to multi-tonne quantities.

name: Ferric chloride
description:
Ferric chloride (CAS 7705-08-0 ), also known commercially as iron trichloride, is an inorganic iron salt used across water treatment, metal processing, and chemical synthesis. It functions primarily as a coagulant, etchant, and catalyst depending on the application sector.

In municipal and industrial water treatment, ferric chloride precipitates suspended solids and phosphates, making it a standard coagulant-flocculant for effluent clarification. This process is essential for meeting environmental discharge regulations.

PCB manufacturers and metal fabricators use it as an etchant to selectively dissolve copper and other metals with controlled precision. This chemical milling process is vital for high-accuracy electronic component production.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a mordant to fix dyes and improve color fastness on natural fibers. This ensures that pigments remain stable and vibrant throughout the lifecycle of the finished material.

In chemical synthesis and pharmaceutical manufacturing, it acts as a Lewis acid catalyst for Friedel-Crafts reactions and other electrophilic processes. Its reactivity makes it a versatile tool for complex organic transformations.

Ferric chloride is supplied as an anhydrous solid, hexahydrate crystals, or as a liquid solution. It is typically provided at 40–45% concentration for large-scale water treatment and industrial applications.

Standard grades include technical, industrial, and reagent-grade specifications to meet the requirements of different end uses. These grades ensure the material meets specific purity levels for sensitive laboratory or manufacturing work.

Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or tankers is common for large-scale water treatment procurement. Solid forms are also available in bags or drums to accommodate various storage and handling preferences.

name: Nickel Dichloride
description:
Nickel Dichloride (CAS 7718-54-9 ) is an inorganic nickel salt used across electroplating, catalysis, and surface treatment industries. It is a primary source of soluble nickel ion, enabling controlled deposition and chemical reactivity.

In electroplating and metal finishing, it serves as a key electrolyte component in nickel plating baths. It delivers consistent coating hardness and corrosion resistance on metal substrates for demanding industrial processes.

Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant to fix dyes onto fibers and hides, improving color fastness and uniformity. In chemical synthesis, it functions as a catalyst precursor for cross-coupling reactions.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing utilizes this compound for various hydrogenation processes. Biotechnology and life sciences applications include its use as a reagent in enzyme inhibition studies and specialized research.

It is also employed in nickel-affinity chromatography systems for protein purification. Nickel Dichloride is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as the hexahydrate form, with the hexahydrate being the more common grade.

Standard supply grades include technical and laboratory-reagent purity levels. Concentrations are typically specified at 98% or higher to meet rigorous industrial and scientific requirements for consistency.

Bulk quantities are available for industrial buyers, with smaller pack sizes offered for laboratory and specialty formulation use. This ensures flexibility for both large-scale manufacturing and small-scale research.

name: Vanadium trichloride
description:
Vanadium trichloride (CAS 7718-98-1 ) is an inorganic vanadium salt used primarily as a catalyst precursor in industrial chemical synthesis. It delivers active vanadium(III) centers that initiate and control polymerization reactions.

This compound serves as a critical building block for Ziegler-Natta and related coordination catalyst systems. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it is used to produce ethylene-propylene copolymers like EPM and EPDM rubbers.

Precise catalyst activity directly affects molecular weight distribution and product consistency in these materials. It also serves as a precursor for generating vanadium-based homogeneous catalysts used in olefin polymerization.

This is particularly important where narrow polydispersity is required for high-performance applications. Beyond polymers, it functions as a starting material for synthesizing other vanadium compounds and coordination complexes.

These complexes are frequently used in specialty chemical research and catalyst development programs. Vanadium trichloride is supplied as a solid powder, typically in anhydrous form to preserve its chemical reactivity.

Technical and research grades are the most commonly available, with purity specifications generally ranging from 97% upward. Packaging is moisture-sensitive, so it is typically offered in sealed, inert-atmosphere containers.

These specialized storage solutions are suited for industrial and laboratory procurement needs. The material must be handled with care to maintain its integrity and performance during the chemical manufacturing process.

name: Thionyl chloride
description:
Thionyl chloride (CAS 7719-09-7 ), also known as sulfurous oxychloride and commonly referenced by its formula SOCl2, is a reactive chlorinating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis and specialty chemical manufacturing.

It converts carboxylic acids, alcohols, and other functional groups into their corresponding acid chlorides or chlorinated derivatives, enabling downstream reactions that would otherwise require more complex reagents.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, SOCl2 is a preferred reagent for producing acid chlorides as activated intermediates in API synthesis, where reaction efficiency and yield directly affect production economics.

Agrochemical producers rely on it to chlorinate precursor compounds during the manufacture of herbicides, insecticides, and fungicide active ingredients for the global agricultural market.

It also functions as a dehydrating agent in the preparation of sulfonyl chlorides and other specialty intermediates used in dye and fine chemical production across various industrial sectors.

Battery electrolyte formulations, particularly in lithium-thionyl chloride primary cells, represent a distinct industrial application where SOCl2 acts as both solvent and active cathode material.

Thionyl chloride is supplied as a fuming liquid, typically in drums, ISO tanks, or cylinders depending on volume requirements. Technical and synthesis-grade specifications are standard across the market.

Purity levels commonly range from 97% to 99%+ for pharmaceutical and fine chemical applications, ensuring high performance and consistency for demanding chemical synthesis and manufacturing processes.

name: Ferrous sulfate
description:
Ferrous sulfate (CAS 7720-78-7 ) is an inorganic iron salt supplied as a heptahydrate or anhydrous form, used across water treatment, agriculture, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an iron source, reducing agent, and precipitating agent in industrial processes. In municipal water treatment, it acts as a coagulant and phosphate precipitant.

This chemical helps remove impurities and control algae in reservoirs. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as the active iron source in oral iron-deficiency supplements and fortified food products.

In agriculture, it corrects iron chlorosis in soils and turf, and serves as a moss control agent in lawn care formulations. Mining operations apply it in hydrometallurgical processes.

Applications include the precipitation of metals from leach solutions and as a reducing agent in chromate treatment of effluent. It is available as a heptahydrate in granular or crystalline form.

The product is also offered as a dried or anhydrous powder with lower water content for applications requiring reduced moisture. Recognized grades include USP , BP , and food-grade ( FCC ).

These standards ensure suitability for pharmaceutical and nutritional use, alongside technical and agricultural grades for industrial supply. Bulk availability supports high-volume procurement.

Packaging options include bags, supersacks, and bulk tanker quantities. This ensures reliable distribution across all major end-use sectors for global manufacturing and processing needs.

name: Potassium permanganate
description:
Potassium permanganate (CAS 7722-64-7 ), also known commercially as Condy's crystals, is a strong inorganic oxidizing agent used across municipal, industrial, and pharmaceutical applications.

It delivers controlled oxidation for disinfection, odor control, and chemical treatment processes where consistent reactivity and purity are critical sourcing requirements for global manufacturers.

In water treatment, it oxidizes dissolved iron, manganese, and hydrogen sulfide, enabling their removal before filtration. This is a standard step in both municipal and industrial water conditioning systems.

Textile and paper manufacturers use it as a bleaching agent to achieve uniform whitening of fibers and pulp without the residue concerns associated with chlorine-based alternatives.

Mining operations apply it in effluent treatment to neutralize cyanide-bearing wastewater before discharge. Pharmaceutical compounders rely on its biocidal activity for antiseptic preparations.

Potassium permanganate is supplied as dark purple crystalline granules or powder. Technical grade is standard for water treatment and industrial oxidation applications across various sectors.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications is available for healthcare and compounding use. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk supersacks.

name: Monoammonium phosphate
description:
Monoammonium phosphate (CAS 7722-76-1 ), commonly known as MAP or designated E342 in food applications, is an inorganic ammonium salt used industrially as a flame retardant and pH buffering agent.

It delivers both nitrogen and phosphorus in a single compound, making it a practical input across agriculture, construction, and industrial processing. In agriculture, MAP is a high-analysis fertilizer applied directly to soil.

It can be dissolved for fertigation, supplying phosphorus and nitrogen in plant-available form. Flame retardant formulations for textiles, paper, and cellulosic materials rely on MAP to interrupt combustion at the fiber level.

This helps in meeting fire safety specifications in treated fabrics and packaging. In construction, it is incorporated into intumescent coatings and fire-retardant board treatments where controlled char formation is required.

Buffer solutions and pH adjustment processes in leather processing and industrial manufacturing also use MAP to maintain consistent process conditions. Monoammonium phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

Granular forms predominate in agricultural supply chains. Standard grades include technical, food-grade, and fertilizer-grade, each carrying distinct purity and contaminant thresholds for various industrial uses.

Agricultural MAP is typically specified at 11-52 (11% N, 52% P₂O₅) and is available in bulk, supersack, and bagged formats. These options ensure flexibility for large-scale industrial and agricultural operations.

name: Hydrogen peroxide
description:
Hydrogen peroxide (CAS 7722-84-1 ), commonly abbreviated as H2O2, is an oxidizing agent and bleaching compound used across industrial, food-grade, and pharmaceutical supply chains.

It functions as a disinfectant, bleach, and chemical intermediate depending on concentration and application sector. In pulp, paper, and textile processing, it is the primary bleaching agent.

It brightens fibers without the chlorine residues that complicate downstream effluent management. Water treatment facilities use it to oxidize organic contaminants and break down biofilm.

It supports advanced oxidation processes alongside ozone or UV systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into hair bleaching and tooth-whitening products for active oxygen release.

In food processing and pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a surface and equipment sterilant. This is critical in aseptic packaging lines and cleanroom environments.

Hydrogen peroxide is supplied as an aqueous solution in concentrations typically ranging from 3% to 70%. The 35%, 50%, and 60% solutions are the most common industrial grades.

Food-grade and USP specifications are available for applications requiring purity documentation in regulated environments. These standards ensure safety for sensitive manufacturing.

name: Tetrasodium pyrophosphate
description:
Tetrasodium pyrophosphate ( CAS 7722-88-5 ), commonly known as TSPP or designated E450(iii) in food applications, is an inorganic phosphate salt used across food processing, industrial cleaning, and construction sectors.

It functions primarily as a sequestrant, buffering agent, and dispersant, controlling metal ions and pH in complex formulations. In food manufacturing, TSPP acts as an emulsifying salt in processed cheese.

It also serves as a moisture-retention agent in seafood and meat products. Detergent and industrial cleaning formulators use it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, preventing scale buildup and improving surfactant performance.

In hard-water conditions, it enhances cleaning efficiency. In cement and construction materials, it serves as a dispersant and set retarder, improving workability of cementitious mixes during the application process.

Water treatment operations apply TSPP to control metal ion precipitation and inhibit scale formation in process water systems. This ensures the longevity and efficiency of industrial piping and equipment.

Tetrasodium pyrophosphate is supplied as a white anhydrous powder or granules. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant) and technical-grade for various industrial applications and manufacturing needs.

Buyers sourcing for food or regulated end uses should confirm compliance with relevant regional food additive specifications. This ensures the material meets the necessary safety and quality requirements for the market.

name: Phosphorus
description:
Phosphorus (CAS 7723-14-0 ), commonly supplied in its red or amorphous form, is a reactive non-metallic element used as a base material in flame retardant systems and specialty chemical synthesis.

It serves as a precursor to phosphoric acid, phosphine, and a broad range of organophosphorus compounds that underpin industrial fire protection and materials processing across various sectors.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, amorphous phosphorus is incorporated into intumescent and halogen-free flame retardant formulations for engineering resins, cable jacketing, and electronic housings.

The electronics industry relies on phosphorus-derived compounds for flame retardant printed circuit board laminates and semiconductor dopant applications to ensure safety and performance standards.

Aerospace and defense sectors source it for pyrotechnic compositions and smoke-generating agents used in signaling and obscurant systems, requiring high reliability and specific chemical properties.

In mining and metals processing, it functions as a reducing agent and alloying additive to modify steel and cast iron properties, enhancing the durability and strength of the final metal products.

Amorphous (red) phosphorus is the standard commercial form, supplied as a fine powder or stabilized granules to reduce reactivity during handling and transport for safer industrial operations.

Technical and industrial grades are the primary market offerings, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99.9% depending on end-use requirements and specific manufacturing protocols.

name: Bromine
description:
Bromine (CAS 7726-95-6 ) is a halogen element supplied in liquid form and used industrially as a powerful oxidizing and biocidal agent. It serves as a foundational raw material across pharmaceutical synthesis and agrochemical production.

The material is also essential for water treatment and oilfield chemistry. In water treatment and cooling systems, bromine functions as a broad-spectrum biocide, controlling algae, bacteria, and biofilm effectively.

It operates at lower concentrations than chlorine across a wider pH range. Oilfield operators use brominated compounds derived from elemental bromine in completion fluids and as hydrogen sulfide scavengers in drilling operations.

Pharmaceutical and agrochemical manufacturers rely on bromine as a key brominating agent in the synthesis of active ingredients, intermediates, and crop protection compounds for global distribution.

Industrial bleaching operations also utilize bromine-based chemistry for textile and fiber processing where selective oxidation is required. This versatility makes it a critical component in modern chemical manufacturing.

Bromine is supplied as a dense, dark reddish-brown liquid in bulk quantities, typically in lead-lined or corrosion-resistant steel drums, IBCs, and ISO tank containers for safe transport.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-purity grades meeting specifications for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical synthesis. Buyers should confirm purity levels and packaging compatibility.

Regional transport compliance is vital when evaluating supply options. Ensure all safety protocols are met for this hazardous material to maintain operational integrity and regulatory adherence during procurement.
