name: Potassium persulfate
description:
Potassium persulfate (CAS 7727-21-1 ), also known by the abbreviation KPS and the food additive designation E922 , is an inorganic oxidizing agent used across polymer manufacturing and bleaching operations.

Potassium peroxodisulfate is the preferred IUPAC-aligned term recognized in European technical and regulatory contexts, while Anthion appears in some legacy industrial references for surface treatment processes.

In emulsion and suspension polymerization, KPS acts as a free-radical initiator for producing acrylic, styrene-butadiene, and vinyl acetate-based polymers at controlled reaction temperatures.

Hair bleaching and color formulations in the personal care industry rely on it to activate oxidative lightening without requiring high-temperature processing during the application phase.

Textile and paper producers use it to bleach fibers and pulp, improving whiteness and surface uniformity before dyeing or coating. In water treatment, it functions as an oxidant for organic contaminants.

It also serves as a persulfate-based activator in advanced oxidation processes. Potassium persulfate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule for various industrial and commercial uses.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial polymerization and bleaching, as well as food-grade material conforming to E922 specifications for permitted food applications.

Purity levels typically range from 99% and above for technical and high-purity grades. This ensures consistent performance across sensitive chemical reactions and large-scale manufacturing workflows.

name: Liquid nitrogen
description:
Liquid nitrogen (CAS 7727-37-9 ), also supplied as a cryogenic gas and regulated as E941 in food applications, is produced by fractional distillation of air. It is used industrially as an ultra-low-temperature refrigerant and inert blanketing agent.

Its primary commercial function is rapid cooling, freezing, and cryogenic preservation across food processing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and life sciences. In food production, it enables cryogenic tunnel freezing of meat, seafood, and baked goods.

This method delivers faster freeze rates than mechanical systems while reducing product dehydration loss. Pharmaceutical and biotech operations rely on it for cryopreservation of cell lines, biological samples, and vaccines.

It is essential for API intermediates requiring storage below −150°C. Electronics and semiconductor manufacturers use it to purge process chambers and cool components during precision machining. It also maintains inert atmospheres during sensitive fabrication steps.

In beverage and packaging lines, it is injected into containers before sealing to displace oxygen and extend shelf life. Liquid nitrogen is supplied in bulk dewars, ISO tanks, and cryogenic cylinders, with delivery formats scaled to site volumes.

Food-grade supply conforming to E941 specifications and industrial-grade product are the standard commercial distinctions. Purity levels typically range from 99.998% for high-purity applications to standard industrial grades.

Supply chain options include on-site generation systems for high-volume users. This ensures a consistent supply for critical manufacturing processes and large-scale industrial cooling requirements across various global sectors.

name: Barium sulfate
description:
Barium sulfate (CAS 7727-43-7 ), also sold as blanc fixe in its precipitated form, is an inorganic mineral used across coatings, plastics, and industrial manufacturing as a dense, chemically inert filler and opacifying agent.

Its combination of high specific gravity and near-zero reactivity makes it a preferred functional filler where brightness, weight, and chemical resistance all factor into material selection for various industrial applications.

In coatings and paints, this compound improves surface gloss, film hardness, and opacity without interfering with pigment systems. It is particularly effective in automotive primers and high-end decorative finishes.

Plastics compounders incorporate it as a weighting and stiffening filler in polypropylene, PVC, and engineering polymers. It is essential where dimensional stability and X-ray opacity are required for the final product.

The pharmaceutical and medical imaging sectors use high-purity grades as a radiocontrast agent in gastrointestinal diagnostic procedures. It functions as an inert extender filler that maintains compound viscosity in rubber.

Barium sulfate is available as a fine white powder in both precipitated and natural grades. Standard specifications include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical applications and medical use.

Technical and coating grades are differentiated by particle size and brightness. Precipitated grades offer tighter particle size distribution and higher purity, while natural grades are used in industrial and construction applications.

name: Ammonium persulfate
description:
Ammonium persulfate (CAS 7727-54-0 ), also known as APS and approved as E923 , is a strong inorganic oxidizer used across polymer manufacturing, electronics processing, and surface treatment industries.

Its high oxidizing potential makes it effective as a polymerization initiator, bleaching agent, and etchant across a broad range of industrial processes. In plastics and polymer production, APS initiates free-radical polymerization.

It is used for acrylic, styrene, and vinyl-based monomers, forming the backbone of emulsion and suspension polymerization systems. Printed circuit board manufacturers rely on it as a microetchant to clean copper surfaces.

This process ensures consistent adhesion in multilayer board fabrication by roughening surfaces before plating. Textile and paper processors use it to bleach natural fibers and pulp, removing color bodies effectively.

The chemical works without degrading substrate integrity during the bleaching process. In water treatment, it functions as an oxidizing agent to break down organic contaminants and support advanced oxidation processes.

Ammonium persulfate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial applications and food-grade material meeting specific regulatory requirements.

name: Sodium tetraphosphate
description:
Sodium tetraphosphate (CAS 7727-67-5 ) is a condensed phosphate salt used across industrial and food-grade applications for its ability to sequester metal ions and buffer pH levels.

It modifies the behavior of mineral suspensions and is distinct from the more common STPP, occupying a specific niche where higher-chain phosphate chemistry is required for performance.

In water treatment, it controls scale formation and stabilizes metal ions in distribution systems, effectively reducing fouling in pipelines and industrial equipment during long-term operation.

Textile, leather, and paper processors use it to sequester hardness ions in process water, preventing interference with dyes, tanning agents, and various chemical fiber treatments.

In food manufacturing, it functions as a sequestrant and buffering agent in processed formulations where mineral control affects the final texture and overall shelf stability of the product.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it to enhance detergent performance by binding calcium and magnesium ions that would otherwise reduce surfactant efficiency in hard water.

Sodium tetraphosphate is typically supplied as a white powder or granule. Technical grade is the most common commercial form, with food-grade material available for direct food contact.

Buyers should confirm chain length and purity specifications with suppliers, as condensed phosphate products vary in composition across different production sources and manufacturing methods.

Water (CAS 7732-18-5 ), also supplied as purified water or distilled water, is the foundational solvent and carrier medium across virtually every manufacturing and processing industry.

It dissolves, dilutes, suspends, and transports active ingredients in formulations ranging from pharmaceutical preparations to industrial cleaning concentrates used in various sectors.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, purified water meets strict compendial standards as a process solvent, excipient diluent, and equipment rinse medium for high-level production.

Food and beverage producers use it as a direct ingredient, process water, and carrier for flavors, colorants, and functional additives to ensure consistent product quality and safety.

Industrial and household cleaning formulations rely on water as the primary carrier to deliver surfactants, builders, and disinfectants at specific working concentrations for effective use.

Water treatment operations consume large volumes for diluting treatment chemicals, preparing dosing solutions, and calibrating analytical systems to maintain strict environmental compliance.

Supplied as a liquid in bulk tankers, IBCs, and drums, with grades ranging from technical and demineralized to food-grade and compendial specifications for diverse industrial applications.

Textile and leather processors apply it during dyeing and tanning operations to fix colorants and control microbial growth in process baths. Pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in ophthalmic solutions and astringent formulations.

name: Chromic acid

Chromic acid (CAS 7738-94-5 ) is a strong inorganic oxidizing acid used primarily in metal surface treatment and industrial finishing operations. In practice, it exists as an aqueous solution of chromium trioxide and is sourced and handled in that form by most industrial buyers.

Anodizing operations for aluminum use chromic acid electrolyte processes where a thin, corrosion-resistant oxide layer is required. This is particularly critical in specialized aerospace and defense applications.

In the textile and leather industries, it functions as an oxidizing bleach and surface modifier. This improves dye uptake and prepares fiber substrates for various types of downstream processing.

Mining and metals operations use it in passivation treatments to protect metal surfaces against oxidation during storage and transit. This ensures the integrity of the metal before it reaches the end user.

Chromic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with chromium trioxide dissolved in water to produce the active acid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for most industrial applications.

Concentration is typically specified by the buyer according to specific process requirements. Industrial supply is subject to regulatory controls in many jurisdictions due to hexavalent chromium content.

Buyers should confirm compliance documentation alongside standard quality specifications. Proper handling and storage protocols must be maintained to ensure safety and environmental protection during use.

name: 2-(2-ethoxyethoxy)acetic acid
description:
2-(2-Ethoxyethoxy)acetic acid (CAS 7743-94-4 ) is a glycol ether-derived organic acid used as a reactive solvent and pH modifier in specialty chemical formulations.

Its ether-acid structure allows it to function simultaneously as a carrier and a buffering agent, reducing the need for separate additive systems in complex industrial processes.

In coatings and adhesives, it improves resin compatibility and aids in pH adjustment of waterborne systems, helping formulators meet application viscosity and stability targets.

Textile and leather processors use it as a processing aid where controlled acidity and solvent action are needed in dyeing or finishing baths for consistent results.

Industrial and institutional cleaning formulations incorporate it to enhance soil solubilization while maintaining a stable pH profile across various dilution ranges.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface treatment processes where both wetting and mild acidic conditioning are required to ensure high-quality finished products.

2-(2-Ethoxyethoxy)acetic acid is supplied as a liquid and is available primarily in technical grade, suited to industrial formulation and processing applications.

Packaging options typically range from drums to IBC containers, depending on volume requirements, ensuring safe transport and storage for large-scale manufacturing needs.

name: Glyceryl behenate
description:
Glyceryl behenate (CAS 77538-19-3 ), also sold under the trade name Compritol 888 ATO, is a mono-, di-, and triglyceride ester of behenic acid used as a lipid-based excipient.

It serves as a functional emulsifier across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing. Its high melting point makes it a preferred choice for solid-form processing and controlled-release matrix systems.

In pharmaceutical tablet and capsule manufacturing, it functions as a sustained-release matrix former and lubricant. This enables precise drug release profiles in various solid dosage forms.

Hot-melt extrusion and direct compression processes both rely on it to improve flow and reduce tablet sticking. This is achieved without compromising the dissolution properties of the final product.

In cosmetic formulations, it thickens and stabilizes emulsions in creams, lipsticks, and stick-format products. It is ideal where a waxy, structured texture is required for the application.

Food applications include fat-based coatings and confectionery fillings. In these uses, it modifies crystallization behavior and improves the overall shelf stability of the food products.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white waxy powder or flakes. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to specifications aligned with Ph.Eur. and NF monographs.

Compritol 888 ATO remains the most recognized commercial grade for these industries. Food-grade supply is also available for all applicable end-use categories and manufacturing needs.

name: Potassium nitrate
description:
Potassium nitrate ( CAS 7757-79-1 ), also known as saltpeter and sold under E252 in food applications, is an inorganic salt used across agriculture, food processing, and industrial sectors.

It functions primarily as an oxidizer, curing agent, and nitrogen source depending on the end application. In food and meat processing, E252 acts as a curing agent and preservative in products such as cured meats.

It is used in hard cheeses and charcuterie, controlling microbial growth and maintaining color stability. Agriculture relies on potassium nitrate as a water-soluble fertilizer delivering both nitrogen and potassium.

These nutrients are delivered directly to crops through fertigation and foliar spray systems. In the mining and explosives industry, it serves as an oxidizing component in blasting agents and pyrotechnic formulations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it in desensitizing toothpaste formulations and as an active ingredient in certain topical preparations. Potassium nitrate is available as white crystalline powder, prills, and granules.

These forms are suited to different handling and dosing requirements. Recognized grades include food-grade (E252), agricultural-grade, technical-grade, and USP / BP specifications for pharmaceutical applications.

Purity levels and particle size vary by grade, with high-purity pharmaceutical and food grades typically exceeding 99% assay. This ensures consistent performance across sensitive industrial and medical applications.

name: Sodium sorbate
description:
Sodium sorbate (CAS 7757-81-5 ), also known commercially as E201 , is the sodium salt form of sorbic acid used as a preservative in food and personal care products.

It inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria, extending shelf life across a broad range of formulations. In food manufacturing, it is used to preserve baked goods and dairy products.

This additive is ideal for beverages and processed foods where pH-neutral or mildly alkaline conditions favor the sodium salt over sorbic acid itself. It ensures stability in diverse environments.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and wet wipes as a preservative that performs effectively in higher-pH systems. It is also applied in wine and fruit-based products.

The compound prevents refermentation without significantly altering taste profiles. Cosmetic manufacturers sourcing alternatives to parabens increasingly evaluate it as part of preservation systems.

Sodium sorbate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, ensuring high purity for industrial food applications.

Cosmetic-grade supply aligns with standard purity requirements for personal care applications. Packaging typically ranges from small retail units to bulk bags suited for industrial procurement.

In detergent manufacturing, it acts as a filler and flow-control agent in powdered formulations, improving bulk density and dispensing consistency. Kraft pulp mills use it as a make-up chemical.

It is used in the sulfate pulping process to maintain the chemical balance of the recovery cycle. Textile dyeing operations rely on it to regulate dye uptake on cellulosic fibers, improving color uniformity.

In pharmaceutical solid-dose manufacturing, it serves as an excipient and desiccant component, supporting moisture control in tablet and powder formulations across various batch processes.

Sodium sulfate is supplied as a white anhydrous powder or granule, with the decahydrate form available for specific applications. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ) and industrial use.

name: Sodium sulfite
description:
Sodium sulfite (CAS 7757-83-7 ), also known as sodium sulphite and approved as food additive E221 , is an inorganic reducing agent and antioxidant used across food processing and water treatment.

Its oxygen-scavenging capability makes it a practical choice for preserving product quality and controlling oxidative degradation in both aqueous systems and dry formulations for industrial manufacturing.

In food and beverage production, E221 functions as a preservative and antioxidant in dried fruits, wines, and starch products, inhibiting browning and microbial growth during the storage process.

Water treatment operations use it to dechlorinate process water and boiler feedwater, neutralizing residual chlorine before discharge or reuse to protect sensitive equipment and the environment.

Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it in kraft and sulfite pulping processes to delignify wood fiber and control brightness. In textile and leather processing, it acts as a reducing agent.

It is also used as a stripping agent to correct uneven dyeing in dyebath preparation. Sodium sulfite is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules in the anhydrous form for easy handling.

Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E221), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , BP ), and technical-grade for industrial applications. Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities.

Magnesium hydrogen phosphate (CAS 7757-86-0 ), also known as dibasic magnesium phosphate or MDHP, is an inorganic salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications as a pH buffer and mineral source.

Its controlled solubility and buffering capacity make it a practical choice for formulators managing pH stability and mineral fortification simultaneously. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, MDHP functions as a tablet excipient and buffering agent.

This material helps to stabilize active ingredients sensitive to pH shifts. Feed and agricultural applications use it as a bioavailable magnesium and phosphorus supplement, supporting mineral balance in livestock nutrition programs.

Water treatment processes employ it to adjust pH and reduce corrosion in distribution systems by maintaining stable carbonate equilibrium. Food manufacturers incorporate it as a mineral additive and acidity regulator.

name: Dicalcium phosphate
description:
Dicalcium phosphate (CAS 7757-93-9 ), commonly abbreviated as DCP and listed as E341ii in food applications, is an inorganic calcium phosphate salt used as a mineral supplement.

It serves as a buffering agent and flow aid across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural industries. Calcium phosphate dibasic is the designation most frequently referenced in pharmaceutical compendial standards.

In food manufacturing, DCP functions as a leavening acid in baked goods and as a calcium and phosphorus fortification source in cereals, infant formula, and nutritional supplements.

Tablet and capsule production relies on DCP as a direct-compression excipient and diluent, where its compressibility and low moisture uptake support high-speed tableting lines.

In animal feed, it delivers bioavailable calcium and phosphorus to support bone development in poultry, swine, and cattle, and is a standard ingredient in premix formulations.

Fertilizer blends and soil amendment products also incorporate DCP as a controlled-release phosphorus source for crop nutrition programs to ensure optimal plant growth.

DCP is supplied as a white powder or granule, with granulated forms preferred for tableting. Recognized grades include FCC , USP / Ph. Eur. , and feed-grade specifications.

Each grade carries distinct purity and heavy metal specifications. Both anhydrous and dihydrate forms are commercially available, with the dihydrate being the more common food and pharma grade.

name: Potassium bromate
description:
Potassium bromate (CAS 7758-01-2 ), also known as E924 , is an inorganic oxidizing salt used commercially as a flour treatment agent and chemical oxidizer. It strengthens dough structure in baking and supports oxidation processes in industrial applications.

In commercial baking, E924 acts as a dough conditioner that improves gluten network development, resulting in greater loaf volume and a finer crumb structure in bread production. It is also evaluated as a flour bleaching and maturing agent.

name: Disodium pyrophosphate
description:
Disodium pyrophosphate ( CAS 7758-16-9 ), also known as SAPP and sodium acid pyrophosphate, is an inorganic phosphate salt used across food manufacturing and water treatment as a buffering, leavening, and sequestering agent.

Approved as E450a in the EU, it controls pH, binds metal ions, and stabilizes formulations where precise acidity management is critical. In baked goods, SAPP acts as a leavening acid in baking powder and self-rising flour.

It reacts with sodium bicarbonate to generate controlled CO₂ release during baking. Potato processors rely on it to inhibit after-cooking darkening by chelating iron and other trace metals that trigger enzymatic discoloration.

In seafood and meat processing, it functions as a moisture stabilizer and texture modifier, reducing drip loss in frozen products. Water treatment operations use it to sequester hardness ions and control scale formation.

Disodium pyrophosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granule grades available for improved flowability in dry blending operations. Standard market grades include food-grade material.

name: Sodium chlorite
description:
Sodium chlorite (CAS 7758-19-2 ) is an inorganic oxidizing salt used industrially as a precursor to chlorine dioxide generation and as a direct bleaching and antimicrobial agent.

It delivers controlled oxidative action across multiple processing environments where conventional chlorine-based treatments are unsuitable or regulated for specific industrial applications.

In water treatment, it is activated with acid or chlorine to generate chlorine dioxide on-site for disinfection of municipal and industrial water systems and cooling towers.

Textile and pulp processors use it to bleach fibers and paper stock without the fiber degradation associated with hypochlorite-based systems, ensuring high material integrity.

In food processing environments, approved dilute solutions are used for surface sanitation of equipment and antimicrobial treatment of fresh produce and poultry processing lines.

Leather processing operations apply it during hide preparation to achieve uniform whitening and to control microbial load during critical wet processing stages in the tannery.

The product is supplied as a stabilized aqueous solution, most commonly at 25% and 31% concentrations, and as a dry technical-grade solid for various industrial requirements.

Food-grade and water treatment grades are available and must meet applicable regulatory standards for the intended application to ensure safety and compliance in the supply chain.

name: Monocalcium phosphate
description:
Monocalcium phosphate (CAS 7758-23-8 ), also known as MCP and classified as E341i , is a calcium phosphate salt used primarily as a leavening acid and pH regulator in food manufacturing.

Its fast acid-release profile makes it a preferred choice in baking systems where rapid CO₂ generation is required. In baked goods, it acts as a fast-acting leavening acid, reacting with sodium bicarbonate to produce lift.

This chemical is essential for products such as self-rising flour, baking powder blends, and pancake mixes. Feed manufacturers incorporate it as a bioavailable phosphorus and calcium supplement in poultry and swine diets.

It is also used in aquaculture diets to support bone development and feed conversion. Food processors use it as a buffering and sequestering agent in processed cheeses and canned products to stabilize pH levels.

In fertilizer applications, it functions as a soluble phosphate source that improves nutrient uptake in high-value crop programs. This versatility makes it a staple in both the agricultural and food processing sectors.

The product is supplied as a white powder or granule, with granulated forms preferred in feed and fertilizer blending for improved flowability. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant) for baking.

Other available options include feed-grade for animal nutrition use. These quality standards ensure the material meets the rigorous safety and performance requirements of global industrial and food manufacturing supply chains.

name: Sodium tripolyphosphate
description:
Sodium tripolyphosphate (CAS 7758-29-4 ), commonly known as STPP or E451i , is a polyphosphate salt used across detergent manufacturing, food processing, and industrial treatment applications.

It functions primarily as a sequestrant, builder, and dispersing agent, binding calcium and magnesium ions to improve process efficiency and product performance across various sectors.

In detergent and cleaning product formulations, STPP acts as a builder that softens water by sequestering hardness ions, boosting surfactant performance in both household and industrial cleaners.

Food manufacturers use it under the E451i designation as a moisture-retention and texture agent in processed meats, seafood, and dairy products to maintain quality and yield.

Water treatment operations rely on STPP to control scale formation and disperse mineral deposits in industrial cooling and boiler systems, ensuring long-term equipment protection and efficiency.

In ceramics and paper production, it functions as a deflocculant, reducing slurry viscosity and improving material processability during the manufacturing and refining stages of production.

Sodium tripolyphosphate is supplied as a white powder or granule, with granulated forms preferred where dust control matters in bulk handling and large-scale industrial operations.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC , E451i compliant) and technical-grade for industrial applications. Both anhydrous and hydrated forms are available for global trade.

name: Betaine aldehyde chloride
description:
Betaine aldehyde chloride (CAS 7758-31-8 ), also known as trimethyl(2-oxoethyl)azanium chloride, is a quaternary ammonium aldehyde salt used primarily as a biochemical intermediate and synthetic precursor.

It functions as a key building block in the enzymatic and chemical synthesis of betaine and related compounds, supporting research and manufacturing workflows across pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a direct precursor in the production of betaine and choline-pathway metabolites, supporting active pharmaceutical ingredient development for various applications.

Biotechnology researchers use it as a substrate in enzyme activity assays, particularly for studying betaine aldehyde dehydrogenase, making it a standard reagent in metabolic pathway research.

In personal care formulation development, it supports the synthesis of moisturizing actives where betaine derivatives are the target end product for high-quality cosmetic manufacturing.

It also appears in specialty chemical research where controlled aldehyde-amine reactivity is required for constructing quaternary nitrogen scaffolds and other complex molecular structures.

Betaine aldehyde chloride is typically supplied as a crystalline solid or aqueous solution, with concentration and purity specifications varying by the intended industrial or laboratory use.

Research and reagent-grade material is the most commonly available form, supplied in small to mid-scale quantities suited to laboratory and pilot-scale applications for chemical buyers.

This includes table salt, spice blends, and protein supplements while simultaneously delivering a bioavailable calcium source. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a tablet excipient and calcium supplement active.

Its buffering capacity supports consistent dosage form performance. In animal feed, TCP supplies phosphorus and calcium to support bone development in livestock and poultry, meeting nutritional specifications.

Construction and industrial applications include use as a flame retardant additive and filler component in specialty materials. Tricalcium phosphate is supplied as a white free-flowing powder.

name: Ferrous chloride
description:
Ferrous chloride (CAS 7758-94-3 ), also known as FeCl2 or iron dichloride, is an iron(II) salt used across water treatment, metal processing, and chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a coagulant, reducing agent, and catalyst precursor in industrial-scale operations.

In municipal and industrial wastewater treatment, it acts as a coagulant and flocculant, precipitating phosphates and heavy metals from effluent streams. Textile and leather processors use it as a mordant to fix dyes and as a reducing agent in dyebath chemistry.

These applications improve color fastness and process consistency across various manufacturing sectors. In mining and hydrometallurgy, it supports leaching operations and metal recovery processes where controlled iron chemistry is required for efficiency.

Chemical manufacturers also source it as a catalyst precursor for synthesis routes involving iron-based catalytic systems. This versatile chemical is essential for maintaining high standards in modern industrial and environmental management protocols.

The product is available in anhydrous powder form and as a tetrahydrate in solid crystalline form. The tetrahydrate is the more common commercial supply format for most global distribution and storage requirements.

Liquid solutions of varying concentration are also offered for direct dosing in water treatment applications. Technical grade is the standard specification for most industrial buyers, ensuring reliable performance in large-scale chemical processes.

Purity and iron content are strictly verified against supplier certificates of analysis to meet industrial needs. This ensures that every batch complies with the necessary safety and performance benchmarks required by professional chemical engineers.

name: Copper sulfate
description:
Copper sulfate (CAS 7758-98-7 ), also known as E519 , is an inorganic copper salt supplied primarily as a blue crystalline pentahydrate or anhydrous powder. It functions across agriculture, water treatment, mining, and industrial processing.

The compound serves as a biocide, algaecide, catalyst precursor, and chemical reagent. In agriculture, it controls fungal diseases on crops and is a core active in Bordeaux mixture, a widely formulated plant protection product.

Water treatment facilities use it to eliminate algae blooms in reservoirs, drinking water systems, and aquaculture environments. Mining operations rely on it in froth flotation processes to selectively activate sulfide minerals.

This activation improves ore separation efficiency during the extraction process. In textiles and leather processing, it acts as a mordant to fix dyes onto fibers and hides, ensuring color fastness in finished goods.

Copper sulfate is available as the pentahydrate in granular, crystal, or fine powder form, and as the anhydrous grade in powder form. Standard grades include technical, agricultural, and feed-grade options for various industries.

Food-grade material conforms to E519 specifications for permitted food and feed applications. Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99%+ depending on the specific grade and the end-use requirements of the client.

name: Silver nitrate
description:
Silver nitrate (CAS 7761-88-8 ), historically known as Lapis infernalis, is an inorganic silver salt produced by dissolving silver in nitric acid. It functions as a primary source of ionic silver across industrial, analytical, and biomedical processes.

Its ability to precipitate halides and deliver controlled antimicrobial action drives demand across various sectors. In electronics and printed circuit board manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for conductive silver coatings and mirror deposition processes.

Water treatment operations use it to test for chloride contamination and to calibrate analytical methods for halide detection. Pharmaceutical and healthcare manufacturers incorporate it into topical preparations and medical device coatings.

These applications are critical where surface antimicrobial performance is required. In printing and photographic chemistry, it remains a key reagent for silver-based imaging systems and specialty ink formulations.

The chemical is supplied as a colorless crystalline solid or as an aqueous solution at various concentrations. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. for pharmaceutical procurement and compliance.

Technical and reagent grades are also available for industrial and laboratory buyers. Packaging is typically in amber glass or light-protected containers to prevent photodegradation during storage and transit.

It is used as a flavoring agent in teas, ready-to-drink beverages, and functional food products. Nutraceutical formulators incorporate it into dietary supplements and capsule blends targeting antioxidant support positioning.

In personal care, it is used in skin-facing formulations such as creams, serums, and toners. Its polyphenol content supports oxidative stability and aligns with clean-label ingredient preferences for modern brands.

name: Sodium thiosulfate

Sodium thiosulfate (CAS 7772-98-7 ), also sold as sodium thiosulphate and approved as E539 , is an inorganic salt used industrially as a reducing and dechlorinating agent.

It neutralizes excess oxidants in process streams and protects sensitive materials from chlorine damage across multiple manufacturing sectors. In water treatment, it dechlorinates municipal and industrial effluent.

This is a standard step where residual chlorine would interfere with biological treatment. Textile and paper manufacturers use it to neutralize chlorine bleach after whitening operations, preventing fiber or pulp degradation.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an antioxidant stabilizer in injectable formulations and as an active ingredient in antidote preparations for cyanide and heavy metal exposure.

Photographic and printing workflows historically relied on it as a fixing agent to clear unexposed silver halides, a use still relevant in specialty analog processes for high-quality imaging.

Sodium thiosulfate is supplied as pentahydrate crystals, the most common commercial form, and as anhydrous powder where lower moisture content is required for specific chemical reactions.

name: Stannous chloride
description:
Stannous chloride (CAS 7772-99-8 ), also known by its food additive designation E512 , is an inorganic tin salt used across industrial and food-grade applications as a reducing agent, catalyst, and stabilizer.

It prevents oxidative discoloration in processed foods, accelerates polymerization reactions, and supports metal surface treatment processes. In food and beverage processing, E512 is approved to prevent color degradation.

This additive is particularly effective in canned and preserved products, such as white asparagus and certain seafood. Textile and leather manufacturers use it as a mordant to fix dyes and improve color fastness.

It is applied to both natural and synthetic fibers to ensure long-lasting results. In plastics and polymer production, it functions as a catalyst or catalyst precursor in the synthesis of polyurethanes.

The chemical is also vital for other polymer systems. Printed circuit board and packaging manufacturers apply it in tin plating and surface sensitization processes to prepare substrates for further metallic coating.

Stannous chloride is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as the dihydrate crystalline form, with the dihydrate being the more common commercial grade. Standard grades include food-grade, technical, and reagent-grade.

name: Potassium bisulfite
description:
Potassium bisulfite (CAS 7773-03-7 ), also known commercially as E228 , is an inorganic sulfite salt used industrially as a preservative, antioxidant, and reducing agent. It inhibits microbial growth and oxidative degradation across food, water treatment, and industrial processing applications.

In food and beverage production, E228 is approved for use in wines, fruit juices, and dried foods to prevent browning and extend shelf life. Water treatment operations use it to neutralize residual chlorine in process water and wastewater effluent before discharge or reuse.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a bleaching and reducing agent in dyebath preparation and hide treatment. Controlled reduction chemistry is critical in these environments to achieving consistent color results and material integrity during the manufacturing process.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an antioxidant stabilizer in injectable formulations and oral solutions to protect active ingredients from oxidative breakdown. This ensures the potency and safety of medical products throughout their intended shelf life and storage period.

Potassium bisulfite is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade meeting E228 specifications and technical grade for industrial applications where high purity is less critical for the final outcome.

Buyers sourcing for food or pharmaceutical use should confirm compliance with relevant regional purity standards such as FCC or Ph.Eur. . These certifications ensure the material meets the rigorous safety requirements for human consumption and medical applications.

name: Calcium chloride hexahydrate
description:
Calcium chloride hexahydrate (CAS 7774-34-7 ), commonly referenced as CaCl2·6H2O, is the fully hydrated crystalline form of calcium chloride used across industrial and food-grade applications.

It functions as a desiccant, brine agent, setting accelerator, and preservation aid depending on the sector. Buyers typically source it where controlled water release or ionic calcium activity is required.

In food processing, it acts as a firming agent and preservative in canned vegetables, tofu production, and cheese making, where it restores calcium ions lost during pasteurization.

Oil and gas operators use it to formulate completion and workover brines, where its high density and solubility help control wellbore pressure without the use of solids.

In concrete and construction, it accelerates cement hydration, shortening set times in cold-weather pours. Water treatment facilities apply it for calcium hardness correction in systems.

Calcium chloride hexahydrate is supplied as white crystalline flakes or granules. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade material.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities depending on application requirements. This material is highly hygroscopic and must be stored in a cool, dry environment.

name: Sodium chlorate
description:
Sodium chlorate (CAS 7775-09-9 ), sold under trade names including Atlacide and Asex, is a strong inorganic oxidizer used across agriculture and industrial processing. It functions primarily as a herbicide and defoliant in crop management.

In pulp and paper production, this compound is the primary feedstock for generating chlorine dioxide on-site, which is used to bleach wood pulp to high brightness levels. This process is essential for modern paper manufacturing.

Agricultural applications include pre-harvest desiccation of cotton and non-selective weed control, where it is applied as a soil-active herbicide. It helps farmers manage crop cycles and clear unwanted vegetation efficiently.

Textile and leather processors use it as an oxidative bleaching agent for natural fibers and hides, improving uniformity before dyeing or finishing. This ensures a high-quality surface for subsequent chemical treatments.

It also serves as an intermediate in the production of perchlorates and other specialty oxidizing chemicals. Its reactive properties make it a versatile building block in various chemical synthesis pathways.

Sodium chlorate is supplied as a white crystalline solid, available in granular and powder forms suited to both agricultural and industrial handling requirements. These formats allow for easy dissolution and application.

Technical grade is the standard for industrial bleaching and chemical synthesis applications, while agricultural-grade material meets specifications for registered herbicide formulations. Both grades ensure consistent performance.

Bulk supply in bags, drums, and bulk containers is typical for high-volume industrial and agrochemical buyers. Proper storage and handling are required to maintain the stability of this powerful oxidizing agent.

name: Sodium chromate
description:
Sodium chromate (CAS 7775-11-3 ) is an inorganic chromium(VI) salt used industrially as a corrosion inhibitor and oxidizing agent across metal processing, textile, and water treatment sectors.

Disodium chromate is a recognized alternative name buyers may encounter in technical procurement contexts. In metal finishing and mining operations, it functions as a passivation agent applied to steel surfaces.

It is used on non-ferrous surfaces to prevent oxidative degradation in aggressive environments. The textile and leather industries use it as a mordant in dyeing processes, fixing chromium-based dyes to fiber substrates.

This application ensures improved color fastness and durability for various materials. In industrial water treatment systems, particularly cooling towers, it inhibits corrosion of metal infrastructure by forming a protective film.

This film on pipe surfaces protects recirculating water circuits from damage. Paper manufacturing operations also employ it as an oxidizing agent in certain pulp treatment and surface chemistry processes.

The product is supplied as a yellow crystalline powder or anhydrous solid, with the tetrahydrate form also available. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial end uses.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and chromium(VI) content with suppliers. These requirements often vary significantly between industrial and process-specific grades depending on the final application.

name: Sodium dithionite
description:
Sodium dithionite (CAS 7775-14-6 ), also sold as sodium hydrosulfite, is a powerful reducing agent used industrially for bleaching, stripping color, and preventing oxidation across multiple manufacturing sectors.

Its strong reducing capacity makes it a go-to reagent wherever controlled decolorization or oxygen scavenging is required at scale. In textile manufacturing, it is the primary reducing agent for vat dye application.

It reduces insoluble dyes to their soluble leuco form so they can penetrate fiber, then re-oxidize to fix color. Pulp and paper producers use it to brighten mechanical pulp without the fiber degradation associated with chlorine.

In food processing, it functions as an antioxidant and preservative, protecting products such as dried fruits, starches, and wine from discoloration and oxidative spoilage during storage and transport.

Water treatment operations apply it for dechlorination and oxygen removal in boiler feed systems and reverse osmosis pretreatment. It is supplied as a white to pale yellow powder or granules for industrial use.

Technical-grade material is the dominant commercial form, though food-grade specifications are available for applications in food and beverage processing where strict regulatory compliance is required.

Purity levels typically range from 85% to 90% for technical grade, with higher-purity grades available for sensitive applications. All batches are tested to ensure they meet necessary safety and performance metrics.

name: Sodium metaborate
description:
Sodium metaborate (CAS 7775-19-1 ), also referenced commercially as NaBO2, is an inorganic boron-containing salt used across industrial processes for pH regulation, corrosion inhibition, and biocidal activity.

It functions as an alkaline buffer and preservative in formulations where controlled boron release and stable pH are both required. In water treatment, it controls pH and inhibits corrosion in recirculating systems.

This chemical reduces metal degradation in pipelines and cooling towers. Textile and leather processing operations use it as an alkaline scouring and cleaning agent to remove grease and organic contaminants from surfaces.

In agriculture, it serves as a boron micronutrient source in soil treatment programs targeting boron-deficient crops. Paper manufacturing applies it in pulping and bleaching stages for consistent process chemistry.

Its buffering capacity supports consistent process chemistry and helps protect equipment surfaces. Sodium metaborate is supplied as an anhydrous powder or as hydrated crystalline forms, most commonly the tetrahydrate.

Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial applications across water treatment, textile, and paper sectors. Buyers should confirm anhydrous versus hydrated form when specifying for their needs.

Boron content and solubility behavior differ between grades, making specification critical. This versatile chemical remains a staple for industrial manufacturers requiring reliable alkaline buffering and protection.

name: Sodium persulfate
description:
Sodium persulfate (CAS 7775-27-1 ), also sold as sodium peroxydisulfate, is a strong inorganic oxidizing salt used across industrial manufacturing and treatment processes.

It functions primarily as a polymerization initiator, bleaching agent, and oxidative treatment chemical in demanding production environments. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it initiates reactions.

It is used for emulsion and suspension polymerization reactions for acrylic, vinyl, and styrene-based resins. Printed circuit board fabrication relies on it as a micro-etchant to clean surfaces.

It is used to roughen copper surfaces before lamination or plating. Textile and paper producers use it to bleach fibers and pulp without the residue concerns associated with chlorine-based alternatives.

In groundwater and soil remediation, it oxidizes organic contaminants in situ. This makes it a practical choice for environmental treatment projects where controlled reactivity is required.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule, with granular forms preferred where dust control is a handling priority. Standard commercial grades include technical grade.

name: L-fructose
description:
L-Fructose (CAS 7776-48-9 ), also known as L-Arabino-2-hexulose, is the non-natural mirror-image isomer of common fructose. It is produced for specialized research and commercial applications where chirality is a critical factor.

Unlike its natural counterpart, it is not metabolized by conventional enzymatic pathways. This unique property makes it a target ingredient for low-calorie and non-glycemic formulation work in various industries.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical development, it is evaluated as a non-metabolizable sugar substitute for patients requiring strict glycemic control. Biotechnology researchers use it as a chiral reference standard and substrate.

It is essential in enzyme specificity studies where distinguishing between enantiomers is necessary for experimental validity. Food technologists exploring next-generation sweetener systems incorporate it into prototype formulations.

These experts assess taste profiles and functional behavior at a small scale to determine commercial viability. Its flavoring role also extends to controlled sensory studies comparing L- and D-sugar perception.

The product is supplied primarily as a white crystalline powder in research and specialty commercial quantities. It is available under analytical and research-grade specifications through fine chemical manufacturers.

Bulk procurement options are limited compared to commodity sugars due to its specialized nature. Buyers should confirm lot-specific purity documentation when sourcing for formulation or regulatory submissions.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a tablet diluent and binder, particularly in solid dosage forms requiring low moisture sensitivity. It is also used in agriculture to improve soil structure in clay-heavy soils.

The material supplies calcium and sulfur to crops without significantly altering soil pH. Calcium sulfate is available as a fine white powder and in granular form, with particle size varying by intended use.

Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and technical grade, each carrying different purity and impurity thresholds. These standards ensure the material meets specific safety and performance requirements.

Anhydrous material is standard for desiccant and pharmaceutical applications, while hemihydrate and dihydrate forms serve construction and food sectors respectively. This versatility makes it a staple in industrial chemistry.

Textile dyeing operations use it as a mordant to fix dye onto natural fibers, improving wash and light fastness in finished fabric. Metal finishing and anti-corrosion treatments rely on it to passivate steel and aluminum surfaces.

These treatments are essential for extending service life in demanding environments. In mining and metallurgy, it functions as a flotation reagent and surface modifier during complex ore separation processes.

Potassium dichromate is supplied as orange-red crystalline granules or powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with laboratory-grade material available for analytical and quality control applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a buffering excipient in liquid formulations and cleaning-in-place (CIP) solutions where controlled alkalinity is critical for maintaining equipment hygiene.

name: Calcium hypochlorite

Food processing plants use it to sanitize surfaces, equipment, and produce wash water in compliance with food safety protocols. This ensures that microbial levels remain within safe limits during production.

Textile and paper manufacturers apply it to bleach natural fibers and pulp. This process achieves consistent whiteness without the handling complexity often associated with gaseous chlorine systems.

Tablet forms are common for pool and water treatment applications due to controlled dissolution rates. These formats allow for precise dosing and easier handling in industrial and commercial settings.

name: Potassium perchlorate
description:
Potassium perchlorate (CAS 7778-74-7 ), also known commercially as Astrumal and Peroidin, is an inorganic oxidizing salt used across industrial and defense-related manufacturing. It functions as a controlled oxidant and energetic material component where precise, stable oxygen release is required.

In aerospace and defense, potassium perchlorate serves as an oxidizer in solid rocket propellants, pyrotechnic compositions, and airbag inflator formulations. Consistent burn characteristics are critical to performance specifications in these high-stakes applications.

The printing and packaging industry uses it in the production of photochemical processing compounds and specialty inks requiring controlled oxidative chemistry. These processes rely on the material's stability and predictable reaction rates during manufacturing.

Pyrotechnic manufacturers incorporate it into signal flares, fireworks, and explosive initiators as a lower-sensitivity alternative to ammonium perchlorate. This makes it a preferred choice for safety-conscious production environments and specialized displays.

It also appears in certain electrochemical and analytical applications where a stable, soluble perchlorate source is required for reference or process use. Its chemical properties allow for high precision in laboratory and industrial testing scenarios.

Potassium perchlorate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Technical and industrial grades are the standard commercial forms, with particle size distribution often specified to meet propellant or pyrotechnic processing requirements.

name: Monopotassium phosphate
description:
Monopotassium phosphate (CAS 7778-77-0 ), commonly sourced as MKP or E340i , is an inorganic potassium salt used across food, agricultural, and industrial sectors as a pH buffer, nutrient source, and sequestrant.

Its dual potassium and phosphorus content makes it a preferred input wherever both minerals must be delivered simultaneously in a controlled, soluble form. In food and beverage manufacturing, MKP functions as a buffering agent.

It is used in sports drinks, dairy products, and processed foods where pH consistency directly affects shelf life and texture. Fertilizer producers and hydroponic growers rely on it as a fully water-soluble NPK input.

This is particularly useful in drip irrigation and foliar feed systems where nutrient uptake efficiency is critical. Pharmaceutical formulators use it to prepare buffer solutions and as an excipient in oral preparations.

These preparations meet strict compendial standards for safety and efficacy. Water treatment operations apply it for corrosion inhibition in distribution systems by controlling mineral scaling and sequestering metal ions.

Monopotassium phosphate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC , E340i), USP / BP for pharmaceutical applications, and technical grade for industrial use.

name: Potassium sulfate
description:

It is used for tobacco, citrus, grapes, and vegetables, delivering sulfur alongside potassium without the chloride load of muriate of potash. Food manufacturers use it as a firming agent and acidity regulator in processed products.

This is particularly useful where sodium reduction is a formulation priority. Pharmaceutical producers incorporate it as an excipient and mineral source in oral dosage forms and electrolyte preparations to ensure high quality.

In industrial chemistry, it serves as a flux in glass and cement production and as a catalyst precursor in certain sulfation processes. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule, with granular forms predominating.

Standard grades include technical, food-grade ( FCC ), and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), each meeting distinct purity thresholds for their respective end markets. These standards ensure the material is fit for purpose.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in laxative preparations and as a buffering agent in tablet and powder formats. Food producers incorporate it as an acidity regulator and sequestrant to stabilize color.

It helps extend shelf life and control mineral interactions in processed products. In personal care formulations, it acts as a pH adjuster and chelating agent in rinse-off and leave-on products where mineral control affects stability.

name: Decanal dimethyl acetal

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, fluorine is used to introduce fluorine atoms into active pharmaceutical ingredient structures, improving metabolic stability and bioavailability in drug candidates.

Electronics fabrication relies on fluorine gas for plasma etching and cleaning of semiconductor surfaces, enabling precise patterning in chip production for the global technology sector.

Mining and metals processing uses fluorine-based treatment to separate and refine ore concentrates, particularly in uranium and rare earth extraction for industrial energy and manufacturing.

Specialty chemical producers also use it to manufacture fluorinated intermediates, polymers, and reagents that feed downstream industrial supply chains and various commercial applications.

Fluorine is supplied as a compressed gas in high-pressure cylinders and tube trailers, typically at concentrations ranging from diluted mixtures to higher-purity streams for specific needs.

name: Graphite
description:
Graphite (CAS 7782-42-5 ) is a crystalline form of elemental carbon used across heavy industry as a solid lubricant and conductive additive. Supplied in natural and synthetic grades, it performs reliably in high-temperature and high-pressure environments.

In metalworking and mining, graphite is applied as a dry lubricant in die forging, wire drawing, and drilling operations. This material reduces tool wear under extreme mechanical loads where liquid lubricants often fail to provide protection.

Plastics and polymer compounders incorporate graphite powder to improve wear resistance and reduce friction in engineering components. Common applications include the manufacturing of bushings, seals, and various bearing housings for machinery.

Refractory and foundry applications use graphite in crucibles, mold release agents, and furnace linings. In these settings, thermal stability is the primary requirement for maintaining structural integrity during high-heat processing.

Conductive grades are also blended into electrodes, battery anodes, and antistatic coatings. Consistent electrical performance drives sourcing decisions for these specialized industrial and energy storage applications.

Graphite is available as fine powder, flakes, granules, and colloidal dispersions. Natural flake and synthetic grades are the most commercially traded forms, with particle size and purity specifications varying by end-use.

Technical and battery-grade specifications are standard across the market. High-purity synthetic grades are frequently utilized in energy storage applications to ensure maximum efficiency and longevity in modern battery systems.

name: Selenium
description:
Selenium (CAS 7782-49-2 ), commonly abbreviated as Se, is a trace element sourced and traded in elemental form across industrial, agricultural, and pharmaceutical supply chains. It functions as a critical micronutrient supplement and a semiconductor material.

Depending on the target application, it also serves as a metallurgical additive. In electronics manufacturing, Se is used in the production of photovoltaic cells, rectifiers, and photocopier drums, where its photoconductive properties determine performance.

Animal feed and fertilizer producers incorporate it as a micronutrient additive to correct selenium deficiency in livestock and selenium-depleted soils. This ensures proper health and growth across various agricultural sectors and livestock management programs.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use elemental selenium as a precursor in the synthesis of selenium-based active ingredients and dietary supplement compounds. These applications require high levels of precision and strict adherence to chemical purity.

Selenium is available commercially as powder, pellets, granules, and shot, with powder being the most common form for chemical processing applications. These various physical forms allow for flexible integration into different manufacturing workflows.

Pulp and paper producers use it to bleach cellulose fibers, achieving the brightness levels required for printing and packaging grades for various industrial sectors.

Textile and leather processors apply it to whiten natural fibers and prepare hides for dyeing by breaking down pigment structures during the manufacturing phase.

Pharmaceutical manufacturing relies on chlorine-based disinfection for cleanroom environments and process water sanitation where microbial limits are tightly regulated.

Catalyst manufacturers use it as a precursor to molybdenum-based catalysts applied in hydrodesulfurization, oxidation reactions, and petrochemical refining. These applications are critical for modern industrial efficiency and chemical synthesis.

In agriculture, it serves as a micronutrient source for molybdenum-deficient soils. It is frequently incorporated into fertilizer blends and foliar spray formulations to ensure optimal crop health and yield across various regions.

The mining and metals sector uses it in ore processing and as a starting material for producing molybdenum salts and pigments. This versatility makes it a staple component in heavy industrial manufacturing and mineral processing.

Molybdic acid is supplied as a white to slightly yellow powder. It is available in technical grade, with purity levels typically specified at 85% or higher MoO₃ equivalent, depending on the specific application requirements.

name: Tungstic acid
description:
Tungstic acid (CAS 7783-03-1 ), also referenced as H2WO4, is an inorganic tungsten compound used primarily as a catalyst and catalyst precursor in industrial chemical processing.

It serves as a key entry point for producing tungsten-based catalysts and downstream tungsten compounds across metallurgical and chemical manufacturing operations.

In catalyst manufacturing, tungstic acid is processed into supported tungsten oxide catalysts used in petroleum refining and hydrocracking units for various industrial applications.

Tungsten metal powder and tungsten trioxide production rely on tungstic acid as a controlled-purity precursor, feeding directly into powder metallurgy and hard metal supply chains.

It also functions as an intermediate in preparing ammonium paratungstate (APT), one of the primary traded forms of tungsten in global commodity markets today.

Specialty chemical producers use it to synthesize heteropolyacid catalysts applied in oxidation and acid-catalyzed organic reactions within the fine chemicals sector.

Tungstic acid is supplied as a yellow powder in technical and reagent grades. Purity specifications typically range from 99% upward for catalyst and precursor applications.

Moisture content and tungsten oxide assay are standard quality parameters. Packaging is available in multi-kilogram bags through to bulk quantities depending on grade.

name: Ammonium sulfate

Ammonium sulfate (CAS 7783-20-2 ) is an inorganic salt supplying both nitrogen and sulfur to crops, making it one of the most established nitrogen fertilizers in commercial agriculture.

Beyond agriculture, it functions as a pH buffer, protein precipitant, and process chemical across food, industrial, and water treatment applications. It is a versatile chemical used globally.

In fertilizer production and direct soil application, it delivers readily available nitrogen and sulfur to sulfur-deficient soils, particularly for crops like canola, wheat, and corn.

Food and fermentation manufacturers use it as a yeast nutrient and dough conditioner, where it supports consistent fermentation performance in baked goods and brewing processes.

In water treatment, it serves as a source of ammonia for chloramine disinfection, helping utilities maintain residual disinfectant levels across distribution networks for safety.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a pH buffer in dyeing baths, improving dye uptake uniformity and process control. This ensures high-quality finishes in industrial manufacturing.

Ammonium sulfate is supplied as white crystalline granules, standard granules, and fine powder. Agricultural-grade material is available in bulk and bagged formats for large-scale use.

In agriculture, DAP is one of the most concentrated phosphorus-nitrogen fertilizers available, applied directly to soil or blended into NPK compound fertilizers to support crop nutrition programs.

Textile and leather processors use it as a flame-retarding treatment for fabrics, paper, and hides, where it reduces flammability ratings to meet regulatory standards in various markets.

In construction materials, DAP is incorporated into fireproofing formulations for wood, insulation boards, and coatings. It also functions as a fermentation nutrient and pH buffer in yeast-based processes.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial flame retardant and fertilizer use, and food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications for permitted food processing applications.

name: Stannous fluoride
description:
Stannous fluoride (CAS 7783-47-3 ), also known commercially as tin difluoride, is an inorganic tin salt used primarily as an active ingredient in oral care and pharmaceutical formulations.

It delivers fluoride ion activity combined with antimicrobial action, making it a distinct functional choice compared to sodium fluoride or amine fluoride systems for manufacturers.

In toothpaste and mouth rinse formulations, it is used as both a caries-prevention agent and an antibacterial active, targeting plaque and gingivitis at concentrations typically ranging from 0.4% to 0.454%.

Pharmaceutical oral care products, including prescription-strength gels and professional dental treatments, rely on it where dual fluoride and antimicrobial efficacy is required by the formulation brief.

It also appears in specialty whitening and sensitivity-relief dentifrice systems, where its stannous ion component contributes to tubule occlusion and stain-blocking performance for the end user.

Some industrial surface treatment applications use this material in metal finishing processes, though oral care remains the dominant commercial demand for this specific chemical compound.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. USP and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are the most commercially relevant, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

These levels meet compendial standards, and FCC grade material is available for suppliers serving food-adjacent or oral care markets requiring food-safe certification for their products.

This addition helps to control the bath ratio and improve current efficiency, directly impacting metal yield and energy consumption. In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it functions as a flame retardant additive.

It helps compounded materials meet fire resistance specifications for wire and cable, construction profiles, and automotive components. As a catalyst or catalyst precursor, it supports fluorination and isomerization.

These reactions are essential in petrochemical and specialty chemical production. It also sees use as a preservative in fermentation control, where it inhibits enzymatic activity in brewing and fermentation processes.

Aluminum fluoride is available as a white crystalline powder or granules, with anhydrous and trihydrate forms both present in the market. Standard supply grades include technical grade for metallurgical applications.

Bulk supply is common for smelter-scale procurement, with smaller packaging available for catalyst and specialty chemical applications. This ensures flexibility for various industrial and laboratory requirements.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is supplied to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications, while technical-grade powder serves industrial and construction uses. These standards ensure the highest level of purity for sensitive applications.

Food-grade variants meeting FCC standards are available for regulated food and nutraceutical applications. This versatility makes it a critical component for manufacturers requiring reliable chemical performance across diverse global markets.

name: Silver bromide
description:
Silver bromide (CAS 7785-23-1 ), commonly referenced as AgBr, is an inorganic silver salt used primarily for its light-sensitive properties in photographic and electronic applications. It forms the basis of light-reactive coatings and surface treatments where controlled photochemical response is required.

In traditional and specialty photographic film manufacturing, AgBr is the active emulsion component that captures latent image data upon light exposure. Printed circuit board fabrication uses silver bromide-based chemistry for photoresist and surface modification processes.

These processes are essential where precise patterning is critical for high-performance electronics. Specialty optical coatings and infrared-transmitting materials incorporate AgBr for its transparency in specific wavelength ranges, supporting sensor and detector manufacturing.

Antimicrobial surface treatments in electronics and medical device components also draw on silver bromide's controlled ion-release behavior. This functionality is used to inhibit microbial growth on contact surfaces in sensitive environments.

Silver bromide is supplied as a pale yellow crystalline powder, typically handled and packaged under light-protected conditions to preserve reactivity. Technical and high-purity grades are available to meet various industrial requirements.

Purity specifications commonly range from 98% to 99.9%+ to meet the demands of photographic emulsion and electronics manufacturing. Packaging is generally provided in light-proof, moisture-resistant containers for stability.

These containers are available in quantities ranging from laboratory-scale to bulk industrial supply. Our logistics team ensures that all shipments maintain the integrity of the light-sensitive material during transit to your facility.

name: L-Alpha-Pinene
description:
L-Alpha-Pinene (CAS 7785-26-4 ), also known as (-)-α-pinene, is the levorotatory enantiomer of alpha-pinene, derived primarily from turpentine fractions of coniferous trees. It functions as a bio-based solvent and fragrance ingredient across industrial and consumer product manufacturing.

In coatings and printing inks, it acts as a renewable solvent carrier that supports resin dissolution and controlled evaporation profiles suited to high-speed production. Adhesive and sealant formulators use it as a reactive diluent and terpene resin precursor.

Its specific optical activity matters for consistent polymer performance in specialized industrial applications. In flavor and fragrance work, it contributes a fresh, piney, coniferous character to fine fragrances, household products, and food flavoring systems.

The compound is assigned FEMA 2902 and is widely utilized in the food industry. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into aerosol sprays, shaving preparations, and scented cosmetics where a natural-origin terpene solvent is preferred.

This material is often selected over petrochemical alternatives to meet sustainability goals. L-Alpha-Pinene is supplied as a clear, mobile liquid in drum and IBC quantities for large-scale industrial use and distribution.

It is available in fragrance-grade and technical-grade specifications, with high-purity optical isomer grades offered for applications where enantiomeric excess is a formulation requirement. Food-grade material conforming to FCC standards is also commercially available.

The product meets rigorous quality benchmarks to ensure stability and performance across diverse sectors. Our supply chain ensures that the material maintains its chemical integrity from the point of distillation to final delivery.

name: Sodium trimetaphosphate
description:
Sodium trimetaphosphate (CAS 7785-84-4 ), commonly abbreviated as STMP, is an inorganic cyclic phosphate salt used across food processing, water treatment, and industrial manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a crosslinking agent, chelating agent, and buffering compound, enabling formulators to modify texture, stabilize systems, and control mineral interactions.

In food processing, STMP crosslinks starch granules to improve heat and shear stability in canned goods, sauces, and instant food products. This ensures consistent viscosity and shelf stability.

Water treatment operations use it to sequester calcium and magnesium ions, preventing scale formation in distribution systems and industrial cooling circuits. This protects equipment from mineral buildup.

In textile and paper manufacturing, it acts as a dispersing and sequestering agent during processing baths. This helps to control metal ion interference that would otherwise degrade product quality.

Leather processing operations apply it as a buffering and chelating agent to regulate pH during tanning stages. This ensures uniform chemical penetration and high-quality leather finishes.

STMP is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade material is available to FCC specification, supporting use in regulated food and starch modification applications.

Technical-grade material is supplied for industrial uses in water treatment and textile processing where food compliance is not required. It remains a versatile chemical for diverse sectors.

name: Manganese sulfate
description:
Manganese sulfate (CAS 7785-87-7 ), also sold as manganous sulfate, is an inorganic manganese salt used across agriculture, nutrition, and industrial processing as a concentrated, bioavailable source of manganese.

It functions as a micronutrient supplement, catalyst precursor, and process chemical depending on the application sector. In agriculture, it corrects manganese deficiency in crops through foliar sprays and soil amendments.

This directly improves yield in cereals, legumes, and fruit crops. Feed and premix manufacturers incorporate it as a trace mineral source in livestock and poultry nutrition programs to ensure optimal animal health.

In battery and electronics manufacturing, it serves as a precursor in the synthesis of electrolytic manganese dioxide and cathode materials. Water treatment operations use it to support oxidation processes.

These processes are essential for iron and manganese removal from potable water supplies. Manganese sulfate is available as a monohydrate powder, which is the most commercially prevalent form in the market.

Higher hydrate forms are also present in some markets. Recognized grades include feed-grade, fertilizer-grade, and technical-grade, with food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material available for specific needs.

These high-purity options meet stricter requirements such as FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , or ACS standards. Standard packaging ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities for industrial buyers.

name: Sodium aluminum phosphate
description:
Sodium aluminum phosphate ( CAS 7785-88-8 ), also known by its food additive designation E541 , is an inorganic salt used primarily as a leavening acid and buffering agent in food manufacturing.

SAIP is the common industry shorthand buyers use when sourcing this material for baked goods applications. In commercial baking, it acts as a slow-release leavening acid in self-rising flours and baking powders.

It provides controlled gas release during oven spring rather than on mixing in refrigerated dough systems. Processed cheese production relies on it as an emulsifying salt that sequesters calcium ions.

This improves melt characteristics and texture consistency in sliced and block formats. It also functions as a pH buffer in certain pharmaceutical tablet formulations where acid-stable processing conditions are required.

In processed meat and seafood applications, its sequestering action helps stabilize color and extend shelf stability. The material is supplied as a white powder in both acidic and basic forms.

The acidic form is the dominant commercial grade. Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the standard for most procurement, with pharmaceutical-grade material available for regulated applications.

Bulk supply is typical in multi-tonne quantities, with smaller packaging available for formulators. This chemical remains a staple for manufacturers requiring precise control over leavening and emulsification.

name: Magnesium chloride
description:
Magnesium chloride (CAS 7786-30-3 ), also sold as E511 in food applications, is an inorganic salt sourced from seawater, brine, and mineral deposits. It functions across industries as a coagulant, dust suppressant, de-icer, and mineral supplement.

In food production, E511 acts as a coagulant in tofu manufacturing and a firming agent in processed foods, where controlled magnesium ion release is critical to texture. Road maintenance and mining operations use it for dust suppression.

It is used for ice control on unpaved surfaces and haul roads, where its hygroscopic behavior keeps surfaces bound under dry conditions. In water treatment, it supports pH adjustment and serves as a magnesium source.

It is used in remineralization processes for drinking water. Pharmaceutical and agricultural formulators use the anhydrous form as a catalyst precursor in Grignard reactions and as a magnesium supplement in fertilizer blends.

It is also utilized in animal feed mineral mixes. Magnesium chloride is supplied as hexahydrate flakes, prills, or powder, and in anhydrous form for chemical synthesis applications across various industrial sectors.

Food-grade material is available to FCC specification; pharmaceutical-grade material meets USP and Ph. Eur. standards. Technical-grade flakes and liquid brine solutions are the standard commercial forms.
