name: Nickel sulfate
description:
Nickel sulfate (CAS 7786-81-4 ), also sold as NiSO4, is an inorganic nickel salt primarily used as an electrolyte source in industrial electroplating and surface finishing operations. It delivers controlled nickel deposition onto metal substrates and serves as a precursor in catalyst manufacturing.

In electroplating, it is the standard nickel source for decorative and functional coatings on automotive parts, electronics connectors, and hardware. Deposit quality and bath stability depend on consistent nickel ion concentration during the process.

Battery manufacturers use it as a key precursor in synthesizing nickel-rich cathode materials for lithium-ion cells, particularly NMC and NCA chemistries. This application is critical for the production of high-capacity energy storage systems.

In textile and leather processing, it acts as a mordant to fix dyes onto fiber substrates, improving color fastness in finished goods. This ensures that the pigments remain stable and vibrant throughout the lifecycle of the material.

Mining operations use nickel sulfate solutions in hydrometallurgical refining to recover and purify nickel from ore concentrates. This chemical process is essential for obtaining high-purity metals from raw geological sources.

Nickel sulfate is supplied as a crystalline solid in both hexahydrate and anhydrous forms, with the hexahydrate being the dominant commercial grade. Standard supply specifications include technical grade and electroplating grade.

Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5% depending on the specific industrial requirement. Bulk quantities are available in bags or drums, with high-purity battery-grade material increasingly offered to meet EV supply chain requirements.

description:
Barium sulfite (CAS 7787-39-5 ), also referenced as barium sulphite, is an inorganic barium salt used industrially as a reducing and preservative agent. It functions primarily to control oxidative degradation and microbial activity in process streams and treatment baths.

In water treatment, it acts as an oxygen scavenger and pH buffer, helping to protect process equipment from corrosive degradation. Textile and leather processing operations use it in dyebath preparation and tanning liquors.

Controlled reduction chemistry improves dye uptake and process consistency within these specialized industrial environments. Pulp and paper manufacturers incorporate it into bleaching and pulping stages to moderate oxidative conditions.

This application helps extend the working life of process chemicals during large-scale manufacturing cycles. It also serves preservation functions in industrial formulations where sulfite-based biocidal activity is required.

This activity is essential to inhibit microbial growth in aqueous systems and maintain product stability over time. Barium sulfite is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules for easy handling.

Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial applications across various sectors. Buyers should confirm purity specifications and barium content with suppliers before finalizing procurement orders.

Beryllium chloride (CAS 7787-47-5 ) is an inorganic salt used primarily as a catalyst and precursor in specialized chemical synthesis. BeCl2 serves as a key entry point for producing high-purity beryllium metal.

This compound is essential for beryllium-based materials required across advanced industrial sectors. In electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, it acts as a precursor for depositing beryllium oxide coatings.

These coatings are valued for their thermal management performance in high-power components. Aerospace and defense applications rely on it as a starting material for producing beryllium metal used in structural alloys.

It is also utilized in gyroscopes and guidance systems. In metallurgical processing, it functions as a flux and alloying agent precursor for copper-beryllium alloys, which are specified for precision tooling.

Semiconductor and electronics manufacturers use it in specialized etching and deposition processes where isotopic purity affects process control. It is essential for maintaining the integrity of advanced electronic components.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it supports isotope labeling studies and stable isotope-tagged API synthesis. Here, deuterium incorporation is a deliberate design element for drug development and metabolic studies.

Life science researchers rely on D₂O in cell culture and metabolic flux studies to trace biochemical pathways without radioactive materials. This provides a safe and effective method for observing complex biological systems.

Deuterium oxide is supplied as a clear liquid, with isotopic purity typically ranging from 99.8% to 99.96% atom % D depending on intended use. NMR-grade and analytical-grade specifications are the most commonly stocked.

name: Potassium fluoride
description:
Potassium fluoride (CAS 7789-23-3 ), commonly abbreviated as KF, is an inorganic fluoride salt used across chemical synthesis, surface treatment, and industrial processing. In pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, KF serves as a nucleophilic fluorinating reagent, enabling halogen-exchange reactions to introduce fluorine into active pharmaceutical ingredients and specialty intermediates.

Electronics manufacturers use it as a flux and surface treatment agent for metal components, improving solderability and removing oxide layers prior to assembly. This ensures high-quality connections in sensitive electronic devices.

In textile and leather processing, KF-based formulations act as preservatives and pH buffers, controlling microbial activity and maintaining process bath conditions. This helps in achieving consistent results during large-scale production cycles.

Flame retardant compounding also draws on KF as a precursor or synergist, particularly in formulations targeting polymer and fiber substrates. Its chemical properties make it a versatile component in modern material science applications.

Potassium fluoride is supplied as a white anhydrous powder or granules, with anhydrous and dihydrate forms both available commercially. Standard grades include technical, reagent, and pharmaceutical-grade material.

Optical-grade fluorite is machined into lenses, prisms, and windows for UV and infrared imaging systems. Its broad spectral transmission is the primary procurement driver for high-end optical and imaging equipment manufacturers.

The pulp and paper industry uses it in the production of hydrofluoric acid, which is then applied in bleaching and wood pulp processing. In mining and mineral processing, it functions as a flotation reagent for various ores.

Metallurgical grades typically range from 85–97% CaF2, while optical and acid-grade specifications reach 97–99% or higher. Technical and acid-grade specifications are standard for chemical manufacturing applications globally.

High-purity optical-grade material is available in processed crystal form for precision photonics applications. These specialized forms ensure maximum performance in sensitive laser and imaging systems across the technology sector.

In pharmaceutical and biochemical manufacturing, it is used to oxidize polysaccharides and glycoproteins. This is a critical step in conjugate vaccine production and drug intermediate synthesis for various medical applications.

Textile processors apply it to modify cellulose fibers, improving dye uptake and enabling functional finishing treatments. In water treatment, it acts as a biocide and oxidant to control microbial growth.

It is also used to break down organic contaminants in industrial effluent systems. Paper and pulp operations use it as a selective bleaching agent to improve brightness without degrading the underlying fiber structure.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granular solid. It is available in technical grade for industrial applications and in high-purity grades meeting reagent or ACS specifications.

name: Calcium tungstate
description:
Calcium tungstate (CAS 7790-75-2 ), also referenced commercially as C.I. 77250, is an inorganic calcium salt of tungsten used as a functional material in specialized industrial and electronic applications.

It occurs naturally as the mineral scheelite and serves as a primary source mineral for tungsten extraction in mining operations. In mining and metallurgy, calcium tungstate ore concentrates are processed.

These concentrates are used to recover tungsten metal and intermediate compounds used in hard alloy and tooling production. The compound is also used in scintillation applications for industrial imaging.

Its luminescent response to X-ray and gamma radiation makes it a material of interest for detector components and imaging screens. In electronics, it is evaluated as a substrate or functional material.

It is utilized in thin-film and optical device manufacturing. Pigment applications under C.I. 77250 also exist in specialty coatings where controlled luminescence or whiteness is required for the finish.

Calcium tungstate is available as a white crystalline powder in varying particle size distributions to suit processing requirements. Technical and high-purity grades are the most commonly supplied.

Purity levels are typically specified at 99% or above for electronic and scintillation uses. Synthetic grades are distinguished from natural scheelite concentrates, which are supplied as ore fractions.

name: Calcium pyrophosphate
description:
Calcium pyrophosphate ( CAS 7790-76-3 ), also known as dicalcium diphosphate and abbreviated as CPP, is an inorganic calcium salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

It functions primarily as an acidity regulator, buffering agent, and mild abrasive, depending on the application sector. In oral care, CPP serves as a polishing and abrasive agent in toothpaste formulations.

This material provides controlled enamel cleaning without excessive surface wear. Food manufacturers use it as an acidity regulator and leavening component in processed foods, baked goods, and dry mixes.

It is particularly useful where pH stability during processing is critical. In pharmaceutical solid dosage forms, it acts as a calcium supplement excipient and diluent in tablet manufacturing.

Personal care formulators also incorporate it into specialty powders and cleansing products where mild mechanical action is required. The material is supplied as a white, fine powder in varying particle sizes.

These distributions suit specific abrasive or blending applications. Food-grade and USP pharmaceutical-grade specifications are the most commonly traded, with technical-grade material available for industrial uses.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in multi-kilogram bags or supersacks. Smaller packaging is also available for laboratory and development-scale procurement to meet diverse manufacturing needs.

name: Hypochlorous acid
description:
Hypochlorous acid (CAS 7790-92-3 ), also known as HOCl, is a chlorine-based oxidizing acid produced through electrolysis of saline or dilute chlorine solutions. It functions as a broad-spectrum antimicrobial and oxidizing agent.

This chemical delivers high-level disinfection and sanitization performance across food processing, healthcare, and water treatment environments. In food processing and produce handling, HOCl is applied as a no-rinse sanitizer on contact surfaces.

It is used on equipment and fresh produce, meeting food-safety compliance requirements without chemical residue concerns. Water treatment facilities use it as a primary disinfectant to control microbial load in potable water.

It is also utilized in cooling towers and wastewater systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into wound care sprays, skin sanitizers, and eye-safe cleansing products where conventional preservatives are unsuitable.

In healthcare and pharmaceutical environments, it serves surface and instrument disinfection where low-toxicity, non-corrosive biocidal action is a procurement priority. The solution is highly effective against pathogens.

Hypochlorous acid is supplied as a liquid solution, typically in concentrations ranging from 50 to 500 ppm for consumer and food-grade applications. Higher concentrations are available for industrial use.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to support regulated end-use applications. These products meet rigorous quality standards including FCC , USP , Ph.Eur. , BP , EP , and ACS .

Packaging ranges from small-volume containers to bulk IBC totes depending on application scale and concentration. This ensures flexible logistics for various industrial and commercial requirements worldwide.

name: Chlorosulfonic acid
description:
Chlorosulfonic acid (CAS 7790-94-5 ), also known as chlorosulfuric acid or CSA, is a highly reactive sulfonating and chlorosulfonating agent used across chemical synthesis and industrial manufacturing.

It introduces sulfonic or sulfonyl chloride groups into organic molecules, enabling the production of a broad range of downstream intermediates and active ingredients for various sectors.

In agrochemical synthesis, CSA is used to manufacture herbicide and pesticide intermediates, particularly sulfonamide-class compounds where precise sulfonation is required for efficacy.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it to produce sulfonyl chloride intermediates that feed into APIs and specialty drug substances. It is a critical component in modern medicinal chemistry.

In the textile and leather industries, it functions as a precursor in the production of synthetic dyes and optical brighteners, where sulfonation determines solubility and fastness properties.

Polymer chemists also apply CSA in the sulfonation of polystyrene and similar backbones to produce ion-exchange resins and proton-exchange membranes for industrial filtration and energy applications.

Chlorosulfonic acid is supplied as a fuming liquid, typically in concentrations at or near 99% purity. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for most industrial processes.

High-purity grades are available for pharmaceutical and specialty chemical synthesis. It is packaged in corrosion-resistant containers suited to its highly reactive and fuming nature.

name: Cobalt chloride hexahydrate
description:
Cobalt chloride hexahydrate (CAS 7791-13-1 ), also known as cobalt (II) chloride hexahydrate, is an inorganic cobalt salt supplied as a distinctive pink-to-red crystalline solid.

It functions across industrial chemistry as a catalyst precursor, colorant, and surface treatment agent, with demand driven by its reactivity and solubility in aqueous and polar systems.

In electroplating and surface finishing, it is used to deposit cobalt-containing layers that improve hardness and corrosion resistance on metal substrates for various industrial applications.

Textile and leather processors apply it as a dye mordant, fixing colorants to fiber and improving wash fastness in finished goods to ensure long-lasting color quality and durability.

Agricultural formulations incorporate it as a cobalt micronutrient source in fertilizers and animal feed supplements where cobalt deficiency must be corrected for optimal livestock health.

In catalyst manufacturing, it serves as a precursor for hydrodesulfurization and Fischer-Tropsch catalysts, where controlled cobalt loading on support materials is critical to performance.

Cobalt chloride hexahydrate is supplied as pink crystalline powder or granules. Standard commercial grades include technical, reagent, and laboratory-grade material for diverse uses.

Purity levels typically range from 97% to 99%+. Packaging ranges from small drums to bulk quantities depending on specific application requirements and logistical needs of the client.

name: Magnesium chloride hexahydrate
description:
Magnesium chloride hexahydrate (CAS 7791-18-6 ), commonly referenced as MgCl2·6H2O, is the hydrated crystalline form of magnesium chloride used across industrial, agricultural, and food-grade applications.

It functions primarily as a mineral source, coagulant, and pH-buffering agent in processes requiring soluble magnesium delivery. In food manufacturing, it acts as a coagulant for tofu and soy-based products.

It also serves as a magnesium fortification source in functional foods and beverages. Water treatment operations use it to support flocculation and pH adjustment in both municipal and industrial effluent systems.

In oil and gas drilling, it serves as a dense brine component for well completion and workover fluids where controlled density and low formation damage are priorities for the operator.

Agricultural applications include soil conditioning and foliar magnesium supplementation to correct deficiencies in magnesium-depleted crops. This ensures optimal growth and yield in various farming environments.

Magnesium chloride hexahydrate is supplied as white crystalline flakes or granules, with liquid brine solutions also available for bulk industrial use. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ).

Other available standards include pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) and technical-grade for industrial processes. Purity levels and packaging formats vary significantly by the specific grade required.

Food and pharma specifications require tighter limits on heavy metals and impurities. This ensures the material meets the rigorous safety standards necessary for human consumption and medical applications.

name: Sulfuryl chloride
description:
Sulfuryl chloride (CAS 7791-25-5 ), also known as sulfuric oxychloride and abbreviated SO2Cl2, is a reactive inorganic chlorinating and sulfonating agent used across chemical synthesis and industrial processing.

It delivers both chlorination and sulfonation in a single reagent, reducing the need for multiple process steps. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a chlorinating agent in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

This reagent is particularly valued in intermediates where precise reactivity control is required. Pulp and paper producers use it as a bleaching agent to achieve target brightness levels in processed fiber.

Textile and leather processors apply it for whitening treatments and surface modification of natural substrates. In water treatment, it functions as a biocidal agent contributing to disinfection and microbial control.

These applications are critical for maintaining hygiene in industrial water systems. Sulfuryl chloride is supplied as a fuming liquid, typically in cylinders, drums, or ISO tank containers depending on volume.

It is available in technical grade, with purity levels commonly at 97% or higher for industrial applications. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting stricter purity specifications is also available for regulated synthesis.

name: Vinyltriethoxysilane
description:
Vinyltriethoxysilane ( CAS 78-08-0 ), commonly abbreviated as VTEO, is an organosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic substrates and organic polymer matrices. It functions as a reactive monomer and surface modifier across adhesives, sealants, and coatings.

In crosslinked polyethylene (XLPE) production, VTEO is grafted onto polyethylene chains to enable moisture-cure crosslinking. This is a critical process for wire and cable insulation where durability is paramount.

Rubber and silicone sealant formulators use it to improve adhesion to glass, metal, and mineral fillers. This directly affects bond durability in various construction and automotive assemblies during the manufacturing process.

In coatings and primers, VTEO-treated surfaces improve adhesion of organic topcoats to glass fiber and silica. It is also effective on other inorganic substrates to ensure long-term coating integrity and performance.

Electronics manufacturers apply it as a surface treatment for encapsulants and laminates. This is necessary where moisture resistance and interfacial adhesion are strict qualification requirements for the final product.

Vinyltriethoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drums and IBC containers for industrial volumes. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly at 97% or higher.

Specialty electronic and high-purity grades are available from select producers to meet tighter process requirements. These grades ensure that the material meets the rigorous demands of advanced chemical manufacturing.

name: Tetraethyl silicate
description:
Tetraethyl silicate (CAS 78-10-4 ), commonly known as TEOS or ethyl silicate, is a silicon alkoxide used as a reactive binder, crosslinker, and silica precursor across industrial and specialty chemical applications.

On hydrolysis, it deposits amorphous silica, enabling durable surface treatments, protective coatings, and ceramic structures without requiring high-temperature sintering. In zinc-rich and inorganic coatings, it acts as the silicate binder.

This material cures at ambient temperature to form hard, corrosion-resistant films on steel structures and industrial equipment. Semiconductor and display manufacturers use it as a CVD/sol-gel precursor to deposit silicon dioxide dielectric layers.

In building and construction, it consolidates porous stone, concrete, and masonry by penetrating the substrate. It forms a silica network that restores structural integrity and protects against environmental degradation over time.

Formulators of heat-resistant adhesives and sealants incorporate it as a crosslinking agent to improve thermal stability. This enhances adhesion to glass and metal surfaces in demanding industrial environments and high-heat applications.

Tetraethyl silicate is supplied as a clear liquid, available in both pure form and as partially pre-hydrolyzed grades. Most notably, Ethyl Silicate 40 offers higher silica content for specialized coating applications.

Standard purity grades range from technical to high-purity electronic grade for semiconductor use. Packaging typically covers drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities to meet various industrial supply chain requirements.

name: Pentaerythritol tetranitrate
description:
Pentaerythritol tetranitrate (CAS 78-11-5 ), also known as penthrite, is a high-energy nitrate ester used across pharmaceutical and defense applications. In medicine, it functions as a vasodilator active ingredient.

In defense and aerospace, it serves as a primary explosive and detonator component. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is formulated into sustained-release tablets and transdermal patches for angina pectoris.

Controlled release of the active compound is critical to dosage performance. Defense and aerospace contractors use it as a base charge in detonators and as a component in flexible linear shaped charges.

It serves as a booster explosive in munitions trains and is compounded into PETN-based sheet explosives used in aerospace structural severance systems and satellite separation mechanisms.

Specialty pyrotechnic formulators incorporate it into detonating cord, where its high detonation velocity ensures reliable signal transmission across long distances for complex industrial systems.

Pentaerythritol tetranitrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder, typically wetted or desensitized with water or an inert plasticizer to meet transport and handling regulations.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to BP and Ph. Eur. specifications for use in medicinal formulations. Defense-grade supply follows military specifications and strict licensing.

All shipments are subject to end-user certification and export control requirements. Our technical team ensures that every batch meets the rigorous safety and purity standards required for your industry.

name: Triethyl phosphate
description:
Triethyl phosphate (CAS 78-40-0 ), commonly abbreviated as TEP, is a phosphate ester used primarily as a flame retardant and reactive intermediate across industrial manufacturing. It functions by introducing phosphorus into polymer systems or formulations to reduce flammability.

In plastics and polymer processing, TEP acts as a reactive flame retardant additive incorporated into resins, coatings, and laminates destined for automotive and aerospace components. This improves thermal stability in demanding environments.

Textile manufacturers apply it during fiber treatment and finishing processes to impart durable flame resistance to synthetic and blended fabrics. In the construction sector, TEP is used in flame-retardant coatings and insulation materials.

These applications are critical where building codes require specific fire performance ratings. It also functions as a catalyst and solvent in the production of pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and specialty chemicals, where its controlled reactivity supports synthesis.

Triethyl phosphate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial packaging, including drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs). Technical grade is the primary commercial form for industrial and synthesis applications.

Purity levels are typically at 99% or higher for most industrial uses. Specifications are generally aligned with technical-grade standards, and buyers should confirm purity and phosphorus content with suppliers when sourcing for reactive end uses.

Tris(2-ethylhexyl) phosphate (CAS 78-42-2 ), commonly abbreviated as TEHP, is an organophosphate ester used across industrial manufacturing as a plasticizer, flame retardant, and solvent.

Coatings and adhesives manufacturers incorporate it as a solvent and plasticizing agent to control viscosity, film formation, and substrate adhesion in various industrial formulations and applications.

The textile and leather industries use TEHP as a processing aid and finishing component, where its compatibility with synthetic fibers and surface treatments supports durable end-product performance.

In lubricants and metalworking fluids, it acts as an extreme-pressure additive and functional solvent, extending fluid service life under demanding operating conditions and high-stress environments.

Floor polish and wax formulations rely on TBEP to control leveling and gloss. In these applications, it acts as a coalescing agent for polymer emulsions to ensure a smooth and consistent finish.

Textile and leather finishes incorporate it to impart softness and reduce ignition risk in treated fabrics and hides. This makes it a vital component for high-performance materials in the upholstery industry.

In rubber compounding, it cross-links EPDM, silicone, and natural rubber to improve heat resistance and compression set performance in seals, gaskets, and automotive components.

Polyolefin producers use it to initiate cross-linking in PE and PP, producing materials suited for wire and cable insulation, pipes, and high-performance foam products.

It also functions as a polymerization initiator in the production of specialty resins and thermoplastic elastomers where precise molecular weight control is needed for manufacturing.

Supplied as a liquid or absorbed onto an inert carrier as a diluted paste or powder blend, standard commercial concentrations include 90% active content liquid and diluted grades.

The Technical grade is the primary market specification, with purity and active oxygen content confirmed by certificate of analysis for every batch produced.

name: Azobisisobutyronitrile
description:
Azobisisobutyronitrile (CAS 78-67-1 ), commonly known as AIBN, is a free-radical initiator used to drive polymerization reactions across a broad range of industrial polymer production processes.

It decomposes at moderate temperatures to generate nitrogen gas and carbon-centered radicals, triggering chain growth in both bulk and solution polymerization systems.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, AIBN initiates the production of PVC, polystyrene, polyacrylates, and other vinyl-based polymers where controlled radical generation is critical.

Coating formulators use it to cure acrylic and styrenic resin systems, directly influencing film hardness, adhesion, and cross-link density in the final coating application.

In adhesives and sealants, AIBN supports the synthesis of pressure-sensitive and structural adhesive polymers where consistent initiation efficiency affects batch-to-batch performance.

Printing and packaging applications rely on AIBN-initiated resins for UV-stable inks and barrier coatings applied to flexible substrates for various industrial uses.

AIBN is supplied as a white crystalline powder and is the standard commercial form for industrial use. Technical grade is the predominant specification available for buyers.

Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher. Packaging ranges from small quantities to bulk volumes, with temperature-controlled handling required throughout the supply chain.

name: Isopentane
description:
Isopentane (CAS 78-78-4 ), also supplied under the refrigerant designation R-601a, is a highly volatile hydrocarbon solvent used across industrial, laboratory, and specialty gas applications.

Its rapid evaporation rate makes it a preferred carrier and blowing agent where low residue and fast flash-off are critical procurement requirements for various manufacturing processes.

In the pharmaceutical and biomedical sector, isopentane is used as a cryogenic tissue-freezing medium, enabling rapid specimen preservation without the cracking associated with liquid nitrogen.

As a blowing agent in expandable polystyrene and polyolefin foam manufacturing, it controls cell structure and density in insulation and packaging materials for the construction industry.

In the oil and gas industry, it functions as a component in natural gasoline blending and as a reference standard in hydrocarbon analysis for laboratory testing and calibration.

Flavor manufacturers also use isopentane as a low-boiling solvent carrier in the extraction and processing of volatile aroma compounds to ensure high-quality sensory profiles in final products.

Isopentane is supplied as a liquefied gas or pressurized liquid at ambient temperature, typically in cylinders, drums, and isotanks depending on specific volume requirements of the client.

Standard commercial grades include high-purity research grade and technical grade for industrial blowing agent applications. Anhydrous and low-sulfur specifications are available to meet process sensitivity.

In plastics processing, it functions as a solvent cement for bonding PVC and ABS substrates. It also serves as a carrier in polymer coatings applied to textiles and leather for durable industrial finishes.

name: Isopropanolamine
description:
Isopropanolamine (CAS 78-96-6 ), also known as MIPA or Threamine, is an amino alcohol used across coatings, personal care, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions as a pH regulator and neutralizing agent.

This versatile chemical serves as a curing component in a broad range of formulated products. In architectural and industrial coatings, MIPA neutralizes acidic resins to improve emulsion stability and adjust pH levels.

Personal care formulators use it to neutralize carbomer and acrylate polymers in gels, creams, and lotions. Controlled viscosity and pH are critical to finished product performance in these specific applications.

In adhesive and sealant systems, it acts as a crosslinking agent and curing accelerator for epoxy and polyurethane formulations. This ensures structural integrity and performance in industrial bonding.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers source MIPA as a buffering agent in topical preparations. Consistent pH directly affects stability and regulatory compliance for medical and therapeutic consumer products.

name: Phenyltriethoxysilane
description:
Phenyltriethoxysilane (CAS 780-69-8 ) is an organosilane monomer used to modify surfaces and build silicone-based polymer networks across multiple industrial sectors. It introduces phenyl functionality into silane chemistry, enabling improved thermal stability.

This chemical allows for better compatibility with organic substrates and controlled crosslinking behavior in downstream formulations. In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a surface modifier and coupling agent for various materials.

It improves adhesion between inorganic substrates, such as glass or metal, and organic resin systems. Formulators in the electronics industry incorporate it into encapsulants and dielectric coatings where phenyl-modified networks offer resistance.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it acts as a crosslinking agent and compatibilizer, influencing mechanical performance. It also affects surface wetting in filled systems, making it a versatile component for industrial manufacturing.

Personal care formulators use it as a building block for phenyl silicone emollients and film-forming agents. These deliver specific sensory and spreading properties in skin and hair products, enhancing the final consumer experience.

Phenyltriethoxysilane is supplied as a clear liquid in standard packaging ranging from drums to IBC containers for bulk procurement. It is available in technical and high-purity grades for diverse needs.

Purity specifications are typically at 97% or higher depending on application requirements. Silicone and specialty chemical distributors commonly stock it for use in both R&D and industrial-scale production environments.

name: Hydroxylamine
description:
Hydroxylamine (CAS 7803-49-8 ), also known as azanol, is an inorganic amine used industrially as a reducing agent, oxime-forming reagent, and pH buffer across chemical manufacturing.

It is commercially available primarily as aqueous solutions or as its stable salt forms, hydroxylamine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine sulfate. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it is a critical intermediate.

This chemical is essential for producing oximes, caprolactam, and active pharmaceutical ingredients where selective nitrogen functionalization is required. Agrochemical manufacturers use it in the synthesis of herbicides.

It is also utilized in fungicides and other crop protection compounds. In textile and paper processing, it functions as a reducing agent to strip dyes and control oxidative degradation during bleaching.

Rubber producers apply it as a stabilizer and vulcanization auxiliary, where it moderates cure rates in specialty elastomer formulations. It is supplied as stabilized aqueous solutions, typically at 50% concentration.

Solid salt forms include hydroxylamine hydrochloride and hydroxylamine sulfate. Technical and reagent grades are the most commonly stocked, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to meet USP standards.

The material also meets Ph. Eur. specifications for high-purity applications. Packaging ranges from drums to IBC totes depending on the specific grade and concentration required for your facility.

name: Ammonium metavanadate
description:
Ammonium metavanadate (CAS 7803-55-6 ), also known as AMV, is an inorganic vanadium salt used primarily as a catalyst precursor and vanadium source across chemical processing and metallurgical industries.

It delivers controlled vanadium content in applications where precise dosing and consistent purity are critical to process performance. In catalyst manufacturing, AMV serves as the primary vanadium precursor.

It is used for producing vanadium pentoxide catalysts used in sulfuric acid production via the contact process. The mining and metals sector uses it as a reagent in vanadium recovery circuits.

It is also used for preparing vanadium electrolyte solutions in redox flow battery systems. Pharmaceutical and analytical laboratories rely on AMV as a reagent for colorimetric assays.

It acts as a buffering agent in specific biochemical protocols. It is also applied in ceramic glazes and specialty coatings where vanadium compounds contribute to color development and surface properties.

Ammonium metavanadate is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-purity reagent grade for industrial use.

Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5%+. Packaging options commonly range from small laboratory quantities up to bulk industrial supply with moisture-controlled packaging specified.

name: Hydrazine hydrate
description:
Hydrazine hydrate (CAS 7803-57-8 ) is a concentrated aqueous solution of hydrazine used across chemical manufacturing as a reducing agent, oxygen scavenger, and reactive intermediate.

The Hydrazine hydrate (1:1) designation refers to the same product and carries no distinct commercial identity. Its primary industrial value lies in its ability to drive synthesis reactions.

It is used to remove dissolved oxygen from process streams and initiate polymerization. In boiler water and power plant systems, it scavenges dissolved oxygen to prevent corrosion in high-pressure pipelines.

Pharmaceutical and agrochemical manufacturers rely on it as a building block for synthesizing active ingredients, including hydrazide-based drug compounds and herbicides for global markets.

In polymer production, it initiates polymerization and acts as a chain extender in certain polyurethane and hydrogel systems. Mining and oil and gas operations use it in corrosion inhibition programs.

It also serves as a reducing agent in metal refining and hydrometallurgical processes. Hydrazine hydrate is supplied as a clear aqueous liquid, most commonly at 64% and 80% concentrations.

Technical grade is standard for industrial applications, while higher-purity specifications are available to meet pharmaceutical intermediate requirements for specialized manufacturing.

Bulk supply is typically in drums or IBC containers, with concentration and purity confirmed against established analytical specifications to ensure consistent performance in all applications.

name: Hypophosphoric acid
description:
Hypophosphoric acid ( CAS 7803-60-3 ), also recognized under the systematic name hypodiphosphoric acid, is an inorganic phosphorus acid occupying a distinct oxidation state between phosphorous and phosphoric acid.

It functions industrially as a pH regulator, chelating agent, and corrosion inhibitor across water treatment, mining, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications. In water treatment systems, it sequesters metal ions.

The chemical inhibits scale formation and pipe corrosion in industrial cooling and process water circuits. Mining and metallurgical operations use it for metal ion control during ore processing and leaching stages.

Selective chelation affects downstream metal recovery in these environments. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a reagent and pH-buffering intermediate in synthesis processes requiring precise acid-stage control.

In agricultural chemistry, it serves as a phosphorus-source intermediate in the production of specialty fertilizer formulations and crop protection compounds. This versatility makes it a vital component for many industrial sectors.

Hypophosphoric acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with concentration and purity specifications determined by the intended application. Technical-grade material is the primary commercial form available to industrial buyers.

Pharmaceutical and synthesis-grade material may be available from specialist suppliers, with batch documentation provided on request. All shipments are handled according to strict safety protocols for inorganic acids.

name: Alcohols, C9-11-iso-, C10-rich, ethoxylated
description:
Alcohols, C9-11-iso-, C10-rich, ethoxylated (CAS 78330-20-8 ) is a nonionic surfactant derived from branched-chain fatty alcohols with a predominant C10 carbon distribution. It delivers low-foam emulsification, wetting, and detergency across a broad range of industrial and consumer formulations.

In home care and industrial cleaning, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in hard surface cleaners, degreasers, and laundry formulations where controlled foam and strong soil removal are required.

Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform penetration of dyes and treatment chemicals into fiber substrates. This ensures high-quality finishes and consistent results during the manufacturing process.

Agricultural formulators incorporate it into emulsifiable concentrates and spray adjuvants to improve droplet spreading and active ingredient uptake on leaf surfaces. This enhances the overall efficacy of crop protection products.

Personal care applications include rinse-off products and emulsion systems where it supports oil-in-water emulsification without contributing significant viscosity. It is valued for its stability and compatibility with various cosmetic ingredients.

This product is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid, with viscosity and HLB value varying by degree of ethoxylation. Grades are differentiated by the number of ethylene oxide units, typically ranging from 3 to 8 moles.

The specific mole count determines application fit across low-foam industrial and higher-EO emulsification uses. This versatility allows for precise formulation adjustments based on the specific requirements of the end-use application.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for this chemical. It provides a reliable and cost-effective solution for manufacturers seeking high-performance nonionic surfactants for diverse industrial sectors.

name: Diazolidinyl urea
description:
Diazolidinyl urea (CAS 78491-02-8 ), also known commercially as Germall 11, is a formaldehyde-releasing preservative used across personal care and pharmaceutical formulations.

It provides broad-spectrum antimicrobial protection against bacteria, yeast, and mold, extending the shelf life of water-containing products in various industrial applications.

In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetics, including lotions, shampoos, and conditioners, it is used at low concentrations to prevent microbial contamination throughout the product lifecycle.

Liquid and gel-based personal care formulations benefit from its water solubility, allowing straightforward incorporation without disrupting the stability of the emulsion system.

Pharmaceutical topical preparations such as creams and ointments rely on it to meet preservation efficacy requirements under standard challenge testing protocols for safety.

It is frequently paired with parabens or other co-preservatives to achieve broader coverage and reduce the required use level of each individual ingredient in the final blend.

Diazolidinyl urea is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, conforming to USP and BP monographs.

Standard packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for formulators to bulk drum supply for larger manufacturing operations, ensuring consistent quality for all industrial clients.

name: Magnesium monoperoxyphthalate
description:
Magnesium monoperoxyphthalate ( CAS 78948-87-5 ), commercially known as MMPP or Interox H-48, is a stable solid peroxy acid salt used as an oxidizing agent across industrial and specialty cleaning applications.

Unlike liquid peroxide systems, it delivers controlled oxidative activity in dry formulations, making it a practical choice for formulators handling bleaching and biocidal functions in a single ingredient.

In textile and paper processing, MMPP bleaches natural fibers and pulp without the aggressive fiber degradation associated with hypochlorite systems. Leather manufacturers use it to oxidize tanning residues.

This chemical helps achieve consistent surface brightness in finished hides. In home care and industrial cleaning formulations, it functions as an active bleaching agent in powder detergents and stain removers.

It is also utilized in disinfectant blends and personal care applications. These include tooth-whitening preparations and topical antimicrobial formulations where a stable, dry oxidant source is required.

Magnesium monoperoxyphthalate is supplied as a white to off-white powder, typically with an active oxygen content specification relevant to its oxidizing performance for various industrial needs.

It is available in technical grade, with supply quantities ranging from laboratory-scale packaging to bulk industrial quantities. Buyers should confirm active oxygen content and moisture specifications.

Evaluating lots for formulation use ensures the material meets the necessary standards for efficacy. This stable oxidant remains a versatile component for modern chemical manufacturing and cleaning solutions.

name: Trichloroethylene
description:
Trichloroethylene (CAS 79-01-6 ), commonly abbreviated as TCE and sold under trade names such as Trilene and Triclene, is a chlorinated solvent used primarily for degreasing metal surfaces.

Its high solvency power and low flammability make it a preferred choice in precision cleaning and synthesis applications across various industrial manufacturing sectors worldwide.

In metal fabrication and electronics manufacturing, TCE is used in vapor degreasing systems to remove oils, greases, and machining residues from metal components before coating or assembly.

In the plastics and polymers sector, it functions as a reaction medium and chemical building block in the production of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and other fluoropolymers.

Printing and packaging operations have historically used TCE as a carrier solvent for inks and adhesives requiring fast evaporation and strong substrate penetration.

It also serves as a key feedstock in the synthesis of hydrofluorocarbon refrigerants, particularly HFC-134a, which is essential for modern cooling and refrigeration systems.

Trichloroethylene is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and stabilized grades for vapor degreasing.

Specifications are typically aligned with ISO and ASTM standards relevant to industrial solvent purity requirements to ensure consistent performance in demanding chemical processes.

name: Chloroacetyl chloride
description:
Chloroacetyl chloride (CAS 79-04-9 ), also known as CAC, is a highly reactive acylating agent used as a key building block in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients and agrochemical compounds.

Its reactivity toward amines, alcohols, and other nucleophiles makes it a preferred reagent for introducing the chloroacetyl group in multi-step synthesis programs for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, CAC is used to synthesize a range of APIs including local anesthetics, cardiovascular drugs, and CNS compounds where the chloroacetyl moiety is a critical structural feature.

Agrochemical producers rely on it as an intermediate in the production of herbicides and fungicides, particularly chloroacetamide-class herbicides used in crop protection formulations for global agriculture.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it serves in the preparation of reactive intermediates and labeling reagents used in research-scale synthesis and specialized laboratory applications across the sector.

Industrial chemical manufacturers also use CAC to produce thioethers and other specialty compounds through nucleophilic substitution reactions, ensuring high yields and consistent chemical performance.

Chloroacetyl chloride is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums or ISO containers suited to its corrosive and moisture-sensitive handling requirements for safe transport and storage.

It is available in technical and synthesis-grade specifications, with purity levels commonly at 98% or higher for industrial and pharmaceutical intermediate use in high-demand manufacturing environments.

name: Acrylamide
description:
Acrylamide (CAS 79-06-1 ), also abbreviated as AMD, is a reactive monomer used as the primary building block in the synthesis of polyacrylamide and its copolymers. It enables the production of water-soluble and cross-linked polymer systems.

These systems function as flocculants, thickeners, and retention aids across multiple process industries. In water treatment and mining, polyacrylamide derived from acrylamide acts as a flocculant to separate suspended solids.

This process is essential for cleaning process water and effluent streams. Oil and gas producers use acrylamide-based polymers in enhanced oil recovery formulations and drilling fluid rheology modification for better efficiency.

Pulp and paper manufacturers incorporate polyacrylamide as a retention and drainage aid. This improves fiber recovery and sheet formation during the manufacturing process to ensure high-quality output for industrial clients.

In textile and leather processing, acrylamide copolymers function as sizing agents and surface modifiers. These chemicals help to control coating adhesion and substrate penetration during the finishing stages of production.

Acrylamide is supplied primarily as an aqueous solution, with 50% concentration being the most common commercial form. This format is ideal for polymer synthesis applications requiring high reactivity and easy handling.

Solid acrylamide in crystalline or granular form is available for applications requiring low-moisture handling or specific dosing precision. Technical grade is the standard specification for industrial polymerization use.

name: Propionic acid
description:
Propionic acid (CAS 79-09-4 ), also designated E280 in food additive legislation, is a short-chain carboxylic acid used commercially as a preservative, acidulant, and chemical intermediate.

Its antimicrobial action against mold and certain bacteria makes it a primary active ingredient across food, feed, and industrial preservation applications. In baked goods and dairy products, it extends shelf life.

By inhibiting mold growth at low inclusion rates, it allows formulators to reduce or replace synthetic preservative blends. Grain and silage preservation is a major agricultural outlet for this versatile chemical.

Propionic acid is applied directly to harvested crops to prevent spoilage during storage. Flavor and fragrance manufacturers use it as a building block for propionate ester synthesis including ethyl and isoamyl propionate.

These esters contribute fruity notes to food and beverage formulations. In chemical synthesis, it functions as a catalyst precursor and intermediate in the production of herbicides, pharmaceuticals, and plastics.

Propionic acid is supplied as a clear liquid, typically at 99%+ purity for technical and industrial grades. Food-grade material is available conforming to FCC and E280 specifications.

These grades meet purity and impurity thresholds required for direct food contact use. Bulk supply is standard in drums, IBCs, and tanker quantities depending on the specific application volume required.

name: Acrylic acid
description:
Acrylic acid (CAS 79-10-7 ), also known as vinylformic acid and commonly abbreviated as AA, is a reactive monomer used as the foundational building block for polyacrylate synthesis across polymer and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its ability to undergo controlled polymerization or co-polymerization makes it a primary raw material for producing superabsorbent polymers, dispersants, and coating resins. AA is the primary feedstock for superabsorbent polymers used in hygiene products.

These applications include disposable diapers and adult incontinence articles. In water treatment and detergent formulations, it is polymerized into dispersants and scale inhibitors that prevent mineral deposit buildup in industrial systems.

Acrylic acid co-polymers form the backbone of pressure-sensitive adhesives, surface coatings, and textile sizing agents where controlled adhesion and film formation are required. These materials are essential for modern industrial manufacturing.

Personal care formulators use polyacrylate thickeners derived from AA as rheology modifiers in gels, creams, and hair styling products. This versatility ensures its widespread use in the cosmetic and pharmaceutical sectors globally.

Acrylic acid is supplied as a stabilized liquid, typically with hydroquinone monomethyl ether added to inhibit premature polymerization during storage and transport. This ensures the material remains stable for industrial use.

Standard commercial grades include glacial and technical grades, with purity levels commonly at 99%+ for polymer-grade applications. These products meet rigorous industrial specifications for high-performance chemical synthesis.

Bulk supply is available in drums, ISO tanks, and flexi-tanks depending on volume requirements. Our logistics network ensures safe and efficient delivery of this essential monomer to your facility according to your specific needs.

name: Chloroacetic acid
description:
Chloroacetic acid (CAS 79-11-8 ), also sold as monochloroacetic acid (MCA), is a halogenated organic acid used as a high-reactivity chemical intermediate across agrochemical, pharmaceutical, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its primary commercial role is as an alkylating and carboxymethylating agent in the synthesis of downstream derivatives. In agrochemicals, MCA is a critical building block for herbicide active ingredients including glyphosate and 2,4-D.

It is also essential for chloroacetamide-class compounds. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to produce carboxymethyl-substituted APIs and intermediates, including certain amino acid derivatives that require high precision during synthesis.

In the textile and paper industries, it drives the production of carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), a thickening and binding agent used in coatings, adhesives, and sizing formulations for various industrial applications.

It also serves as a precursor in the manufacture of surfactants, dyes, and thioglycolic acid used in leather processing. Chloroacetic acid is supplied as white to off-white crystalline flakes or as a molten liquid.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP specifications. These standards ensure the material is suitable for sensitive chemical manufacturing processes.

Purity levels typically range from 98% to 99.5%+, with both monomer-grade and synthesis-grade options available. The choice of grade depends entirely on the specific requirements of the downstream application and final product.

name: Glycolic acid
description:
Glycolic acid (CAS 79-14-1 ) is the smallest alpha-hydroxy acid, giving it exceptional skin penetration relative to other AHA compounds used in cosmetic formulations. Industrially, it functions as a pH regulator, chelating agent, and descaling chemistry across a broad range of manufacturing processes.

In personal care, it is the active ingredient in chemical exfoliant products — peels, serums, and anti-aging creams — where concentration and grade determine regulatory classification. Textile and leather processors use it for pH control during dyeing and tanning operations.

Consistent acidity directly affects color uptake and hide quality in these industrial settings. Water treatment applications rely on its chelating action to sequester metal ions and inhibit scale formation in boiler and cooling systems.

In food-contact and industrial cleaning formulations, it serves as a descaling and surface-conditioning acid where low residue and biodegradability are procurement advantages. Glycolic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at 70% concentration.

Lower concentrations are available for specific end-use requirements. Technical and industrial grades cover the cleaning and process chemistry markets, while cosmetic-grade material meets purity standards required by personal care manufacturers.

Food-grade specifications are also available for applications requiring compliance with food-contact or FCC standards. This ensures the material meets the rigorous safety and quality benchmarks necessary for sensitive industrial applications.

name: Methyl acetate
description:
Methyl acetate (CAS 79-20-9 ), also known by its FEMA 2676 designation, is a fast-evaporating ester solvent used across food flavoring and personal care manufacturing. Tereton is a recognized trade name encountered in certain European markets.

Its rapid evaporation rate makes it a preferred carrier in formulations where residual solvent presence must be minimized. In food and beverage production, methyl acetate functions as a FEMA-approved flavoring agent.

It contributes fruity, apple-like top notes to confectionery, beverages, and baked goods. Personal care manufacturers use it as a solvent in nail polish removers, aerosol formulations, and fragrance delivery systems.

In these applications, clean evaporation is critical. In flavor compounding, it acts as a carrier solvent that helps disperse and stabilize aromatic ingredients without masking the target flavor profile.

It also appears in cosmetic sprays and hair care aerosols where a low-residue solvent is required for finish quality. Methyl acetate is supplied as a clear liquid in drums, IBCs, and bulk tanker quantities.

Food-grade material conforming to FEMA and FCC specifications is available for flavoring applications, while technical-grade is standard for industrial solvent use.

Purity levels typically range from 99% and above for commercial supply. This high level of purity ensures consistent performance across both food-grade and industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Peracetic acid
description:
Peracetic acid (CAS 79-21-0 ), commonly abbreviated as PAA and also known as peroxyacetic acid, is a high-performance oxidizing biocide and disinfectant used across food processing, water treatment, and industrial sanitation.

It delivers rapid, broad-spectrum antimicrobial action and leaves no persistent residues, making it a preferred alternative to chlorine-based disinfectants in regulated environments. In food and beverage processing, PAA is used to sanitize equipment.

It is applied to conveyors and packaging surfaces where chemical residue limits are strictly controlled. Pulp and paper manufacturers apply it as a bleaching agent to brighten pulp without the chlorinated byproducts associated with traditional bleaching.

Municipal and industrial water treatment operations use PAA to disinfect effluent and process water, particularly where discharge regulations restrict chlorine use. Pharmaceutical and healthcare facilities rely on it for sterilization.

It is used for production environments and medical device decontamination. Peracetic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly in concentrations ranging from 5% to 40%, with equilibrium mixtures containing acetic acid.

These mixtures also contain hydrogen peroxide. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet regulatory requirements in sensitive applications. Industrial-grade supply is standard for paper bleaching.

It is also the standard for wastewater treatment end uses. This versatile chemical ensures high safety standards across various sectors while maintaining environmental compliance through its biodegradable nature.

name: Hydroxymethanesulfinic acid
description:
Hydroxymethanesulfinic acid ( CAS 79-25-4 ), commercially supplied as its sodium salt form, is a reducing agent used across textile, paper, and cleaning industries. It functions primarily as a bleaching and stripping agent.

The compound works by breaking down colorants and oxidized compounds under controlled conditions. In textile and leather processing, it serves as a discharge agent for vat and reactive dyes, enabling precise color removal.

This chemical allows for effective processing without damaging fiber substrates. Paper manufacturers use it to brighten mechanical pulp and control residual color in recycled fiber streams during the production process.

In industrial and institutional cleaning formulations, it targets stubborn stains and oxidized soils where conventional alkaline cleaners fall short. It provides a specialized solution for difficult cleaning tasks.

Water treatment operations apply it as a reducing agent to neutralize excess oxidants such as chlorine or hydrogen peroxide prior to discharge. This ensures that effluent meets environmental safety requirements.

This product is available in powder and granular forms, with the sodium salt being the predominant commercial grade supplied to industrial buyers. Technical-grade specifications are standard across most supply channels.

Purity levels and active content are typically confirmed by titration or redox assay to ensure consistency. Packaging ranges from small bags to bulk quantities depending on specific application volume requirements.

name: 1,1,2,2-tetrabromoethane
description:
1,1,2,2-Tetrabromoethane (CAS 79-27-6 ), also known as TBE or Muthmann's liquid, is a dense halogenated solvent with a specific gravity significantly above most organic liquids. This property makes it a selective tool for density-based separation and analytical processes across several industrial sectors.

In mineral processing and ore analysis, TBE functions as a heavy liquid medium for sink-float separation, allowing laboratories and mining operations to isolate minerals by density without mechanical crushing.

Pharmaceutical and chemical manufacturers use it as a solvent in specialized synthesis steps where halogenated media are required for reaction control or intermediate processing. It provides a stable environment for complex chemical transformations.

In biotechnology and life sciences, TBE serves as a reference liquid and density gradient medium in laboratory-scale separations and microscopy preparation workflows. Its high density also makes it a calibration reference in analytical instrumentation.

The product is used for quality control in research environments where precise density measurements are required. 1,1,2,2-Tetrabromoethane is supplied as a liquid, typically in reagent-grade and technical-grade specifications.

Reagent-grade material is available for laboratory and analytical applications, while technical-grade supply supports larger-scale industrial use. It is commonly packaged in smaller quantities reflecting its specialized demand profile.

name: Isobutyric acid
description:
Isobutyric acid ( CAS 79-31-2 ), also known as isobutanoic acid, is a short-chain branched carboxylic acid used across food, fragrance, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a chemical intermediate and flavoring agent.

The compound is identified by FEMA 2222 and serves as a pH regulator in industrial and specialty formulations. In flavor and fragrance production, it serves as a precursor to isobutyrate esters.

These compounds deliver fruity, cheesy, and buttery notes in food products and perfumery. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a synthetic intermediate in the production of active ingredients and excipients.

It is particularly useful for applications requiring branched-chain acid building blocks. In personal care formulations, isobutyrate derivatives contribute to fragrance profiles in lotions and shampoos.

The acid also functions as a catalyst precursor and pH-adjusting agent in specialty chemical synthesis and fermentation processes. It is supplied as a colorless liquid in drum, IBC, and bulk quantities.

Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is available for flavor and food additive applications. Technical-grade material is offered for industrial synthesis and non-food uses.

name: L-lactic acid
description:
L-Lactic acid (CAS 79-33-4 ) is the naturally occurring, single-enantiomer form of lactic acid, produced commercially through fermentation of carbohydrate feedstocks. It functions as an acidulant, pH regulator, and preservative across food, pharmaceutical, personal care, and industrial manufacturing sectors.

In food and beverage production, it acidifies and preserves products including pickled vegetables, dairy alternatives, meat preparations, and ready-to-eat meals. This is particularly important where clean-label fermentation-derived sourcing is a specification requirement for the final product.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators use it for pH adjustment in topical preparations and oral solutions. It also serves as a chiral building block in API synthesis, meeting strict USP and BP quality standards for medical applications.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into exfoliating creams, toners, and moisturizing formulations. Its dual role as a humectant and mild keratolytic agent drives consumer product differentiation in high-end skincare lines and professional cosmetic treatments.

In leather processing and textile finishing, it controls bath pH and acts as a mild acidulant during dyeing and tanning operations. This ensures consistent color uptake and material integrity throughout the industrial manufacturing process.

L-Lactic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 80% and 88% concentrations being the most commercially standard. Ph.Eur. and food-grade variants are available to meet specific regulatory requirements across different global end markets.

Bulk liquid supply in IBC containers or tankers is typical for industrial volumes. Smaller drum packaging is also available for specialty and pharmaceutical procurement, ensuring flexibility for various production scales and storage requirements.

name: Methacrylamide
description:
Methacrylamide (CAS 79-39-0 ) is a reactive monomer used to build functional polymer networks across specialty chemical manufacturing. It is commercially recognized under the name methacrylic acid amide in some supplier and regulatory contexts.

Its primary industrial role is as a co-monomer that introduces amide functionality into polymer backbones, enabling controlled surface chemistry and hydrogel formation. In biotechnology and life sciences, it is a key building block for polyacrylamide-based hydrogels.

These hydrogels are used in cell culture scaffolds, drug delivery matrices, and gel electrophoresis systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into film-forming and conditioning polymers where surface adhesion and moisture retention are critical.

name: Methacrylic acid
description:
Methacrylic acid (CAS 79-41-4 ), commonly abbreviated as MAA, is a reactive monomer and organic acid used as a foundational building block in polymer synthesis. It enables the production of acrylate and methacrylate copolymers that underpin a broad range of industrial and consumer materials.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, MAA is copolymerized with acrylates, styrene, or vinyl monomers to produce resins with controlled adhesion, flexibility, and pH-responsive behavior. These characteristics are critical for coatings, adhesives, and ion-exchange materials.

Personal care formulators incorporate MAA-based polymers into carbomer-type thickeners, film formers, and fixative resins used in haircare and skincare products. These polymers provide the necessary texture and performance required for modern cosmetic formulations.

In specialty coatings and dispersions, MAA content determines carboxyl group density, directly influencing crosslink density and substrate adhesion in industrial finishes. This allows for the creation of durable surfaces that withstand harsh environmental conditions.

Pharmaceutical and controlled-release applications use MAA copolymers to engineer enteric coatings that govern drug release profiles. These systems ensure that active ingredients are delivered effectively within the human body at the correct physiological stage.

Methacrylic acid is supplied as a liquid, typically with inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Standard commercial grades include technical and glacial specifications to meet various industrial needs.

Purity levels are commonly at 99% or higher for polymerization-grade material, ensuring consistent performance in sensitive chemical reactions. Bulk quantities are available in drums, IBCs, and isotank shipments for global distribution.

name: Thiolactic acid
description:
Thiolactic acid (CAS 79-42-5 ), also known as alpha-mercaptopropionic acid, is a sulfur-containing organic acid used across pharmaceutical synthesis, personal care manufacturing, and industrial processing.

Its thiol and carboxylic acid groups make it a reactive intermediate for building complex molecules and a functional agent in formulation chemistry. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of active ingredients and chiral building blocks where precise stereochemistry is required. Personal care formulators use it in hair waving and straightening products for styling.

Controlled reduction of disulfide bonds in keratin enables permanent styling effects. Leather processors apply it during hide treatment to modify protein structure and improve softness and dye uptake.

In textile processing, it supports fiber preparation and finishing steps where controlled pH and reducing conditions are needed. Thiolactic acid is supplied as a liquid, typically at 80–85% aqueous solution.

Higher purity grades are available for pharmaceutical applications. Technical-grade material is standard for industrial textile and leather uses. Pharmaceutical-grade supply is available for specific customers.

This supply is for customers requiring documentation aligned with GMP manufacturing standards. The material ensures high performance across diverse industrial, cosmetic, and medicinal chemical applications.

name: Pantolactone
description:
Pantolactone (CAS 79-50-5 ), also supplied as DL-Pantolactone, is a cyclic lactone intermediate used across pharmaceutical synthesis, cosmetic formulation, and food processing. It functions primarily as a chiral building block and stabilizing agent.

This chemical is essential in the production of pantothenic acid (Vitamin B5) and related compounds. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key precursor in the synthesis of pantothenic acid and coenzyme A derivatives.

Controlled stereochemistry drives sourcing decisions for this material in medical applications. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin care products for its moisture-retention properties, supporting hydration in serums and creams.

It is also utilized in hair conditioning treatments to improve texture and health. In food and flavor applications, it contributes stabilizing functionality to nutrient premixes and various fortified products.

Research and fine chemical producers source it as a resolved or racemic chiral synthon for asymmetric synthesis programs. The material is available as a white crystalline powder or solid for industrial use.

It is supplied in both racemic (DL) and optically active forms to meet specific needs. Purity grades range from technical to high-purity pharmaceutical-grade material, often meeting USP or FCC standards.

Packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities to bulk drums, depending on application requirements. This versatility ensures that both laboratory and large-scale manufacturing needs are met efficiently.

In cosmetics and skincare, it is incorporated into moisturizers, serums, and anti-aging formulations where it supports skin renewal. It acts as a lipid-soluble antioxidant to protect product integrity and enhance the overall efficacy of topical applications.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it to fortify products such as dairy alternatives, infant formula, and margarine to meet regulatory Vitamin A requirements. It is a critical component for ensuring nutritional compliance in large-scale food production.

Pharmaceutical producers incorporate it into oral supplements, multivitamin preparations, and topical drug products as a bioavailable retinol source. It also serves nutritional premix manufacturers supplying fortified feed and food ingredient blends at industrial scale.

Retinyl palmitate is supplied as an oily liquid, a dry powder, or in oil dispersion form depending on the target application. Standard grades include USP , BP , and food-grade specifications, with potency typically expressed in IU/g.

name: Pantothenic acid
description:
Pantothenic acid (CAS 79-83-4 ), commonly known as Vitamin B5, is a water-soluble B-vitamin used across food, feed, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. In formulated products, it functions as a nutrient source and humectant.

It supports moisture retention in topical applications and metabolic function in nutritional contexts. In animal feed and premix production, it is incorporated to meet the B-vitamin requirements of poultry and swine.

It is also used in aquaculture species, where deficiency directly impacts growth performance. Food and beverage manufacturers use it to fortify products such as energy drinks, infant formula, and dietary supplements.

In personal care, it acts as a humectant in skin creams, shampoos, and conditioners. It often serves as a precursor to panthenol, improving moisture retention in the finished formula for various cosmetic applications.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers include it in multivitamin tablets, capsules, and injectable preparations targeting nutritional supplementation. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder for industrial use.

The calcium salt form, calcium pantothenate, is the predominant commercial grade due to its superior stability. Recognized grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade FCC specifications.

Both the free acid and calcium salt forms are available for global distribution. Purity levels are typically at 98% or higher for pharmaceutical and food applications to ensure the highest quality standards.

name: Tetrabromobisphenol a
description:
Tetrabromobisphenol A (CAS 79-94-7 ), commonly abbreviated as TBBPA, is the most commercially produced brominated flame retardant in the world. It functions as a reactive or additive flame retardant in polymer systems.

The chemical interrupts combustion cycles to prevent ignition and limit fire spread in finished materials. In electronics manufacturing, TBBPA is reacted directly into epoxy resin matrices during the production of FR-4 printed circuit boards.

It becomes a permanent part of the cured laminate in these applications. Automotive and aerospace components use TBBPA-containing polymers to meet stringent flammability standards in interior panels, housings, and structural parts.

In building and construction, it is incorporated into ABS, HIPS, and polycarbonate compounds. These materials are used for insulation panels, cable sheathing, and electrical enclosures across the global infrastructure sector.

Plastics compounders also use TBBPA as a precursor to produce derivative flame retardants. These include TBBPA-based epoxy oligomers and carbonate oligomers for use across multiple industrial end markets.

TBBPA is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use. Standard commercial grades include technical-grade material, with purity typically specified at 97% or higher for consistent performance.

Supply is available in bulk bags and fiber drums to suit various manufacturing scales. Specifications are strictly aligned to industrial and electronics-sector requirements for high-performance chemical additives.

name: Fluazifop-p-butyl
description:
Fluazifop-p-butyl (CAS 79241-46-6 ), sold commercially as Fusilade Super, Fusilade II, and Fusilade 2000, is a selective post-emergent herbicide used in broad-spectrum grass control across row crops and specialty agriculture.

It targets grassy weeds without affecting broadleaf crops, making it a preferred active ingredient for weed management programs where crop selectivity is critical for the grower.

In soybean, cotton, and sunflower cultivation, it controls annual and perennial grass species such as volunteer cereals and couch grass at post-emergence stages to ensure high yields.

Vegetable and oilseed crop producers apply it to protect yield by eliminating competitive grass pressure during early crop development. It is also formulated into ready-to-use herbicide products.

The chemical is used in tank-mix programs where graminicide activity is required alongside broadleaf herbicides. Turf and ornamental growers use it to manage grass weed encroachment in non-cereal systems.

Fluazifop-p-butyl is supplied as an emulsifiable concentrate (EC), typically at 125 g/L or 150 g/L active ingredient concentrations. Technical-grade material is available for formulators producing finished products.

Supply is offered in bulk drums and intermediate bulk containers (IBCs) to support both formulation-scale and distribution requirements. Our material meets rigorous industrial quality standards for purity.

description:
Sertraline hydrochloride (CAS 79559-97-0 ), commonly referenced as sertraline HCl in pharmaceutical procurement, is the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) form of sertraline.

It is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) used in the manufacture of finished oral dosage forms. It is sourced by drug manufacturers and generic pharmaceutical producers.

The primary application is in the manufacture of oral solid dosage forms, including film-coated tablets and capsules, where sertraline HCl is the API at specified therapeutic concentrations.

Generic pharmaceutical manufacturers source it to produce bioequivalent products following patent expiry of the originator brand. CDMOs use it in formulation development projects.

Regulatory submissions for finished drug products in major markets require sertraline HCl to meet pharmacopoeial or ICH-aligned specifications for safety and efficacy.

name: Decaglycerin monooleate
description:
Decaglycerin monooleate (CAS 79665-93-3 ) is a polyglycerol ester derived from decaglycerol and oleic acid, functioning as a nonionic emulsifier and solubilizer across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications.

Its high hydrophilic character makes it effective at stabilizing oil-in-water systems where conventional mono- and diglycerides fall short. In food manufacturing, it emulsifies fat-based fillings and bakery shortenings.

This ingredient improves texture consistency and shelf stability in margarine and other spreads. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a carrier and solubilizer for lipophilic active ingredients in oral and topical delivery systems.

In personal care, it stabilizes emulsions in creams and lotions while supporting the dispersion of oils in water-based formulations. It also functions as a co-emulsifier in low-fat and reduced-calorie food products.

Clean-label polyglycerol esters are often preferred over synthetic alternatives in modern formulations. Decaglycerin monooleate is typically supplied as a viscous liquid or paste at ambient temperature.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC or regional food additive specifications is the most commonly traded form. Technical-grade material is available for cosmetic and industrial applications.

This versatile chemical ensures high performance in complex formulations where food compliance is not required. It remains a staple for manufacturers seeking reliable emulsification and solubilization properties.
