name: Kojic acid dipalmitate
description:
Kojic acid dipalmitate (CAS 79725-98-7 ), commonly abbreviated as KAD, is a lipophilic ester derivative of kojic acid used primarily as a skin-brightening and antioxidant active in cosmetic formulations.

Unlike its parent compound, KAD offers enhanced oil-solubility and improved stability, making it suitable for incorporation into anhydrous and emulsion-based systems.

In personal care, KAD functions as a tyrosinase inhibitor incorporated into serums, creams, and sunscreens targeting uneven skin tone and hyperpigmentation.

Its oil-compatible profile allows formulators to load it into lipid-rich vehicles such as facial oils, balms, and color cosmetics without the stability concerns associated with kojic acid.

In plastics and polymer processing, KAD is evaluated as a stabilizing additive to limit oxidative degradation during compounding for various industrial applications.

Lubricant formulators have also explored it as a functional additive where antioxidant protection of the base oil is a critical formulation requirement for performance.

Kojic acid dipalmitate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, the standard form demanded by personal care manufacturers.

Bulk quantities are typically offered in kilogram and metric ton packaging, with technical-grade material available for industrial applications and large scale manufacturing needs.

name: Decaglycerin monostearate

Decaglycerin monostearate (CAS 79777-30-3 ) is a polyglycerol ester derived from decaglycerol and stearic acid. It is used as a food-grade emulsifier and rheology modifier across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Its high hydrophilic character makes it effective at stabilizing oil-in-water emulsions where conventional mono- and diglycerides underperform. In food production, it stabilizes emulsified sauces, dressings, and low-fat spreads.

The compound improves fat dispersion and prevents phase separation during processing and shelf life. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into creams and lotions to control viscosity and achieve stable emulsion textures.

It allows for stable formulations without the need for heavy wax systems. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as an excipient in topical and oral formulations where controlled release is required.

It ensures uniform dispersion of active ingredients in various medical applications. Bakery applications benefit from its ability to interact with starch and delay crumb firming in bread and soft baked goods.

This pigment is ideal for use where durability under processing or outdoor exposure is a primary sourcing requirement. In automotive OEM and refinish coatings, it meets the stringent weathering and heat resistance standards required for exterior topcoats.

Plastics compounders select it for engineering polymers and masterbatch production where processing temperatures are critical. It ensures long-term color retention in various polymer matrices and high-performance plastic applications.

Packaging and commercial printing applications benefit from its high tinting strength in offset, gravure, and flexographic ink systems. It provides a bright, stable yellow needed in pigment printing pastes or surface coatings.

name: Bisphenol a

Bisphenol A (CAS 80-05-7 ), commonly abbreviated as BPA, is a high-volume industrial monomer used primarily to manufacture polycarbonate plastics and epoxy resins. It functions as a foundational building block in polymer synthesis.

This chemical enables the production of durable, heat-resistant materials across multiple industrial sectors. In epoxy resin formulations, BPA reacts with epichlorohydrin to produce bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (BADGE).

This substance serves as the base resin used in protective coatings, adhesives, and industrial laminates. Polycarbonate production accounts for a significant share of BPA consumption globally.

name: 4,4'-Sulfonyldiphenol

The paper and textile industries use BPS as a color developer in thermal recording papers and as a dye-fixing agent in fabric treatment processes for industrial applications.

Formulators in personal care and cosmetics evaluate BPS as a functional ingredient in product stabilization systems. It also serves as a pharmaceutical intermediate in the synthesis of active compounds.

Its antioxidant character supports its use in stabilizing polymer formulations against degradation during processing. 4,4'-Sulfonyldiphenol is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

name: Cumene hydroperoxide
description:
Cumene hydroperoxide (CAS 80-15-9 ), also known as CHP or isopropylbenzene hydroperoxide, is an organic peroxide used industrially as a free-radical source for initiating polymerization and curing reactions.

It functions as a highly effective oxidizing agent in rubber and polymer manufacturing, where controlled radical generation is critical to process consistency. In rubber compounding, CHP acts as a cross-linking agent.

This chemical is used to vulcanize silicone and specialty elastomers, producing materials with improved heat resistance and mechanical performance. Polymer producers use it to initiate emulsion and solution polymerization.

It is effective for styrene, acrylates, and other vinyl monomers in the manufacture of resins and synthetic rubbers. It also serves as a co-agent in redox initiator systems where it pairs with reducing agents.

This enables low-temperature polymerization, which is a requirement in cold rubber processes. Tire manufacturers rely on CHP-based curing systems to achieve consistent crosslink density in high-performance rubber compounds.

Cumene hydroperoxide is supplied as a liquid, typically as an 80% or 88% active solution in cumene. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial polymerization and curing applications.

Bulk liquid supply in drums and IBC containers is the norm, with concentration and purity confirmed by titration or GC analysis per buyer specification to ensure high quality standards.

name: Ethyl Tosylamide
description:
Ethyl Tosylamide (CAS 80-39-7 ), also known by the abbreviation ETSM, is a sulfonamide-based plasticizer and solvent used across polymer processing and industrial formulation. It functions primarily as a plasticizer and carrier.

The material is highly effective at improving flow and reducing brittleness in finished parts. The textile and leather industries use it as a softening agent and carrier solvent in finishing formulations for various substrates.

In these applications, it aids the penetration of active components into fiber or hide substrates. In metalworking and lubricant formulations, it functions as a functional solvent that improves additive compatibility.

The product also enhances film-forming properties in industrial coatings. Paper treatment applications employ ETSM to modify surface flexibility and coating adhesion, ensuring high-quality results in specialized manufacturing processes.

Ethyl Tosylamide is supplied as a pale to off-white solid, typically in flake or powder form. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity specifications commonly at 99% or above.

Packaging is available in bags or drums suited to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures safe handling and efficient logistics for large-scale manufacturing operations requiring consistent chemical supply.

name: Dicumyl peroxide
description:
Dicumyl peroxide (CAS 80-43-3 ), also known as cumyl peroxide, is an organic peroxide used industrially as a cross-linking agent and free-radical polymerization initiator. It enables controlled vulcanization of elastomers and curing of thermoplastics.

This chemical is essential for thermosets across demanding manufacturing environments. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it cross-links EPDM, silicone, and natural rubber compounds to improve heat resistance and mechanical durability.

Wire and cable producers use it to cure polyethylene insulation, producing XLPE with the electrical and thermal performance required for medium- and high-voltage applications. This ensures long-term stability in infrastructure.

Automotive and aerospace component manufacturers rely on it to cure molded rubber seals, gaskets, and vibration-dampening parts. Peroxide curing outperforms sulfur systems in long-term heat aging scenarios.

It also initiates controlled grafting and polymerization reactions in polymer modification processes. This includes the production of impact-modified polypropylene compounds used in various industrial sectors.

Dicumyl peroxide is supplied as a white crystalline powder and in granule form. The active oxygen content is typically specified at 98% purity minimum to ensure consistent performance in chemical reactions.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering for most buyers. Concentrations and carrier-based masterbatch forms are available to meet handling and dosing requirements in industrial compounding lines.

name: Methyl methacrylate
description:
Methyl methacrylate ( CAS 80-62-6 ), commonly known as MMA, is a reactive monomer used as the primary building block for polymerization processes across coatings, plastics, and adhesive systems.

It polymerizes readily to form poly(methyl methacrylate) and serves as a co-monomer in a broad range of acrylic polymer formulations. In coatings and surface treatments, MMA is polymerized to produce acrylic resins.

These resins deliver optical clarity, UV resistance, and durability in automotive, architectural, and industrial finishes. Adhesive and sealant formulators use MMA-based systems where fast cure and high bond strength are required.

These systems include structural acrylic adhesives used for bonding metals and plastics. In plastics manufacturing, MMA is the feedstock for cast and extruded PMMA sheet, used in signage, displays, and optical components.

Printing and packaging applications rely on MMA copolymers in UV-curable inks and barrier coatings. These applications are critical where adhesion to film substrates is a primary requirement for the final product.

MMA is supplied as a stabilized liquid monomer, typically inhibited with hydroquinone monomethyl ether (MEHQ) to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. This ensures product stability.

Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and technical applications. Inhibitor levels and purity specifications vary by end-use requirement to meet specific manufacturing standards for industrial buyers.

Bulk liquid, IBC, and drum packaging are the standard supply formats for industrial buyers. These logistics options ensure that the monomer is delivered safely and efficiently for large-scale chemical production.

name: 1,1,3,3-Tetramethylguanidine
description:
1,1,3,3-Tetramethylguanidine (CAS 80-70-6 ), commonly known as TMG, is a strong, non-nucleophilic organic superbase used as a catalyst and proton acceptor across polymer chemistry and specialty synthesis.

Its high basicity without nucleophilic interference makes it a preferred choice where conventional amine catalysts cause unwanted side reactions. In polyurethane and epoxy formulations, TMG accelerates cure by activating isocyanate or epoxide crosslinking reactions.

This allows formulators to tune gel times and processing windows effectively. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it to promote room-temperature curing in silicone and polyurethane systems for better performance.

In coatings, it functions as a neutralizing agent for acid-functional resins, improving dispersion stability and film formation. It achieves this without introducing nucleophilic contamination to the final product.

Polymer producers also employ TMG as a base catalyst in ring-opening polymerizations and condensation reactions. These applications are critical where selectivity and controlled initiation are required for quality.

TMG is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC quantities. Technical grade is the primary commercial form, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher for catalyst-grade applications.

Specification requirements should be confirmed with the supplier, as purity thresholds vary by end-use process sensitivity. This ensures the material meets the specific needs of your industrial chemical process.

name: Petroleum
description:
Petroleum (CAS 8002-05-9 ), also known as raw oil, is a naturally occurring hydrocarbon mixture extracted from geological formations and refined into the foundational feedstocks that power modern industry.

It functions as the primary source material for fuels, lubricants, solvents, and petrochemical intermediates across virtually every manufacturing sector. In the energy sector, it is processed into gasoline and diesel.

Through fractional distillation, it becomes the core input for combustion-based power generation and transportation. Lubricant manufacturers draw on specific fractions to produce base oils used in engine oils and industrial greases.

Solvent-grade cuts derived from this material are used as carrier fluids in coatings, adhesives, and metalworking formulations where controlled evaporation and solvency are required for high-performance applications.

Petrochemical producers also use it as a cracking feedstock to manufacture ethylene, propylene, and other building-block chemicals for plastics and synthetic materials used in global manufacturing chains.

name: Pine oil
description:
Pine oil (CAS 8002-09-3 ), also recognized under FEMA 2907 , is a natural terpene-based oil derived from pine wood and needles. It functions as a disinfectant, cleaning agent, froth flotation collector, and fragrance ingredient across a broad range of industrial and consumer applications.

In household and institutional cleaning products, pine oil is formulated into disinfectant cleaners, floor cleaners, and all-purpose degreasers. Here it provides both antimicrobial action and characteristic pine fragrance for various surfaces.

Mining operations rely on it as a froth flotation collector and frother to improve the separation of sulfide ores and coal. In personal care and cosmetics, it contributes fragrance and preservative properties to soaps and bath products.

Textile and leather processing facilities use it as a scouring and degreasing agent to remove oils and contaminants from raw materials. This process is essential before dyeing or finishing to ensure high-quality results in the final product.

Pine oil is supplied as a liquid in technical and industrial grades, with purity levels typically ranging from 50% to 85% alpha-terpineol content. The specific concentration depends on the intended application and performance requirements.

Food-grade material is available for flavoring applications under the FEMA 2907 designation. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with technical grade being the most common form for cleaning and mining end uses.

name: Rapeseed oil
description:
Rapeseed oil (CAS 8002-13-9 ), also known as rape oil, is a vegetable oil pressed or extracted from the seeds of Brassica napus and related species. It functions as a base oil, plasticizer, and lubricant across food, cosmetic, and industrial manufacturing sectors.

In food manufacturing, it serves as a cooking and frying medium, a carrier oil in flavor systems, and a base for margarine and shortening production. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, hair conditioners, and lip products.

In these cosmetic applications, it acts as an emollient and spreading agent. Industrial grades are used as a base fluid in metalworking lubricants, hydraulic fluids, and release agents, where its natural lubricity reduces friction and tool wear.

In rubber and tire compounding, it functions as a process oil and softener, improving the workability of rubber compounds during mixing. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for manufacturers seeking sustainable plant-based alternatives.

Rapeseed oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in bulk tankers, IBCs, and drums. Food-grade specifications are available meeting FCC and edible oil standards, while technical and industrial grades are offered for non-food applications.

Refined, bleached, and deodorized (RBD) variants are the most commonly traded forms across both food and industrial markets. These processes ensure the oil meets the necessary purity and stability requirements for long-term storage and use.

name: Tall oil
description:
Tall oil (CAS 8002-26-4 ), also marketed under trade names such as Yatall MA and Westvaco CTO, is a byproduct of the kraft pulping process refined into a commercially traded fatty acid and resin acid mixture.

It functions as a low-cost, bio-based raw material for surface modification, lubrication, and rheology control across multiple industrial sectors. In coatings and adhesives, tall oil derivatives act as emulsifiers and tackifiers.

These components contribute to film formation and substrate adhesion in solvent-borne and water-borne systems. The rubber and tire industry uses it as a processing aid and softener to improve compound flow.

This application helps in reducing mixing viscosity during compounding. Textile and leather processors apply it as a lubricant and wetting agent to improve fiber handling and surface penetration of treatment chemicals.

In pulp and paper operations, it supports sizing formulations and internal lubrication of paper machine components. Tall oil is supplied as a dark viscous liquid, with crude tall oil and distilled tall oil representing the primary grades.

Refined fractions, including tall oil fatty acids and tall oil rosin, are available for applications requiring tighter acid value and resin content specifications. Technical grade is the standard market offering.

Specifications for this material are typically defined by acid value, rosin content, and unsaponifiable matter. This ensures consistent performance across various industrial manufacturing and chemical processing environments.

name: Tar oils
description:

In rubber compounding, these oils act as processing aids and softeners that improve the workability of natural and synthetic rubber stocks during mixing and calendering. This ensures better consistency during the manufacturing process.

Coatings and sealant formulators incorporate them as carrier solvents in bituminous and protective coatings applied to infrastructure, pipelines, and roofing systems. They provide essential durability for long-term industrial protection.

The printing and packaging industry uses these fractions as solvent components in certain ink systems where high-boiling aromatic solvents are required. This application is critical for specialized high-speed printing environments.

In construction-grade adhesives and sealants, they contribute to tack development and substrate penetration in heavy-duty bonding applications. This allows for superior adhesion on difficult industrial surfaces and materials.

These products are supplied as dark, viscous liquids, with specific distillation cuts available to meet different boiling range requirements. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form for most buyers.

In confectionery, it is the primary structuring fat in chocolate, controlling snap, gloss, and mouthfeel in finished bars and coatings. Cosmetic formulators use it as an emollient base.

In lip balms, body butters, and skin creams, its solid-to-liquid transition at skin temperature delivers a characteristic skin-feel. Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on it as a suppository base.

It takes advantage of its sharp, consistent melting point for controlled drug release. It also functions as a binder and coating agent in tablet manufacturing and medicated confectionery.

name: Sulfated castor oil
description:
Sulfated castor oil (CAS 8002-33-3 ), also known as Turkey-red oil and commercially as SCO, is produced by treating castor oil with sulfuric acid to yield a self-emulsifying anionic surfactant.

It was among the first synthetic-process surfactants used in industry and remains a benchmark emulsifier and wetting agent across multiple manufacturing sectors for various industrial applications.

In textile processing, SCO enables uniform dye penetration and fiber lubrication during dyeing and finishing operations, particularly for cotton and wool. This ensures high-quality results in fabric production.

Leather manufacturers use it as a fat-liquoring and softening agent to improve hide flexibility and surface uniformity. In personal care formulations, it functions as an emulsifier and humectant.

It is commonly found in bath oils, hair preparations, and skin creams where oil-in-water dispersion is required. Agricultural formulators incorporate it as a wetting and spreading agent in pesticide concentrates.

Sulfated castor oil is supplied as a viscous amber liquid, typically at 75% active matter content, though concentrations vary by supplier specification. Standard grades include technical and industrial quality.

Textile and leather grades are the most commonly traded forms of this chemical. Buyers should confirm sulfation degree and active content against application requirements for optimal performance.

These specific parameters directly affect emulsification performance and the overall stability of the final product. Proper testing ensures the material meets the necessary industrial standards for use.

This versatile ingredient is used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. In food production, it is used in chocolate, margarine, baked goods, and salad dressings to prevent fat separation and improve texture consistency.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into oral and injectable lipid formulations and liposomal drug delivery systems. It is also essential for soft-gel capsule coatings where controlled release and bioavailability are critical factors.

In personal care, it functions as an emollient and emulsion stabilizer in creams, lotions, and serums. This is particularly valuable where natural-origin ingredients are a specific formulation requirement for the brand.

Feed and agricultural applications include its use as a fat-coating agent for pelleted animal feeds. It also serves as an effective carrier for pesticide emulsions, ensuring uniform distribution during application.

Lecithin is supplied as a viscous liquid, de-oiled powder, or granules depending on the processing method. Standard commercial grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP /NF), and feed-grade options.

Soy lecithin remains the most widely traded form in the global chemical market. However, sunflower-derived lecithin is increasingly available for allergen-sensitive or non-GMO formulations to meet specific consumer demands.

name: Paraffin wax

In food production, it serves as a frying medium, shortening base, and margarine component due to its oxidative stability at high temperatures. Personal care formulators use it as a skin-conditioning base in soaps, lotions, and creams.

Its fatty acid profile supports emollient performance in various cosmetic applications. In home care and industrial cleaning products, it acts as a surfactant precursor for many formulations.

Saponified palm oil is a primary feedstock for soap noodles and fatty acid derivatives. Rubber and tire compounders incorporate it as a processing softener to improve compound flow and reduce mixing viscosity.

This ingredient serves as a cost-effective protein source in formulated foods. In commercial baking, it is added to flour blends to strengthen dough structure and improve gas retention during fermentation.

These properties help achieve consistent loaf volume in high-output bread production. Meat analogue and plant-based protein manufacturers rely on it as the primary structural ingredient in seitan and textured protein products.

It is also incorporated into pet food formulations and aquaculture feeds as a concentrated, digestible protein binder. This application reduces the need for more expensive animal-derived proteins in the final mix.

Pasta and noodle producers use it to correct low-protein flour and maintain cooking tolerance in finished products. Gluten is commercially supplied as a dry, off-white to cream-colored powder for industrial use.

name: 1-hydroxybenzotriazole hydrate
description:
1-Hydroxybenzotriazole hydrate (CAS 80029-43-2 ), commonly sourced as HOBt hydrate, is a coupling additive used in peptide synthesis and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It suppresses racemization and activates carboxyl groups during amide bond formation.

This chemical directly impacts the purity and yield of active pharmaceutical ingredients. In solid-phase and solution-phase peptide synthesis, HOBt hydrate is used alongside carbodiimide reagents such as DCC or EDC to produce coupling-ready active esters.

These reactions result in reduced epimerization during the manufacturing process. API synthesis routes for small-molecule drugs rely on it to achieve high-purity amide intermediates under controlled conditions for various applications.

Contract manufacturers and research organizations use it in the preparation of peptide-based therapeutics. Stereochemical integrity at each coupling step is a critical quality parameter for these complex medical products.

It also supports the synthesis of peptidomimetics and specialty heterocyclic intermediates in medicinal chemistry programs. HOBt hydrate is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder for industrial use.

The hydrate form is the standard commercial offering, preferred over the anhydrous grade for its improved handling safety profile in bulk storage and transport. It is available in research quantities through to multi-kilogram lots.

Specifications are typically aligned to pharmaceutical-grade purity requirements, often reaching levels of ≥98% by HPLC. This ensures consistency and reliability for sensitive chemical synthesis and large-scale production cycles.

name: Alitame
description:
Alitame (CAS 80863-62-3 ), also known by its EU designation E956 , is a high-intensity dipeptide sweetener approved for use in food and beverage applications.

It delivers sweetness approximately 2,000 times that of sucrose, allowing formulators to achieve target sweetness profiles at very low inclusion rates in various food systems.

In low-calorie and sugar-free beverages, it provides clean sweetness without the bitter aftertaste associated with some alternative high-intensity sweeteners used in the industry.

Confectionery and chewing gum manufacturers use it to replace bulk sugar while maintaining acceptable mouthfeel and flavor balance for the end consumer in these specific applications.

It performs well in baked goods and dairy-based products where heat stability during processing is a formulation requirement for maintaining the integrity of the final product.

Tabletop sweetener blends also incorporate this ingredient to reduce the total sweetener load while meeting target sweetness intensity for health-conscious consumers and dietary needs.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Food-grade is the standard commercial specification, with material typically conforming to regulatory requirements where approval applies.

Buyers should confirm regional regulatory status prior to sourcing, as approval varies across jurisdictions. This ensures compliance with local safety and labeling standards for food additives.

name: Saccharin
description:
Saccharin (CAS 81-07-2 ), also known as O-benzosulphimide, is a synthetic, non-caloric sweetener approximately 300–500 times sweeter than sucrose. It is used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries.

This versatile ingredient serves as a sugar substitute and taste-masking agent. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used in tabletop sweetener blends, diet soft drinks, and low-calorie confectionery where caloric reduction is required.

Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it to mask the bitter taste of active ingredients in oral syrups, chewable tablets, and liquid dosage forms. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into toothpastes and mouthwashes.

These applications deliver sweetness without fermentable sugars. Industrial applications include its use as a corrosion inhibitor in electroplating baths, where it also acts as a brightening agent in nickel plating processes.

Saccharin is supplied as a white crystalline powder, and as the sodium or calcium salt form. Sodium saccharin is the most commercially traded form due to its significantly higher water solubility in various formulations.

Standard grades include Food Grade ( FCC ), USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. , supporting use across regulated food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic applications. Technical grade is available for industrial and electroplating applications.

name: Dexpanthenol
description:
Dexpanthenol (CAS 81-13-0 ), also known as pantothenyl alcohol and D-pantothenol, is the biologically active alcohol analogue of pantothenic acid (vitamin B5). In both pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing, it functions as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent.

This pro-vitamin converts to pantothenic acid upon absorption into the skin or hair. In topical pharmaceutical formulations, it is the active ingredient in wound-healing creams, nasal sprays, and eye drops, where it supports epithelial repair and tissue regeneration.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into shampoos, conditioners, and leave-in treatments to improve hair fiber moisture retention and reduce breakage. Skin care products such as lotions, serums, and barrier creams use it to deliver sustained hydration.

The ingredient supports the skin's natural recovery process and is frequently used in baby care products. It also appears in post-procedure skincare lines where a well-tolerated, efficacious moisturizing active is required for sensitive skin.

Dexpanthenol is supplied as a viscous liquid, typically at 75% or 98%+ concentrations. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. specifications for high-purity manufacturing requirements.

Cosmetic-grade material is also commonly offered for personal care applications. Bulk supply is standard in drums or IBCs, with smaller quantities available for development and QA purposes to meet various production scales.

name: Indanthrone Blue

Indanthrone Blue (CAS 81-77-6 ), also known as C.I. Pigment Blue 60 or Indanthrene, is a high-performance vat-derived organic pigment prized for its deep, reddish-blue hue and outstanding lightfastness.

It is used across demanding colorant applications where long-term color stability under UV exposure and heat is a primary selection criterion. In industrial and architectural coatings, it delivers durable blue shades.

These shades resist fading in exterior environments, making it a preferred choice for high-specification paint systems. Plastics processors incorporate it into polyolefins, engineering resins, and masterbatches.

It is ideal where processing temperatures and outdoor weathering would degrade lesser pigments. Textile dyeing operations use it as a vat pigment to achieve wash-fast, lightfast blue shades on cotton and cellulosic fibers.

Printing ink formulators select it for packaging applications requiring consistent, migration-resistant color across long press runs. Indanthrone Blue is supplied as a dry powder, typically in press cake or finished pigment form.

The form depends on the downstream application. Standard grades are available to meet C.I. Pigment Blue 60 specifications, with surface-treated variants offered for optimized dispersion in specific resin systems.

Both crude and conditioned grades are commercially available, with particle size and surface chemistry selected to match coating, plastic, or ink end-use requirements for various industrial sectors.

name: 4-bromo-1,8-naphthalic anhydride
description:
4-Bromo-1,8-naphthalic anhydride (CAS 81-86-7 ) is a halogenated cyclic anhydride used as a reactive intermediate in the synthesis of naphthalimide-based dyes, fluorescent pigments, and specialty polymers.

Its bromine substituent provides a versatile handle for further functionalization, making it a key building block in dye chemistry and materials science for various industrial applications.

In textile and printing applications, it serves as a precursor to high-performance fluorescent dyes used in fabric brightening and inkjet colorants. Polymer chemists incorporate it into polyimide backbones.

These high-temperature polymer backbones are utilized where controlled optical or electronic properties are required. The compound is also used in pharmaceutical intermediate synthesis for bioactive candidates.

The naphthalimide scaffold is elaborated through palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling or nucleophilic substitution at the bromine site. In specialty pigment manufacturing, it contributes to the production of vat dyes.

It is also used for solvent dyes for plastics coloration and packaging inks. 4-Bromo-1,8-naphthalic anhydride is supplied as a solid powder, typically in off-white to pale yellow form.

It is available in technical and high-purity research grades, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 97% to 99%+ depending on the intended application and specific requirements.

Packaging options range from small laboratory quantities to multi-kilogram industrial lots. This ensures flexibility for both research development and large-scale commercial manufacturing processes.

name: 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane
description:
1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane (CAS 811-97-2 ), commercially known as R-134a and marketed under the trade name Suva 134a, is a hydrofluorocarbon refrigerant and propellant used across industrial and specialty applications.

It replaced ozone-depleting chlorofluorocarbons in refrigeration and aerosol systems, becoming the standard in multiple regulated sectors. In automotive and commercial HVAC systems, R-134a functions as the primary refrigerant.

It is used in air conditioning circuits, meeting OEM specifications for vehicle climate control. Aerospace and defense procurement teams source it for environmental control systems in aircraft cabins and ground support equipment.

In aerosol formulations, it acts as a propellant and carrier solvent for technical sprays, including contact cleaners and precision electronics maintenance products. The oil and gas sector uses it in specialized leak detection equipment.

It is also utilized in portable cooling units operating in field environments. 1,1,1,2-Tetrafluoroethane is supplied as a liquefied gas in pressurized cylinders, recovery tanks, and bulk ISO containers.

Refrigerant-grade (R-134a) is the dominant commercial specification, with purity levels typically meeting AHRI 700 standards for moisture content, acidity, and non-condensable gases.

Reclaimed and virgin grades are both available, with virgin material required for OEM and aerospace applications. This ensures high performance and reliability across all industrial cooling and propellant systems.

name: Tetracosahexaenoic acid
description:
Tetracosahexaenoic acid (CAS 81247-23-6 ) is a 24-carbon polyunsaturated fatty acid of research and nutritional interest. Commercially referenced as Fatty Acid 24:6, it is evaluated for its role in lipid metabolism pathways.

It serves as a functional ingredient in specialty nutritional formulations and is used as a reference standard in fatty acid profiling studies. This compound is essential for functional food development and lipid biochemistry research.

Pharmaceutical researchers source it for investigating lipid biochemistry and formulating investigational nutraceutical preparations targeting metabolic health. It is a critical component for those studying advanced nutritional science and lipidomics.

In animal feed and agricultural nutrition, it is assessed as a dietary lipid supplement to support fatty acid composition in livestock and aquaculture species. This application helps improve the nutritional profile of various animal products.

Quality control laboratories also use it as an analytical reference material for validating fatty acid quantification methods. This ensures accuracy and consistency across various testing protocols in the chemical and food industries.

Tetracosahexaenoic acid is typically available in small research quantities as a neat liquid or dissolved in solvent. It is ideally suited to laboratory and formulation development use where high precision is required.

Supply is generally offered at high purity grades appropriate for research and analytical applications. Bulk commercial availability is limited, reflecting its current status as a specialty and investigational fatty acid.

As a specialty chemical, it remains a niche product rather than a commodity ingredient. Its unique structure makes it a valuable asset for specialized industrial and scientific applications worldwide.

name: Bismuth citrate

Bismuth citrate (CAS 813-93-4 ) is an inorganic bismuth salt used primarily as a pharmaceutical intermediate and active ingredient precursor in gastrointestinal and antimicrobial drug formulations.

It functions as a stabilizing agent and buffering component in formulations where controlled bismuth delivery is required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key starting material for synthesis.

This material is essential for synthesizing colloidal bismuth subcitrate and related compounds used in peptic ulcer and H. pylori treatment protocols. Topical and dermatological formulations incorporate it as a mild preservative.

It acts as a stabilizer particularly where metal-based biocidal activity is needed at low concentrations. In cosmetic manufacturing, it supports pH regulation and acts as a stabilizing agent in creams and ointments.

Food-contact and nutritional supplement applications represent a smaller but established market. In these sectors, it is evaluated as a mineral source under controlled regulatory frameworks for specific consumer products.

Bismuth citrate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications, with technical-grade material available for industrial use.

name: Calcium citrate
description:
Calcium citrate (CAS 813-94-5 ), also marketed as E333iii , is the calcium salt of citric acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions as a buffering agent, chelating agent, and mineral supplement source.

In food and beverage production, it stabilizes pH in processed products and acts as a sequestrant to prevent metal-catalyzed oxidation in canned goods and beverages. This ensures product stability and shelf life.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a bioavailable calcium source in dietary supplement tablets and capsules. Its absorption profile suits formulations targeting populations with low gastric acid levels effectively.

In personal care, it buffers pH in topical formulations and chelates trace metals that would otherwise degrade active ingredients. This helps maintain the overall efficacy of preservatives within the final product.

It also functions as a firming agent in fruit and vegetable processing, maintaining texture in canned and frozen products. This application is vital for preserving the structural integrity of processed produce.

Calcium citrate is supplied as a white powder in both anhydrous and tetrahydrate forms. The anhydrous grade is the standard for most dry supplement and food applications requiring high purity and stability.

Recognized grades include FCC , USP , and Ph. Eur. , supporting use across food, nutraceutical, and pharmaceutical supply chains. These standards ensure the material meets rigorous global safety requirements.

Bulk quantities are available in fiber drums or multi-wall bags for large-scale manufacturing. Technical-grade material is also available for specific industrial applications outside of the food and drug sectors.

name: Calcium thioglycolate
description:
Calcium thioglycolate ( CAS 814-71-1 ), also known commercially as Ebacream and Depil, is the calcium salt of thioglycolic acid used primarily as a depilatory active in personal care formulations.

It breaks down the disulfide bonds in keratin, enabling effective hair removal without mechanical action. In depilatory creams and lotions, it is the functional ingredient that dissolves hair at the skin surface.

This allows hair to be wiped away cleanly. Formulators select it over ammonium thioglycolate in depilatory applications where a milder odor profile and lower alkalinity are preferred for sensitive skin products.

It is also evaluated in professional salon and at-home hair removal formats, including rinse-off creams and gel systems targeting legs, underarms, and facial areas for various consumer demographics.

Some formulation chemists incorporate it into keratin-modifying treatments where controlled bond disruption is required. Calcium thioglycolate is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as an aqueous solution.

The concentration varies by supplier specification. Technical and cosmetic-grade material is available, with cosmetic-grade product meeting purity requirements relevant to finished personal care applications.

Buyers typically source it in bulk bags or drums depending on production scale. This chemical remains a staple for manufacturers seeking reliable performance in the global hair removal market segment.

It is also used in radiolabeling processes where controlled tin(II) chemistry is critical. Water treatment applications leverage its chelation activity to manage trace metal interference.

name: Dibutyltin oxide
description:
Dibutyltin oxide (CAS 818-08-6 ) is an organotin compound used as a catalyst and reactive intermediate across polymer processing and surface coating industries. It drives esterification, transesterification, and condensation reactions where precise control over cure rate is required.

In polyurethane and silicone sealant formulations, it functions as a curing catalyst, controlling gel time and final mechanical properties of the elastomeric network. Coating manufacturers use it to catalyze alkyd and polyester resin synthesis.

Adhesive formulators working with moisture-cure systems also rely on it to regulate cross-linking speed in structural bonding applications. This versatility makes it a staple in the production of high-performance industrial adhesives and sealants.

name: 2-hydroxyethyl acrylate
description:
2-Hydroxyethyl acrylate (CAS 818-61-1 ), commonly abbreviated as HEA, is a reactive hydroxyl-functional monomer used to introduce pendant hydroxyl groups into polymer backbones.

Ethylene glycol monoacrylate is a recognized alternative name in some supplier and regulatory contexts. It enables controlled crosslinking and adhesion performance in UV-curable and thermally cured polymer systems.

In UV-curable coatings and inks for printing and packaging, HEA acts as a reactive diluent that reduces viscosity while contributing hydroxyl functionality to the cured network.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it into acrylic pressure-sensitive adhesives to tune peel strength and cohesion through isocyanate or melamine crosslinking.

In waterborne and solvent-based coatings, it serves as a comonomer to improve substrate adhesion and coating flexibility without sacrificing crosslink density.

Polymer manufacturers also use HEA to functionalize acrylic resins destined for two-component polyurethane systems. HEA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically stabilized with a polymerization inhibitor.

This stabilization helps maintain shelf stability during storage and transport. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with purity specifications commonly at 96% or higher.

Bulk quantities are offered in drums and IBC containers, with inhibitor type and concentration often specified on request to suit downstream processing requirements.

name: Polyquaternium 10
description:
Polyquaternium-10 (CAS 81859-24-7 ) is a cationic cellulose-derived polymer used across personal care and industrial formulations for its conditioning and film-forming properties. It deposits a substantive coating on negatively charged surfaces.

This coating improves texture, manageability, and moisture retention on hair and skin. Formulators source it primarily as a rheology modifier and conditioning agent in both rinse-off and leave-on systems for various applications.

In hair care, it is incorporated into shampoos, conditioners, and styling products to reduce static and improve combability. It provides a smooth, detangled finish after rinsing, making it a staple in professional hair care lines.

Skin care formulators use it in lotions and body washes to deliver a soft, moisturized feel without heavy residue. It enhances the sensory profile of the product while maintaining a lightweight feel on the skin surface.

In textile processing, it functions as a surface modifier to improve fiber softness and antistatic performance during finishing operations. This versatility makes it valuable for industrial applications beyond personal care products.

Home care and industrial cleaning products use it to modify viscosity and enhance surface wetting in liquid formulations. It ensures consistent performance and stability in a wide range of household and commercial cleaners.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or granule. It is available in multiple grades differentiated by charge density and molecular weight, which directly affect conditioning intensity and viscosity contribution.

Cosmetic-grade material conforming to standard industry specifications is the most commonly traded form. These grades ensure high purity and performance reliability for manufacturers seeking consistent results in their final formulations.

name: Phenylperi acid
description:
Phenylperi acid (CAS 82-76-8 ), commercially abbreviated as 1,8-ANS, is an aminonaphthalenesulfonic acid derivative used as a UV stabilizer and antioxidant in industrial formulations. It functions by absorbing ultraviolet radiation and inhibiting oxidative degradation.

This chemical intermediate is essential for extending the service life of finished materials. In coatings and adhesives, it is incorporated to protect substrates from UV-induced yellowing and mechanical property loss over time.

Textile and leather processors use it as a dye intermediate and stabilizer, where it contributes to colorfastness and resistance to light-induced fading. It is a versatile component in many specialty chemical processes.

Polymer compounders add it to plastics formulations requiring long-term UV stability, particularly in outdoor or high-exposure applications. This ensures that structural integrity is maintained even under harsh environmental conditions.

In printing inks and packaging materials, it supports pigment stability and prevents premature degradation of colorants under light exposure. This makes it a valuable additive for the commercial printing and labeling industries.

Phenylperi acid is supplied as a crystalline powder, typically in technical grade. Standard packaging includes drum and bag formats suited to industrial procurement volumes for large-scale manufacturing operations.

Buyers should confirm purity specifications and batch consistency directly with the supplier, as grade designations vary by manufacturer. Proper storage and handling are required to maintain the chemical stability of the product.

It is used in skin and hair products to improve texture and film-forming performance. Lubricant formulators incorporate it as a base component or additive in metalworking fluids and specialty greases.

The specific chain length contributes to film durability under load. Food-grade applications include its use as an acidulant or processing aid in regulated formulations where long-chain diacids are permitted.

It also serves as a building block in polyamide and polyester synthesis. The C14 backbone influences the flexibility and melting profile of the resulting polymer during the manufacturing process.

name: Sodium myristate
description:
Sodium myristate (CAS 822-12-8 ), also known as sodium tetradecanoate, is the sodium salt of myristic acid used commercially as a surfactant and emulsifier. It delivers effective foam generation, emulsification, and cleaning action across personal care, food processing, and industrial applications.

In soap and personal care formulations, it contributes firm bar texture and dense, stable lather. This makes it a preferred fatty acid soap component alongside stearate and palmitate blends for high-quality cleansing products.

Textile and leather processors use it as a scouring and degreasing agent to remove oils and contaminants from fiber and hide surfaces. This step is essential before dyeing or finishing to ensure uniform results across the material.

In food-grade applications, it functions as an emulsifier to stabilize fat-in-water systems in processed food manufacturing. It helps maintain consistency and shelf stability in various edible products and industrial food preparations.

Paper industry formulators incorporate it into surface treatments and sizing formulations where controlled foam and dispersion are required. Its chemical properties allow for precise control over the texture and finish of paper products.

Sodium myristate is supplied as a white powder or flake. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially prevalent, with technical-grade material available for industrial textile and paper applications.

Purity levels and grade compliance vary by manufacturer, so buyers should confirm specification sheets against their requirements. Common standards for high-purity batches may include FCC or USP depending on the intended end-use.

Plastics processors use it as an internal and external lubricant and stabilizer during PVC compounding. This improves melt flow and prevents degradation during extrusion, ensuring high-quality finished plastic products for various industrial uses.

In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it acts as a base component in dry lubricant formulations. It also serves as an effective release agent for metal forming operations, reducing friction and wear on machinery.

Food-grade material is used as an emulsifier and anti-caking agent in select processed food applications. It is supplied as a white powder or flakes, with particle size and purity varying by the specific application grade required.

Stearyl acetate (CAS 822-23-1 ), also known as octadecyl acetate, is a long-chain fatty acid ester used as a lubricant, emollient carrier, and dispersing agent across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its waxy, low-polarity character makes it effective in applications where controlled slip, film formation, or solubilization of actives is required. In personal care, it functions as an emollient and texture modifier.

It is used in creams, lotions, and hair conditioners, contributing a smooth, non-greasy skin feel without heavy residue. Formulators incorporate it as a carrier solvent for fragrance oils and UV filters.

It is also utilized for lipophilic actives in leave-on and rinse-off products. In lubricant and metalworking formulations, it acts as a base fluid component or additive to reduce friction and improve adhesion.

The compound also serves as a dispersing medium for pigments and waxes in cosmetic color products such as lipsticks and pressed powders. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance manufacturing.

Sodium saccharinate (CAS 82385-42-0 ) is the hydrated sodium salt form of saccharin, commercially recognized as sodium saccharin hydrate. It functions as a high-intensity, non-caloric sweetener used across food and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

This versatile ingredient is essential where sugar-free formulation is required. In food and beverage production, it delivers intense sweetness at very low use levels, making it a cost-effective sucrose replacement.

It is frequently utilized in tabletop sweeteners, diet drinks, and confectionery. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into oral dosage forms such as syrups, chewable tablets, and lozenges to mask bitter active ingredients.

This masking capability helps improve patient compliance across various treatments. Personal care formulators use it in toothpastes, mouthwashes, and lip care products to provide sweetness without promoting tooth decay.

It also appears in nutraceutical and dietary supplement formulations where caloric content must be minimized. Sodium saccharinate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules for industrial use.

description:
Calcium salicylate ( CAS 824-35-1 ), also known as calcium disalicylate, is the calcium salt of salicylic acid used across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing. It functions as a preservative and pH-buffering agent.

This chemical is often selected for formulations where sodium or free-acid forms are unsuitable due to solubility or compatibility constraints. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of salicylate-based active ingredients.

It also acts as a buffering component in tablet and oral formulation development. Personal care formulators incorporate it into topical preparations where controlled preservation and mild acidity management are required.

The compound provides these benefits without the irritation profile of free salicylic acid. It is also evaluated in dermatological formulations targeting exfoliation and skin conditioning for various consumer products.

The calcium salt form offers a more neutral delivery vehicle for sensitive applications. Compounding pharmacies and specialty chemical manufacturers source it as a starting material for further salt conversions.

It is also utilized for custom API development in specialized medical fields. Calcium salicylate is supplied as a white crystalline powder available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications aligned with compendial standards.

name: Chapso
description:
CHAPSO (CAS 82473-24-3 ), also known as 3-[(3-Cholamidopropyl)dimethylammonio]-2-hydroxy-1-propanesulfonate, is a zwitterionic detergent developed specifically for membrane protein research and biochemical applications.

It solubilizes biological membranes while preserving the native structure and activity of membrane-bound proteins. This is a critical requirement in research and biopharmaceutical workflows for maintaining protein integrity.

This product is the detergent of choice for solubilizing and stabilizing integral membrane proteins during purification. It has become a standard reagent in receptor binding studies and enzyme activity assays.

In pharmaceutical research, it supports the isolation of functionally intact membrane protein targets used in drug discovery programs. Its mild solubilization profile makes it suitable for two-dimensional crystallization.

Harsher detergents would cause irreversible denaturation in these sensitive environments. It is also used in lipid-protein reconstitution systems where maintaining bilayer-like environments is required for success.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available primarily in research-grade and high-purity biochemical grades, with lot-specific purity documentation typically required for industrial use.

Documentation is often necessary for GMP-adjacent pharmaceutical applications. Pack sizes range from small laboratory quantities up to bulk procurement for large-scale bioprocessing facilities.

description:

The polymer reduces static and enhances shine without weighing hair down. Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and body washes where it builds a smooth, substantive feel on the skin surface.

In textile processing, it modifies fiber surfaces during finishing operations to improve softness. It also enhances antistatic performance and handle characteristics in various industrial fabric treatments.

Paper and leather manufacturers use it as a surface modifier to influence wetting behavior. This application ensures surface uniformity during complex industrial processing and manufacturing stages.

Polyquaternium-68 is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active polymer content varying by grade. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications are available to serve diverse requirements.

It bridges the performance gap between synthetic emulsifiers and naturally derived alternatives. This chemical offers formulators a mild, skin-compatible option with multifunctional utility for diverse product lines.

In personal care formulations, it stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions in creams, lotions, and conditioners. It simultaneously contributes to skin-feel and moisture retention for high-end cosmetic applications.

Cleansing products benefit from its ability to solubilize oils without stripping the skin. This is particularly useful in facial cleansers and micellar systems targeting sensitive skin types and delicate areas.

In metalworking and industrial lubricant formulations, it functions as a bio-based lubricating additive. It improves surface slip and reduces friction in cutting fluids and other heavy-duty industrial processes.

Home care and cleaning product manufacturers incorporate it into concentrated surfactant blends. It is ideal where emulsification of oily soils is required alongside mildness to various substrates and surfaces.

Methyl glucose dioleate is typically supplied as a liquid or semi-solid paste, depending on temperature and grade. Personal care grades are available to meet cosmetic-quality specifications for global distribution.

name: Bis(trimethoxysilylpropyl)amine

It bonds inorganic substrates to organic polymer matrices, improving adhesion and mechanical performance at the interface. In rubber and polymer compounding, it functions as a crosslinker and coupling agent.

For silica-filled systems, it improves filler dispersion and reinforces the silica-polymer network in tire treads and technical rubber goods. Coating and adhesive formulators use it to prime glass, metal, and mineral surfaces.

This increases wet adhesion and long-term durability under demanding environmental conditions. In fiberglass and composite manufacturing, it is applied as a sizing component to strengthen the fiber-resin interface.

This is critical for structural parts in automotive and aerospace assemblies. Electronics manufacturers apply it as a surface treatment on substrates where strong, moisture-resistant bonding is required.

It is particularly effective between inorganic surfaces and encapsulants or underfill resins. Bis(trimethoxysilylpropyl)amine is supplied as a liquid and is available in technical grade for industrial use.

name: Beta-sitosterol
description:
Beta-sitosterol (CAS 83-46-5 ) is a plant-derived sterol extracted primarily from vegetable oils, nuts, and seeds. It is one of the most commercially significant phytosterols, recognized across pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, and cosmetic supply chains.

In formulation, it functions as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and active ingredient in cholesterol-management and skin-conditioning applications. In nutraceuticals and functional foods, it is incorporated into fortified margarines and dietary supplements.

It is used in cholesterol-lowering food products, where it competes with dietary cholesterol absorption in the gut. Cosmetic formulators use it to build stable emulsions in creams and lotions for skin-care products.

Its waxy character supports lipid barrier reinforcement in topical applications. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a raw material or reference standard in the production of steroid-based active ingredients.

In food-grade applications, it also serves as an antioxidant co-stabilizer in fat-based systems. This helps in extending shelf life in oils and fat blends while maintaining the integrity of the final product formulation.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or crystalline solid. It is available in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications, with high-purity grades typically 95%+ or 99%+ used in drug applications.

Phytosterol blends containing this compound as the primary component are also commercially available for food fortification use. These products meet rigorous industry requirements for purity and performance in global markets.

name: Phytic acid
description:
Phytic acid (CAS 83-86-3 ), also known as IP6 and carrying the food additive designation E391 , is a naturally derived phosphoric acid ester extracted primarily from cereal grains and legumes. It functions as a chelating and sequestering agent, binding metal ions to prevent oxidative degradation.

In food manufacturing, phytic acid controls metal-catalyzed rancidity and discoloration in oils, fats, and processed grain products where trace mineral contamination accelerates spoilage. This ensures product stability and maintains sensory profiles over time.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into anti-aging and skin-brightening products, where its metal-chelating action inhibits melanin synthesis pathways triggered by copper-dependent enzymes. It is a versatile ingredient for high-end cosmetic applications.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturers use IP6 as an antioxidant stabilizer in tablet and capsule formulations to extend shelf life by scavenging free iron and copper. This prevents the degradation of sensitive active pharmaceutical ingredients.

In industrial cleaning and surface treatment, it acts as a sequestrant to prevent mineral scaling and improve the performance of cleaning agents. Its natural origin makes it an attractive alternative to synthetic chelating agents in green chemistry.

Phytic acid is supplied as a liquid solution, typically at 50% or 70% concentration, and less commonly as a dried powder. Standard grades include food-grade and technical-grade material, with food-grade product subject to purity specifications aligned with FCC requirements.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or Ph.Eur. standards is available from select suppliers. These high-purity grades ensure compliance with rigorous international safety and quality benchmarks for sensitive manufacturing processes.

Pharmaceutical-grade batches serve as intermediates in the synthesis of skin-active compounds and topical drug formulations requiring documented purity. These applications often demand compliance with rigorous quality standards like USP or EP .

It also appears in combination actives alongside niacinamide, vitamin C derivatives, or kojic acid. In these formulations, specialists stack complementary tyrosinase-inhibiting pathways to enhance the overall efficacy of the final product.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard commercial grades include cosmetic-grade with purity specifications typically at 99% or higher, which are verified by HPLC to ensure consistent performance.

Pharmaceutical-intermediate grades with full documentation packages are available for regulated applications. These packages include COA, residual solvent testing, and stability data to meet the requirements of global manufacturers.

name: Ciprofloxacin
description:
Ciprofloxacin (CAS 85721-33-1 ) is a broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic active ingredient supplied to pharmaceutical manufacturers under trade names including Ciprobay and Velmonit.

It targets a wide range of gram-negative and gram-positive bacteria, making it a core API in prescription antimicrobial formulations globally for various medical applications.

The primary commercial application is in finished oral and injectable antibiotic drug products, where ciprofloxacin is formulated as tablets, infusion solutions, and extended-release dosage forms.

Ophthalmic and otic preparations represent a distinct formulation category, with ciprofloxacin incorporated into drops and ointments for localized infection treatment in clinical settings.

In personal care and cosmetic preservation research, it is evaluated as a biocidal reference compound in antimicrobial efficacy testing protocols to ensure product safety and stability.

Ciprofloxacin is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. pharmacopoeial specifications for industrial use.

name: Bismuth naphthenate
description:

In coatings and sealants, it functions as a drying catalyst and cure accelerator, replacing lead-based alternatives in alkyd and polyurethane systems for industrial applications.

Metalworking and lubricant formulators incorporate it as an extreme-pressure additive and anti-wear agent in cutting fluids and gear oils to enhance performance under stress.

In the oil and gas sector, it is used in pipeline and downhole fluid formulations where corrosion inhibition under high-temperature conditions is required for equipment longevity.

name: N-nitrosodiphenylamine
description:
N-Nitrosodiphenylamine (CAS 86-30-6 ) is an industrial chemical used primarily as a polymerization inhibitor and retarder in rubber and polymer processing. It controls cure rates and prevents premature vulcanization.

This chemical gives manufacturers greater control over processing windows during production. In rubber compounding, it functions as a prevulcanization inhibitor, delaying the onset of cure during mixing and extrusion.

This delay helps to reduce scorch risk in tire and technical rubber production. Polymer manufacturers use it to stabilize reactive monomer systems during storage and transport, preventing unwanted polymerization.

In plastics processing, it acts as a stabilizer to extend the safe handling window of peroxide-cured compounds. It is also used as an antioxidant additive in certain polymer formulations where degradation is a concern.

N-Nitrosodiphenylamine is typically supplied as a solid in powder or crystalline form. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for industrial rubber and polymer applications.

name: Fluorene
description:
Fluorene (CAS 86-73-7 ), also known as o-biphenylenemethane, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon used as a core building block in the synthesis of advanced organic materials and pharmaceutical intermediates.

Its rigid, planar structure makes it a preferred starting material where precise molecular architecture is required in downstream synthesis. In electronics and optoelectronics, it serves as a foundational monomer.

Fluorene is used for polyfluorene-based polymers in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) and organic photovoltaic devices. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients.

The dibenzofuran-adjacent scaffold supports target binding profiles in medicinal chemistry. In specialty polymer production, derived monomers are incorporated into high-performance engineering resins and optical films.

These materials are valued for their thermal stability and controlled refractive index. Biotechnology applications include its use as a precursor in fluorescent probe synthesis and labeled reagent development.

Fluorene is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid or flake. It is available in technical grade for industrial polymer and chemical synthesis applications, as well as in high-purity grades.

The high-purity grades (98%–99%+) are suited for pharmaceutical intermediate and electronic material manufacturing. Packaging options typically range from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial supply.

name: 1-Naphthaleneacetic acid
description:
1-Naphthaleneacetic acid ( CAS 86-87-3 ), commonly abbreviated as NAA and also known as 1-naphthylacetic acid, is a synthetic auxin used in commercial agriculture to regulate plant growth and development.

It mimics the action of natural plant hormones, enabling precise control over rooting, fruit set, and thinning at the crop production scale. NAA is applied in fruit production to prevent pre-harvest drop in apples and pears.

This application protects yield quality ahead of harvest windows. In propagation operations, it promotes adventitious root formation on cuttings, accelerating establishment of ornamental, horticultural, and forestry stock.

Turf and nursery managers use it to stimulate uniform rooting in transplanted sod and container-grown plants. At low concentrations, it also functions as a fruit-thinning agent in apple orchards.

This process improves fruit size and marketable grade. 1-Naphthaleneacetic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial use.

Material is also available at higher purity levels to meet formulation requirements for registered agrochemical products. It is typically offered in kilogram and multi-kilogram packaging suited to manufacturers.

These bulk quantities are ideal for concentrate manufacturers and formulation houses. The product ensures consistent performance across various agricultural and horticultural applications in global markets.

name: Potassium methoxide
description:
Potassium methoxide (CAS 865-33-8 ), also sold as potassium methylate or potassium methanolate, is a strong alkoxide base used primarily as a catalyst and reagent in industrial chemical synthesis.

It also catalyzes the production of specialty polyesters and polyethers. Potassium methoxide is supplied as a solution in methanol, with concentrations typically ranging from 25% to 32%.

It is also available as a dry powder or free-flowing solid for applications where solvent-free handling is required. Standard technical and industrial grades are available for various uses.

name: Cupric citrate
description:
Cupric citrate (CAS 866-82-0 ), also known as copper citrate, is an inorganic copper salt used across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural applications as a source of bioavailable copper and a chelating agent.

It binds metal ions and delivers controlled copper content in formulations where ionic copper alone would be too reactive or unstable. In food and dietary supplement manufacturing, it functions as a copper mineral fortifier.

The material is added to infant formulas, multivitamins, and functional foods to meet declared copper content requirements. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a copper source in parenteral nutrition solutions.

It is also utilized in oral mineral preparations where precise dosing and stability are critical. In agriculture, it serves as a micronutrient additive in animal feed premixes and fertilizer blends.

This compound is effective for correcting copper deficiencies in livestock and crops. Its biocidal properties also support use in antimicrobial coatings and preservation systems where slow copper ion release is required.

Cupric citrate is supplied as a fine powder or crystalline solid. It is available in food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with some suppliers offering material compliant with USP or FCC monographs.

Purity levels and copper content declarations vary by grade, so buyers should confirm specification sheets against their formulation requirements to ensure the product meets all necessary safety standards.

name: Potassium citrate
description:
Potassium citrate (CAS 866-84-2 ) is a potassium salt of citric acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, sequestrant, and acidity regulator, helping formulators maintain stability.

In food and beverage production, it regulates acidity in dairy products, jellies, and low-sodium formulations where sodium-based alternatives are unsuitable. This versatility makes it a staple for modern food processing.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an active ingredient in urinary alkalinization products and as an excipient in effervescent tablets. It is also found in oral solutions to ensure consistent delivery of active compounds.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, skin creams, and oral care products to control pH. It effectively chelates metal ions that would otherwise degrade active ingredients in cosmetic formulations.

It also acts as a sequestrant in processed foods, binding calcium and magnesium ions to extend shelf life and improve texture. This ensures that products remain fresh and appealing to consumers over longer periods.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granules, with granulated forms preferred for direct compression. Standard grades include FCC , USP , and Ph.Eur. , covering all procurement requirements.

Monohydrate and anhydrous forms are both commercially available for various industrial applications. Grade selection typically depends on moisture sensitivity requirements in the target formulation and manufacturing process.

name: Potassium bitartrate
description:
Potassium bitartrate (CAS 868-14-4 ), commercially recognized as cream of tartar and listed as E336 , is a naturally derived acid salt produced as a byproduct of wine fermentation.

In food and personal care manufacturing, it functions as a leavening acid, buffering agent, and stabilizer across a broad range of formulations. In baking, it activates baking soda to provide controlled leavening.

This ingredient is essential for cakes, cookies, and baked mixes, while simultaneously stabilizing whipped egg whites and meringues against collapse. Confectionery manufacturers use it to prevent sugar crystallization.

By preventing crystallization in candies, frostings, and syrups, it improves texture consistency in finished products. Food processors rely on it as a pH buffer and tartrate source in processed vegetables.

It helps retain color and firmness during thermal treatment in various food applications. In personal care formulations, it functions as a mild acidulant and buffering agent in dental powders and skin-brightening preparations.

Potassium bitartrate is supplied as a fine white crystalline powder. Food-grade material conforming to FCC and E336 specifications is the standard commercial form for industrial use.

High purity USP and BP grades are available for pharmaceutical and personal care applications. Bulk supply is typical for industrial food processing, with smaller packaging available for specialty markets.

It stabilizes pH in sensitive formulations and binds metal ions that would otherwise degrade product quality or shelf life. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as a buffering component in oral solutions and effervescent tablets.

This chemical is essential for laxative formulations where controlled pH is critical to active ingredient stability. Food producers use it to regulate acidity and improve texture in processed foods, confectionery, and beverages.

As a chelating agent, it sequesters calcium and magnesium ions in food processing environments, preventing unwanted mineral interactions in finished products. It also appears in analytical and laboratory reagents.

name: 2-Hydroxyethyl Methacrylate
description:
2-Hydroxyethyl Methacrylate (CAS 868-77-9 ), commonly known as HEMA, is a hydroxyl-functional methacrylate monomer used to introduce reactive sites into polymer networks.

Its pendant hydroxyl group enables controlled crosslinking, adhesion promotion, and compatibility with a broad range of resin systems across coatings, adhesives, and structural composites.

In UV- and peroxide-cured coatings, HEMA acts as a reactive diluent and crosslinking co-monomer, improving film hardness and adhesion to metal and plastic substrates.

It enhances chemical resistance in automotive and industrial finishes. Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it into acrylic and methacrylate systems where hydroxyl functionality supports bonding.

This includes difficult substrates such as composites used in aerospace structures. Electronics manufacturers use HEMA-based resins in conformal coatings and encapsulants where controlled cure profiles are critical.

In construction, it contributes to polymer-modified mortars and structural bonding adhesives where durability under mechanical and environmental stress is required for long-term performance.

HEMA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically with an inhibitor added to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Standard commercial grades are available for industrial use.

Purity levels are commonly at 97% or higher. Technical and high-purity grades are offered depending on end-use sensitivity, particularly for electronics and optical applications.

name: Dimethyl Phosphite

The compound acts as an effective stabilizer where it inhibits thermal degradation during processing. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use DMP as a synthetic intermediate for active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly in phosphonate-based drug synthesis.

In water treatment chemistry, it contributes to the production of scale inhibitors and corrosion control agents applied in industrial cooling and boiler systems. This versatility makes it a critical component for various chemical processes.

name: Propylheptyl caprylate
description:
Propylheptyl caprylate (CAS 868839-23-0 ), commercially known as Cetiol Sensoft, is a branched-chain ester used as an emollient, solvent carrier, and lubricant across personal care and industrial formulations.

Its low-viscosity, dry-skin-feel profile makes it a preferred alternative to silicones and traditional esters in premium cosmetic systems. In personal care, it functions as a lightweight emollient and solvent.

It is used in skin creams, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, delivering a non-greasy after-feel that formulators actively seek as a silicone replacement. Industrial coatings and adhesive formulations use it as a plasticizing carrier.

This helps to improve substrate wetting and film flexibility. In lubricant and metalworking applications, it acts as a base fluid or additive carrier where low volatility and good lubricity on metal surfaces are required.

It also serves as a dispersant vehicle for pigments and active ingredients in both cosmetic and specialty coating systems. Propylheptyl caprylate is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care and industrial buyers respectively. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC containers for bulk procurement.
