PEG-120 methyl glucose dioleate (CAS 86893-19-8 ), commercially known as Glucamate DOE-120, is a polyethylene glycol ester of methyl glucose used as a mild, water-soluble emulsifier and rheology modifier.

It functions primarily to stabilize emulsions and thicken aqueous formulations in personal care and pharmaceutical systems. In rinse-off and leave-on cosmetic formulations, it builds viscosity in surfactant-based systems.

This ingredient is ideal for shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers without requiring salt thickening. It stabilizes oil-in-water emulsions in lotions and creams, helping to uniformly disperse active ingredients.

In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it acts as a carrier and emulsification aid where skin compatibility and low irritation potential are procurement priorities. It also supports the formulation of mild baby care.

This material is particularly useful for sensitive-skin products where conventional thickeners may be unsuitable. It is supplied as a viscous liquid or semi-solid paste, depending on temperature and packaging conditions.

It is available in cosmetic and personal care grades, with suppliers typically offering material conforming to standard industry specifications for purity and HLB consistency. Bulk supply is common in drums.

These models are essential for evaluating anticancer drug candidates and treatment protocols. Pharmaceutical researchers use it to study carcinogenesis mechanisms, particularly in gastric and bladder cancer models, supporting the development of new therapeutic compounds.

It also serves as a reference compound in genotoxicity and mutagenicity assays, where reproducible DNA alkylation activity is required for comparative studies. Regulatory toxicology programs may source it as a positive control substance.

name: Choline bitartrate
description:
Choline bitartrate (CAS 87-67-2 ), also known as choline hydrogen tartrate, is the tartaric acid salt form of choline used to deliver bioavailable choline in nutritional and pharmaceutical applications.

It functions as a stable, solid-form choline source preferred over more hygroscopic alternatives in dry formulations. Choline tartrate is the form most commonly referenced in bulk ingredient sourcing and manufacturing.

In dietary supplements, it serves as the active choline source in capsules, tablets, and powdered blends targeting cognitive and liver health support. Food manufacturers incorporate it into functional foods and fortified products.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it in solid oral dosage forms where consistent choline content and low moisture uptake are critical to product stability. This ensures long-term efficacy in various medical applications.

In personal care, its humectant and emulsifying properties support use in skin conditioning formulations and leave-on products. It provides versatile benefits across multiple industrial and consumer sectors.

Choline bitartrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both standard and anhydrous grades. Common specifications include USP , FCC , and food-grade, with BP and Ph. Eur. grades available.

Bulk packaging typically ranges from kilogram quantities up to multi-tonne lots to accommodate both R&D and commercial-scale production. This flexibility meets the needs of diverse global supply chains.

name: Hexachlorobutadiene
description:
Hexachlorobutadiene (CAS 87-68-3 ), commonly referred to as HCBD, is a dense chlorinated solvent historically used in industrial cleaning and chemical processing operations.

It functions primarily as a solvent for other chlorine-containing compounds and has been applied in high-temperature or chemically aggressive environments where conventional solvents fail.

In oil and gas processing, HCBD has been used to recover chlorine-containing byproducts generated during the production of chlorinated solvents such as trichloroethylene and tetrachloroethylene.

It serves as a fumigant and grain protectant in legacy agricultural applications, though regulatory restrictions have significantly curtailed this use in modern industrial settings.

In lubricant and metalworking contexts, its chemical stability under thermal stress made it a candidate for specialized hydraulic fluids and heat transfer media for various systems.

It has also been used as a wash liquid in gas scrubbing systems to remove impurities from chlorine-based process streams, ensuring higher purity levels for downstream manufacturing.

Hexachlorobutadiene is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions. Technical-grade material is the standard commercial form, typically offered in drums or bulk quantities for procurement.

Buyers should verify current import, export, and handling regulations, as HCBD is subject to restrictions under international chemical conventions in multiple global jurisdictions.

name: Tartaric acid
description:
Tartaric acid (CAS 87-69-4 ), also known by its food additive designation E334 , is a naturally derived organic acid sourced primarily from wine production byproducts. It functions as an acidulant, pH regulator, and antioxidant stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In food and beverage production, it sharpens tartness in confectionery, soft drinks, and baking powders where its interaction with sodium bicarbonate drives leavening performance. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a buffering agent and excipient in effervescent tablet formulations.

In these medical applications, it is essential for controlling dissolution rate and palatability. In personal care, it acts as a pH adjuster in creams, serums, and exfoliating products, where maintaining precise acidity directly affects formulation stability and skin compatibility.

Winemaking remains a primary industrial use, where it corrects acidity in must and finished wine to meet sensory and regulatory targets. This versatile acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules to suit various manufacturing processes.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC , E334, and BP / Ph.Eur. specifications is the most commonly traded form. These high-purity standards support both food and pharmaceutical procurement requirements for global distribution.

Technical-grade material is also available for non-consumable industrial applications. Whether for flavor enhancement or chemical stabilization, this organic acid remains a cornerstone ingredient in modern industrial chemistry and food science.

name: D-tagatose
description:
D-Tagatose (CAS 87-81-0 ), also approved as E963 , is a low-calorie monosaccharide sweetener derived from lactose that delivers approximately 92% of sucrose's sweetness with a significantly reduced glycemic impact.

It functions as both a bulk sweetener and humectant across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care formulations. In reduced-calorie and diabetic-friendly food products, it replaces sucrose in confectionery and dairy.

It is particularly effective in baked goods where browning behavior and mouthfeel comparable to sugar are required. Its prebiotic activity supports its use in functional food and nutrition products targeting gut health claims.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a low-glycemic excipient in oral dosage forms, chewable tablets, and nutraceutical preparations where sweetness and stability are both needed for the final product.

In personal care, it acts as a humectant and stabilizer in topical formulations, helping retain moisture in creams and oral care products. D-Tagatose is supplied as a white crystalline powder for industrial use.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC and E963 specifications is the standard commercial form for food and supplement applications. This ensures high purity and safety for consumer consumption.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available for buyers requiring tighter purity thresholds aligned with nutraceutical or oral dosage form manufacturing standards. This grade meets the rigorous demands of the medical industry.

name: Trichloroisocyanuric acid
description:
Trichloroisocyanuric acid ( CAS 87-90-1 ), commonly known as TCCA, is a chlorine-based oxidizing agent and biocide used across water treatment, sanitation, and industrial processing.

It delivers controlled, sustained chlorine release, making it a preferred active ingredient where consistent disinfection or bleaching performance is required for various applications.

In water treatment, TCCA is the active compound in swimming pool and potable water disinfection tablets, where its slow-dissolving profile maintains residual chlorine levels over time.

Textile and paper processors use it as a bleaching agent to whiten fibers and pulp without the handling risks associated with liquid chlorine or other volatile chemicals.

Food processing facilities apply TCCA-based solutions for equipment and surface sanitation, meeting hygiene standards where chlorine-releasing disinfectants are approved for use.

In personal care manufacturing, it functions as a preservative and antimicrobial active in certain industrial cleaning formulations targeting microbial contamination and growth.

TCCA is supplied as white tablets, granules, and powder, with tablet size varying by application from small pool tabs to larger industrial formats for heavy-duty use.

Standard commercial concentrations are typically 90% available chlorine content. Technical and industrial grades are the primary market forms available for global distribution.

name: Xylitol
description:
Xylitol (CAS 87-99-0 ), also known by its E-number E967 , is a naturally derived sugar alcohol used as a low-calorie sweetener and humectant across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care markets.

It delivers sweetness comparable to sucrose while supporting moisture retention in formulations. In food and confectionery manufacturing, it replaces sucrose in sugar-free gums, mints, chocolates, and baked goods.

Its non-cariogenic profile is a key commercial differentiator for manufacturers. Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it as a sweetening and bulking agent in chewable tablets, syrups, and oral care products.

Common applications include toothpastes and mouthwashes where it provides a cooling effect. In personal care, it functions as a humectant in skin creams, lotions, and hair care formulations.

This ingredient helps finished products retain moisture and improve texture stability. Nasal sprays and saline rinse products also use it to support mucosal hydration without introducing fermentable sugars.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP , Ph. Eur. ), and technical-grade options for various industries.

Pharmaceutical specifications are the most commonly requested for oral and topical drug formulations. Bulk quantities are available in bags and supersacks to meet high-volume manufacturing requirements.

Purity is typically at 99% or higher across commercial grades. This ensures consistent performance and compliance with global regulatory standards for food and medicinal applications.

name: Dioctyltin oxide
description:
Dioctyltin oxide (CAS 870-08-6 ), commonly abbreviated as DOTO, is an organotin compound used as a catalyst and flame retardant across polymer and coating systems. It functions primarily to accelerate curing reactions and improve thermal stability in industrial formulations.

In polyurethane and silicone systems, DOTO catalyzes condensation and crosslinking reactions, enabling controlled cure profiles in sealants and elastomers. Coating formulators use it to improve adhesion and durability in industrial protective coatings.

Where heat resistance is a processing requirement, this compound provides essential stability. In PVC and thermoplastic compounding, it acts as a stabilizer-catalyst combination, helping processors manage thermal degradation during high-temperature extrusion.

Adhesive manufacturers incorporate DOTO where flame retardancy requirements must be met alongside structural bonding performance. This versatile chemical ensures that materials maintain their integrity under rigorous manufacturing conditions and environmental stress.

Dioctyltin oxide is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder or paste. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 95% to 99% depending on the intended application.

Bulk supply is available in fiber drums or multi-layer bags, with smaller packaging options for laboratory or specialty formulation use. Proper storage in a cool, dry environment is recommended to maintain the chemical stability of the product.

name: Sodium formaldehyde bisulfite
description:
Sodium formaldehyde bisulfite ( CAS 870-72-4 ), also known as sodium hydroxymethanesulfonate or SFB, is an adduct compound that functions as a controlled formaldehyde releaser and reducing agent across multiple industrial sectors.

Its ability to slowly release formaldehyde under specific conditions makes it a practical preservation and biocide active where direct formaldehyde use is restricted or impractical for various manufacturing processes.

In water treatment, SFB is used as a biocide to control microbial growth in cooling towers, industrial process water, and oilfield injection systems. Textile and leather processors apply it as a reducing agent and fixative.

These applications in dyeing operations help in improving color consistency and overall process efficiency. In personal care formulations, it functions as a preservative in rinse-off products where low-level formaldehyde release is permitted.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an excipient and reducing agent in certain drug formulations and API synthesis steps. Sodium formaldehyde bisulfite is commercially available as a white crystalline powder or in aqueous solution.

Standard supply grades include technical grade for industrial applications and higher-purity grades suitable for pharmaceutical and personal care use. Bulk quantities are typically offered in bags or drums for transport.

Solution concentrations vary by supplier specification to meet diverse industrial needs. The material must be handled according to safety protocols to ensure stability and efficacy in its intended chemical applications.

name: Octadecanedioic acid
description:
Octadecanedioic acid (CAS 871-70-5 ) is a long-chain dicarboxylic acid used as a functional building block and performance additive across lubricant, coating, and personal care formulations.

Its symmetrical 18-carbon diacid structure enables surface modification, emulsification, and lubrication functions that shorter-chain diacids cannot match in industrial applications.

In lubricant and metalworking fluids, it acts as a friction modifier and corrosion inhibitor, improving film persistence on metal surfaces under load for better performance.

Coating and adhesive formulators incorporate it into polyamide and polyester resins to enhance flexibility, adhesion, and substrate wetting in various industrial finishes and protective layers.

Personal care manufacturers use it to modify emulsion texture and improve spreadability in skin-conditioning products, providing a smooth and consistent application for the end user.

Sealant and elastomer compounders also source it as a chain extender or crosslinking co-monomer to tune mechanical properties in specialty polymer systems and high-performance materials.

Octadecanedioic acid is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flake. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial applications including lubricants and coatings.

Higher-purity grades are available for personal care and cosmetic formulations where tighter specification control is required to meet the rigorous demands of the beauty industry.

name: Vinylene carbonate
description:
Vinylene carbonate (CAS 872-36-6 ), commonly abbreviated as VC, is a cyclic carbonate ester used primarily as an electrolyte additive and film-forming agent in lithium-ion battery manufacturing.

At low concentrations, it polymerizes on electrode surfaces to form a stable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), directly improving cycle life and capacity retention in battery cells.

In lithium-ion and lithium-polymer battery production, VC is added to carbonate-based electrolyte formulations at 1–5% loading to suppress electrolyte decomposition at the anode surface.

Battery manufacturers targeting high-cycle applications, such as EV packs, consumer electronics, and grid storage, specify VC to reduce irreversible capacity loss during formation cycling.

As a reactive monomer, it also serves as a building block in specialty polymer synthesis, including polycarbonate coatings and functional films requiring controlled crosslink density.

In personal care formulations, it has been explored as a carrier solvent and plasticizing component in film-forming systems. It is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid.

It is available in standard technical and high-purity electronic grades, with battery-grade specifications typically requiring purity ≥99.5% and tightly controlled water content.

Packaging options commonly include small quantities for R&D use through to drum volumes for industrial electrolyte blending, ensuring stability during transport and storage.

name: n-methyl-2-pyrrolidone

N-Methyl-2-Pyrrolidone (CAS 872-50-4 ), commonly abbreviated as NMP, is a high-boiling polar aprotic solvent used across demanding industrial and specialty chemical applications.

It dissolves a broad range of polymers, resins, and active compounds that resist conventional solvents, making it a preferred choice where solvent strength and thermal stability both matter.

In lithium-ion battery manufacturing, NMP is the standard solvent for slurry preparation, dispersing electrode binders like PVDF onto current collectors during cell production.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a carrier solvent in topical drug delivery systems and as a processing aid in API synthesis where high solvency and controlled evaporation are critical.

Electronics manufacturers rely on NMP for photoresist stripping and semiconductor cleaning, where residue-free performance directly affects yield in high-tech environments.

In polymer processing, it functions as the process solvent for producing aramid fibers, polyimide films, and engineering membranes used in gas separation and water treatment.

NMP is supplied as a clear liquid, typically in drums, IBCs, and bulk tankers. Standard commercial grades include technical, electronic, and pharmaceutical-grade material.

name: Bis-ethylhexyl hydroxydimethoxy benzylmalonate
description:
Bis-ethylhexyl hydroxydimethoxy benzylmalonate (CAS 872182-46-2 ) is an oil-soluble UV absorber and antioxidant used in personal care and industrial formulations. Derived from syringic acid chemistry, it functions by absorbing UV radiation and quenching free radicals.

This chemical protects substrates from photodegradation. Buyers source it primarily as a multifunctional stabilizer where both UV protection and oxidative stability are required in a single ingredient for high-performance applications.

In suncare and skincare formulations, it provides broad UV absorption and is often combined with other organic filters to boost SPF performance and photostability. It is a versatile choice for modern cosmetic chemistry.

Polymer and plastics compounders incorporate it to extend the service life of materials exposed to outdoor weathering. This is particularly important where color retention and mechanical integrity are top priorities for the manufacturer.

Coating and adhesive formulators use it to prevent UV-induced yellowing and surface degradation in clear and pigmented systems. Its oil solubility makes it directly compatible with solvent-based and emollient-rich matrices.

The ingredient integrates easily without requiring additional solubilization steps. Bis-ethylhexyl hydroxydimethoxy benzylmalonate is typically supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity oil for ease of handling in production.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suitable for personal care applications, as well as technical-grade material for industrial end uses. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers.

Smaller quantities are available for formulation development and pilot testing. This ensures that manufacturers can validate the performance of the stabilizer before moving to full-scale commercial production runs.

name: 3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexanone
description:
3,3,5-Trimethylcyclohexanone (CAS 873-94-9 ) is a cyclic ketone used in fragrance formulation and as a specialty solvent in personal care applications. Isophorone is its structurally related industrial counterpart.

This compound occupies a distinct niche as a fragrance ingredient with a characteristic woody, camphoraceous odor profile. It functions both as a scent contributor and as a carrier solvent in finished formulations.

In fragrance compounding, it serves as a building block for woody and fresh accords, particularly in fine fragrance and functional fragrance applications such as detergents and fabric care products.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into rinse-off and leave-on products where controlled odor release is required. Its solvent properties support the dissolution of fragrance concentrates.

The material is also used for resinous materials in cosmetic bases. It is also evaluated as a flavoring agent in contexts governed by FEMA -recognized ingredient lists for various applications.

3,3,5-Trimethylcyclohexanone is supplied as a clear liquid in standard drum and intermediate bulk container quantities. Fragrance-grade material is the primary commercial specification for the industry.

Purity levels are typically at 98% or above for standard batches. Smaller pack sizes are available to support laboratory evaluation and pilot-scale formulation work for research and development teams.

name: Euterpe oleracea extract
description:
Euterpe oleracea extract (CAS 879496-95-4 ), commonly known as açaí extract, is derived from the fruit of the South American açaí palm. It delivers a concentrated source of polyphenols and anthocyanins used across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical formulations.

This ingredient serves as a natural antioxidant and colorant in various industrial applications. In functional food and beverage manufacturing, it is incorporated into energy drinks, smoothie blends, and fortified snack products.

Natural antioxidant positioning supports premium product claims for these consumer goods. Nutraceutical formulators use it in capsules, softgels, and powdered supplements targeting the growing consumer demand for botanical antioxidant products.

In personal care, the extract is used in anti-aging serums, facial creams, and hair care formulations. Its polyphenol content supports the oxidative stability of the finished product while providing skin-conditioning benefits.

Pharmaceutical and health product manufacturers also source it as an active botanical ingredient in standardized herbal preparations. The extract is available as a spray-dried powder, liquid extract, and freeze-dried powder.

Spray-dried forms are the most common for industrial use due to their stability and ease of handling. Standardized grades specifying anthocyanin content are available for nutraceutical and cosmetic applications.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the primary commercial offerings for global buyers. Some suppliers also provide organic-certified material to meet specific regulatory and consumer requirements in niche markets.

name: Chloroxylenol
description:
Chloroxylenol (CAS 88-04-0 ), commonly known as PCMX, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used across personal care, healthcare, and industrial formulations. It delivers effective bactericidal and fungicidal activity.

This chemical is effective against a wide range of gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, making it a reliable preservation and disinfection ingredient for formulators and manufacturers worldwide.

In personal care and OTC healthcare products, PCMX is the active ingredient in antiseptic hand soaps, surgical scrubs, wound care preparations, and medicated skin cleansers for professional use.

Industrial and institutional disinfectant formulations rely on it for surface sanitization in healthcare facilities, food processing environments, and various veterinary settings requiring high hygiene standards.

Textile and leather processors use it as a preservative biocide to prevent microbial degradation during wet processing and storage. In plastics, it functions as an antioxidant and stabilizer.

Chloroxylenol is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder or flakes. Standard grades include USP , BP , and technical grade, with pharmaceutical specifications being the primary requirement.

Minimum purity of 98–99% is typical for pharmaceutical-grade material, while technical grade serves industrial preservation and polymer applications where high-level purity is less critical for the end result.

name: Vinylpyrrolidone
description:
Vinylpyrrolidone ( CAS 88-12-0 ), commonly abbreviated as NVP, is a reactive monomer used as a building block in polymer synthesis and UV-curable resin systems. It functions primarily as a reactive diluent and co-monomer.

This chemical enables formulators to tune viscosity, crosslink density, and adhesion in finished polymer networks. In UV-curable printing inks and coatings, NVP acts as a reactive diluent that reduces viscosity without adding inert solvent.

This process improves cure speed and film adhesion to difficult substrates. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a precursor in the production of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), a binder and film-former found in tablets.

It is also utilized in topical formulations and controlled-release systems. Personal care formulators incorporate NVP-based copolymers into hair fixatives, skin adhesives, and conditioning agents where film-forming performance is critical.

In specialty plastics and optical applications, NVP copolymers provide UV stabilization and surface hydrophilicity in contact lenses and protective coatings. These properties are essential for high-performance materials.

NVP is supplied as a clear liquid monomer, typically stabilized to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport. Standard commercial grades are available for industrial and pharmaceutical intermediate applications.

Purity specifications commonly range from technical grade to high-purity grades meeting pharmaceutical intermediate requirements. Our product ensures consistent performance across various specialty polymer applications and industrial uses.

name: 2-acetylthiophene
description:
2-Acetylthiophene (CAS 88-15-3 ), also known as methyl 2-thienyl ketone, is a sulfur-containing heterocyclic compound used as a flavoring and fragrance ingredient.

It delivers a roasted, nutty, and slightly meaty character that food and fragrance formulators rely on to build complex aroma profiles in various industrial applications.

In flavor creation, it contributes roasted and savory notes to snack seasonings, meat analogs, and processed food products where depth and warmth are required for the consumer.

Fragrance houses incorporate it into compositions targeting smoky, woody, or gourmand accords, particularly in fine fragrance and personal care applications for high-end markets.

It is also used in coffee and cocoa flavor systems, where its roasted sulfurous character reinforces natural aroma authenticity and enhances the overall sensory experience.

Tobacco flavor formulations represent another established end use, where it supports the characteristic warm and earthy profile required for traditional and modern products.

This product is supplied as a liquid at standard commercial purity levels, typically 98% and above, ensuring consistent performance across different manufacturing batches.

It is available in flavor-grade quality suitable for food and cosmetic applications, with documentation to support regulatory compliance in all major global markets.

name: 2,6-Di-tert-butyl-4-(dimethylaminomethyl)phenol
description:
2,6-Di-tert-butyl-4-(dimethylaminomethyl)phenol (CAS 88-27-7 ), sold commercially as Ionol 103, is a hindered phenolic antioxidant with an integrated amine functionality. It protects hydrocarbon-based materials from oxidative degradation during processing and long-term service.

In lubricant formulations, it functions as a multifunctional additive that delivers both antioxidant protection and mild metal-passivating activity. This extends oil service life in industrial and automotive systems.

Rubber compounders incorporate it to inhibit thermal and oxidative aging in finished goods such as seals, hoses, and tire components. This ensures the durability and performance of rubber products over time.

Polymer processors use it to stabilize polyolefins and other plastics against degradation during high-temperature extrusion and molding. It prevents the loss of mechanical properties during the manufacturing process.

In oil and gas applications, it is added to fuel streams and process fluids to prevent oxidative deterioration during storage and transmission. This maintains the quality and stability of the chemical streams.

The product is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for industrial antioxidant applications across lubricants, rubber, and polymer sectors.

Bulk supply is common in drums or IBC containers, with packaging options aligned to industrial procurement volumes. This ensures efficient handling and integration into large-scale chemical manufacturing workflows.

name: 2-tert-butyl-4-hydroxyanisole
description:
2-tert-Butyl-4-hydroxyanisole (CAS 88-32-4 ), one of the two isomers that together constitute commercial BHA, functions as a synthetic antioxidant and preservative across food, cosmetic, and industrial formulations.

It inhibits oxidative degradation in fats, oils, and polymer systems, extending shelf life and protecting product integrity. In food manufacturing, it is incorporated into edible fats, oils, and fat-containing products.

This additive helps to retard rancidity and meet regulatory antioxidant requirements. Cosmetic and personal care formulators use it to stabilize lipid-based products such as creams, lotions, and lip products.

Oxidative spoilage often shortens the usable life of these goods. In plastics and polymer processing, it acts as a processing stabilizer, protecting materials from thermal oxidation during compounding and extrusion.

Lubricant and metalworking fluid manufacturers add it to mineral oil-based formulations to suppress oxidative breakdown. This is particularly effective under high-temperature operating conditions found in industrial settings.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid or flakes. Standard grades include food-grade material meeting FCC and BP / Ph.Eur. specifications for regulated applications.

name: Phthalic acid
description:
Phthalic acid (CAS 88-99-3 ), also known as orthophthalic acid, is an aromatic dicarboxylic acid used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and specialty chemical manufacturing. It functions primarily as a pH buffer, acidulant, and catalyst precursor in synthesis and formulation processes.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, phthalic acid serves as a buffering agent in tablet coatings and controlled-release formulations where precise pH management affects drug dissolution profiles. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into pH-adjustment systems for creams and serums.

These rinse-off products require stability across a defined acidity range which is critical to shelf life. As a catalyst precursor, it is used in the production of phthalate esters and specialty resins where the acid form is the preferred starting material.

In preservation systems, its acidic character contributes to microbial control in formulations where low-pH environments are part of the preservation strategy. This versatility makes it a staple in modern chemical synthesis and industrial applications.

Phthalic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP and BP specifications is available for regulated applications, ensuring high purity and compliance with international standards.

Technical-grade product serves industrial synthesis and resin manufacturing where high-volume production is required. Packaging options typically range from kilogram-scale bags to bulk sacks depending on the specific application volume and logistics.

name: Polyquart pro a
description:
Polyquart Pro A (CAS 880345-00-6 ) is a cationic polymeric conditioning agent used across personal care and cleaning formulations. It functions as both a rheology modifier and surface modifier.

This versatile ingredient allows formulators to adjust texture while improving substrate deposition and wetting in a single step. In hair care, it deposits onto negatively charged hair fibers to deliver conditioning.

It provides excellent detangling performance in shampoos, conditioners, and leave-in treatments. Skin care formulators incorporate it into lotions and cleansers where controlled viscosity and a smooth after-feel are required.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it modifies surface wetting behavior to improve soil release and substrate coverage. It is also used in fabric care formulations where uniform polymer deposition occurs.

This deposition across fiber surfaces affects softness and finish quality in various textile applications. Polyquart Pro A is supplied as an aqueous solution for easy incorporation into water-based systems.

It is available in technical and cosmetic grades suited to personal care and industrial cleaning applications. Standard packaging includes drums and intermediate bulk containers for diverse logistics needs.

Supply quantities are appropriate for both development-scale and commercial production volumes. This ensures consistent performance and reliability for manufacturers across the global chemical supply chain.

name: Ethylhexyl triazone
description:
Ethylhexyl triazone (CAS 88122-99-0 ), also known as octyl triazone and commonly abbreviated as EHT, is a high-performance UVB filter used in sun care and personal care formulations.

It absorbs UV radiation in the 280–320 nm range, protecting both the end user and the formulation itself from photodegradation. This makes it an essential component for modern sun protection products.

EHT is primarily used in sunscreens, day creams, and SPF-boosting formulations where high UVB protection efficiency is required at relatively low use levels. It offers excellent photostability in various systems.

In color cosmetics and leave-on products, it stabilizes other UV filters and active ingredients that would otherwise degrade under sun exposure. This ensures the longevity and efficacy of the final product.

Coatings and polymer manufacturers incorporate it to prevent UV-induced yellowing and surface degradation in outdoor-exposed materials. It provides a critical barrier against environmental stressors.

Adhesives and sealants intended for exterior applications also benefit from its inclusion to extend product service life. This chemical helps maintain structural integrity and appearance over time.

Ethylhexyl triazone is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in cosmetic-grade specification, meeting requirements referenced in the EU Cosmetics Regulation and comparable international standards.

Technical-grade material is also available for industrial applications in coatings and polymer systems. Our product ensures consistent performance across all specified personal care and industrial applications.

name: Terbutryn
description:
Terbutryn (CAS 886-50-0 ), also sold under the trade names Igran, Shortstop, and Terbutrex, is a selective triazine herbicide used in both agricultural and non-agricultural settings. It controls broadleaf weeds and grasses by inhibiting photosynthesis in target plants.

This chemical has established use as a biocide in construction materials. In cereal and grain crop production, it is applied pre- and post-emergence to suppress competitive weed species without damaging established crops.

Formulators incorporate it into facade paints, renders, and building material coatings where algae and fungal growth on exterior surfaces must be controlled over extended periods. It is also used in aquatic and industrial water management contexts.

The substance helps to limit algal proliferation in various environments. Herbicide manufacturers include it as an active ingredient in suspension concentrates and wettable powder formulations for both agricultural and industrial end-use markets.

The product is supplied as a technical-grade active ingredient, typically as a solid or powder, for downstream formulation into registered end products. Standard concentrations for technical material are commonly specified at 95% purity or above.

Procurement is primarily directed at agrochemical formulators, biocide manufacturers, and registered product producers operating under applicable regulatory frameworks. This ensures compliance with safety and environmental standards during the manufacturing process.

name: Dipropylene glycol methyl ether acetate

Dipropylene glycol methyl ether acetate (CAS 88917-22-0 ), commonly abbreviated as DPMA and sold under the trade name Dowanol DPMA, is a slow-evaporating glycol ether ester solvent used across coatings, electronics, and printing industries.

name: Guaiacol
description:
Guaiacol (CAS 90-05-1 ), also known commercially as 2-Methoxyphenol, is a naturally derived phenolic compound obtained from wood creosote and lignin distillation. In industry, it functions as a flavoring agent and fragrance intermediate.

It also serves as a pharmaceutical precursor across multiple manufacturing sectors. In food and flavor production, it delivers the characteristic smoky, woody note found in smoked meats, whiskeys, and specialty flavor blends.

The compound carries FEMA 2532 status for use as an approved flavoring substance. Fragrance formulators use it as a building block for creating leather, tobacco, and phenolic accords in fine fragrance products.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key starting material for synthesizing expectorants and other active pharmaceutical ingredients. Antioxidant and preservative applications also draw on its phenolic activity.

This activity helps to stabilize formulations against oxidative degradation. The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid at ambient conditions, with solidification occurring near room temperature.

Standard commercial grades include food-grade material meeting FCC specifications. Pharmaceutical-grade material is also available, conforming to USP or BP standards for high-purity applications.

Technical-grade product is available for industrial synthesis and fragrance intermediate use. This versatile chemical remains a staple for manufacturers requiring consistent quality and reliable performance in diverse formulations.

name: 1-naphthol
description:
1-Naphthol (CAS 90-15-3 ), also sold under the dye intermediate designations Zoba ERN, Ursol ERN, and Tertral ERN, is a hydroxylated naphthalene compound used primarily as a chemical intermediate.

It is used in the synthesis of dyes, pigments, and active pharmaceutical ingredients. Its reactivity toward coupling and oxidative reactions makes it a reliable building block across colorant manufacturing and specialty chemical production.

In textile and leather dyeing, it functions as a coupling component in the production of azo dyes. It reacts with diazonium salts to generate deep, fast colors on fiber substrates for various industrial applications.

Pigment manufacturers use it as a key intermediate for producing naphthol-based pigments found in printing inks and packaging coatings. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a precursor to active ingredients.

It is also utilized as an antioxidant stabilizer used in drug formulations. Personal care formulators source it for oxidative hair dye systems, where controlled coupling reactions produce specific target shades.

The product is supplied as a white to pale yellow crystalline solid or flake. Technical grade is the standard commercial form, with purity typically at 98% or higher for most industrial manufacturing processes.

Pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP specifications is available for regulated synthesis applications. This ensures high quality and compliance for sensitive chemical and medical production needs.

name: 2-phenylphenol
description:
2-Phenylphenol (CAS 90-43-7 ), also known as OPP, Torsite, and Rotoline, is a broad-spectrum antimicrobial active used across food contact, agricultural, and industrial preservation applications.

It functions primarily as a biocide and fungicide, controlling microbial and fungal growth on surfaces, produce, and in formulated products. In post-harvest agriculture, it is applied as a surface treatment.

This treatment is used on citrus, pears, and other fresh produce to suppress mold and extend shelf life during storage and transit. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as an intermediate in synthesizing active compounds.

It also serves as a preservative component in topical and veterinary formulations. Personal care formulators incorporate it into disinfectant soaps, surface sanitizers, and cosmetic preservative systems.

In flavor and fragrance applications, it contributes a faint phenolic note and is recognized under FEMA 3959 for use in approved flavoring contexts. It is supplied as a white crystalline powder.

Technical and food-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with material sourced to meet regulatory requirements for food contact and agricultural use in relevant markets.

Purity grades typically range from 98% to 99%+, with documentation available to support compliance in regulated end-use categories. It meets various global standards for industrial and chemical safety.

name: Mandelic acid
description:
Mandelic acid (CAS 90-64-2 ), also known as phenylglycolic acid, is an alpha-hydroxy acid derived from bitter almonds that functions as a pharmaceutical intermediate, preservative, and skin-active ingredient.

It is used across pharmaceutical synthesis, cosmetic formulation, and specialty chemical manufacturing where controlled exfoliation, antimicrobial activity, or chiral building block chemistry is required.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a chiral intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients including antibiotics, anticoagulants, and antispasmodics, where its optical isomers are resolved.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into chemical peel systems and leave-on exfoliant products, where its larger molecular size relative to glycolic acid allows for a more controlled skin penetration profile.

This characteristic makes it particularly suited to sensitive skin formulations. As a preservative and pH buffer, it is used in urinary tract preparations and topical antimicrobial products.

In specialty resins and surface treatment chemistry, it functions as a wetting and adhesion modifier. Mandelic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various industrial uses.

Standard grades include pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ) for drug synthesis and cosmetic-grade material for personal care applications. Technical-grade material is available for research.

name: 2,4,6-tris(dimethylaminomethyl)phenol
description:
2,4,6-Tris(dimethylaminomethyl)phenol , also known as CAS 90-72-2 , is a tertiary amine curing agent and accelerator for epoxy resin systems. It accelerates epoxy cure at ambient or elevated temperatures, reducing processing time across a broad range of industrial formulations.

In structural adhesives and composite manufacturing, this chemical initiates and accelerates epoxy crosslinking, enabling room-temperature cure without external heat input. This efficiency is vital for large-scale production cycles.

Coatings formulators use it to harden epoxy floor coatings, protective linings, and corrosion-resistant topcoats where controlled pot life and full cure development are critical. It ensures the durability of industrial surfaces.

In electrical encapsulation and potting compounds, it ensures complete cure of epoxy systems around sensitive components. This supports dimensional stability under thermal cycling and protects delicate electronic hardware.

Polyurethane and phenolic resin producers also incorporate it as a catalyst to drive crosslink density in elastomers and sealants. This versatility makes it a staple in modern polymer chemistry and material science.

The product is supplied as an amber to yellow liquid. Standard commercial grades are available at high purity, typically greater than or equal to ninety-eight percent, for industrial and specialty applications.

Technical-grade material is the predominant market form, with packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities to drum-scale supply for production environments. It meets rigorous industrial requirements for consistency.

name: Gluconolactone
description:
Gluconolactone ( CAS 90-80-2 ), also known as GDL and E575 , is a naturally derived lactone used commercially as a slow-release acidulant and mild humectant across food and personal care markets.

Unlike fast-acting acids, it hydrolyzes gradually in aqueous systems, giving formulators precise control over pH reduction without sharp sensory impact. In food manufacturing, GDL is used to acidify tofu and processed meats.

It triggers protein coagulation without requiring heat or starter cultures in dairy analogues. Baked goods and ready-meal formulations use it as a leavening acid in combination with sodium bicarbonate for better results.

Its slow release improves texture and crumb structure in various bakery applications. In personal care, GDL functions as a mild exfoliant and pH adjuster in leave-on skincare products, particularly serums and toners.

These products often target skin renewal through gentle acidification. Cured and fermented meat products rely on it to lower pH rapidly during processing, improving food safety and slice firmness across the production line.

Gluconolactone is supplied as a white crystalline powder in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications. FCC and E575-compliant grades are standard for food applications to ensure high safety standards.

High-purity grades meeting cosmetic industry requirements are also commercially available for specialized formulations. Bulk supply is typically offered in 25 kg bags, with packaging suited to moisture-sensitive handling.

name: Gum arabic
description:
Gum arabic (CAS 9000-01-5 ), also traded as gum acacia and E414 , is a natural exudate harvested from Acacia trees and refined for use across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets.

It functions as an emulsifier, stabilizer, and film-former, enabling manufacturers to control texture, dispersion, and moisture retention in finished products. In food and beverage production, it is used to encapsulate flavors.

The additive stabilizes emulsions in soft drinks, confectionery coatings, and powdered flavor systems. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a binder and suspending agent in tablet formulations and oral suspensions.

Consistent viscosity and compatibility with active ingredients are critical in these medical applications. Personal care formulators incorporate it into setting sprays, serums, and hair fixatives for its film-forming properties.

In printing and lithography, it protects plate surfaces and acts as a desensitizing agent during offset printing processes. The material is supplied as a spray-dried powder, roller-dried flakes, or as a liquid solution.

Powder is the dominant commercial form for most industrial buyers. Recognized grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and BP / Ph.Eur. specifications to meet regulatory requirements across different end markets.

Spray-dried grades are available in varying mesh sizes to suit encapsulation, tableting, or direct dispersion applications. These standards ensure the material meets the rigorous demands of global supply chains.

name: Carrageenan
description:
Carrageenan (CAS 9000-07-1 ), also known as E407 and carrageenan gum, is a natural polysaccharide extracted from red seaweed used commercially as a gelling, thickening, and stabilizing agent.

It controls texture and suspension across food, personal care, and pharmaceutical formulations where precise rheological behavior is critical to product performance and long-term stability.

In dairy and plant-based food products, including chocolate milk, yogurt, and meat alternatives, carrageenan prevents ingredient separation and delivers a consistent, high-quality mouthfeel for consumers.

Infant formula and nutritional beverages rely on it to maintain stable emulsions and prevent protein aggregation during shelf life, ensuring the product remains safe and effective for use.

In personal care, it thickens lotions, shampoos, and toothpaste while improving the suspension of insoluble actives. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a binder and controlled-release matrix in tablets.

Carrageenan is supplied as a refined or semi-refined powder, with refined grades offering higher purity for sensitive applications. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant) for global safety.

Pharmaceutical-grade options meeting Ph. Eur. and USP standards are available to meet regulatory requirements across markets. Kappa, iota, and lambda types are commercially available for specific needs.

Each type is selected based on gel strength, texture, and compatibility requirements of the end formulation. This versatility makes it an essential ingredient for modern industrial manufacturing processes.

name: Carboxymethyl cellulose
description:
Carboxymethyl cellulose ( CAS 9000-11-7 ), commonly sourced as CMC or cellulose gum ( E466 ), is a water-soluble cellulose derivative used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets.

It functions as a thickener, binder, and stabilizer. Its ability to control viscosity and retain water at low use levels makes it a high-volume ingredient in both aqueous formulations and dry-mix systems.

In food manufacturing, CMC functions as a texture modifier and stabilizer in ice cream, bakery fillings, sauces, and low-fat dairy products. It provides essential mouthfeel and shelf stability.

Pharmaceutical tablet production relies on CMC as a binder and disintegrant. Crosslinked carboxymethyl cellulose serves specifically as a superdisintegrant in various solid dosage forms for rapid release.

Detergent and household cleaning formulations use cellulose gum as an anti-redeposition agent. This prevents loosened soil from re-adhering to fabric during the washing cycle for better results.

In construction, CMC improves workability and water retention in tile adhesives, gypsum compounds, and cement-based mortars. It is supplied as a white to off-white powder in various viscosity grades.

Food-grade material is available to FCC specifications. Pharmaceutical grades meet USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards to ensure the highest level of safety and compliance for manufacturers.

Technical grades serve industrial applications in textiles, paper sizing, and drilling fluids. These grades are optimized for specific processing requirements and high-performance industrial environments.

name: Galbanum gum
description:
Galbanum gum (CAS 9000-24-2 ), also known as Ferula resin, is a natural oleoresin exudate harvested from Ferula species native to the Middle East and Central Asia. Registered under FEMA 2502 , it delivers a sharp, green, balsamic character.

Perfumers and flavorists rely on this material for distinctive aromatic profiles. In fine fragrance and personal care formulations, it contributes a distinctive green, woody topnote found in chypre and fougère compositions.

Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a natural flavoring agent. The FEMA 2502 status supports its use in confectionery, baked goods, and savory products at controlled levels to ensure consistent taste profiles.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical formulators incorporate it into traditional remedy preparations and botanical extracts. This is particularly common where the resin's natural origin is a primary sourcing requirement for the final product.

Incense and aromatic product manufacturers also source it as a base resin for blending with other natural gum exudates. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient across several industrial sectors requiring high-quality resins.

Galbanum gum is supplied as a raw resin lump, soft paste, or processed powder depending on extraction and handling method. It is available in natural or crude grade for fragrance compounding and specialized applications.

Purified or standardized extract forms are available for food and pharmaceutical applications. Buyers should confirm moisture content, resin versus gum ratio, and botanical source documentation when evaluating supplier specifications.

name: Guar gum
description:
Guar gum (CAS 9000-30-0 ), also sold as Cyamopsis gum, guar flour, and classified as E412 in food applications, is a natural galactomannan polysaccharide derived from the guar plant.

It functions as a high-performance thickener, binder, and stabilizer across food, industrial, and personal care markets. In food manufacturing, it thickens and stabilizes products such as ice cream and sauces.

It is also used in dairy beverages and gluten-free baked goods, where it controls texture and prevents syneresis. Personal care formulators incorporate it into shampoos, conditioners, and lotions.

This ingredient helps to build viscosity and improve sensory feel without synthetic polymers. In oil and gas drilling, it acts as a viscosifier in hydraulic fracturing fluids, suspending proppants.

It is also used for improving fluid recovery in industrial settings. Textile and paper processors use it as a sizing and finishing agent to improve fiber binding, surface strength, and print definition.

The product is supplied as a free-flowing off-white to cream-colored powder in a range of mesh sizes. Food-grade material is available to FCC specifications; pharmaceutical-grade supply meets USP standards.

The material also complies with Ph. Eur. standards for pharmaceutical applications. Industrial grades are offered for oilfield, textile, and paper applications with specific viscosity grades.

These grades are selected based on end-use hydration requirements. The versatility of this polysaccharide makes it an essential component for achieving desired textures and stability in diverse formulations.

name: Karaya gum

In food manufacturing, it stabilizes ice cream, salad dressings, and processed meats by controlling texture and preventing syneresis. Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a bulk laxative base and tablet binder for various applications.

Its swelling capacity supports controlled-release and mucoadhesive dosage forms in medical settings. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into denture adhesives, hair-setting lotions, and skin creams for its moisture-retention and film-forming behavior.

In textile and paper processing, it functions as a sizing and finishing agent, improving fiber cohesion and surface quality. Karaya gum is supplied as an off-white to pinkish-tan powder in various mesh sizes for industrial use.

name: Locust bean gum
description:
Locust bean gum ( CAS 9000-40-2 ), also known as carob gum and E410 , is a natural galactomannan polysaccharide extracted from the seeds of the carob tree. In commercial formulations, it functions as a thickener, gelling agent, and water-binding agent across food, personal care, and industrial applications.

In food manufacturing, LBG is used to control texture and water activity in dairy products, ice cream, and processed meats. It is highly effective at preventing ice crystal formation and syneresis during freeze-thaw cycles.

Combined with xanthan or carrageenan, it produces synergistic gel structures used in low-fat spreads, sauces, and bakery fillings where texture stability is critical. These combinations allow for precise control over the final product mouthfeel.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into creams, lotions, and hair conditioners to build viscosity and improve moisture retention on skin and hair surfaces. It provides a smooth, non-greasy application experience for high-end cosmetic products.

In textile and paper processing, it functions as a sizing and coating agent, improving fiber adhesion and surface smoothness in finished goods. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient in various industrial manufacturing sectors.

Locust bean gum is supplied as an off-white to cream-colored powder in food-grade and technical-grade forms. Standard specifications include FCC , E410-compliant food grade, and cosmetic-grade material meeting relevant purity thresholds.

Viscosity grades vary to suit different application requirements, from low-viscosity textile uses to high-viscosity food and personal care formulations. Our material ensures consistent performance across all specified industrial and commercial standards.

name: Shellac
description:
Shellac (CAS 9000-59-3 ), also known as lac resin and designated E904 , is a natural resinous secretion refined for use as a film-forming and surface-finishing agent across food, coating, and industrial applications.

Sourced primarily from the lac insect, it is processed into flake, wax-free, and bleached forms to meet the demands of diverse manufacturing sectors. In food production, E904 is applied as a glazing agent on confectionery and fresh produce.

It is also used on pharmaceutical tablets to deliver a protective, high-gloss finish that extends shelf life. The coatings and printing industries rely on shellac-based formulations for wood lacquers, ink binders, and overprint varnishes.

These applications are ideal where fast drying and adhesion to multiple substrates are required. Leather finishing operations use it to build durable, flexible surface films that resist scuffing and retain appearance through processing.

In paper and packaging, shellac functions as a moisture-barrier coating and adhesive component for labels, seals, and specialty paper treatments. Shellac is supplied as dry flakes, the most common commercial form.

It is available in wax-containing and dewaxed variants. Bleached and orange grades are standard market offerings, with dewaxed bleached shellac preferred for food and pharmaceutical use.

Food-grade material conforming to E904 specifications and pharmaceutical-grade material meeting USP or BP standards are both commercially available for global distribution.

The gum delivers reliable viscosity control in both aqueous and semi-solid systems. In food manufacturing, it stabilizes salad dressings, confectionery fillings, and ice cream by preventing phase separation and controlling texture.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a binding and suspending agent in tablet coatings, lozenges, and oral liquid preparations. This is particularly useful where consistent rheology is critical for the final product performance.

Personal care producers incorporate it into creams, gels, and toothpaste to build viscosity and improve product spreadability. In textile and paper processing, it acts as a sizing and printing paste thickener.

name: Pectin
description:
Pectin (CAS 9000-69-5 ), also designated E440a , is a natural polysaccharide extracted primarily from citrus peel and apple pomace. It functions as a gelling agent, thickener, and stabilizer across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing.

In food production, pectin is the standard gelling agent for jams, jellies, and fruit preparations, where controlled gel strength and set time are critical to finished product consistency.

Beverage manufacturers use it to stabilize acidified dairy drinks and fruit juices, preventing protein aggregation and phase separation. This ensures a smooth texture and long shelf life for liquid formulations.

Derived from Bacillus strains, it operates efficiently at elevated temperatures, making it a preferred choice for high-throughput industrial starch processing. In baking, it improves dough extensibility, crust color, and loaf volume by degrading damaged starch.

Brewing and bioethanol production rely on it to liquefy and saccharify grain mashes, directly increasing fermentable sugar yield ahead of yeast fermentation. Textile and paper manufacturers use it to desize starch-coated fabrics and to modify paper pulp viscosity.

It acts on alpha-1,4-glycosidic bonds in starch chains, breaking down complex carbohydrates into dextrins, maltose, and glucose. In baking and flour milling, it improves dough extensibility and crust color.

This enzyme enhances shelf life by converting damaged starch into fermentable sugars that support yeast activity. Brewing and distilling operations rely on it to liquefy and saccharify starch-rich mash.

Brewers use it to prevent chill haze in beer by hydrolyzing haze-forming proteins before cold storage. In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is incorporated into digestive enzyme formulations and anti-inflammatory supplements.

Catalase (CAS 9001-05-2 ), also supplied under trade names such as Equilase and Caperase, is an oxidoreductase enzyme that decomposes hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. In industrial settings, it functions as a biological catalyst to eliminate residual peroxide from process streams.

This enzyme protects product quality and downstream process integrity by neutralizing oxidative agents. In dairy and food processing, it removes hydrogen peroxide used as a cold sterilant in milk and cheese production, enabling compliant, residue-free output.

Textile and paper manufacturers use it to decompose bleaching peroxide before dyeing or coating steps. This prevents uneven results and chemical interference during the manufacturing process. Pharmaceutical and biotech producers incorporate it into enzymatic reaction systems.

In baking, GOX strengthens dough by generating hydrogen peroxide in situ, which oxidizes gluten proteins to improve dough handling and loaf volume. It functions as a clean-label alternative to chemical oxidants like bromate in commercial bread production.

Diagnostic manufacturers use it as the active enzyme in glucose biosensors and test strips for blood glucose monitoring. Its high substrate specificity is critical to measurement accuracy in medical and laboratory settings.

Invertase ( CAS 9001-57-4 ), also known commercially as E1103 , Invertin, and Sucrase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into glucose and fructose.

In confectionery, invertase is used to produce soft-centered chocolates. The enzyme liquefies a solid sucrose fondant center after enrobing, eliminating the need for liquid filling during production.

In the pharmaceutical industry, it converts sucrose syrups into invert sugar for use as an excipient or sweetening agent in liquid dosage forms and other medicinal preparations.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a model enzyme in fermentation research and as a reagent in biosensor development for sucrose detection and analysis.

Invertase is supplied as a liquid enzyme concentrate or as a dried powder. Food-grade material meeting FCC specifications is the standard commercial offering for confectionery.

Polyisobutene (CAS 9003-27-4 ), also known as polyisobutylene or PIB, is a synthetic hydrocarbon polymer produced by the polymerization of isobutylene. Across lubricant, sealant, and polymer processing industries, it functions as a viscosity modifier.

It acts as a plasticizer and tackifier depending on the specific molecular weight grade selected for the application. In lubricant and gear oil formulations, high-molecular-weight PIB acts as a viscosity index improver.

It serves as a base fluid component, extending film strength under load. Rubber compounders incorporate mid-range grades as a softening and processing aid, improving flexibility and reducing hardness in finished seals.

It is also used in gaskets and profiles. In automotive sealants and adhesives, PIB provides long-term tackiness and resistance to gas permeation, making it a preferred binder in various butyl-based formulations.

Low-molecular-weight grades are used as plasticizers in polyolefin blends, improving melt flow and surface finish in extruded and injection-molded parts. Polyisobutene is supplied as a viscous liquid or semi-solid.

Viscosity and molecular weight determine the commercial grade. Standard grades are differentiated by number-average molecular weight, typically ranging from low (300 to 1,000 Mn) to high (above 50,000 Mn).

Food-contact and pharmaceutical-grade PIB meeting FCC and USP specifications is available for applications requiring regulatory compliance. These grades ensure safety and quality for sensitive industrial uses.

name: Polybutylene
description:
Polybutylene (CAS 9003-28-5 ), also marketed as poly-1-butene, is a semi-crystalline polyolefin resin used across plastics processing, construction, and automotive manufacturing. It functions primarily as a flexibility modifier and rheology agent in polymer blends and finished resin systems.

In pipe systems for hot and cold water distribution, polybutylene delivers long-term creep resistance and pressure retention, making it a preferred resin for extruded plumbing tube. Automotive manufacturers incorporate it into under-hood components and flexible tubing.

Where sustained heat exposure demands dimensional stability from the base polymer, this resin provides reliable performance. In polyolefin blending, it acts as a softening modifier to adjust stiffness and flow characteristics in polypropylene and polyethylene compounds.

This adjustment occurs without sacrificing processability during high-speed manufacturing. Film and packaging converters also use it to improve seal strength and flexibility in multilayer structures, ensuring product integrity during transport.

Polybutylene is supplied as pellets or granules suited for extrusion and injection molding processes. It is available in isotactic grades differentiated by melt flow index and molecular weight to match specific processing equipment.

These grades are designed to meet various end-use performance targets in industrial settings. Technical and pipe-grade specifications are the most commonly traded forms in industrial procurement for global chemical distribution networks.

Contact us for supply of Polybutylene

name: Polybutylene
description:
Polybutylene (CAS 9003-29-6 ), also supplied under the trade designation Amoco 15H, is a semi-crystalline polyolefin produced from butene monomer. It is used across plastics compounding and construction applications to modify flow behavior.

This material is essential to impart flexibility to finished polymer systems. In hot melt adhesives and sealants, it functions as a tackifier and rheology modifier, improving open time and bond flexibility without compromising structural integrity.

Pipe and plumbing systems in building construction have historically utilized this polymer for its resistance to creep under sustained pressure. This makes it a specified material in cold and hot water distribution networks.

Automotive underhood and interior components benefit from the material when compounded into polyolefin blends. In these applications, it softens rigid matrices and improves low-temperature impact performance for durable parts.

It is also incorporated into film and packaging formulations as a processing aid that reduces melt viscosity. This addition enhances surface finish and improves the overall efficiency of high-speed manufacturing lines.

The product is commercially available as pellets and granules suited for melt processing on standard extrusion equipment. Grades are differentiated primarily by molecular weight and melt flow index to match specific targets.

Supply is typically offered at technical grade, with specifications confirmed against manufacturer datasheets on a per-lot basis. This ensures consistent performance across various industrial injection molding applications.

name: Polyisoprene
description:
Polyisoprene (CAS 9003-31-0 ) is a synthetic or natural-derived polymer that replicates the structure of natural rubber, offering high elasticity and resilience for demanding rubber applications.

Available in both natural and synthetic forms, it is used across rubber compounding, adhesives, and polymer blending where controlled elastic performance is required for industrial use.

In tire manufacturing, it is compounded into tread and sidewall formulations where consistent tensile strength and flex fatigue resistance are critical to meeting the product specification.

Medical and industrial glove producers use it as a latex-free alternative to natural rubber, meeting the purity requirements of healthcare and cleanroom environments for safety and hygiene.

Adhesive formulators incorporate it into pressure-sensitive and hot-melt systems to control tack, peel strength, and the rheological profile of the final adhesive product during application.

In polymer blending, it functions as a softening and rheology-modifying component, adjusting the flow and mechanical behavior of thermoplastic compounds for various manufacturing processes.

Polyisoprene is supplied as baled solid, crumb, or pelletized rubber for synthetic grades, and as concentrated latex or dry bales for natural-derived material for easy processing.

Standard grades include technical rubber grades differentiated by Mooney viscosity, as well as pharmaceutical-grade synthetic polyisoprene meeting USP and ISO specifications for medical devices.

name: Phenol formaldehyde resin
description:
Phenol formaldehyde resin (CAS 9003-35-4 ), commonly known as phenolic resin or PF resin, is a synthetic thermosetting polymer produced by reacting phenol with formaldehyde.

It functions as a binder, adhesive matrix, and curing agent across demanding industrial applications where heat resistance and structural integrity are non-negotiable for the end user.

In the wood panel and construction industry, PF resin bonds plywood, OSB, and engineered lumber, delivering moisture-resistant joints that meet structural load requirements for safety.

Automotive and aerospace brake components rely on phenolic resin as the primary binder in friction materials, where it maintains performance under extreme thermal cycling and pressure.

Foundry operations use PF resin as a shell mold binder, enabling precise casting of metal parts with clean release and dimensional accuracy during the manufacturing process.

In coatings and laminates, it crosslinks with other resins to produce hard, chemically resistant surface finishes for industrial flooring, electrical laminates, and decorative panels.

Phenol formaldehyde resin is supplied as a liquid resole, solid novolac flake or powder, and solution-grade variants at defined solid content levels for various industrial needs.

Standard grades include technical-grade resoles for wood bonding and novolacs for molding compounds. Specifications are defined by viscosity, free phenol content, and gel time.

name: Polyvinylpyrrolidone
description:
Polyvinylpyrrolidone (CAS 9003-39-8 ), commercially known as povidone or PVP, is a synthetic water-soluble polymer used across pharmaceutical, food, and personal care manufacturing.

Approved as a food additive under E1201 , it functions primarily as a binder, film former, and stabilizing agent in finished product formulations for various industrial applications.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, PVP is a standard tablet binder and also used as a solubilizer to improve bioavailability of poorly soluble active ingredients in solid dosage forms.

Personal care formulators rely on it as a film-forming agent in hair sprays, styling gels, and contact lens solutions where controlled hold and clarity are required for the consumer.

In the food industry, E1201 is approved for use as a clarifying and stabilizing agent in beverages, particularly wine and beer processing to ensure product quality and shelf stability.

Textile and paper industries use PVP to improve dye uptake and surface adhesion during finishing operations, providing consistent results across large-scale manufacturing batches.

PVP is supplied as a white to off-white powder or as aqueous solution concentrates. It is available in multiple molecular weight grades with K-value indicating viscosity and chain length.

Recognized grades include USP , Ph.Eur. , FCC , and technical, supporting sourcing across regulated and industrial end markets for global distribution and compliance.

name: Polystyrene
description:
Polystyrene (CAS 9003-53-6 ), commonly abbreviated as PS, is a synthetic thermoplastic polymer produced from styrene monomer and used across packaging, construction, and electronics manufacturing.

It provides rigidity, dimensional stability, and ease of processing in both solid and foam forms. In packaging, PS is thermoformed into food containers, disposable cutlery, and protective inserts.

These applications require clarity and stiffness at a low cost. Expanded polystyrene foam serves as structural insulation board in building panels and cavity wall systems, delivering thermal resistance without weight.

In electronics, PS is injection-molded into housings, connectors, and display components. These parts rely on tight dimensional tolerances and excellent electrical insulation properties for long-term performance.

The printing industry uses PS sheet stock as a substrate for signage, point-of-sale displays, and screen-printed graphics. Polystyrene is supplied as pellets or granules for injection molding and extrusion.

It is also available as expandable beads for foam processing. Standard commercial grades include general-purpose PS (GPPS) for transparent applications and high-impact PS (HIPS) for toughened, opaque end uses.

Food-contact grades compliant with FDA and EU regulations are available for packaging applications. Our material meets rigorous industrial specifications to ensure consistency across various manufacturing batches.

name: Styrene-acrylonitrile resin
description:
Styrene-acrylonitrile resin (CAS 9003-54-7 ), commonly known as SAN or AS resin, is a rigid thermoplastic copolymer used across packaging, automotive, and electronics manufacturing. It delivers higher chemical resistance and clarity than standard polystyrene.

This material is a preferred base where transparency and structural integrity are both required. In consumer packaging and housewares, SAN is injection-molded into transparent containers, bottles, and kitchenware that must withstand contact with oils.

These products are designed to resist detergents and mild solvents during regular use. Automotive manufacturers use it for interior trim components, instrument panels, and light covers where dimensional stability under heat is a priority.

In electronics, SAN is specified for housings and connectors that require good surface finish and resistance to processing chemicals. It also functions as a matrix component or impact modifier carrier in ABS systems.

The resin influences melt flow and stiffness balance in compounded formulations. Styrene-acrylonitrile resin is supplied as pellets or granules, the standard form for injection molding and extrusion processing workflows.

Acrylonitrile content typically ranges from 20–30%, with grade selection directly affecting chemical resistance and heat deflection performance. Technical and engineering grades are available for various industrial needs.

Some producers offer food-contact compliant specifications for packaging applications. These materials meet rigorous safety requirements for use in the global food and beverage supply chain and consumer goods sectors.

name: Styrene-butadiene
description:
Styrene-butadiene (CAS 9003-55-8 ), commercially known as styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), is a synthetic copolymer used across rubber and polymer manufacturing. It delivers controlled elasticity and abrasion resistance.

This material offers excellent processability in high-volume industrial applications. In tire manufacturing, SBR is the dominant tread compound material, offering wear performance comparable to natural rubber at lower cost.

It provides greater batch consistency for large scale production. Building and construction applications include flooring adhesives, waterproofing membranes, and asphalt modification where it improves flexibility.

Printing and packaging converters use SBR-based latex as a binder in paper coatings and carpet backing. This helps in controlling rheology and surface adhesion for various industrial substrates.

Automotive seals, gaskets, and conveyor belting also rely on SBR compounds for durable, cost-effective elastomeric performance. It is a versatile solution for many mechanical rubber goods.

Styrene-butadiene is supplied as dry bales, crumb rubber, and aqueous latex dispersions. Standard grades are differentiated by styrene-to-butadiene ratio and Mooney viscosity for specific processing.

Emulsion-polymerized and solution-polymerized variants are available for different performance profiles. Food-contact and indirect-contact grades are recognized under E1585 for regulated applications.

name: Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene
description:
Acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (CAS 9003-56-9 ), commonly known as ABS plastic, is a thermoplastic terpolymer used across manufacturing industries for its balance of rigidity, toughness, and processability.

It is a primary material choice where impact resistance and dimensional stability are required in finished parts. In automotive manufacturing, ABS plastic is used to produce interior trim panels and dashboards.

These structural housings must withstand mechanical stress and temperature variation. Electronics manufacturers rely on it for device enclosures, keyboard components, and connectors where precise molding tolerances are critical.

In building and construction, ABS is specified for pipe fittings, drainage systems, and protective housings. This material is chosen where long-term durability under load is required for infrastructure projects.

Consumer goods producers use it extensively in appliance casings and power tool bodies. In these applications, surface finish quality and structural integrity are both essential procurement priorities for the manufacturer.

ABS is supplied as pellets or granules, the standard form for injection molding, extrusion, and thermoforming operations. Grades are differentiated by impact resistance, heat deflection temperature, and flame retardancy.

General-purpose, high-impact, and flame-retardant classifications are available to meet specific industrial needs. Specialty grades include plating-grade ABS for electroplating and transparent ABS for aesthetic end uses.
