name: Styrene-divinylbenzene copolymer
description:
Styrene-divinylbenzene copolymer (CAS 9003-70-7 ) is a crosslinked polymer resin produced by copolymerizing styrene with divinylbenzene to create a rigid, porous bead structure. It functions as a base matrix for ion exchange resins and chromatographic media.

This material is essential for solid-phase extraction sorbents across water treatment, pharmaceutical, and life sciences applications. In water treatment, the resin matrix is functionalized to produce cation and anion exchange resins.

These resins are used for demineralization, softening, and removal of heavy metals from industrial effluents. Pharmaceutical manufacturers rely on functionalized grades as the backbone of purification resins used in API isolation.

The polymer is also utilized in chromatographic separation processes and solid-phase extraction. In these roles, the unfunctionalized or lightly modified polymer captures organic compounds from aqueous matrices for analytical sample preparation.

Biotechnology applications include use as a support matrix in affinity and size-exclusion chromatography columns. These systems are vital for protein and biomolecule purification in laboratory and industrial settings.

The product is supplied as spherical beads in dry or pre-swelled form, with particle size distributions tailored to specific requirements. Grades are available across a range of crosslink densities for various uses.

The crosslink density determines the pore structure and surface area for the intended downstream functionalization. Technical and chromatographic-grade materials are both commercially available for industrial buyers.

The latter meets tighter specifications for use in regulated pharmaceutical manufacturing environments. This ensures consistent performance and reliability for high-purity applications in the chemical and medical sectors.

name: Lactoperoxidase
description:
Lactoperoxidase (CAS 9003-99-0 ) is a naturally occurring enzyme derived from bovine milk and colostrum, commercially supplied for its antimicrobial and oxidative activity. It functions as the catalytic component of the lactoperoxidase system.

The enzyme generates bactericidal compounds when combined with hydrogen peroxide and thiocyanate. This mechanism makes it a recognized preservation and stabilization tool across food, pharmaceutical, and biotechnology applications.

In food and dairy processing, it is used to extend the shelf life of raw milk and liquid dairy products without heat treatment. This specific method is endorsed by FAO/WHO guidelines for global food safety.

Personal care and oral hygiene formulators incorporate it into toothpastes, mouthwashes, and saliva-substitute products targeting antimicrobial efficacy. It provides a natural alternative to synthetic preservatives in these formulations.

Diagnostic and life science manufacturers use it as a labeling reagent for radioiodination of proteins. It also serves as a critical component in enzyme-linked assay systems for various laboratory research applications.

Pharmaceutical researchers evaluate it as a biopreservative in protein-based formulations where conventional preservatives are incompatible. It is supplied as a lyophilized powder or liquid concentrate with activity expressed in units.

Grades include food-grade and research-grade specifications, with purity and specific activity defined per supplier standard. Material sourced from bovine milk is the predominant commercial form for industrial use.

Buyers should confirm activity retention and cold-chain requirements when evaluating suppliers. Ensuring the material meets necessary quality standards is essential for maintaining the efficacy of the lactoperoxidase system.

name: Lipoprotein lipase
description:
Lipoprotein lipase ( CAS 9004-02-8 ), also known as clearing factor lipase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of triglycerides in lipoproteins, releasing free fatty acids for cellular uptake.

In industrial and research contexts, it functions as a biocatalytic tool for lipid processing, diagnostic assay development, and metabolic pathway research. In pharmaceutical research, it is used to model lipid metabolism disorders.

This enzyme supports drug discovery programs targeting dyslipidemia and cardiovascular conditions. Diagnostic kit manufacturers incorporate it into enzymatic assay systems for measuring triglyceride levels in clinical laboratory testing.

Biotechnology applications include its use as a reagent in lipoprotein characterization studies and in vitro metabolic modeling. It also supports formulation research where controlled lipid hydrolysis is required.

This is essential to evaluate lipid-based drug delivery systems. The product is supplied as a lyophilized powder or liquid enzyme preparation, typically in buffered solution formats suited for laboratory and research-scale use.

Activity is expressed in units per milligram of protein, with specifications varying by source organism, commonly bovine or bacterial origin. Research-grade and reagent-grade designations are standard for these materials.

Buyers should confirm specific activity, purity, and storage requirements when sourcing. The material is handled according to strict laboratory protocols to ensure the stability and efficacy of the enzymatic activity.

name: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose
description:
Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CAS 9004-32-4 ), commonly known as CMC or E466 , is a water-soluble cellulose derivative used across industrial and consumer markets as a thickener, binder, and stabilizer.

Its ability to modify viscosity and control water retention makes it a functional workhorse in formulations ranging from food products to drilling fluids. In oil and gas drilling, CMC controls fluid loss and stabilizes wellbore mud.

This directly affects drilling efficiency and formation protection. Food manufacturers use it under the E466 designation to improve texture and shelf stability in products such as ice cream, sauces, and baked goods.

In paper and textile processing, it functions as a surface sizing agent and warp sizing agent, improving coating adhesion and yarn strength respectively. Construction product formulators incorporate it into tile adhesives.

It is also used in cement renders and dry-mix mortars to extend open time and improve workability. Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a broad range of viscosity grades.

These are typically defined by degree of substitution and solution concentration. Established grades include food-grade (E466/ FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / Ph. Eur. ), and technical-grade for industrial applications.

Purity and viscosity specifications vary significantly by end use, making grade selection a critical procurement consideration for manufacturers seeking consistent performance in their specific chemical formulations.

name: Cellulose

Microcrystalline Cellulose (MCC, CAS 9004-34-6 ), also known commercially as Cellulose 248 and Kingcot, is a purified, partially depolymerized cellulose used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing.

Approved as E460 , it functions primarily as a binder, filler, and rheology modifier in solid and semi-solid formulations. In pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing, MCC acts as a direct compression binder.

This material improves tablet hardness and disintegration without requiring wet granulation. Food producers use it as an anti-caking agent and fat replacer in low-calorie products, where it maintains texture and bulk.

In construction materials, cellulose-based additives modify the rheology of cement and gypsum-based compounds. These additives are essential for controlling water retention and overall workability during application.

Paper and textile processors use refined cellulose grades as a functional filler and coating agent. These applications help to improve surface properties and dimensional stability in the final manufactured goods.

MCC is supplied as a white, free-flowing powder in a range of particle size grades. These variations are suited to different compaction and flow requirements across various industrial and laboratory settings.

Established grades include USP /NF, Ph. Eur. , BP , and FCC , covering pharmaceutical and food-grade applications. These standards ensure the highest level of safety and performance.

Crystalline cellulose grades are also available for specialty industrial applications. These are used where higher purity and defined crystallinity are required for specific chemical or mechanical processes.

name: Cellulose acetate
description:
Cellulose acetate (CAS 9004-35-7 ), also supplied as cellulose triacetate (CTA), is an acetylated biopolymer derived from natural cellulose and used across textile, film, and filtration manufacturing.

CA functions as a film-forming resin and fiber-forming polymer, enabling manufacturers to produce shaped, extruded, or cast end products with controlled mechanical properties.

In textile production, CA is the base polymer for acetate fiber — spun into filament yarns used in linings, blouses, and luxury apparel where a silk-like drape is required.

Cigarette filter tow represents one of the largest single-use applications, where CA tow is crimped and processed into acetate filter rods for the tobacco industry.

In plastics and packaging, it is compounded into injection-molded or extruded sheet products, including eyeglass frames, tool handles, and transparent film for graphic arts.

Membrane and filtration manufacturers also use CA to cast reverse osmosis and ultrafiltration membranes for water treatment and dialysis equipment applications.

Cellulose acetate is supplied as flake, powder, or tow depending on the target application. Standard grades include textile-grade tow, plastics-grade flake, and membrane-grade powder.

Technical and industrial grades are the most common commercial forms; pharmaceutical-grade CA meeting USP or Ph. Eur. standards is available for controlled-release coating applications.

name: Cellulose acetate butyrate
description:
Cellulose acetate butyrate ( CAS 9004-36-8 ), commonly known as CAB, is a mixed cellulose ester produced by reacting cellulose with acetic and butyric acids. Compared to standard cellulose acetate, CAB offers lower moisture absorption.

It provides improved compatibility with a broader range of plasticizers and resins, which are factors that directly influence grade selection for formulators. It functions primarily as a film-forming binder and rheology modifier.

CAB acts as a flow-control agent across coatings, plastics, and printing applications. In industrial and automotive coatings, it controls metallic flake orientation and prevents pigment settling during application, improving finish consistency.

Thermoplastic compounders incorporate it into transparent and tinted plastic parts where low haze and UV stability are priorities. In printing inks, CAB contributes to adhesion, gloss, and controlled viscosity across solvent-based formulations.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a modifier to adjust tack and film flexibility without compromising bond strength. CAB is supplied as a free-flowing white to off-white powder or granule, with particle size varying by grade.

Commercial grades are differentiated by butyrate content, viscosity, and acetyl-to-butyryl ratio. These are key parameters buyers specify to match processing conditions. Technical and industrial grades are standard for most industrial uses.

Food-contact compliance varies by specific grade and regional regulation. This versatile polymer remains a staple for manufacturers requiring high-performance film properties and reliable chemical stability in demanding environments.

name: Cellulose acetate phthalate
description:
Cellulose acetate phthalate (CAS 9004-38-0 ), commonly abbreviated as CAP, is a cellulose-derived polymer ester used primarily as an enteric coating agent in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It controls the release profile of oral dosage forms by remaining intact in gastric acid while dissolving in the higher pH environment of the intestine. CAP is the material of choice for enteric coating tablets.

It is used for capsules and granules where protection from stomach acid is required, particularly for acid-sensitive active pharmaceutical ingredients. It is also used in sustained-release pellet systems.

In these systems, coating thickness and polymer concentration determine the dissolution lag time. Formulators incorporate CAP into film-coating solutions alongside plasticizers to achieve consistent coating uniformity.

This process is essential at commercial batch scale. Beyond solid dosage forms, it functions as a binder and matrix former in controlled-release granulation processes for various pharmaceutical applications.

Cellulose acetate phthalate is supplied as a white to off-white powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications meeting USP and Ph. Eur. standards for global compliance.

These are the primary grades demanded by regulated drug manufacturers. Suppliers typically offer it in fiber drum or multi-wall bag packaging suited to GMP production environments and large scale logistics.

name: Dextrin
description:
Dextrin (CAS 9004-53-9 ), also known commercially as E1400 , is a starch-derived carbohydrate produced through partial hydrolysis or thermal treatment of starch. It functions as a binder, adhesive, thickener, and carrier across food, industrial, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

In food production, E1400 acts as a bulking agent and encapsulation carrier for flavors, oils, and spray-dried ingredients. This improves the shelf stability and flowability of finished powders in various commercial applications.

Corrugated board, paper bag, and envelope manufacturing rely on dextrin-based adhesives for their fast-tack, water-based bonding performance. These industrial solutions provide reliable adhesion for high-speed production lines.

Textile and printing operations use it as a thickener in screen printing pastes and a sizing agent to improve fabric stiffness. This process enhances yarn processability and ensures consistent quality in textile finishing.

In pharmaceutical tablet and capsule manufacturing, it functions as a binder and diluent, supporting granulation and controlled disintegration. It is a critical component for ensuring the structural integrity of medicinal dosages.

Dextrin is supplied as a white to off-white powder, with granulated forms available for specific industrial applications. Established grades include food-grade ( FCC compliant), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade.

Conversion degree and solubility profiles vary by grade, so buyers typically specify dextrin type based on application requirements. Common varieties include white, yellow, or British gum depending on the desired chemical properties.

This versatile compound serves as a rheology modifier across pharmaceutical, biotech, and food applications. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, specific molecular weight fractions are used as intravenous plasma expanders and carriers in drug delivery formulations.

Biotech and life science laboratories rely on this material as a size-exclusion chromatography standard. It also serves as a scaffold for conjugating proteins, antibodies, and diagnostic reagents for various analytical procedures.

Food-grade material is used in bakery applications to improve dough rheology, crumb structure, and moisture retention during shelf life. In cosmetic and topical formulations, it acts as a humectant and film-forming agent.

It is frequently used for pellet encapsulation, where it regulates active ingredient dissolution rates. Solvent-based printing inks rely on EC resins to achieve fast-drying, abrasion-resistant films on flexible packaging substrates.

Industrial coatings and adhesives use EC to build moisture-resistant barrier layers and improve hot-melt adhesion on paper, foil, and plastic surfaces. In food applications under E462, it functions as a glazing agent.

description:
Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose (CAS 9004-58-4 ), also known by the trade name Etulos and approved as E230G , is a non-ionic cellulose ether used to control viscosity and flow behavior across water-based systems.

It functions as a rheology modifier, humectant, and emulsion stabilizer in formulations where consistent texture and film formation are critical. In architectural and industrial coatings, it thickens water-borne paints.

This material improves open time, reducing brush drag and sagging on vertical surfaces. Construction mortars and tile adhesives rely on it for water retention and workability, preventing premature drying during application.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators use it to build viscosity in shampoos, lotions, and gels without compromising clarity or skin feel. It is highly effective in maintaining stability in complex mixtures.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it supports controlled-release tablet coatings and serves as a binder in solid dosage forms. It meets various regulatory requirements for safety and performance in medical applications.

Ethyl hydroxyethyl cellulose is supplied as a free-flowing white to off-white powder. It is available in multiple viscosity grades to suit low- and high-shear processing requirements across different formulation types.

Both technical and pharmaceutical-grade material can be sourced depending on end-use regulatory requirements. Our product ensures consistent quality and performance for demanding industrial and commercial applications.

This material is essential where consistent viscosity under heat is required. Pharmaceutical tablet and coating formulations use it as a film-former and binder, contributing to controlled release and coating integrity.

In construction mortars and tile adhesives, it improves workability and water retention, extending open time for application. Coatings and textile finishing formulations rely on it to adjust flow behavior and improve substrate adhesion.

Ethyl methyl cellulose is supplied as a white to off-white powder in varying viscosity grades. Higher-viscosity grades are suited to construction and industrial applications, while lower-viscosity grades are preferred in food processing.

Food-grade material is available to E465 specification, while pharmaceutical-grade supply meets USP and Ph. Eur. standards. This ensures compliance with international safety and quality requirements for sensitive applications.

name: Hyaluronic acid
description:
Hyaluronic acid (CAS 9004-61-9 ), also known as HA, is a naturally derived polysaccharide used across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and biotech manufacturing. Commercially recognized under names such as Luronit and Sepracoat, it functions as a high-performance humectant.

It acts as a viscosity modifier in formulations requiring sustained moisture retention and texture control. In skincare and topical cosmetics, HA is incorporated into serums, creams, and sheet masks to deliver and sustain surface hydration across varying molecular weight grades.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a viscoelastic agent in ophthalmic solutions and as a carrier matrix in injectable formulations for joint therapy. In wound care and medical device coatings, it provides a biocompatible hydrating layer that supports tissue contact applications.

Biotech and life science suppliers also source HA as a scaffold component in cell culture media and tissue engineering substrates. Hyaluronic acid is supplied as a white to off-white powder, with sodium hyaluronate being the most commercially prevalent salt form.

Standard grades include cosmetic, food-grade, and pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / EP ), with molecular weight ranges specified to match application requirements. These ranges include low, medium, and high molecular weights to ensure optimal performance in final products.

Bulk quantities are available alongside smaller research and pilot-scale packaging to serve both industrial formulators and laboratory buyers. This ensures a reliable supply chain for diverse manufacturing needs across the chemical and life science sectors.

name: Hydroxyethyl cellulose
description:
Hydroxyethyl cellulose (CAS 9004-62-0 ), commercially known as Natrosol or HEC, is a water-soluble polymer derived from cellulose used primarily as a thickener and rheology modifier across industrial and consumer formulations.

It builds viscosity in aqueous systems without requiring heat activation, making it a practical choice for formulators working across multiple end-use sectors. In architectural and industrial coatings, HEC controls sag resistance.

It improves brush drag, directly affecting application quality and shelf stability. Construction product manufacturers use it in tile adhesives, cement renders, and joint compounds to extend open time and improve workability.

Personal care formulators rely on it to thicken shampoos, lotions, and topical gels, where it also contributes moisture retention to the finished product. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, Cellosize-grade material is used.

It is utilized in ophthalmic solutions and tablet coatings where consistent viscosity and purity are critical to product performance. Hydroxyethyl cellulose is supplied as a free-flowing white to off-white powder.

Grades are available across a broad viscosity range, including low, medium, and high, to suit different formulation requirements. Recognized specifications include USP , Ph.Eur. , and technical grades.

Food-contact and cosmetic-compliant variants are also available from established producers. These materials meet rigorous industry benchmarks for consistency and performance in diverse chemical applications.

name: Hydroxypropyl cellulose
description:
Hydroxypropyl cellulose ( CAS 9004-64-2 ), commonly abbreviated as HPC and listed as E463 in food applications, is a water-soluble cellulose ether used across pharmaceutical, food, and industrial formulations.

It functions primarily as a thickener, binder, and film-former, giving formulators precise control over viscosity and texture across a broad range of processing conditions. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, HPC is a standard binder.

It is used in tablet wet granulation and as a film-coating polymer for immediate-release dosage forms. Food producers use it as a stabilizer and emulsifier in processed foods, bakery products, and dietary supplements.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into gels, creams, and hair-fixative products to build viscosity and improve product spreadability. In construction, it functions as a water-retention agent in tile adhesives.

It is also used in cement-based mortars, reducing premature drying during application. HPC is supplied as a white to off-white powder in multiple viscosity grades, with low-, medium-, and high-viscosity variants available.

These variants are designed to match specific process requirements. Standard grades include FCC (food-grade), USP /NF, and Ph.Eur. , supporting regulated applications across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic sectors.

The product also meets BP and EP standards where required. Bulk supply is typically offered in 25 kg bags, with industrial quantities available in fiber drums for large-scale manufacturing needs.

Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (CAS 9004-65-3 ), commercially known as HPMC and approved as food additive E464 , is a cellulose-derived polymer used across pharmaceuticals, construction, food, and personal care.

It is used for controlled-release matrix systems and capsule shells, including vegetarian alternatives to gelatin. Tile adhesives, cement renders, and dry-mix mortars rely on it to extend open time.

This material improves workability on construction sites. Food manufacturers use E464 to stabilize emulsions, control texture in low-fat products, and prevent moisture migration in baked goods.

In personal care, it thickens shampoos, gels, and ophthalmic solutions while providing a smooth, non-tacky film on skin and hair. HPMC is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a range of viscosity grades.

It is typically characterized by methoxy and hydroxypropoxy substitution levels. Established grades include USP /NF, Ph.Eur. , BP , and food-grade ( FCC /E464-compliant) specifications to meet regulatory requirements.

These standards ensure safety across various global industries. Technical-grade material is also available for construction applications where pharmaceutical or food compliance is not required.

name: Methyl cellulose
description:
Methyl cellulose ( CAS 9004-67-5 ), also known by the food designation E461 and abbreviated as MC, is a cellulose-derived polymer used to control viscosity, texture, and stability across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial formulations.

Unlike most thickeners, it gels upon heating and dissolves when cooled. This unique property drives its selection in specific processing and formulation scenarios where thermal gelation is required to maintain structure.

In food manufacturing, MC functions as a binder and fat replacer in meat analogues, bakery products, and low-fat processed foods. It is essential for maintaining product integrity during high-temperature cooking cycles.

Pharmaceutical formulators use it as a controlled-release matrix material and film-coating agent in tablet production. Consistent viscosity grades are critical to ensuring dosage uniformity and predictable drug release profiles.

In construction, MC is a key additive in tile adhesives, renders, and dry-mix mortars. It significantly improves workability and water retention during application, preventing premature drying and ensuring a strong bond.

Personal care manufacturers incorporate it as a thickener and emulsion stabilizer in gels, lotions, and ophthalmic preparations. It is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a range of viscosity grades.

Established grades include USP , Ph. Eur. , FCC , and technical-grade, each targeting specific regulatory requirements. These standards ensure the material meets the necessary purity for its intended use.

Food and pharmaceutical procurement typically specifies viscosity grade alongside purity standards to ensure application fit. This ensures the polymer performs correctly within the specific chemical environment of the final product.

name: Nitrocellulose
description:
Nitrocellulose (CAS 9004-70-0 ), also known as Celloidin in certain specialty applications, is a nitrated cellulose polymer used as a film-forming binder and rheology modifier across coatings, printing inks, and adhesive systems.

Its rapid solvent release and hard, glossy film formation make it a primary resin choice where fast drying and surface clarity are commercial priorities. In flexographic and gravure printing inks, it provides fast-drying films.

These abrasion-resistant films are required for flexible packaging printed on films, foils, and paper substrates. Coatings formulators incorporate it into wood lacquers and leather finishes where a hard surface must cure quickly.

In adhesive and sealant systems, it functions as a binding agent in contact cements and specialty bonding products for leather goods and footwear manufacturing. It ensures high-gloss finishes under production line conditions.

Aerospace and defense applications include propellant formulations and pyrotechnic compositions. In these sectors, its controlled burn characteristics meet stringent performance specifications for specialized industrial use.

Nitrocellulose is supplied as alcohol-wetted chips, flakes, or isopropanol-wetted paste to meet transport safety requirements. Standard grades are differentiated by nitrogen content and viscosity for various applications.

Industrial and lacquer grades are the most commercially prevalent options available today. Technical and specialty grades are available to meet specific ink, coating, or propellant formulation requirements for global manufacturers.

name: Methoxypolyethylene glycols
description:
Methoxypolyethylene glycols ( CAS 9004-74-4 ), commonly abbreviated as MPEG and also marketed as Polyethylene Glycol Monomethyl Ether, are mono-end-capped PEG derivatives used across industries as solubilizers, carriers, and surface modifiers.

The terminal methoxy group blocks one reactive end, making MPEG the preferred choice when controlled reactivity and steric stabilization are required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, MPEG serves as a carrier and solubilizer in drug delivery systems.

This includes PEGylation of active compounds to extend circulation time and improve bioavailability. Personal care formulators incorporate it into skin creams, serums, and hair conditioners as a humectant and texture modifier.

It improves spreadability without tackiness in cosmetic applications. Industrial cleaning formulations use MPEG as a low-foaming surfactant component and coupling agent to stabilize mixed solvent systems effectively.

In polymer chemistry, it functions as a macromonomer for grafting onto polyurethane, acrylic, or cement-based systems. This helps to improve dispersion and reduce particle agglomeration in various industrial processes.

MPEG is supplied as a waxy solid or viscous liquid depending on molecular weight, with common grades ranging from MPEG 350 to MPEG 5000. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications.

Technical-grade product serves polymer and industrial cleaning applications where high purity is still essential. These versatile chemical intermediates provide reliable performance across a wide range of commercial sectors.

name: Polyethylene glycol monobutyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol monobutyl ether (CAS 9004-77-7 ), commercially available as DCP 208 and Adeka Carpol M2, is a nonionic surfactant and solvent used across industrial and personal care manufacturing.

Its butyl-capped polyethylene glycol structure delivers controlled hydrophilic-lipophilic balance, making it effective for emulsification, dispersion, and surface-active cleaning applications.

In textile and leather processing, it functions as a leveling and dispersing agent, improving dye uptake uniformity and finish consistency across various substrates during the manufacturing process.

Metalworking and industrial cleaning formulators incorporate it into water-based cutting fluids and degreasers, where it solubilizes oils and facilitates rinsing without the need for aggressive solvents.

Personal care manufacturers use it as a solvent and emulsifier in rinse-off formulations, helping to disperse actives and condition processing behavior for high-quality consumer products.

In paper manufacturing, it supports surface sizing and coating formulations by improving pigment dispersion and film-forming agent compatibility, ensuring a smooth and consistent finish.

Polyethylene glycol monobutyl ether is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy liquid. It is available in technical and industrial grades, with molecular weight variants determining HLB value.

Buyers should specify chain length or equivalent grade designation when sourcing. Bulk liquid supply in drums and IBCs is standard for industrial procurement and large-scale chemical distribution.

In coatings and adhesives, it acts as a reactive diluent and solvent, improving flow and substrate wetting during application. Home care and industrial cleaning formulations incorporate it to extend product shelf life.

name: Polyethylene glycol monolaurate
description:
Polyethylene glycol monolaurate is a nonionic ester surfactant produced by esterifying polyethylene glycol with lauric acid. It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and foam control agent across food, personal care, and industrial manufacturing applications.

Identified by CAS 9004-81-3 , this versatile chemical acts as an emulsifier in baked goods, shortenings, and dairy-based formulations. It is essential where stable fat-in-water dispersion is required for high-quality food processing.

Personal care formulators use it to build stable emulsions in lotions, creams, and hair conditioners. Its humectant character supports moisture retention in leave-on products, making it a staple in cosmetic science and dermatology.

Textile and leather processing operations employ it as a lubricant and dispersing agent during fiber treatment and dyeing. This improves process uniformity and ensures consistent quality across large-scale industrial manufacturing runs.

In personal care manufacturing, SLES is the primary foaming and cleansing agent in shampoos, body washes, liquid soaps, and facial cleansers, where its mildness supports consumer-grade formulations.

Textile processors use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove oils, waxes, and sizing agents from fiber prior to dyeing or finishing to ensure high-quality results.

In leather processing, it assists in degreasing hides during beam house operations to ensure uniform tanning penetration. Industrial formulators incorporate it into hard surface cleaners and laundry detergents.

SLES is supplied as a clear to slightly hazy aqueous liquid, most commonly at 70% active content, with 28% also available for applications requiring easier handling or lower viscosity.

Grades are differentiated by ethoxylation degree, typically 2 EO or 3 EO, which affects mildness and cold-water solubility. Technical and cosmetic-grade specifications are both standard in the market.

Sea buckthorn extract ( CAS 90106-68-6 ), also sourced and traded as Sea Buckthorn Berry Oil and Hippophae rhamnoides extract, is derived from the berries, leaves, or seeds of the shrub. It delivers concentrated antioxidant activity and natural pigmentation.

Formulators across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical sectors rely on this ingredient for functional performance. In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it supplies a naturally dense profile of carotenoids and tocopherols.

These flavonoids support antioxidant-positioned finished products. Food and beverage producers use it as a natural flavoring and acidulant in functional drinks, fruit preparations, and fortified foods where a tart berry character is required.

Cosmetic and personal care formulators incorporate it into serums, creams, and lip products for its moisturizing and skin-conditioning properties. It is particularly effective in anti-aging and barrier-repair product lines.

Pharmaceutical applications include inclusion in soft gels and standardized botanical preparations targeting oxidative stress. The extract is available as a liquid oil, dry powder, and concentrated juice or paste depending on the source.

Common supply grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade, with standardized extracts specifying carotenoid or flavonoid content. Organic-certified material is commercially available for suppliers serving clean-label markets.

Contact us for supply of Sea buckthorn extract
otherNames: ext. | Sea Buckthorn Berry Oil | Omega-7 Extract.

name: Polymethyl methacrylate
description:
Polymethyl methacrylate ( CAS 9011-14-7 ), commonly known as PMMA, is a synthetic thermoplastic polymer used across plastics fabrication, coatings, and structural applications. It delivers exceptional optical clarity and surface hardness.

This material offers superior weatherability, making it a preferred alternative to glass and polycarbonate in demanding environments. In construction and automotive glazing, PMMA sheet and rod stock are fabricated into transparent panels.

These components are used for skylights and vehicle light housings where impact resistance and UV stability are critical. Coatings and adhesive formulators use PMMA resins as film-forming binders that improve scratch resistance.

These resins also enhance gloss retention in architectural and industrial finishes. In aerospace and defense, machined PMMA components serve in canopies, instrument covers, and display panels where optical precision is required.

Dimensional stability is a key feature for these high-performance applications. As a rheology modifier, PMMA microspheres and powders are incorporated into coatings and sealants to control flow behavior and application consistency.

PMMA is supplied as pellets, powder, sheet, rod, and liquid dispersion depending on the processing route. Standard grades include general-purpose, impact-modified, and optical-quality variants for diverse industrial needs.

Some powder forms are available to USP specification for pharmaceutical and medical device applications. Molecular weight and MFI ratings vary across grades to suit extrusion, injection molding, or solution-based processing.

Contact us for supply of Polymethyl methacrylate

name: Isobutyl methacrylate polymer
description:
Poly(isobutyl methacrylate) (CAS 9011-15-8 ) is an acrylic polymer resin used across coatings, adhesives, and polymer formulation. It functions as a film-former and rheology modifier, contributing flexibility and adhesion to finished systems.

In solvent-based coatings and lacquers, it builds durable, clear films with good gloss retention. This makes it a preferred binder for wood and metal finishing applications where clarity and durability are essential.

Adhesive and sealant formulators incorporate it to balance tack, cohesion, and substrate wetting. It is particularly effective in pressure-sensitive and contact adhesive systems requiring specific performance profiles.

As a plasticizing resin in rigid polymer blends, it reduces brittleness and improves processability. It is valued because it does not migrate out of the matrix over time, ensuring long-term stability.

Industrial cleaning and maintenance products use it as a film-forming agent in protective coatings. It is also frequently utilized in strippable masking formulations for temporary surface protection.

The material is typically supplied as beads, granules, or as a solution in organic solvent. The choice of format depends on the intended processing method and the specific requirements of the manufacturing line.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering for this polymer. Molecular weight and solution viscosity are the key specification parameters buyers should confirm with their chemical suppliers.

Bulk and drum quantities are the common supply formats for industrial procurement. These packaging options ensure efficient handling and storage for large-scale manufacturing and formulation processes.

Contact us for supply of Isobutyl methacrylate polymer

name: Maleic anhydride-methyl vinyl ether copolymer
description:
Maleic anhydride-methyl vinyl ether copolymer (CAS 9011-16-9 ), commercially known as PVM/MA copolymer, is an alternating copolymer used across industrial formulations as a rheology modifier, dispersant, and surface-active binder.

Its reactive anhydride groups allow crosslinking or functionalization on contact with amines, alcohols, or water, making it a formulation-active ingredient rather than an inert additive.

In coatings and adhesives, it functions as a film-forming binder and adhesion promoter, improving substrate wetting and coating uniformity on difficult surfaces during the application process.

Home care and industrial cleaning formulations use it to suspend particulates, stabilize emulsions, and prevent soil redeposition on hard surfaces for enhanced cleaning efficiency and performance.

Textile and paper processing operations apply it as a sizing agent and surface modifier, where its reactivity with fiber hydroxyl groups improves overall strength and final printability.

In personal care-adjacent industrial applications, it acts as a thickener and film former in hair fixative and topical delivery systems formulated at a large industrial scale for consistency.

Supplied as a white to off-white powder in a range of molecular weight grades, with viscosity specifications used to differentiate performance tiers for specific manufacturing requirements.

Both anhydrous and half-ester variants are commercially available, with the hydrolyzed form offering water solubility. Technical and specialty grades are standard for industrial buyers.

name: D-Glucan
description:
D-Glucan (CAS 9012-72-0 ), also known as D-Glucosan, is a naturally derived polysaccharide sourced from plant, fungal, or microbial origins. It functions as a rheology modifier and moisture-retention agent across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care formulations.

In food and nutrition, it is incorporated into functional foods, dietary supplements, and fiber-enriched products where it contributes to texture and viscosity control. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a binder and film-forming agent in solid dosage forms.

It also serves as an excipient in controlled-release tablet systems. Personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing creams, serums, and lotions where its humectant properties support water retention in the skin matrix.

In agriculture and animal feed, it is used as a functional additive to support gut health and palatability in feed formulations. This versatile polysaccharide is available as a fine powder and in soluble granule forms suited to both dry blending and aqueous processing.

Standard grades include food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with specifications aligned to FCC and USP standards depending on the application. Purity levels and molecular weight profiles vary by source.

Oat, yeast, and barley-derived grades are the most commercially prevalent. These variations allow for precise selection based on the specific viscosity and solubility requirements of the final product formulation.

name: Chitosan
description:
Chitosan (CAS 9012-76-4 ), also known as Chitin N-deacetyl- and commercially as Kytex H, is a natural polysaccharide derived from the deacetylation of chitin found in crustacean shells.

In industrial applications, it functions as a biopolymer flocculant, antimicrobial agent, and film-forming rheology modifier across food, pharmaceutical, agricultural, and water treatment sectors.

In water treatment, it acts as a natural coagulant-flocculant to remove suspended solids, heavy metals, and turbidity from municipal and industrial effluents as a biodegradable alternative to synthetic polyacrylamides.

Food manufacturers use it as a preservative coating on fresh produce and seafood, extending shelf life by inhibiting microbial growth on product surfaces to maintain high quality standards.

Pharmaceutical formulators incorporate it into controlled-release tablet matrices and wound dressings, where its film-forming capacity supports drug delivery and tissue adhesion during the recovery process.

In agriculture, it is applied as a seed treatment and foliar biostimulant that activates plant defense responses and improves crop resistance to fungal pathogens in various environmental conditions.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white powder or flakes in varying molecular weights which directly affect viscosity. Standard grades include food-grade, USP , and technical specifications.

Degree of deacetylation, typically 75–95%, is a key specification buyers should confirm when sourcing for pharmaceutical or functional food applications to ensure the material meets specific project needs.

name: Terminalia chebula extract
description:
Terminalia chebula extract (CAS 90131-48-9 ), derived from the dried fruit of the haritaki tree, is a concentrated botanical ingredient used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

Standardized for polyphenol and tannin content, it functions as a natural antioxidant and stabilizing agent in finished formulations. In nutraceutical and dietary supplement production, it is incorporated into capsules and tablets.

Functional food products targeting antioxidant support frequently utilize this extract. Personal care formulators use it in anti-aging creams, serums, and scalp treatments where oxidative stress protection is a primary objective.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as a botanical active for inclusion in herbal preparations and standardized plant-based products. Food producers apply it as a natural antioxidant to extend shelf stability.

Terminalia chebula extract is supplied as a fine powder, typically spray-dried or vacuum-dried, suitable for direct blending or encapsulation. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications.

Material is commonly standardized to defined polyphenol or tannin percentages. Organic-certified material is available from select suppliers to meet clean-label and natural product requirements for global distribution.

The ingredient meets rigorous quality benchmarks including FCC and USP standards where applicable. This ensures consistency and safety for high-volume industrial applications across the chemical and food sectors.

name: Tomato extract
description:
Tomato extract (CAS 90131-63-8 ) is a concentrated botanical ingredient derived from Solanum lycopersicum fruit, standardized for its naturally occurring lycopene, carotenoids, and polyphenol content.

It functions as both a flavoring agent and an antioxidant stabilizer across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical applications. In food and beverage manufacturing, it delivers authentic tomato flavor and color.

This extract is used in sauces, soups, seasonings, and processed food products without requiring fresh fruit handling. Nutraceutical and supplement formulators use standardized tomato extract as a lycopene source.

It is commonly found in softgels, capsules, and functional food formats targeting antioxidant positioning. Personal care manufacturers incorporate it into skin-care formulations such as serums, creams, and masks.

Its carotenoid content supports antioxidant claims in product marketing. Pharmaceutical and health product developers also use it as a botanical active in standardized herbal preparations for various health products.

Tomato extract is supplied as a spray-dried powder, liquid concentrate, or oil-dispersible form, depending on the intended application. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available.

Some suppliers offering standardized grades defined by lycopene content typically ranging from 5 to 20 percent. Organic-certified material is available from select sources for clean-label and natural formulation requirements.

Contact us for supply of Tomato extract

name: Tribulus terrestris extract
description:
Tribulus terrestris extract (CAS 90131-68-3 ), derived from the puncture vine plant and also known commercially as Gokshura or Caltrop extract, is a standardized botanical ingredient used across nutraceutical, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical formulations.

It is primarily sourced for its steroidal saponin content, particularly protodioscin, which drives demand across multiple finished product categories. In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it is formulated into capsules and tablets.

The extract is also used in powdered blends targeting sports nutrition and general wellness product lines. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into anti-aging creams, serums, and scalp care products where antioxidant activity supports oxidative stress protection.

Pharmaceutical and life sciences researchers use standardized extracts as reference material and active ingredient input for botanical drug development. Food and functional beverage producers apply it in fortified products for premium positioning.

Tribulus terrestris extract is supplied as a fine powder, available in varying saponin standardizations, commonly 40%, 60%, and 90% saponin content by HPLC. Both food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available.

The material is manufactured to meet rigorous quality requirements, including USP and FCC standards where applicable. Bulk quantities are typically offered in fiber drums or foil-lined bags suited for moisture-sensitive botanical materials.

name: Polyoxyethylene dinonylphenyl ether
description:
Polyoxyethylene dinonylphenyl ether (CAS 9014-93-1 ) is a nonionic surfactant built on a dinonylphenol ethoxylate backbone, delivering strong emulsification, wetting, and detergency across industrial formulations.

It is distinct from monononylphenol ethoxylates and is selected specifically where the branched dinonyl structure offers enhanced stability and lower foam profiles during chemical processing.

In textile processing, it functions as a scouring and wetting agent, helping to remove oils, waxes, and sizing agents from fiber surfaces before dyeing or finishing procedures begin.

Leather manufacturers use it in degreasing baths to penetrate hides uniformly, improving the uptake of tanning agents. Industrial and institutional cleaning formulators incorporate it into hard-surface degreasers.

It is highly effective in alkaline cleaners where robust emulsification of mineral oils and greases is required. In agrochemical formulations, it acts as an emulsifier and dispersant in concentrates.

This ensures stable droplet distribution during field application. Polyoxyethylene dinonylphenyl ether is supplied as a liquid or viscous paste, depending on the specific degree of ethoxylation required.

The Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with ethoxylation levels typically ranging across variants to suit different HLB requirements for various industrial applications.

Drum and IBC packaging are the common supply formats for industrial buyers. This chemical remains a staple for manufacturers requiring high-performance nonionic surfactants in bulk quantities.

name: Viola odorata extract
description:
Viola odorata extract (CAS 90147-36-7 ), also known as violet oil, is derived from the flowers and leaves of the sweet violet plant. It delivers the plant's characteristic floral, powdery scent and delicate flavor profile to finished products.

This versatile ingredient is utilized across cosmetics, food, and pharmaceutical applications. In fragrance formulation, it contributes a soft, powdery violet note to fine perfumes, eau de toilette, and personal care products.

Manufacturers of lotions and soaps value its aromatic properties for premium lines. Food and beverage producers incorporate it as a natural flavoring in confectionery, baked goods, and specialty beverages where a floral character is required.

Cosmetic formulators use it in skin care and lip care products targeting botanical or natural-positioned lines. It is particularly effective in formulations requiring a sophisticated, nature-identical scent profile for high-end consumers.

Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical product developers source it as a botanical flavoring agent. It is frequently used to mask unpleasant tastes in syrups and oral formulations, improving patient compliance and product palatability.

The extract is available as a liquid extract or concentrated oil, with solvent-extracted and CO₂-extracted variants offered. These options allow for flexibility depending on the specific application requirements and desired potency.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly supplied. Documentation is provided to support use under relevant flavor and fragrance regulations, ensuring full compliance for industrial manufacturers and distributors.

Packaging typically ranges from small amber glass units for specialty buyers to bulk quantities for industrial formulators. This ensures the stability and integrity of the extract during transport and long-term storage.

name: Yucca extract
description:
Yucca extract ( CAS 90147-57-2 ), also known as Yucca Schidigera Extract, is a plant-derived ingredient sourced from the Mojave yucca plant. It is used commercially as a natural foaming agent, flavor component, and surfactant across food, feed, and personal care markets.

FEMA 3121 status confirms its recognized use as a flavoring substance in food and beverage applications. Its steroidal saponin content drives both its foam-stabilizing and ammonia-binding functions across multiple industries.

In animal feed and livestock operations, it reduces ammonia and odor emissions in poultry and swine housing, supporting compliance with environmental standards. This makes it a vital component for sustainable farming practices.

Beverage manufacturers use it as a natural foaming agent in root beer and other carbonated soft drinks. In these applications, it delivers stable foam without the need for synthetic additives or complex chemical stabilizers.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a natural surfactant and conditioning agent in shampoos and cleansers. Agricultural applications include its use as a soil wetting agent and adjuvant to improve water penetration.

Yucca extract is supplied as a liquid concentrate, spray-dried powder, and viscous paste. Food-grade and feed-grade designations are the most commonly traded specifications, ensuring high quality for various industrial needs.

Liquid forms are typically standardized by saponin content to ensure consistent performance. Powder grades offer extended shelf life and easier handling for dry blend formulations in large-scale manufacturing environments.

Contact us for supply of Yucca extract

name: Polydimethylsiloxane
description:
Polydimethylsiloxane ( CAS 9016-00-6 ), commonly known as PDMS, is a silicone-based polymer used across industrial and consumer manufacturing as a defoamer, lubricant, and surface modifier.

Its thermal stability and low surface tension make it a preferred base material and functional additive in formulations where conventional organics fall short in performance.

In coatings and sealants, PDMS controls surface flow, improves leveling, and prevents cratering in both solvent-borne and waterborne systems for high-quality finishes.

Automotive and aerospace manufacturers use it as a mold release agent and component lubricant, reducing friction in assemblies and extending the overall tooling life.

Personal care formulators incorporate PDMS into skin creams, hair conditioners, and antiperspirants to deliver slip, spreadability, and a desirable non-greasy skin feel.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal or external lubricant and plasticizer, improving mold release and reducing surface defects in extruded or injection-molded parts.

PDMS is supplied as a clear viscous fluid, with viscosity grades ranging from low to ultra-high to suit different processing requirements and specific industrial needs.

Emulsion and compound forms are available for waterborne applications. Grades include cosmetic quality, food-contact compliant, and technical-grade for industrial use.

name: Polyethylene glycol nonylphenyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol nonylphenyl ether (CAS 9016-45-9 ), commercially known as Nonoxynols or by the abbreviation NPE, is a nonionic surfactant used across industrial and institutional cleaning.

The ethoxylate chain length varies across grades, allowing formulators to select specific HLB values suited to their process requirements for emulsification and wetting applications.

In textile processing, NPE functions as a scouring and wetting agent, enabling uniform dye penetration and soil removal from fiber substrates during the manufacturing process.

Agricultural formulations rely on it as an emulsifier and dispersant in pesticide concentrates, improving active ingredient delivery and tank-mix stability for various crop applications.

Industrial and institutional cleaners use NPE for its degreasing performance on hard surfaces, metal parts, and process equipment in heavy-duty environments.

In pulp and paper manufacturing, it supports pitch control and acts as a process wetting agent during sheet formation to ensure high-quality finished paper products.

NPE is supplied as a liquid or paste depending on the degree of ethoxylation, with lower EO grades typically yielding more viscous or solid forms for industrial use.

Standard technical grades are the most common supply form for industrial buyers, with concentrations typically expressed by ethylene oxide mole count such as NPE-9 or NPE-10.

name: Polymethylene polyphenylene isocyanate
description:
Polymethylene polyphenylene isocyanate ( CAS 9016-87-9 ), commercially known as Polymeric MDI, is a dark brown liquid isocyanate used as a reactive building block in polyurethane synthesis.

It functions as a crosslinker and chain extender, reacting with polyols to form rigid or semi-rigid polymer networks across a broad range of industrial applications.

In construction and insulation, Polymeric MDI is the primary isocyanate component in rigid polyurethane and polyisocyanurate foam systems used for panels, spray foam, and pipe insulation.

Automotive and industrial manufacturers use it to produce structural reaction injection molded parts, seat foam, and under-hood components requiring dimensional stability.

In adhesives and sealants, it delivers strong substrate bonding across wood, metal, and composite materials, particularly in wood composite panels such as OSB and LVL.

Coatings formulators use it to build moisture-cure and two-component systems for flooring, protective coatings, and elastomeric membranes for various industrial surfaces.

Polymeric MDI is supplied as a liquid in bulk tankers, ISO containers, and drum quantities. Standard commercial grades vary by NCO content and viscosity for rigid foam applications.

Technical grade is the predominant market form; food-contact or pharmaceutical grades are not applicable for this product as it is intended for industrial use.

name: Sodium cocoyl alaninate
description:
Sodium cocoyl alaninate (CAS 90170-45-9 ), also known commercially as N-coco acyl alanine sodium salt, is an amino acid-derived anionic surfactant produced by condensing coconut fatty acids with L-alanine.

It delivers effective cleansing and foaming performance while remaining compatible with sensitive skin formulations, making it a preferred choice for mild personal care and specialty cleaning applications.

In rinse-off personal care products such as facial cleansers, shampoos, and body washes, it provides gentle yet thorough cleansing with a dense, stable foam profile suited to low-irritation formulations.

Formulators also incorporate it into conditioning shampoos and scalp treatments where surfactant mildness is a key selection criterion alongside cleaning efficacy for high-end cosmetic applications.

In home care and industrial cleaning concentrates, it contributes emulsification and degreasing performance at moderate use levels. Textile and leather processing operations use it as a scouring agent.

It serves as a dispersing agent where biodegradable surfactant chemistry is required to meet environmental compliance standards. This versatility makes it a staple in modern green chemistry formulations.

The product is supplied as an aqueous solution, typically in the 28–30% active content range. It is available in cosmetic-grade quality conforming to standard personal care raw material specifications.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers, with documentation including COSMOS/ECOCERT certification available from select producers to ensure full compliance with international safety standards.

Contact us for supply of Sodium cocoyl alaninate

name: Watermelon extract
description:
Watermelon extract (CAS 90244-99-8 ), also marketed as Citrullus lanatus extract, is a botanical-derived ingredient obtained from the fruit of the watermelon plant. It delivers characteristic fresh, sweet watermelon flavor and fragrance notes to finished products.

The extract also contributes antioxidant activity relevant to formulation stability. In food and beverage manufacturing, it is used to flavor confectionery, beverages, and functional snacks where natural fruit character is required.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into lip products, skin serums, and hair care lines to deliver both scent profile and antioxidant support. This appeals to clean-label positioning and consumer demand for natural ingredients.

Flavor houses use it as a building block in fragrance compositions targeting fresh or fruity olfactory profiles. Nutraceutical and supplement manufacturers apply it in functional formulations where botanical fruit extracts are specified.

Watermelon extract is supplied as a liquid, powder, or spray-dried form depending on the intended application and processing requirements. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications for industrial use.

These documents confirm standardization and solubility characteristics to ensure compatibility with the final product matrix. This ensures the extract meets the necessary performance criteria for high-quality manufacturing standards.

name: Hemicellulase
description:
Hemicellulase (CAS 9025-56-3 ) is an enzyme that breaks down hemicellulose, a structural polysaccharide found in plant cell walls, into fermentable sugars and simpler oligosaccharides. Sold under trade names including Gammanase, Pentopan, and Pulpzyme, it is used across food processing and manufacturing.

The enzyme is utilized in pulp and paper production and textile manufacturing to improve process efficiency and end-product quality. In baking, it improves dough handling and crumb structure by degrading arabinoxylan networks in wheat flour.

This process reduces water absorption variability across batches, ensuring consistent results. Pulp and paper producers use it as a biobleaching aid, where enzymatic hemicellulose removal before chemical bleaching reduces chlorine consumption.

This application also improves pulp brightness and overall sustainability. In textile and fiber processing, it supports retting and fiber separation, reducing reliance on harsh chemical pre-treatments during the manufacturing cycle.

Biotechnology applications include biomass pre-treatment for second-generation bioethanol production. Here, it acts alongside cellulases to maximize sugar yield from lignocellulosic feedstocks for more efficient energy conversion.

Hemicellulase is supplied as a liquid concentrate or dry powder, with activity expressed in units per gram or milliliter. Food-grade and technical-grade variants are both commercially available for industrial use.

The food-grade material conforms to FCC specifications to ensure safety and compliance. Specific activity levels and pH optima vary by microbial source, so buyers typically specify application conditions when sourcing.

name: Tannase
description:
Tannase (CAS 9025-71-2 ), also known as tannin acylhydrolase, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ester and depside bonds in hydrolyzable tannins, releasing gallic acid and glucose.

It is used across food processing and biotechnology to reduce astringency, improve clarity, and enhance the bioavailability of polyphenolic compounds in tannin-containing substrates.

In beverage production, tannase is used to clarify tea extracts and cold-brew tea concentrates, preventing the haze formation that occurs when tannins interact with proteins at low temperatures.

Instant tea and ready-to-drink tea manufacturers rely on it to produce stable, clear products without sacrificing flavor profile. In wine and fruit juice processing, it reduces excess tannin load.

This enzymatic treatment improves mouthfeel and product consistency. Biotechnology applications include its use in gallic acid production, a key intermediate for propyl gallate and pharmaceutical antioxidants.

This is achieved through controlled enzymatic hydrolysis of tannin-rich plant materials. Tannase is supplied as a liquid enzyme preparation or as a dried powder, depending on the intended processing conditions.

Activity is expressed in units per gram or per milliliter, with food-grade specifications available for beverage and food processing applications. Technical-grade preparations are available for industrial use.

These preparations are ideal for gallic acid production and fermentation processes. The enzyme ensures high purity and efficiency in industrial applications while meeting necessary safety requirements.

name: Disodium coco-sulfosuccinate
description:
Disodium coco-sulfosuccinate (CAS 90268-37-4 ) is a mild, coconut-derived anionic surfactant used across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations. Derived from fatty alcohols of coconut oil and sulfosuccinic acid, it delivers effective cleansing.

It provides excellent foam generation while remaining gentle on skin and compatible with sensitive formulation systems. In personal care, it functions as a primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, body washes, and baby care products.

Home care formulators incorporate it into liquid dish soaps and hard surface cleaners where it boosts grease removal. It is particularly valued for maintaining skin tolerance during repeated contact in manual cleaning tasks.

Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to improve substrate penetration during pre-treatment. It is also utilized in dyeing operations to ensure uniform application across various fiber types.

In paper manufacturing, it supports pulp dispersion and surface sizing processes where consistent foam behavior is critical. Its compatibility with process water makes it a reliable choice for large-scale industrial paper production.

Disodium coco-sulfosuccinate is typically supplied as an aqueous solution, with active matter content commonly in the range of 30–40%. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades for diverse industrial needs.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements for personal care applications and high-end formulations. Packaging is generally offered in drums and IBC containers suited to bulk industrial procurement and logistics.

name: Beta-galactosidase
description:
Beta-galactosidase (CAS 9031-11-2 ), commercially available under the trade name Lactozym® Pure, is an enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of lactose into glucose and galactose.

Sourced for use across food processing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and biotechnology, it enables lactose reduction in dairy products and supports downstream bioprocessing applications.

In dairy manufacturing, this enzyme is used to produce lactose-free milk, yogurt, and cheese, meeting consumer demand without altering nutritional profiles or the final product quality.

Pharmaceutical formulators apply it in the development of lactose-intolerance therapies and as a processing aid in oral dosage form development for various therapeutic applications.

In biotechnology, it functions as a reporter enzyme in gene expression assays and cell-based screening platforms, where accurate activity measurement is critical to assay design.

Food ingredient producers also use it to improve sweetness and solubility in whey-based products by converting lactose to more fermentable sugars for industrial use.

The product is supplied as a liquid enzyme concentrate or lyophilized powder, depending on the application and required activity units for specific manufacturing processes.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available, with grades conforming to FCC and USP standards available for regulated manufacturing environments.

name: Glucoamylase
description:
Glucoamylase (CAS 9032-08-0 ), also referred to as glucose amylase, is an exo-acting enzyme that cleaves glucose units from the non-reducing ends of starch and dextrins. It is the primary enzyme used across food processing and fermentation industries.

This enzyme is essential to convert liquefied starch into fermentable glucose syrups. In fuel ethanol and potable alcohol production, it is dosed into saccharification vessels to generate the high-glucose wort required for efficient yeast fermentation.

Glucose syrup and high-dextrose corn syrup manufacturers rely on it to achieve DE values above 95. This allows them to meet specifications for confectionery, baking, and beverage sweetener markets globally.

Brewers apply it in low-calorie and light beer production to hydrolyze residual dextrins, reducing final carbohydrate content. In pharmaceutical starch hydrolysate manufacturing, it supports production of defined glucose polymers.

These polymers are used as excipients and parenteral nutrition substrates. The product is supplied as a liquid enzyme concentrate, typically standardized by activity units such as GAU or AGU per mL.

Dry granulated forms are available for applications requiring extended shelf life or easier handling. Food-grade and industrial-grade designations are standard, with food-grade material produced under GMP and compliant with FCC specifications.

Activity levels and temperature or pH optima vary by strain source. Technical datasheets should be reviewed against process conditions before procurement to ensure the enzyme meets specific industrial requirements.

Contact us for supply of Glucoamylase

name: Hydroxyethyl methyl cellulose
description:
Hydroxyethyl methyl cellulose (HEMC, CAS 9032-42-2 ) is a non-ionic cellulose ether produced by the combined etherification of cellulose with methyl and hydroxyethyl groups. It functions primarily as a rheology modifier, thickener, and water-retention agent across construction, personal care, and industrial formulations.

In dry-mix mortars, tile adhesives, and cement-based renders, HEMC controls workability and prevents premature water loss during curing. This directly affects open time and bond strength in high-performance building materials.

Personal care formulators use it to build viscosity in shampoos, lotions, and gel-based products while improving spreadability. In interior and exterior paints, it provides sag resistance and stabilizes pigment dispersion throughout the coating's shelf life.

Textile and paper processing operations apply it as a surface sizing and finishing agent to improve coating uniformity and substrate adhesion. This versatile polymer ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing environments.

HEMC is supplied as a white to off-white free-flowing powder. Viscosity grades vary widely, typically ranging from low to high molecular weight variants, allowing formulators to match product performance to specific application requirements.

Both technical-grade and pharmaceutical-grade material is available for global distribution. Pharmaceutical supply conforms to USP or Ph.Eur. specifications to ensure the highest levels of purity and safety for sensitive applications.

name: Sweet almond oil
description:
Sweet almond oil (CAS 90320-37-9 ), extracted from the kernels of Prunus amygdalus dulcis, is a light carrier oil used across cosmetics, food, and pharmaceutical manufacturing. It functions primarily as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent.

The oil serves as an effective carrier medium for active ingredients and flavors. In personal care, it forms the base of facial oils, massage oils, body lotions, and hair serums for various applications.

Its skin absorption profile supports the delivery of actives without leaving a heavy residue. Food manufacturers use it as a specialty culinary oil and flavoring carrier in confectionery and baked goods.

It is also utilized in premium edible coatings for the food industry. Pharmaceutical and nutraceutical producers incorporate it as an excipient in topical preparations and soft gel capsule fill bases.

The oil is ideal for oral formulations requiring a neutral lipid carrier. In coatings and sealant formulations, it functions as a bio-based plasticizing component and lubricant additive for industrial use.

This material is essential where renewable-origin content is a specification requirement. Sweet almond oil is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in bulk drums, IBCs, and smaller formats.

Cosmetic-grade and food-grade specifications are the standard commercial offerings. Refined and cold-pressed variants are available depending on the specific application requirements of the manufacturer.

Pharmaceutical-grade material conforming to Ph.Eur. and BP monographs is also available for regulated end uses. This ensures the highest quality standards for sensitive production environments.

name: Alpinia officinarum extract
description:
Alpinia officinarum extract (CAS 90320-42-6 ), also known commercially as lesser galangal extract or by its FEMA designation 2499 , is derived from the rhizome of the galangal plant.

It is used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications as a flavoring and antioxidant agent. The extract delivers a characteristic spicy, ginger-like aromatic profile valued in both functional formulations and flavored consumer products.

In food and beverage manufacturing, it functions as a natural flavoring ingredient in spice blends, bitters, liqueurs, and seasoning systems where warm, pungent notes are required for the final product.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skincare and haircare products for its antioxidant activity, helping to stabilize formulations against oxidative degradation. This ensures product longevity and maintains efficacy over time.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement production, it appears in standardized extracts and herbal blends targeting digestive and metabolic support claims. It is a versatile botanical component for health-focused brands.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a botanical active or excipient in traditional medicine preparations across European and Asian markets. It meets various regional regulatory requirements for herbal medicine production.

Alpinia officinarum extract is supplied as a dry powder or liquid extract, with concentration and standardization varying by supplier specification. Food-grade material conforming to FEMA 2499 status is the most common.

Technical and cosmetic-grade variants are also available depending on end-use requirements. This ensures that manufacturers can select the appropriate purity level for their specific industrial or consumer applications.

name: Octylphenol-polyoxyethylene ether
description:
Octylphenol-polyoxyethylene ether (CAS 9036-19-5 ), commonly abbreviated as OPE and sold commercially as Triton X-405, is a nonionic ethoxylated surfactant used across industrial cleaning, textile processing, and agricultural formulations.

It functions primarily as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and dispersant, enabling stable mixing of oil and water phases in complex formulations. In industrial and household cleaning concentrates, OPE solubilizes oils and greases into aqueous systems.

This improves detergent performance on hard surfaces and fabrics. Textile processors use it to improve fiber wetting and dye penetration during scouring and finishing operations, ensuring uniform treatment across substrates.

In agrochemical formulations, it stabilizes emulsifiable concentrates and suspension concentrates, helping active ingredients distribute evenly on leaf surfaces. Leather and paper manufacturers apply it as a wetting and softening aid.

During processing baths, consistent surface penetration is critical to product quality. Octylphenol-polyoxyethylene ether is supplied as a liquid or viscous solution, with the 70% aqueous solution being the most standard form.

Technical grade is the predominant specification for industrial buyers, though formulation-grade variants are available depending on application requirements. Drum and IBC packaging are typical for bulk procurement.

name: Arabinogalactan
description:
Arabinogalactan (CAS 9036-66-2 ), also marketed under the trade name FiberAid and approved as E409 , is a naturally derived polysaccharide extracted primarily from larch wood. It functions as a dietary fiber source and prebiotic agent.

This multifunctional texturizer is used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In food and beverage formulations, it acts as a low-viscosity bulking agent and fiber-enrichment ingredient for various products.

It enables high inclusion rates without significantly altering product texture or mouthfeel. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a tablet binder and excipient, and it is increasingly incorporated into immune-support dietary supplements.

Due to its prebiotic classification, it is a popular choice for gut health formulations. In personal care, it improves skin feel and moisture retention in serums, creams, and leave-on treatments without adding heavy viscosity.

Agricultural applications include its use as a carrier and dispersant in crop protection formulations. This improves the delivery of active ingredients while maintaining stability in diverse environmental conditions for industrial use.

The product is supplied as a free-flowing white to off-white powder. It is available in food-grade and USP -compliant specifications, with FCC -grade material commonly sourced for dietary supplement and functional food applications.

name: Polyalkylene glycol monobutyl ether
description:
Polyalkylene glycol monobutyl ether (CAS 9038-95-3 ), also marketed as polyethylene-polypropylene glycol monobutyl ether, is a block or random copolymer of ethylene oxide and propylene oxide capped with a butyl group.

It functions as a nonionic surfactant, solvent, and wetting agent across cleaning, lubrication, and textile processing applications. In industrial and household cleaning formulations, it improves soil release and degreasing performance.

This chemical is particularly effective at low use levels in hard surface cleaners and degreasers. Metalworking fluid formulators incorporate it as a lubricity modifier and emulsifier for various industrial systems.

Its controlled hydrophilic-lipophilic balance helps stabilize cutting and rolling oil emulsions effectively. Textile processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and fiber preparation.

In paper and leather processing, it acts as a surface modifier to control absorption and improve treatment uniformity. The product is supplied as a clear liquid across a range of molecular weights for diverse needs.

The EO/PO ratios are tailored to specific HLB requirements for different industrial applications. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with product specifications varying by molecular weight.

Suppliers typically offer multiple grades differentiated by viscosity and ethylene oxide content to suit different formulation targets. This versatility makes it a staple component in modern chemical manufacturing and processing.
