name: Sodium cocoyl glycinate
description:
Sodium cocoyl glycinate (CAS 90387-74-9 ), also marketed as sodium lauroyl glycinate, is a mild amino acid-based surfactant derived from glycine and coconut fatty acids. It functions as a gentle cleanser, foam booster, and emulsifier across personal care and cosmetic formulations.

In facial cleansers, shampoos, and body washes, it delivers effective cleansing with low irritation potential. This is a key consideration for sensitive-skin and baby-care product lines where mildness is a primary requirement.

Formulators incorporate it into solid bars and syndet formats where it contributes lather quality and skin-feel. It provides these benefits without the harshness associated with conventional sulfate surfactants used in traditional soaps.

Its compatibility with amphoteric and nonionic co-surfactants makes it a practical choice for sulfate-free formulation systems. These systems are often used when targeting premium or natural-positioned brands in the global marketplace.

In oral care products such as toothpastes and mouthwashes, it supports mild foaming and cleaning performance at low use levels. This versatility allows it to be used across a wide range of hygiene and beauty applications.

Sodium cocoyl glycinate is supplied as a powder or as an aqueous solution, with solution concentrations typically ranging around 30%. Both technical and cosmetic-grade material are available for industrial procurement.

Cosmetic-grade product conforms to standard purity requirements for personal care applications. Buyers should confirm the fatty acid chain profile, such as pure lauroyl versus coconut-derived mixed-chain, when specifying for formulation consistency.

name: Decaglycerin
description:
Decaglycerin (CAS 9041-07-0 ), also known as Polyglycerin-10, is a polyol produced by condensing ten glycerol units into a single hydrophilic chain. It functions as an emulsifier, humectant, and solubilizer across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

In food production, it is used as an emulsifier in fat-based systems such as margarine, chocolate coatings, and bakery shortenings. It improves texture and fat dispersion stability in these applications.

Personal care formulators incorporate it into moisturizing creams, serums, and cleansers as a humectant that draws and retains moisture in the skin matrix. Its high water solubility and low irritation profile make it a preferred carrier.

It is often used for active ingredients in topical pharmaceutical preparations and dermocosmetic products. In surfactant-based systems, it acts as a co-emulsifier to stabilize oil-in-water emulsions without synthetic ethoxylated ingredients.

This is a relevant consideration for clean-label and natural-certified formulations. Decaglycerin is supplied as a clear to pale yellow viscous liquid that is easy to handle in industrial processes.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commonly available, with some suppliers offering material conforming to FCC or JP standards. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers.

name: C12-15 alkyl ethylhexanoate
description:
C12-15 Alkyl Ethylhexanoate (CAS 90411-66-8 ), also known as hexanoic acid, 2-ethyl-, C12-15-alkyl esters, is a synthetic ester derived from branched-chain fatty acid and mid-chain alcohols.

It functions as an emollient, solvent carrier, and lubricant across personal care, coatings, and industrial applications. In personal care formulations, it acts as a lightweight skin-conditioning emollient.

It is commonly used in lotions, sunscreens, and color cosmetics, delivering a dry, non-greasy skin feel that improves spreadability. Coatings and resin formulators use it as a coalescing solvent and dispersant aid.

This helps to reduce viscosity and improve pigment wetting in solvent-borne systems. In adhesives and sealants, it contributes plasticizing and carrier functions that support processing and film formation.

Lubricant and metalworking applications leverage its ester structure for boundary lubrication and as a base fluid component in specialty formulations. It is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid.

It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care and industrial buyers respectively. Packaging typically ranges from drums to IBC totes.

Bulk options are available for high-volume procurement. This versatile ester provides excellent stability and compatibility across a wide range of chemical formulations and industrial processes.

Cetearyl ethylhexanoate (CAS 90411-68-0 ), also sold under the component description Cetyl 2-ethylhexanoate, is a synthetic ester of fatty alcohols and 2-ethylhexanoic acid. It is used as an emollient and skin-conditioning agent in cosmetic formulations.

In industrial applications, it functions as a plasticizer, lubricant, and dispersing medium across coatings and specialty formulations. In personal care, it is used in creams, lotions, and color cosmetics to deliver a lightweight feel.

This ingredient provides a non-greasy skin feel while improving spreadability and moisture retention. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a plasticizing component to enhance film flexibility and substrate adhesion in specialty systems.

In lubricant and metalworking applications, it acts as a base fluid or additive carrier where low volatility is required. It is valued for its good film-forming behavior and stability in various industrial environments.

name: Dextran sulfate
description:
Dextran sulfate (CAS 9042-14-2 ), also referenced commercially as Dextran sulfate 500 in reference to its high-molecular-weight form, is a sulfated polysaccharide used across pharmaceutical and biotechnology applications.

It functions primarily as a biochemical reagent, anticoagulant agent, and cell culture supplement in research and manufacturing contexts. In molecular biology workflows, it accelerates nucleic acid hybridization.

This material is used in Southern and Northern blotting protocols, reducing assay time and improving signal sensitivity. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reference compound in heparin-binding studies.

It also serves as a model anticoagulant in preclinical research. In lipid research and clinical diagnostics, it is used in precipitation assays to isolate LDL cholesterol fractions from serum samples.

Biotechnology producers also incorporate it into cell expansion media to support suspension culture stability. This helps reduce aggregation in bioreactor systems during large-scale production cycles.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white powder and as aqueous solution concentrates. It is available in multiple molecular weight grades, most commonly 5,000, 40,000, and 500,000 Da.

The 500 kDa grade is the standard for hybridization and cell culture use. Research-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet various industry requirements.

The sodium salt form is the predominant commercial offering. All batches are tested to ensure they meet rigorous internal quality controls and relevant USP or EP standards where applicable.

name: Phospholipase A1
description:
Phospholipase A1 (CAS 9043-29-2 ) is an enzyme that cleaves the sn-1 ester bond of phospholipids, releasing fatty acids and lysophospholipids from membrane and dietary lipid substrates.

Across food processing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, and biotech research, it functions as a precision biocatalyst for modifying lipid composition and generating specific lipid-derived intermediates.

In edible oil and fat processing, degumming treatments convert non-hydratable phospholipids into hydratable forms, improving oil yield and reducing refining losses during the production cycle.

Bakers and dough conditioner formulators use it to generate lysophospholipids in situ, which improve crumb structure, loaf volume, and dough stability without adding emulsifiers directly.

In pharmaceutical and nutraceutical manufacturing, it is used to produce enriched lysophosphatidylcholine fractions from lecithin feedstocks, supporting the formulation of targeted lipid-based drug delivery systems.

Biotech and analytical laboratories also apply it as a research tool for lipidomics studies and membrane lipid profiling to better understand complex cellular lipid interactions and structures.

The enzyme is supplied as a liquid preparation or lyophilized powder, with activity expressed in units per milliliter or per gram. Food-grade material is produced under GMP conditions.

Technical-grade specifications are also available for industrial applications. These offerings meet the necessary regulatory requirements for enzyme use in various global food processing sectors.

name: Polyethylene glycol isotridecyl ether
description:
Polyethylene glycol isotridecyl ether (CAS 9043-30-5 ), also designated E1310 , is a nonionic ethoxylated alcohol surfactant derived from isotridecanol. It functions as an emulsifier, dispersant, and cleaning agent across industrial and personal care applications.

The performance of this chemical is highly tunable by the ethoxylation degree. In textile processing, it acts as a scouring and wetting agent, removing oils, waxes, and sizing agents from fiber surfaces ahead of dyeing or finishing.

Leather manufacturing uses it to degrease hides and improve penetration of tanning agents into the substrate. Personal care formulators incorporate it as an emulsifier and solubilizer in creams, lotions, and cleansing products.

It is particularly effective where stable oil-in-water systems are required. In industrial cleaning formulations, it delivers low-foam degreasing performance suited to hard-surface and process equipment cleaning.

Polyethylene glycol isotridecyl ether is supplied as a liquid or paste, depending on the ethoxylation degree. Lower EO variants tend toward liquid form, while higher EO grades are more viscous or paste-like.

It is available in technical and industrial grades, with ethoxylation levels typically ranging from approximately 3 to 20 moles of ethylene oxide. Drum and IBC packaging are standard for bulk procurement.

Polypropylene glycol diamine (CAS 9046-10-0 ) is a difunctional amine-terminated polyether used as a reactive building block in polymer systems. Its terminal amine groups enable direct participation in curing and crosslinking reactions.

This versatile chemical is essential for chain extension across a broad range of thermoset and elastomeric applications. In epoxy coating systems, it acts as a flexible curing agent, improving impact resistance and elongation.

It is widely utilized in protective and floor coatings to enhance durability. Polyurethane and polyurea formulations use it as a chain extender to tune mechanical properties and processing characteristics in spray-applied membranes.

Adhesive manufacturers incorporate it into structural and elastic bonding systems where controlled flexibility is required. It ensures superior substrate adhesion and performance in demanding industrial environments.

In construction composites and grouts, it contributes to toughened resin matrices with improved crack resistance. This makes it ideal for applications subject to dynamic loads and environmental stress over time.

name: Dialdehyde starch
description:
Dialdehyde starch (CAS 9047-50-1 ) is a chemically modified starch produced by periodate oxidation, which introduces aldehyde groups along the polymer backbone. These reactive groups enable cross-linking with proteins, cellulose, and other polymers.

This chemical structure makes it a functional binder and cross-linking agent across several industrial sectors. In paper and pulp manufacturing, it improves wet and dry strength by cross-linking cellulose fibers.

This process directly impacts sheet performance and reduces fiber loss during production. Textile finishing operations use it to impart crease resistance and dimensional stability to woven fabrics without relying on formaldehyde-based systems.

In leather processing, it acts as a tanning auxiliary, cross-linking collagen fibers to improve firmness and water resistance in the final hide. Food-grade applications include use as a rheology modifier and texture agent.

It is particularly useful in starch-based formulations where controlled viscosity and gel stability are required. The product is typically supplied as a white to off-white powder with varying degrees of oxidation.

The oxidation level is commonly expressed as the percentage of aldehyde groups per anhydroglucose unit. Technical and food-grade specifications are available, with oxidation levels generally ranging from 20% to 100%.

The specific grade depends on the intended application and required reactivity. Packaging is standard in multi-kilogram bags or bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes for global distribution.

name: Hydroxypropyl starch
description:
Hydroxypropyl starch (CAS 9049-76-7 ), listed as E1440 in food additive regulations, is a modified starch produced by introducing hydroxypropyl groups onto a native starch backbone. This modification improves freeze-thaw stability and water retention.

The chemical structure provides resistance to retrogradation, making it a functional ingredient across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing. In food production, it is used to stabilize sauces, soups, and dressings.

It is particularly effective in frozen foods where texture consistency across temperature cycles is critical. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a binder and disintegrant in tablet formulations and as a film-forming agent in coating systems.

In personal care, it functions as a rheology modifier in creams, lotions, and gels, controlling viscosity and improving sensory profile. It also serves industrial applications in paper coating and adhesive formulations.

Hydroxypropyl starch is supplied as a white to off-white powder in food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications. Food-grade material is available conforming to regulatory standards for global distribution and safety compliance.

Pharmaceutical grades are supplied to USP and Ph. Eur. monograph requirements. Degree of substitution varies by grade and directly affects functional performance in end formulations, so buyers should confirm values when sourcing.

name: Calcium carboxymethyl cellulose
description:
Calcium carboxymethyl cellulose (CAS 9050-04-8 ) is a water-soluble cellulose derivative in which calcium counterions replace the sodium found in standard CMC grades. It functions as a rheology modifier, dispersant, and moisture-retention agent across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial manufacturing processes.

In pharmaceutical tablet manufacturing, it acts as a disintegrant and binder, supporting controlled release profiles where sodium content must be minimized. Food processors use it to stabilize emulsions, control texture, and retain moisture in baked goods and dairy alternatives.

Construction product formulators incorporate it into tile adhesives and cement-based mortars to improve water retention and workability during application. In textile and paper processing, it functions as a sizing and coating agent, improving surface uniformity and reducing fiber dusting.

Calcium carboxymethyl cellulose is supplied as a white to off-white powder in varying particle sizes and viscosity grades. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available, with purity and substitution degree typically defined per batch documentation.

Technical grades are also offered for construction and industrial applications where tighter pharmaceutical controls are not required. This versatile chemical ensures consistent performance across diverse manufacturing environments and specialized product formulations.

The material is handled according to standard safety protocols for cellulose derivatives. It remains a preferred choice for manufacturers seeking high-purity additives that meet rigorous industrial and regulatory requirements for stability and performance.

name: Hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose phthalate
description:
Hydroxypropyl methyl cellulose phthalate ( CAS 9050-31-1 ), commonly known as HPMCP, is a cellulose-based enteric polymer used in pharmaceutical manufacturing. It forms acid-resistant films that dissolve at defined pH thresholds in the intestinal tract.

This material enables controlled drug release without gastric degradation, ensuring the integrity of the dosage form. HPMCP is the primary enteric coating material for tablets and capsules where active ingredients must bypass the stomach.

It is essential for protecting acid-sensitive APIs such as proton pump inhibitors and certain biologics. In solid dosage form development, it is used in both film coating and hot-melt extrusion processes to engineer delayed-release profiles.

Formulators also incorporate it into enteric matrix granules and multiparticulate systems for modified-release oral drug products. Its defined dissolution pH range makes it a specification-critical excipient in generic drug development.

HPMCP is supplied as a white to off-white powder in standard pharmaceutical grades. Two primary grades are commercially recognized, HP-50 and HP-55, which are differentiated by their specific pH dissolution thresholds.

These grades offer thresholds of approximately 5.0 and 5.5 respectively to meet diverse formulation needs. Material is available to Ph.Eur. , USP /NF, and JP specifications for global regulatory compliance.

The product is supported by comprehensive documentation packages suitable for IND and NDA filings. This ensures that manufacturers can meet the rigorous quality standards required for modern pharmaceutical applications.

name: Maltodextrin
description:
Maltodextrin ( CAS 9050-36-6 ), also recognized under E1400 , is a starch-derived carbohydrate used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing as a carrier and bulking agent.

Dextrin malto is a related term buyers may encounter when sourcing specific DE-range grades. In food manufacturing, it is used to encapsulate spray-dried flavors and stabilize various emulsions.

It improves the flowability of powdered products such as soups, sauces, and infant formula. Pharmaceutical producers use it as a filler and binder in tablet and capsule formulations for manufacturing.

Consistent DE values ensure predictable compressibility and dissolution behavior. In sports nutrition and functional food, it acts as a rapidly digestible carbohydrate carrier for active ingredient delivery.

Personal care formulators incorporate it as a film-forming agent and powder binder in dry shampoos. It is also found in pressed powders and skin-care bases to improve the overall texture.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white free-flowing powder. It is available in a range of dextrose equivalent values, typically DE 5, DE 10, DE 15, DE 18, and DE 20.

Selection is driven by sweetness level, hygroscopicity, and solubility requirements. Grades include food-grade ( FCC ), USP , and pharmaceutical-grade with non-GMO and organic-certified options.

name: Cetearyl phosphate
description:
Cetearyl phosphate (CAS 90506-73-3 ), also supplied under trade names such as Botanimulse CSP and Empiphos TM, is a phosphate ester of cetearyl alcohol used as an emulsifier and wetting agent.

It stabilizes oil-in-water and water-in-oil systems while modifying surface behavior to improve ingredient compatibility and texture in cosmetic and cleaning formulations.

In skin and hair care, it functions as the primary emulsifier in creams, lotions, and conditioners, providing stable emulsion architecture across a range of pH conditions.

Formulators in color cosmetics use it to disperse pigments and achieve uniform coverage in foundations and tinted moisturizers for high-performance applications.

In home care and industrial cleaning products, it improves substrate wetting and helps solubilize oils and soils in liquid detergent systems for better efficiency.

It is also selected for mild or natural-positioned formulations where a plant-derived phosphate emulsifier is a specific formulation requirement for the manufacturer.

Cetearyl phosphate is typically supplied as a waxy solid or flake. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suited to personal care manufacturing needs.

Some suppliers offer plant-derived variants to support natural or organic product positioning. Packaging is commonly offered in bags or drums sized for batch manufacturing.

name: Superoxide dismutase
description:
Superoxide dismutase (CAS 9054-89-1 ), commonly abbreviated as SOD, is an enzyme that catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide radicals into oxygen and hydrogen peroxide.

In commercial applications, it functions as a biological antioxidant, neutralizing reactive oxygen species in formulations, biological systems, and food matrices where oxidative degradation is a primary quality concern.

In cosmetic and personal care formulations, SOD is incorporated into anti-aging creams and serums to protect skin cells from oxidative stress-driven degradation during daily exposure.

Food and nutraceutical manufacturers use it as a functional ingredient in dietary supplements targeting cellular antioxidant support. Pharmaceutical and biotech applications include its use as an active component.

It is utilized in topical drug products and as a research reagent for oxidative stress assays. In food processing, SOD is evaluated for extending shelf life in products where lipid oxidation limits stability.

Superoxide dismutase is supplied as a lyophilized powder or liquid concentrate, with activity expressed in units per milligram. Grades available include food-grade and cosmetic-grade material.

Research-grade preparations with defined specific activity are also available for laboratory use. Sourcing origin varies between bovine, human recombinant, and plant-derived sources like melon.

Each source carries different regulatory and labeling implications for buyers. These variations ensure that the enzyme meets specific industry requirements for purity and biological activity levels.

name: Pullulan
description:
Pullulan (CAS 9057-02-7 ), also designated E1204 in food applications, is a naturally fermented polysaccharide produced from starch by the fungus Aureobasidium pullulans. It functions as a film-former, binder, and moisture-retention agent across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care manufacturing.

In oral solid dosage manufacturing, pullulan is the primary material for producing thin, rapidly dissolving oral strips and hard capsule shells as a gelatin alternative. Food manufacturers use it to coat confectionery, nuts, and snack products.

This ingredient extends shelf life by forming an oxygen-barrier film that reduces oxidative degradation. In cosmetic formulations, it delivers a tightening, skin-smoothing film effect in serums and face masks, supporting texture and on-skin performance claims.

Tablet coating and granulation processes also use pullulan as a binder where clean-label or plant-based positioning is a commercial requirement. It is highly valued for its versatility and ability to meet diverse industrial needs.

Pullulan is supplied as a white to off-white free-flowing powder. Commercially recognized grades include PF 10, PF 20, and PF 30, which differ primarily in molecular weight and viscosity profile for specific applications.

Viscosity is a key selection criterion for determining film thickness and dissolution rate in final products. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet various global regulatory requirements.

The food-grade material is compliant with regulatory status in applicable markets. This ensures that manufacturers can maintain high safety and quality standards while utilizing this multifunctional polysaccharide in their production lines.

name: TEA-C12-14 alkyl sulfate
description:
TEA-C12-14 Alkyl Sulfate (CAS 90583-18-9 ) is an anionic surfactant produced by neutralizing C12-14 fatty alcohol sulfates with triethanolamine. It delivers effective surface-active performance across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

The chemical functions primarily as a foaming, cleansing, and emulsifying agent. In personal care, it acts as the primary or co-surfactant in shampoos, body washes, and liquid hand soaps, generating stable lather.

It is highly effective at removing oils and soils from skin and hair. Home care and industrial cleaning products rely on it for degreasing hard surfaces, where its anionic character supports soil suspension.

The product ensures excellent rinsability in liquid detergent concentrates. Textile processing uses it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove sizing agents, oils, and contaminants from fiber before dyeing.

In leather and paper manufacturing, it supports emulsification of processing oils. It also aids in the uniform dispersion of treatment chemicals across various substrates during the production process.

TEA-C12-14 Alkyl Sulfate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with active matter content commonly ranging from 35% to 40%. It is available in technical and cosmetic grades for various uses.

Cosmetic-grade material meets purity requirements suitable for rinse-off and leave-on formulations. Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBC containers to meet the needs of large-scale industrial manufacturers.

name: Neochlorogenic acid
description:
Neochlorogenic acid ( CAS 906-33-2 ), also known as 5-Caffeylquinic acid, is a naturally occurring hydroxycinnamic acid derivative found in plant-based sources including stone fruits and coffee.

It functions as a bioactive antioxidant and phenolic reference compound used across food, pharmaceutical, and agricultural research and formulation. In food and nutraceutical development, it serves as a functional antioxidant ingredient.

This compound is utilized in botanical extracts, dietary supplements, and standardized plant-based formulations. Pharmaceutical and biotech researchers use it as an analytical reference standard for quantifying polyphenol content.

It is essential for measuring raw materials and finished products according to USP or Ph.Eur. guidelines. In agricultural applications, it is evaluated as a natural plant defense modulator for crop protection.

The substance is also incorporated into feed additive research programs. Flavor chemists reference it when characterizing the acidulant and astringency profiles of fruit-derived ingredients and coffee extracts.

Neochlorogenic acid is typically supplied as a fine powder, often at high-purity grades suited to analytical and research use. Standard offerings include purities of 98% and above for laboratory applications.

Material is sourced from plant extraction or synthesis depending on the supplier requirements. Quantities range from milligram-scale reference material to gram-level research batches for various industries.

Larger commercial volumes are available on inquiry to meet specific production needs. All batches are tested to ensure they meet rigorous FCC or ACS specifications for consistency and safety.

It is also used in wet granulation formulations to ensure rapid disintegration of oral solid dosage forms across a broad range of APIs. Type A, Type B, and Type C grades allow formulators to select sodium levels.

These grades are matched to specific API sensitivities and regulatory requirements. In topical and cosmetic formulations, SSG functions as a thickener and texture modifier in gels, creams, and cleansing products.

name: Sodium hyaluronate
description:
Sodium hyaluronate (CAS 9067-32-7 ), the sodium salt form of hyaluronic acid (HA), is a high-molecular-weight polysaccharide sourced from microbial fermentation or animal-derived raw materials.

It functions as a humectant, film-former, and viscosity modifier across cosmetic, pharmaceutical, and biomedical formulations. Healon is a recognized trade name in ophthalmic applications.

In skincare and topical formulations, HA binds moisture to the skin surface and improves product texture in serums, creams, and sheet masks. Molecular weight selection determines depth of hydration.

Ophthalmic surgeons and device manufacturers use pharmaceutical-grade material as a viscoelastic agent in cataract procedures and as a base for eye drop formulations targeting dry eye syndrome.

Intra-articular injectable grades are used in viscosupplementation therapies for osteoarthritis, where it acts as a synovial fluid supplement. In biotechnology, it is used as a scaffold material.

Sodium hyaluronate is supplied as a white to off-white powder in a range of molecular weights, typically categorized as low, medium, and high. Available grades include USP and Ph. Eur.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade materials are also widely stocked for various industrial needs. Molecular weight and purity specifications are the primary procurement differentiators across end-use segments.

name: Sodium polystyrene sulfonate
description:
Sodium polystyrene sulfonate ( CAS 9080-79-9 ) is a synthetic cation-exchange resin used across pharmaceutical, water treatment, and biotech applications. It selectively binds positively charged ions in solution, enabling controlled removal or exchange of specific cations.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it functions as the active substance in oral and rectal potassium-binding preparations used to manage elevated potassium levels. This makes it a critical API for renal care drug products and clinical treatments.

Water treatment operations use it to remove hardness-causing calcium and magnesium ions from process streams. This is particularly effective where precise ion control is required for industrial water purification and chemical processing.

In biotechnology and life sciences, it serves as a polyelectrolyte in layer-by-layer coating systems for microencapsulation. These systems are essential for controlled-release research platforms and advanced drug delivery studies.

Its rheology-modifying behavior also supports use as a thickening or stabilizing agent in aqueous formulations. This is highly beneficial where viscosity control is commercially relevant for specialized chemical mixtures and industrial fluids.

Sodium polystyrene sulfonate is supplied as a fine powder or aqueous suspension, depending on the intended application. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and BP specifications for drug manufacturers.

These are the primary standards demanded by regulatory submissions and global healthcare providers. Technical-grade forms are also available for industrial and research procurement where pharmacopeial compliance is not required.

It also appears in animal repellent sprays applied to crops, fencing, and garden materials to discourage browsing by deer and rabbits. This compound is supplied as a white crystalline powder for various uses.

In agrochemical formulations, it enables stable suspension concentrates and wettable powder products by keeping active ingredients uniformly dispersed throughout the product's shelf life.

Leather tanning and paper manufacturing also use NNO to control pigment and tannin dispersion, improving surface uniformity in finished goods and enhancing overall product quality.

name: Aluminum starch octenylsuccinate
description:

This versatile ingredient is utilized across personal care, food, and pharmaceutical applications. In cosmetic formulations, it improves the slip and skin feel of pressed and loose powders, helping to absorb sebum and reduce shine.

It is frequently found in color cosmetics and dry shampoos to manage oil. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsifier and encapsulating agent, particularly for stabilizing flavor oils and fat-soluble ingredients in spray-dried powder systems.

In pharmaceutical solid dosage forms, it acts as a flow aid and anticaking agent, improving powder handling during tablet and capsule manufacturing. It also appears in topical formulations where controlled oil absorption is required.

The material provides a smooth, non-greasy finish for various skin applications. Aluminum starch octenylsuccinate is supplied as a fine white to off-white powder and is available in food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications.

Product quality is typically aligned to FCC standards for food applications and relevant pharmacopeial or industry monographs for pharmaceutical use. Particle size and moisture content are key specification parameters.

name: Ammonium coco-sulfate
description:
Ammonium coco-sulfate (CAS 90989-98-3 ), also known commercially as coconut oil sulfated ammonium salt, is an anionic surfactant derived from coconut oil fatty acids. It functions as a primary cleansing and foaming agent across personal care and cleaning formulations.

In shampoos and body washes, it delivers high-foam lather and effective sebum removal, making it a preferred alternative to sulfate systems where a coconut-derived positioning is desired.

Liquid hand soaps and facial cleansers use it to balance cleansing efficacy with mildness at typical use concentrations. In household and industrial cleaning products, it contributes to grease emulsification and soil suspension.

Its compatibility with other anionic and amphoteric surfactants also supports its use in co-surfactant blends for customized foam and viscosity profiles in hard surface cleaners and dishwashing liquids.

Ammonium coco-sulfate is typically supplied as an aqueous liquid or paste, with active matter content commonly ranging around 30–40%. It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications suitable for personal care formulations.

It is used across surface treatment, lubrication, and emulsification applications in industrial and personal care manufacturing. In personal care, the blend acts as an emulsifier and skin-conditioning base in creams and lotions.

It is also utilized in cleansing formulations. Coatings and adhesives manufacturers use it as a surface modifier and wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and film formation during the production process.

Lubricant formulators incorporate it into metalworking fluids and process oils where fatty acid chemistry provides boundary lubrication under load. This ensures high performance in demanding industrial environments.

In plastics processing, it functions as an internal or external lubricant and dispersing aid during compounding and extrusion. This material is typically supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid for easy handling.

name: Naphthalene
description:
Naphthalene (CAS 91-20-3 ), also known commercially as white tar and tar camphor, is a polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived primarily from coal tar and petroleum refining. It functions as a chemical intermediate and precursor feedstock across a broad range of industrial manufacturing processes.

In the pharmaceutical and agrochemical sectors, this compound serves as a key intermediate in synthesizing active ingredients, including fungicides and insecticides. It is also essential for producing drug compounds such as beta-blockers for medical applications.

Textile and leather processors use naphthalene-derived sulfonates as dispersants and leveling agents in dye baths. These chemical additives are critical for improving color uniformity across various fiber types and leather goods during the manufacturing cycle.

In the printing and packaging industries, it contributes to the production of phthalocyanine pigments used in high-quality inks and coatings. These pigments are valued for their stability and vibrant color properties in commercial printing.

Moth-repellent blocks and fumigant formulations for storage protection represent a direct end-product application in consumer and industrial pest control. The material acts as an effective biocide to protect fabrics and stored goods from insect damage.

The product is supplied as white flakes, pellets, or molten liquid for bulk industrial shipment. Technical grade is the most common specification, with purity levels typically ranging from ninety-six percent to over ninety-nine percent.

Refined grades meeting higher purity thresholds are available for pharmaceutical intermediate and specialty chemical manufacturing. These high-purity options ensure compliance with rigorous industrial standards for sensitive chemical synthesis and laboratory use.

name: Ethoxyquin
description:
Ethoxyquin (CAS 91-53-2 ), also known by its EU food additive designation E324 and the abbreviation EMQ, is a synthetic antioxidant used to prevent oxidative degradation in animal feed, fish meal, and agricultural commodities.

It protects fats, oils, and fat-soluble vitamins from rancidity during storage and transport, extending shelf life across feed and food ingredient supply chains. In aquaculture and livestock feed production, it is applied to fish meal and compound feeds.

This chemical inhibits lipid oxidation and preserves nutritional value through extended storage cycles. Spice and paprika processors use it to prevent color fading and oxidative spoilage in dried botanical ingredients during processing.

It also functions as a stabilizer for fat-soluble vitamins, particularly vitamins A and E, in premix formulations. This protects potency during pelleting and storage, ensuring the nutritional integrity of the final feed product.

In fruit handling, it has been used as a post-harvest treatment to prevent superficial scald on apples and pears during cold storage. This application helps maintain the aesthetic quality and marketability of fresh produce over time.

The product is supplied as an amber to dark brown liquid. Technical and feed-grade are the primary commercial grades, with purity levels typically at 95% or higher to meet industrial requirements for various applications.

Drum and IBC packaging are standard for bulk procurement to ensure safe handling and transport. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale agricultural and industrial operations globally.

Textile and paper finishing operations use these resins to impart wrinkle resistance and dimensional stability to treated substrates. In polymer compounding, it acts as a flame retardant additive, contributing char-forming behavior.

description:
Cholesteryl chloride (CAS 910-31-6 ), also known as cholesterol chloride and 3-chlorocholest-5-ene, is a reactive cholesterol derivative used primarily as a synthetic building block in pharmaceutical and biotechnology research.

Its activated C-3 position makes it a key starting material for introducing cholesterol moieties into complex molecules during multi-step synthesis. In pharmaceutical development, it is used to synthesize cholesterol-conjugated compounds.

These include prodrugs and lipid-based drug delivery systems designed to improve membrane permeability and cellular uptake. Biotechnology researchers employ it to prepare cholesterol-tagged oligonucleotides and siRNA conjugates.

Cholesterol attachment enhances in vivo stability and tissue targeting in these applications. It also serves as an intermediate in the preparation of steroid derivatives and cholesterol esters used as reference standards.

These derivatives are often utilized as analytical reagents in QC workflows. Specialty lipid formulators use it to introduce cholesterol anchors into liposomal and nanoparticle systems currently under development.

Cholesteryl chloride is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid. It is available primarily in research and development quantities, with purity grades typically ranging from 95% to 98%+ by GC or HPLC.

It is used in creams, lotions, and lip products, contributing texture and moisture retention to the finished formula. Food manufacturers use it as a structuring fat and emulsifier in confectionery coatings and bakery shortenings.

It is also utilized in compound chocolate, where controlled melting behavior is critical. In adhesives and hot-melt systems, it acts as a rheology modifier, adjusting viscosity and setting characteristics of the final product.

Personal care stick formats, including deodorants and solid sunscreens, rely on its wax-like consistency to build structural rigidity. Hydrogenated palm glycerides are supplied as solid flakes, pastilles, or waxy slabs.

Melting point ranges vary by hydrogenation degree. Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are both commercially available, with food-grade material typically conforming to FCC or regional food additive standards.

Buyers should confirm the mono/di/triglyceride ratio and iodine value when specifying for a particular application. This ensures the material meets the specific performance requirements of the intended industrial or consumer use.

name: Adansonia digitata extract

Adansonia digitata extract (CAS 91745-12-9 ), derived from the baobab tree, is sourced commercially for its concentrated nutrient and antioxidant profile. Known in trade as baobab extract, it functions as a humectant and antioxidant active across cosmetic, food, and nutraceutical formulations.

In personal care, baobab extract is incorporated into skin creams, serums, and hair conditioners where its moisture-retention properties support hydration claims and product stability. Food and beverage manufacturers use it as a functional ingredient in energy drinks and protein bars.

By leveraging its natural vitamin C and amino acid content, it is ideal for fortified powders. Nutraceutical formulators incorporate it into dietary supplement capsules and blends targeting antioxidant and nutritional positioning for various health-conscious consumer markets.

Pharmaceutical and wellness product developers also use it as a natural excipient or active botanical in health-oriented formulations. This versatile extract provides a robust profile of bioactive compounds suitable for high-performance product development.

Adansonia digitata extract is supplied primarily as a fine powder, with spray-dried forms being standard for food and supplement applications. Liquid and standardized extract concentrates are available for cosmetic manufacturing to ensure ease of integration.

name: Guava extract
description:
Guava extract (CAS 91770-12-6 ), also sourced and referenced under Psidium guajava extract, is a botanical-derived ingredient used across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

It delivers characteristic tropical flavor notes alongside antioxidant activity, making it commercially relevant for both sensory and functional formulation goals in various industrial sectors.

In food and beverage production, it contributes authentic guava flavor to fruit drinks, nectars, confectionery, and dairy products where natural tropical taste profiles are required for the consumer.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skincare and haircare products for its antioxidant properties, targeting formulations positioned around natural botanical actives and clean label beauty standards.

In nutraceutical and dietary supplement manufacturing, it functions as a plant-based antioxidant ingredient in capsules, powders, and functional food formats for health-conscious market segments.

Flavor houses also use concentrated forms to build tropical flavor systems for use in finished product blending, ensuring consistency and potency across large-scale manufacturing batches.

Guava extract is supplied as a liquid extract, spray-dried powder, or concentrated paste depending on application requirements and the specific needs of the production facility.

In food and beverage formulations, it contributes a distinctive mild, fruity flavor profile to functional drinks, confectionery, and dietary supplements. Nutraceutical manufacturers incorporate it into capsule and tablet formats targeting antioxidant-positioned product lines.

In personal care, the leaf-derived extract is used in facial serums, toners, and anti-aging creams where botanical antioxidant activity supports formulation claims. Flavor houses also source it for use in natural flavor systems requiring fruit-forward botanical notes.

In cosmetics and skin care, it is used as a base ingredient in body butters, lip balms, and solid lotions where it provides a rich, skin-conditioning texture without synthetic additives. This material is highly valued for its stability and skin-feel.

As a cocoa butter equivalent or extender, it is used in confectionery coatings and chocolate manufacturing where its compatible triglyceride profile supports tempering and melt behavior. This makes it a versatile ingredient for large-scale food production.

name: Sodium C12-13 alkyl sulfate
description:
Sodium C12-13 alkyl sulfate (CAS 91783-23-2 ) is an anionic surfactant derived from a narrow-cut blend of C12 and C13 fatty alcohols. It delivers high-performance foaming, detergency, and emulsification across personal care and industrial cleaning formulations.

In shampoos, body washes, and facial cleansers, it functions as the primary surfactant, generating dense, stable foam while effectively removing oils and residues from skin and hair.

Home care and institutional cleaning products rely on it for grease cutting and soil suspension in dish detergents, hard surface cleaners, and laundry formulations. This versatility makes it a staple in the cleaning industry.

Textile processors use it as a scouring and wetting agent to remove sizing, oils, and contaminants from fiber surfaces before dyeing or finishing. It ensures that fabrics are properly prepared for subsequent chemical treatments.

In paper and leather processing, it supports emulsification of treatment chemistries and aids uniform dispersion of coatings and finishing agents. This helps maintain consistency and quality in the final manufactured goods.

Sodium C12-13 alkyl sulfate is typically supplied as a liquid or paste, with active matter concentrations commonly ranging from 28% to 70%. Both technical-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are available for various needs.

name: Lithium citrate
description:
Lithium citrate (CAS 919-16-4 ), also known as trilithium citrate, is the lithium salt of citric acid used as a flavoring agent and acidulant in food and pharmaceutical applications. It delivers controlled lithium ion activity in formulations where precise dosing and compatibility with aqueous systems are required.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, lithium citrate is formulated into oral liquid preparations as an alternative to lithium carbonate, particularly where faster dissolution and patient tolerability are priorities. Beverage producers have historically used it as an acidulant and flavor modifier.

This compound was most notably used in early citrus-flavored soft drink formulations. In dietary supplement production, it serves as a lithium source in low-dose mineral supplements targeting nutritional lithium intake for specific consumer health applications.

Pharmaceutical compounding operations also use it to prepare custom-strength lithium solutions for clinical dosing scenarios where solid dosage forms are not suitable. This flexibility makes it a vital component in specialized medical and nutritional manufacturing environments.

Lithium citrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder in both anhydrous and tetrahydrate forms. Anhydrous lithium citrate is the more common commercial form, available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications meeting USP and BP standards.

Food-grade material is also available for applications requiring compliance with food additive regulations. The material is processed to ensure high purity and consistent particle size distribution for seamless integration into large-scale industrial production lines.

name: (3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane
description:
(3-Aminopropyl)triethoxysilane (CAS 919-30-2 ), commonly sourced under the abbreviation APTES, is an aminosilane coupling agent that bridges inorganic surfaces and organic polymer matrices.

It bonds to glass, metals, and mineral fillers while presenting reactive amine groups toward resins, adhesives, and coatings, improving interfacial adhesion across composite systems.

In fiber-reinforced composites and filled rubber, APTES is applied as a surface treatment for glass fibers and silica, significantly improving mechanical strength and moisture resistance.

Epoxy adhesive and sealant formulators use it both as a coupling agent and adhesion promoter, particularly where bonding to metal or glass substrates is critical for the application.

In electronics, it functionalizes silicon wafers, sensor surfaces, and printed circuit board substrates to enable controlled deposition of coatings or bioactive layers for advanced devices.

Coatings producers incorporate it to improve adhesion of primers and topcoats to difficult substrates, including aluminum and treated plastics, ensuring long-term durability and performance.

APTES is supplied as a liquid, typically at 98–99% purity for technical and research-grade applications. It is available in packaging ranging from small laboratory quantities up to bulk drums.

No standard food or pharmacopeial grades apply; procurement specifications typically reference purity, amine content, and hydrolysis stability to ensure consistent chemical performance.

name: Byk 354 Surface Additive
description:
BYK 354 Surface Additive (CAS 919533-63-4 ) is a silicone-free, acrylate-based surface control additive used to reduce surface tension and improve leveling in coating and ink formulations.

It prevents surface defects such as cratering, orange peel, and Bénard cell formation without affecting recoatability or intercoat adhesion. In industrial and decorative coatings, it improves flow and leveling.

This additive is effective in both solvent-borne and high-solids systems, delivering smooth, defect-free film surfaces. UV-curable and radiation-curable ink formulations benefit from its ability to reduce surface tension.

It improves substrate wetting across difficult surfaces and helps control surface slip and uniformity during application in adhesive and sealant systems. This ensures consistent quality across various industrial applications.

Plastic coatings and packaging inks use it to ensure consistent print quality and surface finish across high-speed production lines. It is a versatile solution for demanding manufacturing environments.

The product is supplied as a liquid solution, ready for direct incorporation into formulations. It is available in standard packaging sizes suited to industrial procurement volumes, including drums and smaller containers.

This chemical delivers superior emulsification, surface conditioning, and wetting performance across personal care and industrial formulations. In personal care, it is used as a conditioning agent in hair rinses and cream formulations where its cationic charge allows it to deposit onto surfaces.

Textile processors apply it as a fabric softener and antistatic agent during finishing operations. This improves the handle and reduces static buildup in synthetic and blended fabrics during the manufacturing process. In leather processing, it supports fat-liquoring and surface treatment steps.

name: Biphenyl
description:
Biphenyl (CAS 92-52-4 ), also known as diphenyl and approved as E230 in food applications, is an aromatic hydrocarbon used industrially as a heat transfer medium and chemical intermediate.

Its stability at elevated temperatures and antimicrobial activity make it a practical functional input across food packaging, chemical synthesis, and high-temperature processing. As E230, it is applied to citrus fruits.

This application suppresses mold growth during storage and transport, which is a critical function for importers managing long-haul fresh produce logistics. In heat transfer systems, it is blended with diphenyl oxide.

These formulations create high-temperature thermal fluids used in chemical reactors and industrial heating circuits. Biphenyl also serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of liquid crystal polymers and pharmaceuticals.

In fragrance formulation, it contributes a subtle floral-geranium note and is registered under FEMA 3129 for flavor use. Biphenyl is supplied as white to pale yellow crystalline flakes or powder.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade for industrial and heat transfer applications, and food/ FCC -grade material for use under E230 regulatory frameworks. Purity levels typically range from 99% upward.

name: 3-hydroxy-2-naphthoic acid
description:
3-Hydroxy-2-naphthoic acid (CAS 92-70-6 ), commonly known as BON acid or BONA, is a naphthalene-derived organic acid used primarily as a coupling component and intermediate.

Consistent shade reproducibility across batch production is a key requirement for these applications. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it functions as an intermediate in the preparation of active compounds.

It is used for specialty chemicals requiring a hydroxylated naphthoic acid scaffold. Personal care formulators also source it for UV-stabilizing additive development in select cosmetic applications.

3-Hydroxy-2-naphthoic acid is supplied as an off-white to light tan crystalline powder. Technical and pharmaceutical-grade material is available with high purity specifications.

name: Phenothiazine
description:
Phenothiazine (CAS 92-84-2 ), also known as PTZ, is an organosulfur heterocyclic compound used industrially as an antioxidant, polymerization inhibitor, and biocide across multiple manufacturing sectors.

It prevents premature crosslinking, oxidative degradation, and microbial activity in chemical processes and formulated products. In polymer and plastics production, PTZ acts as a monomer stabilizer.

This material inhibits runaway polymerization of vinyl and acrylic monomers during storage and transport. Rubber compounders use it as an antioxidant to extend the service life of tire and industrial rubber goods.

The compound performs exceptionally well under heat and mechanical stress. In lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations, it controls oxidative breakdown at elevated operating temperatures, reducing deposit formation.

Agricultural applications include its use as an anthelmintic active and as a component in veterinary formulations targeting parasitic infections in livestock. It is a versatile chemical intermediate for many sectors.

Phenothiazine is supplied as a light gray to greenish crystalline powder or granules, with granulated forms preferred where dust control is a handling priority for safety and efficiency.

Technical grade is the standard for industrial antioxidant and inhibitor applications. Purity specifications typically range from 98% to 99%+, with documentation including COA and MSDS as standard for bulk procurement.

name: 4-biphenylcarboxylic acid

4-Biphenylcarboxylic acid (CAS 92-92-2 ), also known as 4-phenylbenzoic acid, is an aromatic carboxylic acid used as a building block and intermediate across pharmaceutical, polymer, and specialty chemical manufacturing.

Its rigid biphenyl backbone makes it a preferred structural unit where defined molecular geometry is required in synthesis. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients.

It is particularly useful in the production of sartans and other biphenyl-containing drug compounds. Polymer chemists incorporate it into liquid crystal polymer formulations and high-performance polyesters where thermal stability is critical.

Chain rigidity is a critical processing requirement for these materials. In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as a crosslinking agent and pH modifier, contributing to formulation stability and film integrity.

Specialty catalyst development also draws on this compound as a ligand precursor or co-catalyst component in organometallic reaction systems. 4-Biphenylcarboxylic acid is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder.

Standard commercial offerings include technical grade and pharmaceutical-grade material, with purity specifications typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ by HPLC. Packaging is available in laboratory quantities through to bulk industrial volumes.

These options support both R&D and commercial-scale procurement for global manufacturers. The material is handled according to strict quality protocols to ensure consistency across different production batches and applications.

name: Ethylhexyl cocoate
description:
Ethylhexyl cocoate (CAS 92044-87-6 ) is an ester derived from coconut fatty acids and 2-ethylhexyl alcohol, functioning as an emollient, carrier, and lubricant across personal care and industrial applications.

Its low viscosity and skin-compatible profile make it a practical alternative to mineral oil in cosmetic formulations. Procurement teams source it as a multifunctional base ingredient where lightweight skin feel is a priority.

In personal care, it is used in sunscreens, body oils, and leave-on skin care products as an emollient that improves texture and aids active ingredient delivery without a greasy residue.

Color cosmetics manufacturers incorporate it as a dispersing agent for pigments in foundations and lip products. In lubricant formulations, it functions as a bio-based base fluid or additive.

Low-toxicity and biodegradability are key procurement requirements for this material. Coatings and adhesive formulators use it as a plasticizing component and processing aid to improve flexibility.

Ethylhexyl cocoate is supplied as a clear, pale yellow liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for larger industrial volumes. It is offered in cosmetic-grade specifications.

The material meets the purity requirements of major personal care markets. Technical-grade material is also available for industrial applications in coatings and lubricants to meet diverse needs.

description:

It functions as an emulsifier, moisturizing agent, and surface-active ingredient across personal care, food, and industrial formulations. In personal care, it is incorporated into skin creams and lotions.

Its fatty acid profile supports moisture retention and skin barrier compatibility in hair conditioners. Food manufacturers use it as an emulsification aid in processed fat systems and specialty lipid blends.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it acts as a surface modifier and wetting agent to improve substrate adhesion and film uniformity. This versatility makes it a staple in chemical manufacturing.

Oleochemical processors also use it as a feedstock for producing soaps, esters, and surfactant intermediates. It is supplied as a liquid or low-viscosity oil at ambient to slightly elevated temperatures.

name: Coco glycerides
description:
Coco glycerides (CAS 92045-31-3 ), also known as Edenor PPE, are coconut-derived mono-, di-, and triglyceride blends used as multifunctional lipid ingredients in personal care and food applications.

Derived from coconut oil, they function as emollients, emulsifiers, and consistency agents across a range of formulation types. In skin and hair care, they act as emollients and co-emulsifiers.

These ingredients are used in creams, lotions, and conditioners, improving spreadability and skin feel without heavy residue. Food manufacturers use them as emulsifying and texturizing agents in confectionery.

They are ideal for coatings, bakery fillings, and fat-based systems where controlled crystallization matters. In home care formulations, they contribute to emulsion stability and help disperse active ingredients.

They are frequently utilized in liquid cleaners and fabric treatments. Coatings and adhesive formulators incorporate them as plasticizing components to adjust viscosity and improve substrate wetting.

These properties are essential in solvent-based and hot-melt systems. Coco glycerides are supplied as a solid or semi-solid waxy material, with form varying by mono/diglyceride ratio and processing.

Food-grade specifications conforming to FCC standards are available for edible applications, while cosmetic-grade material meets requirements for personal care use.

Technical grades are also offered for industrial coating and adhesive applications. These versatile lipids provide consistent performance across diverse manufacturing sectors and chemical processes.

name: Hydrotreated microcrystalline wax
description:
Hydrotreated microcrystalline wax (CAS 92045-76-6 ) is a refined petroleum-derived wax produced through hydrotreatment to reduce aromatic and impurity content. It functions as a rheology modifier, lubricant, and plasticizer across coatings, adhesives, rubber, and polymer processing industries.

In hot-melt adhesives and sealants, it controls viscosity and open time while improving flexibility in the final bond. Rubber and tire manufacturers incorporate it as a protective bloom agent and processing aid, extending surface durability against ozone degradation.

Coatings formulators use it to adjust slip, gloss, and mar resistance in industrial and decorative finishes. In plastics compounding, it acts as an internal and external lubricant, reducing melt viscosity and preventing die buildup during extrusion.

Hydrotreated microcrystalline wax is supplied as slabs, pellets, or pastilles, with melt point ranges typically spanning from approximately 60°C to over 90°C to suit different processing requirements.

Grades are available to food-contact and cosmetic standards, including FCC and USP specifications, as well as technical grades for industrial applications. Packing is commonly offered in cartons, bags, or bulk containers.

It functions as an emulsifier, wetting agent, and dispersant across a range of industrial and personal care formulations. In water treatment, it improves the dispersion of scale inhibitors and biocides.

This helps active ingredients reach target surfaces more effectively. Textile and leather processors use it as a wetting and scouring agent to ensure uniform dye penetration and consistent surface preparation.

Formulators in cleaning and degreasing compounds rely on it to emulsify oils and soils in both aqueous and semi-aqueous systems. It provides reliable performance across various fiber types and substrates.

In printing and packaging, it supports ink dispersion and substrate wetting, contributing to print uniformity and adhesion quality. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance chemical manufacturing.

name: Potassium tartrate
description:
Potassium tartrate (CAS 921-53-9 ), also designated E336ii in food regulatory frameworks, is the dipotassium salt of tartaric acid used commercially as a pH buffer and stabilizer.

It occurs naturally in grapes and is recovered as a byproduct of wine production, giving it a well-established supply chain in food and cosmetic markets. In food manufacturing, it functions as a buffering agent.

It is used in confectionery, baked goods, and processed foods where precise acidity control affects texture and shelf stability. Winemakers use it to stabilize tartrate levels and prevent unwanted crystal formation.

In personal care formulations, it serves as a pH adjuster in creams, lotions, and cleansing products. This helps maintain the acidic environment required for skin-compatible formulations and product integrity.

It also acts as a mild antioxidant in food systems, protecting against oxidative degradation in sensitive ingredients. Potassium tartrate is supplied as a white crystalline powder or fine granules.

Food-grade material conforming to FCC specifications is the most commonly traded form. This material meets the purity requirements for direct food contact applications across various global markets.

Cosmetic-grade supply is also available for personal care manufacturers requiring documented quality standards. The material is highly soluble in water and provides consistent performance in aqueous solutions.

description:

Functional beverages and fortified foods utilize this ingredient where high digestibility and amino acid density are priorities. Personal care formulators use it in hair conditioners, skin creams, and serums.

Its peptide fractions bind to keratin and support moisture retention in the finished product. Pharmaceutical applications include its use as a stabilizer and excipient in tablet coatings and wound-care matrices.

In animal feed, it serves as a digestible protein concentrate that improves palatability and supports amino acid intake in livestock and aquaculture diets. It is supplied primarily as a spray-dried powder.

Granulated forms are available for specific processing requirements. It is offered in food-grade and feed-grade specifications, with pharmaceutical-grade material available to USP and BP standards.

Molecular weight fractions vary by application, with low-molecular-weight grades preferred in cosmetic and nutraceutical use. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient for diverse industrial formulations.

name: Hydrogenated lecithin
description:
Hydrogenated lecithin (CAS 92128-87-5 ), also known as HSPC, is a fully or partially saturated phospholipid derived from lecithin through catalytic hydrogenation. This process eliminates unsaturated fatty acid bonds.

The resulting material is a more oxidatively stable emulsifier suited to demanding formulation and processing conditions. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, HSPC is a primary lipid component in liposomal drug delivery systems.

Its higher phase transition temperature enables stable encapsulation of active ingredients. Food manufacturers use this ingredient as an emulsifier in fat-based systems, chocolate coatings, and margarine products.

Oxidative stability is a priority over standard lecithin in these applications. In cosmetic and personal care formulations, it functions as a skin-conditioning emulsifier in creams, serums, and liposomal systems.

It targets active ingredient penetration and serves rheology modification in topical and oral dosage forms. This ensures consistent viscosity across temperature ranges for various specialized industrial applications.

Hydrogenated lecithin is supplied as a white to off-white powder or waxy solid. Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph. Eur. specifications for high-purity manufacturing needs.

These grades feature defined phosphatidylcholine content relevant to liposomal applications. Food-grade supply is also available, with grade selection typically driven by purity requirements and regulatory frameworks.

name: Polyquaternium 4
description:
Polyquaternium-4 (CAS 92183-41-0 ) is a cationic cellulose-derived polymer used as a conditioning and film-forming agent across personal care and industrial applications. The quaternary ammonium groups along its backbone allow it to bind to negatively charged surfaces.

This unique chemical structure makes it highly effective for deposition and retention on hair, skin, and various fibrous substrates. In hair care formulations such as shampoos and conditioners, it improves wet combability and reduces static.

The polymer enhances overall manageability and is frequently found in leave-in treatments. Rinse-off and leave-on skin care products use it as a lightweight film former that improves texture without leaving a heavy or greasy residue.

In textile processing, it is applied as a surface modifier to improve softness and antistatic performance. It also aids in dye retention on both natural and synthetic fibers, ensuring a more durable and high-quality finish for manufacturers.

Paper and nonwoven manufacturers use it to modify surface charge and improve wet strength or bonding in finished sheets. This versatility makes it a staple ingredient in industrial chemical processing and specialty paper production.

Polyquaternium-4 is typically supplied as an aqueous solution or gel, with active polymer content varying by grade. Both cosmetic-grade and technical-grade material are available to meet personal care and industrial processing requirements.

Buyers should confirm active content, viscosity specification, and the specific preservation system when evaluating supplier offerings. Ensuring the material meets necessary quality benchmarks is essential for consistent formulation performance.

It enables controlled crosslinking and adhesion performance across a broad range of polymer systems. In coatings formulations, HPMA reacts with isocyanate or melamine crosslinkers to produce two-component polyurethane.

These acrylic topcoats offer improved hardness and chemical resistance. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to build hydroxyl-functional acrylic backbones that bond well to metal, glass, and plastic substrates.

name: tert-butyl peroxypivalate
description:
Tert-butyl peroxypivalate , commonly abbreviated as TBPP, is an organic peroxide initiator used to trigger free-radical polymerization and crosslinking reactions in polymer manufacturing.

Its relatively low decomposition temperature makes it the preferred choice where controlled, low-temperature initiation is a commercial requirement for CAS 927-07-1 .

In PVC suspension and emulsion polymerization, TBPP initiates chain reactions at temperatures typically between 40–60°C, giving processors tight control over molecular weight distribution.

Acrylic and vinyl acetate polymer producers use it to achieve consistent conversion rates in batch and continuous reactor systems. It is a vital component for high-performance resins.

In the rubber and elastomer sector, it functions as a crosslinking agent to build network structure in EPDM and similar compounds, directly influencing final product hardness.

Specialty coatings and adhesive formulators also rely on TBPP to initiate cure in systems where higher-temperature peroxides would degrade sensitive co-monomers during the process.

Tert-butyl peroxypivalate is supplied as a solution, typically in concentrations around 75% in aliphatic hydrocarbon solvents, due to the handling requirements of organic peroxides.

Technical-grade material is the standard commercial offering, with specifications aligned to active oxygen content. It is transported under temperature-controlled conditions.

name: Calcined kaolin
description:
Calcined kaolin (CAS 92704-41-1 ), also marketed under trade names such as Satintone 1 and M 100, is a thermally processed aluminum silicate clay used as a functional filler and rheology modifier across industrial manufacturing.

The calcination process drives off hydroxyl groups, producing a harder, more chemically inert material than standard hydrous kaolin. In coatings and paints, it improves opacity, controls sheen, and reduces the demand for titanium dioxide.

Paper and board manufacturers use it as a coating pigment and filler to enhance printability, brightness, and surface smoothness in offset and flexographic printing substrates. This ensures high-quality finishes for various commercial uses.

Plastics and rubber compounders incorporate it to improve dimensional stability, stiffness, and electrical resistance in cable insulation and molded components. It serves as a critical component in high-performance industrial materials.

Adhesive and sealant formulators rely on it to adjust viscosity and extend formulations without compromising bond performance. This versatility makes it a staple in construction and automotive manufacturing sectors globally.

Calcined kaolin is supplied as a dry white powder in a range of particle size distributions to suit different processing requirements. Technical and industrial grades are the standard market offering for most chemical buyers.

description:

In sports nutrition and clinical food formulations, it provides rapidly absorbed peptides that support protein fortification targets. This occurs without the digestive load associated with whole proteins.

name: Potassium isopentyl dithiocarbonate
description:
Potassium isopentyl dithiocarbonate (CAS 928-70-1 ) is a xanthate-class collector used in the froth flotation of sulfide ores. It selectively adsorbs onto mineral surfaces, enabling the separation and concentration of target metal sulfides from gangue material.

In copper, lead, and zinc sulfide flotation, it promotes selective mineral attachment to air bubbles, improving concentrate grade and recovery rates. Processing operations targeting polymetallic ores use it where longer-chain xanthates are needed.

These longer chains enhance collector strength on less-reactive sulfide surfaces during mineral processing circuits. It is also evaluated in gold-bearing sulfide circuits, where effective collector performance directly impacts downstream leaching and smelting economics.

Blending with shorter-chain xanthates or other collector types allows flotation plant operators to fine-tune selectivity against iron sulfide gangue minerals such as pyrite. This flexibility is essential for optimizing recovery in complex ore bodies.

Potassium isopentyl dithiocarbonate is supplied as an aqueous solution or as a solid, depending on the producer and regional supply chain. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification for mineral processing applications.

Packaging typically follows bulk industrial formats suited to mine-site consumption, including drums and intermediate bulk containers. This ensures safe handling and efficient transport to remote mining operations globally.

name: Ethylhexyl isopalmitate
description:

name: Propylparaben
description:
Propylparaben (CAS 94-13-3 ), also sold under trade names Tegosept P, Solbrol P, and Protaben P, is a synthetic preservative approved as E216 across food, cosmetic, and pharmaceutical applications.

It inhibits the growth of mold, yeast, and bacteria at low concentrations, making it one of the most cost-effective broad-spectrum antimicrobial options available to formulators today.

In personal care and cosmetics, it is used to preserve lotions, shampoos, and creams against microbial contamination throughout shelf life. This ensures product safety and maintains integrity for consumers.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it as a preservative in oral suspensions, topical preparations, and multi-dose injectable formulations where microbial control is a strict regulatory requirement.

Food and beverage producers apply it under the E216 designation to protect baked goods, sauces, and beverages. It is often used in combination with methylparaben for broader efficacy and protection.

In coatings and adhesive systems, it functions as a biocide to prevent microbial degradation during storage and application. This helps maintain the physical properties of industrial chemical mixtures.

Propylparaben is supplied as a white crystalline powder. Standard grades include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and FCC , covering pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food-grade procurement requirements.

Technical grade is also available for industrial applications such as coatings and adhesive systems. These high-purity standards ensure consistent performance across all manufacturing sectors.

name: Benzoyl peroxide
description:
Benzoyl peroxide (CAS 94-36-0 ), also known as BPO and approved as E928 in food applications, is an organic peroxide used across industries as a free-radical initiator, bleaching agent, and curing catalyst.

Its ability to generate reactive radicals on decomposition makes it a core processing chemical in polymer manufacturing, food treatment, and topical pharmaceutical formulations. In plastics and rubber, BPO initiates free-radical polymerization.

It facilitates the cross-linking of resins, silicones, and elastomers, directly influencing cure speed and final material properties. Food producers use it as a flour bleaching agent to accelerate the natural whitening of wheat flour.

This process improves dough handling characteristics. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the active ingredient in topical acne treatment formulations, where its antimicrobial oxidizing action targets acne-causing bacteria.

Personal care formulators also incorporate BPO into medicated creams and gels at controlled concentrations for the same antimicrobial function. Benzoyl peroxide is supplied as a white powder or granules.

It is typically wetted or diluted with water or plasticizers to reduce explosion risk during handling and transport. Standard commercial grades include 70–75% active content (water-wetted) and 50% dispersions.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP and Ph.Eur. specifications for use in regulated drug product manufacturing. These standards ensure the highest purity for sensitive medical applications.

name: 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid

2,4-Dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (CAS 94-75-7 ), commonly known as 2,4-D, is a systemic herbicide active ingredient used to selectively control broadleaf weeds in agricultural and turf settings.

Industrial vegetation management programs, including utility rights-of-way and railway corridors, use high-concentration formulations derived from this acid.

It also functions as a biocidal component in certain industrial cleaning and weed control products where selective plant elimination is required for maintenance.

It forms stable complexes on copper and copper alloy surfaces, protecting them from oxidative degradation in both aqueous and non-aqueous systems. In lubricants and metalworking fluids, BTA is incorporated as a copper passivator.

This prevents metal-catalyzed oil degradation and staining of non-ferrous components. Water treatment formulations rely on it to protect copper pipework and heat exchanger surfaces in recirculating cooling systems.

Automotive antifreeze and engine coolant products use BTA to inhibit corrosion on brass and copper engine components throughout the coolant circuit. This ensures long-term stability for automotive systems.

In electronics manufacturing, it is applied as a surface treatment to prevent tarnishing of copper contacts and printed circuit board traces during storage and processing. This maintains high conductivity and reliability.

Benzotriazole is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow crystalline powder or as flakes. Standard commercial grades include technical grade and high-purity grades suited to electronics and precision metalworking.

Bulk supply is available in bags or fiber drums, with solution concentrates also offered for direct dosing in water treatment and coolant blending operations. These formats ensure ease of handling for industrial users.
