name: Benzothiazole
description:
Benzothiazole (CAS 95-16-9 ), also known by the trade name Vangard BT, is a bicyclic heterocyclic compound used across rubber processing, flavor formulation, and industrial preservation.

It functions primarily as a chemical intermediate and precursor in the synthesis of accelerators, dyes, and biocidal agents. In rubber and tire manufacturing, it serves as a key building block.

This compound is essential for benzothiazole-based vulcanization accelerators, directly influencing cure rates and compound performance. Flavor and fragrance formulators use it under FEMA 3256 .

It contributes nutty, slightly roasted notes to food and beverage applications. In textile and paper processing, benzothiazole derivatives are incorporated into dye intermediates and optical brighteners.

The heterocyclic core drives chromophore activity in these applications. Industrial preservation systems, including metalworking fluids and coating formulations, rely on benzothiazole-derived biocides.

These biocides control microbial growth and extend product shelf life. Benzothiazole is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid, depending on temperature conditions during handling and storage.

Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial and rubber applications, while higher-purity grades are available to meet flavor and fragrance industry requirements.

It is typically packaged in drums or IBCs for bulk procurement. Our material meets rigorous industry specifications to ensure consistent performance across all manufacturing sectors.

name: 2-(tert-butylaminothio)benzothiazole
description:
2-(tert-Butylaminothio)benzothiazole (CAS 95-31-8 ), commercially known as TBBS, is a delayed-action sulfenamide accelerator used in the rubber vulcanization industry.

It controls the rate and onset of crosslinking during rubber processing, giving manufacturers a reliable processing safety window before cure begins.

TBBS is the accelerator of choice in tire manufacturing, where it is used in tread compounds, sidewalls, and carcass plies to deliver consistent cure rates and mechanical performance.

In industrial rubber goods, including conveyor belts, seals, hoses, and gaskets, it enables processors to balance scorch safety with efficient vulcanization at production temperatures.

It performs effectively in natural rubber, SBR, and blended systems, often combined with secondary accelerators such as DPG or TMTD to fine-tune cure profiles.

Footwear and technical molded rubber components also rely on TBBS where dimensional accuracy and surface quality depend on controlled crosslink density.

TBBS is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or granules, with granular form preferred in automated dosing and mixing operations to reduce dust exposure.

Standard commercial grades meet specifications set by major rubber industry quality frameworks, including purity benchmarks typically at 95% minimum active content.

name: N-cyclohexyl-2-benzothiazosulfenamide
description:
N-Cyclohexyl-2-benzothiazolesulfenamide (CAS 95-33-0 ), commercially known as Accelerator CBS or Accelerator CZ, is a delayed-action sulfenamide accelerator used in the vulcanization of natural and synthetic rubber.

It enables controlled crosslinking by providing a processing safety window before cure onset, which is critical for complex rubber compound manufacturing. In tire manufacturing, CBS accelerates sulfur vulcanization of tread and sidewall compounds.

This is essential where scorch resistance during mixing and extrusion must be balanced against fast cure rates at mold temperatures. Mechanical rubber goods producers, including conveyor belts and hoses, rely on it for consistent performance.

It helps achieve uniform crosslink density across thick-section parts. It is also used in footwear and industrial molded goods where dimensional accuracy depends on predictable flow before the cure initiation begins.

CBS frequently appears in combination systems with secondary accelerators such as TBBS or DPG to fine-tune cure speed and plateau behavior. It is supplied as an off-white to pale yellow powder or granules.

The granular form is often preferred for dust-free handling in industrial compounding operations. Standard commercial grades meet rubber chemical specifications with defined active content and melting point ranges.

It is available in technical grade , with some suppliers offering low-dust or pre-dispersed masterbatch formats for automated dosing lines. This ensures high efficiency and safety during the chemical handling process.

name: o-xylene
description:
O-xylene (CAS 95-47-6 ), also sold as o-xylol, is an aromatic hydrocarbon solvent and chemical intermediate sourced primarily from catalytic reforming of naphtha. Beyond its solvent function, it serves as the principal feedstock for phthalic anhydride production.

This material represents one of the highest-volume downstream uses in the chemical industry. The dominant industrial outlet is oxidation to phthalic anhydride, which feeds directly into plasticizer and alkyd resin manufacturing at scale.

In coatings and industrial cleaning formulations, o-xylene functions as a high-solvency aromatic carrier for resins, epoxies, and heavy-duty degreasers. It is particularly effective where slower evaporation rates are required for application.

Adhesive and sealant producers use it to dissolve synthetic rubbers and polymer binders during compounding. In oil and gas operations, it appears in specialty solvent blends for pipeline cleaning and hydrocarbon extraction processes.

O-xylene is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk tanker, ISO container, and drum formats. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 98% or higher for industrial use.

High-purity grades are available for chemical synthesis applications where isomer contamination must be tightly controlled. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and reliable delivery for large-scale manufacturing requirements.

name: 1,2-dichlorobenzene
description:
1,2-Dichlorobenzene (CAS 95-50-1 ), commonly known as ODCB, is a high-boiling aromatic solvent used across industrial processing and chemical manufacturing. It functions as a process solvent, carrier, and intermediate where thermal stability is required.

This chemical provides strong solvency for non-polar substrates in various industrial environments. In textile and leather processing, ODCB serves as a carrier solvent for disperse dyes, enabling uniform dye penetration into synthetic fibers.

The coatings and adhesives industry uses it to dissolve resins, pigment dispersions, and elastomer compounds. It is particularly effective where conventional solvents lack sufficient solvency power for specialized industrial applications.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a reaction medium and processing solvent. It is used extensively in polyphenylene sulfide (PPS) synthesis and other high-performance polymer production cycles.

Water treatment and industrial biocide formulations also incorporate ODCB as a solvent carrier. It helps deliver active ingredients targeting microbial control in large-scale industrial water systems and cooling towers.

1,2-Dichlorobenzene is supplied as a clear liquid in bulk quantities, including ISO tank, drum, and IBC formats. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher.

Refined grades meeting tighter purity thresholds are available for sensitive synthesis and formulation applications. Our logistics network ensures reliable delivery of high-purity solvents to meet your specific manufacturing requirements.

name: 2-chloroaniline
description:
2-Chloroaniline (CAS 95-51-2 ), also known as o-Chloroaniline, is an aromatic amine intermediate used across dye manufacturing, agrochemical synthesis, and pharmaceutical production.

It functions as a building block for constructing complex organic molecules, particularly azo dyes, pigments, and active ingredient precursors for various industrial sectors.

In textile and printing industries, it serves as a key precursor in azo dye synthesis, enabling the production of colorants applied to fabric, paper, and packaging substrates.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to synthesize active intermediates, where the ortho-chloro substitution pattern directs specific reaction pathways during API construction.

In polymer and rubber processing, it acts as a curing agent and cross-linker, contributing to the structural integrity of finished elastomeric and plastic components.

Agrochemical producers also rely on it as a starting material for herbicide and pesticide synthesis, where chlorinated aniline derivatives define the biological activity of the final compound.

2-Chloroaniline is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions. It is available in technical grade for industrial synthesis applications, with higher-purity specifications offered to meet requirements.

Packaging options typically range from drums to IBC containers, suited to both laboratory-scale procurement and bulk industrial supply for global chemical distribution.

name: o-toluidine
description:
o-Toluidine (CAS 95-53-4 ), also known as o-tolylamine, is an aromatic amine used as a chemical intermediate in the synthesis of dyes, pigments, and curing agents.

It serves as a building block in manufacturing processes where a reactive amine group is required to produce more complex organic compounds for industrial use.

In the dye and pigment industry, this chemical is a key precursor in the production of azo dyes used to color textiles, leather, and paper substrates.

Printing ink formulations rely on pigments derived from these intermediates to achieve specific hue ranges in packaging applications and commercial printing processes.

It functions as a curing agent component and cross-linker in certain resin systems, contributing to the hardening of coatings and high-performance adhesives.

Personal care product manufacturers use derived colorants in formulations where specific synthetic dye chemistry is required for consumer goods and cosmetics.

The product is supplied as a liquid at ambient conditions, typically available in drum and IBC quantities for industrial buyers and large-scale manufacturing.

It is offered primarily in technical grade, with purity specifications commonly ranging from 99% and above to ensure consistent performance in chemical synthesis.

name: 2-aminophenol
description:
2-Aminophenol (CAS 95-55-6 ), also known as o-hydroxyaniline, is an aromatic amine intermediate used across dye manufacturing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and specialty chemical production.

It functions primarily as a building block for azo dyes, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and rubber antioxidants. In textile and leather dyeing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of azo and mordant dyes.

This chemical contributes to colorfast performance on natural fibers. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it to produce benzoxazole-based APIs and other heterocyclic compounds requiring an ortho-amino-hydroxyl substitution pattern.

In personal care, it acts as an oxidative hair dye intermediate, coupling with developer agents to produce brown and auburn shades in professional and retail color formulations.

Rubber and polymer producers incorporate it into antioxidant and antiozonant compounds to extend product service life under thermal stress. It is supplied as an off-white to light tan crystalline powder.

name: Methylhydroquinone
description:
Methylhydroquinone (CAS 95-71-6 ), also known as 2,5-Dihydroxytoluene, is a substituted hydroquinone derivative used across polymer, cosmetic, and flavor industries as an antioxidant and UV stabilizer.

Its ability to scavenge free radicals makes it a functional additive in systems where oxidative degradation or premature cure must be controlled during the manufacturing process.

In plastics and polymer manufacturing, it acts as a polymerization inhibitor, preventing premature crosslinking during storage and processing of reactive monomers and resins.

Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into topical preparations where antioxidant stabilization of the formulation matrix is required to maintain product integrity and shelf life.

In flavor and fragrance applications, it contributes to aroma profiles and functions as a preservative component in finished flavor systems for various consumer goods.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers also use it as a synthetic intermediate in the production of active ingredients and specialty fine chemicals for the global healthcare market.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder and is available in technical and pharmaceutical-intermediate grades with purity levels typically at 98% or higher.

Packaging options range from kilogram-scale bags to bulk drum quantities to suit both R&D and commercial production requirements for industrial and laboratory applications.

name: 3-chloro-4-methylaniline
description:
3-Chloro-4-methylaniline (CAS 95-74-9 ), also known as 2-Chloro-4-aminotoluene and abbreviated as 3-CPT, is an aromatic amine intermediate used primarily in the synthesis of agrochemical active ingredients.

It functions as a key building block in the manufacture of herbicides and other crop protection compounds. 3-CPT is most commonly consumed in the production of herbicide active substances.

Its chloro-substituted aniline structure is incorporated into the final molecule during multi-step synthesis. It is used in the manufacture of urea-based and amide-based herbicides targeting broadleaf and grassy weeds.

Formulators and API manufacturers sourcing this intermediate rely on consistent purity to meet the tight specifications required for regulated agrochemical registration dossiers.

It also serves as a precursor in dye and pigment chemistry, though agrochemical synthesis represents the dominant commercial demand. 3-Chloro-4-methylaniline is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid.

Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with purity typically specified at 98% or higher by GC. Drum and IBC packaging are conventional for industrial quantities.

Smaller quantities are available for R&D procurement. Handling should be conducted in accordance with safety data sheets due to the characteristic toxicity profile of aromatic amines.

name: 5-chloro-2-methylaniline
description:
5-Chloro-2-methylaniline (CAS 95-79-4 ), also known as 5-chloro-o-toluidine and 2-amino-4-chlorotoluene, is an aromatic amine intermediate used in the synthesis of azo dyes, pigments, and specialty chemicals.

Its reactive amine group makes it a building block for colorant and polymer systems across multiple manufacturing sectors. In textile and leather dyeing, it functions as a diazonium coupling precursor for azo dye production.

This enables the manufacture of fast, vibrant colorants applied directly to fiber substrates. Pigment manufacturers use it to produce organic pigments incorporated into printing inks and packaging coatings.

Color strength and substrate adhesion are critical performance criteria in these applications. In polymer and plastics processing, it contributes to cross-linking and curing systems, improving structural integrity.

Personal care formulators sourcing approved colorant intermediates may evaluate it for cosmetic dye synthesis, subject to regional regulatory compliance. The material is supplied as a liquid or low-melting solid.

Physical state depends on purity and temperature conditions during handling. Technical grade is the standard commercial offering, with high-purity grades available for sensitive synthesis applications.

These high-purity options are ideal for processes requiring tighter specification control. Bulk and drum quantities are typical for industrial procurement, with smaller packaging available for laboratory use.

name: Diethyl oxalate
description:
Diethyl oxalate ( CAS 95-92-1 ), also known as ethyl oxalate, is the diethyl ester of oxalic acid used primarily as a chemical intermediate and solvent in organic synthesis. It functions as a reactive building block for introducing the oxalyl group into target molecules.

The compound serves as a catalyst precursor in specialty chemical manufacturing and industrial processes. In pharmaceutical synthesis, it acts as a key condensation reagent for producing active pharmaceutical ingredients, particularly in the manufacture of barbiturates and antimalarials.

It is also utilized in the production of other heterocyclic compounds. Formulators in personal care use it as a fragrance ingredient and fixative, where its mild ester character contributes to scent profiles in fine fragrances and cosmetic products.

As a FEMA -recognized flavoring agent, it is incorporated at controlled levels in food flavor compositions to impart fruity, wine-like nuances. In catalysis applications, it acts as an oxalate precursor for preparing metal oxalate catalyst supports.

The product is also used as an intermediate in various industrial chemical processes. Diethyl oxalate is supplied as a clear liquid in standard commercial packaging ranging from drums to IBC containers for bulk distribution.

Technical grade and high-purity grades are available to meet the differing requirements of industrial synthesis versus pharmaceutical and flavor applications. Buyers sourcing for regulated end uses should confirm grade specifications and purity certificates.

Quality assurance is maintained through rigorous testing to ensure compliance with industry requirements. Please contact our technical sales team for detailed documentation regarding specific application needs and procurement logistics.

name: Agaricus bisporus extract
description:
Agaricus bisporus extract (CAS 95009-14-6 ), also known commercially as Portobello Mushroom Cellular Extract, is derived from the cultivated white button and portobello mushroom. It is standardized for use across food, cosmetic, and nutraceutical applications.

The extract delivers antioxidant activity and moisture-retention properties that formulators target in functional and bioactive product development. In cosmetic formulations, it functions as a humectant and antioxidant active.

It is frequently incorporated into serums, creams, and masks targeting skin hydration and oxidative stress protection. Nutraceutical manufacturers use it in capsule and powder supplement formats to deliver naturally occurring peptides.

These supplements provide amino acids and micronutrients associated with immune and metabolic support. Food and beverage producers incorporate it as a functional ingredient in health-positioned products where natural stabilization is required.

This extract serves as a label-friendly requirement for many modern food applications. Pharmaceutical researchers also evaluate it as a botanical active in standardized extract formulations targeting oxidative biomarkers.

Agaricus bisporus extract is typically supplied as a spray-dried powder or liquid extract concentrate. Standard grades include food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications to meet diverse industrial manufacturing needs.

Some suppliers offer standardized preparations defined by polysaccharide or beta-glucan content. Packaging is commonly available in kilogram quantities through to bulk drum supply for industrial buyers and large-scale production.

Contact us for supply of Agaricus bisporus extract

name: Alkalized Cocoa powder
description:
Alkalized Cocoa Powder (CAS 95009-22-6 ), also known as Dutch-process cocoa, is a treated cocoa ingredient where natural cocoa has been processed with an alkalizing agent to neutralize acidity and deepen color and flavor intensity.

It functions as a flavoring and coloring ingredient across a broad range of food manufacturing applications. In confectionery and bakery manufacturing, it delivers the dark color and smooth, mellow chocolate flavor characteristic of premium cookies.

Beverage producers use it in hot cocoa mixes, chocolate-flavored drink powders, and ready-to-mix formats where a less bitter, more soluble cocoa profile is required for the final consumer product.

Ice cream and dairy dessert formulators incorporate it to achieve consistent chocolate flavor and visual appeal across batch production. It also appears in coating compounds, fillings, and dry seasoning blends.

This ingredient is essential where controlled cocoa intensity is a formulation requirement. The product is supplied as a fine, free-flowing powder in a range of fat contents, typically low-fat and medium-fat grades.

Food-grade specifications are standard, with product commonly meeting FCC requirements. It is available in bulk bags and smaller packaging formats suited to both industrial-scale and mid-volume procurement.

name: Polyquaternium 16
description:
Polyquaternium-16 (CAS 95144-24-4 ) is a cationic copolymer of vinylpyrrolidone and quaternized vinylimidazolium chloride used primarily in personal care and industrial formulations. It functions as a conditioning agent and film-former.

The polymer deposits a substantive charge on hair and skin surfaces to improve texture and manageability. In industrial contexts, it modifies surface charge and rheological behavior across textile, leather, and paper processing applications.

In hair care, it is incorporated into shampoos, conditioners, and styling products where it reduces static and improves combability. It provides hold without excessive buildup in various cosmetic applications.

Rinse-off and leave-in formulations benefit from its ability to adhere to negatively charged hair fibers even under wet conditions. This makes it a versatile ingredient for high-performance hair care systems.

In textile processing, it acts as a softening and antistatic agent applied during finishing stages to modify fabric hand feel. Paper and leather manufacturers use it as a surface modifier to improve coating adhesion.

The chemical helps manage charge distribution across substrates in diverse manufacturing environments. Polyquaternium-16 is commercially supplied as an aqueous solution, typically at active polymer concentrations.

It is available in cosmetic-grade specifications meeting the requirements of major international ingredient standards. Packaging is offered in drums and intermediate bulk containers for industrial-scale procurement.

name: Dibasic ester
description:
Dibasic ester (CAS 95481-62-2 ), commonly referred to as DBE or marketed under the trade name Estasol, is a blend of dimethyl esters of succinic, glutaric, and adipic acids. It is used as a high-boiling solvent and plasticizer across industrial manufacturing.

Its low volatility and strong solvency make it a practical alternative to conventional solvents in demanding coating and polymer applications. In industrial coatings and paint strippers, DBE functions as a coalescing solvent and active stripping agent.

It effectively dissolves cured resins and reduces VOC content in formulations. Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it as a plasticizer to improve flexibility and substrate adhesion in polyurethane and epoxy systems.

In plastics processing, it acts as a processing aid and plasticizer for PVC and other polymer compounds where controlled softening is required. Metalworking fluid formulators use DBE as a carrier solvent and cleaner base.

Its high flash point supports safer handling in industrial environments. Dibasic ester is supplied as a clear liquid in drum and IBC quantities, with bulk tanker options available for large-volume procurement.

It is typically offered in technical grade, with specifications aligned to industrial solvent standards covering ester content, water content, and acid value. Some suppliers offer refined grades with tighter purity controls.

These refined grades are suitable for sensitive coating or polymer applications. The material is managed according to standard industrial safety protocols to ensure consistent performance and reliability in diverse manufacturing sectors.

name: Omeprazole sodium
description:
Omeprazole sodium (CAS 95510-70-6 ) is the sodium salt form of omeprazole, commonly referenced in procurement as Losec Sodium. It functions as a proton pump inhibitor active pharmaceutical ingredient, suppressing gastric acid secretion.

This compound serves as the basis for injectable and solid oral dosage formulations. The primary application is in parenteral formulations, where the sodium salt form offers improved aqueous solubility compared to the free base.

This enhanced solubility enables IV and infusion preparations for hospital use. It is also used in the manufacture of enteric-coated tablets and capsules targeting gastroesophageal reflux disease and peptic ulcer treatment.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers sourcing this material for generic drug production rely on it as a direct API input requiring full regulatory documentation. It is a critical component for high-volume pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Contract formulators developing combination gastric products may also specify this form when targeting rapid-onset delivery profiles. The material ensures consistency across various therapeutic delivery systems and clinical applications.

Omeprazole sodium is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. It is available in pharmaceutical-grade specifications aligned with USP and BP monograph requirements for API use.

Packaging is typically offered in controlled, moisture-protected formats suited to GMP manufacturing environments. This ensures the stability and integrity of the chemical during long-term storage and international transport.

description:
1-(4-tert-Butylphenyl)-3-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1,3-propanediol (CAS 955359-35-0 ) is a specialty diol intermediate used in pharmaceutical synthesis and life sciences research. It functions as a chiral building block and carrier component in the development of active pharmaceutical ingredients and investigational compounds.

In pharmaceutical synthesis, it serves as a structural intermediate for constructing complex molecular frameworks where both the tert-butylphenyl and methoxyphenyl moieties contribute to target binding profiles.

Biotechnology researchers use it in small-molecule libraries and screening programs where defined diol geometry is required for receptor interaction studies. Its bifunctional hydroxyl groups make it applicable as a carrier or solubilizing component.

This chemical is frequently utilized in experimental formulation work. Contract research and API development organizations source it for route scouting and process chemistry at early development stages to ensure efficient synthesis pathways.

Supplied as a solid, it is typically handled under standard laboratory storage conditions for research-grade diol intermediates. It is available at research and development scale from specialty fine chemical suppliers.

Quantities range from milligram to multi-gram lots depending on the specific project needs. Purity specifications are generally confirmed by HPLC, with certificates of analysis provided to meet pharmaceutical procurement and QA documentation requirements.

name: Coco-caprylate
description:
Coco-caprylate (CAS 95912-86-0 ) is a lightweight ester derived from coconut fatty alcohols and caprylic acid, used as an emollient, carrier, and skin-feel modifier in cosmetic formulations.

It delivers a dry, non-greasy skin feel that synthetic silicones traditionally provided, making it a preferred choice in clean-label and silicone-free product development for modern brands.

In skincare and color cosmetics, this ingredient functions as a spreading agent and emollient base in serums, foundations, and sunscreens, improving texture without any unwanted heaviness.

It acts as a solvent and carrier for UV filters, pigments, and active ingredients, enabling uniform dispersion across formulations. In hair care, it is used in leave-on treatments and sprays.

This ester provides lightweight lubrication without residue buildup. Industrial and cosmetic-grade lubricant formulations also use it where a bio-based, low-viscosity ester is needed for surface slip.

The product is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications to meet the requirements of personal care manufacturers and formulators.

Standard packaging includes drums and IBCs, with bulk quantities available for commercial procurement. Our supply chain ensures consistent quality and availability for large-scale industrial manufacturing needs.

name: Cetyl Palmitate
description:
Cetyl Palmitate (CAS 95912-87-1 ), also known as hexadecyl hexadecanoate, is a synthetic wax ester derived from cetyl alcohol and palmitic acid. It functions as an emollient, emulsifier, and consistency agent across personal care and industrial formulations.

Buyers source it primarily to adjust texture, improve skin feel, and provide lubrication in finished products. In cosmetics and skincare, it is used to build structure in creams, lotions, and lip products.

This ingredient contributes a smooth, non-greasy skin feel without heavy occlusion. Sunscreen and color cosmetic formulators use it to stabilize emulsions and control viscosity at low use levels.

In industrial lubricants and metalworking fluids, it acts as a base wax component where controlled slip and film formation are required. This makes it a versatile choice for various manufacturing sectors.

Textile and leather finishing operations use it as a softening and lubricating agent to improve surface handle and processing performance. It is highly valued for its consistent chemical stability.

The material is supplied as a white to off-white waxy solid, typically in flake or pastille form for ease of handling and melting. It is available in cosmetic-grade and technical-grade specifications.

Cosmetic grades commonly meet Ph.Eur. and USP standards to ensure high purity for sensitive applications. Packaging ranges from cartons to bulk pallet quantities depending on volume.

name: Isotridecyl C16-18 fatty acids esters
description:
Isotridecyl C16-18 fatty acids esters (CAS 95912-88-2 ), commercially available as Radia 7513, is a synthetic ester produced from isotridecanol and C16-18 fatty acids. It functions as a lubricant base fluid and plasticizer across industrial formulations.

This chemical is preferred where oxidative stability and low volatility are procurement priorities. In metalworking and industrial lubrication, it serves as a base or co-base fluid in cutting fluids, hydraulic oils, and gear lubricants.

The ester is highly valued in applications where biodegradability and thermal stability are required. Coatings formulators incorporate it as a plasticizing additive to improve film flexibility and substrate adhesion without compromising durability.

In adhesives and sealants, it acts as a softener to adjust rheology and extend open time in both hot-melt and solvent-based systems. Polymer and elastomer compounders use it to improve processability and flexibility in PVC and rubber compounds.

Isotridecyl C16-18 fatty acids esters is supplied as a clear liquid. It is available in technical grade , the standard specification for industrial lubricant, coatings, and polymer applications.

name: Allyl methacrylate
description:
Allyl methacrylate (CAS 96-05-9 ), commonly abbreviated as AMA and sold under the trade name Ageflex AMA, is a bifunctional monomer carrying two distinct polymerizable groups.

This dual reactivity makes it a preferred cross-linking agent in polymer synthesis, where controlled network density and cure response are critical to end-product performance.

In coating formulations, AMA introduces cross-link density that improves hardness, chemical resistance, and adhesion to demanding substrates including metals and plastics.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it into acrylic and methacrylate systems to tune cohesive strength and flexibility across a range of cure chemistries.

Electronics producers use AMA in photoresists and encapsulant resins where precise cross-link architecture determines pattern resolution and long-term dielectric stability.

In plastics and polymer compounding, it functions as a reactive modifier to compatibilize blends or graft functional groups onto polymer backbones.

Allyl methacrylate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically inhibited with hydroquinone monomethyl ether to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport.

It is available in technical and monomer-grade specifications, with purity levels commonly at 98% or higher. Packaging ranges from drum quantities to ISO tank for bulk procurement.

1,2,3-Trichloropropane (CAS 96-18-4 ), also known as glyceryl trichlorohydrin and allyl trichloride, is a chlorinated solvent and chemical intermediate used across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and polymer manufacturing.

It functions primarily as a reactive solvent and building block in multi-step synthesis processes. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as an intermediate in the synthesis of active ingredients requiring halogenated carbon frameworks.

Agrochemical producers use it as a precursor in the preparation of certain pesticide and herbicide compounds. In polymer chemistry, it contributes to the production of epichlorohydrin-derived resins and specialty polymers.

These applications often require trifunctional chlorinated intermediates to achieve specific chemical structures. Its solvent properties also support extraction and reaction processes in fine chemical production where chlorinated media are specified.

name: Diethyl ketone
description:
Diethyl ketone ( CAS 96-22-0 ), also known as DEK or propione, is a mid-chain ketone solvent used across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and flavor applications. It combines effective solvency with a characteristic ethereal, fruity odor.

This chemical is useful in both formulation and flavoring contexts. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, DEK functions as a process solvent for active ingredient synthesis and recrystallization steps where controlled evaporation is required.

Flavor houses incorporate it as a flavoring agent in food products. Its clean, acetone-like yet fruity character contributes to artificial fruit, dairy, and confectionery profiles in various food-grade applications.

In personal care and cosmetic formulations, it acts as a carrier solvent for resins, waxes, and film-forming polymers. It is frequently utilized in nail care and specialty coating products for industrial use.

name: Methyl ethyl ketoxime
description:
Methyl ethyl ketoxime (CAS 96-29-7 ), commonly known as MEKO or 2-butanone oxime, is an oxime compound used primarily as a skinning inhibitor and anti-skinning agent in solvent-based coatings and alkyd systems.

This prevents surface skin formation before the product is applied during container storage. Printing ink manufacturers use it to extend shelf life in oxidatively drying ink systems without compromising cure performance.

Once the ink is exposed to air, the drying process proceeds as intended. In silicone sealants and adhesive formulations, MEKO acts as a crosslinker and release agent for various industrial applications.

This enables moisture-cure systems to achieve controlled adhesion profiles. It also functions as a catalyst precursor and intermediate in specialty chemical synthesis for diverse manufacturing sectors.

Methyl ethyl ketoxime is supplied as a clear liquid in standard industrial packaging, including drums and IBC containers. Technical grade is the predominant commercial specification for this material.

Textile and leather processors use methyl acrylate-based polymers as finishing agents that improve fabric hand, durability, and surface uniformity. These treatments provide superior resistance to wear and environmental factors during use.

Ectoine (CAS 96702-03-3 ) is a naturally derived amino acid derivative produced by extremophilic bacteria as a stress-protection mechanism. In commercial applications, it functions as a highly effective cellular protectant and humectant.

This specialty chemical stabilizes proteins, membranes, and biological structures under environmental stress conditions. In personal care formulations, it is incorporated into moisturizers, anti-aging creams, and sun-care products.

The ingredient protects skin cells from UV radiation, pollution, and osmotic stress. Sensitive skin and barrier-repair products rely on it to reduce inflammatory responses triggered by environmental aggressors.

In biotechnology, it stabilizes enzymes, vaccines, and diagnostic reagents during processing, lyophilization, and long-term storage. This reduces activity loss without the need for synthetic additives.

It also appears in eye drops and nasal sprays as a membrane-protective agent. Its ability to shield epithelial cells from irritants supports product efficacy claims in medical device and pharmaceutical sectors.

The product is supplied as a white crystalline powder with high purity grades suitable for cosmetic and biotechnology applications. Cosmetic-grade material is the most commercially prevalent form available.

Specifications are typically aligned to manufacturer-defined standards given the absence of a pharmacopoeial monograph. Fermentation-derived material from certified production processes is the market standard.

Buyers should confirm microbial source and production documentation when qualifying suppliers. This ensures the material meets the rigorous safety and performance requirements for high-end formulations.

name: Dichlorophen
description:
Dichlorophen (CAS 97-23-4 ) is a chlorinated bisphenol compound used industrially as a broad-spectrum biocide and preservative. It controls microbial and fungal growth across personal care, agricultural, and water treatment applications.

In personal care formulations, it functions as a preservative in shampoos, creams, and topical products where fungal and bacterial contamination must be controlled. Reliable antimicrobial performance is a key requirement.

Agricultural products utilize it as an active ingredient in antifungal treatments for crops and as a component in veterinary antiparasitic preparations. It is highly effective in these specialized environments.

Water treatment operations incorporate it to suppress algae and microbial biofilm formation in industrial water systems and cooling towers. This ensures the efficiency and safety of large-scale industrial cooling processes.

It also serves as a pharmaceutical intermediate in the synthesis of antiparasitic active substances, supporting API manufacturing pipelines. This versatility makes it a valuable chemical for various synthesis routes.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include technical and pharmaceutical-grade material, with specifications aligned to USP and BP requirements.

Quality standards may also align with Ph.Eur. , EP , or FCC depending on the regulated end uses. Packaging typically ranges from kilogram-scale laboratory quantities to bulk industrial orders.

The material is handled according to strict safety protocols depending on the intended application and regulatory context. This ensures consistent quality for all industrial and pharmaceutical customers.

name: Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside
description:
Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside ( CAS 97-30-3 ), also known as alpha-Methylglucoside, is a sugar-derived glycoside used across personal care, pharmaceutical, and food applications.

It functions as a humectant, chelating agent, and stabilizer, helping formulators manage moisture retention and ingredient compatibility in finished products. In cosmetic formulations, it acts as a humectant.

This material binds moisture to skin, supporting hydration claims in creams, serums, and lotions. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a stabilizing excipient in liquid and solid dosage forms.

In these applications, controlled hygroscopicity and compatibility with active ingredients are priorities. In food and nutrition, it serves chelation and antioxidant-stabilizing functions.

This helps protect sensitive ingredients from metal-catalyzed degradation in processed formulations. It also appears in specialty polyol synthesis, where its hydroxyl-rich structure is valuable.

The compound serves as a building block for surfactants and polyurethane intermediates. Methyl alpha-D-glucopyranoside is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule.

Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available, with material commonly tested against USP or FCC standards depending on the target application.

Bulk quantities are standard for industrial procurement, with smaller quantities available for formulation development. This ensures flexibility for both large-scale production and R&D.

name: Eugenol
description:
Eugenol (CAS 97-53-0 ), also known as p-Allylguaiacol, is a naturally derived phenolic compound extracted primarily from clove oil and used across flavoring, fragrance, and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

FEMA 2467 recognized, it functions as a flavoring agent, fragrance ingredient, and antioxidant stabilizer in a broad range of finished products for various industrial sectors.

In food and beverage production, eugenol delivers characteristic clove and spice notes and is used to flavor confectionery, baked goods, and meat products under regulatory approval.

Personal care and cosmetic formulators incorporate it into perfumes, dental care products, and topical preparations for its fragrance contribution and antioxidant stabilizing effect in formulations.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use eugenol as an active and excipient ingredient in dental cements, analgesic formulations, and antiseptic preparations for professional medical and dental use.

In printing and packaging, it functions as a UV stabilizer and antioxidant additive to protect ink systems and coatings from oxidative degradation during the manufacturing process.

Eugenol is supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard commercial packaging. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available, with material conforming to FCC standards.

Material also conforms to BP and Ph. Eur. standards depending on the application. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial uses such as ink and coating stabilization.

name: Isoeugenol
description:
Isoeugenol (CAS 97-54-1 ), also known by its FEMA 2468 designation and commercially as 4-Propenylguaiacol, is a naturally derived phenolic compound sourced from essential oils and produced synthetically for industrial supply.

It functions primarily as a fragrance ingredient and flavoring agent across personal care, food, and industrial applications. In fragrance formulation, it contributes warm, spicy, carnation-like notes to fine perfumes and soaps.

The compound is used in cosmetic products where it also provides antioxidant stabilization to the finished formula. Food manufacturers use it as an approved flavoring to impart clove and spice character in baked goods and confectionery.

In beverages, it provides a distinct aromatic profile. In polymer and plastics processing, its phenolic structure supports UV stabilization and antioxidant protection, extending the service life of polymer compounds exposed to light and heat.

Printing ink formulators incorporate it as a stabilizer to protect resin systems and colorants from oxidative degradation during storage and application. This ensures the longevity and quality of industrial coatings and inks.

The product is supplied as a pale yellow to amber liquid. Standard commercial grades include food-grade material meeting FCC specifications and fragrance-grade product conforming to industry purity requirements.

Technical-grade material is available for polymer and industrial applications where food or cosmetic compliance is not required. This versatile chemical serves a wide range of manufacturing needs across multiple global sectors.

name: Allantoin
description:
Allantoin (CAS 97-59-6 ) is a naturally derived heterocyclic compound used across pharmaceutical and personal care manufacturing. Known commercially as Septalan, Sebical, and Psoralon, it functions as a skin-conditioning agent.

It acts as a keratolytic agent, promoting cell renewal and tissue repair in topical formulations. In pharmaceutical topical preparations, it is incorporated into wound-healing creams and ointments.

Dermatological treatments utilize this compound where it accelerates epithelial regeneration. Personal care manufacturers use it in moisturizers, anti-aging serums, and after-sun products to soothe skin.

Shampoos and scalp treatments rely on this ingredient to condition the scalp and reduce flaking. It is a staple in medicated hair care lines and appears in lip care products and baby formulations.

Mildness and skin tolerance are primary formulation requirements for these sensitive applications. The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder, the standard physical form across all grades.

Pharmaceutical-grade material is available to USP , BP , and Ph.Eur. specifications. These grades meet the purity requirements of regulated drug product manufacturers globally.

Cosmetic-grade material is also widely offered and is the predominant grade used in personal care formulation. It remains a versatile and essential component for modern dermatological and cosmetic science.

name: Ethyl methacrylate
description:
Ethyl methacrylate (CAS 97-63-2 ), commonly abbreviated as EMA, is a reactive methacrylate monomer used as a building block in polymer synthesis and as a flavoring agent in food applications.

It functions as a polymerizable unit in acrylic and methacrylic resin systems, and at trace levels contributes fruity, rum-like flavor notes to food and beverage formulations.

In polymer manufacturing, EMA is incorporated into acrylic emulsions, copolymers, and thermoplastic resins to modify flexibility, adhesion, and film-forming characteristics in coatings and sealants.

Its reactivity profile makes it suitable for cross-linking and curing systems where controlled glass transition temperature is a formulation target for industrial applications.

In plastics compounding, it serves as a comonomer to improve impact resistance and processing behavior in specialty polymer blends and various high-performance materials.

At food-grade purity, EMA is used by flavor houses as a character-impact compound in artificial fruit and dairy flavor compositions to enhance specific aromatic profiles.

Ethyl methacrylate is supplied as a stabilized liquid, typically inhibited with hydroquinone monomethyl ether to prevent premature polymerization during storage and transport.

Technical and polymer grades are the most common commercial forms, with purity levels typically at 99% or higher, meeting rigorous industrial and chemical manufacturing requirements.

name: Itaconic acid
description:
Itaconic acid (CAS 97-65-4 ) is a bio-based unsaturated dicarboxylic acid produced through fungal fermentation, positioning it as a renewable alternative to petrochemical monomers in polymer synthesis.

Its reactive double bond and dual carboxylic groups make it a sought-after building block for specialty resins, coatings, and superabsorbent materials used across various industrial sectors.

In polymer and resin manufacturing, it is copolymerized with acrylic acid, styrene, or vinyl acetate to modify adhesion, flexibility, and hydrophilicity in coatings, binders, and pressure-sensitive adhesives.

Superabsorbent polymer producers incorporate it to tune water absorption performance in hygiene and agricultural products. In personal care, it functions as a co-monomer in film-forming polymers.

Food and flavor applications use it as an acidulant and flavoring agent, where its mild acidity profile suits beverage and confectionery systems requiring precise pH control and stability.

The material is supplied as a white crystalline powder in bags, supersacks, and bulk quantities suited to industrial procurement volumes. Standard commercial grades include technical and FCC specifications.

Purity levels are typically at 99% or above for most applications. Fermentation-derived material dominates the market, and buyers should confirm feedstock origin with suppliers for bio-based claims.

name: L-malic acid
description:
L-malic acid ( CAS 97-67-6 ), also known as L-hydroxysuccinic acid, is a naturally occurring organic acid used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. It functions primarily as an acidulant, pH regulator, and flavor enhancer.

This compound delivers a smooth, tart taste profile preferred over sharper mineral acids in many formulations. In food and beverage production, it acidulates fruit-flavored confectionery, soft drinks, and low-calorie products.

Its lingering tartness often outperforms citric acid in specific applications. Pharmaceutical formulators use it to adjust pH in oral solutions, effervescent tablets, and chewable dosage forms where taste masking is critical.

In personal care, it acts as a pH buffer in leave-on skin formulations and mild chemical exfoliant systems. Its antimicrobial contribution also supports preservation in acidified food systems and topical cosmetic products.

L-malic acid is supplied as a white crystalline powder or granule. Standard grades include food-grade ( FCC ), pharmaceutical-grade ( USP / BP ), and technical-grade for industrial applications.

Packaging typically ranges from 25 kg bags to bulk quantities. Food and pharma grades are supported by full documentation including certificates of analysis and origin to ensure compliance with global safety standards.

name: Tetramethylthiuram monosulfide
description:
Tetramethylthiuram monosulfide ( CAS 97-74-5 ), commercially known as TMTM or Unads, is an organosulfur accelerator used primarily in rubber vulcanization and crop protection formulations.

Unlike its disulfide counterpart, the monosulfide structure offers a distinct cure profile suited to specific processing requirements. In rubber compounding, it functions as a primary or secondary accelerator.

This chemical enables controlled cure rates in natural and synthetic rubber goods including seals, hoses, and molded components. It is also used in agricultural formulations as a fungicide and seed treatment agent.

The product targets soil-borne pathogens in cereal and vegetable crops. Polymer stabilization is another application where it acts as an antioxidant additive in plastic compounds for long-term thermal stability.

In latex systems, it contributes to prevulcanization control, giving formulators tighter command over gel formation and final product consistency. This ensures high performance in specialized manufacturing environments.

The material is supplied as a pale yellow to off-white powder, the standard physical form for rubber and agricultural end uses. Technical grade is the predominant commercial specification for industrial use.

Purity is typically confirmed by active content assay to meet industry requirements. Pre-dispersed masterbatch forms are available for rubber processing applications where dust-free handling is a plant requirement.

name: Disulfiram
description:
Disulfiram (CAS 97-77-8 ), also known commercially as Tetraethylthiuram Disulfide or TETD, is an organosulfur compound with established roles across rubber manufacturing and pharmaceutical production.

It functions primarily as a vulcanization accelerator, biocide, and active pharmaceutical ingredient precursor. In rubber and polymer processing, it acts as an ultra-fast vulcanization accelerator for various applications.

This compound enables rapid crosslinking in latex and dry rubber compounds used in gloves, seals, and industrial goods. Pharmaceutical manufacturers source it as an API or intermediate for alcohol-aversion therapy formulations.

Consistent purity and specification compliance are critical to regulatory approval in these medical contexts. As an industrial biocide and antifungal agent, it is incorporated into preservation systems for coatings and adhesives.

It is also used in agricultural products and functions as an antioxidant stabilizer in certain polymer formulations. This protects materials against oxidative degradation during both processing and long-term storage.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline powder. Standard grades include technical-grade material for rubber and industrial applications, alongside pharmaceutical-grade product meeting USP and BP specifications.

name: Isobutyl methacrylate

Isobutyl methacrylate (CAS 97-86-9 ), commonly abbreviated as IBMA, is a methacrylate monomer used to build flexibility, adhesion, and hardness balance into polymer systems.

In architectural and industrial coatings, IBMA is copolymerized to tune film hardness and outdoor durability without sacrificing flexibility. Automotive refinish formulators incorporate it into acrylic resins.

Controlled glass transition temperature is critical to coating performance in these applications. In pressure-sensitive and structural adhesives, it contributes to tack and cohesive strength.

This occurs when the monomer is balanced against harder or softer comonomers. Printing inks and packaging lacquers use IBMA-based copolymers to achieve adhesion to difficult substrates.

These substrates often include various films and foils used in the packaging sector. Isobutyl methacrylate is supplied as a clear liquid, typically inhibited with MEHQ to prevent polymerization.

Hydroquinone monomethyl ether ensures stability during storage and transport. It is available in technical and monomer-grade specifications suited to industrial polymerization applications.

Standard packaging includes drums and ISO tank containers, with bulk quantities available for high-volume polymer producers requiring consistent material for large-scale manufacturing.

Pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealant formulations incorporate BMA to balance tack and cohesive strength across a range of substrates, ensuring long-lasting bonds in diverse environmental conditions.

Polymer manufacturers use it to produce acrylic resins for injection-molded plastics and extrusion compounds where controlled softness is required for the final structural components.

It forms covalent bridges between polymer chains, improving mechanical strength, solvent resistance, and dimensional stability in cured networks for industrial use.

In acrylic and methacrylic resin systems, EGDMA controls network density, allowing formulators to tune hardness and swelling behavior in contact lenses and dental composites.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers incorporate it to enhance cohesive strength and chemical resistance in structural bonding applications and specialty optical materials.

UV-curable coatings for printing and packaging rely on EGDMA to accelerate cure response and improve surface hardness on films, labels, and flexible substrates.

It also functions as a crosslinker in suspension and emulsion polymerization to produce ion-exchange resins and controlled-release polymer beads for filtration.

EGDMA is supplied as a clear liquid, typically stabilized with a polymerization inhibitor such as MEHQ for safe storage and transport in various environments.

Standard commercial grades are available at purities of 98% and higher, with technical and high-purity grades offered to meet specific polymerization requirements.

name: Triethylborane
description:
Triethylborane (CAS 97-94-9 ), commonly referenced in procurement as TEB, is a pyrophoric organoboron compound used as a radical initiator and catalyst in demanding synthesis and polymerization processes.

Its reactivity with oxygen makes it a controlled but highly effective trigger for reactions that require precise initiation under low-temperature or inert-atmosphere conditions.

In aerospace and defense, TEB is the standard ignition initiator for jet engines and scramjet systems, where reliable ignition at extreme conditions is critical to program qualification.

Polymer manufacturers use it to initiate radical polymerization of fluoropolymers and specialty resins, particularly where conventional peroxide initiators fail to perform.

Pharmaceutical and biotech synthesis teams employ TEB as a boron source and Lewis acid catalyst in carbon–carbon bond-forming reactions, including hydroboration sequences for chiral intermediate production.

It also functions as a co-catalyst with transition metal complexes in Ziegler-Natta and related polymerization systems for polyolefin production across various industrial sectors.

Triethylborane is supplied as a liquid, typically in hydrocarbon solvent solutions at concentrations of 1 M in hexane or THF, suited for controlled dispensing in sensitive reactions.

Neat material is available for industrial-scale users with appropriate handling infrastructure. Supply is generally positioned at research and high-purity technical grades for global distribution.

name: Phosphatidylcholine
description:
Phosphatidylcholine (CAS 97281-44-2 ), commonly sourced from egg yolk or soy lecithin, is a phospholipid used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing as a high-performance emulsifier.

It is the primary functional component in lecithin concentrates and is traded separately where higher purity is required. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it is the principal lipid used to construct liposomal drug delivery systems.

This material enables encapsulation of both hydrophilic and lipophilic active compounds. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into skin creams and serums where it stabilizes emulsions and supports transdermal penetration.

Food producers use it to emulsify fat-in-water systems in products such as dressings, spreads, and infant formula. In biotechnology, it is a critical raw material for producing lipid nanoparticles used in delivery platforms.

Phosphatidylcholine is supplied as a viscous liquid, soft paste, or lyophilized powder depending on concentration and processing method. Standard grades include food-grade, USP , and research-grade specifications.

Purity levels typically range from 70% to 98% phosphatidylcholine content. Egg-derived and soy-derived variants are both commercially available, with sourcing choice often driven by regulatory or allergen requirements.

Its solid physical form offers a distinct formulation advantage over liquid alternatives. Home care manufacturers incorporate it into dishwashing powders, laundry bars, and concentrated cleaning tablets for its strong degreasing performance.

Textile processors use it in scouring baths to strip natural oils and processing residues from raw fibers before dyeing. In paper and leather processing, it supports degreasing and wetting steps where consistent foam control is required.

Sodium coco sulfate is supplied primarily as a white to off-white powder, flake, or noodle form, suited to solid formulation manufacturing. Technical and cosmetic grades are the most commonly traded varieties available.

description:
Shellac wax (CAS 97766-50-2 ) is the refined wax fraction separated from raw shellac resin during dewaxing processes. It functions as a surface modifier and rheology agent across food, cosmetic, and industrial coating applications.

Its high melting point and film-forming characteristics make it commercially distinct from standard shellac. In food processing, it is applied as a glazing and coating agent on confectionery, fresh produce, and dietary supplements.

These applications help to control moisture loss and improve surface appearance. Cosmetic formulators incorporate it into lipsticks, balms, and solid stick formats to adjust hardness, texture, and product stability.

In printing inks and packaging coatings, it contributes to surface slip, rub resistance, and gloss control on flexible and rigid substrates. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance industrial formulations.

Adhesive and sealant manufacturers use it as a rheology modifier to adjust viscosity and prevent settling in hot-melt and solvent-based systems. It is supplied as a hard, brittle solid, typically in flake or powder form.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are the most commercially available. Technical-grade material is also offered for industrial coating and ink applications where specific purity levels are required.

Purity and wax content vary by supplier and processing method, making certificate of analysis review standard practice for procurement. This ensures the material meets the necessary regulatory and performance benchmarks.

Contact us for supply of Shellac wax

name: Valerian extract
description:
Valerian extract (CAS 97927-02-1 ), derived from Valeriana officinalis, is a standardized botanical extract used across food, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries. It delivers the characteristic earthy, woody aromatic profile of valerian root in a concentrated form.

In dietary supplement manufacturing, valerian extract is incorporated into tablets, capsules, and softgels targeting relaxation and sleep support positioning. This represents one of the highest-volume botanical supplement categories globally.

Functional food and beverage formulators use it as a flavoring agent in herbal teas, wellness shots, and fortified drinks where botanical authenticity is a label differentiator. It provides a unique profile for modern wellness products.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers apply it in standardized herbal medicinal products, where consistent valerenic acid content is critical for batch-to-batch compliance. This ensures the extract meets rigorous industrial standards.

In personal care, it appears in aromatherapy blends and topical formulations where its distinctive scent profile contributes to the finished fragrance character. It is valued for its traditional aromatic properties in these applications.

Valerian extract is supplied as a dry powder, liquid extract, or soft extract, with dry forms being most common in supplement and pharma applications. Standard grades include extracts defined by valerenic acid content.

Non-standardized full-spectrum preparations are also available for flavoring use. Food-grade and pharmaceutical-grade specifications are available to meet FCC and Ph.Eur. requirements for global distribution.

Contact us for supply of Valerian extract

name: Boswellia serrata extract
description:
Boswellia serrata extract (CAS 97952-72-2 ), also marketed as Salai extract and Frankincense Resin, is a standardized botanical derived from the resin of the Boswellia serrata tree. It is commercially valued for its boswellic acid content, which drives demand across nutraceutical, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic supply chains.

In dietary supplement manufacturing, it is formulated into capsules, tablets, and softgels targeting joint and mobility support categories. This represents one of the highest-volume botanical supplement segments globally for industrial buyers.

Functional food and nutraceutical producers incorporate it into fortified powders and health beverages where antioxidant-positioned botanicals command premium positioning. These applications require consistent solubility and potency for large-scale production.

Cosmetic formulators use it in anti-aging creams and serums, where boswellic acid content supports claims around skin conditioning and oxidative stress protection. It is a key ingredient for high-end personal care product lines.

Pharmaceutical-grade extracts are also evaluated in topical and oral dosage forms requiring documented boswellic acid standardization. These materials must adhere to rigorous quality control protocols to ensure safety and efficacy.

Boswellia serrata extract is supplied as a fine powder, typically standardized to defined boswellic acid concentrations. Premium supplement grades are commonly standardized to 65% or higher to meet industry benchmarks.

Food-grade and cosmetic-grade specifications are available, with pharmaceutical-grade material meeting stricter purity and heavy metal limits. This ensures compliance with international safety regulations and manufacturing requirements.

Packaging ranges from kilogram quantities for formulators to bulk metric-ton supply for large-scale manufacturers. We provide reliable logistics for global distribution to meet your specific production timelines and volume needs.

name: Furfuryl alcohol
description:
Furfuryl alcohol (CAS 98-00-0 ), also known as FA, is a bio-based furan derivative produced from agricultural residues such as sugarcane bagasse and corn cobs. In industry, it functions as a reactive solvent in resin systems.

It also serves as a flavoring agent in food and fragrance applications. In foundry and resin manufacturing, FA is the primary monomer in furan no-bake binder systems used to produce sand cores and molds for metal casting.

Food and beverage producers use it as a FEMA 2491 -approved flavoring to impart roasted, coffee-like notes in baked goods, confectionery, and beverages. This versatile chemical is essential for high-performance industrial resins.

In fragrance formulation, it contributes warm, caramel-adjacent character to personal care products including perfumes and cosmetic blends. It also functions as a solvent and carrier in specialty coatings and adhesive formulations.

This material is particularly valued where compatibility with furan-based systems is required. Furfuryl alcohol is supplied as a clear to amber liquid in drum and IBC quantities for various industrial needs.

Bulk tanker options are available for high-volume industrial buyers. Technical grade is the standard offering for resin and foundry applications, ensuring consistent performance in manufacturing environments.

Food-grade material meeting FEMA specifications is available for flavor and fragrance end uses. Our supply chain ensures that all products meet rigorous quality standards for global distribution and safety compliance.

name: Furfural
description:
Furfural (CAS 98-01-1 ), also known as 2-Furfuraldehyde, is a bio-based aldehyde derived from agricultural byproducts such as corn cobs, oat hulls, and sugarcane bagasse.

In industry, it functions as a flavoring agent and a platform chemical for producing downstream derivatives used across food, fragrance, and specialty chemical sectors.

In food and beverage, it contributes caramel, almond, and bread-like notes to flavor formulations, recognized under FEMA 2489 for use in approved concentrations.

Fragrance formulators incorporate it into compositions targeting warm, baked, or woody scent profiles for personal care products including creams, lotions, and hair care.

It also serves as a selective solvent in petroleum refining for separating aromatic from aliphatic hydrocarbons, which represents a major industrial consumption route.

Furfural is further used as a chemical intermediate in the production of furfuryl alcohol, tetrahydrofuran, and furan resins applied in foundry binders and adhesives.

The product is supplied as a liquid, typically in drums, intermediate bulk containers, and bulk tankers for large-volume buyers across various industrial sectors.

Standard commercial grades include technical grade and refined grades meeting food and flavor industry purity requirements and regional flavor regulations.

name: Benzenesulfonyl chloride
description:
Benzenesulfonyl chloride (CAS 98-09-9 ), also known as phenylsulfonyl chloride, is a reactive sulfonylating agent used across pharmaceutical synthesis, dye manufacturing, and specialty chemical production.

It introduces sulfonyl groups into organic molecules, enabling the construction of intermediates that would otherwise require multiple synthetic steps. In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key building block.

This chemical is essential for synthesizing sulfonamide drugs, protecting groups, and active pharmaceutical intermediates requiring controlled sulfonylation. Dye and pigment producers use it to manufacture azo dyes.

These reactive dyes are widely applied in textile and leather finishing. Water treatment chemical formulators incorporate sulfonyl chloride-derived compounds as biocidal actives targeting microbial control.

These applications are critical for industrial water systems. Paper processing operations also draw on sulfonyl-based chemistry for surface treatment agents that improve wet strength and resistance properties.

The product is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid in standard drum and IBC packaging suited to bulk industrial procurement. It is available in technical grade and high-purity grades.

These grades meet pharmaceutical intermediate specifications, with purity typically confirmed by GC analysis. Buyers should confirm moisture-controlled packaging requirements with suppliers for safety.

The product is sensitive to hydrolysis during storage and transit. Proper handling ensures the material maintains its chemical integrity for use in sensitive manufacturing and synthesis processes.

name: Benzenesulfonic acid
description:
Benzenesulfonic acid (CAS 98-11-3 ), also known as phenylsulfonic acid, is a strong aromatic sulfonic acid used industrially as a catalyst, pH regulator, and intermediate in the synthesis of dyes, pigments, and surface-active agents.

Its acid strength and water solubility make it a practical processing aid across several chemical manufacturing sectors. In dye and pigment manufacturing, it acts as a sulfonation intermediate and coupling agent.

This chemical directly influences color yield and batch consistency during production. Textile and leather processors use it for pH control during dyeing and tanning operations, where precise acidity affects fiber uptake.

It ensures surface treatment uniformity across various materials. In coatings and resin systems, it functions as an acid catalyst for curing reactions, particularly in baking enamels and crosslinked polymer formulations.

Printing ink formulators incorporate it as a dispersing aid to stabilize pigment suspensions and improve ink flow on press. This versatility makes it a staple in high-performance industrial chemical applications.

Benzenesulfonic acid is supplied as an aqueous solution, most commonly at concentrations around 65–70%, and as a dry crystalline solid. Technical grade is the standard commercial form for industrial synthesis.

Higher-purity grades are available for catalyst and specialty chemical applications where consistent acid content and low impurity profiles are required. These standards ensure reliability in sensitive manufacturing environments.

name: 4-tert-butylcatechol
description:
4-tert-butylcatechol (CAS 98-29-3 ), commonly known as TBC or Synox TBC, is an industrial antioxidant and polymerization inhibitor used across polymer, monomer, and chemical manufacturing.

It prevents premature crosslinking and oxidative degradation during storage, transport, and processing of reactive chemical systems. This chemical is the inhibitor of choice for stabilizing vinyl monomers.

It is used for styrene, butadiene, and acrylates during bulk storage and pipeline transfer, where uninhibited polymerization would cause costly blockages and product loss in industrial systems.

In coatings and adhesive formulations, it extends shelf life by suppressing oxidative cure before application. Rubber and elastomer producers use it to control premature vulcanization and maintain processability.

At lower concentrations, it functions as an antioxidant in lubricant and metalworking fluid formulations. It protects base stocks from oxidative breakdown under high-temperature service conditions.

The product is supplied as a white to off-white crystalline solid, typically in flake or powder form. It is available in technical grade, which covers the majority of industrial inhibitor applications.

Bulk packaging in fiber drums and IBCs is standard, with smaller quantities available for laboratory and specialty use. This ensures safe handling and efficient transport for global chemical supply chains.

name: 3-nitrobenzenesulfonic acid
description:
3-Nitrobenzenesulfonic acid (CAS 98-47-5 ), also known as m-nitrobenzenesulfonic acid, is an aromatic sulfonic acid used primarily as a chemical intermediate and acid catalyst in organic synthesis.

Its combination of a strong acid group and a nitro substituent makes it a selective building block for producing more complex molecules across several manufacturing sectors.

In pharmaceutical manufacturing, it serves as a key intermediate in the synthesis of active pharmaceutical ingredients and fine chemicals, where controlled nitro group chemistry is required.

Dye and pigment producers use it as a coupling component or intermediate in the preparation of azo dyes applied to textile and leather substrates during the manufacturing process.

In textile processing, it functions as a dyeing auxiliary and pH modifier, improving dye uptake and fixation on fiber. Printing ink formulators also source it as a precursor for specialty colorants.

3-Nitrobenzenesulfonic acid is available commercially as a crystalline solid, typically supplied in powder or granule form. Standard supply concentrations include the anhydrous form and sodium salt derivatives.

Technical and pharmaceutical-intermediate grades are the most commonly traded. Packaging ranges from small laboratory quantities to bulk industrial lots depending on specific application requirements.

name: 4-tert-butylphenol
description:
4-tert-Butylphenol (CAS 98-54-4 ), commonly abbreviated as PTBP, is an alkylphenol intermediate used across resin synthesis, fragrance manufacturing, and polymer stabilization. It functions primarily as a chain-stopping agent in phenolic resin production.

This chemical serves as a building block for UV absorbers and antioxidants. PTBP is a key monomer in the production of para-tert-butylphenol-formaldehyde resins, which are used as tackifiers in neoprene-based contact adhesives.

These resins also act as bonding agents for rubber and leather. In coatings and lubricant additive manufacturing, it serves as a precursor to antioxidants and extreme-pressure additive packages for industrial use.

Fragrance compounders use PTBP (FEMA 3918 ) as a phenolic modifier to impart leather, floral, and animalic nuances. It is utilized in both fine fragrance and functional fragrance applications globally.

In UV stabilizer production, it acts as a starting material for benzophenone-type absorbers used in plastics and personal care formulations. This versatility makes it a staple in the specialty chemical sector.

4-tert-Butylphenol is supplied as white to off-white flakes or molten liquid for bulk shipment. Technical grade is the standard commercial specification, with purity typically at 99% minimum for industrial needs.

Packaging options generally include bags, drums, and isotanks for molten material. The material is handled according to strict safety protocols to ensure quality and stability during long-term storage and transport.

name: alpha-terpineol
description:
Alpha-terpineol (CAS 98-55-5 ), also known commercially as Terpineol, is a naturally derived monocyclic monoterpene alcohol used as a fragrance ingredient, flavor component, and solvent carrier across personal care and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

FEMA 3045 status confirms its recognized use in flavoring applications. Its clean, floral-lilac scent profile drives demand in both functional and aesthetic formulations across various industrial sectors.

In personal care, alpha-terpineol is incorporated into perfumes, soaps, lotions, and hair care products where it contributes a fresh, floral character while also enhancing the penetration of active ingredients through the skin.

Fragrance compounders use it as a building block for lily-of-the-valley and lilac accords in fine fragrance and household product lines. Pharmaceutical formulators rely on it as a solvent and carrier to improve delivery.

This compound helps the dispersibility of active compounds in topical preparations. In flavor applications, it appears in food and beverage systems at low use levels to impart subtle floral-citrus notes to the final product.

Alpha-terpineol is supplied as a colorless to pale yellow liquid. It is available in fragrance-grade and food-grade specifications, with food-grade material conforming to FCC standards for safety and purity.

Bulk supply is standard in drums and IBCs, with smaller packaging available for laboratory and development use. This ensures that both large-scale manufacturers and research facilities can access the material they need.

name: Parachlorobenzotrifluoride
description:
Parachlorobenzotrifluoride ( CAS 98-56-6 ), commonly known as PCBTF, is a high-performance exempt solvent used across coatings, chemical synthesis, and industrial cleaning applications.

Classified as a VOC-exempt solvent under U.S. EPA regulations, it offers formulators a compliant alternative to conventional aromatic solvents without sacrificing solvency strength.

In industrial and architectural coatings, PCBTF dissolves high-solids resins and pigment dispersions where regulatory VOC limits restrict conventional solvent use.

Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a reaction solvent and intermediate carrier in active ingredient synthesis, particularly where halogenated aromatic solvents are specified.

In the plastics and polymer sector, it functions as a process solvent for dissolving engineering resins and as a carrier in specialty polymer coatings applied to textiles.

name: 4-hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid
description:
4-Hydroxybenzenesulfonic acid (CAS 98-67-9 ), also known as phenolsulfonic acid or sulfocarbolic acid, is an aromatic sulfonic acid used across industrial processing and formulation chemistry.

It functions primarily as a pH buffer, UV stabilizer, and preservation agent in manufacturing workflows where precise acidity control and oxidative stability are required for the final product.

In textile dyeing and leather tanning, it acts as a fixative and pH regulator, improving dye uptake and process consistency across batch production cycles and large scale industrial operations.

Printing ink and packaging coating formulators incorporate it to stabilize pigment dispersions and extend shelf life against UV-induced degradation in various environmental conditions.

In personal care formulations, it supports preservation systems and contributes to UV stabilization in products where phenolic-based protection is commercially preferred by manufacturers.

Paper treatment processes use it as a buffering agent to control acidity during pulp processing and surface sizing, ensuring the structural integrity and quality of the finished paper goods.

This chemical is supplied as an aqueous solution, with 65–70% concentration being the most commonly traded commercial form for global distribution and bulk industrial procurement.

Technical grade is the standard offering for industrial applications in textiles, printing, and leather processing. Purity specifications may vary depending on specific application requirements.
